## Creating Custom Colors
  * To create a custom color:


  1. On the Color dialog box, click Define Custom Colors. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/cLeARYj7a4ZZINYfpimjYQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=d7754a54eb2ba6a3&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Select the basic color closest to the color you want.
  3. Move the cross hair or change color values—RGB (red, green, blue) or HLS (hue, saturation, and luminescence)—until the color in the Color|Solid box is what you want. 
  4. Click Add to Custom Colors. 
  5. Highlight the new custom color to select it.

## CSVerticalDatumConstants
The CSVerticalDatumConstants enumeration is used to interpret the VerticalDatum field of the [GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XwuKVI_U5ObpDp0hIkR1tA).   
|  Constant  |  Value  |  Meaning  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  csvdUserDefined  |  0  |  User-defined. With this setting the user is allowed to set height storage type.  |  
|  csvdNGVD29  |  1  |  National Geodetic Vertical Datum 1929. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdNAVD88  |  2  |  North American Vertical Datum 1988. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdAHD71  |  3  |  Australian Height Datum 1971. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdIGLD55  |  4  |  International Great Lakes 1955. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdONTGL  |  5  |  Ordnance Newlyn Third Geodetic Leveling. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdTsingtao  |  6  |  Tsingtao. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdUELN55  |  7  |  United European Leveling Network 1955. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdUELN73  |  8  |  United European Leveling Network 1973. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdUELN7381  |  9  |  United European Leveling Network 1973-1981. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdCVR28  |  10  |  Canadian Vertical Reference 1928. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdUELN9598  |  11  |  United European Leveling Network 1995-1998. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdIGLD85  |  12  |  International Great Lakes 1985. Implies orthometric height storage type.  |  
|  csvdNAD83  |  13  |  Height above GRS80 Ellipsoid, tied to the North American Datum 1983. Implies geometric height storage type.   |  
|  csvdGeoid  |  100  |  Height referenced to a geoid model such as NGS Geoid or NGA EGM 96. Implies orthometric height storage type.   |  
|  csvdEllipsoid  |  101  |  Height above an ellipsoid. Implies geometric height storage type.  |

## Defining an Attribute Filter
An attribute-filter is essentially a WHERE statement.
If you have a working knowledge of the syntax used to define SQL statements, you can type your SQL statement directly into the Filter field on the Filter dialog box. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255920?tocId=lDt97i5AOlTbfIljVCl9Bw) Only operators listed on the dialog box are supported. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/MfiJwk_5TxDmhV5K~yJ_Hw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=118165c04e1442ac&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
The Filter dialog box can be used to create ad hoc filters for display control.
If you do not have a working knowledge of SQL syntax, use the following procedure, keeping an eye on the position of the cursor in the Filter field because what you select is placed where the cursor is located. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255920?tocId=lDt97i5AOlTbfIljVCl9Bw): To change a legend item to display only a single feature, you can use the system feature identity key, G3E_FID as a filter. This attribute is not listed in the Attributes section of the filter dialog; however, you can type the value in the Filter field, for example, type G3E_FID = 213874. Only the component with this G3E_FID value displays. 
  * To define an attribute-filter:


  1. To clear an existing filter, click Clear. 
  2. Select an attribute and click the down arrow below the Attributes list. 
  3. Other [operators](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) are available from a drop-down list. If you select an operator from the drop-down list, click the down arrow below the operators. 
  4. To see a list of values associated with the attribute, click Show Values. 
  5. Select or type the value and click the down arrow below the Values list box. 
  6. Verify the syntax of the SQL statement and click OK.

## Dialog Tabs Metadata
To define a dialog tab, enter information in the following metadata tables:
  * [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) — Attributes displayed on a dialog tab must reference a field in a component. A one-to-one mapping between a dialog tab and a component is not required; therefore, a dialog tab can display several attributes from multiple components of the same feature. 
  * [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ) — Defines the tab and is uniquely identified by G3E_DTNO. There is one row for each dialog tab definition in this table. 
  * [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) — Defines the attributes displayed on each dialog tab. Each attribute defined in the G3E_TABATTRIBUTE table must also be defined in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table. 
  * [G3E_DIALOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) — Ties the dialog tabs to a particular feature. This table defines what features use what tabs and in what context they are used. The same dialog tab can be used more than once for different features and can be used in more than one context. The set of dialog tabs is grouped in this table through the G3E_DNO and the G3E_TYPE values. 


The following diagram shows the tables and the connecting columns required for dialog tab metadata. 
![dialogtab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/lYHGcWQDuWGG4hRaypW7iQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=f3614f215a0ea350&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

## DisplayScaleType
These are the DisplayScaleType enumeration values:  
|  Name  |  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  DisplayScaleMetadata  |  3  |  Applies the metadata setting for display scale. That is, whether display scale is on or off for a particular legend entry is controlled by the metadata for that legend entry.   |  
|  DisplayScaleOff  |  2  |  The associated data are displayed regardless of the display scale.  |  
|  DisplayScaleOn  |  1  |  The display scale range of each legend entry is applied to the display of the associated data, regardless of whether that the metadata of the legend entry specifies to use display scale or not.   |

## Interpreting Parameter Values
The analysis program interprets the strings specified in the G3E_VALUE column depending on the value type specified by G3E_VALUETYPE. It is important that value column values be populated properly:   
|  Value  |  Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Integer  |  A constant numeric string representing an integer (whole number) value that can be stored in a short integer variable (16 bits)   |  
|  Long integer  |  A constant numeric string representing an integer (whole number) value that can be stored in a long integer variable (32 bits)   |  
|  Single precision floating point  |  A constant numeric string representing a floating point number that can be stored in a single precision floating point variable   |  
|  Double precision floating point  |  A constant numeric string representing a floating point number that can be stored in a double precision floating point variable   |  
|  Text  |  A constant text string  |  
|  -1  |  Feature attribute  |  A long integer value corresponding to an attribute defined by the G3E_ANO column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE metadata table. This attribute value should be defined for all features that can map into this analysis object.   |  
|  -2  |  SQL lookup  |  A character value for an SQL SELECT statement defined in the G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL table that defines the value for this parameter. Multiple parameters can be determined from the same SQL statement. The SQL statement should use column aliases to specify the column or expression to map to each particular parameter that it defines.   |  
|  -3  |  Calculation interface  |  A numeric value identifying the functional interface to call for determining this parameter value. If this type is specified, the value in the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT column also is sent to the functional interface.   |  
|  -4  |  Child feature attribute  |  A long integer value corresponding to an attribute defined by the G3E_ANO column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE metadata table. This attribute value should be defined in the child feature for all features that can map into this analysis object. The attribute is found in the child feature of the analysis object.   |

## JobLifeCycle Workflow
JobLifeCycle is an executable program that performs batch processing activities on a job using a command argument. JobLifeCycle allows updates and state transitions to occur against a job that has been updated within a work management system. 
Workflow Overview
This is the general workflow for the JobLifeCycle program:
  1. A NetWorks Core work request is generated through a work management system interface. 
  2. A corresponding NetWorks Core job is created using a trigger or through the [Message Monitor service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ). 
  3. Design is done using the NetWorks Core application (placing features, modifying features, and so forth). 
  4. Updates are received from the work management system using triggers or Message Monitor service. These updates are flagged by entries being placed in the G3E_JOBSTATUS table along with the processing action that is to occur. 
  5. NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service queries the G3E_JOBSTATUS table and submits one of the records for [JobLifeCycle](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ID0egdkDcJ7NsZrC8TFpFw) to process by running the executable with Command line parameters. 
  6. JobLifeCycle determines the processing sequence and activity types by metadata settings and performs specified tasks. 
  7. Any processing errors are recorded in the [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE_ERROR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DisCYAkebrotuuwQPDrL9Q) table, except for errors that occur before a connection can be established. These errors are recorded in the Event Viewer > Application Log.

## Notes for NADCON NAD27 to NAD83 and NADCON NAD83 to HARN
NADCON is a datum transformation model for the conversion of point coordinates from the NAD27 datum to the NAD83 datum and vice versa, and from the NAD83 datum to the state High Accuracy Reference Network (HARN) and vice versa. 
The NADCON model is public-domain software from the National Geodetic Survey (NGS Version 2.10). This program is intended to be used to transform latitude and longitude coordinate values between the North American Datum of 1927 (NAD27) and the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD83) or vice versa, and between the North American Datum of 1983 (NAD83) and the High Accuracy Reference Network (HARN) or vice versa. This model can also transform data originally expressed in old island datums, such as those in Alaska and Hawaii, into data referenced to NAD83. 
Data for the following areas are currently available from NGS and are provided within NetWorks Core. 
Grid files for going between NAD27 and NAD83:  
|  Area  |  Description  |  File name  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Alaska  |  Alaska, including Aleutian Islands  |  alaska  |  
|  Alaska: St. George Island  |  Old island datum within Alaska  |  stgeorge  |  
|  Alaska: St. Lawrence Island  |  Old island datum within Alaska  |  stlrnc  |  
|  Alaska: St. Paul Island  |  Old island datum within Alaska  |  stpaul  |  
|  CONUS  |  Conterminous U.S. (lower 48 states)  |  conus  |  
|  Hawaiian Islands  |  Old Hawaiian datum  |  hawaii  |  
|  Puerto Rico and V.I.  |  Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands  |  prvi  |  
Data used in the above files for NADCON datum transformations is selected on an area-by-area basis.   
|  Example If you are performing a datum transformation within the U.S., data contained in the conus file is used in the transformation. However, the island datums of Alaska (St. Lawrence, St. George, and St. Paul) fall within the larger Alaska datum.   |  
| --- |  
When a point being transformed from NAD27 to NAD83 falls within multiple datums, the datum corresponding to the first file found in the list of file names in the /cssruntm/cfg/nadcon/area.par file is used. 
File listed in the delivered /nadcon/area.par file:
  * conus
  * prvistlrnc
  * stgeorge
  * stpaul
  * alaska
  * hawaii


To perform datum transformations for the three Alaska island datums using the Alaska datum instead of the island datums, the alaska entry would need to come before the island datum entries stlrnc, stgeorge, and stpaul. 
St. George Island and St. Paul Island are part of a region also known as the Priblof Islands. Two separate datums, one for each island, were available before NAD83. The old island datums are significantly different from NAD27. Be sure that the input data are consistent with the identified transformation data sets. The transformation of misidentified data can result in very large errors, for example, hundreds of meters.

The area.par file for the NAD83 to HARN datum transformation is /cssruntm/cfg/harn/area.par. The default file list is alphabetical. Because many regions overlap, you may need to rearrange the list to ensure that the needed region is being used for your area. Note that the HARN files for American Samoa are an exception to the general application of the NAD83 to HARN datum transformation, in that these grid files transform from the American Samoa 1962 datum to the NAD83 HARN datum (the original NAD83 datum was never applied to American Samoa). 
The accuracy of the transformations should be viewed with some caution. At the 67% confidence level, this method introduces approximately 0.15 meter uncertainty within the conterminous United States, 0.50 meter uncertainty within Alaska, 0.20 meter uncertainty within Hawaii, and 0.05 meter uncertainty within Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands. In areas of sparse geodetic data coverage, NADCON may yield less accurate results, but seldom in excess of 1.0 meter. Transformations between NAD83 and States/Regions with High Accuracy Reference Networks (HARNs) introduce approximately 0.05 meter uncertainty. Transformations between old datums (NAD27, Old Hawaiian, Puerto Rico, and so forth) and HARN could combine uncertainties (for example, NAD27 to HARN equals 0.15m + 0.05m = 0.2m). In near offshore regions, results are less accurate, but seldom in excess of 5.0 meters. Farther offshore NAD27 was undefined. Therefore, the NADCON computed transformations are extrapolations and no accuracy can be stated. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263654) NADCON cannot improve the accuracy of data. Stations that are originally third-order do not become first-order stations. NADCON is merely a tool for transforming coordinate values between datums. 
This program is based exclusively upon data within the official National Geodetic Reference System (NGRS). Data originating from stations not part of this official reference may not be compatible. Be sure that the data to be transformed is actually referenced to the NGRS.

Automatic Datum Transformations within the CoordSystemsMgr object:
When building AltCoordSystemPaths within a CoordSystemsMgr object, a DatumTransformation object may be automatically built. The algorithm for automatically building these datum transformations is controlled by the file cssruntm/cfg/autodt.ini. This file is well documented, and can be modified to change the algorithm.

## Notes for the Canadian National Transformation (2.0)
The Canadian National Transformation is a datum transformation model for the conversion of geographic points from the NAD27 datum to the NAD83 datum or vice versa, to match points obtained from the Canadian National Transformation PC program INTGRID version 2.0. 
This model was obtained from the Geodetic Survey Division, Geomatics Canada and has been implemented within NetWorks Core. 
The Canadian National Transformation performs a lookup of grid points within a binary grid file containing regularly spaced longitude and latitude shifts. The model then interpolates, using a bilinear interpolation algorithm within the appropriate quad to produce the shifts at a point. These shifts are then applied to the original coordinate to produce the transformed coordinate. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263653) Users of the Canadian National Transformation must obtain the required grid file, Ntv2_0.gsb, and place it in the /cssruntm/cfg/canada subdirectory under the folder where their NetWorks Core executable files reside. This grid file may be obtained from 
Geodetic Survey Division, Geomatics Canada
Natural Resources Canada
615 Booth Street
Ottawa, Ontario K1A0E9 CANADA
The Canadian National Transformation (version 2.0) has been adopted by the Australian Intergovernmental Committee on Surveying and Mapping (ICSM) as the official high-accuracy transformation between the old Australian datums (AGD66 or AGD84, depending upon location) and the new official datum (GDA94). Grid files are being published by regional authorities and are becoming available on the world-wide web. When completed, these are merged into a country-wide grid file which ICSM makes available. The use of the Canadian National Transformation model for Australia has been included in the default entries in the autodt.ini configuration file. However, users must obtain the needed grid file from the Australian authorities, place it in the cssruntm/cfg/canada folder, and edit the /cssruntm/cfg/canada/area.par file to reference the grid file by name. 
The Canadian National Transformation (version 2.0) has also been adopted by Land Information New Zealand (LINZ) as the official high-accuracy transformation between the old New Zealand Geodetic Datum 1949 and the new official datum (New Zealand Geodetic Datum 2000). A grid file is available from LINZ on the world-wide web. The use of the Canadian National Transformation model for New Zealand has been included in the default entries in the autodt.ini configuration file. However, users must obtain the needed grid file from LINZ, place it in the cssruntm/cfg/canada folder, and edit the /cssruntm/cfg/canada/area.par file to reference the grid file by name. 
When the Canadian National Transformation model interpolates a given point, it checks a configurable text file, /cssruntm/cfg/canada/area.par, for the name of the gridded data file to use. Only the first valid grid file found is used during point conversions. The file extension .dac should be left off the entry in the area.par file.

## Picklists Metadata
This is the metadata required to define the three types of picklists: 
Predefined
To define a predefined picklist, an entry is required in the [G3E_PICKLIST (Picklists for Attributes in Property Dialogs Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw) table. Define the specification to use predefined picklists in either the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table or the [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE (Property Dialog Attribute Lists Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) table. 
Domain
To define a domain picklist for an attribute, specify the domain table and field from which to retrieve the values for the drop-down list in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) and [G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) fields, respectively, in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE entry for that attribute. 
Foreign key
To define a foreign key picklist for an attribute, specify the foreign key table and field from which to retrieve the values for the drop-down list in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) and [G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) fields, respectively, in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE entry for that attribute.

When the [Edit tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LqLeE98Nnul3rsMPIM0BwQ) (![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255071?tocId=zaua5XAtX6sdnB~msrItdQ)) is active, you can right-click anywhere in the active window to choose an edit or select set option. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255071?tocId=zaua5XAtX6sdnB~msrItdQ)
The components you add to the select set are based on the option you select:  
|  Option  |  Sets the select mode to  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Only selected components  |  Only components that have been selected.  |  
|  All components  |  All components of a feature.  |  
|  All components in the active legend  |  All components in the active legend.  |  
|  All components displayed at current scale  |  All components displayed at the current scale.  |  
|  All components of the same component type  |  All components of the same legend type. Examples
  * Types can be defined for some electric components grouped as High Voltage or Low Voltage. This is not based on attribution but is a metadata designation on each component definition. 
  * A legend can be designated by the type of work being done in the legend, such as High Voltage type. Your administrator can define other High Voltage type legends that display different High Voltage type components. If you choose All components of the same component type from the right-click menu, you can manipulate all the High Voltage type components of the feature displayed on the current legend and on other High Voltage type legends.

## Specifying an Adjustment Mask
Use the Adjustments dialog box to define the graphic adjustments allowed during feature placement. When you specify a graphic adjustment for a feature, you can adjust additional feature components as well. For example, you may need to move a group of text along a linear component. However, flip operations are not supported for additional feature components. 
Whatever adjustments you select, text geometries do not display upside down or backward. When multiple adjustments are indicated, the Flip executes first, followed by the Rotate, and finally Move. The following adjustment masks are available: 
Flip Inverse
  * Move the origin of the geometry to the other side of the flip component.
  * Rotate the geometry to the inverse angle relative to the flip component.
  * Shift the alignment from top to bottom or bottom to top.


Alignments are not shifted from left to right or right to left, and center (left/right/center) alignments are not modified. You can specify the component that is flipped over in the placement arguments. If you leave the flip relative component blank in the adjustment arguments, or if the relative component does not exist during adjustment of the current component, the user is prompted to locate the element over which to flip. 
You can apply this adjustment to text and oriented point geometry types. Text is adjusted for RightReadingAngle after the flip. 
Use Flip Inverse for text and symbols that you do not want turned upside down. You cannot flip additional feature components.   
|  Example The origin is on the line, so no move takes place. The symbol is at 0 degrees relative to the line, so no rotation takes place, and the alignment is shifted from TopCenter to BottomCenter.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891) The origin is moved from below the line to a point equal distance and direction above the line. The original symbol was 30 degrees below the line, so its rotation was set to be 30 degrees above the line, and its origin was shifted from TopLeft to BottomLeft.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891) The origin is moved from below the line to a point equal distance and direction above the line. The original text was 30 degrees below the line, so its rotation was set to be 30 degrees above the line, and its origin was shifted from TopLeft to BottomLeft.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891)  |  
| --- |  
Flip With angle 180
  * Move the geometry to the other side of the "flip" component
  * Rotate the geometry 180 degrees
  * Shift the alignment from left to right or right to left.


Alignments are not shifted from top to bottom or bottom to top, and (top/bottom/center) center alignments are not modified. You can specify the components that are to be flipped in the placement arguments. If you leave the flip relative component in the adjustment arguments, or if the relative component does not exist during adjustment of the current component, the user is prompted to locate the element over which to flip. You can apply this adjustment to text and oriented point geometry types. Text is adjusted for RightReadingAngle after the flip. 
Use Flip With angle 180 for symbols that you specifically want turned upside down like keeping the triangle symbol point toward the line. You cannot flip additional feature components.   
|  Example The origin of the geometry is on the line, so it is not moved. The symbol is rotated 180 degrees, and because the alignment is Top*Center*, the alignment is not changed.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891) The origin of the geometry is moved from below the line to the other side. The symbol is rotated 180 degrees, and the alignment is shifted from CenterLeft to CenterRight.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891) Because of RightReadingAngle, text ends up like this. ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891)  |  
| --- |  
Rotate Origin
Rotates the geometry interactively around the origin of the component. When the user places the current feature component, the additional feature components are rotated along with the currently placed component as a single unit. The delta offset between the currently placed feature component and the additional feature components is maintained. The angle of the additional feature components is set to the specified new angle plus their relative angle with the currently placed feature component. 
Rotate Around
Rotates the geometry interactively relative to another component. When a user places the current feature component, the additional feature components are also rotated around the same relative point feature component. The delta offset between the currently placed feature component and the additional feature components is maintained. In other words, the delta offset that exists between the additional feature components and the relative point feature component is always the same after the adjustment is complete because they are rotated around the same relative point feature component. The angle of the additional feature components is set to the angle of the currently placed feature component plus their relative angle with the currently placed component. The currently placed feature component and additional feature components are rotated as a single unit. 
Move Independent
Lets the user move the component arbitrarily. When a user places the current feature component, the additional feature components are moved with it as a single unit. The delta offset between the currently placed feature component and the additional feature components is maintained. 
Move Along (no angle adjustment)
Lets the user move the component along a linear element. When a user places the current feature component, the additional feature components is also moved along the specified relative linear component. The currently placed feature component and the additional feature components are moved as a single unit. The delta offset between the currently placed feature component and the additional feature components is maintained. 
Move Along plus angle adjustment
Lets the user move the component along a linear element by setting the angle of the component equal to the angle of the closest segment of the linear element. When a user places the current feature component, the additional feature components are also moved along the specified relative linear component with their offset delta and relative angle with the currently placed component always maintained. The angle of the additional feature components are set to angle of the line segment plus the relative angle with the currently placed feature component. The currently placed feature component and additional feature components are moved as a single unit. 
Move Along plus relative angle adjustment
Lets the user move the component along a linear element by maintaining the relative angle of the currently placed feature component with the current linear segment. When a user places the current feature component, the additional feature components are also moved along the specified relative linear component. Their offset delta and relative angle with the currently placed component are always maintained. The angle of the additional feature components is set to the angle of the line segment plus the relative angle of the currently placed feature component and their relative angle with the currently placed component. The currently placed feature component and additional feature components are moved as a single unit. 
  * To specify graphic adjustments:


  1. In the Operations box of the Adjustments dialog box, select the graphic adjustments you want to define for the component. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/AffV_8L82lnuH5qkA4ZAXQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=b94c663b5bc67c2f&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. If you select an operation that requires a relative component, click the ellipsis button in the empty field. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891)
  3. Select the component relative to which the graphic adjustment is to be made. Each type of adjustment can use a separate relative component. 
  4. Click OK. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256891)
  5. On the Choose Occurrence Type dialog box, specify the occurrence type for the relative component. 
     * All — Not applicable for this command.. 
     * Last placed — The component moves along the last placed component and finds the highest CID. 
     * Same as active — The component moves along the relative component with the same CID as the one being placed. 
     * Geographically nearest to active — The component finds the relative component closest to its initial location. This is most often used for repeating components. 
  6. Click OK. 
The Selected list shows the feature- component pairs that are adjusted with this component. 
  7. Click OK.

## Specifying Interface Arguments
If an interface definition requires an argument, the Specify Arguments dialog box appears when you click the Interface Arguments ellipsis button. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259133)
The grid on this dialog box displays the prompts and the data type required for the argument values. Depending on the data type, the Value cells accept a keyed-in value or display an ellipsis button so you can further refine the argument. If the argument type is GraphicAdjustment, the [Adjustments dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/izIu6qhN7jaPGIqOeh2eZg) appears.

## Supported Operators
|  =  |  Equals  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  >=  |  Greater than or equal to  |  
|  <=  |  Less than or equal to  |  
|  <>  |  Not equal to  |  
|  >  |  Greater than  |  
|  <  |  Less than  |  
|  ( )  |  Parentheses for grouping expressions and Logical and between two expressions or Logical or between two expressions   |  
You create compound expressions with the AND or the OR operator and group expressions with parentheses ( ). The AND operator means that both statements must be true. The OR opertor means that either statement can be true. 
Parentheses can be used to control the order in which an expression is evaluated. By default, all relational comparison operators ( =, >=, <=, <>, >, <) are evaluated first, from left to right. The logical AND operator has a higher precedence than the logical OR operator; so all AND operations are performed first. You can use parentheses to change the order.   
|  Example To find all roads with more than four lanes or divided roads that were paved before 1996, you create the following filter:  last_paved < 1996 and num_lanes > 4 or divided = 'yes'  Because of the precedence of the and operator, this filter returns all roads that are divided or all roads where the number of lanes is greater than four and paved before 1996.  To get the correct results, you should use parentheses as follows: last_paved < 1996 and (num_lanes > 4 or divided = 'yes')  |  
| --- |  
These operators are available from the drop-down list:
  * NOT
  * BETWEEN
  * IS
  * NULL
  * IN

## Trace Types
|  Trace Type  |  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Trace All  |  1  |  Finds all features connected to the seed feature, subject to the stop and filter criteria. The trace stops executing once it can no longer find any new connected rows.   |  
|  Point-to-Point  |  2  |  Starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, subject to the Goal and Filter criteria. Any rows traced that are not on this path from the seed to the goal are removed from the trace results.   |  
|  Minimum Path  |  3  |  Starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, subject to the Goal and Filter criteria and keeping track of the cost from the seed to the goal. Once a goal is found, the trace continues to search for other paths that have a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal.  The trace stops executing when there are no longer any valid rows as defined by the Stop and Filter criteria or there are no longer any potential paths having a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal. Any rows traced that are not on the minimum path from the seed to the goal are removed from the trace results.   |  
|  Sequential Point- to-Point  |  5  |  Starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, subject to the Goal and Filter criteria. If there are any single-node features on a node, they are traced through before the other features connected to that node. Any rows traced that are not on this path from the seed to the goal are removed from the trace results. Any single-node features connected to a node in the first path found from the seed to the goal are included in the trace results.   |  
|  Sequential Minimum Path  |  6  |  Starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, subject to the Goal and Filter criteria and keeping track of the cost from the seed to the goal. If there are any single-node features on a node, they are traced through before the other features connected to that node. Once a goal is found, the trace continues to search for other paths to a goal that have a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal.  If there are multiple single- node features at a node, then the cumulative cost of all the single-node features are used to compute the path through the node. If any of the single nodes have an unknown cost (Null value), then the cost to proceed through the node is unknown and a minimum path through the node is not considered.  The trace stops executing when there are no longer any valid rows as defined by the Stop and Filter criteria or there are no longer any potential paths having a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal. Any rows traced that are not on the minimum path from the seed to the goal are removed from the trace results. Any single- node features connected to a node in the minimum path found from the seed to the goal are included in the trace results.   |

# Configuration and the Facility Data Model

## Commands

### Common Attribute Edit Command
You can simultaneously edit the common attributes of multiple features using[ Edit Common Attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ec5BcNG6iV5Na~T_hlNYDg). Before starting the command, the user must select two or more features—graphically using the map or nongraphically using Feature Explorer. The command finds all common attributes of the selected features. 
Using the [EditCommonAttributesThreshold](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) general parameter, you can limit the number of features a user can select at one time for editing. Using this general parameter reduces the memory usage for editing common attributes. 
Common attributes are determined based on a metadata search, a comparison of field name, type, and if applicable, a defined picklist, alternatively on attribute number. Depending on the selected method for determining of the common attributes an attribute does not have to exist in the same component between the selected features to be considered common. See [ Edit Common Attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ec5BcNG6iV5Na~T_hlNYDg) for more details. 
When the user clicks OK, the Edit Common Attributes command applies the edits. 
Edit Common Attributes displays all common attributes for the selected features based on the selected attribute identification method. However, a feature may not have one of these attributes available for edit. For example, if you select a cable and a terminal feature, run Edit Common Attributes, and then provide a Service MIN value; the common attribute may be ignored if those features do not have a row already specified in their SAP component. This would apply to any editable field that exists in an optional component. 
The G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_EXCLUDEFROMEDIT field identifies which attributes can be edited. A value of Yes (1) indicates that the attribute cannot be edited. A value of No, (0) indicates that the attribute can be edited. 
The Edit Common Attributes command filters out the following system attributes (not displayed in data grid): G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CID, G3E_ID, GDO_GID, G3E_GEOMETRY, G3E_STYLEID, G3E_LABELFORMAT, G3E_ALIGNMENT, G3E_TEXTSTRING, and G3E_DETAILID. 
For one attribute to be considered common with another attribute, the following values (in G3E_ATTRIBUTE) must be the same: G3E_FIELD, G3E_USERNAME, G3E_DATATYPE, and G3E_PNO. If G3E_PNO values are both Null, then G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE values are checked. If G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE values are equal (Null or not Null), then the attributes are considered common. Attributes that are common to all the selected features are listed in a data grid within the Common Attribute Edit dialog box. If a picklist is defined for an attribute, it is made available for edit selections. 
The following is the logic:
attributes are not common by default 
if G3E_FIELD values are equal 
if G3E_USERNAME values are equal
if G3E_DATATYPE values are equal 
if G3E_PNO vales are equal and not null 
attributes are common
if G3E_PNO values are both null
if G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE values are equal and not null
attributes are common
if G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE values are both null
attributes are common

### Communications Commands

#### Cable Fill
[Cable Fill](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/W9aTSOHJUHGo00cdGBYJbw) provides information on how a cable is being used. The usage information is requested for a specific set of pair counts from a Customer Assignment interface and is presented in a report. 
Cable Fill works as a pipe between the assignment interface and the reporting object. Data are gathered from selected features and passed to the assignment interface, which gathers and returns the fill information. The fill information is then passed to the report interface for any post processing and presentation to the user. The HTML reporting engine is used because: 
  * It lets you include script code in the stylesheet to perform post processing operations.
  * It provides a mechanism so you can tailor the report to the requirements of your organization.


The following is a sample output report from Cable Fill:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262193)
The command provides usage data for multiple cables. Also, the resulting data can optionally be grouped by cable gauge. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262193)
Metadata
  * G3E_COMMIFACE
The ProgID for the custom assignment interface object that is used to retrieve the cable fill information is specified in the [G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Gp7g5vbqXez~bEdYaOZHA) table for the Customer Assignment interface. 
  * G3E_REPORT
A report can be configured by adding one or more rows to the [G3E_REPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) table. These rows contain the argument values for the specified report interface. The report interface must accept an XML file as input. The [HTML report interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMGrbdshaeRmWzATJH6P9Q) (PRIface.HTMLReport) is normally used. 
  * G3E_REPORTMAPPING
Populate the [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table with one or more rows that reference the G3E_RPNO values in G3E_REPORT. A value of 14 should be used for G3E_TYPE to indicate a cable fill report. 
  * G3E_LMUFEATURE
The feature number for the cable feature is retrieved from the [G3E_LMUFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~0uc9GXBi8WehfgJz0D8Ww) table for the entry where G3E_TYPE is Cable.

#### Change Feed
[Change Feed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/onIjdyse5HAyuDjo4PryJg)Change Feed to rectify the problem without having to redigitize the entire cable. 
Change Feed allows the user to reverse the direction of a cable, including the direction of node-ordered connectivity and the sequence of points in all linear geometries associated with the cable. Although this command reverses the feed direction, the user is responsible for reversing the pair counts if required. 
Change Feed reverses single cable features only. If several cables joined in a network require reversing, the user must run Change Feed for each individual cable. 
Metadata
  * G3E_COMMIFACE 
The Communications Interface table ([G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Gp7g5vbqXez~bEdYaOZHA)) requires an entry that points to the G3E_REVERSEFEED table. The G3E_REVERSEFEED table contains information necessary for identifying features eligible for processing by the Change Feed command. 
  * G3E_REVERSEFEED 
The [G3E_REVERSEFEED table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mSfoM~uI3Po~Pw0gZs0tgQ) contains two fields used to identify components available for reverse feed. The G3E_FNO field contains the number of the feature that can be manipulated by the command, while the G3E_CNO field contains the number of the linear components within G3E_FNO.

#### Longest Loop
The longest loop function is typically used by engineers to characterize the types of service that can be provided to a service area based on the amount of signal that can be carried to the farthest extremes of the network in that area. NetWorks Core includes a [loop makeup](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ng9Qk3I1KfxmojpCQmDLoA) function that can compute signal loss for any network trace and produce that report in an HTML based format. [Find Longest Loop](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EhSdp30oW8ZPb4Xu6Qbv3A) is a means of identifying the points of the network, typically terminals, which are farthest from the interface of a service area. The user can selectively identify points to feed into the loop makeup function. This provides the (subjective) characteristic signal loss for the service area. 
The user can identify all of the distribution cable loops that are contained inside the boundary (typically a DSA boundary) of the selected interface, beyond the boundary, or both. 
After a Longest Loop is complete, the user is provided with an interactive summary of the terminals that were traced in the distribution network downstream from the selected interface to the end of the network and the distance of cable between the two features. 
Longest Loop does not support the call-for-service functionality.
These metadata tables are associated with the Longest Loop command: 
  * G3E_COMMIFACE
The Communications Interface table ([G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ng9Qk3I1KfxmojpCQmDLoA)) requires five entries. Following are descriptions for each required entry by G3E_TYPE: 
    * Longest Loop Interface—Identifies the progID of the object that processes the longest loop calculation. 
    * Longest Loop—Points to the product specific table where command specific information can be retrieved. More details on this table below. 
    * LongestLoopTraceName—Defines the G3E_TRACE.G3E_USERNAME to use when performing a longest loop. The trace name for this reference cannot be localized. 
    * CableSectionLengthANO—Identifies the section length attribute of the cable feature. Used in the retrieval of cable lengths from the component table. 
    * CableSegmentStartANO—Identifies the segment start location of the cable feature. Used in the retrieval of cable lengths from the component table. 
  * G3E_LONGESTLOOP 
The [G3E_LONGESTLOOP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EhSdp30oW8ZPb4Xu6Qbv3A) table contains specific information to process features for the Longest Loop command. Feature information for each of the following features must be included in the table: 
    * Terminal
    * Interface
    * Boundary
    * Splice
    * Cable
This table also includes a filter column that filters boundary types and a detail CNO column that identifies features containing detail graphics when the geographic components do not exist. The following features require ANOs to identify certain attributes to the command: 
    * The total length attribute ANO is required for the cable feature.
    * The feature type attribute ANO is required for the boundary feature.
    * The system number attribute ANO is required for the terminal feature.

#### Loop Makeup

##### Adding Attribution to an LMU Report
When a loop is processed, all the fields in the source tables and/or views are included as part of the output from LMU. You can update [source views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DHUwlxUkQR6tWTgCheuThQ) to include additional attribution from the source features, and you can retrieve attributes from other data or reference tables using joins to the feature component data. Any changes to source views must include the original fields. You must thoroughly test any changes to ensure no performance degradation has occurred. 
To include additional information in an LMU report, augment the LMU views used for data collection to include the information you need. For example, to include an address or the name of a detail drawing, add the address of the feature to the source view, and update the LMU stylesheet that the user sees as part of the LMU report. 
In the output XML files that the stylesheet uses, the loop feature hierarchical level contains these fields: UID (unique id linking features to the LMU that was performed), G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, description, filter, length, gauge, resistance, loss, and fiber_mode, followed by all the attribution in the source views. Because each LMU source feature can have different field names and the number of fields can differ, some limitations are implied in the format of the output: 
  * Because each source view has different field names, the field names of the output recordset do not match the field names of the source view. Output fields are labeled as SourceField#, where the # represents the ordinal of the field in the source. These new fields are in addition to the existing fields to preserve compatibility with existing stylesheets. 
  * Because each source view can have a variety of fields, the output recordset is padded to accommodate the source view with the most fields. 


This stylesheet example illustrates including the value of a source field in the [HTML output](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMGrbdshaeRmWzATJH6P9Q) for a specific feature. 
Example
<xsl:choose>  
<xsl:when test="[@G3E_FNO = 7000]">
<xsl:value-of select="@SourceField6"/>
</xsl:when>
<xsl:when test="[@G3E_FNO = 7100]">
<xsl:value-of select="@SourceField4"/>
</xsl:when>
<xsl:otherwise>
<xsl:value-of select="@Description"/>
</xsl:otherwise>
</xsl:choose>
In this example, the annotation of the feature is changed based on the FNO of the feature. The value of SourceField6 is included in the HTML report when the feature number is 7000. When the feature is 7100, the values of SourceField4 are displayed. For any other FNO, the default Description field is used.

##### Configuring Design Validation for Loop Makeup
When you populate the Loop Makeup reference tables, consider this list of design elements that Loop Makeup validates: 
Loaded Copper Loops
  * The total resistance is checked against the resistance design limit. The resistance design limit is specified by the [G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4nChDwWvQI6hh31Liru4uw) reference table for the selected service. The user can override the resistance design limit in the Loop Makeup dialog box. 
  * The average distance between load coils is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum average load coil spacing value specified in metadata. It is also checked so that it meets the minimum average load coil spacing value. The minimum and maximum values are specified in the [G3E_LMUIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rrWLXbaY27pSjxJmMjF5TA) table where the G3E_TYPE is MaxLoadcoilSpacingDeviation and MinAverageLoadcoilSpacing. 
  * The distance between each individual load coil is checked so that it does not deviate from the average load coil spacing. The maximum deviation value is specified in the G3E_LMUIFACE table where the G3E_TYPE is MaxLoadcoilSpacingDeviation (for example, 0.03 is 3 percent max deviation). 
  * The customer end section length (the length from the customer point to the first load coil) is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum customer end section length specified in the [G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7qqCS4u483_blCc1IFW4ag) reference table. The following column values are used to determine the correct MAX_LENGTH value: TYPE value = 'CUST', LOADED = <the loaded status of the loop> and SERVICE_TYPE value = <the service code for the service selected>. The SERVICE_TYPE code is described in the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS table for the selected service, service type, and technology. 
The customer end section length is also checked so that it meets the minimum customer end section length specified in the MIN_LENGTH column in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. The same filter criteria are used as described for maximum customer end section length. 
  * The office end section length (the length from the last load coil to the end of the loop) is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum office end section length specified in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. The following column values are used to determine the correct MAX_LENGTH value: TYPE value = 'OFFICE', LOADED = 'L' and SERVICE_TYPE value = <the service code for the service selected>. 
The office end section length is also checked so that it meets the minimum office end section length specified in the MIN_LENGTH column in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. The same filter criteria are used as described for maximum office end section length. 
  * The total dB loss is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum dB loss value specified in the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS reference table. The service, service type, and technology are used to determine the correct value. The user can override the maximum dB loss value in the Loop Makeup dialog box. 
  * The total bridge tap length is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum bridge tap length value specified in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. The bridge tap is any part of the loop not directly between the customer point and the central office. The maximum length is specified in the MAX_LENGTH column where TYPE = 'BT', SERVICE_TYPE = <the service code selected> and LOADED = 'L'. 


Non-loaded Copper Loops
  * The total loop length is checked against the maximum loop length specified in the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS reference table for the selected TYPE_CD (service code). 
  * The total bridge tap length is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum bridge tap length value specified in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. The maximum length is specified in the MAX_LENGTH column where TYPE = 'BT', SERVICE_TYPE = <the service code selected>and LOADED = 'NL'. 
  * The total dB loss is checked so that it does not exceed the maximum dB loss value specified in the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS reference table. The service, service type, and technology are used to determine the correct value. The user can override the maximum dB loss value in the Loop Makeup dialog box. 
  * The total resistance is checked against the resistance design limit specified in RES_DESIGN_LIMIT in the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table for the selected service, type and technology. The user can override the value in the Loop Makeup dialog box. 


Fiber Loops
The total loss is checked against the maximum bay-to-bay loss value specified in MAX_END_TO_END in the [MAX_TRANSMISSIONLOSS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lRH6lw~PkbKKTJvc5z8Hhw) reference table for the selected equipment, optic card, wavelength, and fiber mode. The user can override this value in the Loop Makeup dialog box.

##### Loop Makeup Metadata
The following tables are used to configure specifications for Loop Makeup. 
G3E_COMMIFACE
You must configure an entry in the [G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Gp7g5vbqXez~bEdYaOZHA) table for the object ID of the custom assignment interface object. This object is used to retrieve cross-connect information. The type for this entry is Customer Assignment interface. 
You can also configure your model to start a loop makeup by entering a phone number. Set G3E_COMMIFACE.G3E_TYPE to FindPhoneNumber. The G3E_ANO values specified in G3E_COMMIFACE for the Find Phone Number command map to fields with the same naming convention as the field names used in the recordset returned by the Customer Assignment interface query. 
The Loop Makeup command supports tracing through a feature more than once in uncommon scenarios where a cross-connect occurs on a branch in the loop. In these cases, at least one feature would have to be traced through more than once. Metadata to support identification of these cases is G3E_COMMIFACE.G3E_TYPE = InterconnectionPointFeatures where the value of G3E_PARAMETER1 is the feature numbers that are needed when a loop is traced to check for potential cross- connects. The Upgrade Wizard populates the G3E_COMMIFACE table by asking you for a comma delimited list of feature numbers during metadata upgrade. The Upgrade Wizard also adds the InterconnectionPointFeatures to G3E_COMMINTERFACETYPE.G3E_TYPE. You can add or change the feature numbers listed in G3E_COMMIFACE.G3E_PARAMETER1 using Metadata Explorer. 
G3E_REPORT
The table can be configured by adding one or more rows to the [G3E_REPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) table. These rows contain the argument values for the specified report interface. The report interface must accept an XML file as input. The HTML report interface (PRIface.HTMLReport) is normally used. This interface uses the following four arguments: 
  * Path and file name of the output XML file
  * Path and file name of the input XSL stylesheet file to use in formatting the report
  * Path and file name of the final output HTML file
  * Flag indicating whether the HTML file is displayed


G3E_REPORTMAPPING
The [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table must then be populated with one or more rows that reference the G3E_RPNO values in G3E_REPORT. A value of 11 should be used for G3E_TYPE to indicate a loop makeup report. 
The XSL file controls basic formatting, for example, text color, but more importantly controls formatting, such as the division of sections between interfaces. The XSL file can also control the inclusion or exclusion of features and summaries from the report. 
G3E_LMUIFACE
The [G3E_LMUIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rrWLXbaY27pSjxJmMjF5TA) table contains information necessary for the various aspects of Loop Makeup analysis implementation such as design requirement and processing values. 
Example  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_TABLE  |  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  G3E_PARAMETER1  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  AerialTemperatureLossFactor  |   |   |  1.08  |  
|  GaugeChangeLoss  |   |   |  0.2  |  
|  TraceName  |   |   |  Analytic Trace  |  
G3E_LMUFEATURE
The [G3E_LMUFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~0uc9GXBi8WehfgJz0D8Ww) table contains list of the features that LMU processes. 
Example  
|  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_VIEW  |  G3E_GEOGRAPHICCNO  |  G3E_DETAILCNO  |  G3E_CONTYPE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  7000  |  Cable  |  Cable  |  VLMU_CABLE  |  7010  |  7011  |  0  |  
|  10800  |  Splice  |  Connector  |  VLMU_CONNECTOR  |  18020  |  10821  |  1  |  
When a new feature is added to G3E_LMUFEATURE, ensure that the publish subset post process script PostProcess_T-SQL.sql is in G3E_LMUFEATURE.G3E_VIEW. 
G3E_TRACE
The [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) table supports the inclusion of containing features in the highlighted trace results. The trace used by loop makeup is identified in G3E_LUMIFACE where G3E_TYPE = 'TraceName'. The value for G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO must equal the value specified in G3E_TRACE.G3E_GRAPHICRNO. 
Example  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  G3E_TRACETYPE  |  G3E_GRAPHICRNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Analytic Trace  |  Analytic Trace  |  1  |  6  |  
G3E_METADATASUPPORT
The following rows must exist in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table for the Loop Makeup command to function correctly. The command uses the resulting data to populate picklists.   
|  G3E_MSNO  |  G3E_TABLE  |  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  G3E_XMLKEY  |  G3E_XMLQUERY  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|   |  Null  |  Null  |   |  DISTINCT_GAUGE  |  SELECT DISTINCT GAUGE FROM G3E_COPPERLOSS  |  
|   |  Null  |  Null  |   |  DISTINCT_SERVICE  |  SELECT DISTINCT SERVICE FROM G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS  |  
|   |  Null  |  Null  |   |  DISTINCT_SPLICETYPE  |  SELECT DISTINCT TYPE FROM G3E_FIBERLOSS WHERE CLASS='SPLICE' ORDER BY TYPE  |  
G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS
The [G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4nChDwWvQI6hh31Liru4uw) table describes constraints for various copper services. It can be modified to describe: 
  * Service, type, and technology combinations
  * The loop's loss design limit for the specified service combination
  * The loop's resistance design limit for the specified service combination
  * The loop's maximum length for the specified service combination
  * Whether loading is allowed for the specified service combination
  * The NYQUIST frequency for the specified service combination


Example  
|  TYPE_CD  |  SERVICE  |  TYPE  |  TECHNOLOGY  |  LOSS_DESIGN_LIMIT  |  NYQUIST_FREQ  |  RES_DESIGN_LIMIT  |  LOADING_ALLOWED  |  MAX_LOOP_LENGTH  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  POVOCO1  |  POTS  |  VOICE  |  COPPER  |  8.5  |  1  |  1300  |  Y  |  18000  |  
|  CEVOCL8  |  CENTREX  |  VLMU_CONNECTOR  |  CLE  |  31  |  8  |  1700  |  N  |  Null  |  
To add a new service, a new row must first be added to the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS reference table. A new service code has to be created for the TYPE_CD column. The service code must be unique and should be descriptive of the service. Currently, the coding scheme takes the first two letters of the service, the service type, and the technology and then appends the frequency. For example, the code 'POVOCO1' was used where the service = 'POTS', type = 'VOICE', technology = 'COPPER', and the frequency = 1 (KHz). 
G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA
The data in the [G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7qqCS4u483_blCc1IFW4ag) table describes various bridge tap and end section information for services: whether loading is allowed, whether loading is required, the maximum number of taps, and min and max lengths for end sections and tap. It can be modified to: 
  * Set the minimum customer end section length for the specified service, loading status, and range of load coils present. 
  * Set the maximum customer end section length for the specified service, loading status, and range of load coils present. 
  * Set the minimum office end section length for the specified service, loading status, and range of load coils present. 
  * Set the maximum office end section length for the specified service, loading status, and range of load coils present. 
  * Set the minimum bridge tap length for the specified service, loading status, and range of load coils present. 
  * Set the maximum bridge tap length for the specified service, loading status and range of load coils present. 


After a new service has been added to the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS table, rows must then be added to the G3E_BRIDGETAPDATA reference table. For each service described in G3E_ SERVICECONSTRAINTS, there must be at least three rows added to G3E_ BRIDGETAPDATA. One row to describe the minimum and maximum bridge tap lengths, one row to describe the minimum and maximum office end section lengths, and one row to describe the minimum and maximum customer end section lengths. If loading is allowed with the particular service, then three more rows must be added describing these values for a loaded loop. 
Example  
|  SERVICE_TYPE  |  TYPE  |  LOADED  |  MIN_NO_BT  |  MAX_NO_BT  |  MIN_LENGTH  |  MAX_LENGTH  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  POVOCO1  |  BT  |  NL  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  1800  |  
|  POVOCO1  |  OFFICE  |  NL  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  
|  POVOCO1  |  CUST  |  NL  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  
|  POVOCO1  |  BT  |  L  |  0  |  0  |  0  |  1830  |  
|  POVOCO1  |  OFFICE  |  L  |  0  |  0  |  915  |  3660  |  
|  POVOCO1  |  CUST  |  L  |  0  |  0  |  915  |  3660  |  
If the minimum and/or maximum bridge tap lengths vary depending on the number of bridge tap sections present in the loop, then a row must be added for each range of number of bridge tap sections:   
|  SERVICE_TYPE  |  TYPE  |  LOADED  |  MIN_NO_BT  |  MAX_NO_BT  |  MIN_LENGTH  |  MAX_LENGTH  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  CEVOCL8  |  BT  |  NL  |  1  |  3  |  0  |  1800  |  
|  CEVOCL8  |  BT  |  NL  |  4  |  100  |  0  |  900  |  
G3E_COPPERLOSS
The [G3E_COPPERLOSS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zwDOiNKXOJP9dJXtsgW7qA) table describes per length unit loss values for copper cables for combinations of cable gauge, loop loading status, and the service used on the loop. The table also describes whether loading is allowed for these combinations. It can be modified to describe per length unit loss values for copper cables. The gauge of the cable, the service used on the loop, and the loading status of the loop must be specified. 
Example  
|  TYPE_CD  |  SERVICE_TYPE  |  GAUGE  |  LOADED  |  LOSS  |  BT_ALLOWED  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  POVOCO1  |  19  |  L  |  0.25  |  Y  |  
|  33  |  DC56CO28  |  19  |  NL  |  2.3  |  N  |  
After a new service has been added to the G3E_SERVICECONSTRAINTS table, a row must be added to the G3E_COPPERLOSS reference table for each combination of gauge and loading status for the new service. The G3E_COPPERLOSS is used to describe the per km loss values for copper cables for combinations of gauge, loading status, and the service used on the loop. 
G3E_LOOPRESISTANCE
The [G3E_LOOPRESISTANCE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TX8_MklZmLFdObvXNqlmQw) table describes copper cable per km resistance values. The table can be modified to specify per km resistance values by gauge and loading status. 
Example  
|  TYPE_CD  |  GAUGE  |  LOADED  |  RESISTANCE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  26  |  NL  |  273.3  |  
|  5  |  26  |  L  |  278.9  |  
G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED
The [G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/msCei9_n0yOWf~dqL5A~yA) table describes the equipment that is required for a loop for a range of resistance. The table can be modified to specify equipment that is required on loops with specific resistance ranges. The loop makeup report displays that the equipment is required for the loop. 
Example  
|  ID  |  EQUIP_REQ  |  MIN_RESIST  |  MAX_RESIST  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  2  |  Voice repeater (4dB) and loop extender (24 volt boost)  |  1501  |  2000  |  
|  3  |  Voice repeater (6dB) and loop extender (48 volt boost)  |  2001  |  99999  |  
G3E_FIBERLOSS
The [G3E_FIBERLOSS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2~tVeIbIAPncODihuRP5WQ) table describes loss values for fiber cables and equipment. The table can be modified to describe loss values for fiber equipment including cables. The class of equipment must be specified (cable, connector, and so forth), the type must be specified (cable's alpha code, splice type Biconic, Fusion, and so forth), the fiber mode must be specified, and the wavelength used on the loop must also be specified. 
Example  
|  TYPE_CD  |  CLASS  |  TYPE  |  FIBER_MODE  |  WAVELENGTH  |  LOSS  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  3  |  CABLE  |  DEFAULT  |  SINGLE  |  1310  |  0.6  |  
|  162  |  SPLICE  |  FUSION  |  SINGLE  |  1310  |  0.1  |  
G3E_MAXTRANSMISSIONLOSS
The [G3E_MAXTRANSMISSIONLOSS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lRH6lw~PkbKKTJvc5z8Hhw) table describes the maximum end-to-end transmission loss values for various fiber equipment and wavelength combinations. The table can be modified to specify maximum loss values for the loop. The equipment, optic card, fiber mode, and wavelength must be described. 
Example  
|  TYPE_CD  |  TRANSMIT_EQUIP  |  OPTIC_CARD  |  FIBER_MODE  |  WAVELENGTH  |  MAX_END_TO_END  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  FMT-6  |  NT7H55AA  |  SINGLE  |  1310  |  8.5  |  
|  52  |  OC-12  |  NT7E02JC  |  SINGLE  |  1550  |  29.2  |

#### Pair Count Edit Control

##### Configuring the Pair Count Edit Control
You need to configure two types of metadata before users can use the Pair Count Edit control: 
  * Control-specific metadata
  * Dialog tab definitions


The pair count component of a feature should not be displayed on any other dialog tables, at least not as editable attributes. Editing of these attributes in any context other than Pair Count Edit control can violate the business rules defined in the G3E_PAIRCOUNT table and can cause pair data to be corrupted. 
  * To configure the Pair Count Edit control:


  1. Populate the G3E_PAIRCOUNT table so the Pair Count Edit control knows how to manage all the length attributes on the cable feature. 
This table contains all of the parameters that define the behavior of the Pair Count system, and in turn, the Pair Count Edit control. In Metadata Explorer, navigate to the Communications Applications > Pair Count Parameters node and, add a new row. 
  2. Add dialog tabs.
Use Metadata Explorer to update metadata and create the [dialog tab definitions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MPR6mJuKwSz8gPPCFL27Ag) you need for the Pair Count Edit control. This table summarizes the entries you need to make in the G3E_DIALOG and G3E_DIALOGTAB tables. Repeat this scheme for each feature. 

  
|  G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE   |  G3E_DIALOGTAB Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Review   |  GTCtlInfo.PairCountControl  |  Causes Feature Explorer to display the Pair Count Edit control   |  
|  Edit  |  GTCtlInfo.PairCountControl   |  Causes Feature Explorer to display the Pair Count Edit control   |  
Related Topics
[Pair Count Edit Control Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yAG8nfQyaFg3Epj0hx8ICQ)
[Pair Count Edit Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/95T~vTxkxY8mRGm6omh0xw)

##### Pair Count Edit Control Metadata
Set the [G3E_PAIRCOUNT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iHTy1jqvRAU~kZXlIFqV7A) for default values for these parameters. 
  * Pair Count Edit control parameters
The pair count table indicates the special tokens to use when validating the syntax and semantics of a line of count. 
    * G3E_DESIGNATION_DELIMITER
    * G3E_RANGE_DELIMITER
    * G3E_REVERSE_FEED_DELIMITER
    * G3E_DEAD_INDICATOR
    * G3E_SPECIAL_INDICATOR
    * G3E_OPEN_THROW_DELIMITER
    * G3E_CLOSE_THROW_DELIMITER
  * Pair count designation prefixes 
Specify these parameters only if you want to use pair count designation prefixes.
    * G3E_PREFIX_DELIMITER
    * G3E_PREFIXOPTIONAL
    * G3E_PREFIXDEFAULT
The primary attribute component table for every count-bearing feature must have the G3E_PAIRCOUNTPREFIX field. When added to the primary attribute component, this field stores the last format with or without the designation prefix. The Pair Count Edit control uses the G3E_PAIRCOUNTPREFIX field to set the Include designation prefix in pair count label checkbox to the appropriate default value during edit. The Ripple command and the Throw command also use the G3E_PAIRCOUNTPREFIX field. 
  * Configure messages during validation
Validation occurs when an attempt is made to commit a feature in Feature Explorer. Error reporting can be configurable for three discrete validations as ignore (0), warnings (1), or errors (2). 
    * G3E_SIZE_MISMATCH
    * G3E_DUPLICATE_COUNT
    * G3E_NO_SOURCE_FEED


The [G3E_PAIRCOUNTCLASS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/y~0mmKEqDqkr38WG5Iojhg) stores on a per-feature basis the count classes that are available in the picklist in the Pair Count Edit control. If no classes are specified, the service assumes that the feature does not use classes, and the user does not see a class list. This table also identifies which count classes are validated.

[Pair Count Edit Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/95T~vTxkxY8mRGm6omh0xw)

#### Pair Count Merge Features Interface

##### Pair Count Merge Features Interface Metadata
You configure metadata so that the Pair Count Merge Features interface is invoked for each linear count-bearing feature. 
  1. Use [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGERINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to associate the Pair Count Merge Features Interface with a feature component. G3E_MERGERINO needs to reference [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_RINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) of the Pair Count Merge Features interface. 
    1. Use an SQL editor to retrieve this value. Click [here ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262292)for code. 
SQL> select G3E_RINO from G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE where 
G3E_INTERFACE = 'GTCommSup.CountMerge'
    2. Use an SQL editor to retrieve the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT records for all count bearing components associated with linear features. Click [here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262292) for code. 
SQL> select * from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT where
G3E_CNO in
-- Get G3E_CNO of the count bearing component
(select G3E_PARAMETER1 from G3E_COMMIFACE where G3E_TYPE = 'Pair Count')
and
G3E_FNO in
-- Get G3E_FNO's of features with linear primary geographic component 
(select G3E_FNO from G3E_FEATURE where G3E_PRIMARYGEOGRAPHICCNO in
-- Get G3E_CNO's of linear components 
(select G3E_CNO from G3E_COMPONENT where G3E_TYPE in (4,128))) 
  2. To associate the Pair Count Merge Features interface with all linear count-bearing features, update the G3E_MERGERINO of these records with the G3E_RINO value returned by the first query. 
  3. Verify that [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is set to 1 (Keep records from the first feature).

#### Ripple
Use the [Ripple Count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lSsl1fhjos4dZVEvwBMX6Q) command to propagate count changes to affected features and to display changes to support work prints. 
Ripple Count integrates the[Pair Count control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Oa5wGFKAjuWstNdFJrgbIQ) for editing and provides users with a consistent interface for all count manipulation regardless of what operation they are performing.

#### Throw
The [Throw Count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xZcT3kijc6q4wg8jRX9Vug)[G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JLEIT3y3Zlm4IQJOtEvOeQ) table. Throw Count uses this table to identify which features to throw rather than reanalyzing the whole network. This makes Throw more efficient. As each feature is thrown, the entry in the G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER is removed. 
Throw Count [removes bracketed pair counts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Oa5wGFKAjuWstNdFJrgbIQ) for the work order being thrown. 
Throw Count identifies features that could not be thrown due to work order dependencies. This situation occurs when a user attempts to throw a ripple that has previous ripples that have not been thrown. 
This command provides an interactive summary of the features that were thrown.

#### Trace Pair Count

##### Filtering Traces Based on Pair Count
Tracing in NetWorks Core is performed over the connectivity tables. In a G/Comms model, you may need to filter what parts of a network are traced by a logical pair designation or pair count. To help this, there are two views that join the NetWorks Core pair count table to the node-ordered and ownership connectivity tables. You can configure a trace to execute over this view. If you specify a filter criteria, you can limit the parts of the network traced to those that contain only the specified cable designation and pair. This functionality is used in and required by the Ripple, Loop Makeup, and Trace Pair Count commands. 
These views support filtering traces based on pair counts.
Pair Count and Node- Ordered Connectivity
This view joins pair count and node-ordered connectivity tables together to support filtering traces based on pair counts. When traces are run over a node-ordered network, a filter can be specified that limits the trace to specific pairs. 
SQL> create or replace view VW_COUNT_CONNECT as 
select CNT.G3E_ID, CNT.G3E_FNO, CNT.G3E_FID, CNT.G3E_CNO, CNT.G3E_CID,
CNT.CURRENT_DESIGNATION, CNT.CURRENT_FEED_DIR, CNT.CURRENT_HIGH, CNT.CURRENT_LOW,
CNT.PROPOSED_DESIGNATION, CNT.PROPOSED_FEED_DIR, CNT.PROPOSED_HIGH, CNT.PROPOSED_LOW,
CON.IN_FNO, CON.IN_FID, CON.OUT_FNO, CON.OUT_FID
from GC_COUNT CNT, GC_NR_CONNECT CON
where CNT.G3E_FNO = CON.G3E_FNO
and CNT.G3E_FID = CON.G3E_FID;

Pair Count and Ownership
This view joins pair count and ownership connectivity tables together to support filtering traces based on pair counts. This view is also used by the Pair Count service for querying the source feeds of child features. 
SQL> create or replace view VW_COUNT_OWNERSHIP as 
select CNT.G3E_ID, CNT.G3E_FNO, CNT.G3E_FID, CNT.G3E_CNO, CNT.G3E_CID,

##### Trace Pair Count Metadata
These tables are associated with the Trace Pair Count command: 
  * G3E_COMMIFACE—The trace that is actually executed on the database is defined by the CountTraceName parameter in the [G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Gp7g5vbqXez~bEdYaOZHA) table: 

  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_PARAMETER1  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CountTraceName  |  Analytic Trace  |  
  * G3E_RIPPLE—Trace Pair Count shares the [G3E_RIPPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RSpkgYIYsxS~uQ4ccO7vmQ) table to identify what features have pair counts to be traced and specifies how the features are connected in the network. This tells the Trace Post Processor how to collect the features. 
  * G3E_REPORT—The report for Trace Pair Count is defined in the [G3E_REPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) table and is identified by Trace Count Report.
