The first section is the query as Oracle received it. The second section is the matrix of the overall execution report. 
 |  
There are the three main phases of the query:
  * Parse — Where Oracle finds the query in the shared pool (soft parse) or creates a new plan for the query (hard parse). 
  * Execute — The work done by Oracle upon the open or execute of the query. For a select, Execute is often empty. For an update, Execute is where all of the work is done. 
  * Fetch — For a select, this is where most of the work is done and visible, but an update shows no work. 


The column headings have these meanings:  
|  Text  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  call  |  The phase of the query, whether it is parse, execute, fetch or the total.  |  
|  count  |  How often the above phase occurred, or the total of all. The relative counts of the phases are important.   |  
|  cpu  |  How many CPU seconds were spent in this phase or the total  |  
|  elapsed  |  Wall clock time. The elapsed time relative to CPU time is important.  |  
|  disk  |  How many physical I/Os to the disk occurred.  |  
|  query  |  How many blocks were processed in consistent-read fashion. Normally blocks are retrieved for a query as they existed when the query began, not as they have been changed and/or committed by someone since the query began. This includes the rollback segment.   |  
|  current  |  How many blocks were read in current mode which means as they exist right now. For example, reading the data dictionary to find the extent information for a table to do a full table scan (that information is needed as it is right now, not as it was when the query began).   |  
|  rows  |  How many rows were affected by this phase.  |  
These are several things to consider:
  * Ratio of parse count to execute count
Ideally, you parse an SQL once and execute it frequently. You would like this to be close to 0, which is the inverse of the statspack execute to parse %. You want that ratio to be high. Otherwise, there is too much hard parsing, and this causes latch contention on the shared pool. This includes soft parses. So, the ratio can be improved using the session cursor cache. 
  * Most SQL has an execute count of 1
Most of the SQL is not using bind variables. Therefore, the SQL cannot be reused. Again, this causes too much hard parsing which causes latch contention on the shared pool. 
  * Large disparity between elapsed and CPU time
The query is spending a lot of time waiting for something without doing much work. You can see the Waits in the raw .trc file. 
  * Large CPU or elapsed values
An expensive query that should be examined.
  * Ratio of fetch count to rows fetched
The process running the query is not bulk fetching the rows, which causes excessive round trips to the database. You should investigate this issue. 
  * High disk count
On the first execution, blocks may be fetched from disk. Subsequent executions should find much of the data in memory. But, if disk count is close to the sum of the query and is current, most blocks were fetched from disk. This is very expensive, and you should should investigate the issue. You may have to do some SGA resizing. 
  * An excessively high query or current count
The query is doing a lot of work with a lot of data. This may or may not be an issue for this query. But, this is where work is being done, so it should not be ignored. 


The next line of the report indicates how often the query was executed, but it could not find it in the shared pool causing a hard parse. You would like this to be 0 for most sessions. This can be affected by the size of the shared pool. 
The next line is the execution plan itself. These can be complex, which is acceptable, but you typically do not want to see full table scans (unless it is a tiny table, DUAL, or some metadata tables), full index scans, or the use of an inappropriate index. Often this indicates that indexes are missing, incorrect, or that statistics are missing or out of date (and wrong).   
|  Example 1 TABLE ACCESS FULL B$GC_TERM_T  OR  0 INDEX FULL SCAN IDX_AOIQUERYRESULT_FID (object id 66562)  |  
| --- |

#### Using Statspack to Investigate Performance Problems

##### Buffer Busy Waits
A buffer busy wait means a user wants to access a buffer but cannot because another process is currently using the buffer. Common buffer classes that have buffer busy waits include data block, segment header, undo header, and undo block. 
Identify the type of class contended for by looking at section Buffer wait Statistics for DB: in the STATSPACK report or querying V$WAITSTAT: 
SQL> select * from V$WAITSTAT where count > 0 ORDER BY count DESC;
To identify the segment contended for, check the P1 (File ID) and the P2 (Block ID) in the V$SESSION_WAIT table, and then query DBA_EXTENTS using those values: 
SQL> select owner, segment_name from DBA_EXTENTS where file_id = <&p1> and <&p2> between block_id and block_id + blocks - 1;
  * If the contention is on the segment header, this is most likely [freelist contention](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/S4jvdcIUI__JAf_wLe12pw). 
  * If the contention is on a data block (tables or indexes but not the segment header), check for SQL statements using unselective indexes, or consider using automatic segment-space management, or increasing freelists to avoid multiple processes attempting to insert into the same block. 
  * If the contention is on rollback segment header (undo header) and you are not using automatic undo management, consider creating additional rollback segments. 
  * If the contention is on rollback segment block (undo block) and you are not using automatic undo management, consider making rollback segment sizes larger.

##### CPU Time
An entry in the Statspack report under CPU Time might mean that the system is doing work or it might mean that excessive time is spent spinning trying to get a latch. Check Spin and Sleep times on the [shared pool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mCyfpWPfWY_4VzJPeAk74g).

##### db File Scattered Read
This event signifies that the user process is reading buffers into the SGA buffer cache and is waiting for a physical I/O call to return. A db file scattered read issues a scatter-read to read the data into multiple discontinuous memory locations. A scattered read is usually a multiblock read. It can occur for a fast full scan (of an index) in addition to a full table scan. 
db file scattered read correlates with full table scans and is often caused by a lack of [current statistics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YdEvzqUpbmI6PnVkcAEnNQ) or [missing or incorrect indexes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KfblQgnXlA8KWvy22nxvmw).

##### db File Sequential Read
The db file sequential read event signifies that the user process is reading buffers into the SGA buffer cache and is waiting for a physical I/O call to return. This call differs from a scattered read because a sequential read is reading data into contiguous memory space. A sequential read is usually a single-block read. Single block I/Os are usually the result of using indexes, and this event is typically an indexed read of a table.

##### Direct Path Read
When a session is reading buffers from disk directly into the PGA (opposed to the buffer cache in SGA), it waits on this event. If the I/O subsystem does not support asynchronous I/Os, each wait corresponds to a physical read request. 
This sometimes correlates with full table scans and is often caused by [lack of current statistics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YdEvzqUpbmI6PnVkcAEnNQ) or [missing or incorrect indexes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KfblQgnXlA8KWvy22nxvmw).

##### Enqueue
Enqueues are locks that serialize access to database resources. This event indicates that the session is waiting for a lock that is held by another session. 
Identify the type of lock by looking at section Enqueue activity for DB: in the STATSPACK report or by looking at V$LOCK.TYPE where ID1=V$SESSION_WAIT.P2 and ID2=V$SESSSION_WAIT.P3. 
The CF (control file) enqueue indicates that Oracle is modifying the physical layout of an object which indicates sizing issues. 
The TX (transaction) enqueue indicates that Oracle is waiting on a lock on a database object to modify a block (including a rollback segment). [Buffer wait Statistics for DB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/opVmZNla6SU1Vf8vk7bMhQ): usually shows what class is being waited on. The names of enqueues and their definitions may change from release to release.

##### Latch Free
A latch is a low-level internal lock Oracle uses to protect memory structures. The latch free event is updated when a server process attempts to get a latch and when the latch is unavailable on the first attempt. When the server attempts to access the resource (get a latch) and cannot, it spins some amount; if it still cannot get it, it sleeps for a while. When the server awakens, it tries again. This sometimes corresponds to an excessive use of CPU (CPU Time). 
  1. You can check the V$SESSION_WAIT parameter columns for this wait event:
     * P1—Address of the latch
     * P2—Latch number
     * P3—Number of times process has already slept while waiting for the latch
  2. You can query for latches being waited on:
SQL> Select n.name, SUM(w.p3) Sleeps FROM V$SESSION_WAIT w, V$LATCHNAME n WHERE w.event = `latch free' AND w.p2 = n.latch# GROUP BY n.name;
  3. You can also look in the Latch Activity and Latch Sleep breakdown in the STATSPACK report. Look for sleeps and spins on the shared pool, library cache, and cache buffer chains. You do not want these to get into the thousands. 


Latch contention on the shared pool is the most common problem. The main cause of this problem is excessive parsing. This can be caused by: 
  * Lack of statement reuse
  * Statements not using bind variables
  * Insufficient size of application cursor cache
  * Cursors closed explicitly after each execution
  * Frequent logon/logoffs
  * Shared pool too small

##### Log File Switch Completion
Log file switch completion typically means you do not have enough redo logs. You should have four to five redo logs of 10-20 megabytes each to reduce the waiting on I/O and improve CPU utilization.

### Placement Considerations
Many factors affect placement because it is a big part of NetWorks Core: 
  * The number of components
The number of components, especially the number of required or typically placed components, affects how long it takes to place a feature. A feature where five records are inserted places faster than a feature with 15. Consider combining some component records. See [Normalizing Your Data Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PfCO7mgSITqLQFfJvrEsaA) for more information. 
  * The number of button clicks and keystrokes required for elaborate placement techniques


These affect productivity. For example, require the click to rotate or right-click to skip rotate options only if they are needed. 
  * Attribute population
Combining attribution in a single record reduces the number of database inserts.
  * Common components shared by multiple features
These are a convenient storage mechanism for common attribution, but performance is affected when component views join to these common components. When the common component table is large, it can adversely affect accessing these component views during publish and in deltas processing. 
When the common component record is modified, the modification tracking triggers must also consider whether a record should be inserted into the MODIFICATIONLOG for the various component views (based on G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO). If a record is inserted, the subsequent deltas have to process it. If breaking the common component apart to other components of the various features is not possible, consider copying attribution to these other components to reduce the joining. 
  * The database tables of components that are common to many features
These tables get busy when many users place and edit features. Oracle latch contention can become a problem, causing users to wait in a queue trying to get work done. You can solve this performance issue to some degree with some database tuning. 
  * Triggers, functional interfaces, and relationship attribute interfaces
Make sure they are needed and that the ones you use are simple. Functional interfaces can perform better than triggers because they do not cause a query to the database. 
  * The number of relationships in which a feature participates
This can affect performance in the same way as the number of components. A feature with two relationships places faster than a feature with ten. It also requires less user input. 
  * The combination of display scale and tolerances
This can either streamline the placement and relationship process or severely hinder it. Tailor the metadata that governs display scale and tolerance for the typical user workflow at a recommended display scale. Use appropriately sized symbology and tolerances that are fairly tight around the cursor. Tolerances that find too many features or symbology that is cluttered at the working display scale inhibit the user. A variance in the workflow can require a variation in the legend. This takes a lot of thought and experimentation.

### Analysis Tools

#### Area Management

##### Area Manager Metadata
Area features to be supported by Area Manager are defined in G3E_AREAMGR. This example shows the relationship of [G3E_AREAMGR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AZsA57sOJ39k2_98~w2~PA) metadata table to the GC_AREA_P component table in the data model. All attributes populated by the Area Manager command must be contained in the same component.   
|  Example This component must be marked as a required component ([G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REQUIRED = Yes (1)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w)).

The following example illustrates how to configure the area management metadata. In this example, the building feature does not participate in cross-feature relationships and does not have a location identifier field. ##### Area Manager Permissions
[User roles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew) determine the insert and update privileges for a given user. To control which users can access area management commands, change the value in [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_ROLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) through Metadata Explorer. The default role is EVERYONE. 
Any errors returned when a user is adding areas or manipulating area hierarchies are propagated through Area Manager and appear in a message box.   
|  Example A user tries to change the hierarchy of an area feature that participates in cross- feature hierarchies. Because the user has not been granted the appropriate role for that particular update, an error message is generated and the action is ignored.   |  
| --- |

##### Area of Interest Location Identifier
[Area Manager](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ykH3h9jfqmoM~J7zDdsWEg) lets you specify an active [area of interest](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qHXXugtXmiSdqfVAuqIrFQ). An area of interest defines a geographic area for use in spatial filtering. The active area of interest name is stored in the Property Set (ActiveAOI) of the work space document, and its geometry is stored in the SpatialFilters collection of the work space document. 
An Area of Interest Location Identifier (AOILI) supports commands like Find and Simple Attribute Query. The area of interest location identifier defines a geographic location attribute which can be used to limit a query result set to a particular area without the need for spatial filtering. Area Manager sets the AOILI when an active [area of interest is set](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_eHRwl5U052WNDpbU_nHQ). Since the location identifier for a given area feature instance can be Null, not all active areas of interest have an AOILI. The AOILI is stored in the work space, and the current AOILI value displays in Area Manager, along with the active area of interest name. 
The [G3E_LOCATIONANO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AZsA57sOJ39k2_98~w2~PA) field in G3E_AREAMGR identifies the field in the area feature table used to store the location identifier for an area feature. If the value is Null for a given active area of interest, the command ignores the field, and no AOILI is set for that area feature. If a value is specified in this field, Area Manager has access to the AOILI for an area feature. The AOILI does not apply to work space areas, just to map areas defined as area features.

##### Cross-Feature Relationships
[Area Manager ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ykH3h9jfqmoM~J7zDdsWEg)also supports hierarchies between areas of the same feature class (same G3E_FNO). Some configurations require that the area feature data be split into multiple features (different G3E_FNOs) but still be related. For example, a feature table for user-generated areas and a feature table for third party provide read-only areas, such as landbase boundaries. Area Manager represents this hierarchy in a custom tree view control. All these area features are populated under a Map Areas node, which allows cross-feature relationships to be displayed hierarchically in the tree view. 
The field that stores the identifier of an owning area is still specified by the [G3E_AREAMGR.G3E_LINKANO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AZsA57sOJ39k2_98~w2~PA). This field cannot be Null, has a default of 0, and is indexed. This minimizes the cost of the queries being issued by Area Manager since full table scans are eliminated when each hierarchy level is queried. Area feature instances with a link field value of 0 represent the root level of hierarchy and are populated directly under the Map Areas group node. For example, if area feature table GC_BND_P has a link field called OWNER_FID, all areas in that table with an owner_fid=0 are populated first under the Map Areas group node. 
To support management of relationships between two or more area features (different G3E_FNOs), the G3E_AREAMGR metadata table includes a field called G3E_FNOANO. If an area feature is to participate in cross-feature relationships, this field is populated with the G3E_ANO of the field that stores the G3E_FNO value of the owning feature. The specified owning feature number field must exist in the same component table as the field specified by G3E_IDENTIFIERANO. An area feature that participates in cross-feature relationships can point to an owning area in either its own feature table or in another cross-feature relationship area feature table. 
If an area feature does not participate in cross-feature relationships, set the G3E_FNOANO value to Null. An area feature that does not participate in cross-feature relationships can still maintain hierarchies within its own feature component table.

#### Defining a Color Scheme for a Trace or Query
You can define a color scheme for a preconfigured trace or a preconfigured query.
  * To define a color scheme:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Color Scheme Groups node. 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260581), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. Type a name for the color scheme group to populate the G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUP table.
This table lets you specify a color scheme group so you can rotate a set of colors to be used each time a trace is executed to distinguish the results of traces that start with different features or use different attribute criteria. 
  2. To define a color and a fill color, select the Color Scheme node.
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260581), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. Populate the G3E_COLORSCHEME table:
      1. In the G3E_GROUPNO field, select the color scheme group name.
      2. In the G3E_TYPE field, select Color.
      3. In the G3E_COLOR field, click the ellipsis button, select a color, and click OK. 
      4. Type the ordinal for that color, and click OK. 
    3. To select more colors, repeat Steps a and b.
    4. To define fill colors, repeat Steps a and b with Color Fill in the G3E_TYPE field.
  3. Override the color scheme definition for a [preconfigured query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg) or a [preconfigured trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wT5bRN5qv6aqLtu~XM9Oow).

#### Defining a Symbology Override for a Trace or Query
You can define a symbology override for a preconfigured trace or a preconfigured query.
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260585) You can also use the defined symbology override with ad hoc query, spatial query, report on select set, and other queries. 
  * To define a symbology override:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Symbology Override node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260585), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  3. Populate the [G3E_SYMBOLOGYOVERRIDE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oMk8~MjPY9tN3rUC_XgC5Q) table. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260585) Any color field in this table that you leave Null defaults to the color you set up in Tools > Options. Also, you cannot populate all three of the color fields at the same time. Because of software constraints, one of the fields must be Null.   
|  Example If G3E_COLOR=1, G3E_COLORFILL=2, and G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO=3, you can populate fields 1 and 2, fields 1 and 3, and fields 2 and 3, but not fields 1, 2, and 3.   |  
| --- |  
    1. In the G3E_COLOR field, click the Ellipsis, and select an override color. 
    2. In the G3E_FILLCOLOR field, click the Ellipsis, and select an override fill color. 
    3. In the G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO field, select a color scheme group.
    4. In the G3E_LINEWEIGHT field, type a line weight value.
    5. In the G3E_TRANSLUCENCY and G3E_FILLTRANSLUCENCY fields, type a number for 0-100, inclusive. A value of 0 means that the override is opaque. A value of 100 means that the override is invisible. 
    6. In the G3E_POINTSIZE field, type a point size value.
    7. In the G3E_FONTNAME field, select the font you want to use.
    8. In the G3E_SYMBOL field, click the Ellipsis and select a symbol to use. 
    9. In the G3E_STROKEPATTERN field, select the stroke pattern you want to use.
    10. Click OK. 
  4. Override the color scheme definition for a [preconfigured query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg) or a [preconfigured trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wT5bRN5qv6aqLtu~XM9Oow). 

  
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260585) The translucency overrides apply to the same parts of the style as the colors, [with the exception of hatches](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260585). 
  * The normal color and translucency overrides apply to all parts of all styles that are not area fills. 
  * The fill color and translucency overrides apply to only area fills.
  * The hatches are an exception to this. The hatches get their override color from the normal button, but their override translucency from the fill drop-down list.

#### Defining the Reporting Parameters for Trace and Query
NetWorks Core provides functionality so you can preset the options for the reporting tabs in both Simple Query and Trace. You can preconfigure: 
  * Where the map output is displayed
  * Line weight override
  * Color overrides
  * Preselected reports and post processes
  * Use of the data table
  * Hierarchical tree presentation (trace-only)


This simplifies the interface for the user. For step-by-step instructions, see Step 7 in [Defining a New Preconfigured Trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wT5bRN5qv6aqLtu~XM9Oow) and Step 6 in [Defining a New Preconfigured Simple Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg).

#### Find Commands

##### Configuring Find by Component
The Find by Component function lets a user search for features by searching on attributes carried in a component common to the definition of several features. Since the search is based on components, a mixture of different features may be found in the results. Users must be careful using this command because queries of common components can easily return large numbers of rows (the common component tables are typically very large) if not properly qualified by attribute conditions. Because of that, you may choose to [associate a role](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew) with the Find method so that only select groups of users can have access to the method. 
Metadata
The following metadata tables are associated with Find by Component:
  * G3E_FINDCOMPONENT
For each configured Find by Component, populate one row in [G3E_FINDCOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/owAcB8aWk48hZOjxW4p9eg) where you can specify one or two components by which to search. G3E_FINDCOMPONENT includes a column for specifying a static SQL expression that is applied to the search query in addition to whatever other attribute conditions the user selects. 
  * G3E_FINDCOMPATTRIBUTE
List the attributes from the components that can be used as search criteria in [G3E_FINDCOMPATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ofrAFjjBA1F6OVHzkqITKQ). If none are listed, all attributes from the table or tables associated to the component or components are provided. 
You must populate one row in G3E_FINDCOMPATTRIBUTE for each attribute you want users to be able to include in their find criteria. A column is included to allow the search operators (for example, <, >, =) to be defaulted for each attribute. 


Related Topics
[Find by Intersection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eQVt_XCA3wM5jvahdzOtgQ)
[Find by Phone Number](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1j_W92V2jvwjA3WRfx64Tw)

##### Configuring Find by Intersection
The Find By Intersection method queries for two features, computes their intersections, and displays those intersection geometries in the map view. The graphics displayed for the intersection are temporary and disappear when the Find command exits. Because an intersection between two geometries can be one or more points, a line, or even an area, symbolization is configured in the metadata. You can include as many attributes as you want in the query conditions. All of the attributes in one Find Intersection definition are assumed to come from the same feature (FNO). You can specify default operators for each attribute, define an SQL expression in addition to the user-defined search conditions, and associate a role with the method, which restricts its use to a particular class of database users. 
Metadata
These metadata tables are associated with Find by Intersection: 
  * G3E_FINDMETHOD
The [G3E_FINDMETHOD.G3E_POINTSNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yh_nP3UzVZyGCMF8WCpQg), G3E_FINDMETHOD.G3E_LINESNO, and G3E_FINDMETHOD.G3E_AREASNO fields control intersection geometries display. These fields contain the style number (indexing into [G3E_STYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA)) for the point style, line style, or area style Find Intersection uses to display the intersection. Set G3E_FINDMETHOD.G3E_PROCESSINGFLAG 2 to get a display action associated with Find Intersection. The default setting is 1, which means to find the intersection and to drive the active map view to that location, but not to create a geometry and display it. 
  * G3E_FINDINTERSECTION
Each intersection definition requires one row in [G3E_FINDINTERSECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QuIg__2USUlQTQ149z4HcA) to describe the type or kind of intersection (a user identification string essentially) being searched for and an additional SQL expression that should be applied to the search in addition to the user- supplied conditions (G3E_STATICSQL). 
  * G3E_FINDINTERATTRIBUTE
For each attribute you want users to be able to include in their search conditions, add a row in [G3E_FINDINTERATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jXFvu0m5iAeQT3EiXJKe1Q), with its G3E_FIROWNO value set to the G3E_FIROWNO of the Find Intersection definition from G3E_FINDINTERSECTION. This is where you list the attributes users can specify in their search and a default operator for each. 


Related Topics
[Find by Phone Number](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1j_W92V2jvwjA3WRfx64Tw)
[Find by Component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lRAagLtSpKyym0k0faREkg)

##### Configuring Find by Phone Number
The Find by Phone Number function finds the facility feature to which the users' input phone numbers are assigned. This assumes that the phone number is stored in an external system and is mapped to some other attribute, like address, in the facility database. The external system returns the mapped attribute value, and the find queries the facility database for a feature that has the mapped attribute value. For example, in many communications systems the phone number is stored with the customer data in a database separate from the facility database. Find by Phone Number interfaces to that system through a custom software interface (specified in metadata) and, given the phone number, retrieves an address from the external database. The Find by Phone Number method queries for terminals (the feature class is configurable) that have a matching address. As with the other find functions, Find Phone Number can be [associated to a role](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew) to restrict access to it, and it also obeys the settings of the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME values [FindCountThreshold](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ). 
Metadata
Following is the metadata associated with Find by Phone Number: 
G3E_COMMIFACE
Arguments to the Find method tell it which feature in the facility database to query for and which attribute to use when finding the feature to which the phone number is assigned. The value used in the query is the value returned from the Assignment System Interface. These arguments are specified as a comma-delimited list in the metadata table, [G3E_COMMIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Gp7g5vbqXez~bEdYaOZHA). Set G3E_COMMIFACE.G3E_PARAMETER1 to the comma- delimited list of arguments, and set G3E_TYPE to FindPhoneNumber. The arguments are: FNO, ANO1, ANO2, . . . ,ANOn, where FNO is the feature number of the feature to search for and ANO1, ANO2,…ANOn are the attributes whose values are returned from the Assignment System Interface for use in the feature search condition. 
There is an exact correlation between the list of ANOs to query for and the values returned from the Assignment interface. There is no default behavior when an Assignment System Interface is not available. The method fails with an error message. 
Related Topics
[Find by Intersection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eQVt_XCA3wM5jvahdzOtgQ)
[Find by Component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lRAagLtSpKyym0k0faREkg)

##### Configuring Find Feature
The Find Feature command provides the ability to search for a predefined set of features using attributes from one or two components. You have the option of selecting up to two attributes from the list of attributes and any of the operators for qualifying the search. An inexperienced user can compose find criteria, such as find streets where street_name NOT LIKE 'BOSTON', that return a large number of records, affecting the performance of the database server. 
You may want to limit access to certain Find Feature techniques to advanced users because of its potential to return large numbers of features. A database role (privilege) can be [associated with a specific Find technique](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/98npgjEHVCisPal~SCrP~Q). 
  * To configure a find for features:


  1. Specify the feature to search for and one or two components from which users can select attributes to form their search conditions. 
  2. Define a row in the [G3E_FIND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k34upujY7Schco2~q76sMQ) metadata table for each find statement defined for find by feature. In this table, you specify the FNO of the feature you want to search for and the CNO and ANO for up to two attributes that can be used in the find operation. 


Related Topic
[Find Command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/98npgjEHVCisPal~SCrP~Q)

##### Configuring Quick Reference Find
[Quick Reference Find](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SgekrGq__JC7N5L2OYpoEg) is the default find method for the Find command. Quick Reference Find lets you predefine the search criteria in metadata, limit user input to specified search values. 
Quick Reference Find has these advantages: 
  * The interface for Find is specific and simple so users can perform the same basic finds over and over. 
  * The user performs only necessary searches.
  * The searches are less likely to significantly affects system performance.


Quick Reference Find supports constraining a find technique to an Area of Interest as follows. A special icon denotes Finds that cannot be executed unless an AOILI is set. 
  * Can use Area Manager to set a location value as an [Area of Interest Location Identifier](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ggWdOnoRza0MF7idjBc6oA). 
  * Can include the field that carries the location identifier value.
  * Can restrict the query to an Area of Interest, but with an attribute restriction.


You can configure Quick Reference Find metadata to do the following:
  * Determine if an attribute is required or optional for the search
  * Determine if the value given for one attribute can be silently reused in the query for another search clause 
  * Provide filtered picklists for a more efficient and accurate way to specify search criteria 


  * To configure a Quick Reference Find:


  1. To limit user access to a method to selected user groups, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Find Methods > <method name> node. In the G3E_FINDMETHOD table, select a role in the [G3E_ROLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yh_nP3UzVZyGCMF8WCpQg) field. 
  2. To limit the number of found items that can be displayed for any find operation, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Metadata Administration > General Parameter > FindCountThreshold. Edit the value the [FindCountThreshold](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) general parameter. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Find Methods > node. Edit the [G3E_FINDQUICK](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AoGKL7_Ay5AepP5qmfgKLA) table as follows: 
    1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, specify the descriptive name for the find.
    2. In the G3E_SQL field, specify the SQL for the search.
To include attribute values input by the user, you must use bind variable syntax to specify the location in the SQL of attribute values to substitute. This is standard syntax for Oracle queries with bound parameters.   
|  Example SQL> Select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID from GC_MANHL where ROUTE_NO = ? and ID = ?  |  
| --- |  
    3. To require an AOILI, select Yes in the G3E_AOILI field and add the AOILI information to the SQL statement.   
|  Example LOCATION' is a field carried on all your features, perhaps on a common component, which contains the name of the district that your facility is geographically located within. Area Manager metadata has been defined so that when a district is set to be the Area of Interest, the name of the district is set as the active AOILI. The SQL has this additional clause: And LOCATION = ? If this is the Nth attribute in the SQL, the G3E_ANO value of the attribute with G3E_ORDINAL = 'N' in G3E_FINDQUICKATTRIBUTE is -1, and the G3E_AOILI field of the find definition in G3E_FINDQUICK is set to Yes (1).   |  
| --- |  
    4. To restrict user access to this specific find method, edit the G3E_ROLE field.
  4. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Find Methods > Quick Reference node. Edit the G3E_FINDQUICKATTRIBUTE table for each attribute to be substituted in the SQL: 
    1. In the G3E_ANO field, set the value to -1 to indicate that this is the attribute which is to contain the AOILI value. 
    2. In the G3E_NULL field, set values that allow attributes to be optional:
       * Set G3E_NULL to Yes (1) for the attribute in G3E_FINDQUICKATTRIBUTE.
       * [Code the SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YeiChl92c~QRq7zCYa_8Sw) to allow for Null substitution. 
    3. In the G3E_ORDINAL field, set the numeric order of the attribute in the SQL string.
    4. In the G3E_REFERENCEORDINAL field, specify the ordinal of a previous entry whose attribute value is to be substituted here. It allows one entry by user to be used multiple times in the SQL. 
    5. In the G3E_PROMPT field, specify a prompt for the attribute. The default is the attribute's username from G3E_ATTRIBUTE. 
If G3E_PROMPT is populated, then it is assumed you want to prompt for the attribute again, even though it is the same ANO. If you only want a silent substitution, leave G3E_PROMPT = Null. 
    6. In the G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER field, [set picklist values](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Lkf2mgJjRV7KkYXdPTz7gg) so attributes filter according to a previous selection and interrelate accurately. For example, you can prevent a user from selecting a model of equipment that is not available for a selected manufacturer.

#### Measurement
NetWorks Core provides various measurement tools. Some are configurable and some are not. For the measurement tools to work accurately, the [coordinate system must be configured correctly](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Or1aBR2d0n3BsevDKXaLSg). You specify how to display units of measure, geographic measurements, precision coordinates, angular key-ins, and paper measurements in plots on the [Options dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3nxPh_3LEOwIVQLiXvJj8Q). 
NetWorks Core measurement commands, placement techniques, and construction aids can also be configured on the Options dialog box. The selections on the Options dialog box are not configurable in the database. You can define a work space template to perform measurement in specific units and [save the information in a template](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VhXWMx3pWz3QNSu5HKUrfg) for future use. 
Dimension placement uses units defined on the Options dialog box. The lengths of the dimension lines are stored in the database in meters. The angles of polar dimensions are stored in decimal degrees. [You can configure the units of measure and the format](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WFFVDt7QpsSiaibvihgbrA) of dimension texts displayed in the map view in G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. 
The Placement Length Display control shows various length values as a linear feature is being placed. In the case of cable, it displays the calculated length of the dynamic portion of the linear, the calculated length of the current linear component, and the total length of the cable so far. It also displays the length entered during the [Cable and Component IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg). These length values are all displayed in units specified on the Options dialog box, which are converted using the coordinate system. You can override the units and precision specified on the Options dialog box. If the placement technique lets you specify an ANO for any or all of the measurement fields on the Placement Length Display control, at runtime the Placement Length Display control displays measurements in the format you specified.

#### Optional Parameters in Query and Find
You can specify optional attributes in a simple query or in a Quick Reference Find using '(? is Null OR Column = ? )' or '(? = ' ' OR Column = ? )' syntax. This syntax yields the correct answer; however, '? Is Null' can cause a full table scan which affects performance. In the following query, if the G3E_ID column has an index on it and the TYPE column does not, the '? Is null' clause in the query causes a full table scan even if the value is passed for the optional G3E_ID parameter.   
|  Example SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID From Table1 A where (? is null OR A.G3E_ID = ?) AND A.TYPE = ?;  |  
| --- |  
Any queries you have built using this syntax are valid; however, you can eliminate the (? is null or Column = ?) syntax in G3E_FINDQUICKATTRIBUTE or G3E_SIMPLEQUERYATTRIBUTE for a performance improvement in certain queries which would otherwise result in a full table scan. 
In this approach, the optional parameter appears in the WHERE clause like any other required attribute. However, you must tag each optional parameter in the SQL WHERE clause with a /*G3E#*/ comment, where # is the position of the parameter as specified in the G3E_ORDINAL column in the G3E_FINDQUICKATTR_OPTABLE or the G3E_SIMPLEQUERYATTR_OPTABLE. You need a beginning and ending comment for each optional parameter. 
If a value is supplied for the optional parameter, the clause remains unaltered. If the value is not supplied for the optional parameter, the part of the SQL from the beginning /*G3E#*/ comment to the ending /*G3E#*/ is clipped out. 
Examples
If the query has another required clause, the '/*G3E#*/' comments appear next to each other before the AND: 
SQL> select G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from GC_MANHL where GC_MANHL.COVER_TYPE = ? /*G3E1*/ AND GC_MANHL.ROUTE = ? /*G3E1*/ /*G3E2*/ AND GC_MANHL.NUMBR = ? /*G3E2*/;
If all the parameters are optional, it is more difficult to tag the comment so that the final SQL forms correctly for all combinations of parameters. To overcome a situation like this, you can use a pseudo clause, such as 1 = 1, that does not affect the result or performance. If you add a 1 = 1 clause, the query below can be tagged with /*G3E#*/ comments invalidating syntax.   
|  Example If ROUTE and NUMBER are optional parameters in the query statement, define the SQL as follows:  SQL> select G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from GC_MANHL where 1 = 1 /*G3E1*/ AND GC_MANHL.ROUTE = ? /*G3E1*/ /*G3E2*/ AND GC_MANHL.NUMBER = ? /*G3E2*/; If both parameters are given values, the same SQL is executed. If the ROUTE parameter is not given a value, /*G3E1*/ GC_MANHL.ROUTE = ? /*G3E1*/ is removed from the SQL leaving /*G3E2*/. So, the SQL to be executed is as follows:  SQL> select G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from GC_MANHL where 1 = 1 /*G3E2*/ AND GC_MANHL.NUMBER = ? /*G3E2*/;  |  
| --- |  
The /*G3E#*/ comment pairs can appear wherever you want to. It depends on the nature of the WHERE clause. You must insert the comment appropriately and make sure that removing the part of SQL for an optional parameter (for which a value is not supplied) does not create invalid syntax. 
If all parameters are optional, all the optional parameter columns must have an index. At least one column in the WHERE clause for which a value is supplied must have an index on it so that Oracle does not perform a full table scan.

#### Query

##### AOI Simple Queries
Typically, a simple attribute query executes SQL as specified in metadata and prompts the user for parameter values. The user can further limit the area of the query with an area of interest (AOI). The polygonal boundary of the AOI serves as a spatial filter for the query results. 
An AOI simple query executes a query where no SQL is specified and the only criterion used for selection is the area of interest. To define a simple AOI query in metadata, set the G3E_SQL field in the query definition to Null. When the user selects an AOI simple query, the software executes as normal with a simple query, but does not prompt the user for parameters. 
  * To configure your system to perform attribute queries:


  1. [Set up roles and privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew). 
  2. Edit the following metadata tables:
     * G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY 
Each query type requires a row in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) table. For each row in this table, you leave SQL query statement Null, provide a query type, and specify an AOI or AOILI for the query type. 
     * G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING
The [G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IPzFsM76U2_yKiAgpL06cQ) table lists feature classes returned by each query type. This table is only used for query types that have the [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AOI](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) flag set. This flag is honored for AOI simple queries, such that the only features returned are those specified in this mapping. 
     * G3E_REPORTMAPPING
The [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table specifies reports that can be used by a specific query type. 
     * G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
The [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) = AOIMultiThreshold value lets you control the demand placed by query operations on the database when turning on the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AOI flag. AOIMultiThreshold sets the upper limit to the number of candidate items allowed within an AOI. The client software processes the features associated with the query definition (specified in G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING) within the active AOI. The keys of the features found in the AOI are sent to the database. The AOIMultiThreshold is the number of keys you want to allow the client software to send to the database. The larger the number, the greater the affect on the network and the larger candidate set for any subsequent processing of the query results (for example, in reports and post process operations). You must consider the typical usage of the AOI-constrained queries and estimate reasonable numbers of features that must be processed for the user to accomplish their work. If you set a low number, you may want to allow the user permissions to overwrite this threshold. This gives the user the opportunity to accomplish their task, but consider the size of the candidate data set before proceeding. 
AOIOverwriteThreshold sets the flag that lets users continue when the number of candidate items is greater than specified by AOIMultiThreshold with an AOI. If this flag is set to 1 and the particular user has the G3E_AOIOverwriteThreshold role, the user can continue with queries even when the AOIMultiThreshold is exceeded. 
     * AOIQUERYRESULT
The [AOIQUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yBNbOEGUr6KKiCjros7_vw) table holds temporary results from AOI processing. The combination AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_USERNAME and AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_QUERYNAME values must be unique. If records with a combination already exist, the attribute queries command deletes preexisting records before entering the new records. You should delete from this table records not used by any other queries. You should empty this table often to prevent it from becoming too large.

##### Attribute Queries
An attribute query is a search for features whose attribute values meet specified conditions. You [predefine and build attribute queries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zv8L7oFp4edvAQ_DH~KRNw) in metadata as one of the query types. These definitions appear as query types in the Attribute Query dialog box. A typical user of attribute queries is someone who is not SQL-literate and who is not doing exploratory analysis but who is generating everyday reports required in a company. A user simply must select a connection, give a query a name, select a query type, supply values for the attributes listed for the selected query type, and specify how the query results are to be reported. 
Some predefined query types may require that the user set an active area of interest (AOI) or have an [area of interest location identifier (AOILI)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260778) before the query can be performed. Different icons appear beside each query type that requires an active AOI or AOILI. 
An attribute for a feature that indicates a geographic location. Your system administrator can specify which attribute on the feature carries the location identifier. When using the location identifier for queries, the database is able to restrict the results to an area by attribute comparison, as opposed to true geometric spatial processing. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260778) Simple queries that contain dimensioning features are not supported. 
  * To configure an attribute query:


  1. To limit user access to a query, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries > <query name> node. In the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table, select a role in the [G3E_ROLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) field. 
  2. To limit the number of found items that can be displayed for any query operation, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Metadata Administration > General Parameter > FindCountThreshold. Edit the value the [AOIOverwriteThreshold](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) general parameter. This value lets you control the demand placed by query operations on the database by turning on the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AOI flag. AOIThreshold sets the upper limit to number of candidate items allowed within an AOI. AOIOverwriteThreshold sets the flag that lets users continue when the number of candidate items is greater than specified by AOIThreshold with an AOI. If this flag is set to True (-1), and the particular user has the G3E_AOIOverwriteThreshold role, then the user can continue with queries even when the AOI Threshold is exceeded. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries node. Each query type requires a row in the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table. For each row in this table, you predefine the SQL statement, specify a query type, and specify whether the query type requires an AOI or AOILI. 
  4. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries > <Query Name> > Query Attributes node. The G3E_SIMPLEQUERYATTRIBUTE table lists attributes for each query type that requires user- supplied values. 
To create a field value filter for the query, type a filter in the G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER field, to [set picklist values](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Lkf2mgJjRV7KkYXdPTz7gg). A field value filter causes attributes to filter according to a previous selection and interrelate accurately. For example, you can prevent a user from selecting a model of equipment that is not available for a selected manufacturer. 
  5. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries > <Query Name> > Feature Mapping node. The G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING table lists feature classes returned by each query type. This table is only used for query types that have the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AOI flag set. 
  6. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries > <Query Name> > Reports node. The G3E_REPORTMAPPING table specifies reports that can be used by a specific query type. 
  7. [Fine tune query performance](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GYg1KlgB3a268EoCnfPyyg).

##### Configuring Ad Hoc Queries
Ad hoc queries provide a flexible way to construct database queries for a feature class. A typical user of ad hoc queries is SQL-literate and may be doing exploratory analysis in a company. A user must select a connection, give a query a name, select a feature class, construct a query, and specify how the query results are to be reported. An [active area of interest (AOI)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_eHRwl5U052WNDpbU_nHQ) must be set before running the Ad Hoc Query command. However, users may disable AOI processing if they know that the database query as defined is specific enough to return few rows and that spatial restriction is not needed. Only [certain component types](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MnSNe2k7Xndz0jiF9Wu~6w) are available for user in ad hoc queries. 
  * To configure your system to perform ad hoc queries:


  1. [Set up roles and privileges.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew)
  2. Edit the following metadata tables:
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
The [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) = AOIOverwriteThreshold and the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME = AOIThreshold values allow you to set up controls on a constructed query on the database. AOIThreshold sets the upper limit to the number of candidate items allowed within an AOI. AOIOverwriteThreshold sets the flag that lets users continue when the number of candidate items is greater than specified by AOIThreshold with an AOI. If this flag is set to True (-1), and the particular user has the G3E_AOIOverwriteThreshold role, the user can continue with queries even when the AOI Threshold is exceeded. 
AOIQUERYRESULT
The [AOIQUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yBNbOEGUr6KKiCjros7_vw) holds temporary results from AOI processing. The combination AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_USERNAME and AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_QUERYNAME values must be unique. If records with a combination already exist, the Ad Hoc Query command deletes preexisting records before entering the new records. You should delete records that are not used by any other queries from this table and empty it often to prevent it from becoming too large. 
QUERYRESULT
The [QUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TlHDMU1nPqe2fM51xQZdWQ) holds results from a preexisting query when that query is used in construction of another query. The combination QUERYRESULT.G3E_USERNAME and QUERYRESULT.G3E_QUERYNAME values must be unique. If records with such a combination already exist, then the Ad Hoc Query command deletes preexisting records before entering the new records. You should delete records that are not used by any other queries from this table and empty it often to prevent it from becoming too large. 
  3. [Fine tune query performance.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GYg1KlgB3a268EoCnfPyyg)

##### Configuring Spatial Queries
The [Spatial Query command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EyT3LkUmIyuleQgLTmY8_Q) provides a flexible method for constructing spatial queries. A typical user of spatial queries may be doing exploratory spatial analysis in a company. A user must provide a query name, select feature classes, select existing queries or traces, select spatial operators, and specify how the query results are to be reported. An [active area of interest](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_eHRwl5U052WNDpbU_nHQ) (AOI) must be defined for spatial queries. 
  * To configure your system to perform spatial queries:


  1. [Set up roles and privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew). 
  2. Edit the following metadata tables:
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
The [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) = AOIOverwriteThreshold and the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME = AOIThreshold values allow you to set up controls on a constructed query on the database. AOIThreshold sets the upper limit to the number of candidate items allowed within an AOI. AOIOverwriteThreshold sets the flag that lets users continue when the number of candidate items is greater than specified by AOIThreshold with an AOI. If this flag is set to True (-1), and the particular user has the G3E_AOIOverwriteThreshold role, the user can continue with queries even when the AOI Threshold is exceeded. 
AOIQUERYRESULT
The [AOIQUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yBNbOEGUr6KKiCjros7_vw) holds temporary results from AOI processing. The combination AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_USERNAME and AOIQUERYRESULT.G3E_QUERYNAME values must be unique. If records with a combination already exist, the Spatial Query command deletes preexisting records before entering the new records. You should delete records that are not used by any other queries from this table and empty it often to prevent it from becoming too large. 
QUERYRESULT
The [QUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TlHDMU1nPqe2fM51xQZdWQ) holds results from a preexisting query when that query is used in construction of another query. The combination QUERYRESULT.G3E_USERNAME and QUERYRESULT.G3E_QUERYNAME values must be unique. If records with such a combination already exist, then the Spatial Query command deletes preexisting records before entering the new records. You should delete records that are not used by any other queries from this table and empty it often to prevent it from becoming too large. 
  3. [Fine tune query performance](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GYg1KlgB3a268EoCnfPyyg).

#### Trace

##### Performing a Trace

###### Defining a Trace

###### Additional User Columns for Traces
The trace logic supports the population of user-defined columns in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table during the course of the trace. User-defined columns are those placed on the TRACERESULT by a customer in addition to those required for use by the trace logic. The list of columns and their source values are specified as part of the trace definition in the [G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1f~vq~Sp6_UgJrOEhThl8Q) and [G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCfScaS0GVxKHwguY94sfw) tables. The only sources for data in the user-defined columns are expressions that can see values from the connectivity table or the TRACERESULT table. 
One possible use for this functionality is to populate a user-defined column with the value of a column in the connectivity table, and then to use the user-defined column as part of the filter criteria for the trace. For example, you can populate the user-defined column with the phase information of each row as it is traced. Then the filter criteria could be written to find only those features whose phase value is the same or a subset of the phase of the previously traced feature as stored in the user column. This provides for a dynamic, phase-aware trace of the network as is required for electrical analysis traces. 
You can define the connectivity table any way you want; however, it must properly model the type of connectivity for which it is being used. This makes it possible to include the information from tables other than the connectivity table in the user-defined columns. For example, you can create a representative database view that joins the connectivity table to another table, and that view is used for a trace as the connectivity table, making its information available to the various portions of the trace definition.

###### Defining a New Preconfigured Trace
The [Trace command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nUx1otd4A85WvYyaVA2U~g) requires user input for display and report options which must be repeated every time the trace is run. However, you can define a preconfigured trace in metadata so the information displays on the Trace dialog box. When the user selects a preconfigured trace, the Trace dialog box is preloaded based on the configuration associated with the trace, and all the user must do is click OK. The user can also override the metadata configuration. 
The following is a general workflow for defining a preconfigured trace:
  * To define a new preconfigured trace:


  1. [Populate the G3E_TRACE Table](javascript:;)
  2. [Populate the G3E_TRACEFEATURE Table](javascript:;)
  3. [Populate the G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES Table](javascript:;)
  4. [Optional: Populate the G3E_REPORTMAPPING Table](javascript:;)
  5. [Optional: Populate the G3E_POSTMAPPING Table](javascript:;)
  6. Optional: define a [color scheme](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1~8HuN_D3njzZb39c2n3Lg) and [symbology overrides](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Xbg3uNHPMcbvrpqA8aifrw). 
  7. [Optional: Populate the G3E_TRACEMAPPING Table](javascript:;)
  8. [Optional: Populate the G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS Table](javascript:;)
  9. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260579?tocId=wT5bRN5qv6aqLtu~XM9Oow) to commit the changes to the database. 
  10. [Publish the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ). 
  11. Execute the trace to be sure it works as you intend.

###### Specifying Filter Criteria
Use the filter criteria to include features in the trace, even when those features are connected in the connectivity table. Features that do not meet the filter criteria are not part of the trace results. However, the seed feature is always traced because it, by definition, is the first feature traced. Thus, the seed feature is not subject to the filter criteria. 
To understand how the filter criteria apply to the trace, think of it in the following manner. The trace tries to find all of the rows in the connectivity table that are connected to a feature that has been traced. The filter criteria is basically part of a WHERE clause that controls which features can be considered as candidates for being connected. The trace finds the features whose values in the node number columns are connected to the feature and then rejects those that do not pass the filter criteria. For example, the filter criteria for a specific trace of electrical primary conductors would eliminate secondary conductors from consideration, even though features in these systems are connected in the connectivity table. 
Some criteria inherent in the trace logic do not need to be specified in the filter criteria. The trace already limits the candidate rows from the connectivity table to those that have node 1 or node 2 values equivalent to a node number for an already traced feature. Also, the trace already ignores node values of zero when making the comparisons. 
The connectivity table and the TRACERESULT table are the only two tables whose columns can be specified in the filter criteria. See the Table Aliases section below to see how to qualify these columns properly for the filter criteria. 
Write the SQL to match the rows that are included in the trace.  
|  Example If you only want to trace through electrical features on the A phase and the phase column in the connectivity table is named PHASE, then the filter criteria could be specified as INSTR(PHASE,''A'',1)>0.   |  
| --- |  
The following SQL constructs should not be used within the filter criteria because these result in a syntactically incorrect SQL statement being built by the trace: 
  * GROUP BY
  * ORDER BY
  * HAVING
  * Hierarchical query (START WITH and CONNECT BY) clause
  * UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, and MINUS operators also result in a syntactically incorrect SQL statement being built by the trace. 


Table Aliases
You should qualify all columns used in the filter criteria. The alias for the TRACERESULT table used for filter criteria is ‘tr’. The alias for the connectivity table used in the filter criteria is ‘conn’. Failure to qualify a column existing in both the connectivity and TRACERESULT table causes an SQL parsing error because the column definition is ambiguous. 
The example listed above should have been specified as INSTR(conn.PHASE,''A'',1)>0 to correctly use the qualified table. 
Attribute Substitution
The filter criteria specification can include placeholders for attribute value substitution. Using attribute substitution allows for the specification of more general traces in G3E_TRACE, with the final criteria being determined dynamically.   
|  Example To provide traces that only trace through a single phase, then one trace can be defined in G3E_TRACE with a placeholder for the feature number to be used in the filter criteria. These placeholders instruct the Trace command to display a list of valid values for the attribute and then use the selected value in the actual filter criteria defined for that specific trace.   |  
| --- |  
The format used for specifying an attribute substitution is explained in the description of the G3E_STOPCRITERIA column. 
The preceding example for using attribute substitution for identifying the specific phase to trace through can be written as INSTR(conn.PHASE,''%2$s'',1)>0 with a row in the G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES table for the trace listing the G3E_ANO value for the PHASE attribute with an ordinal value of two.   
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257903)
  * This field should use the database values when writing the criteria for new traces, not the human-readable GUI values. 
  * Use four sequential tics to represent a double tic in the filter.

 |  
| --- |

###### Specifying Hints for the Trace
The [trace starts by finding](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nUx1otd4A85WvYyaVA2U~g) all of the features that are connected to any of the node numbers contained in the rows specified in the call to the Trace.SetSeed database procedure. It searches in all directions from the seed feature to find all of the features connected to those features. There are some traces where the user does not want the trace to search in all directions from the seed. The user may want to provide a hint to the trace by identifying a feature connected to the seed feature that specifies the direction the trace should proceed from the seed. 
You can define a hint by executing the [Trace.SetHint](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gmoVE_PqGobkR5ZI9938mQ) database procedure. Like the Trace.SetSeed procedure, the caller can specify a subset of connectivity rows for the hint feature if it has multiple ones in the connectivity table. 
There are two ways that the hint can be specified for the trace. Either a feature can be specified as the hint; or in the cases where there is an implied order in the connectivity model, the hint can be specified as being either upstream or downstream. The Trace.SetHint database procedure is overloaded, with one version of it supporting each of the two types of hint specifications. For any trace, you should call only one of these two procedures. 
Specifying Features as the Hint
The Trace.SetHint database procedure accepts a feature identifier value as its first parameter to specify a feature as the hint. There are two supported interpretations for how the hint feature should control the trace, and the interpretation is specified by another parameter to this Trace.SetHint procedure: 
  * The hint feature is the only feature connected to the seed feature that should be traced. This is the default behavior. 
  * The hint feature specifies which node of the seed feature from which the trace should be performed. The hint feature and all other features connected to the node that pass the trace criteria are part of the trace. 


Specifying a Direction as the Hint
The Trace.SetHint database procedure accepts a character value as its first parameter to specify a direction as the hint. Calling this procedure is valid only if your connectivity model has an implied direction. The directional hint simply means that the trace considers only one of the nodes of the seed feature as the basis for finding connected features. If the hint is upstream, the trace finds only features connected to the upstream node of the seed. If the hint is downstream, the trace finds features connected to the downstream node of the seed. If the trace is defined to consider whether or not the features are reversed, then this Trace.SetHint procedure respects that. The ReverseValue parameter for the trace relationship as defined in the [G3E_ADD_REL_PARAMS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VZWM99b10ZIUy_Qs_RyCNw) is checked to see whether the seed feature is reversed. 
Related Topic
[Trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PBl0PaWL45I~tGKlJQktSA)

###### Specifying Path Cost
[Path cost](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) specifies an expression whose value can be used to determine the cost of a path in the connectivity network. The primary use for this value is to support Minimum Path tracing. 
  * Table Aliases
You should qualify any column specified as part of the path cost expression. The alias for the TRACERESULT table is 'tr' and the alias for the connectivity table is 'conn'. Failure to qualify a column existing in both the connectivity and TRACERESULT table causes an SQL parsing error since the column definition is ambiguous. 
  * Attribute Substitution
The path cost specification can include placeholders for attribute value substitution. Using attribute substitution allows for the specification of more general traces in G3E_TRACE with the cost expression being determined dynamically. 
The format used for specifying an attribute substitution is explained in the description of G3E_STOPCRITERIA column. 

  
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257968)
  * This field should use the database values when writing the criteria for new traces, not the human-readable GUI values. 
  * Use four sequential tics to represent a double tic in the filter.

###### Specifying Stop Criteria
Use the stop criteria to restrict features from being traced through. Node numbers for rows in the result table that meet the stop criteria are not used to find connected features in the connectivity table. Features that meet the stop criteria are included in the trace results. 
When using stop criteria, the trace works by taking features that have been traced and finding the features in the connectivity table that are connected to them. If a traced feature in the result table meets the stop criteria, then it is not used as the basis for finding additional connected features in the connectivity table. 
The connectivity table and the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table are the only two tables whose columns can be specified in the stop criteria. See the Table Aliases section below to see how to qualify these columns properly for the stop criteria.   
|  Example If you do not want to trace through open electrical switches and the operating status column in the connectivity table is named OPER_STATUS and the value 1 means Open, then the stop criteria could be specified as ‘OPER_STATUS = 1’.   |  
| --- |  
The stop criteria can include any number of conditions based on the valid set of columns from the connectivity and TRACERESULT tables. 
The following SQL constructs should not be used within the stop criteria because these result in a syntactically incorrect SQL statement being built by the trace: 
  * GROUP BY
  * ORDER BY
  * HAVING
  * Hierarchical query (START WITH and CONNECT BY) clause
  * UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, and MINUS operators also results in a syntactically incorrect SQL statement being built by the trace. 


Table Aliases
You should qualify all columns used in the stop criteria. The alias for the TRACERESULT table used for stop criteria is ‘tr_s’. The alias for the connectivity table used in the stop criteria is ‘conn_s’. Not qualifying the distinct connectivity and TRACERESULT columns does not result in incorrect SQL syntax; however, the results of the trace are different than expected. Not qualifying these table columns results in the criteria being applied to potential candidate rows, excluding those rows that meet it. You should use the filter criteria to exclude features from the trace. 
The example above should have specified the stop criteria as ‘conn_s.OPER_STATUS = 1’ to use the qualified table correctly. 
Failure to qualify a column existing in both the connectivity and TRACERESULT table causes an SQL parsing error since the column definition is ambiguous. Example columns in both tables are the NetWorks Core keys (G3E_ID, G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, and so forth) and the node number columns. 
Attribute Substitution
The stop criteria specification can include placeholders for attribute value substitution. Using attribute substitution allows for the specification of more general traces in G3E_TRACE, with the final criteria being determined dynamically. If an electric application wanted to provide traces that stop at a specific type of protective device, then one trace can be defined in G3E_TRACE with a placeholder for the feature number to be used in the stop criteria. These placeholders instruct the Trace command to display a list of valid values for the attribute and then use the selected value in the actual stop criteria defined for that specific trace. 
The format used for specifying an attribute substitution is %n$s, where n is an ordinal number identifying each specific attribute substitution for a trace definition. The attributes that are substituted for each placeholder are defined in the [G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4JEiLQX9fCdOtc8E6UHuhA) metadata table. For a trace, attribute value substitution can be specified for multiple criteria (stop, filter, and path cost) and the same placeholder can be used in more than one criterion. The Trace command only prompts the user for a value once per placeholder, regardless of the number of criteria to which it applies. 
The preceding example for using attribute substitution for identifying the specific protective device at which to stop can be written as ‘tr_s.G3E_FNO=%1$s’ with a row in the G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES table for the trace listing the G3E_ANO value for the G3E_FNO attribute with an ordinal value of one.   
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257905)
  * This field should use the database values when writing the criteria for new traces, not the human-readable GUI values. 
  * Use four sequential tics to represent a double tic in the filter.
