###### Specifying the Feature Where the Trace Starts
All traces start at a specific feature, the rows in the connectivity table for the feature that defines the initial set of node number values to use for determining connected features. Define the start feature by executing the Trace.SetSeed database procedure. If the starting feature has more than one row in the connectivity table, the Trace.SetSeed procedure lets you specify a subset for the connectivity rows of the feature.   

Related Topic
[Specifying where the Trace Stops](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7EwsM0Y~n3UIke2M56gGuA)

###### Specifying Where the Trace Stops
The trace definition can specify when the trace should stop by using a specification of a goal for the trace. The goal for a trace can either be a specific feature identifier (a G3E_FID value) or a specific feature type (a G3E_FNO value). Goals are defined by executing the [Trace.SetGoal](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjPFbch1ZSiRoWIJXn82og) database procedure. 
How the trace reacts to finding a goal depends upon the type of trace being performed. For Point-to-Point and Minimum Path traces having a specified goal, the trace stops all execution once the final goal is found, regardless of whether there are still valid connected features that have not been found previously. This is different from the stop criteria that stops the tracing through specific features but which causes the trace to continue to execute and to trace through all of the other features. For Trace All type traces having a specified goal, the trace stops traversing through the goal feature itself but continues to trace all other features in the other branches. In this case, the goal feature effectively is nothing more than a feature that meets the stop criteria. 
Related Topics
[Stop Criteria](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aXTBFL5lmssKnN1AOkKPmg)
[Specifying the Feature where the Trace Starts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AwL3ksJHbHRXyaj_JMBWyA)

###### Traces Using Iteration Procedures
Control of trace execution is typically achieved by examining the attribute values of a single row in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table. In some situations, the information may not be in this row (attributes of the connectivity record or additional columns associated and populated in the trace). In other situations, the context of other features in the trace to the current point are needed to evaluate whether the trace should continue or not The specification of a trace iteration procedure can achieve control of the trace for either of these purposes. 
This mechanism for populating the additional columns is more robust than what is normally attempted through simple SQL expressions. The procedure is called after each iteration or breadth of the trace. The procedure can terminate the trace by raising an exception. Iteration procedures can be used to compute resistance and/or distance values along a trace. An example trace iteration procedure delivered with NetWorks Core is the [OTDR Compute Stop Criteria procedure](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xLI7mqPZCcmXXfK5BJN~4Q). 
The G3E_ITERATIONPROC column defines the name of a PL/SQL stored procedure that is invoked during the trace processing. The trace is performed using a breadth-first algorithm, and if this column defines a procedure, that procedure is invoked after each level of the trace results is determined. For example, an iteration procedure can be used to compute the values for user-defined columns in the TRACERESULT table for cases where the values needed in the computation are not directly available to the trace logic as it iterates. The information directly available to the trace is the information in the connectivity component for candidate connected facilities and the information in the TRACERESULT table for the features from which the trace is proceeding. 
A database procedure to be called iteratively by the trace, must be defined with two parameters, one that identifies the current trace results and the other identifying the set of rows that should be processed by the procedure. 
SQL> PROCEDURE ExampleIterationProcedure( p_TNO IN NUMBER, p_TraceOrder IN NUMBER );   
|  Argument  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  p_TNO  |  Number  |  Input  |  Required  |  Number of the trace being executed when this procedure is invoked.  |  
|  p_TraceOrder  |  Number  |  Input  |  Required  |  Identifier for the trace iteration for which the procedure is being called.  |  
To find the rows in the TRACERESULT table to be processed by each invocation of this procedure, query the TRACERESULT table for those rows whose G3E_TNO and G3E_TRACEORDER values are the p_TNO and p_TraceOrder parameters values, respectively. 
The logic in this procedure must execute as efficiently as possible; otherwise, the invocation of the procedure can negatively affect the performance of the trace. 
  
Related Topic 
[Trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PBl0PaWL45I~tGKlJQktSA)

###### Executing a Trace
Once the trace has been defined ([Trace.Define](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7mLgFNmifOwLeO1ugQuFdQ)), the seed has been specified ([Trace.SetSeed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lnH_2Gfe9zurP6KAy6xfnQ)), and any applicable goals ([Trace.SetGoal](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjPFbch1ZSiRoWIJXn82og)) and hints ([Trace.SetHint](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gmoVE_PqGobkR5ZI9938mQ)) have been defined, the trace should be executed by calling the Trace.Execute database procedure. This procedure performs the trace based on its definition and populates the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table with its results.

###### Processing Trace Results
Once completed, the results of the trace can be queried from the [TRACERESULT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA). The application performing the trace determines how the data are retrieved and for what it is used. 
There are some internal columns in the TRACERESULT table that can be used to determine the order in which the features were found. This is the order that the trace found them, which is dependent on the seed feature and the specific criteria for the trace. Do not confuse this with the order as related to the flow of electricity or gas through the network. If this order is important to your application, then the query used to retrieve the trace results should order them accordingly. 
Related Topic
[Performing a Trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7wdg1nL~uL749~pvNXTztw)

##### Trace Database Procedures

###### Trace.ConstrainByFIDs
This procedure specifies the database table used to constrain the candidate set of connectivity rows to be considered in the trace. Only features whose G3E_FID values are contained in specified database table are considered in the trace. If a feature's G3E_FID value is not in the specified database table, it is not traced even if it is connected to an already traced feature and matches all of the other trace criteria. 
PROCEDURE ConstrainByFIDs( p_TableName IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT 'G3E_TEMPKEYS');
The p_TableName parameter identifies the table in which the list of FID values can be found. It defaults to the value G3E_TEMPKEYS.

###### Trace.CurrentTraceNumber
This function returns the identifier of the last trace defined by the user in the current database session or the last trace specified by a call to the Trace.SetCurrentTrace. If no trace has been defined in the current database session or the SetCurrentTrace procedure has not been called, then this function returns Null. 
FUNCTION CurrentTraceNumber RETURN NUMBER;

###### Trace.Define
This procedure defines a specific trace to be performed. It specifies the criteria to apply to the trace, the trace name, and other important information. 
PROCEDURE Define( v_Name IN TRACEID.G3E_NAME%TYPE,
n_RNO IN NUMBER, 
v_StopCriteria IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL, 
v_FilterCriteria IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL,
v_StepCost IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL, 
n_TraceId IN NUMBER DEFAULT 1 ), 
v_IterationProc IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL );
The v_Name parameter is the unique name for this specific trace. 
The n_RNOparameter specifies the relationship number for the connectivity model used for the trace. The relationship number is defined in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP metadata table and is used to determine the connectivity table name as well as the names of the columns needed by the trace to understand how features are connected. For node-edge connectivity models, these columns are the Node 1 and Node 2 columns. For node-ordered connectivity models, these columns are the From/To feature number columns and the From/To feature identifier columns. For either model, the relationship number also defines the Reversed flag column. 
The v_StopCriteria optional parameter defines the stop criteria to use for this trace. 
The v_FilterCriteria optional parameter defines the filter criteria to use for this trace. 
The v_StepCost optional parameter defines the SQL expression to use for computing the cost of each path. 
The n_TraceId parameter should be the G3E_TRACEID value of the trace definition in the [G3E_TRACE_OPTABLE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LUxNXN9Fls_q~53n98Pd3g). 
The v_IterationProc optional parameter is the name of the procedure that should be called once during each iteration of the trace. The signature for this procedure is defined in the example Iteration Procedure.

###### Trace.Delete
This procedure deletes the specified trace, removing its records from the TRACEID, TRACERESULT, and TRACELOG database tables. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261576) For SQL Server databases, use the [Delete_](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ubXBuucgsLmTsrfR7yG_7A) procedure instead. 
PROCEDURE Delete( v_Name IN TRACEID.G3E_NAME%TYPE );
The v_Name parameter is the name of the trace to delete as defined in the TRACEID.G3E_NAME column.

###### Trace.Execute
This procedure performs the trace, subject to the trace definition provided in the calls to Trace.Define, Trace.SetSeed, Trace.SetHint, and Trace.SetGoal. 
There are no parameters for this procedure.
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261572) For SQL Server databases, use the Trace.Execute_ procedure instead. 
PROCEDURE Execute;

###### Trace.SetCurrentTrace
This procedure specifies a particular trace that should be returned by the Trace.CurrentTraceNumber function. This may be needed if the CurrentTraceNumber function is called before the user performs a trace in a database session and that function is expected to return a known value. 
Do not call this procedure when performing an actual trace. That is, do not call it between any call to Trace.Define and the subsequent call to Trace.Execute. 
PROCEDURE SetCurrentTrace( v_Name IN TRACEID.G3E_NAME%TYPE );
The v_Name parameter is the name of the trace as defined in the TRACEID.G3E_NAME column.

###### Trace.SetGoal
This procedure specifies a goal to be used in the trace. Only one of these two parameters should be defined when specifying a goal. Goals are required for Point-to-Point and Minimum Path traces. Any goal specified is ignored in Trace All type traces. 
PROCEDURE SetGoal( n_Fid IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL, 
n_Fno IN NUMBER DEFAULT NULL );
The n_Fid parameter is a G3E_FID value for a specific feature to be considered the goal for the trace. 
The n_Fno parameter is a G3E_FNO value for a specific feature type to be considered the goal for the trace. Any instance of a feature of this type is considered a candidate for the goal.

###### Trace.SetHint
You can use the Trace.SetHint procedure to specify a hint using a feature or a value.
Trace.SetHint using a Feature
This procedure specifies a hint feature to use to control the initial direction taken from the seed feature when the trace is executed. The hint feature must be connected to the seed feature. 
Only one of the overloaded SetHint procedures should be called for each trace.
PROCEDURE SetHint( n_Fid IN NUMBER, 
v_CidValues IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL,
c_IdentifiesFeature IN CHAR DEFAULT 'Y' );
The n_Fid parameter is the G3E_FID value for the hint feature. 
The v_CidValues optional parameter is used to identify a subset of the connectivity rows for the hint feature. This parameter should be a comma-delimited list of the G3E_CID values for the row or rows to use for the hint. If this parameter is not specified, all of the connectivity rows for the hint feature are used. 
The c_IdentifiesFeature optional parameter defines how the trace should interpret the hint specification. If this value is set to Y (the default), the hint is interpreted so that the hint feature is the only feature connected to the seed that is traced. If this value is set to N, the hint is interpreted as defining which node of the seed feature from which the trace should be performed. 
Trace.SetHint using a Value
This procedure specifies a value to use to control the initial direction taken from the seed feature when the trace is executed. 
PROCEDURE SetHint( c_Direction IN CHAR );
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257974) For SQL Server databases, this procedure is named SetHint2 because the database does not support overloading of procedures. 
Only one of the overloaded SetHint procedures should be called for each trace.
The c_Direction parameter specifies the direction in which the trace should proceed from the seed. If this value is set to U, the trace only traces from the upstream node of the seed. If this value is D, then the trace only traces from the downstream node of the seed. If the trace is defined to respect the Reverse flag, the ReverseValue parameter specified in the G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS table for the relationship used for the trace is used to determine if the seed is considered reversed.

###### Trace.SetSeed
This procedure defines the seed row or rows for the trace.
PROCEDURE SetSeed( n_Fid IN NUMBER, 
v_CidValues IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL, 
v_GroupValue IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT NULL );
The n_Fid parameter is the G3E_FID value for the feature whose rows are used to seed the trace. 
The v_CidValues optional parameter is used to identify a subset of the connectivity rows for the feature to seed the trace. This parameter should be a comma-separated list of the G3E_CID values for the row or rows with which to seed the trace. If this parameter is not specified, all of the connectivity rows for the feature are used to seed the trace. 
The v_GroupValue optional parameter is defined to support future work that is not available now.

###### Trace.Version
This function returns a character string that lists the current version of the trace procedures. 
There are no parameters for this function.
FUNCTION Version RETURN VARCHAR2;

##### Trace Examples

###### Electric Phase-Aware Trace
This example trace starts at the user-specified seed feature and traces out in all paths from there, only tracing those features that are considered to be part of the primary network and which share at least one phase as the feature that already has been traced. Secondary features should not be considered as part of the trace results. The application uses a node-edge connectivity model for its electrical network. 
The following matrix lists the phase combinations that can occur in this model and how they should be processed:   
|  Phase of feature  
previously traced  
(exists in trace results)   |  Phases of candidate  
connected feature that  
are valid   
(should be traced)   |  Phases of candidate  
connected feature that  
are invalid   
(should not be traced)   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ABC  |  A, B, C, AB, BC, AC, ABC  |   |  
|  A  |  A, AB, AC, ABC  |  B, C, BC  |  
|  B  |  B, AB, BC, ABC  |  A, C, AC  |  
|  C  |  C, AC, BC, ABC  |  A, B, AB  |  
|  AB  |  A, B, AB, BC, AC, ABC  |  C  |  
|  AC  |  A, C, AB, BC, AC, ABC  |  B  |  
|  BC  |  B, C, AB, BC, CA, ABC  |  A  |  
Because it is dependent on the actual phase values of the specific features that have been previously traced, this criterion can only be accurately evaluated while the trace is executing. The phase information for each candidate connected feature is stored in the connectivity table and is readily determinable. However, determining the connectivity information for the already traced feature is more difficult because the only information readily available for it is the information in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table, which does not include the phase information. This dilemma can be resolved by using the additional column functionality supported by the trace. A generic text column (USER_COL2) exists on the TRACERESULT table, and the trace can populate it with the phase information for each traced feature. The metadata to instruct the trace to populate the USER_COL2 column with the trace of the feature is defined in the [G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1f~vq~Sp6_UgJrOEhThl8Q) and [G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCfScaS0GVxKHwguY94sfw). 
Example Trace Definition
G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS Table  
|  Column Name  |  Setting  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TRACNO  |   |  Populate from the G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS_SEQ sequence in an Oracle database  |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALCOLUMN  |  USER_COL2  |  This entry defines how the USER_COL2 additional column on the TRACERESULT table should be populated.   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEEXPR  |  conn.PHASE  |  Set its value to the value of the PHASE column from the connectivity table  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  01/01/2002  |   |  
G3E_TRACE Table  
|  Column Name  |  Setting  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |   |  Populate from the G3E_TRACE_SEQ sequence in an Oracle database  |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Primary circuit phase-aware trace  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Trace in all directions from the starting feature, including only primary features with valid connecting phases   |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  7  |  The node-edge connectivity relationship number in this application is 7.  |  
|  G3E_TRACETYPE  |  1  |  Trace All—Indicates that it traces all paths that are found  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  01/01/2002  |   |  
|  G3E_PROMPTFORGOAL  |  0  |  Do not prompt  |  
|  G3E_PROMPTFORHINT  |  N  |  Do not prompt  |  
|  G3E_STOPCRITERIA  |  conn_s.NORMAL_STATUS=''OPEN''   |  Stop at all open features  |  
|  G3E_FILTERCRITERIA  |  conn.G3E_FNO < 50 and (INSTR(conn.CD_PHASE,NVL(SUBSTR  
(tr.USER_COL2,1,1),''Q''),1)+INSTR  
(conn.CD_PHASE,NVL(SUBSTR  
(tr.USER_COL2,2,1),''Q''),1)+INSTR  
(conn.CD_PHASE,NVL(SUBSTR  
(tr.USER_COL2,3,1),''Q''),1) ) >0  |  G3E_FNO<50 includes only the primary features. The INSTR functions verifies that the feature's phase contains at least one phase the same as the previously traced feature.   |  
|  G3E_PATHCOST  |  Null  |  Not applicable  |  
|  G3E_GOALFNO  |  Null  |  Not applicable to a Trace All type trace  |  
|  G3E_REVERSE  |  0  |  Not applicable since no implied order  |  
|  G3E_IMPLIEDORDER  |  0  |  There is no implied order maintained in this node- edge connectivity model.  |  
|  G3E_HINTIDENTIFIESFEATURE  |  Y  |  Default value. A hint is not applicable since the trace should look in all directions from the seed feature.   |  
|  G3E_GRAPHICRNO  |  Null  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  Null  |   |  
G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE Table (2 rows)  
|  Column Name  |  Setting  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |   |  Populate with the G3E_ID of the trace in the G3E_TRACE table  |  
|  G3E_TRACNO  |   |  Populate with the G3E_TRACNO of the additional column in the G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS table  |  
|  G3E_ADDCOLUMNTYPE  |  1  |  One row should set this value to one for the seed feature  |  
|   |  2  |  One row should set this value to 2 for the other traced features  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  01/01/2002  |   |  
|  G3E_TACPTROWNO  |   |  Populate from the G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE_SEQ sequence in an Oracle database  |

###### Electric Primary Network Trace
This example [G3E_TRACE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) starts at the user specified seed feature and traces out in all paths from there, only tracing those features that are considered to be part of the primary network (secondary features excluded). Secondary features should not be considered as part of the trace results. The application uses a node-edge connectivity model for their electrical network. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262087) This example takes advantage of the feature specifications in the customer's data model to make the trace definition easier. For this model, the primary and secondary features can be easily distinguished based upon the range of their feature numbers. 
Example Trace Definition

| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |   |  Populate from the G3E_TRACE_SEQ sequence in an Oracle database  |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Primary network trace  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Traces only the primary network.  |   |

|  G3E_TRACETYPE  |  1  |  Trace All—Indicates that it traces all paths that are found.  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  01/01/2002  |   |

|  G3E_PROMPTFORHINT  |  N  |  Do not prompt  |  
|  G3E_STOPCRITERIA  |  Null  |  Do not stop anywhere  |  
|  G3E_FILTERCRITERIA  |  conn.G3E_FNO < 50  |  In this data model, all primary features have a feature number less than 50 and all secondary features have a feature number greater than or equal to 50.   |  
|  G3E_PATHCOST  |  Null  |  Not applicable  |  
|  G3E_GOALFNO  |  Null  |  Not applicable to a Trace All type trace  |  
|  G3E_REVERSE  |  0  |  Not applicable since no implied order  |  
|  G3E_IMPLIEDORDER  |  0  |  There is no implied order maintained in this node-edge connectivity model.  |  
|  G3E_HINTIDENTIFIESFEATURE  |  Y  |  Default value. A hint is not applicable since the trace should look in all directions from the seed feature.   |  
|  G3E_GRAPHICRNO  |  Null  |   |

###### Electric Single Phase Primary Trace
This example [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) table starts at the user specified seed feature and traces out in all paths from there, only tracing those features that are considered to be part of the primary network and which contain a specific phase. The trace also should stop at any device that is open. Secondary features should not be considered as part of the trace results. The application uses a node-edge connectivity model for their electrical network. 
For this example, the trace processes only the C phase. The phase information is stored in the PHASE column of the connectivity table, which is assumed to have a not Null constraint. The same mechanism to distinguish primary and secondary features used in the previous example applies in this example as well. The status information, Open or Closed, is stored in the NORMAL_STATUS column of the connectivity table.

|  G3E_PATHCOST  |  Null  |  Not applicable  |  
|  G3E_GOALFNO  |  Null  |  Not applicable to a Trace All type trace  |

|  G3E_IMPLIEDORDER  |  0  |  There is no implied order maintained in this node-edge connectivity model.  |  
|  G3E_HINTIDENTIFIESFEATURE  |  Y  |  Default value. A hint is not applicable since the trace should look in all directions from the seed feature.   |

##### Trace Performance Considerations

###### Factors that Influence Minimum Path Trace Performance
The following factors can influence the performance of minimum path traces: 
Costs of Branch and Join Paths
It is not always feasible for the trace to abandon a potential trace path early. In the following example, once the second path to X is encountered, the trace could choose one of those two paths as the "minimum cost so far" and continue examining only that one path. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258037)
However, that is not generally feasible for the following reasons.
  * The paths encounter the feature at X on different iterations because there are a different number of features along the two paths from A to X. In this example, one path encounters X on the fourth iteration, whereas the other encounters it on the fifth. 
  * The first path has already progressed one feature past X when the second path reaches that point. In general, of course, the first path can be any number of iterations ahead when the second path reaches a given point. 
  * This process can occur on any number of paths because the trace examines all paths in parallel. 


To detect this situation, the trace must determine on each iteration whether any of the features just found had previously been encountered on another path, and whether that other path had a lesser or greater cost. If the other path had a greater cost, then the trace must stop the other path from advancing any further. This requires finding the current end of that other path, which in itself is a trace of the results. In most cases, this is not necessary because the trace is fast enough without it. Performing these checks adds some amount of cost but gains little in most usages. 
Effect of Single-Node Devices
The presence of single-node devices in a sequential minimum path trace is another factor influencing run time. To make a trace results include the single-node devices, the trace processing includes some special conditions for single-node devices, features that have only one connection point. On each iteration, if a path encounters a single-node device, any two-node features encountered in that path are pruned away. Those features are then found in the next iteration, thus making sure that the single-node features appear in their proper position in the trace. 
In the following example, feature B is a single-node device. In the node-edge connectivity model, both feature B and linear 4 are connected to the linear labeled 2. The third iteration of the trace actually finds both of these features but then discards linear 4. Linear 4 is found (again) on the fourth iteration, thus allowing feature B to be properly positioned in the traced path between linear 2 and linear 4. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258037)
This placement does slow down the trace somewhat because it causes the trace to examine some features twice. 
Related Topic
[Trace Performance Considerations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7CJWjG5XUlMd5BvLasCIQ)

###### Minimum Path Trace Performance Solutions
Some minimum path trace performance issues can be resolved with changes to metadata. The following are examples: 
Abandon Cost Altogether
You can abandon the use of a cost function in the trace and make it a point-to-point trace instead. The effect of this change is that trace always chooses the path that passes through the least number of features, subject to other criteria such as exclusions applied by the user. 
However, in cases where there are multiple paths, a point-to-point trace might choose a path that does not have the minimum cost had a cost criteria been applied. The results may not be the expected minimum path. 
Apply a Stop Criteria to the Trace
You can limit the length of the trace (either the length in terms of iterations of the trace or in terms of the accumulated cost) by applying a stop criteria to the trace. This is like the limit on the number of features allowed in an AOI query in that it prevents the user from making a request that requires too much work from the database. You need to experiment with the data model to determine the optimal criteria to apply. 
The effect of this solution is the following:
  * A route might not be found at all if the stop criteria terminates the trace before a minimum path is found. 
  * If the stop criteria limits the depth (number of iterations) of the trace, the trace could abandon some paths earlier than it normally does which could prevent a minimum path from being found. 


The trace can still find a path if there is at least one path whose depth is less than the limit. This result is better performance in some extreme situations but can also result in a less than optimal path. 
Eliminate Single-Node Features
Even with the changes discussed above, the effect of single-node devices is still a factor. If cost is eliminated, this effect is probably fairly small. But if you continue to use a minimum cost trace, this effect can be larger. The effect of course, varies depending on the data. 
Other Trace Criteria
You can apply other criteria to the trace to eliminate paths that are not productive. For example: 
  * Are there attributes on the features that could be used to tell when the trace is following a useless path? For example, is there an attribute like a circuit identifier? 
  * Is there an attribute stating that the feature is abandoned and should not be considered? Is that necessary? 


If so, adding that as a condition on the trace could reduce the number of paths examined, which would make the trace more efficient. 
Related Topic
[Trace Performance Considerations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7CJWjG5XUlMd5BvLasCIQ)

##### Tracing Single-Node Features

###### Regular Tracing of Single-Node Features
The regular approach for tracing single-nodes features is used for Trace All, Point-to-Point, and Minimum Path types of traces. The single-node features are not treated in any special manner and do not affect the tracing of the network at all. They are traced if a feature sharing their node number is traced. Whether they appear in the final trace results depends on the type of trace being performed. 
Trace All 
Single-node features are included in the trace results.
Point-to-Point 
Single-node features are considered when performing a Point-to-Point trace; however, they are never included in the final trace results. The reason for this is simple: the trace uses a breadth-first algorithm for performing the trace. That is, when it is tracing from a feature, it finds all of the features connected to that feature at the same time. 
Consider the following connectivity model:  
|  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  A  |  1  |  2  |  
|  B  |  2  |  2  |  
|  C  |  2  |  3  |  
|  D  |  3  |  4  |  
Features A, C and D have two nodes and Feature B is a single-node feature.
If the Point-to-Point trace is starting at Feature A and its goal is Feature D, both features B and C are traced at the same time. During the next iteration of the trace's breadth-first algorithm, it tries to find the features connected to features B and C and finds Feature D because it is connected to Feature C. Now that the goal has been found, the trace only keeps those features that are part of the first path found from the seed to the goal. That path is A- >C- >D. There is no way for Feature B to be in that path because the path to Feature C is always found from Feature A before it can be found from Feature B. 
For this trace, the trace results look like the following:  
|  Trace Order   |  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  Source Feature   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  A  |  1  |  2  |   |  
|  2  |  C  |  2  |  3  |  A  |  
|  3  |  D  |  3  |  4  |  C  |  
Minimum Path
A Minimum Path is like a Point-to-Point trace, differing in that it is looking for the path having the least cost from the seed to the goal, not just the first path. Single-node features are considered when performing a Minimum Path trace; however, they are never included in the final trace results either. The reason for this is the same as the one for the Point-to-Point trace: trace uses a breadth-first algorithm and although it attempts to process the single-node features, they are never included in the least cost path. 
Consider the following connectivity model:  
|  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  A  |  1  |  2  |  
|  B  |  2  |  2  |  
|  C  |  2  |  3  |  
|  D  |  3  |  4  |  
Features A, C and D have two nodes and Feature B is a single-node feature. All of the features are assumed to have a cost of 1 when determining the least path. 
If the Minimum Path trace is starting at Feature A and its goal is Feature D, both features B and C are traced at the same time. The cost of getting to both of them is 1. During the next iteration of the trace's breadth-first algorithm, it tries to find the features connected to features B and C and finds Feature D because it is connected to Feature C. The cost to get to Feature D is 2. It actually considers the path from Feature B to Feature C, but it rejects it because the cost to get to Feature C from Feature B (2) is more than the cost already found to get to Feature C from Feature A (1). Now that the goal has been found, the trace only keeps those features that are part of the least cost path found from the seed to the goal. That path is A to C to D. Feature B is not included in that path because the cost of a path from Feature A to Feature C is always less than the cost from Feature A to Feature B to Feature C. Note that Minimum Path traces do not support negative path costs. Also note that if Feature B's cost was zero, the path from Feature A to Feature C still takes precedence over the A to B to C path because it is found first. 
For this trace, the trace results look like the following:  
|  Trace Order   |  Feature   |  Path Cost   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  Source Feature   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  A  |  0  |  1  |  2  |   |  
|  2  |  C  |  1  |  2  |  3  |  A  |  
|  3  |  D  |  2  |  3  |  4  |  C  |  
Single-Node Features that Meet the Stop Criteria
The previous examples did not consider what would happen if the single-node features met the stop criteria of the trace. For both the Point-to-Point and Minimum Path trace algorithms, if a single-node feature meets the stop criteria for the trace, then the trace does not proceed through it. In the examples above, if Feature B meets the stop criteria, then the path from Feature B to Feature C is never considered. Feature C is still in the trace results because it is traced from Feature A, unless the filter criteria precludes this. 
Related Topic
[Specifying Where the Trace Stops](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7EwsM0Y~n3UIke2M56gGuA)

###### Sequential Tracing of Single-Node Features
In some connectivity models, some features are modeled as single-node features when logically they should have more nodes defined for them. The most common reason for modeling these features as single-node features is that the complexity that would be required to model all of the actual connectivity paths through them is deemed to be too much. For example, some manhole and conduit connectivity models do this. They model the conduits that are connected between the manholes (or other structures), but they do not directly model the duct paths in the conduit. The manholes and other structures are modeled as single-node features, even though there can be multiple, logical connected paths between the conduits connected to the manhole. Some of the functionality that is based upon a trace wants the trace to treat these single-node features like they had more than one node. That is, the trace needs to consider the single-node feature as being between the features connected to them, just like they would be if they were modeled having three or more nodes. For example, a cable allocation routine run on the manhole and conduit network wants the trace to process the single-node manholes before continuing out into any of the other conduits connected to it. 
There are two trace types that interpret single-node features in this manner: Sequential Point-to-Point and Sequential Minimum Path traces. 
Sequential Point-to-Point
The Sequential Point-to-Point trace algorithm is different from the regular Point-to-Point algorithm. If there are any single-node features on a node, they are traced through before the other features connected to that node. Referring to the same sample network as above,   
|  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  A  |  1  |  2  |  
|  B  |  2  |  2  |  
|  C  |  2  |  3  |  
|  D  |  3  |  4  |  
the path from features A to B are considered; the path from features A to C are not. This results in any single- node features that are along the first path found from the seed to the goal being retained in the trace results. After performing the Sequential Point-to-Point trace, the trace results look like the following:   
|  Trace Order   |  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  Source Feature   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  A  |  1  |  2  |   |  
|  2  |  B  |  2  |  2  |  A  |  
|  3  |  C  |  2  |  3  |  B  |  
|  4  |  D  |  3  |  4  |  C  |  
If there are multiple single-node features at a node, only one of them is traced through in the trace results. That is, the features traced at the next depth have their Source identification columns in the TRACERESULT table refer to just one of the multiple single-node features at the previous depth. However, all of those single-node features are still included in the results of the trace. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258033) The performance of this trace algorithm may be less than the current Point- to-Point trace because it takes more iterations to trace the network if there are single-node features. 
Sequential Minimum Path
The Sequential Minimum Path trace algorithm is different than the regular Minimum Path trace algorithm. If there are any single-node features on a node, they are traced through before the other features connected to that node. Referring to the same sample network as above.   
|  Feature   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  A  |  1  |  2  |  
|  B  |  2  |  2  |  
|  C  |  2  |  3  |  
|  D  |  3  |  4  |  
The path from features A to B is considered; the path from features A to C are not. This results in any single-node features that are along the minimum cost path found from the seed to the goal being retained in the trace results. After performing the Sequential Minimum Path trace, the trace results look like the following:   
|  Trace Order   |  Feature   |  Path Cost   |  Node 1   |  Node 2   |  Source Feature   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  A  |  0  |  1  |  2  |   |  
|  2  |  B  |  1  |  2  |  2  |  A  |  
|  3  |  C  |  2  |  2  |  3  |  B  |  
|  4  |  D  |  3  |  3  |  4  |  C  |  
If there are multiple single-node features at a node, then the cumulative cost of all of the single-node features are used to compute the path through the node. If any of them have an unknown cost (Null), then the cost to proceed through the node is unknown and a minimum path is not considered through it. This interpretation of Null cost is no different than what is done for the non-sequential Minimum Path trace, but this is more likely to happen in the sequential approach. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258033) The performance of this trace algorithm may be less than the current Minimum Path trace because it takes more iterations to trace the network if there are single- node features. 
Single-Node Features that Meet the Stop Criteria
The Sequential tracing algorithms are used to make the trace go through the single-node features at a node before proceeding. If there is any single-node feature at that node that meets the stop criteria, then no other features connected to that node are traced through. All of the single-node features at the node are included in the trace results.

##### Types of Traces

###### AOI Constrained Traces Tables
These are the tables associated with AOI constrained traces:
Database Tables
  * [G3E_TEMPKEYS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qz7ge1G5urinMDvJE0DmSQ)
This table contains the AOI-filtered keys of features.
  * [TRACEID.G3E_FIDCONSTRAINED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9jAzIk25UIl_DKCBfBKwtg)
This table specifies whether or not any feature identifier value constraints were used during the execution of the trace. If a call to the Trace.ConstrainByFIDs database procedure was made before the trace was executed, the value of this column is set to 1; otherwise, it is set to 0. 


Metadata Tables
  * [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ)
Add a row to the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table to support trace threshold, for example:
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME = AOIMULTITHRESHOLD  
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_VALUE = 5000 
  * G3E_RELATIONSHIP
Populate [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_UTILITYPKG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) for detail relationships that use AOI constrained traces. 


Related Topic
[AOI Constrained Traces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/p9D53~9X9JOsEblZEamaIg)

###### AOI Constrained Traces
You can configure the [Trace command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nUx1otd4A85WvYyaVA2U~g) to allow the user to use an area of interest (AOI) to limit the number of trace results. When an AOI is available and used, the command preprocesses trace results by AOI. If a feature participates in the network and part of the feature lies within the active AOI, that feature is included in the trace result. This diagram shows a typical network. The trace is highlighted in orange, and the start node is highlighted in blue. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262068)
As the diagram indicates, only features whose primary geometry overlaps the AOI geometry are included in the trace. When a trace exits and reenters an AOI, the feature is included in the trace. If the next feature is not in the AOI, all other features outside the AOI are excluded from the trace, even if the network reenters the AOI at a later point. 
Related Topic
[AOI Constrained Traces Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~HYnad8ITucbksTOg0PeWw)

###### Traces with Implied Order
Some connectivity models, particularly the node-ordered model, have features that are connected in an orderly manner. To understand these models, it helps to think of the node values in the connectivity table as being a From node value and a To node value. The From node of each feature is the one closest to the source (upstream), and the To node is the one farthest from the source (downstream). The only features that are validly connected upstream of a feature are those whose To node equals the feature's From node. Likewise, the only features that are validly connected downstream of the feature are those whose From node equals the feature's To node. This is the implied order of the connected model. 
If your connectivity model is based upon an implied order, as with node-ordered connectivity, or if you just want a trace to conform to the implied direction during its execution, you need to define your traces accordingly. Set the G3E_IMPLIEDORDER column of the G3E_TRACE table to a value of Yes (1) to instruct the trace to interpret the connected model as having an implied order. 
Using Is Reversed Flags in an Implied Direction Model
It also is common for connectivity models having implied direction to support the concept of an Is Reversed flag on each row of the connectivity table. This allows the system to model cases where the actual flow through a feature is in the opposite direction from the one implied by the From and To nodes. For example, this happens in copper wire telephony when they reverse feed through one or more pairs within a cable. The Is Reversed flag concept is valid only for those models that have implied direction and that are recognized by the trace in implied direction models. 
This flag complicates the determination of which features are connected to which. The only features that are validly connected upstream of a feature are those whose: 
  * To node equals the feature's From node and whose Is Reversed flag is set to the same value 
  * From node equals the feature's From node and whose Is Reversed flag is set to a different value 


Likewise, the only features that are validly connected downstream of the feature are those whose: 
  * From node equals the feature's To node and whose Is Reversed flag is set to the same value 
  * To node equals the feature's To node and whose Is Reversed flag is set to a different value 


If your connectivity model supports the Is Reversed flag concept, you need to define your traces accordingly. Set the G3E_REVERSE column of the G3E_TRACE table to a value of Yes (1) to instruct the trace to consider the Is Reversed flags when performing the trace. 
Related Topic
[Trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PBl0PaWL45I~tGKlJQktSA)

### Attribute Definitions

#### Basic Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
[G3E_ANO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The attribute number is the key in this table and is referenced throughout metadata. The number must be unique but has no other requirements. 
[G3E_CNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) and [G3E_VNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The fields for the component number and the view number are mutually exclusive. This value indicates the associated component or view. Indirectly, this tells NetWorks Core what table or view to query. 
[G3E_FIELD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The field name is the actual Oracle field name within the table or within the view.
[G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The username specification is used throughout the application. Most prominently, it appears when the attribute is referenced on a dialog box tab. 
[G3E_DATATYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Because NetWorks Core formulates a number of queries for data, the type of the column is needed to correctly use quotes around text values. You can populate the data type or the metadata triggers automatically populate it based on the Oracle field type. 
[G3E_IMPORTFIELD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
G3E_IMPORTFIELD applies to imported secondary data. The value corresponds to the attribute name in the secondary connection. This field is necessary to know the mapping from the original name to one that is acceptable to Oracle.

#### Command-Behavior Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
Many commands manipulate or populate attributes as part of their operations. Sometimes, the configuration requires more control over attribution than simply processing the values. The commands described here are limited by your attribute. descriptions. 
[G3E_COPY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Feature Placement uses attribute inheritance to copy values from the previously placed feature. The attribute values are inherited when G3E_COPY is set to Yes (1). The values are not inherited when set to No (0). 
[G3E_EXCLUDEFROMEDIT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The Common Attribute Edit command lets you select a set of features and perform the same edit of attributes in one step on all the selected features. 
There are typically system-maintained attributes that you do not want the user to modify. To prevent these attributes from being edited, set G3E_EXCLUDEFROMEDIT to Yes (1). The default value is No (0), which allows the attribute to be a candidate for editing. 
[G3E_EXCLUDEFROMREPLACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Within the Replace command, G3E_EXCLUDEFROMREPLACE denotes if the attribute should be excluded from the copy operation during the Replace command. The default is No (0), meaning the attribute can be copied. During replace processing, the command first looks at the Feature Replace flag and, if Yes (1), the feature can be replaced. It then looks at the Component Replace flag. If Yes (1), the component is copied from the original feature to the new feature. Then the attributes are reviewed. If this flag is Yes (1), the attribute is not copied. Database defaults are picked up for the attribute. 
[G3E_CATALOGCOPYVALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
For equipment catalog operations or assembly placement, the G3E_CATALOGCOPYVALUE indicates the value that is assigned to this attribute during the copy operation from catalog definitions. This can be a simple value assignment (Null, 0) or a PL/SQL function that returns a value compatible with the attribute. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256938) The word Null should be entered if you want to null out the field value explicitly. Do not leave the metadata entry null. 
[G3E_BREAKCOPY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
During the feature break operation, G3E_BREAKCOPY denotes if the attribute should be copied during feature break. This is only used when processing components of linear features that are broken through a relationship manipulation. For any G3E_DETAILID or G3E_GEOMETRY attribute, this value must be Yes (1). 
[G3E_COPYATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The G3E_COPYATTRIBUTE value denotes if the attribute should be copied during execution of the Copy Feature Attributes command. A value of Yes (1) copies the attribute, while No (0) skips the attribute. If an attribute is not defined in metadata, it is skipped as well. 
[G3E_MERGEEXPRESSION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
In conjunction with the Merge command, G3E_MERGEEXPRESSION produces the new value of the attribute of the resulting merged feature. Typically, the original values of the same attribute of the first and second feature (for example, a.MEASUREDLENGTH + b.MEASUREDLENGTH) are combined in some fashion.

#### Custom-Processing Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
In some cases, you need to do special processing when a component is created or when a particular attribute is set. Often this can occur in the database triggers, but those results are not visible until the next edit of the feature after it has been written to the database. The functional interface objects provide an opportunity for a project implementer to extend the capability of the system to populate attributes. 
The following fields support this definition:
  * [G3E_FINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)—Foreign key to the functional interface object definitions. 
  * [G3E_FUNCTIONALORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)—Indicates the order to call the interface objects when multiples are defined for a component. 
  * [G3E_FUNCTIONALTYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)—Describes when the object should be called. 
  * [G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)—Specifies parameters to the object.

#### Data-Integrity Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
[G3E_REQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Denotes if the attribute must be entered before posting the feature. The database table can be defined so that a Not Null qualifier forces a value to be specified before the row is added to the database. However, since the same schema definition is enabled in the field, a Not Null qualifier may be prohibitive if the data value is retrieved from another system. Accordingly, this specification is included in the metadata and is used by the application's validation component. 
If the field has an associated G3E_DOMAINTABLE or G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE, Null is an acceptable value during model validation unless the field is marked as required (G3E_REQUIRED = Yes (1)). To force the field always to have a value from the domain or foreign reference, set a database default appropriate to the reference table or specify it as required. 
[G3E_DOMAINTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) or [G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The definitions for domain tables or foreign keys are mutually exclusive and differ only in interpretation. A domain table is a static set of values that defines the allowable set of values for the attribute. A foreign key table is more dynamic in nature and implies a formal database foreign key relationship. 
The only real requirement levied by NetWorks Core is that the table specified in either G3E_DOMAINTABLE or G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE be a real table or view in the database. It can be a link to another Oracle database. 
[G3E_DOMAINFIELD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) or [G3E_FOREIGNKEYFIELD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
By specifying a domain or foreign key, you are stating that if a value is specified, it must be in the specified table in the field identified in the G3E_DOMAINFIELD or G3E_FOREIGNKEYFIELD, respectively. Domain and foreign key tables do not appear automatically as picklists. You must create a picklist definition for this table and then reference it either in the G3E_PNO field or on the tab attribute. 
[G3E_ADDITIONALREFFIELDS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Specifies a comma-separated list of additional columns to include when querying for the foreign key or domain table values. The resulting drop-down list for this attribute has multiple columns. 
Since picklists are not automatically created for foreign key or domain tables, this field definition is ignored unless you have specified a G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER for this attribute. With field-value filters, NetWorks Core queries the database to create the drop-down list without a picklist definition. 
When defining picklists for foreign key or domain tables that you want to have multiple columns, you should specify G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS to address this function. 
[G3E_RINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) and [G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Specifies the interface number and interface argument number used with custom attribute edit interfaces. This field is Null if custom interfaces are not used. The type of the relation interface must be Attribute Edit Control, Attribute Edit Control GUI, or Attribute Edit Control Definition.

#### Date Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
Date/time formats control the display of values for attributes of data type Date. Displayed values honor localization settings as defined at the operating system level. Short date format is always used for display purposes. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256926) Examples below assume a short date format of m/d/yyyy, a date separator of "/", a time style of h:mm:ss tt and a time separator of ":".)   
|  Format  |  Description  |  Example: Raw Value  |  Example: Formatted Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Date  |  Short Date  |  dec 12, 96  
01-01-00   |  12/1/1996  
1/1/2000   |  
|  Time  |  Time  |  00:00  
13:13:13   |  12:00:00 AM  
01:13:13 PM   |  
|  Date/Time  |  Short Date-space- Time  |  00:00  
4/28/97 12:00   |  12/30/1998 12:00:00 AM  
4/28/1997 12:00:00 PM   |  
For date fields, the year format presents only the year portion of the date value. If the user enters a date value that contains only the year, the remainder of the date value defaults to January 1 of the specified year and uses 12:00 a.m. as the time.

#### Limiting Edits to Attributes
You can limit user and software access to attributes. The primary effect of setting Attribute Edit Controls is that fields in dialog boxes that present values for editing override their metadata-specified state and set the values to read-only if the attributes do not pass the Attribute Edit Control conditions.   
|  Example You have an attribute containing an identifier from a remote system. Initially, you need to let the user assign its value, but you do not want that value changed once it has been assigned.  To control this, you configure the attribute to appear on a dialog tab as read-write. You then associate the Attribute Edit Control option for SetOnceAttribute on this attribute.  Now, if the value is already populated when the feature is edited, the cell is presented as read-only, even though the metadata definition is read-write.   |  
| --- |  
NetWorks Core delivers one [Attribute Edit Control interface object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkW1UUr9dzJpAJIzYiM5Hw) and two [Attribute Edit Control GUI objects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FVuLoPyYLAkI2uMYMblSxw). In addition, you can create your own Attribute Edit Control interface object through [automation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/71XrUBGIDjNCi2d7~Fi29A).

#### Metadata-Management Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
[G3E_EDITDATE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
All metadata tables contain the G3E_EDITDATE field. The Metadata subsystem maintains this date and uses it to identify fields modified since the last publishing operation. 
[G3E_LOCALECOMMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
All metadata tables that contain localizable fields, such as G3E_USERNAME, have a G3E_LOCALECOMMENT field. You may populate this field with instructions for the translator to describe the meaning and usage of the fields. See the localization section for more details on this process.

#### Numeric Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
Numeric formats control the display of values for attributes of data types Long, Integer, Double, Single or Currency. Depending on the format in use, displayed values honor localization settings as defined at the operating system level.   
|  Format  |  Description  |  Raw Example  |  Formatted Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  General Number  |  Not localized, normal precision, not padded with zeros; uses locale settings to determine decimal symbol.   |  1111.8888  
123.4  
1000000   |  1111.8888  
123.4  
1000000   |  
|  Fixed  |  Not localized, fixed precision, padded with zeros if necessary; uses locale settings to determine decimal symbol.   |  1111.8888  
123.4  
1000000   |  1111.889  
123.400  
1000000.000   |  
|  Standard  |  Localized, fixed precision, padded with zeros if necessary.  |  1111.8888  
123.4  
1000000   |  1,111.889  
123.400  
1,000,000.000   |  
|  Currency  |  Localized, fixed precision, currency sign. Precision is derived from operating system locale settings. Setting precision in the NetWorks Core attribute definition has no effect.   |  1111.8888  
123.4  
1000000   |  $1,111.89  
$123.40  
$1,000,000.00   |  
|  Percent  |  Fixed precision, multiplied by 100, percent sign.  |  .8888  
123.4  
1   |  88.800%  
123400.000%  
100.000%   |  
|  UnitConversion  |  Used for database fields that contain lengths or angles that are stored in units different than required in the display. See UnitConversion below.   |  1.0 (meter)  |  3.25 (feet)  |  
|  CFormat  |  Lets you specify modifiers like adding leading and trailing zeros to the number for display purposes.   |  3.3  |  03.30  |  
For Number Fields
  * The UnitConversion format supports any type of unit conversion supported by the UnitsOfMeasure object in the Coordinate Systems type library. This formatting converts the number stored in the database to the specified measurement unit. For example, the data in the database may be stored in meters but you need to present the data as feet. 
The specification includes the type of data to convert (distance, area, or angle), the database units, and the appropriate output units. The values in this specification must match the numeric values input to the ConvertUnitToUnit method on the UnitsOfMeasure object. These values can be found in the coordinate systems type library CCSCSSERVICES.tlb. 
The function takes four arguments:
    * Unit Type to convert—This is 1 for distance, 2 for angle, or 13 for area.
    * Input Unit—This is the unit of the data in the database. For example, 59 is a distance meter and 65 is distance feet. See the UnitConstants in the CCSCSSERVICES.tlb to find the appropriate value for your data. 
    * Output Unit—This is the unit of the data as you want it displayed. Use the values from UnitConstants in the CCSCSSERVICES.tlb. 
    * Format—This is one of the other formats (General Number, Fixed, and so forth.) that is used to present the value after the unit conversion.   
|  Example This is an example of this expression in G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_FORMAT: UnitConversion(1,59,65,Standard) The example converts a distance measurement (1) from meters (59) to feet (65) and then applies the Standard formatting rules to honor locale settings and precision.   |  
| --- |  
  * The CFormat displays the number using the specified C-like format string. The format descriptor specification is used to do the final update for presentation to include locale settings. 
The function takes two arguments: 
    * Format String—This is the same value that is used in your C "printf" function.
    * Format—This is either "General Number" or "Standard" and is used to present the value.   
|  Example This is an example of this expression in G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_FORMAT: CFormat("%010d", Standard ) The c-formatting in this example results in the decimal number being filled to ten digits using leading zeros and applying the appropriate locale settings.   |  
| --- |

#### Presentation Fields in G3E_ATTRIBUTE
Several of the definitions for an attribute involve presentation characteristics. If you do not include this attribute on a dialog tab, the information may not be pertinent. 
[G3E_TOOLTIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The G3E_TOOLTIP string is displayed for the tooltip when you hover over the attribute name in the vertical or horizontal dialog tabs. This value is best expressed as an instruction to users regarding the kind of information they should enter. 
[G3E_FORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
The formatting or presentation of the attribute value is controlled by G3E_FORMAT. Formatting is defined based on the data type of the field: 
[Numeric formats](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Gr~Zdm1AdWrUm2ywiA9r4Q)  
[Date formats](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MmItYXp5v4PiTf9v4UwMhw)  
[Format summary](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dc7vaYweQMJvMTl8GkE9_Q)
[G3E_PRECISION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Indicates the number of decimal places to display for numeric data. It is used in all numeric formats except General Number. 
[G3E_HYPERTEXT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Indicates this field contains a hyperlink to a file. You must also use the Hypertext format to achieve the blue text with underlining presentation. 
[G3E_PNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Specifies the default picklist. If one is not specified on a particular G3E_TABATTRIBUTE, this one is used. No validation is done against this list. The user may choose from this list or key in another value. This picklist is also used in find and query presentations. 
[G3E_WIDTHINTWIPS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Indicates the number of twips to use to define the width of the descriptive attribute column on horizontal grids. If this value is left Null, the software determines a best fit by calculating the width of the field descriptions. The specification is in TWIPS as that is a resolution- independent unit. 
You can approximate the width as a more familiar measurement unit as follows:
There are approximately 15 twips in one pixel. On applications for the Microsoft® Windows® operating system, there are approximately 96 pixels per logical inch. So, to make the column one inch wide, you would set the twips to 1440. The actual presentation of the data should be checked based on the font used and the resolution of the machine. 
[G3E_WRAPTEXT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)
Indicates whether the attribute's WrapText property presents wrapped text on the [horizontal grid](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928). It turns line wrapping on and off for text presentation, not text entry. You can set G3E_WRAPTEXT to Yes or No. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928)
Yes (1)—presents wrapped text; wrapping occurs before words that would otherwise be partially displayed. The wrap point does not exist as a line break in the data, and the presentation with wrapping does not change the data. 
No (0)—does not present wrapped text; no wrapping occurs and text is clipped at the cell’s right edge. 
[Horizantal Grid Example](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928)
  * This property does not affect what is seen in the map or the [vertical grids](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928). It affects only how text is seen in the horizontal grid cells: wrapped or clipped. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256928)
  * If there is a new line character in the entered string, it will display on the next line – regardless of the G3E_WRAPTEXT setting.

### Attribute Presentation

#### Attribute Inheritance and Preloading

##### Database Defaults
You can set up a database to provide default values for certain fields when you create a record. These default values are displayed to the user on Feature Explorer during feature placement. 
The default values displayed to the user are the ones existing at the time of the last metadata publish. The publish process copies the actual database defaults (USER_TAB_COLUMNS.DATA_DEFAULT) to the [G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/14u1vqSTxyc1WohRdZxqqQ) (in the field DATA_DEFAULT). The software uses these values to present to the user. If you change a database default after the last metadata publish, that default is not displayed to the user in the dialog but is honored when the feature is committed to the database if the user did not enter a value. 
Attribute defaults for features can be configured in the [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_DEFAULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) column. The user can overwrite default attribute values during edit or feature placement. To prevent the user from populating an attribute field, the default value populates the feature attribute field automatically.

##### Derived Attributes

###### Derived Attributes Algorithm
Here is how the auto-population software works:
If a triggering attribute value is changed 
The other triggering attribute values for this set are retrieved, and the filter prepared 
The query to the picklist table is issued 
If number of rows returned is 1 
All auto-populated attributes are populated 
with their indicated values from the picklist 
Else if the number of rows is greater than 1 
If the trigger values and auto populate field values all exist together in a single row, 
then 
no change is made to the auto auto-populate attributes
Else 
Auto Auto-Populated fields are set to NULL
Else if the number of rows is 0 
Auto Auto-populated attribute values are set to NULL
The call to query the picklist with the trigger filter is done for every change to a triggered attribute and is done whether or not the triggering attributes are populated. For example, if one or more of the triggering attributes are Null, the software could skip the attempt to auto auto-populate. However, some implementations carry Nulls deliberately in the picklist tables so that the software cannot take this shortcut.

###### Field Value Filter Example
This example is for analysis and shows that even though the list of values returned by the field value filter is 1, the user must still select the field and the value. The data model contains a pole feature with two attributes, HEIGHT and CLASS. Based on the class of the pole, constrain the height value to be limited to a smaller set than the complete set of heights. 
Attribute definitions:  
|  Attribute #  |  Attribute Name  |  Data Type  |

|  1  |  CLASS  |  Number(5,0)  |  
|  2  |  HEIGHT  |  Number(5,0)  |

|  Tab Attr #  |  Attribute #  |  Picklist  |  Field Value Filter  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  11  |  1  |  CLASS_VALUES  |   |  
|  12  |  2  |  HEIGHT_VALUES  |  #1 = CLASSFIELD  |  
Picklist for the CLASS attribute:  
|  KEYVALUEFIELD  |  
| --- |  
|  1  |  
|  2  |  
|  3  |  
|  4  |  
Picklist for the HEIGHT attribute (configured to display only the KEYVALUEFIELD column):  
|  KEYVALUEFIELD  |  CLASSFIELD  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  30  |  1  |  
|  40  |  1  |  
|  50  |  1  |  
|  50  |  2  |  
|  60  |  2  |  
|  60  |  3  |  
|  70  |  3  |  
|  80  |  4  |  
The Field Value Filter specification illustrates what is presented to the user.
  * #1 is a reference to attribute number 1. That is the CLASS attribute.
  * CLASSFIELD is the name of the additional column in the HEIGHT_VALUES picklist table.

  
|  Tab Attr #  |  Attribute #  |  Picklist  |  Field Value Filter  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  12  |  2  |  HEIGHT_VALUES  |  #1 = CLASSFIELD  |  
The software filters the picklist based on the assignment of a value to the CLASS attribute. The table shows the possible combinations.   
|  User entered CLASS value of:  |  List of HEIGHT values:  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  1  |  30  
40  
50   |
