In this example, the only height option for pole class 4 is 80. The user must select the attribute to present the picklist and then select 80 to make the assignment. The user has set the pole class to 4 and has reduced the selection of values for Height to the single value of 80, but the user still must select the height field and the 80 value. No automatic population has been provided when picklist selections are reduced to a single selection.

##### Job Classification

###### Job Classification Metadata
Populate the following metadata tables to accomplish preloading of attributes based on job classification: 
  * [G3E_JOBCLASSIFICATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ylYbo9sX_hlAaZaFMjuwSQ)
G3E_JOBCLASSIFICATION defines all the possible job classifications and associates them with unique numbers as keys. 
  * [G3E_COMMONJOBCLASS ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mmdABLrxETHK0EWrJwUqRA)
G3E_COMMONJOBCLASS
  * [G3E_FEATUREJOBCLASS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdY84rDOpCx0vvT6aIdEUA)
G3E_FEATUREJOBCLASS handles preloading of feature-specific attributes. This table defines the values to be preloaded for attributes of the particular feature being placed. Because the same attribute can have different values to preload depending on the job classification and which feature is being placed, this table is a mapping of job classification/feature number/attribute number to the value to be preloaded. Job classification, feature number, and attribute number make up the logical unique composite key on the table. 
  * G3E_TABATTRIBUTE
This default job classification is stored in [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_DEFAULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ). 
  * [G3E_JOBDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TBQDr_BsRYh8ej2Rr97t2g)
G3E_JOBDEFINITION defines information about the job table. It should have one row describing the job table. The G3E_CLASSIFICATIONFIELD field holds the name of the column on the job table that holds the job classification. If this is Null, attributes are not preloaded based on job classification.

##### Previously Placed Attributes
A user may need to copy certain attribute values from one feature to another. Once a user enters those attributes for a particular feature, those attributes are copied to the next feature and displayed in the user interface during the next placement for that feature. 
This capability exists regardless of the order in which the user places the features. If the user places a transformer, then a primary conductor, and then another transformer, the second transformer inherits attributes from the first, even though there was a primary conductor placed between the two features. 
The behavior of previously placed attributes by feature holds true even if there are common attributes shared between different features.   
|  Example State is an attribute on a common component shared by transformers and primary conductors. The user follows the same workflow of placing a transformer, then a primary conductor, and then another transformer. The user sets the condition on the first transformer to In Service and then sets the condition on the primary conductor to Proposed. When the user places the second transformer, the attributes that display in the user interface for the second transformer are preloaded to In Service just like the first transformer, not to Proposed like the primary conductor.   |  
| --- |  
This copying capability is valid only within a session. When a user logs on, there are no previously placed features, so the user must populate all the attribute values for the first feature of its kind placed in the NetWorks Core session. 
This restriction also applies within the same NetWorks Core session if the job classification changes. If the user changes jobs and the new job has a different job classification than the previous job, the software is set to have no previously placed features. 
You should not configure all attributes to take advantage of this capability. Attributes that are likely to be configured for copying are those that usually remain the same between features, such as manufacturer name, lot number, or voltage. Attributes that should not be set to take advantage of this capability are ones that change with each feature placed, such as unique identifying numbers or lengths.   
|  Example A utility buys transformers in lots from various manufacturers, and all the transformers from a lot must be used before beginning the next lot. Since the attribute for the transformer manufacturer does not change frequently, this attribute value is a candidate to copy from the previously placed feature. In this case, the you set the G3E_COPY flag to 1 for that particular attribute in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw). Because each transformer has a unique identifying number, the transformer number attribute is not a candidate for copying from the previously placed feature.   |  
| --- |  
Generating Optional and Repeating Occurrences
If you have optional components or repeating components (optional or required) and you want them to be automatically generated during the next feature placement, set G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_GENERATE to Yes (1). If this field is set to zero, the attribute inheritance occurs when the user initiates the component placement. The automatic generation of components is useful for certain data models like wire records within a conductor. The software does not automatically generate geometry components. Optional and repeating components are also pertinent to data models integrated with work management systems. Generate the ancillary CU components so that macro CUs are inherited correctly. 
Subclassifying Features
A feature class can be subdivided into classes so that its attributes that are available for copying are copied from a previously placed feature of that same subclass. These subclasses are treated as though they were different feature classes. This is important because attributes can change greatly depending on the kind of feature a user places. The attributes might not appear on the dialog boxes for one kind of feature as opposed to another. For example, a fiber cable and a copper cable are separate instances of the same feature, but they contain different components and have different attributes, which distinguishes between the two, treating them as if they were different features altogether. 
This differentiation is based on the value of a certain defining attribute. For a cable, an attribute distinguishes a fiber cable from a copper cable. This attribute instructs the software to treat these two as if they were different feature classes. The NetWorks Core software lets you specify the feature type, and the software retains information about these different types just as if they were separate features. As such, the fiber cable attributes are only copied when placing a new fiber cable. 
To enable the copying of previously placed attributes, set the G3E_COPY field to 1 for those attributes in G3E_ATTRIBUTE. If G3E_COPY is Null or zero, copying does not occur. 
To implement this functionality, place the ANO of the defining or distinguishing attribute for that feature in the G3E_CLASSIFICATIONANO field of the [G3E_FEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) metadata table. If there is no G3E_CLASSIFICATIONANO entered for that feature in G3E_FEATURE, there is no need to subclass this particular feature class. All features placed for this feature class are treated the same.

#### Attribute Management

##### Adding and Editing Attribute Values
The attribute drop-down list in the Metadata Explorer content panel lets you select the appropriate value for an attribute reference from a tree-like list of components and their attributes. The components are presented as top-level nodes, and the attributes for each component are presented as children of the component node. You can type partial names to position the tree to the correct component. This data entry is case sensitive. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261956)

##### Checking Attributes During Mouse Move
You can configure NetWorks Core so that when a user interactively places a feature and uses the mouse to establish a relationship, such as connectivity between features, only those features that can participate in the relationship highlights. You can also specify that certain features do not highlight. The software can compare the attribution of the active feature to the candidate features found within range to a value specified in G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION.G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE, or the software can exclude certain features from consideration based on their attribution. If a candidate feature meets the attribute relationship criteria you establish, the feature highlights when the user moves the mouse over it during feature placement or during reestablish relationships. 
The software minimizes the number of candidate features highlighted by weeding out features that fail attribute validation or excludes features based on attribution. Depending on how you configure [G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wu5b0VFREvrf2zqsFMydkQ), all attributes on each feature must match, only one must match, or candidate features with specific attribute values are prevented from being considered for relationships. 
You can use Metadata Explorer to add feature relationships and attribute validation. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Relationships > Attribute Validation, and add features and attributes as needed for your model. 
The following table shows some of the different ways you can configure G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION to highlight or not highlight candidate features. Each row has G3E_MOUSEMOVECANDIDATEFILTER = Yes (1).   
|  G3E_OPERATOR  |  G3E_VINO  |  G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Legal operators (with link to legal operators topic)  |  Null  |  Null  |  
|  EitherOr  |  Null  |  Numerical or range information  |  
|  InSetEitherOr  |  Null  |  between the two values separated by "-"  |  
|  RelatedNotEqualTo  |  Null  |  For example, Removed;Retired in Place. The attribute being validated needs to be part of the published view of the triggering component.   |  
|  CircuitNumber  |  CircuitNumberValidation  |  Null  |  
|  Phase  |  PhaseValidation  |  Null  |  
|  Null  |  Simple Copy  |  Null  |

##### Defining Attributes in Metadata Explorer
You can use Metadata Explorer to create attribute definitions for components and component views. The process of defining an attribute adds a row to the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260834) To enable the display of picklist values when you click Show Values on the[Filter dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OpcuoD9cXoWBKBN0R5c3jg), you must populate the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table to define the attribute for the component view and associate it with a picklist table to display. 
Before defining attributes in Metadata Explorer, the component or component view must exist in the data model and must be defined in the metadata. 
  * To define attributes in Metadata Explorer:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select one of the following nodes:
     * Core Schema Control > Components and Attributes
     * Core Schema Control > Component View Definitions
For example:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/iJEZ7OHv82BQK4aOppnh1g-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=78d6c1deed2f4b6b&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260834), or right-click and select Insert a new row. Select the table to which you added a component. 
  3. A new row opens in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table, for example:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260834)
  4. Fill in the pertinent information about your new component or component view.
  5. Click OK.

You can define a new dialog tab and associate it with a dialog box for a new or existing feature, or you can associate an existing dialog tab with a dialog box for a new or existing feature. After associating the tab with the dialog box, you add attributes to the new or existing tab.

  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialog Tabs > Unassigned Tabs node.

OR
To add the dialog box for an existing feature, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialogs > <dialog type> <feature name> node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256612), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the dialog box. The G3E_DIALOG table appears in the Help panel.

You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete an assigned dialog tab for a specific feature or all the features that reference this tab.

#### Dialog Tabs

##### Dialog Tab Filtering
Sometimes the dialog tabs defined for an edit or review operation are not relevant for particular feature instances. Dialog tab filtering lets you filter out irrelevant dialog tabs on a per feature instance basis.   
|  Example A transformer feature can be one of two types, either a Banked Single Phase transformer or a 3-Phase Unit transformer. Also, a dialog tab called Transformer Bank Attribute is defined as an Edit and/or Review dialog tab for the transformer feature. Attributes on this tab are only relevant to Banked Single Phase transformers. If the transformer type is 3-Phase Unit, this dialog tab should not be displayed while editing the feature. Using dialog tab filtering, you can control the display of the Transformer Bank Attributes dialog tab based on the type of the transformer.   |  
| --- |  
A dialog tab filter is an SQL clause defined per dialog tab used to determine when to display the tab. The SQL clause filters out dialog tabs that do not meet the criteria. The filter is evaluated during edit and review scenarios using Feature Explorer. Using the attribute values in the current feature instance, if the filter evaluates to True, the tab is displayed. 
To filter out the dialog tab for 3-Phase Unit transformers in the above example, define the following SQL statement: 
XFMR_TYPE = 'BANKED SINGLE PHASE'
Invoking the [Edit Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/d4albsW8_6OdtwDpC4mKXg) command evaluates the above Edit dialog tab filter. If the XFMR_TYPE field in the component recordset is Banked Single Phase, the dialog tab displays. If the XFMR_TYPE field in the component recordset is 3- Phase Unit, the dialog tab is not displayed. Similarly, the [Explore Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/52pN2fzrriwgeUjUOoh6mw) command evaluates filters defined for Review dialog tabs. 
Dialog tab filtering is applicable only to dialog tabs defined in the G3E_DIALOG table in the G3E_TYPE field as Edit or Review dialog tabs. To enable Edit or Review dialog tab filtering, define an [SQL clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) in the G3E_FILTER column of the [G3E_DIALOG table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) for dialog tabs with G3E_TYPE equal to Edit or Review. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259366) The NetWorks Core Web applications (for example, <Product5_Short> and NetViewer) do not support Review dialog tab filters defined for nongraphic features. Filters for graphic features are supported, but filters for nongraphic features are ignored.

##### Dialog Tab Presentation
Dialog tabs categorically display attribute values to the user. Each dialog tab is defined once in the [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ) metadata table. This tab definition includes a description that appears on the tab. It also includes the set of attribute values and their orientation (horizontal or vertical), and an optional sorting of the attributes. Attribute values are displayed to the user in a tabular format on each dialog tab. With a vertical orientation, a two-column display is used in which the first column contains a non-editable descriptive name for the attribute value and the second column contains the actual value. With the horizontal orientation, a multi- column display is used where the column headers contain the descriptive names for the attribute values and the rows contain the actual values. Only one row of data are displayed with the vertical orientation, and multiple rows of data are displayed with the horizontal orientation. Typically, repeating components are displayed using the horizontal orientation; however, this is not a requirement, and repeating components can be displayed using the vertical orientation. In this case, only the first occurrence of each component is displayed, and navigation to the other records is not possible. In the case that a horizontal orientation is used and the attributes that is displayed are taken from only one component table or view, the ordering of the attributes may be specified. 
After the dialog tabs are defined, sets of dialog tabs can be associated with a feature or placement configuration in the [G3E_DIALOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) table. Dialog tabs are grouped according to their type; the type of a dialog tab defines the context in which the tab is to be used. For example, one set of dialog tabs may be defined for a feature placement operation while another set of dialog tabs may be defined for a feature review operation. Because the same dialog tab can be used for more than one feature or placement configuration and can be used in more than one context, a dialog tab may appear multiple times in the G3E_DIALOG table. Also, each set of dialog tabs is ordered for display, meaning that the position of a tab within a sequence of dialog tabs is specified. 
Finally, the attributes that are to appear on each dialog tab are designated in the [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) table. This table also allows for the manipulation of the display characteristics of each of these attributes. The following list shows some of these manipulations: 
  * Attributes can be ordered; that is, the positions of the attributes within the attribute set can be specified. 
  * Attributes can be restricted, preventing the user from editing them. These attributes appear on the dialog tab with a gray background. 
  * Attributes can have default values. These values are stored automatically when the user is placing a new feature, and they supersede any database defaults. 
  * Attributes can be flagged as refreshable, causing other attributes within the same dialog tab set to retrieve their latest attribute values, thus ensuring that the most current attribute values are displayed. This is beneficial if the edited attribute fires a functional interface that sets other attributes within the same dialog tab set. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256620) Restrictions for attributes in dialog tabs and tab attributes: 
Attributes must be from the component definition, not the component view.
Only attributes from the feature can be displayed except as provided by [traversable attributes and the foreign key relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zyDeTpVX~ifJmb_qHrCnNQ). 
The [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table also allows the display characteristics of these attributes to be manipulated and provides for additional information about the attribute itself. The following list shows these display characteristics: 
  * The data type of the attribute, that is, whether it is numeric, text, or so forth.
  * How the data should be formatted for display on the dialog tab.
  * If the data should be treated as hypertext, in which case the hypertext data appears in blue and is underlined on the dialog tab. 
  * The descriptive name of the attribute.
  * If the attribute value is required before a job can be posted. Required attributes appear in boldface type on the dialog tab. 
  * A tooltip or string that appears when the user hovers the mouse over the attribute value on the dialog tab. 


Both the G3E_TABATTRIBUTE and G3E_ATTRIBUTE tables allow the user to specify [picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IlbDWhEtofQCqbDOjwdYjQ) information for each attribute.

##### Traversable Attributes
You can use traversable attributes to augment attribute data (that the user sees during feature placement, edit, or review) with records from tables that are not defined as components of the active feature. Traversable attributes are linked to non-component tables and allow you to retrieve the data you want, except for job attribute data. Attribute values from non-component tables appear disabled with other component table attributes of the active feature. There is no limit to the number of attributes from non-component tables that can be displayed for the active feature. 
A non-component table is not a component of the active feature. It can, however, be a component table in another feature. The non-component tables can be one of the following types: 
  * Foreign table
  * Domain table
  * Picklist table


Attributes displayed from these tables are specified in the dialog tab definition just like attributes from the active feature's component tables. Each attribute requires a definition in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) and is specified to display on a particular dialog tab in the [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ). The G3E_TRAVERSALANO field in the G3E_TABATTRIBUTE table must contain the attribute number of the traversable attribute that provides access to the non-component table. Additionally, the attribute in the G3E_TRAVERSALANO field must be an attribute from a component of the active feature and must have an entry in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. This definition sets up the link to the non-component table. The G3E_ATTRIBUTE entry for the traversable attribute must have one of the following defined: 
  * A table name specified in G3E_DOMAINTABLE and a field name specified in G3E_DOMAINFIELD
  * A table name specified in G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE and a field name specified in G3E_FOREIGNKEYFIELD
  * A picklist number specified in G3E_PNO (which links to [G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_TABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw) and G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_KEYFIELD) 


The traversable attribute is a foreign key into the table identified in [G3E_DOMAINTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw), [G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw), or G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_TABLE. The field identified in G3E_DOMAINFIELD, G3E_FOREIGNKEYFIELD, or G3E_KEYFIELD is the primary key of the foreign table. 
If the non-component table is not a component in any feature, an entry in the G3E_COMPONENT table is required for the table identified in G3E_DOMAINTABLE, G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE, or G3E_PICKLIST. Since this special table does not participate in NetWorks Core data management, set the G3E_TYPE value in G3E_COMPONENT to 2048.   
|  Example The select set contains a transformer feature and a pole feature, and the pole feature owns the transformer feature. As the user edits the existing transformer, the pole class that owns the transformer displays. The pole class attribute displays on one of the transformer feature's Edit dialog tabs. Now the pole class attribute is an attribute in the pole feature's component table. The component table's primary key is the POLE_ID attribute. A traversable attribute is required to access the pole feature's component table so that the pole class attribute displays while the user edits. The transformer feature's component table contains an OWNER_ID field that is a foreign key into the pole feature's component table. Construct the link into the transformer feature's non-component table as follows: 
  * Define an entry in the G3E_TABATTRIBUTE table for the pole class attribute so it displays on the transformer feature's Edit dialog tab. The G3E_TRAVERSALANO value for this entry is the attribute number of the OWNER_ID attribute in the transformer feature. 
  * Define an entry in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table for the OWNER_ID attribute as the link to the non-component table. The table name in G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE is the table name to which the OWNER_ID is a foreign key. This is the table to which the pole class attribute belongs. The field name in G3E_FOREIGNKEYFIELD is the primary key field name of the table specified in the G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE, which is the POLE_ID attribute. 

 |  
| --- |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256605)
  * If all the attributes displayed on a particular dialog tab are traversable attributes, all of these attributes must reference the same traversable attribute. That is, the same attribute number is specified in the G3E_TRAVERSALANO field. 
  * If all the attributes displayed on a particular dialog tab are traversable attributes, the G3E_DIALOGTAB.G3E_ORDERBYKEY is applied to sort the presentation of the non-component table or view in a horizontal dialog. All of the fields specified in G3E_ORDERBYKEY must exist in the non-component table or view.

#### Picklists

##### Attributing a Cable Feature Example
The following is an example of attributing a cable feature:
Example
ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE are set to trigger the auto population of MIN_MATERIAL, GAUGE, SHEATH, DIAMETER, and ARMOUR. 
Set G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_TRIGGERPOPULATE = 1 for ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE. This indicates these are the triggering attributes, and every time one of their values changes, a query is made to the picklist table (using the current values for ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE) to determine if there is a unique row for the auto-populated attributes. Because both are required to uniquely select a row from the picklist table, they are placed in the same set, shown by setting G3E_TRIGGERSET.G3E_SETNO = 1. The auto-populated attributes are MIN_MATERIAL, GAUGE, SHEATH, DIAMETER, and ARMOUR, so all have G3E_AUTOPOPULATE entries associated to G3E_SETNO = 1. 
In addition, MIN_MATERIAL is set as a single triggering attribute for populating the other six attributes. Its triggering filter includes ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE, and thus it covers the rare cases where ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE do not produce a unique row selection from the picklist. 
The following are metadata table entries for the example:

After you [define a picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9Yg6ihA3cnFyDNWYJO8G~g), you can use Metadata Explorer to [edit](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uJ2su9LHzXXrmA7Kp1Iwig) or delete it.

###### Editing Picklists in Metadata Explorer
After you [define a picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9Yg6ihA3cnFyDNWYJO8G~g), you can use Metadata Explorer to edit or [delete](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wgDnW2RwuhILy1HCtZTGQg) it. 
To change values in the picklist table, use [Metadata Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WEVSR0d6TDNPZMvRVOGUnQ). To view values that are already in your picklist table, double-click the G3E_TABLE link on the content panel. 
  * To edit a picklist:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Attribute Presentation > Picklists node. Find and select the picklist you want to modify. 
  2. In the content panel, edit the picklist definition as required.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260794) to commit the changes to the database.

##### Domain Foreign Key Query
The Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box lets a user [query into either a domain table or foreign key table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZkZbgsSB5fYFQ8gPPwEdHA) for a candidate set of attribute values. The Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box is the vehicle for constructing the query into the domain table or foreign key table, presenting the query results to the user and allowing the user to select from the query results. It provides a clearer presentation of the data for establishing an appropriate foreign key or domain association. 
For the Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box to be active, an attribute must have either an associated domain table or a foreign key table designated in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table, G3E_DOMAINTABLE column, or G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE column, respectively. To establish the attribute references, define the domain table or foreign key table in the [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table. For the component definition, G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE must contain the name of the domain table or foreign key table. The G3E_TYPE for this component is 2048. 
The Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box requires a dialog tab definition in metadata to identify which attributes are available on the dialog box for query construction. These attributes should reference fields in the table that were specified in the G3E_DOMAINTABLE or G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. Each of the attributes on the dialog box requires a definition in the [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) table and the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. You can define picklists for attributes appearing on the Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box. Currently, extensible picklists and multi-column drop-downs are not supported. 
As with other dialog tabs, the Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box requires an entry in the [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ) table. It is not necessary to specify an orientation in the G3E_ORIENTATION column since this does not apply to the Domain/Foreign Key Query dialog box. 
The dialog box needs at least one entry in the [G3E_DIALOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) table. The G3E_TYPE field in this table is the same as the name of the domain table or foreign key table. Set the G3E_FNO field to 0 or a valid feature number. Set the value to 0 so several features can use the dialog box, providing a more generic search into a domain table or foreign key table; set G3E_FNO to a valid feature number so the dialog box is more feature-specific.

##### Field Value Filters
Field value filters are a way to dynamically narrow the contents of a picklist using other attribute values from within the same feature or literal values. They are useful for instances in which the candidate set of values for a particular attribute depends on the value of a correlating attribute. Field value filters are applicable to predefined, domain, and foreign key picklists and are valid for dialog tab definition, Quick Reference Find, and simple attribute queries. 
Effectively, the filter is a series of [attribute value and attribute name pairs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) in the form of a WHERE clause. There is no limit to the pairs that can be specified in the filter. Moreover, you can use the AND or OR operators to connect the pairs and to group them parenthetically. The field value filter format requires that AND be indicated with an ampersand (&) and OR be indicated with a vertical line (|). For attribute values, a literal value or an attribute number can be specified. This attribute number is a G3E_ANO value from the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. When specifying an attribute number in the field value filter, a pound sign (#) should precede the attribute number. You can set a field value filter expression in [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ), [G3E_FINDQUICKATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/A6ETowTBPX9zvWT8Z7r15w), and [G3E_SIMPLEQUERYATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uJ3P5mNw~7NA~Kusg1kA8Q).   
|  Example A primary conductor has an Insulation Type attribute, a Group Type attribute, and an Operating Voltage attribute. All three attributes appear on a dialog tab for the Primary Conductor feature. The picklist values for the Insulation Type attribute depend on the current attribute values for Group Type and Operating Voltage. Suppose the G3E_ANO for Group Type is 101 and the G3E_ANO for Operating Voltage is 105. The field value filter for the Insulation Type attribute would be constructed as follows:  #101=GROUP_TYPE & #105=OPERATING_VOLTAGE This filter retrieves the values from the picklist table, specified for the Insulation Type attribute, where the GROUP_TYPE column contains the current attribute value for attribute 101 and the OPERATING_VOLTAGE column contains the current attribute value for attribute 105.   |  
| --- |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256624) If a field value filter is in place for an attribute, the software always retrieves the picklist values using the field value filter from the database and not from published metadata tables if publishing is specified for this picklist.

##### Publishing Picklists
A [picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IlbDWhEtofQCqbDOjwdYjQ) is a mechanism to simplify data entry for the user. However, since picklists are really tables in the Oracle database, the retrieval of picklist information can significantly affect database performance and network traffic. A user can use picklists within a feature placement or edit operation for each reference on each attribute within the dialog box tabs. For example, if picklist A is associated with two tab attribute entries, the picklist recordset is requested once for each attribute. If a user reselects the picklist during that placement or edit operation, another database query is not initiated. Most configurations involve many picklists, so it is not uncommon to make ten or more database queries to retrieve these values. 
So, while picklists are beneficial for maintaining data integrity, they can significantly degrade software performance. To minimize this impact, you can publish the picklist as part of the metadata configuration. This eliminates a database query for each picklist. The data are cached for the entire session rather than simply for the feature placement or edit context. To indicate that the picklist should be published, set the [G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_PUBLISH](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw) value to Yes (1). 
Additionally, if you use G3E_PICKLIST for multiple picklists but you are not using it as a multi-column picklist, use the G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS column to specify other columns that must be published. Do not reference the G3E_KEYFIELD, G3E_VALUEFIELD, or G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS columns. The software automatically includes them in the publish. 
There are two limitations:
  * You can only publish a picklist table once. If you need to define two picklists on the same table (perhaps to reference a different column for display), define a view over the table and specify the view as the picklist table. If you instead refer to the same table in each picklist, the combined set of fields listed in G3E_KEYFIELD, G3E_VALUEFIELD, G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS, and G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS must refer to the same fields across these multiple picklists. Otherwise, you may get unpredictable results. 
  * You cannot specify a metadata table as a picklist to be published. Since metadata tables are already published, there is no performance impact. 


Publishing picklists is not applicable in the following circumstances:
  * The content is very dynamic and constantly changing.
  * The picklist is used only in conjunction with [field value filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RTfE9n4VqdlpjpZ18oZDaw). Field value filters associated with a picklist override the publish specification and perform the query in the database. 
  * The picklist is only associated with a [Foreign Key Query dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/p5C~UfrxyhaOaE~180wmVQ) or with [traversable attributes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zyDeTpVX~ifJmb_qHrCnNQ).

##### Restricted, Unrestricted, and Extensible Picklists
Three behaviors define how picklist value selection can occur: restricted, unrestricted, and extensible. 
With a restricted picklist, the user must select values from the drop-down list. The user is not allowed to type any other values. However, an unrestricted picklist allows the user to select from the drop-down list of values or to type a value. 
Extensible picklists are like unrestricted picklists. The user can select from the drop-down list of values or can type a value for the attribute. However, if any typed values are not in the current list of values in the picklist table, these values are added to the picklist table and subsequently displayed in the drop-down list. 
The behavior for a predefined picklist must be explicitly defined in the [G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_VALIDATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw) table. The following list shows valid values for this field: 
  * G3ERestricted
  * G3EUnrestricted
  * G3EExtensible


For domain and foreign key table picklists, the behavior is always unrestricted and does not require a specification in metadata. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260801) For extensible picklists, before any user-supplied values can be stored in the picklist table, the value in the G3E_KEYFIELD field and the value in the G3E_VALUEFIELD field in the G3E_PICKLIST table must contain the same field name.

##### Setting Up the Automatic Population of Derived Attributes
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260784) You cannot use CU or Ancillary CU attributes as triggering or auto-populated attributes. 
You can configure your data model so the software automatically populates derived attribute values based on previous attribute value selections. An attribute can trigger multiple sets of auto-populated attributes, and multiple attributes can be used in combination to determine the unique set of auto-populated attributes. 
The triggering attributes and the attributes they automatically populate are grouped into a set. This set number is carried through metadata as indicated in the [example](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jRmrA3kG49LMCXigDaG4_A). 
As with most attribute presentation and editing capabilities in NetWorks Core, the triggering capability centers around a dialog tab. The definition for what attributes trigger the population of the values of other attributes is specific to the attributes presented on a given tab. An attribute identified as a triggering attribute for one tab may not serve the same purpose for another tab. Sets of related triggering and auto-populated attributes must reference the same picklist table. 
The general software behavior is as follows:
  1. The user fills in values for the triggering attributes.
  2. The software uses the triggering attribute values and the associated filter expression to query the picklist to see if a single row is now selected from the picklist table. 
  3. If the query returns a single row, the values are immediately copied from the picklist to the attributes. 


Keep the following in mind when you set up the automatic population of derived attributes:
  * Multiple sets of triggering attributes are allowed.
  * The same attribute can be derived from several triggering sets. However, you cannot cascade or embed triggering attributes. Automatic population is based on the interaction of the user to set one of the triggering attributes. 


The software does not check for [non-null values before querying the picklist table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/amfyNYp_VNq76KKIPVKKBw). Code the filter to evaluate correctly for a real value.   
|  Example If Attribute A has the value 'ABC' and attribute B has a Null value, and the trigger filter is A=#1001&B=#1002, the simple substitution in the filter is A='ABC' and B = Null.   |  
| --- |  
  * If no rows are returned when the picklist is queried with the current values of the triggering attributes, the derived (auto-populated) attributes in the set are set to Null. Thus, all derived attributes should not be defined to be 'non-nullable'. Further, database defaults other than Null should not be used. 
  * If multiple rows are returned when the picklist is queried, derived attributes do not auto-populate. 
  * All attributes that are auto-populated from a triggering set must come from the same picklist table. 


  * To set up the automatic population of derived attributes:


  1. Flag the triggering attributes in [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_TRIGGERPOPULATE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ). A value of Yes (1) indicates a triggering attribute. 
  2. To populate default values in G3E_TRIGGERSET and G3E_AUTOPOPULATE, execute MG3EDefaultAutoPopulateEntries.plb, which is delivered to \GTechnology\PLSQL\Metadata. This procedure uses the existing [field value filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RTfE9n4VqdlpjpZ18oZDaw) to build default auto-population metadata. 
DefAutoPop.txt is created in the folder on the server according to the [DatabaseLocalDirectory](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) entry in [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ). This file contains any errors created from running this procedure. 
  3. [G3E_TRIGGERSET](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zG_LobLKIH7mt_Rn~9jFzw) lists sets of attributes that constitute a triggering action to automatically populate a subordinate set of attributes. Include the filter expression that indicates how the values for the triggering attributes are used to query the picklist table. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260784) Field value filters use the following syntax: #700106=ALPHA_CODE&#700112=TOTAL_SIZE. Trigger filters use ADO syntax that is appropriate for interfacing to published picklists. The above filter has the following format when used as a trigger filter: ALPHA_CODE =#700106& TOTAL_SIZE =#700112. Test the G3E_TRIGGERSET.G3E_TRIGGERFILTER (a filter using ADO syntax) to see if it yields more than one row. If it does, derived attributes do not populate. To test it, execute a complete SQL statement that includes the G3E_TRIGGERFILTER clause converted from ADO syntax to SQL syntax. 
  4. List the attributes to populate in [G3E_AUTOPOPULATE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lflES5BJWp4JbnTRK~MfeQ). 
  5. List the fields to be included when the picklist is published in [G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw). 
Because you can publish the picklist table only one time, be sure to include all the derived attributes and the triggering attributes in the published column list in G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS. The publishing software automatically includes values in G3E_KEYFIELD, G3E_VALUEFIELD, and G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS. 
  6. [Publish the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ). Publishing the picklist table referenced by the set of driving and derived attributes makes derived attributes populate more quickly.

##### Static Filters
Static filters are used to narrow the contents of predefined picklists. They allow one picklist table to be used for multiple purposes. Essentially, a static filter is an expression in the form of a WHERE clause that is used to filter the contents of the picklist table for which it is defined. The expression is stored in [G3E_PICKLIST.G3E_FILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw).   
|  Example There are two classifications for voltage—one for high voltages and one for low voltages. Instead of defining two predefined picklist tables for each voltage classification, you can define one table for both. In the G3E_PICKLIST table, define two predefined picklists referencing the same table. For each picklist definition, define a static filter that filters out any unwanted voltages for each picklist. For the low voltage classification, define a picklist called LowVoltage in the G3E_PICKLIST table with G3E_FILTER set to VOLTAGE < 100. For the high voltage classification, define a picklist called HighVoltage in the G3E_PICKLIST table with G3E_FILTER set to VOLTAGE >=100.   |  
| --- |

##### Support for Nulls in Picklist Processing
[Field value filtering](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RTfE9n4VqdlpjpZ18oZDaw) of picklists lets you limit the choices of the user for an attribute value to only those values from a picklist table that pass the defined filter. The filter's search values are set from the current values of the feature being edited. 
NetWorks Core allows field-value filtered picklist behavior even when one attribute is Null. In the example table, values of 3, 5, and 8 are selected. 
The filters for the picklists for each of the three attributes depend on the other two attributes. A user cannot pick a HEIGHT that is not valid for the current choices of MATERIAL and DIAMETER or for the other two attributes. If the user picks Material=WOOD and HEIGHT=10, the only valid values of DIAMETER are 3 and 5. 
If your implementation needs to support the use of Nulls in picklist processing, use the [AllowNullsInFilteredPicklists](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME.   
|  Example MATERIAL, HEIGHT, and DIAMETER as attributes for a pole. These attributes are selected based on the following reference table:   
 |  Ref Material   |  Ref Height   |  Ref Diameter   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Wood  |  10  |  3  |  
|  Wood  |  10  |  5  |  
|  Wood  |  12  |  5  |  
|  Wood  |  12  |  8  |  
|  Aluminum  |  10  |  6  |  
|  Aluminum  |  10  |  8  |  
|  Aluminum  |  15  |  8  |  
|  Aluminum  |  15  |  10  |  
|  Steel  |  9  |  5  |  
|  Steel  |  15  |  5  |  
 |

### Component Views

#### Complex Component Views
Many component views are a join on G3E_FID of one or more attribute components and a graphic component of the feature. However, to meet your map display requirements, you may need to create more complex component views. 
Here are some things you can do using complex views:
  * Join on G3E_CID to match attribute and graphic repeating occurrences.
  * Join on more than two components (performance suffers as this increases).
  * Join on reference tables.
  * Join across relationships to other features (modification tracking does not catch this—you must write a trigger on the other feature table to trigger it). 


Use more involved predicates. For example, if you create features with different components that exist in one table, two component views join on that table. The component views must filter on G3E_CNO to select the correct rows. The component views must filter on G3E_CNO to select the correct rows. In fact, you may have created two features that share two components that exist in one table. In this case, the component views must filter on both G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO. 
  * Use an attribute filter to [restrict membership](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw) of a single component. You can vary the display scale of the component, based on attribution, or you can turn part of it on or off. The standard is one component view per G3E_FNO/G3E_CNO pair, but for complex views there are multiple component views over a single G3E_FNO/G3E_CNO pair, and you must use [synthesized components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BHztsPXCkqRWc8ufJn_Dkg). Each such component view is published with just its restricted membership. 
You can also restrict membership creating multiple filtered legend entries over a single component view (and this still works), but this method is less efficient because each legend entry must process and filter out the unwanted records. With synthesized components, the legend entry sees only the correct records and does not have to filter out any records. 


Related Topics

#### Component View Structure
You can build component views over any tables or views in the database. Because the component views' primary purpose is to help display graphic features based on attribution, there are typically joins on G3E_FID over a feature's graphic and attribute component tables. 
Example
SQL> select A.G3E_ID, A.G3E_FNO, A.G3E_CNO, A.G3E_FID, A.G3E_CID, A.G3E_GEOMETRY, B.STATUS, B.HEIGHT, B.MATERIAL from POLE_SYMBOL A, POLE B where A.G3E_FID=B.G3E_FID;
This is a simplified view of the component view V_Pole_Symbol built over the Pole_Symbol graphic component and the Pole attribute component, along with snippets of supporting metadata: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/~AWsz35CZVSDfPW5~plD_A-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=44485779f50a0122&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
[Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8hSRcfouEj6RwErZIamZag) to display a more detailed illustration of this component view over LTT views and B$ tables.

  * The graphic table name is the feature name with graphic type (symbol, label, line, area). 
  * Only DBAs and triggers and procedures access the B$ Tables.
  * There is one component view per FNO/CNO.
  * LTT columns are not selected into LTT view and so are not accessible.
  * Triggers on B$ tables:
    * LTT before insert sets ltt_id, ltt_status. 
    * LTT before update copies original values into buffer, sets ltt_id, ltt_status on current record. 
    * LTT before delete copies original values into buffer, sets ltt_id, ltt_status on current record and copies it into buffer. 
    * LTT after trigger inserts buffered records. 
    * Mod track trigger inserts record into MODIFICATIONLOG for this table. Does not do this if caused by LTT after trigger.

#### Creating Component Views in Oracle Attribute Tables
Before you can [add component views to metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfHMs9jSH0THMWhnXtFnGA), they must be created in the database. You can use Metadata Query or an SQL editor. 
A component view can include the following:
  * One geometry field. A view should have one geometry field called G3E_GEOMETRY. Every component stored in the same underlying table has the same geometry field name. 
  * One alignment field. If the view is associated with a TextPointGeometry component, it needs one alignment field called G3E_ALIGNMENT. 
  * Optionally, the filter expression to retrieve only one component—for example, where G3E_CNO = 3. This is necessary only when more than one component is stored in the underlying database table. 
  * Sufficient attributes to assign labels and to symbolize the geometry. There must be one row generated by the view for each graphic occurrence.   
|  Example Feature definition:  GraphicA — One occurrence  
GraphicB — One occurrence  
GraphicC — One occurrence  
AttrA — One occurrence  
AttrB — One occurrence  
AttrC — Five occurrences  Component view definitions:  GraphicViewA  
select <G3E keys and required columns> from GraphicA GA, AttrA AA where GA.FNO = AA.FNO and GA.FID = AA.FID and GA.CNO=1  GraphicViewB  
select <G3E keys and required columns> from GraphicB GB, AttrA AA where GB.FNO = AA.FNO and GB.FID = AA.FID and GB.CNO=2  GraphicViewC  
select <G3E keys and required columns> from GraphicC GC, AttrC AC where GC.FNO = AC.FNO and GC.FID = AC.FID and GC.CNO=1  GraphicViewA and GraphicViewB both result in one row. The attribute values from AttrA are selected into both views. This is perfectly acceptable and may be required for the style and label rules for each view. GraphicViewC, however, results in five rows where the graphic attributes are redundant and the attribute values differ per row. While this can be done, the result is to draw the same geometry five times, possibly changing the style each time based on the values in the specific occurrence of AttrC. The system does not accommodate a style or label rule that can review values in more than one row of attributes for a single geometry instance.   |  
| --- |  
  * Attributes from components of other features, as long as the relationship is one-to-one.  
|  Example If your data model includes a district or line feature to which all other features are associated, you might include the LINE ID or DISTRICT NAME in the label format for the component.   |  
| --- |  
Also, symbolization may be based on a similar type of attribute. As long as you construct the view to generate at most one row per graphic component, you can include as many attributes as you need. This value is replicated in every row in the published data.

#### Creating Optimized Component Views
Display rules consist of style rules and, optionally, label rules. Display can be time-consuming, especially with complex rule definition. You can alter the component view definitions and create optimized views used to populate the data mapfiles, thus improving display time. The Create Optimized Component Views utility helps you create the optimized component views. 
The Optimized views script path designates where the utility writes the file containing the optimized component view definitions. The Existing views script path designates where the utility writes the file containing the current (existing) component view definitions. You can use the existing views file to remove the optimization. Because only component views that have not been optimized are presented as candidates for optimization, you must retain this file so you can use it to remove the optimization if you change style and/or label rules used by the optimized component views. 
  * To create optimized component views:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Optimize Component Views. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258065?tocId=jjCb~4P9c0X0qN0ytkW4xA)
  2. Type the User name, Password, and Service name information. 
  3. Click OK. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Ed32XzlJn4nMzPkEf5klGA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=4aa6f750760b1dbb&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. Use the arrow buttons to move Component view candidates to or from the Views to optimize column. Press and hold SHIFT to select a contiguous group of component views, or press and hold CTRL to select non-contiguous items. 
  5. In the Optimized views script path field, type the full path to an existing file name and press TAB. 
The file name you typed in the Optimized views script path field automatically appears in the Existing views script path field with Original prepended to the file name. 
OR
Click the Ellipsis to browse to a location for the Optimized views script path. Type a name for the optimized component view, and click Save. 
You are returned to the Optimize Component Views dialog box. The file name and path to the Optimized views script path automatically appear in the Existing views script path field with Original prepended to the file name. 
  6. You can override this name by typing a new value in the Existing views script path, or you can use the Ellipsis to save this file to a new location. 
  7. Click OK. 
  8. To recreate the component views with optimized component view definitions, type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> @<path to optimized views script>;
  9. To optimize additional component views, repeat Steps 4-9.
  10. [Republish the data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KMyb7We6CN6SLJS3Anpyuw). 
  11. Remove the master entries for these component views [by trimming](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FxKVEqytxjQ2yUAlQ681JQ), and remove the job entries by [purging these component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/36P2JjlfzXGWnwVEIkdiqQ). 
  12. Increment the legend number in G3E_LEGEND.G3E_VERSION. See [Legend Versioning Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RQMuAsC16HLHylr8AfRY5Q)
  13. Publish Metadata

#### Defining Component Views in Metadata

##### Creating a Component View Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a component view for a feature and the geographic component within the feature that is associated with the view. Then you define the relationship of the view to the components that comprise its fields in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION table. The component view should have already been [created in the database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DHUwlxUkQR6tWTgCheuThQ). 
  * To create a component view definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the component view. The G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In the G3E_VIEW field, type the name of the component view that already exists in the database. 
  4. In the G3E_CNO field, select the geographic component within the feature that is associated with the view from the drop-down list. 
  5. Leave the G3E_LENO field set to null. You update the field after you define the legend entry for the component view. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997)
  6. Type or select values as needed in other fields to define the component view.
  7. To complete your component view definition, click OK. 
  8. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To add a component view composition definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions > <component view name> > Component View Composition node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the component view composition. The G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. If the G3E_FNO field is not populated, select the feature associated with the view from the drop-down list. 
  4. In the G3E_CNO field, select a component that contributes to the component view definition from the drop-down list. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997)
  5. Type or select values as needed in other fields to define the component view composition.
  6. To complete your component view composition definition, click OK. 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255997) to commit the changes to the database.
