You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete a component view definition. Deleting a component view definition also deletes all of its component view composition entries but does not drop the view from the database. 
  * To delete a component view composition definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions > <component view name> > Component View Composition node. 
  2. Find and select the component view composition you want to remove.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260844), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  4. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260844) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To delete a component view definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions node. 
  2. Find and select the component view that you want to remove.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260844), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  4. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260844) to commit the changes to the database.

##### Editing a Component View Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to edit a component view definition. You can add components to a component view definition, and you can also modify information about the associated component view composition. 
  * To edit a component view definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions node. 
  2. Find and select the component view that you want to modify.
  3. In the content panel, edit the component view values you want to change.
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260842) to commit the changes to the database. 
  5. If the column to be included/excluded is from a component that is defined in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION table, update the table entry by editing the component view composition definition. No further changes are necessary. 
  6. If the component was not defined in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION table, [add the component to this table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfHMs9jSH0THMWhnXtFnGA). If the component has been removed from the view, [delete the component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nhyvpq84mopBnCfpCv9Jfw) from the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION table. Then execute the following using an SQL editor: 
SQL> execute GDOTRIGGERS.Create_GDOTriggers;
SQL> execute G3E_DynamicProcedures.Generate;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260842) If the structure of a table that participates in a component view is changed, the view that represents the component view must be recreated through Oracle. 
  7. [Purge the MODIFICATIONLOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/36P2JjlfzXGWnwVEIkdiqQ). 


  * To edit a component view composition definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Component View Definitions > <component view name> > Component View Composition node. 
  2. Find and select the component view composition that you want to modify.
  3. In the content panel, edit the component view composition values that you want to change. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260842) to commit the changes to the database.

#### Validate Deltas and Component View Consistency
If NetWorks Core does not connect to a configuration properly, run the Validate Deltas Consistency tool to verify that the mapfiles, the database, and the MODIFICATIONLOG are consistent for all the component views in that configuration. If you have run the Validate Deltas Consistency tool and you are still experiencing connection problems, run the batch [DDCScan tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TB18t6t85L_5sL~pfKouTQ). 
  * To validate deltas and component view consistency:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Validate Deltas Consistency. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256075?tocId=LkFm0peoqoy1SlhRgpCA3w)
  2. On the Validate Deltas Consistency dialog box, type the username and password, and select the configuration you want to validate. 
  3. To run a verification on the MODIFICATIONLOG, mapfiles, and the database, check Validate MODIFICATIONLOG consistency, and click Validate. 
OR
To verify the mapfiles and the database only, do not check Validate MODIFICATIONLOG consistency, and click Validate. If this verification does not find errors, check Validate MODIFICATIONLOG consistency, and click Validate. 
The software writes problems to ValidateDeltasConsistency.txt in the temporary folder on your machine. This file is recreated each time you execute ValidateDeltasConsistency.exe. If you validate multiple configurations without closing the dialog box, all reports are retained in the file. 
  4. Fix any problems, [republish the mapfiles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KMyb7We6CN6SLJS3Anpyuw), and [purge the MODIFICATIONLOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/36P2JjlfzXGWnwVEIkdiqQ). 
  5. To validate other configurations, repeat Steps 2 through 4.

### Components

#### Component Core Description Fields
The first set of fields in the [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table is essential to every component. These fields must be populated for every type of component. 
  * G3E_CNO—The G3E_CNO is the component number or identifier. It is part of the feature keys. Once G3E_CNO is assigned, you should not change it. This value must be unique within the table. 
  * G3E_DCNO—The G3E_DCNO is the [data connection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) number. You should correctly associate the component with the data connection that defines or stores the data. If the component is originally from a secondary source but you now plan to manage it with NetWorks Core, you should associate it with the NetWorks Core data connection (development or production). However, if the data are only in the NetWorks Core database as reviewable data, the data connection number should be associated with the secondary connection. 
  * G3E_USERNAME—G3E_USERNAME is the descriptive name of the component. It is presented to users throughout the NetWorks Core application. The first place you see this value is in the placement dialog box. Any format or content is allowed, but the value must be unique in the table. 
  * G3E_NAME—G3E_NAME is a programmatic name for the component. Users never see it, but if you write any functional interface objects, you must use this name. No spaces or special characters are allowed. 
  * G3E_TOOLTIP—G3E_TOOLTIP is also a descriptive name for the component data. If left null, the NetWorks Core software uses the component name. The Select tool uses the component tooltip if the label rule is not specified. 
  * G3E_TABLE—All components must define their storage table (G3E_TABLE) and their type. The data modeling section describes the minimum field requirements for all feature components. Any other fields in the table are based on your data model requirements. You should develop a table naming convention, though the software does not require it. One common convention is to add a suffix to the table to indicate the type of data it contains.   
|  Example "_N" represents nongraphic data, "_PT" represents points, "_LN" represents lines, "_AR" represents areas, and "_LB" represents labels.   |  
| --- |  
Typically, the main portion of the table name describes its purpose or the feature with which it is associated, such as "CONNECTIVITY" or "TRANSFORMER." Table names are restricted in length based on the type of component—24 characters for nongraphic and 16 characters for graphic. NetWorks Core defines these two fundamental types, but there are further qualifications of these types. 
  * G3E_TYPE—Graphic components may be designated as [point, line, area, and coverage](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MnSNe2k7Xndz0jiF9Wu~6w). Point geometry is used for both symbols and labels. Coverage geometry is used for raster-data representation. It contains only the bounding rectangle for the raster data; you must retain the raster files for display by NetWorks Core. 
The difference between graphic and spatial data are semantic. Spatial data are assumed to have a significant geospatial position. It is appropriate to spatially compare it, and moving a feature is equivalent to moving the facility in the real world. Graphic data are annotative, and the geospatial position is not significant. You can move it freely to manage the map presentation. 
You cannot run a spatial query on graphic types of components. Use the spatial designation for component types if you want to use the geometry in spatial comparisons. For secondary metadata, you may need to change the specification that is assigned when you generate the default metadata. 
You cannot include a special view (G3E_TYPE = 2048) as part of a feature. These component definitions support find, query, and attribute traversals. 
  * G3E_LTT—G3E_LTT contains a flag to indicate if [long term transaction](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mIxEcTFc0BsmuME6gcqZTw) (LTT) tracking should be applied to the component.

#### Component Modeling
Although a component is equivalent to a database table, you can organize component definitions so that the component is a view or subset of data in a table. 
When designing your data model, determine if you need [detail](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tW6~FkKty1Km1fCuAtRUtQ) or [alternate components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xeF5peebSrlF9D43aPs2Mw). This modeling decision affects your legend organization, data storage and publishing, and relationships among the data elements. You can have all types of components in your model, and you can have multiple alternate components, but within relationship processing, you are limited to five alternate representations that are processed as part of break operations. 
Typically, database tables are not shared among geographic, alternate, and detail components. However, they can be if the total data volume is not prohibitive for your particular configuration. Usually, while features share component definitions, the data storage is not shared. Sharing offers the advantage of fewer database tables, but you must still define the data views for each component. There is no restriction on sharing the data storage between geographic and alternate components. 
NetWorks Core provides commands to [help convert detail data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mQYiJ6aWbIy02lnSTcXScw). These commands change the type of a component from detail to geographic, and vice versa. The need to convert occurs primarily when data are digitized from paper maps and is digitized as the wrong component. If you anticipate using these commands, the geographic and detail component definitions that match or correspond to one another must be identical in structure except for the G3E_DETAILID field. This field need not exist in the geographic component.

#### Creating Component Definitions

##### Creating a Component Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to create a component definition. The process of defining a component adds a row to the G3E_COMPONENT table. The data table for the component should have already been [created in the database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/I8OIVt66jGCEOz9OAmzqjw). Typically, components are associated with features using the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table, but it is not required. For example, SpecialNonGraphic (2048) components are not associated with a feature. 
  * To create a component definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Components and Attributes node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256250), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the component. The G3E_COMPONENT table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the component.
  4. In the G3E_NAME field, type an internal component name used in naming fields.
  5. In the G3E_TYPE field, select a value from the drop-down list.
  6. In the G3E_TABLE field, type the name of the data table for the component.
  7. Select values for the following required fields: G3E_DETAIL and G3E_DCNO.
  8. Type or select values as needed in other fields to define the component.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256250)
  9. To complete your component definition, click OK. 
  10. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256250) to commit the changes to the database. 
  11. Optional:  [Associate the component with a feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA).

##### Creating a Component Table in the Database
To add a new component to your data model, you first have to create the data table for the component and then add the table to metadata. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256254)
  * If new component table has a column with the data type NUMBER (10), you can only add data with a value less than 2,147,483,647. 
  * Do not rename tables. If the name of the table needs to change, [drop the old table](javascript:;) and create a new one. 


  * To create a component table in the database:


Use an SQL editor for these steps.
  1. Create the data table for the component to be added for an existing feature.
  2. Name the table according to the conventions of the project.
  3. Include at least G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CID, and G3E_CNO columns.
  4. Include a G3E)GEOMETRY column for geometry components.
  5. Include a G3E_DETAILID column for detail components.
  6. Include an ALIGNMENT column for a component with a [type of GraphicsText, SpatialPoint, or GraphicPoint](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MnSNe2k7Xndz0jiF9Wu~6w). The field must be defined as Number. 
  7. Limit the length of the table name to less than 24 characters.

  
|  Example table creation statement create table<component table name> (  
G3E_ID NUMBER(10,0),   
G3E_FNO NUMBER(5,0),   
G3E_CNO NUMBER(5,0),  
G3E_FID NUMBER(10,0),   
G3E_CID NUMBER(10,0),   
G3E_GEOMETRY SDO_GEOMETRY,   
G3E_DETAILID NUMBER(10,0),  
ALIGNMENT NUMBER(5,0));  |  
| --- |

##### Deleting a Component Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete a component definition. The feature that uses the component as the primary attribute component is also deleted. The deletion is not successful if the component is used as the primary geographic or detail component of a feature. The data table for the component and its related database objects is not deleted. 
  * To delete a component definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Components and Attributes node. 
  2. Find and select the component that you want to delete.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260840), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  4. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260840) to commit the changes to the database.

##### Editing a Component Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to edit a component definition. If you change the component type (G3E_TYPE), you must also update the other data. Changing the component type could cause a "disconnect" on the placement interfaces since these are categorized by typemask. For example, a set of placement interfaces for a linear component does not apply to an area component. 
  * To edit a component definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Components and Attributes node. 
  2. Find and select the component that you want to modify.
  3. In the content panel, edit the component values you want to change.
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260838) to commit the changes to the database.

#### Creating Sequences
Create [sequences](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256583) for columns for facility data table in an SQL editor. 
A serial list of unique numbers for numeric columns of a database's table. A sequence simplifies application programming by generating unique numbers. Sequence numbers are independent of tables, so the same sequence can be used for one or more tables. 
  * To create a sequence on a data table:


  1. Execute the following procedure:
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\CreateSequence.sql
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\prvtCreateSequence.plb
  2. To create a G3E_ID sequence on each table in the model:
SQL> execute CREATE_SEQUENCE.create_g3eid_sequence;

#### Defining or Modifying a Component in an Existing Data Model

##### Adding Columns to Existing Component Tables
At times, you might need to add a column to an existing database table. You can use SQL Plus to do this. When the structure of a table that participates in a component view is changed, use Oracle SQL Plus to recreate: 
  * The view that represents the component view.
  * The views and triggers associated with the table.


  * To add a column to an existing component table:


Use Oracle SQLPlus to alter the table.  
|  Example ALTER TABLE B$PREMISE_N ADD EST_LOAD NUMBER(10);  |  
| --- |  
After Adding a Column to an Existing Component Table
  1. In a production schema, execute the following procedures for each updated table:
    1. SQL> execute create_views.create_ltt_view('<B$ table>');
    2. SQL> execute create_triggers.create_ltt_trigger('<B$ table>');
    3. SQL> execute gdotriggers.create_gdotriggers('<updated table>');
Where <updated table> is the name of the database table from the G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE.
  2. Recreate the component views for each modified table so that they contain the newly added attributes. 
  3. Purge the MODIFICATIONLOG. Using the component view name that has been changed, execute the following: 
SQL> execute G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.SyncToComponentView(<'ComponentViewName'>);
  4. Validate all invalid Oracle objects.
  5. Add the changes to the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table.
  6. Add the changes to the G3E_TABATTRIBUTE table.
  7. Publish the metadata.

#### Detail Components

##### Detail Data Model Requirements
The detail component's table is not very different than a geographic component's table. It does include a detail identifier. This identifier is a categorization or grouping of detail graphics. Usually the identifier is a logical grouping and does not correspond to a physical entity in the data model. 
The detail component tables must have a G3E_DETAILID field to hold the identifier of the detail view to which the detail component belongs. The field must have this exact name, and must have an index on it. 
The detail component view must contain the G3E_DETAILID field from the corresponding detail component table. The field must have this exact name, and must be published. 
To create a complete replica of your data model in a detail view, use an alternate set of components instead of detail components. The detail identifier must filter detail views. If you have two million graphics in the view and only 100 are displayed in a particular view, the operation is very expensive. 
A single occurrence of a detail component can participate in only one detail view because storage is limited to one identifier. However, the same component, if repeating, can have different occurrences in different detail areas. 
The second and subsequent detail drawing areas associated with a single geographic referencing component do not appear in the [Open Detail Window tree view](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F5x7EBQ93P5sQG2Ly3HnkA). This data model and workflow are related to features that define multiple detail areas, but only contain one geometry component.   
|  Example In this workflow, the manhole feature is configured with a single occurrence detail indicator (the referencing triggering component) and repeating attribute occurrences. The placement of the detail indicator component generates the first detail area. The user can then use the Reestablish Relationship command to generate another detail area associated with this manhole. This action only generates another attribute record and no other graphics.  The presentation of detail areas for the Open Detail Window dialog box retrieves the list of referencing features and then the triggering component's view name for processing. The detail information, name, legend, and MBR must be published attributes for efficiently populating the tree view.  The component view for the triggering component (detail indicator) is defined as a join between the single graphic component and the N attribute records. This generates N occurrences in the DDC. However, in the initial view definition, the G3E_CID value was always the same. Hence, only one graphic was published to the DDC (or processed in deltas) and only one item appeared in the tree view.   |  
| --- |  
You can select one of these methods to resolve the issue presented in the example:
  * Leave this model the way it is. However, users must select additional windows from the Open Detail Window dialog box when they are presented for the referencing feature. Only a single entry appears in the tree view. Also, if the user selects a feature contained in one of these details, the Open Detail Window dialog box presents it for opening. 
  * Change the data model to [store the attribution in a repeating graphic component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9jNnEgvhRwGxGE8qu5em8w). The user must place additional triggering components. 
  * [Implement a trigger](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdplkN_TMHDZadA0mNAHjg) or a [functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) to automatically generate a corresponding graphic component when the second and subsequent attribute records are created. The geometry could be copied from the one the user placed. The component view must be updated to join on G3E_CID.

##### Metadata Affected by Detail Components
Many metadata tables include detail components. For example, you must create component view definitions for details. But there are no special considerations for those definitions. This topic describes the metadata tables that are directly affected by detail component specifications. 
  * G3E_COMPONENT—Include an entry for each detail component and set the G3E_DETAIL field of this table to Yes (1). 
  * G3E_LEGEND—You must create a separate legend for use by detail views and identify it as a detail legend. If there are multiple types of detail drawings in a system, define multiple detail legends. 
  * G3E_DETAIL—This table specifies which feature-components can define or reference a detail drawing. Specify a detail indicator component to trigger the creation or reference for a detail area. 
  * G3E_DETAILMAPPING—This table specifies which feature-components participate in each detail drawing that is defined. See the detail relationship for information on how to populate this table. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT—Detail components must be added to the feature. Alternate required ("either/or") pairs of components should be specified in this table. That is, a feature is often configured to contain both geographic and detail components, but only one needs to exist.

###### Example Dimension Picklist Scripts
Create an accumulative/incremental picklist table:
SQL> create table PL_DIMACCUMULATIVE ( PL_KEY NUMBER (1), PL_VALUE VARCHAR2 (30) NOT NULL, CHECK (PL_KEY IN (0,1,2)), UNIQUE (PL_KEY) );
  
Populate the accumulative/incremental picklist table:
SQL> insert into PL_DIMACCUMULATIVE ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 0, 'N/A');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMACCUMULATIVE ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 1, 'Accumlative');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMACCUMULATIVE ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 2, 'Incremental');
  
Create a calculated/overridden picklist table:
SQL> create table PL_DIMCALCOVERRIDDEN ( PL_KEY NUMBER (1), PL_VALUE VARCHAR2 (30) NOT NULL, CHECK (PL_KEY IN (0,1)), UNIQUE (PL_KEY) );
  
Populate the calculated/overridden picklist table:
SQL> insert into PL_DIMCALCOVERRIDDEN ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 0, 'Overridden');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMCALCOVERRIDDEN ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 1, 'Calculated');
  
Create a driven/not-driven picklist table:
SQL> create table PL_DIMDRIVEN ( PL_KEY NUMBER (1), PL_VALUE VARCHAR2 (30) NOT NULL, CHECK (PL_KEY IN (0,1)), UNIQUE (PL_KEY) );
  
Populate the driven/not-driven picklist table:
SQL> insert into PL_DIMDRIVEN ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 0, 'Not Driven');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMDRIVEN ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 1, 'Driven');
  
Create a dimension stack position picklist table:
SQL> create table PL_DIMSTACKPOS ( PL_KEY NUMBER (1). PL_VALUE VARCHAR2 (30) NOT NULL. CHECK (PL_KEY IN (0,1,2,4)). UNIQUE (PL_KEY) );
  
Populate the dimension stack position picklist table:
SQL> insert into PL_DIMSTACKPOS ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 0, 'N/A');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMSTACKPOS ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 1, 'Bottom');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMSTACKPOS ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 2, 'Middle');
SQL> insert into PL_DIMSTACKPOS ( PL_KEY, PL_VALUE ) values ( 4, 'Top');

###### Adding Columns to Dimension Component B$ Tables
For storing the dimension text vertical offset, add the following columns to existing dimension component B$ tables. All these columns are of type Number. B$ denotes that LTT is enabled. 
  * To add columns to dimension component B$ tables:


  1. Add columns appropriate to the dimension type.
    1. For simple dimension components, add the following column:
[G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/r10f4ji_zgVMM6oJTh5G1w)  
|  Example SQL> alter table B$SIMPLE_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY NUMBER(28,15));  |  
| --- |  
    2. For orthogonal dimension components, add the following columns:
[G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V6RM4nVFNzCgeMon~w~QOA)
[G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V6RM4nVFNzCgeMon~w~QOA)  
|  Example SQL> alter table B$ORTHO_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1 NUMBER(28,15)); SQL> alter table B$ORTHO_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2 NUMBER(28,15));  |  
| --- |  
    3. For radius-of-two-points dimension components, add the following columns:
[G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7KD~qzqDJfM67X319XNxA)
[G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7KD~qzqDJfM67X319XNxA)  
|  Example SQL> alter table B$R2P_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1 NUMBER(28,15));  SQL> alter table B$R2P_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2 NUMBER(28,15));  |  
| --- |  
    4. For polar dimension components, add the following columns:
[G3E_DIMLENGTHOFFSETY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6UBS9F6tZypFAC_Qj9CPBw)
[G3E_DIMANGLEOFFSETY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6UBS9F6tZypFAC_Qj9CPBw)  
|  Example SQL> alter table B$POLAR_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMLENGTHOFFSETY NUMBER(28,15)); SQL> alter table B$POLAR_I_DIM add (G3E_DIMANGLEOFFSETY NUMBER(28,15));  |  
| --- |  
  2. In a production schema, execute the following procedures for each updated table:
SQL> execute create_views.create_ltt_view('<your B$ table>');
SQL> execute create_triggers.create_ltt_trigger('<your B$ table>');
SQL> execute gdotriggers.create_gdotriggers('<your table>');
  3. Grant all privileges to the database user who runs these procedures.
  4. [Re-create the component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sqf8VCNFLLNrYEIem7lKcQ) for each modified table so that they contain the newly added attributes.

In the dimensioning metadata tables, you populate columns that reference the dimension text vertical offset so that they reference new entries in G3E_ATTRIBUTE.

##### Calculated and Overridden Dimension Text
Dimension text normally shows the length of the dimension line. For polar dimensions, it also shows the angle. Therefore, the dimension text is normally synchronized with the [dimension geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ). It is calculated as the distance between the endpoints of the dimension line or as the angle between two lines. This type of dimension text is called calculated. 
In some cases, though, the positions of the objects on the map do not accurately reflect their real positions.   
|  Example Two pipelines that are actually located above one another are drawn next to each other on the map to make both of them visible. The blue line represents Pipe 1, which is in the real position. The red line represents Pipe 2, whose position on the map is shifted so that it does not overlap Pipe 1.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259172)  |  
| --- |  
Since dimension text should display real lengths and angles, the calculated dimension text cannot be used. Users need to override the calculated values and specify the real values. Such dimension texts are called overridden. The format of overridden dimension text is usually different from the format of calculated dimension text. Overridden dimension text is generally shown in parentheses. You can only represent the calculated or overridden values – the system only maintains one attribute. 
If a designer edits the dimensions with calculated dimension texts, these texts are automatically updated based on the edits. If you have enabled overridden texts, then the values are not automatically updated. If the user edits a calculated dimension text, the dimension geometry is updated automatically so that the geometry is synchronized with the updated text. Editing overridden texts has no effect on the dimension geometry. Similarly, editing the dimension geometry has no effect on the overridden text value. 
The relative angle of polar dimensions can be calculated or overridden in the same manner. 
The dimension text is stored in a separate column of the dimension component table. Moreover, there is a column indicating whether the text is calculated or overridden. For example, for simple dimensions the dimension text is stored in the G3E_DIMTEXT column, and the calculated/overridden flag is stored in G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH. If overridden text must be displayed using a different format than calculated dimension text, a label rule for that dimension text must be defined taking into account this condition.

##### Configuring Orthogonal Dimension Placement
You can use Metadata Explorer to configure the way orthogonal dimensions are placed. Generally, you create a placement configuration and include optional arguments in the Dimensioning IPT that determine which options on the Orthogonal Dimension Construction Aids are preselected. You can create several different placement configurations, each with different options preselected. You can also configure the placement configuration so it places using [two mouse clicks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WBRSG_okwslXm0rXY6zbzA). If you set G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_AUTOREPEAT to Yes (1), the placement configuration loops so the user can place the next dimension in the stack. 
  * To configure orthogonal dimension placement using Metadata Explorer:


  1. [Add a placement configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yyG2ZP60k5hq2jqdS3wFiQ): 
    1. In the G3E_PINO field, select the Dimension IPT.
    2. In the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT field, click the Ellipsis to display the [Interface Argument Editor dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ). 
    3. Select the optional arguments from the [Dimension IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) as required. 
    4. Click OK. 
  2. [Add the placement configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jFXGGj6Okzub1tAkZoFYlg) to the New Feature control.

##### Dimension Component Columns

###### Calculated and Overridden Dimension Text Component Columns
Each dimension text is stored in a separate column of a dimension component table. There is an additional column indicating whether the text is calculated or overridden. For example, for simple dimensions the dimension text is stored in the [G3E_DIMTEXT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/r10f4ji_zgVMM6oJTh5G1w) column, and the calculated/overridden flag is stored in [G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/r10f4ji_zgVMM6oJTh5G1w). 
If overridden text must be displayed using a different format than calculated dimension text, a label rule for that dimension text must be defined that takes this condition into account. 
Related Topic
[Calculated and Overridden Dimension Text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w)

###### Dimension Metadata Tables
These metadata tables support dimensions:
  * [G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA)
  * [G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug)
  * [G3E_DIMRADIUS2POINTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7hBRVpQK4L3xpQaS~hfrBA)
  * [G3E_DIMPOLAR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o5PfFsSr88U1jRFV6DNCCw)
  * [G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jZu02p2uhJNqb6KS~gwFPg)
  * [G3E_DIMSTYLEGROUP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ul1ZNWnC4F6edCUnp9eURQ)

###### Dimensioning Relationship Component Columns
All dimension components must have the [dimensioning relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/u20XyiqjdWo8xx3uutCRBw) columns listed below. In addition, all columns required for each dimension type must have an entry in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw). These entries must be associated with dimension component tables, not with the dimension component views.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMBASECNO  |  CNO of the connected [base feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259303).  A base feature, such as a building, is one for which an absolute position is known. Dimensions are drawn from base features to dimension features.   |  Number (5,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMBASEID  |  G3E_ID of the connected base feature.  |  Number (10,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMBASECNO2  |  CNO of the second connected base feature. This column is required for orthogonal and radius-of-two-points dimensions only.   |  Number (5,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMBASEID2  |  G3E_ID of the second connected base feature. This column is required for orthogonal and radius-of-two-points dimensions only.   |  Number (5,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMENSIONEDCNO  |  CNO of the connected [dimensioned feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259303).  A feature, such as a valve or switch, for which only a position relative to a base feature is known. Dimensions are drawn from base features to dimension features.   |  Number (5,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMENSIONEDID  |  G3E_ID of the connected dimensioned feature.  |  Number (5,0)  |

###### Orthogonal Dimension Component Columns
In addition to the standard graphic component table columns, orthogonal dimension tables must contain the following columns:   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXT1  |  Dimension text associated with the first dimension line. This column contains the length of the line segment of the [orthogonal dimension polyline geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ) representing the first dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  If the dimension polyline geometry contains four vertices, the Null value in this column indicates [orthogonal dimension with witness and dimension line](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hqYNP92CnaQDY_xY69SHIQ).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXT2  |  Dimension text associated with the second dimension line. This column contains the length of the line segment of the orthogonal dimension polyline geometry representing the second dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  If the dimension polyline geometry contains four vertices, the Null value in this column indicates orthogonal dimension with dimension and witness line.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH1  |  Flag indicating whether the value of G3E_DIMTEXT1 is [calculated (1) or overridden (0)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w). Associate the [Calculated/Overridden picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (1,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH2  |  Flag indicating whether the value of G3E_DIMTEXT2 is calculated (1) or overridden (0). Associate the Calculated/Overridden picklist with this column.   |  Number (1,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTPOS1  |  Relative position of the first dimension text along the first dimension line in percent. Zero percent means the start point; 100% means the endpoint. NULL indicates that the default value from metadata (G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL.G3E_DIMTEXTLOC1) should be used. The value of this column is used when [displaying the first dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTPOS2  |  Relative position of the second dimension text along the second dimension line in percent. Zero percent means the start point; 100% means the endpoint. NULL indicates that the default value from metadata (G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL.G3E_DIMTEXTLOC2) should be used. Value of this column is used when [displaying the second dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1  |  Vertical offset of the first dimension text from the first dimension line. This column contains the offset of the first dimension text from the first dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  This column is required for models that support [moving dimension text freely](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g) for a given component rather than along the dimension line. Its value is used when [displaying the first dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w).  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259197) G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSET1 and G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSET2 work together. Either both text components are set to moving freely or both text components are not set to moving freely.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2  |  Vertical offset of the second dimension text from the second dimension line. This column contains the offset of the second dimension text from the second dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  This column is required for models that support moving dimension text freely on the dimension line for a given component rather than along the dimension line. Its value is used when displaying the second dimension text.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DRIVINGDRIVEN  |  Flag indicating whether the dimension is [driven or not- driven](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g). Associate the Driven/Not-Driven picklist with this column.   |  Number (5)  |

###### Polar Dimension Component Columns
In addition to the standard graphic component table columns, polar dimension tables must contain the following columns:   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMLENGTH  |  Dimension text with length. This column contains the length of the dimension line (distance between the second and third vertex of the [polar dimension polyline geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ)). The distance is measured in meters.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMLENGTHPOS  |  Relative position of the dimension text with length along the dimension line in percent. Zero percent means the start point; 100% means the endpoint. NULL indicates that the default value from metadata (G3E_DIMPOLAR.G3E_DIMTEXTLOC) should be used. The value of this column is used when [displaying the dimension text with length](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH  |  Flag indicating whether the value of G3E_DIMLENGTH is [calculated (1) or overridden (0)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w). Associate the [Calculated/Overridden picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (1,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMLENGTHOFFSETY  |  Vertical offset of the dimension text with length from the dimension line. This column contains the offset of the dimension text with length from the dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  This column is required only if [moving of dimension text freely](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g) is supported for a given component. Its value is used when [displaying the dimension text with length](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMANGLE  |  Dimension text with angle. This column contains the angle between the baseline and dimension line (angle between the line segments of the [polar dimension polyline geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ)).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMANGLEPOS  |  Relative position of the dimension text with angle along the dimension line in percent. Zero percent means the start point; 100% means the endpoint. NULL indicates that the default value from metadata (G3E_DIMPOLAR.G3E_DIMTEXTLOC) should be used. Value of this column is used when [displaying the dimension text with angle](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMISCALCANGLE  |  Flag indicating whether the value of G3E_DIMANGLE is [calculated (1) or overridden (0)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w). Associate the [Calculated/Overridden picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (1,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMANGLEOFFSETY  |  Vertical offset of the dimension text with angle from the dimension line. This column contains the offset of the dimension text from the dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in meters.  This column is required for models that support [moving dimension text freely](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g) for a given component rather than along the dimension line. Its value is used when [displaying the first dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DRIVINGDRIVEN  |  Flag indicating whether the dimension is [driven or not- driven](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hzJXw_pp4FujqbSUXP_CJg). Associate the [Driven/Not-Driven picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (5)  |

###### Simple Dimension Component Columns
In addition to the standard graphic component table columns, simple dimension component tables must contain the following columns:   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH  |  Flag indicating whether the value of G3E_DIMTEXT is [calculated (1) or overridden (0)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w). You should associate the [Calculated/Overridden picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (1,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXT  |  Dimension text. Contains the distance between the start and endpoint of the [simple dimension polyline geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g). The distance is measured in meters.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTPOS  |  Relative position of the dimension text along the dimension line in percent. Zero percent means the start point; 100% means the endpoint. NULL indicates that the default value from metadata (G3E_DIMSIMPLE.G3E_DIMTEXTLOC) should be used. The value of this column is used when [displaying the dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY  |  Vertical offset of the dimension text from the dimension line. This column contains the offset of the dimension text from the dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in meters. This column is required only if [moving of dimension text freely](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g) is supported for a given component. Its value is used when displaying the dimension text.   |  Number (28,15)  |  
|  G3E_DRIVINGDRIVEN  |  Flag indicating whether the dimension is [driven or not- driven](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hzJXw_pp4FujqbSUXP_CJg). Associate the [Driven/Not-Driven picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (5)  |

###### Small Dimensions Metadata
To implement small dimensions, populate the following columns in the [G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA) and [G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug) tables: 
  * G3E_REVDIST—Maximum distance for which the dimension is considered as small. 
  * G3E_REVLINEEXT—Length of the dimension line extension on the side of the dimension text. 
  * G3E_REVLINEEXTOPP—Length of the dimension line extension on the end opposite to the dimension text.

###### Stacked Orthogonal Dimension Component Columns
The following additional columns must exist in the orthogonal dimension tables for stacked dimensions to be fully supported:   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMSTACKPOS  |  Position of the orthogonal dimension in the stack. This column is populated automatically after any update of any dimension in the stack. Value of this column may be used in driven or not-driven style rules, for example, to display only the top (longest) dimension line out of the overlapping dimension lines.  The following are the legal values: 0 - Not applicable. This value is set for orthogonal dimensions which are not in the stack.  1 - Bottom dimension in the stack. The dimension with the shortest primary dimension line.  2 - Dimension in the middle of the stack. Not the top and not the bottom dimension. 4 - Top dimension in the stack. The dimension with the longest primary dimension line. Associate the [Stack Position picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (5,0)  |  
|  G3E_DIMSTACKACCUM  |  Indication whether the accumulative or incremental lengths are calculated for the dimension texts at the primary (overlapping) dimension lines. The value of this column must be the same for all dimensions in the stack.  The following are the legal values: 0 - Not applicable This value is set for orthogonal dimensions which are not in the stack.  1 - Accumulative distances are calculated. 2 - Incremental distances are calculated. Associate the [Accumulative/Incremental picklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ydf~GM5fPUmkiqLXP~3BlA) with this column.   |  Number (5,0)  |

##### Dimension Geometry Constraints
Dimension geometries are stored as [polylines](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174). The number of vertices is usually fixed based on dimension type. Each line segment of the polyline is interpreted differently. 
A line with one or more vertices in addition to the beginning and ending points. An orthogonal line, for example, is a polyline. 
NetWorks Core puts constraints on geometries (except for [kickbacks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174)); however, there are additional constraints for polylines representing dimensions. Dimension texts are not stored in the database as separate text components. Dimension texts are generated during display, based on the dimension geometries and the required columns of dimension components. 
Condition in which the current vertex falls on the line segment between the previous two vertices. 
Simple Dimension Constraints
[Simple dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wKJscoIUWiN5Uu4dEAv1~Q) geometry is a polyline with two vertices. 
Orthogonal dimension constraints
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174)
The [orthogonal dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hqYNP92CnaQDY_xY69SHIQ) geometry contains a [baseline](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174) as the first segment of the polyline. In the diagram above, the baseline is shown as dashed line. The baseline usually overlaps or partially overlaps a line segment on the [base feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174). In such a case, the start point of the baseline must be identical to a vertex on the base feature. The baseline can also connect vertices of two base features. Otherwise, the start point of the baseline can be loose (not connected to any feature). 
Baseline is represented by the first line segment of orthogonal and polar dimension geometries (polylines). It indicates how the dimension is anchored to the base feature. 
A base feature, such as a building, is one for which an absolute position is known. Dimensions are drawn from base features to dimension features. 
Orthogonal dimension geometry is a polyline with three, four, five, or six vertices. The number of vertices depends on the type of orthogonal dimension. 
  * An orthogonal dimension with single dimension line requires three vertices. The second line segment represents the dimension line. 
  * An orthogonal dimension with one dimension line and two witness lines requires five vertices. The third line segment represents the dimension line and the second and the fourth line segments represent the witness lines. 
  * An orthogonal dimension with a second dimension line offset requires six vertices. The second and fourth line segments represent the dimension lines. The third and fifth line segments represent the witness lines. 


All other types of orthogonal dimension require four vertices.
  * For an orthogonal dimension with two dimension lines, the second and third line segments represent the dimension lines. For an orthogonal dimension with dimension and witness line, the second line segment represents the dimension line. The third line segment represents the witness line. For an orthogonal dimension with witness and dimension line, the second line segment represents the witness line. The third line segment represents the dimension line. 


The angles in orthogonal dimensions also have special constraints.
  * The angle between the baseline and the next line segment in the polyline geometry may be 0º, 90º, 180º or 270º. If the polyline has only three vertices (orthogonal dimension with single dimension line), only 90º and 270º angles are allowed. 
  * The angles at the other vertices must be right angles.


Stacked Orthogonal Dimension Constraints
A [stacked orthogonal dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vAsnjYWXINWTtu_hw2cVKg) is a collection of orthogonal dimensions. All dimensions in this collection must have the same baseline. 
The following constraints exist in addition to the constraints placed on geometries of individual orthogonal dimensions: 
  * The first points and the second points of all the polyline geometries (all the baselines) are the same. 
  * For all the polylines, the angle at the second vertex, which is the angle between the baseline and next dimension/witness line, must be either right (90 or 270 degrees) or straight (0 or 180 degrees). 


Radius-of-Two-Points Dimension Constraints
[Radius-of-two-points dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oyag6eiB7IrXUv2xDV__jQ) geometry is a polyline with three vertices. The first line segment of the geometry is the first dimension line and the second line segment is the second dimension line. 
Polar Dimension Constraints
[Polar dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Q_4vV6IOXbpLIxVpbGjozg) is a polyline with three vertices. The polar dimension geometry contains a baseline as the first line segment and a dimension line as the second line segment. The following diagram shows the baseline as a dashed line. It usually overlaps a line segment on the base feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259174)

##### Driven and Not-Driven Dimensions
Certain behavior is expected when dimensions or related features are edited. In a [driven dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149), a user updates a dimensioned feature, and the dimension's constructed point is updated so that it is connected again to the dimensioned feature. 
A dimensioned feature that, when updated, updates the constructed points of the related driven dimensions so that their constructed points stay connected to the dimensioned feature.   
|  Example  |   |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |   |  
|  Original dimensioned  
feature   |  Modified dimensioned  
feature   |  Position of the constructed  
point updated so that the  
dimension is connected to   
the dimensioned feature.   |  
The opposite of a driven dimension is a [not-driven dimension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149). This means that if a user updates a dimensioned feature associated with a not-driven dimension, the dimension's constructed point is not updated. The dimension remains unmodified and is not connected to the feature. 
A dimensioned feature that if updated does not update the constructed points of the related not-driven dimensions. Thus their constructed points are no longer connected to the dimensioned feature. 
The G3E_DRIVINGDRIVEN column in dimension component tables determines whether an instance of the dimension component is driven or not-driven. To support driven dimension behavior, the [dimensioning relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/u20XyiqjdWo8xx3uutCRBw) must be defined between dimensions and all possible features by which the dimensions may be driven. 
A dimension is always driven by the base feature. This means that whenever a base feature is moved, the dimension is moved appropriately. Further actions can follow based on whether the dimension is driven or not-driven (by the dimensioned feature). 
A not-driven dimension is moved along with the base feature and disconnected from the dimensioned feature. 
If a dimension is driven, the dimensioned feature is moved with the dimension. The dimension stays connected to the dimensioned feature.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259149)  |  
|  Original dimensioned  
feature   |  Modified base feature  |  Dimension updated so that it is  
connected to the dimensioned   
feature.   |  
To achieve this behavior, a dimensioning relationship must be defined between dimensions and the base features.

##### Moving Dimension Text
After a dimension is placed, its dimension texts are displayed in their default positions. The default positions of dimension text relative to the dimension line are set in metadata. 
However, the default positions might not be the most suitable, as when a dimension text overlaps another feature or another dimension text. In such situations, users can move dimension texts in one of two modes—along the dimension line or freely—using the Move Dimension Text command on the Edit tool. The mode for moving dimension texts is configured per dimension component. 
Moving Dimension Text Along a Dimension Line
In this mode, the dimension text stays the same distance from the dimension line. The distance is specified in metadata. The dimension text can be moved only in a direction parallel with the dimension line. 
For regular dimensions, the dimension text can be moved anywhere in the direction parallel with the dimension line. The following diagram shows the possible positions of the origin of the dimension text for regular dimensions: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259187)
For [small dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IrX~FbRNYEMNuVXwnCfn4Q), the dimension text can be moved away from the endpoints of the dimension line. The following diagram shows the possible positions of the origin of the dimension text for small dimensions: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259187)
Moving Dimension Text Freely
In this mode, the distance of the dimension text from the dimension line is not fixed, and the dimension text can be moved in any direction. 
For regular and small dimensions, the origin of the dimension text can be moved arbitrarily. The following diagrams show the possible positions of the origin of the dimension text for regular and small dimensions that can be moved freely: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259187)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259187)

##### Orthogonal Dimensions
Orthogonal dimensions display the relative position of a dimensioned feature to a base feature as a perpendicular and parallel offset. Orthogonal dimensions can also be combined or stacked to form [stacked dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vAsnjYWXINWTtu_hw2cVKg). 
There are several types of orthogonal dimensions:
Single Dimension Line
An orthogonal dimension with a single dimension line displays the perpendicular offset of a dimensioned feature from an edge of the base feature. The dimension line is perpendicular to one of the coincident lines of the base feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
Two Dimension Lines
An orthogonal dimension with two dimension lines displays the perpendicular and parallel offsets of a dimensioned feature from a vertex on the base feature. The first dimension line is either perpendicular or parallel to one of the coincident edges of the base feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
Second Dimension Line Offset
An orthogonal dimension with a second dimension line offset displays perpendicular and parallel offset of a dimensioned feature from a vertex on the base feature. The line of the first dimension is either perpendicular or parallel to one of the coincident lines of the base feature. This orthogonal dimension is often used when an orthogonal dimension with two dimension lines cannot be used, because the second dimension line would overlap another object on the map. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
Dimension Line and a Witness Line
An orthogonal dimension with a dimension line and a witness line displays the perpendicular offset of a dimensioned feature from a vertex of the base feature. A witness line is a dimension line that does not display the length. The dimension line is either perpendicular or parallel to one of the coincident lines of the base feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
Witness Line and a Dimension Line
An orthogonal dimension with a witness line and a dimension line displays the parallel offset of a dimensioned feature from a vertex of the base feature. The witness line is either perpendicular or parallel to one of the coincident lines of the base feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
Dimension Line and Two Witness Lines
An orthogonal dimension with a dimension line and two witness lines also displays the parallel offset of a dimensioned feature from a vertex of the base feature. This type of orthogonal dimension is used where an orthogonal dimension with a witness and a dimension line cannot be used because the dimension line would overlap another object on the map. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259199) Dimension lines in orthogonal dimensions can be switched to witness lines by deleting the value of the text attribute for the dimension line in Feature Explorer. 
In addition to the standard required columns of component tables, [additional columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V6RM4nVFNzCgeMon~w~QOA) are required for orthogonal dimension component tables. Orthogonal dimension polyline geometries must comply with [additional constraints](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ).

##### Polar Dimensions
Polar dimensions display the offset of the dimensioned feature from a vertex on the base feature. The offset is expressed as the distance from the vertex and the angle between one of the two adjacent edges on the base feature and the dimension line. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259208)
Besides the standard required columns of component tables, [additional columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6UBS9F6tZypFAC_Qj9CPBw) are required for polar dimension component tables. Polar dimension polyline geometries must also comply with [additional constraints](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ).

##### Radius-of-Two-Points Dimensions
Radius-of-two-points dimensions display the distance from two vertices on one or two base features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259203)
In addition to the standard required columns of component tables, [additional columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7KD~qzqDJfM67X319XNxA) are required for radius-of-two-points dimension component tables. Radius-of-two-points dimension polyline geometries must also comply with [additional constraints](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ).

##### Simple Dimensions
Simple dimensions indicate the distance between two features on the map, the base feature and the dimensioned feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259178)
In addition to the standard graphic component table columns, simple dimension component tables must contain [additional columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/r10f4ji_zgVMM6oJTh5G1w). Simple dimension polyline geometries must also comply with [additional constraints](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ).

##### Small Dimensions
Simple and orthogonal dimensions can be displayed as [small dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256641). Where a distinction is made, dimensions that are not small are called regular dimensions. 
Small dimensions are used when the length of the dimension line is less than the reversal distance. On small dimensions, the dimension text is outside the dimension line, usually behind the endpoint. 
On small dimensions, the dimension text is outside the dimension line, usually behind the endpoint. The symbols on the endpoints of the dimension line can be flipped, and the dimension line can be extended beyond its typical endpoints.   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256641)  |  
| --- |  
You must [populate metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EHtd1sxkQwXW1R70A8dkow) to [display small dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OEQtEigV7XYwgtrR5NXAAw).

##### Stacked Orthogonal Dimensions
When two or more orthogonal dimensions are combined to form a single dimension, they are said to be stacked. All dimensions in a stack must have the same baseline. 
Stacked orthogonal dimensions are essentially [repeating components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256830), and the [procedures for stacking orthogonal dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zzJhowEua~0lnGEAfPHbrQ) are the same as for placing any repeating component. Instances of both single and stacked orthogonal dimensions are allowed in the same dimension component. 
A feature component that can occur more than once on a feature instance; for example, a street name that appears several places along a street. 
The following types of orthogonal dimensions can be combined in a stack:
  * With a single dimension line
  * With two dimension lines
  * With a dimension and a witness line


This type of orthogonal dimension can be stacked but cannot be combined within one stack: 
  * With witness and dimension line


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256830)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256830)
The overlapping dimension lines in the stacked dimensions are called primary dimension lines. There are two approaches to calculating the lengths displayed at the primary dimension lines. In the first approach, accumulative lengths are calculated. This means that all the lengths are equal to the offsets from the point on the base feature, as in the diagram above. 
In the second approach, incremental lengths are calculated. This means that only the length of the first (shortest) dimension in the stack is equal to the offset from the point on the base feature. All the other lengths are equal to the offsets from the previous (closest moving away from the baseline) dimension in the stack. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256830)
The accumulative/incremental property of stacked dimensions can be set per dimension feature instance (that is, per stack). The default value is specified in [G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL.G3E_MEASACCUM](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug). 
The orthogonal dimensions with single dimension line can be also grouped into a stacked dimension with offset. All dimensions in the stack with offset display a perpendicular offset from the same edge on the base feature. Each dimension in such stack is represented as a single dimension feature instance. 
If users frequently [place stacked orthogonal dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MFOfkbzhfVwDKg5Fz3SW5A) specifying lengths using the Orthogonal Dimension Construction Aids control, add a placement configuration to the New Feature control. Set stacked orthogonal dimensions in placement configuration to Yes (1) in [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_AUTOREPEAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ). 
If users tend to place stacked orthogonal dimensions without typing lengths in the Orthogonal Dimension Construction Aids control, set [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_AUTOREPEAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to Yes (1). 
Besides the required columns of orthogonal dimension component tables, [additional columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~TeLYAblUXs~qfjGchv8IA) are required for component tables with orthogonal stacked dimensions. Orthogonal dimension polyline geometries in stacked dimensions must comply with [additional constraints](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PV8Oh7S~aqifw4L9JCYaHQ).

#### Graphic Components

##### Alternate Components
Alternate components, which are useful for different representations of data such as static, manually generated schematics as opposed to [automatically generated schematics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UJ7gLta1CN5LDyy_xomXIg), are used primarily in [processing the linear break of a feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HEpZLsnCSeIIDG3qeKL5Yg) and in spatial processing. 
This approach duplicates the graphic elements. In one view, the data are positioned by its accurate geospatial location. In the other (alternate) view, the data are positioned relative to its related features; the geospatial location is not important. Often lines are drawn with only right-angle bends. Since the alternate components are part of the same feature, the relationships are defined only once. 
You are responsible for construction of any alternate component data. There is no capability to automatically generate alternate components. To define a geographic component as alternate, set [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ALTERNATEGEOGRAPHIC](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to Yes (1) and [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to a value between 1 and 5. 
  * G3E_ALTERNATEGEOGRAPHIC—This is a Boolean flag to indicate the component is an alternate primary geographic component. Set the value in this field to zero if there is no alternate presentation of the primary geographic component in the feature to break or consider in spatial filtering and querying. This value should be zero for all annotative graphics, such as labels and leader lines. Do not set this value to Yes (1) for the primary geographic component. For each group of alternate components (those with like values for G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL), set only one component in the group to 1 for this field. If this value is 1, G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL must be greater than zero. 
  * G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL—This is an integer value used when multiple alternate geographic components exist in a feature. The connectivity software matches the alternate ordinal in the active feature (linear being broken) with the same ordinal in the related features. This is a number between 1 and 5 that represents the alternate component set. The value should be 0 for geographic and detail components. 
The selection tools within NetWorks Core use this field to identify the alternate sets of components. This number should also appear on the [legend definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) to define the alternate set of components displayed on the legend. 
When introducing [synthesized component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BHztsPXCkqRWc8ufJn_Dkg), if multiple components are defined to share a database table, those components used in the synthesized views must be defined with the same G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL. If not, the optimized metadata table for the component views is not updated correctly with the G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDIDNAL of the component from which it is derived. 


You place alternate components in a map view that contains a legend that supports this particular alternate component, where the G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL value of the component matches the G3E_LEGEND.G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL value.

##### Determining Arcs
The begin and endpoints and the radius define four possible arcs. Additional information must be stored to specify which of those four arcs. The sign of the radius is used to specify whether the arc sweep is less than or greater than pi. The sign of the third component of the normal vector is used to specify whether the sweep is clockwise or counterclockwise. 
Determine the arc from the following:
  * Begin (A) and end (B) points
  * Radius (two of the three colored lines)
  * Whether sweep angle is less than or greater than pi
  * Whether sweep angle is clockwise or counterclockwise
