#### Configuring Z-Coordinates
You can use several [general parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) settings to configure Z coordinates. 
DefaultZ
You can set the default Z value in meters (displayed in the Active Z field of the Precision Coordinate control) by changing the value in the DefaultZ record of G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME. The default value of DefaultZ is zero (0). 
If you change the default Z value, you can load it from the database by clicking Reset Active-Z ![PrecisionCoordinateControl_ResetActiveZ_BTN](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/289507) on the Precision Coordinate control. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/289507)
3DMeasurementCalculation
This flag indicates whether the Linearlabel and CalculateLength Functional Interfaces are measured in 3D or in 2D. If set to 1, then they are measured in 3D. If set to 0, then they are measured in 2D. The Placement Length Display dialog box and the Component Length dialog box honor this setting. 3D measurement only applies to length calculations and not angles or area. Default value is zero. 
3DSupport
This flag indicates whether 3D functionality is enabled or disabled. It has the highest precedence and has final control on all the new 3D operations. If set to 1, all of the 3D functionality is enabled. If set to 0, all of the 3D functionality is disabled. Default value is zero. 
MaxZ and MinZ
These parameters are user defined and represent the valid z value range in meters.   
|  MinZ  |  MaxZ  |  Result  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  NONE  |  Defined  |  Z-value must be less than or equal to MaxZ to be considered valid.  |  
|  Defined  |  NONE  |  Z-value must be greater than or equal to MinZ to be considered valid.  |  
|  Defined  |  Defined  |  Z-value must be greater than or equal to MinZ and less than or equal to MaxZ to be considered valid.   |  
|  NONE  |  NONE  |  All Z-values are valid.  |

#### Construction Aids
Construction aids are a set of predefined and custom placement tools displayed by certain placement techniques. They are displayed on a dockable control, and you can configure the way the predefined and custom construction aids are presented to users on the control. NetWorks Core delivers the set of [predefined construction aids](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TaEc8F8ZtP3lcKc~jCQK7Q). AutoRepeat is presented as for each button on the Construction Aids control. Freehand is always in the first position. The order of the other predefined construction aids is configured in G3E_CONSTRUCTIONAID.G3E_ORDINAL. 
You cannot delete a predefined construction aid from the database. To remove a predefined construction aid from the control of a specific user, change the role of the user in G3E_CONSTRUCTIONAID.G3E_ROLE. 
You can [implement a custom construction aid](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7fvS48VjZl3tPbDcAvKYWQ), add it to the dockable control, and delete it from the database. 
Use Metadata Explorer to edit the [G3E_CONSTRUCTIONAID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OssNVZBN96cTTeDu5Cc_uw) metadata table to configure these characteristics of both predefined and custom construction aids: 
  * The tooltip that appears when a user hovers over the construction aid button
  * The order in which the construction aid appears on the Construction Aids control after Auto-repeat and Freehand 
  * The user role to which the construction aid is assigned
  * Whether the construction aid defaults to repeating or non-repeating
  * The image used to represent the construction aid
  * The [Shortcut key assigned](javascript:;) to the construction aid 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262020) Because the AutoRepeat and Freehand are not configurable, they are not displayed on the Metadata Explorer tree view. 
Survey Points
Survey Point is the only Construction Aid that requires specific metadata configuration other than G3E_CONSRUCTIONAID. Survey Point generates a vertex using the coordinates of a survey feature from the database. The user selects a value to filter the available Survey Points to a particular batch and selects a particular survey point by number. Insert a line into the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table to indicate the Survey Point component, the Survey Batch filter, and the Survey Point number. Populate the following columns:   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTCNO  |  G3E_VNO of the survey feature's geographic component.  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTANO  |  ANO of survey batch attribute. If a picklist is defined, it is used; otherwise, all possible values are displayed.   |  
|  G3E_PARAMETER1  |  ANO of survey point number attribute. If a picklist is defined, is be used; otherwise, all possible values are displayed   |

#### Feature Explorer Overview
Feature Explorer: 
  * Is a [dockable control](javascript:;) used to review and edit information about specific feature instances. 
  * Deals with attribute information and with information about the relationships between features. For example, if a user reviews a cable feature using Feature Explorer, the attributes of the cable are displayed. If the cable has other features related to it, the following relationship information can be displayed: 
    * Features to which the cable can be connected
    * Features that own the cable
    * Features that the cable owns
  * Does not require specific metadata. It uses metadata defined for placement, edit, and relationships. 


Using Feature Explorer, the user can navigate these relationships to review related features. 
Feature Explorer is divided into the [navigation panel and the information panel](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/52pN2fzrriwgeUjUOoh6mw). The navigation panel presents the relationship information of the feature in a hierarchical tree view. When the [user selects a feature for review,](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/prtfJTrnIZVHPHcyMIPY8g) it is displayed at the top of the tree. Upon expanding the tree, the user is presented with a list of the relationships supported by Feature Explorer in which the feature may participate. The following [NetWorks Core relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6yoxVaGBoikpPqknNdlKyg) are supported in Feature Explorer: 
  * Node-edge connectivity
  * Node-ordered connectivity
  * Ownership
  * Many-to-many ownership


A user can perform the following functions in Feature Explorer: 
  * Place a feature
When the user [places a feature](http://www.), the placement dialog tabs ([G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) = 'Placement') for the feature are displayed in the information panel along with the Graphic Components tab. The relationship panel is disabled and displays the feature name or configuration name being placed. 
  * Edit feature attributes
When the user [edits attribute information](http://www.), the information panel displays the edit dialog tabs (G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Edit') along with the Graphic Components tab. The relationship panel is disabled. 
  * Review feature attributes
When the user [reviews attribute information](javascript:;), the information panel displays the review dialog tabs (G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Review'). However, if the data are secondary data, G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Properties'. 
  * Edit feature relationships
When the user [edits a relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kc4LHXI6I_AF_lk8GkDGqg), the information panel contains the review dialog tabs (G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Review') for the currently selected feature. The user can navigate the relationship panel and edit relationships using drag and drop techniques. The only relationships that the user can edit are directed relationships (ownership, many-to-many ownership, and node-ordered connectivity). 
  * Edit related features
When the user [edits related features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8kKN_gfuZi_1jYbWJc_pvQ), the information panel contains the review dialog tabs (G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Bulk Edit'). 


Related Topic
[Placement and Edit Commands](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYpQa6kBxyn3HyDzRUxajA)

#### Graphic Components Tab
If Feature Explorer is displayed while placement or Feature Edit is running, the available graphic components display on the [Graphic Components tab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YYhNwUjDxh8QLm3dUpgiiA). The following is a general workflow for the Graphic Components tab: 
  1. The user selects a feature from the New Feature control or the Placement Shortcut toolbar. 
  2. The Graphic Components tab in Feature Explorer displays a list of the graphic components available for placement in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL order. 
     * This list controls the order in which the software places graphic components using silent placement techniques, derived components, or required components. 
     * If a detail component's G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is not listed at the top level of the Graphic Components tab, but is listed underneath the geographic component's top-level entry to reduce the number of components listed at the top level. 
  3. The list of components is gathered from the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) and [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table. The feature number (G3E_FNO) of the selected feature is used to access G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT to return the list of all components defined for this feature. 
  4. The component number (G3E_CNO) of each component is mapped to G3E_COMPONENT to get additional details about each component. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259269) For a placement configuration, the Graphic Components tab is populated from the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table, and the bullets above apply. 
Graphic Components Tab Metadata
These tables are associated with the Graphic Components tab: 
  * G3E_COMPONENT
  * Components fall into two basic categories: graphic and nongraphic. A [component's type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MnSNe2k7Xndz0jiF9Wu~6w) is determined by the G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TYPE field. Only the graphic components are considered for inclusion on the Graphic Components tab. All nongraphic components are excluded from this tab. The component names displayed in the Feature Explorer Graphic Components tab are defined in [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). If the component is a detail component include some indication of that fact in the user name. G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT controls how and when components are placed.
    * G3E_DERIVEDFROMCNO
Components that cannot be placed independently from other components are called derived components. An example of a derived component is a pole riser for a pole. A derived component is placed automatically whenever an instance of the component from which it is derived is placed. Define derived components by setting [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DERIVEDFROMCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to the G3E_CNO value of the component from which it should be derived. Because any component that is derived from another component does not appear on the Graphic Components tab, the user has no direct control over the placement of derived components. 
    * G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT
The [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field lets you include or exclude the remaining graphic components within the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table from the Graphic Components tab. Most graphic components are included on the Graphic Components tab and have a default value of Yes (1) for this field. Use a value of 0 in this field to exclude components from placement. Use the G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT field to limit the number of components presented to the user for placement, which excludes those components that are seldom placed as part of the feature. 
Only the New Feature command examines this field when constructing the list of graphic components for placement. Edit Feature and New Component disregard the G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT field and include the graphic component regardless of its setting. 
    * G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO
Optionally populate [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field for geographic components when you want to simplify placement of either the geographic G3E_CNO component or its associated detail G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO component based on the active window type. When populated, it also reduces the contents in the user interface at the top-level. For each component number populated in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO, there should be a corresponding row where G3E_CNO equals that same CNO value. In these corresponding rows, G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT is ignored. Even if G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT is 1, this detail component is not listed separately at the top-level of the Graphic Components tab because G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated. 
    * G3E_ORDINAL
The value in the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field controls the order in which the graphic components appear on the Graphic Components tab. Graphic components are listed in ascending order based on G3E_ORDINAL. This field also controls the order in which the placement techniques for the graphic components are executed and, thus, the order in which a user places components relative to one another. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259269) Set the value of G3E_ORDINAL so that the primary graphic component is the first one placed. See the [Placement Algorithm](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YY5WEAfiFC2VOvip1IxW6A) for more details concerning placement order. 
    * G3E_REQUIRED
Mark a component as required by setting the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field to Yes (1). A required component must exist for the feature to pass validation. However, placement does not require the user to place an instance of a required component before saving the feature. It uses the required field as an indication of when to automatically start the placement technique for a given component. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259269) To enable efficient creation of data, define only the primary graphic component as required. 
If G3E_REQUIRED is set to No (0), the component is optional, and it does not have to exist to pass model validation. 
    * G3E_REPEATING
If a component is marked as repeating, a user can create multiple instances of this component. To specify a repeating component, set [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to Yes (1). A value of No (0) in this field means that a user can create only one instance of this component. [Required and repeating components work together](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7a4EXbGwHfWoLcplgecKEA) to control how many instances of each component a user can create during feature placement. 
    * G3E_AUTOREPEAT
Repeating components are further classified as auto- repeating. The software can repeatedly create multiple instances of an auto-repeating component without the user reselecting the component. Auto-repeating components are designated by setting [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_AUTOREPEAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to Yes (1). Most repeating components are not defined as auto-repeating, so they have the default value of No (0) for G3E_AUTOREPEAT. To create multiple instances of these components, the user must initiate each occurrence by reselecting the component for placement, which places only one occurrence at a time. This diagram shows the metadata structure for defining graphic components for placement. 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259269)

#### How Placement Works Based on the Active Map Window Type

##### Placing a New Component Switching the Active Window

###### User Switches to a Detail Window—New Component
  1. If [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is populated for this geographic component: 
    1. If metadata rules permit (such as G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING), the placement technique for the detail component has the potential to be started. 
      1. If the user has placed any points for the geographic component without finishing the component, the user is prompted: Do you wish to cancel digitizing this component?   
|  The user clicks Yes  |  The geographic component is discarded. The detail component’s placement technique is started.   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  The user clicks No  |  The user continues placing the geographic component. The detail window remains active, but it does not accept clicks. The user must activate the geographic window to continue placing the geographic component.   |  
      2. If the detail component was placed, placement resumes with the component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO, not with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
      3. If a detail component’s G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is not listed in the user interface; only the geographic component's username is listed. 
    2. Otherwise, the user continues placing the geographic component.
  2. If G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is not populated for this geographic component, the geographic placement technique continues with typical feature placement.

##### Placing a New Component Using the Active Window
  1. The user has an active job.
  2. The user selects a feature to which to add components.
  3. The user selects Edit > Features > New Component. 
  4. The New Component dialog appears with available components listed in G3E_ORDINAL order. 
  5. The user selects one or more components to place. The following are some examples:
    1. [Condition 1:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284600) Current component is geographic; a geographic window is active. 
The placement technique for the first geographic component is started.
    2. [Condition 2:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284600) Current component is geographic; a detail window is active. 
      1. If G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated for this geographic component, the detail component’s placement technique is started instead. 
      2. After finishing the detail component, placement resumes with the next selected component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. It does not resume with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
      3. If a detail component’s G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is not listed in the user interface; only the geographic component’s username is listed. 


The placement technique for the first geographic component is started.
  1. If G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated for this geographic component, the detail component’s placement technique is started instead. 
  2. After finishing the detail component, placement resumes with the next selected component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. It does not resume with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
  3. If a detail component’s G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is not listed in the user interface; only the geographic component’s username is listed.

##### Placing a New Feature Switching the Active Window
  1. The user has an active job.
  2. The user selects Edit > Features > New Feature. 
  3. The user selects a simple feature to place.
  4. New Feature uses the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT (Feature-Component Relationship Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to determine the order in which to place required components. 
    1. The current component is geographic; a geographic window is active; a detail window exists. 
      1. The placement technique for the geographic component is started.
      2. [Condition 1:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284581) The user switches to the detail window. 
        1. If [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is populated for this geographic component: 
          1. If metadata rules permit (such as G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING), the placement technique for the detail component has the potential to be started. 
            1. If the user has placed any points for the geographic component without finishing the component, the user is prompted: Do you wish to cancel digitizing this component?   
|  The user clicks Yes  |  The geographic component is discarded. The detail component’s placement technique is started.   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  The user clicks No  |  The user continues placing the geographic component. The detail window remains active, but it does not accept clicks. The user must activate the geographic window to continue placing the geographic component.   |  
            2. If the detail component was placed, placement resumes with the component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO, not with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
            3. If a detail component’s G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is skipped in the placement sequence. 
          2. Otherwise, the user continues placing the geographic component.
        2. If G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is not populated for this geographic component, the geographic placement technique continues with typical feature placement.

    1. If metadata rules permit (such as G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING), the placement technique for the detail component has the potential to be started. 
      1. If the user has placed any points for the geographic component without finishing the component, the user is prompted: Do you wish to cancel digitizing this component?   
|  The user clicks Yes  |  The geographic component is discarded. The detail component’s placement technique is started.   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  The user clicks No  |  The user continues placing the geographic component. The detail window remains active, but it does not accept clicks. The user must activate the geographic window to continue placing the geographic component.   |  
      2. If the detail component was placed, placement resumes with the component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO, not with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
      3. If a detail component’s G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is skipped in the placement sequence. 
    2. Otherwise, the user continues placing the geographic component.
  2. If G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is not populated for this geographic component, the geographic placement technique continues with typical feature placement.

##### Placing a New Feature Using the Active Window
  1. The user has an active job.
  2. The user selects Edit > Features > New Feature. 
  3. The user selects a simple feature to place.
  4. New Feature uses the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) to determine the order in which to place required components. The following lists a few cases: 
    1. [Condition 1:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284575) The current component is geographic; a geographic window is active. 
If metadata rules permit, the placement technique for that geographic component is started. 
    2. [Condition 2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284575): The current component is geographic; a detail window is active. 
      1. If [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is populated for this geographic component, the detail component’s placement technique is started instead. 
      2. After finishing the detail component, placement resumes with the component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. It does not resume with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
      3. If a detail component’s G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is skipped in the placement sequence. The following is an example from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT:   
|  G3E_CNO  |  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO  |  G3E_ORDINAL  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Geo A  |  Detail A  |  1  |  
|  Geo B  |  Detail B  |  2  |  
|  Detail A   |  Null  |  3  |  
Detail A is not started after Geo B because it is associated with Geo A in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of the first row. The row is needed, however, because it contains the placement technique, arguments, and so forth, necessary to place the detail component. 
    3. [Condition 3:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284575) The geographic component cannot be placed because an occurrence already exists (and G3E_REPEATING=0); a geographic window is active; G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated; a detail component occurrence can be placed, but a detail window is not open. 
      1. This component is skipped.
      2. The next required component is started.
      3. This is similar to typical feature placement behavior when a detail component is skipped. The user must open a detail window and click New Component to start placing the detail component. 
    4. [Condition 4:](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/284575) The geographic component cannot be placed because an occurrence already exists (and G3E_REPEATING=0); G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated; a detail component occurrence cannot be placed because an occurrence already exists (and G3E_REPEATING=0). 
      1. This component is skipped.
      2. The next required component is started.


If metadata rules permit, the placement technique for that geographic component is started. 
  1. If [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is populated for this geographic component, the detail component’s placement technique is started instead. 
  2. After finishing the detail component, placement resumes with the component that follows the geographic component containing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. It does not resume with the component that follows the detail component that was just placed. 
  3. If a detail component’s G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component, the detail component is skipped in the placement sequence. The following is an example from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT:   
|  G3E_CNO  |  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO  |  G3E_ORDINAL  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Geo A  |  Detail A  |  1  |  
|  Geo B  |  Detail B  |  2  |  
|  Detail A   |  Null  |  3  |  
Detail A is not started after Geo B because it is associated with Geo A in the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of the first row. The row is needed, however, because it contains the placement technique, arguments, and so forth, necessary to place the detail component. 


  1. This component is skipped.
  2. The next required component is started.
  3. This is similar to typical feature placement behavior when a detail component is skipped. The user must open a detail window and click New Component to start placing the detail component.

  2. The next required component is started.

#### PickQuick

##### PickQuick Dialog Box with Z Values
A PickQuick dialog box with Z values appears during placement or edit operations if all
  * 3DSupport is set to 1 in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table.
  * The Element Z mode is enabled. 
  * The Z-Lock mode is disabled. 
  * There is more than one Z value at the snap or calculated point.


There is only one Z value per feature in the PickQuick dialog box (that is, a single feature with two coincident points, overlapping segments, and so on only return the first point found). 
Example Workflow
The user:
  1. Clicks the intersection construction aide.
  2. Selects the two features to calculate the intersection.
The intersection is calculated and NetWorks Core determines that there are two Z values at the intersection point (141 and 337). The PickQuick dialog box appears. 
  3. Selects the Z value to use.


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/338208) If the user closes the PickQuick dialog box without selecting a Z value, the value in the Active Z field of the Precision Coordinate control is used.

#### Placement Algorithm
The following steps generally describe feature placement:
  1. The user selects a feature from the New Feature control or Placement Shortcut toolbar.
  2. A new feature instance is created with rows for each required component using the default values from the metadata/database parameters. 
If metadata is configured correctly, a geographic feature is created if the user has a geographic map window active. A detail feature is created if the user has a detail map window active. See [How Placement Works Based on the Active Map Window](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MrDAKCAz0fN4KhIE~yfd7g) for more information. 
  3. The list of graphic components included in placement is retrieved from metadata and ordered based on [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). 
  4. The dialog tabs defined for placement are retrieved and displayed in Feature Explorer. Each dialog tab is formatted for the attribute sets described in metadata. The final tab displayed in Feature Explorer is the Graphic Components tab. It contains the ordered list of graphic components retrieved in the previous step. 
  5. The placement technique defined for the first required graphic component (implied by the ascending list of G3E_ORDINAL values) is automatically started. Any service software in support of feature relationships for this component (such as connectivity and ownership) is also initiated. 
  6. The placement technique detects mouse events and reflects the event status by changing the glyph on the mouse cursor to indicate the snap points of existing graphics. Each [relationship service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e2tt5qpeYNY9MM7Wm73iAw) also detects mouse events and reflects the event status by highlighting existing graphics that are relationship candidates. 
  7. As the user digitizes the component, the graphics are displayed in dynamics according to the style rules defined for this feature. The style rules are evaluated, and a style is chosen based on the attribute values that are currently set for this feature. 
  8. When the user completes digitization of the component, the relationship services are notified and they automatically perform the work necessary to establish any applicable relationships. The geometry value is set for the graphic component. 
  9. Any components derived from the component just placed are automatically placed.
  10. The next component in the graphic components list, as ordered by G3E_ORDINAL, is considered for automatic placement. Its [placement technique](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) is automatically started if this is a required component or if this component's placement technique is silent. The cycle continues, with each graphic component in the list being reviewed for placement until all the graphic components have been examined. 
  11. From the [Graphic Components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0ty9o5qn8MoLl0c25buTHw) tab, the user can select any optional or repeating graphic components to digitize. Once a component is selected, the associated placement technique for that component is started to perform the digitization. 
  12. If Feature Explorer is visible, the user must explicitly click Save Edits and Continue or Save Edits to commit the feature instance to the database along with any edits to other features that resulted from establishing relationships. Save Edits and Continue allows the user to place additional features interactively; Save Edits terminates the placement command. The user can click Cancel Edits to discard the data and cancel the command operation. 
  13. If Feature Explorer is not visible, the feature instance is automatically committed to the database along with any edits to other features that resulted from establishing relationships. 
  14. The command starts another cycle to place another feature instance. The user can press ESC to cancel the next iteration. Or, the user can select a different feature from the New Feature control to begin placement of a different feature. 


Placement Algorithm Metadata
These are a few of the metadata tables that drive the placement algorithm:
  * [G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CER72g2Ys4bpQ9~jNI78Ng)
This table determines which features are presented to the user in the New Feature control. 
  * [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w)
The G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT[G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ) table determines which graphic components are listed on the Graphic Components tab and also controls automatic placement. 
  * [G3E_DIALOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw)
The G3E_DIALOG, [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ), or [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) table determines which nongraphic components to present in Feature Explorer. 
  * [G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fy4Cx0Y1oeQuVI6b1cIi6A)
This table determines how each graphic component is digitized.
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/19xFJqi2WdZ~OXlIOWc1Hg)
This table determines which relationships to process for each graphic component.

#### Placement and Edit Commands

##### Add Related Features
[Add Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yGHl~jR_3R42zeO46VPsGg) gives the user a mechanism for creating features that are related to an existing feature. The only relationships supported by Add Related Features are simple ownership and many-to-many ownership.   
|  Example Add Related Features is useful for creating inside plant features (those features in the communication model that do not have any graphics associated with them). The user can select a building (a graphic feature) in the map view and run Add Related Features to create floors and rooms in the building. Using Feature Explorer, the user can select an existing floor or room and rerun Add Related Features to place equipment in the room.   |  
| --- |  
Add Related Features can also be used to add a previously configured piece of equipment to an assembly. You must [set up the equipment catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/L8MGaF~BdvFSXRWNgC9BPg) and save the configurations to the catalog using [Save To Catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RYJriFHhlSXe6gVhAFCtoQ). 
You can filter the features available to users in Add Related Features by [role](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RqEa9u_KeRBkkgazf~_C0g). 
Related Topics
[Edit Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e6vZLByjrTVM4DuZIv9IQg)
[Edit Feature Relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ObsaXyKUGM~B6vch_6Macw)

##### Edit Feature Relationships
The Edit Feature Relationships command allows the user to manipulate the relationships between features within [Feature Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kc4LHXI6I_AF_lk8GkDGqg). When the command is invoked, the selected feature is placed at the root of Feature Explorer if it is not already in the tree view. The user reviews existing relationships to locate candidate feature relationships and establishes the relationship by dragging one node of the tree and dropping it on the other. When all relationship editing is complete, the user commits the changes to the database using the Feature Explorer toolbar. 
Because Edit Feature Relationships uses [existing relationship metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KdIvObivteb7qRPsJbt3xQ), there is no special metadata required for this command to function. However, only relationships that are available for review within Feature Explorer are candidates for drag and drop editing. Also, for a relationship to be established between two features, it must be a [directed relationship](javascript:;), and the user must drop the subordinate feature on the superior feature. For example, the user must drop a transformer feature on a pole feature to establish the ownership relationship between a pole and a transformer where the pole owns the transformer. The pole does not highlight the transformer as a candidate relationship in this case. 
Using [roles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RqEa9u_KeRBkkgazf~_C0g), you can restrict the set of features that can have their relationships edited in the Edit Feature Relationships command. 
  
Related Topics 
[Add Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDLhzjJQSDupgERtBVPE4w)
[Edit Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e6vZLByjrTVM4DuZIv9IQg)

##### Edit Feature
The Edit Feature command allows the user to make updates to existing feature instances. After selecting an existing feature, the user can: 
  * Digitize optional and/or repeating graphic components
  * Add optional and repeating attribute components
  * Delete existing graphic components
  * Delete existing optional and/or repeating attribute components
  * Modify existing attribute values


The user can only edit a single feature instance, the one in the select set.
The Edit Feature command is very like the New Feature command in presentation and functionality. See the topics about [Placement Overview](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n_~E4ANbb0BKzWjJlwLt9w), the [Placement Algorithm](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YY5WEAfiFC2VOvip1IxW6A), and the [New Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JUbUryqlV~NrkxTa1~50UQ) command for a broader look at how placement works. 
The New Feature command begins by displaying the [New Feature selection control](http://www.), from which the user selects the type of feature they want to create. However, the Edit Feature command does not display this control. Instead, the user identifies the feature to edit by putting it in the select set. 
Only individual features can be edited with Edit Feature, not [placement configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly0oRFTHG1UNGrc60ApgVQ). Edit Feature works solely from the feature description in the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) table, even if the feature being edited was placed as part of a placement configuration defined in [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ). Unlike New Feature, Feature Explorer is always displayed during Edit Feature. The [Graphic Components tab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0ty9o5qn8MoLl0c25buTHw) and [attribute dialog tabs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/a9IuHmWBr90wvsjdhK~akQ) are displayed on Feature Explorer, just as they are displayed in New Feature. The attribute dialog tabs displayed are those that are defined for edit. These tabs display the existing data for the feature. Any graphic components that have been placed are included on the Graphic Components tab, and the attribute dialogs contain the record instances and attribute values that have already been created. 
Unlike New Feature, the Edit Feature command does not automatically create any components or initiate any [placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg). Placement Techniques are not automatically fired for required components that do not exist, nor for components that can be placed silently. The user selects a component from the Graphic Components tab to initiate all graphic placement activities. The user can create or delete any graphic components available on the Graphic Components tab. 
When a user selects a component for placement, the [placement technique](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) defined for this component in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table initiates. Just as in New Feature, the placement technique can be interactive or silent. Silent placement techniques can reference any component that is part of the feature definition, including those placed before running or during Edit Feature. When the placement technique is initiated, relationship services defined for this component are initiated. If the correct conditions are met, relationships with other features are established as the component is digitized. 
Auto-repeating components are handled like they are in the New Feature command. When the user places an auto-repeating component, the placement technique for that component is continually executed in a loop, creating multiple instances of that component. Auto-repeat continues until the user presses SHIFT+ESC. 
[Component configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nle~UWesm54Oz6c1lGFMQA) are available during Edit Feature if they are defined at the feature level. Component configurations defined only within a placement configuration are not available for edit operations. New Feature and Edit Feature handle component configurations the same way. When a user selects a component configuration from Edit Feature, all placement techniques for all components that are part of that configuration are executed based on their G3E_ORDINAL values. A component configuration can be defined and placed as auto-repeating, and so too can any individual components within the configuration. 
The user clicks Save Edits and Continue to commit changes at any time during Edit Feature. When all edits are complete, the user clicks Save Edits to save final changes. The user clicks Cancel Edits to discard edits made since the last save and exit the command. 
Edit Feature Metadata
The metadata required for Edit Feature is nearly identical to the [metadata required for New Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JUbUryqlV~NrkxTa1~50UQ). The following discussion points out the differences between the two operations. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENENT
When gathering the list of graphic components to present on the Graphic Components tab, the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field is not consulted. All graphic components are eligible for editing as long as they are not derived components. 
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) is used in Edit Feature to determine the order in which the graphic components are listed on the Graphic Components tab. Since placement techniques are not automatically fired during Edit Feature, G3E_ORDINAL has no bearing on when placement techniques are executed. The user initiates all placement techniques. 
  * G3E_DIALOG
There is a slight difference in the metadata definition of the attribute dialog boxes for Edit Feature. New Feature presents attribute dialog boxes defined for placement, where G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE = 'Placement'. But Edit Feature presents attribute dialog boxes defined for edit, where [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) = 'Edit'. 
You can control which attribute dialog boxes display during Edit Feature using [edit dialog filtering](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VRNGMMcGhlNA0gN6mJ~nIA). This allows some attribute dialog boxes to be filtered out based on attribute values.

[Placement and Edit Commands](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYpQa6kBxyn3HyDzRUxajA)

##### Edit Related Features
NetWorks Core provides a means for simultaneously editing multiple features all owned by a single parent feature. Only simple ownership is supported. The list of candidate features includes the input feature and all descendants of the selected feature, for example, children and grandchildren, and so forth. After the software determines the candidate features, the user can select any subset of those features for editing. 
These are the editing operations the user can perform:
Edit Attributes Common to All the Features in the Set
The [edit function](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8kKN_gfuZi_1jYbWJc_pvQ) of the Edit Related Features command lets the user edit specified attributes common to all selected features. Thus, the set of available common attributes must come from components that are common in the set of features to be edited. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256021) Attributes are not common simply because they have the same name and type. They must exist as fields on components common to all the features in the edit set. 
The common attributes are displayed in Feature Explorer where the user can supply one or more values to apply to all the selected features. There are special Bulk Edit dialog tabs that must be defined in metadata to perform this operation. 
Repeating components are supported as long as they appear on vertical dialog tabs. The edits of the user are applied to each existing record in the repeating component. 
Relate the Set to Another Graphic Feature
The [relate function](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HlSMGagXFwXx9tenAigB8Q) of the command allows the user to choose a graphic feature to which all selected features are to be related. When a user clicks Relate, they are prompted to select a graphic feature on the map. The only features eligible for selection are those to which all selected features can be related. Once a feature is selected on the map, the user interface of the command establishes the ownership relationship with each of the selected features. The software performs attribute validation on each pair of related features. Each feature selected in the user interface is validated against the graphic feature that was selected on the map. The relate function is available only if there are one or more common ownership relationships for all of the selected features. These other ownership relationships must be different than the original ownership instance used to determine the list of related features presented in the user interface.   
|  Example A card is nongraphically owned by a shelf, as well as graphically owned by a vault splice of a building. If the nongraphic ownership relationship is used to determine the list of related features presented in the user interface, then only the graphic ownership relationship can be established by the relate function.   |  
| --- |  
Delete the Set
The [delete function](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/27UI3eck4OO~G2OfBZX1Tg) of the Edit Related Features command deletes all selected features and any children of the selected features, regardless of whether the children were selected in the user interface.   
|  Example A rack that contains several shelves is selected, but none of the shelves themselves are selected. The shelves are still deleted. The confirmation dialog indicates if more features are going to be deleted than were actually selected. During delete processing, all ownership relationships to the deleted features are removed.   |  
| --- |  
Only simple ownership relationships are removed. Therefore, features defined for bulk edit operations (G3E_FEATURE.G3E_BULKEDIT = Yes (1) should be only those that participate in an instance of simple ownership. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256021) No other relationship type is removed as a result of the delete. For example, if a deleted feature is also part of the connectivity model, the feature to which it is connected still references the deleted feature. If the related data are master data, no validation errors appear when posting these deletions. 
Edit Related Features Metadata
These tables are associated with the Edit Related Features command: 
  * G3E_FEATURE
The [G3E_FEATURE.G3E_BULKEDIT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) field identifies which features can participate in bulk edit operations. A value of Yes (1) indicates the feature can be bulk edited by the Edit Related Features command. A value of No (0) indicates the feature cannot be bulk edited by the Edit Related Features command. This flag applies to the input feature only. It is not applied to the features owned by the input feature. 
  * G3E_DIALOG and G3E_DIALOGTAB
You must define dialog tabs for bulk-edit scenarios with the following settings:
    * Set [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw) to Bulk Edit. 
    * Set [G3E_DIALOGTAB.G3E_ORIENTATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ) to V, indicating a vertical dialog tab. Only vertical dialog tabs are supported for Bulk Edit definitions. 
To edit multiple feature types at the same time (FNOs), define a dialog tab for each FNO so that they share the same G3E_DTNO. A common dialog is one that includes attributes from a component that the features have in common. 
Think about which fields you want your users to be able to bulk edit. The attributes you show in a Bulk Edit scenario are likely a subset of the attributes seen in a simple Edit Feature scenario. A unique identifier is one example of an attribute that should not appear on a Bulk Edit tab definition. 


Post Processing Procedures
Functional interfaces do not execute during the Edit Related Feature command. However, a post-process procedure is invoked after an Edit or Relate operation. In this post processing procedure, you can implement your own business rules required for such edits. When this procedure is called, all edit or relationship operations have been saved in the database, and you have an opportunity to apply other business rules within the same transaction. 
The procedure interface is stubbed in the G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG. It is delivered in the \GTechnology\PLSQL\LTT\PostProcessPkg.sql file. You can supply your implementation there. If you construct an IN clause in your processing, you may need to break the FID list into smaller blocks due to Oracle limitations. 
procedure PostProcessBulkEdit (
FNOList in G3E_CommonUtils.tFNOList,
FIDList in G3E_CommonUtils.tFIDList
); 
FNOList is a table with one field, defined as Number (5).
FIDList is a table with one field, defined as Number (10).
These two tables have the same number of rows. The first row in the FNOList table corresponds to the first row in the FIDList table. The second row in the FNOList table corresponds to the second row in the FIDList table, and so forth.

##### Move Related Features
The [Move Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vheVbbre4pJkujiEba9h3w) command moves a selected feature along with the features that are related to it. This command does not activate the relationship software because it is specifically intended to maintain the current relationships. The following is a general workflow for the Move Related Features command: 
  1. The user selects the feature (active feature) and invokes the Move Related Features command. 
  2. The command finds all the features that are related to the active feature through connectivity or ownership relationships. 
  3. The command presents the active feature with all its related features in a dialog. From there, the user chooses which features to include in the move. 
  4. When the user selects the features and clicks OK, the relationship [triggering components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdplkN_TMHDZadA0mNAHjg) of the active feature and the related feature or features are put in dynamics. 
  5. The command prompts the user to select a location for the move.
  6. The user clicks somewhere on the map view.
If the triggering component of the related feature is a point, the command moves the related component with respect to the triggering components of the active component. 
If the triggering component of the related feature is a line, the command stretches the line by moving the endpoint of the line that is closest to the active feature. The non-triggering components are not shown in dynamics. They are moved with respect to that feature's triggering component. 
If the triggering component is an area, the command modifies the begin/endpoint of the polygon. This has the effect of modifying the shape of the polygon. 
  7. The label components are moved to the same relative position with respect to the triggering component of that feature. 
  8. The label components are rotated to make them parallel to the triggering component if the label was parallel to the triggering component before the move. 


How Move Related Features Works—Diagrams
These diagrams show how the Move Related Features command works. 
The first diagram shows a pole owning two conductors and a transformer. The relationship-triggering component for the linear is the line component: for the pole feature, it is the pole symbol; for the transformer, it is the transformer symbol. When the user selects the pole and invokes Move Related Features, the command moves the pole to the new position. The pole label is moved to the new location, keeping the same relative position with the pole symbol. The transformer moves with respect to the pole symbol. The line component, being the relationship-triggering component, is stretched. The label components are also moved with respect to their respective triggering components within the features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260998)
The second diagram shows a primary conductor (PC1) connected to conductor PC2, transformers XFMR1 and XFMR2, and Pole1 and Pole2. Pole1 owns XFMR1, and Pole2 owns XFMR2. PC2 is connected to PC3, Pole2, Pole3, and XFMR2. The user selects PC1, and invokes Move Related Features. The diagram shows the move after Move Related Features is complete. The point features are moved and the linear features are stretched. Also, the label components of the linear features are moved with respect to the linear feature. The labels are rotated because they were parallel to the line before move. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260998)
The third diagram shows a Site that owns a primary conductor (PC1). The primary conductor (PC1) is connected to Fuse 1 and Fuse 2. The user selects PC1, and invokes Move Related Features. The diagram shows the move after Move Related Features is complete. The Fuse and Conductor features are moved, and the begin/endpoint of the polygon is moved, which stretches the site (area) feature. In this case, the area feature behaves like a line. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260998)
Move Related Features Metadata
The only metadata specific to the Move Related Features command is the [MoveRelatedRepeatingLocTol](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table. This value associates labels with linear components when repeating components of the linear exist within the related feature. 
Handling Z-Values
The command changes the z-values of the geometries participating in the move only under these circumstances: 
  * The administrator has enabled 3-D support in the database metadata.
  * The user presses the Shift key when clicking to accept the location of the feature(s).
  * The point has been moved in 2-D space.

[Placement and Edit Commands](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYpQa6kBxyn3HyDzRUxajA)

##### New Component
[New Component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3K66~xWZPy2POUz_rvqXPA) lets the user add missing, optional, and/or repeating graphic components to an existing feature. It is a specialized tool for quick generation of graphic components. The following is a general workflow for the New Component command: 
  1. The user clicks on a feature for component addition.
  2. The user is presented with a list of components and component configurations, repeating components, and any nonrepeating components that have not been placed based on the following criteria: 


  * Component configurations are added to the list only if all the components within a configuration can be placed based on their definition of repeating and how many instances of the component already exists. The [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) field determines whether a component is repeating or nonrepeating. 
  * Derived components, [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DERIVEDFROMCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) = 1, are excluded from the list. 
  * The component names displayed in the list are defined in [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). 
  * Detail components are not listed if the detail component's G3E_CNO appears in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO field of a geographic component. See [How Placement Works Based on the Active Map Window](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MrDAKCAz0fN4KhIE~yfd7g). 
  * The list of components is displayed in ascending order based on the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) value. 


  1. The user selects one or more components and/or component configurations from the list.
  2. The user clicks OK to begin placement of the selected items. The components are placed in the order defined by G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_ORDINAL. 
  3. As the user digitizes the component, relationships are established when the component is a triggering component of the relationship as defined in the respective relationship tables G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO field. 
  4. When digitization of this component is complete, the [placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) for any derived components are started. After the user places all the derived components for the first component, the placement technique for the next selected component is started. This process continues until all selected components are digitized. 
  5. The command is finished and is terminated.


New Component can only operate against individual features. A user cannot add components to a placement configuration. New Component works solely from the feature description in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table, even if the selected feature was placed as part of a placement configuration defined in [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ). 
New Component Metadata
New Component uses the same placement metadata as Edit Feature except for the attribute dialog boxes, because these dialog boxes are not available during New Component processing. For details on how to define placement metadata, see the [Edit Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/d4albsW8_6OdtwDpC4mKXg) and [New Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JUbUryqlV~NrkxTa1~50UQ) commands.

##### New Feature
The New Feature control allows a user to [identify a feature](http://www.) or a predefined set of features (a configuration) from a list and start digitizing the selected feature or features. 
The New Feature control is a toolbar that can be [docked or floating](javascript:;). It always remembers its position on the screen and the position is persisted even if you exit the application. The features displayed in the tree view of the control are defined in metadata. The tree structure can have several levels that logically group features. 
After the user chooses a feature or placement configuration from the control, a new instance of the feature or configuration is created and initialized with default attribute values. The user completes the feature or configuration by digitizing needed graphic components and specifying attribute values. 
Because there is only one New Feature control for each data set, you use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jFXGGj6Okzub1tAkZoFYlg) to update the [G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CER72g2Ys4bpQ9~jNI78Ng) metadata table and create the list of features for all users of a data set. This diagram shows the metadata structure for defining features and placement configurations for placement. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256040)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256040) [Publish metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8mZ26z5s1FoQIYb~qO7CmQ) after you create or make changes to the New Feature control. 
To support user workflows and to enable one-click placement, the New Feature control is accompanied by a [Placement Shortcut](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uEcsPoEGzpk30H_xXF1RlQ) bar. The Placement Shortcut bar allows the user to define a set of frequently placed items that are available at all times when placement is logically possible. 
The G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION.G3E_ICONORDINAL field [identifies the icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xGgxn7TZS~Le32Qi7DBg6w) to be used in the New Feature control and Placement Shortcut toolbar. This number is a 1-based index into the icon resource file specified in the PlacementSelectionIconDRXFile parameter in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table. The default file name is PlacementIcons.DRX. 
The following are also required to configure New Feature:
  * [Graphic components tab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0ty9o5qn8MoLl0c25buTHw)
  * [Attribute dialog tabs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/a9IuHmWBr90wvsjdhK~akQ)
  * [Feature relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PA3nsdBDE~bGs2_t540rBg)
  * [Storing graphics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iYsvs4I6gOXUWcX90Ubkvw)
  * [Detail](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/m4kxjUyA22umXrLUTwBVcw) and [alternate geographic components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xeF5peebSrlF9D43aPs2Mw)
  * [Refreshable components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q_91dE1cdaNG4ihSskaT4A)

##### SelectZ
The [Select Z command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AB0nLxY3mxVCN0zmftUltQ) sets the Active Z value from the Z values of existing geometry. 
When the command is active, the Z value(s) of the mouse cursor’s position display in the tooltip and change as the mouse is moved. If the mouse cursor is over empty space, nothing is displayed. 
  * To use the Select Z Command:


  1. Click ![SelectZ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/338258) or press a predetermined keyboard shortcut. 
  2. Move the mouse cursor over the geometry until the Active Z Update tooltip displays the target Z value. 
  3. Click the left mouse button. The Active Z field is updated to the new value, and the feature placement or edit operation resumes.

##### Z-Lock
The Z-Lock command sets the Active Z to the Z of the last placed/modified vertex and locks the field until Z-Lock is turned off. Element Z mode is not available while Z-Lock is on. Z-Lock is available during feature placement or edit operations. This mode overrides the Active Z and Element Z rules. When Z-Lock is exited the previous Active Z is restored to the field. 
When the user clicks Z-Lock or presses F6: 
  * The Active-Z field is set to the Z value of the last-placed vertex. 
  * The Active-Z field is disabled. 


The following Construction Aids and Edit Tool and Edit Geometry operations support the Z-Lock command:   
|  Construction Aids  |  Edit Tool and Edit Geometry  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Freehand  |  Move Component and Vertex  |  
|  Offset  |  Continue Geometry and Add Vertex  |  
|  Intersection  |  Trim  |  
|  Perpendicular  |  Extend to Point  |  
|  Arc  |  Extend to Line  |  
|  Project Orthogonal New Baseline  |  Extend by Key-In Distance  |  
|  Project Orthogonal Current Baseline  |   |  
|  BiRadial  |   |  
|  Point Distance Along Linear  |   |  
|  Point by Distance and Angle  |   |  
|  Midpoint  |   |  
|  Orthogonal  |   |

#### Placement Configurations

##### Adding a Placement Configuration Using Metadata Explorer
You can use Metadata Explorer to add a [placement configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly0oRFTHG1UNGrc60ApgVQ) to define logical groups of features and/or components used to drive the placement commands. 
A placement configuration contains a row for each unique FNO/FINDEX/CNO combination within the configuration you are defining. Typically, all the required graphic and attribute components are included in the configuration. 
You can accelerate component placement by using [silent placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GzV5EH6F0CeRfiAfTZS7Ag).   
|  Example A user can interactively place the switch gear box, but the first switch is placed using a silent technique, offsetting its location from the start of the switch gear box itself. From there, the first bus is placed offset from the switch, and the second switch is placed relative to the end of the first bus, and so on. After the user places the switch gear box, the remaining components are automatically placed using silent placement techniques.   |  
| --- |  
  * Before adding a placement configuration:


  1. You must be connected to a database for which you have administrative privileges.
  2. Define each component in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table before adding it to the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table. 


  * To add a placement configuration:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Placement > Placement Configurations node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259381), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  3. Populate the new row in the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table:
    1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a unique descriptive name for the placement configuration.
Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259381) to see the name in the Metadata Explorer tree view. This is the placement configuration name users see in the NetWorks Core New Feature control. 
    2. Select a feature and a component for the placement configuration from the G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO fields. 
    3. In the G3E_PINO field, select the placement technique for this placement configuration.
    4. If the placement technique has arguments, click the Ellipsis in the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT field. 
The [Interface Argument Editor](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ) dialog box appears. 
    5. Type values for the arguments, and click OK. 
    6. In the G3E_FEATUREINDEX field, type the feature index number. This number is 1 unless the feature exists more than one time in a configuration. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/oj6xPuMW5fT7CYLWsmscTA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=abc319f9e1d64446&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
    7. Type or select values to complete the row definition.
    8. Click OK. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259381) to commit the changes to the database. 
This adds a row to the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table.
  5. Refresh the metadata edits:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259381). 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Placement Selection under Placement & Edit. 
    3. Click OK. 
  6. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259381) to refresh the display in Metadata Explorer.

##### Placement Configuration Metadata
[Placement configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly0oRFTHG1UNGrc60ApgVQ) are defined in the [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ) table. This table is used to group features and their components together to form a placement configuration. Each placement configuration has a unique number in the G3E_PCNO field. Each configuration needs a descriptive username defined in G3E_USERNAME. This name is displayed in the New Feature control. You can use [Metadata Explorer to define a placement configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yyG2ZP60k5hq2jqdS3wFiQ). 
If you are defining a more complex placement configuration that consists of multiple instances of the same feature, for example a switch gear box with multiple switches and busses inside it, identify which instances of the switches and busses are to be placed and when 
Example  
|  G3E_PCNO  |  G3E_USERNAME   |  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_CNO   |  G3E_FEATUREINDEX  |  G3E_REQUIRED   |  G3E_REPEATING  |  G3E_AUTOREPEAT   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Switch Gear Box   |  987  |  123   |  1  |  1   |  1  |  1   |  
|  1  |  Switch Gear Box   |  987  |  123   |  2  |  1   |  1  |  1   |  
|  1  |  Switch Gear Box   |  987  |  123   |  3  |  1   |  1  |  1   |  
|  1  |  Switch Gear Box   |  987  |  456   |  1  |  1   |  1  |  0   |  
|  1  |  Switch Gear Box   |  987  |  456   |  2  |  1   |  1  |  0   |  
In this example:
  * There is one placement configuration called "Switch Gear Box." This configuration defines how a Switch Gear Box feature (FNO 987) is to be placed. 
  * The Switch Gear Box feature is composed of a switch (CNO 123) and a bus (CNO 456).
  * Because, there are three switches and two busses to be placed, there are three sets of switch components with G3E_FEATUREINDEX values of 1, 2, and 3, and two sets of bus components with G3E_FEATUREINDEX values of 1 and 2. 
  * All rows in the G3E_REQUIRED column are set to Yes (1). This means that each component is placed automatically. Setting G3E_REQUIRED on a component within a placement configuration does not override the definition of the component within the feature, nor does it affect feature validation. It simply drives the automatic placement functionality. If G3E_REQUIRED is not explicitly set in this table, it assumes the value from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REQUIRED for this FNO/CNO combination. 
  * G3E_REPEATING controls whether a component can repeat within a placement configuration. Set G3E_REPEATING to No (0) to denote a nonrepeating component; or set it to Yes (1) to denote a repeating component. A repeating component can have one or more instances. Setting G3E_REPEATING in this table does not override the definition of the component within the feature, nor does it affect feature validation. If G3E_REPEATING is not explicitly set in this table, it assumes the value from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING for this FNO/CNO combination. 
  * Set G3E_AUTOREPEAT controls whether a component can autorepeat within a placement configuration. Set G3E_AUTOREPEAT to Yes (1) to mark individual components within a placement configuration as auto-repeating. This setting causes placement to loop when executing the placement technique for this component, creating multiple instances of that component. Auto-repeat continues until the user presses SHIFT+ESC, at which point placement moves on to the next component within the configuration. You can set auto-repeat only on components that are marked as repeating in G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION. This diagram shows the metadata structure for relationships between placement configurations and feature definitions: 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259386)
After you define the graphic components for the configuration, define the placement dialog tabs for the sets of attributes that define this configuration. These dialog tabs are defined in a similar manner to the dialog tabs used during New Feature and Edit Feature. The G3E_TYPE of these dialog tabs should be the name of the configuration itself, as specified in G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_USERNAME. Whether defining a configuration containing several features or a specialized feature type, you can set the tab attribute defaults to define a placement configuration for a very specific need. This lets you create configurations to place common facilities such as a 40foot wooden pole versus a 60-foot concrete pole. 
  * To define a placement configuration:


  1. Define each component in the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) table. 
  2. [Add the placement configuration to the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yyG2ZP60k5hq2jqdS3wFiQ). 
  3. [Add the placement configuration to the New Feature tree](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jFXGGj6Okzub1tAkZoFYlg).

#### Refreshable Components
Graphic components can appear on the Graphic Components tab as well as on various attribute dialog tabs within feature placement. For example, the cable section type and the cable section geometry can be stored on the same component. This component appears on an attribute dialog to allow editing of the cable section type attribute, and it appears on the Graphic Components tab to allow digitization of the cable section. When this situation arises, keep the component instances on these various tabs synchronized. 
Refreshable Components Metadata
The attribute dialog boxes notify the Graphic Components tab when the user creates or deletes an attribute record on a component instance or edits an attribute value that has a functional interface defined for it. The attribute dialog box tabs must also be notified when a graphic component is added or deleted from the Graphic Components tab. The affected attribute dialog boxes update to reflect the latest addition or deletion. The Graphic Components tab updates its Active column to show the additions or deletions made to the component on the attribute dialog box tabs. To keep the instances synchronized on all tabs in which they appear and to avoid extraneous refreshes (causing performance degradation), set the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REFRESH](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) flag to Yes (1). 
This diagram shows the metadata structure for describing graphic components.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260995)

#### Relating Features During Placement
When a user places a component, the placement technique and any [relationship services](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e2tt5qpeYNY9MM7Wm73iAw) defined for this component are initiated. The relationship services establish relationships between features. While the user digitizes the active component, the relationship services search for candidate features and establish relationships when the correct conditions are met. However, placement does not require relationships to be established before saving the feature. The relationship mapping in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/19xFJqi2WdZ~OXlIOWc1Hg) table tells placement which relationships to process for each component.
