[Add Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDLhzjJQSDupgERtBVPE4w)
[Edit Feature Relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ObsaXyKUGM~B6vch_6Macw)

#### Validating Z Coordinates
Invalid Z-values are not used in calculations or displayed in PickQuick dialog boxes or tooltips. Conversely, Z-values are not tested when they are added to the Geometry tab of Feature Explorer. Z-values are tested under any of the following conditions: 
  * The user enters a new Active Z value in the Active Z
  * The Active Z-value from a saved work space is tested when the work space is opened. 
  * Enable Element Z calculation is clicked and a user snaps to an existing geometry during a placement or edit operation. 
  * Enable Element Z calculation is clicked and the user selects a construction aid that calculates an interpolated Z value (Midpoint, Intersection, Extend to Line, and so on) 
  * The user starts the Select Z command and hovers over an existing geometry. 
  * A Public API sets the Active Z- value.


If a Z-value is found to be invalid, one of the following happens:
  * The user is informed (in the case of the Active Z
  * An error is generated (in the case of API)
  * The DefaultZ value defined in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER is used (in the case of calculations). 
If there is no DefaultZ field in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table, then 0 is used.


A Z value is considered valid by the following rules:
  * The Z-value equals the DefaultZ value defined in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table.
  * The Z-value is within the MinZ and MaxZ range defined in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table. If these fields do not exist, then all Z-values are considered valid. The following table explains. 

  
|  MinZ  |  MaxZ  |  Result  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  NONE  |  Defined  |  Z-value must be less than or equal to MaxZ to be considered valid.  |  
|  Defined  |  NONE  |  Z-value must be greater than or equal to MinZ to be considered valid.  |  
|  Defined  |  Defined  |  Z-value must be greater than or equal to MinZ and less than or equal to MaxZ to be considered valid.   |  
|  NONE  |  NONE  |  All Z-values are valid.  |  
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/649365) Geometries that contain out of range Z-values do not stop the [data publishing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw) process.

### Features

#### Assemblies

##### Assembly Model
In an assembly model, you can define an assembly or a subassembly. Both must have a simple ownership relationship. 
This diagram shows a switch gear that contains various electric devices: a switch, a fuse, and a bus. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256025)
Assembly Component
One component of an assembly facility controls the placement of the child facilities. This is designated as the assembly component. 
To place the assembly component, use one of the three [assembly placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) (Assembly IPT, Assembly Rectangle IPT, and Assembly Rectangle By 2 Points IPT) to place a geographic or a detail component. The child facilities are placed, scaled, and rotated relative to this component. If you use a detail component to control placement of child facilites, designate it as the subassembly component. In this case, the geographic components of the cataloged assembly are placed relative to the primary geographic component. 
Subassembly Components
Subassembly components add subassemblies to an assembly. To place a subassembly component, use one of the [subassembly placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) (SubAssembly IPT, SubAssembly Rectangle IPT, and SubAssembly Rectangle By 2 Points IPT ). A subassembly component is [required](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256025) and can be [repeating](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256025). The geometry or attribute of this component is never actually placed but triggers the subassembly placement technique. The subassembly component can be a geographic or detail component. The child facilities are placed, scaled, and rotated relative to this component. If you use a detail component to control placement of child facilites, designate it as the subassembly component. In this case, the geographic components of the cataloged assembly are placed relative to the primary geographic component. 
Component that must be placed on the map for a feature to be valid.
A feature component that can occur more than once on a feature instance; for example, a street name that appears several places along a street.

##### Generating the Catalog Tables
After you have finished installing and setting up the G3E_DEEPCOPY procedure, you can generate catalog tables for storing catalog entries. Catalog tables are identical to the model tables (LTT views) and are generated automatically when you run the database procedure G3E_DeepCopy.CreateCatalog located in the\GTechnology\PLSQL\LTT folder. 
These tables are identical to the model tables with the following exceptions:
  * The table name is prefixed with E$.
  * No constraints, triggers, and so forth, are applied to the catalog tables. The procedure assumes that all business-rule logic is applied to the model tables, and that these rules guarantee the data before being copied into the catalog. 
  * The owner of the data model owns the catalog tables. Do not grant users access to these tables. All access is through the stored procedures and the Save to Catalog command. 
  * Changes in the data model require you to drop all catalog tables and recreate the catalog. If you have a great deal of data existing in the catalog, you can alter the catalog tables the same way that you alter model tables. 


  * To generate catalog tables:


You must execute the procedure as the owner of the source tables for the catalog. The only parameter for this procedure is the feature number of the highest-level parent in the ownership tree that you need to store in the catalog. 
  1. Execute the CreateCatalog program.   
|  Example If the large item you need to store is an Equipment Line Up, feature number 14000, type the following in an SQL editor:  SQL> execute G3E_DeepCopy.CreateCatalog(14000);  |  
| --- |  
  2. Execute the CreateCatalog procedure several times if your data model contains disjointed ownership trees. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259969) Each time you execute the CreateCatalog procedure, it creates tables for each component of the feature specified and all of its children. Children are defined using the relationship specified in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER value [CatalogRelationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ). If errors occur, the program logs the errors and continues.

##### Generating the Equipment Catalog Entries
After you have generated the tables, you can generate equipment catalog entries and test them. 
  * To generate equipment catalog entries:


  1. Populate the G3E_ATTRIBUTE column [G3E_CATALOGCOPYVALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) to test the use of the catalog during this process. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259971) This column provides an override to a simple copy operation when data are copied from the catalog (E$ tables) to the model. The most common use of this column is to Null columns that are not appropriate when copied. The content of this column is any valid select list entry to be substituted in place of the column. 
  2. Validate your entries by executing the contents of this column in an SQL editor:
SQL> select<G3E_CatalogCopyValue contents>from dual;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259971) Make sure you have all the necessary quotes (') on fixed-text values. For example, if the phrase "User entry required" is needed for a column when it is copied from the catalog, the G3E_CATALOGCOPYVALUE must include the quotes so that this phase is a valid select list parameter. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259971) If you defined a database function for the copy operation, inputs to the function are limited to the columns defined within this table. 
  3. Publish the metadata after you generate it to create the optimized tables required by Deep Copy.

##### Installing G3E_DEEPCOPY
Before you can use the Save to Catalog command to create predefined assemblies of features and to store them in the database as an equipment catalog, install and set up the package G3E_DEEPCOPY. 
  * To install G3E_DEEPCOPY:


  1. Use an SQL editor to install and run the package G3E_DEEPCOPY:
SQL> @\GTechnolgy\plsql\ltt\g3e_deepcopy.sql;
SQL> @\GTechnolgy\plsql\ltt\prvtg3e_deepcopy.plb;
  2. Populate the CatalogRelationship and CatalogSchemaOwner columns in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table. 
  3. Use an SQL editor to turn on logging during the initial creation of the catalog.
SQL> execute G3E_DeepCopy.SetLogLevel(1);
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259967) This analysis log is only enabled during the session in which it is executed. 
  4. To help database designers and others understand the extensions of the equipment catalog definition (or the G3E_DEEPCOPY interpretation of your metadata definition), execute the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> set long 500  
Select G3E_DEEPCOPY.TreeSQL(14001) from dual;

##### Maintaining the Equipment Catalog
You can test your metadata definition and catalog creation directly from SQL; however, this approach does not allow users to use saved items. Maintenance of the catalog index [(CATALOGENTRYLIST)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zopkmXfDZUayy8mN_ais2w) is performed by the Save to Catalog command. You can use the Catalog Feature Identifier (G3E_IDENTIFIER) and Catalog Feature Number (G3E_FNO) as input to the assembly placement techniques. Reference this table in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
New identifiers are not created when you copy features from the model into the catalog. The examples in this topic start the definition of an equipment line, manually generate two racks, and add a third rack that is identical to the first. 
Use an SQL editor to execute the statements in the steps below.
  * To maintain the equipment catalog using SQL statements:


  1. Query information about a tree of equipment in the model:
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.tracemodel(<Feature number>,<g3e_fid>);
The results of this process are stored in the table RTREETRACE, which is generated as a part of [creating the catalog tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nXeFlMu8xybwrZ8QpAAn3g). A view called TreeTraceResults is also created on this table for your active session. 
  2. To view the results of the above procedure, execute the following:
SQL> select * from TreeTraceResults order by seq_no;
The results of this query indicate that feature 14000 (Equipment Line Up) owns two 14400 (Racks), and that one of the 14400 (Racks) owns a 14600 (Shelf).   
|  SEQ_NO  |  G3E_FNO   |  G3E_FID  |  G3E_PARENT   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  121  |  14000  |  6639  |   |  
|  122  |  14400  |  6640  |  6639  |  
|  123  |  14600  |  6641  |  6640  |  
|  124  |  14400  |  6642  |  6639  |  
  3. Store a feature in the catalog:
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.copytocatalog(<Feature number>,<g3e_fid>);
  4. Using the data from the previous trace as a guide, execute the following statement to store one of the racks in the catalog: 
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.copytocatalog (14400,6640);
  5. To see the results of this procedure, query the catalog tables, or execute the Trace Catalog procedure which has the same syntax as the Trace Model procedure. 
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.tracecatalog(<Feature number>,<g3e_fid>);
The results of this procedure are stored the same as the model trace. This is the result of the catalog trace, copytocatalog:   
|  SEQ_NO  |  G3E_FNO   |  G3E_FID  |  G3E_PARENT   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  149  |  14400  |  6640  |   |  
|  150  |  14600  |  6641  |  6640  |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259975) Because all Deep Copy functions are performed as part of the current transaction, you can undo this copy operation using a standard Oracle rollback statement. 
  6. Remove items from the catalog:
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.deletefromcatalog(<Feature number>,<g3e_fid>);
  7. Copy entries from catalog tables to the model:
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.copytomodel(<Catalog feature number>,<Catalog g3e_fid>,<Model owning feature number>,<Model owning g3e_fid>);
  8. Add another rack to the Equipment Line Up listed in the first model trace in Step 1: 
SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.copytomodel(14400,6640,14000,6639);
Here are the results if you trace the model as described above.  
|  SEQ_NO  |  G3E_FNO   |  G3E_FID  |  G3E_PARENT   |

SQL> execute g3e_deepcopy.copytocatalog(14000,6639);
This request generates the following error: 
execute g3e_deepcopy.copytocatalog(14000,6639);  
ORA-20001: Specified feature or a related feature to the specified feature has been previously copied to the catalog  
ORA-06512: at "GCOMMS.G3E_DEEPCOPY", line 194  
ORA-06512: at line 2
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259975) To avoid this error, always delete the cataloged feature trees, and then copy the tree back from the catalog before generating the next catalog entry.

##### Saving to the Equipment Catalog
You can generate predefined assemblies in the database using standard [placement and editing techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly0oRFTHG1UNGrc60ApgVQ) and using the Add Related Feature command. After you generate the assembly, the Save To Catalog command lets you copy it from the database to the equipment catalog. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256032) Before you can use the Save to Catalog command, install and set up G3E_DEEPCOPY in your database to create the catalog into which you save the equipment assemblies. 
  * To save to the equipment catalog:


  1. [Select the feature](http://www.) you want to add to the equipment catalog. 
  2. From the Administrative menu, select Save to Catalog. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256032)
  3. Enter a description for the equipment.
  4. Click Add. 
  5. Optional: If the equipment description already exists in the catalog, a message appears asking you if you want to replace it. 
  6. Click OK to delete the old assembly name and save the new one. 


  * To remove an entry from the equipment catalog:


  1. Do not select a feature in the map view.
  2. From the Administrative menu, select Save to Catalog. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256032)
  3. On the Save to Catalog dialog box, select the feature or catalog entry you want to delete. 
  4. Click Delete.

##### Setting Up the Assembly Model and Equipment Catalog
You can store [predefined assemblies](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XSFGrKZNVyzM_4Pbf5E5IA) of features in the database using the [Save to Catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RYJriFHhlSXe6gVhAFCtoQ) command. After these features are stored in the catalog, the user can access them using the [Add Related Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yGHl~jR_3R42zeO46VPsGg) command. 
Following is the workflow for using assemblies and the equipment catalog in your data model: 
  * To set up an assembly model and equipment catalog:


  1. Install the equipment catalog:
    1. [Install the G3E_DEEPCOPY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~i9wss5uLmdKF0Eb4YIY3Q) package. 
    2. Generate the [catalog tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nXeFlMu8xybwrZ8QpAAn3g). 
    3. Generate the [equipment catalog entries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tbghqU0SDHG7fMU1JG8k2A). 
    4. This updates [G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_CATALOGCOPYVALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw). 
    5. Create the [CATALOGENTRYLIST](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zopkmXfDZUayy8mN_ais2w) table. 
    6. This table contains the index of the catalog entries. The Save to Catalog command [maintains this table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VeieGapR8j1gRguCKznIwQ). 
    7. The Catalog Feature Identifier (G3E_IDENTIFIER) and Catalog Feature Number (G3E_FNO field) can be used as input to the assembly placement techniques. 
    8. Reference this table in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
  2. Define the assembly feature:
    1. [Associate an assembly placement technique with the assembly component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA) and optionally a subassembly placement technique with the subassembly component. 
    2. Because you do not have specific assembly configurations at this point, leave the arguments to the assembly placement technique blank. 
  3. Define a specific assembly configuration:
    1. [Place the parent assembly](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oS_xK~vm5902oe3XP3Y50w) feature in the map view. 
    2. Place the child features of the assembly feature. Normal ownership processing establishes the parent-child relationship. 
  4. Save to the equipment catalog:
    1. Identify the parent assembly feature.
    2. Run the [Save to Catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RYJriFHhlSXe6gVhAFCtoQ) command to save the specific assembly configuration to the equipment catalog. 
  5. Optional:  [Define assembly placement configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yyG2ZP60k5hq2jqdS3wFiQ). This updates the [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ) table. After you define specific assembly configurations and save them to the equipment catalog, you can use them as arguments to the assembly placement techniques. 
  6. Optional: If you define a placement configuration, [add it to the placement selection controls](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jFXGGj6Okzub1tAkZoFYlg) to update the [G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CER72g2Ys4bpQ9~jNI78Ng) table. 
    1. Also, [define dialog boxes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MPR6mJuKwSz8gPPCFL27Ag) to be used with the placement configurations. Use the placement configuration name in the G3E_TYPE field. 
  7. Optional:  [Define the post process procedure](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GgUa7j1DZagSZ6O13Omj4w), such as validation triggers to be fired when a user places an assembly feature, to be called from the Add Related Features command. Use the g3e_deepcopypostprocess.sql and g3e_deepcopypostprocessexample.sql in \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt. 
  8. [Maintain your equipment catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VeieGapR8j1gRguCKznIwQ).

##### Validating Features Placed from an Equipment Catalog
To validate features placed from an equipment catalog, you must define procedures or triggers. 
The Add Related Feature command does not automatically set the [subsetting attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/i3pWvOjTRdBMjaEs4pPmsA). However, you can define and implement a database procedure to set this attribute. See \GTechnology\PLSQL\LTT\G3E_DeepCopyPostProcessExample.sql for an example of how to implement this database procedure. The sample emulates the [Simple Copy Relationship Attribute interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sy9iZejet2kjZVL5QuFXoA). You must configure metadata to copy the subsetting attibute value from the parent to the children features placed using the Add Related Features command. 
You can define and implement a trigger for features placed using the assembly placement techniques. See the \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt\G3E_CatalogCopyValueTriggerExample.sql for an example of how to implement this trigger. This sample also emulates the Simple Copy Relationship Attribute interface.

#### Feature Definitions

##### Basic Feature Modeling
You begin defining a feature by creating a row in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for every component that belongs to or defines the feature. You must already have populated the [G3E_FEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7a4EXbGwHfWoLcplgecKEA) table and the [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261360) You should never include [synthesized components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BHztsPXCkqRWc8ufJn_Dkg) or [special views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/G1XMMOhqsk1xDWq0Z0x5PQ) in this relationship definition. Either one of these components occurring in the feature-component definition can introduce errors in placement and edit operations.   |  
| --- |  
These are the key G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT fields:
  * G3E_FCNO—A unique key for the table. Can be populated with the sequence, G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT_SEQ. It is never used as a foreign key to another metadata table. 
  * G3E_FNO—The feature you are defining. 
  * G3E_CNO—The component included in the feature. 
  * G3E_REQUIRED and G3E_REPEATING—The [cardinality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261360) of the components within the feature. A [component's cardinality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7a4EXbGwHfWoLcplgecKEA) can be different when it is used in different features. 
The nunber of cardinal (basic) members in a set. In tables, cardinality is the number of rows. 
NetWorks Core does not explicitly define a cardinality, such as the number of occurrences allowed.   
|  Example You can define a transformer bank feature with a required/repeating transformer component, but you cannot limit the number of occurrences to three per feature through the metadata definition. You can, however, enforce such cardinality in either a [database trigger](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdplkN_TMHDZadA0mNAHjg) or a [functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg).   |  
| --- |  
The feature validation process checks the cardinality of the components based on the matrix. There is one exception to the required minimum-one-occurrence rule. If you specify an alternate component in the G3E_ALTERNATEREQUIREDCNO field, one or the other of the components must exist, but both are not required. This is particularly important when modeling a feature that may or may not have a detail representation. The value in this field is the component number of the other component that validation checks before failing the cardinality test. 
  * G3E_INSERTORDINAL and G3E_DELETEORDINAL
The order in which components are [inserted and deleted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6qZoTJ8kh0Egqi1EdbL74g) is very important to maintain relationships. The values in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w).G3E_DELETEORDINAL and G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_INSERTORDINAL control the order in which components are created, updated, or deleted.

##### Break Processing Fields
A break operation applies only to a linear feature, creating two new features by dividing the primary graphic component at some point. These metadata fields in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) control how the other components associated with the linear are assigned during a break operation: 
  * G3E_BREAKACTION
  * G3E_COMPONENTELIMINATION
  * G3E_COMPONENTASSIGNMENT
  * G3E_COMPONENTADJUSTMENT
  * G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE
  * G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO
  * G3E_RINO
  * G3E_RIARGGROUPNO


Related Topics
[Break Subsystem](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HEpZLsnCSeIIDG3qeKL5Yg)
[Break Subsystem Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SKsWyM4WVVlG4iTu~fqedg)

##### Component Insert and Delete Ordinals
NetWorks Core provides several mechanisms for populating attributes and building relationships in the client software. You can have database triggers that either populate or validate the feature's components. For triggers to be successful, you must know the order in which the components are created, updated, or deleted. The values in G3E_INSERTORDINAL and G3E_DELETEORDINAL control this order. The insert ordinal controls both the insert order and the update order. The delete ordinal controls the delete order. 
Define the ordinals so that the triggering component is inserted before the related component and so that the triggering component is deleted before the related component. [Metadata validation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDGAu21AUa_I~XZxIPvJzw) checks for the order and reports errors if the ordinals are defined in an improper order. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261352) An attribute component that contains label information is deleted before the graphic component that it describes. A graphic component with no label information could remain on the map if there is some problem that stops the deletion of the graphic component. 
In the edit scenario, the entire set of components might not be involved. However, additional components honor the applicable subset of the order specification when they are updated.

##### Creating and Editing Feature Definitions

###### Creating a Feature Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a feature, which adds a row to the G3E_FEATURE table. Then you associate the feature with the components and component configurations that comprise the feature. The components and component configurations must have been defined before you can associate features with them. 
  * To create a feature definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257891), or right-click and select Insert a new row. A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the feature. The G3E_FEATURE table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a name for the feature.
  4. In the G3E_PRIMARYATTRIBUTECNO field, pick a component that contains the significant attribute data for the feature from the drop-down list. 
  5. Select values for the following required fields: G3E_REPLACE, G3E_MERGE, G3E_BULKEDIT, G3E_EDITROLE, G3E_EDITRELATIONSHIPSROLE, G3E_SELECTROLE, G3E_DELETEROLE, and G3E_ADDRELATEDROLE. 
![GTAdmin_AddRelatedRoll](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/~Y6~fb5dxc4ZUwBg~1ALlg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=a664f788ab6f3cb1&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  6. Type or select values as needed in other fields to define the feature.
  7. To complete your feature definition, click OK. 
  8. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257891) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To associate a feature with a component or a component configuration:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Feature Components node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257891), or right-click and select Insert a new row. A grid appears in the content panel so you can configure the feature component relationship. The G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In the G3E_CNO field, select a component that you want to associate with the feature from the drop-down list. 
OR
In the G3E_CCNO field, select a component configuration that you want to associate with the feature. 
  4. Select or type values for the following required fields: G3E_REQUIRED, G3E_REPEATING, G3E_PINO, G3E_ORDINAL, G3E_INSERTORDINAL, and G3E_DELETEORDINAL. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257891)
  5. Type or select values as needed in other fields to define the feature component relationship.
  6. To complete your feature component definition, click OK. 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257891) to commit the changes to the database.

###### Deleting a Feature Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete a feature definition and an associated component or component configuration for a feature. Deleting a feature does not delete its components, although deleting all the components that make up a feature does delete the feature. 
  * To delete an associated component or component configuration for a feature:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Feature Components node. 
  2. Find and select the component or component configuration that you want to delete.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257897), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  4. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257897) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To delete a feature definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features node. 
  2. Find and select the feature definition you want to delete.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257897), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  4. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. The row in the G3E_FEATURE table and all the rows in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table for the feature are deleted. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257897) to commit the changes to the database.

###### Editing a Feature Definition in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to edit the components and component configurations for a feature definition. You can add components and component configurations to a feature definition, and you can also modify information about the feature. 
  * To edit a feature definition:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features node. 
  2. Find and select the feature definition you want to modify.
  3. In the content panel, edit the feature definition values you want to change.
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257895) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To edit an associated component or component configuration for a feature:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <connection name> > Features > <feature name> > Feature Components node. 
  2. Find and select the component or component configuration that you want to modify.
  3. In the content panel, edit the component or component configuration values you want to change. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257895) to commit the changes to the database.

##### External Interface Support Fields
Two of the fields associated with the feature definition are for external interface support. 
  * G3E_IMPORTFEATURENAME—Used to retain the association to the original data if the feature has been imported from a secondary connection and is still managed by the secondary connection. 
  * G3E_NAME—Available for a number of interfaces to other systems that need to exchange data. This field contains the name of the feature as it is known in the other system. Since NetWorks Core manages the feature by number, this additional field provides flexibility to store a name. 
G3E_NAME is used by the [STORMS interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/auyB5RmhpDOhQmPvHTX9sA). This is the STORMS feature class name for the level one keywords in the FACILITY group. G3E_NAME is also used by the [WMIS (Logica) interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/g9sQD9Auhkh5aDigQQrbPg). It maps to the CU_CATEGORY_CODE inside the CONSTRUCTION_UNIT table.

##### Feature Core Description Fields
The core description fields in the metadata tables must be populated for every type of feature. Here are some guidelines about these key fields: 
  * G3E_FNO—Feature number or identifier. It is part of the feature keys. Once assigned, do not change it. This value must be unique within the table. 
  * G3E_DCNO—[Data connection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) number. Associate the feature with the data connection that defines or stores the data. If the feature is originally from a secondary source but you now plan to manage it with NetWorks Core, associate it with the NetWorks Core data connection (development or production). However, if the data are only in the NetWorks Core database as reviewable data, associate the data connection number with the secondary connection. 
  * G3E_USERNAME—Descriptive name of the feature. It is presented to the user throughout the NetWorks Core application. The first place the user sees this value is in the placement selection or in relationship processing. Any format or content is allowed, but the value must be unique in the table. 
  * G3E_TOOLTI —Also a descriptive name for the feature data. If left null, the NetWorks Core software uses the feature username. 
  * G3E_NUMBEROFNODES—Applicable to any feature that participates in the [node-edge connectivity relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lVlHcmN8aYrqo9dkv2agMA). The allowable values are 0, 1, or 2. Zero is applicable to features that are not part of a connectivity relationship. The one or two values indicate the number of connection points available on the feature. NetWorks Core does not model more than two connection points for a single feature. 
  * G3E_DEFAULTNECONNECTIONTYPE—Applicable to any feature that participates in the node-edge connectivity relationship. Controls the initially selected connection type when the Node-Edge Connectivity dialog is displayed when placing or editing this feature. 
    * Tapped—“Connect on end” connection type initially selected
    * Inline—“Connect between two existing features” initially selected

##### Merge Processing Fields
Merge processing is essentially the opposite of break procssing. These metadata fields in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) allow the software to determine when a merge is allowed and how to process the components when creating one feature from two: 
  * G3E_MERGEMAXDISTANCE
  * G3E_MERGECOMMONPRECOND
  * G3E_MERGEPRECOND
  * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
  * G3E_MERGERINO
  * G3E_MERGERIARGGROUPNO

##### Placement and Edit Fields
These fields in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) are interpreted by the feature placement and edit commands, component addition commands, and the Edit Tool and Edit Geometry commands. 
  * G3E_ORDINAL—Controls the presentation of graphic components in the graphics tab of Feature Explorer. 
  * G3E_AUTOREPEAT, G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT, and G3E_DERIVEDFROMCNO—Related to the processing algorithm for placement. 
  * G3E_PINO and G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT—Define the way the geometry is generated. To understand how to populate these fields, see [Feature Placement and Edit Functionality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n_~E4ANbb0BKzWjJlwLt9w), [Placement Algorithm](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YY5WEAfiFC2VOvip1IxW6A), and the [New Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JUbUryqlV~NrkxTa1~50UQ) topics. 
  * G3E_REFRESH—A special indicator used during feature placement and edit operations. The symbolization of a particular component is usually based on multiple components of the feature. However, during placement, the default style is determined by the components that exist at the start of component placement. The components needed for the correct style choice may not yet exist because they are optional. By setting this Boolean value to Yes (1), you denote that the addition or deletion of a component should force the placement software to recalculate the attribute displays, symbology, and labels. The typical occasion to set this value to Yes (1) is when attributes from a graphic component are shown on a dialog tab. 
Additions or deletions of components through the attribute controls must be reflected on the Graphic Component display. To avoid extraneous refreshing, (a performance penalty), this property should be set to Yes (1) only in this case or when the addition of an attribute (or graphic) component generates a corresponding graphic (or attribute) component through a functional interface. The default is No (0). 
  * G3E_CCNO—Indicates a component configuration defined for placement within the feature. This field must match a value in [G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YHO9TgRk7Beh5fF22~iN_g).G3E_CCNO. Set this field to a non-null value only when a component configuration is to be specified as part of a feature. When this field is set to a non-null value, set the G3E_CNO field in this table to Null. If you are specifying an individual component instead of a component configuration, set G3E_CCNO to Null and G3E_CNO to a non-null value. See the [Component Configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nle~UWesm54Oz6c1lGFMQA) topic for more details. After component configurations are placed, they cannot be edited as a group. They are also not validated as a special unit. The standard cardinality rules for the components in the feature apply. 
  * G3E_REPLACE—Controls whether the component is copied to the new feature during a replace operation. The value must be zero or one and defaults to Yes (1), indicating that the component is copied during the replacement. Typically, history or audit components are not copied. For this property to be honored, set the G3E_FEATURE.G3E_REPLACE value to Yes (1).

##### Required-Repeating Components
G3E_REQUIRED and G3E_REPEATING work together to determine if a component is required or optional and if a user can place one or more instances of a component.   
|  Attribute Setting  |  G3E_REQUIRED = No (0)  |  G3E_REQUIRED = Yes (1)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_REPEATING = No (0)  |  Optional, nonrepeating—Can create at most one instance of this component  |  Required, nonrepeating—Must create one and only one instance of this component  |  
|  G3E_REPEATING = Yes (1)  |  Optional, repeating—Can create one or more instances of this component  |  Required, repeating—Must create at least one component and can create more than one component   |

##### Special Processing Fields
These values associated with the feature definition are for specialized processing. 
  * G3E_REPLACE—Controls the Replace Feature command. 
  * G3E_MERGE—Controls the Merge Feature command. 
  * G3E_CLASSIFICATIONANO—Classification attribute number. An attribute within one of the components of the feature that contains the type or classification of the feature. This is used by the [attribute inheritance software](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ApHR51I4syRo4MVrpr5f4A) to provide the ability to inherit attribute values from like features.   
|  Example You can inherit from copper cable and fiber cable independently on new placements rather than from the last cable feature placed. You can omit this specification for features that have no type. However, if a type is specified and the software encounters a Null value, the data are treated as a particular type of the feature.   |  
| --- |  
This attribute should exist on a required component of the feature.
  * G3E_IDENTIFIERVIEW—A view used by Feature Explorer to achieve a more descriptive label rather than the feature name and identifier. This view should expose only the NetWorks Core key fields (minimally G3E_FID) and any fields needed by the label rule specified in the primary attribute component for the feature. 
This view defines the fields available to both the label rule processing and the label formatting and determines what graphic component, if any, Feature Explorer should use. The view also reduces the database queries required to retrieve each feature in the explorer relationship tree and produce its identifier.

##### Validating Features Using a Batch Process
You can use a batch process to validate the integrity of features outside of the NetWorks Core environment. When you execute this batch process, it writes the start and end system time, process ID, and program errors into a log file (BatchValidation.log) located in the system temporary folder (or c:/ if a system temporary folder is not defined). Each error contains a unique process ID (G3E_PROCESSID) per session to differentiate between validation sessions. 
The validation process exercises the Validate method of these interface objects defined in your model: 
  * IGTFunctional 
  * IGTRelationshipGeometry 
  * IGTRelationshipAttribute 


However, the validation process does not execute any IGTFeatureValidation methods.
In batch processing, feature transactions are not supported, and the following application objects are not available: 
  * IGTRelationshipService
  * IGTBreakLinearService
  * IGTFeatureExplorerService
  * IGTFeaturePlacementService
  * IGTMergeFeaturesService 
  * IGTMultiSectionCableService


  * To validate features using a batch process:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Batch Validation. 
OR
From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder and type BatchValidation.exe with the following command line parameters: 
Connection Configuration Name  
Login  
Password  
Feature Key Table Name  
Feature Table Name  
WHERE condition on the feature keys table 
This is the syntax:
BatchValidation.exe Config=<Configuration>;Username=<userID>;Password=<Password>;[KeyTable=<Feature Keys Table>;][FeatureTable=<Feature Table>;][where=<sql condition>;] [SAPSYSNUM=<SAP system No>; SAPLANG=<Language>; SAPUSERID=<SAP UserID>; SAPPASSWD=<SAP User Passwd>; SAPSYSNAME=<SAP System Name>; SAPCLIENT=<SAP Client No>; SAPAPPSRV=<SAP Server>; SAPGROUP=<SAP Environment(group)>;]   
|  Example Batchvalidation.exe Config=APPLDB; Username=appldb; Password=appldb; KeyTable=common_n; FeatureTable=COMMON_N; where G3E_FID between 5065349 and 5067722 and G3E_FNO=315;  |  
| --- |  
If you do not enter command line parameters, the Batch Validation dialog box appears. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259059)
User name—Login 
Password—Password 
Configuration—NetWorks Core connection configuration name 
Feature table—Name of the table to get feature recordset. All features with a component in this table are validated. If this field is left blank, the software uses COMMON_N as the feature table name. Example entries for this field are POLE_N, BUS_N, and DCG_POLE_S. 
Feature keys table—Name of the table where feature ID (G3E_FID) keys are stored. If this field is left blank, the software uses [DATACONVFIDKEYS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rccLC~tqhXis3m5qO_gSxg) as the feature keys table name. If you create a new feature keys table, add the name of the table to [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
WHERE condition on feature keys table—SQL condition for a filter on the feature keys table to get all or a subset of the records. If this field is left blank, the software gets all records in the feature keys table. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259059)
     * You may need to run Batch Validation multiple times under the following circumstances:
       * If the features to be validated do not have at least one component as part of the feature table specified in the command line. Specify a different feature table in the command line each time you run Batch Validation. 
       * If the filter (WHERE condition) does not include all of the features to be validated. Change the filter each time you run Batch Validation. 
     * B$ tables are not allowable input tables.
  2. Type the batch validation parameters.
  3. Click OK. 
The software validates the features identified in the feature keys table. Any features that fail validation are logged into an error log table ([G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6VoYc8OGQufN8mFMjCJ_qQ)). Add the name of this table to G3E_DATASUPPORT to create a synonym for it. Go to Step 6. 
OR
If the configuration you selected supports SAP, the Batch Validation — SAP Login dialog box displays. All SAP parameters are required. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259059)
User name—SAP login 
Password—SAP password 
System number—System number. Defaults to 0 on the dialog box, but is required on the command line. 
System name—The name of the system 
Client—SAP client 
Language—Language. Defaults to EN (English) on the dialog box, but is required on the command line. 
Application server—Server IP address (for example, abc.xyz.com). 
Environment (Group name)—Group 
  4. Type the SAP parameters. If you do not enter all SAP parameters, the system logs the syntax information in the log file and exits. 
  5. Click OK. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259059) The software validates the features identified in the feature keys table. Any features that fail validation are logged into an error log table (G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR). For each time batch validation is run, the error log shows the date and time of validation (start and end times), system date, and process ID. When batch validation is complete, a message box appears telling you that batch validation is finished. 
  6. Use the error log to generate validation error reports.

#### Feature-Component Relationships
After you define features and components, you define how they are related. The relationship is specified in the Feature- Component table, [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). The feature number (G3E_FNO) and component number (G3E_CNO) are the keys that build the relationship. 
G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT provides the following information:
  * Defines the characteristics of components for validation and placement.
  * Identifies special processing characteristics of the components related to the break and merge of linear features. 
  * Defines a relationship, the components that comprise the feature.
  * Defines rules about [cardinality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261365) and behavior. These rules are validated during the post operation for long-term transaction features. 
The nunber of cardinal (basic) members in a set. In tables, cardinality is the number of rows.

#### Nongraphic Features
A feature with no geometry component or representation is used typically for two reasons. Either the feature has no true physical location, or its size cannot be represented, which means it is too small or its volume is too great for a small geographic space; for example, cards or racks in a communications network. Trying to draw and lay out these items would make the management of the geographic maps nearly impossible. 
Some operations are limited when a feature has no geometry. The main limitation is that nongraphic data cannot be displayed or highlighted in the map window. To review or edit a nongraphic feature, it must be displayed in Feature Explorer. To do this, you can display in Feature Explorer a feature that references the nongraphic feature, and select the nongraphic feature from the grid. Or you can display a nongraphic feature through Find or as the result of a query. You must send the results of queries to a data grid and select from the grid to display the nongraphic feature in Feature Explorer.

### Graphics Presentation

#### Ad Hoc Backdrop Display

##### Ad Hoc Backdrop Display in Export
When Export is supported in your data model, a CAD file format can be any number of named configurations. Named configurations have style mappings in metadata and use the Export interface. Each named configuration can have multiple style mappings for each format. When the MicroStation and AutoCAD files are configured in this way, they do not use the special legend entry for display. In this case, a CAD file is read by Export or GDAL/Teigha logic and published to a DDC file for attachment. The published DDC file is stored in the work space folder. The DDC file formats are created through the Export[](javascript:;). The generated files can be used by other clients. 
Export definitions support the following file formats: 
  * AutoCAD
  * MicroStation
  * ArcView
  * MapInfo
  * KML
  * KMZ
  * GeoJSON 


Systems without Export definitions support native MicroStation and AutoCAD formats for ad hoc backdrop display. 
MicroStation now supports both V7 and V8 formats. Provide proper version of Seed file and Cell library file based on the Version selected in the following parameters dialog. Incorrect input files will cause export failure. 
![MicroStationUpdate](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/CEHFK5POdsx2eu6l2APthA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=338b41384734cd06&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

##### Ad Hoc Backdrop Display Metadata
To attach the native format (MicroStation and AutoCAD) and DDC files, you must have the following items in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) metadata table: 
  * AutoCADFeatureNumber
  * AutoCADComponentNumber
  * AutoCADBackdropStyleRule
  * AutoCADBackdropTempStyleRule
  * AttachDDCDisplayScaleRange


To attach the named configurations (with Export configuration) files, you must populate the following metadata tables: 
  * [G3E_EXPORTIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/w_3GBp6CrR6DNa_wkMw6Ug)
  * [G3E_EXPORTFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fgoa~LZSw7ue4wnXnguX0A)
  * [G3E_IMPORTLIST](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Q0Re32nlBfOvgWDHFp2QYw)


If these tables are not defined in the database, use \GTechnology\PLSQL\MetaData\Optional\NetExport\MMCreateNetExportTables.plb to create them, and use \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateNetExportMetadata.sql to populate the required records in G3E_EXPORTIFACE and G3E_EXPORTFORMAT tables. After you create and populate these tables, populate G3E_IMPORTLIST with the file formats you want to suppport.

##### Attaching MicroStation Files for Ad Hoc Backdrop Display
You can use MicroStation files as your ad hoc backdrop display. If your MicroStation files contain text or symbols that use [MicroStation fonts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6sXDMBHAktACjEAhMxEPcA) stored in a resource files (.rsc files), add the full path or folder path of the .rsc file in the \GTechnology\Program\gt.ini file. You can store MicroStation font files or line style files on the local computer or access them across the network. 
Also, if your MicroStation files contain user-defined line styles, add the full path or folder path of the line styles resource file in the gt.ini file. You can have multiple MicroStation font .rsc file. You provide a complete path to the file or files or to the folder where the .rsc files are stored. The last file in the list has the highest priority when multiple file paths are specified in the gt.ini file for the DgnFontRscFile or DgnLineStyleRscFile parameters. 
MicroStation user-defined line styles are stored in line style libraries. A line style consists of a name and one or more line style components. Line style components are stroke patterns, point symbols, and compound components (a combination of point symbols and stroke patterns). 
If the fonts referenced by the MicroStation file are not found in the .rsc files in the location specified in the gt.ini file, or if no location has been specified in the gt.ini file, the \GTechnology\Program\tt_dgn.map file can be used. The tt_dgn.map file maps MicroStation font numbers to TrueType fonts. You can edit the font numbers, add fonts, or delete fonts in this file. If the software finds a MicroStation font number in the tt_dgn.map file, it uses the corresponding TrueType font. If the software does not find the required MicroStation font in the gt.ini file or in the tt_dgn.map file, it uses a default built-in MicroStation font. 
To enable font mapping, you tell NetWorks Core to use the tt_dgn.map file by adding UseDgnFontMapping=1 to the \GTechnology\Program\gt.ini file. To disable font mapping, you remove that parameter from the gt.ini file or you set UseDgnFontMapping=0. 
Performance
You can improve performance for attaching a MicroStation design file to NetWorks Core by changing the UseDGNCacheRegen parameter in the GT.ini file to a value of 0. When caching is disabled, a display list is created during the first draw, and then subsequent draws are performed using the data in this display list, which gives a significant speed improvement 
If you set UseDGNCacheRegen to 1, cache of the elements that are visible in the current the map window are regenerated for each zoom/pan/rotation operation causing performance to be reduced. 
However, if you set the UseDGNCacheRegen parameter to 1 in the gt.ini file and the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\DGNDefaultLineStyleNumPatterns registry key to a value greater than 10000, you see better display results when you use the Attach Vector command. 
To see better results when rotating a NetWorks Core map in a Plot window, set the UseDGNCacheRegen parameter to 1 and set theLinetypeScaleMultiplier parameter to an appropriate setting to provide good display results. Also, set the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\DGNDefaultLineStyleNumPatterns registry key to a value that provides good display results. 
The table below defines the parameters in the gt.ini file:   
|  Parameter Example  |  Applies to  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  DgnFontRscFile=\\\ServerName\  
MicroStationResourceFiles\fonts.rsc; D:/MicroStationfiles   |  MicroStation fonts  |  
|  DgnLineStyleRscFile=\\\ServerName\  
MicrostatioResourceFiles\lstyle.rsc;   
D:/MicroStationfiles   |  MicroStation user-defined line styles  |  
|  ShapePath=\\\ServerName\AutoCADFontFiles  |  AutoCAD user-defined line styles  |  
|  UseDgnFontMapping=0  |  MicroStation fonts  |  
|  UseDgnCacheRegen=0  |  Design file cache regeneration.   |  
|  LinetypeScaleMultiplier  |  Set the factor to display the Dash..Gap..Dot sequence of default MicroStation line styles and patterns without stretching.  The default is 7.2  |

##### Configuring a Font Resource File Using MicroStation Version 7
The example below uses MicroStation Version 7 to configure your font resource file (.rsc). The MicroStation tool is Font Installer. The resulting .rsc files are used in NetWorks Core workflows to attach DGN files or to export DGN files. Both MicroStation Version 7 and MicroStation Version 8 are supported. 
  * To configure a font resource file:


  1. In [G3E_FONTNAME.G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KkSHDKALPAaJHyESmRqk9Q), find the list of fonts used in your data model. 
  2. Copy the fonts needed for attach DGN to NetWorks Core and export to DGN workflows (TrueTtype, .rsc type, and so forth) from C:\Windows\Fonts to a local folder, for example, C:\temp\fonts. 
  3. Use MicroStation Version 7 to open any saved design file.
  4. From the Utilities menu, select Install Fonts. 
![UtilitiesMenu](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/ETQHe5zYXXTKWLJpJXI0sw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=8d2205e39ca02201&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  5. Click Open (under the Source File box) and navigate to the folder to which you copied the fonts in Step 2. 
![FontInstallerOpenSourceFile](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/PPZmJ_6P_Tmi14WgnoYxjg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=eca98602437623ff&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  6. If your fonts are True Type fonts, in the Type list, select True Type(*.tt*).
  7. Select one or more True Type fonts, and click Add to add them to the File List. 
  8. Click Done after adding all the fonts you need. 
![OpenSourceFontFile](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/yysikXawSCfaFwnZ7jj_LA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=fe6c2371b89b4528&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
The Font Installer dialog box redisplays. 
![NewOrOpenFontRscFile](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/W9ogVrOSNCiFjazs8ImIxQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=f87bba3f51b96a57&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  9. Click New (Under the Destination File box)
This example workflow creates a new font resource file; however, you can add these fonts to an existing font resource fille. Typically, the font resource file for NetWorks Core is font.rsc and is stored in the \Bentley\Workspace\standards\symb folder.
![CreateFontLibrary](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/hYj5Gka6rjB7DW2gMoLsEQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=fb8aa6acc47a53e6&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  10. Type font.rsc in the Files box, and click OK. 
  11. In the Source File list, highlight the font you are adding to the font.rsc file. Click Copy to copy the required font into the new font.rsc file. To remove a file from the font.rsc file, click Remove. Click Done when you are finished. 
![CopyFontToDestinationRSCFile](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/0I2sCv5Xf94t6Rgn_zdiBg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=1e0cf934847d30ef&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  12. Copy the new file to Intergraph\GTechnology\templates\DesignFiles so NetWorks Core can read the file. 
  13. Copy the new file to C:\Bentley\Workspace\system\symb so MicroStation can read the file.

##### Publishing CAD Files as DDC Files for Ad Hoc Backdrop Display

###### Limitations and Considerations for Publishing a CAD File to a DDC File
  * Each published CAD file, when attached to a map window, uses a maximum of 8MB of virtual space: 
    * 4MB for the DDC file where the layer information resides
    * 4MB for the CDT file that actually includes the data 
To limit the user from rendering too much CAD data, you can set the AttachDDCDisplayScaleRange parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER. This parameter specifies the display scale range for a DDC file attached using Attach Vector Data. The format for this parameter is: <Minimum Display Scale>:<Maximum Display Scale>. The DDC file content is displayed only when the display scale is between the <Minimum Display Scale> and <Maximum Display Scale> values. The default value for this parameter is 1:10000. The user can use the display scale ON/OFF to control the display of the file content both at the file and layer level. 
  * Ensure that the default style rule specified by the AutoCADBackdropStyleRule parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER includes at least a style per geometry type filter. The associated style IDs should point to a valid style related to the geometry type. For example, if the filter is "G3E_GEOMETRYTYPE = ‘PolygonGeometry’", the style ID associated with this should be of the type area style. Ensure that the G3E_OFFSET value is not populated for the line styles (in the G3E_LINESTYLE table) because it could cause problems for the vectorized text where the simplified geometries are shifted due to the offset value. 
  * As part of the CAD element to NetWorks Core geometry translation, the text elements are also vectorized to generate simplified geometries (line, arc, polyline, or polygon). This is done to maintain better fidelity for font types (SHAPE or RSC) not supported by NetWorks Core. If the text elements are associated with these unsupported font types, ensure that the GT.ini file is updated to include the RSC or SHAPE file paths before the publish process is called. If the fonts are embedded within the CAD file itself, there is no need to modify the GT.ini file. Because the vectorization of a text string can lead to multiple discreet geometries, a geometry collection object is created, which lets the user to highlight it as a single geometry when locate is turned on. 
  * For the default styles, ensure that the stroke pattern value is not a customized or stroked line style. 
  * In CAD, the line weight is view-scale independent.
For example, in MicroStation the line weight is defined in pixels. Regardless of the zoom scale, the line weight is always rendered as n number of pixels. Unless the styles are defined as scale independent, the converted point scale value for the line width might not appear the same as in CAD. 
  * NetWorks Core cannot support styling per element within a geometry collection. 
For example, in MicroStation an element in a cell can have different colors per element. During publish, NetWorks Core extracts the color from the cell's header element and assigns that as the color of the collection geometry. 
  * In addition to the generated G3E key fields and style data, the intermediate layer recordset includes the fields listed in the table below. These fields can be used in the style rule filters to file tune for better display fidelity. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/481791) Most of these fields are available when the style information captured from the CAD elements is applied on the default styles using style overrides. The final style is written as a style BLOB into the published DDC that is later consumed by the display pathway. In short, you can use these fields to define your style rules, but they may not be available in the final published layer recordset.   
|  Field Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  LAYERNAME  |  Specifies the value of the layer/level to which this CAD element belongs  |  
|  BLOCKNAME  |  Specifies the name of the BLOCK or CELL element  |  
|  FONTNAME  |  Specifies the name of the text font. In case of SHAPE or RSC fonts, this field includes the base name of the font file   |  
|  TEXTSTRING  |  Specifies the text string  |  
|  G3E_GEOMETRYTYPE  |  Specifies the geometry type. Valid values are: PolylineGeometry PolygonGeometry OrientedPointGeometry TextPointGeometry CollectionGeometry  |  
  * Customized line styles and stroke patterns are not supported.
  * Fill hatch patterns are not supported.
  * Multileader objects are not supported.
  * The solid fill state of a polygon is determined by the dynamic view setting in CAD; therefore, the fill is not honored by the rendering of the published CAD file. 
  * The Z-value is not captured from the CAD environment into the published DDC files.
  * After you attach an ad hoc DDC file to a version 10.2 SP1 workspace or later, that workspace cannot be opened using any previous NetWorks Core version.

#### Configuring Export to CAD

##### Configuring Export to a MicroStation Design File

###### Color Table for Export to a MicroStation Design File
Colors in NetWorks Core are specified using a long integer that contains the intensity values for the red, green, and blue color components (RGB). Colors in design files are specified using a byte value that serves as an index into a 255-element color table of RGB color values. 
As NetWorks Core components are converted to design file format, their DGN color number is set by comparing the component's style color value to the color values in the seed file's color table. The resulting DGN element is assigned the color number of the best matching color. 
To achieve the best color fidelity between NetWorks Core and the exported design file file, a site-specific color table should be attached to any site-specific seed file. The color table should contain all of the colors that are used in the your style definition metadata. You can use SQL queries into the style tables to determine the color numbers of styles in your database.

###### Configuring TTF Fonts for MicroStation Version 8
NetWorks Core point features and labels use PointSyle and TextStyle, respectively. For point symbols, you can specify the font name in the [G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KkSHDKALPAaJHyESmRqk9Q) table. Similarly, you can specify the font name for labels in the G3E_TEXTSTYLE table. In addition to the font name, for labels you can specify bold and italic flags in the [G3E_TEXTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0yRaZQ44AZMeTckCYodWaQ) table. While exporting point and text data to MicroStation V8 or V7, you have to include these fonts in the resource file (.rsc). 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/561684) MicroStation V7 does not support TrueType (TTF) fonts, so TTFs are not honored while exporting to MicroStation V7. 
Point Symbols
While exporting from NetWorks Core to a MicroStation V8 design file, the software searches for the fonts for point symbols in the RSC file. If the software does not find the required point symbol font in the RSC file, the software searches for it in the Windows TrueType (TTF) font (\Windows\Fonts). 
Text
Similarly, while exporting from NetWorks Core to a MicroStation V8 design file, the software searches in the RSC file for fonts to display labels. If the software does not find the required text font in the RSC file, the software searches for it in the in Windows TTF font (\Windows\Fonts). A text style is created with the TTF font name along with text attributes (bold and italic), and this newly created text style is applied to text labels. 
Use the following table for guidance to set fonts for exporting to MicroStation V7 or V8 and for the SaveAsDGN API.   
|  MicroStation V8  |  MicroStation V7  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 
  * If the font is in the RSC file, its font id is applied.
  * If the font is not in the RSC and is in Windows fonts (TTF font), the font is used to export. 
  * If the font is not in both the RSC file and in Windows fonts, font id 0 is applied.

 | 
  * If the font is in the RSC file, its font id is applied.
  * If font is not in the RSC file, font id 0 is applied.

 |  
Examples

  * Pole Miscellaneous Label is configured with the Arial Black TTF font. The bold flag is set on this label in the G3E_TEXTSTYLE table.

###### Export to a MicroStation Design File Metadata
The G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP metadata table determines which NetWorks Core components are exported to which MicroStation design file levels. NetWorks Core delivers this table so that you can use the functionality without further configuration. However, you can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to modify the level mapping, including adding and removing rows from the table. 
The mapping is done depending of whether you are exporting to MicroStation version 7 or version 8: 
  * For version 7, the mapping is done by [level number](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/083yC2fPUrKvBg6PSHO_FQ) and is limited to levels 1 through 59. 
  * For version 8, the mapping is done by [level name](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PdmXHQBNOvUfwcbozDljDQ) and the number of levels is not limited. Level mapping applies to "normal" features and components (including synthesized components), that is, features and components listed in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION table. 


For other elements such as redlines, schematics, and queries and traces, graphics are mapped by default either to a specific version 7 level or to a named version 8 level rather than based on metadata specification. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260961) If G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP does not exist in your metadata tables, the Export to CAD command automatically performs a default level mapping. However, if the table does exist and a specific component is either not listed in it or is listed but G3E_V7LEVEL or G3E_V8LEVEL (depending on your target version) field is not populated, the component is not exported. 
The G3E_UDLS and G3E_MICROSTATIONSTYLENAME rows in the [G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_FP8Es~ev0K7MCcH9086w) table must be populated for user-defined line styles to export properly to MicroStation version 7 and version 8. 
  * To define new features and components to export to a MicroStation design file:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Design File Mapping > Export to DGN node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260961), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  3. Populate the new row in the [G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/t5gF9a9N77AGcH6U9Av0SA) table. 
    1. In the G3E_FNO field, select the feature you want to export.
    2. In the G3E_CNO field, select the component you want to export for that feature.
    3. In the G3E_V7LEVEL field, type the level number (1-59) to which you want to feature to be exported, or in the G3E_V8LEVEL field, type the level name to which you want to feature to be exported. 
Example  
|  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_CNO   |  G3E_V7LEVEL  |  G3E_V8LEVEL   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  100  |  101   |  1  |  "Primary"   |  
|  100  |  102   |  1  |  "Primary"   |  
|  200  |  201   |  2  |  "Secondary"   |  
    4. Click OK. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260961) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To modify existing features and components to export to a MicroStation design file:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Design File Mapping > Export to DGN > <Feature Name> > Components > <Component Name> node. 
  2. Modify the fields as required.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260961) to commit the changes to the database.
