###### Export to a MicroStation Design File Performance Considerations
The amount of data in the map window and the number of legend entries displayed at the current view scale affects performance of the export to a MicroStation design file functionality in the Export to CAD command. Performance depends on the following: 
  * Number of legend entries exported
  * Amount of data displayed by each legend entry
  * Distribution of the legend entry data within the legend


Performance is degraded more when large amounts of data are in legend entries with lower display priority. For example, with all other factors being equal and assuming a large number of legend entries (more than 150), a map window with thousands of elements in the lowest display priority legend entry (the bottommost legend entry) take longer to export than a map window with thousands of elements in the highest display priority legend entry (the topmost legend entry). A map window with one legend entry turned on (or on by scale) exports faster than a map window with the same number of elements displayed, but distributed over many legend entries. 
Another factor affecting performance of Export to CAD is the version of MicroStation to which you are exporting the map window. Using Export to CAD, exporting data to MicroStation version 7 format is faster than using the command to export to MicroStation version 8 format. For very large amounts of data (more than 5,000 components exported), exporting to version 7 can take 50-60 percent less time than exporting to version 8. 
Related Topic
[Configuring Export to CAD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n~vogNNoea5w75MB9nIhgg)

###### Mapping to MicroStation Version 7 Levels
By default, each NetWorks Core component is mapped to a MicroStation version 7 level from 1 through 59. Levels 60-63 are reserved for export to CAD. When the G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP is populated for export to version 7, all components for a specific feature are exported to the same level and each feature is exported to a different level. If more than 59 features are being exported, the features wrap levels. For example, the sixtieth feature is put on the same level as the first feature. 
In a design file output from version 7, the feature tooltip displays as the type of element plus the level that the element is on. For example, if you hover over a line, the tooltip displays Line String [Level <level number>]. If you hover over any text or any symbols (pole, transformer, and so forth), Text[Level <level number>] appears. NetWorks Core exports point components as Text. 
The following table describes the reserved levels:  
|  Level Number  |  Reserved For  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  60  |  Attached redline data. Attached redline data including plot window redlines.  |  
|  61  |  Queries and traces.  |  
|  62  |  Schematics.  |  
|  63  |  Other data. Any data that is not a component view and is not a query, trace, schematic, or redline, for example, ad hoc attached DDC data or temporary geometry.  Includes raster images that represent objects embedded in a plot window.  |

###### Mapping to MicroStation Version 8 Levels
For MicroStation version 8, all the components of a specific NetWorks Core feature are exported to the same level. The level name is the same as the feature name (as defined in G3E_FEATURE.G3E_USERNAME). MicroStation version 8 level names have [some restrictions on the characters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/t5gF9a9N77AGcH6U9Av0SA) you can include in the name. If a G3E_V8LEVEL value that contains any of the restricted characters is encountered, the restricted characters are replaced by the underscore (_) character. For example, My*Level is converted to My_Level and My&Other*Level is converted to My_Other_Level. When the G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP is initially populated during metadata upgrade, any restricted characters that exist in G3E_FEATURE.G3E_USERNAME is changed to the underscore (_) character before populating the G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP.G3E_V8LEVEL. 
The version 8 seed file does not have to have the level names defined. If a level name does not already exist in the version 8 file, it is created during the Export to CAD process. In a design file output from version 8, the feature tooltip displays the level name from G3E_EXPTODGNLEVELMAP. For example, if you hover over a linear feature, the tooltip displays as Linestring [Conductor]. 
The following types of data are exported to their own named levels for MicroStation version 8: 
  * Each query and trace
  * Each schematic network
  * Each attached redline file
  * Each temporary geometry
  * Each ad hoc attached DDC vector file.

###### NetWorks Core Stroke Pattern to MicroStation Style Mapping
NetWorks Core stroke patterns are mapped to the six standard MicroStation styles. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/273948) MicroStation style 0 corresponds to solid. 
The following mapping is used:  
|  NetWorks Core Stroke Pattern  |  MicroStation Style  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Dotted   |  1(Dotted)  |  
|  Medium Dashed   |  2(Medium Dashed)  |  
|  Long Dashed   |  3(Long Dashed)  |  
|  Dot Dashed  |  4(Dot Dashed)  |  
|  Short Dashed   |  5(Short Dashed)  |  
|  Dashed Dot Dot   |  6(Dashed Dot Dot)  |  
|  Long Dash Dot Dot Dot  |  6(Dashed Dot Dot)  |  
|  Long Dash Dot   |  6(Dashed Dot Dot)  |  
|  Long Dash Dot Dot  |  6(Dashed Dot Dot)  |  
|  Long Dash Short Dash   |  7(Long Dash Short Dash)  |  
|  Medium Dash Short Dash  |  7(Long Dash Short Dash)  |  
|  Long Dash Medium Dash  |  7(Long Dash Short Dash)  |  
|  Long Dash Medium Dash Medium Dash  |  7(Long Dash Short Dash)  |  
For a given stroke pattern instance, the dash gap values may vary by up to 10 percent from the NetWorks Core default stroke pattern dash gap values and still be considered a match. If a stroke pattern cannot be matched to a NetWorks Core default stroke pattern, the line is exported as a solid line.

###### Seed Files, Line Style Resource Files, and Font Resource Files for Export to a MicroStation Design File
So that you can use the export to a MicroStation design file functionality of the Export to CAD command without further configuration, NetWorks Core delivers seed2dv7.dgn, seed3dv7.dgn, seed2v8.dgn, seed3dv8.dgn, lstyle.rsc and font.rsc in the \GTechnology\Templates\DesignFiles folder. If you create customized seed files, font resource files, or linestyle resource files, place them at the location you specify in your [FileUNCPaths.xml](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vy3dclvmNhGSudMj5ZLOug) file. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260941) For export to MicroStation, if the font.rsc file is not defined in the FileUNCPaths.xml file under the <ExportToDgn> section, for example, 
<Resource>
<Location Type="UNC">C:\XYZABC\DesignFiles\resources</Location>
</Resource>
NetViewer Client uses the font.rsc file by default from the C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GTechnology\Program location. 
Designer/Analyst uses the font.rsc file by default from C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GTechnology\templates\DesignFiles. 
where the installation directory is C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GTechnology. 
To achieve the best text and symbol display fidelity between NetWorks Core and the exported design file, you can use the [MicroStation Font Installe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6sXDMBHAktACjEAhMxEPcA)r to import specific True Type fonts into a font resource file. You can use the NetWorks Core font.rsc file or any other font resource file as a basis.

[Configuring Export to CAD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n~vogNNoea5w75MB9nIhgg)

###### Symbology Supported By Export to a MicroStation Design File
NetWorks Core supports the following styles for export to a MicroStation design file: 
  * Color. An index into DGN file's [color table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CsDgwcdUKYNVhdCSqy70qg). 
  * Weight. A value between 0 and 31 that represents the width of the element.
To override the width of a NetWorks Core line style when exporting to MicroStation, type an override line weight in [G3E_LINESTYLE. G3E_MICROSTATIONOVERRIDEWEIGHT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b3vQwQ~YtLlgn5feW4cuvA) and republish metadata. 
  * Style.
    * G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE.G3E_UDLS = 0. 
A value between 0 and 7 that represents the standard DGN line styles, where 0 represents solid, and 1-7 represent the standard DGN dash/gap patterns. 
    * G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE.G3E_UDLS = 1.
The style specified in G3E_NORMALIZEDSTYLE.G3E_MICROSTATIONSTYLENAME is applied if provided in the resource file. If the style name is not supplied, a solid line style is applied. 
  * Fill color. Determines whether or not a closed shape is filled.
  * Font. The name of the font to apply to a text element.
  * Character. A single character and/or symbol within a font.
  * Text height and text width. Loosely correlates to True Type font size. Text height and text width is determined by the NetWorks Core style's font Size attribute, without taking display scale into account.

##### Configuring Export to an Export Format
Before you can use [Export to CAD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~Thp_tu3UDIGZXKmJ_Fl3w) to export a named configuration, Export[ must be installed and configured](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NjNjJtV52Q2gRb~v6IDx1g) for your site. You specify named configurations in metadata. On the Export to CAD dialog box, a named configuration displays after the native CAD formats. There can be multiple named configurations (style mappings) for each format supported by Export, for example AutoCADExport1 or AutoCADExport2. 
In addition to creating the named configurations, you specify component views to be exported for each defined named configuration. This relieves the user from preparation of the data to be exported, but the user can provide the exported data extent and overrides, if needed. Depending on the current view extent and the Display Control settings, the user may or may not be able to see the data to be exported in the map view. Named configurations of AutoCAD and MicroStation CAD format types use Export/Teigha logic for exporting. 
Named configurations are created in the G3E_EXPORTx table, and can be exported to the following formats: 
  * AutoCAD
  * MicroStation
  * MapInfo
  * ArcView
  * KML
  * KMZ
  * GeoJSON 


When the user selects File > Export to CAD, Export to CAD verifies that Export is configured by finding two entries in the G3E_ANALYSIS table for G3E_TYPE as "Net Export" with G3E_USERNAME as "Net Export" and "Export List". Export to CAD finds named configurations from G3E_EXPORTLIST.G3E_USERNAME. 
Export to CAD requires the Export Web, File, and Application Server information. The Export Configuration Wizard adds the Export Server name to the FileUNCPaths.xml file based on selections in the user interface of the wizard. If you manually configure the Export servers, you must manually create the following entries in the [FileUNCPaths.xml](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) file: 
<NetExport>
<ApplicationServer>
<Location Type="UNC">\\\ComputerName<\Location>
</ApplicationServer>
<FTPServer>
<Location Type="UNC">\\\ComputerName<\Location>
</FTPServer>
<WebFolder>
<Location Type="URL">http:\\\ComputerName\FileServerFolder<\Location>
</WebFolder>
<WebServer>
<Location Type="URL">http:\\\ComputerName\WebServerFolder<\Location>
</WebServer>
</NetExport>
Also, write access must be allowed on Export File Server to the owner of Export application service. 
If Export is configured to use secure HTTPS and FTPS protocols. FileUNCPaths.xml should look like this: 
<NetExport>
<ApplicationServer>
<Location Type="UNC">\\\ComputerName<\Location>
</ApplicationServer>
<FTPServer>
<Location Type="URL">ftps://ComputerName.domain.com<\Location>
</FTPServer>
<WebFolder>
<Location Type="URL">https://ComputerName.domain.com/FileServerFolder<\Location>
</WebFolder>
<WebServer>
<Location Type=”URL”>https://ComputerName.domain.com/WebServerFolder<\Location>
</WebServer>
</NetExport>
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260970) Both WebServer and WebFolder should use same security protocol, i.e. either both should be HTTPS or both should be HTTP. Mixed mode is not allowed. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260970) WebServer and FTP case supports mixed mode, i.e. none, either one, or both can be secure. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260970) The HTTPS URL should use the website name as provided in the Certificate “Issued To” section. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260970) While configuring HTTPS for Export, you have to manually edit FileUNC with the correct URL based on the certificate value.

##### Configuring Export to CAD Limitations
Export to CAD has some limitations for the export to AutoCAD and the export to MicroStation functionality. 
Export to AutoCAD Limitations
The following are limitations for the export to AutoCAD functionality:
  * AutoCAD supports only 256 colors, so the NetWorks Core color may not appear exactly the same. The RGB value of the NetWorks Core color is mapped to the closest available color palette entry. 
  * For a stroke pattern to appear correctly, it must be configured in the line type definition file; otherwise, it is defaulted to the CONTINUOUS (solid) line type. 
  * The text height is computed to exactly match the glyph displayed in NetWorks Core; however, due to the different rendering worlds, the text may appear a little larger. The difference may not be noticeable. 
  * The line spacing between individual lines of text in a multiline text may not appear the same between NetWorks Core and AutoCAD. 
  * For symbols, the size is computed based on the assumption that the symbol is drawn using the complete EM-square. In AutoCAD, the symbol may appear larger if it violates this assumption. 
  * For symbology overrides applied to either queries or traces, the stroke pattern may not appear correctly. This is because the symbology overrides do not adjust the stroke patterns based on the width of the line, causing the gaps to the filled by the end caps. This may cause the line to appear solid in NetWorks Core even when the associated stroke pattern is not solid. The export to AutoCAD functionality displays these lines using the original stroke pattern as long as it is configured in the line type definition file. 
  * The fill color and fill pattern are not supported.
  * Styles for text boxes are ignored.
  * Styles for text underlines are ignored.
  * Text and symbols are exported only if their origin is within the extents of the map window. The text or symbols are not clipped at the map window extents, which means that you get the complete text or symbol even if it crosses the map extent boundary. 
  * If a 3D AutoCAD file is generated, the line types or the line width does not appear correctly since they are both not supported by AutoCAD for 3D entities. The linear and areal entities display with a CONTINUOUS line type and the line width is defaulted to a thin line. 
  * Only BMP files and Excel spreadsheets inserted in the plot window export successfully for AutoCAD or MicroStation formats. It is not supported for GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, and ArcView SHP formats. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260945) Objects inserted in a plot window that are not BMP files or Excel spreadsheets (such as Visio files) do not export even though a message displays indicating a successful export. 


Export to MicroStation Limitations
The following are the limitations for the export to MicroStation functionality:
  * NetWorks Core supports RichTextFormat, Unicode, and plain text in GeoMedia TextPoint geometries. All three formats work in all known situations, except one. Exporting GeoMedia RichTextFormat TextPoint geometries is not guaranteed to work. 
  * Symbols within a stroke pattern are ignored unless you have configured user-defined line styles. 
  * Start and end symbols for linear geometry are ignored unless you have configured user-defined line styles. 
  * Nonzero offset values (for line styles) are ignored unless you have configured user-defined line styles. 
  * The symbology characteristics for a linear element being drawn by a composite line style are determined by the bottom-most style. That is, the line style that is drawn first by the composite line style. All other line styles within the composite line style are ignored. 
  * The constraints described under the Linear heading also apply to line styles used as the boundary style for an area. 
  * Hatch patterns specified on an area style are ignored
  * Symbol masking used in NetWorks Core is ignored. 
  * Styles for text boxes are ignored.
  * Text masking is ignored.
  * Styles for text underlines are ignored.
  * [Text justification](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ggFaiKt9NqW~WksePI7QZg) is ignored and [text alignment ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg)is preserved. 
  * Bold styles are ignored.
  * Italic styles are ignored.
  * Only BMP files and Excel spreadsheets inserted in the plot window export successfully for AutoCAD or MicroStation formats. It is not supported for GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, and ArcView SHP formats. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260945) Objects inserted in a plot window that are not BMP files or Excel spreadsheets (such as Visio files) do not export even though a message displays indicating a successful export. 
  * API limitations:
    * The SaveAsDGN method to export backdrop data has the following limitations:
      * Cell headers and Shared cells are exploded into individual elements while exporting.
      * Fonts included in the resource files are exported based on font id. So use the same resource file which is used to create the attached file during the export. 
      * Text nodes are exported as individual text elements.
      * Ellipse and elliptical arcs are not supported, so they are exported as circle and circular arcs respectively 
      * AutoCAD line styles should be defined in MicroStation resource files.

You can use Metadata Explorer to create a new scale-independent style for a line, a composite line style, a text style, or a point style or change an existing style from the default of scale dependent to make the style scale independent.

##### Converting Between Points and Ground Units
Typically, you know how large the symbols and text should appear on paper when plotted at a certain scale, so you need to work from this information to assign the right point size to text and symbols in your model. All sizes defined in the style objects represent the size on the screen at the specified display scale, not the size on the ground. The measured size when viewed, printed, or plotted matches your calculation only when viewed at the scale defined on your legend — the [nominal paper scale (NPS)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256657). In NetWorks Core, the symbols get bigger as you zoom in and smaller as you zoom out. 
The scale of a reduced earth model. The constant factor that multiplies all X,Y coordinates on the true-to-scale map to reduce it to the needed map scale. On a given map, the actual map scale is equal to the nominal map scale at the locations that have no scale distortion (for example, along the latitude of true scale). 
To calculate the number of points when you know the required ground size, use the following formula: 
P = (G * I * 72) / NPS
Where
P = points 
G = specified ground units 
I = number of inches per [ground unit](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256657)
Linear measurement system associated with your data or calculations. For example, feet, meters, or inches are common ground units. 
72 = fixed value since there are 72 points per inch 
NPS = nominal paper scale   
|  Example Determine the number of points to assign the symbol style to create a 50-foot symbol on paper at 1:5000 display scale.  P = (50 * 12 * 72) / 5000  And P = 8.64   |  
| --- |  
Before you begin to determine style point sizes, answer the following questions:
  * What is my style size in ground units?
  * What is my nominal paper scale?


From there, you can determine the appropriate number of points to assign to the style. The following is the formula for metric systems: 
P = (M * 100 * (1 / 2.54) * 72) / NPS
Where
P = points 
M = number of meters 
100 = centimeters per meter 
1 / 2.54 = inch per centimeters 
72 = points per inch 
NPS = nominal paper scale 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256657)
  * You cannot specify the size of symbols in ground units—for example, 90 feet.
  * The behavior for symbols, text, and line weight in NetWorks Core is to change the size with each zoom. They get bigger when you zoom in and smaller when you zoom out. 
  * The size of the symbol is specified in paper units points. One point equals 1/72 of an inch. 
  * Because the symbol changes size when you zoom in and out, you might wonder when your symbol is sized to your specifications. The symbol is the specified size when the display scale equals the Nominal Paper Scale. 
  * The anchor point or alignment of a text or symbol relative to the geographic location is not determined by information in the font itself. For symbols, you specify alignment in the style object. [You have nine options](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg). For text, you specify alignment in the geometry component's attribute fields. You have the same nine choices. 
  * You can expect to measure the plotted results within 0.01mm accuracy, but only when they are plotted at the defined paper scale. This tolerance is based on the point sizes you specify at the paper scale you specified. If you specified a line width of 18 points at 1200 paper scale, the line width should measure ¼ inch — plus or minus 0.01 mm. Any view adjustment either in or out from that scale changes the size of the plotted data. 
The granularity of your printer can affect your accuracy as well. You must also consider the quality and resolution of your printer. Does it have a draft option that is less crisp in its line drawing? Also, you can specify some rounding that adversely affects the accuracy of the measurement. If your calculations resulted in a determination that the point size should be 12.8572 and you specified 12.86, the measurement is less accurate (greater variation) than 0.01 mm.

##### Creating Connectivity Symbols in Metadata Explorer

You can adjust the display priorities of the legend entries associated with a work space legend. Before you define the work space legend priorities you must:

###### Enabling the Display Scale Status Checkbox
Use role assignment to control whether a user can change the display scale status to view all features regardless of the display scale specified. Assign the G3E_DisplayControlDisplayScaleEnabled role in [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_OBJECTCONTROL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) to users who need this capability.

###### Legend Content Metadata
These tables in the legend Metadata subsystem control legend content: 
  * [G3E_LEGEND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg)
The Legend table (G3E_LEGEND) contains the names of each legend definition table and its corresponding display control table. You must assign unique legend definition and Display Control table names for each legend. These names must be less than or equal to 80 characters. You can define a legend as geographic or detail, and you can flag one of each type as the default geographic or default detail legend. Each legend can have a paper scale that affects map presentation and plotting output. 
  * [G3E_LEGENDSETTINGS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5TsqlYTiAxwXTGbEqbC3Fg)
The Legend Settings table (G3E_LEGENDSETTINGS) contains the username of the legend settings. You can flag the geographic or detail legend as default, 
  * [G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/37fQRgD9_K5cgp1rZXsMGg)
A Legend Definition (G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE) table defines an ordered set of legend entries. Each legend entry within a legend has an associated component view and filter. The component view contains the data that is drawn. The filter is an SQL WHERE clause that restricts what is displayed in a map. This filter restricts/subsets what is displayed in a component view for a given legend entry. See the [Legend Filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pz~McDHO~Zxm6VIhecliBw) topic for more details. 
  * [G3E_SETTINGSTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5UJi_D2EF3RLbqldV6jGhQ)
A Legend Definition (G3E_SETTINGSTABLE) table defines a set of display characteristics and locate mode. The set of display characteristics dictate how and when the data in the component view is drawn. The locate mode determines if the user can select or locate items in the component view. For example, a pole must be selected before it can be moved. This, too, is a default setting the user can override using the Display Control interface in the NetWorks Core application. When the mode is off, the user cannot select feature components within this component view. When the mode is On, the user can select the components.

###### Legend Display Metadata
These tables in the legend Metadata subsystem control legend display characteristics:
  * [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw)
The G3E_LEGENDENTRY table is the complete set of legend entry definitions in the utility model. G3E_LEGENDENTRY contains fields that determine how and when the data from a view are drawn. Each legend definition table you create includes references to some or all of the rows of G3E_LEGENDENTRY. Each [legend entry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e7yPWzKDClZ5gnxr2ug01A) contains a reference to the component view whose data are to be drawn for that legend entry. 
Also associated with each legend entry is its style rule (G3E_STYLERULE) and/or label rule (G3E_LABELRULE). These two characteristics determine how the data are presented (for example, color, size, symbol, label content) to the user. 
  * [G3E_DISPLAYCONTROL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U27QBJy1LkijFwfEFQHj0Q)
The Display Control (G3E_DISPLAYCONTROL) table defines a hierarchical feature presentation that is realized in the NetWorks Core Display Control user interface. Each Display Control definition has a separate legend definition. Within the Display Control table, you can group feature components in a multilevel hierarchy to achieve a logical organization of the utility model. See [Display Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/O9cxll~BWxmEI~RD5kLjmw) for more detailed information. 
  * [G3E_LEGENDFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5rnD0G0WMgaIv5a4qryJvA)
The Legend filter table (G3E_LEGENDFILTER) lets you define a filter (for example, an attribute-based filter) that can be applied at any level in the Display Control hierarchy. This filter can be applied using the Display Control user interface in the NetWorks Core application. See [Legend Filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pz~McDHO~Zxm6VIhecliBw) for more information. 


Legend Entry Display Characteristics
This table defines the legend entry display characteristics:  
|  Legend Entry Display Characteristic  |  Definition  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Attribute-based display  |  How a given feature is drawn is determined by a style rule ([G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA)). A style rule is an ordered set of filters that is evaluated by the NetWorks Core display architecture. Each filter is like an SQL WHERE clause and may include one or more attributes. The job of a style rule is to identify which style to use when drawing a feature component. A style is a group of display characteristics like color, size, font, or symbol.  Example For a Transformer, a simple style rule could be based on its STATE attribute. In Service transformers might be drawn as a green triangle. Proposed transformers might be drawn as an orange triangle, and so forth.   |  
|  Attribute-based labels  |   |  
|  Display Ordinal  |  Dictates the order that a given legend entry is drawn relative to other legend entries within a single legend. Typically, a data model needs areas drawn first so that they do not mask symbols, labels, lines, and so forth. The [display ordinal gives you that control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/37fQRgD9_K5cgp1rZXsMGg). The ordinal numbers of the items to draw on the bottom are the largest numbers while the items to draw on top (like text) have a small ordinal number. Ordinal numbers may be repeated, but then the exact order for drawing the data are determined by the Oracle query results.   |  
|  Display Mode  |  Default setting the user can override using the [Display Control](javascript:;) interface in the NetWorks Core application. If the mode is Off, the component view is not drawn. If On, the component view has the potential to be drawn. When On, the Display Scale Mode must be checked to determine if the component view should be drawn.   |  
|  Display Scale Mode  |  Default display setting the user can override using the Display Control interface in the NetWorks Core application. When the scale mode is Off, the Display Mode (described above) dictates whether the component view is drawn. When the Display Scale Mode is On (and the Display Mode is On), the Display Scale Range is honored. When the current map scale falls within the Display Scale Range, the component view is drawn.   |  
|  Display Scale Range  |  [Minimum and maximum display scale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5TsqlYTiAxwXTGbEqbC3Fg) (for example,. 1:1 to 1:1000) that dictates whether a given component view is drawn as the user zooms in or zooms out on the map.   |

###### Legend Entries
The legend entry refers to a [component view](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VPnAdb8GziKP4NU7jimaVw) as the representation of a feature component as a line, area, symbol, or text. The legend entry defines how the component view is named in the Display Control, how the component view is drawn (for example, color, symbol, or size,) and how the text is displayed (for example, the content of the label.) This table provides more information about some of the columns in the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Identifies the component view in the utility model. The view name reflects the designated nomenclature and is how the user identifies the feature. You can identify a transformer symbol view as V_XFMR_PT, but the user sees it as Transformer Symbol.   |  
|  G3E_VNO  |  Refers to the [component view definition table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw). It links the feature, feature attributes, and component number in the utility model. Depending upon how the component is displayed in the utility model, a view exists for each presentation.   |  
|  [G3E_SRNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/A4cS3c4qexeiByfe4rw2qQ)  |  Determines how the user draws the component view in the model. [Style rules can be based on multiple attributes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/W7pjiMzeqEYP57uUsoOa4w). So, if state is not sufficient, you can use any other distinguishing characteristics of your data to drive the presentation of a component view. You must publish all attributes that participate in a style rule.   |  
|  G3E_LRNO  |  Defines the label rule ([G3E_LABELRULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XhCqhW831qxPA3~bdSlxhw)) number using the Designer/Analyst tools. [Label presentation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/W7pjiMzeqEYP57uUsoOa4w) can vary based on feature state or any other published attribute. This display characteristic is peculiar to text feature components. The content of a label component is determined by a label rule.   |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257684) To prevent a user from changing a feature's display status, locate status, or display scale status, you can add an item to the legend definition by adding the component view directly to the legend's database table. The item does not appear on the Display Control. 
You can have multiple entries of the same component view but with different style rules.

###### Legend Filters

###### Defining a Legend Filter
Using the legend metadata, you can filter what is displayed in a component view for a given legend entry. This filter is an [SQL WHERE clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) that restricts what is displayed in a map. 
You can use this metadata capability to have multiple legend entries for the same component view, filtering what is displayed in each legend entry. Feature state is a common example. One legend entry shows STATE = 'Proposed' transformers while another shows STATE = 'In Service' transformers. 
You define a legend filter using Metadata Explorer. This method updates [G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE.G3E_FILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/37fQRgD9_K5cgp1rZXsMGg) and employs attribute comparisons to get the correct display.   
|  Example 1000 transformers (some In Service, some Proposed, and so forth) are being drawn in the current map viewing area. For each legend entry with a state-filter, the software must do 1000 state comparisons to make sure that only Proposed transformers are drawn for this legend entry. Then 1000 more statement comparisons must be done to make sure that only InService transformers were drawn for that legend entry, and so forth. The software makes 1000 comparisons for each of the other state-filtered legend entries.   |  
| --- |  
The filtering process determines what feature is drawn rather than how it is drawn (for example, symbol, symbol size, color). [Style rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/A4cS3c4qexeiByfe4rw2qQ) determine how a feature is drawn. 
When to Use Legend Filtering
Use this type of filtering under the following circumstances:
  * When data volume in the component view is very small, approximately 1000 feature components or less. 
  * When only a small percentage of data are filtered out of a single legend entry.
  * When combining legend filtering with a specific display scale range. The main objective here is to draw the same data differently at each mutually exclusive scale range. Drawing differently implies using a different style rule for each legend entry that references that component view. Keep the number of Display Scale-based legend entries to two or three at the most.

###### Metadata for Ad hoc Legend Filters
To allow the user to define ad hoc filters for individual legend entries or for a group of legend entries in the [Display Control](javascript:;), you need make some entries in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table. 
When the metadata is set up as in the following description, the Display Control lets the user select ad hoc filtering. 
  * To provide user access to ad hoc legend filters and drop-down lists on the Display Control: 


  * Populate a row in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table for the fields in the component view. Of particular importance, you must define a row for each attribute related to the view that the user can filter on. 
  * Establish the picklist reference in the G3E_PNO field.


If you omit a value from the G3E_PNO field, the user is able to create an ad hoc attribute filter from the Display Control, but does not have access to a drop-down list.

###### Preconfigured Legend Filters
You can define filters for an individual legend entry or for a group of legend entries in the Display Control hierarchy. Filters defined for groups can only reference attributes that are common for all legend entries in the group. In addition, only published attributes are available for filtering. 
The [Display Control](javascript:;) lets the user select either ad hoc or predefined filtering. Predefined is disabled if no predefined filters exist in metadata for the selected legend entry or display group. If no predefined legend filters exist in metadata for the Display Control's selected item, Filter always displays the [ad hoc filter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ff4u07DlIHC_TsGq5Ox5uw) interface. 
If predefined legend filters exist in metadata for the selected item, Filter displays the [predefined filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k3Bmniay6JU8fJuh_hkFfA) interface which shows all the defined filters for the selected item plus all defined filters for higher-level (parent) items in the tree. 
When the user selects a filter and clicks OK, the Display Control applies the filter to the selected item and its children (for example, lower level items in the Display Control tree view), if any. Once applied, the map window is updated. 
Metadata
You must populate the [G3E_LEGENDFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5rnD0G0WMgaIv5a4qryJvA) table to provide access to defined legend filters to use the Display Control. These are the most important columns: 
G3E_LNO
G3E_DCROWNO
G3E_USERNAME
G3E_FILTER  
|  Example  
 |  G3E_LFROWNO  |  G3E_LNO  |  G3E_DCROWNO  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  1  |  155  |  STATE = 'In Service'  |  In Service Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  2  |  1  |  155  |  STATE = 'Proposed'  |  Proposed Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  3  |  1  |  155  |  STATE = 'Proposed Removed'  |  Proposed Removed Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  4  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'STEP_DOWN'  |  Step Down Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  5  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'DELTA'  |  Delta Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  6  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'OPEN DELTA'  |  Open Delta Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  7  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'WYE'  |  Wye Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  8  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'UNIT'  |  Unit Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
|  9  |  1  |  156  |  BANK_TYPE = 'SINGLE'  |  Single Transformers  |  06/05/2002  |  
 |  
The G3E_LNO is 1 and corresponds to the row in the [G3E_LEGEND table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) whose G3E_LNO is 1. The numbers below correspond to the G3E_DCROWNO. This field is in both the G3E_LEGENDFILTER table and the legend's corresponding [Display Control table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U27QBJy1LkijFwfEFQHj0Q). 
155 Transformer (Group)
156 Transformer Symbol   
157 Transformer Label   
158 Transformer Miscellaneous Label   
159 Transformer Leader Line 
  * If the user selects Transformer group (155) in the Display Control, three predefined filters are available in the Predefined Filters interface: 
    * In Service Transformers
    * Proposed Transformers
    * Proposed Removed Transformers
  * If the user selects Transformer Symbol in the Display Control, all 9 predefined filters are available: the 6 defined for G3E_DCROWNO = 156 plus those defined for the Transformer group. 
  * If the user selects Transformer Label, Transformer Miscellaneous Label, or the Transformer Leader Line, only the predefined filters for the group are available because no filters are defined where G3E_DCROWNO is 157, 158, or 159. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257678) BANK_TYPE must be a published attribute in the Transformer Symbol component view. STATE must be a published attribute in the Transformer Symbol, Transformer Label, Transformer Miscellaneous Label, and the Transformer Leader Line component views.

###### Legend Versioning

###### Legend Versioning Metadata
The [G3E_LEGEND.G3E_VERSION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) field stores the legend version number that you assign. You can update this number when you make changes to a legend's definition, and you must decide when a legend modification is significant enough to warrant a change to the version number. This value is saved in the NetWorks Core work space. 
There are cases where you need to change a legend version number:
  * Optimize component views optimized for style Id (field G3E_STYLEID), the label format (field G3E_LABELFORMAT), or both. 
  * Remove optimization for component views for style Id (field G3E_STYLEID), the label format (field G3E_LABELFORMAT), or both. 


Here are some cases where you might change a legend version number:
  * Add a legend entry to a legend. This is a change to a particular [G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/37fQRgD9_K5cgp1rZXsMGg). 
  * Remove a legend entry from a legend. This is a change to a particular G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE.
  * Associate a different style rule or label rule with a legend entry. This is a change to the pertinent legend entry in the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table. 
  * Change the display order of one legend entry relative to another. This is a change to G3E_DISPLAYORDINAL in a particular row of a particular G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE table. 
  * Add or change Web Map Service (WMS) metadata tables: G3E_ILAYER or G3E_ILAYERMAPPING.


Although the decision is subjective, these are some cases in which you might not change the version number: 
  * Change the display scale maximum (G3E_DISPLAYSCALEMAX) from 1:600 to 1:500. This is a change to a particular row in a G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE table. 
  * Change the username of a legend entry from Transformer to Transformer Symbol. This is a change to a particular row in the appropriate [G3E_DISPLAYCONTROLTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U27QBJy1LkijFwfEFQHj0Q) and the G3E_LEGENDENTRY table. 
  * Change the Display Control presentation by moving a legend entry to a different subgroup. This is a change to a particular row in the appropriate G3E_DISPLAYCONTROLTABLE. 


This table describes when a Legend is considered out-of- date:  
|  Version is in the work space  |  Metadata Version  |  Out-of-date?  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  No. Old work spaces may not have a version saved.  |  0. The default  |  No  |  
|  No. Old work spaces may not have a version saved.  |  Non-zero  |  Yes  |  
|  Yes  |  Different  |  Yes  |

###### Validating a Legend
You must validate legends before you can post them to the database.
  * To validate a legend:


  1. From the Administrative menu, select Metadata Versions. 
  2. In the Metadata changes box, click Validate. 
  3. Correct any errors associated with the legend entries you just defined, and close the Validate Metadata Changes dialog box. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/ZOn_3ZDHlf6Xojocbs~oVA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=7caf197269a3ca75&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. To dismiss the Metadata Versions dialog box, click Close.

##### Display Symbols at Different Scales
Typically, NetWorks Core symbols display as scale dependent, that is, at a size that is based on the [nominal paper scale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/m9lzB9R3v0Qi1rXcru8sdg) as defined in the legend. The size of symbols increases or decreases as you zoom in or out from nominal paper scale. However, using Metadata Explorer you can [change the Style Scale (G3E_STYLEUNITS)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CD68nZk6gyC8AaeX35tApg) setting on the metadata tables that define lines, composite line styles, points, and text so that the symbol [appears the same size](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9xXW_64QzmXmvbEjkUgs6A), or as scale independent, regardless of the map scale. 
If a style is specified as scale independent, any style associated with the style is also scale independent, regardless of the actual setting on the associated style.   
|  Examples
  * If a line style is scale independent, any associated start symbol, end symbol, or stroke pattern is treated as scale independent. 
  * If a composite line style is scale independent, any associated line style, start symbol, and end symbol is treated as scale independent. 
  * If a text style is scale independent, any associated underline style is treated as scale independent. 

 |  
| --- |  
The following are areas of NetWorks Core in which users are affected by styles that are scale dependent or scale independent. 
  * Zooming [in](javascript:;)
  * Zooming [out](javascript:;)
  * [Plot windows](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wQDWzPvwoXqkdeW3yCYULw)

###### Adding a Format or a Filter to an Existing Label Rule in Metadata Explorer
A label rule can have several formats or filters, depending on how you are using the label, and you can add a format or a filter to an existing label rule. 
  * To add a format or filter to an existing label rule:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Label Rules node. Find and select the label rule to which you want to add a new format or filter. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262005), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the label rule. The G3E_LABELRULE table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. Type an SQL WHERE clause in the G3E_FILTER field for the new format or filter.
  4. In the G3E_FILTERORDINAL field, type a value to indicate the order of the evaluation of the filter. 
  5. In the G3E_LFNO field, select the label format for this rule from the drop-down list.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262005)
  6. To complete your label rule definition, click OK. 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262005) to commit the changes to the database.

You can delete a filter associated with a label rule in Metadata Explorer.

  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Label Rules > <label rule name> > Rules node. Find and select the label format from which you want to remove the filter.

  3. Press Enter.

###### Defining Area Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define an area style. 
  * To define an area style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Area Styles node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256701), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the area style. The G3E_AREASTYLE table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. Type a name for the area style in the G3E_USERNAME field.
  4. Select or type values as required to define [a background and foreground color](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pc2hVU3pqDZg6gFQThjRnA), a fill mode and type, and hatch spacing and width for your new area style. 
  5. In the G3E_BACKTRANSLUCENCY and G3E_FORETRANSLUCENCY fields, type a number from 1-100, inclusive. A value of 0 means that the area is opaque. A value of 100 means that the area is invisible. 
  6. In the G3E_PLOTREDLINE field, specify whether you want the style to be available for plot redlines. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256701)
  7. To complete your style definition, click OK. 
Changes are automatically committed to the database.
  8. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256701).

###### Defining Composite Line Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a composite line style. 
  * To define a composite line style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Composite Line Styles node.

  3. A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the composite line style. The G3E_COMPOSITELINESTYLE table appears in the Help panel. 
  4. In G3E_USERNAME field, type a name for the composite line style.
  5. In the G3E_LINE1 through G3E_LINE5 fields, the G3E_STARTSYMBOL, and the G3E_ENDSYMBOL fields, select from the drop-down lists as required. 
  6. In the G3E_PLOTREDLINE field, specify whether you want the style to be available for plot redlines. 
  7. In the G3E_STYLEUNITS field, specify if this style is to be [scale dependent or scale independent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LQj_lStZf4yiDRgXuRol0w).

  10. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256669).

###### Defining Line Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a line style. To define a double-underlined style for text, create two line styles with one offset from the other. 
  * To define a line style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Line Styles node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256699), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the line style. The [G3E_LINESTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b3vQwQ~YtLlgn5feW4cuvA) table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In G3E_USERNAME field, type a name for the line style.
  4. In the G3E_COLOR field, click the ellipsis button, select [a color](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pc2hVU3pqDZg6gFQThjRnA), and click OK. 
  5. If the line you are defining is part of a double underline, type a value in G3E_OFFSET.
  6. Select or type values as required to define the end symbol, the start symbol, the stroke pattern, and the width for your new line style. 
  7. In the G3E_PLOTREDLINE field, specify whether you want the style to be available for plot redlines. 
  8. In the G3E_STYLEUNITS field, specify if this style is to be [scale dependent or scale independent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LQj_lStZf4yiDRgXuRol0w). The G3E_STARTSYMBOL, G3E_ENDSYMBOL, and G3E_STROKEPATTERN you select for this line style can be either scale dependent or scale independent. 
  9. In the G3E_TRANSLUCENCY field, type a number from 0-100, inclusive. A value of 0 means that the line is opaque. A value of 100 means that the line is invisible. 
  10. Optional: In the MS OverrideWt field, type a number to override the line weight for export to MicroStation. 
![Line Style](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/34oO~PYumgOMd4ShXRF_Xw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=1587a7614c03ec1a&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  11. To complete your style definition, click OK. 
Changes are automatically committed to the database.
  12. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256699).

###### Defining Point Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a point style. 
  * To define a point style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Point Styles node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256684), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the point style. The G3E_POINTSTYLE table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. Type a name for the point style in G3E_USERNAME field.
  4. In the G3E_COLOR field, click the ellipsis button, select [a color](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pc2hVU3pqDZg6gFQThjRnA), and click OK. 
  5. Select or type values to define [a symbol](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LB2MPNjHc6fqi4_f~tmBEA), font name, alignment, mask symbol, and so forth, for your new point style. 
  6. In the G3E_PLOTREDLINE field, specify whether you want the style to be available for plot redlines. 
  7. In the G3E_STYLEUNITS field, specify if this style is to be [scale dependent or scale independent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LQj_lStZf4yiDRgXuRol0w). 
  8. In the G3E_TRANSLUCENCY and G3E_MASKTRANSLUCENCY fields, type a number from 0-100, inclusive. A value of 0 means that the feature or mask is opaque. A value of 100 means that the feature or mask is invisible. 
![Point Style](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256684)
  9. To complete your style definition, click OK. 
Changes are automatically committed to the database.
  10. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256684).

###### Defining Style Rules in Metadata Explorer

###### Deleting Style Rules in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete a style rule, to delete a rule step, or to delete a filter associated with a style rule. 
  * To delete a rule step associated with the style rule:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Style Rules > <style rule name> > Rule Steps node. Find and select the rule step that you want to remove. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256737), or select Delete the current row from the right-mouse menu. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256737) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To delete a filter associated with a style rule:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Style Rules > <style rule name> > Rule Steps node. Find and select the rule step from which you want to remove the filter. 
  2. In the G3E_FILTER field, click the ellipse button, delete the SQL statement, and press ENTER. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256737) to commit the changes to the database. 


  * To delete a style rule:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Style Rules node. Find and select the style rule that you want to remove. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256737), or select Delete the current row from the right-mouse menu. Click Yes on the deletion confirmation message. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256737) to commit the changes to the database.

###### Defining Styles and Display Definitions
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define new styles, or update styles, then use the [Project Tool (GPT)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/E7m~K_5GdHVzot5L0Ghb1g) to update the component view for that component so that it displays on the map view. 
The following is a general workflow:
  1. Use Metadata Explorer to [define new styles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GVwibq0NSEYvsKV~8WKhfA). 
  2. On the Metadata Explorer toolbar, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259668) so that your edits show up properly in Metadata Explorer. 
  3. Use Metadata Explorer to [define the style rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q4dl7dWIs5NZfqbJsgqufQ) for the styles. 
  4. Use Metadata Explorer to [define label content](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZsMmdgNiF72jdjOSKypTRQ) and [label rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/D9vkMG6TKLHXXMJCYLzxHg). 
  5. Use GPT to [update the legend entry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~Y_EGm85mI~wtmOLuZGyIw), which is the same as updating the component view, so the style displays on the map view.

###### Defining Text Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define a text style. You can create text styles with no underline or with multiple underlines. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256704) Text weight and text width-to-height ratio are honored only for TrueType fonts. Non-scalable fonts cannot be displayed correctly and accurately in all contexts or display scales. TrueType fonts (font files with a .TTF extension) are scalable; others, such as fonts with an .fon extension, are generally not scalable. For example, the Courier New font is a scalable font; Courier is not. Arial is a scalable font; MS Sans Serif is not. 
  * To define a text style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Text Styles node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256704), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
A grid appears in the content panel so you can define the text style. The G3E_TEXTSTYLE table appears in the Help panel. 
  3. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a name for the text style.
  4. In the G3E_COLOR field, click the ellipsis button, select [a color](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pc2hVU3pqDZg6gFQThjRnA), and click OK. Background color values are not supported for this field. 
  5. Make selections from the drop-down and color fields to configure the text style.
  6. In the G3E_PLOTREDLINE field, specify whether you want the style to be available for plot redlines. 
  7. In the G3E_JUSTIFICATION field, select Justification Left, Justification Center, Justification Right, or Justification Alignment. 
  8. To define an underlined text style, first define the line style or composite line style (for more than one underline), and then select the appropriate line style from the drop-down list in the G3E_UNDERLINESNO field. 
  9. In the G3E_XXXXXTEXTBOXOFFSET fields, specify an offset from the text to the text box. If your text style is underlined, the G3E_BOTTOMTEXTBOXOFFSET needs to accommodate the underline. 
  10. In the G3E_XXXXTRANSLUCENCY fields, type a number from 0-100. A value of 0 means that the style is opaque. A value of 100 means that the style is invisible. 
  11. In the G3E_STYLEUNITS field, specify if this style is to be [scale dependent or scale independent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LQj_lStZf4yiDRgXuRol0w). 
  12. In the G3E_HATCHCOLOR field, click the ellipsis button, select [a color](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pc2hVU3pqDZg6gFQThjRnA), and click OK. 
![Text Style](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/28mBH6AeJKRu6ABzVVRjtQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=9b44fc4814176de1&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  13. To complete your style definition, click OK. 
Changes are automatically committed to the database.
  14. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256704).

###### Defining Underlined Text Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to define an underlined text style. You can create text styles with no underline or with multiple underlines. The style creates a line geometry coincident with the bottom of the text, extending to the left and right to exactly coincide with the left and right edges of the text extents. The leftmost vertex of this line is the same as the calculated origin used to draw text. (This is the same as the origin of the text if its alignment was bottom left.) The line is below any character descenders. To create underlining as it is generally done by font underlining, an offset is required to make the line correspond to the font baseline.   
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256706)  |  
| --- |  
|  Orange dots are bottom-left and center-center positions of the text geometry. Blue underline is offset at a negative value. If the text has descenders, a negative offset is required to get underlining like you see in a Microsoft Word document.  Red double underlines are offset at a positive value.  |  
The G3E_RIGHTTEXTBOXOFFSET, G3E_BOTTOMTEXTBOXOFFSET, G3E_TOPTEXTBOXOFFSET, and G3E_LEFTTEXTBOXOFFSET fields in G3E_TEXTSTYLE give you complete and precise control over the text box layout relative to the text and any associated underlines. You must take the underlines into account when specifying the bottom offset for the text box. The units for the offsets are the same units as the text size, which lets you easily specify offsets relative to the text height. 
The following is a general workflow for creating an underlined text style.
  * To define an underlined text style:


  1. [Define new line styles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V95KhfGh9X9UqzVdBbB7jA) for the underlines, for example, Linestyle1, Linestyle2, and Linstyle3. 
  2. [Define a composite line style](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zs3ZceYXgssoIemgON42gQ). 
  3. [In the G3E_TEXTSTYLE.G3E_UNDERLINESNO field drop-down list](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CpXL2BFXY4jhHmnoqlMLZA), select the line or composite line style that represents the underlines in the text style. The items in the drop-down list are from the G3E_LINESTYLE and G3E_COMPOSITELINESTYLE tables. 
  4. [Define a style rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q4dl7dWIs5NZfqbJsgqufQ) for the underlined text. 
  5. Associate the style rule with a legend entry used for a specific view in Graphic Display > Legend Entries or with a style group, for example a dimension style group, under Graphic Display > Dimension Style Groups.

###### Deleting Styles in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to delete a style. 
  * To delete a style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles node. 
  2. Under the Area Styles, Composite Line Styles, Line Styles, Point Styles, or Text Styles nodes, select the [style record you want to delete](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdfDUp2LnJSlCK91ZXurjA) and click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256679), or right-click and select Delete the active row. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256679) to commit the changes to the database.

###### Maintaining Styles for a Non-Default Language in Metadata Explorer
You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to set up styles for non-default language if your database is configured for multiple languages in [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ). To display a style differently than it is displayed in the default language when the client machine's locale setting is not in default language, you have to first define a new style that you want to display for the non-default language and then reference it as the alternate style in the style language mapping table. When making changes in Metadata Explorer, make sure your machine locale is set to the non-default language that you want to use. 
  * To define a new style for a non-default language:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles node. 
  2. Under the Area Styles, Composite Line Styles, Line Styles, Point Styles, or Text Styles nodes, select the style you want to localize. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256747), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  4. Define the style as you want it to display in the non-default language.
  5. To complete your style definition, click OK. 
Changes are automatically committed to the database.
  6. To [preview your style definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hm5EfZ~TfTEaxI2uXieW5A), click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256747). 


  * To reference the new style as the alternate style:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Style Language Mapping > <language name> > Localized Names node. 
  2. Locate and select the style for the default language that you want to localize.
  3. In the G3E_ALTERNATESNO field, select the new style you defined above for the non-default language. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256747) to commit the changes to the database. 
  5. Refresh metadata if you want to see if the style is displayed as you defined above on the map window. 


  * To edit the style for the non-default language:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles node. 
  2. Under the Area Styles, Composite Line Styles, Line Styles, Point Styles, or Text Styles nodes, locate and select the style for the non-default language that you want to edit. 
  3. In the content panel, edit the style values you want to change.
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256747) to commit the changes to the database. 
  5. Refresh metadata if you want to see your changes in the map window.

##### Overview Window
Because many map views are very complex, a user may need to zoom in to view congested areas. However, zooming in can make it difficult to retain a visual context (where the user is in the overall network) especially if the network is not geographically oriented. The [Overview window](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uLEgvsO5NKhN4ZBD8ObPVA) lets the user zoom to any level of detail, but still see where the active view is located in the context of the overall network. Detail windows and plotting windows cannot use the Overview window. 
Overview Window Metadata
The Overview window displays the legend defined as an overview legend in G3E_LEGEND.G3E_OVERVIEW. You can define a separate legend for the Overview window or use the existing one. You can define only one Overview window for a specific configuration. 
  * To define a legend for an Overview window:


  1. If required, [define a new legend](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8CMKUYPvnuScyWh3noLYSQ). 
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Graphics Presentation > Legends, and select the legend you want to be the legend for the overview window. Update the following fields in the [G3E_LEGEND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) table: 
    1. Set the G3E_OVERVIEW field to Yes (1).
    2. Set the G3E_DETAIL to No (0).
    3. In the G3E_STYLE field, select the style ID for the overview rectangle. This must be an Area style ID. The rectangle color defaults to the color the user sets on the Options dialog box Map Display tab. The user can change the rectangle color on the Overview Properties dialog box. 
    4. Select or type information in other fields as required.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261965) to [commit your edits to the database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q~kYnyD_idgThLejq0JT4g). 
  4. Refresh the metadata edits to view the Overview window:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261965). 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Legends and Styles under Graphic Display. 
    3. Click OK. 
  5. When the Overview window is correct, [Publish metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ).

##### Paper Scale
Nominally, [paper scale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256661) is the [display scale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256661) at which you expect to output your data to paper. You choose your styles (including font sizes and line weights) to be the size you want them to be when you display data at a display scale equal to the paper scale. You can define the G3E_STYLEUNITS field on several style metadata tables to determine if the style should be [scale dependent or scale independent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LQj_lStZf4yiDRgXuRol0w). 
The ratio of the contents of your screen to the printed page.
The ratio of the distance on the screen to the corresponding actual length or distance on the ground. Also, the scale at which map objects are displayed in the map window.   
|  Example If you choose a font size of 12 points and a paper scale of 1000, your text is 12 points high when the display scale is 1000. At a display scale of 2000, that text is only 6 points high. If you choose a font size of 12 points and a paper scale of 2000, the text is 12 points high when the display scale is 2000. At a display scale of 1000 (in this case), the text is 24 points high, and at a display scale of 4000 the text is 6 points high.   |  
| --- |  
Line weights, dash lengths, and gap lengths work the same way because they are also specified in points. Fractional point sizes are supported. However, in the final conversion to the Microsoft Windows [himetric units](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256661), some rounding may occur. 
Unit of measure used by Microsoft Windows to actually draw the elements. Points are converted to himetric where one himetric unit equals 0.01 mm. To convert to himetric, multiply your points by 35.277. The himetric value sent to the Windows draw operation is a double precision floating point number. There is no fixed limit on the size of an element to draw. However, at some point, Microsoft Windows can determine that the element is too thick or large and not draw it.

##### Printing PDF Layers Versus Translucency
Printing PDF layer information is mutually exclusive to printing true translucency. If a map view or plot window has any translucency shown on it, it does not produce PDF layer information. 
Though your screen might not appear to have translucency, it could. A translucent feature could be hidden behind another feature, be displayed almost off the screen, or be displayed just barely off the screen. If this is the case, PDF layer information is not produced. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/283011) If you have translucency turned on for any feature in NetWorks Core, data in an output PDF might appear less clearly than if you do not have translucency turned on.

##### Styles

###### Alignment
Alignment specifies where the geographic coordinate is located relative to the tile or box surrounding a symbol [glyph](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256649). Alignment is also referred to as the origin or anchor point of the symbol. The symbol is in dynamics at the mouse cursor (cross hair). The symbol appears at the origin or alignment point relative to the cross hairs. In the Edit Tool and the Edit Geometry commands, the vertex or handle is displayed at the origin. In the following diagram, the symbol is a circle, and the handle is near the center: 
Symbol that appears on a cursor when the cursor moves to within a specified tolerance of a locatable feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256649)
To specify alignment, identify the [nine possible anchor points](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg) on the tile of the symbol. Each red dot in the following diagram represents an anchor point. The box is the EM square or tile containing your glyph. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256649)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256649) Your glyph can be much smaller than this tile, but it should not extend outside the tile. However, if it is smaller than the tile, the size calculation does not yield the exact results as described in the [formula](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yaE5QGIICsjFjoj8vWsWEA). 
When you are trying to determine the best anchor location for your symbols, you must also consider how the symbol height is determined. The point size of a font is the distance between the top of the ascender and the bottom of the descender. The ascender is normally the top of the capital letters, and the descender is the bottom of lowercase letters like g and y. Additionally, the default configuration of a font leaves additional whitespace around these characters. Thus, if you only draw between the ascender and the baseline (like a capital letter), the center justification is actually lower in your glyph than you expect. That also means that your symbol does not measure to the height you expected—it falls short by the percentage between the baseline and the descender of the total height of the tile. 
Therefore, Top is defined as the ascender, and Lower is defined as the descender. Center is half way between the ascender and descender. See [Creating Symbol Fonts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/C5zi718155FcdOKeTpc0RA) for a description of how to set properties to make the alignment and size calculations clearer and more predictable.

###### Creating Symbol Fonts

###### Choosing Character Cells
You can use any character cell when defining your symbols, although it is best to avoid nonprintable cells (cells with no printable ASCII equivalent). Moreover, certain cells have special significance to the NetWorks Core graphics engine. 
The graphics engine takes the average height of the five cells corresponding to the ASCII characters ADMXZ to determine size information about the font. Among other things, this size information is used to decide whether to draw the actual text or symbol or to draw a small rectangle because the text or symbol would be too small to see. 
For each of these character cells (ADMXZ), define the cell to contain a character that fills the em-square or do not use that cell at all. If you define one of these cells to contain a blank character or a character that is very short, the average height could be much smaller than expected, and your symbols could be drawn as small rectangles at much larger scales than you would expect. It may also cause other unacceptable results.

###### Point Size
Style sizes in NetWorks Core are specified in [points](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261987). The style size that appears on the screen depends on the size specified in the [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bsqSDkGcycg9jcWq41ZCKg) and on the current display scale. 
Unit of measure defined by the printing industry. A point is 1/72 of an inch. Symbol and text sizes are defined in points. Line width and dash / gap lengths are defined in points as well. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261987) Text weight and text width-to-height ratio are honored only for TrueType fonts.
