###### Style Rule Sample Table
You need to [define a style rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q4dl7dWIs5NZfqbJsgqufQ) for each displayable feature. Select the symbol from a TrueType font to depict the feature symbology. Select the size and color of the symbol based on feature attribution. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257670) Text weight and text width-to-height ratio are honored only for TrueType fonts.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_SRROWNO  |  G3E_SRNO  |  G3E_RULE  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  G3E_SNO  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  1  |  ChooseTransformer_Symbol  |  STATE = 'In Service'  |  1  |  7  |  5/14/2002  |  
|  2  |  1  |  ChooseTransformer_Symbol  |  STATE = 'Proposed'  |  2  |  1  |  5/14/2002  |  
|  3  |  1  |  ChooseTransformer_Symbol  |  STATE = 'Abandoned'  |  3  |  3  |  5/14/2002  |  
|  4  |  1  |  ChooseTransformer_Symbol  |  STATE = 'Retired'  |  4  |  4  |  5/14/2002  |  
|  5  |  1  |  ChooseTransformer_Symbol  |   |  5  |  6  |  5/14/2002  |  
This style rule is associated to the Transformer Symbol component view. The NetWorks Core display architecture applies the style rule to find out how to draw each feature component (what color, size, or symbol to use). Attribute comparisons are done based on the G3E_FILTERORDINAL. 
Put the most frequently used filter first to reduce the number of attribute comparisons. In this style rule example, the data are primarily 'In Service'. Therefore, the STATE = 'In Service' filter is first. Continuing with the example, if the transformer is not in one of the first four states, the software uses a Null filter. This is a special catch-all filter that says all other transformers should use this style. 
Using this example, as the legend entry draws, a STATE comparison is done to determine which style to apply to the transformer.

###### Symbol Masking
The default mechanism for symbol masking is to derive a rectangle, based on the font size, and to draw that rectangle in the background color. The symbol is then drawn on the masked area. A second option allows for a symbol to be used as the mask. Typically, if this option is used, the font containing the required symbols would contain mask symbols. These mask symbols allow for greater control over what gets masked. The mask symbols can be 100% translucent (transparent), or 0% trasnlucent (opaque). See [Defining Point Styles in Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bsqSDkGcycg9jcWq41ZCKg) for configuration information.   
|  Example You have a circular symbol with a letter inside. To mask only the circular area where the symbol is to appear, you define a symbol in the font that has the same diameter as the circular symbol and is solid. When it is used as a mask, it masks only the area where the circular symbol is to appear.  This point style is drawn with no mask. The linear feature component is behind the 38 symbol.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261999) This point style is drawn with a rectangular mask. The rectangle is determined by the extents of the symbol itself. A filled rectangle is drawn in the background color, effectively erasing whatever was drawn there before. The symbol is then drawn in this erased area.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261999) This point style is drawn with a symbol mask. In this case, a mask symbol in the shape of the 38 symbol is used. It is the same shape as the rounded box that surrounds the 38. This mask symbol is drawn in the background color, effectively erasing an area that is the exact shape of the symbol that is to be drawn. The symbol is then drawn in this erased area. The lower-right corner of the symbol differs from that of the previous example. In the previous example, a simple rectangle is used, resulting in a small white patch being created. With the symbol masking, only the required area is erased.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261999) The point style can also be used to draw a symbol at the start and/or endpoints of a linear feature component and to draw symbols along a linear feature component (using a stroke pattern).   |

###### Text Justification
You can set the style of NetWorks Core text to right justify, left justify, center justify, or to justify based on the alignment of the text box. NetWorks Core text alignment defaults to left justified. 
[Alignment](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~6VeMGRDMTO4Znaq3Xabvw) refers to the [possible anchor points](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg) of the text box relative to the geometry point. Text justification refers to the position of the text within the text box.   
|  Left Justified multiline  
text with a long line of data   |   |  Center Justified  
multiline text with a long line of data   |   |  Right Justified  
multiline text with a long line of data   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
Use [Metadata Explorer to define text styles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CpXL2BFXY4jhHmnoqlMLZA) in the [G3E_TEXTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0yRaZQ44AZMeTckCYodWaQ) metadata table. If you select the text justification based on alignment in the G3E_JUSTIFICATION field, text is justified according to the alignment you specified for the text box. For example, if the alignment is upper right, center right, or lower right, text is placed right justified. Based on alignment, text may or may not be placed as you intended. 
If user moves text along a line and right-reading angle is applied, the justification is affected by the alignment change, and the result may not be as expected. If the user rotates text around a symbol and right-reading angle is applied, the justification is affected by the alignment change and the result is probably exactly as the user expected.   
|  Examples A pole label is placed with the justification set to justification based on alignment. ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256821) If that text is rotated around the pole, the right-reading angle flips the text, and the justification is again based on the alignment. The text is aligned to the right, next to the pole symbol.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256821) This multiline text label is moved along a line with the "maintain relative angle" option so that the text remains aligned with the line, and a right- reading angle is applied. Setting the justification to alignment in this situation may not produce an appropriate result because the alignment changes if the text is modified to maintain right-reading angle. You must set the justification to the appropriate justification value (left, center, or right).  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256821)  |

###### Text Masking
Text Masking allows text to be drawn so any graphics behind the text are masked or hidden, so the text can be read more clearly. A text mask is actually a filled rectangle drawn in the background color just before the text is drawn. The text style implements the text masking capability. Text mask parameters are configured using Metadata Explorer at the same time as other [text style parameters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CpXL2BFXY4jhHmnoqlMLZA) are configured. The size of the text mask is configurable and is expressed as a percentage of the font size. Different percentages may be used to configure the mask height and the mask width. 
A value of 100% results in a text mask that is approximately equal to the text style's font size. Due to variations in font definitions, a value of 100% can allow parts of some characters, such as [descenders](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261994), to extend beyond the text mask. For support of legacy styles, the default percentage is 108%, resulting in a mask that is approximately 8% larger than a text style's font size. This is a good starting point for you to begin your text mask definition. If you need a very tight mask, try decreasing the percentage. You can set the percentage to be less than 100%, but a percentage lower than 100 usually results in parts of characters extending beyond the text mask. This is especially true for many uppercase characters and any characters with descenders. If you need a larger mask, try increasing the percentage. 
The part of a lowercase letter that descends below the main body of the letter. For example, g, j, p, q, and y all have descenders while a, b, c, d, and e do not. 
Here is an example of a text style with no mask. The linear feature obscures the label.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261994)
Here is an example of a text style with a mask. The linear feature no longer obscures the label. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261994)

###### Upgrading Styles
If you are [upgrading from an older version of NetWorks Core](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b7TctiIMycWJUQgOgmNDHA), the Upgrade Wizard automatically upgrades style definitions in your database to the new version. 
During upgrade, the software ensures that the style definition is consistent with the processing NetWorks Core expects. One aspect of the style that could be incorrect is the indicator used for determining the style's width characteristics. NetWorks Core always calculates width based on the size value as points interpreted with the legend's map scale to [determine the ground unit equivalent](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yaE5QGIICsjFjoj8vWsWEA) value. 
The upgrade process creates a log file called StyleExtractUpdates_<DatabaseName>.log of all the styles that had an incorrect indicator. The log file records the Style Number, Style Type, and Style Username of the styles that you can adjust so that the weights are based on paper unit. The file is located in the %TEMP% folder, as established in your environment variables. The information is provided to help you understand the difference in behavior that might occur after the upgrade.

###### Using True Type Fonts
If you use a [TrueType font](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261990) in a Microsoft Word document, save the document, reopen the document, and try to change the font to something else, such as Arial. All of the characters display as blocks. Similarly, you cannot copy any of these characters to Notepad or any other text-based editor. The same behavior can be produced with the WingDing font as with a custom symbol font. 
The format of character glyphs used by Microsoft Windows for presentation. A TTF file contains many [glyphs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261990). 
Symbol that appears on a cursor when the cursor moves to within a specified tolerance of a locatable feature. 
When Microsoft Word saves a document, it stores characters with a symbol font using its Unicode representation. Since each Unicode character is unique, its association with an alphabetic character is lost. When you reopen the document and change the font of those characters to a non-symbol font, the characters are mapped to box characters. This is documented in [Microsoft Knowledge Base Article Q212396](http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;en-us;212396). 
When using custom symbol fonts and their presentation in Microsoft Word, uncheck the Use Symbol encoding option to prevent improper mapping. However, because Word sees the custom symbol font as a non-symbol font, it displays the font name in the font pull-down list using the font's characters rather than readable characters. To be able to tell what character to type to get each symbol, include this information in your system documentation. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261990) You are not required to define the NetWorks Core fonts as symbol fonts.

##### Using the Connectivity Symbol Editor
The Connectivity Symbol Editor appears when you click the Ellipsis in the G3E_SYMBOL column in the [G3E_CONNECTIVITYSYMBOL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/56cF4Pb4pvwkJzEEApNvdQ) metadata table. This symbol editor lets you draw or edit connectivity symbols. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256232)
Use the following guidelines when drawing or editing a connectivity symbol:
  * Draw the symbol to match the orientation of the symbol as it is defined in the font file. For linear features, this should be a horizontal line. 
  * A connectivity symbol must have the same number of connect points as the number of nodes that are defined for the triggering component in the connectivity relationship. 
  * Add one or two connect points to the symbol that correspond to the logical connect points Node1 and Node2 in the network model. The order of placement should match the default Node1 and Node2 positions for the feature. 


During feature placement, the Connectivity PickQuick control connects symbols to components by connect points as they are defined by the connectivity model; so Connect Point 1 is connected to Connect Point 2, and so on. The orientation of the symbol is defined by its orientation on the map, and linear symbols are oriented by determining the angle between the first and last point of the geometry. 
Use the buttons on the Connectivity Symbol Editor to do the following:

#### Creating Placement Selection Icons
Using any application capable of creating 16x16-pixel icons, you can create a PlacementSelectionIconDRXFile as a resource-only DLL. Icons of other sizes are ignored. 
  * To create icons for the New Feature control and the Placement Shortcut toolbar:


  1. Build a resource-only DLL containing the icons for the New Feature tree.
  2. Copy the DLL into the appropriate folder as specified in the [FileUNCPaths](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) file. The software searchs for the file in that location. 
  3. Make sure that the file name stored in [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) matches the file name of your resource-only DLL. The PlacementSelectionIconDRXFile parameter specifies the exact file name of your resource-only DLL containing the icons. 
  4. Assign the icon in the resource-only DLL to the placement item in [G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION.G3E_ICONORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CER72g2Ys4bpQ9~jNI78Ng). Specify the 1-based index of each icon in the file. 
  5. Publish metadata.

#### Dimensioning Display System

##### Dimension Line Endpoint Symbols
Internally in the display path, oriented point geometries are generated on both endpoints of each dimension line. These points are given to the display system so that it can render them using the style rules for the point geometries. The orientation of these point geometries is derived from the bearing of the dimension line. 
To make dimensions appear with arrowheads on both ends of the dimension lines, define a single style rule referencing a single style that references a symbol in a TrueType font with the shape of an arrowhead. This style rule must be referenced by all the item's endpoint entries of the [dimension style group](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9h~~CUCYK9Oug1JGLWnigg). Populate the following tables: 
[G3E_STYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA)  
|  G3E_SNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_TYPE  |  "Symbol"  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  909  |  Dimension Line Endpoint Symbol  |  PointStyle  |  <  |  
[G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA)  
|  G3E_RULE  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  G3E_SNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Dimension Line Endpoint Symbol  |   |  1  |  909  |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260743) Text weight and text width-to-height ratio are honored only for TrueType fonts. 
In some situations, like with right-angle symbols, the appearance of the endpoint symbol depends on the angle between the adjacent lines. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260743)
The style rule must know the angle between the adjacent lines. In the display path, a new column, G3E_DIMANGLE, is added, which contains the rounded-up value of the angle. G3E_DIMANGLE can contain one of the following values: 0, 90, 180, or 270. For the right angle situation, define two new styles. 
[G3E_STYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA)  
|  G3E_SNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_TYPE  |  "Symbol"  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  911  |  RightAngle90  |  PointStyle  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260743)  |  
|  912  |  RightAngle270  |  PointStyle  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260743)  |  
[G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA)
The style rule in G3E_STYLERULE must distinguish between 90 and 270 angles:  
|  G3E_RULE  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  G3E_SNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  RightAngleSymbol  |   |  2  |  911  |  
|  RightAngleSymbol  |  G3E_DIMANGLE = 270  |  1  |  912  |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260743) The G3E_DIMANGLE column is added only for orthogonal dimensions.

##### Dimension Style Groups
The NetWorks Core display system disassembles the dimension geometries into smaller elements and displays them in the map window. Each element can be displayed in a different style. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260745)
This is a simple dimension geometry as it is stored in the database.
As shown in the following diagrams, simple dimension geometry is disassembled into elements to be displayed. More than one style rule is needed to display a dimension. A separate style rule is needed to display a dimension line, dimension text, and so forth. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260745)   
Dimension text — A text style rule determines the display. 
  
  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260745)   
Start and endpoints of the dimension line — Point style rules determines the display — one for the start point and one for the endpoint. 
  
  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260745)   
Dimension line — A line style rule determines the display. 
The simple dimension is displayed as one item on the legend. Dimension style groups allow you to do this, though multiple style rules are used to display dimensions. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260745)
Dimension style groups are defined in the [G3E_DIMSTYLEGROUP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ul1ZNWnC4F6edCUnp9eURQ) table. The table assigns style rules to different elements of the dimension (dimension lines, dimension texts, for example). The legend entry for the dimension component references a dimension style group instead of a style rule and uses the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY.G3E_SRNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) column.

##### Dimension Text Content
Dimension text content is determined by a label rule. This label rule is referenced from the metadata of the dimension component. Each dimension text requires a separate reference to a label rule from the dimension metadata table. The following table lists the columns referencing the label rules for each dimension type.   
|  Dimension Type  |  Columns Referencing Label Rule  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO  
Label rule for the dimension text   |  
|  Orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO1  
Label rule for the first dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO2  
Label rule for the second dimension text.   |  
|  Radius-of-Two-Points  
([G3E_DIMRADIUS2POINTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7hBRVpQK4L3xpQaS~hfrBA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO1  
Label rule for the first dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO2  
Label rule for the second dimension text.   |  
|  Polar ([G3E_DIMPOLAR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o5PfFsSr88U1jRFV6DNCCw))   |  G3E_DIMLENGTHLRNO  
Label rule for the dimension text with length.  
G3E_DIMANGLELRNO  
Label rule for the dimension text with angle.   |  
The label rule can reference a label definition where the content references the dimension text column (for example, G3E_DIMTEXT in a simple dimension component table). Ordinarily, label rules for dimension texts distinguish between the [calculated and overridden dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Cj_VuxjS3t55QO3mYTUd7w). The label rule includes references to two label definitions, one for calculated value and one for overridden value. The label definition for calculated value references the dimension text column, so the label displays the content of this column (for example, 10.25). The label definition for overridden value displays the content of the dimension text column in parentheses (for example, (10.25) ). 
This is an example of the label definitions for simple dimensions:  
|  G3E_LFNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_CONTENT  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  9050  |  Calculated Dimension Text  |  [G3E_DIMTEXT]  |  
|  9051  |  Overridden Dimension Text  |  ([G3E_DIMTEXT])  |  
The label rule for simple dimensions references the above label definitions. It filters based on the value in the column with the calculated/overridden flag.   
|  G3E_RULE  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  G3E_LFNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Dimension Text  |   |  2  |  9050  |  
|  Dimension Text  |  G3E_DIMISCALCLENGTH = 0  |  1  |  9051  |

##### Dimension Text Position
Various parameters determine the final position of the origin of dimension text. Moreover, the calculation of the position of the dimension text origin depends on whether the dimension text can be moved [along the dimension line](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aE0QgNEPVGcWa4LswAOGuQ) or [moved freely](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jp5js99i7pf88sIML6X0Ag). 
Moving Along Dimension Line Mode
The calculation of the position of the origin of the dimension text is illustrated in the following diagram. The red arrow tip represents the start point of the dimension line. If the dimension text is placed at the arrow tip, the relative dimensions text position is 0%. The blue arrow tip represents the endpoint of the dimension line. The relative dimension text position is 100%. The diagram also gives other positions. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259185)
1—Relative position along the dimension line. This position is stored per dimension text in the database. The names of the columns with relative position have the pattern G3E_DIM*POS*. If the value of database field is NULL, the default value is retrieved from metadata.  
2—Vertical offset. It is specified in metadata per dimension component. Vertical offset is always added when calculating the dimension text position.  
3—Horizontal offset. Horizontal offset is added only if the value of the field with position relative to the dimension line (1) is NULL.  
4—Position of the origin or the dimension text. (1) + (2) + (3). 
Default relative positions along the dimension line are stored in the dimension component metadata tables. They are specified in percent. Horizontal and vertical offsets are stored in dimension component metadata tables. They are specified in coordinate system units. The following table gives the list of columns with the horizontal and vertical offset for each dimension type.   
|  Dimension Type  |  Columns Referencing Label Rule  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLOC  
Default relative position along dimension line.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETX  
Horizontal offset.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY  
Vertical offset.   |  
|  Orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLOC1  
Default relative position along dimension line for the first dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETX1  
Horizontal offset for the first dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1  
Vertical offset for the first dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTLOC2  
Default relative position along dimension line for the second dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETX2  
Horizontal offset for the second dimension text.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY2  
Vertical offset for the second dimension text.   
 |  
|  Radius-of-Two-Points  
([G3E_DIMRADIUS2POINTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7hBRVpQK4L3xpQaS~hfrBA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLOC  
Default relative position along dimension line.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETX  
Horizontal offset.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY  
Vertical offset.  
 |  
|  Polar ([3E_DIMPOLAR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o5PfFsSr88U1jRFV6DNCCw))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTLOC Default relative position along dimension line for both texts.  
G3E_DIMLENGTHOFFSETX  
Horizontal offset for the dimension text with length.  
G3E_DIMLENGTHOFFSETY  
Vertical offset for the dimension text with length.  
G3E_DIMANGLEOFFSETX  
Horizontal offset for the dimension text with angle.  
G3E_DIMANGLEOFFSETY  
Vertical offset for the dimension text with angle.   |  
Dimension text is normally placed above the dimension line. In terms of adding the vertical offset, this means that a positive or negative offset is added to generate the dimension text position above the dimension line. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259185)
Freely Movable Mode
In the [freely movable mode](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jp5js99i7pf88sIML6X0Ag), the user can place the dimension text arbitrarily both above and below the dimension line. The algorithm for calculating the position of the dimension text origin is like the algorithm for the moving along the dimension line mode. If the dimension text is placed at the default relative position along the dimension line, the vertical and horizontal offsets from metadata are used. Both the relative position along the dimension line (1) and the vertical offset (2) are stored in component tables per dimension instance. If not NULL, they replace the metadata values.

##### Dimension Text Precision and Units of Measure
The length and angle values in dimension text columns are calculated with the maximum possible precision. Values stored in dimension text columns contain floating-point numbers with approximately 10 decimal places. To display only the required number of decimal places in the map window and in the properties dialog boxes, [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) entries for dimension text attributes must be populated and must be associated with dimension component views as follows: 
  * Set G3E_CNO to Null.
  * Set the value in G3E_PRECISION. This field determines the number of decimal places in the dimension text. This value also determines the number of trailing zeros in the dimension text. 
  * Populate G3E_FORMAT:
    * Use 'CFormat' in G3E_FORMAT to specify both leading and trailing zeros.
    * Populate G3E_FORMAT with appropriate 'UnitConversion()' if lengths need to be displayed in units other than meters and angles need to be displayed in units other than degrees. 
    * Use 'Standard' or 'Fixed' if you want the value displayed in meters with no other format adjustment.

##### Dimension Text Readability
Dimension text can be readable either from the logical south or from the dimension origin. Readability from logical south means that dimension text orientation is between -90º and 90º. Thus, the dimension text is never upside down when displayed in the map window or when viewing the printed map from the bottom. Readability from the dimension origin means that the dimension text is never upside down when viewed from the origin of the dimension (for example, when the printed map is rotated so that the dimension is viewed from the bottom, as shown in the following diagram). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259165)
You can set dimension text readability attributes in the dimension metadata tables. Each of these tables contains the G3E_DIMTEXTREADABILITY of column. A value of 1 indicates that the dimension text is readable from the logical South, and a value of 2 indicates that the dimension text is readable from the dimension origin.

##### Small Dimension Display
You can define [small dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IrX~FbRNYEMNuVXwnCfn4Q) only for simple and orthogonal dimensions. The length of the dimension line determines if a dimension is small. If the length of the dimension line is smaller than reversal distance, the dimension is considered small. The value of reversal distance is stored in component metadata tables for simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA)) and orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug)) dimensions in the G3E_REVDIST column. If G3E_REVDIST contains a Null value, small dimensions are not required for a given component. 
Small Dimensions Style Rules
In most situations the style rules for regular dimensions do not have to be extended for small dimensions to display properly. If small dimensions must be considered in the style rules, the attribute filters can use the value of the G3E_ISSMALLDIM column, which is added in the display path. The value of this column is 1 if the dimension is small, 0 if the dimension is regular, and Null in case it is not possible to determine whether the dimension is small. The G3E_ISSMALLDIM column is added only if the G3E_REVDIST column contains a non-null value 
Small Dimension Text Position
See the [Dimension Text Position](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g) topic for a general algorithm for calculating the dimension text position. For all dimension texts after the placement and for dimension texts movable along dimension line anytime, the correction of the relative position along the dimension line takes place. Dimension text on a small dimension is placed either behind the endpoint of the dimension line or in front of the start point based on the relative position along the dimension line. If it is less than 50%, the dimension text is displayed in front of the start point. Otherwise, it is displayed at the start point. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260739)
1—Endpoint of the dimension line.  
2—Add vertical offset. Vertical offset is added to endpoint position (1).  
3—Add horizontal offset. Horizontal offset is added to the vertical offset (2).  
4—Position of the origin or the dimension text. (1) + (2) + (3). 
The vertical offset for small dimensions is the same as the vertical offset for regular dimensions. In the [freely movable mode](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g), the vertical offset is retrieved from the dimension component table. In the moving [along dimension line mode](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g), the vertical offset is retrieved from metadata. 
The default horizontal offset for dimension texts on small dimensions may be different from the default horizontal offset on regular dimensions. The metadata fields below specify the default horizontal offset for dimension texts on small dimensions.   
|  Dimension Type  |  Columns with Horizontal Offset for Small Dimensions  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETXREV  
Dimension text horizontal offset for small dimensions.   |  
|  Orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETXREV1  
Horizontal offset for the first dimension text for small dimensions.  
G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETXREV2  
Horizontal offset for the second dimension text for small dimensions.   |  
Small Dimension Text Alignment
Dimension text alignment for small dimensions is defined separately from the dimension text alignment for regular dimensions. This is the alignment at the end of the dimension line. For all dimension texts after the placement and for dimension texts movable along dimension line anytime, the alignment is flipped if the dimension text is at the beginning of the dimension line.   
|  Dimension Type  |  Alignment Columns for Small Dimensions.  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTALIGNREV  
Dimension text alignment for small dimensions.   |  
|  Orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug))   |  G3E_DIMTEXTALIGNREV1  
Alignment of the first dimension text for small dimensions.  
G3E_DIMTEXTALIGNREV2  
Alignment of the second dimension text for small dimensions.   |  
Small Dimension Line Extensions
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260739)
The dimension line is extended on both sides of a small dimension. In general, it is extended more on the side of the dimension text than on the other side. The values of these extensions are stored in the following dimension component metadata tables.   
|  Dimension Type  |  Dimension Line Extensions Columns for Small Dimensions  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Simple ([G3E_DIMSIMPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfhDQyz58L_~pIoCe39kUA))   |  G3E_REVLINEEXT  
Dimension line extension on the side of the dimension text.  
G3E_REVLINEEXTOPP  
Dimension line extension on the side of opposite of the dimension text.   |  
|  Orthogonal ([G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug))   |  G3E_REVLINEEXT  
Dimension line extension on the side of the dimension text.  
G3E_REVLINEEXTOPP  
Dimension line extension on the side of opposite of the dimension text.   |  
Small Dimension Line Endpoint Symbols
Dimension line endpoint symbols for small dimensions are generated in the same way as for [regular dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P9b6Vi8DNnTkE~AtckBr_g). The only difference is that they are rotated 180°.

##### Stacked Dimension Display
In most cases, a user can display [stacked dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vAsnjYWXINWTtu_hw2cVKg) using the same style rules as single (non-stacked) orthogonal dimensions unless the overlapping dimension lines must be displayed using a line style other than solid. Display results can be unpredictable; for example, if all the overlapping dimension lines are displayed using the dashed line style. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260752)
One approach to avoid this is to display only the longest (top) dimension line. The attribute G3E_DIMSTACKPOS in G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL provides this information. The value 4 indicates the longest (top) dimension in the stack. The following is an example style rule in [G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA) which enforces the display (assuming that style 905 defines the line style for dimension lines).   
|  G3E_RULE  |  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  G3E_SNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  PrimaryDimLine  |  G3E_DIMSTACKPOS IN (0,4)  
OR  
G3E_DIMSTACKPOS IS NULL   |  1  |  905  |  
You can use this style rule for both stacked and non-stacked dimensions because G3E_FILTER evaluates to True for non-stacked dimensions (G3E_DIMSTACKPOS=0 OR G3E_DIMSTACKPOS IS NULL).

##### Text Position in Orthogonal Dimensions
On the first dimension lines of orthogonal dimensions, you can choose between dimension text above the dimension line and dimension text on the opposite side of the following dimension/witness line. The latter option is useful when the dimension text might overlap the dimension/witness line.   
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259223)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259223)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Dimension text above  
dimension lines.   |  Dimension text on opposite   
side of the following   
dimension/witness line.   |  
This option is controlled by the G3E_DIMTEXTPRIMOPPOSITE column in the [G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Lt9dORBI5z89d0W7e03Ug) table. A value of 1 indicates that the dimension text of the primary dimension line should be on the opposite side of the following dimension/witness line. A value of 0 indicates that the dimension text should be placed following the [standard set of rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gBHeiPBKryunAbnj5c6l8g).

##### Underlined Dimension Text
In stacked dimensions, you can distinguish individual dimensions in the stack by [underlining](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/84lxXcYsaWA1QjsqQKyryQ) or double-underlining dimension texts, or by other variations of dimension text styles. 
You can use the following synthesized fields when you define style rules for dimension text:   
|  Field Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIMSUBTYPE  |  Contains the information about the subtype of the orthogonal dimension. The field can contain one of these values:  1—Single dimension line 2—Two dimension lines 4—Dimension and witness line 8—Witness and dimension line 16—Dimension and two witness lines 32—Second dimension line offset (two dimension and two witness lines) 0—The subtype cannot be determined (invalid geometry or attributes) Null—The geometry is Null  |  
|  G3E_DEFINESSTACK  |  These are the valid values: 1 (True)—Subtype is single dimension line (it is a 3-point polyline), and the first and the third points are identical.  0 (False)—Subtype is single dimension line (it is a 3-point polyline), and the first and the third points are not identical.  Null—Subtype is not a single dimension line.  |  
These fields are added in the display path for orthogonal dimensions only.
On this diagram, the baseline runs from the lower-left corner of the top building to the upper-right corner of the bottom building, that is, it is fully overlapped by the longest dimension in the stack (32.94). This is the stack-defining dimension. Other orthogonal dimension subtypes cannot be stack defining. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262016)
The first dimension texts are underlined and double underlined using the following rules: 
  * The dimension text on the stack-defining dimension (32.94) is double underlined.
  * The dimension text on all dimensions showing an offset in the direction of the baseline (10.25) is underlined. 
  * All other dimension texts are not underlined.


This style rule defines this requirement:  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  Text Style  |  Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  [G3E_DIMSTACKPOS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~TeLYAblUXs~qfjGchv8IA) <>  
0  
AND  
G3E_DIMSUBTYPE = 1  
AND  
G3E_DEFINESSTACK = 1   |  1  |  Double- underlined  |  Stacked dimension and single dimension line subtype and stack- defining dimension   |  
|  G3E_DIMSTACKPOS <>  
0  
AND  
G3E_DIMSUBTYPE = 1   |  2  |  Underlined  |  Stacked dimension AND single dimension line subtype  |  
|   |  3  |  Default (not underlined)  |   |  
The metadata in [G3E_DIMSTYLEGROUP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ul1ZNWnC4F6edCUnp9eURQ) must indicate that this style rule is applied to the first dimension text.

#### Display Control
The [Display Control](javascript:;) is a dockable control that lets a user display features. Each map window has its own Display Control. The Display Control contains a set of buttons for controlling the display, scale, and locatability of features. It also contains a tree view that displays nodes for the names of the database connection and legend, display group, and features. The Display Control contains node checkboxes that control display status, control if the feature is locatable, determine the display scale range, and indicates if a legend item is filtered. 
The [RemoveUnusedQueries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) general parameter controls what happens after all uses of a specific query or trace are removed from the Display Control. When this parameter is enabled, unused traces and queries are removed from the queries collection, thus reducing memory usage. 
The default is 0; the query or trace is retained in the queries collection, so the user can redisplay it on the Display Control. A value of 1 in the parameter removes the query or trace, and it cannot be redisplayed. 
If the trace or query being removed was previously used as input to other 
  * Ad Hoc Query
  * Spatial Query
  * Spatial Difference Query


When the RemoveUnusedQueries parameter is set to remove any queries/traces from the queries collection when they are no longer used in the Display Control (1), removing all uses of a query or trace from the Display Control also removes that same query or trace from the Analysis tab in the Feature group, select [Queries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/laVRwEfbYQPL6CoM4CahMA). 
[Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660) to see an example of how the RemoveUnusedQueries parameter works. 
  1. Highlight TestQuery01 in the Display Control.
![QueriesList](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660)
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660)to remove TestQuery01. 
  3. From the Analysis tab in the Feature group, select Queries. 
  4. In the Queries drop-down, verify that TestQuery01 is removed from the Queries tree. If the RemoveUnusedQueries general parameter is set to 1, TestQuery01 is not shown. The query is removed from the queries collection, reducing memory usage. 
![QueryDeleted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660)
If the RemoveUnusedQueries general parameter is set to 0, which is the default, TestQuery01 is not removed from the queries collection and memory usage is not reduced. 
![QueriesList_Analysis](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660)


A one-to-one relationship exists between a Display Control ([G3E_DISPLAYCONTROLTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U27QBJy1LkijFwfEFQHj0Q)) table and a legend definition ([G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/37fQRgD9_K5cgp1rZXsMGg)) table. The Display Control table is created and named as each [legend is created](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8CMKUYPvnuScyWh3noLYSQ). 
The legend Display Control table is a hierarchical arrangement of the [legend entries for a given legend](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DnvNHhZOfwOqsDzTuQ3cpA). This table lets you organize legend entries into display groups (a named group of legend entries), nesting them at any level in the hierarchy. A display group governs the presentation of the data for on/off control.   
|  Example A display group might be defined by the following class definitions: Structure  
Primary  
Secondary  A display group might be defined by a group of feature components: Pole symbol  
Pole text  
Pole leader line   |  
| --- |  
Legend entries cannot exist at the same level in the hierarchy as a display group. Legend entries must be children in a display group; they cannot be at the same level as a display group. The G3E_ORDINAL column dictates the order in which same level (G3E_LEVEL) items are displayed.   
|  Example The Primary group (in this case, the DEFAULTLEGDEF Legend) is positioned at level 1. This is typically a general display group heading. The CableNew group is positioned at level 2 under the Primary group. In this example, CableNew corresponds to a feature and is seen as a child of the DEFAULTLEGDEF Legend. Individual feature components, such as the Primary Conductor Line and Label are positioned at level 3 under the CableNew group.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/_Fw8AThQ~dzGSH2PwwoGSg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=6f3a250343044ed7&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal) The user interface for the NetWorks Core Display Control depicts this metadata in a tree view presentation, showing the hierarchy that was defined using the NetWorks Core tools.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660)  |  
| --- |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257660) If you find that data are displayed even after turning off all items in the Display Control, make sure there is a row in the Display Control table for each legend entry in the corresponding Legend Definition table of the Display Control.

#### Optimizing Display Performance

##### Creating Optimized Component Views
Display rules consist of style rules and, optionally, label rules. Display can be time-consuming, especially with complex rule definition. You can alter the component view definitions and create optimized views used to populate the data mapfiles, thus improving display time. The Create Optimized Component Views utility helps you create the optimized component views. 
The Optimized views script path designates where the utility writes the file containing the optimized component view definitions. The Existing views script path designates where the utility writes the file containing the current (existing) component view definitions. You can use the existing views file to remove the optimization. Because only component views that have not been optimized are presented as candidates for optimization, you must retain this file so you can use it to remove the optimization if you change style and/or label rules used by the optimized component views. 
  * To create optimized component views:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Optimize Component Views. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258065?tocId=rFZh6Qztdkn4w3D9zyMoVw)
  2. Type the User name, Password, and Service name information. 
  3. Click OK. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Ed32XzlJn4nMzPkEf5klGA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=4aa6f750760b1dbb&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. Use the arrow buttons to move Component view candidates to or from the Views to optimize column. Press and hold SHIFT to select a contiguous group of component views, or press and hold CTRL to select non-contiguous items. 
  5. In the Optimized views script path field, type the full path to an existing file name and press TAB. 
The file name you typed in the Optimized views script path field automatically appears in the Existing views script path field with Original prepended to the file name. 
OR
Click the Ellipsis to browse to a location for the Optimized views script path. Type a name for the optimized component view, and click Save. 
You are returned to the Optimize Component Views dialog box. The file name and path to the Optimized views script path automatically appear in the Existing views script path field with Original prepended to the file name. 
  6. You can override this name by typing a new value in the Existing views script path, or you can use the Ellipsis to save this file to a new location. 
  7. Click OK. 
  8. To recreate the component views with optimized component view definitions, type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> @<path to optimized views script>;
  9. To optimize additional component views, repeat Steps 4-9.
  10. [Republish the data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KMyb7We6CN6SLJS3Anpyuw). 
  11. Remove the master entries for these component views [by trimming](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FxKVEqytxjQ2yUAlQ681JQ), and remove the job entries by [purging these component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/36P2JjlfzXGWnwVEIkdiqQ). 
  12. Increment the legend number in G3E_LEGEND.G3E_VERSION. See [Legend Versioning Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RQMuAsC16HLHylr8AfRY5Q)
  13. Publish Metadata

##### Label Format Optimization
NetWorks Core lets you explicitly define the label format definition for a label. Label rules govern the content of a label. Like style rules, label rule execution selects a label specification that defines the content of the graphic label. As with style rule optimization, the results of the rule execution can be stored in the published component view. However, label format optimization requires the actual label content string to be stored in the G3E_LABELFORMAT column of the component view. The data type of this field must be the same as [G3E_LABEL.G3E_CONTENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3cbIOFsKiLyGeaWd3nw3nQ). 
If you optimize label configuration, the table G3E_LABELRULE or G3E_LABELFORMAT values are not populated. During feature placement, the application uses this metadata to construct the label in dynamics. If you do not populate this information, the user sees only a default row in Feature Explorer that displays the label Default. When the user modifies label attributes and clicks Refresh, the software does not refresh the contents of the label on the map. It is necessary to replicate the optimized database processing in the G3E_LABELRULE and G3E_LABELFORMAT metadata if you want this dynamics and refresh behavior. 
Using the CASE statement function available with Oracle® to move a label rule execution into the definition of the component view. The label rule definitions are used to construct the CASE statement using the same technique as described for [style rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yOcXFQla8Qs_8l1km8Rmw). The value of this new field is retrieved from the G3E_CONTENT field of the G3E_LABEL metadata table. The G3E_LABEL table is joined to [G3E_LABELRULE.G3E_LFNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XhCqhW831qxPA3~bdSlxhw). 
SQL> select case when <g3e_filter> then <g3e_content>
when <g3e_filter> then <g3e_content>
. . .
else <g3e_content>
end G3E_LABELFORMAT,
<remainder of existing view definition>; 
After a G3E_LABELFORMAT value is defined as a column in the component view, you cannot override the value with a label rule definition. As a result, if more than one legend entry references a single component view and these legend entries specify different label rules, you must create another component view to perform the optimization. 
If your database requires support for multiple languages, you cannot use label format optimization. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258069) Using brackets in a label name results in a validation warning in mdval.txt. If the brackets are balanced, you can ignore this warning.

##### Legend Optimization

###### Data for Legend Optimization
Table name: G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDATA 
Contains statistic information about the data in component views used in legends.  
|  Column  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_VNO  |  Number of the component view. Reference to G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION.G3E_VNO.  |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  Filter of the legend entry used in combination with the component view in G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE.G3E_FILTER.  |  
|  G3E_SQL  |  SQL statement used to check if a component view/ filter combination contains data.  |  
|  G3E_EMPTY  |  1 if a component view/filter combination is empty (contains no data), 0 if it contains data.   |  
|  G3E_CHANGED  |  1 if the G3E_EMPTY value has changed since the previous check.  |  
|  G3E_USED  |  1 if the view/filter combination is used in a legend that should be optimized. Used temporarily during check of emptiness.   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date of last modification.  |

###### Database Packages for Legend Optimization
MG3ELegendTool
Procedure name: CountComponentViewData 
This procedure checks all legends defined with G3E_LEGEND.G3E_OPTIMIZE = 1 and counts the records in the component view/legend filter combination of each legend entry. 
The algorithm is as follows:
  1. Insert all component view/legend filter combinations used in the legends defined with G3E_LEGEND.G3E_OPTIMIZE = 1 to G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDATA. 
  2. Remove all unused component view/legend filter combinations.
  3. Update the G3E_CHANGED flag of all records in G3E_OPTIMIZELEGEND to 0.
  4. Count the records for the component view/legend filter in G3E_OPTIMIZELEGEND and update the G3E_EMPTY flag if required. Update the G3E_CHANGED flag if the value of G3E_EMPTY has changed since the previous check. 
  5. Increase the legend version if G3E_CHANGED equals to 1 for any legend entry of a legend.


LTT_USER
Procedure name: The ViewAllJobsNoCommit 
Like LTT_USER.ViewJobNoCommit, the procedure ViewAllJobsNoCommit activates all jobs for viewing. That means that if a feature was placed or edited in any job, the job data rather than the posted data is visible. That also means that if a feature was deleted in any job, the feature is not visible. Call LTT_USER.DoneNoCommit after viewing the jobs.

###### Metadata for Legend Optimization
Table name: G3E_LEGEND 
Defines the legends that should be optimized.  
|  Column  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZE  |  1 if the legend should be optimized.  |

###### Parameters for Legend Optimization
Parameter name: OptimizeLegendsUseJobData 
If this parameter exists in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER and is equal to 1, then the job data of all jobs is used during legend optimization.

###### Workflow for Legend Optimization
  * To implement legend optimization:


  1. Define legends.
For all legends that should be optimized set G3E_LEGEND.G3E_OPTIMIZE to 1.
  2. Define parameters.
Set G3E_GENERALPARAMETER OptimizeLegendsUseJobData to 1 if job data should be considered during legend optimization. 
  3. Create optimized tables.
Call MG3ELegendTool.CountComponentViewData before creating the optimized tables with MG3EOTCreateOptimizedTables or similar tools. 
  4. Publish metadata.
Call MG3ELegendTool.CountComponentViewData before publishing metadata.

##### Style Rule Optimization
The software adds the G3E_STYLEID field in each component to explicitly define which style is used to display an item. If the G3E_STYLEID field exists in the component view, NetWorks Core uses its contents as the style identifier and bypasses standard style rule execution. The data type of this field must be the same as [G3E_STYLE.G3E_SNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA). This strategy is best used for static data, but can be used for all data. 
The software uses the CASE statement function available with Oracle® to move a style rule definition into the component view definition. This approach allows for the dynamic determination of the style identifier. Style rule definitions from metadata are added into the component view definition as follows: 
SQL> select case when <g3e_filter> then <g3e_sno>
when <g3e_filter> then <g3e_sno>
. . .
else <g3e_sno>
end G3E_STYLEID,
<remainder of existing view definition>;
In the above SQL statement, a WHEN clause is generated for each row of the style rule ([G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA) metadata table) that has a G3E_FILTER value of not Null. If G3E_FILTER is Null, an else clause is generated, and the case is terminated regardless of any additional defined filters. This sql provides the same function as the NetWorks Core rule evaluation logic. The WHEN clauses are defined in the same order as the style rules defined by [G3E_STYLERULE.G3E_FILTERORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA). 
After the G3E_STYLEID value is defined as a column in the component view, you cannot override the value with a style rule definition. As a result, if more than one legend entry references a single component view and these legend entries specify different style rules, you must create another component view to perform the optimization.

#### Raster

##### Cleaning Up Raster Files
The Update File Paths utility lets you clean up older versions of edited raster files. It accepts two parameters: a valid database connection string and a valid SQL statement that identifies the set of features whose raster files need the version removed. The utility executes the query and attempts to remove the version for each file returned by doing the following: 
  * Strips the version folder out of the file name.
  * Moves the file from the db-location (non-stripped) to the stripped location.
  * Updates the RASTERNAME attribute to reference the stripped name.


Before adjusting the raster file information, these features are checked to see if they have any pending edits. If the features have pending edits, the versions are not stripped from the raster files. The utility also removes all older versions of the file that reside in folders for earlier versions, as well as the version folders if they no longer contain raster files. 
The program produces a report of the validation problems it detects in a file called UpdateFilePaths.log that is written to your system %TEMP% folder. If problems occur while the utility is moving or deleting the raster files or updating the database, entries are made in the UpdateFilePaths.log file. The log file provides you with the information to resolve any mismatch between the file location and the value of the corresponding feature's RASTERNAME attribute value.   
|  Example For a given raster feature, the RASTERNAME field currently specifies //localserver1/rasterfiles/lowvoltage/0007/A123file.tif as the location of a raster file. When a query selects this raster feature, the utility moves the file to the //localserver1/rasterfiles/lowvoltage/A123file.tif folder and updates the RASTERNAME attribute of the feature to match. Versions of the file found in the 0006, 0005, 0004, 0003, 0002, and 0001 folders are deleted. Empty folders are also deleted.   |  
| --- |  
  * To run the Update File Paths utility:


  1. From a command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
/UpdateFilePaths.exe <user/password@alias> <SQL select statement>
where user/password@alias is an Oracle connection string specifying a user name, password, and alias. The database user specified as part of the connection string must be granted the SHORTTERMTRANSACTIONS role. SQL SELECT statement identifies the set of features whose raster files need to be unversioned. The SQL query must contain values for the following columns:   
|  Column Name  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The feature identifier  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The number of the raster feature component where the RASTERNAME attribute is stored  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The component identifier for the row in the raster feature component for the file  |  
|  RASTERNAME  |  The current full path to the versioned raster file  |  
  2. Check the UpdateFilePaths.log file to see if there were any errors updating the raster file paths. 
     * If there was an error moving the raster files, the database record for that file is not updated. 
     * If there was an error updating the database records, none of the RASTERNAME attribute value changes are saved in the database, and you must manually match the RASTERNAME attribute values to the new location of the raster files.

##### Color for Binary Raster Images

###### Overriding the Color of Binary Raster Images
Users who have the appropriate role can [override the color of raster features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PP3gqMZm4jmJpcO1vWPI_g). These examples describe what happens if users with different user roles share work spaces:   
|  Examples
  * User X has the G3E_BinaryRasterColorOverride role, and user X saves a NetWorks Core work space with a color override. If that work space is given to user Y who does not have this role, the color override is not applied when user Y opens the work space. That is, user Y does not see user X's override color. User X's override color is reset to the metadata-defined color or black if a color has not been defined. 
  * User X has the G3E_BinaryRasterColorOverride role, and user X applies a color override. User X runs the Workspace Legends command to create a legend using the map with a color override as the source. User X saves work space and user Y, who does not have this role, opens the same work space. If user Y opens the work space and uses the work space legend that has the color override, the color override is not applied. That is, user Y does not see user X's override color. User X's override color is reset to the metadata- defined color or black if a color has not been defined. 

 |  
| --- |  
  * To set a user role to override the color of binary raster images:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Access Control > Behavioral > G3E_BinaryRasterColorOverride node. 
  2. Select the appropriate role from the G3E_ROLE drop-down list in the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table. Users with this role can apply overrides from the Display Control's Symbology toolbar button. 
  3. Commit the edits to the database.

##### Configuring Erase Raster
Raster images are typically used as a backdrop to new and changed information that is drawn as vector feature data. The [Erase Raster command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nun4uXc6ai7~CWwOktsP7A) creates a new raster file with user-identified portions of the raster file blanked. The effect of blanking is achieved by defining components with a style that draws in the map view background color. Other aspects of the style may be important, such as line weight and symbol size. This function works on one raster feature instance at a time. The [EraseRaster placement technique](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) aids in this process. 
The command creates a new window in which the raster feature is the only thing displayed. This display is used to create a new copy of the raster file with the appropriate portions erased. Because NetWorks Core stores the edited files in version folders and stores the full path to the file in the raster feature record, multiple users can edit a common set of raster files. The [Update File Paths](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pYX5qgEbIfaoKoGpDugI1w) utility cleans up old version of the edited raster files. 
Consider the following when setting up the data model for erase raster:
  * The blanking component must be a component of the raster feature, but not the primary graphic component. 
  * You can have as many blanking components as required.
  * You must assign an appropriate style to your blanking component to get the visual effect you need. Make sure the blanking component is unique so the user does not confuse it with other components in the product. 
  * Set the color to the system- defined view background color to guarantee that the component is always drawn in the background color of the map view no matter how often the background color is changed. 
  * To configure the blanking components so that they do not appear on the Feature Explorer Graphic Components tab, set G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_INCLUDEINPLACEMENT to No (0) for the component. 
  * The Erase Raster command assumes a one-to-one relationship between raster features and the raster file such that: 
    * The [raster record locks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uCaWVmlCbmbAZgK12Vr0Ww) that prevent two users from having conflicts when editing work only for conflicts at the Raster feature instance, not the raster image file. 
    * The Erase Raster command warns a user who tries to edit a raster feature if it already has pending edits. Edit feature, Edit Tool, Edit Geometry, and Reregister Raster also detect that a raster feature has pending edits in another job and block editing until those edits are posted or discarded. The [RasterFileLockingEnabled](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER indicates whether raster file locking should be turned on for all these commands. 
  * The Erase Raster command’s drop-down list is populated with all components except the G3E_PRIMARYGEOGRAPHICCNO component. 


  * To configure a blanking component:


The following is a suggested workflow:
  1. [Create a component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/w7IdMbVr9I28f0Eka8KQ2w) to use as the blanking component, or use an existing component. Add the component to [the feature definition](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA). 
  2. Use an appropriate placement technique and placement adjustments for placing these blanking components. 
  3. [Define the component view](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WfHMs9jSH0THMWhnXtFnGA) for the blanking component as you would any graphic component. 
  4. [Define two legend entries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DnvNHhZOfwOqsDzTuQ3cpA) for this component view. Use one legend entry to define the style for drawing a boundary component during placement, and use a different legend entry to display it in the legend after the feature edit is saved. 
Define the legend entry for placing the component in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION.G3E_LENO field for the blanking component's component view. 
     * Define the legend entry for displaying the component on the legend that is active when you run the Erase Raster command (after the feature is saved). 
These two definitions provide a legend entry to show the boundary while digitizing but not to show it after the component is placed. 
  5. Define the styles for each of the legend entries. Select the mapview background color for the erasing style's foreground color. 
The value of G3E_AREASTYLE.G3E_FORECOLOR must be -3, and the value of G3E_AREASTYLE.G3E_FILLTYPE must be 1 to achieve the erasure of the raster image. The following are example values in G3E_AREASTYLE. The first entry is a style for use by the legend entry for use when placing the component; the second is a legend entry for use in the legend (that is, when erasing the raster): 
Example  
|  G3E_SNO  |  G3E_USERNAME   |  G3E_BACKCOLOR  |  G3E_BOUNDARY   |  G3E_BOUNDARYON  |  G3E_FILLMODE   |  G3E_FILLTYPE  |  G3E_FORECOLOR   |  G3E_HATCHSPACING  |  G3E_HATCHWIDTH   |  G3E_PLOTREDLINE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  24800002   |  Blanking Polygon Style During Placement  |  -3   |   |  0  |  1   |  0  |  0   |  282.2216  |  282.2216   |  0  |  
|  24800009   |  Blanking Polygon Style – For Erasure  |  8454143   |  24730131  |  1   |  0  |  1   |  -3  |  105.8331   |  70.5554  |  0   |  
  6. To ensure that the blanking components are drawn after the raster image's primary graphic component and before any vectors, use the display ordinal in the legend definition table.

##### Missing Raster Images
NetWorks Core uses the [FileUNCPaths](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) file technique to find raster files. A user could experience a problem with a missing raster image or with a raster image that is skewed. 
The file could have been moved or renamed, or it could be on a network connection that has been broken. In this case, the software shows a raster image that says "Image Not Found," alerting the user that there is a problem finding the file. 
You should then restore the connection or replace the missing file. In most cases, this restores everything to normal. 
However, if you performed the following steps before restoring the image file or connection, the raster may be skewed: 
  * Posted a raster
  * Transformed the coordinate system between the database coordinate system and the DDC coordinate system 
  * Connected to the system while the raster file is not available, or published while the raster file is not available 


To remedy a skewed image, you must force the [Deltas subsystem](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~kJgM~~k_2IhsOp7sY8JZg) to recompute the raster geometry after the raster file has been restored. Use an SQL editor to edit the affected raster geometry, and post the change. Edit a field to contain the same value it had before, commit the transaction, and post the change.   
|  Example SQL> update <raster component table> set <a field name> = <value the field had previously> where G3E_ID =<G3E_ID of the record>;   |  
| --- |

##### Raster Features
Including a raster feature in a NetWorks Core database is the same as including any other feature in a NetWorks Core database. Just as for all other features, you must place raster features on a legend. You can define raster features as either a [long-term transaction feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mIxEcTFc0BsmuME6gcqZTw) (that is, B$ tables with LTT views) or as a [short-term transaction feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qBbmjUjXgiBtmUuF9ufCLQ). 
Raster Features Metadata
For a raster feature to be placed using the GFPlaceTech.ImageIPT, the raster-based geographic component of the feature must have the following metadata settings: 
  * G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE
[G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE.G3E_PINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fy4Cx0Y1oeQuVI6b1cIi6A) is the unique identifier for the placement technique from the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
The [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_PINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) holds the placement technique name. 
  * G3E_COMPONENT
Set the [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) value of the raster-based geographic component of the feature to 32. Set the [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_GEOMETRYTYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) to RasterGeometry as required by both the GFPlaceTech.ImageIPT and the Load Images command. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261623) Metadata is not required for using raster images with the Attach Raster command. 
Add the columns from the raster component table to the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. These should include the RASTERNAME, RASTERMATRIX1-16 columns. After adding these attributes to the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table, execute the following procedure to generate the necessary PL/SQL packages: 
SQL> execute G3E_DynamicProcedures.Generate;
NetWorks Core raster core control to display raster features requires that the raster-based geographic component's base table include 16 columns, in addition to the required NetWorks Core columns (G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID, G3E_GEOMETRY, and the LTT columns if defined as a long-term transaction feature) to hold the raster matrix information. One additional column in the raster-based geographic component's base table holds the complete path to the actual raster image file. The actual raster image file is referenced from database records for ancillary information, and the file may have to be moved from time to time. Therefore, the NetWorks Core FileLocater object uses a combination of the paths listed in the <OTHERPATHS> section of the FileUNCPaths file and the raster image file name to determine the location of a raster image file.

#### Storing the Graphics
After the user digitizes a component, its geometry is stored in the database. The G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE field determines the table in which the geometry is stored. The type of geometry created is determined by the value in the [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_GEOMETRYTYPE field](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). 
The resulting geometry is stored in the component table in the field specified by the G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_GEOMETRYFIELD field. If the geometry type is TextPointGeometry or OrientedPointGeometry, an alignment value specifying the justification of the text is also stored in the component table in the field specified by the G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_ALIGNMENTFIELD field. [Alignment values](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg) allow the user to specify the point of origin of a text component. This point of origin, or handle, is the control point for edit operations. This diagram shows the metadata structure for storing graphics. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259272)

#### Tooltip Labels (Feature Identification)

##### Tooltip Labels (Feature Identification) Metadata
The [tooltip label information](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0GAtWySWNjkncGP2cplBuQ) is specified in the metadata tables [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) and [G3E_FEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ). The column [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_LRNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) refers to a [label rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZsMmdgNiF72jdjOSKypTRQ) number to use to identify the component. You populate this column differently for graphic and attribute components. 
For graphic components, the label rule references only the attributes in the component view recordset for the view associated with the component (applies to the Map Window tooltips). Graphic component attributes are published so the tooltip label displays without accessing the database. 
For nongraphic feature presentation (for example, Feature Explorer or Feature Allocation), the software uses the label rule number of the primary attribute component. This label rule references only the attributes in the table or view identified by the [G3E_FEATURE.G3E_IDENTIFIERVIEW](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ).
