### Long-Term Transactions

#### Closing a Job
After posting a job, the job can be [closed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/62sxkBtV6zTG9bN1vuAcpg). The job must be active and cannot be closed if there are pending edits in the job. Closing a job updates the job record in the G3E_JOB table to Closed so no one else can see it. It is still in the table for historical reasons, but users do not see it. 
If there are no edits in the job, LTT_ADMIN.CLOSEJOB procedure is called. This procedure deletes the job's record from the LTT_IDENTIFIERS table. The job can no longer be activated. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_ADMIN package.

#### Conflict Detection
A conflict occurs when someone posts a change to a record after you edited the same record, but before you post your changes. The conflict must be [resolved](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/heF3oex8IXnA60RkpnJEWw) before a job can be posted. 
If a job is in optimistic mode, the user can view changes in the job that conflict with the master record. Conflicts occur in optimistic mode only when someone else updates the master record after a user has made a copy of it for the job. If the date of the master record is different than the changed record, then another user has made a change. This constitutes a conflict. A user must be editing the job to run this command. 
To determine if conflicts exist in a job, the LTT_USER.FINDCONFLICTS procedure is called. This procedure queries the LTT_UNDO_LOG and for each change determines if the master record's date is different from the job record's date. It puts the keys of these records into the Conflicts table. For each conflict, it shows the job feature and the master feature. It also shows the graphic and the attribution. 
The user can accept the master feature and discard the change or selectively choose between attributes of the job and the master, and then the user can override the master. The user can also generate a report to aid in deciding which changes to accept and which to discard. 
You can use the ConflictDetection.xsl template, which is in the <NetWorks Core installation folder>\templates folder, as a sample to create your own Conflict Detection report. The metadata should be updated to create a HTML Report with Conflict Detection as the report type. 
See the [Hierarchical Shape Recordset](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RB~h_xQYKWoMGlcPVt~paA) that is sent as an input recordset to the report interface. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Creating a Long-Term Transaction
To initiate a long-term transaction, a user must create a [new job](http://www.). Once the new job is created, it must be activated to allow placement and editing of facility data. 
The default name of a new job is <Default>. The user may change this name to provide a specific name for the new job, or they may accept the default name. If a user does not give the job a name, the name of the job will be a concatenation of a metadata-defined name followed by a number. G3E_JOBDEFINITION.G3E_JOBPREFIX defines the metadata name for a job, and G3E_JOB_IDENTIFIER sequence is used to supply the number (for example JOBNO13534). 
The creation of the job inserts a row into the G3E_JOB table. It uses the next value of the G3E_JOB_SEQ sequence to get the G3E_ID column value. 
The LTT_LOCKS.LOCKS procedure is called to determine if this database uses optimistic or pessimistic locking. You set locking mode when you set up a development schema. 
  * Pessimistic locking is a long-term transaction mode in which the database records that the user edits are locked so that users in other jobs cannot update them until the records are posted or discarded. 
  * Optimistic locking is a long-term transaction mode in which there can be multiple edits to the original database records by multiple jobs. The different jobs changes are isolated from each other. 


A database should not have a combination of both optimistic and pessimistic long-term transactions because if either of the following occurs, the behavior of the database software is undefined: 
  * An optimistic long-term transaction encounters records modified by a pessimistic long-term transaction 
  * A pessimistic long-term transaction encounters records modified by an optimistic long-term transaction 


To determine the locking mode of the database, type the following statement
SQL> select LTT_LOCKS.LOCKS from dual;
The LTT_ADMIN.CREATEJOB procedure is called, passing in the job name (G3E_IDENTIFIER) and the optimistic or pessimistic mode. This procedure creates a new entry in the [LTT_IDENTIFIERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6bUuSH4zVwUoHnjk182RXg) table. It sets the date and user and uses the next value of the LTT_IDS sequence to get the next LTT_ID value, which is the internal identifier for the job and which is stored on records modified by the job. You must have execute privileges on the LTT_ADMIN package. 
To create or edit facility data, the job must be activated. When this happens, the LTT_USER.EDITJOB procedure is called using the job name. This procedure puts a record into the [LTT_SESSIONS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Hzp4Xl13ss3bF0xesorykg) table that indicates that this Oracle session is editing this job. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Discarding Long-Term Transactions
A user can [discard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qgvKGBWQ0~8XLZUTw~~yyg) an entire long-term transaction (LTT) before posting. All job edits or individual job edits may be discarded. The job must be active to discard its edits. 
Discarding of job edits calls the LTT_USER.DISCARDJOB procedure. 
LTT_USER.DISCARDJOB queries the LTT_UNDO_LOG table for all records of all tables affected by this job. The procedure then eliminates all of those records and clears out the LTT_UNDO_LOG. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Editing a Long-Term Transaction
A user can add and edit records in an existing long-term transaction (LTT) by [activating a job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Da~wSlck5PhOZGHELgovbA). 
The user can add or remove jobs from the environment and activate the job to put it into edit mode, which allows for the placement and editing of facility data. Only one job can be activated at a time. 
Activating a Job 
  * Updates the job record in the job table setting G3E_PROCESSINGSTASUS to 1 to indicate the job is in edit mode 
  * Calls the LTT_USER.EDITJOB procedure to insert a record into the LTT_SESSIONS table setting LTT_MODE to “EDIT” to indicate that LTT edits can occur 


Removing an Active Job
  * Updates the job record in the job table setting G3E_PROCESSINGSTATUS to 0 to indicate the job is not in edit mode 
  * Calls the LTT_USER.DONE procedure to remove the record in LTT_SESSIONS for the job

#### Hierarchical Recordset Structure
The following is the structure of the shape recordset, which is input to the report interface. Use this example to configure a conflict detection report. 
SHAPE APPEND 
{SELECT * FROM <Job Table> WHERE <Job Identifier Field> = ‘<Active Job Name>’} 
((SHAPE APPEND NEW adInteger As FeatureNumber, 
NEW <Job Identifier Type> As <Job Identifier Field>, 
NEW adBigInt As FeatureID, 
NEW adBSTR As FeatureName, 
NEW adBSTR As FeatureLabel, 
((SHAPE APPEND NEW adInteger As FeatureNumber, 
NEW adBigInt As FeatureID, 
{SELECT * FROM <Job Table> WHERE <Job Identifier Field> = 
‘<Job Name that last updated the master>’}) AS MASTERJOBINFO 
RELATE FeatureNumber TO FeatureNumber, FeatureID TO FeatureID), 
((SHAPE APPEND NEW adInteger As FeatureNumber, 
NEW adBigInt As FeatureID, 
NEW adInteger As ComponentNumber, 
NEW adBSTR As ComponentName, 
NEW adBSTR As ComponentTable, 
((SHAPE APPEND NEW adInteger As FeatureNumber, 
NEW adBigInt As FeatureID, 
NEW adInteger As ComponentNumber, 
NEW adBigInt As ComponentID, 
NEW adBSTR As AttributeName, 
NEW adBSTR As AttributeField, 
NEW adBSTR As MasterValue, 
NEW adBSTR As JobValue) 
AS ATTRIBUTEINFO RELATE 
FeatureNumber TO FeatureNumber, FeatureID TO FeatureID, 
ComponentNumber TO ComponentNumber)) 
AS COMPONENTINFO RELATE 
FeatureNumber TO FeatureNumber, 
FeatureID TO FeatureID)) 
AS FEATUREINFO RELATE 
<Job Identifier Field> = <Job Identifier Field>)

#### LTT Fields

##### LTT_DATE Field
The LTT_DATE field is used to validate whether a conflict has occurred during posting of an optimistic long-term transaction (job). When a master record is edited in a job, a copy of the master record is created as the job record and given the LTT_ID of the job and the LTT_DATE of the master record (along with all the other attributes of the master record). When the job is posted, the job record’s LTT_DATE field value must match the master record’s LTT_DATE field value or there is a conflict. If the master record’s LTT_DATE is different, then the master record has changed since the job record was copied from it (either another job posted it or it was modified by a Short Term Transaction). If the two records’ LTT_DATE field values match, then the record can be posted as the new master. The existing master is deleted and the job record’s LTT_ID is set to 0 and it receives a new LTT_DATE value to distinguish it. The format of this field is DATE.

##### LTT_ID Field
It is important to associate an LTT's changed records and to distinguish them from master records and other LTTs' changed records. This requires a column on each data table whose value identifies the set of changed records. This is the long-term transaction ID or LTT_ID column. Master records have an LTT_ID=0. All other values indicate a job record. 
The value could uniquely identify the user, but a user may operate on separate, mutually exclusive sets of records. It could identify the node that is being used, but a user may move to a different machine, and another user could begin using the current machine. Thus, the set of changed records needs its own unique identifier. 
The set of changed records constitutes a job, and the LTT_ID is equivalent (but not identical) to a job. A unique long LTT_ID is generated for a unique job and is stored in the [LTT_IDENTIFIERS table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6bUuSH4zVwUoHnjk182RXg). The Job Identifier is frequently assigned by a job management system.

##### LTT_STATUS Field
The LTT_STATUS field contains a range of values that define the status of the record in this row. The following table of values indicates the possible range of values.   
|  Value  |  Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ADD  |  This record in the database is a proposed addition to the table. The identity of this record should be table unique.   |  
|  EDIT  |  This record is a proposed edit to a record in the table with the same identifier as this record.   |  
|  DELETE  |  This record is a proposed delete to the record in the table with the same identifier as this record.   |  
|  IADD  |  This record is a previously proposed addition to the table. This addition has since been modified by another edit or delete operation. This record is reactivated when the Undo function is executed.   |  
|  IEDIT  |  This record is a previously proposed edit to the table. This edit has since been modified by another edit or delete operation. This record is reactivated when the Undo function is executed.   |  
|  UADD  |  This record is an ADD record that has been undone.  |  
|  UEDIT  |  This record is an EDIT record that has been undone.  |  
|  UDLETE  |  This record is a DELETE record that has been undone.  |  
|  UIADD  |  This record is an IADD record that has been undone.  |  
|  UIEDIT  |  This record is an IEDIT record that has been undone.  |  
|  COPIED  |  This master record has been copied by at least one LTT.  |  
|  LOCKED  |  This master record is locked by a user. A user running in pessimistic long-term transaction mode has proposed an edit or delete operation on this record. This record is reserved for that user/job.   |  
|  Null  |  Master Record  |

##### LTT_TID Field
The LTT_TID field contains the identifier of the unit of work in which this record was modified. The unit of work is equivalent to the Oracle transaction ID, but it is actually generated from the next value of the LTT_UNDO_ID sequence. The LTT triggers set this field as part of the record copy process. LTT_TID is the internal transaction ID and is used by Undo.

#### LTT Triggers

##### After Update or Delete (TABLE_NAMERSAFTER)
This trigger inserts into the table the two records stored by the Delete trigger or the one record stored by the Update trigger. This causes the Insert trigger to fire.

##### Before Delete (TABLE_NAMERDELETE)
LTT_STATUS = Null or Copied 
A master record is being deleted. The Before trigger cannot prevent the delete action. Thus, the trigger must store the column values of the original record before the delete occurs so they can be restored afterward by an After trigger as the master for other users. For that master copy, it stores an LTT_STATUS of LTTOLD as a hint to the Insert trigger later. It also stores a copy of the original record as a flag of the deletion. For this second copy, it stores the following: 
  * LTT_STATUS of LTTDEL
  * LTT_ID as this LTT identifier
  * LTT_TID corresponding to the Oracle transaction ID (this copy is needed as a flag to the LTT view that the master record has been deleted in this job and should not be shown in this job). 


Both the master and the second copy are readded by the After trigger. 
LTT_STATUS = Edit
This is a deletion of a record that has been updated in this job. This is like a deletion of a master record (the Delete action cannot be prevented), but the first copy to be reinserted gets an LTT_STATUS of LTTIED as a hint to the Insert trigger. It is a placeholder that can be reinstated by Undo. The second copy is a flag of the deletion as above. For this second copy, it stores the following: 
  * LTT_STATUS of LTTDEL
  * LTT_ID as this LTT identifier
  * LTT_TID corresponding to the Oracle transaction ID (this copy is needed as a flag to the LTT view that the master record has been deleted in this job and should not be shown in this job). 


Both of these copies are readded by the After trigger.
The trigger checks for a special case by comparing the current Oracle transaction to the LTT_TID of the current record. If they are the same, then this delete action is occurring against an EDIT from the same transaction. The purpose of storing interim records is to support Undo, and since Undo reverts to the state of the previous transactions, storing interim record modifications within the same transaction is unnecessary. It just needs to store one record with LTT_STATUS of LTTDEL; LTT_ID and LTT_TID have already been set (this copy is needed as a flag the LTT view that the master record has been deleted in this job and should not be shown in this job). This one copy is readded by the After trigger. 
LTT_Status = Add
This is a deletion of a record that was inserted in this job. Again, the Delete action cannot be prevented, and this time the copy to be reinserted gets an LTT_STATUS of LTTIAD as a hint to the Insert trigger. It is a placeholder that can be reinstated by Undo. There is no need for a second copy when the LTT_STATUS is ADD. There is no need to flag this to the LTT view as there is no master record. 
The trigger checks for a special case by comparing the current Oracle transaction to the LTT_TID of the current record. If they are the same, this delete action occurs against an ADD from the same transaction. The purpose of storing interim records is to support Undo, and since Undo reverts to the state of the previous transactions, storing interim record modifications within the same transaction is unnecessary. 
In this case, check if this ADD record is an edit of a record added in a previous transaction. If so, then store the copy with LTT_STATUS of LTTIAD as a hint to the Insert trigger. It is a placeholder that can be reinstated by Undo. 
If the ADD occurred in this transaction, the record did not exist before this transaction, and the delete makes it nonexistent after this transaction. Do not make any copies of it; let the delete remove all references to it just like it never existed. 
At the termination of the trigger, the originally intended delete occurs.

##### Before Insert (TABLE_NAMERINSERT)
This trigger checks to see if the LTT_STATUS for new record is NULL. If so, a new master record is added for this job. Before inserting it, set the LTT_STATUS to ADD and LTT_ID to this LTT identifier. 
If the LTT_STATUS for the new record is LTTOLD, then this is a reinsert of an existing record because the Delete or the Update trigger has set the LTT_STATUS to LTTOLD. If in optimistic mode, the status should be set to COPIED. If in pessimistic mode, the status should be set to LOCKED. This is a hint to the LTT view that there is at least one LTT copy of this master record. 
If the incoming LTT_STATUS is LTTDEL, this is the Add of record of the deleted record for the job. The Delete trigger set the LTT_STATUS to LTTDEL. It should have also set the LTT_ID to this LTT identifier. 
If the incoming status is LTTIED, this is the reinsert of an interim placeholder record for Undo. Set the LTT_STATUS to IEDIT. 
If the incoming status is LTTIAD, this is the reinsert of an interim placeholder record for Undo. Set the LTT_STATUS to IADD.

##### Before Update (TABLE_NAMERUPDATE)
LTT_STATUS = Null or Copied 
A master record is being updated for the first time for this job. The Before trigger cannot truly prevent the update action. Thus, the trigger stores the column values for the original record before the update occurs so that the values can be restored afterward by an After trigger as the master for other users. For the master copy, it stores LTT_STATUS of LTTOLD as a hint to the Insert trigger. The trigger causes the following: 
  * LTT_STATUS of this updated record to be EDIT
  * LTT_ID to be this LTT identifier
  * LTT_TID corresponding to the Oracle transaction ID


Thus, at the termination of the trigger, the requested Update occurs but with these modified LTT_STATUS and LTT_ID values. The original master copy is readded by the After trigger. 
LTT_STATUS = Edit
This is an update of a record that has been updated in this job. This is like an update of a master record (the update action cannot be prevented), but the copy to be reinserted gets an LTT_STATUS of LTTIED as a hint to the Insert trigger. It is a placeholder that can be reinstated by Undo. The LTT_STATUS of the currently updated record remains EDIT, but its LTT_TID is updated to the current Oracle transaction. 
The trigger checks for a special case by comparing the current Oracle transaction to the LTT_TID of the current record. If they are the same, then this delete action is occurring against an EDIT from the same transaction. The purpose of storing interim records is to support Undo, and since Undo reverts to the state of the previous transactions, storing interim record modifications within the same transaction is unnecessary. In this case do nothing, make no copies. 
LTT_STATUS = Add
This is an update of a record that was inserted in this job. Again, the update action cannot be prevented, and this time the copy to be reinserted gets an LTT_STATUS of LTTIAD as a hint to the Insert trigger. It is a placeholder that can be reinstated by Undo. The LTT_STATUS of the currently updated record remains ADD, but its LTT_TID is updated to the current Oracle transaction. 
The trigger checks for a special case by comparing the current Oracle transaction to the LTT_TID of the current record. If they are the same, then this delete action is occurring against an ADD from the same transaction. The purpose of storing interim records is to support Undo, and since Undo reverts to the state of the previous transactions, storing interim record modifications within the same transaction is unnecessary. So in this case, make no copies.

##### Project Triggers
The LTT subsystem has certain states where your project Triggers should execute your business logic and certain states where they should not. Project triggers should follow these rules when encountering and raising exceptions: 
All Triggers Must Honor Long-Term Transaction Mode
Triggers generated for specific sites need to be aware of the various LTT states because they can govern whether your trigger should actually do work. A trigger can get the LTT mode by calling the function GETMODE on the package LTT_ADMIN (LTT_ADMIN.GETMODE). 
LTT_ADMIN.GETMODE  
|  State  |  Description  |  Action  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  DISCARD  |  Discards entire job  |  Do nothing  |  
|  DISCARDFID  |  Discards by Feature ID  |  Do nothing  |  
|  LONG  |  Long-term transaction mode – normal  |  Do your trigger work  |  
|  LONGPPOST  |  Posts selected features  |  Do nothing  |  
|  POST  |  Posts entire job  |  Do nothing  |  
|  READ ONLY  |  Read Only mode  |  Cannot edit  |  
|  SetDate  |  Conflict Detection in Optimistic LTT  |  Do nothing  |  
|  SHORT  |  Short-term transaction mode  |  Usually bulk loading  |  
|  UNDO  |  Undo mode  |  Do nothing  |  
The normal editing mode is LONG, and that is when your triggers should do their integrity or model work. 
DISCARD throws the entire job away. Anything you did is thrown away so there is no need to take action. 
UNDO throws away the last transaction. Anything you did is thrown away as well, so there is no need to take action. 
SHORT usually allows special case operations to load or modify the database or model. Your triggers can fire here, but typically what is being loaded is supposed to be correct. 
In general, you should include code like the following at the beginning of all your triggers: 
If (LTT_ADMIN.GETMODE <> 'LONG') THEN  
RETURN;  
END IF; 
Insert Triggers Must Ignore LTT Reinsertions of Updated or Deleted Records
The LTT After trigger reinserts the master record or an interim placeholder record after an Update or Delete operation to UNDO. Your Insert triggers do not need to do anything at this point. Your Update or Delete triggers fired on the initial operation. To test for that, check whether a package counter, <Table_Name>_PKG.v_NumEntries, is greater than 0. If so, this indicates that this is an insert by the After trigger, and your trigger should do nothing and just return. The package name is the name of your table appended with _PKG (this includes the B$ prefix). 
In general, you should include code something like the following at the beginning of your Insert triggers: 
If (<Table_Name>_PKG.v_NumEntries > 0) THEN
RETURN;
END IF;
All Triggers Must Clean Up When Raising Exceptions
If you raise an exception in your PL/SQL, the transaction is going to be rolled back. Any master or interim placeholder records that were going to be reinserted into the table by the LTT After trigger are discarded by the rollback. However the package counter <Table_Name>_PKG.v_NumEntries mentioned above remains. To reflect the rollback, you must set <TABLE_NAME>_PKG.v_NumEntries =0 so that the system (including your triggers) knows that there is nothing to be done. 
In general, you should include code like the following when you raise an exception:
EXCEPTION
WHEN OTHERS THEN 
<Table_Name>_PKG.v_NumEntries := 0;
RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(your_error_number,your_error_string);
All Triggers Must Reraise Exceptions
Do not ignore exceptions; judiciously raise them. It is your responsibility to understand your business logic to determine behavior when encountering various exceptions. If you ignore them, software continues to execute despite the error condition it has encountered, and there may be cases where you know that this is acceptable. In general, this undermines data integrity, plus you must account for the fact that other triggers may have already set <Table_Name>_PKG.v_NumEntries := 0 when they encountered the exception. 
The following statement is incorrect and compromises your data integrity:
exception
when others then NULL;
Insert For Each Row Triggers Should Ignore G3E_ID=-1
In general, you should include code like the following at the beginning of your Insert For Each Row triggers: 
If (NEW.G3E_ID=-1) THEN  
RETURN;  
END IF; 
Alternately, you could include this logic in the WHEN clause of your Insert For Each Row triggers: 
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER <Trigger_Name>
BEFORE INSERT ON <Table_Name> FOR EACH ROW 
WHEN (NEW.G3E_ID != -1 or NEW.G3E_ID IS NULL);
All Triggers Should Be Designed for Performance
SQL executed in a trigger is parsed every time the trigger is fired. To avoid this, you can encapsulate the SQL into a package or procedure and call the package or procedure from the trigger. Then the Oracle PL/SQL engine manages (and reuses) the cursor without parsing (provided the shared_pool still contains it and you have enough session_cached_cursors). 
It is logical to modularize SQL and pass variables into the procedure, but only if the SQL can still be executed without being dynamically generated and executed. If several triggers execute SQL that is equivalent except for the table name (searching for a particular G3E_FID for example), then enapsulating this SQL into a single procedure where the table name is passed in is not very efficient. The procedure has to dynamically parse the SQL. It is more efficient in these circumstances to create a package for each table that contains the SQL specific to that table. A trigger fires when an operation is performed against a table; the trigger knows the table, and thus can know the package. It can call a procedure on that package, passing in appropriate parameters and the procedure executes the SQL without parsing, taking advantage of Oracle's PL/SQL cursor management. 
Do Not Query Tables Using SELECT *
Oracle considers the SELECT * construct to be a poor practice. If any column in the table or view contains a geometry object, the query fails. You should explicitly name the columns you want returned from your query.

#### LTT Views

##### LTT View Directly Subsetted Example
If the component is [directly subsetted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw), the LTT view restricts the selected rows to the appropriate regions for this configuration. See the [Regional Subsetting](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pojLH5IuIFXzS9HmohODXQ) topic for more information. 
select A.* from B$TABLE A 
where 
SUBSETATTRIBUTE IN (select G3E_REGIONNAME from --subset based on Configurations 
G3E_CONFIGURATIONS where 
G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME=LTT_USER.CONFIGURATION) and 
(( 
(A.LTT_STATUS IS NULL) --uncopied master records 
or 
( 
A.LTT_STATUS IN( 'COPIED', 'LOCKED') --plus copied master records 
and NOT EXISTS --that were not copied by my job 
( --i.e. drop master records copied by my job 
select * from B$TABLE B, TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) X 
where B.G3E_ID=A.G3E_ID and B.LTT_ID = X.COLUMN_VALUE 
) 
) 
) 
or 
( 
A.LTT_ID IN --plus any records added or copied by my job 
( 
select COLUMN_VALUE from TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) 
) 
and A.LTT_STATUS IN ( 'ADD','EDIT') --don't get copied DELETED records. 
) 
)

##### LTT View Indirectly Subsetted Example
If the component is [indirectly subsetted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw), the LTT view restricts the selected rows by joining to an LTT view that is directly subsetted. See the [Regional Subsetting](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pojLH5IuIFXzS9HmohODXQ) topic for more information. 
select A.* from B$TABLE A 
where 
EXISTS (select * from SUBSETTEDVIEW C where --subset based on Configurations 
A.G3E_FID= C.G3E_FID) and 
(( 
(A.LTT_STATUS IS NULL) --uncopied master records 
or 
( A.LTT_STATUS IN( 'COPIED', 'LOCKED') --plus copied master records 
and NOT EXISTS --that were not copied by my job 
( --i.e. drop master records copied by my job 
select * from B$TABLE B, TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) X 
where B.G3E_ID=A.G3E_ID and B.LTT_ID = X.COLUMN_VALUE 
) 
) 
) 
or 
( 
A.LTT_ID IN --plus any records added or copied by my job 
( 
select COLUMN_VALUE from TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) 
) 
and A.LTT_STATUS IN ( 'ADD','EDIT') --don't get copied DELETED records. 
) 
)

##### LTT View Normal Example
This LTT view is the most commonly used.
select A.* from B$TABLE A 
where 
( 
(A.LTT_STATUS IS NULL) --uncopied master records 
or 
(  A.LTT_STATUS in( 'COPIED', 'LOCKED') --plus copied master records
and NOT EXISTS --that were not copied by my job 
( --i.e. drop master records copied by my job 
select * from B$TABLE B, TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) X
where B.G3E_ID=A.G3E_ID and B.LTT_ID = X.COLUMN_VALUE 
)
)
)
or 
( 
A.LTT_ID in --plus any records added or copied by my job 
( 
select COLUMN_VALUE from TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID))
)
and A.LTT_STATUS in ( 'ADD','EDIT') --don't get copied DELETED records. 
)

##### LTT View Partitioned Example
If the underlying B$table and G3E_ID index are [partitioned on an attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw), the LTT view should take advantage of that when it performs the self-join. In this case, a join on the partitioning attribute (for example, G3E_FNO) is warranted. 
select A.* from B$TABLE A 
where 
( 
(A.LTT_STATUS IS NULL) --uncopied master records 
or 
( 
A.LTT_STATUS in( 'COPIED', 'LOCKED') --plus copied master records 
and NOT EXISTS --that were not copied by my job 
( --i.e. drop master records copied by my job 
select * from B$TABLE B, TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) X
where B.G3E_ID=A.G3E_ID and 
B.G3E_FNO=A.G3E_FNO and --Join on FNO 
B.LTT_ID = X.COLUMN_VALUE
)
)
) 
or 
( 
A.LTT_ID in --plus any records added or copied by my job 
( 
select COLUMN_VALUE from TABLE(CAST(LTT_USER.GETLTTMAP() AS TLTTID)) 
) 
and A.LTT_STATUS in ( 'ADD','EDIT') --don't get copied DELETED records. 
)

##### LTT View Publishing Example
Only master records need to be published into the DDC. There is no need to check for job records that supersede master records. The LTT views for publishing strip out LTT records. 
SELECT A.* from B$TABLE A 
WHERE (a.ltt_status IS NULL) OR (a.ltt_status IN ('COPIED', 'LOCKED'))

#### Posting Long-Term Transactions
When changes to a job are complete, the user [posts them](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KjQgbJSTeMO172Qy1IDZBg) to the master database. This ends the job's isolation from the master and from other users. When this happens, job changes become part of the master record, replacing the current master record. The job being posted must be active. 
Posting a job checks for conflicts, validates the jobs edits, and then, if there are no conflicts or validation errors, calls the LTT_POST.POST procedure. This procedure deletes the original master record, changes the job record to the master record, delete all the intermediate copies needed to support undoing, and clears all edits for the job from LTT_UNDO_LOG. 
If the changes are being performed in a pessimistic mode, no other user can make changes because the records are locked. In this case the posting should proceed normally. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_POST package.

#### Reviewing Job Edits
A user [can view all the changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HzSxqwYTAINZyZzf9u58jQ) that have occurred as part of the job validated. 
To get the list of job edits LTT_USER.FINDPENDINGEDITS procedure is called. This procedure queries the LTT_UNDO_LOG table for all records of all tables affected by this job. It stores the keys of each change in the PENDINGEDITS table along with the job name. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Undoing and Redoing Changes
A user can [undo changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zRwIqyzODVmB56_yWDhz5g) in a job or [redo changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zog0AQ5OWh4fS3tO6BufKA) that have been undone while in the same active job and NetWorks Core session in which the changes were made. 
The job must be active to allow undoing of changes. Job changes are undone in the order the changes were made. Repeated undoing of changes will eventually undo changes for the active job back to the beginning of the session. 
With each LTT transaction:
  1. The LTT transaction is added to the beginning of the Undo operations list.
  2. The Redo operations list is cleared.


When you undo an operation, it is removed from the Undo operations list and added to the Redo operations list. The most recent LTT transaction is undone first, then the next most recent, and so on. You can continue undoing LTT transactions for the active job back to the beginning of the session. 
When you redo an operation, it is removed from the Redo operations list and added to the Undo operations list. Because the Redo operations list is cleared with each new LTT transaction, you must redo any desired LTT transactions that have been undone before another LTT transaction is executed. Redo operates on the most recent LTT transaction that was undone. 
  * To undo the most recent LTT transaction:


  1. From the Edit tab in the Actions group, select Undo. 
OR 
Select the Undo drop-down to undo up to 10 transactions at one time. 


  * To redo the most recent LTT transaction that was undone:


  1. From the Edit tab in the Actions group, select Redo. 
OR 
Select the Redo drop-down to redo up to 10 transactions at one time. 


The following are some of the actions that clear both the Undo and Redo operations lists: 
  * Changing or removing the active job. For example:
    * New Job
    * Close Job
    * Remove Job
    * Add Job
  * Post and Partial Post Job
  * Discard Job Edits
  * Discard by FID
  * Conflict Detection
  * Closing a document and opening a new one in the same session.


  * LTT Processing Details:


  * The LTT_USER.UNDO procedure is called to undo the most recent LTT transaction. This procedure queries the [LTT_UNDO_LOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5KYguO2vvWlHTncvoBdRJw) for tables and records that changed in the most recent LTT transaction. 
  * The LTT_USER.REDO procedure is called to redo the most recent LTT transaction that was undone. 


The LTT process makes a copy of modified records to distinguish them from master records. These copies of modified records are sequentially added to the tables with the Oracle transaction ID. Undoing an LTT transaction updates the [LTT_STATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8FT~5Y3poj3RX8Ygw5c7yw) of those record copies with a specific status indicating the transaction has been undone. 
If a feature has component tables that do not have LTT installed, master records are not copied, no entries are inserted into the LTT_UNDO_LOG, and the change to that feature cannot be undone. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Validating Edits
At any time the changes in an active job may be [validated](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Vf80LbonyfEAJpsWHOS2MQ). Job changes must be valid before a job can be posted. 
The job validation process calls the LTT_USER.FINDPENDINGEDITS procedure to validate edits. This procedure queries the LTT_UNDO_LOG table for all records of all tables affected by this job. It stores the keys of each change in the PENDINGEDITS table along with the job name. 
Validation will call the appropriate FunctionalInterface and ValidationInterface Validate methods for each modified feature. Any feature that fails validation is displayed in a grid. 
You must have execute privileges on the LTT_USER package.

#### Viewing a Long-Term Transaction
A user can view edits of an LTT transaction [without activating a job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0P01jGw8RVtD3NL1e3Uaog). Unlike activating a job, multiple jobs may be viewed. If multiple jobs are being viewed that contain edits to the same record, then only one of the edits will be seen. 
Viewing a Job
  * Calls the LTT_USER.VIEWJOB procedure to insert a record into the LTT_SESSIONS table setting LTT_MODE to “VIEW” to indicate that LTT edits can only be viewed 


Removing an Active Job
  * Calls the LTT_USER.DONE procedure to remove the record in LTT_SESSIONS for the job

#### Working in Long-Term Transaction Mode
The software allows users to perform long-term transaction (LTT) changes (unapproved) in the database while keeping these changes isolated from other LTTs (users working on the approved master records and those working on their own not-yet-approved LTTs). These changes can be deletions of and modifications to existing records as well as additional records. In this way users can initiate an LTT and perform inserts, updates, and deletes in that LTT. 
Long-term transactions can be performed in pessimistic or optimistic mode. In pessimistic mode, the records that the user edits are locked so that others cannot update them. In optimistic mode, other users can still edit the original records while the changes of one user are isolated.

### Map Redlines

#### Generating Metadata to Support Redlines
Redlines in NetWorks Core can be saved as a redline file. Those redlines can then be [attached in a NetWorks Core client session](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TRyBrGrZ55ObT7EUPgsM1w). Because the underlying drawing systems are different, you need to define a NetWorks Core style rule that maps the characteristics of the Web products' styles to styles in the NetWorks Core metadata. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260810) The information in this topic applies only to redlines attached using[View > Attach > Redlines](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TRyBrGrZ55ObT7EUPgsM1w) attached redline functionality. 
The SQL script AddRedlineStyleRule.sql populates the appropriate metadata. It can be found in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries folder and is automatically installed in the database when you use \GTechnology\Services\CreateInitialDatabase\InstallGTechObjects.bat to create a new schema.   
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260810) The AddRedlineStyleRule.sql script deletes the styles and stroke patterns referenced by the old redline style rule if it already exists. If you are recreating the redline style rule in your database, make sure that the styles named like "GeoGraphicRedline%" are not referenced by a style rule other than the redline style rule. Also make sure that the stroke patterns named like "NetViewer %" are not referenced by line styles other than the styles named like "GeoGraphicRedline%". If you do need to reference these styles and stroke patterns, you have to create a duplicate record with different name and change the reference to the duplicate record.  In addition, make sure the RedlineFeatureNumber and RedlineComponentNumber parameters in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) table are set up correctly.   |  
| --- |  
You can use an SQL editor to run AddRedlineStyleRule.sql to regenerate the redline style rule. AddRedlineStyleRule.sql creates entries in the following tables:   
|  Table Name  |  Purpose  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g)  |  RedlineStyleRule—Assigns a generated style rule number.  |  
|  [G3E_STYLERULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA)  |  Creates a new style rule referenced from the general parameter table. The filters in the rule map to the types of data available from the Web product redline files.   |  
|  [G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_FP8Es~ev0K7MCcH9086w)  |  Definitions of the following strokes are added:
  * NetViewer Dot Dashed
  * NetViewer Dotted
  * NetViewer Long Dash Double Dot
  * NetViewer Long Dashed 

 |  
|  G3E_STYLE and the specific style tables:
  * [G3E_AREASTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Lx3eocRf6Z02p0woA5Lf2Q)
  * [G3E_LINESTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b3vQwQ~YtLlgn5feW4cuvA)
  * [G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KkSHDKALPAaJHyESmRqk9Q)
  * [G3E_TEXTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0yRaZQ44AZMeTckCYodWaQ)

 |  New style objects named like "GeoGraphicRedline%" are defined to support the different conditions.   |

#### Localizing Categories.xml and NamedSketch.xml
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260232) Localization of Categories.xml and NamedSketch.xml is supported for NetViewer/Field Review
Before sending any XML string to the client, the NetViewer server side software loads the XML file and processes the XML string to perform a string replacement algorithm. While processing the XML strings, if the software encounters a string in the format _GTECHRSC(<Resource Name>), it replaces this with the value from the resource string file, Strings.txt located in the \GTechnology\Program\GViewerApp\Resources folder.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260232) In Strings.txt prefix the strings to be translated with an underscore ("_") to avoid conflicts with product resources. Since this process is a global replacement technique, you can use it to localize anything in the XML.   |  
| --- |  
  * To localize Categories.xml and NamedSketch.xml: 


  1. In the Strings.txt file for your language, add customized category names or prompts for named sketches. Add an underscore (_) in front of each resource name and type the translated text to the right of the = sign. The text plus the underscore is the resource name.   
|  Example _LegendToolTip=Legende _JobToolTip=Job _AreaManagerToolTip=Flächenmanager _SelectStartingFeaturePrompt=Bitte lokalisieren und wählen Sie ein Anfangsobjekt, um fortzufahren _SecondaryConductor=Sekunkärer Leiter  |  
| --- |  
  2. Use the ResGen.exe application delivered with Microsoft .NET Framework SDK to convert the Strings.txt file into a Strings.resource file. 
  3. Update the appropriate .xml file: 
    1. In the Categories.xml file, type the resource name from the Strings.txt file in the Username attribute for the customized category.   
|  Example Username="_GTECHRSC(_SecondaryConductor)"  |  
| --- |  
    2. In the NamedSketch.xml file, type the resource name from the Strings.txt file in the Value attribute for the Prompt and NextPrompt properties for each customized named sketch.   
|  Example <Property Name="Prompt" Type="String" Value="_GTECHRSC(_SelectStartingFeaturePrompt)" />  |  
| --- |

#### Redline Modes
The Redline control always operates in either a passive display-only mode, in a Select or Edit mode, or in one of several placement modes. For the interactive placement modes, the user can enter a world coordinate value in the key-in field on the main toolbar any time a left-mouse down, up, or click is expected. 
These are the possible values for the redline mode of operation:  
|  Mode  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  HideRedlines  |  Hide redlines, ignore user events  |  
|  DisplayOnly  |  Displayredlines, ignore user events  |  
|  SelectEdit  |  Select, edit, or deselect redlines  |  
|  PlaceLine  |  Place line by left mouse down, drag, and up  |  
|  PlaceRectangle  |  Place rectangle by left mouse down, drag, and up  |  
|  PlaceEllipse  |  Place ellipse by left mouse down, drag, and up  |  
|  PlaceLinestring  |  Place line string vertices by left clicks; double-click to end  |  
|  PlacePolygon  |  Place closed polygon vertices by left clicks; double-click to end  |  
|  PlaceText  |  Place text string by left click  |  
|  PlaceSymbol  |  Place character from symbol font by left click  |  
|  FenceDynamic  |  Define fence in world coordinates  |  
|  LinestringDynamic  |  Define linestring dynamic in world coordinates  |  
|  PolygonDynamic  |  Define polygon dynamic in world coordinates  |  
|  PlacePlotBoxes  |  Place PlotBoxes by point or line  |  
|  Inactive  |  Redines in view get activated by left click  |  
|  PanHand  |  Dynamic pan  |  
|  PlaceGroup  |  Place group  |  
|  PlaceArc  |  Place arc by 3 points  |

#### Redline XML Document

##### Attributes

###### BaseRedlineType
The BaseRedlineType describes the common structure of all redline instances. Every kind of redline has one or more points as child elements, except for Rect and Ellipse, which are defined by their boundary attributes alone. 
The optional NumPoints attribute has a count of the X,Y pairs in the Points attribute. Every redline has a set of boundary box attributes that define the smallest box that can enclose the geometry of the redline. 
Redline instances can have zero or more user-defined properties. The DisplayScaleAtCreation attribute is used to scale some style attributes (for example, line width, text height.) for those redlines whose Category Operations attribute contains the ViewScaleDependent value. 
The style attribute group that appears on the Category element defines the default set of styles for all redline instances under the category. However, if the Operations attribute of the category contains the EditSymbology value, it is possible to have one or more style attributes on the redline instances to represent the overrides. 
The element types are derived from the BaseRedlineType, which contains the following attributes:   
|  RedlineType  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ID  |  An identifier that is guaranteed to be unique only within the current session. Custom code that has a need for redlines to be uniquely identified across sessions should use a Property element to defined their own concept of uniqueness. During a session, redline events pass ID lists in the callback functions and the APIs that edit existing redlines all take an ID or ID list as an argument.   |  
|  ToolTip  |  An HTML string that displays in a small pop-up box when the user hovers over any redline that fires the hover event.   |  
|  Boundary Box group  |  The Top, Left, Bottom, and Right attributes define a minimum bounding rectangle around the redline geometry.   |  
|  Style Override group  |  The same set of style attributes that are defined for the Category element can be individually overridden on every redline.   |  
|  IsSelected  |  Indicates that the redline is currently in the select set.  |  
|  LegendNum  |  The G3E_LNO that was in use when the redline was created. A value of 0 indicates that the redline should be displayed on all geographic legends. In general, a redline is displayed only when the LegendNumber and DetailId values match the currently displayed legend and detail.   |  
|  DetailId  |  Indicates the detail ID of the legend that was in use when the redline was created.  |  
|  NumPoints  |  The number of X,Y pairs in the Points attribute.  |  
|  Points  |  A string of alternating X and Y coordinate values in ground units.  |  
|  GroupID  |  Identifies all redline objects within a group. Equal to the ID of the parent redline group object.   |

###### PlotBox
The PlotBoxRedlineType is a special redline used by the Define Plot command in NetWorks Core. It extends the BaseRedlineType by adding the extra attributes that describe the plot boxes that surround the invisible line the user drew to define the plotting areas.   
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  PlotBoxHeight  |  The height of the plot area in ground units.  |  
|  PlotBoxWidth  |  The width of the plot area in ground units.  |  
|  NumPlotBoxes  |  A count of the number of plot boxes encoded in the points attribute. The Points attribute describes a sequence of four point polygons (bottom left, top left, top right, bottom right). Hence, three plot boxes would require 12 points in the Points attribute.   |  
|  Rotation  |  The angular rotation of the line of plot boxes in degrees.  |

###### TextRedlineType
A TextRedlineType is the type of all symbol and text redlines. It extends the BaseRedlineType with attributes for the symbol or text string value; and includes attributes for the text metrics that define the extents of the text. Text geometry is represented by three points: the left of the text baseline (also known as the move handle), the right of the text baseline (also known as the rotate handle), and the lower left of the text box.   
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Escapement  |  The angular rotation of the text baseline in tenths of degrees.  |  
|  TextHeight, TextWidth, and TextDescent   |  The world unit distance from the text baseline to the top of the text, the width of the text, and the distance from the text baseline to the text box bottom. For view-scale-dependent text styles, these values change every time the display scale changes. These attributes help position other redlines relative to the text box extents.   |

##### Category
A redline category is a kind of metadata that defines default styles, operational behavior, and types of geometry. It also provides grouping for display purposes. There are two lists of behaviors: EventsFired and Operations. Both are strings that consist of a list of comma-separated enumeration values. 
A redline Category element represents a group of related redlines that share a default set of styles, a set of events, and a set of operational permissions or behaviors. The redlines under a specific category are all displayed or are all hidden using the IsDisplayed attribute. 
Categories are always output in a bottom-to-top display order based on the DisplayLevel attribute. Two special categories, Default and Dynamics, are always the last two categories. 
The optional set of user-defined Property elements under every category can be used for any custom purpose. For example, custom code could use the Property elements at this level to further classify categories, or the property elements could be used by custom code as seed values for the property elements that appear under each redline instance 
Each redline element has one or more Redlines elements as children. The child elements must be one of the following:   
|  Line Rect Ellipse PlotBox  Polyline   |  Polygon Arc Symbol Text [RedlineGroup](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qswKG4MzEREahpCLY9PRag)  |  
| --- | --- |

##### Properties

###### RedlineGroup Element
Redline groups let users [group different redline elements](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fwzufGTRj8vB3joji93mrQ), [group different redline elements](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HYDZ84htpgoppzqlfjvZyw) into a single redline entity. The grouped redline objects can be selected, moved, or deleted as a single entity. The RedlineGroup element is derived from the RedlineGroupType which is derived from the BaseRedlineType to support all the basic characteristics of a redline object and includes all the basic redline types so that the redline group can be persisted from one work session to the next.   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260358) The following excerpt from the saved redline file shows the XML that creates the redline group.  <RedlineGroup Name="_DefaultGroup" Left="6048708.64355719" Bottom="1373287.06373872" Right="7011720.9699244" Top="1658781.8684582" MapScale="16105007.2000648" LegendNumber="0" DetailID="0" ID="39" IsSelected="1" GroupID="0"> <Ellipse Left="6159497.67225431" Bottom="1373287.06373872" Right="7011720.9699244" Top="1624692.9365514" MapScale="16105007.2000648" LegendNumber="0" DetailID="0" ID="40" IsSelected="0" GroupID="39" /> <Text Left="6091319.8084407" Bottom="1475553.85945913" Right="6773098.44657677" Top="1552253.95624944" MapScale="16105007.2000648" LegendNumber="0" DetailID="0" ID="41" IsSelected="0" GroupID="39" NumPoints="3"  Points="6091319.808441,1475553.859459,6091319.808441,1488337.208924,6773098.446577,1488337.208924"  TextHeight="76700.0967903081" TextWidth="681778.638136075" TextDescent="12783.3494650512" Escapement="0" TextValue="Redline group example" TextBox="0" /> <Rect Left="6048708.64355719" Bottom="1437203.81106398" Right="6785881.79604183" Top="1658781.8684582" MapScale="16105007.2000648" LegendNumber="0" DetailID="0" ID="42" IsSelected="0" GroupID="39" /> </RedlineGroup>  |  
| --- |

#### Redlines XML Schema Definition (.xsd) File
The Redlines.xsd is delivered in the GTechnology\Program folder 
<xs:schema targetNamespace="urn:Redlines.xsd" elementFormDefault="qualified" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
xmlns="urn:Redlines.xsd">
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
A Redlines XML document, RedlineDocument, contains one or more category elements 
followed by zero or more user defined properties. The user defined properties at 
this level are intended to contain information that applies to the entire 
redline collection.
Every RedlineDocument has a Configuration attribute that indicates the 
GTechnology configuration that the user was logged into when the redlines were
created.
Every RedlineDocument also carries a version string attribute.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:element name="RedlineDocument" type="RedlineDocumentType" />
<xs:complexType name="RedlineDocumentType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:element name="Category" type="CategoryType" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded" />
<xs:element name="NamedSketch" type="RedlineGroupType" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>
<xs:element name="Properties" type="PropertiesType" minOccurs="0" />
</xs:sequence>
<xs:attribute name="ProgID" type="xs:string" use="required" />
<xs:attribute name="Version" type="xs:string" use="required" />
<xs:attribute name="Configuration" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SessionID" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:anyAttribute processContents="lax" />
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
A redline Category element represents a group of related redlines 
that share a default set of styles, a set of events, and a set of operational
permissions (behaviors). The redlines under a specific category are either 
all displayed or are all hidden (via the IsDisplayed attribute).
The optional set of user defined Property elements under every category can
be used for any custom purpose. For example, custom code could use the 
Property elements at this level to further classify categories, or the property
elements could be used by custom code as seed values for the property elements
that appear under each redline instance.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="CategoryType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:element name="Properties" type="PropertiesType" minOccurs="0" />
<xs:element name="Redlines" minOccurs="0">
<xs:complexType>
<xs:choice maxOccurs="unbounded">
<xs:element name="Line" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Rect" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Ellipse" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="PlotBox" type="PlotBoxRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Polyline" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Polygon" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Arc" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Symbol" type="TextRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Text" type="TextRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="RedlineGroup" type="RedlineGroupType" />
</xs:choice>
</xs:complexType>
</xs:element>
</xs:sequence>
<xs:attribute name="Name" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Username" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="IconFileName" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="IsDisplayed" type="xs:integer" />
<xs:attribute name="DisplayLevel" type="xs:integer" />
<xs:attribute name="DefaultMode" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Modes" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="IconFile" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attributeGroup ref="BehaviorAttributeGroup" />
<xs:attributeGroup ref="StyleAttributeGroup" />
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The BaseRedlineType describes the common structure of all redline 
instances. Every kind of redline will have one or more points as 
child elements, except for Rect and Ellipse, which are defined 
by their boundary attributes alone. The optional NumPoints attribute 
has a count of the X,Y pairs in the Points attribute. Every redline has 
a set of boundary box attributes that define the smallest box that can
enclose the redline's geometry.
Redline instances can have zero or more user defined properties.
The DisplayScaleAtCreation attribute is used to scale some style 
attributes (e.g. line width, text height, etc.) for those redlines 
whose Category Operations attribute contains the ViewScaleDependent value. 
The style attribute group that appears on the Category element defines
the default set of styles for all redline instances under the category.
However, if the category's Operations attribute contains the EditSymbology
value, then it is possible to have one or more style attributes on the 
redline instances to represent the overrides.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="BaseRedlineType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:element name="Properties" type="PropertiesType" minOccurs="0" />
</xs:sequence>
<xs:attribute name="ID" type="xs:long" />
<xs:attribute name="ToolTip" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attributeGroup ref="BoundaryBoxAttributeGroup" />
<xs:attributeGroup ref="StyleAttributeGroup" />
<xs:attributeGroup ref="DisplayAttributeGroup" />
<xs:attribute name="NumPoints" type="xs:integer" use="optional" default="0" />
<xs:attribute name="Points" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="GroupID" type="xs:long" use="optional" default="0" />
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The PlotBoxRedlineType is a special redline that is used by the Define Plot 
command in the NetViewer web application. It extends the BaseRedlineType by
adding the extra attributes that describe the plot boxes that surround the 
invisible line that the user drew to define the plotting areas.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="PlotBoxRedlineType">
<xs:complexContent>
<xs:extension base="BaseRedlineType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:element name="PlotArea" type="PlotAreaType" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded" />
</xs:sequence>
<xs:attribute name="PlotBoxHeight" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="PlotBoxWidth" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="NumPlotBoxes" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="Rotation" type="xs:double" use="optional" default="0.0" />
<xs:attribute name="PlotBoxVertices" type="xs:double" />
</xs:extension>
</xs:complexContent>
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
A PlotAreaType defines the center point and rotation angle of a plot box area.
A single plotbox redline can have several plot areas in a row.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="PlotAreaType">
<xs:attribute name="CenterX" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="CenterY" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="Rotation" type="xs:double" use="optional" default="0.0" />
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
A TextRedlineType is the type of all Symbol and Text redlines. It 
extends the BaseRedlineType with attributes for the Symbol or Text string
value; and includes attributes for the text metrics that define the 
extents of the text.
Text geometry is represented by three points: the left of the text baseline 
(also known as the move handle), the right of the text baseline (also known 
as the rotate handle), and the lower left of the text box. 
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="TextRedlineType">
<xs:complexContent>
<xs:extension base="BaseRedlineType">
<xs:attribute name="Escapement" type="xs:integer" />
<xs:attribute name="TextHeight" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="TextWidth" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="TextDescent" type="xs:double" />
</xs:extension>
</xs:complexContent>
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
A PropertiesType is a collection of user defined triples of attributes 
(Name/Type/Value). The meaning of the three attributes is left up to the 
custom code.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="PropertiesType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:element name="Property" maxOccurs="unbounded">
<xs:complexType>
<xs:attribute name="Name" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Type" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Value" type="xs:string" />
</xs:complexType>
</xs:element>
</xs:sequence>
</xs:complexType>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The boundary attribute group is required on every redline instance.
A boundary is a set of 4 values that specify the smallest box that 
can be drawn around the geometry of the redline instance. The values 
are in UORs. Top is always greater than Bottom; and Right is 
always greater than Left.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:attributeGroup name="BoundaryBoxAttributeGroup">
<xs:attribute name="Top" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="Left" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="Bottom" type="xs:double" />
<xs:attribute name="Right" type="xs:double" />
</xs:attributeGroup>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The behavior attribute group is carried on the Category elements.
There are two lists of behaviors: EventsFired and Operations. Both 
are strings that consist of a list of comma separated enumeration
values. (See the design specification for the list of possible values.)
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:attributeGroup name="BehaviorAttributeGroup">
<xs:attribute name="EventsFired" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Operations" type="xs:string" />
</xs:attributeGroup>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The display attribute group is carried on every redline instance.
The IsSelected attribute indicates whether or not the redline is 
currently in the select set. The LegendNum and DetailId attributes
indicate where the redline should be drawn. If the LegendNum value is 
0, then the redline will be drawn on all geographic legends.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:attributeGroup name="DisplayAttributeGroup">
<xs:attribute name="IsSelected" type="xs:integer" />
<xs:attribute name="LegendNumber" type="xs:integer" />
<xs:attribute name="DetailID" type="xs:integer" />
</xs:attributeGroup>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The style attribute group contains all of the style settings that 
a Category or a redline instance might have. Note that only the 
styles that make sense for the redline geometry type need to be 
specified. 
This attribute group is an abstraction of the GDI style system.
Hence, the allowable values of the styles listed below are exactly 
the same as the corresponding GDI style values. For example, PenStyle 
values come from PS_SOLID, PS_DASHED, etc. A FontWeight of 400 will
use the regular font, whereas a value of 700 will use the bold font 
from the specified FontName family.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:attributeGroup name="StyleAttributeGroup">
<xs:attribute name="LineColor" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="LineTranslucency" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="LineStyle" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="LineWidth" type="xs:double" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FillColor" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FillTranslucency" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FillStyle" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FillHatch" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FontColor" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FontTranslucency" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FontName" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FontSize" type="xs:double" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="FontStyle" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolColor" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolTranslucency" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolFontName" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolFontCharset" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolSize" type="xs:double" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="SymbolValue" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="TextValue" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="ViewScaleDependent" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="MapScale" type="xs:double" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="TextBox" type="xs:integer" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="StartSymbol" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="EndSymbol" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:anyAttribute processContents="lax" />
</xs:attributeGroup>
<xs:annotation>
<xs:documentation>
The RedlineGroupType is a set of redline elements grouped together as a single
entity.
</xs:documentation>
</xs:annotation>
<xs:complexType name="RedlineGroupType">
<xs:complexContent>
<xs:extension base="BaseRedlineType">
<xs:sequence>
<xs:choice maxOccurs="unbounded">
<xs:element name="Line" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Rect" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Ellipse" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Polyline" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Polygon" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Arc" type="BaseRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Symbol" type="TextRedlineType" />
<xs:element name="Text" type="TextRedlineType" />
</xs:choice>
</xs:sequence>
<xs:attribute name="Name" type="xs:string" />
<xs:attribute name="Username" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
<xs:attribute name="IconFileName" type="xs:string" use="optional" />
</xs:extension>
</xs:complexContent>
</xs:complexType>
</xs:schema>

### Model Validation

#### Attribute Validation and Manipulation Metadata
The G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION and G3E_VALIDATIONINTERFACE metadata tables control which related features and attributes participate in attribute validation and manipulation operations, whether operations are to occur at placement time or validation time, which values are legal, and possibly which interface objects are to be used for validation and/or manipulation of related attributes. 
Before you configure metadata for attribute validation and manipulation operations, consider which attributes meet the following criteria: 
  * Must be the same between related features
  * Cannot be null
  * Must be within a given range
  * Must fall within a given set of possible values
  * Should be copied from existing features to those being placed


You must also separate attribute operations into three categories:
  * Validation during placement mouse-move operations
  * Validation during model validation
  * Manipulation or copy during placement and edit


Then create the metadata for each operation: 
[G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wu5b0VFREvrf2zqsFMydkQ)
This table controls all relationship attribute validation and manipulation operations.
These are the general steps for configuring the G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION table:
  1. Determine which attributes in related pairs of features are significant, and populate these significant feature pairs and their respective attributes. 
[Examples](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261955)
     * The model requires that connected primary conductors share the same voltage and requires a voltage check at validation time. 
Populate a row in the table with the primary conductor feature number in both the G3E_ACTIVEFNO and G3E_RELATEDFNO fields. Then place the attribute number for voltage in both the G3E_ACTIVEANO and G3E_RELATEDANO fields. 
     * The model requires that pipes of different diameter not be shown as relationship candidates.
Place the feature number of the pipe in the G3E_ACTIVEFNO and G3E_RELATEDFNO fields and the attribute number for diameter in the respective ANO fields. 
  2. Populate the operation control fields:
    1. Set the G3E_MOUSEMOVECANDIDATEFILTER field to Yes (1) to check the attribute pair being validated during placement mouse move operations. 
Validation is done using the component view recordset of the related feature. For mouse move validation to work properly, publish the attribute to be checked on the related feature to the component view. If this field is set to 1, no interface information can be set up because only simple validation operations (set up in G3E_OPERATOR) can be used due to performance issues during mouse move. 
    2. Populate the G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE field with the relationship that is calling the attribute and validation software. 
If the G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE is populated, the calling relationship must match the value in this field or the entry is not processed. If you are not sure how the G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE field is to be used, leave the field Null so that all relationship operations initiate validation of this entry. 
[Example](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261955)
To place a transformer with multiple attribute validation rows, place two rows in G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION, as follows: 
      1. Verify the voltage rating attribute of a light fixture that connects to the transformer.
      2. Ensure that the class attribute of the pole on which the transformer hangs is appropriate.
      3. On each row, specify ownership or node-edge connectivity in the G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE field so that the software does not perform an unnecessary validation. 
    3. Set the G3E_OPERATIONTYPE field for each row to control whether or not the row is executed during: 
Validation—1
Manipulation—2
Validation and manipulation—3
  3. Populate the general validation operation fields for each row.
These fields determine the type of validation to be performed (if not using a relationship attribute interface object), give validation comparison values, and provide error priorities to be returned if a discrepancy is found during validation. 
    1. Populate the G3E_OPERATOR field with a relational operator, such as =, <, or >, or with a group operation (EITHER OR, IN SET). 
    2. Populate the G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE field with the value for comparison.
    3. If the general validation operations are not sufficient for the attribute validation or if you want attribute manipulation operations, populate interface information in the G3E_VINO and G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT fields. 


G3E_VALIDATIONINTERFACE
The [G3E_VALIDATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mjofNzYibqeHFKBQSJveFQ) table holds interface information the software uses to create and execute interface objects. This table links to G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION.G3E_VINO and G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION.G3E_INTERFACEARUMENT. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261955) If interface information is populated for a row, general validation fields are ignored as the interface object does the work that is required. 
For information about the available product interfaces, see [Delivered Relationship Attribute Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sy9iZejet2kjZVL5QuFXoA).

[Attribute Validation Interface Errors](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kKmBMu63xLsKgraFKtwo1w)

#### Attribute Validation and Manipulation
During the placement and edit of related (for example, connected or owned) features and during model validation, attributes of related features can be validated and/or manipulated based on parameters set in metadata. This is useful because related features often share the same attribution to describe attributes like voltage, circuit number, diameter, pressure, and type. You can use the software to maintain these parameters by copying attributes from existing features to features being placed or edited. You can also validate attribution between related and/or potentially related features to ensure that only those features with appropriate attribution are related. 
When using attribute validation during placement, features with opposing attribution can be eliminated from potential relationship candidates or certain attributes eliminated from consideration during [mouse move operations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~sTq6BQTYdrbngf8Q~WGyQ).   
|  Example A fiber cable should not be allowed to connect to copper cables. You can set up parameters in metadata to ensure that only fiber cables are shown as candidates.  When placing a run of primary conductors, all of these conductors might be composed of the same phases. Using the phase number copy functionality, the phase number can be copied from the existing, connecting conductor to the conductor that is being placed. Attributes such as circuit numbers can also be copied.   |  
| --- |  
Attributes can also be checked between related features during model and feature validation to ensure that related features have the proper attributes. You can make comparisons to determine that the voltage between two conductors is the same or to ensure that the voltage between a conductor and a transformer is one value (for the high-voltage side, for example) or another (the low-voltage side, for example). The software can also ensure that a required field, such as inspection code, is populated for a given pole.

[Attribute Validation Interface Errors](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kKmBMu63xLsKgraFKtwo1w)

#### Configuring Model Validation
The G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table contains two entries that affect command processing associated with validation: 
  * [ValidationPriorityFilter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ)
Lets you filter or reduce the errors presented to the user. Use an SQL editor to determine which errors are presented: 
SQL> select * from g3e_validation_error where errorpriority < ValidationPriorityFilter;
All of the resulting rows from G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR for this query are displayed.
  * [ValidationPriority](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ)
Lets you configure the post operation such that even though the validation process may generate errors, the user can still post the data with these errors. Use an SQL editor to determine which errors are allowed: 
SQL> select * from g3e_validation_error where errorpriority <= ValidationPriority;
If this query returns any rows from G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR, the job may not be posted.
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259068) G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR is representative of a table of errors. ErrorPriority is a column in the G3E_VALIDATION_ERROR table that contains the priority of the error. 


Related Topics
[Model Validation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dTPnspzwT2tlaDn2jOUheQ)
[The Validation Process](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9PPVtTP3frVFYjbk7fQ2yA)

#### The Validation Process
The validation process begins with the selection of features for validation. The selection process varies with the command that initiates the validation. 
Once the feature set is defined, each unique feature instance is analyzed. Deleted features, which are features with no components based on a delete operation during the job, are not validated. 
Feature Structure Validation
Compares the feature data to the metadata definitions for required and repeating components. Any alternate required component definitions are considered as well. 
Attribute Validation
Compares the feature data to the metadata definitions for the entries in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) for each component of the feature. This validation includes checks for required attributes, comparison of values in domain or foreign key tables, and execution of functional interface validation methods. These are client-side validations based on NetWorks Core metadata. No Oracle schema validations are performed. 
Relationship Validation
  * Determines the relationships in which the feature participates.
  * Executes each validate method on those relationships.
  * Performs the associated attribute and relationship geometry validations (if the feature does participate in the relationship). 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259066) If a feature is configured for a child-to-parent relationship, for example, but does not currently participate in that relationship, the relationship attribute interfaces do not execute. 


Error Reporting 
Queues errors encountered during each step of the analysis and displays the errors and the feature keys of the features involved in the data grid. The component identifier (G3E_CNO) and occurrence (G3E_CID) are from the first component that contains an edit in this job. These values do not necessarily match the component that generates the error. All errors for the feature instance have the same component and occurrence values. 
Error Format
NetWorks Core software denotes errors by priority where a priority of one (1) as the most severe and four (4) as the least severe. The text strings P1, P2, P3, and P4 are used by the software. You should follow a similar convention with your custom validation rules. It is acceptable to introduce additional levels such as P5 and P6.

[The Validation Process](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9PPVtTP3frVFYjbk7fQ2yA)
