#### Validating Metadata Changes

##### Creating a Metadata Validation Folder
A metadata validation folder is required for validating and publishing metadata. The G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY oracle directory ([created when you initially created the database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg)) object is used for the metadata validation log file folder. This value is defined in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME field DatabaseLocalDirectory. 
To verify that the correct value is defined, use this query:
SQL> SELECT G3E_VALUE FROM G3E_GENERALPARAMETER WHERE G3E_NAME= ‘DatabaseLocalDirectory';
To use Metadata Explorer, use the following workflow:
  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Metadata Administration > General Parameter. 
  2. Select and edit the DatabaseLocalDirectory parameter with the Oracle Directory name G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY. 


Related Topics
[Validating Metadata Changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDGAu21AUa_I~XZxIPvJzw)
[Reviewing Metadata Changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1fHOxa1K2OT_BlU4YSWPrw)

##### Reviewing Metadata Changes
Before validating, publishing, and posting your metadata changes to the database, use the Review command to view any metadata edits since you last published. 
  * To review the current metadata changes:


  1. From the Administrative menu, select Metadata Versions. 
  2. On the Metadata Versions dialog box, click Review. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/88M93YPMJREYMupbLjbfcw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=ca77ae832a21c98e&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. Review the list of pending metadata edits. The Pending Changes list contains:   
|  Column  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Type  |  The type of change found, Insert/Update, or Delete.  |  
|  Table Name  |  The name of the table where the edit was found.  |  
|  Information  |  List of attributes and values edited. A semicolon is used to separate list items. For example, G3E_Type=ServiceExtension; G3E_FNO=22; G3E_DTNO = 105.   |  
|  Edit Date  |  The date created or last edited.  |  
  4. To save your list of pending changes to a .csv file:
    1. Check Save as CSV file. 
    2. Type the location and name of the .csv file. You can also click Browse to select an existing file. 
If you checked Save as CSV file, the file is created.

##### Validating Metadata
Metadata validation creates a log file that you can review so you can make corrections to the metadata tables if necessary. 
  * To validate metadata:


  1. Verify that the path in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_VALUE for DatabaseUNCDirectory is accessible. 
  2. Use an SQL editor to execute the following depending on the metadata to be validated:
To validate all metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgmetadatavalidation.validatemetadata; 
Errors will be be written to a file named mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate placement and analysis metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateAdminCorePlaceAnalysis; 
Errors will be be written to a file named AdminCorePlaceAnalysis_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate styles, legends, and dialogs execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidatePresentatnStyleDialog; 
Errors will be be written to a file named PresentatnStyleDialog_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate relationship and trace metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateRelationsTrace; 
Errors will be be written to a file named RelationsTrace_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate job metdata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateJobWorkManagement; 
Errors will be be written to a file named JobWorkManagement_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate electric metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateElectricTables; 
Errors will be be written to a file named ElectricTables_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate inspection metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateFieldTables; 
Errors will be be written to a file named FieldTables_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate Pipeline metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidatePipelineTables; 
Errors will be be written to a file named PipelineTables_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate Communications metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateCommTables; 
Errors will be be written to a file named CommTables_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate dimension, allocation, duct, and export metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateMultiIndDataModel; 
Errors will be be written to a file named MultiIndDataModel_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate plotting and role metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidatePlottingRole; 
Errors will be be written to a file named PlottingRole_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate interactive trace metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateInteractiveTrace; 
Errors will be be written to a file named InteractiveTrace_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate reqired metadata execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.ValidateRequiredMetadata; 
Errors will be be written to a file named RequiredMetadata_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
To validate and enable metadata constraints execute the following
SQL> execute mg3epkgMetadataValidation.EnableMetadataConstraints; 
Errors will be be written to a file named MetadataConstraints_mdval.txt in the physical folder that is associated with the Oracle directory object (G3E_DATABASELOCALDIRECTORY) 
For client access to these error files, use the UNC path defined in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER DatabaseUNCDirectory. 
  3. Review the error files. 
  4. [Use Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to make any necessary corrections to the metadata tables.

#### Validating Z Values in Geometry
The ValidateZ utility isolates invalid Z-values in geometries based on [metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DjQodICbl7r_MxBx3AMSng). It creates a log table, G3E_VALIDATEZ, and inserts the geometry that has invalid Z values into the log table. You can identify where the geometry is from based on the data in the log table. The G3E_VALIDATEZ.G3E_TABLE column shows which table the invalid geometry is from. The other columns in the log table identify rows from the original table. 
  * To validate Z values:


  1. Load the package into the database.
     * SQL> @<G/Technology installation path>\PLSQL\ValidateZ\ValidateZ.sql;
     * SQL> @<G/Technology installation path>\PLSQL\ValidateZ\prvtValidateZ.plb;
  2. Use an SQL editor to execute the following scripts: 
     * If validating Z values in a geometries within a specific table in the database:
SQL> EXECUTE ValidateZ.ValidateByTable('<Table Name>');
<Table Name> is the value in G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE or the MODIFICATIONLOG table. If it is graphic component table, the procedure validates all geometries in the component table and its catalog table if it exists. 
     * if validating Z values in a geometries within all the tables in the database::
SQL> EXECUTE ValidateZ.ValidateAll;
This statement validates geometries within all graphic component tables, and in their catalog tables if they exist and the ModificationLog table.

#### Validation Errors

##### Attribute Validation Interface Errors
The circuit number validation failed for the component <Component name> related to the component <related component name>.
Cause: The software compares the circuit identifier values in the current feature and the related features. If one of the attribute values in the active or related feature is Null, this error is generated. If both values are Null, the validation passes. To accommodate switchable features, two fields typically contain the circuit identifiers. For non-switchable features, only one attribute must be populated. It must match the identifier of the related feature. For switchable features, both attributes must be populated and must match the identifiers in the related features. 
Priority: Configurable 
Phase Validation failed for feature <feature name> <FID> with phase <phase value>.
Cause: The software compares the phases found in the active feature with the phases found in each of the related features at each node. Validation passes if all of the phases of the active feature are found in the phases of related features at a given node. If a phase is not found in the union of the phases of the related features for at least one node, the error is reported. Neutral phases (N or n) are ignored. 
Priority:
The simple copy validation failed for the component <Component name> related to the component <related component name>.
Cause: The software compares the value in the current feature to the related feature. If one or both contain Null values, this error is generated. If the values are not Null but do not match, this error is generated. 
Priority: Configurable

Priority: P1 
<Component name> component (number <G3E_CNO>) of feature number <G3E_FNO> has illegal repeating instances.

<Component name> component (number <G3E_CNO>) of feature number <G3E_FNO> is required.
Cause: [G3E_FEATUREPLACEMENT_OPTABLE.G3E_REQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Dh4b6uAhZhz2mTi6vy7snA) = 1 and there is no alternate required component specified. 
Priority: P1 
<Component name> component (number <G3E_CNO>) or <Component name> alternate component (number <G3E_CNO>) of feature number <G3E_FNO> is required.
Cause: An alternate required component is specified but does not exist where the original component was marked as required (G3E_FEATUREPLACEMENT_OPTABLE.G3E_REQUIRED = 1) 
Priority: P1 
Error returned by functional interface object with ProgID: <identifier of the object>.
This is reported for a catastrophic error with creating the object.

Priority: P1 
<username> attribute of component <Component name> contains values that do not exist in field <field name> of foreign key table <table name>.
Cause: [G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE.G3E_FOREIGNKEYTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/14u1vqSTxyc1WohRdZxqqQ) is populated, but the value in the feature's attribute is not found in that table. 
Priority: P1 
<username> attribute of component <Component Name> contains values that do not exist in field <field name> of domain table <table name>.
Cause: [G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE.G3E_DOMAINTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/14u1vqSTxyc1WohRdZxqqQ) is populated, but the value in the feature's attribute is not found in that table. 
Priority: P1 
<username> attribute of component <Component name> is required.
Cause: [G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE.G3E_REQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/14u1vqSTxyc1WohRdZxqqQ) = 1 for this attribute, and the value is Null. 
Priority: P1 
Error creating or using relationship support interface object named <username> (ProgID: <identifier of the object>).
This is reported for a catastrophic error with creating the object.
Cause: [G3E_FEATRELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qoDmMUYKqAIPI2n8ub4M1A) is populated for components within this feature. But, a failure occurs during software execution, and the interface object cannot return an error message.

##### Functional Interface Errors
Each [functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) defines its own semantics. Since you can add your own interface objects, this list may not include all the errors a user might encounter. 
General Functional Interface Errors
Error creating functional interface <ProgID>
This is reported for a catastrophic error with creating the object.
Cause: A failure occurs when the validation software attempts to create the functional interface object. 
Priority: P1 
Error initializing functional interface <ProgID> - <Error description>
This is reported for a catastrophic error with initializing the object.
Cause: A failure occurs when the validation software attempts to initialize the functional interface object. 
Priority: P1 
Error using functional interface <ProgID> - <Error description>
This is reported when a software error occurs during the processing of the functional interface object. The error returned from the object is appended. 
Cause: The functional interface object encounters an error during processing. 
Priority: P1 
Error recording functional interface results for <ProgID> - <Error description>
This is reported when a software error occurs during the recording of errors from the functional interface object. 
Cause: The validation software cannot properly read errors from the functional interface object 
Priority: P1

The NetWorks Core relationship functionality returns these errors: 
Dimensioning
As in the dimensioning functional interface, the relationship software performs a series of comparisons between the dimension geometry and the geometry of the related features. 
The dimension is not coincident with the related feature, the expected component of the related feature does not exist.
Priority: P4 
Invalid base relationship for orthogonal dimension.
Priority: P2 
The dimension is not coincident with the base component.
Priority: P2

Priority: P4

Priority: P4

Priority: P1

Priority: P4 
The dimension secondary base component was not found in the database.
Priority: P1 
The dimensioned component was not found in the database.
Priority: P1 
The dimension is not connected to any base component.
Priority: P4 
Detail
Detail ID value is Null
Cause: When validating a detail component, the detail identifier value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail ID value is 0. This value should be non-zero.
Cause: When validating a detail component, the detail identifier value must not be zero. 
Priority: P1 
Detail component exists in invalid detail window.
Cause: When validating a detail component, the detail identifier value must correspond to a detail reference feature that can contain this feature, as defined in [G3E_DETAILMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e2tt5qpeYNY9MM7Wm73iAw). 
Priority: P1 
Detail username is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail username value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail legend number is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail legend number value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail MBR XLo is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail MBR XLo value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail MBR XHigh is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail MBR XHigh value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail MBR YLo is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail MBR YLo value must not be Null. 
Priority: P1 
Detail MBR YHigh is Null
Cause: When validating a detail referencing component, the detail MBR YHigh value must not be Null 
Priority: P1 
Node-Edge Connectivity
The feature is not part of the connected model and a connection is required.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifiers are zero, null or the component does not exist and [G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg) = 1. 
Priority: P1 
The feature is not part of the connected model and a connection is optional.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifiers are zero, null or the component does not exist and G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 0. 
Priority: P4 
The connectivity (node identifier value) is invalid or no longer exists in the database.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifier is not found in the connectivity table. You can get this error in the Post Partial command because the related feature is not part of the partial posting operation. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 1 Else P4 
This feature has more than one other feature connected at node <node identifier>. Only one feature should be connected to this node.
Cause: Determines the number of feature pairs that share this node identifier. This only occurs in the pipeline connectivity model. This error is reported if more than one pair is found. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
The node 1 and node 2 connectivity fields for <feature name> <feature identifier> have different identifier values. One node features should have identical node 1 and node 2 identifier values.
Cause: A one node device has two node values. Both node values should be identical for one node devices. 
Priority: : P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
The distance between <feature class> <feature identifier> and <feature class> <feature identifier> is <actual distance>. This exceeds the MaxOffset value of <maximum offset value>.
Cause: Compares the geometry of the active feature to the related features. This error is reported if the distance between endpoints and related features is greater than the value specified in G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_MAXOFFSET. 
Priority: Uses the value specified in G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORIT. If this is NULL, uses the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority. 
The node value <node identifier> that connects <active feature name-FID> and <related feature name-FID> is not on graphically adjacent endpoints.
Cause: Assumes that node identifier one of a linear corresponds to the start point of the geometry, and that node identifier two corresponds to the endpoint of the geometry. This test compares the distance between the expected points to the actual related features. This error is reported if the beginning point of the line is not a shorter distance to the related feature at node identifier one than the endpoint of the line. This check is performed to help ensure the presentation of data in the [graphical node-edge connectivity dialog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VfbJLUnk4lGa5XMUeX83Jw) is logical and understandable. Even though the node identifiers may be reversed from this definition, the software properly traces the network, but the graphical node-edge connectivity presentation may be difficult to understand. 
Priority: P5 or the value specified in G3E_ADD_REL_PARAMS_OPTABLE for the entry <RNO>-end pointValidationPriority 
The node 1 and node 2 connectivity fields for <feature name and identifier> have different identifier values. Single-node features should have identical node 1 and node 2 identifier values.
Cause: Compares the values in the node 1 and node 2 identifier fields in the connectivity component for the feature. This error is reported if these values are not the same for a single-node feature. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
Phase Validation failed for feature <feature name> <feature identifier> with phase <phase value>
Cause: This error is reported if phase validation is defined for the feature being validated and the phase values are out of range with related features. 
Priority: P4 
Node-Ordered Connectivity
Connecting feature ID <value> of feature >feature class> (FNO of <feature number>) has been deleted.
Cause: Attempts to locate the feature specified by the FNO/FID values stored in the relationship data of the active feature. The feature cannot be found. This may be the result of a post partial operation that does not include the related feature. 
Priority: P1 
Edge feature not connected in Node-Ordered Connectivity
Cause: No node ordered connectivity record exists in this feature. 
Priority: P1 
The edge feature has more than one connectivity record in the Node-Ordered Connectivity model. It should have just one.
Cause: There is more than one node ordered connectivity record for this feature 
Priority: P1 
The edge feature is not connected for <Node Ordered Connectivity relationship instance name>.
Cause: The FNO and FID fields that define the feature connected to this edge feature are 0. 
Priority: P1 
Ownership
The parent identifier is null and is required.
Cause: Compares the attribute of the active feature that contains the parent identifier. It is a Null value. This error is shown only if [G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) = 1 or 3 
Priority: P1 
The optional parent identifier is null.
Cause: Compares the attribute of the active feature that contains the parent identifier. It is a Null value. This error is shown only if [G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) = 0 or 2 
Priority: P4 
The parent identifier is zero and is required.
Cause: Compares the attribute of the active feature that contains the parent identifier. It is a zero value. This error is shown only if [G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) = 1 or 3 
Priority: P1 
The optional parent identifier is zero.
Cause: Compares the attribute of the active feature that contains the parent identifier. It is a zero value. This error is shown only if [G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) = 0 or 2 
Priority: P4 
The parent identifier (G3E_ID value) invalid or no longer exists in the database. In a partial post operation, the parent may not be posted yet and is not included in the partial post selection.
Cause: Attempts to locate the feature specified by the identifier value stored in the relationship data of the active feature. The feature cannot be found. This may be the result of a post partial operation that does not include the related feature. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 1 or 3 Else P4 
The distance between <feature class> <feature identifier> and <feature class> <feature identifier> is <actual distance>. This exceeds the MaxOffset value of <maximum offset value>.
Cause: Compares the geometry of the active feature to the related features. This error is reported if the distance between endpoints and related features is greater than the value specified in [G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_MAXOFFSET](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ). 
Priority: Uses the value specified in G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY. If this is NULL, uses the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority. 
Many-to-Many Ownership
The distance between <feature class><identifier> and <related feature class> <identifier> exceeds the MaxOffset value of <max offset parameter>.
Cause: Compares the geometry of the active feature to the related features. This error is reported if the distance between endpoints and related features is greater than the value specified in [G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP.G3E_MAXOFFSET](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ). 
Priority: Uses the value specified in G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY. If this is NULL, uses the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority. 
At least one parent feature is required for this child feature.
Cause: No parent feature was found for the child being validated. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 1 
This child feature has no related parent
Cause: No parent feature was found for the child being validated.

Too many (<count>) related features in relationship specified as OneToMany.

### Modification Tracking

#### Enhanced Modification Tracking
In order to manipulate data faster, this enhancement prevents the modification log from being populated. It eases the administrative efforts when performing admin tasks and smooths deployment of the Oracle database management tools (monitoring and the like). 
Granting Roles and Privileges
NetWorks Core Admin provides predefined roles that can be assigned to users. These roles also include privileges that are essential for different levels of access. See [Granting Roles and Privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KfGUZVurERUNF384ngn2ug) for more details. 
For modification tracking, the following new role is available:  
|  Role  |  Privileges  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  NOMODIFICATIONTRACKING  |  This role is checked in the Modification Tracking Triggers (see [Modification Tracking Triggers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yx6ZJuobhZM62uk4hDv2Vg) for more details). Modification logging and triggers will be disabled when this role is granted to a user.   |  
Technical Information
  * A new g3e_commonutils.IsRoleGranted function checks if a role is granted to the active user. 
  * The GDOTRIGGERS package is modified to add the following lines at the beginning of AMT triggers: 


IF g3e_commonutils.IsRoleGranted('NOMODIFICATIONTRACKING') = 1 THEN
return;
END IF;
  * NOMODIFICATIONTRACKING role is created automatically during NetWorks Core upgrade. 
  * AMT triggers are automatically recreated during NetWorks Core upgrade.

#### Installing Modification Tracking
You must create the MODIFICATIONLOG table and install the [triggers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261908) needed for modification tracking. Make sure that you have already populated the G3E_COMPONENT, G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION, and G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION metadata tables. Modification triggers end in AMT. 
A piece of code that tells a database management system what other actions to perform when certain SQL statements have been executed. 
Use an SQL editor to install the following packages and to execute the procedures:
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\g3etriggers.sql;
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\prvtg3etriggers.plb;
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\g3ecreatemodlog.sql;
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\prvtg3ecreatemodlog.plb;
SQL> execute g3e_create_modlog.createmodificationlog;
SQL> execute g3e_create_modlog.createmodlogsequence;
SQL> execute gdotriggers.create_gdotriggers;

#### Modification Tracking Metadata
The modification tracking triggers and the procedures that create them use metadata to determine their behavior. You must populate the tables listed below to get the correct behavior. These tables define the component views and the components that belong to them. Because the procedures that create the modification tracking triggers use the optimized tables, you must publish metadata before you can create the modification tracking triggers. 
  * [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw)
  * [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw)
  * [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/X9EcOVIWIsiQzIZGdzin3A)

#### Modification Tracking Triggers
The first step in deltas processing is accomplished with database triggers on all components that participate in component views. These triggers, which are called modification tracking triggers, are generated with a PL/SQL package, GDOTRIGGERS. 
After every change to the database, whether the change is an insert, update, or delete, the modification tracking triggers put an entry into the [MODIFICATIONLOG table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4SuOwTsXAXirwxZCrM8VSQ). Modification tracking triggers delete previous entries for each specific record. The entries are obsolete because they have been overridden with the database changes. The triggers mark their entries as new in the MODIFICATIONLOG by putting a 0 in the PROCESSED_FLAG field. 
The modification tracking triggers are defined as after row level triggers on a specific table. They fire after every insert, update, or delete on that table for each row affected by the insert, update, or delete. 
The modification tracking triggers are created and installed using a database package called GDOTRIGGERS. This package is installed by executing the following commands in an SQL editor: 
SQL> @<PATH>/G3ETRIGGERS.SQL;  
SQL> @<PATH>/PRVTG3ETRIGGERS.PLB;
where <PATH> is the location of the database packages for your NetWorks Core installation. 
Installing on a Schema
The modification tracking triggers must be installed on the entire schema. To install the modification tracking triggers for the entire schema, use an SQL editor to execute the following command: 
SQL> execute GDOTRIGGERS.CREATE_GDOTRIGGERS;
Installing for Tables
To install the modification tracking triggers for a single table, use an SQL editor to execute the following command: 
SQL> execute GDOTRIGGERS.CREATE_GDOTRIGGERS('<TABLE_NAME>');
where <TABLE_NAME> is the name of the database table from [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). 
GDOTRIGGERS.CREATE_GDOTRIGGERS creates the trigger <TABLE_NAME>AMT for every graphic and attribute table. . 
Enabling and Disabling
The GDOTRIGGERS package has a convenient way to enable and disable all modification triggers. True means the triggers are enabled. False means they are disabled. 
To enable all modification tracking triggers, type the following in an SQL editor:
SQL> execute gdotriggers.ENABLEMODTRACKTRIGGERS(TRUE);
To disable all modification tracking triggers, type the following in an SQL editor:
SQL> execute gdotriggers.ENABLEMODTRACKTRIGGERS(FALSE);
The modification triggers check if the NOMODIFICATIONTRACKING role is granted to the current database user. If the role is granted, the modification triggers do nothing; modification logging is disabled.

#### The MODIFICATIONLOG

##### For Deltas Resynchronization
To resynchronize deltas, UpdateDeltas determines which component views are affected by the component records that the modification tracking triggers put in deltas. It then adds records to the MODIFICATIONLOG to describe the changes to those component views. The MODIFICATIONLOG stores component view data to reduce repetitive database queries to satisfy multiple client requests for the same record. 
The MODIFICATIONLOG contains three kinds of records based on the PROCESSED_FLAG:
  * Records with a PROCESSED_FLAG of 0 are inserted into the MODIFICATIONLOG by the [modification tracking triggers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yx6ZJuobhZM62uk4hDv2Vg). The PL/SQL procedure UpdateDeltas uses these seed records as the basis to put new records in the MODIFICATIONLOG to describe the component view data affected by this particular entry in the MODIFICATIONLOG. 
  * Records with a PROCESSED_FLAG of 1 are seed records UpdateDeltas has seen and processed, but they are not useful for the actual resynchronization of deltas on the client-side. 
  * Records with a PROCESSED_FLAG of 2 contain the actual new component view attribute and geometry data for a component view record. These are the records used to keep client-side deltas current. 


For deltas resynchronization, the following columns in the MODIFICATIONLOG are not used: 
  * MODIFIEDDATE
  * G3E_ID


Furthermore, G3E_CID is not used for original seed records, but it is loaded correctly by UpdateDeltas for loading the additional records whose PROCESSED_FLAG is 2. In fact, G3E_ID and G3E_CID cannot be correctly loaded for many component seed entries. 
If a certain change is due to a graphic component, the G3E_ID and G3E_CID that are loaded by the modification tracking triggers would be useful because a component view gets its identity from the graphic component over which it is built. Conversely, if a change is due to an attribute component, the modification tracking trigger does not know to which graphic record the change corresponds. The G3E_FIDs match, but the G3E_CIDs and G3E_IDs do not because the component view gets its identity from the graphic component, not from any attribute component. 
The G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO in the original seed records are used to determine in which component views this record participates. G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO are used to join on the G3E_COMPVIEWCOMP_OPTABLE for this purpose.

##### Job and Master Changes
Sometimes users want to see only the changes made to the current job, and sometimes they want to see both job changes and master changes. Master changes are those database updates that become permanent, non-job related changes. This happens when a job is posted. 
The NetWorks Core client software makes assumptions as to when these two operations occur. Under some circumstances, the client makes the screen reflect only job changes; in others, the screen reflects master changes as well. 
When a user places a feature, NetWorks Core displays only those items that affect the current job. If another user has posted a job with a lot of features near the feature the first user is placing, the first user does not see the posted data when placement is finished, and deltas are resynchronized. 
If on the other hand, the user changes the job context, NetWorks Core assumes the user wants to see master changes and displays the posted data. 
If one user places a feature in a job and then another user places a feature in the same job, the second user sees the new feature from the first user since it belongs to the same job. NetWorks Core does not resynchronize the client with changes from only one user. Note that the Refresh from Server command displays both job and master changes. 
Watermarks
Two [watermarks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261629)
Highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. When DDCs are published, they are burned with the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This is referred to as the watermark. Queries to the MODIFICATIONLOG use this watermark to limit the records returned. These queries yield new highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER/watermarks to be used in subsequent queries.

##### Last MODIFICATIONLOG Keys (Watermarks)
Once the DDC is published, master entries in the MODIFICATIONLOG are irrelevant for the component views within the DDC because they are already included. Since the DDC is a collection of files, you can selectively publish these files. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261910) The following discussion applies to each file individually. 
To manage the process of ignoring data that is already included in the DDC from the master database, each DDC is branded with the highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER from the MODIFICATIONLOG when the publish is started. This highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER is referred to as the last MODIFICATIONLOG key, watermark, or high watermark. Its existence signals the Deltas subsystem to ignore MODIFICATIONLOG entries up to that point and to form its queries only on entries newer than the last MODIFICATIONLOG key. Every time Deltas resynchronizes, it obtains a new key from the MODIFICATIONLOG and uses that for the base of its next query. The watermark, even within one session, gets higher and higher in the queries issued to the database. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261910) It is recommended that you record the watermark when you publish DDCs. 
Any new watermark is read at the beginning of processing, be it publish or resynchronization. This ensures the processing of a lowest common denominator. Entries made after the high watermark but before the end of processing are processed during the current pass because the queries request MODIFICATIONLOG entries higher than the old watermark. They are processed during the next pass as well, because their modification numbers are higher than the new high watermark. 
This causes no conflict because the Deltas subsystem treats that entry as modifying a record with its own data. On a small scale, the performance is not noticeably affected. However, if a publish is done while some large jobs are posting data, newly posted entries might be processed twice and cause performance to degrade the first time users log on after the publish. For this reason, you should avoid publishing during intense posting activities. 
If you publish each DDC file independently, each DDC file has its own watermark. The deltas processing handles this situation, but its startup queries are more complicated because it has various beginning watermarks to query against within the same query. Such queries, which are performed only the first time a user logs on after the [PersistedDeltas.dlt](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xdzsZaesK_i6EnQA~XWRHw) file has become stale, might slightly affect software performance. This situation does not occur often.

##### MODIFICATIONLOG Conflicts
Since all NetWorks Core clients access the same UpdateDeltas PL/SQL procedure in the database, you might expect race conditions and bottlenecks. However, NetWorks Core avoided these issues in its technique of accessing the database.

##### Purging the MODIFICATIONLOG
When a component view changes, or if the MODIFICATIONLOG should become corrupted, you must purge the incorrect component view records from the MODIFICATIONLOG. These are the records with the PROCESSED_FLAG of 2 (two) that have been put in by UpdateDeltas. If you know the component view that has been changed, execute the following: 
SQL> execute G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.SyncToComponentView(<'ComponentViewName'>);
If there are too many component views, or you are not sure which component views were changed, you can perform the operation on the entire MODIFICATIONLOG: 
SQL> execute G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.ResetToDatabase;
These two procedures call [UpdateDeltas](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iO3C34QTCkhOByr1Q~SUBA).

##### Short-Term Transaction Features
Short-term transaction features are features placed within a job context that are entered into the database as master changes as soon as they are placed. Short-term transaction features are available immediately without posting.   
|  Example Design areas are typically short- term transaction features because defining design areas as short-term transaction features lets all concurrent users see where work is occurring.   |  
| --- |  
To process these features correctly, the query to the MODIFICATIONLOG by client-side Deltas resynchronization must contain an additional clause in the job part of the query. Such features do not have LTT views installed on the data tables. 
A feature's components must be homogeneous with respect to this definition. That is, if one component is modeled as short-term transaction feature, then all components of the feature must be defined as such.

##### Trimming Obsolete Records
Two types of records become obsolete and need to be trimmed from the MODIFICATIONLOG, master records, and job records. 
Trimming Obsolete Master Records
As changes are made to facility data, they are recorded in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This table contains the delta between the master records published in the DDC files and the records in the data tables. Only master records are published into the DDC files. Master records in the MODIFICATIONLOG are identified by an LTT_ID value of 0. 
After publishing, the records in the MODIFICATIONLOG for master deltas are no longer needed for the Deltas subsystem because deltas between the DDC files and the database no longer exist. So, records in the MODIFICATIONLOG with an LTT_ID of 0 may be deleted selectively after data publishing. 
You must consider the following when selecting master records to delete from the MODIFICATIONLOG:
  * NetWorks Core lets you publish the DDC to a preparatory location (<PrepCCMPaths>) while users are on the system and then switch the <CurrentCCMPaths> with the <PrepCCMPaths> so users begin using the newly published DDC the next time they log in. This means that records are being entered into MODIFICATIONLOG as you publish. 
Therefore, you must not delete those master records entered into the MODIFICATIONLOG after you began publishing. You must delete only master records that existed in the MODIFICATIONLOG before you began publishing. The best way to do this is to use an SQL editor to obtain the maximum modification number from MODIFICATIONLOG before publishing. 
SQL> select max(MODIFICATIONNUMBER) from MODIFICATIONLOG;
After publishing, use an SQL editor to delete those master records with MODIFICATIONNUMBER less than or equal to the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER recorded before you started the publish. 
SQL> delete from MODIFICATIONLOG where LTT_ID=0 and MODIFICATIONNUMBER< <max number + 1>;
The max number refers to the integral part of the MODIFICATIONNUMBER you obtained from the previous query. Depending on the SQL tool you use, there might be a decimal part to the MODIFICATIONNUMBER that you should ignore before adding 1 (one). 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257579) Posting or short-term transaction changes could be occurring while issuing the query to determine the watermark/MODIFICATIONNUMBER used to trim the modification log. These changes might not be committed to the database yet, and they might be less than the MODIFICATIONNUMBER you discovered with the query. Therefore, you need to either ensure that all posting and short term transactions are finished before issuing the query, or chose a lower watermark to account for either circumstance. 
  * If you have distributed the DDC to more than one DDC server site, do not delete the master delta records from the MODIFICATIONLOG until all those sites have incrementally published (or received the new DDC from the central site). Since each site publishes at a different time, you must only delete those master records that existed in the MODIFICATIONLOG before the first site began publishing. 
  * The same applies to DDCs on field machines. If masters are cleared out without replicating data (including new DDCs) to field machines, the display of new master data might be incorrect. Either the field user has to be aware of this issue or the field user has to replicate data after the MODIFICATIONLOG is trimmed. 


As soon as users begin editing in the database after a publish, new deltas are created in the MODIFICATIONLOG. 
As new records are added to the MODIFICATIONLOG, a new MODIFICATIONLOG number (column MODIFICATIONNUMBER) is generated from an Oracle sequence. Do not change that sequence as you clean out or truncate the MODIFICATIONLOG. 
Trimming Obsolete Job Records
The same technique used with the masters cannot be used with job Deltas because they are not published into the DDC. The job delta records in the MODIFICATIONLOG are still needed until the job is posted or discarded. 
The act of posting or discarding job edits trims the job records from the MODIFICATIONLOG. So, very little trimming of job deltas is required. However, there might be scenarios in which some cleaning up of job deltas is necessary: 
  * Jobs that have been forgotten. In this case, the job has data throughout the database and not just in the MODIFICATIONLOG. Those jobs should be manually discarded and closed using NetWorks Core. This way the MODIFICATIONLOG is automatically trimmed. The manual step is necessary because software cannot determine if a job is forgotten and needs to be cleaned up, or if it is just old and needs to be preserved. 
  * Jobs that have been discarded and closed in previous versions of NetWorks Core. Previous versions did not trim the MODIFICATIONLOG as an integral part of discarding job edits. Therefore, there could be residual entries in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This situation is discovered by the lack of an entry in the LTT_IDENTIFIERS table for those records. These entries can be cleaned up with the following SQL: 
SQL> Delete from MODIFICATIONLOG M where not exists (select NULL from LTT_IDENTIFIERS L where L.LTT_ID = M.LTT_ID);


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257579) Discard by Feature ID does not trim records from the MODIFICATIONLOG for that job. Any user of that job has data in the Client Deltas system for that FID in that job. Discard by Feature ID actually places records in the MODIFICATIONLOG like Undo. These records tell the Client Deltas system how to undo the data for that FID in that job.

#### The Persisted Deltas File

##### Correcting Stale Persisted Deltas
The publish operation invalidates a [PersistedDeltas.dlt file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xdzsZaesK_i6EnQA~XWRHw), but the software detects this condition and adjusts accordingly by ignoring its contents. 
The PersistedDeltas.dlt file can become invalid without the software detecting the invalid condition under the following circumstances: 
  * The database crashes and must be restored.
  * The MODIFICATIONLOG has been fixed manually to change or delete invalid, obsolete, or non-used entries (though there is little reason to do so). 
  * G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.ResetToDatabase or SyncToComponentView has been run without republishing.


To fix an invalid persisted deltas file, do the following:
  * Delete the persisted deltas file if you are not using the [Centralized Persisted Deltas Service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/l7posd6nmSB_U5uOTad9sw). 
  * Stop and restart the NetWorks Core[ Persisted Deltas Service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/l7posd6nmSB_U5uOTad9sw) if you are using the Centralized Persisted Deltas Service. 
  * Republish the map files, especially if you have run G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.ResetToDatabase or SyncToComponentView.

##### Setting up a Central Persisted Deltas File

###### Centralized Persisted Deltas Service Interactive Configuration
From the NetWorks Core[ setup tree](javascript:;), select Persisted Deltas Service. Follow the prompts to install the Persisted Deltas Service. When the installation is complete, the Configuration section in Hexagon Setup Manager displays the word Configure. Click Configure and follow the prompts to complete the configuration process.   
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/483540) The [configuration wizards](javascript:;) for each application or service stops and/or restart the application and service appropriately, depending upon the option selected in a configuration wizard.   |

###### Centralized Persisted Deltas Service Manual Configuration
Use the steps listed below to perform manual installation and maintenance of the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service: 
  * Installing 
  * Registering 
  * Optional: Reconfiguring 
  * Deleting all the PersistedDeltas.dlt files 
  * Uninstalling


  * To install and run the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service:


If required, map a drive to the NetWorks Core deployment share. 
  1. From the command prompt, type the following:
Setup.exe /s GTechnology /ni ACCEPT_EULA=1 ADDLOCAL=Persisted_Deltas_Service
  2. On the server, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following at a command prompt: 
CreatePersistedDeltas /Install
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/483551)
  3. Type the username, password, and configuration name.
  4. Type the interval in minutes to produce the PersistedDeltas.dlt. 
  5. Check the Report number of deltas in Event Log box to record the total number of deltas written to the PersistedDeltas.dlt. 


  * To register the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service:


  1. At a command prompt, type the following:
CreatePersistedDeltas/Service
  2. On the Control Panel, navigate to Services. 
  3. Right-click NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service and select Properties. 
  4. Click the Log On tab. 
  5. Click This Account and verify that the log-on credentials are those of a user with access to the mapfile server. 
  6. Set the Startup Type to Automatic. 
  7. Click OK. 
  8. Right-click the service name and select Start. 
  9. Reconfigure the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service. 


  * To reconfigure the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service (Optional): 


Use these command line options to reconfigure the CreatePersistedDeltas service in a batch process and schedule tasks for running multiple configurations. 
  1. Stop the CreatePersistedDeltas service:
Open a command window and type NET STOP CreatePersistedDeltas
  2. Reconfigure the persisted deltas:
At the command prompt, type CreatePersistedDeltas/Reconfigure <Username> <Password> <Configuration> <Interval> <LogDeltas>
Where: 
<Configuration> = the database name.
<Interval> = time in minutes between swapping files (5 minutes is the recommended minimum). 
<LogDeltas> = 0 (Do Not report) or -1 (report) details related to the total number of deltas written to the PersistedDeltas.dlt in the Event log.   
|  Example CreatePersistedDeltas /Reconfigure SMITH PASS1 ALLTEST 10 -1  |  
| --- |  
  3. Start the CreatePersistedDeltas service:
At the command prompt, type NET START CreatePersistedDeltas.
Although validation is not performed for the /Reconfigure arguments, if there is an incorrect number of arguments, the following error is logged in the Event log: 
Incorrect options on the command line for Reconfigure. Use /Reconfigure <UserName> <Password> <Configuration> <Interval> <LogDeltas>. 


  * To delete all the PersistedDeltas.dlt files (the limit is 10): 


Stop and restart the service:
  1. On the Control Panel, navigate to Services. 
  2. Right-click the service name, select Stop, and then Start. 
OR
Click Restart. 


  * To uninstall the service


Stop the service, and type the following at the command prompt:
CreatePersistedDeltas/UnregServer
If You Encounter Problems
Errors caused by the service are written to the operating system event log. Errors are also written to the optional PersistedDeltasTrace.txt log and to the optional DeltasTrace.txt log file. See [Creating Log Files](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NKHNIHQKDhLoGtt_Cp6~ig) for more information. 
This list covers most of the errors generated by the NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service, as well as some possible solutions. 
Server Errors
These messages are output to the operating system event log only.  
|  Error  |  Cause/Solution  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  PersistedDeltas server cannot open a file to output to.  | 
  * The disk is full.
  * The service does not have the permissions necessary to write to the specified share.

 |  
|  Cannot update the deltas.  | 
  * Check for the following:
    * If the Oracle database is still started.
    * If a component view has been changed without publishing or cleaning the MODIFICATIONLOG.
    * If the network is up, and so forth.
    * If the MODIFICATIONLOG is out of synchronization with newly defined or changed component views.  To determine if the MODIFICATIONLOG is out of synchronization, run ValidateDeltasConsistency.exe to [check the consistency](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EDODAmcLctOR521WtAnL0w) of the component view definitions in the DDCs, database, and MODIFICATIONLOG. 

 |  
|  Unable to read login information, processing suspended.  |  The registry entry has been deleted or corrupted.  |  
|  Cannot open the database.  |  Check the username and password, location of CCM, location of DDCs, and that the Oracle database is started.  Try to open a desktop connection on the same configuration.  |  
Client Errors  
|  Error  |  Cause/Solution  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  There are many PersistedDeltas.dlt files on the server. Perhaps need to lengthen the interval.   |  See "To install and run the PersistedDeltas service" above. The service might create new files for the following other reasons:
  * If a client crashes and locks a PersistedDeltas.dlt file, the service must create a new one. 
  * If the operating system gets out of synchronization and marks a file as used when it is really not, the service creates a new one. 

In all cases, when the client detects too many PersistedDeltas.dlt files, it writes this message to the operating system event log and to [NetWorks Core diagnostics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7xX7B_vERfkLcHh~OUHqFA). This should be no problem if the service has been working for a long time, but it signals a problem if it happens soon after the service is started. See "To delete all the PersistedDeltas.dlt files (the limit is 10)" above.   |  
Other Errors
Some errors are output to NetWorks Core[ diagnostics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7xX7B_vERfkLcHh~OUHqFA) and some are output to the optional [PersistedDeltasTrace.txt log file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NKHNIHQKDhLoGtt_Cp6~ig).

### Overview of the Define CAD Server Schema File Utility

#### Advanced Database Linkage Dialog
Use the Advanced Database Linkage dialog to specify the database linkage options when you want the CAD server to serve up attribute data from a database. Define what characteristic(s) of the elements in the map file the CAD server is to use to define the database linkages. Enabled only when a feature class exists with the database linkages. 
Dialog Options
Select graphic to database table linkage
Graphic Attribute Name - Displays a list of the available graphic attributes. Click the checkbox to specify what graphic attribute has to be used to define the graphic-to-database-table linkages. EntityNumber is the default for MicroStation (IGDS) template. 
Database Scanner Attribute Name - Displays a list of the available database scanner attributes. Change theOccurrenceNumber is associated with the MSLINK column by default in the Graphic to database row linkage group (for MicroStation- IGDS template). If your database column name is different, you must edit the Database Scanner Attribute Name to match your database. 
Select graphic to database row linkage
Graphic Attribute Name - Displays a list of the available graphic attributes. Click the checkbox to specify what graphic attribute has to be used to define the graphic-to-database-row linkages. OccurrenceNumber is the default for MicroStation (IGDS) template. 
Database Scanner Attribute Name - Displays a list of the available database scanner attributes. Change theOccurrenceNumber is associated with the MSLINK column by default in the Graphic to database row linkage group (for MicroStation- IGDS template). If your database column name is different, you must edit the Database Scanner Attribute Name to match your database. 
OK - Saves your changes and closes the dialog. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121468) For .csd files based on the MicroStation V7 template, the Database Scanner Attribute Name, for both graphic to table linkage (typically EntityNumber), and graphic to row linkage (typically MSLINK) must be referenced in the database table MSCATALOG.

#### Appendix

##### CAD Server Schema
The CAD Server schema provides the definition of the feature classes for the CAD GDO server. The Define CAD Server Schema File utility is used to assist you in defining your feature classes. This task requires that you define the parameters needed by the Define CAD Server Schema File utility. You define your feature classes based on the different types of attributes that a graphic element may contain. This schema definition is stored in a Microsoft Access database. The Define CAD Server Schema File utility uses the template files delivered with the product to assist you in defining your feature classes. The following three templates are delivered with the product for MicroStation (IGDS), MicroStation Version 8, and AutoCAD: 
  * MstnTemplate.csd
  * MstnV8Template.csd
  * AutoCadTemplate.csd


The schema provides the following:
  * Describes the storage for feature class definitions.
  * Defines the storage of a graphic index.
  * Defines the storage for the metadata of the element’s attributes (non-database attributes). This encompasses all attributes, even those that do not participate in the definition of a feature. 
  * Allows server builders to add more attribute metadata and more feature definitions.
  * Does not allow feature definition to be based on the attributes of a database table.
  * Is the same for all CAD servers.


If an attribute table exists for a feature class, all the elements of that feature class may or may not contain a linkage to that table. 
In order to reduce the complexity of the schema, the following assumptions are made:
  * The primary unique key for a graphic-only feature class (that is, no database linkage) consists of one attribute, and it is the same for all graphic-only feature classes defined in the schema. The schema defines the key. ID is the default primary unique key defined for the graphic-only feature classes. 
  * The primary unique key for a feature class that has a database attribute table consists of one attribute, and it is the same for all feature classes that have attribute tables. The schema defines the key. In the MicroStation (IGDS) template file, mslink is the default primary unique key for any feature class with database linkages. In the MicroStation Version 8 and AutoCAD template files, ID is the default primary unique key for any feature class with database linkages.

##### Error Handling
In any particular command, all the mandatory information has to be filled in before clicking OK. If any such information is missing or is invalid, you are prompted with an error message to enter a valid value. In the case of the defining a feature class, all the information on all the tabs is validated when you click OK. 
While creating or opening a .csd file, the input .csd file is validated and appropriate error messages will be given. For example: 
  * If the template file is corrupt, then the following error message is displayed:
  * The selected template file is either invalid or corrupt.
  * If the .csd file is corrupt, then the following error message is displayed: 
  * The selected CAD Schema definition file is either invalid or corrupt.
  * If the .csd file contains folders that do not exist, then the following error message is displayed: 
  * One or more folders cannot be found. Use "Select Maps" or Select Coordinate System Files" to change the folders.
  * If the .csd file contains map files that do not exist, then the following error message is displayed: 
  * One or more map files cannot be found. Use the "Select Maps" command to edit.
  * If the .csd file contains coordinate system files that do not exist, then the following error message is displayed: 
  * One or more coordinate system files cannot be found. Use the "Select Coordinate System" command to edit.


In the Select Maps or the Select Coordinate System Files command the following messages are displayed:

  * This folder cannot be found. Do you want to change the folder?

  * This folder is also used for coordinate system files. Do you want this same change to the coordinate system files folder?
  * While changing the folders in the Select Coordinate System Files command, the above message is changed accordingly. 
  * If selected map files are unselected or folders containing selected map files are removed, then when you click on OK, the decision message displayed is: 
  * Some of the unselected or removed map files are associated with feature classes or with coordinate system files.  
Click Yes to disassociate the map files.
  * While in Select Coordinate System Files, the above message is changed accordingly, as follows: 
  * Some of the unselected or removed coordinate system files are associated with feature classes or map files  
Click Yes to disassociate the coordinate system files.
  * If you change the folder of coordinate system files and the already selected map files are also contained in the new folder then the following message is displayed:

Do you want to continue?
  * When you try to remove an existing folder in the Select Map Files dialog box, the following message is displayed:

Do you want to continue?

##### IGDS Scanner
The CAD Data Server provides an interface for serving data from CAD warehouses. The IGDS graphic scanner reads the design files for the CAD server. This section documents the IGDS scanner. 
Native Data Model
Geometry Storage
The geometry is stored in the design files as per the IGDS format. None of the Bentley-MicroStation extensions of IGDS format are supported except shared cell. 
Z values in 2D design files
In 2D files the Z range will be set in IGDS/MicroStation, by default, to maximum negative 32 bit integer value. If the contour value is not set, these applications put -2 billion value as the low Z range and not zero. This is because zero is also considered as a valid elevation point. 
Versions and Variations
IGDS Scanner supports the geometry types as mentioned in the Native-to-GDO Geometry Type Mapping table. MicroStation-K and higher version design files are not supported. 
Native-to-GDO Field Type Mapping
The following table identifies the native field types.  
|  Native Field Name as exposed in the .csd file  |  Native Field Meaning  |  Can this graphic attribute be used to set criteria?  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  CellName  |  The name of the MicroStation Cell element.  |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleX  |  Specifies the scale factor along the x-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleY  |  Specifies the scale factor along the y-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleZ  |  Specifies the scale factor along the z-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementColor  |  The color of an element. This is stored as a value in the 0-255 range.  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementLevel  |  The level (from 0- 63), on which an element is placed. Data in the design file is segregated into 63 drawing levels. Levels are similar to transparent overlays that can be put together to form a complete drawing.   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementStyle  |  Part of the symbology of an element. For example, whether a line is solid, continuous dashes, dots and dashes, and so on. This is an index in the range 0 to 7.  The values 0 to 7 represent the following line styles.  0 - Solid  1 - Dotted  2 - Medium Dash  3 - Long Dash  4 - Dot Dash  5 - Short Dash  6 - Dash Double Dot  7 - Long Dash Short Dash  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementType  |  This specifies the type of the MicroStation element.  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementWeight  |  The line weight of an element in pixels, stored as a value in the 0-31 range, where 0 is lightest (narrowest) and 31 is heaviest.   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementZ  |  Specifies the Z coordinate value associated with the IGDS element in either a 2D or 3D design file.   |  No  |  
|  EntityNumber  |  This corresponds to the entitynum column in the MSCATALOG row for a particular table. This contains the entity number of the table. The entity number is a positive integer from 1 to 65535 that uniquely identifies the table to the database. Each table used with a design file must have a unique entity number.   |  Yes  |  
|  FontNumber  |  Specifies the font number of the IGDS text element.  |  Yes  |  
|  FullName  |  Specifies the name of the map file along with its path. This is not an element of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  GraphicGroupNumber  |  Specifies the number associated with a graphic group.  |  Yes  |  
|  GraphicTextString  |  This field is not the attribute of a MicroStation element header. This field is used to populated the text valued associated with a text element as gdbText.   |  No  |  
|  GraphicTextStringMemo  |  This field is not the attribute of a MicroStation element header. This field is used to populated the text valued associated with a text element as gdbMemo.   |  No  |  
|  ID  |  This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element. This is used to serve as the primary key for the CAD data server.   |  No  |  
|  MapName  |  Specifies the name of the map file in which the element is present. This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  OccurrenceNumber  |  Specifies the row of the database table that is linked to the element.  |  Yes  |  
|  PathName  |  Specifies the path of the map file in which the element is present. This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  TextHeight  |  Specifies the height of the text characters in an IGDS text element in decimal master design file units of the corresponding design file.   |  Yes  |  
|  TextWidth  |  Specifies the width of the text characters in an IGDS text element in decimal master design file units of the corresponding design file.   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementColorRGB  |  This field is used to populate the element color as RGB value. This field is used for the LE extension.   |  No  |  
|  ElementFillColorRGB  |  This field is used to populate the element fill color as RGB value. This field is used for the LE extension.   |  No  |  
|  FontName  |  This field is used to populate the font name used while serving text geometry. The font name is retrieved by reading the INI parameters. This field is used for the LE extension.   |  No  |  
|  FontSizeHiMetric  |  This field is used to populate the font size of the text element in HiMetric units. This value is calculated by multiplying the text height with a value of (35.27777777777775) and the font scaling factor as mentioned in the INI file. This field is used for the LE extension.   |  No  |  
The attributes MapName, PathName, and FullName have been added to allow the user to track the origin of each of the features that came from different design files. 
In the case of orphan and unnamed cells (served as BoundaryGeometry), the graphic attributes of the first element in the sequence are used to populate the graphic attributes of the feature. In case of named cells, the graphic attributes of the cell header are used to populate the graphic attributes of the feature. 
For a sequence of complex shapes, the first of which is solid and subsequent ones holes (served as BoundaryGeometry), the graphic attributes of the first element in the sequence are used to populate the graphic attributes of the feature. 
GeoMedia Style Property to GField Mapping
The GFields used to set the various properties on StyleDefinition are explained in the following table:   
|  GeoMedia style type  |  Style property  |  GFields / ABS expression used for the property value   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Symbol style  |  OverrideColor  Size  |  EntityColorRGB ElementWeight*26.45833 (See Note below.)  |  
|  Simple Line Style  |  Color Width SequenceType  |  ElementColorRGB ElementWeight*26.45833 IF (ElementStyle>=0 AND ElementStyle<=7, ElementStyle, 0)  |  
|  Fill style  |  Color  |  ElementFillColorRGB  |  
|  Text style  |  Color FontName FontSize  |  EntityColorRGB Font Name FontSizeHiMetric  |  
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121450) Concerning the ElementWeight*26.45833 field: GeoMedia’s Style Definition expects the Size of the Symbol Style, Width of the Simple Line style, and FontSize of the Text style to be in HiMetric units. Hence the conversion is needed to convert the value to HiMetric units 
Native-to-GDO Geometry Type Mapping
For 2D files, the Z coordinate is populated with the minimum Z value of the range in the element header. If this value exceeds the threshold of –1.8 billion, the Z coordinate is populated with a value of 0.0. This is because there cannot be NULL coordinates in the geometry blob. For 3D design files, the actual Z coordinate will be served. 
The following table identifies the mapping used when converting from native geometry types to GDO geometry types.   
|  Native Geometry Type  |  Native Meaning  |  GDO Geometry Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Cell - named (Type 2)  |  A complex element composed of a group of primitive or other complex elements that is stored in a cell library for repeated placement. This has a name associated with it.   |  OrientedPointGeometry/ TextPointGeometry/ CollectionGeometry. This is served based on the .ini file variables   |  
|  Cell - orphaned (Type 2)  |  A complex element composed of a group of primitive or other complex elements that is stored in a cell library for repeated placement. This has no name associated with it and the hole flag is set to TRUE.  Orphan cells of a particular form (composed only of shape (type 6), ellipse (type 15) or complex shape (type 12) elements - the first element should be solid and the rest holes) result in the generation of Boundary geometry. Otherwise the cell will be treated as a named cell.   |  BoundaryGeometry  |  
|  Cell - unnamed (Type 2)  |  Unnamed cells are identified by the lack of a cell name in the header. Since there is no name, there can be no corresponding element in the cell library and the hole flag setting is irrelevant. They are handled the same way as orphan cells.   |  BoundaryGeometry  |  
|  Line (Type 3)  |  An open graphic element composed of points connected to each other.  |  PolylineGeometry/OrientedPointGeometry. In case of degenerate lines, OrientedPointGeometry is served.  |  
|  LineString (Type 4)  |  An open graphic element composed of up to 100 line segments connected at the vertices.  |  PolylineGeometry  |  
|  Shape (Type 6)  |  Closed primitive element composed of up to 100 linear segments.  |  PolygonGeometry  |  
|  Ellipse (Type 15)  |  Ellipse  |  PolygonGeometry  |  
|  Arc (Type 16)  |  A regularly curved open element that has a constant radius around a single center point.   |  PolylineGeometry/ArcGeometry ArcGeometry is served for circular arcs.  |  
|  Complex String (Type 12)  |  An open complex element that is formed from a series of open elements, such as lines, line strings, and arcs.   |  CompositePolylineGeometry  |  
|  Complex Shape (Type 14)  |  A closed complex element formed from a series of open primitive elements.  |  CompositePolygonGeometry BoundaryGeometry is served for a sequence of complex shapes, the first of which is solid and subsequent ones holes.   |  
|  Curve (Type 11)  |  Curve element  |  CompositePolylineGeometry  |  
|  Text (Type 17)  |  Text element  |  TextPointGeometry The text will be served up in rich text format, thus maintaining the text color, height, and width.  The text justification and font are forced through the .ini variables   |  
|  TextNode (Type 7)  |  Multiple text elements grouped in a complex element.  |  TextPointGeometry (collection) The text will be served up in rich text format, thus maintaining the text color, height, and width.  The text justification and font are forced through the .ini variables.   |  
|  Shared Cell (Type 35)  |  A cell whose elements are stored only once in the design file, regardless of how often the cell is placed. Any change made to one instance of a shared cell is reflected in all instances of that shared cell.   |  OrientedPointGeometry  |  
Mapping of GeoMedia Style Property 
GFields used
The GFields used to set the various properties on StyleDefinition are explained in the following table:   
|  GeoMedia style type  |  Style property  |  GFields / ABS expression used for the property value   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Symbol style  |  OverrideColor  Size  |  EntityColorRGB EntityWeightHiMetric  |  
|  Simple Line Style  |  Color Width SequenceType  |  EntityColorRGB EntityWeightHiMetric gmgroSequenceTypeCustom CustomSequence  |  
|  Fill style  |  Color  |  Not supported  |  
|  Text style  |  Color FontName FontSize  |  EntityColorRGB Font Name FontSizeHiMetric  |  
Serving text:
MicroStation text and textnode elements will be served in rich text format with the color, size and font details read from the IGDS element. The IGDS text/textnode element has the text height and width stored in the design file in UORs. MicroStation saves its coordinates as 32-bit integers. Accordingly, the design plane has 232 points in each dimension. The distance between two adjacent points is the smallest distance MicroStation can address. This distance is one positional unit or unit of resolution (UOR) The mapping of the color, size and the font details are explained below: 
  * Font: The font number of the IGDS element is mapped to the font name based on the .ini settings. The mapped font name is served in the rich text syntax, along with the actual text. If no matching font is found, Arial is used as the default. 
  * Size: The text height of the IGDS element will be mapped to the font size of the rich text using the font scaling factor defined in the .ini file. The character scaling value (specified by \charscalex, as a percentage of font size) will be calculated using the text height and text width. 
  * Color: If the MicroStation design file has the color table attached to it (this is determined by the presence of type 5 color table element in the design file), the color index stored in the element’s display header is mapped to the RGB color using the color table. If no color table is attached to the design file (determined by the absence of type 5 color table element), the color index stored in the element’s display header is mapped to the RGB color using the default color table delivered with the CAD-IGDS data server. In the absence of the type 5 color table element and the default color table file, the color is not served with the rich text. 


The delivered MicroStation color table file color.tbl will be used by the IGDS scanner. 
Limitations and issues
The following is a limitation of the IGDS scanner:
  * Custom line styles like Border, Center, and DashDot are not mapped to corresponding styles in GeoMedia (while serving the LegendEntry extension). These are instead mapped to Solid line style.

##### MicroStation Version 8 Scanner
Native Data Model
Geometry Storage
MicroStation v8 has graphical elements with same element types as in its older versions. However the element definitions have changed to support increased workspace, size of elements, and higher precision through floating point coordinates. The storage format of the graphical elements in the design file is not open to the user unlike in the older versions. 
Geometry Indexing
There is no geometry indexing.
Attribute Storage
Graphic attributes of each element are defined in the element header, display header, and with the element. The data types of all graphic attributes in v8 have been enhanced over the earlier versions to support increased range. 
Data linkage to the graphical elements is through the attribute offset as in earlier versions. However, data linkages will not be read by the v8 scanner. 
Database Linkages
The linkage information is stored on the element in the design file. When a database row is linked to a graphical element, attribute data, in the form of an attribute linkage containing the MSLINK and entity number, is written to the element. The entity number corresponds to the table in the external databases (as defined in the MSCATALOG table). The MSLINK value is a numeric value that corresponds to a row of data in the table. 
The linkages can be represented in an eight-word format (following the format used in ODBC, Oracle, Informix and other database management software) or a four-word format (the DMRS format). The eight-word format contains the entity number in the fourth word and the MSLINK in the fifth and sixth words. The four-word format contains the entity number in the second word, the MSLINK in the third word, and the high order byte in the fourth word. The database linkages are represented as hexadecimal numbers. 
Range of valid MSLINK values
With the eight-word format, four bytes are available for storing the MSLINK number: 0 to 232–1 
With the four-word format, three bytes are available for storing the MSLINK number: 0 to 224–1 
Fonts
Fonts are not embedded in the design file. MicroStation v8 supports TrueType and AutoCAD SHX fonts natively, along with the traditional MicroStation fonts (stored in the resource file "font.rsc”). Each font type has a specific font number range, as follows: 
  * MicroStation fonts: 0-255
  * AutoCAD SHX fonts: 512- 1023
  * TrueType fonts: 1024-65535


The underline and italic qualifiers for a particular text element are stored along with the text element as user data linkages. 
Versions and Variations
This data server is designed to support MicroStation versions 8.0 and 8.1.
Native-to-GDO Field Type Mapping
The following table identifies the native field types.  
|  Native Field Name, as exposed in the csd file  |  Native Field Meaning  |  Can this graphic attribute be used to set criteria?  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  CellName  |  The name of the MicroStation Cell element.  |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleX  |  Specifies the scale factor along the x-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleY  |  Specifies the scale factor along the y-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  CellScaleZ  |  Specifies the scale factor along the z-axis. This is applicable only to elements of Type 2 (cell) and Type 35 (shared cell instance).   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementColor  |  Symbology. Color of element. Similar to style of element.  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementId  |  Unique ID of the element, which is persistent throughout the life of the .dgn file.  Every element in .dgn file has unique ID (Int64). Though there is no equivalent GDO field Type, this attribute needs to be exposed.   |  No  |  
|  ElementLevelName  |  Named level. Levels are similar to transparent overlays that can be put together to form a complete drawing. Levels are stored as Int 32 values. User interacts only as named values. Name/value pairs are stored as level table elements. When a .dgn file is created there is one level named as "default".   |  Yes  |
