|  ElementLevelNumber  |  Level Number in which the element resides.  |  Yes. If criteria is set on both level name and on level number, elements that have either matching level name or matching level number will be returned. This is because level number or level name actually mean the same thing.   |  
|  ElementStyle  |  Symbology. Style of an element. Stored as Int32 value. Each level can have a default style set. The style of an element can be independently set or "by level". If set to "by level" the default symbology settings of the level in which the element lies get attributed to this element.  The values 0 to 7 represent the following line styles.  0 - Solid  1 - Dotted  2 - Medium Dash  3 - Long Dash  4 - Dot Dash  5 - Short Dash  6 - Dash Double Dot  7 - Long Dash Short Dash  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementType  |  Type of element  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementWeight  |  Symbology. Weight of element in pixels. Similar to style of element.  |  Yes  |  
|  ElementZ  |  Specifies the Z coordinate value associated with the element in a 2D or 3D design file. This will be the minimum Z value of the range of the element.  For 2D .dgn files, if the minimum Z of the range of the element exceeds the threshold of –1.8 billion, a NULL will be served.   |  No  |  
|  EntityNumber  |  This corresponds to the entitynum column in the MSCATALOG row for a particular table. This contains the entity number of the table. The entity number is a positive integer from 1 to 65535 that uniquely identifies the table to the database; each table referenced by a design file must have a unique entity number.   |  Yes  |  
|  FontNumber  |  Specifies the font number of the MicroStation v8 text element.  |  Yes  |  
|  FullName  |  Specifies name of the map file with its path. This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  GraphicGroupNumber  |  Specifies the number associated with a graphic group  |  Yes  |  
|  GraphicTextString  |  This field is not the attribute of a MicroStation element header. This field is used to populate the text value associated with a text element as a gdbText field.   |  No  |  
|  GraphicTextStringMemo  |  This field is not the attribute of a MicroStation element header. This field is used to populate the text value associated with a text element as a gdbMemo field.   |  No  |  
|  GraphicTextJustification  |  This field is not the attribute of a MicroStation element header. This field is used to populate the justification value associated with the text element.  The possible justification values are  LeftTop - 0, LeftCenter - 1,  LeftBottom - 2, CenterTop - 6, CenterCenter - 7, CenterBottom - 8, RightTop - 12, RightCenter - 13, RightBottom - 14   |  No  |  
|  ID  |  This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element. This is used to serve as the primary key for the CAD data server. This is an auto number field generated by the server and is hidden from the client, GeoMedia   |  No  |  
|  MapName  |  Specifies name of the map file in which the element is present. This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  ModelName  |  Model is a named set of elements in a .dgn file. A .dgn file can have multiple models. When a .dgn file is created, a model by name "default" is created. A model can be placed as a cell or attached as a reference.  Every element in the .dgn file belongs to a specific model or to a default model.   |  Yes  |  
|  OccurrenceNumber  |  Specifies the row of the database table that is linked to the element. Valid values are 0 to (232-1).   |  Yes  |  
|  PathName  |  Specifies path of the map file in which the element is present. This is not an attribute of the MicroStation element.   |  No  |  
|  TextHeight  |  Specifies the height of the text characters in the text element in decimal master design file units of the corresponding design file.   |  Yes  |  
|  TextWidth  |  Specifies the width of the text character in the text element in decimal master design file units of the corresponding design file.   |  Yes  |  
|  ElementColorRGB  |  This field is used to populate the element color as RGB value.  |  No  |  
|  ElementFillColorRGB  |  This field is used to populate the element fill color as RGB value.  |  No  |  
|  FontName  |  This field is used to populate the font name used while serving text geometry. The font name is retrieved by reading the INI parameters.   |  No  |  
|  FontSizeHiMetric  |  This field is used to populate the fontsize of the text element in HiMetric units. This value is calculated by multiplying the text height with a value of (35.27777777777775) and the font scaling factor as mentioned in the INI file.   |  No  |  
In the case of orphan and unnamed cells (served as BoundaryGeometry), the graphic attributes (GraphicGroupNumber, ElementLevelName, ElementLevelNumber, ElementStyle, ElementWeight, and ElementColor) of the first element in the sequence will be used to populate the graphic attributes of the feature and to set the criteria. In case of named cells, the graphic attributes of the cell header will be used. 
For a sequence of complex shapes, the first of which is solid and subsequent ones holes, (served as BoundaryGeometry), the graphic attributes of the first element in the sequence are used to populate the graphic attributes of the feature. 
GeoMedia Style Property to GField Mapping
The GFields used to set the various properties on StyleDefinition are explained in the following table:   
|  GeoMedia style type  |  Style property  |  GFields / ABS expression used for the property value   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Symbol style  |  OverrideColor  Size  |  EntityColorRGB ElementWeight*26.45833 (See Note below.)  |  
|  Simple Line Style  |  Color Width SequenceType  |  ElementColorRGB ElementWeight*26.45833 IF (ElementStyle>=0 AND ElementStyle<=7, ElementStyle, 0)  |  
|  Fill style  |  Color  |  ElementFillColorRGB  |  
|  Text style  |  Color FontName FontSize  |  EntityColorRGB Font Name FontSizeHiMetric  |  
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121452) Concerning the ElementWeight*26.45833 field: GeoMedia’s Style Definition expects the Size of the Symbol Style, Width of the Simple Line style, and FontSize of the Text style to be in HiMetric units. Hence the conversion is needed to convert the value to HiMetric units 
Database Attributes
The database attributes are served using the existing CAD ODBC scanner. The ODBC scanner will read the database attributes from the external database table bases on the values of the EntityNumber and OccurrenceNumber fields populated by the graphics scanner. 
For the data server to serve the database attributes for a database-linked feature class, at least one of the linkage attributes (EntityNumber/OccurrenceNumber) must be exposed in the .csd file, and the database linkage attribute (EntityNumber) should be used in setting the criteria. 
If neither entity number nor occurrence number participates in the feature class definition (criteria), and if the element has one or more linkages, then the EntityNumber and OccurrenceNumber fields are populated with the first linkage values. 
Non-Graphic Attributes
Support for Tags
The tag elements come as name-value pairs, and the data type of the TAG is not specified. The user has to update the .csd file with the list of exposed TAGs (TAG name and type). If a TAG (as defined in the .csd file) is not associated with a particular element, the data server will populate the GField value of that record with NULL value. Similarly, the data server will populate all the GField values (for TAGs) of non-block entity records with NULL values. The TAGs are determined by their names. Unnamed TAGs are not supported. 
Native-to-GDO Geometry Type Mapping
For 2D design files, the Z coordinate is populated with the minimum Z value of the range of the element. If this value exceeds the threshold of –1.8 billion, the Z coordinate is populated with a value of 0. This is because there cannot be NULL coordinates in the geometry blob. 
For 3D design files, the actual Z coordinate will be served.
The following table identifies the mapping used when converting from native geometry types to GDO geometry types.   
|  Native Geometry Type  |  Native Meaning  |  GDO Geometry Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Cell - named (Type 2)  |  A complex element composed of a group of primitive or other complex elements that is stored in a cell library for repeated placement. This has a name associated with it. Hole flag for the cell is set to false.  Orphan / shared cells can also be constituent elements. Incorrectly constructed orphan cells will be treated as a named cell. Nested cells are also supported.  |  OrientedPointGeometry / TextPointGeometry / CollectionGeometry. This is served based on the .ini file variables   |  
|  Cell - orphaned (Type 2)  |  A complex element composed of a group of primitive or other complex elements for repeated placement. This has a name associated with it but the hole flag is set to TRUE - indicating that there is no corresponding element in the cell library.  Orphan cells of a particular form (composed only of shape (type 6), ellipse (type 15) or complex shape (type 12) elements - the first element should be solid and the rest holes) result in the generation of Boundary geometry. Otherwise the cell will be treated as a named cell.   |  BoundaryGeometry  |  
|  Cell - unnamed (Type 2)  |  Unnamed cells are identified by the lack of a cell name in the header. Since there is no name, there can be no corresponding element in the cell library and the hole flag setting is irrelevant. They are to be handled the same way as orphan cells (if the form is appropriate, create a boundary geometry, otherwise treat as a named cell).   |  BoundaryGeometry  |  
|  Line (Type 3)  |  An open graphic element composed of 2 points connected to each other.  |  PolylineGeometry / OrientedPointGeometry In case of degenerate lines, OrientedPointGeometry is served  |  
|  LineString (Type 4)  |  An open graphic element composed of line segments connected at the vertices. A line string element can have a maximum of 5000 vertices. If more than 5000 vertices are defined, a complex chain consisting of one or more line string elements is created.   |  PolylineGeometry  |  
|  Shape (Type 6)  |  Closed primitive element composed of up to 100 linear segments.  |  PolygonGeometry  |  
|  TextNode (Type 7)  |  Multiple text elements grouped in a complex element. When a text is placed in MicroStation V8 product "along element," a text node is placed with each letter of the text string placed as an independent text (Type 17) element.   |  GeometryCollection (TextPointGeometry) / TextPointGeometry If the text node is composed of only single-character and zero length text elements; then it is served as a composite text collection. For this, the options field of each text blob is set to gptCompositeText (0x01).  See the SERVE TEXTNODE AS MULTILINE TEXT INI keyword section for more details.  |  
|  Curve (Type 11)  |  Curve element  |  PolylineGeometry (Stroked)  |  
|  Complex String (Type 12)  |  An open complex element that is formed from a series of open elements, such as lines, line strings, and arcs.   |  CompositePolylineGeometry  |  
|  Complex Shape (Type 14)  |  A closed complex element formed from a series of open primitive elements.  |  CompositePolygonGeometry BoundaryGeometry is served for a sequence of complex shapes, the first of which is solid and subsequent ones holes.   |  
|  Ellipse (Type 15)  |  MicroStation Ellipse (Type 15)  |  PolygonGeometry  |  
|  Arc (Type 16)  |  Regularly curved open element that has a constant radius around a single center point.  |  Stroked PolylineGeometry for elliptical arcs / ArcGeometry for circular arcs  |  
|  Text (Type 17)  |  Text string element  |  TextPointGeometry  |  
|  Point string (Type 22)  |  A string of points with each point associated with orientation. The points will be assigned zero orientation.   |  GeometryCollection (OrientedPointGeometry)  |  
|  Shared Cell (Type 35)  |  A cell whose elements are stored only once in the design file, regardless of how often the cell is placed. Any change made to a shared cell is reflected in all instances of that shared cell.  Orphan, named and shared cells can also be constituent elements.  |  OrientedPointGeometry / TextPointGeometry / CollectionGeometry. This is served based on the .ini file variables   |  
|  All other MicroStation V8 types, like Multiline, Cone, Surface, Solid, Bspline, Dimensions, Raster, etc.   |   |  Not supported.  |  
Serving Text
MicroStation text and text node elements will be served in rich text format with the color, size, and font details read from the MicroStation element. The MicroStation text/text node element has the text height and width stored in the design file in UORs. The mapping of the color, size, and the front details are explained below: 
Font: For MicroStation fonts, the font number of the MicroStation text element is mapped using the FONT NUMBER mapping specified in the .ini file. For AutoCAD SHX fonts, the font is mapped using the FONT NAME mapping specified in the .ini file. If no matching font is found, Arial is used as the default. 
Size: The text height of the MicroStation text element will be mapped to the font size of the rich text using the font scaling factor defined in the .ini file. The character scaling value (specified by \charscalex, as a percentage of font size) will be calculated using the text height and text width. 
Color: If the MicroStation design file has the color table attached to it, the color index of the text element is mapped to the RGB color using the color table. If no color table is attached to the design file, the color index stored in the element's display header is mapped to the RGB color using the default color table delivered with GeoMedia. In the absence of the type 5 color table element and the default color table file, the color is not served with the rich text. 
Limitations and issues
The following are the limitations of the MicroStation V8 scanner:
  * Multiple database linkages and multiple databases are not supported.
  * Custom line styles like Border, Center, and DashDot are not mapped to corresponding styles in GeoMedia (while serving the LegendEntry extension). These are instead mapped to Solid line style.

##### Rich Text Format (RTF) Specification
Font pitch
The control word, denoted as \fprqN, specifies if the font is Fixed or Variable. If the font pitch is Fixed, every character has the same width. If the font pitch is Variable some letters are wider than others (that is, the letter "i" is not as wide as the letter "W"). Values for N are 0 (default pitch), 1(fixed pitch) and 2 (variable pitch). 
Font family
RTF supports font families so that applications can attempt to intelligently choose fonts if the exact font is not present on the reading system. RTF uses the following control words to describe the various font families.   
|  Control word  |  Font family  |  Examples  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  \fnil  |  Unknown or default fonts (the default)  |  Not applicable  |  
|  \froman  |  Roman, proportionally spaced serif fonts  |  Times New Roman, Palatino  |  
|  \fswiss  |  Swiss, proportionally spaced sans serif fonts  |  Arial  |  
|  \fmodern  |  Fixed-pitch serif and sans serif fonts  |  Courier New, Pica  |  
|  \fscript  |  Script fonts  |  Cursive  |  
|  \fdecor  |  Decorative fonts  |  Old English, ITC Zapf Chancery  |  
|  \ftech  |  Technical, symbol, and mathematical fonts  |  Symbol  |  
|  \fbidi  |  Arabic, Hebrew, or other bidirectional font  |  Miriam  |  
Charset
The control word, denoted as \fcharsetN, specifies the character set of a font in the font table. Values for N are defined by Windows header files, as follows:   
|  0  |  ANSI  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Default  |  
|  2  |  Symbol  |  
|  3  |  Invalid  |  
|  77  |  Mac  |  
|  128  |  Shift Jis  |  
|  129  |  Hangul  |  
|  130  |  Johab  |  
|  134  |  GB2312  |  
|  136  |  Big5  |  
|  161  |  Greek  |  
|  162  |  Turkish  |  
|  163  |  Vietnamese  |  
|  177  |  Hebrew  |  
|  178  |  Arabic  |  
|  179  |  Arabic Traditional  |  
|  180  |  Arabic user  |  
|  181  |  Hebrew user  |  
|  186  |  Baltic  |  
|  204  |  Russian  |  
|  222  |  Thai  |  
|  238  |  Eastern European  |  
|  254  |  PC 437  |  
|  255  |  OEM  |

#### CAD Server Definition Workflow
This topic describes the Define CAD Server Schema File dialog workflow. Each step is described in detail in the topics that follow. 
  1. Start the Define CAD Server Schema File utility by selecting  > > Define CAD Server Schema File from Start menu. 
  2. Select File > Open or File > New to open an existing .csd file or to create a new .csd file. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121428)When using the File > New option, you need to select the appropriate CAD template based on the type and version of CAD to which you are going to connect. 
  3. Select Feature Class > Select Maps and Feature Class > Select Coordinate System Files from the Feature Class menu to select maps and coordinate system files. 
  4. Select Feature Class > Define Feature Class from the Feature Class menu to open the Define Feature Class dialog . 
  5. Click New on the Define Feature Class dialog and use the different tabs of the New <FeatureClass Name> dialog to set the feature class definition parameters. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121428) When you create a new .csd file, you are prompted to enter the minimum required information and the dialogs used to enter that information are displayed. At a minimum, you are required to use the following dialogs to create a .csd file: 
     * Select Map Files dialog - Select the map files to be processed. 
     * Select Coordinate System Files dialog - Select the coordinate system (.csf) files be applied to the data. 
     * Define Feature Class dialog - Click New, and in the New <feature class name> dialog, enter the criteria for a new feature class. 
     * New <feature class name> dialog - Specify the criteria that define the new feature class. 
  6. Select Feature Class > Edit Coordinate System to Map Associations from the Feature Class menu to associate the map files with the respective coordinate system files. 
  7. Select Feature Class > Edit Coordinate System to Feature Class Associations from the Feature Class menu to associate the feature classes with the respective coordinate system files. 
  8. Select Feature Class > Edit Feature Class to Map Associations from the Feature Class menu to associate the feature classes with the respective map files. 
  9. Use the Options menu to specify the connection-specific parameters for your CAD data, specify the primary unique key for CAD data with database linkages, specify advanced database linkage parameters, or update map MBRs. If your feature class has database linkages, use the Specify Connection Parameters dialog to specify the information necessary to connect to the database.

#### Define CAD Server Schema File Dialog
The resizable Define CAD Server Schema File dialog is the main dialog for the Define CAD Server Schema File utility. Access the menus and other dialogs to create and edit CAD Server Schema (.csd) files. 
Dialog Options
Menus - When you first start the Define CAD Server Schema File utility, the dialog opens with only the File and Help menus. Once you have opened a new or existing .csd file, the Feature Class and Options menus are displayed. 
Status bar - Displays the template type (scanner type) – MicroStation V7, MicroStation V8, or AutoCAD. If the chosen template is neither MicroStation V7 nor MicroStation V8 nor AutoCAD, then the status bar shows the value ”Unknown”. This information is displayed immediately after creating or opening a .csd file.

#### Define CAD Server Schema File
The Define CAD Server Schema File utility allows you to specify the parameters the software uses when creating connections with the CAD data server. The CAD data server allows you to use IGDS (MicroStation V7) design files, MicroStation V8 design files, or AutoCAD files as a data source. 
Note that in order to make full use of the Define CAD Server Schema File utility you must have a complete understanding of your CAD data structure. For example, you would need to know the following: 
  * CAD criteria such as level, layer names, color, and so forth
  * The conventions used for digitizing and assigning attributes to features in your project
  * Whether graphics in the project have attributes
  * The nature and structure of the attribute data

#### Define Feature Class Dialog
Use the resizable Define Feature Class dialog to create, edit, copy, or delete feature definitions. The list view contains the list of feature classes already defined in the .csd file, along with the buttons for New, Edit, Copy, Delete, and Close. When you select multiple feature classes, the Edit and Copy buttons are disabled. 
Dialog Options
Feature classes - Lists all the feature classes. Multiple feature classes can be selected at a time. The first feature class are selected automatically. Ctrl+click on a selected feature class to de-select a feature class. 
New - Opens the New - <feature class name> dialog to define the new feature class. Always enabled. 
Edit - Select any single feature class and edit it. Enabled only when a single feature class is selected. 
Copy - Copy the selected feature class definition. Select a feature class and then click Copy to open the Copy - <feature class name> dialog with the properties of the selected feature class. You can modify and rename this copy of the original feature class to quickly create a feature class definition that shares many of the parameters of the original feature class definition. Enabled only when a single feature class is selected from the given list. 
Delete - Deletes the selected feature classes from the schema file. Enabled when you select one or more feature classes. Confirm whether you want to delete or not. 
Close - Closes the dialog.

#### Edit Coordinate System to Feature Class Associations Dialog
Use the resizable Edit Coordinate System to Feature Class Associations dialog to edit the associations of feature classes with a coordinate system files. The workflow of this command is similar to the Edit Coordinate System to Map Associations dialog. Enabled only when the coordinate system files have been selected and the feature classes have been defined. 
Dialog Options
Available coordinate system files - Lists all the coordinate system files or the selected coordinate system files depending on the option you selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog. This list is single-selectable. 
All/Associated/Dissociated feature classes - Lists all the feature classes defined in the .csd file. Multi-selectable. Title and content of this list changes depending on what Display option you have selected. 
Coordinate system to feature class associations - Shows the association of each coordinate system file with one or more feature classes. The coordinate system files are the root nodes and the feature class(es) associated with them form the leaf nodes below the coordinate system files. 
Associate - Associate a coordinate system file with one or more feature class(es). Select a coordinate system file in the Available coordinate system files list and select one or more feature classes in the All/Dissociated feature classes list, then click Associate to associate the selected feature classes with the selected coordinate system file. Enabled when you select a feature class that is not associated with a coordinate system file. 
Dissociate - Disassociate a coordinate system file from one or more feature class(es). Select a coordinate system file in the Available coordinate system files list and select one or more feature classes in the All/Associated feature classes list, then click Dissociate to dissociate the selected feature classes from the selected coordinate system file. Enabled when you select a feature class that is associated with a coordinate system file. 
Display - Select one of these options from the list. 
All feature classes - Displays all the available feature class names in the All feature classes list. 
Associated feature classes - Displays the feature classes that are associated with the selected coordinate system file from the Available coordinate system files list. 
Disassociated feature classes - Displays the feature classes that are not associated with the selected coordinate system file from the Available coordinate system files list. 
OK - Closes the dialog and saves your changes. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes.

#### Edit Coordinate System to Map Associations Dialog
Use th resizable Edit Coordinate System to Map Associations dialog to edit a map file's association with the coordinate system files. Enabled only when the map files and coordinate system files have been selected. 
Dialog Options
Available coordinate system files - Lists all the coordinate system files or the selected coordinate system files depending on the option you have selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog. This list is single-selectable. 
All/Associated/Dissociated map files - Lists the map files you selected on the Select Map Files dialog. This list is multi-selectable. The title and content of this list changes depending on what Display option is selected. 
Coordinate system to map associations - Shows the association of each coordinate system file with one or more map(s). In this tree view, the coordinate system files are the root nodes and the map(s) associated with them form the leaf nodes below the coordinate system files. 
Associate - Associate a coordinate system file with one or more map(s). Select a coordinate system file in the Available coordinate system files list and select one or more maps in the All/Dissociated map files list, then click Associate to associate the selected map files with the selected coordinate system file. Enabled when you select a map file that is not associated with a coordinate system file. 
Dissociate - Dissociate a coordinate system file from one or more map(s). Select a coordinate system file in the Available coordinate system files list and select one or more maps in the All/Associated map files list, then click Dissociate to dissociate the selected map files from the selected coordinate system file. Enabled when you select a map file that is associated with a coordinate system file. 
Display - Select one of these options from the list. 
All map files - Displays all the available map file names in the All map files list. 
Associated map files - Displays the map files associated with the selected coordinate system file from the Available coordinate system files list box. 
Disassociated map files - Displays the map files that are not associated with the selected coordinate system file from the Available coordinate system files list box. 
OK - Closes the dialog and saves your changes. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes.

#### Edit Feature Class to Map Associations Dialog
Use the resizable Edit Feature Class to Map Associations dialog box to edit the association of map files with the feature classes. Enabled only if the map files have been selected and the feature classes have been defined. 
Dialog Options
Available feature classes- Lists all the feature classes available in the .csd file and is multi-selectable. 
All/Associated/Dissociated map files - Lists the map files available in the .csd file and is multi- selectable. The title and content of this list changes depending on what Display option you have selected. 
Feature class to map associations - Shows the association of each feature class with one or more map files. In this tree view the feature classes are the root nodes and the map files associated with them form the leaf nodes below the feature classes. 
Associate - Associate map file(s) to one or more feature classes. Select a feature class in the Available feature classes list and select one or more maps in the All/Dissociated map files list, then click Associate to associate the selected map files with the selected feature class. Enabled when you select a map file that is not associated with a feature class. 
Disassociate - Dissociate map file(s) from one or more feature classes. Select a feature class in the Available feature classes list and select one or more maps in the All/Associated map files list, then click Dissociate to dissociate the selected map files from the selected feature class. Enabled when you select a map file that is associated with a feature class. 
Display - Select one of these options from the list. 
All map files - Displays all the available map file names in the All map files list. 
Associated map files - Displays the map files associated with the selected feature class from the Available feature classes list. 
Disassociated map files - Displays map files that are not associated with the selected feature class from the Available feature classes list. 
OK - Closes the dialog and saves your changes. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes.

#### Menus

##### Feature Class Menu
Once you have opened a .csd file, the Feature Class menu is added to the Define CAD Server Schema File dialog. When you first start the Define CAD Server Schema file utility, this menu is not displayed. The Feature Class menu contains the following options: 
Select Maps - Opens the Select Map Files dialog to select the folders and maps for feature classes. 
Select Coordinate System Files - Opens the Select Coordinate System Files dialog to specify the coordinate system files to be associated with the feature classes and with the map files. 
Define Feature Class - Opens the Define Feature Class dialog to create, edit, copy, or delete feature definitions. 
Edit Coordinate System To Map Associations - Opens the Edit Coordinate System to Map Associations dialog to edit the association of map files with the coordinate system files. 
Edit Coordinate System To Feature Class Associations - Opens the Edit Coordinate System to Feature Class Associations dialog to edit the association of feature classes with a coordinate system files. This command workflow is similar to the Edit Coordinate System To Map Associations dialog. 
Edit Feature Class To Map Associations - Opens the Edit Feature Class to Map Associations dialog to edit the association of map files with the feature classes. This command workflow is similar to the Edit Coordinate System To Map Associations dialog.

##### File Menu
The File menu contains the following options: 
New - Open the New dialog with the default path set to the CADSchemaDefinition templates folder - <GeoMedia program folder>\templates\CADSchemaDefinition> where all the template files are stored. The dialog has a filter of CAD Schema Template Files (*.csd). 
By default, the product delivers three template files:
  * AutoCadTemplate.csd - Select this template when you are using AutoCAD data.
  * MstnTemplate.csd - Select this template when you are using MicroStation V7 data.
  * MstnV8Template.csd - Select this template when you are using MicroStation V8 data.


After you select a template, a new .csd file opens with the default name Untitled.csd, based on the selected template. Keyboard shortcut is Ctrl+N. If there is a .csd file currently open, you are prompted to save that file before the template selection file dialog opens. 
In order to help you with the normal workflow for defining your .csd file, the Define CAD Server Schema File utility enters a wizard mode that opens the dialogs that you must use to define the new .csd file. 
Once you have selected a template and click New, the Select Maps dialog opens to select the map files you want to process. 
Once you have selected your maps and click OK, the Select Coordinate System Files dialog opens to select the coordinate system files you want to use. 
Once you have selected the coordinate system files and click OK, the Define Feature Class dialog opens to define the feature classes for your .csd file. 
Clicking Cancel on the Select Maps dialog or the Select Coordinate System Files dialog exits this wizard mode to use the menus to select commands manually. 
Open - Open the Open dialog to select and open an existing .csd file. Shortcut keys are Ctrl+O. If a .csd file is already open, you are prompted to save that file (if appropriate) before the Open dialog opens. To open a .csd file, select the file and click Open. The title bar changes, displaying the name of the .csd file. The Save, Save As and Close menu options are activated. The dialog has a filter of CAD Schema Definition Files (*.csd). The selected folders, map files, and coordinate system files are validated for their existence when a .csd file is opened and appropriate error messages are given. 
Close - Close the active .csd file. If any changes were made to the file, then you are prompted to save the file before closing. If the file has not been saved to disk, then clicking Yes opens the Save As dialog to specify the filename and path to save the file. The options Save, Save As, and Close are disabled. 
Save - Save the active .csd file. If the current .csd file has not been saved before, then this option works just like Save As. Otherwise, it saves the current definition to disk. Enabled only when a .csd file is open. Shortcut keys are Ctrl+S. For read-only files, the Save As dialog opens to specify a different file name. 
Save As - Open the Save As dialog to enter or select a filename to be used for the output .csd file. If the file already exists, you are prompted whether to overwrite the file. Enabled only when a .csd file is open. 
Exit - Exit the utility. If any changes were made, a message prompts you to save the file. When you click Yes, then the changes to the file are saved. When the file has not been saved to disk, then clicking Yes on the message opens Save As dialog to specify the filename and path to save the file.

##### Help Menu
The Help menu contains the following options: 
Help Topics F1 - Opens this help file.

##### Options Menu
Once you have opened a .csd file, the Options menu is added to the Define CAD Server Schema File dialog. When you first start the Define CAD Server Schema file utility, this menu is not displayed. The Options menu contains the following options: 
Connection - Opens the Specify Connection Parameters dialog to specify the connection parameters for your .csd file. 
Primary Unique Key - Opens the Primary Unique Key dialog to specify which graphic attribute the CAD server is to use to define the primary unique key for all graphic-only feature classes and for all database-linked feature classes. 
Advanced Database Linkage - Opens the Advanced Database Linkage dialog to specify the database linkage options if you want the CAD server to serve up attribute data from a database. 
Update Map MBRs - Opens the Update Map MBRs dialog to update the MBR information for the map files in your .csd file.

#### New (Feature Class Definition) Dialog

##### Criteria Tab
The Criteria tab allows you to specify the Attribute Name and Classification Criteria that allow the CAD data server to identify and serve up a feature class. 
Tab Options
Attribute Name
Lists the attributes available for the feature class. This tab has a grid that is populated with all those graphic attributes that can be used to set the criteria for the feature class. The Attribute Name column of the grid is read only. 
Type
Lists the data type defined for each attribute. The Type column of the grid is read only. 
Classification Criteria
Allows you to specify the criteria for a particular attribute that the CAD data server is to use to identify the feature class. You must set the criteria on a particular attribute by selecting the attribute (using the checkbox in the first column) and specifying the values in the Classification Criteria column. These values define the criteria the CAD data server uses to decide if a graphic element is a member of the feature class. See the appendix for the list of supported feature class definition attributes. The criteria must be set on at least one attribute for the feature class definition to be complete. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121454) EntityNumber must be included in the feature classification criteria for MicroStation database-linked feature classes. Therefore, it will be automatically selected and cannot be de-selected if the This feature has database linkages option is selected. 
You can key in individual values or a range of values. For attributes of the Boolean type, you must enter either 1 for true or 0 for false. For example, if all road features reside on level 1, you could key in 1 in the Classification Criteria field. If road features were on levels 1 through 5, you could key in: 
1-5
1,2,3,4,5
OR
1,2,3-5
OK
Saves all the changes you have made and closes the dialog box. If any map files have been selected on the Select Maps dialog box and if no map file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default all the selected map files will be associated with the feature class. If any coordinate system files have been selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog box and if no coordinate system file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default the first coordinate system file will be associated with the feature class. 
Cancel
Closes the dialog box without saving your changes.

##### General Tab
The General tab allows you to specify the Name, Geometry type, and Primary geometry for a feature class. You can optionally specify whether you want to serve/expose database attributes by enabling the database linkage option. For AutoCAD .csd files, you can also specify whether the feature class has tags. 
For AutoCAD .csd files, there is an additional This feature class has tags checkbox on the General tab and two additional tabs (Tags and Linkages). These two tabs are enabled only if the respective checkboxes are selected. In case of an "unknown" type of scanner the feature class will have neither the database linkage nor the block attributes. 
For .csd files of type “MicroStation V8”, there is an additional checkbox This feature class has tags on the General tab and an additional tab (Tags). This tab is enabled only if the This feature class has tags checkbox is selected. 
Tab Options
Name
Allows you to specify the name of the new feature class. You can edit the feature class name. You must key in a valid, unique name for the feature class in the Name field. 
Geometry type
Allows you to specify the geometry type for the new feature class by selecting the checkbox by one or more geometry types. This is a list of all the geometry fields. Select the Geometry type(s) for the feature class by checking the respective checkbox(es) to the left of each Geometry type. You can select multiple geometry types for a feature class. In this case, the feature class will have multiple geometry columns. Graphic elements that do not conform to the geometry type chosen are served up with NULL values in the geometry column. For example, if Line is chosen as the geometry type and if the feature class is defined as all graphics (that is, all the graphics of the Compound geometry type) on level 1, then Point, Text, and Area geometries that are found on level 1 will be served up with NULL as the value in the geometry column. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121444) Point geometry will contain the origin point for text and text node elements. If you want to use a text feature for spatial operations, both Point and Text attributes should be exposed, and Point should be selected as the primary geometry. 
Primary geometry
Allows you to specify the geometry type that is the primary geometry type for the new feature class, by selecting it from the drop-down list of geometry types. The choices available on the list are: 
  * PointGeometry
  * LinearGeometry
  * AreaGeometry
  * TextGeometry


This is a mandatory field. TextGeometry can be set as the primary geometry type only when no other geometry type is selected. 
This feature class has database linkages
Allows you to specify that the new feature class has database linkages. This option (along with the Tags tab and the Linkages tab) will appear only for AutoCAD, MicroStation V7, and for the MicroStation V8 template .csd files. This checkbox must to be checked if the feature class has block attribute information (which is also known as Tags). Upon checking this checkbox, the Linkages tab is enabled. If a feature class is linked to a database table, all the attributes from that table will be exposed in GeoMedia. The Linkages tab allows you to specify the database table name and the link field name associated with the feature class. If the primary key for database linked feature classes has not been specified, then by default the link field name will be taken as the primary unique key. 
This feature class has tags (block attributes)
Allows you to specify that the new feature class has tags. This option only appears if your .csd file is of the AutoCAD type. Select this option if the feature class has block attribute information (also known as tags). When you select this option, the Tags tab will be enabled. 
This feature class has tags
Allows you to specify that the new feature class has tags. This option only appears if your .csd file is of the MicroStation V8 type. Check this option if the feature class has non-graphical information (also known as tags). When you select this option, the Tags tab will be enabled. 
OK
Accepts your input and closes the dialog box.
Cancel
Dismisses the dialog box without saving the parameters you entered.

##### Graphic Attributes Tab
The Graphic Attributes tab allows you to select the graphic attributes for a feature class. Any enabled graphic attributes will be available for use in GeoMedia. 
Tab Options
Graphic Attribute Name
Lists the available graphic attributes that you can select for the feature class. This tab has a grid that is populated with the list of all the graphic attributes (defined in the template file). To add a particular graphic attribute to the schema of the feature class, you must to check the corresponding checkbox to the left of the Graphic Attribute Name. The Graphic Attribute Name column of the grid is read only. You must select all the graphic attributes you want the CAD data server to expose for the new feature class. See the [AutoCAD Scanner](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ouuEadlzn5bEMqacl7aWIg), [IGDS Scanner](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7LJ6g6bqgDbBEoPp5pQyYw), and[MicroStation Version 8 Scanner](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5P8BldmiKu5axScwPR0wZw) sections in the Appendix for the list of the supported graphic attributes for each of the CAD data server scanners. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121446) For IGDS/MicroStation V8 -based projects, if the data has database linkages and if the CAD data server has to serve up attribute data from the database, both the Database to to Table Linkage (that is, EntityNumber) and the Database to Row Linkage attribute (that is, OccurenceNumber) will be selected by default. Either of the linkage attributes (EntityNumber/OccurenceNumber) must be selected for every database-linked feature class. 
Type
Lists the data type defined for each graphic attribute. The Type column of the grid is read only 
Select All
Selects all of the graphic attributes for the feature class.
Unselect All
Unselects all of the graphic attributes.
OK
Saves all of your changes and closes the dialog box. If any map files have been selected on the Select Maps dialog box and if no map file has previously been associated with the feature class, then by default all the selected map files will be associated with the feature class. If any coordinate system files have been selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog box and if no coordinate system file has previously been associated with the feature class, then by default the first coordinate system file will be associated with the feature class. 
Cancel
Closes the dialog box without saving your changes.

##### Linkages Tab
In case of template file of AutoCAD type the Linkage tab will be enabled. The Linkage tab is available only with AutoCAD .csd files. The Linkage tab allows you to specify the database Table Name and the Link Field Name associated with the feature class. If a feature class is linked to a database table, all the attributes from that table will be exposed in GeoMedia. 
Tab Options
Table Name
Allows you to specify the database Table Name associated with the feature class. 
Link Field Name
Allows you to specify the Link Field Name associated with the feature class. If you have not specified the primary key for database linked feature classes, then by default the Link Field Name will be taken as the primary unique key. 
OK
Saves all the changes you have made. If any map files have been selected on the Select Maps dialog box and if no map file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default all the selected map files will be associated with the feature class. If any coordinate system files have been selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog box and if no coordinate system file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default the first coordinate system file will be associated with the feature class. 
Cancel
Closes the dialog box without saving your changes.

##### Tags Tab
The Tags tab appears for AutoCAD and MicroStation V8 .csd files where you have selected the This feature class has tags option. This option can be found in the CAD Schema Definition under the General tab. 
Tab Options
Name
Lists the available tags. You can select the tags that apply to the feature class by checking the checkbox to the left of the tag Name. 
Type
Lists the Type of the available tags. 
Size
Lists the Size of the available tags. 
Show Available Tags
This button will be enabled if map file(s) are selected. Clicking this button causes the grid to be populated with the available block attributes found in the associated map files. If no map files are associated with the feature class, then the grid is populated with the tags (block attributes) from all the selected map files. Once you select tags (block attributes), the selection is retained irrespective of changes in the map file list. 
Select All
Selects all of the displayed tags for the feature class.
Unselect All
Unselects all of the displayed tags.
OK
Saves all the changes you have made. If any map files have been selected on the Select Maps dialog box and if no map file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default all the selected map files will be associated with the feature class. If any coordinate system files have been selected on the Select Coordinate System Files dialog box and if no coordinate system file has been previously associated with the feature class, then by default the first coordinate system file will be associated with the feature class. 
Cancel
Closes the dialog box and you will lose all the changes done to the feature class definition.

#### Primary Unique Key Dialog
Use the Primary Unique Key dialog to specify which graphic attribute the CAD server is to use to define the primary unique key for all graphic-only feature classes and for all database-linked feature classes. Set the primary key options: 
  * Select primary unique key for all the graphic-only feature classes
  * Select primary unique key for all the database-linked feature classes


The lists are populated with the list of the graphic attributes.
Dialog Options
Select primary unique key for all the graphic only feature classes
Name - Displays a list of the default graphic attribute names. The Name corresponds to the name of the graphic attribute. 
Check the corresponding checkbox of a particular attribute to make it a primary unique key. 
You can modify the primary key name once you have selected it as the primary key. Once the primary key is selected the name text becomes editable. 
You can set the primary key on only one graphic attribute. 
By default, the graphic attribute ID is selected as the primary key for all the graphic-only feature classes and the database-linked feature classes. If ID is set as the primary key, then it is added to the list of graphic attributes to be exposed for the feature class. Note that the ID field is not listed in the graphic attributes tab of the feature class definition dialog (for example the New - <Feature Class Name> dialog). 
Select primary unique key for all the database linked feature classes
Name - Displays a list of the default graphic attribute names. The Name corresponds to the name of the graphic attribute. 
Check the corresponding checkbox of a particular attribute to make it a primary unique key. 
You can modify the primary key name once you have selected it as the primary key. Once the primary key is selected the name text becomes editable. 
You can set the primary key on only one graphic attribute. 
By default, the graphic attribute ID is selected as the primary key for all the graphic-only feature classes and the database-linked feature classes. 
OK - Saves your changes and closes the dialog. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121467) In the case of AutoCAD template type, nothing might be selected as primary unique key for all the database-linked feature classes. In that case, by default, the respective link field name will be taken as the primary unique key for the database-linked feature classes.

#### Running Define CAD Server Schema File
  1. Select  > Define CAD Server Schema File from Start menu. 
The Define CAD Server Schema File dialog opens.
  2. Select File > New to create a new CAD server schema file. 
OR 
  3. Select File > Open to open an existing CAD server schema file. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121427)You can also double-click an existing CAD Server Definition (.csd) file to open it in the Define CAD Server Schema File utility.

#### Select Coordinate System Files Dialog
Use the resizable Select Coordinate System Files dialog to specify the coordinate system files to be associated with the feature classes and with the map files. While working with IGDS design files, you can use either a .dgn file that contains a type-56 element as the coordinate system file, or you can use a .csf file. When working with AutoCAD drawing files or MicroStation V8 design files, you must use a .csf file. This command works in the same way as Feature Class > Select Maps command. 
Dialog Options
Available folders - Lists all the available folders you have selected. Initially it is empty. If the list is not empty when the dialog is initially opened, the first folder in this list is pre-selected. 
New - Opens the Browse For Folder dialog to browse for and select the folder or folders that contain your map files. You can select any folder in which the required maps exist. The new folder is automatically made the active folder. 
Change - Change the selected folder to a new folder. All the selected files of selected folder are attached to the folder irrespective of their existence in the new folder location. The changed folder is automatically made the active folder. Enabled when a folder is selected in the Available folders list. 
Remove - Remove the selected folder from the Available folders list. Enabled when a folder is selected in the Available folders list. 
Coordinate system files - Lists all of the coordinate system files in the selected folder. This list is pre-populated with all available selected coordinate system files. If all the folders are selected, it lists all the coordinate system files of all the folders. Select a coordinate system file by clicking the associated checkbox. 
Files of type - Change the filter that controls which map files are displayed in the Coordinate system files list. You can use wild card filter strings separated by semicolons, such as par*.csf; inter*.csf. This does not affect the selected coordinate system files. The filter is persisted in the .csd file. 
Select All - Selects all the unselected files. Enabled when map files are available in the Coordinate system files list and at least one map file is not selected. Once all the coordinate system files are selected, the button is disabled. 
Unselect All - Unselects all the selected files. Enabled when map files are available in the Coordinate system files list and at least one coordinate system file is selected. When you click this button, all the selected files are unselected and the button is disabled. 
OK - Saves your changes and closes the dialog. By default, the first selected coordinate system file is associated with all the selected map files and with all the feature classes that do not have an association with coordinate system file. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121440)
  * When you remove a folder in this command and there are map files in this folder that are associated with feature classes, then a message informs you that the action will de-select those map files and the association of feature class to map file will be lost. 
  * When you select .csf files, then the first available newly selected .csf file gets associated with all the map files and feature classes that are not associated with any .csf files. 
  * The same .csf files also get associated with all the feature classes that are not associated with any .csf files. 
  * The already selected .csf files (available when you enter the command) do not get associated with either map files or feature classes.

#### Select Map Files Dialog
Use the resizable Select Map Files dialog to select the folders and maps for feature classes. 
Dialog Options
Available folders - Lists all the available folders you have selected. Initially it is empty. If the list is not empty upon opening, the first folder in this list is pre-selected. The existing folders are associated with the folder icon. The missing folders are associated with a different folder icon and are shown in red color. 
New - Opens the Browse For Folder dialog to browse and select the folder or folders that contain your map files. You can select any folder in which the required maps exist. The new folder is automatically made the active folder. 
Change - Change the selected folder to a new folder. Enabled when a folder is selected in the Available folders list. 
If the selected folder also contains any selected coordinate system files, then upon changing the folder, a message asks if the change should reflect the selected coordinate system files. 
When you click No, then a new folder is added to the folders list and all the selected map files of the previous folder are attached to the new folder irrespective of their existence and the coordinate system files are not disturbed. 
When you click Yes, then the previous folder is changed to the selected folder and both selected map and coordinate system files are attached to the changed folder irrespective of their existence. The changed folder is automatically made the active folder. 
Remove - Remove the selected folder from the Available folders list. Enabled when a folder is selected in the Available folders list. 
Map files - Lists all of the map files in the selected folder. This list is pre-populated with all selected map files of all the folders and all the available map files in the selected folder. If all the folders are selected, it lists all the map files of all the folders. Select a map file by clicking the associated checkbox. Any non-existing map files are displayed in red. 
Files of type - Change the filter that controls which map files are displayed in the Map files list. You can use wild card filter strings separated by semicolons, such as par*.dgn; inter*.dgn. This does not affect the selected map files. The filter is persisted in the .csd file and is used for the selected folders. For any new folder, the default filter is used. The default filter is *.dgn for a MicroStation V7 or MicroStation V8 template, and *.dwg;*.dxf for the AutoCAD template. 
Select All - Selects all the unselected files. Enabled when map files are available in the Map files list and at least one map file is not selected. Once all the map files are selected, the button is disabled. 
Unselect All - Unselects all the selected files. Enabled when map files are available in the Map files list and at least one map file is selected. When you click this button, all the selected files are unselected and the button is disabled. 
OK - Saves your changes and closes the dialog. If you have selected coordinate system files, the first coordinate system file is associated with each newly selected map that does not have an associated coordinate system and all the newly selected map file will be associated with all the feature classes that are not associated with map files. 
Cancel - Closes the dialog without saving your changes. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121439)
  * When you remove a folder and there are .csf files in the folder that are associated with feature classes or map files, then a message informs you that the action will de-select those .csf files and the respective association will be lost. 
  * When you select map files, then the newly selected map files are associated with the first available .csf file. 
  * The same map files also get associated with all the feature classes that are not associated with any map files. 
  * The already selected map files (available when you enter the command) do not get associated with either .csf files or feature classes.

#### Specify Connection Parameters Dialog
Use the Specify connection Parameters dialog to specify the connection parameters for your .csd file. 
Dialog Options
Warehouse configuration file - Specify the warehouse configuration file name. You can use the Warehouse Configuration Utility to create .ini files. 
![reference_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121462)See [.INI File](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DxrCDdmZzGfpYcQ7r4dDDA) section for more information about .ini file variables. 
Browse - Browse for the warehouse configuration file. The Select a warehouse configuration file dialog opens, defaulted to INI Files (*.ini). The All Files filter is also available. 
ODBC data source - Select an ODBC data source from a list of all available ODBC data sources on your system. Required when you want to expose CAD attributes that are stored in a database. You can also enter any other name in the text field and create the ODBC data source name at a later time. Validation of the ODBC data source is not done. The ODBC data source name should point to the database where the CAD attributes are stored. 
User ID - Specify the user id of the ODBC data source, if required. 
Password - Specify the password for the ODBC data source, if required. 
Additional ODBC parameters - Specify additional information (if any) about the ODBC data source. 
![light_bulb_icon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/121462) Consult your database vendor or web resources for ODBC connection-specific parameters.

#### Update Map MBRs Dialog
Use the resizable Update Map MBRs dialog to get the minimum bounding rectangle (MBR) information for the map files in your .csd file. Enabled only when the map files have been selected. 
Dialog Options
Select All - Select all of the unselected map files for processing. 
Unselect All - Unselect all of the selected map files. 
Apply - Processes the selected map files for MBR values and updates them to the .csd file. Enabled when you select one or more map files. 
Clicking Apply updates the X Low, X High, Y Low, and Y High fields and saves the values to the .csd file. If the map file cannot be processed, the X Low, X High, Y Low, and Y High are updated with NULL values. If a particular map file could not be opened, then the Status column is updated with relevant information. For "Unknown" .csd file type, clicking Apply updates the keyed-in MBR values to the .csd file. 
Close - Closes the dialog. 
Grid Control 
1st column - Select the map file.
2nd column - Selected map files irrespective of their association to a feature class.
X Low, X High, Y Low, Y High MBR columns - Non-editable for .csd files built from the known template files (AutoCAD, MicroStation V7, and MicroStation V8). For "unknown" type .csd files, you must key in these values. 
Map File Status column - Present only for known template files (AutoCAD, MicroStation V7, and MicroStation V8). 
Once you select at least one map, click Apply. The files are populated with the MBR coordinates of the map files and saves those coordinates to the .csd file. If a particular map file could not be opened, then the Map File Status column is updated with the relevant information. If the map file cannot be processed, the MBR values are updated with NULL values. 
For "unknown" type .csd files, the X Low, X High, Y Low, and Y High columns are editable to key in MBR values. You can update the MBR values by keying in the values by selecting a particular map file. 
Click Apply to update the keyed in MBR values to the .csd file. If a particular map file could not be opened, then the Map File Status column is updated with the relevant information. If the map file cannot be processed, the MBR values are updated with NULL values. 
  * Updating Map MBRs


Update the MBR coordinates of the selected map files of a .csd file in one of the following ways: 
  * Running the DefCSD utility -- If you have a .csd file for which MBR coordinates of the selected map files are not updated, then you can run the preferred Update MBRs command from the Options menu after opening the .csd file. 
  * Using command line -- If you want to update only the MBR coordinates of an existing .csd file without opening the dialog, then use either of these two command line options. 
    * defcsd <.csd file name with the path> /u - where the argument /u causes the software to update the MBR coordinates without opening the dialog. The software displays an error message if automatic MBRs calculation functionality is not supported for a particular type of scanner. In this case, you must explicitly open the Define CAD Server Schema File utility and key in the MBR coordinate values for each map using the X Low, X High, Y Low, and Y High fields. 
    * updatembr <csd file name with the path> - This option is supported for backward compatibility. The functionality of this command line option is exactly the same as the earlier one. The UpdateMBR executable is a wrapper around the DefCSD functionality. The UpdateMBR utility internally calls the DefCSD utility with the parameter /u.

### Plotting

#### Custom Redlines Metadata
These are metadata tables are associated with custom redline creation objects: 
  * G3E_REDLINEGROUPIFACE
The [G3E_REDLINEGROUPIFACE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2zLpSeWM1XonE0hAY_YKKA) defines each unique custom redline group interface object required in your system. NetWorks Core does not provide default custom redline objects. 
  * G3E_REDLINEGROUPARG
The [G3E_REDLINEGROUPARG table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NL6PCZbCp__M6v55dIUy~A) specifies the arguments to each of the objects defined in G3E_REDLINEGROUPIFACE. These two tables together define the complete set of custom interfaces available in your system. You can think of these definitions as you would a procedure definition in a programming language: G3E_REDLINEGROUPIFACE defines the procedure names, and G3E_REDLINEGROUPARG defines their parameters. This is also like the entries in G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE, but in this case a separate table is used to define the arguments. 
  * G3E_REDLINEGRPMAPPING and G3E_REDLINEGROUPARGVAL
The [G3E_REDLINEGRPMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e~mCuZXLUDMTjWYvePuZkQ) and [G3E_REDLINEGROUPARGVAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iRX_xaLS7VLwqc2FxPxQJA) tables define the complete set of choices of custom redline creation options your user needs. You can use the same redline group object with different arguments to create several different kinds of custom redline groups. Each row in G3E_REDLINEGRPMAPPING defines a choice presented to the user. The entries in G3E_REDLINEGROUPARGVAL provide the argument values to use for each of those choices.

[Custom Redlines](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jI56RpglLnD56nEJll_MnQ)

#### Custom Redlines
NetWorks Core provides basic tools to create and edit redline elements (points, text, lines, areas, and embedded objects) in your plots. In some cases, users may need to place more complex redline constructs repetitively. For example, a user may need to create a rectangle containing several text elements and symbols to document a work order associated with a plot. You can write custom objects to create these complex constructs with minimal user input to ease these repetitive tasks. 
The following graphic shows a plot sheet containing a map frame and several redline groups that have been placed using custom redline objects: 
  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262150)
The four text blocks on the left are four separate redline groups that were placed using custom objects. All of the information in these groups was derived from a feature called a work point in the map frame. The custom redline group object asked the user to identify the work point and then generated these redline groups. At the top left is a list of materials required for the construction associated with the work point. Below that (beginning with "1 STA") is some detailed information about the transformer to be installed as part of this work. Below that are two blocks identifying other features to be placed as part of the work point. Note the use of the same symbol in the redline (around the numbers 1 and 2) that is used in the map to identify the feature. This was accomplished with the custom object using an appropriate style. 
These redline groups each consist of multiple text blocks arranged in a specific format. That format and the textual content itself were all generated by the custom object using a minimal amount of user input. This saves users considerable time required to get the layout just right, as well as the time required to look up the information and type it in. If the information changes as the design and construction progress, these redline groups can be regenerated easily from information in the database. 
This example could have been generated by a single custom object or multiple objects. A single object, in a single invocation, can generate multiple redline groups, so this example could have been done in one operation. Alternatively, each group could be generated by a separate custom object if needed.

#### Insert Legend Command
The [Insert Legend command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tBlyeo1mCWt~fHdH~Gj37A) works without configuration; however, users might find that the styles for the legend title and legend key descriptions are not adequate. You can use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) to configure two areas of the legend: 
  * The text styles for the legend title and legend entry key descriptions. Create text styles so that users can easily find suitable text styles in the Title and Style fields on the Insert Legend dialog box. 
  * The content of the legend entry key descriptions so that they make sense on the legend. Users do not have to manually edit each legend entry key description. 


The steps in the following workflow are optional.
  * To configure styles for Insert Legend:


  1. Verify that the styles you want to use are set [for use with plot redlines](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9VpaS6vw9LwAYX9NprEfag). 
  2. [Define a new text style](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CpXL2BFXY4jhHmnoqlMLZA) or edit an existing style to use as a legend title. For example, type Legend Title as the G3E_USERNAME so it is easy for users to find in the Insert Legend dialog box Title field. 
  3. Repeat Step 2 to create a text style—for example, Legend Entry Description—so it is easy for users to find in the Insert Legend dialog box Style field. 
  4. Create more readable content for legend key descriptions:
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Styles Rules > <Rule Name> > Rule Steps > <Rule Step> node to update the G3E_STYLERULE table. 
    2. In the G3E_DESCRIPTION field, edit the text so that it makes sense on the legend.
This text is defaulted from the G3E_xxxxSTYLE.G3E_USERNAME field of a normalized table where the G3E_SNO field matches the G3E_STYLERULE.G3E_SNO field. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258401?tocId=PNGW2qKKX4y46tZ7w9rg0Q) You can create a new point, area, or line style with a username that is more readable and [link it to a style rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q4dl7dWIs5NZfqbJsgqufQ). 
    3. To see where the text in the G3E_DESCRIPTION field comes from, double-click the G3E_SNO field (the foreign key).

[Plot Templates](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mAYVGnmy5m9gobvD8F4zNw)

#### Plot Templates
Much of the configuration for plotting centers around the creation and maintenance of plot templates. A plot template is simply a named plot stored in a work space that users copy or use in batch plotting. A plot template does not differ significantly from any other kind of named plot, although templates used in batch plotting usually contain elements not typically used in interactive plots. The word template indicates primarily an intended use of the named plot. 
Users typically prepare several different kinds of plots for various purposes. Some may be used for construction, others for maintenance tasks, and still others for record keeping. Users produce some plots interactively and others on a regular basis using batch procedures. Each kind of plot typically has a specific layout it must follow, specified as part of the business rules of the utility. Plot templates capture those layouts and allow the user to concentrate on filling in the information that varies from one instance to the next. You can use the Insert Legend command to [create a prepopulated legend](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tBlyeo1mCWt~fHdH~Gj37A) for a plot template. This legend should contain a legend entry for each feature-component representation that might be displayed in a plot that uses this template. 
Interactive Plot Templates
Plot templates prepared for interactive use typically contain one or more map frames with a legend already attached, but they may not display any particular area. You should set the scale that is generally used for that type of plot. 
The typical template also contains a title block or other identifying element. You can construct these using redlines, or you can use embedded objects, such as a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258395) Microsoft Excel spreadsheets are an excellent way to create title blocks consisting of rectangles with text. 
You can also use Microsoft Word documents or any other OLE embedded object.
Plot templates can also include a scalebar and a north arrow control. There can be at most one of each of these per plot sheet, and they must be associated with a map frame. Typically, a plot sheet contains one of the following: 
  * A single map frame.
  * One map frame which is the primary frame and more map frames that are overviews or detail views. 


You create plot templates just as you create work space templates (.gft files). This allows a user to [open a new work space as a copy of one of these templates](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/imSrOdq03uDbB7mK~f9Qdg) and helps ensure that the original template is not inadvertently overwritten. You can store multiple plot templates in each work space, or you can have only one template per work space. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258395) Users can save copies of these work spaces many times. If you put all your templates in one work space, but users typically use only one or two of those templates at any one time, the users' work spaces may be much larger than necessary and may take longer to open and save.

#### Plotting Styles
The redline elements you draw on a plot sheet use styles defined in metadata just like graphic elements in the map view. In many cases, however, you do not want (or need) all of the map-related styles for creating redlines. You can also create styles that are only used for plotting redlines. 
NetWorks Core lets you restrict the set of styles presented to the user when creating redline elements. This reduces the list of styles from which to choose, and it helps enforce plot conventions.

#### Style Substitutions
To make style substitutions available on the [Plot Sheet Properties dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CrXbtAQ1O7aD3PXPGkL2Dw), you must first define them in metadata. Using Metadata Explorer, you identify a group of mapped styles in the [G3E_STYLETYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c27M~vRL2FzhPQcHTHljFw) table. Each style type consists of multiple style mappings set in [G3E_STYLEMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U6KvxykaaQx6sJIyvSrBzg). Style mappings are pairs of style numbers, one indicating the style to map and the other indicating the new style to use in its place. 
  * G3E_STYLETYPE
G3E_STNO contains the unique style number.  
G3E_USERNAME contains the name of the style or product. 
  * G3E_STYLEMAPPING
G3E_STNO points to the style type to which this mapping applies.
G3E_LEGENDSNO identifies the style number that can be found on the legend entry.
G3E_SNO contains the style number to use in place of the one on the legend entry.
