### Regional Subsetting

#### Area Ownership Versus Regional Subsetting
Using an area as a parent feature for several subordinate features is like using regional subsetting. In both cases, subordinate features are related to a containing area. However, you should use area ownership in cases where only a limited number of features are contained (for example, features inside a substation or a manhole). In cases where all of the features in a large region are to be contained (could be thousands of features, for example, a wire center), you should use regional subsetting because regional subsetting is optimized to manage large sets of subordinate features during validation processing.

#### Configuration Coordinate System
When viewing multiple regions, a different coordinate system may be more appropriate than that used when viewing any of the individual regions. Since the software does not transform coordinates in the display pathway, you must transform the coordinates for all regions to the appropriate target coordinate system during publish. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260859) You do not have to transform data to a different coordinate system when publishing a configuration, but this option is available. 
You must provide information about the coordinate system for each configuration. Then the publish process can transform the coordinates of the published data to the appropriate coordinate system for the combination of regions for that configuration. If no coordinate system is specified, no transform is performed, and the configuration is published in the same coordinate system as that of the database. 
This information is captured in [G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_CSNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vWwv39pUkFaofbuloNJ4lQ). 
Related Topic
[Configurations to View Multiple Regions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/M6CmBQ8Cjebxnv0771miKw)

#### Configurations to View Multiple Regions
Working in a regional subset presents the challenge of smooth editing at the borders of the regions. For jobs whose primary area of work straddles the regions, it helps to work with a different DDC published over both regions. This is also true for work involving a larger area over multiple regions. 
Instead of publishing just a single region, configurations should span a set of regions. For this reason, metadata needs to associate configurations with a number of regions. The [G3E_CONFIGURATIONS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vWwv39pUkFaofbuloNJ4lQ) table maps configurations to their regions. 
If a configuration of the G3E_DATACONNECTION table is not found in the G3E_CONFIGURATIONS table, the configuration is neither subsetted nor transformed. This is misleading because if the tables in the database have a subsetting attribute in the G3E_COMPONENT table, they are subsetted, and the absence of the configuration name in this table implies that everything is filtered out and nothing found. Thus, when a database begins to be subsetted, all configurations over that database need to have entries here. 
  * To map a region to a configuration:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Metadata Administration > Configurations to View Multiple Regions and [add a new row](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KJ7j6x3pPcUJxgHyeT4Snw) to G3E_CONFIGURATIONS table. 
    1. In the G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME field, type the name of an existing production database. This value comes from [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) where G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_TYPE = 3 ( designating a Production database). 
    2. In the G3E_REGIONNAME field, type a name for the region. 
    3. In the G3E_CSNAME field, select a coordinate system. 
If you do not select a coordinate system for the configuration, data are published in the coordinate system of the database. 
  2. Click OK. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260857) to commit the changes to the database. 


Related Topic
[Configuration Coordinate System](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ec1JGzcKhzhuR4DMQx6Eeg)

#### Defining Features for Subsets
Each feature you want to subset must have at least one subset component. You indicate which features to subset in [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_SUBSETATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). These components are directly subsetted. An indirectly subsetted component does not contain an entry in the G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_SUBSETATTRIBUTE and is subsetted by joining on G3E_FID to a directly subsetted component of the feature. 
Direct and Indirect Subsetting
A feature that contains a directly subsetted component is considered subsetted, and all components of that feature are also considered subsetted, either directly or indirectly. Therefore, a feature cannot contain subsetted and non-subsetted components. Shared indirectly subsetted components cannot be members of features that contain different directly subsetted components. 
For indirectly subsetted components, the directly subsetted component used in the LTT view to identify the membership of the subset must be required and nonrepeating. This ensures that subset membership is based on one and only one directly subsetted component instance. 
For indirectly subsetted features, the primary geographic component should be the first component inserted, and the directly subsetted component must be the last component deleted. If the directly subsetted component is inserted before the primary geographic component, the LTT insert trigger fails because the region name attribute is not set. If the directly subsetted component is deleted before other components, those components are not deleted when the feature is deleted. The insert and delete orders are controlled by [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_INSERTORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) and [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_DELETEORDINAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). 
The value of the subset attribute determines the region of which a given record is a part. These come from the region name attribute of the region feature in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table. See [Defining Regions for Subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~oPA5bbq4~dBEaAkest0tA) for more information. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256244) Feature types that cross regions do not have to be subsetted. They are published in their entirety. 
Related Topic
[Setting the Subsetting Attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/i3pWvOjTRdBMjaEs4pPmsA)

#### Defining Regions for Subsets
You must set up metadata to indicate available regions to be viewed. This indicates the criteria by which tables may be subsetted. The geometry of each region determines the location of a new feature. The geometries of regions should not overlap. The complete set of region feature instances is considered a continuous layer of geographic areas when pieced together. Areas are expected to align with each other. Any gaps in the layer should be geographic locations that are not part of the service territory. 
A regions area feature contains the available regions. The regions feature is specified in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table to help segregate work. 
  * To create a region area feature:


  1. Create an area feature to use as the region boundary, if one does not already exist.
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Work Management Systems and [add a new row](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KJ7j6x3pPcUJxgHyeT4Snw) to G3E_WORKMGMT table. 
    1. In the G3E_TYPE field, select Region. 
    2. In the G3E_TABLE field, select G3E_CONFIGURATIONS. 
    3. In the G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE field, type G3E_CONFIGURATIONS_OPTABLE.
    4. In the G3E_PARAMETER field, type a string consisting of G3E_FNO, G3E_ANO. The feature number is the area feature you want to use for the region boundary. The attribute number is in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table of the column containing the region name which is used as a subsetting attribute. 
Region features are placed as regular features and the name attribute is required.
  3. Click OK. 


Related Topics
[Defining Features for Subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pdikTUhuJAlLXRcY9ehfAA)
[Setting the Subsetting Attribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/i3pWvOjTRdBMjaEs4pPmsA)

#### LTT Views to Subset Regions
For [tables being directly subsetted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Kfrd556X1U3aclQDLSLvCw), the procedure creating the LTT view adds the following statement at the beginning of the WHERE clause of the LTT view: 
SubsetAttribute is null or SubsetAttribute in (Select  
G3E_RegionName from G3E_Configurations where  
G3E_ConfigurationName=LTT_USER.CONFIGURATION) and 
If the [G3E_CONFIGURATIONS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vWwv39pUkFaofbuloNJ4lQ) table is empty, this statement is not added. 
All queries through the LTT view restrict access to the appropriate records. Once the session has specified the appropriate configuration and thus specified the regions, nothing else needs to be done (except transform) by the publishing process, the client, or the component views. Finds, queries, and edits all get the correct records. 
For NetWorks Core workflows, subsetting the primary attribute and/or the primary tabular component is sufficient to achieve the required subsetting. Most, if not all, published component views reference either or both of the primary tabular and graphic component tables. Given that, the published DDC is so subsetted. The subsetting attribute does not have to be selected into the component view. 
Most data access in NetWorks Core is driven by selection in the DDC or queries against the primary tabular component. Most subsequent queries to the database are restricted to the keys returned. Thus, queries to non-primary tables are qualified by key, and those tables may not need to be subsetted in the LTT views. This may not be the case for third-party applications running against the database. 
Rather than populating the subset attribute on every row of every table for tables not directly subsetted, the software determines if there are any tables of that feature that are subsetted (must be a required, nonrepeating component). If so, it gets one of those tables' names—"SubsettedView," for example—and adds the following statement to the LTT view WHERE clause: 
exists (select * from SubsettedView C where A.G3E_FID = C.G3E_FID);
… where a is the required, nonrepeating component table. 
This achieves the indirect subsetting. If the subsetted table does not yield a record, the join yields nothing for this table. This extra join to a common table is convenient for the data model, but it generates extra work in the server on every query and access to this LTT view. Directly subsetting by putting the subset attribute on every table is more efficient. 
Shared tables need not be directly subsetted unless they are the primary attribute table. This assumes that the component table to join with (SubsettedView) is appropriate for all the features that share this table. 
No trigger on a directly subsetted table can modify a table that is indirectly subsetted using the directly subsetted table. This causes a circular reference back to the original subsetted table. Such triggers are referred to as mutating the table (ORA-4091 error). 
For performance reasons, you must create an index for the subset attribute.
Related Topic
[Subsetting a Database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8Is19Jg8morgvxnDvNHsqA)

#### Setting the Subsetting Attribute
To maintain the subsetting process, inserted records of the appropriate tables must have the subsetting attribute set to the correct value. When configurations comprise a single region, this is easy for either the client or the LTT insert trigger to do. Simply set the value to that of the region being viewed. 
For configurations comprised of multiple regions, some work must be done to determine which region is appropriate for the record. 
The SetSubsettingAttribute Functional interface on the client-side sets the region. This Functional interface is given access to the feature component recordset, can access geometry from the primary graphic component, and can set the attribute on the subsetted tables' recordsets (there may be more than one). It determines the subsetted component table recordsets and attribute names from the G3E_COMPONENT metadata. Since this Functional interface is typically defined as an "Update" Functional interface (see [G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_FUNCTIONALTYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)), it fires when the transaction is committed. If the feature is not subsetted, no tables are subsetted and there is nothing to set. Otherwise it determines the region for the feature based on the feature's geometry and the geometry of all the regions features being viewed. For those tables that are subsetted, it sets the subsetting attribute value to this region name. 
The Functional interface uses the geometry from the component view in the DDC for the primary graphic component for the FNO of the regions feature in G3E_WORKMGMT. The attribute with subset attribute values indicated by the ANO in G3E_WORKMGMT must be selected into this same component view, and the attribute name must not be aliased. 
If a feature overlaps regions, the Functional interface uses the first one it finds that the feature overlaps. This is in the order that the region features come out of the component view, not the order that the feature's vertices cross. Configurations overlap and share regions to handle features that cross regions. 
The SetSubsettingAttribute Functional interface checks that the subsetting attribute is valid for this configuration. If it is not valid, it raises an exception. 
Even when the subsetting attribute value is appropriate for a configuration, users can later log into a different configuration with fewer regions, edit the same job and post. Users may not see all the records they initially created because they are filtered out by region. Hence, the feature and validation do not see them as part of the job. Validate sees them in the Pending Edits table, but does not find them in the configuration causing a post to the database to fail. 
Related Topics
[Defining Features for Subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pdikTUhuJAlLXRcY9ehfAA)
[Defining Regions for Subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~oPA5bbq4~dBEaAkest0tA)

#### Subsetting a Database
The following is a general workflow for subsetting a database:
  1. Define the [area feature to be used as the region boundary](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~oPA5bbq4~dBEaAkest0tA). 
  2. Define the [features for the subset](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pdikTUhuJAlLXRcY9ehfAA). 
  3. Map the [region to a configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/M6CmBQ8Cjebxnv0771miKw). 
  4. In NetWorks Core, [place the region feature](http://www.) around the area you want to subset to create the region boundary of the subset. 
  5. Populate the subset attribute of the subset components with the region name you defined in Step 3. 
  6. Define the [SetSubsettingAttribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) functional interface to maintain the subset attribute. 
  7. [Add support for regional subsetting](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kCEf5MQL~JwsztXU7P3sGQ) within the LTT view. Set the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER [IgnoreSubsettingForLTT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) to 0. 
OR 
If you are subsetting the database for Field Review only, you do not need LTT view subset support. Set the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER [IgnoreSubsettingForLTT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) to 1 to prevent the LTT views from subsetting. 


To publish a subset on a laptop, add these steps:
  1. [Configure the computer on which to publish subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/z4IfPaBvERXHt8vvYNfk_g) to install on mobile computers. 
  2. Verify that you are [ready to publish](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCr0Ij6u3vCWJqtAxzJ6hA) subsets. 
  3. [Publish the subset](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/46qbwFX5xtEWsDh3DJmsBQ). 
  4. [Install the subset](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sUwNYtkgHOqUP~VaUVHW5A) on the mobile computer.

#### Viewing All Regions
Once a G3E_CONFIGURATIONS table with regions has been set up, you need to define a configuration that includes all regions to see all regions. 
If a configuration of the G3E_DATACONNECTION table is not found in the G3E_CONFIGURATIONS table, the configuration is neither subsetted nor transformed. This can be misleading because if the tables in the database have a subsetting attribute in the G3E_COMPONENT table, they are subsetted, and the absence of the configuration name in this table implies that everything is filtered out and nothing is found. Once a database begins to be subsetted, all configurations over that database need to have entries. 
Related Topics
[Viewing Configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oLv6z1_bY2FcQv6gpcqTxg)
[Defining Regions for Subsets](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~oPA5bbq4~dBEaAkest0tA)

#### Viewing Configurations and Their Regions
Users specify which configuration and regions to view, like how they specify jobs. This means running a procedure, LTT_USER.SetConfiguration('ConfigurationName'), to specify the configuration and the regions. Since users have already selected the configuration, this is something the NetWorks Core server calls after connecting to the Oracle database. It is available to SQL users and other applications to restrict queries to the database, although they are not using DDC files by configuration name. 
Only one configuration may be specified for a connection. NetWorks Core uses the G3E_CONFIGURATIONS table to map the configuration name to the regions. 
LTT_USER.SetConfiguration('ConfigurationName') sets a property on the LTT_ADMIN package called Configuration. This is specific to the current session. 
Related Topic
[Viewing All Regions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mYpmwqBkPtjSNe2tOdmguQ)

### Relationships

#### Break Subsystem

##### Cable Allocation After Break

###### Cable Allocation After Break Assumptions
NetWorks Core software that allocates a child feature after a break is based on several assumptions: 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259892) NetWorks Core software does not validate these assumptions. The software cannot determine whether the assumptions are met because they depend on the intentions of the user. When the software can detect a potential violation of the assumptions, it reports violations as ambiguities for the user to resolve. 
  * The feature that is broken was [correctly allocated](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U8CqO9ZEqAO1imM7NZbfvA) before the break. If this assumption is violated, the software may report ambiguities in the [allocation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259892) after the break. 
The process of establishing a relationship, typically some sort of ownership or containment, between two features. 
  * Detail graphic sections are placed in the detail drawings associated with any node (for example, a manhole) in the infrastructure network where: 
    * The cable begins or ends.
    * The cable can be broken.
    * Duct assignments may change.
  * At locations where the cable enters or leaves the underground network, one of the following must be true: 
    * A detail section must be placed in the detail drawing associated with the node (for example, manhole) where the cable enters or leaves the network. 
    * A geographic section must be placed within a metadata-specified tolerance of the last containing feature in the path where the cable enters or leaves the network. 
  * The linear components of the broken feature have already been correctly assigned to the resulting features. This is especially important for the detail sections because they are used to help determine how the infrastructure is linearly related to the broken feature. How these components are assigned is not critical, but it must be done. For cable and wire in the communications model, component assignment is based on the section start location attributes assigned to each cable section. 
  * Breaking a cable in a detail section implies that the physical location of the break lies within the bounds of the referencing feature of that detail.   
|  Example Breaking a cable in a manhole detail implies that the break physically occurs inside the manhole (and not in a conduit section connected to the manhole).   |  
| --- |  


Given these assumptions, the software can use the following to determine how the resulting features of the break should be allocated: 
  * Assignment of the geo and detail cable sections
  * Connection between the cable sections and the detail-referencing feature
  * [Node-edge connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lVlHcmN8aYrqo9dkv2agMA) relationship of the container features 
  * Spatial proximity of the geo sections to those containers


The software analyzes the node-edge connectivity paths that connect any two adjacent detail-referencing features. Adjacent means that the path does not pass through any other intermediate detail-referencing feature. For each such path, the software make these conclusions about the allocation based on the assignment of the detail sections within the endpoint referencing features: 
  * If both endpoints contain a section that was assigned to the original feature, the original feature must go through that path, so it should be allocated to the path connecting the endpoints. 
  * If both endpoints contain a section that was assigned to the copy feature, the copy feature must go through that path, so it should be allocated to the path connecting the endpoints. 
  * A [loopback](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259892) is a situation where a feature goes through the same container twice. This situation is typically ambiguous unless it can be resolved using a duct attribute. Therefore, ambiguities cause the software to allocate part or all of a path to both features. Such cases are also flagged with a [repair feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U8CqO9ZEqAO1imM7NZbfvA). 
A situation in which the feature is allocated to the same container (conduit or duct) going into and out of the loop. If the feature is allocated to different ducts in the same path, the software resolves the allocation successfully or marks the ambiguity. 
  * If a [duct](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259892) or [inner duct](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259892) container is marked as ambiguous, use a metadata-specified attribute (for example, the duct assignment) to attempt to resolve the ambiguity. If another duct in the same path segment has the same duct assignment and is not ambiguous, the software marks the ambiguous duct as original or copy, according to the designation of the unambiguous matching duct. 
In an underground model, a container of some sort, usually a pipe. A duct is used to contain other facilities like cables or conductors. 
A container within a duct modeled as a separate feature. It is also used to contain other facilities like cables. The types of feature in the inner ducts do not have to be the same as the types of features in the duct. 
  * If a path begins or ends (or both) at a feature other than a detail-referencing feature, the software finds one or more geographic sections of the broken feature spatially near the first or last container feature in that path. The software uses the assignment of those components to the original or copy feature in the same way it uses the detail sections. If a connected set of container features ends without a detail referencing feature and there are no geographic sections in proximity to the end of that set, the path is ambiguous.

##### Interior Node-Edge Connectivity Node Assignment Algorithm

###### Diagram for Interior NEC Node Assignment Algorithm
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Cu4sr_zMoVjnJ4IatoIhEw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=cdfd2687b55db25f&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

###### Interior NEC Fifth (Final) Pass Node Assignment Algorithm Logic
  1. If the UnresolvedFifthPass list is empty or there are no Tier5 linear related features, the algorithm proceeds to the [Final Manual Resolution Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uI7_So6zaFJQsQ2eUlQwGw). 
  2. Otherwise, each related feature in the UnresolvedFifthPass list is processed again to find the closest feature in the Tier5LinearRelatedFeatures list. 
  3. If the related feature is within tolerance of the closest Tier5 linear component, the following items occur: 
    1. The related feature is updated with the same node value that was set on the nearest Tier5 linear feature. Node1 or Node2 is updated depending on which one matched the original N1 or N2 value. 
    2. If the related feature is a one-node device, both Node1 and Node2 are updated with same node value. 
  4. If the related feature is not within tolerance of the Tier5 linear, the feature must be manually resolved in the [Final Manual Resolution Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uI7_So6zaFJQsQ2eUlQwGw) (that is, UnresolvedFinalAB).

###### Interior NEC Final Manual Resolution Logic
  1. The UnresolvedFinalAB list is populated in two places:
     * Step 1 in the [First Pass Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fKc~NB6UPoQpkSt5_xMO3Q) - the related feature's triggering geometry is NULL. 
     * Step 4 in the [Fifth (Final) Pass Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/S5kotDu7CGokG8uU2JOVHw) - the related feature is not within tolerance to any linear feature in tiers 1 through 5. That is, it is not within tolerance of the broken linear feature or any other related linear feature 
  2. If the UnresolvedFinalAB list is empty, all related features have been automatically reconnected to either FeatureA or FeatureB. 
  3. If the UnresolvedFinalAB list is not empty, the [Resolve Node-Edge Connectivity dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WsEncm3rBB4nKdAa5BcLCA) is displayed so the user can resolve them. Only the Feature A or B tab is seen in this final manual resolution step.

###### Interior NEC Node Assignment Algorithm First Pass Logic
In the first pass, each related feature's geometry is compared to the two linear segments resulting from the break. The related feature's geometry can come from different triggering components depending on the map window in which the break occurred. The geographic triggering component is used in geographic window cases; the alternate geographic triggering component is used in alternate geographic window cases; and the detail triggering component is used in detail window cases. 
  1. If the related feature's triggering geometry is NULL, the related feature cannot be automatically assigned to FeatureA or FeatureB. Therefore, it must be manually resolved after processing all other related features. This particular related feature can be manually assigned to either FeatureA or FeatureB because its distance to each cannot be determined (that is, UnresolvedFinalAB - see the [Final Manual Resolution Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uI7_So6zaFJQsQ2eUlQwGw) topic). Return to Step 1 to process the next related feature. 
  2. If the related feature's triggering geometry is not NULL, it is projected to both FeatureA and FeatureB to determine which feature is closer. The related feature might be offset from the linear. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259902)
    1. To be resolved in this first pass, the related feature must be within the broken feature's defined tolerance. The tolerance is defined in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). For each linear triggering component, the G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE value is defaulted to the [AverageSymbolSize](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) general parameter, but you can change the value to achieve better results. 
      1. If the related feature is linear, it is remembered so that it can be used in the second pass of the algorithm (that is, in Tier2LinearRelatedFeatures). The lime green linear features [in the image](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259902) are Tier2 linear features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Cu4sr_zMoVjnJ4IatoIhEw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=cdfd2687b55db25f&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
      2. If the related feature is closer to FeatureA, FeatureA's geometry is used in the comparisons in Step 3. In the example above, Related1 is closer to FeatureA. Proceed with Step 3. 
      3. If the related feature is closer to FeatureB, FeatureB's geometry is used in the comparisons in Step 3. In the example above, Related2 is closer to FeatureB. Proceed with Step 3. 
      4. If the related feature is the same distance to FeatureA and FeatureB, it must be manually resolved after all features have been processed in the first pass. This related feature can be manually assigned to either FeatureA or FeatureB because it is the same distance to each feature (that is, UnresolvedFirstPassAB - see Step 4 in the First Pass Logic). Return to Step 1 to process the next related feature. 
    2. If the related feature is not within tolerance, it is processed again in a subsequent pass (that is, UnresolvedSecondPass; see [Second, Third, and Fourth Pass Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j00nKruLwNki2CaLLrGdpw)). Return to Step 1 to process the next related feature. 
  3. FeatureA and FeatureB are internally broken at their respective midpoints to create internal segments: FeatureA's Node1 and Node2 segments; FeatureB's Node1 and Node2 segments. The internal break happens one time before the first pass. It is for algorithmic purposes only; it is not saved as part of the break operation. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259902)
    1. Consider Related1. It is closer to FeatureA so it is compared to FeatureA's Node1 and Node2 segments to determine which node assignment to make. Since it is closer to FeatureA's Node2 segment, N2' is set on the appropriate node of Related1. It might be Related1's Node1 or Node2 value depending on which one matched the original N1 or N2 value. If Related1 is a one-node device, both Node1 and Node2 are updated with N2'. 
If Related1 is the same distance to FeatureA's Node1 and Node2 segments, it must be manually resolved after all features have been processed in the first pass. If Related1 is closer to FeatureA and it is the same distance to FeatureA's Node1 and Node2 segments, it can only be assigned FeatureA's Node1 or Node2 values (that is, UnresolvedFirstPassA - see Step 4 in the First Pass Logic). 
    2. Consider Related2. It is closer to FeatureB, so it is compared to FeatureB's Node1 and Node2 segments to determine which node assignment to make. Since it is closer to FeatureB's Node1 segment, N1' is set on the appropriate node of Related2. It might be Related2's Node1 or Node2 value depending on which one matched the original N1 or N2 value. If Related2 is a one-node device, both Node1 and Node2 are updated with N1'. 
If Related2 is the same distance to FeatureB's Node1 and Node2 segments, it must be manually resolved after all features have been processed in the first pass. If Related2 is closer to FeatureB and it is the same distance to FeatureB's Node1 and Node2 segments, it can only be assigned FeatureB's Node1 or Node2 values (that is, UnresolvedFirstPassB - see Step 4 in the First Pass Logic). 
    3. Return to Step 1 to process the next related feature.
  4. Before proceeding with the second pass of the algorithm, any related features that were within tolerance but could not be automatically resolved must be resolved now: UnresolvedFirstPassAB, UnresolvedFirstPassA, UnresolvedFirstPassB. 
    1. If there are not any items in these lists, execution continues to the [Second, Third, and Fourth Pass Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j00nKruLwNki2CaLLrGdpw). 
    2. If there are items in at least one of these lists, the [Resolve Node-Edge Connectivity dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WsEncm3rBB4nKdAa5BcLCA) is displayed so the user can resolve them. 
      1. Here are reasons why related features that are within tolerance [(G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) of FeatureA or FeatureB still might not be automatically resolved in the first pass: 
The related feature is the same distance to FeatureA and FeatureB. These unresolved related features appear on the Feature A or B tab only. If there are not any, the Feature A or B tab is omitted. See Step 2.a.iv. 
The related feature is closer to FeatureA and it is the same distance to FeatureA's Node1 and Node2 segments. These unresolved related features appear on the Feature A tab only. If there are not any, the Feature A tab is omitted. See Step 3.a.i. 
The related feature is closer to FeatureB and it is the same distance to FeatureB's Node1 and Node2 segments. These unresolved related features appear on the Feature B tab only. If there are not any, the Feature B tab is omitted. See Step 3.b.i. 
      2. Resolving these features after the first pass is important because more features along the second and subsequent linear tiers can be automatically assigned. 
      3. After resolving these features, execution continues with the [second pass](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j00nKruLwNki2CaLLrGdpw).

###### Interior NEC Second, Third, and Fourth Pass Node Assignment Algorithm Logic
  1. If the UnresolvedSecondPass list is empty or there are no Tier2 linear related features, the algorithm skips any subsequent passes and proceeds to the [Final Manual Resolution Logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uI7_So6zaFJQsQ2eUlQwGw). 
  2. Otherwise, each related feature in the UnresolvedSecondPass list is processed again to find the closest feature in the Tier2LinearRelatedFeatures list. The related feature must be within tolerance of the closest Tier2 linear feature to be resolved in this pass. Again, the tolerance is defined in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for the closest Tier2 linear feature, not the related feature being processed. 
    1. [In the diagram](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909), the Tier3 linear features should be in the UnresolvedSecondPass list. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Cu4sr_zMoVjnJ4IatoIhEw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=cdfd2687b55db25f&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
    2. There should also be several unresolved single node point features along the Tier2 and Tier3 linear features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909)
In the figure below, the Tier2 lime green linear features and the single node point features within tolerance of the broken Tier1 linear feature should already be resolved. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909)
  3. If the related feature is within tolerance of the closest Tier2 linear, the following items occur: 
    1. If the related feature is linear, it is remembered so that it can be used in a subsequent pass of the algorithm (that is, in Tier3LinearRelatedFeatures). The purple linear features [in the diagram](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909) are Tier3 linear features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Cu4sr_zMoVjnJ4IatoIhEw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=cdfd2687b55db25f&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
    2. If there is only one Tier2 linear within tolerance, the related feature is updated with the same node value that was set on the nearest Tier2 linear feature. Node1 or Node2 is updated depending on which one matched the original N1 or N2 value. 
    3. If there are multiple Tier2 linear features within tolerance, the nearest Tier2 linear is used and its node values are updated as stated above. 
    4. If there are multiple Tier2 linear features within tolerance and they are the same distance to the related feature, the following items occur. This logic applies to passes two through five. The N in TierN refers to the current pass (for example, 2, 3, 4, or 5): 
      1. If the TierN linear features that are the same distance to the related feature were assigned the same node value, the related feature is updated with that node value. Or if these same TierN features were disconnected in an earlier pass, then the related feature is disconnected as well. 
      2. If the TierN linear features that are the same distance to the related feature were not assigned the same node value, or if at least one was disconnected and at least one was assigned a node value, the related feature is added to the UnresolvedWithinTolerancePassN list to be resolved in step 5 of each pass. 
    5. If the related feature is a one-node device, both Node1 and Node2 are updated with same node value. 
  4. If the related feature is not within tolerance of the closest Tier2 linear, the related feature is processed in a subsequent pass (that is, UnresolvedThirdPass). 
    1. If the UnresolvedThirdPass list is empty or there are no Tier3 linear related features, the algorithm proceeds to the Final Manual Resolution Logic. Otherwise, the third pass compares each related feature in the UnresolvedThirdPass list to the features in the Tier3LinearRelatedFeatures. 
      1. Using the figure below, there should still be some unresolved single node point features along the Tier3 linear features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909)
      1. The Tier3 linear features and the single node point features within tolerance of the Tier2 linear features should already be resolved. In the figure below, the one purple, Tier3 linear feature and the one aqua single node point feature should be resolved. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259909)
    2. If the UnresolvedFourthPass list is empty or there are no Tier4 linear related features, the algorithm proceeds to the Final Manual Resolution Logic. Otherwise, the fourth pass compares each related feature in the UnresolvedFourthPass list to the features in the Tier4LinearRelatedFeatures. If there are still unresolved features (UnresolvedFifthPass), a [fifth pass](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/S5kotDu7CGokG8uU2JOVHw) is performed. 
  5. The last step in passes two through five is to check the UnresolvedWithinTolerancePassN list. If it is populated, the [Resolve Node-Edge Connectivity dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WsEncm3rBB4nKdAa5BcLCA) is displayed so the user can resolve these related features.

##### Repair Allocation Reports
If NetWorks Core cannot completely and automatically determine the correct allocation, it places a [repair feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/INbE7zFbCgdLyTPjKm1STQ), as [configured in metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KR86c2s5ZCQOCD1zzNo8ow), near the break point. The repair feature is annotated with references to the containing features that could not be resolved. The software also allocates both resulting features to ambiguous containers. 
The user can select the repair feature and invoke the [Report Using Select Set](javascript:;) command to run the Repair Allocation report. Depending on how you configure the report, it displays options like queries and traces for the output of the report, including map output, data table, and other reporting options. The Repair Allocation report displays both features resulting from the break plus all containing features that are common to those features. The report includes the complete containment hierarchy, not just immediate containers, so it includes the formations, conduits, and ducts common to both features. However, the display is not ordered in any particular way, and it does not display the hierarchical relationship of the containers. 
These metadata values are associated with configuring a repair allocation report:
  * G3E_REPORTINTERFACE
A row in [G3E_REPORTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KXVHO74HoXhacwlIbL4kIQ) describes the repair allocation report interface.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_INTERFACE  |  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  10  |  Repair Allocation Report  |  PRIface.RepairAllocationReport  |  BLOB  |  BLOB  |  12/09/07  |  
 |

    * G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT—Specify the report interface number to be used to display the output data" is the prompt.

This is expected to be the [G3E_REPORT.G3E_RPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) of the [generic map output report](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bEI6j_HfLHLKK2lg2wSvZg) or any customized report interface that you want to configure. The metadata upgrade adds this row. 
  * G3E_REPORT
[G3E_REPORT.G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) specifies G3E_RPNO of the generic map output report interface.

##### Repair Feature

###### Repair Feature Metadata
These tables are specifically related to using a repair feature:
  * G3E_REPAIRIFACE
[G3E_REPAIRIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2TUSsCOJLmRvbbgVeifteQ) specifies several parameters related to repair. Each row in this table contains a G3E_TYPE value indicating the meaning of the other values. A row has values in either the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields or values in the G3E_PARAMETER1 and G3E_PARAMETER2 fields. 
  * G3E_REPAIROFFSET
Entries in the [G3E_REPAIROFFSET](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5HkffS92iyUV167AsHrU1A) table specify where to place each component of the repair feature. The location is specified as a pair of X- and Y-offsets along with the G3E_FNO/G3E_CNO of the break feature and the G3E_CNO of the repair-feature component.
