##### Triggering a Break

###### Break Subsystem Metadata
The first significant metadata in Break processing determines whether a feature is a breaking feature. This is only significant during placement and edit since the Break command breaks at a user-defined point, not at the point of placement of a breaking feature. When the software places a feature, the relationship services use metadata in their respective [pairing tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eqqpUrQ7TIQTuw40JNeAzQ) to determine if a feature is a breaking feature. If it is, the relationship initiates a break operation. 
To set up a feature as a breaking feature, set the G3E_BREAKLINEAR flag on the feature (as the source feature) and the linear feature to be broken.   
|  Example A weld breaks a pipe segment. To define the connectivity relationship between the weld and the pipe segment, set the [G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_BREAKLINEAR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg) field to Yes (1).   |  
| --- |  
A feature set up to break one type of related linear feature may not break all linear features to which it is related. This is determined by related-feature pairing.   
|  Example A fuse may be defined to break a primary conductor, but it may not be defined to break a bus. Each pairing row may or may not define the feature as a breaking feature.   |  
| --- |  
The following metadata further controls break processing:
  * G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.BreakModelType
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.[BreakModelType](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) describes the use of detail linear components so that the Break software can properly assign these components. 
  * G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_BREAKCOPY
When break processing begins, the software copies each attribute field from the original feature to the copy feature except for those attribute values whose [G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_BREAKCOPY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) field is set to No (0). 
Attributes that should not be copied during Break processing include some relationship attributes, node values, and owner information. Examine other attributes to determine if they should be copied to the new feature during break. Detail ID relationship attributes are the only attributes that should be copied during a break copy. G3E_GEOMETRY attributes should always have the G3E_BREAKCOPY value set to Yes (1). 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) fields control most break operations: 
    * Assignment of components
    * Use of alternate geographic components
    * Use of Break interface objects
Break assigns components that were with the original feature to the proper linear feature resulting from the break operation. Break begins with a single linear feature and ends with two distinct linear features that begin or end at the point of the break on the original linear feature. Parameters in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT control the component assignment and all subsequent component geometry adjustments. 
The following G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT fields control component breaking, elimination, assignment, and adjustment: 
    * G3E_BREAKACTION
Components must be appropriately handled within the two features resulting from the break. You may want to break a linear component that is different from the original triggering component. 
Some detail linear components are not modeled as continuations of their geographic counterparts but are a dual representation of the geographic linear. In this case, the dual representation may need to be broken to accurately reflect the changes made in the geographic window. Set the G3E_BREAKACTION for this component to 4 (Break at Ratio) within the context of the breaking feature. 
If possible, the software breaks the component at the same ratio along the detail linear as the geographic component. The software calculates a ratio by measuring the length of the prebreak linear component as well as the length from the start of the prebreak linear component to the break point. 
Because the user may have digitized the two linear components in different directions, the software cannot determine which way to apply the ratio unless there are related features associated with the feature being broken. The related features provide the directional flow of the linear component being broken. If the software cannot determine the matching direction in the second linear feature, the software breaks this component at its midpoint. 
If you want a component such as a detail linear component modeled as a continuation of its geographic counterpart to be broken, set G3E_BREAKACTION for this component to 1. 
[G3E_COMPONENTELIMINATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wb8GGcxnHKVQ_nOEKQpu2w)
This field determines the destiny of each component within the broken linear feature. You can delete components from both of the features resulting from the break, keep with the original or with the copy [(A or B)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZZ96nKdPkWxZxpz~0CL3UA), keep with both, assign to the closer feature (A or B), or assign to one of the features using a [custom Component Elimination](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RJgTroQdYiGQ335ebCmUbA) interface. 
    * G3E_COMPONENTADJUSTMENT
This field directs the software in graphic adjustments made to components of the broken feature. For example, to place a length label that was originally at the midpoint of the original, prebreak linear, set the G3E_COMPONENTADJUSTMENT field to 1 (offset by ratio). When this field is set to 1 for a given component within the context of its feature, the software determines the ratio at which the component existed on the original feature and applies this ratio to the position of the component along the new broken features. If offset by ratio is not needed for a component, set this field to 3. 
    * G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE
This field defines a distance value used to compute a zone around a triggering component during a break operation where interior node-edge connectivity is involved 
    * G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO
This field specifies the target component for which a component should be destined.  
|  Example A feature might contain a geographic linear component, a geographic label component, an alternate geographic linear component, and an alternate geographic label component.  The break software breaks both the geographic and the alternate geographic linear components and then uses the geographic proximity of the labels to their linear counterparts to determine to which feature the geographic and alternate geographic label components should be assigned. However, the software must be told which linear component goes with which label component.  Therefore, the G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO of the label components is the component number of their counterparts, and the geographic linear component number is set in the G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO field of the geographic label. Likewise, the component number of the alternate geographic linear component is set in the G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO field for the alternate geographic label. Because the linear components are being broken, they are not to be assigned using any other component. Therefore, the G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO field can be Null on the linear components.   |  
| --- |  
    * G3E_ALTERNATEGEOGRAPHIC
This field indicates that this component is an alternate primary geographic component. The user can break and assign alternate geographic components using Break. Alternate geographic components use alternate geographic components of other features to perform Break at Ratio just as detail components use related features to determine the direction the ratio should be applied. 
A user can place a feature that is related to a linear feature, requiring alternate geographic linear components to be broken. For the software to determine the direction of the linear used to apply the ratio, the user must place an alternate geographic component from a related feature near the alternate geographic linear component that is to broken 
    * G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL
This field matches alternate geographic components from different features to determine direction. For example, if a conductor has alternate linear one and two components, the conductor must also have alternate fuse components one and two. These components must have ordinals set so that the corresponding one and two alternate geographic components are set with the same ordinal. By setting alternate geographic components from different features with the same ordinal on similar alternate geographic components, the Break software use ratios to better determine the break direction. 
    * G3E_RINO and G3E_RIARGGROUPNO
These fields define a custom Component Elimination interface.
  * G3E_RELATIONSHIP and G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING
Along with metadata from the [relationship pairing metadata tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eqqpUrQ7TIQTuw40JNeAzQ), [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) and [G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/19xFJqi2WdZ~OXlIOWc1Hg) set up relationships between the breaking feature and the two features resulting from the break. If the Break command invokes the Break software, this step is skipped because there is no breaking feature. However, if a breaking feature triggered the break, the software establishes relationships between the two features resulting from the break and the breaking feature. 
  * G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE
Post Break interfaces and custom Component Elimination methods are defined in the [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) table.

#### Configuring Relationship Behavior in Edit Tool and Edit Geometry
Performing some [Edit Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LqLeE98Nnul3rsMPIM0BwQ) and [Edit Geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nhrcUnzM97Wyap2sE3VqVQ) operations (such as Move Component, Rotate Around, and Extend) is not allowed in cases where reestablishing the relationships of the edited feature(s) might be ambiguous. The ambiguity is usually caused when there is more than one triggering component being edited. To prevent this, use Metadata Explorer to configure the Edit Tool and Edit Geometry behavior of relationships. 
  * To configure the Edit Tool and Edit Geometry behavior of a relationship:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Relationships > Edit Tool and Edit Geometry Behavior node to display the relationships whose behavior is configurable. 
  2. Select a relationship node to display a list of the features that participate in that relationship. 
  3. Select a feature node to display a list of triggering components for the relationship.
  4. Select a triggering component node to display the G3E_EDITTOOLRELPROC value for the selected row of the G3E_EDITTOOLRELATIONSHIPS table. 
  5. Select one of the following values for G3E_EDITTOOLRELPROC:
     * Reestablish Relationship (1)
     * Remove Relationship (2)
     * Ignore Relationship (3)
This value is updated in the G3E_EDITTOOLRELPROC field of the G3E_EDITTOOLRELATIONSHIPS table. 
  6. Refresh the metadata edits:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261928) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Relationship Definitions under Placement & Edit. 
    3. Click OK. 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261928) to refresh the display in Metadata Explorer. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261928) The Edit Tool and Edit Geometry commands use the G3E_EDITTOOLRELPROC field of G3E_FEATRELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE when validating the contents of the [select set](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261928) and when updating the relationships after an edit. If this field does not exist or if it has a value other than Reestablish, Remove, or Ignore Relationship for the current relationship, the default value is used: Reestablish Relationship (1). 
One or more map objects selected for simultaneous manipulation.

#### Connectivity Symbol Editor
Connectivity symbols are symbols used in the Connectivity PickQuick dialog box. The [Connectivity PickQuick](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VfbJLUnk4lGa5XMUeX83Jw) is a dialog box that graphically depicts complicated connection scenarios using symbols so that the user can make intelligent choices about the interconnection of multi-node devices. For example, when the user places a primary conductor on a fuse, the Connectivity PickQuick gives a choice of connecting to either the protected or unprotected side of the fuse. Without the Connectivity PickQuick, it would be difficult to present this choice to the user in an understandable manner. The Connectivity PickQuick uses symbols generated through the Connectivity Symbol Editor using [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v3mAWLnohO4lMKVGDzeSuA). With the editor, you can generate symbols that emulate graphic symbols used in the map. Also, you can generate hot spots on the symbols that represent connection points. 
When you create a new symbol, it is stored in the [G3E_CONNECTIVITYSYMBOL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/56cF4Pb4pvwkJzEEApNvdQ) table where it is mapped to the corresponding component number. Later the Connectivity PickQuick uses G3E_CONNECTIVITYSYMBOL to create and display connectivity symbols on the dialog box. 
When setting up a connectivity model, define a connectivity symbol for [each triggering component](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdplkN_TMHDZadA0mNAHjg) in the model. Generally, this symbol should look much like the map symbol for the component. However, since the Connectivity PickQuick presents symbols in a schematic-like representation, these symbols may look more like their schematic (either manually generated or [automatically generated schematics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UJ7gLta1CN5LDyy_xomXIg)) counterparts. The choice does not affect the behavior of the software. 
When creating the symbols, use the TrueType Font (TTF). If the TTF glyph is horizontal, make the connectivity symbol horizontal. Draw all symbols at the same relative size. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260910) Text weight and text width-to-height ratio are honored only for TrueType fonts. 
No matter how many node-edge connectivity models you have in your database, you need only one G3E_CONNECTIVITYSYMBOL table per complete model because there can only be one connectivity symbol definition per component. So, no matter what connectivity relationship model the component is in, it has the same connectivity symbol definition.

#### Controlling Relationships
After setting up the relationship data models, you create metadata to control the relationship software. Set up general relationship metadata first, then the [metadata for specific relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1fPS5aeknfBgMKV4Dc2YLw). 
These are the metadata tables used by all relationship services.
[G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
The G3E_RELATIONSHIP metadata table is the most general table because it holds a listing of all of the relationships that are supported in the model. For each relationship definition, this table holds the following information 
  * Which metadata tables are to be used for each relationship
  * Which piece of software controls the relationship
  * Which component is to be the supporting (attribute) component for this relationship
  * Miscellaneous pieces of information pertaining to the definition and control of the relationship. 


[G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/19xFJqi2WdZ~OXlIOWc1Hg)
The G3E_RELATIONSHIP table is used to generate the G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING table, which is a metadata table generated internally during metadata publish and which is not to be edited manually. This table is used by relationship-aware software to determine in which relationship or relationships a feature and/or triggering component participates. While you should not create this table manually, it is sometimes helpful to view it to determine what relationships are being fired during the placement and edit of a given feature. 
[G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7_heOl8BM78BX77MZpLweQ) and [G3E_RELPARAMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/En8LtrzH~9G~5NWcfFEm~A)
After setting up the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, additional parameters may be required to describe the metadata setup or the composition of the data model. Parameters of this type are stored in the G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS metadata table. The NetWorks Core product center has set up G3E_RELPARAMS to define valid parameter names you can use in the G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS table. View the G3E_RELPARAMS table to see if there are any parameters specific to the relationships that you are setting up. If there are, you place these parameters and a parameter value in the G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS table to describe your model and metadata. 
[G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ)
Use the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table to set up parameters that describe general properties like the model type, how breaks are to be processed, and the average size of map symbols. The Relationship subsystem and other NetWorks Core subsystems use this table. 
[G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA), [G3E_RELATIONARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8wQ6QXF6KRS1RYXSNnxgWQ), and [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA)
Use these metadata tables to describe interfaces and arguments to software modules that are used in the Break subsystem component elimination and post break phases, relationship geometry adjustments, and merge processing.

#### Detail Relationships

##### Detail Metadata
These tables are associated with the detail relationship:
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261484) There can be only one set of detail relationship metadata tables per model. There is enough flexibility built into the metadata that the use of multiple detail relationships is not necessary. 
  * [G3E_DETAIL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KQ6KvBLCBEmFQgTzRgky2w)
The G3E_DETAIL metadata table defines which features can reference a detail and stores the feature numbers and the referencing and attribute components for each referencing feature. Each row in this table contains information about which attribute stores the Minimum Bounding Rectangle (MBR) and offset information. 
The information in each row in the G3E_DETAIL table is used when setting up a new detail view.   
|  Example If the detail-referencing feature is a vault, G3E_FNO contains the number for the vault. Then, the component number of the detail indicator or referencing component is set in the G3E_GEOGRAPHICCNO field. The component number of the detail attribute component is set in the G3E_ATTRIBUTECNO field. This component stores all of the attribution related to the referenced detail view.   |  
| --- |  
The detail-referencing component referenced in the G3E_ATTRIBUTECNO field must contain fields in which it holds detail attribute information. This component must have a field for the following information: 
    * Detail identifier number (referenced by G3E_IDENTIFIERANO)
    * Detail username (referenced by G3E_USERNAMEANO)
    * Detail legend settings number associated with the detail (referenced by G3E_LEGENDSETTINGSNUMBERANO)
    * Minimum bounding rectangle (MBR) consisting of X and Y high and X and Y low (referenced by G3E_DETAILMBRXLOANO, G3E_DETAILMBRYLOANO, G3E_DETAILMBRXHIGHANO, and G3E_DETAILMBRYHIGHANO) 
    * Default MBR offsets for X and Y (referenced by G3E_DEFAULTMBRXOFFSET, and G3E_DEFAULTMBRYOFFSET)
    * Detail type (referenced by G3E_DETAILTYPEANO)


For each detail view referenced by the referencing feature, the attribute component must have a row that contains the information listed above. If the attribute component is repeating, there can be several detail views pointed to by a single referencing feature. In this case, a single feature can have multiple rows in the attribute component that point to different details with different MBRs and/or legends, or they can point to the same detail view, but with a different MBR. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261484) One or many features can reference a single detail window. 
  * [G3E_DETAILMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4RVcJ_lR5CP0zvnMst~Oag)
The G3E_DETAILMAPPING table defines which detail components can exist in a detail view based on the referencing feature. This table maps a referencing feature to a number of detail components.   
|  Example The G3E_DETAILMAPPING table defines that a switchgear can have fuse detail components, switch detail components, bus detail components, and conductor detail components. It defines that a detail view pointed to by a manhole can contain a cable, splice, terminal, conduit, and a passage connector. The G3E_DETAILMAPPING table maps the features that are to be modeled within the detail view to their referencing counterpart.   |  
| --- |  
  * [G3E_DETAILLEGEND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k3Of_zOwp6Fil6d~QaB9AQ)
The G3E_DETAILLEGEND metadata table allows control over which referencing features use which detail legends. For instance, a given model can have five different detail legends. However, a detail window pointed to by a substation can have only one detail legend that logically belongs with the window. This table allows legends to be filtered by referencing features. 
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
After you set up the three detail relationship metadata tables, catalog the detail relationship in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table so the Placement and Edit subsystem is aware of the relationship. If a model supports the detail relationship, add two rows to the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table. 
The first row you add to the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table defines the relationship from the perspective of the referencing feature. This row has the name of the table that defines the referencing feature (usually G3E_DETAIL) in the G3E_TABLE field. Set the G3E_FNOFIELD column to G3E_FNO. Set the G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD field to G3E_GEOGRAPHICCNO. Set the G3E_SUBORDINATE field to 0. 
The second row you add to the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table defines the relationship from the perspective of the detail feature. This row represents the detail features (or detail components) that are contained in a detail view. This row also contains the name of the table that defines which components of detail features can be placed within a detail view (usually G3E_DETAILMAPPING) in the G3E_TABLE field. Set the G3E_FNOFIELD field to G3E_CONTAINEDFNO. Set the G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD field to G3E_CONTAINEDTRIGGERINGCNO. Set the G3E_SUBORDINATE field to 1. 


This diagram shows detail metadata relationships.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/iDgnKQee7D4Vcn8NMBwEcw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=685cae3ac7694de1&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

##### Detail Positioning Algorithm
The detail drawing positioning algorithm calculates the center point of the detail window minimum bounding rectangle (MBR) when a new detail is generated. 
The input parameter to the algorithm is the detail identifier. The first part of the algorithm converts this simple sequence number into a progressively growing grid, as shown in the diagram below. The numbers within each square represent the detail identifier. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259141)
The position in the grid is calculated using the following Microsoft Visual Basic code: 
Private Sub DetermineGridLocation(lDetailID As Long, _ 
lRow As Long, _ 
lCol As Long) 
Dim dSR As Double 
Dim lDepth As Long, lPosition As Long 
dSR = Sqr(lDetailID) 
lDepth = Int(dSR) 
lPosition = lDetailID - (lDepth * lDepth) 
If lPosition = 0 Then 
lRow = lDepth 
lCol = lDepth 
Else 
If (lPosition Mod 2#) > 0 Then 
lRow = lDepth + 1 
lCol = Int(lPosition / 2#) + 1 
vElse 
lRow = Int(lPosition / 2#) 
lCol = lDepth + 1 
End If 
End If 
End Sub
With the row and column position determined, the actual origin of the data are a function of the overall origin of detail drawings and the size of each detail, as specified in [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ).

##### Detail Referencing
When you create a mapping between features that reference detail windows and features that may be contained inside drawings referenced by these features, you must set up referencing feature detail indicator components and referencing feature detail attribute components. Both these indicator and attribute components must be a part of the detail-referencing feature.   
|  Example A vault feature that references a detail window must have a geographic component that is used as an indicator that a detail window may be referenced by the vault. The vault feature must also have a component that stores attributes that describe the detail windows it references.   |  
| --- |  
The detail indicator component that is a part of the referencing feature can be the primary graphic component of the feature, or it can be an auxiliary graphic component whose sole purpose is to indicate that a detail is referenced by a particular feature.   
|  Example A substation feature has a substation outline geographic component. This geographic component may be chosen as the detail indicator component.  However, since this outline component would probably exist in the geographic window, regardless of the existence of a detail window, you may want to create a detail indicator geographic component that would exist only if a detail window were referenced by this substation feature. Either way, the detail indicator component must be a geographic component of the referencing feature.   |  
| --- |  
A detail attribute component must exist as a part of the referencing feature. Any component can be used to store detail attributes; however, there are some things to consider when you choose a detail attribute component. 
  * If you want a given referencing feature to be able to reference more than one detail window, the attribute component must be repeating. 
  * The detail attributes can be stored on the same component as the detail indicator component. To do this, you place a new indicator component for each detail window to be referenced. 
  * If the attributes are stored on a separate, repeating attribute component, one indicator component can reference many detail windows. The indicator component must be nonrepeating in this case. 


You must set up the indicator and attribute components properly. There are several combinations of these components that are acceptable, and their repeating/nonrepeating status must be considered. The following list shows three possibilities. The first two are preferred so that you can publish the attribution in the graphic component view. 
  * The indicator and attribute components are the same component.
  * The indicator component is nonrepeating, and a different, nonrepeating attribute component exists. 
  * The indicator component is nonrepeating, and a different, repeating attribute component exists. 


After setting up the detail referencing feature and its indicator and attribute components, you set up detail graphic components. These components can exist in any feature that may need to be included in a detail window. 
The following diagram shows the relationship of a detail attribute component to many detail graphic components. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259144)

##### Detail Relationship Attributes
There are several attributes that need to be stored on the detail attribute component of the referencing feature. The attribute component should have fields for the detail ID, username, legend number, and fields for the X and Y high and low minimum bounding rectangle coordinates. 
The Detail Identifier field stores a system-assigned number that maps a referencing feature to graphic detail components that are stored within that detail view. This number is created by a database sequence and is assigned automatically to all detail graphics placed within the detail view pointed to by this referencing feature. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259123) This requires that a numerical database sequence be created for the generation of these detail identifier numbers. 
The username is the name you give to the detail view.
The Legend Number field is used to store the number of the legend chosen for this detail view. Legend numbers are acquired from the [G3E_LEGEND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) metadata table. This field is read when opening a detail view to ensure that the proper legend is attached to the window. 
There are four attribute fields dedicated to storing the minimum bounding rectangle of the detail view. These fields are populated when a detail view is created or when the Refresh > [Detail Extents](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MC7iqijJmIKEHKD2DGCzfg) command is run against a detail window. 
Along with the detail attribute of the referencing feature, the graphic detail components to be included in a detail window must have relationship attribution. These graphic components must have a field defined in which the detail ID is stored. 
The following fields must exist in the detail attribute component to create a detail relationship. 
Referencing Feature Detail Attribute Component  
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Detail Identifier  |  Identifier of the detail window. Generated by database numeric sequence.  |  Number(10)  |  
|  Detail Username  |  Name provided by user that describes the detail window.  |  Varchar2(80)  |  
|  Legend Number  |  Number of the legend to apply to the detail window. Chosen by the user when setting up the detail window.   |  Number(10)  |  
|  MBR X High  |  Coordinate describing the extents of the detail window. Set based on the center point of the detail referencing feature in the geographic window and based on the default x and y offset values in metadata.   |  Number  |  
|  MBR Y High  |  See MBR X High description.  |  Number  |  
|  MBR X Low  |  See MBR X High description.  |  Number  |  
|  MBR Y Low  |  See MBR X High description.  |  Number  |  
Detail Graphic (Contained in a Detail) Component  
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Detail Identifier  |  Identifier of the detail window. Generated by database numeric sequence. Used to map this graphic component to the window in which it is contained.   |  Number(10)  |

##### Modeling Detail Relationships
There are significant modeling elements you use to model a detail relationship. These elements are detail-referencing features that include referencing feature detail indicator components, referencing feature detail attribute components, and detail graphic components. 
Referencing Feature Detail Indicator Components and Feature Detail Attribute Components
The first thing to determine when setting up a detail model is which geographic features reference detail drawings. These features are used as entry points into detail windows. Features, such as substations, vaults, cabinets, and buildings, that generally contain a subset of features are natural choices for detail referencing features. When you place or edit these features, they can be used to set up a new detail view or they can reference an existing detail window. Also, when you review these features, they can show what detail views they reference. 
Detail Graphic Components
The next step is to determine which features need to be included in detail windows.  
|  Example In a detail window referenced by a substation, features such as switches, breakers, fuses, buses, regulators, and transformers might have a detail graphic component.   |  
| --- |  
Any feature can have a detail graphic component as well as geographic and attribute components. By adding a detail graphic component to a feature, the feature can then be placed in a detail window. A feature can have geographic components, detail graphic components, or both.

#### Dimensioning Relationships

##### Dimensioning Relationship Metadata
These tables are associated with the dimensioning relationship: 
  * [G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jZu02p2uhJNqb6KS~gwFPg)
The G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP table enumerates of all dimensioning relationships between individual dimension and non-dimension features. If a relationship is required between a dimension and a building, the G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP table contains a record specifying this relationship. The record indicates whether this is a dimension-base or dimensioned-feature sub-relationship. 
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
The G3E_RELATIONSHIP table must contain two records for the dimensioning relationship. One record specifies the dimension-to-related-feature relationship. The other record specifies the related-feature-to-dimensioning relationship. This example table shows how to populate the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table for a dimensioning relationship: 

  
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RNO  |  11  |  12  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  6  |  6  |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Dimension to Related Feature  |  Related Feature to Dimension  |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP  |  G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP  |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  [G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SiNb2yYD4mWTILZqYTOLOw)  |  G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP_OPTABLE  |  
|  G3E_TOOLTIP  |  Dimensioning relationship  |  Dimensioning relationship  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE  |  G3ERelationships.DimRelationship  |  G3ERelationships.DimRelationship  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTREVIEW  |  1  |  1  |  
|  G3E_FNOFIELD  |  G3E_DIMFNO  |  G3E_CONNECTEDFNO  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTCNO  |   |   |  
|  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD  |  G3E_DIMCNO  |  G3E_CONNECTEDCNO  |  
|  G3E_PROPERTYACTIONS  |  3(= g3eamsraHighlight |g3eamsraAttributes)  |  3(= g3eamsraHighlight |g3eamsraAttributes)  |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS  |   |   |  
|  G3E_SUBORDINATE  |  1  |  0  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  05/15/2002  |  05/15/2002  |  
 |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259240)
  * The G3E_TYPE value is 6, the internal NetWorks Core code for dimensioning relationship. 
  * The G3E_TABLE column references the G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP table, and the G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE column references the G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP_OPTABLE optimized table. 
  * G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE contains the string G3ERelationships.DimRelationship, a ProgID of the dimensioning relationship software. 
  * The G3E_FNOFIELD and G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD columns reference columns in the G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP table. Set the value in the G3E_SUBORDINATE column to Yes (1), indicating a two-way relationship.

#### Many-to-Many Ownership Relationships

##### Many-to-Many Ownership Data Model
Use many-to-many ownership to model the ownership relationship among many parent and many child features. This relationship models the containment of many cables by many conduits, but its ability to model relationships with cardinality M-to-N supports specific workflows in several industries.   
|  Example One workflow that is supported by the many-to-many ownership is the pipeline protection zone or the political land hierarchy, where many parcels make up one parcel block, many parcel blocks make up a county, and so forth.   |  
| --- |  
In some models, the same feature can participate in multiple many-to-many ownerships. In most cases, single many-to-many ownerships can be used to model all M-to-N relationships. However, you might need to organize the many-to-many ownerships to split the relationships by industry or to set a specific argument for a group of features.   
|  Example You can set an argument specific to land hierarchy features, where the relationship candidates (parcel blocks) have to be gathered using the whole area of the child feature (county).   |  
| --- |  
Attribute Component
The relationship information that maps a parent feature to a child feature is stored in a join table, the many-to-many ownership common connectivity component. Both parent and child must share a supporting component that is used to store the relationship attribution. This component should be dedicated to the storage of a given relationship per row pair in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table. 
The common connectivity component is required for both parent and child feature and must be set to repeating in the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) metadata table. The common connectivity component for the parent may have its owner FNO and owner FID fields set to 0 if it is not owned by another feature within the many-to-many ownership hierarchy. 
The following diagram shows the entity-relationship of n poles (parent) to n cables (children): 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261920)
Many-to-Many Ownership Relationship Attributes
When you set up the many-to-many ownership, the unique feature identifier (G3E_FID) and feature number (G3E_FNO) of the parent feature are stored in the ownership attribute component of the child feature, as shown in the following diagram: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261920)
The following fields must exist in the attribute component to create a many-to-many ownership relationship:   
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Owner Feature Identifier  |  Recursive key that holds the G3E_FID of the parent  |  Number(10)  |  
|  Owner Feature Number  |  Recursive key that holds the G3E_FNO of the parent  |  Number(10)  |

##### Many-to-Many Ownership Metadata
Before you configure your many-to-many ownership relationships software, consider these three functional areas: 
  * [Delete logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ)
  * [Break logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ)
  * [Break proximity logic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ)


These tables are associated with the many-to-many ownership relationship:
  * [G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ)
The G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP table describes the mapping of parent features to child features. Each row in this table defines an owner (parent) to child association. If a parent has many potential children, create a different row for each child that maps to this parent. After you create a row defining a parent-to-child mapping, the reciprocal relationship (child-to-parent) is discernable from that same row. 
Although you need only one G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP table to define all many-to-many ownership relationships, you can create a separate G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP metadata table for each many-to-many ownership relationship defined in the model. These metadata tables names are limited to 22 characters. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257740) If you do not use the standard table or if you use an additional table to store the information that would normally go into this table, configure other metadata tables so that the system can find this table and can create the respective optimized table. You also must provide the procedure that creates the optimized table. 
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
After you define a separate table with identical column definitions as the original G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP table for each ownership model, populate the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table to catalog the relationships. For each relationship, place two rows in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, one for each direction of the relationship. Place a row in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table to denote the parent-to-child relationship and the child-to-parent relationship, one subordinate and one not. So, you need two rows in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table per each many-to-many ownership relationship table in the model. Both rows should have the same optimized table name (G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE) and [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_VALIDATIONSETPKG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) values. One should have [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_SUBORDINATE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) set to No (0) and the other to Yes (1). These rows must point to the same table modeled after G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP. Also, you must set several parameters in [G3E_RELATIONSHIP. G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA). 


This diagram shows many-to-many ownership metadata relationships.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257740)
Tips and Tricks
  * To get a list of related parent features, run the following SQL statement replacing <MMOCONNECTIVITY> with the table associated with the component reference as the G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_SUPPORTCNO for the relationship: 
SQL> select * from <MMOCONNECTIVITY>  
where   
(G3E_FID, G3E_CID) in   
(select G3E_FID, min(G3E_CID) from   
(select B.* from<MMOCONNECTIVITY> A, <MMOCONNECTIVITY> B where A.G3E_FNO=<MyChildFNO> and  
A.G3E_FID=<MyChildFID> and  
A.G3E_OWNERFID=B.G3E_FID and  
A.G3E_OWNERFNO=B.G3E_FNO)  
group by G3E_FID);
  * To get a list of related child features, run the following SQL statement replacing <MMOCONNECTIVITY> as you did above: 
SQL> select * from <MMOCONNECTIVITY>  
where G3E_OWNERFNO=<MyParentFNO> and G3E_OWNERFID=<MyParentFID>;
  * To update the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/19xFJqi2WdZ~OXlIOWc1Hg) use an SQL editor to run G3E_FEATRELATIONSHIPS_PKG.RepopulateRelshipMap: 
SQL> exec G3E_FEATRELATIONSHIPS_PKG.RepopulateRelshipMap;
The table is updated when you execute this statement or when you run metadata validation.
  * To display the content of G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP in a user-friendly way, use the following statement: 
SQL> select a.G3E_USERNAME CHILD, b.G3E_USERNAME CHILDCNO, c.G3E_USERNAME PARENT,  
d.G3E_USERNAME PARENTCNO  
from   
G3E_FEATURE a, G3E_COMPONENT b, G3E_FEATURE c, G3E_COMPONENT d,  
G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP m  
where   
a.G3E_FNO=m.G3E_SOURCEFNO and b.G3E_CNO=m.G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO and  
c.G3E_FNO=m.G3E_OWNERFNO and d.G3E_CNO=m.G3E_OWNERTRIGGERINGCNO;


If You Encounter Problems
Follow these steps to make sure that both the parent and child feature have a common component. 
  1. Check that both features are defined such that they include the component. You can do this by looking at the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). Make sure the [optimized metadata tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257740) are published. 
Optimized tables; tables that result from joining metadata tables. Optables are published into the metadata mapfiles and ADO-based RAW files. Using optables makes the software run more efficiently. 
  2. Check that the component was created for both features. You can do this by looking at the common connectivity component table. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257740) Prefix this table with B$ for production schemas. 
This statement should return at least one row for both MyParentFID and MyChildFID. 
select * from <MMOCONNECTIVITY> where G3E_FID=<MyParentFID> or G3E_FID=<MyChildFID>; 
If none of the returned child records contains <MyParentFID> in the G3E_OWNERFID field, the features are not related.

#### Merge Subsystem

##### Merge Subsystem Metadata
The following metadata tables contain fields that control merge processing: 
  * G3E_FEATURE
[G3E_FEATURE.G3E_MERGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) controls whether two feature instances with the same feature number can be merged. A value of Yes (1) indicates that the feature instances can be merged. A value of No (0) indicates that feature instances must not be merged. Even if G3E_MERGE is set to Yes (1), the feature instances must pass further testing, for example, geographical and attribute preconditions and verification by relationship software, before the merge is actually done. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
The G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT metadata table specifies the geographical and attribute preconditions the software needs to check before the merge and specifies how individual components are merged. Because this metadata is specified in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT, you can specify a different merge behavior for the same component if it is part of different features. These fields in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT control merge behavior: 
    * G3E_MERGEMAXDISTANCE
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGEMAXDISTANCE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) specifies the distance in meters that allows the linear geometries to be merged. The merge is allowed for this component if at least one component instance of the first feature and one component instance on the second feature are within the G3E_MERGEMAXDISTANCE. Use Null for components whose geometries should not be merged, for example, nonlinear components and leader lines. Also, use Null for attribute components and relationship components. Use a number greater than 0 for parcels and buildings. This attribute is used in Step 5 of the [Merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw). Merge of components whose geometries should not be merged is driven by G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES. 
    * G3E_MERGEPRECOND
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGEPRECOND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) specifies a precondition for the software to test individually on the first and on the second feature. For example, a cable can be merged only if its status is different from 'Abandoned.' Type the following string in G3E_MERGEPRECOND: 
Status <> 'Abandoned'
The Merge Features command creates this SQL SELECT statement: 
SQL> select Count(*) from <component_table> where G3E_FID = <G3E_FID of the feature being tested> and Status <> 'Abandoned' 
If the query returns a number greater than 0, the precondition is satisfied. This attribute is used in Steps 2 and 4 of the Merge workflow. 
    * G3E_MERGECOMMONPRECOND
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGECOMMONPRECOND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) specifies a comparison between the first feature and the second feature. For example, the diameter of the first pipeline must be the same as the diameter of the second pipeline. Type the following string in G3E_MERGECOMMONPRECOND: 
a.Diameter = b.Diameter
The Merge Features command creates the following SQL SELECT statement: 
SQL> select Count(a.G3E_FID) from <component_table> a, <component_table> b where a.G3E_FID = <G3E_FID of the first feature> and b.G3E_FID =<G3E_FID of the second feature> and a.Diameter = b.Diameter; 
If the query returns a number greater than 0, the precondition is satisfied. This attribute is used in Step 5 of the Merge workflow. Use Merge Features interfaces to specify preconditions that cannot be expressed as an SQL WHERE clause. 
    * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) specifies how to process the occurrences of the same component that are not merged interactively. This attribute is used in Step 10 of the Merge workflow. 
    * G3E_MERGERINO and G3E_MERGERIARGGROUPNO
G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGERINO and G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGERIARGGROUPNO fields hold the information needed to use a [merge features interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0DX4hO837bnMJyrM2DZO2g). 
  * G3E_ATTRIBUTE
[G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_MERGEEXPRESSION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) specifies the formula for calculating the new value of an attribute of the merged feature based on the attribute values of the first and second feature. An example is a pipeline feature that contains an attribute of the actual length of the pipeline as in the field but not calculated by the software. After merging two pipeline features, the new value of the measured length must be equal to the sum of the measured lengths of the original first and second feature. Type the following string in G3E_MERGEEXPRESSION: 
a.MeasuredLength + b. MeasuredLength
The Merge Features command sets the new value by executing the following SQL statement in the database: 
SQL> update <component_table> set MeasuredLength =  
(select a.MeasuredLength + b. MeasuredLength from <component_table> a, <component_table> b where a.G3E_FID = <G3E_FID of the first feature> and b.G3E_FID = <G3E_FID of the second feature>)  
where G3E_FID = <G3E_FID of the first feature>; 
This attribute is used in Step 10 of the [Merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw). 
  * G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
The [BreakModelType](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter describes whether the detail linear components are continuations of geographic components or their dual representations. If this parameter is not specified or its value is 1 (Detail as continuation), detail linear components represent a continuation of their geographic counterparts. If the features being merged contain detail components, the Merge Features command checks whether the detail linear components are within the distance specified by G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MAXMERGEDISTANCE. If such components exist, that is, the features can be merged using a detail component, the merge is not prohibited even if there are no geographic components which are within their G3E_MAXMERGEDISTANCE. If the features cannot be merged using a detail component, all geographic components must be within their G3E_MAXMERGEDISTANCE. 
If the value of BreakModelType is 2 (Detail as dual representation) or 3 (Detail as dual representation with alternate geo representation), detail linear components represent another view of their geographic counterparts. For merge is prohibited unless all geographic and detail components must be within their G3E_MAXMERGEDISTANCE.

##### Relationship Support for Merge

###### Detail Relationship Support for Merge
NetWorks Core software allows merging of detail components only in the same detail view (that is, the G3E_DETAILID value is the same). This requirement is checked by the Merge Features command. The detail relationship software does not perform any additional checking for detail components. 
Merging detail-referencing components is allowed and approved by the detail relationship software only if all detail views referenced by the first and the second feature are also referenced by the final feature, that is, no detail reference is lost when merging two features. For example, if two features with non-repeating, detail-referencing components are merged and each component references a different detail, the detail-referencing component in the final feature cannot reference both detail views, and the merge is not allowed. 
The merge functionality in the detail relationship software does not perform any automatic merges of different detail views referenced by the features being merged. 
If the relationship software does not allow the merge of detail-referencing components because a detail reference would be lost, the user can take one of these corrective actions to enable the merge: 
  * If one or both the detail views are referenced by another feature, the user can use the Reestablish Relationship command to drop the relationship to the feature being merged. 
  * If none of the detail views is referenced by another feature, the user can use the Reestablish Relationship command to delete the contents of one (or both) of the detail views and delete the detail relationships. 
  * The user can use the Reestablish Relationship command to assign the detail view to another referencing feature and to delete the relationship between the feature to be merged and this detail view. 


These are recommended metadata settings in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for detail-referencing components support in merge: 
  * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
If features with detail-referencing components are merged often, configure these components as repeating to guarantee that the final feature references the detail views from the first and the second feature. It is also possible to merge features with nonrepeating detail components. However, if such features reference different detail views, the merge is not allowed. 
If the detail-referencing component is repeating, set G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES to 3 (Keep component instances from both features) so all detail references from the second feature are copied to the final feature. This is checked in metadata validation. 
If the detail-referencing component is nonrepeating, set G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES to 0. The detail relationship software always updates the final feature with the reference to the detail from the first or the second feature. Values 1 and 2 in G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES are also acceptable, but then the order of selecting features becomes significant. If G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES is 1, the feature referencing the detail must be selected first. If G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES is 2, the feature not referencing any detail must be selected first.

###### Dimensioning Relationship Support for Merge
The Merge Features command does not allow merging of features containing dimension components. The dimensioning relationship software always [allows](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261878) and [approves](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261878) the merging of base and dimensioned features. After the merge, the [first ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261878)or [final feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261878) keeps its original dimensioning relationships. It also inherits the dimensioning relationships of the[ second feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261878). Where the dimension is associated with a point or a line segment that is moved during the merge, the dimension is modified to remain associated with the corresponding point or line segment on the final feature. If such a modification is not possible, the relationship is dropped. 
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge. 
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge. 
For merge, the feature the user selects first.
For merge, component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature, resulting in a final feature that stays in the database. 
For merge, the feature the user selects second. Component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature and the second feature is deleted from the database. 
The Merge Features command updates the relationships and possibly the dimensions in Step 15 of the [merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw).

###### Many-to-Many Ownership Relationship Support for Merge
In general, the many-to-many ownership relationship software [allows](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257747) and [approves](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257747) every merge. The final feature initially inherits the relationships from the first and the second feature. Then the relationship software validates the spatial criteria (only for relationships not established silently) and runs attribute validation between the final feature and the related feature or features. If the spatial criteria validation fails, the relationship is not preserved. The relationship is also not preserved if the attribute validation returns an error with a priority that prevents posting the job. 
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge. 
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge. 
If [relationship geometry interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mi0ODepyCt5l3S56WNpZfQ) are configured, they also allow and approve merge, applying stricter spatial and/or attribute criteria on the features being merged. After the merge, relationship geometry interfaces can adjust the related geometries and/or do additional filtering of relationships inherited by the final feature. 
Processing is more complicated for duct management features when they are merged. This processing is done so that if a conduit is broken and the resulting conduits are merged afterward, the merged conduit contains the same hierarchy of the duct management features as the conduit before the break. 
Allowing of the merge and resolving the relationships after the merge is driven by the following metadata columns in [G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ): 
  * G3E_PARENTMERGEALLOW
The G3E_PARENTMERGEALLOW column specifies when to allow the merge of parent features with respect to their child features. 
  * G3E_CHILDMERGEALLOW
G3E_CHILDMERGEALLOW column specifies when to allow the merge of child features with respect to their parent features. 
  * G3E_MERGEBEHAVIOR
The initial inheritance of the relationships is driven by G3E_MERGEBEHAVIOR.
  * G3E_IGNOREOFFSETONMERGE
The spatial criteria are validated only if G3E_IGNOREOFFSETONMERGE is Yes (1).
Other metadata columns in G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP are honored or not honored as follows:
  * G3E_ENFORCEMENT
The many-to-many ownership relationship software does not honor the G3E_ENFORCEMENT flag in the merge processing. Therefore, the final feature or the features previously related to the first and/or the second feature might end up without relationship although this flag requires a relationship to post the feature. This approach is consistent with placement and edit workflows, where the flag is also not honored. 


These are recommended metadata settings in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for the many-to-many ownership component: 
  * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
For the many-to-many ownership component, G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES must be 0. This is the indication to the Merge Features command that the component is updated outside the command (by the many-to-many ownership relationship software in this case).
