###### Merging Conduit Examples
The following examples show how the NetWorks Core many-to-many ownership relationship software works when conduits are merged in a communications data model. The examples assume that the data model contains at least formation, duct, and inner duct children of the conduit features. The examples also show two types of children that the many-to-many ownership relationship software processes. One type, represented by formation, duct, and inner duct, is a structural child. A structural child feature is never the child of more than one parent. The other type, represented by cable, air pipe, and so forth, is a content child and represents the typical definition of [containment](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257884). 
A relationship of many features to many other features. For example, a duct can contain many cables, and a cable can be contained in many ducts. 
The following rules can apply when two features that act as parents in a many-to-many ownership relationship are merged: 
  * Both features must have the same set of content children – that is, the exact same set of features must be children of both parents. This condition must be applied recursively to matching pairs of structural children. 
  * Content children are checked for spatial proximity, because in many cases the relationship is established through non-spatial mechanisms, such as [feature allocation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jwse1SI0SaeqSPM5D49ISA). 
  * Both features must have matching structural children. They obviously cannot contain the same structural children, but there must be a one-to-one correspondence between the structural children of the two features. 
  * When merging two features with structural children, the redundant set of children is deleted. 

  
|  Scenario  |  Example  |  Results  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Conduits contain no formations at all.  |  Conduit can directly contain cables or other similar features, but they must be the exact same set of children.   |  Allow the merge. The resulting conduit has the same children as the two candidate conduits (which were the same). Spatial proximity is considered, because the containment may have been established by [feature allocation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MQxtF5cGVmgOeVIgq62NvA).   |  
|  Both conduits contain a single formation, which are identical in duct structure.  |  Conduit C1 Formation F1 Duct 1 Duct 2 Duct 3 Duct 4 Conduit C2 Formation F2 Duct 1 Duct 2 Duct 3 Duct 4 Ducts may contain cables, air pipes, and so forth, but corresponding ducts must have the same set of children.   |  Allow the merge. Formation F2, along with its four ducts, are deleted. However, the children of the ducts are not deleted. The resulting conduit and ducts have the set of children from the first conduit (C1). The graphics for formation F1 may be incorrect for the merged conduit - if both a To and From set of graphics were placed, one of those sets is probably in the wrong place. However, the user can easily replace the graphics using the [Place Formation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/76EATu7MgiaMcS7PvLjl_Q) command.   |  
|  Both conduits contain a single formation, which are identical in duct structure and inner ducts are added.   |  Conduit C1 Formation F1 Duct 1 Inner Duct a Inner Duct b Duct 2 Duct 3 Inner Duct a Duct 4 Conduit C2 Formation F2 Duct 1 Inner Duct a Inner Duct b Duct 2 Duct 3 Inner Duct a Duct 4  Ducts and inner ducts may contain cables, air pipes, and so forth, but corresponding ducts must have the same set of (non- duct) children.   |  Allow the merge. Formation F2 and its duct children are deleted. In this more complicated scenario, the inner duct children of ducts 1 and 3 are deleted, but other children such as cables are not deleted. If the graphics for formation F1 are incorrectly placed after the merge, correction is up to the user.   |  
|  Conduits have different formations.  |  Conduit C1 Formation F1 Duct 1 Duct 2 Formation F2 Duct 21 Duct 22 Duct 23 Conduit C2 Formation F3 Duct 10 Duct 11 Duct 12  |  Disallow the merge. This scenario represents a structural impossibility.  |  
|  Conduits contain different cables   |  Conduit C1 Cable A Conduit C2 Cable B  |  Disallow the merge. Assuming the relationships were correct before merging, inheriting both relationships is incorrect.   |

###### Node-Edge Connectivity Relationship Support for Merge
Generally, the [final feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887) inherits the node-edge connectivity relationships of the [first](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887) and the [second feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887). If any relationship on the final feature would become invalid, the merge is not [allowed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887) or [approved](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887). The merge is also not allowed or approved if any relationship would be dropped. For example, the merge is not allowed for two pipes connected using a valve because the valve cannot be related to the merged pipe. The features being merged must also pass an attribute validation if it is configured. The attribute validation between the final feature and any of the related features (if configured) must not return an error with a priority that would prevent posting the job. The [ValidationPriority parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER defines a threshold between postable and nonpostable validation errors. In the Merge subsystem, this parameter defines the threshold between allowable and not allowable merges for attribute validation errors. 
For merge, component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature, resulting in a final feature that stays in the database. 
For merge, the feature the user selects first.
For merge, the feature the user selects second. Component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature and the second feature is deleted from the database. 
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge. 
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge. 
The following table shows several typical scenarios of how the relationship software decides whether to allow the merge:   
|  Scenario  |  Example  |  Graphic  |  Results  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  No intermediate feature is related at the merge point. Pipes not related.  |  Both pipes have no relationship.  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887)  |  Allow the merge.  |  
|  No intermediate feature is related at the merge point. Pipes related at the merge point.   |  Pipe A and Pipe B are related.  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887)  |  Allow the merge. The relationship ceases to exist after the merge.  |  
|  No intermediate feature is related at the merge point. Pipes have relationships at the other ends.   |  Pipe A is related to Valve 1 and Pipe B is related to Valve 2.  |   |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887)Allow the merge. The final pipe inherits relationships to both valves. The merge is also allowed when one of the relationships is missing. The existing relationship is inherited. If there is a relationship between Pipe A and Pipe B, the merge is also allowed and this relationship ceases to exist after the merge.   |  
|  Pipes are connected using a valve at the merge point.  |  Pipe A and Pipe B are related to valve 1.  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887)  |  Disallow the merge. The user must first delete Valve 1 or drop its relationships to both Pipe A and Pipe B.   |  
Most of this checking is done in step 6 of the [merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw). In some cases, the checking is delayed until step 12 after the final geometries are merged. In this diagram, the upper and lower ends of the pipes can be merged. If the user merges the lower ends, the final pipe inherits the relationship to valve 1, and the merge is approved. If the user merges the upper ends, the relationship to valve 1 is dropped, and the merge is not approved. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261887)
In step 6 of the merge workflow, attribute validation for the features being merged is run, if configured. For example, two pipes can be related only if they have the same diameter, or two cables can be related only if they have the same phase and voltage. The same criteria is applied to allow the merge, that is, it must be possible to relate the features to merge them. If this attribute validation returns an error with a priority that would prevent a job from being posted, the merge is not allowed. 
The node-edge connectivity relationship software further checks the relationships to be inherited in step 12 of the merge workflow. Initially, the final feature is expected to inherit the relationships from both the first and the second feature. Then, the relationship software validates the spatial criteria and runs attribute validation between the final feature and the related feature or features. If the spatial criteria validation fails, the merge is not approved. The merge is also not approved if the attribute validation between the final feature and any of the related features (if configured) returns an error with a priority that would prevent posting the job. 
The node-edge connectivity relationship software updates the connectivity information is step 15 of the [merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw). 
If [relationship geometry interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mi0ODepyCt5l3S56WNpZfQ) are configured, they also allow and approve the merge, applying stricter spatial and/or attribute criteria on the features being merged. After the merge, they may adjust the related geometries and/or do additional filtering of relationships inherited by the final feature. 
These are recommended metadata settings in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for node-edge connectivity support for merge: 
  * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
For the node-edge connectivity component, G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES must be 0. This is the indication to the Merge Features command that the component is updated outside the command (by the node-edge connectivity relationship software in this case).

###### Node-Ordered Connectivity Relationship Support for Merge
The node-ordered connectivity software does not [allow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880) a merge of these types of features: 
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge. 
  * Two point features participating in the node-ordered connectivity relationship.
  * Two area features participating in the node-ordered connectivity relationship.
  * Two linear features participating in the node-ordered connectivity relationship if any of the related point features became unrelated after the merge. (Some of this checking can be done only in [approve](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880) mode.) 
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge. 


For example, the software does not allow the merge of two cables connected using a splice because the relationship to the splice would have to be dropped. 
The following table shows several typical scenarios of how the node-ordered connectivity relationship software decides whether to allow the merge:   
|  Scenario  |  Example  |  Graphic  |  Results  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Cables are not related at the merge point.  |  Cable A has an input relationship but no output. Cable B has an output relationship but no input. There is no connected splice at the merge point.   |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880)  |  Allow the merge. The final cable inherits A's input and B's output. The merge is also allowed when one or both relationships are missing. The existing relationships are inherited.   |  
|  Cables are related using a splice at the merge point.  |  Cable A has an output relationship to a splice that is also the input for Cable B. The splice occurs at the merge point for the two cables.   |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880)  |  Disallow the merge. The user must delete the splice first or drop the relationships to the cables.   |  
|  Cables are fed by a common node.  |  Cables A and B have an input relationship to the same splice.  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880)  |  Disallow the merge. The user must delete the splice first or drop the relationships to both cables. The same analysis applies if both cables have an output relationship to the same splice.   |  
|  Cables are fed by different nodes.  |  Cables A and B have an input relationship to different splices.  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880)  |  Disallow the merge. The user must delete both splices first or drop their relationships. The same analysis applies if both cables have an output relationship to different splices.   |  
Most of this checking is done in Step 6 of the [merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw). However, in some cases, the checking must be delayed until Step 12 after the final geometries are merged. In this diagram, the upper and lower ends of the cables can be merged. If the user merges the lower ends, the final cable inherits the input and output relationships, and the merge is approved. If the user merges the upper ends, both input and output relationships are dropped, and the merge is not approved. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261880)
In Step 12 of the [merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw), the node-ordered connectivity relationship software further checks the relationships to be inherited. Initially, the final feature is expected to inherit the relationships from both the first and the second feature. Then, the relationship software validates the spatial criteria and runs attribute validation between the final feature and the related feature or features. If the spatial criteria validation fails, the merge is not approved. The merge is also not approved if the attribute validation between the final feature and any of the related features (if configured) returns an error with a priority that would prevent posting the job. The [ValidationPriority parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER defines a threshold between postable and nonpostable validation errors. In the Merge subsystem this parameter defines, for attribute validation errors, the threshold between allowable and not allowable merges. 
The node-ordered connectivity relationship software updates the connectivity information in Step 15. 
If [relationship geometry interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mi0ODepyCt5l3S56WNpZfQ) are configured, they also allow and approve merge, applying stricter spatial and/or attribute criteria on the features being merged. After the merge, they may adjust the related geometries and/or do additional filtering of relationships inherited by the final feature. 
These are recommended metadata settings in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for node-ordered connectivity support for merge: 
G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
For the node-ordered connectivity component, G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES must be 0. This is the indication to the Merge Features command that the component is updated outside the command (by the node-ordered connectivity relationship software in this case).

###### Ownership Relationship Support for Merge
In general, the ownership relationship software [allows](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261893) and [approves](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261893) all merges. The [final feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261893) initially inherits the relationships from the first and the second feature. Then the relationship software validates the spatial criteria (only for relationships not established silently) and runs attribute validation between the final feature and the related feature or features. If the spatial criteria validation fails, the relationship is not preserved. The relationship is also not preserved if the attribute validation returns an error with a priority that prevents posting the job. When child features are merged and the resulting number of parents is greater than the allowed number (one or two), [PickQuick](javascript:;) is displayed so the user can select the correct parent feature or features. 
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge. 
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge. 
For merge, component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature, resulting in a final feature that stays in the database. 
If relationship geometry interfaces are configured, they also allow and approve merge applying stricter spatial and/or attribute criteria on the features being merged. After the merge, the relationship geometry interfaces can adjust the related geometries and/or do additional filtering of relationships inherited by the final feature. 
If the [first](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261893) and/or the [second feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261893) have the repair ownership established, the merge is not allowed ([merge workflow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v_~1GLqscDntwOIGhvrVYw) Step 6) because the software should not merge possibly invalid features. 
For merge, the feature the user selects first.
For merge, the feature the user selects second. Component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature and the second feature is deleted from the database. 
The metadata columns in [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) are honored or not honored as follows: 
  * G3E_ENFORCEMENT
The ownership relationship software does not honor the G3E_ENFORCEMENT flag in the merge processing. Therefore, the final feature or the features previously related to the first and/or the second feature might end up without relationship, although this flag requires a relationship to post the feature. This approach is consistent with placement and edit workflows, where the flag is also not honored. 
  * G3E_ALLOWINTERIORRELATION
The ownership relationship service honors the G3E_ALLOWINTERIORRELATION flag. Some relationships established using endpoints may become relationships established by interior points after the merge. If G3E_ALLOWINTERIORRELATION is No (0), the interior relationships are dropped as part of the spatial criteria validation. 


These are recommended metadata settings in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for the component containing ownership relationship information: 
  * G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES
For the ownership relationship component, G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES must be 0. This is the indication to the Merge Features command that the component is updated outside the command (by the ownership relationship software in this case). If there is a record in this component for the first feature, it is updated with the relationships after the merge. If there is no such record for the first feature, it is copied from the second feature to the first feature and updated with the relationship or relationships after the merge.

#### Node-Edge Connectivity

##### Defining Triggering Components for Node-Edge Connectivity
Triggering components for node-edge connectivity are components defined as graphic components for participating features. There are two ways to define triggering components for node-edge connectivity: 
  1. Define one component type per feature as triggering.  
|  Example Define all of your primary geographic components as triggering.  |  
| --- |  
In this case, connectivity is established only by placing features in geographic windows.
  2. Define geographic and detail components of features as triggering.  
|  Example Define the geographic line and detail line components of a linear feature as triggering, allowing connectivity to be established in geographic and detail windows for this feature.   |  
| --- |  


These are the things you cannot do when defining triggering components for node-edge connectivity: 
  * Identify multiple detail components as triggering within the same feature.
  * Define the geographic, detail, and alternate geographic components of a feature as triggering. Define only one of these component types as triggering or, at most, define the geographic and detail components as triggering. 
  * Define the detail and alternate geographic components of a feature as triggering. If you use the alternate geographic component as triggering, the software does not expect detail components as part of the relationship model. 
  * Define triggering components for node-edge connectivity as repeating. Failure to comply with this caveat causes erratic connectivity behavior during placement and edit operations when establishing node-edge connectivity. 


Although the definition of triggering components is limited for connectivity during placement, break metadata allows multiple, non-triggering components to be manipulated during break processing.

##### Modeling Node-Edge Connectivity
When modeling node-edge connectivity, keep in mind the implications of node-attribute storage and how the software uses these values. The node-edge connectivity attribute table must have two columns, one for Node1 and another for Node2. Software using this table assumes that a value stored in the Node1 field corresponds to the start point of a linear and that a value stored in the Node2 field corresponds to the endpoint of a linear. There is no such assumption for point and area features. 
So when you create connectivity data for linear features, remember that Node1 = Start point and Node2 = Endpoint. If you get this wrong, the connectivity model does not trace properly, but placement and edit operations on connected features may not be consistent in their presentation in Connectivity PickQuick. 
If a linear feature crosses from a geographic window into a detail window, Node1 = Start point and Node2 = endpoint do not apply. In this case, there are two linear triggering components for one linear feature, meaning that there are two start points and two endpoints. In this situation, there is no way to determine which start point of which linear component corresponds to Node1. The same applies to endpoints and Node2. 
Users should always place and connect the geographic linear component first. This causes geographic features to be connected at Node1. Then when they place the detail linear component of the same feature, they should use Node2 when connecting to detail components. Migrated data should follow this same convention.

##### Modeling Three-Node Devices
You can use three two-node devices to simulate a three-node device like a triple-wound transformer. Three-node devices can be placed using a [placement configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly0oRFTHG1UNGrc60ApgVQ) or [an assembly](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XSFGrKZNVyzM_4Pbf5E5IA). 
  1. Connect the three devices to each other at Node 2.
  2. Place Node 1 of the three devices at the origin point of each device so that during placement a component can snap to these for connection. This is particularly useful to distinguish multiple circuits at this location so that the connecting linears can be drawn parallel to each other. 


To keep this component together during a graphic edit, use one of the following methods:
  * [Create a functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BlRuvPIYy~dNhw9uq~oa8A)
  * Configure a database trigger
  * The user selects multiple features


The user should turn off relationship updates during edits so the three devices maintain their connectivity. Since each switch is a separate feature, you have normal access to attributes like the switching status to control trace operations. 
This diagram and example illustrate modeling a three-node device.  
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259955) The red and blue devices are switches to control flow. The black device is a fuse or a bus. For inventory purposes, configure a special triple-wound transformer feature as the owner of the three two-node features with no connectivity.   |  
| --- |

##### Node-Edge Connectivity Metadata
After you define the components and features for your data model (containing their triggering and attribute components), configure the metadata describing node-edge connectivity relationships. The Placement and Edit subsystem uses this metadata to create and maintain relationships. These tables are associated with the node-edge connectivity relationship: 
  * [G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg)
Node-edge connectivity is a feature-to-feature relationship. A single feature represents a single connecting device. Internal connections within a feature are not modeled. Feature-to-feature mappings are maintained within the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table. This table contains a row for every feature-to- feature pairing. Every row placed in the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table must have a reciprocal row. 
The G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY metadata table lets you define which feature types allow connectivity. Placement and edit software uses this definition when it builds a candidate list for establishing connectivity. Some feature types may be present at a node, but filtered out of the candidate list because they were not configured to allow connectivity with the feature type being placed.   
|  Example If a pipe connects to a weld when the pipe is placed, create a row in the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table that holds the feature number of the pipe as the G3E_SOURCEFNO and the feature number of the weld as the G3E_CONNECTINGFNO. To make the weld connect to the pipe when the weld is placed, create the reciprocal row, using the feature number for the weld as the G3E_SOURCEFNO and the feature number of the pipe as the G3E_CONNECTINGFNO.   |  
| --- |  
When you consider which features can and cannot be connected, remember that an implied relationship can exist in your model between two features, even though these features are not configured to be connected to each other using rows in the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table. For instance, you may have configured a secondary conductor to connect to a streetlight. You may also have configured a secondary conductor to connect to a secondary dead end. If a single secondary conductor feature connects to both a streetlight and a secondary dead end and all of these features share the same node, the streetlight and secondary dead end are connected. Their relationship, while not directly defined in metadata, is implied by their relationship with the secondary conductor. 
If two features should never share the same node (and thus never be connected), define the metadata so that implied relationships between these two features do not exist. The following are two ways to ensure that two features are never connected: 
    * Do not create a row with the pair of features in the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table.
    * Make sure the two features that must not connect do not have a connectivity relationship with the same third feature. 
If the two features that must not connect do have a common related feature, they can share a node through this common feature. 
Use the G3E_SOURCECONNECTINGNODE and G3E_RELATEDCONNECTINGNODE fields to drive the connectivity software to use only particular nodes when establishing relationships. This ensures that certain features are connected only to a given node of a multi- node feature. For example, primary conductors should only connect to the high voltage side of a transformer, and secondary conductors should only connect to the low voltage side of a transformer. To accomplish these connections, use the G3E_SOURCECONNECTINGNODE and G3E_RELATEDCONNECTINGNODE fields to set the related connecting node to 1 on the row where the transformer is the related feature, and set the source connecting node to 1 on the row where the transformer is the source feature. On both rows, set -1 in the connecting node field pertaining to the linear feature. 
Create a table modeled after G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY for the node-edge connectivity model. For instance, if the model contains both [pipeline and electrical connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/333KlCE6aS8wb_WqaxO~Ig), you need two tables containing all the columns of the G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table, perhaps G3E_PIPELINECONNECTIVITY and G3E_ELECTRICALCONNECTIVITY. 
  * [G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7_heOl8BM78BX77MZpLweQ)
Use the G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS table to store node ID names, node sequence names, and the maximum number of nodes. 
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
After you create the feature pairing tables (that is, the connectivity relationship tables) for all of the connectivity models, register the tables that support their models in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table. This adds the connectivity models to the catalog of relationships that are within the data model. Add only one row to this table per connectivity relationship. This row contains general information about the relationship and a link from the row to the connectivity table using the G3E_TABLE field. 


This diagram shows node-edge connectivity metadata relationships.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259090)
Tips and Tricks
  * Use an SQL editor to determine the features that are connected to a feature that participates in a node-edge connectivity relationship. Execute the following queries, replacing CONNECTIVITY_COMPONENT with the component name of your node-edge connectivity relationship and replacing <FID>with the FID which you are reviewing. 
SQL> select * from CONNECTIVITY_COMPONENT 
where G3E_FID= <FID>;
This query displays the row from the connectivity component that represents the feature you are reviewing. From this row, get the node identifier values, usually in the fields labeled like NODE1_ID, NODE2_ID. 
With the node values of the feature being reviewed, construct the following SQL query, replacing the node values with the nodes values found in the initial query. Be sure to add the AND statement to exclude the review feature from the results. 
SQL> select * from CONNECTIVITY_COMPONENT
where
((NODE1_ID = 97227774 or NODE1_ID = 97227777)
or (NODE2_ID = 97227774 or NODE2_ID = 97227777))
and G3E_FID <> 1324350;
  * Node-edge connectivity validation posts an error for every pair of related features whose distance between each other exceeds the G3E_MAXOFFSET value defined in metadata. The priority of the error comes from the G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY field. If that is NULL, then the priority comes from the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority.

##### Node-Edge Connectivity Relationships Overview
Node-edge connectivity is a many-to-many relational model used to determine flow in a connected network of features. This relationship uses virtual "nodes" to describe the connectivity between features. Node-edge connectivity is non-directional. For example, a pole connects to span, an air pipe connects to passage connector, or a conduit connects to conduit. 
The node-edge connectivity relationship software maintains this model through the support of placement and edit commands. The software also supports the review of connectivity relationships. The following list shows what the node-edge connectivity relationship software does: 
  * Establishes relationships between connecting features by creating virtual nodes
  * Supports the reestablishing of connectivity relationships between related features
  * Supports the review of connected features
  * Supports the validation of connectivity attributes and offset distances
  * Supports break functionality by creating nodes at break points and updating the node values of features that were previously connected to the feature being broken 
  * Supports the deletion of connected features by cleaning up node values when shared by connected features 
  * Supports pipeline connectivity constraints.

##### Supporting Attribute Components for Node-Edge Connectivity
To set up a node-edge connectivity relationship, you must use a supporting component. This supporting component must be contained in every feature that is to participate in a given node-edge connectivity relationship. Each participating feature has a corresponding row in the component table that holds node-edge connectivity attribution.   
|  Example The following diagram shows the entity-relationship of a primary conductor to a transformer through the supporting attribute component:  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259947)  |  
| --- |  
Node-Edge Connectivity Relationship Attributes
There must be two attribute fields in each row for use by the node-edge connectivity relationship. Generally, these fields are called NODE1_ID and NODE2_ID. These fields store the sequence-generated node values that are shared between the current feature (represented by a given row) and other features that are connected at the same node. If the feature is a two-node device, a distinct node value may be stored in each attribute field. If the feature is a single-node device, both fields contain the same node value. 
The following diagram shows the relationship of interconnecting rows in the connectivity attribute component: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259947)
The following fields must exist in the attribute component to create a node-edge connectivity relationship:   
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Node 1 Identifier  |  Recursive key that holds the sequence-generated node value  |  Number (10)  |  
|  Node 2 Identifier  |  Recursive key that holds the sequence-generated node value  |  Number (10)  |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259947) The Node 1 and Node 2 data columns must have non-Null default values defined (for example, 0) for the component specified. Without this default value, errors occur during the break process.

##### Using Node-Edge Connectivity in a Pipeline Model
Node-edge connectivity software enforces pipeline connectivity. To model the connections between facilities in a pipeline model, add the pipeline connectivity parameter with a value of -1 in the [G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7_heOl8BM78BX77MZpLweQ) table. Pipeline connectivity allows, at most, two features to connect at a single node. For example, if a weld is modeled as a two-node device, only one pipe can connect to each end of the weld. This is a departure from normal node-edge connectivity because many features are allowed to connect at a given point. 
Not only is connectivity restricted while placing features, connectivity validation verifies that no more than two features are connected at a given node in a pipeline connectivity model.

#### Node-Ordered Connectivity

##### Node-Ordered Connectivity Metadata
These tables are associated with the node-ordered connectivity relationship:
  * [G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tMxlPZA20x7Zb1PWZXWOow)
This table has an entry for every feature/triggering component to feature/triggering component combination that can be connected. 
For every row you place in the G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table, you must place a reciprocal row. Also, you must list every triggering component in a separate entry in this table.   
|  Example Cables relate to splices, so splices must relate to cables, which requires two rows in the G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table. A geographical cable component can initiate a NOC relationship with a geographical splice component, but also a detail cable component can initiate a NOC relationship with a detail splice component. This example creates four rows in the G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table:  Cable geographical triggering component with splice geographical triggering component Cable detail triggering component with splice detail triggering component Splice geographical triggering component with cable geographical triggering component Splice detail triggering component with cable detail triggering component  |  
| --- |  
If your data model contains several different node-ordered connectivity relationships, you can model them with different relationships altogether, thus creating two additional rows in G3E_RELATIONSHIP and an additional table patterned after G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY. However, it is simpler to add more entries to the existing G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table. 
  * [G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tMxlPZA20x7Zb1PWZXWOow)
This table must contain the column names in the support component that contains the actual NOC relationship information. You must define the column names for the input and output relationships in the form of the Input FNO, Input FID, Output FNO, and Output FID. So, the table has four rows with name-value pairs. The column name you need is the parameter name. The value is that column name. To form the name part of the name-value pair, use the relationship number for NOC in G3E_RELATIONSHIP followed by a dash, followed by the column for which you want the name.   
|  Example The relationship number of node-ordered connectivity is 9. 9-InputIdentifier. This gives the Input FID column name. Usually this results in IN_FID. This column must be selected into the primary geographic component view and the primary detail component view of the feature.  9-InputFeatureNumber. This gives the Input FNO column name. Usually this results in IN_FNO.  9-OutputIdentifier. This gives the Output FID column name. Usually this results in OUT_FID. This column must be selected into the primary geographic component view and the primary detail component view of the feature.  9-OutputFeatureNumber. This gives the Output FNO column name. Usually this results in OUT_FNO.   |  
| --- |  
  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
In this table, the implementation of node-ordered connectivity implies a different relationship instance to implement the in and out directions. 

  
|  Example  
 |  Column Name  |  In Relationship Value  |  Out Relationship Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  12  |  13  |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  9  |  9  |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  NodeOrdered Input  |  NodeOrdered Output  |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY  |  G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY  |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  [G3E_NODEORDCONN_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/G6i84YmKyB511wdoAJgebA)  |  G3E_NODEORDCONN_OPTABLE  |  
|  G3E_TOOLTIP  |  NodeOrdered Input  |  NodeOrdered Output  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE  |  G3ERelationships.NodeOrdConnectivity  |  G3ERelationships.NodeOrdConnectivity  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTREVIEW  |  1  |  1  |  
|  G3E_FNOFIELD  |  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTCNO  |  53  |  53  |  
|  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD  |  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  
|  G3E_PROPERTYACTIONS  |  3(= g3eamsraHighlight |g3eamsraAttributes)  |  3(= g3eamsraHighlight |g3eamsraAttributes)  |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS  |   |   |  
|  G3E_HELPCONTEXTID  |  2  |  2  |  
|  G3E_SUBORDINATE  |  1  |  0  |  
|  G3E_PROMPTONREESTABLISH  |  1  |  1  |  
The in NOC relationship has a different row than the out relationship. These two rows have the same information, except for these fields: 
  * G3E_RNO, since this is the unique key.
  * G3E_USERNAME, since the two relationships have different names, for example Node-Ordered Input and Node-Ordered Output. 
  * G3E_TOOLTIP, since the two relationships have different names.
  * G3E_SUBORDINATE. The in relationship is considered to be subordinate, so it has Yes (1) in the G3E_SUBORDINATE column. The out relationship is non-subordinate and has No (0) in the G3E_SUBORDINATE. 
These are explanations for the other rows in the example table:
  * G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS field is null.
  * G3E_SUPPORTCNO has the CNO of the table that contains the actual relationship data. This points to the component of the features in the model, which is typically the linear feature that has the FNO and FID of the two point features to which the linear feature is related (connected). 
G3E_FNOFIELD and G3E_TRIGGERINGCNOFIELD contain the names of the source fields in G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY. These values are the same for both input and output relationships and generally are G3E_SOURCEFNO and G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO, respectively. G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE and G3E_TABLE point to the metadata table describing just the node-ordered relationship. 

 |  
This diagram shows node-ordered connectivity metadata relationships.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261931)

##### Node-Ordered Connectivity Relationships
Node-ordered connectivity (NOC) is a one-to-many relational model that determines direction in a connected network of features. Node-ordered connectivity describes connectivity between features, and uses actual facilities, such as splices and terminals, as connect points. In node-ordered connectivity, direction is maintained, for example, an optical cable connects to splice. 
The node-ordered connectivity relationship software maintains this model by supporting placement and edit commands. The software also supports the review of connectivity relationships. The following list shows what the node-ordered connectivity relationship software does: 
  * Establishes relationships between connecting features
  * Supports the reestablishing of connectivity relationships between related features
  * Supports the review of connected features
  * Supports the validation of connectivity attributes and offset distances
  * Supports break functionality by updating existing relationships on the feature being broken and by calculating the new relationships for the new feature resulting from the break 
  * Supports the deletion of connected features by cleaning up entries in the relationship table. 


After completing the data model containing all of the features (containing their triggering and attribute components), configure the metadata describing node-ordered connectivity relationships. The Placement and Edit subsystem uses node-ordered connectivity to create and maintain relationships. Only the linear features contain a connectivity component while point-oriented and area- oriented features have an implied participation in the relationship model. 
The [component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DHUwlxUkQR6tWTgCheuThQ) for the primary geographic component view and the primary detail component view of features that participate in node-ordered connectivity must select the [IN_FID and OUT_FID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/p9trq__MS~3HpDlYSZplUA) from the node-ordered connectivity component data table.

##### Supporting Attribute Components for Node-Ordered Connectivity
In node-ordered connectivity, the relationship is at a feature level. Therefore, a key for node-ordered connectivity is the feature number (FNO) and feature identifier (FID). These two values are entered in the attribute component to uniquely define the relationship. One set of FNO/FID pairs are for the single row for the linear, and two sets of FNO/FID pairs are used for the input and output point or area features for that linear.   
|  Example The following diagram shows how node-ordered connectivity is stored: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259115)  |  
| --- |  
Node-Ordered Connectivity Relationship Attributes
The attribute component is a component of the linear, so it has the five NetWorks Core keys: G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CID, and G3E_ID. It also contains the input FNO and FID for the point or area that is related to the input side of the linear and the output FNO and FID for the point or area that is related to the output side of the linear. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259115) The names of the in and out point feature keys are defined in metadata. 
The following diagram shows this relationship:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259115)
The following fields must exist in the attribute component to create a node-ordered connectivity relationship:   
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  NetWorks Core key   |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  NetWorks Core key and identifier of linear being related   |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  NetWorks Core key   |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  NetWorks Core key and identifier of linear being related   |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  NetWorks Core key. Should be 1.   |  Number (10)  |  
|  IN_FNO  |  FNO for input point or area feature. Name of this is in metadata  |  Number (5)  |  
|  IN_FID  |  FID for input point or area feature. Name of this is in metadata  |  Number (10)  |  
|  OUT_FNO  |  FNO for output point or area feature. Name of this is in metadata  |  Number (5)  |  
|  OUT_FID  |  FID for output point or area feature. Name of this is in metadata  |  Number (10)  |

#### Ownership

##### Ownership Data Model
Ownership is a relational model that describes a one-to- many association among features.  
|  Example A pipe owns many leak indicators or a cabinet contains many fuses and switches. In these examples, the pipe and the cabinet play the role of parent and the leak indicators, switches, and fuses are all children.   |  
| --- |  
In general, a parent can have many children, but children have only one parent, except in the case of linear features. Linear features (such as primary conductors, pipe segments, and conduits) can have one parent or two parents, one per end. Depending on the modeling circumstances, it may be helpful to have two owners for a linear feature. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261915) In this relationship, a feature (FNO) may not own itself or appear multiple times in the parentage hierarchy. That is, a pole cannot own another pole. A pole owning a pad that owns a pole would also be invalid. If you need to model this kind of relationship, you can use the Many-to-Many Ownership model.   
|  Example To account for spans in an electrical system, you have two owners for primary conductors, allowing a different pole to own each end of the conductor. If one of the poles is moved or removed, then the conductor must be accounted for since it is a child of the pole.   |  
| --- |  
You can define a child feature to have one or two owners. This must be consistent in all ownership relationships in which this child feature participates.   
|  Example A linear feature is defined as owned on each end by poles; so this feature must have a first and second owner field defined in each ownership relationship.   |  
| --- |  
Multiple Ownership Models
In some models, you may need multiple ownership relationships. In a communications model, for example, it might be helpful to model ownership for inside-plant equipment in a model that is separate from outside-plant facilities. 
Such a separation of models can make ownership lookups faster. If a different attribute component is used for each model, that significantly reduces the size of the table. Separation can also make metadata easier to model and maintain. 
For creating two or more distinct ownership models, consider the following:
  * No feature should participate in more than one ownership relationship unless there is no overlap or ambiguity in the features involved in each relationship.   
|  Example
    * In a model with inside and outside plant communications ownership models, a card feature should not be modeled in both the inside and outside plant models. 
    * A valve feature cannot participate in both an overview ownership relationship and a facility-level ownership relationship in a pipeline model where ownership must be established to a pipe feature in both relationships. 
 |  
| --- |  
Because of this, a single feature can never be used as a bridge or link between two ownership models. 
  * It is feasible to use the same common component to store attribution from every ownership relationship. However, depending on modeling conditions, it may be advisable to have distinct attribute components for every different ownership model.

##### Ownership Metadata
These tables are associated with the ownership relationship: 
  * [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ)
Ownership is a feature-to-feature relationship. The G3E_OWNERSHIP table describes the mapping of parent features to child features. Each row in this table defines an owner (parent) to child association. If a parent has many potential children, create a different row for each child that maps to this parent. After you create a row that defines a parent-to-child mapping, the reciprocal relationship (child-to-parent) is discernible from that same row. 
You can establish ownership relationships that include a nongraphic feature only with product commands, such as Edit Feature Relationships (using drag-and-drop in Feature Explorer) and Add Related Feature, and by the placement of equipment catalog entries that include nongraphic features. Relationships with nongraphic features cannot be silently established using a public API. 
    * Triggering components
For every feature in a row in the G3E_OWNERSHIP table, there is a corresponding triggering CNO field. These triggering CNO fields are used to define a component of the corresponding feature as the component that spatially creates the relationship. This field usually contains the primary geographic or primary detail component number. You may also define two rows for a given feature pair where one row identifies the geographic triggering components and the other defines the detail triggering components. 
There are times, however, when a nongraphic component can be set as a triggering component.

  
|  Example A floor owns a footprint feature where the footprint feature can be defined as both graphic and nongraphic. In this case, multiple rows must be put in place in the G3E_OWNERSHIP table to describe the relationship. In all of these rows, the G3E_OWNERFNO and G3E_SOURCEFNO remain the feature numbers of the floor and footprint, respectively. However, the G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO and G3E_OWNERTRIGGERINGCNO numbers changes from row to row.   |  
| --- |  
In the example, the floor is always the nongraphic parent. The G3E_OWNERTRIGGERINGCNO is defined in each row with these features as the primary attribute component number for the nongraphic floor. For the G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO of the footprint, one row defines the primary attribute component number of the footprint, a second row defines the primary geographic component, and the last row defines primary detail components of the footprint. 
In all cases of defining a pair of triggering components for a feature pairing, the triggering components must come from the same class of components (geographic-to-geographic, detail-to-detail) unless an attribute component is involved. In the case of relating a nongraphic feature to a graphic feature, mixing the primary attribute component with a geographic or detail triggering component is acceptable. 
  * Multiple ownership models
Only one G3E_OWNERSHIP table is needed per ownership relationship. However, there must be a separate G3E_OWNERSHIP metadata table created for each ownership relationship defined in the model. For example, for an Outside Plant ownership and an Inside Plant ownership relationship, you need two metadata tables to describe these different relationships, perhaps called G3E_OSP_OWNERSHIP and G3E_ISP_OWNERSHIP. You must define the metadata table names for additional relationships. The names are limited to 22 characters. 


  * [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)
After you define a separate table with identical column definitions as the original G3E_OWNERSHIP table, populate the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table for each ownership model. For each ownership model, you need two rows in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table that point to the same table modeled after G3E_OWNERSHIP. Place two rows in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, one for each direction of the relationship, for example the parent-to- child ownership relationship and the child-to-parent ownership relationship. 


This diagram shows ownership metadata relationships.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257737)
Tips and Tricks
  * Set the value of the G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_SUBORDINATE field to Yes (1) for the row representing the ownership relationship from the perspective of the child. 
  * Ownership validation posts an error for every pair of related features whose distance between each other exceeds the G3E_MAXOFFSET value defined in metadata. The priority of the error comes from the G3E_OWNERSHIP.G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY field. If that is NULL, then the priority comes from the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority. 


If You Encounter Problems
If you place a row in the G3E_OWNERSHIP table defining a related pair of features, but when you try to establish a relationship between them neither feature sees the other feature as a relationship candidate, check the following: 
  * Make sure that you have run metadata validation. 
  * Verify that your G3E_MAXOFFSET value in the new row is large enough to encompass the offset from one feature to the other. If this field is Null or -1, check the AverageSymbolSize value in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table.

##### Ownership Relationship Attributes
When you set up an ownership relationship, the unique identifier (G3E_ID) of the parent is gathered from the parent's row in the supporting component and is stored in an ownership attribution field in the row of the child in the same supporting component table. This recursive relationship of the supporting component allows the ownership relationship from both the parent and the child. Both the parent and child must share a supporting component that is used to gather and store attribution. This component can be a component that is dedicated to the storage of a given ownership relationship, or it can be a common component that is used generically in every feature. 
The following diagram shows the entity-relationship of a pole (parent) to n fuses (child). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261917)
To create an ownership relationship, the following fields must exist in the attribute component (ownership join component):   
|  Field  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Owner Identifier  |  Recursive key that holds the G3E_ID of the parent  |  Number(10)  |  
|  Owner 2 Identifier  |  Recursive key that holds the G3E_ID of a second parent. This field is necessary only if a feature is defined to have two owners.   |  Number(10)  |

#### Reestablishing Relationships
The [Reestablish Relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hMCMc5UmYugQjcZd4wVyFA) command lets a user change current feature relationships. Depending on the relationship, the user can select a feature for which relationship changes should be made, select a relationship in which the feature participates, and then select a new related feature with which to associate the chosen feature. Some types of relationships, such as the connectivity relationship, allow the user to choose a new feature for the relationship. Other types of relationships, such as the detail relationship, begin the process of establishing or reestablishing new relationships without further user interaction. 
Because some relationships require user interaction to select a candidate with which to relate and some do not, metadata is required to distinguish between the two. 
Configuring Reestablish Relationships
  * G3E_RELATIONSHIP 
The [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_PROMPTONREESTABLISH](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) column determines whether to allow selection of a new feature with which to associate the selected feature. For some relationships, for example the detail relationship, set the G3E_PROMPTREESTABLISH field to No (0) for no prompting. Most other relationships need prompting, so set the G3E_PROMPTONREESTABLISH field to Yes (1). 
  * Relationship pairing tables
The remaining metadata used in the Reestablish Relationship command is accessed from the [relationship pairing tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eqqpUrQ7TIQTuw40JNeAzQ) and the G3E_RELATIONSHIP metadata table. These metadata tables are configured when creating various relationships and no further metadata is needed to control the Reestablish Relationship command. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
If the detail attribute component of a referencing feature is nonrepeating, a message appears when the user tries to reference more than one detail. To allow users to reference more than one detail drawing from a georeferencing feature, set the referencing attribute component as repeating in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). 
  * G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
To change the behavior of the Edit Tool Reestablish Relationships button or the Edit Geometry Reestablish Relationships context menu checkbox, update the [AdjustRelationshipsInEditTool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) parameter.

#### Relationship Data Model Considerations
These data model considerations are common to all relationships: 
Triggering Components
A triggering component is a graphic component of a feature. When a trigger component is placed or edited, the relationship software executes and establishes a relationship. In other words, a triggering component is the component that makes the relationship software do its work. 
When you create related features, each of the features must have a triggering component so placement and edit commands know when to execute relationship software. Usually, the triggering component is the primary graphic component of a feature. However, with some features, you may want to use a component such as the primary detail graphic component as the triggering component. 
Each feature can have only one triggering component unless the feature participates in a detail relationship,in which case the feature can have two triggering components: one geographic component and one detail component. 
Since triggering components are graphic components of a feature, no further consideration of triggering components is needed when you set up a data model. Triggering components must be considered later, however, when you configure relationship metadata. 
Attribute Components and Relationship Attribution
An attribute component is a component of a related feature that the relationship software uses to store and retrieve information about the relationships of the feature. An attribute component must be present in every feature that participates in a relationship. The attribute component can be the graphic triggering component, although in most relationships it is not. 
Depending on the relationship that is being created, attribute components may be separate, unique components with attribute fields that pertain only to the relationship at hand. Other components used to store relationship attribution may be components that store a variety of feature attribution. 
Each relationship attribute component is composed of fields, some of which are used to store relationship information. The configuration of these relationship attribute fields varies from relationship to relationship. 
The creation and use of an attribute component depends upon the relationship for which the attribute component is created. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261924) It is usually best to set the attribute component as a required component of the feature in the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) metadata table.

#### Relationship Triggering and Attribute Components
After setting up general relationship metadata that is relative to the overall model, you create metadata for individual relationships. When configuring metadata for individual relationships, you need a clear understanding of how the relationship software uses triggering components and attribute components. 
Triggering Components
A triggering component is a graphic component of a feature that, when placed or edited, causes relationship software to fire and establish a relationship. In other words, a triggering component is the component that makes the relationship software do its work. 
Triggering components are defined in the metadata table that describes each relationship.  
|  Example When setting up a node-edge connectivity relationship between a primary conductor and a fuse, the primary conductor geographic line component is a good choice for the triggering component of the primary conductor feature. The fuse geographic symbol component is a good choice of triggering component for the fuse. In this example, both of these components are the primary graphic component of the feature. Using the primary graphic component for the triggering component is the usual choice, but is not required.   |  
| --- |  
Generally, there is only one triggering component per feature. However, in a model that contains details, there can be a maximum of two triggering components per feature, a geographic triggering component and a detail triggering component. Using the previous example, a primary conductor feature can have both its primary conductor geographic line and primary conductor detail line selected as triggering components. The same could hold true of the fuse if the node-edge connectivity relationship between the primary conductor and fuse is to extend to relationships within detail windows. 
Attribute Components
Attribute components store identifiers that associate one feature with another. In feature relationships, every feature that participates in a relationship must have attribute components, and you must identify these components when you set up relationship metadata. Metadata for each relationship defines which attribute component is to be used with which feature.

#### Relationship-Specific Metadata
After populating metadata tables containing general relationship information, you can create individual relationship metadata tables. These tables define which features can be related and which can contain other parameters that control establishing, editing, and breaking related features. 
Use Metadata Explorer to populate these metadata tables for your data model. The metadata tables for these relationships are delivered with NetWorks Core: 
  * Detail ([G3E_DETAIL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KQ6KvBLCBEmFQgTzRgky2w) and [G3E_DETAILMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4RVcJ_lR5CP0zvnMst~Oag)) 
You can use Metadata Explorer to configure detail relationships. In the tree view, select the Core Schema Model > Details > Detail Defining Features node and Detail Mapping node and [add a new row](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KJ7j6x3pPcUJxgHyeT4Snw) to each node. 
  * Dimension ([G3E_DIMRELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jZu02p2uhJNqb6KS~gwFPg)) 
You can use Metadata Explorer to configure dimensioning relationships. In the tree view, select the Relationships > Relationship > <dimensioning relationship> or <feature dimensioning relationship> > Display Relationship Definition node and [add a new row](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KJ7j6x3pPcUJxgHyeT4Snw). 


Procedures to Create Tables for Relationships Not Delivered with NetWorks Core 
You can use delivered procedures to create relationship tables for relationships not delivered with NetWorks Core. After you run the procedure to create the table, insert a row in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table for the table you just generated. You can then populate the new table with the features and components that are involved in the specific relationship. You can also generate the optimized table package for the table using procedures delivered with NetWorks Core. [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/333KlCE6aS8wb_WqaxO~Ig) to see a sample workflow for configuring pipeline and electrical connectivity relationships in the same model. 
The metadata tables for these specific relationships are not delivered with NetWorks Core: 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259094) For these database procedure calls, the <TableName> argument is the name of the relationship table that you want to create. It is required and must be <= 26 characters. However, the <TableAbbreviation> argument is optional. Specify it if the <TableName> argument is longer than 16 characters and you want to name the constraints on the table specifically. If you pass in this optional argument, it must be <= 16 characters. 
Node-Edge Connectivity
To create a [node-edge connectivity table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg) and its constraints, triggers, and sequences, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3ENodeEdgeConnectivity_Utils.CreateTable ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>'); 
To create the optimized table packages for all node-edge connectivity tables listed in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3ENodeEdgeConnectivity_Utils.GeneratePackages;
Node-Ordered Connectivity
To create a [node-ordered connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tMxlPZA20x7Zb1PWZXWOow) table and its constraints, triggers, and sequences, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3ENodeOrdConnectivity_Utils.CreateTable ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>'); 
To create the optimized table packages for all node- ordered connectivity tables listed in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3ENodeOrdConnectivity_Utils.GeneratePackages;
Ownership
To create an [ownership table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) and its constraints, triggers, and sequences, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EOwnership_Utils.CreateTable ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>'); 
To create the optimized table packages for all ownership tables listed in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EOwnership_Utils.GeneratePackages;
Many-to-Many Ownership
To create a [many-to-many ownership table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ) and its constraints, triggers, and sequences, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EManyOwnership_Utils.CreateTable ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>'); 
To create the optimized table packages for all many-to- many ownership tables listed in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP table, run the following database procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EManyOwnership_Utils.GeneratePackages;

#### Setting Up Relationships
This is a general checklist for creating relationship models: 
Data
  1. Create data model entities to be used for each type of relationship:
[Ownership](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RpsZ73aRldqjrd9DEFwDOg)
[Many-to-many ownership](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vyfdb7qnQ3hpydWg0LQKJQ)
[Node-edge connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~Iaaul~lbbCWJ83rLbSIeQ)
[Node-ordered connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/h1g8aks~6q0db8QKEv369w)
[Dimensioning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/u20XyiqjdWo8xx3uutCRBw)
[Details](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HVyGrogrBbjFc6FhdVAC4g)
  2. [Create related features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA). 
  3. [Create triggering and attribute components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qdplkN_TMHDZadA0mNAHjg), and add these to related features. 
  4. [Create relationship attribute fields](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/a_mC_mVfhrC1BSIXN3ZsjQ) in attribute components. 


Metadata
  1. [Create rows in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1fPS5aeknfBgMKV4Dc2YLw) table to catalog each relationship. 
  2. [Add rows to relationship- specific metadata tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9ncF8A_sNfv5v74np61BUg) (G3E_OWNERSHIP, G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY, G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP, and G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY) defining related features. 
  3. Create numerical sequences for the node-edge connectivity relationship by running the following SQL procedure. Make sure the metadata has been republished in the previous steps. 
SQL> execute CREATE_SEQUENCE.Create_g3e_node_sequence;

#### Silent Relationships

##### Silent Relationships Metadata
Silent relationships for placement configurations are defined in the G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP table. 
If G3E_SILENTRGNO is set for a given component, the relationships defined as silent are processed after the user digitizes the component. Any other relationships defined for this component are processed interactively on each mouse click. This means you can have a combination of silent and interactive relationships being processed for a single component. If G3E_SILENTRGNO is not set, all applicable relationships for this component execute interactively on each mouse click. 
This diagram shows relationships between silent relationship and placement configuration metadata. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261935)
  * To define a silent relationship:


  1. Create a row, and specify the [G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fkOOdphFCekSUjtVVUyL_Q) of the relationship interface to execute. 
  2. Set the connection point indicators for the active and related features by setting the [G3E_ACTIVECONNECTPTINDICATOR and G3E_RELATECONNECTPTINDICATOR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fkOOdphFCekSUjtVVUyL_Q) fields. 
The connection points refer to the node numbers or parent attributes in which to store the relationship data. The active feature represents the feature currently being placed. The related feature refers to a previously placed feature within this configuration. 
     * To specify the related feature, set [G3E_RELATEFNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fkOOdphFCekSUjtVVUyL_Q) to the appropriate feature type (such as the switch). 
     * Set [G3E_RELATEFEATUREINDEX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fkOOdphFCekSUjtVVUyL_Q) to the appropriate feature index using a value from [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_FEATUREINDEX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ). This is where, [for example, you specify switch 1, 2, or 3](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GzV5EH6F0CeRfiAfTZS7Ag). 
  3. Group the silent relationship rules for a particular FNO/FINDEX/CNO combination, (representing the active component) and assign each group a unique silent relationship number. 
The silent relationship number identifies the group of relationships to fire for a particular component of the configuration, allowing one or more relationships to be silently established for a single component. Within the group, the active FNO/FINDEX/CNO combination is constant, but the related FNO and feature index may differ, as well as the relationship interface to be executed. Because silent relationship rules are unique to a specific configuration, they are not generally shared between configurations. 
  4. To process silent relationships during a placement configuration, assign the appropriate silent relationship number from the G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP table to the [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_SILENTRGNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ) field of the triggering component of the active feature. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261935) When you define a silent relationship group, make sure the features within the group participate in a valid relationship with the current placement configuration feature. For example, if the placement configuration feature is a bus, and connectivity is defined between the bus and the circuit breaker, make sure you have indicated a legal relationship between the bus and the circuit breaker in the appropriate connectivity table (for example, G3E_OWNERSHIP, G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY).
