#### Validating Feature Relationships
You can configure the ownership, many-to-many ownership, and the node-edge connectivity relationships to reduce the number of errors reported to the user during validation. The G3E_ENFORCEMENT field in the [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ), [G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ), and [G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg) metadata tables governs the priority level of relationship errors used during validation. The node-ordered connectivity relationship is always required. 
In general, you select an option to determine if the relationship is required, or you can select from two options if the relationship is optional. For optional relationships, the many-to-many ownership, ownership, and node-edge connectivity relationships let you determine if validation has warning messages presented to the user (as P4) or if no warning messages are presented to the user. 
The ownership relationship has two additional enforcement options to identify the priority of relationship errors for cases where a child feature has two owner fields but only one owner is specified. 
  * To configure validation enforcement for a relationship:


  1. In the [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) tree view, navigate to the Relationships > Relationship > <relationship type> Display Relationship Definition node, and select the triggering component under the related pair you want to modify. 
  2. In the G3E_ENFORCEMENT field, select the appropriate validation option.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261926) to commit your edits to the database.

### Report Interfaces

#### Delivered Report Interfaces

##### Area Reports
You can use the AreaReportUtility.exe in the \GTechnology\Program folder to perform spatial analysis against an area feature and to store the resulting feature identifiers in a table in the database. 
The AreaReportUtility.exe finds features whose primary geographic component is within the bounding area. Additionally, if the Detail Indicator feature is found within the boundary area for any features specified in the FNOList, then any feature with Detail components in those details are included in the report. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261142) Only features from single level Detail window are processed within the bounding area. Detail indicator features within the multilevel Detail Window (Detail in detail) are not processed. 
Area Report Utility is a Microsoft Visual Basic standalone executable that can be run from a command prompt or batch file. 
When you execute this batch process, the software writes the start and end system time to the LogTableName table. The results of the process are written to the table identified by the TableName argument. The executable also creates the AreaReport.log file in your system %TEMP% folder. It contains the same information as written in the TableName and LogTableName tables in the database. 
Arguments for the Area Report Utility
The arguments for the executable are listed in "name=value" pairs separated by semicolons:
AreaFNO=G3E_FNO;  
AreaANO=G3E_ANOFromAreaView;  
FNOList=G3E_FNO1,G3E_FNO2,G3E_FNO3;  
Percent=TrueOrFalse DefaultFalse;  
GeographicReferenceSpace=TrueOrFalse DefaultFalse;  
QueryName=PhraseWith %1$s WhereAreaANOValueShouldBe;  
Config=ConnectionConfigurationMapConfigurationName;  
Username=DatabaseUsername;  
Password=DatabasePassword;  
TableName=TableForOutputKeys;  
LogTableName=TableForStatusMessages;  
AreaName=AreaANOValue;  
FilterClause="Where clause spec";  
FIDQuery=Select statement that results in an FID list;  
LogFileDirectory=DirectoryName;  
ShortLogFile=TrueOrFalse DefaultFalse; 
AreaFNO= The feature number (FNO) of the area feature, such as a district or region feature in which to find the features listed. AreaFNO typically represents spatial partitioning of the service territory. There should not be many such features in the table, probably fewer than 50,000. 
AreaANO= The area attribute number (ANO) of an attribute from the primary graphic component view of the area feature. 
FNOList= A comma-separated list of features (FNOs) to be found within the area feature, such as poles, valves, street lights, pipe segments, and so forth. The feature identifiers (FIDs) found are stored in the G3E_FID column of the results database table. Features from secondary connections are not processed. 
Percent= Set to True or False. If set to True and the FNOList feature is linear or area, percentages of the original linears and areas are calculated and stored in the G3E_PERCENT column of the results database table. Because G3E_PERCENT alone cannot determine the percentage of the total feature for the repeating component, it also populates the G3E_MEASURED_LENGTH field. The value of this field is the calculated length for linear features, calculated area for areal features, and 1.0 for point features. The value of 1.0 for the point features does require you to differentiate between the point and linear (areal) features when calculating the total percentage of a feature using the support tools that you developed. If set to False, all values in G3E_PERCENT are 1.0, and all values in G3E_MEASURED_LENGTH are NULL. 
GeographicReferenceSpace= Indicates the reference space value to pass to MeasurementService when calculating linears and areas. If set to True, the geographic is used. If set to False, the projection is used. The default is False (projection). 
QueryName= The value to be stored in the G3E_QUERYNAME field of the results database table. This value should contain %1$s to substitute the value from the AreaANO field. If %1$s is not included, the results are incomplete. However, this is not necessary if only one area (AreaName) is being processed. 
Config= Configuration name from the connection configuration map. 
Username= Database login name. Leave it blank to use the operating system login. The database login name is stored in the G3E_USERNAME column of the results database table. 
Password= Database password. Leave it blank to use the operating system login. 
TableName= Name of the results table in the database. If this table does not already exist in the database, it is created when you run the executable. Entries in the results table are automatically cleaned out each time you execute AreaReportUtility.exe. 
LogTableName= Name of the log table in the database for messages. If this table does not already exist in the database, it is created when you run the executable. It should be designed as follows:   
|  Column Name  |  Null  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Not Null  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  
|  G3E_QUERYNAME  |  Not Null  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  
|  G3E_MESSAGE  |  Not Null  |  Varchar2 (1024)  |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Not Null  |  Number (10)  |  
AreaName= Optional. To analyze a single area instance, use an area name. 
FilterClause= Optional. The string containing a where- clause condition (for example, CD_TYPE='District') that is applied to the area component view recordset processed by the utility. The clause can reference only fields of the component view for the specified area feature. This string can contain anything that you can put after the WHERE keyword in SQL. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261142) AreaName and FilterClause are mutually exclusive.
FIDQuery= Optional. Limits the features processed within the areas not only by the feature class (FNOList), but also by the feature identifier. This is useful if you want to report on modified features only. FIDQuery should not be an expensive SQL and should not return thousands of FIDs, but hundreds or fewer FIDs. 
LogFileDirectory= The directory path for the log file. If the directory does not exist, the AreaReport.log file is created in a system-defined temporary directory. This file informs the user of an invalid directory. 
ShortLogFile= Set to True or False. If set to True, the SQL used to process the feature keys is not written to the log file. If set to False or the parameter is omitted, the SQL used to update the key tables is written to the log file. 
Example
areareportutility
AreaFNO=301;AreaANO=301010002;FNOList=91,92,93,94;Percent=False;  
QueryName=%1$s;Config=kcpldev;Username=kcpldev7;Password=kcpldev7;  
TableName=ces_featuretilerelation;LogTableName=ces_logmessage;  
FilterClause="type='AREA'";  
FIDQuery="select distinct G3E_FID from modificationlog   
where modifieddate > 'Jan 1 2002'";

##### Creating a Cable Pairs Report
Use Cable Fill to query and to report basic network cable- use information. The report types (for example, Cable Fill and Cable Fill by Gauge) are specified in your database. ##### Creating a Loop Makeup Report

###### Adding Attribution to an LMU Report
When a loop is processed, all the fields in the source tables and/or views are included as part of the output from LMU. You can update [source views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DHUwlxUkQR6tWTgCheuThQ) to include additional attribution from the source features, and you can retrieve attributes from other data or reference tables using joins to the feature component data. Any changes to source views must include the original fields. You must thoroughly test any changes to ensure no performance degradation has occurred. 
To include additional information in an LMU report, augment the LMU views used for data collection to include the information you need. For example, to include an address or the name of a detail drawing, add the address of the feature to the source view, and update the LMU stylesheet that the user sees as part of the LMU report. 
In the output XML files that the stylesheet uses, the loop feature hierarchical level contains these fields: UID (unique id linking features to the LMU that was performed), G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, description, filter, length, gauge, resistance, loss, and fiber_mode, followed by all the attribution in the source views. Because each LMU source feature can have different field names and the number of fields can differ, some limitations are implied in the format of the output: 
  * Because each source view has different field names, the field names of the output recordset do not match the field names of the source view. Output fields are labeled as SourceField#, where the # represents the ordinal of the field in the source. These new fields are in addition to the existing fields to preserve compatibility with existing stylesheets. 
  * Because each source view can have a variety of fields, the output recordset is padded to accommodate the source view with the most fields. 


This stylesheet example illustrates including the value of a source field in the [HTML output](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMGrbdshaeRmWzATJH6P9Q) for a specific feature. 
Example
<xsl:choose>  
<xsl:when test="[@G3E_FNO = 7000]">
<xsl:value-of select="@SourceField6"/>
</xsl:when>
<xsl:when test="[@G3E_FNO = 7100]">
<xsl:value-of select="@SourceField4"/>
</xsl:when>
<xsl:otherwise>
<xsl:value-of select="@Description"/>
</xsl:otherwise>
</xsl:choose>
In this example, the annotation of the feature is changed based on the FNO of the feature. The value of SourceField6 is included in the HTML report when the feature number is 7000. When the feature is 7100, the values of SourceField4 are displayed. For any other FNO, the default Description field is used.

##### Defining a New Preconfigured Simple Query
The [Simple Attribute Query command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zv8L7oFp4edvAQ_DH~KRNw) requires user input for display and report options, which must be repeated every time the query is run. However, you can define a preconfigured simple attribute query in metadata so the information displays on the Attribute Query dialog box. When the user selects a preconfigured simple attribute query, the Attribute Query dialog box is preloaded based on the configuration associated with the query, and all the user must do is click OK. The user can also override the metadata configuration. 
The following is a general workflow.

  1. [Populate the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274174)
  2. [Populate the G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING table.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274175)
  3. [Populate the G3E_SIMPLEQUERYATTRIBUTES table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274176). 
  4. Optional: [Populate the G3E_REPORTMAPPING table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274177). 
  5. Optional: Define a [color scheme](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1~8HuN_D3njzZb39c2n3Lg) and [override symbology](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Xbg3uNHPMcbvrpqA8aifrw). 
  6. [Edit the G3E_ANALYSISOUTPUT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274180). 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260583?tocId=YGaPdV8OoYwiwo_qHtUteQ) to commit the changes to the database. 
  8. [Refresh the metadata edits](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1wKkKpk8Uf4b7Tu2icaMqg?section=274181). 


The following workflows are specific to populating or editing the tables, defining the color scheme used in preconfigured queries, and refreshing the metadata edits. 
  * To refresh the metadata edits:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260583?tocId=YGaPdV8OoYwiwo_qHtUteQ). 
  2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Simple Query and Post Process under Analysis. 
  3. Click OK.

##### Duct Occupancy Reports

###### Style Sheets for Duct Occupancy Reports
Most of the customization involved in creating a duct occupancy report is writing the XSL stylesheet. The stylesheet controls the content and formatting of the final report. To write or modify this stylesheet, you must know how the input XML file looks. 
The Duct Occupancy Report XML file is a hierarchical structure containing the facility data for the selected feature or features and all of their related features through the [many-to-many ownership](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Vqt2Qr0hUpLn1pdFL4RMTQ) relationship. This structure is created by saving a hierarchical ADO recordset. (If you view this file in a text editor, you can see a node named s:Schema that contains information about the ADO recordset structure. You do not typically need to look at that data.) 
The structure starts with a node named xml/rs:data that contains one child node for each of the selected features; these nodes are all named z:row and contain the following properties:   
|  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_FID   |  G3E_OWNERFNO   |  G3E_OWNERFID   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
This XSL construct includes information about the selected (top-level) feature or features in your report:   
|  Example <xsl:for-each select="xml/rs:data/z:row"> instructions to generate report content </xsl:for-each>  |  
| --- |  
Each of those top-level nodes has one child node named FCRS and zero or more child nodes named RELATEDFNO, where FNO is replaced by the specific feature class number. (For example, the node named RELATED2300 corresponds to feature class 2300.) There is one RELATEDFNO field for each possible feature instance that the parent feature contains through many ownership. Each RELATEDFNO node has the same structure as the top-level nodes illustrated above. 
The FCRS node has two properties, G3E_FNO and G3E_FID, and contains child nodes for each component instance owned by that particular feature instance. The name of each child node is the same as the name of the table containing the component instances. (For example, if component 51 is stored in the GC_NETELEM table, the child nodes for that component are named GC_NETELEM.) The properties of these nodes are the columns of the component table, so the FCRS node represents the facility data for that feature instance. 
The following table contains a condensed XML file with descriptions of the nodes and their meanings. Not all components or fields are included.   
|  Example Text in italics represents data that is replaced with actual database values. The indentation level indicates the position in the hierarchy. Feature class numbers, component class numbers and names, and G3E_FID values are hypothetical and provided for illustration only.   
 |  Node  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <z:row G3E_FNO='2400'  
G3E_FID='232026667'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2200'  
G3E_OWNERFID='231955945'>  |  A top-level row in the hierarchy. This node would be a child of the xml/rs:data node. This node represents a Formation feature, which was the feature selected to run the report.   |  
|  <FCRS G3E_FNO='2400'   
G3E_FID='232026667'>  |  Begins the facility data for the feature instance represented by the parent node.  |  
|  <GC_NETELEM G3E_ID='231799632'   
G3E_FNO='2400' G3E_FID='232026667'   
G3E_CNO='51' G3E_CID='1'   
JOB_ID=string JOB_STATE=string   
FEATURE_STATE=string   
YEAR_PLACED='1973'/>  |  Content of the GC_NETELEM component instance for this feature.  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257731) The ending slash indicates this tag begins and ends here; there are no child nodes.   |  
|  <GC_FORM G3E_ID='230045189'   
G3E_FNO='2400' G3E_FID='232026667'   
G3E_CNO='2401' G3E_CID='1'   
FEATURE_TYPE='STRAIGHT'   
NUM_DUCTS='6'   
STALE_FLAG_FROM='0'   
STALE_FLAG_TO='0'/>  |  The primary attribute component of the formation.  |  
|  ....  |  Other components omitted.  |  
|  </FCRS>  |  Ends the FCRS node  |  
|  <RELATED2300   
G3E_FNO='2300' G3E_FID='232007207'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2400'   
G3E_OWNERFID='232026667'>  |  Represents a Duct feature owned by the formation. ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257731) The G3E_OWNERFNO and G3E_OWNERFID correspond to the parent node's G3E_FNO and G3E_FID.  This node has the same structure as the parent node. This structure repeats at each level in the many ownership hierarchy.   |  
|  <FCRS G3E_FNO='2300'  
G3E_FID='232007207'>  |  Begins the facility data for the duct.  |  
|  . . .  |  Data omitted. Child nodes have the same structure as the FCRS node illustrated above, but with the components for the duct rather than the formation.   |  
|  </FCRS>  |  End of facility data for duct.  |  
|  <RELATED7000 G3E_FNO='7000'  
G3E_FID='231964723'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2300'   
G3E_OWNERFID='232007207'>  |  A cable contained in this duct. Same structure as before. Since a cable cannot contain anything through many ownership, this node does not have any RELATEDFNO child nodes.   |  
|  <FCRS . . .>  |  Facility data for the cable.  |  
|  <GC_CONTAIN   
G3E_ID='230455221'   
G3E_FNO='7000'   
G3E_FID='231964723'   
G3E_CNO='65' G3E_CID='1'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2200'   
G3E_OWNERFID='231955943'/>  |  A record from the containment (many ownership) relationship component for this cable.  |  
|  <GC_CONTAIN  
G3E_ID='230455224'   
G3E_FNO='7000'   
G3E_FID='231964723'   
G3E_CNO='65' G3E_CID='2'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2300'   
G3E_OWNERFID='232007207'/>  |  This cable is contained in multiple features, so it has repeating instances of the GC_CONTAIN component. This illustrates how repeating components are represented in the XML file.   |  
|  . . .  |  More components of the cable.  |  
|  </FCRS>  |   |  
|  </RELATED7000>>  |  End of first cable.  |  
|  <RELATED7000 G3E_FNO='7000'  
G3E_FID='231964722'   
G3E_OWNERFNO='2300'   
G3E_OWNERFID='232007208'>  |  Another cable contained in the same duct. ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257731) The same node name is repeated.   |  
|  . . .  |  An FCRS node here, but no RELATEDFNO nodes.  |  
|  </RELATED7000>  |  End of second cable  |  
|  </RELATED2300>  |  End of the contained duct.  |  
|  </z:row>  |  Ends the top-level row  |  
 |

##### HTML Reports

###### HTML Report Metadata
This is the metadata associated with an HTML report: 
G3E_REPORTINTERFACE, G3E_REPORT, and G3E_REPORTMAPPING
The HTML report object is defined in the G3E_REPORTINTERFACE table. The [G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KXVHO74HoXhacwlIbL4kIQ) field defines parameters for [G3E_REPORT.G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg).   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_INTERFACE  |  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  HTML Report Interface  |  PRIface.HTMLReport  |  1. Specify the output path and file name for the XML file.  
2. Specify the input path and file name for the XSL file.  
3. Specify the output path and file name for the HTML file.  
4. Specify whether report displays or not (0 or 1).  
5. Specify whether verbose persistence is used (0 or 1).   |  
 |  
The [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table is used to map report interfaces to actual reports a user can execute. 
The [G3E_REPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) table is used to define an HTML report and its parameters. The G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT field defines the following parameters: 
  * XML file name—The name of the XML file to which to output the recordset. If this parameter is not specified, a default file name is applied. 
  * XSL file name—The name of the XSL file that is used to transform the XML into HTML.
  * HTML file name—The name of the HTML file to which to output the report. If this parameter is not specified, a default file name is applied. 
  * Display Report—Specifies if the report should automatically be displayed after it is generated. 
  * Persistence Mechanism—Specifies how the recordset is persisted to XML (verbose includes empty fields, or compact excludes empty fields). 

  
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RPNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  51  |  View Pairs Report  |  View Pairs HTML Report  |  5  |  default  
templates/xslt/GenericTable.xsl  
default  
1  
1   |  
 |

##### Implementing Predefined Report Interfaces
Configuring a predefined Report interface that a user can select on the Reporting tab of the query or trace dialog box can be as simple as adding a row to the [G3E_REPORTMAPPING table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) to link a Report to a specific query or trace or to a user-defined select set. But if you want more control, there is much more you can do. 
  * To implement a predefined Report interface:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Software Interfaces > Report node and select the report interface you want. 
The G3E_REPORTINTERFACE table row for the selected report interface appears.  
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682)  |  
| --- |  
  2. Describe the report interface in G3E_REPORTINTERFACE:
    1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the report interface.
    2. Click the G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT field.

  3. Configure the Report interface for processing:
    1. In the tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Reporting > Reports node. 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682) or select Insert a new row from the right-mouse menu. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682)
    3. Populate the new row in the G3E_REPORT table:
       * In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for your object.
       * In the G3E_DESCRIPTION field, explain what the Report object does.
       * In the G3E_RINO field, select your interface from the drop-down list.
       * If the interface requires arguments, click the Ellipsis in the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT field.  
The Interface Argument Editor appears. 
       * [Enter values for the arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ), and click OK. 
       * When the focus returns to the table row, click OK. 
  4. Map the object to the report/query combination:
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Reporting > Report Mapping by Report node. 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682) or select Insert a new row from the right-mouse menu. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682)
    3. Populate the new row in the G3E_REPORTMAPPING table:
       * In the G3E_RPNO field, select your object from the drop-down list.
       * Populate G3E_QNO with the number of the attribute query or trace that can use this report. These values correlate to G3E_TRACE.G3E_ID or G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AQNO. 
       * In the G3E_TYPE field, select the category of the report type from the drop-down list.
       * If the G3E_TYPE is SelectSet, in the G3E_FNO field select from the drop-down list the number of the feature (G3E_FEATURE.G3E_FNO) to which this report applies.  
If you omit the G3E_FNO value, the report applies to any feature in the select set. If the report applies to multiple features, list the report multiple times. 
       * Populate G3E_ROLE with the name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The name should match a name in G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_ROLE. 
       * Click OK. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682) to commit the changes to the database. 
  6. Refresh the metadata changes:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260682). 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Reports & Post Process under Custom Software and under Analysis. 
    3. Click OK.

##### Linking Reports to Query Results
The standard reporting mechanism in NetWorks Core requires only that you map one of the delivered Report interfaces to a specific query or trace or, more generally, to a select set defined by the user. This is accomplished in the [G3E_REPORTMAPPING table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w). 
  * To link a report to a specific query:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Finds, Queries, Traces and Reports > Simple Queries node. 
  2. Under the query you want to link, select the Reports node.
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260704), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260704)
  4. Populate the new row in the G3E_REPORTMAPPING table:
    1. From the G3E_RPNO field drop-down list, select the report.
    2. From the G3E_TYPE field drop-down list, select the report type.
    3. Populate G3E_ROLE with the name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The name should match a name in G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_ROLE. 
    4. Click OK. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260704) to commit the changes to the database. 
  6. Refresh the metadata changes:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260704). 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Reports & Post Process under Custom Software and under Analysis. 
    3. Click OK. 
  7. Verify that the report appears in the Output as report field on the Reporting tab of the Attribute Query dialog box.

##### Map Output Reports
The Map Output Report interface can be used to display the features in the input recordset. Once the Map Output Report interface is executed, the input recordset is added as a node on the Display Control. The user can check or uncheck the node to control the display of the input recordset. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260685) The input recordset added as a node on the Display Control is available only for the current work session. 
These are the metadata values associated with the Generic Map Output Report interface. This report object has no arguments.

A row in [G3E_REPORTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KXVHO74HoXhacwlIbL4kIQ) describes the Generic Map Output Report interface.

|  9  |  Map Output Report  |  PRIface.MapOutputReport  |  BLOB  |  BLOB  |  12/09/06  |

A row in [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) maps report interfaces to actual reports a user can execute.

##### Repair Allocation Reports
If NetWorks Core cannot completely and automatically determine the correct allocation, it places a [repair feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/INbE7zFbCgdLyTPjKm1STQ), as [configured in metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KR86c2s5ZCQOCD1zzNo8ow), near the break point. The repair feature is annotated with references to the containing features that could not be resolved. The software also allocates both resulting features to ambiguous containers. 
The user can select the repair feature and invoke the [Report Using Select Set](javascript:;) command to run the Repair Allocation report. Depending on how you configure the report, it displays options like queries and traces for the output of the report, including map output, data table, and other reporting options. The Repair Allocation report displays both features resulting from the break plus all containing features that are common to those features. The report includes the complete containment hierarchy, not just immediate containers, so it includes the formations, conduits, and ducts common to both features. However, the display is not ordered in any particular way, and it does not display the hierarchical relationship of the containers. 
These metadata values are associated with configuring a repair allocation report:
  * G3E_REPORTINTERFACE
A row in [G3E_REPORTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KXVHO74HoXhacwlIbL4kIQ) describes the repair allocation report interface.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_INTERFACE  |  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  10  |  Repair Allocation Report  |  PRIface.RepairAllocationReport  |  BLOB  |  BLOB  |  12/09/07  |  
 |  
These are the arguments for the repair allocation report interface:
    * G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT—Specify the report interface number to be used to display the output data" is the prompt. 
    * G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE—Number is the data type. This is expected to be the [G3E_REPORT.G3E_RPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) of the [generic map output report](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bEI6j_HfLHLKK2lg2wSvZg) or any customized report interface that you want to configure. The metadata upgrade adds this row. 
  * G3E_REPORT
[G3E_REPORT.G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) specifies G3E_RPNO of the generic map output report interface.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RPNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  107  |  Repair Allocation Report  |  Repair Allocation Report  |  10  |  BLOB  |  12/09/03  |  
 |  
  * G3E_REPORTMAPPING
The repair allocation report interface should appear in the select set report interface only if the selected feature is a [repair feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/INbE7zFbCgdLyTPjKm1STQ). To achieve this, add a row to the [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RPMNO  |  G3E_RPNO  |  G3E_QNO  |  G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  101  |  107  |   |  4  |  19200  |  12/09/03  |  
 |

##### Review Feature Allocation Reports
The [Review Feature Allocation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U8CqO9ZEqAO1imM7NZbfvA) command has several output options. One of the options is to output information as a report. The command uses the standard report selection control, which allows custom reports to be defined. 
These metadata values are associated with configuring a review feature allocation report: 
  * G3E_REPORTINTERFACE
A row in [G3E_REPORTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KXVHO74HoXhacwlIbL4kIQ) describes the report interface that is used.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_INTERFACE  |  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  3  |  CSV Report Interface  |  PRIface.CSVReport  |  BLOB  |  BLOB  |  1/19/04  |  
 |  
These are the arguments for the repair allocation report interface:
    * G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT—Full UNC Path to CSV report file is the prompt.
    * G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE—String is the data type. This is expected to be the path and file name that points to where the CSV report file is written. 
  * G3E_REPORT
[G3E_REPORT.G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~2VhQpRQSi_R90iNba9YSg) specifies G3E_RPNO of the [generic map output report](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bEI6j_HfLHLKK2lg2wSvZg) interface.   
|  Example  
 |  G3E_RPNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  108  |  CSV Report  |  CSV Report  |  3  |  BLOB  |  1/19/04  |  
 |  
This is the argument used when calling the CSV report interface:
G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT—<where you want the report to be located>/csvreport.csv
  * G3E_REPORTMAPPING
The review feature allocation report interface should appear in the report selection list on the Review Feature Allocation dialog box. To achieve this, add a row to the [G3E_REPORTMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTE5K~kT9KX2yH7cssn59w) table.

#### Implementing Custom Report Objects

##### GTHTML Object

###### Methods

###### ExploreFeature Method
Applies To
[GTHTML Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eRUCQhf9jywhd0y~hy7eOQ)
Description
The ExploreFeature method lets the user double-click a row in an HTML report and view the selected feature in Feature Explorer. 
When the user selects the feature specified by the FNO and FID parameters, the feature is added to the select set, and the feature appears in review mode in Feature Explorer. 
Syntax
Object.ExploreFeature(FNO, FID, OpenDetail)
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  FNO  |  Integer  |  Input  |  Required  |  The feature number of the feature to select and open in Feature Explorer.   |  
|  FID  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  The feature ID of the feature to select and open in Feature Explorer.   |  
|  OpenDetail  |  Boolean  |  Input  |  Required  |  Specifies whether a detail window should be opened automatically if the feature being selected does not exist in any open window and contains detail components only.   |  
Remarks
This functionality can be encoded in an XSL style sheet which can then be used to transform the contents of an ADO recordset persisted in XML format into an HTML report. The IGTHelperService.RunReport method does this transformation when an RPMNO for an HTML report is specified. The RPMNO must have a report interface argument that points to an XSL style sheet that contains a function call such as the following:   
|  Example <xsl:attribute name="__OnDblClick">OnDblClickRow(<xsl:value-of  
select="@G3E_FNO"/>,<xsl:value-of  
select="@G3E_FID"/>,0,0,0)</xsl:attribute>  |  
| --- |  
Each row that needs to be double-clickable must include this function and specify the FNO and FID of the feature to be selected. In the example above, the feature keys are extracted from the XML file. 
Note that the __OnDblClick event name is prefixed with two underbars. These are removed when the style sheet is processed and is replaced with OnDblClick in the HTML report. This conforms to standard style-sheet namespace rules to ensure proper transformation of the attribute nodes. 
You do not need to implement the OnDblClickRow function in the style sheet. This function is included in the HTML report as part of the style sheet transformation performed by the RunReport method. The following JavaScript is automatically added to the HTML report:   
|  function OnDblClickRow(FNO,FID,CNO,CID,OpenDetail)  {  try  { var h = new ActiveXObject("GTHTMLAuto.GTHTML"); h.ExploreFeature(FNO,FID,OpenDetail);  } catch(e){}  }  |  
| --- |  
The function creates the GTHTML object and calls the ExploreFeature method. The CNO and CID parameters to the OnDblClickRow function are not used but exist to avoid breaking previous style sheets that used these functions.

###### SelectFeature Method
Applies To
[GTHTML Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eRUCQhf9jywhd0y~hy7eOQ)
Description
The SelectFeature method lets the user click a row in an HTML report and view the selected feature in the active map window. 
When the user selects the feature specified by the FNO and FID parameters, the feature is added to the NetWorks Core  select set. 
Syntax
Object.SelectFeature(FNO, FID, OpenDetail)
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  FNO  |  Integer  |  Input  |  Required  |  The feature number of the feature to select and window to.  |  
|  FID  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  The feature ID of the feature to select and window to.  |  
|  OpenDetail  |  Boolean  |  Input  |  Required  |  Specifies whether a detail window should be opened automatically if the feature being selected does not exist in any open window and contains detail components only.   |  
Remarks
This functionality can be encoded in an XSL style sheet which can then be used to transform the contents of an ADO recordset persisted in XML format into an HTML report. The IGTHelperService.Runreport method does this transformation when an RPMNO for an HTML report is specified. The RPMNO must have a report interface argument that points to an XSL style sheet that contains a function call such as the following:   
|  Example <xsl:attribute name="__OnClick">OnClickRow(<xsl:value-of  
select="@G3E_FNO"/>,<xsl:value-of   
select="@G3E_FID"/>,0,0,0)</xsl:attribute>  |  
| --- |  
Each row that needs to be clickable must include this function and specify the FNO and FID of the feature to be selected. In the example above, the feature keys are extracted from the XML file. 
Note that the __OnClick event name is prefixed with two underbars. These are removed when the style sheet is processed and are replaced with OnClick in the HTML report. This conforms to standard style-sheet namespace rules to ensure proper transformation of the attribute nodes. 
You do not need to implement the OnClickRow function in the style sheet. This function is included in the HTML report as part of the style sheet transformation performed by the RunReport method. The following JavaScript is automatically added to the HTML report:   
|  Example function OnClickRow(FNO,FID,CNO,CID,OpenDetail)  {  try  {  var h = new ActiveXObject("GTHTMLAuto.GTHTML"); h.SelectFeature(FNO,FID,OpenDetail);  }  catch(e){}  }  |  
| --- |  
The function creates the GTHTML object and calls the SelectFeature method. The CNO and CID parameters to the OnClickRow function are not used but exist to avoid breaking previous style sheets that used these functions.

##### OTDR Marker Placement Report Interface
When the trace execution is complete, the OTDR Marker Placement Report interface locates the point of the cable faults and places a graphic marker at the specified distance on the geographic network. The marker is created by the OTDR Create Marker interface as a temporary geometry. When determining the fault points, all cables whose cumulative distance/resistance is greater than or equal to the input stop criteria value are considered as candidates for marker placement. To produce a different result than graphic markers on the map, you can replace the delivered interface with a custom interface. 
The OTDR Marker Placement Report interface is implemented as a COM object.  
|  Parameters  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  OTDR Compute Marker Location Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  Parameter to specify OTDR Compute Marker Location interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Marker Location Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  Parameter to specify OTDR Compute Marker Location interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Geo Point Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Compute Geo Point interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Geo Point Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Compute Geo Point interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Create Marker Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Create Marker interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Create Marker Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Create Marker interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  Stop Criteria Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the input stop criteria value. Derived from user input.   |  
|  Cable Value Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the calculated value derived from the TRACERESULT table.   |  
|  Cumulative Value Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the cumulative value derived from the TRACERESULT table.   |

##### Deleting Features Imported from a Secondary Source
You can delete geometry and component records that have been previously imported, which lets you reimport secondary data that has changed. First you create a delete file, and then you run the data-delete process. 
  * To delete secondary data features:


  1. Create a text file containing the following information:
//Deletes File — Key words to distinguish this as a delete file.  
//Removal List — Feature name, primary key column, value  
//where  
//Feature Name — Name of feature to delete. Can be g3e_username or  
// g3e_importfeaturename from g3e_feature  
//Primary Key Column — Name of primary key field to use to identify feature  
//Primary Key Value — Value of primary key field used to identify specific instance of feature to delete
Example delete file
//Deletes File
EX_ANNO,graphic_id,101823714  
EX_ANNO,graphic_id,101823668  
EX_ANNO,graphic_id,101823766  
EX_ANNO,graphic_id,101823938
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257595) Slashes (//) at the beginning of a line signify a comment. 
  2. From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
Importremoval.exe <username/password@alias> <location of deletes.txt file>   
<configuration name>

#### NetWorks Core - GeoMedia Interoperability

##### GeoMedia Feature Component Data Tables
NetWorks Core[-GeoMedia interoperability](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cM_6pak7sXF2Cycb700xpg) provides for GeoMedia feature component table information to be populated into NetWorks Core metadata and for those tables [and their geometry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gG79jCB7px1trXqyoPhSQ) to be accessible and visible to (and editable by) NetWorks Core. One potential limitation with viewing GeoMedia features inside NetWorks Core, however, is encountering geometry that NetWorks Core is not familiar with or interprets differently. 
The NetWorks Core data access layer—including Deltas, component, and publish—should insulate you from any unexpected occurrences due to differences in modeling, but you should be aware of this limitation as something unexpected could occur. GeoMedia and Oracle support geometry types not supported by NetWorks Core, but these should be hidden from most NetWorks Core software except for publish, Deltas, and the geometry service.

#### Publishing Secondary Data

##### Publishing Facility Data
After [publishing metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ), you must publish the facility component views into DDC files to create the snapshot of the graphic and attribute data necessary for efficient display. The component views available for publishing come from facility data, including details, and from secondary data sources. Publishing for facility data are handled from the command prompt, so you can set up a task to run publishing at a convenient time. 
The publish process is controlled by a UDB file. This file contains information about whether to do a full or incremental publish, the views to publish, and the DDC files to which the views should be published. The component views may be published to a single DDC or to several DDCs, or each component view may be published to its own DDC. Only views from the same data source should be placed in the same DDC file. 
  * A [full publish](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw) is a bulk extract of component view records for each view in the UDB file into one or more DDC files. 
  * An [incremental publish](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KMyb7We6CN6SLJS3Anpyuw) updates views in the existing DDC files using deltas from the server. 


All views selected for publishing must already exist in the configuration. When you publish facility data for the first time, you must perform a full publish because there are no existing cache files available. 
You can create the UDB file anywhere on the local machine. The following example shows part of a data UDB file.   
|  Example MAPFILESIZE=0  
PUBLISHTYPE=1  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_LL.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_LL   
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_ML.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_ML   
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_PT.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_PT   
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_SL.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_SL   
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANNOTXT_LB.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANNOTXT_LB  
… …[mapfiles and views continue…]   |  
| --- |  
Before you execute the PublishMapFiles command, a ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file that includes the configuration you are publishing must exist at both the <CurrentCCMPaths> and the <PrepCCMPaths> locations. 
  * To publish facility data DDC files (full publish):


  1. To create the data UDB file that contains the component views to be published, open a blank document in a text editor and type the following: 
MAPFILESIZE=0  
PUBLISHTYPE=1
MAPFILESIZE=0 indicates there is no size limit to the DDCs to be created.  
PUBLISHTYPE=1 indicates that this is a full publish. 
  2. While connected to the database of the configuration, use an SQL editor to execute the following statement: 
SQL> select 'VIEWS= '||G3E_VIEW from G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION order by G3E_VIEW;
  3. Copy and paste the output into your text document after the PUBLISHTYPE lines.
  4. Group the component views into the appropriate DDC files by adding one or more MAPFILE= statements. 
     * Each MAPFILE= statement should contain the complete path and file name of the DDC file to be created by the publish process. 
     * A given component view can appear only once in the UDB file.
     * To put each component view in a separate DDC named for the component view, use the following statement to create both the DDC and VIEWS statements: 
SQL> select 'MAPFILE=<path to file>\'||G3E_VIEW||'.ddc  
VIEWS= '||G3E_VIEW from G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION order by G3E_VIEW;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258075?tocId=MtyxnJLWjnzSNQ2HgFkolQ) This approach is only for initial development until the component view definition is stable. The production system should minimize the number of DDC files by combining several views into one file. Generally, you should have one DDC per feature with all component views for that feature grouped in one file. 
     * The VIEWS statements can be rearranged as needed to obtain the grouping you want. 
  5. Copy and paste the output into your text document after the PUBLISHTYPE lines.
  6. Save the file as <ConfigurationName>.udb. 
  7. From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and execute the following statement: 
PublishMapFiles <path to UDB file><ConfigurationName>.udb {0 or 1 or 2}<Username/Password@alias> [uid;pwd]
     * <ConfigurationName> must be the same as the configuration to be published. This name is matched against the G3E_LOCATION field of the [G3E_DATACONNECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) table. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258075?tocId=MtyxnJLWjnzSNQ2HgFkolQ) <ConfigurationName> must also match the case of the entry in G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION for the configuration being published. 
     * The publishing process always updates the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file specified by the PrepCCMPaths value to reflect the path to the DDC files specified in the UDB file. 
     * Username, password, and alias must match the NetWorks Core configuration to be published. 
     * The second parameter on the command line indicates whether the <CurrentCCMPaths> and <PrepCCMPaths> values in the [FileUNCPaths](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) file should be left unchanged or swapped when publishing completes. 
0 = Unchanged  
1 = Swapped 
2 = Restricts CCM updates and Swapping
       * When the second parameter value is either 0 or 1, the publishing process updates the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file specified by the PrepCCMPaths value to reflect the path to the DDC files specified in the UDB file. 
       * When the second parameter value is 2, there are no updates in the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file. 
       * Option 0 leaves the values unchanged so that you can check the log file for errors and test the DDCs before the current CCM file is updated. 
       * Option 2 is useful for executing parallel publish, but the publish.log file in %Temp% is not updated appropriately because of a timing issue. All publish processes update the same file. 
     * The fourth parameter is a user ID and password for an MGE connection if views from an MGE secondary data source are included in the UDB file. 
The PublishMapFiles.exe returns an exit code based on publish status: 
0 = Publish success Publish Complete
-1 = Publish fails: Publish Complete with errors
  8. Check the publish.log file in the %TEMP% folder for errors that occurred during the publishing process. Depends on the exit code, a Publish Complete or Publish Complete with errors message is added at the end of the log file. Most of the errors reported are typically geometry errors that do not stop the publishing process. Decide if the geometries need immediate attention. Fix other kinds of errors before continuing. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258075?tocId=MtyxnJLWjnzSNQ2HgFkolQ) During incremental publishing, bad geometry errors are not reported because the errors are found and discarded before the actual publish process. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258075?tocId=MtyxnJLWjnzSNQ2HgFkolQ) Because publishing does not fail when encountering bad geometries, it is easy to not realize you have bad geometries. Check your publishing log file to find them. It is recommended that you fix these bad geometries as soon as possible. If the bad geometries are not fixed, the maps do not reflect the data and data are lost. 
  9. Check the appropriate ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file (<CurrentCCMPaths> or <PrepCCMPaths>) to ensure the paths and file names of the DDC files for your configuration are correct. There should be seven metadata DDC files in addition to the data DDC files. 
  10. Assuming you published to the <PrepCCMPaths> location, after testing the newly published DDC files from the Prep location, modify the FileUNCPaths file so that the <CurrentCCMPaths> location is now what was your <PrepCCMPaths> location and vice versa.

##### Secondary Metadata

###### Generating Custom Secondary Metadata
When you select the Custom metadata from secondary source option, the grids on the dialog box display the default settings for the secondary metadata. The grids are read-write, so you can change certain column settings to customize the look of the metadata. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257635)
  * Because the process for creating metadata for imported secondary data are different from the process for secondary data that has not been imported, verify that you appropriately checked the [Import source column](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ibxD7CxHVNpkwz117fKMJQ) on the Secondary Database Connections dialog box. 
  * Unless the source is imported, the system does not generate label entries. Each feature or component should have a unique style object and rule specified, although no attempt is made to derive symbology from the source data. 


  * To generate custom secondary metadata:


  1. From the Administrative tab in the Secondary group, select Generate Metadata. 
  2. From the drop-down list, select the connection you want to use to generate the secondary metadata. 
  3. Select Custom metadata from secondary source. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Rb5Gbk3yXhAry1mssD5uDw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=630e45f0d5b96a58&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. Select the features and attributes you want to display in Feature Explorer. To exclude a feature while generating metadata, uncheck the Include feature/component? column. 
The data are not being added to the database, but the attributes are added to metadata tables. 
  5. In the Metadata default features grid, click the row containing the definition you want to change and make your changes in the following columns:   
|  Column Name  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Include feature- component?  |  If checked, the feature- component is included in the metadata.  |  
|  User Name  |  Feature name.  |  
|  Combine Geometry/Attributes?  |  If checked, one component for everything in the GDO feature class is created except secondary geometry fields. The component contains the geometry component. To create a secondary component identified in the last column, uncheck. This component contains just attribute data.   |  
|  Geometry Component Name  |  GEOMETRY component name and/or data type.  |  
|  Attribute Component Name  |  Attribute component name. This column is blank if you are combining it with geometry. Otherwise, it defaults to geometry component name followed by ATTR.   |  
  6. In the Attributes grid, remove the check to indicate that the attributes are not included. By default all attributes are checked. 
  7. Click OK. 
Once all the secondary metadata has been generated, you should see a message box with the status of the metadata generation. A log is created on your local folder. In addition two files are created: ScndMetaSQL.txt, a text file listing the secondary data features  
ScndMetaSQL.log, a script for all the metadata entries made for the imported features. 


[Next: Modify the styles created by the secondary metadata generation process.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GVwibq0NSEYvsKV~8WKhfA)

###### Generating Default Secondary Metadata
NetWorks Core generates the secondary metadata by default. The feature name is the same as the feature class name in the secondary data, and the component name is the <feature class name>_<geometry field name>.   
|  Example The feature class name is Roads in the secondary data. The NetWorks Core feature name is Roads, and the component name is Roads_Geometry.   |  
| --- |  
If the feature has associated attributes, the attributes are combined with the graphic component. 
If you select the Default metadata from secondary source option on the Generate Secondary Metadata dialog box, the grids on the dialog box display the default settings used to generate the secondary metadata. The grids are read-only. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257632)
  * Because the process for creating metadata for imported secondary data are different from the process for secondary data that has not been imported, verify that you appropriately checked the [Import source column](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ibxD7CxHVNpkwz117fKMJQ) on the Secondary Database Connections dialog box. 
  * Unless the source is imported, the system does not generate label entries. Each feature or component should have a unique style object and rule specified, although no attempt is made to derive symbology from the source data. 


  * To generate default secondary metadata:


  1. Generate Metadata.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/wSh2AbXzgpx47fdNgY1fxQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=f8c788360d806bd2&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Select the secondary connection for which you want to create metadata from the drop-down list. 
  3. Select Default metadata from secondary source. 
  4. Click OK. 


[Next: Modify the styles created by the secondary metadata generation process.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GVwibq0NSEYvsKV~8WKhfA)

###### Publishing Metadata
When you need to update or publish the metadata DDC (mapfiles) to include all metadata with any changes you have made since the last publish, check the Include changes option on the Metadata Versions dialog box. Checking this option ensures that the Metadata Versions table is updated and that all metadata-optimized tables are recreated. If you do not check the Include changes option, the existing metadata-optimized tables are used, and changes are not included. This publish process produces DDC files and RAW files. The Versions command updates the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file to point to the new DDC and RAW files.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256049?tocId=_E6_BPV9bhukfDGq7NiiLg)
  1. The [language settings for Oracle](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0X9oQyI8GXBmjQuIdUiWTg) on the publish machine must be consistent with the database. If they are not, publishing fails. 


  * Verify that the [G3E_SCHEMAOWNER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER is set to the schema-owner user name. If it is not, publishing fails. 

 |  
| --- |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256049?tocId=_E6_BPV9bhukfDGq7NiiLg) All fonts must be installed on the publish server during metadata publish. 
  * To publish metadata dynamic display cache files and raw files:


  1. From the Administrative tab in the Metadata group, select Versions.
  2. On the Metadata Versions dialog box, check Publish. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/GbvpF2FBLP0ZTjCYe0rUtQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=154d7beb61ef78ea&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. To include your current metadata changes, check Include changes. 
  4. To publish all seven dynamic display cache files, select All in the Publish mode group box. 
  5. To publish only selected dynamic display cache files, select one of these options in the Publish mode group box: 
     * All to publish all the RAW files. 
     * Metadata to publish only the metadata optable RAW files. 
     * Picklist to publish only the picklist RAW files. 
     * Default features to publish only the RAW files associated with tables containing data default values. These are the RAW files that begin with CNO. 
  6. In the File location box: 
To publish to the location specified in the current CCM file, expand the My Computer node and click Click to add UNC path and add the path. 
OR
To publish to a another location, select the location for the published files. 
In either case:
     * You must have write access to the selected location.
     * The command updates the current ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file to reflect the selected location. 
  7. Once you have defined the publish criteria, click Execute.

#### Secondary Database Connections

##### Creating a Secondary Database Connection
From the Administrative tab in the Secondary group, select Connection. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/TkDQy4oNjMvEl1nOKoYvnw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=a63b0c92e2e1b50c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  1. Click New. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/vs~yeByMDu2Q6Hf_04IB7w-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=d47b60731e04d9e4&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Select the type of connection appropriate for your data, and click Next. 
  3. Type a name for the connection. The name should describe or identify the secondary data. 
  4. Type or browse to select the complete path to the database, project, or folder; and type a description of the connection. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/531753)
  5. Click Finish
The connection status changes to Open. If you exit NetWorks Core, the connection status changes to Closed. Before you can generate secondary metadata, you must change the status to Open by selecting it from the Status drop-down list. 
  6. If you are connecting to an MGE data source, type the user name, password, and service name for the MGE data source. 
  7. On the Secondary Database Connections dialog box, click Close. 


[Next: Generate secondary metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IFe3ufPP_DKJ5bXW2kdD0w) so you can view the data from the secondary source.

##### Deleting a Secondary Database Connection
When you no longer want to use a secondary data source, you can delete the database connection. 
  * To delete a secondary database connection:


  1. From the Administrative tab in the Secondary group, select Connection. 
  2. On the Secondary Database Connection dialog box, click the row-selector button to select an existing connection. 
  3. Press DELETE.
  4. Click OK on the confirmation dialog box. 
The selected connection is removed from the grid as well as from the work space.
  5. On the Secondary Database Connections dialog box, click Close.

##### Editing a Secondary Database Connection
Generally, you edit a secondary database connection to change its status or the location of the secondary data source. You cannot change the connection name or connection type of an existing connection. 
  * To edit a secondary database connection:


  1. From the Administrative tab in the Secondary group, select Connection. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/TkDQy4oNjMvEl1nOKoYvnw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=a63b0c92e2e1b50c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Click the row-selector button to select an existing connection.
  3. Change the appropriate editable column or columns in the secondary connection you selected.   
|  Column  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Status  |  Database status: Open or Closed. When the connection is closed, the database is not accessible and features cannot be displayed.   |  
|  Import source  |  Whether this connection is used as an import source or not. A check indicates that it is an import source. If the column is unchecked, it is not an import source.   |  
|  Location  |  UNC path of the parameter file where the server software has to get information to create the connection. For example, the project.MGE file would be the parameter file for MGE.   |  
|  Connect info  |  MGE data source only: Connection information required to connect to an MGE server. For example, ODBC;DSN=fpcland;SERVER=fpctst.   |  
|  Output Dir  |  Import connections only: Name of the folder to store the generated SQL*Loader files for an import type of connection.   |  
|  Last Assigned FID  |  Import connections only: Value of the last assigned G3E_FID for features imported from a GDO server.   |  
|  CSName  |  Coordinate system associated with the connection. This must refer to an already defined coordinate system.   |  
  4. To save your entries, TAB out of the last cell. 
  5. On the Secondary Database Connections dialog box, click Close.

### User-Defined Datums

#### Sample IGMUserSuppliedTransformation Implementation
This example illustrates how to implement the interface in a user-supplied object in a way that enables NetWorks Core geodetic transformation objects to use the object. This example object implements a simple datum transformation that applies constant shifts to geographic coordinates. The shift values are given to the object through its IGMUserSuppliedTransformation.ConfigurationParameters property. 
The following is a Visual Basic implementation of the IGMUserSuppliedTransformation object. The code implements a datum transformation that consists of geographic shifts. This transformation operates in either the forward or inverse direction and requires the input and output points to be among the point types that are geographic. Both input and output must have the same heights (Z) type. 
The example code presumes that the ConfigurationParameters string has the format
LonShift=<VALUE>;LatShift=<VALUE>; 
where the shift values are expressed in decimal degrees.
A private function named ExtractKey (not detailed here) extracts the named values from the ConfigurationParameters string. 
The Visual Basic project is named "GTExample," and the code is in a .cls file that defines the class module named "GeogShiftDT". That produces a ProgID of "GTExample.GeogShiftDT". There is also a named datum "My 2004 Datum" that is a local refinement of NAD83, and the example user-supplied datum transformation is used to transform between NAD27 and the named datum. 
  1. Define the named datum in NamedHDatum.ini: 
My 2004 Datum,csgdNAD83
  2. Add an entry in autodt.ini, all on one line. 
  3. csgdNAD27,My 2004 Datum,csdtUserSupplied,ProgID=GTExample.GeogShiftDT;LonShift=0.4875;LatShift=0.3125;


TypeLibraries/OCXs required
IGMUserSuppliedTransformation 1.0 (C:\Program Files\Common Files\Intergraph\Coordinate Systems\Program\ CCSUserSuppliedTransformation.tlb) 
Class
The user-supplied object being implemented (*.cls) file 
IGMUserSuppliedTransformation.ConfigurationParameters Property
Option Explicit 
Private m_ConfigurationParams As String 
Private m_LonShift As Double 'Longitude shift in radians
Private m_LatShift As Double 'Latitude shift in radians
Implements IGMUserSuppliedTransformation 
Property Let IGMUserSuppliedTransformation_ConfigurationParameters( _
ByVal ParamString As String) 
Dim dblDegToRad As Double 'degrees to radians conversion 
Dim strShift As String 'extracted from configuration param string
'Initialize conversion factor 
dblDegToRad = 3.14159265358979 / 180# 
'Save given string 
m_ConfigurationParams = ParamString 
'Extract geographic shift settings from string 
If (0 <> Len(ParamString)) Then 
'Longitude shift 
strShift = ExtractKey("LonShift=", ParamString) 
If (0 <> Len(strShift)) Then 
'Shifts are defined in decimal degrees, so convert to radians 
m_LonShift = dblDegToRad * CDbl(strShift) 
Else 
'Default to zero shift if key is null or not found 
m_LonShift = 0# 
End If 
'Latitude shift 
strShift = ExtractKey("LatShift=", ParamString) 
If (0 <> Len(strShift)) Then 
'Shifts are defined in decimal degrees, so convert to radians 
m_LatShift = dblDegToRad * CDbl(strShift) 
Else 
'Default to zero shift if key is null or not found 
m_LatShift = 0# 
End If 
Else 'Else entire configuration string is empty 
'Default to zero shifts if no configuration parameters given 
m_LonShift = 0# 
m_LatShift = 0# 
End If 
End Property 
Property Get IGMUserSuppliedTransformation_ConfigurationParameters() As Sring 
IGMUserSuppliedTransformation_ConfigurationParameters =_ ConfigurationParams 
End Property
IGMUserSuppliedTransformation.IsTransformationValid Method
Option Explicit 
Private m_ConfigurationParams As String 
Private m_LonShift As Double 'Longitude shift in radians 
Private m_LatShift As Double 'Latitude shift in radians 
Implements IGMUserSuppliedTransformation 
Public Sub IGMUserSuppliedTransformation_IsTransformationValid( _ 
ByVal InputPointType As USTPointConstants, _ 
ByVal OutputPointType As USTPointConstants, _ 
ByVal TransDirection As USTDirectionConstants, _ 
ByRef IsValid As Boolean) 
'This transformation performs a geographic shift, so we handle the
'geographic point types, while retaining the heights type (since 
'we ignore heights in our transformation). 
'Note that either direction is valid. 
If (((ustLLG = InputPointType) And (ustLLG = OutputPointType)) Or _
((ustLLO = InputPointType) And (ustLLO = OutputPointType)) Or _ 
((ustLLU = InputPointType) And (ustLLU = OutputPointType))) Then 
IsValid = True 
Else IsValid = False 
End If 
End Sub
IGMUserSuppliedTransformation.TransformPoints Method
Option Explicit 
Private m_ConfigurationParams As String 
Private m_LonShift As Double 'Longitude shift in radians 
Private m_LatShift As Double 'Latitude shift in radians 
Implements IGMUserSuppliedTransformation 
Public Sub IGMUserSuppliedTransformation_TransformPoints( _ 
ByVal InputPointType As USTPointConstants, _ 
ByVal OutputPointType As USTPointConstants, _ 
ByVal TransDirection As USTDirectionConstants, _ 
ByRef Buffer As Variant) 
Dim Cntr As Long 'Counts points 
Dim Index As Long 'Indexes to double ordinates (x, y, or z) 
Dim OrdinateCnt As Long 'Locally computed ordinate count (# doubles in Buffer) 
Dim LocCnt As Long 'Locally computed count of points 
'Calculate point count 
OrdinateCnt = UBound(Buffer) - LBound(Buffer) + 1 
LocCnt = OrdinateCnt / 3 
'Loop through all points 
For Cntr = 0 To LocCnt - 1 
Index = (Cntr * 3) 
'Add shifts in forward direction, subtract them in inverse direction 
If (ustForward = TransDirection) Then 
Buffer(Index) = Buffer(Index) + m_LonShift 
Buffer(Index + 1) = Buffer(Index + 1) + m_LatShift 
Else 
Buffer(Index) = Buffer(Index) - m_LonShift Buffer(Index + 1) = Buffer(Index + 1) - m_LatShift 
End If 
Next Cntr 
End Sub
