##### Defining a WFS Web Source Connection

###### Advanced Options

###### WFS Advanced Options
The WFS Advanced Options dialog box appears when you click Advanced on the Web Source Connection Wizard. In the case of a secure service, you might need to enter the username and password. 
![AdvancedOptionsNew2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/C~SfYOKEpj~80LzNhp3~zA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=b411fc64ae00a950&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  * Swap coordinates
    * Optional: Geographic: Check this box to swap the geographic coordinates.This option is unchecked by default. 
    * Optional: Projected: Check this box to swap the projected coordinates. This option is unchecked by default. 
  * Authentication
When accessing a secure service, it may be necessary to enter a user name and a password.
    * User name: Type your user name to access a secure service. 
    * Password: Type your password to access a secure service. 
  * Optional: Select feature classes to be loaded and override default coordinate system assignment: Use this option to select the feature classes and the available coordinate systems delivered by the service and override the coordinate system if necessary. This option is unchecked by default. 
Before checking this option, the Web services URL must be set. The data server requests the list of available feature classes from the service alongside the list of accepted coordinate systems. The default coordinate system is highlighted. 
The grid contains:
    * checkbox: check to present the feature class in the connection. This is checked by default. To select or deselect all features, double-click the column header. 
    * Name: the value of the Name tag from the GetCapabilities response. 
    * Title: the value of the Title tag from the GetCapabilities response. 
    * Preferred SRS/CRS: the list of the accepted coordinate systems for the feature class. The default is highlighted. 
    * CSF File: a CSF file to be used to override the preferred coordinate system if necessary. To select the file, use the Browse button. 
To order the feature list by Name or Title, click the column header.
When the user chooses to override default coordinate system assignments, the data server populates the grid with rows for each available feature class. The user can: 
    * select the feature classes to be served from the WFS. 
    * select the preferred coordinate system for each selected feature class, from among the coordinate systems supported by the WFS. 
    * override the coordinate system in HxGN NetWorks Core metadata using a CSF file. 
When the user selects an EPSG code or CSF file, a dialog asks whether the designated coordinate system is to be applied to all feature classes, or just the selected feature class. 
The Refresh button, located near the top of the grid, can be used to refresh the list with any change in the service. 
  * Maximum number of features to return: Use this option to set the maximum number of features to request from the server. This is usually used for obtaining sample data from the server. Default value: All features. 
  * In case of issues with the WFS service implementation
    * Download feature classes and process locally: Select this option when the service response cannot be parsed, for example, due to a namespace mismatch or data sorting problems. A common symptom of such a condition is no feature classes being served. If checked, the GetFeature response is downloaded from the server and processed locally. This can impact performance. 
    * Ignore schemas defined in GML: Select this option in combination with Download feature classes and process locally, in case of incorrect or inaccessible schema files in the GetFeature GML. 
  * Additional parameters: Use this option to set additional parameters. The syntax is as follows: 
parametername1=value1; parametername2=value2

  
|  Parameter Name  |  Alternate parameter name  |  Allowed values  |  Default value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  HTTPRequestTimeout  |  HRT  |  Integer > 0  |  180  |  Timeout in seconds for HTTP requests  |  
|  SRSDimension  |  D  |  2 or 3  |  2  |  Indicates whether there are 2 (XY) or 3 (XYZ) dimensions in the coordinates of the GML geometry. Can be used in case the SRSDimension definition is missing from the GetFeature response (GML 3.2.1 encoding).   |  
|  ProxyUsername  |  PUSR  |  String*  |  null  |  Used to set a user name when the system proxy for internet access needs authentication  |  
|  ProxyPassword  |  PPWD  |  String*  |  null  |  Used to set the password when the system proxy for internet access needs authentication  |  
* If a parameter is provided that corresponds to a different control on the dialog, the parameter provided here is the one used for the connection. 
* If these parameters include the characters “;” “,” or “=”, they must be doubled when entered in the Additional parameters text box. For example, a proxy password like pwd;=5 must be entered as ProxyPassword=pwd;;==5.

###### Connecting to a WFS Server
Before connecting to a WFS (Web Feature Server) warehouse, indicate the following:
  * WFS connection name and optional description
  * Web Feature Server (WFS) URL


WFS URL
Type the WFS URL in the following format: 
http://host[:port]/path?{name[=value]&}
If the name-value parameters are specified, the request type is 'GetCapabilities', and the REQUEST parameter is specified only as 
"REQUEST=GetCapabilities"   
|  Example formats http:// host[:port]/path OR http://host[:port]/path?REQUEST=GetCapabilities&SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=(2.0.0/1.1.0/1.0.0) Example URL http://webservices.ionicsoft.com/unData/wfs/UN?REQUEST=GetCapabilities&SERVICE=WFS  |  
| --- |  
The WFS GetCapabilities document contains versions implemented by the service. Those currently supported by HxGN NetWorks Core are 1.0.0, 1.1.0, or 2.0.0. When making requests, HxGN NetWorks Core uses the highest available version advertised by the WFS server. However, there are situations when a particular server does not function properly with a later version but works fine with a previous one. The specific version can be set by adding the VERSION parameter to the query string, for example, the same address presented above can be set to http://webservices.ionicsoft.com/unData/wfs/UN?VERSION=1.1.0.

##### Editing or Deleting a WFS Connection
You can edit or delete a WFS web source connection using WFS Connections. 
From the Administrative tab in the Web Source group, select WFS Connection. The [WFS Connections dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/285721) appears. 
![WFSConnections](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/f65fxNtutRcL50c6IUkPAw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=a03464b715645761&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
Status: Displays current status of the connection (Open, Closed). 
Connection name: Unique name for the connection. 
Connection type: Web address for WFS. 
Location: Web address for WMS or WFS. 
Password: Shows ****** if a password has been specified. 
  * To edit a WFS web source connection:


  1. On the WFS Connections dialog box, open a connection so that metadata can be generated for the web source. 
OR
Click Edit to display the WFS Connection dialog, and then complete these Steps: 
  2. Change the location, connection information, or password, and so on, as needed. 
  3. After changing the connection information, click Finish.
The data are updated in the grid on the main dialog box.


  * To delete a WFS web source connection:


  1. Click the row-selector button to select an existing connection.
  2. Press DELETE, and then click OK on the confirmation dialog box. 
The selected connection is removed from the grid and from the work space.
Any feature metadata defined for the connection is deleted from the database.

#### Troubleshooting WFS Connection Errors
Although the Web Feature Service is an OGC standard, in practice there are many situations when WFS services do not interact according to the protocol. As a client, the WFS data server of NetWorks Core is capable of detecting some common deviations from the standard and applying several automatic workarounds to minimize user intervention (for example, it tries POST requests first and, in case of failure, it switches to GET requests). It is difficult to imagine all possible non-compliant behavior that a WFS implementation may have, but it is possible in some cases to obtain different results depending on the method used for interaction. The following guide can be used as a progressive approach for working around incorrectly implemented WFS services. 
Possible Causes of WFS Interaction Errors
A normal communication workflow between the WFS data server of NetWorks Core (meaning the client) and a WFS service (the server) can be briefly described as follows: 
  * First step: the client constructs a GetCapabilities request using the given WFS URL, to which the server must respond with a properly formatted document containing the following important information: 
    * General service information and capabilities such as: allowed versions, implemented operations, transaction support, filter capabilities, and the like. 
    * Endpoint URLs and request methods (GET, POST) for implemented operations. 
    * A list of feature classes (or feature types in WFS terminology) and allowed coordinate systems for each class. 
  * Second step: the client invokes the DescribeFeatureType operation, to which the server must respond with the descriptions (i.e. attributes names and types) of the feature types, in the form of valid XSD schemas. Using this information, the WFS data server can construct the metadata necessary for NetWorks Core, and the connection is established. 
  * Next steps: any time a user displays a feature class or a query accessing WFS data, the WFS data server invokes the GetFeature operation to request the actual data from the server. 


Most common WFS problems are caused by non-compliance with the standard protocols as defined by OGC and W3C, or by misconfiguration on the server side. Users may see the following issues when trying to use problematic WFS services: 
  * The connection cannot be made, and various error messages are displayed. Most likely there are communication issues or wrong URL addresses. 
  * The connection is made, but no feature classes are available to NetWorks Core. These situations are caused by differences between names (including namespaces) and / or types of feature classes / feature types and attributes as they are reported by the WFS server during GetCapabilities and DescribeFeatureType operations. Sometimes, the DescribeFeatureType calls fail or return unusable data. 
  * Feature classes are available and can be used with NetWorks Core, but attribute and/or spatial queries fail. This happens because these queries are performed server-side using the advertised filtering capabilities, which may give errors if not properly implemented. 


Recommended Steps to Follow in Case of WFS Connection Issues
  1. Check the WFS address
A first step could be to check the validity of the WFS address. This is useful when there are errors while connecting to the service. When making the connection, the first interaction between the WFS data server and the WFS server is by accessing the GetCapabilities document. This document can be visualized using a standard web browser and accessing the WFS address using two parameters in the query string – REQUEST=GetCapabilities and SERVICE=WFS. For example, if the WFS address is as follows: http://webservices.ionicsoft.com/unData/wfs/UN, we ask for the following URL: http://webservices.ionicsoft.com/unData/wfs/UN?REQUEST=GetCapabilities&SERVICE=WFS. 
If the browser does not display or download a properly formatted XML document, the connection cannot be made from NetWorks Core because of obvious server issues. 
The same check can be made within NetWorks Core when defining the WFS connection, by showing the Advanced Options dialog and clicking the Select feature classes to be loaded and override default coordinate system assignments checkbox, which uses the same GetCapabilities document to fill the list below it. If errors are obtained or the list is empty, it is clear that a successful connection cannot be made until these major server problems are solved. 
  2. Force a specific version
The WFS GetCapabilities document contains versions implemented by the service. Those currently supported by NetWorks Core are 1.0.0, 1.1.0, or 2.0.0. When making requests, NetWorks Core uses the highest available version advertised by the WFS server. However, there are situations when a particular server does not function properly with a later version but works fine with a previous one. The specific version can be set by adding the VERSION parameter to the query string, for example: http://webservices.ionicsoft.com/unData/wfs/UN?VERSION=1.1.0.” 
  3. Choose specific layers
Depending on the WFS server, sometimes single layers can be read when multiple layers cannot; or some layers may have inaccurate data while others might be acceptable. It can help to experiment with specific layers by using the same Select feature classes to be loaded and override default coordinate system assignments checkbox from the Advanced Options dialog, and selecting individual layers. The same list allows redefinition of the corresponding coordinate systems, if needed, by choosing another available one or overwriting the definition. 
  4. Increase the HTTP timeout
In some cases, when the internet connection is poor or data coming from the server is large (many and/or very complex features), it can help to tell the WFS data server to wait longer than the default value of 180 seconds before a timeout is declared. This is set in the Additional parameters text box, using the syntax HTTPRequestTimeout=<number of seconds>. Also, for testing purposes, the server response can be limited to a subset of features by setting the “Maximum number of features to return” value. 
  5. Compose the model from downloaded data
One very common issue with WFS server implementations manifests as a successful connection but with zero feature classes available to NetWorks Core. This is caused by different names assigned to feature classes and attributes across XML documents and schemas presented by the server, or by errors received during DescribeFeatureType operations. In this case, the WFS data server can be instructed to avoid using the DescribeFeatureType operation and to compose the data model from downloaded data instead by setting the Download feature classes and process locally checkbox. 
Considering that NetWorks Core needs a fully-defined data structure at the moment the connection is finalized, and this structure was obtained through the DescribeFeatureType operation which in this case is no longer used, it is necessary to use other operations to build the feature classes definitions. This is achieved by downloading some data from the WFS server (with a limited GetFeature operation) which is analyzed to compose the data model. Together with ignoring feature descriptions, another parameter that can be set is Ignore schemas defined in GML, meaning that the WFS data server also ignores the schemaLocation attribute from the received GML file and composes the data model only by analyzing the GML data content. 
Users are warned that this mechanism for composing the data model is a workaround for problematic servers, that may affect data completeness and/or quality with missed attributes or wrong data types, and also may affect performance. In order to understand the implications, here is a technical explanation of the data access strategy used when these options are set: 
DescribeFeatureType is an operation that provides descriptions for the data model (schemas for feature classes) and it is used by NetWorks Core before accessing the data in order to prepare the metadata. In case DescribeFeatureType does not work well, there are other options: the GML files obtained from the GetFeature operation should also contain a schemaLocation attribute that normally indicates a schema identical to the one from the DescribeFeatureType operation (and many times it’s exactly a URL containing a DescribeFeatureType call). There can be situations when a GetFeature operation can give a correctly-formatted GML file with the schemaLocation containing not a DescribeFeatureType call but an http link to a valid XSD schema file. As a result, there are two possibilities to get the data model without using the DescribeFeatureType operation, but using GetFeature: 
     * The GML file contains a valid schemaLocation attribute and the obtained schema is usable. In this case, a GML with only one feature is enough and the correct collection of feature classes inside NetWorks Core may be found after the connection is made. 
     * The GML file contains an invalid schemaLocation attribute (either the same failing DescribeFeatureType call or another invalid address), or the obtained schema is unusable. In this case, even if Download feature classes and process locally was checked, the feature classes collection of NetWorks Core is still empty. The next logical step is to check the Ignore schemas defined in GML option and in this case, the WFS data server uses only the GML file content to construct the schema model by parsing it to discover the attributes. Because it is not feasible to get all the feature class data in advance (otherwise the connection time can be very long), the initial data gathering is limited to a reasonable number of features using the GetFeature operation with the count or maxFeatures parameter to only retrieve the first 10 elements. This time, more than one element is recommended, because a characteristic of GML files is to not list attributes that have null values. As a result, if some attributes of a particular feature class have null values for the first 10 records, these are not present in the first “schema-composing” GML file so are not taken into account when generating the NetWorks Core data model. After the connection is made and NetWorks Core requests all the data for display, these attributes, if they have non-null values in subsequent records, are ignored. Also, because it is difficult to determine the real data type only from the attributes’ values, the final NetWorks Core data model has only attribute fields of data type Memo, and geometry fields of type AnySpatial (compound). 
A consequence of these potential data-altering workarounds (with different namespaces, different attributes names or types) is a strong possibility for server-side filters to fail or give incorrect results. To avoid this situation, when Ignore feature descriptions is checked, the WFS data server disregards the server filtering capability and uses local NetWorks Core components for this functionality. A disadvantage of this method can manifest when dealing with large quantities of data and some filters must be applied by the user before accessing all the elements from the feature class in order to limit the transferred data. Increasing the HTTPRequestTimeout value may be needed in this case. As a result, the Download feature classes and process locally option can also be used with WFS servers that work fine in general except when they give errors during execution of attribute queries or spatial filters. 
  6. Use the log file
For clients with advanced technical knowledge about WFS interactions or in case the previous methods did not work, a log file can be configured where NetWorks Core will append brief descriptions of the attempted operations and results. The file must be named GDONET.log and located in the folder defined at the operating system level as the TEMP user variable (this location can be identified, for example, using the “echo %temp%” command from a command prompt window). 
Simply creating an empty file with this name before launching NetWorks Core will trigger the logging feature. Because this file is never deleted by NetWorks Core, only appended, it is important to move or delete it manually from the designated location when the logging session is finished. Depending on the types of errors described in the log file, it may be interpreted by the customer or sent to Hexagon Technical Support personnel for analysis.

## Localization

### Dropping a Language
If you no longer need a language you have defined, remove the row from [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ), and drop the language sub-tables with the following script: 
SQL> execute MG3EDropMetadata.DropAllSubTables( '<LCID>');

### Language Sub-Tables
NetWorks Core provides a script to create the appropriate set of language sub-tables. A sub-table is a copy of some subset of the fields from a normalized metadata table. When synchronized, the same number of rows exists in the normalized table and the sub-table. There is one sub-table per normalized table per language identified in [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ). 
The naming convention for sub-tables is <NORMALIZED TABLE> <LCID>, where LCID is replaced by the same identifier found in G3E_METADATALANGUAGE.G3E_LCID. In the case of G3E_FEATURE, for example, the database also contains G3E_FEATURE_0009 in an English configuration. 
The sub-table duplicates the key and edit date fields of the normalized table. It also includes the fields that must be localized and a special G3E_LOCALECOMMENT field, which is also copied from the normalized table. 
Once you define the languages, you must create and synchronize the language sub-tables before publishing. 
Creating the Sub-Tables
To create the sub-tables for all languages, execute this procedure:
SQL> execute MG3ELanguageSubtableUtils.CreateAllSubtables;
To create the sub-tables for one language, execute this procedure:
SQL> execute MG3ELanguageSubtableUtils.CreateSubtables('<LCID>');
Populating the Sub-Tables
NetWorks Core provides database procedures to populate the sub-tables. You maintain the default language's sub-tables simply by running the synchronization script: 
SQL> execute MG3ELanguagesubtableUtils.Synchronizesubtables;
Then publish the metadata.
For any other language, you must run this same procedure, modify the descriptive values in the language sub-tables, and then publish metadata. When you publish a new metadata version, the software always runs the synchronization script to ensure that the correct number of rows exists in the sub-tables. 
The synchronization process for the default language completely replaces the contents of the sub-table with values from the normalized tables. The synchronization process for the other languages matches entries in the sub-table with the normalized table. Any rows that no longer exist in the normalized table are removed from the sub-table. Any new rows are added with default values copied from the normalized tables. Any rows that match are left intact. This lets you update the sub-tables incrementally without losing your edits. 
Metadata validation reports errors related to the language sub-tables and indicates which scripts to run to correct the errors. 
Enabling Intelligent Localization
You can provide the language sub-tables to the localization team by generating either flat files (.csv), Oracle export files, or Access database files. This activity should be reviewed with the localization team for the preferred approach. 
To convey the intent of the fields in the language sub-table to the localization team, add a comment to the G3E_LOCALECOMMENT column in each base table with localizable fields. The project implementer should provide this description. The creation of the language sub-tables replicates this comment field. One comment field is provided per table, but you may need to describe multiple fields that require localization (for example, username and tooltip in the feature metadata).

### Language-Optimized Views
Supporting multiple languages influences the publishing of metadata. Because the administrator publishes metadata to enable quicker access for all client machines, metadata must be published for each language. The CCM files reference the root or parent folder for metadata. Under this folder, a subfolder exists for each language identified by the language code identifier (LCID). The complete set of metadata tables is published once for each language referenced in [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ). 
To access the correct metadata, the client software retrieves the operating system's current LCID value, configures the database session to use that LCID and opens the appropriate metadata files under the root folder specified in CCM. 
The language-optimized views rely on the package variable MG3ELanguage.ActiveLCID which is set using MG3ELANGUAGE.SETACTIVELCID('<LCID>'). The client sets this variable automatically. Should a third-party application need to read correctly localized metadata before querying the optimized views, set this variable for a database session from the third-party application. 
Optimized metadata tables which can be localized rely on the existence of language specific subtables. Views are used to serve the rows combining the base table information with the language specific data from the subtables. The correct subtable for language is determined by the variable MG3ELanguage.ActiveLCID. 
Networks Core is using two language optimization approaches:
  1. <BASE_TABLE_NAME>_XXXX
These are views that are defined as unionized queries over the subtables and are filtered to return the data for a single language. The optimized tables that reference these views are a view over the normalized tables and the XXXX views. 
  2. < BASE_TABLE_NAME>_OPTLANG
An _OPTLANG table contains a set of rows for all languages. The metadata publish process creates and maintains the content of these tables. The optimized table is a view over the _OPTLANG table to filter the data to return a single language.

### Localizing .NET Assemblies

#### Creating a Localized Satellite Assembly
NetWorks Core delivers sample a VB script \GTechnology\Program\Samples\LocalizeSatelliteAssemblies\MakeSatAsm.vbs for assembling all translated .resx files into a satellite assembly. The script uses Resource File Generator (resgen.exe) to convert .resx files to .resources files. Next, using the Assembly Linker (Al.exe), the script assembles the .resources files to a satellite assembly. If needed, correct the location of Resource File Generator and Assembly Linker by opening MakeSatAsm.vbs in a text editor and updating the constant RESGEN and ALEXE values. Type the following from a command prompt: 
cscript MakeSatAsm.vbs /n:SatAsmName /p:ResxFolder /c:CultureCode [/k:KeyFileName] [/v:AssemblyVersion] [/f:FileVersion]  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  SatAsmName  |  Required argument of string data type. Specifies satellite assembly name (for example, CmdMisc).   |  
|  ResxFolder  |  Required argument of string data type. Specifies the folder containing the translated .resx files (for example, C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr).   |  
|  CultureCode  |  Required argument of string data type. Specifies the culture code of your translated localized satellite assembly (for example, fr for neutral French).   |  
|  KeyFileName  |  Optional argument of string data type. Specifies the location of strong name key file.  |  
|  AssemblyVersion  |  Optional argument of string data type. Specifies the satellite assembly version. The default value is 1.0.0.0. Typically, the satellite assembly version is same as that of corresponding main assembly version. Assembly version value is listed under main assembly file properties.   |  
|  FileVersion  |  Optional argument of string data type. Specifies the satellite assembly file version. The default value is 1.0.0.0.   |  
Initially, set the satellite contract version same as that of main assembly version. When the main assembly is updated, its assembly version number is incremented. 
However, you might not want to ship new copies of your satellite assemblies if the existing ones are sufficient and compatible with the newer version of your product. In this case, increment the main assembly's version number, but leave the satellite contract version number the same. 
If you need to revise a satellite assembly but not the main assembly, increment the version number on your satellite. In this case, ship a policy assembly along with your satellite assembly, stating that your new satellite assembly has backward compatibility with your old satellite assembly. The Resource Manager still uses the old contract number written into your main assembly; however, the loader binds to the satellite assembly version as specified by the policy assembly. 
The following workflow is an example. 
  * To create a localized satellite assembly:


  1. If it does not already exist, create a temporary folder and move all translated .resx files to it. For example, create the C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr folder and move all translated neutral French .resx files. 
  2. From the command prompt change to the \GTechnology\Program\Samples\LocalizeSatelliteAssemblies folder and type the following: 
cscript MakeSatAsm.vbs /n:CmdMisc /p:C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr /c:fr /k:..\\..\GTechPublicKey.snk 
The C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr\CmdMisc.resources.dll file is created and is partially signed with the NetWorks Core public key.

#### Disabling Strong Name Verification
Because skipping verification creates security vulnerability, you should disable strong name verification only during development. The primary reason for disabling strong name verification is for testing a localized satellite assembly. The .NET Framework Strong name Utility (sn.exe) is delivered with Microsoft Visual Studio SDK under the default location %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin. 
  * To disable strong-name verification:


From the command prompt,change to the GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
"%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin\sn" -Vr *,GTechPublicKey[<GTechPublicKeyToken>](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/L15G7m16D2qef9PappxJLQ)

#### Finding the NetWorks Core Public Key Token
The NetWorks Core token for the public key is stored in the \GTechnology\Program\GTechPublicKey.snk and can be found using the .NET Framework Strong Name Utility (sn.exe) that is delivered with Microsoft Visual Studio SDK under the default location %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin. 
  * To find NetWorks Core public key token:


From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
"%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin\sn" -t GTechPublicKey.snk
The NetWorks Core public key token is displayed in the command prompt window.

#### Removing Disabling of Strong Name Verification
After you complete testing of your localized assembly, you need to remove disabling of strong name verification before you send the assembly to Hexagon to sign the assembly. The .NET Framework Strong Name Utility (sn.exe) is delivered with Microsoft Visual Studio SDK under the default location %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin. 
  * To remove disabling of strong-name verification:


From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
"%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin\sn" -Vu *,GTechPublicKey[<GTechPublicKeyToken>](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/L15G7m16D2qef9PappxJLQ)

#### Translating Resources

##### Translating Resources Examples
Any .NET assembly can contain only UI resources, only string resources, or both. The following are example workflows. (You must have [extracted](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZstgICxP~nVjterJ93~~eQ) *.en.resources files from a neutral English satellite assembly and converted *.en.resources files to *.en.resx files. 
  * To translate string-only .resx files: 


  1. If necessary, create a C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr folder for neutral French. 
  2. Using Notepad, open C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.Properties.Resources.en.resx. 
  3. Search for the node CMDMISC_M_NE_PAPERSCALE.
  4. Translate the node value "Paper scale should be numeric." If you do not know the translation, you can prefix a string with the culture name to denote that translation should be done, for example, "French - Paper scale should be numeric." 
  5. Complete translation of other <data> <value> nodes.
  6. Save the Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.Properties.Resources.en.resx file in the localized culture folder, and use the culture-specific file name. Save the file as C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.Properties.Resources.fr.resx. 
  7. Translate the remaining string-only .resx files and save as culture-specific file names in your localized culture folder. For CmdMisc, there are no more string-only .resx files. 


  * To translate UI .resx files:


  1. If necessary, create a temporary folder for your localized culture. Create C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr folder for neutral French. 
  2. Open a UI .resx file using Windows Forms Resource Editor. From the command prompt, type the following: 
"%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin\winres" C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.ExportToCAD.ExportToCADForm.en.resx
  3. Translate the Export To CAD dialog box caption. If you do not know the translation you can prefix a string with culture to denote that translation should be done, for example, "French - Export To CAD" 
  4. Complete translation for other of UI elements.
  5. In Windows Forms Resource Editor, select File > Save As. 
  6. Select French and click OK. Verify that the file C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.ExportToCAD.ExportToCADForm.fr.resx is created. 
  7. Move C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.ExportToCAD.ExportToCADForm.fr.resx
to C:\Temp\GTLocalize\fr\Intergraph.GTechnology.Private.CmdMisc.ExportToCAD.ExportToCADForm.fr.resx. 
  8. Open the other UI .resx files and repeat steps 3 to 6 for each file.

#### Using Microsoft Tools to Localize .NET Assemblies

##### Microsoft SDK Localization Tools
These tools are delivered with Microsoft Visual Studio SDK under the default location %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft SDKs\Windows\<SDK Version>\Bin: 
  * MSIL dissambler—ildasm.exe
  * Resource File Generator—resgen.exe
  * Windows Forms Resource Editor—winres.exe. 
  * .NET Framework Strong name Utility—sn.exe. 


Assembly Linker, Al.exe, is used to embed the translated resources files in the localized satellite assembly. Assembly Linker is delivered with the .NET Framework under the default location %windir%\Microsoft.NET<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\Al.exe.

#### Using Sample Scripts to Localize .NET Assemblies

##### Converting .resources Files to .resx Files
NetWorks Core setup delivers sample VB script \GTechnology\Program\Samples\LocalizeSatelliteAssemblies\MakeResx.vbs for converting .resources files to .resx files. The MakeResx.vbs takes a folder location as an argument. It converts every .resources file in the specified folder to corresponding .resx file using the Resource File Generator (resgen.exe) that is delivered with Microsoft Visual Studio SDK under the default location %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin. If necessary, you can correct the location of Resource File Generator by opening MakeResx.vbs in text editor of your choice and updating the constant RESGEN value. 
Type the following from a command prompt:
cscript MakeResx.vbs ResourcesLocation  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ResourcesLocation  |  Required argument of string data type and specifies the folder containing .resources files   |  
The following workflow is an example: 
  * To convert .resources files to .resx files


  1. If needed, [create a temporary folder and move all .resources files to it](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZstgICxP~nVjterJ93~~eQ). 
  2. From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program\Samples\LocalizeSatelliteAssemblies folder and type the following: 
cscript MakeResx.vbs C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en 
The C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en folder now contains converted *.en.resx files.

##### Extracting .resource Files from a Neutral Satellite Assembly
To extract all .resources files from a satellite assembly, type the following at a command prompt: 
ildasm SatelliteASM /out=FileName /UTF8  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  SatelliteASM  |  Required argument of string data type. Specifies the source satellite assembly name (for example, neutral English satellite assembly name CmdMisc.resources.dll).   |  
|  FileName  |  Required argument of string data type. Specifies the output file name of IL assembler code.   |  
The following workflow is an example:
  * To extract .NET resources:


  1. Create a temporary folder, for example, C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en. 
  2. Copy the source satellite assembly from GTechnology\Program\en\CmdMisc.resources.dll to C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en folder. 
  3. From the command prompt, change to the, C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en folder, and type the following: 
"%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Visual Studio 8\SDK\v2.0\Bin\ildasm" CmdMisc.resources.dll /out=CmdMisc.il /UTF8
The C:\Temp\GTLocalize\en folder now contains *.en.resources files extracted the from the neutral English satellite assembly CmdMisc.resources.dll.

### Localizing Error Messages
NetWorks Core provides English versions of database messages. A master list of messages is delivered in \GTechnology\Program\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateG3EDatabaseMessagesTable.sql and is included in setup. 
However, if messages for another locale are needed, they can be added to the [G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jVEycV6Ab3RBcAcPh_iRXg). To create this table, run the script creDatabaseMessagesTable.sql. Then you can copy all of the strings for the English messages in the table, assign them the new locale identifier, and run a series of update statements to set the appropriate message strings for that locale. 
To create the initial copy of the messages, type the following in an SQL editor:
SQL> insert into G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES( G3E_FUNCTIONALID,  
G3E_MSGNO, G3E_LCID, G3E_MESSAGE )   
select G3E_FUNCTIONALID, G3E_MSGNO, '<new locale ID>',  
G3E_MESSAGE from G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES where G3E_LCID='0009';
For each message that has been localized for the new locale ID, generate the following SQL and execute it in the database: 
SQL> update G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES set G3E_MESSAGE =  
'<localized message string>'where G3E_LCID='  
<new locale ID>' and G3E_FUNCTIONALID=<value>;   
and G3E_MSGNO=<value>;
Verify that the G3E_LCID (new locale ID), G3E_FUNCTIONALID, and G3E_MSGNO are correct for each localized message being updated.

### Localizing Metadata Explorer Display Names
Metadata Explorer contains information about NetWorks Core metadata and contains strings that are displayed to users who may speak different languages. PublishMENames.exe lets you publish the names displayed in Metadata Explorer from the language-specific database tables in Oracle to the data structures used by Metadata Explorer. Changes in the database are seen in Metadata Explorer and are displayed in the language of your locale. 
  * To localize Metadata Explorer display names:


  1. If your default language is not English, verify that the appropriate mw.msf file for the default language is available in the locale folder. (\GTechnology\Program\resdlls\<localeid>\mw.msf). If necessary, create the folder, and copy the mw.msf file from the \GTechnology\Program\resdlls\0009 folder to the folder you created. For example, create the folder \resdlls\000C, and copy the mw.msf file to it. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258500) Verify that the mw.msf file is not read-only. 
  2. If the G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME table is empty in your database, make sure your machine locale is set to the default language. From a command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
PublishMENames.exe username/password@servicename /extract
OR
In the \GTechnology\Program folder, run PublishMENames.exe. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258500)
    1. Type the user name, password, and service name for your database.
    2. Check Extract to database. 
    3. Click OK. 
A file named Script.sql is created in the folder specified by your %TEMP% environment variable. The file contains the SQL insert statements to populate the G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME table for all of the fields in the mw.msf file provided with product delivery. 
  3. If your default language is not English, update the Script.sql script to change values in [G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/d2texECkBoX_LSx6qPG2tg) to the default language for display in Metadata Explorer before you run it in the database. 
  4. Run all the insert into G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME statements in the Script.sql script in your database, and commit the changes. 
  5. If your machine locale is not the default language and if the G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME language sub-table (G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME_xxxx where xxxx denotes localeid on your machine) for the language of your locale is not present in the database, use an SQL editor to run the following statement: 
SQL> INSERT INTO G3E_METADATALANGUAGE COLUMNS (G3E_MLNO,  
G3E_LCID, G3E_USERNAME, G3E_DEFAULT, G3E_EDITDATE)  
VALUES (G3E_METADATALANGUAGE_SEQ.NEXTVAL, '<language LCID for your locale>', '<language name>', 0, SYSDATE);
SQL> exec MG3ELanguageSubTableUtils.CreateSubTables('<language LCID for your locale>') 
The values from the normal table are copied to the language sub-table (G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME_xxxx).
  6. Verify that the appropriate mw.msf file for the language of your locale is available in that locale folder. (\GTechnology\Program\resdlls/<localeid>\mw.msf). If necessary, create the folder, and copy the mw.msf file from the \GTechnology\Program\resdlls/<LCID for the default language> folder to the folder you created. For example, create the folder \resdlls\0007, and copy the mw.msf file to it. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258500) Verify that the mw.msf file is not read-only. 
  7. Change values in G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME_<language LCID for your locale>.G3E_USERNAME to the language for your locale for display in Metadata Explorer. 
  8. From a command prompt, navigate to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
PublishMENames.exe username/password@servicename
OR
Double-click PublishMENames.exe. 
  9. On the Connection dialog box: 
    1. Type the user name, password, and service name for your database.
    2. Do not check Extract to database. 
    3. Click OK.

### Localizing Metadata
The database can store only one format or language for the data. To support the language display appropriate to your locale, the data model must be configured with picklists for language translation of character data. Each locale references a different presentation column for the data, while the stored data are either language neutral or in the language of the larger set of users. 
Because fields in many metadata tables are presented on the user interface, fields holding strings must be translated into the appropriate language. Clients of different languages can use a single NetWorks Core database instance.   
|  Example A facility database in Canada may have English-speaking clients and French- speaking clients. Each of these clients can load a localized version of NetWorks Core in their own language. They need access to localized metadata as well.  To support this, a set of language sub-tables containing only metadata columns that need to be localized as well as key fields are created and populated for the default and other supported languages.   |  
| --- |  
Default values in the database schema need to be language- neutral or formatted as English. In any table that needs to be localized, populate the G3E_LOCALECOMMENT field with a definition that explains how the metadata should be translated. 
So you can have different values for different locations, metadata publishing does not change existing rows in localized metadata tables you update using Metadata Explorer. If you do not want this behavior for any of the metadata entries, truncate the localized tables. Publishing repopulates the locale-specific table as a copy of the default language. To selectively use the default language value, you update the specific rows in the locale-sensitive table.   
|  Example Style values can be localized, but many values are the same in all languages. You can truncate the localized tables (for example, G3E_STYLE_0007.G3E_VALUE) before you publish.   |  
| --- |  
If you want specific values to be the same for all languages, use standard Oracle tools to copy the value from the default table to the locale-specific table.   
|  Example Copy the value in G3E_STYLE.G3E_VALUE to the G3E_VALUE field of the locale-specific table. If the locale identifier is 0007 and the G3E_SNO number of the common style is 101, use this update statement:  Update G3E_STYLE_0007 set G3E_VALUE = ( select G3E_VALUE from G3E_STYLE where G3E_SNO = 101) where G3E_SNO = 101;  |  
| --- |  
When you populate metadata in parameter fields or for arguments to interface arguments, specify the numeric values using English separators. This does not present a problem for the user because they can enter data based on locale, and the numbers are stored in a neutral format and presented based on the locale. Many of the arguments to interfaces are stored in character fields and must be converted programmatically. You should not maintain multiple sets of metadata to accommodate arguments that are never evident to the user, but you must be aware of this requirement. Specification of a numeric value stored in a character field with the non-English locale causes a runtime error.   
|  Example The right-reading angle parameters in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER must be specified with English decimal separators.   |  
| --- |  
  * To support metadata localization:


  1. [Create the default metadata schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg). 
  2. Add a row in the [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ) table with English as the default language: 
     * Populate the G3E_LCID column with the primary language identifier defined in the Microsoft SDK for national language support. 
     * Populate the G3E_DEFAULT column with the value Yes (1).
  3. Add a row in the G3E_METADATALANGUAGE table for every language besides English that you want the system to recognize: 
     * Populate the G3E_LCID column with the language identifier defined in the Microsoft SDK for national language support. 
     * Populate the G3E_DEFAULT column with the value No (0).
  4. Use an SQL editor to create all the language sub- tables:
SQL> execute MG3ELanguageSubTableUtils.CreateAllSubTables;
  5. [Define metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/N9HSfb3W4SNvrtTIvNKiTw) for the application using English as the default language. 
  6. Use an SQL editor to populate all the language sub- tables:
SQL> execute MG3ELanguageSubTableUtils.SynchronizeSubTables;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258496) All the language sub-tables are populated with values in the default language. 
  7. Update the language sub-tables for non-default languages with locale-appropriate values. Use standard SQL update statements to make these modifications. 
  8. [Publish metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ). 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258496) The Metadata Versions command creates a complete list of languages and publishes all the languages simultaneously. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258496) Publishing metadata creates N sets of metadata DDC files, one set for each language. It creates one set of optimized tables that is filtered by a language property through view definitions.

### Specifying a Language
Every metadata configuration has at least one language specification, which is indicated by an entry in [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ). The default entry is English. If English is not your primary language, you can change the entry to match your locale. You do not always need to define metadata in English and then in a second language. However, you must have a language entry for every locale used by the NetWorks Core clients. The locale is tied to the configuration parameters of your operating system. It is very important that you correctly identify one language as the default. NetWorks Core assumes that the default language is the one used in the normalized metadata tables. All values are always copied from the normalized tables to the default language's sub-tables. 
Normally, you work in a single language until the majority of the metadata is configured. This is not a requirement, but it simplifies the process and reduces work for the localization team if the metadata is stable before they begin the localization process. 
Remember to specify the LCID value in this table, matching the case specified by the operating system. This is usually uppercase.

### Posting Metadata

#### Logging Into the Import and Export Databases During Posting
As part of the posting of data to another database or generating an import script, you must log in to the import and export databases. The fields that are enabled depend on how you defined posting. 
  * To log into the database:


  1. On the Metadata Versions dialog box, define the post criteria and click Execute. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256994)
  2. Type the username and password for the export database, the import database, and the generate script for the location to import, if necessary. 
  3. Click OK.

#### Posting Metadata from the Command Prompt
  * To import or export metadata from the command prompt:


  1. Before you perform this task the first time, load Oracle's import / export tools (imp.exe and exp.exe) on the administrative client computer. 
  2. Make sure a current, valid backup (Oracle export) is available before dropping the tables. 
  3. Drop the existing metadata tables in the production schema, as follows:
    1. Using an SQL editor, log in as the schema owner.
    2. To drop the metadata tables, execute the following procedures:
SQL> execute mg3eDropMetadata.DropAllOptimizedTables;
SQL> execute mg3eDropMetadata.DropAllLegendTables;
SQL> execute mg3eDropMetadata.DropAllMetadataTables;
  4. To export the metadata from the development schema, execute the Export command, exp.exe, from the command prompt.   
|  Example exp.exe gtechemc/gtechemc@dev7 FILE=//usrlogin/c_temp/gtechdev/gtechdev721.dmp ROWS=Y CONSISTENT=Y LOG=//usrlogin/c_temp/gtechdev/gtechdev721.log TABLES=G3E_LEGDEF5_OPTABLE G3E_LEGDSPCTRL5_OPTABLE   |  
| --- |  
  5. To import the metadata to the production schema, execute the import command, imp.exe, from the command prompt.   
|  Example imp.exe gtechemc7/gtechemc7@dev7 FILE=gtechdev721.dmp fromuser=gtechdev7 TOUSER=gtechemc7 LOG=//usrlogin/c_temp/gtechdev/ImpToGTECHEMC721.log   |  
| --- |

### Refreshing Metadata Edits
When you edit metadata using Admin commands (such as Metadata Explorer) or an SQL editor, you can see the changes you make and test them by refreshing the metadata instead of republishing. Republishing metadata creates a completely new set of [DDC and RAW files](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ) in the metadata folder from the optimized tables in the database. However, refreshing applies edits to the subset of the metadata optimized tables depending on the areas you check on the Refresh Metadata dialog box. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256047) Some of the parameters in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER tables require a full publish after you change a setting, not just a refresh in Metadata Explorer. See the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) topic to find out which parameters require a full publish. 
Typcially, you must have administrative privileges to use Refresh Metadata Edits. However, you can allow a non-administrative user to refresh metadata edits. Use an SQL editor to grant select privileges to that user as follows: 
SQL> grant select on G3E_METADATAVERSION to <user name>;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256047) Because refreshing metadata edits can take some time, check only the areas for which you want to refresh the metadata. If you need to add new metadata or edit or delete existing metadata for several metadata tables, refresh metadata after you have finished all the updates. 
The optimized tables are updated in the database during a refresh, but their values are queried only by NetWorks Core; thus, their contents are not written to disk. If you refresh metadata edits, only you can see these changes. 
Republish instead of refreshing metadata if you:
  * See a significant performance delay in desktop functions from refreshing all metadata dynamically 
  * Have tested and are satisfied with your changes
  * Make a metadata change that is not part of the defined groups on the Refresh Metadata dialog box 
  * Want all users to see your changes
  * Want to update the metadata in a production schema


The metadata tables associated with refreshing metadata edits are G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY and G3E_OPTABLESET. You should not change these tables. Use Metadata Explorer or the Metadata Versions command to refresh your metadata. 
  * To refresh metadata edits:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256047) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
OR
From the Administrative menu, select Metadata Versions, and click Refresh on the Metadata Versions dialog box. 
  2. Select the functional group for which you want to refresh metadata.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/0E~tWbR2W0A989GXpQJTaw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=0e53aae87e72b802&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256047) If all the items under a node are selected, the parent node is selected. If only part of the items under a node are selected, the parent node appears gray. 
  3. Click OK. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256047) The refresh processing determines the optimized tables associated with the selections you made from the [G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JRfBDMzh4plgRdWK7cYPjg) and [G3E_OPTABLESET](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qRTCgelWutUCWwW5QNpSAA) metadata tables. The software runs the optimization packages required for the selections. The metadata recordsets are reset to look at the database optimized tables rather than the published metadata mapfiles. The refreshed tables are broadcast to NetWorks Core components that need notification of the changes. 
  4. You can continue with your testing. If you make more metadata changes, repeat steps 2-4.

### Related Groups of Tables
Once these related groups of tables are populated, you can revise them in any order, as long as you do not violate any foreign key constraints among the tables. Many of these groups have an interface table (G3E_<GROUPNAME>IFACE) that primarily holds parameters for this subsystem and references all the related tables. 
Some of the tables contain raw data fields. These must be populated with Admin commands. All other fields may be populated with any Oracle-compatible database tool. 
The following logical sets of metadata tables should be populated together:
Add-Ons
Defines an Add-On in NetWorks Core metadata. This table replaces the use of the G3E_ANALYSIS for defining non-NetWorks Core functionality and metadata. 
[G3E_ADDON](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VBl9fkdnZlDTNU50bY_XFA)
Telecommunications and Fiber

### Required Metadata Tables
Certain sets of [metadata tables are optional](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw) or tied to specific functionality, such as electrical analysis, but certain metadata tables must exist in every schema. Metadata publishing fails if any one of these tables does not exist. Some of them may be empty, but they must exist. 
The metadata tables are closely interrelated. The integrity constraints on the tables require that you populate the tables in an order that does not violate these constraints.   
|  Example You cannot create a definition in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT until you create entries in G3E_FEATURE and G3E_COMPONENT, because the feature and component numbers are required inputs.   |  
| --- |  
The required tables listed below are classified into logical groups. Most are populated by the system or by various scripts delivered with the system. 
Metadata Administration Tables
These tables are used by the Metadata subsystem for tracking metadata tables. The metadata software or the basic population of the tables is the only requirement for maintaining these tables. 
[G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256007) Much of NetWorks Core is controlled by metadata. This is typically accomplished with a metadata table specifically designed for a command or set of commands. Occasionally, however, a simple value is all that is required to provide the configuration control of the system. The G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table defines these single-value controls within NetWorks Core. The values that should exist in your table are described in the [G3E_NAME field](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) of the General Parameter table. You must adjust the actual values to match your data model characteristics.

### Rolling Back Pending Edits
After you have edited metadata using Metadata Explorer, you can roll back the pending edits 
  * To roll back pending edits:


  1. In Metadata Explorer, add a new row, delete a row, or edit attributes. The pending edits and all parent nodes are highlighted. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261197)
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261197) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to roll back all changes. 


Related Topics
[Committing Pending Edits to the Database](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q~kYnyD_idgThLejq0JT4g)
[Refreshing Metadata Edits](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BjKfaBm1ZdzY9Gs0KVlKVQ)

### Setting the Active User
You can use Metadata Explorer to change the roles assigned to the metadata definitions and then to filter that metadata by logging in as a user with those roles. You can do the following: 
  * Edit role assignments for the metadata entries.
  * Set the active user as a user with those roles.
  * Refresh metadata.


You can test the results without having to exit and reconnect as that user.
Typcially, you must have administrative privileges to use Active User. However, you can allow a non-administrative user to set the active user. Use an SQL editor to grant select privileges to that user as follows: 
SQL> grant select on G3E_METADATAVERSION to <user name>;
  * To set the active user:


  1. Edit metadata to set the role required for each specific piece of metadata.
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261199) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261199)
  3. From the drop-down list on the Active User dialog box, select the user who has the roles you specified in Step 1. 
  4. Click OK. 
  5. To refresh metadata edits, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261199) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261199) Check the boxes on the [Refresh Metadata dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BjKfaBm1ZdzY9Gs0KVlKVQ) depending on the level in which you expect to see changes. If you have changed any roles that affect the list of commands available to the user, check Custom Software. 
  6. Test to see if the correct functionality is active for the user you selected in Step 3. This setting is valid only for the current NetWorks Core session. 


Related Topic
[Role Association Table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg)

### Tools for Working with Metadata

#### Metadata Explorer

##### Adding and Editing an SQL Statement
You can click the Ellipsis in the appropriate metadata table field to add or edit an SQL statement. Metadata Explorer provides [shortcut keys](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5fhal~bbTMhid1UeA7Uzlw) to help you write the statements. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256227)

##### Adding and Editing Predefined Parameters
Parameter lookups are predefined lists of acceptable values and user-friendly names that are like code-listed values. They are displayed as a drop-down list in the Metadata Explorer content panel. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261846)

##### Changing the Metadata Explorer Attribute Display
You can control Metadata Explorer attribute presentation through the Display Options dialog box. 
  * To change the attribute display:


  1. Right-click the Metadata Explorer navigation panel or content panel, and select Display Options. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261844)
  2. Check the options you need:  
|  Option  |  Use to   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Display reference key value  |  Display the value of the applicable reference column  |  
|  Display user- friendly name  |  Display the username value for the field  |  
|  Display database column name  |  Display the actual field name from the metadata table  |  
|  Display value as referenced  |  Display a more readable representation of the field value  |  
|  Display key value  |  Display an actual field value from the metadata table.  |  
  3. Click OK.

##### Creating a Metadata Explorer Script File
You can create a named script file that keeps a record of changes made to metadata from within Metadata Explorer. The database actions that take place when modifying metadata are output to scripts. For example, when you click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) to commit a change to the database or ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) to roll back changes, those statements are added to the script. You can use these SQL statements to apply the same data manipulations within other databases. 
You can start or stop script generation, override information in an existing script, or append information to an existing script. The script contains time stamp information at the start of the file and at any point where the script is appended and you can add a comment to the time stamp information. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) If you want to record every change you make to the database in Metadata Explorer and you inadvertently turn script recording off, you can manually update the script file before you apply it to another database. However, remember that any manual changes you made to the script file have not been applied to your original database. 
BLOB or RAW Data
If you record actions in Metadata Explorer that produce BLOB or RAW data, the actual SQL scripts are not recorded. A comment is added to the script file to indicate that an export has occurred and the row of data are copied to a temporary table. The contents of the temporary table are exported to a file that is named in a format of <Table Name>_<Key Value>.dmp. 
The .dmp file is located in the folder you specified for the script file. A .log file with the same name as the .dmp file is generated in the same folder and provides a record of errors. You can use Oracle IMP utility from the command prompt to import the .dmp file into a temporary table in the destination database: 
For example, if you [customize the menu or toolbar layout](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zSZsIpXCcgAPF~FlMbQ8JQ) and the entire G3E_MENULAYOUT table, not just the individual row, is exported to the files G3E_MENULAYOUT.dmp, G3E_MENULAYOUT.bat, and G3E_MENULAYOUT.dat in the folder you specified for the script file. G3E_MENULAYOUT.log file records any errors. You can use the Oracle IMP utility.   
|  Example imp.exe gtechdev/gtechdev@dev FILE=G3E_MENULAYOUT.DMP fromuser=gtechdev TOUSER=gtechnewdev LOG=//usrlogin/c_temp/gtechnewdev/ImpToG3E_MENULAYOUT.log  |  
| --- |  
  * To create a Metadata Explorer script file:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
  2. In the Record Script dialog box, type a path and a name for the script; or click Browse on the Save As dialog box, navigate to the appropriate location, type a name for the script in the File name field and click Save. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate the script in the Comment field. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842)
  4. Click OK. 
  5. To stop recording the SQL, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 

  
|  Code Example -- 12/8/2006 9:50:52 AM  -- Trying another script on Friday morning  --  set autocommit off  -- 12/8/2006 9:51:32 AM  -- Trying another script on Friday morning  --  set autocommit off  insert into g3e_feature values( 504, 'FourthFeature', 'Fourth Feature', 31602,30602, 1, NULL,  TO_DATE('12/8/2006 9:51:38 AM','MM/DD/YYYY HH:MI:SS AM'),  NULL, NULL, 1, NULL, NULL,1, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL, 'ELECTRIC', 'EVERYONE', 'EVERYONE', NULL, NULL)  -- 12/8/2006 9:56:48 AM  -- Trying another script on Friday morning  --  set autocommit off  -- 12/8/2006 9:57:05 AM  -- A second try  --  set autocommit off  insert into g3e_feature values( 506, 'SixthFeature', 'Sixth Feature', 25802,25801, 1, NULL, TO_DATE('12/8/2006 9:57:10 AM', 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MI:SS AM'),NULL, NULL, 0, NULL, NULL, 1, NULL, NULL, 0, NULL, 'ELECEDITOR','EVERYONE', 'EVERYONE', NULL, NULL)  |  
| --- |  
  * To append to an existing Metadata Explorer script file:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
  2. Select the script from the Script name drop-down list. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate this portion of the script in the Comment field. 
  4. Click OK, then click Yes on the message box that appears. 


  * To overwrite an existing Metadata Explorer script file:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261842) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
  2. Select the script from the Script name drop-down list. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate this script in the Comment field. 
  4. Click OK. 
  5. Click No. 
  6. Click OK on the message boxes that appear.

##### Defining Interface Arguments
Interface arguments are used by various parts of the Metadata subsystem, particularly by those that perform specialized functions like relationship attribute interfaces, functional interfaces, and placement techniques. Some interface arguments are defined as entries in the argument definition metadata tables and some as blobs in the database, that is, the argument data are stored in binary format. The software decodes this data and displays it in a readable format. When you click the description field for G3E_<interfacetable>.G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT in the Metadata Explorer content panel, you can add or [edit interface arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ). 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259130)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259130) Because they can vary, you [specify values for the arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U7hZwUeA5e5Te3SY3WX6Kg) when you define components. 
  * To define interface arguments:


  1. Click the first cell of the empty row marked with an asterisk (*) at the bottom of the grid. 
  2. Type the prompt associated with the argument.
  3. Type the [data type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Fq1pfuicpDm0jwjnFaF0tA) associated with the argument. 
  4. Click OK.

##### Displaying Foreign Key Values
Reference lookups substitute the display of a foreign key value from the current metadata record with a value from another metadata table so you can more easily read the content of the metadata record. These fields appear as hyperlinks on the field name section of the grid in the Metadata Explorer content panel. You can to jump to a reference and jump back to your previous location. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Dw3xpdiET25laqW6~XoOCA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=d14bbbc82dde4788&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
The Query or G3E_AQNO field value is displayed as Building. The G3E_AQNO field is a foreign key into the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table. Using this foreign key value, Metadata Explorer displays the G3E_USERNAME value from the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table as the value for the G3E_AQNO field value. 
  * To jump to a reference lookup:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer content panel, double-click a reference lookup link.
The navigation panel display goes to the definition of the foreign key value, and the Help panel updates its display. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/NoiEzstHv3c4Oa8QwPEOJQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=7610538c9552b8f3&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
The content and navigation panels go to the building query's definition in the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY table, and the Help panel displays the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY Help topic. 
  2. To go back to the previous display, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261208) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar.

##### Displaying Metadata Reference Tables
Metadata fields can refer to tables that are not an explicit part of the metadata. Fields that refer to these types of tables are also displayed as hyperlinks on the field name section of the grid in the Metadata Explorer contents panel. When you double-click the field name, Metadata Explorer displays a grid containing the contents of the referenced table. For example, you can use reference tables to display the contents of picklist tables and reference tables required by the Electric Design Tools. Use an SQL editor to create or edit reference tables. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261193)

##### Editing Interface Arguments
If an interface definition requires an argument, click the Ellipsis in the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT field to display the Interface Argument Editor dialog box. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256888)
The grid on this dialog box displays the prompts required for the argument values. #### Metadata Query
The Metadata Query command lets you query the database much like SQL Plus. The control provides a user interface, buttons, and hot keys to make database manipulation, review, and comparisons easy. 
Metadata Query also lets you use SQL queries to edit the database. If you execute a query that edits the database, you must type commit, and you must click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256788) to commit the change to the database. 
When you type or build a query and click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256788), the control displays the results in a grid. You can add a grid for each query to compare results, use the results to execute a command, and view a list of the queries you have made. You can also copy records from each grid to the clipboard. 
Metadata Query provides [shortcut keys](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5fhal~bbTMhid1UeA7Uzlw) so you can select SQL key words, the names of metadata tables, and the table names from [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) and [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw). The shortcut keys are active when focus is on the upper text box. Press the spacebar before using the hot keys after the first entry in the statement. 
Initially, the Metadata Query dialog box has two tabs. The Status tab displays the SQL executed, the number of records selected or affected by the SQL, and the execution time of the statement. The Grid tabs display the results of queries. After you select a specific grid, you can click the column headings to sort the query output.

## More Information

### Attribute Validation and Manipulation Metadata EX1
  * The model requires that connected primary conductors share the same voltage and requires a voltage check at validation time. 
Populate a row in the table with the primary conductor feature number in both the G3E_ACTIVEFNO and G3E_RELATEDFNO fields. Then place the attribute number for voltage in both the G3E_ACTIVEANO and G3E_RELATEDANO fields. 
  * The model requires that pipes of different diameter not be shown as relationship candidates.
Place the feature number of the pipe in the G3E_ACTIVEFNO and G3E_RELATEDFNO fields and the attribute number for diameter in the respective ANO fields.

### Attribute Validation and Manipulation Metadata EX2
To place a transformer with multiple attribute validation rows, place two rows in G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION, as follows: 
  1. Verify the voltage rating attribute of a light fixture that connects to the transformer.
  2. Ensure that the class attribute of the pole on which the transformer hangs is appropriate.
  3. On each row, specify ownership or node-edge connectivity in the G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE field so that the software does not perform an unnecessary validation.

### Mixed feature type select set WF
  1. The user creates a select set with more than one feature. If the user has Delete permission for some of the features but not all of them, only those features with the Delete permission can be deleted. 
  2. The user creates a select set with more than one feature. If the user has Edit permission for some of the features but not all of them, no geometry edit buttons or menu items (except for Delete, assuming Delete permission exists for some of the features) are enabled as long as the feature or features that do not have Edit permission are in the select set.

### Pair Count Merge Features Interface Metadata 1 CODE
SQL> select G3E_RINO from G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE where 
G3E_INTERFACE = 'GTCommSup.CountMerge'

### Pair Count Merge Features Interface Metadata 2 CODE
SQL> select * from G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT where
G3E_CNO in
-- Get G3E_CNO of the count bearing component
(select G3E_PARAMETER1 from G3E_COMMIFACE where G3E_TYPE = 'Pair Count')
and
G3E_FNO in
-- Get G3E_FNO's of features with linear primary geographic component 
(select G3E_FNO from G3E_FEATURE where G3E_PRIMARYGEOGRAPHICCNO in
-- Get G3E_CNO's of linear components 
(select G3E_CNO from G3E_COMPONENT where G3E_TYPE in (4,128)))

### User has Delete but not Edit role WF
  1. User selects a feature for which they have been granted Delete permission, but not Edit permission 
  2. The user starts the Edit Tool command.
All of the buttons on the control and the pop-up menu entries are disabled except for the Delete button/entry.

### User has Edit but not Delete role
  1. User selects a feature for which they have been granted Edit permission, but not Delete permission. 
  2. The user starts the Edit Tool command. 
Delete is disabled on the control and pop-up menu. 
  3. If the user presses the DELETE key, a message displays stating that permissions have not been granted for the specific feature.

### User has neither Edit nor Delete role WF
  1. User selects a feature for which they have been granted neither Edit nor Delete permissions.
  2. The user starts the Edit Tool command. 
An error appears stating neither edit nor delete permissions have been granted for that specific feature. 
  3. All of the Edit Tool buttons are disabled as are the options on the right-click pop-up menu.
