## Multiple NetWorks Core Connections
The NetWorks Core data model and some dialog boxes in the user interface, such as the New Job dialog box and the Area Manager dialog box, indicate that you can connect to more than one database at the same time. However, except for viewing [secondary data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v3113UNgbPH6WFKi8CQOpQ), it is not recommended that you allow connections from multiple databases. 
The following are some areas in which issues could arise if you manipulate data from more than one database: 
  * Metadata and select set processing: Processing features from different databases could produce conflicts in the feature numbers.   
|  Example In the first connection, a pole could be feature identifier number 3143176, while that identifier could represent a totally different feature in the second connection. If a command is not written to process multiple connections, errors might occur when the identifier is found in more than one connection. Incorrect information might be presented to the user.   |  
| --- |  
  * [API](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gTrSNQf1ydnItT2IJBwWUQ): .NET commands are retrieved from the first connection only. 
  * [Role behavior](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/riuQCyd4KdgQgV1LvibEew): Operational behavior is based on permissions established in the first connection. Users might have permission to use a specific command in one connection but not in the second connection. Or worse, they could do things they should not in the second connection because they have permissions from the first connection. 
  * Jobs: The columns in the jobs tables must be identical in the databases if you want to view jobs from multiple connections.

## NetWorks Core Interfaces

### Analysis Interfaces

#### Parameter Specification Issues in Analysis Interfaces
If the analysis interface metadata states that a feature type being traced results in the creation of an analysis object, the application metadata needs to specify how the value for each [analysis parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FXNPndwIEcZCuXXeY8Cf~w) of that object is determined. 
There are several different methods for specifying how the parameter value should be determined for each traced feature. 
Constant Values
The parameter value can simply be defined to always be a constant value for each analysis object created from each traced feature of a certain type. This value should be of the correct data type for the analysis parameter for which it is defined. For example, if the analysis package was expecting a real number value for this parameter, setting the constant value to a string would cause problems. The following table shows example constant strings:   
|  1.0  |  A real number constant  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  some string  |  A string constant  |  
|  300  |  An integer constant  |  
Attribute Values
The parameter value can also be defined as a database expression that references an attribute for the feature from which the analysis object is being created. The expression should contain long integer values corresponding to one or more attributes defined by the G3E_ANO column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE metadata table for the traced feature. Multiple attributes can be defined in the expression only if they exist in the same component table. 
The attribute numbers in this expression must be delineated by enclosing them in square brackets. The following table shows example G3E_VALUE strings:   
|  [2473]  |  Just use the attribute value  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  NVL(SUBSTR([13], 1,  
(INSTR([13],'-') -1)), '0')   |  SQL expression using an attribute value  |  
SQL Lookup Values
The parameter value can be defined to be a column selected from an SQL SELECT statement defined in the G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL table. Multiple parameters can be determined from the same SQL statement. The SQL statement should use column aliases to specify the column or expression to map to each particular parameter that it defines. 
The following kinds of SQL statements can be used:
  * Generic SQL statement—This type of statement is independent of the features that create the analysis objects for which it is supplying parameter values. In other words, any valid SQL that results in one or more selected columns having aliases referencing the required parameters can be used. The only exception to this would be those SQL statements that reference feature attributes, which are described in the SQL containing an attribute definition discussion. 
These types of SQL statements are interpreted as defining multiple constant parameter values for the analysis object. Typically, they would select these constant values from some sort of lookup table. The following example shows an SQL string referenced from the G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL table: Example select 3 TYPE, ''FUS150'' NAME, 4 CURVE_ID, 1 OPER_CAT, 140 VOLT_RTG, 4 WIDGIT from FUSE_CATALOG_TABLE; 
  * SQL containing an attribute definition—This type of statement is dependent upon the features that create the analysis objects for which it is supplying parameter values. They are interpreted as defining multiple dynamic parameter values for the analysis object and are expected to select these values from a lookup table. However, the main difference is that the criterion for these SQL statements is not known beforehand. It is based upon the attributes of each feature that is being extracted and which must be evaluated for each traced feature. 
This type of SQL parameter definition is like the feature attribute and related feature attribute types. They should contain long integer values corresponding to attributes defined by the G3E_ANO column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE metadata table for the traced feature. Multiple attributes can be defined only if they exist in the same component table. The attribute numbers in this expression must be delineated by enclosing them in square brackets. 
The following list shows limitations to the types of SQL statements that may be defined containing attributes: 
    * Write the SQL WHERE clause to select the values from the lookup table, making reference to the attribute or attributes from the feature's nongraphic component. 
    * The lookup table name must be aliased in the FROM clause using the letter L as the alias. All of the columns from the lookup table in the SELECT and WHERE clauses must be qualified using this table alias. The attribute column determined from the specified attribute number or numbers are properly aliased for you. 
    * Column aliases must be used to map the expressions in the SELECT statement to the corresponding analysis parameter name. It is expected that the WHERE clause in the defined SQL statement correctly joins the lookup table to the attribute table, which is known from the specified attribute number value or values. 
    * It is expected that, when evaluating this SQL statement for each traced feature, only a single row from the lookup table is returned. 
    * This SQL statement should not include nested SELECT statements or subqueries of any form. 
    * Do not use set operators (for example, UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, MINUS) in the SQL statement. 
    * Do not define GROUP BY or ORDER BY clauses in this SQL statement. This implies that a HAVING clause is invalid as well. 
    * Hierarchical queries should not be defined for this SQL statement.
    * Avoid using the FOR UPDATE clause.
    * Do not include a semicolon or forward slash at the end of the SQL statement.


In other words, define simple queries of the following form:`
select <list of scalar expressions>
from <lookup table> L
where <conditions, including a join between the attribute table and the lookup table>; 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261344) The SQL statement for this definition is not the one that is actually executed against the database. The extraction logic modify the statement to perform the correct table joins between the lookup table and the table containing the referenced attribute or attributes. This type of parameter definition was developed expecting the SQL to be a basic lookup into a single table. 
The following example shows an attribute SQL string referenced from the G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL table:   
|  Example select L.R-PLUS R1 L.X-PLUS X1, L.B-PLUS B1, L.R-ZERO R0, L.X-ZERO X0, L.B-ZERO B0 from CONDUCTOR_CATALOG L where L.COND_TYPE = [24354]  |  
| --- |  
Child Feature Attribute Values
The parameter value can be defined as a database expression that references an attribute for a child of the feature from which the analysis object is being created. The expression should contain long integer values corresponding to one or more attributes defined by the G3E_ANO column in the G3E_ATTRIBUTE metadata table for a feature that is a child of the traced feature. If this type is specified, the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO and G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO columns defined in the G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ table for the specific feature that create this analysis object are used to find the children of the traced feature. 
The parameter value should be set in the same manner as for a Feature Attribute value parameter definition. The only difference is that the attribute numbers are expected to be for the child feature, not the traced feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261344) These types of parameter definitions are not valid for analysis objects that model nodes. Node analysis objects are BUS for CADPAD and NODE for SynerGEE and the PSS/Engines. 
Calculation Interface Values
The parameter value can be defined to be determined as the result of calling a calculation interface. Specify the name of the calculation interface to call for determining this parameter value. If this type is specified, the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT column also should be set, and its contents are sent to the calculation interface as its argument array. 
Calculation interface parameters should be used sparingly, if at all, because they cause the attributes to be determined for each traced feature one at a time. This results in the extraction taking longer than if the parameters were specified as being determined using one of the previous methods. 
The data model should be designed so that all of the parameters for all of the analysis objects can be determined using the methods discussed in this topic. 
Related Topics
[Trace Issues in Analysis Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IIUoRcWIdLmrpoJVLHLcfQ)
[Setting Up an Analysis Checklist](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~KqCuHFzk_c7nmg69~hkmQ)

#### Setting Up an Analysis Checklist
These are the steps involved in setting up the analysis interfaces for NetWorks Core.
  * To set up an analysis checklist:


  1. Determine which analysis products are used in your application. Identify them in the [G3E_ANALYSISPACKAGES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg) table. 
  2. For each of the analysis products you are using:
     * Understand the model used by that product to represent the network being analyzed. That is, what devices and other equipment (analysis objects) are modeled in that product and how they are related and connected to each other. Specify these objects in metadata ([G3E_ANALYSISOBJECTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xwapz0TYuwBMG7xyE03lgA)). 
     * Determine which of your NetWorks Core features map to these analysis objects. Specify this in metadata ([G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Z2b_eU9ra1SI__6xCIsZfw)). 
     * Understand what information is needed for each analysis object in that analysis package for it to be usable for analysis. This can be understood by reading the documentation provided by each analysis program. 
     * Understand the NetWorks Core analysis parameters that must be specified for the analysis object. These parameters are a subset of the information required by the analysis package because the NetWorks Core extraction is able to determine some of the information itself. 
     * Understand the different approaches that can be used to get the value of an [analysis parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FXNPndwIEcZCuXXeY8Cf~w). 
     * Map the information in your data model to the analysis parameters for each analysis object created from each feature that may be analyzed. In metadata, specify how the parameter values are determined ([G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~Ph4Bg4UcJzi2171RVz7w), [G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Xh_FAYkk15iQd_aGJ~lRQ)). 
     * For the analysis package, specify the configuration values for the analysis ([G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/95Dik0JxQHCezVJl5D2V8w)). 
     * In metadata, define the traces to be used for the analysis (G3E_TRACE* tables). In metadata, specify that these traces are valid to be used for the analysis ([G3E_ANALYSISTRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~m5ngUac5MKL1JPLbUlZ1Q)).

#### Trace Issues in Analysis Interfaces
The analysis extraction uses a trace to define the features to be considered for extraction. In most cases for electrical analysis, the trace should be configured to start at a feature, like a substation transformer, that is considered a source in the analysis. Also, the trace should be configured so that the features are traced in the same direction that the power is flowing for the circuit. This allows the electric analysis extraction to infer the upstream and downstream sides of each feature. If the electrical connectivity has loops, configure the trace so that at the endpoint of the loop, where the phases converge back together, the trace only continues in the downstream direction and does not backtrack up the features in the upstream direction. Typically, specifying the trace filter criteria to only trace features whose phase is a subset of the feature previously traced does this. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261340) Traces for the SynerGEE Electric and CADPAD extractions must start at the source feature and trace downstream from there. 
A trace for the PSS/Engines extraction is not required to start at the source feature, although it likely makes the definition of some of the analysis parameters easier if it does. There are some analysis objects whose node parameter values can be specified as being the upstream or downstream node, and those options make sense only if the trace starts at the source.

### Attribute Edit Control Interfaces

#### Delivered Attribute Edit Control Definition Interface
The ReadWriteRoleControl is a delivered Attribute Edit Control Definition interface delivered with NetWorks Core. This interface is used to change an attribute's presentation from read / write to read-only. It is implemented using the PFIface.ReadWriteRoleControl for the role specified as input to the Attribute Edit Control object. If the user does not have the role defined in the argument group number associated with the attribute, edits are not allowed. 
To see the interface definition in Metadata Explorer, select the Read / Write Control Definition node under Software Interfaces > Attribute Edit Control. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082)
  * To configure the ReadWriteRoleControl Interface:


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082) To perform these steps, you must be connected to a database for which you have administrative privileges. 
  1. Associate the interface with an attribute:
    1. In the tree view, navigate to the attribute with which you want to associate your interface, and select it: 
Core Schema Control > Components and Attributes > <xxx component> > Attributes > <xxx attribute>. 
    2. In the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table, scroll to the Attribute relation interface (G3E_RINO) field, and select Read Write Control Definition from the drop-down list. 
    3. Press ENTER.
    4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082) to commit the change. 
  2. To change the default role name assigned to the attribute group:
    1. Under the node of the attribute you just associated with the interface, select the Attribute Edit Control Interface Arguments node. 
    2. In the G3E_VALUE field of the G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS table, type the role name. This role name grants read / write access to the attribute. If a user is not assigned the specified role, they cannot edit the attribute. 
    3. Press ENTER.
    4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082) to commit the change. 
  3. Refresh the metadata edits:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082). 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Relationships under Custom Software and Attribute Presentation. 
    3. Click OK. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257082) to refresh the display in Metadata Explorer. 
  5. Test the new interface by placing or editing a feature with the component that has the attribute you just associated with the interface. On the appropriate attributes tab in Feature Explorer, the Attribute Value field should be read / write if the user does not have the assigned role.

#### Delivered Attribute Edit Control GUI Interfaces
The following delivered Attribute Edit Control GUI interfaces are delivered with NetWorks Core: 
EditAttributeIfNotNull
Implemented using the PFIface.CanEditIfNonNull object; the type is "Attribute Edit Control GUI." It prevents users from modifying values in GUI but allows software modifications. 
The interface requires no arguments and is typically associated with the Segment Start Location attribute. This interface does not allow modification of the start location until the cable management software has determined a default position. This interface can be used in other situations where you do not want the user to specify a value until a functional interface or other software has initially populated it. 
EditSectionLength
Implemented using PFIface.CanEditSectionLength object; the type is "Attribute Edit Control GUI." It prevents users from modifying values in GUI but allows software modifications. 
The interface requires no arguments and is typically associated with the Segment Length attribute. The interface does not allow modification of the length attribute after the component length label is placed. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260413) You can create a custom Attibute Edit Control GUI interface through [automation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/71XrUBGIDjNCi2d7~Fi29A)

#### Delivered Attribute Edit Control Interface
The following delivered Attribute Edit Control interface is delivered with NetWorks Core: 
SetOnceAttributes
This interface is implemented using the PFIface.UserOverride object; the type is "Attribute Edit Control." It prevents user and programs from modifying an attribute after it has been set. This interface requires no arguments. 
Because software access is prohibited, you should not configure this control on attributes that can be copied by the Copy Feature Attributes command or which are accessible by the Common Attribute Edit command or the Edit Related Features command. 
This interface does not support an override by privileged users. Normally, once the value is set, the user cannot change its value. However, if the user is granted the role defined in the [Role Association table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) for the G3E_SetOnceOverride object control type (G3E_OBJECTCONTROL), that user can modify the attribute even if it has been set. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256944) You can create a custom Attribute Edit Control interface through [automation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/71XrUBGIDjNCi2d7~Fi29A)

### Calculation Interfaces (Deprecated)

#### Defining a Calculation Interface (Deprecated)
After adding a Calculation interface definition to the metadata, you associate it with the appropriate table. 
  * To define a Calculation interface in metadata:


  1. Insert a new row into the [G3E_CALCULATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0eR4dzDTEb6mas3HPyo_sw) metadata table: 
    1. G3E_CINO should be unique for the newly inserted row.
    2. In the G3E_USERNAME column, add a descriptive name for the interface—for example, GetValue. 
    3. In the G3E_INTERFACE column, add the ProgID of this automation class—for example, CITemplate.ExampleCalculation. 
    4. If the Calculation interface takes arguments, define them in G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT and G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE. 
  2. Add the reference to the interface by editing the interface column of the row containing the attribute that needs to be associated with the Calculation interface. 
[G3E_SAPFLATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UfQJ9_gTvc_abyIR8JIeRg)
[G3E_SAPFLDESCRIPTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LILn3CMmVpvZ9trlzZVpYA)
[G3E_SAPEQUIPATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YKG5QyH64KihCjfLSa5Onw)
[G3E_SAPEQUIPDESCRIPTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/14KfO1CrkQIJy8d1PG4pVQ)
[G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~Ph4Bg4UcJzi2171RVz7w)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260709) Different tables have different fields to contain the cross-reference to the interface link. These steps use the G3E_SAPFLATTRIBUTE metadata table as an example. 
    1. In the G3E_TYPE column, enter -3 to indicate a calculation interface.
    2. In the G3E_CINO column, enter the Calculation interface as defined in G3E_CALCULATIONINTERFACE.
    3. In the G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT column, enter the argument values.
  3. [Publish the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ).

CalculateConductorPhaseCode
The CalculateConductorPhaseCode interface is used to calculate conductor phase values by examining field attribute values from the Primary Conductor feature component recordset.   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Example  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  WireComponentName  |  String  |  "PRIMARY_WIRE_RECORD"  |  The name of the repeating wire component.  |  
|  WireFieldName  |  String  |  "CD_PHASE"  |  The value of G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELD where the G3E_CNO matches that of the component in the previous argument.   |  
|  WireFieldValue  |  String  |  "Neu"  |  This string is compared to the attribute value of WireFieldName to determine if the neutral indicator is on the conductor.   |  
|  PhaseComponentName  |  String  |  "CONNECTIVITY_RECORD"  |   |  
|  PhaseFieldName  |  String  |  "CD_PHASE"  |  The value of G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELD where the G3E_CNO matches that of the component in the previous argument.   |  
Prompts: None 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260707) For the implementation of the CalculationInterface_GetValue 
  * Look at the repeating wire component. If you find any component where WireComponentName.WireFieldName.Value = WireFieldValue, then a neutral indicator is on the conductor. 
  * The conductor phase value is a 4 digit number wxyz where 
w = conductor position of phase A
x = conductor position of phase B
y = conductor position of phase C
z = neutral position
  * The first column of the [phase perm table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Od_LCqd6UW~hdRTKYAjIhw) contains the PhaseComponentName.PhaseFieldName.Value. 
The following calculation is returned:
wxyz as Variant. W, x, y, and z should be between 0 and 4. No position, except 0, should be repeated. Zero implies phase or neutral does not exist. 


Phase Perm Table  
|  Neutral  |  With Neutral  |  No  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ABC  |  1234  |  1230  |  
|  ACB  |  1324  |  1320  |  
|  BAC  |  2134  |  2130  |  
|  BCA  |  3124  |  3120  |  
|  CAB  |  2314  |  2310  |  
|  CBA  |  3214  |  3210  |  
|  AB  |  1304  |  1300  |  
|  AC  |  1034  |  1030  |  
|  BA  |  3104  |  3100  |  
|  BC  |  0134  |  0130  |  
|  CA  |  3014  |  3010  |  
|  CB  |  0314  |  0310  |  
|  A  |  2004  |  --  |  
|  B  |  0204  |  --  |  
|  C  |  0024  |  --  |

#### SAP Calculation Interfaces (Deprecated)
The following Calculation interfaces assist in determining the values to use in populating the SAP database. The CalculationInterface_GetValue method uses the Application property. Therefore, it must be set before the GetValue method can be invoked. 
GetMask
For a given feature, the GetMask interface generates a mask containing the planning area in which the primary graphic component of the feature lies, the type of feature and the next sequence number. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260727) The priority for using these arguments is as follows: 
  1. If valid PickListFieldName is available, use it.
  2. Else, if valid component and attribute names, use it.
  3. Else, use the literal.

  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ComponentName  |  String  |  If the value is non-empty, this Component is used to retrieved to determine the type of the feature (OH/UG/NET..).   |  
|  FieldName  |  String  |  This field is used to get the value of the type of the feature.  |  
|  Literal  |  String  |  If the Attribute Number is zero, this Literal determines the type of the feature.  |  
|  PickListFieldName  |  String  |  If this argument has a valid Picklist/Domain Table field Name, then the value from the field is used to determine the feature type.   |  
Prompts: None 
GetCoordinates
The GetCoordinates interface returns the coordinate values for X,Y or concatenated values for X,Y for the primary geographical component of a feature, depending on the output value requested.   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  OutputValue  |  Integer  |  This variable determines the return value.  |  
|  Delimiter  |  String  |  This is used when the X and Y coordinates are concatenated.  |  
Prompts: None 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260727) For the implementation of the CalculationInterface_GetValue method, the following calculation is returned: 
(CalculatedValue) as Variant
This variant contains a string depending on the OutputValue:  
|  OutputValue  |  Return Value  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  1  |  X coordinate  |  
|  2  |  Y coordinate  |

### Component Elimination Interfaces

#### Custom Component Elimination Interface Methods
If assigning components by their geographical proximity during the break workflow is not appropriate for your data model, you can use a custom Component Elimination method. NetWorks Core delivers the following Component Elimination interface methods: 
CompSortByAttribute
Assigns components according to an attribute value. CompSortByAttribute applies only to data models in which the linear component is repeating, such as the multisegment cable model used in NetWorks Core. CompSortByAttribute assumes the feature contains multiple linear components with a logical ordering imposed on them by an attribute value, such as length. 
CompSortByAttribute compares an attribute of the component to be destined (the subject component) to an attribute value of the broken component. If the subject component's attribute value is less than that of the broken component, the subject component is assigned to the original feature; otherwise, it is assigned to the copy. 
CompAssignByProximityHierarchy
Assigns components based on their proximity to one or more other components. CompAssignByProximityHierarchy uses geographical proximity, but it has a metadata-defined hierarchy of other components to which it compares and a metadata- specified tolerance to determine which of the components in the hierarchy to use for proximity testing. The method compares the proximity of the component to be destined to all instances of the first component in the hierarchy. If it is within tolerance to any instance of that component, the component is destined based on that proximity. Otherwise, the method moves on to the next component in the hierarchy, making a similar comparison at each step. If all previous comparisons fail the tolerance test, the last component in the hierarchy is used for proximity analysis—no tolerance is used for the last component. 
You can configure the system to first check to see if the label component is within a specified tolerance of a leader line; if it is, the software assigns the label to whichever feature the leader line was assigned. Otherwise, the software assigns the label based on its proximity to the linear component. That is a two-level hierarchy. A hierarchy of up to three levels can be used if needed. 
CompAssignByProximityOrID
Assigns components based on either their proximity to another component or by finding another instance of the component to be destined. This component's destiny has already been established and has an identity attribute equal to that of the component to be destined. Proximity is used if the component is within a metadata-specified tolerance to another component; otherwise, the identity attribute is used.   
|  Example A label is normally placed near a linear component, but occasionally it must be placed far away when the linear component is in a congested space. In the latter case, a stub box (a number or other identifier inside a box) is placed near or on the linear component, and a second stub box (with the same identifier) is placed in another location with the label placed nearby. Both stub boxes use CompAssignByProximityOrID. The one near the linear is destined by its proximity, and the other by its identifier. The arguments to this method specify that the stub box is destined by its proximity to the linear component if it is within a certain tolerance; otherwise, it is destined by finding another instance of the stub box component with the same identifier attribute value whose destiny has already been established.  The label placed near the outlying stub box is probably destined using CompAssignByProximityHierarchy. In fact, this example could be combined with the leader-line example to create a three-level hierarchy in which the label is destined based on its proximity to a leader line, a stub box, or the linear component itself.   |  
| --- |  
CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak
If the original cable section has a component length label within a specified tolerance of the break point, CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak ensures that the component elimination step assigns the Component length label to the original cable section (not the copy). To change the component elimination interface referencing, you must update G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT. 
CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak interface takes one argument, Tolerance to use in the proximity analysis against G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO, and this should be defined in the G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS table. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257926) You can create a custom Component Elimination interface through automation. See NetWorks Core API Desktop Reference for more information. 
Related Topics
[Component Elimination Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dONaaMCKCqImkAJeU0B1BA)
[How Component Elimination Works](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wb8GGcxnHKVQ_nOEKQpu2w)

#### How Component Elimination Works
Component elimination works by managing two lists of components to be destined, the SubjectList and the DestinationList. During the third step of the break workflow, each component instance that has not been destined with a break is added to the SubjectList for destining (all component instances that have been broken—the breakable linear components—are already in the DestinationList at this point). 
The break software iterates over the components in this list trying to destine each component instance. Destining of each component is driven by the metadata parameter for component elimination. This parameter might call for simple assignment to the break or copy feature, destining a component by deleting the component instance from the feature farthest away from the component instance or destining the component by a Component Elimination object. The SubjectList is iterated until all components are removed from this list and added to the DestinationList with their proper destiny. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257928) During this process, no data in the IGTKeyObject has yet been changed. Only the instructions for what happens to the components have been changed in the DestinationList. 
Since the SubjectList is iterated until all components are removed and added to the DestinationList, components that depend on the destiny of other components for the determination of their destiny may have their destining delayed until the next iteration of the loop. 
Assigning components during break by their [geographical proximity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZZ96nKdPkWxZxpz~0CL3UA) to another component (typically the broken component) is not always sufficient for some data models. When geographic proximity is not sufficient, there are other [product-delivered implementations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oqlFu917uHRUKgEtuhb4DA) available for special cases. When none of the built-in component elimination implementations meet your needs, you can implement your own. See [Implementing Component Elimination Objects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RJgTroQdYiGQ335ebCmUbA) and [Component Elimination Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dONaaMCKCqImkAJeU0B1BA) for more information. Also, see NetWorks Core API Desktop Reference for more information.

[Component Elimination Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dONaaMCKCqImkAJeU0B1BA)

### Foreign Key Query Interfaces
Foreign Key Query interfaces provide a common interface point where users can get the current value of a selected attribute, replace it with a new value based on queries against the foreign or domain table (or foreign system data), add new rows, or edit attributes in other components based on the current value of selected attribute, such as CU. On foreign systems, the interface is also available in review mode. 
The Foreign Key Query interface provides the following capabilities:
  * Presentation of a custom dialog box to find foreign key references.
  * Access to the current value of a selected attribute.
  * Access to the foreign or domain table name and the field name that is used to get the foreign key reference. 
  * Returning a new value for a selected attribute.
  * Access to all the component attributes of the current feature.
  * Ability to update attributes within the current or different component.
  * Ability to add or delete rows from the components of the current feature.
  * Launching of the interface, even if the foreign or domain table is not defined, allows the user to present their own customized dialog box, based on the current value of the selected attribute. 
This is particularly useful when the secondary data relationship is not stored in a table readily accessible by NetWorks Core. 

  
|  Example Use a Foreign Key Query interface to build customized CU Selection capabilities or to populate attributes of the same or other components, based on the value of the selected attribute. The interface can also be used in creating an association with the secondary data systems.   |  
| --- |  
The Foreign Key Query interface can be launched by the following commands:
  * New Feature
  * Edit Feature
  * Review Feature


Whenever the user executes a feature placement, edit, or review command, the Feature Explorer control is updated with the attribute tabs of all the components associated with the feature. If the user right-clicks an attribute from any of the attribute tabs while editing or reviewing and the selected attribute is associated with a Foreign Key Query interface, a pop-up menu indicates whether the user wants to Query in Edit mode or Review in Review mode. When the user clicks either of these menu options, the Foreign Key Query interface associated with the selected attribute is launched.

### Functional Interfaces

#### Delivered Functional Interfaces
The following functional interfaces are delivered with the application.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256902) In the following descriptions, the InterfaceType indicates a typical usage of an interface. In many cases, the interfaces can be defined as other types. 
CalculateArea
Associated with the geometry field, this functional interface measures the geometric area and stores it in the field specified in its argument list. The measurement is stored in the same units of the database as defined in the coordinate system object.   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  sComponentName  |  String  |  [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). Name of the component that contains the attribute to store the area value   |  
|  sAttributeAreaField  |  String  |  Name of the field to contain the area value  |  
|  iReferenceSpace  |  Integer  |  Indicates how to use the curvature of the Earth when considering the measurement. 0 - Measurements are taken on the surface of the ellipsoid, which takes the curvature of the Earth into account. The returned measurements do not contain projection distortions.  1 - Measurements are taken on the projection plane, which does not take the curvature of the Earth into account. The returned measurements contain projection distortions.   |  
InterfaceType:  SetValue 
Prompts:  None 
Execute Processing:  Perform the measurement and store the value in the specified field of the specified component. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Verify that the area is not Null. Redo the calculation and compare the results. If not equal, report an error of severity P3. This prevents the user from overriding the calculated value. 
CalculateLength
Associated with the geometry field, this functional interface measures the geometric length and stores it in the field specified in its argument list. The measurement is stored in the same units of the database as defined in the coordinate system object. If the geometry that is measured is an area, then the length is equivalent to the perimeter of the area.   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  sComponentName  |  String  |  [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw). Name of the component that contains the attribute to store the length value   |  
|  sAttributeAreaField  |  String  |  Name of the field to contain the length value  |  
|  iReferenceSpace  |  Integer  |  Indicates how to use the curvature of the earth when considering the measurement  |  
|  sUpdateFlag  |  String  |  Optional. Indicates when the length attribute should be updated. Leave the parameter blank if any edit to the geometry should reflect a changed length.  IfNull (case sensitive) — Allows the user to modify the length. The software stores only the geometric length of the attribute field if the current value of the length attribute is Null or empty.   |  
|  bOverridable  |  Boolean  |  Optional. Indicates whether or not the user can change the length attribute such that it is different from the measured length and still pass validation.  -1 — Lets the user update the length  
0 or blank — The stored length must match the measured length   |  
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Perform the measurement and store the value in the specified field of the specified component. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Verify that the length is not Null. Redo the calculation and compare the results. If not equal, report an error of severity P3. This prevents the user from overriding the calculated value. 
CopyAttribute
In some situations, an attribute value may be stored in one or more components in a feature definition. The most likely occurrence of this is the replication of the state attribute to the connectivity record. While this would be a natural database trigger or procedure, the copy operation may be more selective than for the entire table. The functional interface can be assigned more selectively than the database trigger. 
The functional interface copies the value stored in the field with which the functional interface is associated. The data types of the two fields are assumed to be the same.   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  sCopyToComponentName  |  String  |  Name of the component ([G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_NAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw)) that contains the field to copy into   |  
|  sCopyToAttributeFieldName  |  String  |  Name of the field to contain the copied value  |  
InterfaceType: SetValue, Update 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Perform the copy. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Ensure that the value still matches. Issue a P3 error if they do not match. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256902) If the component has no occurrences, this interface creates the "Copy to Component" specified in the sCopyToComponentName argument. 
DataConsistencyCheck
Checks data consistency between static attributes and CU values in either the STORMS or WMIS work management interfaces. If the CU ID is not populated, data consistency check is not performed. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: Edit, Update 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: None 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Checks the data consistency. If the associated field (CUID) value is blank, no data consistency check is done and no error messages are returned. If the user-entered CUID value and any of the associated static attribute values do not match the corresponding CU value, an appropriate error messages is returned (to model validation pipe). 
Dimensioning
Ensures that a valid geometry and consistent attribution are stored in the database so that the dimension graphics can be derived during display. 
Associate this interface with all of the attributes that control the dimensioning components and with the geometry field. 
Parameters: None 
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing:
  * Every time the geometry changes, the attributes with length or lengths and angle must be updated if this is required by the Boolean flags for calculated or overridden values. 
  * If the attributes with length and angle change as a consequence, the geometry is updated if this is required by the Boolean flags for calculated or overridden values. 
  * If a part of the dimension geometry changes, the rest of the geometry might have to be updated to comply with all the rules for dimension geometries. Based on those changes, the attributes with length and angle must also be updated. 


CancelUpdate Processing: Clean-up 
Update Processing: Only necessary for stacked dimensions, this processing ensures that all of the subordinate components that make up the stack of dimensions is correctly updated when one component is updated. 
Validate Processing: Ensures that the geometry stored in the database conforms to the rules for the particular type of dimension defined. If it does not, a P1 error is returned. It also validates the geographic dimension length to the stored dimension length. If these do not match, a P4 error is returned. Where applicable, the angle of the geometry is also validated. A P4 error is returned on detecting discrepancies. 
Delete Processing: For stacked dimensions only, synchronizes the other dimensions in the stack. 
LinearLabel
Updates the cable section length, section start locations, and cable total length when a component length label is deleted. No processing is performed when the geometry is modified or the length value is modified. Geometry modifications are assumed to be for cartographic cleanup. Other modifications should always be performed through the CableEditControl hosted in Feature Explorer, which updates the other length-related values. LinearLabel also performs the following model validation: 
  * Validates that the sum of the component lengths equals (to a metadata- specified tolerance) the segment length. If a segment has no associated component lengths, no validation is performed. 
  * Validates that the segment start location plus segment length equals (to a metadata-specified tolerance) the start location of its following segment. (Not applied to the last segment). This was performed previously by CableTotalLength.· Validates that the total length of the segments is equal (to a metadata-specified tolerance) to the sum of the individual lengths. 
Configure LinearLabel on one attribute of each component length label component as a SetValue-type functional interface on the geometry attribute. This ensures that the functional interface fires on a deletion and that the results are visible immediately to the user, yet the functional interface does not fire needlessly when the length value or other attributes are modified. 

  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  LINEAR_CNO  |  G3E_CNO of the linear segment to which the component length is associated.  |  
|  MAX_OFFSET_FROM_LINEAR  |  The maximum offset, in ground units, that a component length can be from its associated linear segment. Validation reports an error if a component length is farther from its associated linear segment than this offset.   |  
|  COMP_LENGTH_ANO  |  The attribute number of the length attribute of the component length label.  |  
|  COMP_LENGTH_LINEAR_CID_ANO  |  The attribute number of the attribute where the CID of the associated linear segment is stored. The G3E_CID of the linear segment is stored in this attribute on the component length label.   |  
|  SEGMENT_LENGTH_ANO  |  The attribute number of the attribute where the associated linear segment's length is stored.   |  
|  TEXT_ANO  |  The attribute number of the prefix attribute. This is a text attribute displayed in the Deletion dialog box to help the user identify the component length label.   |  
|  VALIDATION_PRIORITY  |  The priority of any validation errors detected. If this value is None, then no validation is performed at all.   |  
|  VALIDATION_TOLERANCE  |  Specifies the maximum difference, in database units, allowed between: The sum of the component lengths and the length of the associated segment The comparisons of section start locations The sum of the section lengths and the total length  |  
|  START_LOCATION_ANO  |  The attribute number of the attribute where the associated linear segment's start location is stored.   |  
|  DETAIL_SEGMENT_LENGTH_ANO  |  The attribute number of the detail segment's length attribute. If LinearLabel is associated with a detail component length label, though, this is actually the geo segment's length attribute. (In that case, SEGMENT_LENGTH_ANO would be the detail segment's length attribute.)   |  
|  DETAIL_START_LOCATION_ANO  |  The attribute number of the detail segment's start location attribute. If LinearLabel is associated with a detail component length label, though, this is actually the geo segment's start location attribute. (In that case, START_LOCATION_ANO would be the detail segment's start location attribute.)   |  
|  TOTAL_LENGTH_ANO  |  The attribute number of the attribute where the cable's total length is stored.  |  
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: None 
CancelUpdate Processing: Clean-up 
Update Processing: None 
Delete Processing: Display the dialog box and update either the previous or next component length or the section length. If the section length is updated, all following sections' start locations and the total length are updated. 
Validate Processing: Report some error conditions. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256902) The ProgID is PFIFace.LinearLabel 
NullDependentAttr
Retrieves all the dependent attributes of the current attribute and presents them to the user. The user is asked for permission to set the dependent attributes to Null. If yes, the attributes are set to Null. If no, the current attribute is reset to its original value. 
The ANO of the fldAttribute is considered the independent attribute. Its value is used to query for all its dependent attributes. These dependent attributes are then considered independent attributes and are use to query for their own dependent attributes until no more dependent attributes are found. 
Parameters: None 
InterfaceType: Update 
Prompts: The message box states that changing this attribute sets the following attributes to Null, the list of dependent attributes, an OK to proceed prompt, and Yes/No buttons. If the user selects Yes, the attributes are Nulled. If No, the current attribute is restored to its value before it was changed. 
Execute Processing: Begins by retrieving all dependent attributes for the attribute passed in fldAttribute. The ANO is located using the rsComponent and the fldAttribute parameters. This ANO is used to query the [G3E_DIALOGATTRIBUTES_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/padkJs2Ag9Xe0BKXj~7GDw). G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER for occurrences of '%#ANO%'. The values from G3E_DIALOGATTRIBUTES_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO are the dependent attributes. The dependent attributes are then used to query the same table for other second- generation attributes. This process is repeated until no more dependent attributes are found. Only attributes that are found on Edit or Placement dialog boxes([G3E_DIALOGS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MKuj1q449pMZ2DcfcWnlWw).G3E_TYPE) are retrieved. Using a message box, the dependent attributes are presented to the user sorted by Edit and Placement with the dialog tab names where the dependent attributes are located. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None 
ParcelCentroid
In conjunction with land data management, ensures the centroid stays within the parcel area. 
Parameters: None 
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: If the user moves the centroid outside of the parcel area or areas, it is returned to the previous position 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: Applicable only if 'LabelAttachedToCentroid' = 1 in G3E_LMIFACE. Checks whether the centroid is inside a parcel area. If not, exit. Locate the label or leader line in the same parcel area where the centroid is located. If the label position or leader line start point is not identical with the centroid, update them so that they are identical with the centroid. 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Check whether the centroid is inside a parcel area. If not, return a P1 error "Parcel centroid is not inside of any parcel area". Applicable only if 'LabelAttachedToCentroid' = 1 in G3E_LMIFACE. Locate the label or leader line in the same parcel area where the centroid is located. If the label position or leader line start point is not identical with the centroid, return P2 error "Label or leader line start point not identical with the parcel centroid". 
ParcelLabel
In conjunction with land data management, ensures that the label for the parcel is inside the area or attached to a leader line associated with the parcel area. 
Parameters: None 
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Applicable only if 'LabelAttachedToCentroid' = 1 in G3E_LMIFACE. If the user moves the label and it is inside of the parcel area with a centroid, the label is snapped to the centroid (that is, coordinates of the centroid is copied into the label). This happens only if there is already no such label. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing:
  * If the updated record contains a label that is outside of a parcel area, the FI checks whether there is a leader line pointing from the label into a parcel area. If there is a one, exit. Otherwise, look for a loose leader line (that is, leader line with no label attached). If there is a one, attach it back to the label and exit. Otherwise, create a leader line from the label to the nearest parcel area without a label. 
  * If the updated record contains a label that is inside of a parcel area, the FI checks whether there is a leader line pointing from this label inside parcel area. If there is one, delete it. 
  * Applicable only if 'LabelAttachedToCentroid' = 1 in G3E_LMIFACE. If the updated record contains a label that is inside of a parcel area, the FI checks whether there is a centroid inside the same area. If there is one, snap the label to the centroid (that is, coordinates of the centroid is copied into the label). 


Delete Processing: If the record to be deleted contains a label that is outside of a parcel area, the FI checks whether there is a leader line pointing from the label into a parcel area. If there is one, it is deleted 
Validate Processing: If the label is outside of a parcel area, check that there is a leader line attached to the label that points inside a parcel area. If there is not one, display an error: "There is no leader line pointing from the label inside a parcel area". Applicable only if 'LabelAttachedToCentroid' = 1 in G3E_LMIFACE. If the label is inside of a parcel area with the centroid, check that the coordinates of the label and the centroid are the same. 
RelativeComponent
Copies a nongraphic attribute from a component specified by FromFNO, FromCNO and FromANO to a component/field specified by ToANO. The ToANO must reference the current component (the one associated to the interface) in the feature. The from component is a graphic component like a cable or pipe segment. The interface determines the location of the from component (uses geometry of the component) relative to the component associated with the interface. This relative component might be a label that is along the cable.The interface finds the nearest from component (if UseNearestFromCNO is True) or it finds all the from components within tolerance from the current component. If there is only one candidate for the from component, a nongraphic attribute (like G3E_CID specified in FromANO) value from the from component is copied to the specified attribute of the to component. If more than one candidate for the from component is found, the interface displays a PickQuick dialog box for the user to make a choice. Allows the application to build inter- component proximity relationships. All component and attribute references must be within the same feature. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256902) If you use CableAndComponentIPT and ComponentLengthLabelIPT, you do not need to configure RelativeComponent on the component length labels; that function is performed by the placement techniques.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  FromFNO  |  Must be the same as the FNO associated with the current component that has been assigned this interface.   |  
|  FromCNO  |  Component within the current feature to determine the proximity. This might be a linear component and the component associated with the interface a label.   |  
|  FromANO  |  Attribute value to copy.  |  
|  ToANO  |  storage location for copied attribute within the current component.  |  
|  UseNearestFromCNO  |  Applies when multiple occurrences of FromCNO exist. If true, do not prompt user to choose correct association.   |  
InterfaceType: Update 
Prompts: User is prompted to select the appropriate FromCNO when multiple occurrences exist and UseNearestFromCNO is false. 
Execute Processing: Compare the current component (associated to the interface) with the component specified in FromCNO. Either the closest component is retrieved or the user indicates the correct relationship. Once the FromCNO occurrence is found, the software copies an attribute value from that component to an attribute in the current component. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None 
SetAttributeByType
Examines the current value of the attribute it is associated with and updates another attribute based on a series of comparisons to the specified values (up to four).   
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  sStorageComponentName  |  String  |  Name of the component that contains the field to hold one of the specified storage values ([G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_NAME.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw))   |  
|  sStorageAttributeName  |  String  |  Name of the field in which to store the selected storage value.  |  
|  sComparisonValue1  |  Variant  |  Value to which to compare the setting of the active attribute. The active attribute is the one associated with this functional interface.   |  
|  sStorageValue1  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute's value is equal to sComparisonValue1, store this value in the storage attribute specified in the first two arguments.   |  
|  sComparisonValue2  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute value does not match sComparisonValue1, compare it to this value.   |  
|  sStorageValue2  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute's value is equal to sComparisonValue2, store this value in the storage attribute specified in the first two arguments.   |  
|  sComparisonValue3  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute value does not match sComparisonValue1 or sComparisonValue2, compare it to this value.   |  
|  sStorageValue3  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute's value is equal to sComparisonValue3, store this value in the storage attribute specified in the first two arguments.   |  
|  sComparisonValue4  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute value does not match sComparisonValue1, sComparisonValue2, or sComparisonValue3, compare it to this value.   |  
|  sStorageValue4  |  Variant  |  If the active attribute's value is equal to sComparisonValue4, store this value in the storage attribute specified in the first two arguments.   |  
InterfaceType: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Compare the value of the current attribute to sComparisonValue1. If it matches, assign the sStorageComponentName.sStorageAttributeName the value of sStorageValue1. If it fails, repeat with the second set of values. Continue through the fourth attribute. If no match is found, do not set the storage attribute. This generates an error during validation. 
Comparison and storage values after the first two can be Null. The first Null or empty comparison value is treated as a wildcard value for any value. 
CancelUpdate Processing: None 
Update Processing: None 
Validate Processing: Perform the comparisons again and check if the storage attribute contains the value that it should. Issue a P2 warning if it does not.

#### Functional Interface Types
The component-placement behavior described below occurs when a feature is placed or a component added. The component-edit behavior occurs when the feature properties—attributes or graphic components—are edited. 
All interfaces defined for the attributes in a component are launched on AddNew, Edit, or Update, whereas only the ones specifically associated with the attribute are launched on SetValue. SetValue type interfaces are not launched on AddNew, Edit, or Update.   
|  Functional Type  |  Component Placement  |  Component Edit  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  AddNew  |  Fires when the occurrence is created (Recordset.AddNew)  |  No action  |  
|  Edit  |  Fires when the recordset is put into edit mode if the AddNew operation occurred during a previous feature edit   |  Fires when the recordset is put into edit mode (Recordset.Edit)  |  
|  Update  |  Fires when the user indicates completion of data entry, effectively just before Recordset.Update  |  Fires when the user indicates completion of data entry, effectively just before the Recordset.Update   |  
|  SetValue  |  Fires after the field value is modified (that is, when you set the Field.Value property). In this case, the FunctionalInterface acts like a triggering event.   |  Fires after the field value is modified (that is, when you set the Field.Value property). In this case, the FunctionalInterface acts like a triggering event.   |  
It is possible to use the AddNew or Edit interfaces to warn the user of an illegal edit.   
|  Example An AddNew or Edit interface could be specified associated with the G3E_FID field for each significant component (primary graphic, primary detail graphic, and attribute records). The interface could check the state of the feature as recorded by the work management system. If the state does not support edits, an error message could be displayed indicating that any modification to the feature cannot be posted to the master database. However, NetWorks Core lets the actual edit operation continue. The interface is again executed for validation purposes (on demand or automatically using post work). The error reported at that time would prevent the work from being committed back to the master model and would prevent the transfer of incorrect or illegal information to the work management system.   |  
| --- |  
In the case of the SetValue interfaces, if the function fails, the operation should be undone and the user informed. This method can also be used to populate other attributes based on the setting of this one.

#### Length Management Functional Interfaces
The Length Management system uses several functional interfaces to maintain the lengths of the features in the many-ownership hierarchy. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Functional interfaces for use with Length Management. 
GTLengthComponentGeometryFunctional
Associated with the geometry field of a length component, this functional interface updates all the length attribute values of the length component and the length feature to which it belongs. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Every time the geometry changes, this functional interface performs the following: 
  * Updates the geometric length of the length component.
  * Updates the total geometric length by adding the difference in geometric length, if it is to be included in the total. 
  * Updates the length of the length component if configured. 
  * Updates the total length by adding the difference in length, if it is to be included in the total. 


Delete Processing: Every time a geometry is deleted, this functional interface performs the following: 
  * Updates the total geometric length by subtracting the difference in geometric length, if it is to be included in the total. 
  * Updates the total length by subtracting the difference in length, if it is to be included in the total. 


Validate Processing: None 
GTLengthComponentIncludeGeometricLengthFunctional
Associated with the include-geometric-length field of a length component, this functional interface updates the length feature's total geometric length. In an instance-based model, the user is displayed an include-geometric-length attribute that lets them determine whether a specific length component should be included in the total geometric length of the length feature. When that attribute value is changed, the total geometric length changes appropriately as well, depending on whether the component is included or not. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: If the geometric length of the length component is included in the total geometric length of the length feature, the geometric length is added to the total. Otherwise, the geometric length is removed from the total. 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None 
GTLengthComponentIncludeLengthFunctional
Associated with the include-length field of a length component, this functional interface updates the length feature's total length. In an instance-based model, the user is displayed an include-length attribute that lets them determine whether a specific length component should be included in the total length of the length feature. When that attribute value is changed, the total length changes appropriately as well, depending on whether the component is included or not. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: If the length of the length component is included in the total length of the length feature, adds the length to the total, otherwise, removes the length from the total. 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None 
GTLengthComponentLengthFunctional
Associated with the length field of a length component, this functional interface updates the length feature's total length, if the length component is to be included in the total. The user is displayed a length attribute that lets them specify a length that is different from the actual geometric length of the component. When that attribute value is changed, the total length changes appropriately as well, depending on whether the component is included in the total or not. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: If the length of the length component is included in the total length of the feature length, the difference in length is added to the total. This functional interface also updates the start location attribute value of all the length component instances that follow the edited instance. 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None 
GTLengthFeatureTotalLengthFunctional
Associated with the total length field of a length feature, this functional interface updates the length components of all related child features. 
Parameters: None 
Interface Type: SetValue 
Prompts: None 
Execute Processing: Every time the total length of a length feature is updated, this functional interface updates the length components of all related child features. Each child length feature has a length component that represents the parent length feature. When the total length of the parent length feature is updated, the functional interface finds all the length components that are represented by the parent length feature. When those length components are updated, if they are included in the total length of the child feature, the child feature's total length is updated. If that child feature is also a parent to other child length features, the process repeats itself on all of the related child features. 
Delete Processing: None 
Validate Processing: None

### Loop Makeup Interfaces

#### Implementing Loop Makeup Objects
You can implement the custom [Loop Makeup interface](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Interfaces_IGTLoopMakeup.htm) by modifying one of the examples in \GTechnology\Services\Samples\NETSamples\LoopMakeup. 
You need to modify the IGTLoopMakeup_ProcessFeature, IGTLoopMakeup_PostProcess, and IGTLoopMakeup_ReportTitle methods of the example. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ) To perform these steps, you must be connected to a database for which you have administrative privileges. 
To implement an interface using .NET, [click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ). 
This is an overview workflow for implementing a .NET custom extension in NetWorks Core. 
  * To implement a .NET custom extension:


  1. Produce a .NET custom extension type in a .NET custom extension assembly:
     * The .NET custom extension project must add a reference to the Intergraph.GTechnology.dll assembly located in the \GTechnology\Program folder. This assembly is not deployed in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC). The assembly contains the public namespaces Intergraph.CoordinateSystems, Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces, and Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * Inherit a .NET custom extension type from a NetWorks Core public interface defined in the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces. The .NET custom extension type can use .NET helper objects from the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * The .NET custom extension type should carefully consider the type of work performed and the access to feature data. On occasion, it is necessary to force system Garbage Corrector (GC) to reclaim unused memory. When the NetWorks Core session is terminated, the framework does the required cleaning. As part of the clean-up processing, the framework forces GC to run. However, if you manipulate a large number of ADO recordsets and/or a large number of NetWorks Core features, it is also appropriate to force GC to run in those .NET custom extensions. 
It is also an essential .NET coding practice to call the Dispose method, when available, and when you are done using those .NET objects. For example, call the IGTFeaturePlacementService.Dispose method when you are done using the .NET helper object from your .NET custom extension type. This is the proper garbage collection sequence: 
Call any Dispose methods on objects that you are using;
Release any objects that do not naturally fall out of scope
Call the garbage collection sequence noted here when you have processed a large number of ADO recordsets and/or IGTKeyObject. 
GC.Collect();
GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
GC.Collect();
     * ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ) There are some programming practices that must be followed in custom code: 
       * Only use local variables to store pointers to NetWorks Core windows. Never store them as global variables or even class variables. 
       * Never call methods that refresh the database while there are objects in the select set. These APIs (and maybe more) refresh the database: 
- GTJobManagementService.RefreshJobEnvironment
- GTTransactionManager.RefreshDatabaseChanges
- GTTransactionManager.Commit
- The methods on JobHelper that change the job context
       * Never change the job context when writing functional interfaces, especially validation interfaces. 
  2. Place the .NET custom extension assembly in the \GTechnology\Program folder for testing purposes. 
  3. Using Metadata Explorer, populate the required NetWorks Core interface point metadata to add the .NET custom extension, and refresh or publish metadata. 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Software Interfaces node and navigate to the appropriate .NET interface, for example, Compute Partial Start Length 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Populate the new row in the interface table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel: 
      1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the object.  
This name appears in the tree view. 
      2. In the G3E_INTERFACE field, type a name for the .NET assembly. The value in the G3E_INTERFACE field must be in the following format:  
AssemblyName:TypeName  
where 
AssemblyName is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension, and TypeName is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.   
|  Example GTDotNetSamples:Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample  AssemblyName is GTDotNetSamples. TypeName is Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample with namespace as Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples and classname as GTDisableEditToolSample.  |  
| --- |  
      3. Click OK. 
    4. To update existing arguments for your object:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Select the argument you want to update.
      3. Update the fields that are available for edit, and click somewhere else on the screen.
      4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ) to commit your edits to the database. 
      5. Repeat these steps for each argument.
    5. To add arguments to your interface:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260564?tocId=b0glBoZd99Q4atQv2YnOqQ), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
      3. In the argument table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel:
       * Type a number to indicate the order of the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL field.
       * Type a name for the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTNAME field.
       * Describe the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTDESCRIPTION field.
       * From the G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE drop-down list, select a data type.
       * Click OK. 
      1. Repeat Steps ii and iii for each argument you want to add.
    6. [Complete configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LDawReDio_37hAl4p5itA) of the new interface by associating it with a feature, component, attribute, and so forth so that a user can access it. 
  4. Test the .NET custom extension type by running a NetWorks Core command that exposes the interface point. If you are implementing a custom command, then you would invoke your custom command to test your code. 
  5. Publish and distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension assembly either to a shared location defined in the [FileUNCPaths.xml file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) under the <CUSTOMIZATION> and <DOTNET> tags or distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension to every local client machine. 
On the client machine, the .NET custom extension assembly should be either placed in the \GTechnology\Program folder or deployed into the GAC, so that users can access the assembly at runtime. 
The .NET custom extension assemblies can be deployed into the GAC by using Windows Explorer to drag assemblies into GAC, by using a Windows Installer package you have developed, or by using the developer GAC tool, Gacutil.exe, which is delivered with the .NET framework SDK. 


If a location is defined in FileUNCPaths.xml, and .NET custom extension assemblies exist on both local and remote machines, the local copy takes precedence.

### Merge Features Interfaces

#### Length Management Merge Features Interfaces
Merge Features interfaces for Length Management manage the lengths of the length feature when it is merged with another length feature. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Merge Features interfaces for use with Length Management. 
GTLengthMergeFeatures
The Length Management Merge Features interface performs the following operations:
  * Updates the resultant length feature's total geometric length.
  * Updates the resultant length feature's total length.
  * Updates the start location attributes of the sections that are copied from the feature that is deleted as part of the merge operation. 
  * Updates each existing related child instance that represented the first parent to have the first parent's new length. 
  * Deletes each existing related child instance that represented the second parent.


Related Topic
[Length Management Overview](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMmx8LEmlrbbDHinlTKB6w)

#### Tips for Implementing Merge Features Interfaces
The calling sequences described below explain which IGTMergeFeatures methods should be implemented for which kind of processing. 
Two-point Lines
This IGTMergeFeatures sequence merges two-point lines. It creates a new two-point line by eliminating the two closest endpoints. 
[G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_MERGEOCCURRENCES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) should be 0 so that user interaction is skipped. 
  * Allow. Do not allow merge in the two linear geometries in ambiguous cases, such as when the lines are opposite edges of the imaginary rectangle. 
  * MergeComponents. Merge the two linear geometries.
  * Approve. No processing.
  * PostProcess. No processing.


Maintain Label Ratio
This IGTMergeFeatures sequence repositions the label on the final feature based on the position relative to the first feature. 
  * Allow. Calculate label's relative position to the linear component of the first feature.
  * MergeComponents. No processing.
  * Approve. No processing.
  * PostProcess. Reposition the label so that it is in the same relative position to the linear component of the final feature. 


Related Topic
[Implementing Merge Features Objects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gNSx8Pe_EyS9KAcfig354g)
