#### OTDR Compute Geo Point Interface
If the marker exists in the detail window, it does not add value to the accessibility information because it does not provide the necessary information to the maintenance staff about where to dig and repair this fault. If the marker location exists in the detail window, it should be projected back to the containers in the geographic window. The OTDR Compute Geo Point interface calculates the projected geo point for the given detail marker location point. You can replace the delivered interface with a custom interface. 
In some models, the underground cables are drawn in the detail window, but the cable containers (conduits) are displayed in the geographic window. Depending on the span of the cable and number of times it enters and exits the underground network, the cable passes through several containers. 
Because there is no direct relationship between the cable section and the exact conduit that contains it, the OTDR Compute Geo Point interface calculates the projected point only if all the [assumptions regarding allocating a child feature after a break](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5qc_gOoYeZMTTEX8YRRIlg) and projected geo point assumptions are satisfied. If the data model violates any of the allocation or geo point assumptions, the OTDR Compute Geo Point interface does not return an error but returns a point equal to the point of the detail node feature (for example, manhole) that contains it. These are the geo point assumptions: 
  * A length attribute must exist for the conduit features.
  * If a length of cable is coiled inside a manhole, the calculated marker point might not be accurately calculated because the system did not account for the coiled length. The user can add this length to the previous conduit; however, a manhole can contain more than one cable and each cable can have its own coiled length. There is no direct way to represent this length, therefore; the geo point in this situation is only an approximation of the location. 
  * The cable length of the detail section represents the total length of all the conduits in the infrastructure network until a prior cable section is encountered. If the prior section is a geographic section, then infrastructure network is considered up to the manhole or conduit nearest to the geographic section If the prior section is a detail section, then the stopping point in the infrastructure network is clearly defined by that detail location. If there is only one detail cable component and no geographic cable/component, or the section selected is the first in the order, the marker location point is equal to the point of the referencing feature (for example, manhole) symbol. 


This interface requires four parameters:  
|  Parameters  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Infrastructure Linear Feature FNOs  |  Text  |  Input  |  Required  |  List of comma- delimited linear infrastructure containment FNOs. There can be more than one linear component in the infrastructure containment hierarchy that contains the length attribution required for calculating the projected geo point.   |  
|  Infrastructure Linear Feature Length ANOs  |  Text  |  Input  |  Required  |  List of comma- delimited length attribute ANOs. Each of the features provided by Infrastructure Linear Feature FNOs must have a length attribute. The number of linear infrastructure features specified must be equal to the number of length attribute numbers.   |  
|  Infrastructure Linear Component CNOs  |  Text  |  Input  |  Required  |  List of comma- delimited linear component CNOs. Must equal the number of infrastructure features specified by the Infrastructure Linear Feature FNOs argument. The geometric length of any linear infrastructure feature may or may not be equal to the stored length.   |  
|  Locate Geo Tolerance  |  Double  |  Input  |  Required  |  Tolerance value required to locate the geo component. The software must know if a geo cable component is in near the infrastructure feature (this is required at points where the cable exits the infrastructure contained network as in the case of going from underground to aerial).   |

#### OTDR Compute Marker Location Interface
The OTDR Compute Marker Location interface computes the appropriate points on the candidate cables where the markers should be placed. You can replace the delivered interface with a custom interface. 
The calculation of the points where the markers exist varies based on the data model. NetWorks Core accounts for the following data model variations: 
  * The actual length stored in the attributes of the cable feature can be different than the geometric length. Because the marker must be placed on this cable, the calculation considers the ratio between the two lengths to compute the appropriate point on the cable. 
  * The OTDR Compute Marker Location interface works for both the single and multisection cable models to compute the marker location points. 
  * In a multisection cable model, the cable is a repeating linear component with each section mapped onto the physical cable using two attributes, section start location and section length. 
  * The marker point can exist on one of these sections; therefore, the interface considers all the sections when deciding on a point to place the marker on a given cable. 
Each cable section can be associated with a component length label. The component length label point projected to the cable linear component indicates the distance of the label from the previous component label or the start point. The component length labels may or may not be distributed appropriately on the section geometry.   
|  Example The geometric length of the section is 10 meters. The [component length label](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Uutp4ZFBuzi4bHXGXoNdww) can exist at 2.5 meters but can still represent the component length of 5.0 meters. The remaining 7.5 meters of the cable represents the rest of the 5.0 meters.   |  
| --- |  
  * When computing a marker location, the resistance calculation is different from the distance calculation. The resistance of a cable depends on its gauge and is always described in terms of resistance per length. Given the computed resistance of the cable feature, cumulative resistance up to that cable, and the input value that indicates the marker location (the stop criteria value for the trace), the software calculates the exact point on the cable using resistance per length information. The OTDR Compute Marker Location interface uses this factor to determine the marker location point: 
Factor = 1 - [(cumulative value - stop criteria value) / candidate cable value] The factor gives you the flexibility to write a different trace (for example, dB Loss) and to still use the delivered NetWorks Core OTDR Compute Marker Location interface to compute the marker location points. 


The OTDR Compute Marker Location interface requires two parameters. The value of these arguments is 0 (zero) if the cable follows the multisection cable model. For the multisection cable model, the cable characteristics are derived from [G3E_CABLEEDITATTR.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MF3LH6S6jV5Mx2jjObPygg).   
|  Parameters  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Geo Cable Linear Component Number  |  Integer  |  Input  |  Required  |  The geo component of the candidate cable feature.  |  
|  Detail Cable Linear Component Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  The detail component of the candidate cable feature.  |  
If a value of -1 is defined for these arguments, the primary geo and primary detail components for the candidate cables are used in the interface processing to calculate the marker location.

#### OTDR Compute Partial Start Value Interface
The delivered .NET OTDR Compute Partial Start Value interface calculates and returns a value representing the length of the part of the specified feature upstream from the specified point. The resulting value from the interface is used by the Trace command to update the seed row in the trace results. 
The calculation of the length varies based on the data model. NetWorks Core accounts for the following data model variations: 
  * The actual length stored in the attributes of the cable feature can be different than the geometric length. The calculation considers the ratio between the two lengths. 
  * The interface works for both the single and multisection cable models to calculate the length. In a multisection cable model, the cable is a repeating linear component with each section mapped onto the physical cable using two attributes, section start location, and section length. The interface considers all the sections when calculating the length. 
  * Each cable section can be associated with a component length label. The component length label point projected to the cable linear component indicates the distance of the label from the previous component label or the start point. The component length labels may or may not be distributed appropriately on the section geometry.   
|  Example The geometric length of the section is 10 meters. The component length label can exist at 2.5 meters but can still represent the component length of 5.0 meters. The remaining 7.5 meters of the cable represents the rest of the 5.0 meters.   |  
| --- |  


The OTDR Compute Partial Start Value interface requires no arguments.

#### OTDR Compute Stop Criteria Procedure
The Compute Stop Criteria procedure computes resistance and/or distance values along a trace. The procedure is called for each iteration of a trace. The Trace command passes the trace number and trace order to the procedure, and the procedure updates the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table with the computed current and cumulative resistance or distance values. When the cumulative value exceeds the input stop criteria value, the trace stops at that feature without continuing further downstream. 
The procedure is called after each iteration of the trace algorithm and is provided with the identifier for the trace being performed and the iteration that has just been completed. This allows the procedure to determine the exact set of rows in the TRACERESULT table it should process. For example, in a breadth first trace, this is the set of all entities connected 'next' to the previously traced components. Because the iteration-based approach reduces the number of invocations to the depth of the traced network, trace processing runs faster, especially if the trace is a branch trace. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257911) The sample procedure works on the pair count trace only if pair count filters are defined as part of the trace attribution in the G3E_TRACE definition. The trace must also be constrained to go in one direction. You can control trace direction with the G3E_PROMPTFORHINT parameter in G3E_TRACE. Since the procedure updates the current cable's cumulative value with the cumulative length/resistance values from its source plus its length/resistance, make sure that the current cable does have unique source cables, that is, the same cable occurrence is not acting as source to the current cable occurrence. 
The procedure computes the current and cumulative resistance/distance value of each cable in the traced network using this resistance-based calculation: 
Resistance per Length * (Total Length / 1000.0)
The resistance per length is derived from [G3E_LOOPRESISTANCE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TX8_MklZmLFdObvXNqlmQw) table based on the gague of the given cable. For distance-based traces, the distance is the total length (GC_CBL.TOTAL_LENGTH) of all the sections of the given cable. The procedures update the calculated distance/resistance value and the cumulative resistance/distance value in the TRACERESULT table. 
Before you can use Compute Stop Criteria, you must install it in your database:
SQL> @ \11.01.2501\PLSQL\ltt\g3estopcriteria.sql;
SQL> @ \11.01.2501\PLSQL\ltt\prvtg3estopcriteria.sql;
Compute Stop Criteria Configuration
To replace the procedure provided with NetWorks Core with a custom computational procedure, update [G3E_TRACE.G3E_ITERATIONPROC](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) with the new procedure to be called by the configured OTDR trace. Metadata validation verifies that the procedure names specified in this column exist in the database. 
As currently implemented, the procedure uses joins on the GC_CBL (the primary attribute component of the cable model), G3E_LOOPRESISTANCE, and TRACERESULT tables to update the current and cumulative values in one SQL statement. 
Because the procedure is called for each iteration of the trace, you must carefully write any custom SQL code that updates the columns in the TRACERESULT table to avoid poor performance. Any added procedure requires only two parameters, the number of the trace being executed and the iteration for which the procedure is being called. The procedure computes the current and cumulative values for a given feature along a trace and then populates the corresponding fields in the TRACERESULT table. 
Syntax: Procedure ComputeStopCriteria(p_tno IN NUMBER,p_torder IN NUMBER )  
|  Argument  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  p_TNO  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Number of the trace being executed when this procedure is invoked.  |  
|  p_TRaceOrder  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Identifier for the trace iterations for which the procedure is beig called.  |  
Remarks: You can find which rows in the TRACERESULT table are processed by each invocation of this procedure by querying the TRACERESULT table rows whose G3E_TNO and G3E_TRACEORDER values are the p_TNO and p_TraceOrder parameters values, respectively.

#### OTDR Marker Placement Report Interface
When the trace execution is complete, the OTDR Marker Placement Report interface locates the point of the cable faults and places a graphic marker at the specified distance on the geographic network. The marker is created by the OTDR Create Marker interface as a temporary geometry. When determining the fault points, all cables whose cumulative distance/resistance is greater than or equal to the input stop criteria value are considered as candidates for marker placement. To produce a different result than graphic markers on the map, you can replace the delivered interface with a custom interface. 
The OTDR Marker Placement Report interface is implemented as a COM object.  
|  Parameters  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  OTDR Compute Marker Location Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  Parameter to specify OTDR Compute Marker Location interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Marker Location Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  Parameter to specify OTDR Compute Marker Location interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Geo Point Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Compute Geo Point interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Compute Geo Point Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Compute Geo Point interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Create Marker Interface Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Create Marker interface identifier.  |  
|  OTDR Create Marker Interface Argument Group Number  |  Long  |  Input  |  Required  |  OTDR Create Marker interface argument group identifier.  |  
|  Stop Criteria Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the input stop criteria value. Derived from user input.   |  
|  Cable Value Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the calculated value derived from the TRACERESULT table.   |  
|  Cumulative Value Field Name  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  Field names in the input recordset of the report interface for the cumulative value derived from the TRACERESULT table.   |

#### OTDR Processing Overview
NetWorks Core delivers OTDR interfaces from which you can customize the software to meet the needs of your data model. The following general processing overview shows you when each customizable component is launched in the workflow. 
The user selects the start feature, selects Analysis > Trace, and provides the input stop criteria—for example, the distance or resistance or pair counts, as part of the trace attribution. The user then selects the OTDR Marker Placement Report interface and executes the Trace command. 
  1. If [G3E_TRACE.G3E_PARTIALVALUERINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) is populated with the interface name specified in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.RINO, the user is prompted to select a point on the starting feature. 
    1. The [specified interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OjTYtBfEJE0sJCWaf7Bf8w) calculates the length of the feature upstream from the selected point. 
    2. The procedure defined in G3E_TRACE.G3E_PRETRACEPROC is called and given the partial length value from the previous step. The procedure calculates the partial value (resistance or distance, depending on which procedure is configured) based on the input value. It updates the stop criteria in TRACERESULT for the start feature. 
  2. After each trace iteration, the trace procedure invokes the [Compute Stop Criteria database procedure](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xLI7mqPZCcmXXfK5BJN~4Q). This procedure computes stop criteria (resistance or distance, depending on which function is configured) and updates the trace results with the computed stop criteria and the cumulative stop criteria values. 
  3. After the trace procedure execution is complete, the Trace command queries the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) data table for the output recordset and adds the input stop criteria field (defined by G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES.G3E_OUTPUTFIELDNAME) along with its value to this recordset. 
  4. The Trace command creates and invokes the [OTDR Marker Placement Report interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_cPtxzNkHm8LX1c~If6U9w) and sends the recordset generated in the previous step as input to the report interface. 
    1. Loops through the report interface's input recordset and generates a new recordset containing candidate features whose cumulative value is greater than or equal to the input stop criteria value. 
    2. Creates the [OTDR Compute Marker Location interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jVOvHAghGSmsGRB_jgiX~Q) and invokes the Compute method with Candidate Feature recordset as the input argument. 
For each record in the Candidate Feature recordset:
       * Computes the marker location point on the candidate feature.
       * If the candidate feature belongs to a multisection cable model, the OTDR Compute Marker Location interface uses the GTMultiSectionCable object to consider the cable sections and component length labels when determining the marker location points. 
       * Creates a new recordset containing the marker location point (X,Y), candidate feature FNO, candidate feature FID, and the detail ID if the candidate is part of the detail drawing. 
    3. Creates [OTDR Compute Geo Point interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_li0VQJLsQTcENANb9B~6Q) and invokes the Compute method with Marker Location recordset as the input argument. 
Clones the Marker Location recordset (Projected Geo Point recordset).
For each record in the Marker Location recordset, if the detail ID is set, computes the projected geo location for the detail point and adds a new record to the cloned input recordset. 
    4. Creates [OTDR Create Marker interface ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~XmpF~B5aaiJkRciakeq7g)and invokes Trace Name as the input argument. 
For each record in the Projected Geo Point recordset:
       * If the detail ID is not populated, creates a temporary geometry at the specified marker location point. 
       * If the detail ID is populated, sees if a corresponding detail drawing is open. If the corresponding detail drawing is open, then creates a temporary geometry at the specified marker location point.

### Placement Technique Interfaces

#### Delivered Placement Techniques
The following Placement interfaces (techniques) are delivered with <aProduct>. You cannot change these definitions; however, you can create your own placement techniques using the API. 
Area By Areas IPT
Creates an area, which is a union of areas selected by the user. The area being created must be a [cadastral](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256028) or [political](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256028)
A large-scale map indicating the boundaries and dimensions of subdivisions and individual tracts of land to show ownership. 
A map that shows government boundaries.
Parameters: None 
Area By Edges IPT
Creates an area (parcel/lot or building) based on cadastral edges selected by the user. This IPT queries the G3E_LMIFACE table to retrieve the metadata, such as FNO and CNO of the cadastral edge, which is used to create the parcel/lot or building area.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Include holes  |  Determines whether the holes should be created in the boundary geometries. The following values are allowed:  0-Do not create holes  
1-Create holes  
2-Prompt  This argument is not required. If not specified, 1 is assumed for boundary geometries, and 0 is assumed for polygon and composite polygon geometries.   |  
Assembly IPT
Places points, lines, and areas. Optionally, an assembly from the [equipment catalog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RYJriFHhlSXe6gVhAFCtoQ) can be placed. If a catalog feature number and feature identifier are not specified, a dialog is displayed to let the user pick an assembly to place. The assembly is placed relative to the component being placed. The software assumes that the first point you place is the lower left point of the polygon.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
|  CatalogFNO  |  Short integer—Feature number of catalog entry  |  
|  CatalogFID  |  Long integer—Feature identifier of catalog entry  |  
Assembly Rectangle IPT
Places a rectangle at a user-specified point and angle. Optionally, an assembly from the equipment catalog can be placed. If a catalog feature number and feature identifier are not specified, a dialog is displayed to let the user pick an assembly to place. The assembly is placed relative to the component being placed. The software assumes that the first point you place is the lower left point of the polygon.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  AngleComponentIndicator  |  String with "/" delimiters for FNO/FIDX/CNO/CID of the relative component for the angle   |  
|  AngleValue  |  Angle value in decimal degrees  |  
|  LengthComponentIndicator  |  Specifies the relative component for length  |  
|  Length  |  Length value  |  
|  WidthComponentIndicator  |  Specifies the relative component for width  |  
|  Width  |  Width value  |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
|  CatalogFNO  |  Short integer—Feature number of catalog entry  |  
|  CatalogFID  |  Long integer—Feature identifier of catalog entry  |  
Assembly Rectangle By 2 Points IPT
Places a rectangle at two user-specified points that represent the diagonal of the rectangle. Optionally, an assembly from the equipment catalog can be placed. If a catalog feature number and feature identifier are not specified, a dialog is displayed to let the user pick an assembly to place. The assembly is placed relative to the component being placed. 
After a user places the first point of a feature, the lines appear in dynamics and the user can stretch the rectangle to the second placement point. If the user stretches the rectangle up and to the right to place the second point, the rectangle is placed at zero degrees. If the user stretches the rectangle down and to the left to place the second point, the rectangle is placed at 180 degrees.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
|  CatalogFNO  |  Short integer—Feature number of catalog entry  |  
|  CatalogFID  |  Long integer—Feature identifier of catalog entry  |  
CableAndComponent IPT
Populates and brings up the Placement Length Display control once started. It updates the lengths on the control until it completes placement. This technique displays the linear segment in dynamics. The dynamic linear segment is from the previous key vertex to the current snap point. It also prompts the user to edit the component length and prefix attribute values.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ComponentLengthANO  |  Long—Specifies the attribute number of the component length attribute of the component length label   |  
|  SectionLengthANO  |  Long—Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the associated linear section's length is stored   |  
|  DetailSectionLengthANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the associated detail linear section's length is stored   |  
|  SectionStartLocationANO  |  Long—Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the associated section start location is stored   |  
|  TotalLengthANO  |  Long—Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the total linear length is stored   |  
|  PrefixANO  |  Long—Specifies the attribute number of the prefix attribute  |  
|  ComponentLengthLabelCNO  |  Integer—Specifies the component number of the length label. This value is used to create the component graphics object for component length label.   |  
|  XOffset  |  Double—Specifies the X-offset that a component length is placed from last vertex  |  
|  Offset  |  Double—Specifies the Y-offset that a component length is placed from last vertex  |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move). The value of the length label does not change during adjustment.   |  
Component Length Label IPT
Intended for use when a component length is added to an existing cable section before, after, or in between existing component lengths. The cable linear is placed using the CableAndComponentIPT placement technique, which places component length labels concomitantly with the linear. This technique populates the Placement Length Display control and displays the linear segment in dynamics. The dynamic linear segment is from the start point of the linear section to the current user snap point. This technique also prompts the user to input/modify the component length and prefix attribute values. The dialog box lets the user adjust the adjacent component length or the section length.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ComponentLengthANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the length attribute of the component length  |  
|  FirstSectionLengthANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the length attribute where the current (geo or detail) associated linear section's length is stored   |  
|  SecondSectionLengthANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the length attribute where the alternative (detail or ) associated linear section's length is stored   |  
|  FirstSegmentStartLocationANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the current (geo or detail) associated segment start location is stored   |  
|  SecondSegmentStartLocationANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the alternative (detail or ) associated segment start location is stored   |  
|  TotalLengthANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the total linear length is stored  |  
|  ComponentLengthLinearCIDANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the attribute where the CID of the associated linear segment is stored   |  
|  PrefixtANO  |  Specifies the attribute number of the prefix attribute. This is a text attribute that the dialog displays and allows entry of for user convenience.   |  
|  XOffset  |  Specifies the X offset, in ground units, that a component length is placed from its associated linear segment by default   |  
|  YOffset  |  Specifies the Y offset, in ground units, that a component length is placed from its associated linear segment by default.   |  
|  MaxOffsetFromLinear  |  Specifies the maximum offset, in ground units, that a component length can be from its associated linear segment. This value is used in finding the linear segment associated with a new component length.   |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
Dimension IPT
Enables the construction of all types (simple, orthogonal, radius-of-two-points, polar) of dimension elements. The dimensions can be placed in several ways depending on what data for placement is available. 
For example, if the start and endpoints of a dimension are known, the user clicks the start and endpoints. If the start point, length, and azimuth are known, the user clicks on the start point and types the length and azimuth in the dockable control. A mixed workflow is also possible where the user can click the start point and type in the length. The azimuth is determined from the mouse click. 
For orthogonal and polar dimensions, the user must select the baseline of the dimension as the first step. A baseline is selected by identifying a line segment on another linear or area feature. 
You can use optional parameters to create as many special placement configurations as you need. The special placement configuration can control which buttons are preselected on the Orthogonal Dimension Construction Aids control or it can control two-point placement for orthogonal dimensions. You can create several placement configurations, each with a different set of buttons preselected. You must create separate a placement configuration to enable two-point placement. Users access the placement configurations from the New Feature control.   
|  Argument Ordinal / Option  |  Argument Value  |  Ortho Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1 / Orthogonal Dimension Subtype  |  1  |  Dimension with single dimension line  |  
|  2  |  Dimension with two dimension lines  |  
|  4  |  Dimension with dimension and witness line.  |  
|  8  |  Dimension with witness and dimension line  |  
|  16  |  Dimension with one dimension and two witness lines.  |  
|  32  |  Dimension with second dimension line offset.  |  
|  2 / Baseline Selection  |  1  |  Baseline overlaps a line segment  |  
|  2  |  Baseline connects two vertices  |  
|  4  |  Baseline is loose  |  
|  3 / Direction  |  1  |  Perpendicular to baseline  |  
|  2  |  Parallel with baseline  |  
|  4 / Anchoring  |  1  |  Start point anchoring  |  
|  2  |  Endpoint anchoring  |  
|  5 / Extend/Trim  |  True  |  When placing the constructed point of an orthogonal dimension with single dimension line, the dimension line is extended or trimmed to the nearest linear or area geometry.   |  
|  False  |  When placing the constructed point of an orthogonal dimension with single dimension line, the dimension line is neither extended nor trimmed.   |  
|  6 / Special placement workflow  |  0  |  No special workflow  |  
|  1  |  2-point placement of orthogonal dimension with single dimension line. Other parameters are ignored for this workflow.   |  
Erase Raster SPT
Automatically creates a polygon the exact size of the raster image so that the image file is completely blanked. This lets the files remain but their contents to be removed to support mapping environments where each file represents a grid section in the overall map grid. The technique checks if the component being placed is a component of the raster feature, if it is a polygon geometry type, and if the primary geometry of that raster feature already exists.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RasterCNO  |  The CNO of the component carrying the raster geometry  |  
Fixed Segment Length IPT
Places the first segment of a polyline or a composite polyline with a fixed (metadata-specified) length. Once the first segment (the first two points) of the polyline has been placed, all subsequent interactions with the placement service are simply a pass through operation to the InteractiveIPT function. This technique also supports the Adjustment behavior (by virtue of calling InteractiveIPT).   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  FixedLength  |  Length of first segment. The units are implied to be in the units of the published data. No conversion is performed.   |  
|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
Formation And Ducts IPT
Places a formation with a user-specified number of ducts on the map window and establishes a relationship between the formation and the conduit. This IPT requires a placement configuration that contains a conduit and a formation. You must specify this technique in the appropriate steps of the placement configuration. 
The placement configuration steps that use the GFPlaceTech.FormationAndDuctsIPT must occur after the step that defines the conduit. The conduit must contain attributes that define the number of rows and columns of ducts to create. The user must specify the number of rows and columns of ducts to create before the formation and Ducts IPT begins.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Conduit FNO  |  Short integer—Feature number of the conduit  |  
|  Conduit Row ANO  |  Long integer—The attribute number of the duct rows  |  
|  Conduit Column ANO  |  Long integer—The attribute number of the duct columns  |  
|  RNO  |  Short integer—The number to use to establish a relationship between the conduit and the formation.   |  
|  Mirroring  |  Boolean— 1 – mirroring occurs.  0 – mirroring does not occur.  |  
|  Sorting Mode  |  Short integer—The following values determine the sorting mode of the ducts.  1 – Bottom Left – Right 2 – Top Left – Right 3 – Bottom Left – Up 4 – Top Left – Down 5 – Bottom Right – Left 6 – Top Right – Left 7 – Bottom Right – Up 8 – Top Right – Down  |  
|  Graphical Adjustments (Optional)  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |  
Gas IPT
Enables automated placement of a service segment, which runs from premise to the tap and then to the main segment.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  PlacementType  |  1 = Simple; 2 = Quick; 3 = Connect  |  
|  MainSegFNO  |  Main Segment Feature Number  |  
|  MainSegCNO  |  Main Segment Component Number  |  
|  PremiseFNO  |  Premise Feature Number  |  
|  PremiseCNO  |  Premise Component Number  |  
|  TapFNO  |  Service Tap Feature Number  |  
|  TapCNO  |  Service Tap Component Number  |

Image IPT
Enables placement of raster images. The [file type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Uhnb2CU3apCRE9vHcAS6PA) and certain information in the file determine whether an image can be placed automatically or if it must be placed interactively. 
Automatic placement inserts geo-registered images directly into the database, preserving image geometry. There are two types of automatic placement options: GeoReferenced (only if they contain GeoTIFF tags or geo-tie-packet information) and By Header. 
Interactive placement entails entering data points in matching pairs, one in the temporary image map window and one in the active map window. The image is registered to the active map window based on the paired points. The number of control-point pairs determines the method used to best fit the original raster image: 
  * One control-point pair causes a simple translation (shift) in X and Y.
  * Two control-point pairs produce a Helmert transformation that performs
    * Translation (shift) in X and Y 
    * Scale (same scale in X and in Y) 
    * Rotation
  * Three or more control-point pairs produces an Affine transformation that performs
    * Translation (shift) in X and Y 
    * Scale in X – scale in Y (possibly different than the scale in X) 
    * Rotation 
    * Skew


Parameters: None 
Interactive IPT
Enables interactive placement of points, lines, and areas with the Construction Aids control. The technique honors snap preferences and adjustments. 
Unless the input geometry type is an oriented point or text point, each mouse click appends a new point to the geometry. A double-click ends placement for linear and area geometries. When placement is started, the Construction Aids control appears. When placement ends, the control disappears. 
The user can change the append mode at any time during this technique. Linear and area geometries are drawn in dynamics. Point components (oriented or text) are drawn "on the cursor" and updated as the cursor moves until the user enters a final click.

|  Adjust Mode Arguments  |  Specifies post-placement adjustments (Flip, Rotate, Move)  |

### Post Break Linear Interfaces

#### Delivered Post Break Linear Interfaces
The following Post Break Linear interfaces are delivered with NetWorks Core: 
PostBreakAdjustByRatio
PostBreakAdjustByRatio applies to any data model in which linear features have an associated length attribute that can differ from the measured length. The difference is true for underground features, such as conduits, but can also be true for above-ground features, such as cables and conductors.   
|  Example If a conductor runs up a steep hill, the 2D distance on the map can be much shorter than the length of the actual cable. In these cases, you can use the [CalculateLength functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) to default the length as it is measured but also to allow the user to override this length manually.   |  
| --- |  
You can apply PostBreakAdjustByRatio to these features to provide a reasonable approximation of the length attribute for each feature resulting from the break. PostBreakAdjustByRatio adjusts the length attribute of the original feature by multiplying the prebreak length attribute value by the break ratio (the ratio of the measured length of the initial portion of the broken linear element to its entire measured length). It sets the length attribute of the new feature to the prebreak value minus the new length computed for the original feature. Thus, the two lengths still add up to the original value, and their ratio is the same as the ratio of the measured lengths. 
This algorithm assumes that the difference between the measured length and the length attribute is evenly distributed along the entire element. If this is not true, the algorithm does not yield the correct result.   
|  Example If the difference is because of a sudden change in elevation along the length of the feature—an underground cable goes under an obstruction, for example—all of the difference can remain with the original feature, or it can all be associated to the new feature.   |  
| --- |  
The user must remain aware of these possibilities and correct the value when necessary. PostBreakAdjustByRatio is intended only to give a reasonable approximation. 
These are the arguments for PostBreakAdjustByRatio:  
|  Argument Ordinal  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  ADJUST_ATTRIBUTE_ANO  |  ANO of attribute to be adjusted  |  
Apply this PostBreakLinear interface to the linear graphic components whose length is represented in the specified length attribute. 
PostBreakCableLengths
The PostBreakCableLengths is required to maintain the [multisection cable model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NlBF~fhuOAmRrMXoSw0GQQ). It adjusts the section start locations, section lengths, and total length attributes to maintain the [multisection cable model business rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wPhcd90lYTMqtokNiD3M2Q). 
If the original cable has no component length label within a specified tolerance of the break point, the PostBreakCableLengths interface generates a new component length label at a specified offset from the break point and associates the label to the original cable segment. No interactive adjustments are allowed during this automatic placement. The offset is applied relative to the angle of the line segment so the X-offset always specifies an offset in the direction of the line segment, while the Y-offset specifies an offset perpendicular to the line segment. You must specify the negative X-offset to ensure the label is placed some distance backward along the line away from the break point to prevent it from overlapping the arrow end symbol of the line. 
This operation displays the Component Length at Break Linear dialog box, which allows the user to override the default length for the label. The length on the dialog box is defaulted to the measured length from the preceding component length on that segment or from the beginning of the segment. This dialog box allows only the adjustment of the preceding or following component length label because the segment length must remain unchanged. 
The option to adjust the next component length applies in this case to the component length label following the break point; that is, the next one along the unbroken cable. 
The segment lengths of the two resulting segments are set to the sum of the respective set of component lengths. If the original segment has no component lengths at all, this is the equation that calculates segment length after break processing:   
|  NewSectionLength =  |  MeasuredLengthAfterBreak  |  x OldSectionLength  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  MeasuredLengthBeforeBreak  |  
The arguments for PostBreakCableLengths need to be defined in the G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS table. 
Example 1: Breaking a Geo linear feature such as a geo cable or geo wire  
|  Argument Ordinal  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  SECTION_LENGTH  |  ANO of geo cable section length  |  
|  2  |  SEGMENT_START_LOCATION  |  ANO of geo cable segment start location  |  
|  3  |  SECTION_LENGTH  |  ANO of detail cable section length  |  
|  4  |  SEGMENT_START_LOCATION  |  ANO of detail cable segment start location  |  
|  5  |  SEQ  |  ANO of geo component length SEQ  |  
|  6  |  COMP_LENGTH  |  ANO of geo component length LENGTH  |  
|  7  |  PREFIX  |  ANO of geo component length PREFIX  |  
|  8  |  TOTAL_LENGTH  |  ANO of cable total length  |  
|  9  |  SECTION_LENGTH_TOLERANCE  |  Section length tolerance value  |  
|  10  |  COMP_LENGTH_TOLERANCE  |  Component length label proximity tolerance value  |  
|  11  |  COMP_LENGTH_MAXOFFSET  |  Component length label maximum offset from cable section  |  
|  12  |  COMP_LENGTH_X_OFFSET  |  X-offset at which to place component length label at break point  |  
|  13  |  COMP_LENGTH_Y_OFFSET  |  Y-offset at which to place component length label at break point  |

![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257934) You can create a custom Post Break Linear interface through [automation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UFvJAZtDGGF1RW8fY89O6w).

#### Length Management Post Break Linear Interfaces
Post Break Linear interfaces for Length Management manages the lengths of the original length feature and the length feature the results from the break operation. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Post Break Linear interfaces for use with Length Management. 
GTLengthPostBreakLinear
The Length Management Post Break Linear interface performs the following operations:
  * Updates the geometric lengths of both features to their new measured lengths.
  * Updates the total geometric lengths of both features if the lengths are included in the total. 
  * Updates the length attributes of both features using the break ratio to provide a reasonable approximation. 
  * Updates the total lengths of both features if the lengths are included in the total.
  * Destines the sections to the appropriate length feature using the start location attribute of the original feature. The sections are either kept with the original length feature or moved to the length feature that results from the break operation, depending on where the break occurred and what the start location is. 
  * Updates the start locations of the sections that are moved to the length feature that results from the break operation. 
  * Updates each existing related child instance that represented the original parent to have its parent's new length. 
  * Updates each related child length feature to have a new component instance that represents the new parent resulting from the break. The new instance's length is set to match the length of the new parent. 


Related Topic
[Length Management Overview](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMmx8LEmlrbbDHinlTKB6w)

### Post Process Interfaces

#### Delivered Post Process Interfaces
The two Post Processes interfaces delivered with NetWorks Core apply only to electric data models. Both of these interface objects are expected to map to the results. 
Update Circuit ID
Use this post-trace process with a trace definition that stops at open features.
The Update Circuit ID post-trace process updates the Circuit1 field in the connectivity table with the user- selected value for the corresponding features in the trace for features in the trace whose Circuit1 is not already equal to the new value. 
Where there is an open feature such as a switch, circuit2 is updated with the circuit1value from the feature connected to the open feature. If more than one feature is connected to the open feature, the circuit2 value is taken from the first feature returned in the query.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Connectivity table Circuit ID 1 column  |  Defines the name of circuit1 column in the connectivity table   |  
|  Connectivity table Circuit ID 2 column  |  Defines the name of the circuit2 column in the connectivity table   |  
|  Connectivity table Node 1 ID column  |  Defines the name of node 1 ID column in the connectivity table   |  
|  Connectivity table Node 2 ID column  |  Defines the name of node 2 ID column in the connectivity table   |  
|  Connectivity table G3E_FID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the connectivity table where the feature identifier is found, typically G3E_FID   |  
|  Query source table ID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the recordset (typically from the traceresult table) that uniquely defines the set of records. In the traceresult table, this is G3E_TNO.   |  
|  Query source table G3E_FID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the recordset (typically from the traceresult table) where the feature identifier is found – typically G3E_FID   |  
|  Open feature expression  |  Defines part of a WHERE clause appended to the SELECT statement that looks for open features in the trace. Column names must be in the Connectivity table and must use the table alias C. Do not include WHERE in this clause.  Example C.STATUS = ‘Open’ It may be necessary to include parentheses around this expression to correctly form the entire WHERE clause. This expression is appended to the SELECT statement as constructed as follows:  SQL> select C.G3E_FID, C.NODE1_ID, C.NODE2_ID from CONNECTIVITY C where C.G3E_FID IN (select S.G3E_FID from TRACERESULT S where S.G3E_TNO =<current trace identifier>) and <open feature expression>;   |  
Prompts: None 
Change Phase
The ChangePhase post-trace process updates the Phase field in the Connectivity table with the target phase value for the corresponding features in the trace whose phase meets a candidate phase criterion. The target phase and candidate phase values are determined by the phase of the initial (seed) feature and the user-selected phase. Both phase values are defined in the [G3E_POSTPROCESSCHANGEPHASE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3nElroj_WZ9J3aVLPh48uA) data table, which defines the relationships between the seed feature, the user-selected phase, the phase of each candidate feature, and the target phase. Only features whose phases meet the criteria in this table are updated.   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Connectivity table phase column  |  Defines the name of phase column in the connectivity table  |  
|  Connectivity table G3E_FID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the connectivity table where the feature identifier is found, typically G3E_FID   |  
|  Phase table  |  Defines the name of the table where the phase code list is found  |  
|  Phase table column  |  Defines the name of the column in the phase table where the phase code list is found  |  
|  Query source table ID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the recordset (typically from the traceresult table) that uniquely defines the set of records. In the traceresult table, this is G3E_TNO.   |  
|  Query source table G3E_FID column  |  Defines the name of the column in the recordset (typically from the traceresult table) where the feature identifier is found, typically G3E_FID   |  
Prompts: None

#### Post Processing Example Package
The example package \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PostProcessExamplePkg.sql updates the LastJobModified field. 
Code Example
-- Start of DDL script for G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG
-- Package G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG
CREATE OR REPLACE
package G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG AS
------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- This package is used to manipulate the trace results.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
type oFeatureIDs is table of Number(10) index by binary_integer;
procedure POSTPROCESS(FeatureIDs in oFeatureIDs,QueryName in VarChar2,ProgID in VarChar2 ); 
-- FeatureIDs: the array of FID of all features involved in the trace results
-- QueryName: the Query Name of the trace results
-- ProgID: the ProgID for the post process object
End G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG;
/
-- End of DDL script for G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG
CREATE OR REPLACE
Package Body G3EPOSTPROCESSPKG
IS
v_ErNum NUMBER;
v_ErTxt VARCHAR2(200);
---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Private procedure.
---------------------------------------------------------------------
procedure SetLastJobModified(FeatureIDs IN oFeatureIDs) IS
v_indexFID integer;
v_FID number;
sTableName VARCHAR2(30);
sActiveJob VARCHAR2(30);
cur INTEGER;
cur1 integer;
status integer;
sSQLUpdate varchar2(512);
stmt VARCHAR2(4000);
rows_processed INTEGER;
sFIDList VARCHAR2(4000);
x NUMBER;
BEGIN
--Get active job
sActiveJob := ltt_user.getactivejob;
--Get the component table name from G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE
cur := DBMS_SQL.OPEN_CURSOR;
cur1 := DBMS_SQL.OPEN_CURSOR;
stmt := 'select G3E_COMPONENTTABLE from G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE where G3E_ANO = (select G3E_SUPPORTANO from G3E_WORKMGMT where G3E_TYPE = ''JobIdentifier'')'; 
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(stmt);
DBMS_SQL.PARSE(cur1, stmt, dbms_sql.v7);
DBMS_SQL.DEFINE_COLUMN(cur1, 1, sTableName,30);
rows_processed := DBMS_SQL.EXECUTE(cur1);
rows_processed := DBMS_SQL.FETCH_ROWS(cur1);
DBMS_SQL.COLUMN_VALUE(cur1, 1, sTableName);
if sTableName is not null then
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(sTableName);
-- Build FID list
sFIDList := '(';
v_indexFID := FeatureIDs.first;
While v_indexFID < FeatureIDs.Last loop
v_FID := FeatureIDs(v_indexFID);
sFIDList := sFIDList || v_FID || ',';
end loop;
sFIDList := sFIDList || v_FID || ')';
-- Check to see if the table contains the fid.
stmt := 'select count(*) FROM ' || rtrim(sTableName) || ' where G3E_FID IN ' || sFIDList; 
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(stmt);
DBMS_SQL.PARSE(cur1, stmt, dbms_sql.v7);
DBMS_SQL.DEFINE_COLUMN(cur1, 1, x);
rows_processed := DBMS_SQL.EXECUTE(cur1);
rows_processed := DBMS_SQL.FETCH_ROWS(cur1);
DBMS_SQL.COLUMN_VALUE(cur1, 1, x);
IF x > 0 THEN
--Update the component table
--Build SQL string 1
sSQLUpdate := 'Update ' || rtrim(sTableName) || ' set JOB_LAST_MODIFIED = ''' || sActiveJob || ''' where G3E_FID in ' || sFIDList; 
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(sSQLUpdate);
DBMS_SQL.PARSE(cur, sSQLUpdate, dbms_sql.v7);
status := DBMS_SQL.EXECUTE(cur);
end if;
v_indexFID := FeatureIDs.Next(v_indexFID);
end if;
DBMS_SQL.close_cursor(cur);
DBMS_SQL.CLOSE_CURSOR(cur1);
EXCEPTION
WHEN OTHERS THEN
if DBMS_SQL.is_open(cur) then
DBMS_SQL.close_cursor(cur);
end if;
if DBMS_SQL.is_open(cur1) then
DBMS_SQL.close_cursor(cur1);
end if;
v_ErNum := SQLCODE;
V_ErTxt := SUBSTR(SQLERRM,1,200);
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'SetLastJobModified' || CHR(10) || v_ErTxt);
RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR (-20001, 'SetLastJobModified' || CHR(10) || v_ErTxt ); 
end SetLastJobModified;
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Public procedure.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
PROCEDURE POSTPROCESS
( FeatureIDs IN oFeatureIDs,
QueryName IN VarChar2,
ProgID IN VarChar2)
IS
-- Define local variables
BEGIN
--The customer's SQL add here
if ProgID = 'PPPSvcs.UpdateCircuit' then
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( ProgID );
SetLastJobModified(FeatureIDs );
end if;
EXCEPTION
WHEN OTHERS THEN
v_ErNum := SQLCODE;
V_ErTxt := SUBSTR(SQLERRM,1,200);
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'POSTPROCESS' || CHR(10) || v_ErTxt);
RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR (-20001, 'POSTPROCESS' || CHR(10) || v_ErTxt );
END; -- procedure POSTPROCESS
END;-- package POSTPROCESS
/

### Redline Group Interfaces
Redline Group interfaces allow the user to group one or more plot redline elements (lines, points, or areas) together as a redline so that certain operations affect all redline elements in the group. 
This interface is launched when the user makes a selection on the Redline Group Type drop-down list available from the Plotting/Redlining toolbar, which is available when a plot window is active. The interface can display dialog boxes for additional user input. 
The workflow for running a Redline Group interface is as follows:
  1. Open a work space.
  2. Open a new plot window.
  3. Click Place Redline Groups to place. 
The Redline Group interface is invoked. This interface determines the geometry of the redline elements to create and returns them to the caller. It also determines whether the group can be moved by the user before placement. 
If the Redline Group interface allows the user to move the group, it displays in dynamics.
  4. Click in the plot window to place the redline group. Otherwise, the redline group is placed at the location determined by the interface object. 


Related Topic
[Implementing Redline Group Objects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n4IzB9zzeDfxQVL3l9yAow)

### Relationship Attribute Interfaces

#### Delivered Relationship Attribute Interfaces
NetWorks Core delivers the following Relationship Attribute interfaces: 
CircuitNumberValidation
Retrieves the attribute from the related feature that contains the circuit identifier and copies it into the active feature. On most features, the same operation is configured and performed on only one attribute of the two designating the circuit when the feature is not switchable. In this case, the same value is copied to both attributes if both fields are specified as input to the interface. For switchable devices, the validation software determines if the feature is associated with multiple circuits and stores the identifiers in the appropriate fields.   
|  Parameter  |  Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  bSwitchable  |  Boolean  |  A value of -1 (True) for devices such as switches that can connect two circuits or a value of 0 (False) for most features in the network—for example, conductor, transformer, or fuse   |  
|  sCircuitField1  |  String  |  Name of the attribute containing the circuit designation for the first circuit  |  
|  sCircuitField2  |  String  |  Name of the attribute containing the circuit designation for the second circuit  |  
The metadata entries in G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION should include one row for each non-switchable feature specifying the circuit one attribute in both the active and related features. For switchable features, a set of rows should exist that compares the circuit one attribute in the switchable feature to the circuit one attribute in all of the related non-switchable features. A second set of rows should exist that compares the circuit two attribute in the switchable features to the circuit one attribute in the related, non-switchable features. 
A data model trigger is appropriate for the non-switchable features to copy the circuit one attribute value into the circuit two attribute value. 
Execute Processing: On non-switchable features, set both circuit one and circuit two to the same value as is contained in one of the connected features. On switchable features, check all of the related features, and copy the identifiers appropriately. 
Validate Processing: Compare the circuit identifiers to the related features. Flag mismatches. The severity level of the error is as specified in metadata. 
PhaseValidation
Compares the phase value in the active feature to the related feature. If both features have a phase, the active feature is compared to the related one to ensure that each phase exists in the related feature. 
Parameters:  None 
Execute Processing: Retrieve the phase attribute from the related feature. If not Null, determine whether or not the active feature's phases are contained in the related feature. 
Validate Processing:  Verify that the value in the attribute matches the related feature's attribute. The severity level of the error is defined in metadata. 
SimpleCopy
Copies an attribute from the related feature to the feature being placed based on the input parameter.   
|  Parameter  |  Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  bCopyOnlyOnNull  |  Boolean  |  A value of -1 (True) indicates that the value should only be copied if the current value is Null. A value of 0 (False) indicates the value should always be copied.   |  
Execute Processing:  If specified, only copy from the related feature when the active feature's value is Null. Otherwise, copy the attribute from the related feature to the active feature. 
Validate Processing: Verify that the values match based on the copy indicator. The error severity is configured in metadata.

### Relationship Geometry Interfaces

#### Land Management Relationship Geometry Interfaces
Relationship Geometry interfaces for Land Management propagate changes through the hierarchy of cadastral features only from parents to children. So, if a cadastral edge (the child of two cadastral nodes) is updated by NodeEdgeRGI as a consequence of one of its parent cadastral node's being moved, the change is further propagated only to the parcels related to the cadastral edge (children of the updated cadastral edge), and not to the parent cadastral nodes. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Relationship Geometry interfaces for use with Land Management: 
NodeEdgeRGI
NodeEdgeRGI is invoked when a cadastral node is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between a cadastral node and a cadastral edge only if the node is coincident with one of the edge's endpoints. If a cadastral node is moved, the NodeEdgeRGI moves the previously connected endpoints of related cadastral edges so that they remain coincident with the node.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  
|  Situation before   
moving a   
cadastral node.   |  User moves the  
cadastral node.   |  NodeEdgeRGI updates the  
related cadastral edges.   |  
During validation, this RGI checks that a cadastral node is coincident with one of the related cadastral edge's endpoints. 
EdgeNodeRGI
EdgeNodeRGI and the EdgeAreaRGI are invoked when a cadastral edge is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between the cadastral edge and cadastral nodes only if the edge's endpoints are coincident with the nodes. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the cadastral edge's endpoints are coincident with the related cadastral nodes. 
EdgeAreaRGI
EdgeAreaRGI and the EdgeNodeRGI are invoked when a cadastral edge is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between a cadastral edge and a parcel or building only if the cadastral edge is identical to one of the edges on the parcel's or building's boundary. 
If a cadastral edge is modified (usually by NodeEdgeRGI as a consequence of a moved cadastral node), EdgeAreaRGI updates the related parcels or buildings so edges on their boundaries remain identical to the cadastral edge. 
For each related parcel or building, EdgeAreaRGI collects all related cadastral edges and regenerates the parcel or building. Relationships must be established between the cadastral edges selected to regenerate the area and cadastral nodes common to these edges. EdgeAreaRGI considers two cadastral edges to be connected only if their common endpoints are related to the same cadastral node. Coincidence of endpoints is not sufficient to consider the cadastral edges to be connected.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  
|  Situation before   
modifying  
cadastral edges.   |  User modifies  
cadastral edges.   |  EdgeAreaRGI updates the  
related parcel.   |  
During validation, this RGI checks that the cadastral edge is identical with one of the edges on the parcel's/building's boundary. 
AreaEdgeRGI
AreaEdgeRGI is invoked when parcel or building is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between the parcel or building and the cadastral edge only if the edge on the parcel's or building's boundary is identical to the cadastral edge. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the edges on the parcel's or building's boundary are identical to the related cadastral edges. 
LowerToHigherAreaRGI
LowerToHigherAreaRGI is invoked for cadastral and political areas where there is a higher-level related area for the active feature, such as for a parcel if there is a related block. The RGI approves the relationship between a lower-level (parcel) and higher-level area (block) only if the lower-level area is completely covered by the higher-level area. 
If a lower-level area is updated (usually as a consequence of moving a cadastral node and propagating the change through the hierarchy of cadastral features), the LowerToHigherAreaRGI updates the related higher-level area. Accordingly, it continues to cover the lower-level area.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=uLFIR1lsC3CdRkS72jh33A)  |  
|  Situation before modifying   
the parcels (block covering the two parcels is  
identical with the union of   
the parcels).   |  User modified the   
parcels (parcels are  
dashed).   |  LowerToHigherAreaRGI updates the related block.  |  
During validation, this RGI checks that the lower-level area is completely covered by the higher-level area. 
When updating a higher-level area based on the modifications of the lower-level areas, one of the following approaches can be used: 
  * Always generated as the union of lower-level areas
  * Generated as the union of lower-level areas and itself

|  Example Assume that 5 is the G3E_RINO of the LowerToHigherAreaRGI.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  1  |  Lower2HigherIsUnion  |  1 if higher- level area has to be the union of lower- level areas, 0 otherwise  |  4  |

HigherToLowerAreaRGI
HigherToLowerAreaRGI is invoked for cadastral and political areas where there is a related lower-level area for the active feature—for example, for a block where there is a relationship between the block and a parcel. The RGI approves the relationship between a higher-level (block) and lower-level area (parcel) only if the higher-level area completely covers the lower-level area. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the higher-level area completely covers each of the related lower-level areas. It further checks that none of the related lower-level areas overlap each other. The RGI can also check whether the union of related lower-level areas is identical with the validated higher-level area. This optional checking is configurable in metadata.   
|  Example Assume that 6 is the G3E_RINO of the HigherToLowerAreaRGI.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  6  |  1  |  Higher2LowerIsUnionn  |  1 if higher- level area has to be the union of lower-level areas, 0 otherwise  |  4  |  
 |

#### Length Management Relationship Geometry Interfaces
Relationship Geometry interfaces for Length Management propagate changes through the hierarchy of length features from parents to children. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Relationship Geometry interfaces for use with Length Management. 
GTLengthManyOwnershipRelationshipGeometry
When a length feature is related to another length feature through a many-ownership relationship, a length component instance representing the parent is inserted into the child length feature. If that length component instance is to be included in the total length of the child length feature, its total length is updated, which updates its related child length features. When a length feature is disassociated from another length feature through a many-ownership relationship, the length component instance that was representing the parent is removed from the child length feature. If that length component instance was included in the total length of the child feature, its total length is updated, which updates its related child length features. 
Related Topic
[Length Management Overview](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMmx8LEmlrbbDHinlTKB6w)

### Report Interfaces

#### Delivered Report Interfaces
NetWorks Core delivers the following predefined report interfaces. To see which ones are available in your data model, navigate to the Software Interfaces > Report node in Metadata Explorer. 
See [Implementing Predefined Report Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8g6lZTNafOb3EiTc0FTQIg) for instructions on how to make these Report interfaces available to users. 
  * Cable Pairs Report Interface—A [Cable Pairs Report](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/W9aTSOHJUHGo00cdGBYJbw) interface available in GComms generates a report containing basic network cable-use information. The report types, such as Cable Fill and Cable Fill by Gauge, are specified in the database. The report displays in HTML format. 
  * CSV Report Interface—PRIface.CSVReport writes out a comma-separated value (CSV) file that reflects the contents of the recordset resulting from the analysis. Any previous CSV file contents are replaced. The first line in the CSV file contains the field names separated by commas. This format is useful for transferring information to other applications. 
  * Duct Occupancy Report Interface—A [PRIface.DuctOccupancyReport interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WDgdZO~hBI_C13GMP_8akg) generates an output recordset and passes it to a second report interface for presentation, typically the HTML report interface. 
  * Excel Report Interface—PRIface.ExcelMacroReport writes out a CSV file, replacing any previous contents, and creates a new Excel workbook using the template. The object then executes the macro, passing the path to the CSV file. The macro opens the CSV file and copies its contents into the appropriate worksheet cells for charting. 
This object requires that the Microsoft Excel Object Library delivered with Microsoft Office exist on the client system. 
  * HTML Report Interface—The [HTML Report interface object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMGrbdshaeRmWzATJH6P9Q) provides a way to take the results of the analysis and to convert it to an XML file. This XML is combined with a stylesheet specification (XSL) to produce a formatted HTML file. A Microsoft Internet Explorer window is launched to present the results to the user. 
  * Loop Makeup Report Interface—The [Loop Makeup Report interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IAaHhjNw97qdwL0R5nAFcg) is integrated into the loop makeup functionality available in GComms. 
  * Map Output Report Interface—[PRIface.MapOutputReport](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bEI6j_HfLHLKK2lg2wSvZg) displays features in an input recordset. After the Map Output Report interface is executed, the input recordset is added as a node on the Display Control. The user can check or uncheck the node to control the display of the input recordset. 
  * Oracle Report Interface—PRIface.ADOOracleReport executes the report file using the Oracle report runtime executable, rwrun.exe, which passes the following information to the Oracle report. This executable must exist on the client system. 
    * Report file (*.rdf) retrieved from the argument array 
    * User name, password, and alias that it retrieved from the CCM object and the Connection object 
    * USERNAME=<username>  
QUERYNAME=QueryName  
JOBNAMES=JobNames  
DESTYPE=FILE  
DESNAME=OutputfileName  
DESFORMAT=PDF 
NetWorks Core uses the document path—C:\Documents And Settings\username\My Documents, for example—as the output file path. The output file name uses the report file name (*.rdf) plus file number and changes the extension from .rdf to .pdf. The file number starts at 1 and increases each time the report is run. 
You can create many different report definitions (.rdf), and use the single OracleReport object. 
  * OTDR Marker Placement Report Interface—The [PRIface.OTDRMarkerPlacementReport interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_cPtxzNkHm8LX1c~If6U9w) locates the point of the cable faults and places a graphic marker at the specified distance on the geographic network. To produce a different result than graphic markers on the map, you can replace the delivered interface with a custom interface. 
  * Repair Allocation Report Interface—A [Repair Allocation report](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P7rkbdkGhCA2zKCzcp7seA) displays both features resulting from a break plus all containing features that are common to those features. The report includes the complete containment hierarchy, including the formations, conduits, and ducts common to both features. 
  * ReviewFeatureAllocation Report Interface—The [Review Feature Allocation Report interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rBpMphlft2WYKhC5XH_zuw) available in GComms is integrated into the Review Feature Allocation functionality. The Review Feature Allocation command uses the standard report selection control, which allows custom reports to be defined. 
  * Store Keys Report Interface—PRIface.ADOStoreKeysReport gets the username from the database and writes the recordset keys to the specified table. The first two columns of this table should be G3E_USERNAME and G3E_QUERYNAME. The rest of the columns should exactly match the structure of the query result. This object typically is used in conjunction with another operation.

### Temporary Geometry Placement Interfaces
Temporary geometry is geometry that cannot be selected, edited, or saved to the database or to the work space. It is used primarily in the construction of permanent feature/component geometry—to define guides or construction lines to create better maps during the initial facility placement operations, for example. 
You can do the following with Temporary Geometry Placement interfaces:
  * Add and selectively delete temporary geometry features.
  * Snap, locate, and use construction aids.
  * Create classes for specific temporary geometry placement workflows.
  * Create and destroy temporary geometry during custom construction aids or custom placement techniques as well as custom commands. 
  * Display temporary geometries on the Display Control.


Temporary geometries are placed using the [New Temporary Geometry command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/endZodX0Ib1AasNtajQu0g). After placement, the geometry is added to the legend hierarchy under the Temporary Geometries node.   
|  Examples of temporary geometry
  * A linear component that connects the corners of two buildings to allow the user to place a component somewhere along that line. 
  * A grid of points to which the user can snap for keeping components evenly spaced.

 |  
| --- |  
Using the API, you can design and implement custom Temporary Geometry Placement interfaces tailored to the needs of your site. NetWorks Core delivers the following sample Temporary Geometry Placement interfaces, which you can use as templates, in \GTechnology\Services\Samples\GTCustomization\Interfaces\RelationInterfaces: 
  * SamplePoint.cs for Temporary point
  * SampleLinear.cs for Temporary line
  * SampleArea.cs for Temporary boundary geometry with holes 
  * SampleGrid.cs for Temporary snap grid


[Icons](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4zGWlZmbqI0vhZ1l7qyrLQ) and example Help files for these temporary geometries are delivered with the samples. 
To make the geometries available to client systems, you must install them during setup and then [import and configure them in metadata](javascript:;).

## Optional Data Model

### Communications Tools

#### Pair Count Overview

##### Configuring Pair Count and Strip-Based Pair Count in the Same Database
You can configure the Pair Count subsystem to simultaneously support both pair count and strip-based pair count within the same configuration. A communications company can have private exchanges and outside plant that are built and mapped using the pair count model but which use the strip model in their other exchanges. In these types of configurations, some mechanism is required to inform the count control of whether the current feature's count is defined with pair count or strip-based pair count. The count control uses the naming conventions defined in the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute of the feature's primary attribute component. The value of this attribute defines a single notation from the enumerated notations. If the current feature instance does not contain this attribute, a default notation defined in metadata can be used. These are the different configurations or application behaviors that depend on whether the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute value is defined in the primary attribute component of the current feature and whether a G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT value is defined in metadata. 
  * G3E_COUNTFORMAT and G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT values not defined
If the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute value is not defined in the primary attribute component and the G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT metadata value is not defined, the count control defaults to using the pair naming conventions. This functionality is backward compatible. This configuration is used by communications companies that only use the pair count naming conventions. 
  * G3E_COUNTFORMAT value not defined and G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT value defined
If the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is not defined in the primary attribute component and the G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT metadata value is defined, the count control defaults to the naming conventions defined in metadata. This removes the burden of having to add a G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute to every count- bearing feature's primary component. This configuration is used by communications companies that use a single nomenclature that is not the pair nomenclature. 
  * G3E_COUNTFORMAT value is not Null and G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT value not defined
If the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is defined as not Null and the G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT metadata value is not defined, the count control uses the specified value in the primary component. 
  * G3E_COUNTFORMAT value is Null and G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT value is defined
If the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is defined as Null in the primary attribute component and the G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT metadata value is defined, the count control defaults to the nomenclature defined in metadata. 
  * G3E_COUNTFORMAT value is Null and G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT value is not defined
If the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is defined as Null in the primary attribute and the G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT metadata value is not defined, the count control displays an error message that the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is not set and the software cannot format counts. 
The count control displays on the count tab only when the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute is populated successfully. The error message is configurable and indicates to the user what to do to populate the attribute. You can define a functional interface that fires during AddNew and determines in which exchange the user is placing the feature and sets the naming conventions based on that exchange. 


Data Model Requirements
If a database allows multiple naming conventions to be defined, the count table requires the following field:   
|  Field  |  Type  |  Null  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_COUNTFORMAT  |  NUMBER (1,0)  |  Y  |  
This field stores the format that was used to persist the feature's count into the count table. A value of 1 indicates that the count was persisted using the pair naming convention; a value of 2 indicates that the count was persisted using the strip naming convention.
