##### Preparing a Count-Bearing Feature for Subset Publishing
To allow [publishing of a job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/46qbwFX5xtEWsDh3DJmsBQ) that includes features that have rippled counts, the Upgrade Wizard automatically populates the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_CNO field of count- bearing features as identified as in [G3E_RIPPLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RSpkgYIYsxS~uQ4ccO7vmQ). Pair Count Edit Log Table is the username for the [G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JLEIT3y3Zlm4IQJOtEvOeQ) table. If you add a count- bearing to your data model, you can use Metadata Explorer and manually update the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table. 
This attribute component should not be exposed in Feature Explorer since its contents are maintained by the pair count software when the user runs the [Ripple Count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lSsl1fhjos4dZVEvwBMX6Q), [Throw Count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xZcT3kijc6q4wg8jRX9Vug), and [Cancel Ripple](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xY6xdVb6vXoQXH6oP4jW6Q) commands. 
  * To prepare a count-bearing feature for subset publishing manually:


  1. Select a count bearing feature under Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <Data Connection> > Features > <Feature Name> > Feature Components. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260496), or right-click and select Insert a new row. Insert a new row in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table. 
  3. In the G3E_CNO field, select the Pair Count Edit Log Table (this is the username for G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER) from the drop- down list. 
  4. [Populate the other fields](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA) in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table. 
  5. Click OK. 
  6. Repeat Steps 1-5 for each count bearing feature.
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260496) to commit your edits to the database.

##### Strip-Based Pair Count
Strip-based pair count defines a unique assignment of a group of conductors within a cable throughout the entire cable network and is used the same way the [pair count naming convention is used](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zTD5yIbEQ1ZTB8HqmZUi9w). A strip is a bundle of pairs within a cable. In the 10-pair or decade model, a strip is a bundle of 10 pairs; therefore, a 100-pair cable contains 10 strips. Strip 001 contains pairs 1-10, strip 002 contains pairs 11-20, and so on. Not all data models use the decade model; some use bundle sizes of 50 and 100. All these example diagrams assume use of the decade model. The diagram below illustrates a 100-pair cable with a cable designation of 023:   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260477)  |  
| --- |  
The strip naming conventions also allow multiple non-contiguous ranges to be defined on the same line. The diagram below is another example of a 100-pair cable using multiple non-contiguous ranges per line:   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260477)  |  
| --- |  
In most cases a distribution point is fed by a whole number of strips. For example, a terminal is fed by 10 pairs, 20 pairs, and so on. However, sometimes it is necessary to split a strip to provide service to more than one distribution point from a single strip. When this happens the network planners need to record which pairs within the strip are within each of the splits. The network planners assign each split strip a class identifier and define which pairs are in the split. The following example shows the first five pairs of strip 3 feeding the left-most terminal with a class identifier of 'A' and the last five pairs of strip 3 feeding the right-most terminal with an assigned class identifier of 'B'. The diagram below displays the nomenclature used to define the counts for the feature:   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260477)  |  
| --- |  
Some data models do not display the whole definition when annotating split strips to map views. These models remove the pair definition from the annotation so that only the strip number and the split strip class identifier are annotated as follows:   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260477)  |  
| --- |  
Occasionally, multiple distribution points are fed by the same strip. These are called parallel strips. Parallel strips are defined by a special parallel indicator, 'P', and a specified identifier. The diagram below shows two terminals being fed by strip 1:   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260477)  |  
| --- |  
Data Model Requirements
If a database allows multiple noncontiguous count ranges to be defined on the same line of count, the count table requires the following field:   
|  Field  |  Type  |  Null  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  RANGE_SEQ  |  NUMBER (38,0)  |  Y  |  
This field stores the order in which the count ranges were defined. The value is used when the software recreates the counts when a count-bearing features is explored or edited.

##### Supporting Pair Count Manipulation
These communications functions support [pair count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zTD5yIbEQ1ZTB8HqmZUi9w) manipulation: 
Pair Count Control
The [Pair Count control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tWqHedpQwg8moXcskPQLMw) is an optimized user interface that allows a user to edit pair counts on features. It provides a list of source feeds for the feature being edited and support for drag and drop editing. A user can drag a count from the source to the current feature to assign that count to the feature. 
The Pair Count control also supports grouping of pair count lines into classes. Available classes are defined by metadata on a per-feature basis. A class name can be modified after it is added to the count to allow the user to refine the details about a group of counts, for example, the source and destination switch. 
Pair counts are dynamically parsed during edit, and visual feedback is provided for any syntactical errors in the entered count. 
Before a count is committed to the database, the Pair Count control performs metadata driven validation of source feeds, total size, pair duplication, and designation prefix. Based on the defined validation error levels, the user is presented with an error, a warning, or nothing at all when validation errors occur. 
Ripple
The [Ripple command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lSsl1fhjos4dZVEvwBMX6Q) is used to propagate count changes to affected features and to display those changes to support work prints. 
The Ripple command integrates the Pair Count control for editing and provides users with a consistent interface for all count manipulation regardless of what operation they are performing. 
After the ripple is completed, the user is provided with an interactive summary of the features that were rippled. This report can be output to a printable report format like HTML and can be used to push features into Feature Explorer for further editing. This report provides a concise view of the changes that the Ripple command made to the counts of all affected features by presenting the user with a view of how the pair count looked before and after the ripple. 
The Ripple command ripples both pair counts and associated work order numbers, thus keeping changes to counts in sync with the jobs that initiated their modification. 
Rippled features are logged in the [G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JLEIT3y3Zlm4IQJOtEvOeQ) table to support the Throw command, eliminating the need to reanalyze the network to determine which features need to be thrown. This makes the Throw command more efficient.   
|  Example Pairs 51 through 100 of cable 10 are rippled downstream to cable 20, pairs 1 through 50.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260473)  |  
| --- |  
Throw
The [Throw command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xZcT3kijc6q4wg8jRX9Vug) is used to collapse rippled counts after work has been completed in the field. By default, the Count subsystem always collapses contiguous lines of rippled counts. If the software is [configured to not collapse contiguous lines](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iHTy1jqvRAU~kZXlIFqV7A) of rippled counts, edits made in Feature Explorer also exhibits the same behavior and not collapse them either. The Throw command collapses the counts before the job is closed. 
Throw removes bracketed pair counts for the work order being thrown. It can identify features that could not be thrown due to work order dependencies. This situation occurs when a user attempts to throw a ripple that has previous ripples that have not been thrown. This command provides an interactive summary of the features that were thrown.   
|  Example Pairs 51 through 100 of cable 10 are thrown downstream to cable 20, pairs 1 through 50  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260473)  |  
| --- |

### Duct Management

#### Configuring Duct Management in an Existing Database

##### Configuring Duct Management Attributes
NetWorks Core requires the following attributes for a duct feature to describe the row and column positions for both ends of the duct. The information is populated in the [G3E_DUCT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bdWhvnmf~2S3I4TRh9CzHw) metadata table: 
G3E_ASSIGNMENTANO  
G3E_FROMROWPOSANO  
G3E_FROMCOLPOSANO  
G3E_TOROWPOSANO  
G3E_TOCOLPOSANO 
If a user creates or repositions a duct using the Duct Configuration control, the appropriate geometry is marked as [stale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262174). This assists in the incremental placement of the duct, because only stale ducts need to be placed and/or replaced. The following attributes, also populated in the G3E_DUCT table, are required to store the current state of the duct geometry, one for each end: 
When you use Feature Explorer and the Duct Configuration control to change the layout of the ducts in a formation, the graphics on the map no longer match the layout as defined in the Duct Configuration control; the graphics are now stale with respect to the attribution that defines the formation layout. Use the Place Formation command to replace or update the graphics. The Duct Configuration control and the Place Formation command use the stale graphics flags (defined in metadata) to communicate this information. 
G3E_FROMGEOMSTALEANO  
G3E_TOGEOMSTALEANO 
The formation, populated in the [G3E_FORMATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zStlwzYYFFlYHe5QtjPZ9Q) table, that contains the duct also needs two attributes to record the From and To end of a stale formation: 
G3E_FROMGEOMSTALEANO  
G3E_TOGEOMSTALEANO 
  * To configure the duct and formation attributes:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Ducts. 
  2. Select the duct feature, and select values for the required attributes from the drop-down lists. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Duct Management Formation Definition. 
  4. Select the formation and select attributes from the drop-down list.

##### Configuring Duct Management Metadata
You can use Metadata Explorer to configure your metadata for duct management. This workflow assumes that you have already created duct, inner duct (optional), and formation features and attributes. 
The [G3E_GEOMGENINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/B0KQ9olEVKTY~SpGdpJtdA) table and the [G3E_GEOMGENARGUMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uI5AmeasvMWdCHqhzstKoQ) are both populated when you run the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateDuctMetadata.sql for a new database or \GTechnolog\PLSQL\metadata\installduct.sql for an existing database. These tables reference other duct management metadata tables and you typically do not have to change them. 
  * To configure duct management metadata:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Duct Management Interface node, and select a parameter to edit. 
The [G3E_DUCTIFACE.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WU8MlP9KTpz4DA2jW5KJ1w) values show the interrelationships of the duct management tables. This table is populated when you run the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateDuctMetadata.sql for a new database or \GTechnolog\PLSQL\metadata\installduct.sql for an existing database, and you select or type values in the parameters to suit your data model. 
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Ducts node, and add a new row to the G3E_DUCT table. 
The [G3E_DUCT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bdWhvnmf~2S3I4TRh9CzHw) table is where you define ducts and inner ducts. From the drop-down lists, select the duct or inner duct feature and select attributes for the duct or inner duct. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Formation Definitions node, and add a new row to the G3E_FORMATION table. 
The [G3E_FORMATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zStlwzYYFFlYHe5QtjPZ9Q) table is where you define the formation that contains the ducts. Select the formation and the attributes for it from the drop-down lists. 
  4. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Duct Management Formation Definitions node, and add a new row to the G3E_DUCTFORMATION table. 
The [G3E_DUCTFORMATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tKLWvtuvQ6XDR4N0HD89gQ) table is where you define the number of columns and rows for each duct formation. Create a row-column definition, select the duct feature from the drop-down list, and assign row and column numbers to that definition. 
  5. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Duct Graphic Configuration node, and add a new row to the G3E_DUCTCONFIGGRAPHIC table. 
The [G3E_DUCTCONFIGGRAPHIC](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0_fusOYXeV2LW7qKBQMbDg) table is where you specify the graphic components to create when you place a new formation or duct feature. When you place a formation or duct, you probably have to place more than one graphic component. From the drop-down lists, you specify if the component is a From or To component, and specify if the component is a DuctPoint or FormationPoint from the predefined G3E_GEOMGENINTERFACE table. 
  6. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Duct Management > Ducts and Formations > Geometry Generation Interfaces > <arguments> node. 
The [G3E_GGDATA](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s_2yRcE3PZqMF6G74GVkxA) table is where you specify the layout and spacing of the formation and duct components on either the Xoffset or Yoffset argument node. 
  7. To configure an alternative to the functional interface SetJobIdentifierAttribute for updates performed using the Duct Configuration control, use the G3EDUCTCONTROLEDITPKG package delivered in the \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt folder. 
There may be attributes that need to be updated when edits occur in the Duct Configuration control, For example, the Job Identifier attribute for a duct might need to have a custom value placed in it for new ducts. Since the processing of the Duct Configuration control is done in the database and not on the client, a functional interface does not work for this automatic update. Instead, use the G3EDUCTCONTROLEDITPKG PLSQL package. An example for this package is provided in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries folder. 
  8. To add custom code that makes changes to features placed using the[Add Related Feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yGHl~jR_3R42zeO46VPsGg) command, use the G3E_DEEPCOPYPOSTPROCESS package in the \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt folder. An example for this package is also delivered in the \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt folder. 
  9. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257702) to commit your changes to the database.

##### Configuring the Duct Configuration Control
The [Duct Configuration control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AKYI3Kuz~5qBsCiyjhGFrQ) appears as a tab inside Feature Explorer. If a user does not select a duct on the map or in the Feature Explorer tree view, by default the attributes for all the ducts are displayed in the grid and editing an attribute changes that attribute in all the ducts. If the user selects one or more ducts, the attribute grid displays the attributes for the selected ducts. 
The attributes that are shown on the grid are determined by the number of ducts selected and by the dialog type you specify for the feature in [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw). The dialog types let you determine which attributes to present to a user and when to present them. These are dialog types available for the Duct Configuration control: 
  * Single Edit. Used when the control is in Edit mode and only one duct is selected
  * Multi Edit. Used when the control is in Edit mode and more than one duct is selected or no ducts are selected 
  * Single Review. Used when the control is in Review mode and only one duct is selected
  * Multi Review. Used when the control is in Review mode and more than one duct is selected or no ducts are selected 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700) The assignment ANO (G3E_DUCT.G3E_ASSIGNMENTANO) for duct and inner duct should not be included on Duct Configuration dialog tabs when the dialog type is Multi Review and Multi Edit. 
  * To configure the Duct Configure control:


  1. Create a new dialog tab:
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialog Tabs > Unassigned Tabs node and create a new tab. 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Type a name for the dialog tab in the G3E_USERNAME field and select the tab's orientation from the G3E_ORIENTATION field. 
    4. In the G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE field, select GTCtlInfo.DuctConfigurationControl from the drop-down list. 
    5. Select or type values as required to define the tab.
    6. To complete your dialog tab definition, click OK. 
  2. Associate the tab with a dialog box for a new or existing feature:
To add the dialog box for a new feature, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialogs > <dialog type> node. 
OR
To add the dialog box for an existing feature, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialogs > <dialog type> <feature name> node. 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. In the G3E_DTNO field, select the new dialog tab you just added.
    3. In the G3E_FNO field, select the appropriate feature.
    4. In the G3E_ORDINAL field, type a value that determines where the tab is presented during review or edit operations. 
    5. To complete your dialog tab definition, click OK. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700) to commit the changes to the database. 
  4. Add tab attributes to the tab:
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Attribute Presentation > Dialogs > <dialog type> > <feature name> > Tabs > Tab Definition > Tab Attributes node. 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Select or type values as required to define attributes for the tab.
    4. To complete your tab attribute definition, click OK. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257700) to commit the changes to the database.

#### Duct Management Data Model Constraints
The following are constraints on the duct management data model:
  * Formations and ducts are features in the model, and you can create more than one formation feature and more than one duct feature. However, formations and ducts cannot be components of another feature. 
  * Formations and ducts can not have required graphic components. Any graphic components are optional. 
  * Attributes on the duct feature store the row and column positions for each end, but those attributes can be stored in any component. Graphic components can be deleted and recreated when graphics are placed without loss of information. This means that graphic components cannot carry other attribution attribution significant to the feature itself. 
  * You need different graphic components to represent each end (From and To) of the conduit. For example, the component for the duct symbol for the From end has a different component number than the component for the duct symbol for the To end. 
  * The graphics for a duct formation can be generated based on a regular grid pattern. The software lets you specify the horizontal and vertical spacing of this grid in metadata. NetWorks Core software assumes that the spacing is constant for a given formation feature. Different formation features can have different spacing, but a specific formation always has the same spacing. 


Related Topic
[Merging Conduit Examples](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/29Rtiz9KI7PoAK7WWQSgAg)

#### The Duct Management Data Model
In a communications data model, [formations and ducts are required features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4L_r3AO0MdmVh8CUuZAj7Q). Inner ducts are optional. You can have a container level above formation (such as conduit). All the features are modeled as distinct features. Typically, a conduit owns zero or one formations, and a formation owns one or more ducts. A duct can contain zero or more inner ducts. A duct is owned by one formation, and an inner duct is owned by one duct. 
The concepts of duct, formation, conduit, and inner duct are modeled as separate features. The formation and duct features require several [attributes to describe them](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ITSxQ2MbplkJg7r_vbnB5g). Conduits have a primary graphic component; they are the principle graphic element in this context, because formations are not required to have graphics. This diagram shows the many-to-many ownership relationship between these features: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262172)
Duct, inner duct, and formation features need specific components for placement, though they can have others as required by your model.

### Feature Allocation

#### Configuring Data for Feature Allocation
To configure your data for feature allocation, you must first [define your features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~RXdRpXhMKGt2ZtFIW14cA) (manhole, pole, conduit, formation, duct, inner duct, cable) and the many-to-many ownership relationship between these features. For determining the route between two nodes, you must [configure a trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nXMqbwDUkoJX17h94CAHLQ) and create at least one [allocation business rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8axlYgxqujUMQeJwBvvt6Q).

#### Custom Processing for Feature Allocation
The G3EFEATUREALLOCCONTROLPKG PL/SQL database procedure performs custom processing at the end of a [feature allocation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jwse1SI0SaeqSPM5D49ISA) operation instead of firing functional interfaces. Typically you are implementing the equivalent of one or more functional interfaces in this procedure. 
NetWorks Core delivers a version of the G3EFEATUREALLOCCONTROLPKG PL/SQL package that you can modify to perform post processing for feature allocation. Use an SQL editor to implement the interface to this package: 
SQL> CREATE OR REPLACE package G3EFEATUREALLOCCONTROLPKG AS   
FUNCTION Version return Varchar2; 
pragma restrict_references (Version,WNDS,WNPS,RNDS); 
FUNCTION CMVersion return Varchar2; 
pragma restrict_references (CMVersion,WNDS,WNPS,RNDS); 
procedure FeatureAllocated(FNO in NUMBER, 
FID in NUMBER, 
AllocationFeatures in G3E_ALLOCATION_TYPE); End G3EFEATUREALLOCCONTROLPKG;
The FeatureAllocated procedure is called after a feature has successfully been allocated to the set of allocation features that are supplied in the AllocationFeatures argument to this procedure. This is the same set of features returned by the [feature allocation business rule's RouteAndAllocationFeatures](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8axlYgxqujUMQeJwBvvt6Q) function. The allocated feature is identified by the FNO and FID arguments. That feature is already contained in all of the features where AllocationFeatures.G3E_ALLOCATE=1 when the FeatureAllocated procedure is called.   
|  Example An attribute on a series of ducts indicates whether the duct is occupied or not occupied. After a feature allocation operation, you need to update that attribute on each duct in the AllocationFeatures table where G3E_ALLOCATE=1.   |  
| --- |  
By default, the empty version of the G3EFEATUREALLOCCONTROLPKG package is installed in the database. You must have some version of this package installed even if you do not use feature allocation in your data model. An example version of this package, which performs the same function as the SetJobIdentifierAttribute functional interface for a particular data model, is also supplied with the product. These files and their locations are as follows:   
|  File Name  |  Definition  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  \GTechnology\PLSQL\ltt\g3efeaturealloccontrolpkg.sql  |  Empty version of package  |  
|  \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\g3efeaturealloccontrolexamplepkg.sql  |  Example version  |

#### Factors that Influence Feature Allocation Trace Performance
Typically [you define](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1OetDdzTXoJ69eME_R_e3w) a [sequential minimum path](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/m_SRhE7t~Ja5kQNBkdiQsQ) trace for Feature Allocation. This trace finds the path between two features (the start and end features of the allocation route) that has the minimum cost; in this case, the cost is simply the accumulated length of the conduits and other features in the path. The intent is to find the shortest path, that is, the one that requires examining the least amount of conduit and/or ducts. 
In most uses of minimum cost tracing, the destination feature is found quickly, so a possible minimum cost becomes known quickly. Moreover, other paths typically exceed this cost fairly soon, so the trace does not examine a large number of paths. Also, most networks in which minimum cost tracing is used have additional criteria on the trace to prevent tracing all those paths. 
The following factors may [degrade the performance](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PwHhb9MVp_bp0e9M3MO7og) of a Feature Allocation trace based on a minimum path algorithm: 
  * The network consists of many branches and join points, which multiplies the number of possible paths that may be considered as paths by the trace. 
  * User requests routes that are very long, spanning hundreds of iterations. This requires the trace to consider many more paths before it has an estimate of the minimum cost. 
  * The distance that a route can span is not limited, so users are unconstrained in the work they can impose on the database and the system. 
  * The costs of [branch and join](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYgzMHmWT1EeCkUOq9FzCQ) paths are very similar, thus very few of them can be abandoned in the early iterations since it is less likely that their cost exceed a known minimum cost to the goal. 
  * The requirement to include [single-node devices](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYgzMHmWT1EeCkUOq9FzCQ) like manholes and passage connectors in the route requires using a sequential trace algorithm, which is more expensive to perform than regular traces. 


These factors are discussed in more detail in the [Factors that Influence Minimum Path Trace Performance](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SYgzMHmWT1EeCkUOq9FzCQ) topic and some solutions are proposed in the [Minimum Path Trace Performance Solutions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PwHhb9MVp_bp0e9M3MO7og) topic. 
Related Topic
[Trace Performance Considerations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c7CJWjG5XUlMd5BvLasCIQ)

#### Feature Allocation Business Rules

##### Defining Business Rules for Feature Allocation
You can use Metadata Explorer to define [business rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8axlYgxqujUMQeJwBvvt6Q) and map them to features. A business rule determines the allocation of the feature. 
  * To define business rules for feature allocation:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Feature Allocation Parameters node to update the [G3E_ALLOCATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VQo3uLhknT61yGnW1A1QAQ) table. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258019) Because this table is populated when you you run \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateDuctMetadata.sql to begin configuring duct management in your database, the TraceIdentifier parameter is the only parameter you need to update. Type the number of the trace for feature allocation in the G3E_PARAMETER1 field. 
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Packages node and add a row to the [G3E_ARPACKAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fQI8b_eNDGU84RUhY1g2YA) table, which contains a list of the Allocation Business Rule Packages. In the G3E_PACKAGE field, type a name for the package you are defining. You can define any number of packages to suit your data model. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Packages > <Package Name> node, and add a new row to the [G3E_ALLOCATIONRULEARG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fc~a6q2jCdfi5eXKJorySQ) table, which contains a list of arguments to be passed to an allocation business rule package. 
    1. In the G3E_ARGUMENTNAME field, type a name for the argument. 
    2. In the G3E_DESCRIPTION field, type a description for the argument. 
    3. In the G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE field, select the type for the argument from the drop-down list. 
  4. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Allocation Rules > <Rule Name> > Rule Arguments node, and update the [G3E_ALLOCRULEARGVAL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jPbtDwlWH5GHUIczqtPTKQ) table which is used to specify the argument values to be passed to the database package that implements an allocation business rule. Type a value for the argument in the G3E_VALUE field. 
  5. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Allocation Rule node, and add a new row to the [G3E_ALLOCATIONRULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/02GSTlMYF2i3uBj4cHuHzA) table, which contains a list of the allocation business rules. This table associates an allocation business rule package with a group of allocation rule arguments. 
    1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a name for the business rule. 
    2. In the G3E_ARPNO field, select the package name to use for the rule. 
  6. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Core Schema Control > Feature Allocation > Mapping node, and add a new row to the [G3E_ALLOCATIONRULEMAP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/h6fXt5oDXOBoRnL6uPVROA) table, which maps features to be allocated with the allocation business rule package to be used to determine their allocation. 
    1. In the G3E_FNO field, select the feature to be allocated from the drop-down list. 
    2. In the G3E_ARNO field, select the package name you want to map to the feature from the drop-down list. 
    3. In the G3E_RNO field, select the relationship to be used to allocate the feature. 
  7. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258019) to commit your changes to the database.

#### Oracle Object Types
These Oracle object types are temporary data tables produced by executing the allocation business rules. The allocation business rules return their information using a recordset with these definitions. 
Your business rules can use these types of names to declare nested tables in your package to hold your results. 
G3E_ALLOCATION_TYPE  
|  Field Name  |  Field Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ALLOCID  |  Long  |  Unique ID for rows within this table  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Long  |  FNO of feature in this allocation  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Long  |  FID of feature in this allocation  |  
|  G3E_INPUT  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that this feature was an input feature to the AllocationBusinessRule.Execute procedure. Usually this indicates that the feature is part of the original trace.   |  
|  G3E_ALLOCATIONORDINAL  |  Long  |  The ordinal of this feature within this table. Sorting on this column causes the features in this table to be in trace traversal order from the first feature of the trace to the last feature of the trace.   |  
|  G3E_CANALLOCATE  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that the input feature may be allocated to this feature.  |  
|  G3E_ALLOCATE  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that AllocationBusinessRule.Execute has determined that the input feature should be allocated to this feature.   |  
|  G3E_HASALTERNATIVES  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that AllocationBusinessRule.Execute had more than one valid feature to choose from when it picked this feature as an allocation feature.   |  
|  G3E_LEVEL  |  Long  |  Hierarchical level of this feature within the trace/allocation. This field is used by AllocationBusinessRule.Execute to communicate the level of a feature. This field allows the FeatureAllocationControl to display the route allocation in a manner that is appropriate for the user.   |  
|  G3E_DISPLAY  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that this route and/or allocation feature should be displayed in the FeatureAllocationDialog. This property is useful if you want to use your G3E_ALLOCATION object to store features that the user see.  Example If an allocation feature has alternates (G3E_HASALTERNATIVES = True ), you may want to save those alternates rather than recalculate them in your AlternateAllocationFeatures procedure. If you set G3E_DISPLAY = False, those features are not displayed.   |  
G3E_AA_TYPE  
|  Field Name  |  Field Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_AAID  |  Long  |  Unique ID for rows within this table.  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Long  |  FNO of feature in this alternate Aalocation.  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Long  |  FID of feature in this alternate allocation.  |  
|  G3E_INPUT  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that this feature was the input feature to the AllocationBusinessRule.AlternateRouteAllocationFeatures procedure.   |  
|  G3E_AAORDINAL  |  Long  |  The ordinal of this feature within this table.  |  
|  G3E_CANALLOCATE  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that the input feature can be allocated to this feature.  |  
|  G3E_ALLOCATE  |  Boolean  |   |  
|  G3E_LEVEL  |  Long  |  Hierarchical level of this feature within the trace/allocation. This field is used by AllocationBusinessRule.AlternateRouteAllocationFeatures to communicate the level of a feature. This field allows the FeatureAllocationControl to display the route allocation in a manner that is appropriate for the user.   |  
|  G3E_DISPLAY  |  Boolean  |  True indicates that this alternate allocation feature should be displayed in the FeatureAllocationDialog. This property is useful if you want to use your G3E_ALTERNATEALLOCATION object to store features that the user should not see.  Example You can choose to store all of the alternate allocation features for all allocation features that have alternates rather than recalculate them in your AlternateAllocationFeatures procedure. By setting G3E_DISPLAY = False, those features that are not alternate allocation features for the input allocation feature are not displayed.   |

### Land Management Overview

#### Implementing Land Management Functionality
This is a general workflow for implementing Land Management functionality in NetWorks Core. 
  * To implement Land Management functionality:


  1. [Create the data model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LZGU8_epoi_74nONgyh4WA) containing cadastral and pipeline-specific features. 
  2. Assign appropriate [interactive placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) to the geographic components of the cadastral and pipeline-specific features. 
  3. [Define relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sVMxzZxYc182TAA332~GGA) for the cadastral and pipeline-specific features. 
  4. Configure [Relationship Geometry Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zML1iGev760nENBuAzW8gg) for the cadastral features.

#### The Land Management Data Model

##### Cadastral Features
The Land Management functionality supports the following cadastral features:  
|  Feature   |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Cadastral nodes  |  Required before you can place cadastral edges.  |  
|  Cadastral edges  |  Required before you can place parcels and buildings.  |  
|  Cadastral areas  |  Include parcels, blocks, and block groups. Blocks are required before you can place block groups. Block groups are required before you can place community features, and so forth.   |  
|  Parcels  |  Required before you can place blocks.  |  
|  Buildings  |  Optional for the Land Management functionality. Other features do not depend on the presence of this feature.   |  
|  Political areas  |  Include districts, counties, states, and countries, which are optional for the Land Management functionality. These features may or may not exist in the data set.   |  
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806) Cadastral node — ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806)  
Cadastral edge — ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806)  
Parcel and building — ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806)  
Political area — ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806)  |  
| --- |  
Cadastral Nodes
Cadastral nodes are survey points that are measured by surveyors and delivered to the map producers. All other cadastral features are derived directly or indirectly from cadastral nodes. 
Cadastral nodes are placed using the [Interactive IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg). 
Cadastral Edges
Cadastral edges are two-point lines or [arcs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806) that define the boundaries of parcels and buildings. The endpoints of cadastral edges must coincide with cadastral nodes. Before you can digitize a cadastral edge, both parent cadastral nodes must already exist in the data set. 
Curved shape within a polyline, polygon, or area boundary feature. An arc has a constant radius around a single center point. 
Cadastral edges are placed using the [LMEdge IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. 
Parcels
Parcel features consist of the following geographical components: 
Parcel areas
Parcel areas are often referred to simply as parcels. They are the building blocks of higher-level cadastral areas. In general, a parcel feature instance may contain several parcel areas ("islands"). The boundaries of parcels coincide with cadastral edges. Before you can digitize a parcel, all cadastral edges determining its boundary must already exist in the data set. 
Parcels are placed using the [AreaByEdges IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. 
Parcel Centroids
Parcels may or may not have associated [centroids](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806). If centroids are required, there is always one centroid per parcel feature instance. 
A point, text element, or text node used in area features to attach attribute information for those features. A centroid is not always placed in the exact center of an area feature. 
Centroids are a legacy from data models that separated graphics and attributes and used centroids to link to the database and to reference the parcel attribute data. Now that graphics are stored in the database with attribute data, centroids may not be needed, although some countries still require them. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806) Centroids are still used if they serve as more than a link to the database. 
Parcel Labels
Parcels may or may not have associated labels. There may be one label per parcel feature instance, or there may be one label per each parcel area ("island") within a parcel feature instance. 
Parcel Label Leader Lines
A parcel label leader line points from a parcel label to the interior of the parcel. Leader lines are used for small parcels where the parcel label does not fit into the parcel area. Some data sets may require that one endpoint of the leader line coincide with the centroid (if the leader line points into a parcel area with a centroid). 
Űberhaks
Űberhak is a German word. Űberhaks are used for parcels consisting of several areas to indicate that those areas belong to each other. They are placed at the parcel boundaries and point from one area to another area. Uberhaks are normally drawn as glyphs with a 1 or Z shape. 
The following illustration shows a Z glyph between the adjacent sections of Parcel 1 at the top of the drawing while the 1 glyph is used to jump across Parcel 2 to indicate the associated area of Parcel 1 at the bottom of the drawing. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806)
Buildings
Buildings are areas. Boundaries of buildings are identical to cadastral edges. Before you can digitize a building, all cadastral edges determining its boundary must already exist in the data set. 
Buildings are placed using the [AreaByEdges IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. 
Cadastral Areas
Cadastral areas in order of increasing area size are as follows:
Parcels  
Blocks  
Block groups 
Each type of cadastral area must be defined as a separate feature. Areas on the same level do not overlap. There is a one-to-many [relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sVMxzZxYc182TAA332~GGA) between cadastral areas on adjacent levels (for example, parcel and block) based on the spatial relationships. For a block and parcels, for example, the one-to-many relationship means that the block completely covers the related parcels, and a single block covers any parcel. 
Except for parcels, cadastral areas are created from areas on the closest lower level. To place a cadastral or political area, you select all the areas on the lower level to identify the area being placed. 
Cadastral areas except for parcels are placed using the [AreaByAreas IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. 
Political Areas
Political areas in order of increasing area size are as follows:
Community  
District  
County  
State  
Country 
You must define each type of political area as a separate feature. Areas on the same level do not overlap. There is a one-to-many relationship between areas on adjacent levels (for example, community and district) and between block group and community. 
Political areas are created from areas on the closest lower level. To place a political area, you select all the areas on the lower level to identify the area being placed. 
Political areas are placed using the [AreaByAreas IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257806) There may be data sets with cadastral features, such as states or countries, with slightly different meanings than those assumed by the Land Management functionality. For example, in large-scale maps the states and countries might be linear features because there are only partial boundaries present in those maps. In such cases, the Land Management interactive placement techniques, relationships, and metadata would be set up so that they do not reference those features. Thus, to the Land Management functionality, they would appear to be regular features. 
Related Topic
[Changing the Shape or Position of Cadastral Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NRJlO1E7ia8k0BEi~PRneg)

##### Changing the Shape or Position of Cadastral Features
Because all cadastral features are directly or indirectly derived from cadastral nodes, you can modify only cadastral nodes. If the position of a cadastral node is modified, the derived cadastral edges are automatically modified so that they remain coincident with the cadastral nodes. 
Modifying cadastral edges triggers modifications in adjacent parcels and buildings. Modifying parcels triggers further modifications of blocks. Changes in the shapes of the blocks are further propagated to changes in block groups, and so forth.   
|  Example This is a cadastral node before it is modified. The block covering the two parcels is identical to the union of the parcels.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822) The cadastral node is moved: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822) The related cadastral edges get updated: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822) The parcels related to the updated cadastral edges get updated: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822) The parcels have been updated (dashed) while the block is not updated yet: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822) Finally, the block related to the updated parcels gets updated: ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257822)  |  
| --- |  
You cannot directly modify the geometries of cadastral features other than cadastral nodes. Since cadastral features are always created from lower-level features based on geographical coincidence, it is important that this coincidence be maintained.

##### Land Management Relationship Geometry Interfaces
Relationship Geometry interfaces for Land Management propagate changes through the hierarchy of cadastral features only from parents to children. So, if a cadastral edge (the child of two cadastral nodes) is updated by NodeEdgeRGI as a consequence of one of its parent cadastral node's being moved, the change is further propagated only to the parcels related to the cadastral edge (children of the updated cadastral edge), and not to the parent cadastral nodes. 
NetWorks Core delivers the following Relationship Geometry interfaces for use with Land Management: 
NodeEdgeRGI
NodeEdgeRGI is invoked when a cadastral node is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between a cadastral node and a cadastral edge only if the node is coincident with one of the edge's endpoints. If a cadastral node is moved, the NodeEdgeRGI moves the previously connected endpoints of related cadastral edges so that they remain coincident with the node.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  
|  Situation before   
moving a   
cadastral node.   |  User moves the  
cadastral node.   |  NodeEdgeRGI updates the  
related cadastral edges.   |  
During validation, this RGI checks that a cadastral node is coincident with one of the related cadastral edge's endpoints. 
EdgeNodeRGI
EdgeNodeRGI and the EdgeAreaRGI are invoked when a cadastral edge is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between the cadastral edge and cadastral nodes only if the edge's endpoints are coincident with the nodes. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the cadastral edge's endpoints are coincident with the related cadastral nodes. 
EdgeAreaRGI
EdgeAreaRGI and the EdgeNodeRGI are invoked when a cadastral edge is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between a cadastral edge and a parcel or building only if the cadastral edge is identical to one of the edges on the parcel's or building's boundary. 
If a cadastral edge is modified (usually by NodeEdgeRGI as a consequence of a moved cadastral node), EdgeAreaRGI updates the related parcels or buildings so edges on their boundaries remain identical to the cadastral edge. 
For each related parcel or building, EdgeAreaRGI collects all related cadastral edges and regenerates the parcel or building. Relationships must be established between the cadastral edges selected to regenerate the area and cadastral nodes common to these edges. EdgeAreaRGI considers two cadastral edges to be connected only if their common endpoints are related to the same cadastral node. Coincidence of endpoints is not sufficient to consider the cadastral edges to be connected.   
|  Example  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  
|  Situation before   
modifying  
cadastral edges.   |  User modifies  
cadastral edges.   |  EdgeAreaRGI updates the  
related parcel.   |  
During validation, this RGI checks that the cadastral edge is identical with one of the edges on the parcel's/building's boundary. 
AreaEdgeRGI
AreaEdgeRGI is invoked when parcel or building is the active feature. The RGI approves the relationship between the parcel or building and the cadastral edge only if the edge on the parcel's or building's boundary is identical to the cadastral edge. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the edges on the parcel's or building's boundary are identical to the related cadastral edges. 
LowerToHigherAreaRGI
LowerToHigherAreaRGI is invoked for cadastral and political areas where there is a higher-level related area for the active feature, such as for a parcel if there is a related block. The RGI approves the relationship between a lower-level (parcel) and higher-level area (block) only if the lower-level area is completely covered by the higher-level area. 
If a lower-level area is updated (usually as a consequence of moving a cadastral node and propagating the change through the hierarchy of cadastral features), the LowerToHigherAreaRGI updates the related higher-level area. Accordingly, it continues to cover the lower-level area.   
|  Example  |   |   |

|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257776?tocId=AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg)  |

the parcels).   |  User modified the   
parcels (parcels are  
dashed).   |  LowerToHigherAreaRGI updates the related block.  |  
During validation, this RGI checks that the lower-level area is completely covered by the higher-level area. 
When updating a higher-level area based on the modifications of the lower-level areas, one of the following approaches can be used: 
  * Always generated as the union of lower-level areas
  * Generated as the union of lower-level areas and itself

HigherToLowerAreaRGI
HigherToLowerAreaRGI is invoked for cadastral and political areas where there is a related lower-level area for the active feature—for example, for a block where there is a relationship between the block and a parcel. The RGI approves the relationship between a higher-level (block) and lower-level area (parcel) only if the higher-level area completely covers the lower-level area. 
During validation, this RGI checks that the higher-level area completely covers each of the related lower-level areas. It further checks that none of the related lower-level areas overlap each other. The RGI can also check whether the union of related lower-level areas is identical with the validated higher-level area. This optional checking is configurable in metadata.   
|  Example Assume that 6 is the G3E_RINO of the HigherToLowerAreaRGI.  
 |  G3E_RINO  |  G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL  |  G3E_ARGUMENTNAME  |  G3E_ARGUMENTDESCRIPTION  |  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  6  |  1  |  Higher2LowerIsUnionn  |  1 if higher- level area has to be the union of lower-level areas, 0 otherwise  |  4  |  
 |

##### Land Management Relationships Metadata
The predefined [Land Management Relationship Geometry interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg) should be listed in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE. 
To use the Land Management Relationship Geometry interfaces, you must edit, at a minimum, the G3E_RELATIONSHIP, G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY, and G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP metadata tables. Depending on the interface and your requirements, you might also have to edit G3E_RELATIONARGUMENT and G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257798) See the [Land Management feature and component numbers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GL7kCSkSRPByhh~wIge0wg) used in the examples below to map numbers to objects (features, components, relationships). 
G3E_RELATIONSHIP
The [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table should contain a definition of the ManyOwnership relationship, as in the example below. 
To establish the relationships, set the value of G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS to CandidatesViaEntireGeometry, even if the related features do not have coincident vertices. 
In the following example, a relationship is established between technical objects and technical object protection zones, even when the technical object is a point in the center of the square representing the protection zone.

ManyOwnership  |  1  |  G3E_OWNERFNO  |  2000  |  G3E_OWNERTRIGGERINGCNO  |  3 (= g3eamsraHighlight | g3eamsraAttributes)  |  CandidatesViaEntireGeometry  |  0  |  1  |  7/3/2001  |  
|  14  |  8  |  Land Management Child to Parent  |  G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP  |  G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP_OPTABLE  |  Land Management Child to Parent Relationship  |  G3ERelationships. ManyOwnership  |  1  |  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  2000  |  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  3 (= g3eamsraHighlight | g3eamsraAttributes)  |  CandidatesViaEntireGeometry  |  1  |  1  |  7/3/2001  |  
Although a single ManyOwnership relationship is sufficient to represent all ownership relationships among cadastral and pipeline-specific features, you can split this single ManyOwnership into several ManyOwnerships if it better suits your requirements. 
G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY
The example below shows how the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/09ZyDQ3titfSWGWgohp1Xg) table should be populated. It references the G3E_RINO values from the example G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE table and G3E_RIARGGROUPNO from the example G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS table below. 
  * Rows with G3E_RGNO 11 and 12 introduce NodeEdgeRGI and EdgeNodeRGI for cadastral nodes and cadastral edges. 
  * Rows with G3E_RGNO 13 and 14 introduce EdgeAreaRGI and AreaEdgeRGI for cadastral edges and parcels. 
  * Rows with G3E_RGNO 15 and 16 introduce EdgeAreaRGI and AreaEdgeRGI for cadastral edges and buildings. 
  * Rows with G3E_RGNO 17 and 18 introduce LowerToHigherAreaRGI and HigherToLowerAreaRGI for parcels and blocks.

G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP
The [G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cLQKIifBDRbAd4EkpI9HgQ) table is populated for the hierarchy of ownerships of cadastral features (rows 11 to 14 in the example below). 
  * G3E_ENFORCEMENT is set to Yes (1) to ensure that features are not posted without the appropriate owners. For example, a cadastral edge is not posted if it does not have related cadastral nodes. 
  * G3E_DELETE is set to 4 to prevent the deletion of parent features while child features exist. 
  * G3E_BREAKLINEAR is set to Yes (1) for the relationship between cadastral nodes and cadastral edges so that it is possible to break a cadastral edge by placing a cadastral node on it. 
  * G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR has affect only if G3E_BREAKLINEAR is Yes (1). G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR is set to 0 for the relationship between cadastral nodes and cadastral edges to reestablish the relationship on the original and copy features based on the geographic proximity. 


G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP also contains records for the pipeline-specific features (rows 15 to 19 in the example below). 
  * G3E_ENFORCEMENT is set to Yes (1) to ensure that protection zones and areas are not posted without their owners—technical objects, pipelines and parcels (for protection areas). 
  * G3E_DELETE is set to 1 to delete child features (protection zones and areas) when the parent features are deleted.

##### Land Management Relationships
The hierarchy of ownerships among cadastral features is as follows:  
|  [Cadastral nodes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/omUt8DZdq4BUnW3Js1N0QA) are on top of the hierarchy. They are owners of:   |  
| --- |  
|   |  [Cadastral edges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/omUt8DZdq4BUnW3Js1N0QA), which are owners owners of:   |  
|   |  [Cadastral areas](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/omUt8DZdq4BUnW3Js1N0QA), which include parcels and buildings. In addition, cadastral area features can have subordinate features. For example, parcels are owners of blocks.   |  
In Land Management, [relationships](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QtTqwZUa6Mj_0zqbNGxIyA) are used to store topology information for cadastral features. The following restrictions apply: 
  * The relationship between a cadastral node and a cadastral edge can be established only if the node is coincident with an endpoint of the edge. 
  * The relationship between a cadastral edge and a parcel can be established only if the cadastral edge is coincident with an edge on the boundary of the parcel. 
  * The relationship between a parcel and a block can be established only if the parcel is completely covered by the block. 


Since a change in the position of a cadastral node should propagate through the hierarchy of cadastral features, related edges are modified based on the position of the node, related parcels are updated based on the modifications of edges, and related blocks are modified based on the updates of the parcels. 
A single ManyOwnership relationship can be used for the hierarchy of ownerships. The relationships should be defined to achieve the following objectives: 
  * Cadastral features should reference related cadastral features. For example, cadastral edges reference the parent cadastral nodes, parcels reference cadastral edges, blocks reference the parent parcels, and so on. 
  * The integrity of cadastral data should be checked. For example, the system checks that the cadastral nodes are coincident with the endpoints of the related cadastral edges, that parcel edges are identical with the cadastral edges, that parcels are completely covered by the blocks, and so on. 
  * An update of the position of a cadastral node triggers a sequence of updates of directly and indirectly related child features. So, after an update of the position of a cadastral node, the related cadastral edges are updated so that they remain coincident with the cadastral node. Afterward, the parcels and buildings related to the updated edges are modified so that their boundaries remain overlapping the edges. 
In the next step, if necessary, the blocks are updated so that they continue to overlap the updated parcels, and so on. 


The ManyOwnership relationship must be further defined for pipeline-specific features. There is a relationship between technical objects (owners) and technical object protection zones (owned features), between pipelines (owners) and pipeline protection zones (owned features), and between parcels, technical objects and pipelines (owners) and protection areas (owned features). During the placement of protection zones, the relationship to the owners is established. When protection areas are created from protection zones, the ownership of protection zones is copied to the resulting protection areas. The same ManyOwnership relationship can be used for both cadastral features and pipeline-specific features. 
To creare a many-to-many ownership relationship among cadastral features, you must do the following: 
  * Define the [many-to-many ownership relationship](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Vqt2Qr0hUpLn1pdFL4RMTQ) between features on adjacent levels of the cadastral hierarchy (between a cadastral node and a cadastral edge). 
  * Assign the appropriate [Land Management RGI](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AZrTB4g_C7iCUAzSKxP4eg) to each pair of the related cadastral features. 

  
|  Example Define the relationship between a cadastral node (source feature) and a cadastral edge (related feature), and define the relationship between a cadastral edge (source feature) and a cadastral node (related feature). Then, in G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY, assign an RGI to each pair of related features: 
  * Assign the NodeEdgeRGI to the relationship between a cadastral node (source feature) and a cadastral edge (related feature). 
  * Assign the EdgeNodeRGI to the relationship between a cadastral edge (source feature) and a cadastral node (related feature). 

 |  
| --- |

##### Merging Parcels and Buildings
Parcel merge is a process whereby two parcel features (Parcel1, Parcel2) are merged into a single parcel feature (Parcel1). During the parcel merge, the parcel areas of Parcel2 are first added to Parcel1, and then Parcel2 is deleted. If there are common boundaries between the areas of Parcel1 and Parcel2, these areas are merged into a single area. 
Building merge works the same way as parcel merge. Parcels and buildings are merged using the [Merge Features](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6I_x_SevdUQTkVXuLgKXOA) command.

##### Parcel and Building Geometries
Parcel and building geometries may be either BoundaryGeometry or CompositePolygonGeometry types. CompositePolygonGeometry may contain both PolylineGeometry and ArcGeometry items. PolylineGeometry items may contain only two points. Exteriors of BoundaryGeometry must be CompositePolygonGeometry obeying the previously mentioned rules. Parcels and buildings are created from cadastral edges. The items of CompositePolygonGeometry (PolylineGeometry and ArcGeometry) must be identical to the corresponding geometries of cadastral edges (PolylineGeometry or items of CompositePolylineGeometry). 
These rules need to be taken into account when migrating cadastral data from other data sources. The [AreaByEdges IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) should be used for placement of parcels and buildings. This placement technique creates the parcel and building geometries according to the above rules. 
Polygon: A group of points where the last point is the same as the first.
Composite Polygon: A collection of linear geometries where the first point of the first one is the same as the last point of the last one. Composite polygons can contain arcs.

##### Pipeline-Specific Features
Pipeline-specific features and their relationships are listed in the [G3E_PROTAREAIFACE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly3YV53piSLXxhlle0Y~Iw). 
Pipelines are associated with technical objects such as signposts. Both pipelines and technical objects occupy corridors called [protection zones](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832). Where these corridors overlap parcels, regions called protection areas are established. Each protection area has an associated contract between the pipeline owner and the parcel owner that establishes access rights and lease costs. The Land Management functionality supports the following pipeline- specific features: 
A buffer zone around a pipeline or a square around a technical object. Creating a protection zone is the first step in creating a protection area 
  * [Technical object protection zones](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uK4YB91p7ien7rPOScARtg), which are an intermediate step in creating protection areas. They do not need to be defined in the data set if you are not required to display protection zones and areas around technical objects. 
  * [Pipeline protection zones](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uK4YB91p7ien7rPOScARtg), which are an intermediate step in creating protection areas. 
  * [Protection areas](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uK4YB91p7ien7rPOScARtg), which are created from protection zones. 


Technical Object Protection Zones
Technical object protection zones are square areas around technical objects. To create a technical object protection zone, you identify the technical object and provide the protection zone size and orientation. The default orientation is derived from the orientation of the technical object. 
Technical object protection zones are placed using the [TechObjProtZone IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. For the IPT to work, specify the following in the G3E_PROTAREAIFACE table: 
  * Which features are technical objects (G3E_TYPE is TechObject)
  * Which feature is the technical object protection zone (G3E_TYPE is TechObjectProtZone).


Pipeline Protection Zones
Each pipeline protection zone is a buffer zone around a section of a pipeline. If the selected section starts or ends at the start or end of the pipeline, a square end cap is added to the buffer zone. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832)
To create a pipeline protection zone, you identify the start and endpoints on a pipeline. These points are snapped to the intersection of the pipeline with a parcel boundary. If a pipeline begins or ends on the interior of a parcel, you can also snap to the start point of the pipeline. In this case, the placement technique snaps to whichever point is the nearest, pipeline start point or parcel boundary intersection point. After you provide the protection zone left and right width, the protection zone is created. 
Pipeline protection zones are placed using the [PipelineProtZone IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique. For the IPT to work, specify the following in the G3E_PROTAREAIFACE table: 
  * Which feature is the pipeline (G3E_TYPE is Pipeline)
  * Which feature is the pipeline protection zone (G3E_TYPE is PipelineProtZone)


Also, you need to specify which feature is the parcel (G3E_TYPE is Parcel) in the [G3E_LMIFACE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6jHbOc7Q92oyp6mJuh5c0g). 
Protection Areas
Protection areas are derived from both pipeline and technical object protection zones as the spatial intersection of the parcel fabric and the protection zones. The result is a collection of area features, where each feature is associated with one protection zone or an intersection of several protection zones. In addition, each of these areas overlaps only one parcel. 
Protection zones must exist before you can create protection areas. Creating protection areas takes two steps. First you overlay the protection zones with the parcel fabric and with each other to create new protection areas. Each topological face of this spatial overlay becomes a protection area. If there is more than one topological face for any protection zone/parcel combination, these faces are treated as a single feature instance with repeating component instances. 
The following illustration shows a pipeline protection zone overlapping two parcels and a technical object protection zone: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832)
The following illustration shows how protection areas are generated for the protection zones above: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832)
While creating protection areas, the Land Management functionality software copies relationships from the source protection zones to the protection areas. In the illustration above, the relationships of the pipeline protection zone would be copied to ProtectionArea1, ProtectionArea2, and ProtectionArea4. The relationships of the technical object protection zone would be copied to ProtectionArea3 and ProtectionArea4. 
The second step in the creation of protection areas is the processing of existing protection areas, which are overlapped by the protection areas created in the first step. When an existing protection area (ProtectionArea5) is overlain by a protection area created in the first step (ProtectionArea1), the two protection areas are further processed as follows. In the illustration below, only Parcel1 is shown. 
  * ProtectionArea1 is spatially subtracted from ProtectionArea5. The resulting area becomes a new ProtectionArea5. 
  * The original ProtectionArea5 is spatially subtracted from ProtectionArea1. The resulting area becomes a new ProtectionArea1. 
  * A new protection area, ProtectionArea15, is generated as a spatial intersection of ProtectionArea1 and ProtectionArea5. 

  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832)  |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257832)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  At the beginning of Step 2, the existing protection area   
(ProtectionArea5) and the newly created protection area (ProtectionArea1) overlap.   |  At the end of Step 2, ProtectionArea1 and ProtectionArea5 are updated, and ProtectionArea15 is added.   |  
For the new protection areas created in this step, the relationships are copied from the source protection areas to the new protection areas. In the illustration above, the relationships of ProtectionArea1 and ProtectionArea5 would be copied to ProtectionArea15. 
Protection areas are created with the [Create Protection Area](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qDR04ymPhQSzMeFBq2VGFw) command. For the command to work, you need to populate the G3E_PROTAREAIFACE and G3E_LMIFACE tables. Besides metadata for protection zone placement (see above), [G3E_PROTAREAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ly3YV53piSLXxhlle0Y~Iw) must contain a record where G3E_TYPE = 'ProtArea'. This record specifies the protection area feature. The relationships, which are copied from protection zones to protection areas, are specified by the records with G3E_TYPE equal to ProtZoneMMOwnership and ProtAreaMMOwnership.

##### Primary Geographic Components for Land Features
All Land Management features must contain the primary geographic components described below. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257881) In the following tables, the component names are the same as the feature names to which the components belong. This is done only for clarity and is not required. The Geometry Type column contains the geometry types required by the Land Management functionality.   
|  Component  |  Geometry Type  |  Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Cadastral node  |  PointGeometry or OrientedPointGeometry  |  This must be a nonrepeating component.  |  
|  [Cadastral edge](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bwTdAWTUgoBdoL2ZQO_u6g?section=274418)  |  PolylineGeometry or CompositePolylineGeometry  |  The cadastral edge component may be a two-point line or arc. If only two-point lines are required, it is sufficient to use the PolylineGeometry type. If arcs are also required, the cadastral edge component must have geometry type CompositePolylineGeometry.  This should be a nonrepeating component.  |  
|  [Parcel area and building](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/S2K7MTYyp912LjStI1WxFQ)  |  CompositePolylgonGeometry or BoundaryGeometry  |  If holes are required, the geometry type must be BoundaryGeometry. These two components should be repeating.  |  
|  Block, block group, community, district, county, state, country  |  PolylgonGeometry, CompositePolylgonGeometry or BoundaryGeometry  |  If holes are required, the geometry type must be BoundaryGeometry. If any of these components may consist of several areas, they should be defined as repeating.   |  
|  Technical object protection zone  |  PolylgonGeometry  |  This component must be nonrepeating.  |  
|  Pipeline protection zone  |  PolylgonGeometry, CompositePolylgonGeometry or BoundaryGeometry  |  In some cases, the area generated from the intersection of the pipeline buffer zone and parcel fabric is an area with a hole. If the component has the type PolylgonGeometry, these holes are ignored.  This component must be repeating.  |  
|  Protection area  |  PolylgonGeometry, CompositePolylgonGeometry or BoundaryGeometry  |  The geometry type of a protection area should be the same as the type of parcel component to ensure the correct processing of holes.  This component must be repeating.  |

Cadastral edge geometry types can be PolylineGeometry or CompositePolylineGeometry. PolylineGeometry geometries can contain only two points, the start point and the endpoint. CompositePolylineGeometry can contain only PolylineGeometry or ArcGeometry. If the CompositePolylineGeometry contains PolylineGeometry, then it can contain only two points. 
These rules need to be followed when migrating cadastral data from other data sources. The [LMEdge IPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement technique should be used for cadastral edges because it creates the cadastral edge geometries according to these rules.

##### Splitting Parcels
Parcel split is a process whereby a single parcel feature (Parcel1) is split into two parcel features (Parcel1 and Parcel2). During the parcel split, Parcel1 is copied into Parcel2. The parcel areas of Parcel1 are divided between Parcel1 and Parcel2 based on user input. 
Before you can split a parcel, a split line must be present on the map. A split line can be a cadastral edge or a chain of cadastral edges. Both endpoints of the split line must be connected to the cadastral nodes on the boundary of the parcel being split. You can also define several split lines for splitting a single parcel. 
The diagram below illustrates a split line:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257874)
Parcels are split using the [Split Parcel](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PPQntq_jF6WyFhniVW0VTA)
