### Length Management Overview

#### Length Management Sections
The Length Management system supports a multisection data model similar to the [Multisection Cable Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NlBF~fhuOAmRrMXoSw0GQQ). The Length Management Multisection Model has extended the Multisection Cable Model by allowing components that are owned by other features to be non-graphic. 
In the Multisection Cable Model, any sections of cable that are owned by other features, such as conduit features, require the user to digitize a detail graphic section to represent the length of cable contained in the conduit. In the Length Management Multisection Model, the user is not required to digitize the detail graphic section. 
During the placement and edit workflows of configured length features, the Length Management system automatically manages the owned sections as non-graphic sections. 
![lengthmanagementsections](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/983119)
For instance, in the example above, if a direct buried fiber duct is placed at one end of a conduit and a second section is placed at the other end of the conduit, the Length Management system would automatically create a third, non-graphic, section to represent the length of the fiber duct that exists within the conduit. 
In the above example, data would exist as follows in the fiber duct geographic component table.   
|  Section Number  |  Start Location  |  Length  |  Owner Number  |  Owner Identifier  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  0  |  9  |   |   |  
|  2  |  9  |  18  |  2200  |  1  |  
|  3  |  27  |  9  |   |   |  
The first section begins at the left-most handhole and is 9m in length. The second section, contained within the conduit, starts 9m from the start of the fiber duct and is 18m in length. The third section starts at the end of the conduit, which is 27m from the start of the fiber duct and 9m from the right-most handhole. 
Related Topic
[Length Management Overview](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aMmx8LEmlrbbDHinlTKB6w)

#### Length Management Upgrade
The Length Management system was introduced in NetWorks Core 10.04.1906. The Length Management system manages its own [Length Management Multisection Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Q7ImeP58TkG_mRn72Oz6cQ). The [G3E_LENGTHFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fILlCWNR_U7tQa7J7OZ0Jg) and [G3E_LENGTHCOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6WbM6830atnFaFlho9jamQ) metadata tables are used to define attributes that are used by the Length Management Multisection Model. When upgrading an existing feature with the required attributes to become a length feature, you must initialize the data properly. If the attribute data is not initialized with the appropriate values, the Length Management system may not exhibit the expected behavior during future workflows. 
Length Features
Each length feature can have two optional attributes: a total length attribute and a total geometric length attribute. 
Total Length
The total length of a length feature is the sum of all of the lengths of the appropriate sections associated with the feature. This attribute is typically stored in the primary attribute component of the feature; however, it can be contained in any non-repeating component of the feature. The attribute is typically configured as a read-only attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. If the feature does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to a component of the feature. 
Total Geometric Length
The total geometric length of a length feature is the sum of all of the geometric lengths of the appropriate sections associated with the feature. The geometric length of each geometry is measured with a measurement service. This attribute is typically stored in the primary attribute component of the feature; however, it can be contained in any non-repeating component of the feature. The attribute is configured as a read-only attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. If the feature does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to a component of the feature. 
Length Components
Each length feature can be configured with multiple length components. Typically, a length feature is configured with two length components, a geographic component and a detail component. Each length can have five optional attributes, a section start location, a section length, a geometric length, an include-in-the-total-length, and an include-in-total-geometric-length attribute. If the length feature participates in many-ownership relationships with other length features, the geographic length component must also be configured with a G3E_OWNERFNO and a G3E_OWNERFID attribute to indicate the length feature that the component is representing. These attributes must be stored in the same component. If the length component contains a G3E_GEOMETRY attribute, these attributes must be stored in that same component. 
Section Start Location
The section start location is the distance along the length feature where the section starts. The attribute is configured as a read / write attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. The first section of a length feature begins at 0. The Length Management system uses this attribute to order the sections. If the component does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to the component. If any of the length components can be broken with other features, this attribute is required, and the length component must be configured with the delivered Length Management post break linear interface. The post break linear interface uses the section start location to destine each section to the appropriate feature, either the original feature or the feature that results from the break operation. This attribute is updated automatically during other workflows, such as break, merge, and reestablish relationship. 
Section Length
The section length is the actual length of the component as entered by the user. Its default value is the geometric or measured length of the geometry associated with the graphic component instance. The attribute is configured as a read / write attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. If the length feature is configured with a total length attribute and a section is to be included in the total, the section length attribute is added to it. This attribute is an optional attribute. If the component does not already contain this attribute, it must be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to the component. 
Geometric Length
The geometric length is the measured length of the geometry associated with a graphic component instance. The attribute is configured as a read-only attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer and is defaulted to the length of geometry as measured by a measurement service. If the length feature is configured with a total geometry length attribute and a section is to be included in the total, the geometric length attribute is added to it. This attribute is an optional attribute. If the component does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to the component. 
Include-in-Total-Length
This include-in-total-length attribute indicates whether the length of a section should be included in the total length of the feature. The attribute is configured as a read / write attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. This attribute is optional. It is only required in models where the user needs to manually specify whether a specific section instance should be included in the total length of the feature. If the component does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to the component. 
Include-in-Total-Geometric-Length
This include-in-total-geometry-length attribute indicates whether the geometric length of a section should be included in the total geometric length of the feature. The attribute is configured as a read / write attribute when displayed in Feature Explorer. This attribute is an optional attribute. It is only required in models where the user needs to manually specify whether a specific section instance should be included in the total geometric length of the feature. If the component does not already contain this attribute, it needs to be initialized with an appropriate value when the attribute is added to the component. 
Parent
The G3E_OWNERFNO and G3E_OWNERFID attributes indicate the parent instance that the length component represents. These attributes are only required in the geometric component of a length feature that participates in many-ownership relationships. These attributes are not typically displayed in Feature Explorer but may appear as read-only. If the component does not already contain these attributes, they need to be initialized with the appropriate values when the attribute is added to the component.

### Multisection Cable Model

#### Cable Edit Control Metadata
Besides the metadata entries specific to CableEditControl, you must also define certain dialog boxes and dialog tabs to properly display the data in Feature Explorer. See [Configuring the Cable Edit Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zn_9lmDaJE11oZfURbtkRg). 
Control-Specific Metadata
To manage all the length attributes on cable features, CableEditControl must know how to access those attributes. The [G3E_CABLEEDITATTR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MF3LH6S6jV5Mx2jjObPygg) table provides that information. This table is also used by the node-ordered relationship software to support cable break between cable sections. G3E_TYPE = StartLocANO is used to determine the geo component number of the section, as well as its segment start length attribute field. G3E_TYPE = DStartLocANO is used to determine the detail component number of the section and its segment start length attribute field. 
From this metadata, the node-ordered relationship software can allow a break to be triggered if it is determined that the break point occurs at endpoint of a cable section and if that point exists between cable sections. The software checks the segment start length of the section being "broken" and compares it with the segment start length values of the remaining cable sections (both geo and detail) of the cable to determine if the break point exists between sections. If so, a break is triggered. In this case, no cable section is actually broken, but the sections on either side of the break point are assigned to the two resulting cables, respectively. 
Dialog Tab Definitions
As with all dialog boxes appearing in Feature Explorer, the definitions for CableEditControl start with an entry in [G3E_DIALOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw). You typically have three entries in G3E_DIALOG for each feature that uses CableEditControl: 
  * One for Review
  * One for Edit
  * One for Placement


You cannot have two references to this control within a given feature. If you have placement configurations that include multisection features, you also need a G3E_DIALOG entry for each configuration. Each of these entries references a G3E_DTNO value that corresponds to an entry in [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ). 
The G3E_DIALOGTAB entry referenced in G3E_DIALOG should have G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE = 'GTCtlInfo.CableEditControl'. This dialog tab definition must be vertical (G3E_ORIENTATION = "V"). The attributes referenced by this dialog tab definition appear on the bottom grid of the CableEditControl, so minimally you would include the total length attribute in this definition. You can include other attributes of the feature as well. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256015) You should make the total length attribute read-only on all tab definitions, even for Edit and Placement, because the user should not edit that attribute; CableEditControl maintains that attribute from the component and section length values. All editable attributes on this grid must have set G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_REFRESH= Yes (1). 
Top Grid
The top grid is defined by a combination of G3E_DIALOG/G3E_DIALOGTAB entries. For each of the three modes (Review, Edit, and Placement), you must have two G3E_DIALOG entries (one for geo, one for detail). The G3E_TYPE values for these entries are as follows: 
  * 'Cable Edit Review Geo'
  * 'Cable Edit Review Detail'
  * 'Cable Edit Edit Geo'
  * 'Cable Edit Edit Detail'
  * 'Cable Edit Placement Geo'
  * 'Cable Edit Placement Detail'


Middle Grid 
The middle grid (which actually belongs to the MergedAttributeGrid hosted by CableEditControl) is controlled by another G3E_DIALOG/G3E_DIALOGTAB combination. There should be two entries in G3E_DIALOG for Review, two for Edit, and two for Placement with G3E_TYPE equal to 'Merged Review', 'Merged Edit', or 'Merged Placement', respectively. You do not need entries for placement configurations here; all placement configurations use the 'Merged Placement' definition. There are two entries for each because there must be one for the geo cable sections and another for the detail sections. The G3E_DTNO values in those entries should reference a G3E_DIALOGTAB entry that defines a horizontally oriented grid containing the attributes for the cable sections. The pairs of entries must be identical in the number and types of attributes referenced, and corresponding attributes must have the same field name in the data table so that the MergedAttributeGrid displays both the geo and detail sections on the same grid. All of the editable attributes must have G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_REFRESH=Yes (1). 
These G3E_DIALOG entries must reference corresponding entries in G3E_DIALOGTAB that define horizontally oriented grids containing the component length label attributes. You may include any attributes from the component lengths, but minimally you should include the length value attribute so the user can modify the lengths. All editable attributes must have G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_REFRESH=Yes (1). 
Edit and Placement Modes
For the Edit and Placement modes, make the following values editable when configuring [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE definitions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ) for the dialog tabs: 
  * Component length values
  * Section length values
  * Section start location values


However, editing of the section lengths and start locations is further controlled by the definitions of those attributes in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw). The entries for the section length should have a G3E_RINO that references a G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE entry with G3E_INTERFACE='PFIface.CanEditSectionLength' and G3E_TYPE='Attribute Edit Control GUI'. The entries for start locations should have a G3E_RINO that reference a G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE entry with G3E_INTERFACE='PFIface.CanEditIfNonNull' and G3E_TYPE='Attribute Edit Control GUI'. These interface objects restrict editing of those attributes such that the user can only modify a section length if there are no component lengths associated to that section. The user can modify the section length or start location only after the linear section has been completely digitized and the placement techniques have initialized those values. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256015) The length attributes displayed on the CableEditControl grids should not be displayed on any other dialog tabs. Editing of these attributes in any context other than CableEditControl does not preserve the proper length relationships.

#### Cable Edit Control
NetWorks Core provides a specialized control that should be configured on a Feature Explorer [dialog tab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VRNGMMcGhlNA0gN6mJ~nIA) for editing features that use the multisection cable model. The [Cable Edit control automatically manages](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zShx51_S2tI2axLHsPTegQ) all of the length-related attributes so that the model integrity is maintained. 
The Cable Edit control displays two horizontal attribute grids and one vertical attribute grid for editing cable sections: 
  * The middle grid displays the cable sections, both geo and detail, merged together and sorted by the section start location. 
  * The top grid displays the component lengths (if any), associated with the cable section selected in the middle grid. 
  * The bottom grid is a vertical grid that can be configured to display any appropriate attributes, but typically it would include the cable's total length. This provides a convenient display of all of the length-related attributes. 


You must [configure dialog tab definitions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zn_9lmDaJE11oZfURbtkRg) for each of these grids. 
The following are examples of the control in Feature Explorer:

This presentation is shown when Cable Edit control's height is less than the width:
![CableEditControlHorizontal](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/ExOz1tUlUdKii8Tj4rcE8A-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=b6376872b7b5a069&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

#### Cable Management Break Processing
The integrity of the multisection cable model requires additional processing when a cable is broken into two features. The cable sections must be assigned to the resulting features according to their section start locations. NetWorks Core uses [custom Component Elimination](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dONaaMCKCqImkAJeU0B1BA) methods to assign the cable sections. The various length attributes (component lengths, section lengths, section start locations, and total length) may all need adjustment after a break operation. NetWorks Core uses a [Post Break Linear interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b4yEJdY9OaWQ_jI2eFS~LQ) to perform these adjustments. 
Configure CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak (Component Elimination) and PostBreakCableLengths (Post Break Linear) interfaces for assigning Component Length components appropriately at break and for calculating component lengths, section lengths, section start locations, and total lengths of resulting features as follows: 
  1. In the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) table, define the argument value for CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak. This tolerance value is the geographic distance from the break point to a component length label. A label that is found within this distance from the break point is assigned to the original cable. Any label outside this tolerance is assigned based on geographic proximity to the cable section. An example configuration is shown below. You must choose the G3E_RIARGGROUPNO value and it must match the value referenced in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w). 
Component length label proximity tolerance value (or Tolerance to use in the proximity analysis against G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO)  
|  Example  
 |  G3E_ARGROWNO  |  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO   |  G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL  |  G3E_VALUE   |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  99   |  704202  |  1   |  2  |  30-Sep- 03   |  
 |  
  2. In the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) table, define G3E_COMPONENTELIMINATION as Custom (7) and see the G3E_RINO corresponding to CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak interface in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE and to G3E_RIARGGROUPNO defined above. This definition applies to the component length label component. Typically, there is one for geo and one for detail.

#### Cable Management Functional Interfaces
NetWorks Core uses two [functional interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) to maintain the multisection cable model: LinearLabel and RelativeComponent. 
LinearLabel
The LinearLabel functional interface maintains the component length, section length, and total length values when a component length label is deleted. Also, during model validation, it confirms that those length values are correct. (This means that cables with no component lengths are not validated.) 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257942) LinearLabel is not required if your data model does not use component length labels. In that case, there is no model validation provided for the length attributes. 
Configure this functional interface on the geometry attribute of the component length label with a type of SetValue. 
RelativeComponent
The RelativeComponent functional interface is used to maintain the symbology relationship between labels and their corresponding cable section. RelativeComponent copies the G3E_CID of the linear section to an attribute of the label. This attribute can then be used in constructing the label's component view to retrieve attributes from the cable section used in the style or label rules. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257942) If you use [CableAndComponentIPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) and [ComponentLengthLabelIPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) placement techniques for the component length labels, do not configure RelativeComponent. Those placement techniques perform that processing automatically. 
CalculateLength
If you are using the CableAndComponentIPT placement technique, the CalculateLength functional interface is not needed; do not configure it on the cable sections. Doing so interferes with the Length Management software.

#### Cable Management Placement Techniques
NetWorks Core provides two special placement techniques to help maintain the multisection cable data model: CableAndComponentIPT and ComponentLengthLabelIPT. These techniques manage all the various length values associated with this model. They also make the placement of the lines and labels easier and more intuitive for the user. 
CableAndComponentIPT
This placement technique provides all the capabilities of InteractiveIPT for placing cable lines (also called cable sections), and it also allows the user to place a [component length label](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rpyXtHTHDfHzhRP07INdKA) at the last-placed vertex of the line (except the first vertex) while digitizing the line. Pressing the letter "L" while digitizing places a component length label near the last vertex (at a metadata-specified offset). The offset is applied relative to the angle of the line segment, and the label is rotated to that angle. You can also configure the technique to allow adjustments of the label like move along. A dialog box displays that lets the user override the measured length. 
This technique uses a dockable control, the [Placement Length Display](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FlHLeOfQay3NN36WBCcBOw), to display helpful measurements of the cable during placement. This control displays (1) the length of the line placed so far, (2) the length from the last component-length label, (3) the total length of all cable sections, and (4) the length of the portion of line in dynamics. Both measured and user-entered lengths are displayed. 
This technique supports all the same construction aids that InteractiveIPT supports.
ComponentLengthLabelIPT
This placement technique is used to add component length labels [to an existing cable section](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ObhyhETfb1btYrnt4GRSpw). The technique highlights the portion of the cable section from its beginning to the point nearest the mouse position as the user moves the mouse. The [Placement Length Display dockable control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/FlHLeOfQay3NN36WBCcBOw) displays the length of this highlighted line, and the readouts are the same as would be seen if the user had placed the cable section, with all the associated component length labels, up to the vertex preceding the end of the highlighted section. Thus, the dynamic length readout reflects the length from that preceding vertex up to the mouse position. The objective is to give the user the same information that CableAndComponentIPT would display in the same situation. 
The length label is placed at a metadata-specified offset from the point on the cable nearest the point where the user clicked. Like CableAndComponentIPT, the offset is applied relative to the angle of the line segment, and the label is rotated to that angle. 
This technique supports all the same construction aids that InteractiveIPT supports when placing a point feature. 
Configuring the Cable Management Placement Techniques
Configure both [CableAndComponentIPT and ComponentLengthLabelIPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vE8Hb9VLNt1zN2b7s3_nYg) for the geo and detail linear components of any feature that uses component length labeling.

##### Configuring the Cable Edit Control
You need to configure two types of metadata before users can use the [Cable Edit control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zShx51_S2tI2axLHsPTegQ):

  * Dialog tab definitions


  * To configure the Cable Edit control:


  1. So that the Cable Edit control knows how to manage all the length attributes on the cable feature, populate the [G3E_CABLEEDITATTR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MF3LH6S6jV5Mx2jjObPygg) table. Each row in this table contains a <G3E_TYPE, G3E_ANO> pair. The type field indicates the meaning of the attribute, and the ANO field specifies the attribute number.

Repeat this scheme for each feature.

#### Multisection Cable Model Business Rules

##### OTDR-Specific Business Rules

###### OTDR Marker Placement Calculations on Graphic Conductors
This topic describes scenarios in which a cable has geometry, and it is contained by multiple infrastructure features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/471743) In image below, the number indicates the order of feature placement. For example, “4-Length 6" indicates that the section is the fourth conduit in the order of placement and has a length of 10 m. 
Cable 1 Section 2 is contained by Conduits 1and 2. Similarly Cable 2 Section 2 is contained by Conduit 3 and 4. Section lengths are calculated on the geometric length of the conduits. 
![KnownIssueOTDR](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/SdCb8UgxOmSNNKKnTUpbfA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=ecb904332a83eaf4&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
Calculation Example
If the OTDR marker length is 12, then the OTDR marker calculations are as shown below for this scenario: 
The length of the cable 1 sections in the 1st and 2nd manholes are:
1st detail section in the 1st manhole: 10
2nd detail section in the 2nd manhole: 10
The sum of the cable sections is 10+10=20
The sum of both cable sections is greater than 12 (OTDR marker length) and sum of the cable sections is 20, therefore the marker should exist between the 1st and the 2nd manhole. 
The Marker Distance factor = (Marker distance on the cable 2nd section) / (length of the cable 2nd section) 
= (12 – 10)/10 = 2/10 = 0.2
The length of both conduits between the 1st and the 2nd manhole = 30 (1st conduit) + 40 (2nd conduit) =70. 
By rule, proportionate length of all conduits between the 2 manholes = proportionate length of the cable 2nd section, therefore marker distance = Total length of all conduits * Marker Distance Factor 
= 70 * 0.2 = 14.
This marker distance is less than the lengths of the 1st conduit; therefore, the marker should be placed on the 1st conduit. The marker should be at 14 from the start point of the 1st Conduit. 
  * Tracing from left to right:
    * OTDR length is greater than 10 and less than 14.28, marker places on conduit 1.
    * OTDR length is greater than 14.28 and less than 20, marker places on conduit 2.
    * OTDR length is greater than 20 but less than 30, marker places on Manhole B.
    * OTDR length is greater than 30 but less than 34.5, marker places on conduit 3.
    * OTDR length is greater than 34.5 but less than 40, marker places on conduit 4.

###### Special Considerations for Nongraphic Conductors
This topic describes scenarios in which a cable does not have graphic feature, and it is contained by infrastructure features. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/470503) In images below, the number indicates the order of feature placement. For example, “4-Length 10" indicates that the section is the fourth conduit in the order of placement and has a length of 10 m. 
In the first scenario, all the conduits/ducts contain a single cable, and they are in one direction graphically. The OTDR marker is placed as shown in the image below.

OTDR Marker placement
  * Tracing from left to right:
    * OTDR length is less than 10, marker places on conduit 4.
    * OTDR length is greater than 10 but less than 30, marker places on conduit 2.
    * OTDR length is greater than 30 but less than 60, marker places on conduit 1.
    * OTDR length is greater than 60 but less than 100, marker places on conduit 3.

  * Tracing from right to left:

    * OTDR length is greater than 50 but less than 90, marker places on conduit 3.
    * OTDR length is greater than 90 but less than 120, marker places on conduit 1.
    * OTDR length is greater than 120 but less than 140, marker places on conduit 2.
    * OTDR length is greater than 140 but less than 150, marker places on conduit 4.


In the second scenario, all the conduits/ducts contain a single cable, and they are in different directions graphically. The OTDR marker is placed as shown in the image below. In this scenario, the conduit placed first is in the opposite direction when compared to its neighboring conduits. NetWorks Core software checks whether the first conduit’s direction is like any one of its neighboring conduits' direction. If not, it aligns to direction of neighboring conduits 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Ntz8TlkS6hyBCjbyR_Wa_w-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=5db848d19281e4a8&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
OTDR Marker placement
  * Tracing from left to right:
    * OTDR length is less than 10, marker places on conduit 4.
    * OTDR length is greater than 10 but less than 30, marker places on conduit 2.
    * OTDR length is greater than 30 but less than 60, marker places on conduit 1.
    * OTDR length is greater than 60 but less than 100, marker places on conduit 3.
    * OTDR length is greater than 100 but less than 150, marker places on conduit 5.
  * Tracing from right to left:
    * OTDR length is less than 50, marker places on conduit 5.
    * OTDR length is greater than 50 but less than 90, marker places on conduit 3.
    * OTDR length is greater than 90 but less than 120, marker places on conduit 1.
    * OTDR length is greater than 120 but less than 140, marker places on conduit 2.
    * OTDR length is greater than 140 but less than 150, marker places on conduit 4.

##### Rules for Allocating a Feature after a Break
  * The cable must be allocated correctly to the containing infrastructure (conduit, fiber duct, or fiber inner duct). 
  * Detail graphic sections are placed in the detail drawings associated with any node (for example, a manhole) in the infrastructure network where: 
    * The cable begins or ends. 
    * The cable can be broken. 
    * Duct assignments might change.
  * At locations where the cable enters or leaves the underground network, one of the following must be true: 
    * A detail section must be placed in the detail drawing associated with the node (for example, a manhole) where the cable enters or leaves the network. 
    * A geographic section must be placed within a specified tolerance of the last containing feature in the path where the cable enters or leaves the network. The tolerance is specified in the configuration of the OTDR processing components. 
  * Breaking a cable in a detail section implies that the physical location of the break lies within the bounds of that detail referencing feature (for example, a manhole) and not somewhere in the conduit. If the break is actually in the conduit, an opening like a handhole or passage connector should be created to break the conduit. Then, the conductor can be properly modeled with detail sections at this opening and the break can occur in this access point.

#### Multisection Cable Model Component Lengths
NetWorks Core provides a type of smart label called a component length as part of the multisection cable model. A component length label displays the length of cable from the preceding component length label (if any) on that section or from the beginning of the section. These labels can indicate anything a user needs; for example, they can indicate where equipment should be placed or changes in the direction of the cable, or they can indicate significant changes in elevation (where the length of cable is not the same as the two-dimensional distance on the ground).

[Multisection Cable Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NlBF~fhuOAmRrMXoSw0GQQ)

#### Multisection Cable Model Maintenance
NetWorks Core provides several tools to help you maintain the multisection model. 
  * Special [placement techniques](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Uutp4ZFBuzi4bHXGXoNdww) (CableAndComponentIPT and ComponentLengthLabelIPT) help you to place component lengths and to maintain all the length attributes correctly during placement. 
  * The [Cable Edit Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gG12vPDJmk0rUyku5s3LTg) provides assistance in editing the length-related attributes. 
  * The [LinearLabel functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/94QSUMLS5Ena_K_I69SO9Q) manages the length attributes when a component length is deleted, and it provides some length validation. 
  * The [RelativeComponent functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/94QSUMLS5Ena_K_I69SO9Q) provides the ability to copy the G3E_CID attribute from a linear section to a label attribute to maintain the label-to- section mapping required for section-specific symbology. When a cable feature is broken, several interface objects are involved: 
    * The [CompSortByAttribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oqlFu917uHRUKgEtuhb4DA) custom component elimination method assigns cable sections by their start location. 
    * The [CompAssignToOriginalAtBreak](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oqlFu917uHRUKgEtuhb4DA) custom component elimination method ensures that any component length label near the break point is associated to the end of the original cable section after the break. 
    * The [PostBreakCableLengths](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b4yEJdY9OaWQ_jI2eFS~LQ) post break interface maintain the component, section, start location, and total length attributes. 


Related Topic
[Multisection Cable Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NlBF~fhuOAmRrMXoSw0GQQ)

#### Multisection Cable Model Sections
NetWorks Core models multisection cables as a combination of up to two repeating linear components, one for geographic views and one for detail views. Each section is mapped onto the physical cable using two attributes: 
  * One represents the section start location attribute.
  * One represents the section length.


A total cable length is carried on the primary attribute component of the cable feature.
The section start location is simply the length from the beginning of the physical cable where the associated section begins. Thus, the sections are mapped onto the physical cable by ordering them according to their section start location. The first logical section has a section start location of zero. The next logical section has a section start location that is equal to its predecessor's section start location plus its length. 
Detail linear sections are typically used to represent portions of the cable that are contained in conduit or ducts. The user can draw short graphic sections in detail drawings to represent a much longer physical section of cable.   
|  Example A cable section in a manhole detail drawing represents the length of cable from another manhole to this one through a section of conduit. Thus, the start location and length values are entered to describe the section of cable modeled. The graphic is merely an index to that information since the graphic's scale has nothing to do with the actual portion of the cable modeled.  This use of detail sections as a means of modeling the underground cable is not a requirement of the model. A user can draw all cable sections at scale and only use geographic sections.   |  
| --- |  
Labels that must be associated to a particular cable section must carry an attribute on the label that identifies the G3E_CID of the associated section. This attribute can be used in the label's component view to join with the cable section to pick up section-specific attributes. 
Related Topic
[Multisection Cable Model](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/NlBF~fhuOAmRrMXoSw0GQQ)

### Schematics

#### Adjusting the Appearance of a Schematic

##### Adjusting the Paper Scale for a Schematic

###### Adjusting the Minimum Whitespace for a Schematic
Because [paper scale](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lbnabi4MyAsO~OwN_i8enw) influences the whitespace in a schematic, you should set the paper scale first. Whitespace and paper scale values are relative to each other. Thus, a whitespace parameter of 0.25 with a paper scale parameter of 1,000 is the same as a whitespace parameter of 1 with a paper scale parameter of 4,000. And a whitespace parameter of 100 has more effect on a schematic with a paper scale of 100 than one with a paper scale of 1,000. 
The best whitespace value is normally a fraction of the size (in ground units) of a representative symbol or text style in your schematic. This typically results in enough spacing between elements for good readability, yet not so much space that the diagram becomes too large to be displayed at a reasonable scale. 
If the minimum whitespace is not set correctly in conjunction with the paper scale setting, the elements in your schematic could appear too close together to read comfortably or so far apart that the schematic does not fit in the required space.   
|  Example The text style in a schematic is defined as being 12 points, which is 1/6 of an inch.
  * The paper scale is 1000. If the ground units are in meters, 12 points translates into 4.23 ground units (meters). A whitespace parameter of 1 (meter) is about 1/4 the size of the text, since whitespace is calculated in ground units. The layout algorithm places a label using this text style relatively close to the line it labels, resulting in a pleasing appearance. 
  * Now reduce the paper scale to 10. The text is .0423 ground units. The whitespace parameter of 1 is now almost 24 times as large as the text, which causes the label to appear very far away from the line it labels. If you zoom out far enough to see much of the schematic, the text can be too small to see. Because you cannot decrease the whitespace parameter to less than 1, you must increase the paper scale. 

 |  
| --- |  
[Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259870) to see examples of how whitespace and paper scale values work together to produce a readable schematic. 
The examples below show a schematic with a paper scale value of 1000 and a whitespace value from 0.25 to 4. The schematic starts out congested and becomes more spread out as the whitespace value increases. In these examples, whitespace values of .25 and 1 produce schematics that are too congested, and a whitespace value of 4 produces a schematic that is too spread out. A whitespace value of 2 produces a schematic with clear readability.

Paper scale = 1000

![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259870)
  * To adjust the minimum whitespace for a schematic:


Adjust the [MinimumWhitespace parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/miNcYVOYLmpqWMEoLz5HnQ) in the generation of the schematic XML to modify the presentation. Use Visual Studio to modify the following line in the sample Schematic Manager custom command:   
|  Example AddAttributeToElement("Schematic", "MinimumWhitespace", 10);   |

OR
Adjust the MinimumWhitespace property on the IGTSchematicGeneratorService. 
See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information.   
|  Example _generatorService.MinimumWhitespace = 10;  |

If the schematic is too tight (the lines are short or symbols and labels are too close to each other or to the lines), increase the whitespace value. 
If the schematic is too spread out, decrease the whitespace value.

##### Customizing the Data in Schematic Layouts

###### Schematic Layout
Schematics generated in NetWorks Core are oriented rather than topological or geographic. An oriented, or circuit-board, type schematic represents a network where nodes are connected with linear elements at right angles with no overlapping. 
The circuit-board style presentation of schematic elements allows the following:
  * Orthogonal line-work for edges.
  * Minimal bends in the line-work.
  * Minimal line crossing.
  * Linear simplification, which means collapsing consecutive linear features into a single feature without losing identity. 
  * The ability to specify the minimum amount of white space to be maintained between label boxes and nodes or edges and also between nodes. 
  * The ability to append additional network data and have it merged into the existing diagram with common entities kept spatially coincident. 


The custom command controls the symbology and the input data to schematics layout processing.   
|  Example A custom command can take the input trace recordset and filter out unwanted features before passing it on to the schematics processor.   |  
| --- |  
The schematic graphic layout is completely defined in [XML format](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EiTld4gNjBEFlnYRQrGJLQ). Symbology for nongraphic features is not defaulted. 
Related Topic

Include the BusLayout attribute in the generation of the schematic XML to modify the structure of the schematic.

###### Default Metadata for Editable Schematics
Running the G3E_SCHEMATICS package procedures, AddSchematicCompsByRel() and AddSchematicCompsByFNO(), modifies data tables and creates the schematic components and component views, styles, labels, and legend: 
The procedure adds new columns:  
|  SCHEMATIC_NAME  |  ASPECTRATIO  |  TRACE_SEEDFID  |  TRACE_HINTCIDVALUES  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  SCHEMATIC_TYPE  |  NOTES  |  TRACE_STOPCRITERIA  |  TRACE_GOALFID  |  
|  SCHEMATIC_FORMAT  |  SIMPLIFIED,  |  TRACE_FILTERCRITERIA  |  TRACE_GOALFNO  |  
|  PAPERSCALE  |  NETWORKDEF  |  TRACE_PATHCOST  |   |  
|  MINWHITESPACE  |  TRACE_ID  |  TRACE_SEEDCIDVALUES  |   |  
|  DEFINITION  |  TRACE_NAME  |  TRACE_HINT  |   |  
into the detail attribute component table, whose component number is the value in G3E_DETAIL.G3E_ATTRIBUTECNO. Also, it recreates the ltt view for this component when new columns are added by running AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure. 
The procedure creates schematic components for the indicator features and referencing features that are part of the given connectivity relationship. 
  * If indicator component is placed in Geo window, it creates a schematic indicator component, GC_<FNO>_SCHEMIND_S, which is point type geometry. <FNO> is an indicator feature number. If the feature is involved either in node-edge or in node-ordered connectivity relationship, it creates non-indicator components, point type and text type. The component name is DGC_<FNO>_SCH_X. X is the graphic type (T or P). 
  * If indicator component is placed in Detail window, it creates a schematic indicator component, DGC_<FNO>_SCHEMIND_S, which is point type geometry and has G3E_DETAILID column. <FNO> is an indicator feature number. If the feature is involved either in node-edge or in node-ordered connectivity relationship, the procedure creates non-indicator components, point type and text type. The component name is DGC_<FNO>_SCH_X. X is the graphic type (T or P). 
  * It creates schematic components for the referencing features. The component’s name is DGC_<FNO>_SCH_X. <FNO> is a referencing feature number and X is the graphic type (T, L, or P). It updates G3E_FEATURE.G3E_PRIMARYSCHEMCNO value as the new schematic component number. If the feature is not text type, then it also creates text type schematic component for the label. It updates G3E_FEATURE.G3E_LABELSCHEMCNO value as the text type schematic component number. 
  * If there is no linear type for the artificial edge, it creates linear type artificial edge indicator component, DGC_ARTEDGE_SCH_L, which has G3E_STYLEID column. For its component view, it creates a new style rule which uses the style number from the general parameter, SchematicsArtificialEdgeStyleID. Also, it installs not-null constraints into the G3E_STYLEID column in the base table B$DGC_ARTEDGE_SCH_L with the default value from G3E_GENERALPARAMETER. For the point type feature, it updates G3E_FEATURE.G3E_SECONDARYSCHEMCNO value as the artificial edge indicator component number. 


The procedure creates component views for the new schematic components. First, it looks for the component view that any non-editable schematic might use to drive style rules from the G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table. If no such component views exist in the table, it looks for the component views for its primary geometry component or primary detail component. Then, it creates component view including all the columns from the attribute tables that are discovered in the found component view (as defined in G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION). 
  * If indicator component is placed in Geo window, it creates a schematic indicator component view, VGC_<FNO>_SCHEMIND_S. <FNO> is an indicator feature number. It has G3E_DETAILID column from the detail attribute component. 
  * If indicator component is placed in Detail window, it creates a schematic indicator component view, VDGC_<FNO>_SCHEMIND_S. <FNO> is an indicator feature number. It has G3E_DETAILID column from the geometry component and G3E_REFERENCINGDETAILID column from the detail attribute component’s G3E_DETAILID. 
  * If the indicator feature is involved either in node-edge or in node-ordered connectivity relationship, it creates non-indicator component views for point type, text type, and linear type for the artificial edge, VDGC_<FNO>_SCH_X. <FNO> is an indicator feature number and X is the graphic type (T, L, or P). It has G3E_DETAILID from the detail attribute component and SCHEMATIC_STATE from its geographic component. 
  * It creates schematic component views for the referencing features. The component view’s name is VDGC_<FNO>_SCH_X. <FNO> is a referencing feature number and X is the graphic type (T, L, or P). It has G3E_DETAILID from the detail attribute component and SCHEMATIC_STATE from its geographic component. 
  * If schematic component is point type, it creates component view for the artificial edge, VDGC_<FNO>_SCH_L. <FNO> is a feature number. All columns including G3E_STYLEID are from the artificial edge indicator component which is filtered by the feature number. 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/378301) If the schematic component causes a validation error, you can regenerate the schematic component views. 
The procedure creates style rule and label rule for new schematic components.
If the style rule and label rule for the indicator feature or referencing feature exist in G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table, it uses them for the new schematic component. It provides consistency to use the same style between non-editable schematic and editable schematic. But if the schematic symbology is not defined, it creates new style and label rules for them and adds the data entry into G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table. If style rule in G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_PRIMARYSRNO maps to the area style, it creates a new default point style and a new style rule which maps to it and updates the value in G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_PRIMARYSRNO with the new style rule number. 
The procedure creates legend for the new schematic components.
  * If indicator component is placed in Geo window, the procedure adds its component views into the default geographic legend and new schematic legend. 
  * If indicator component is placed in Detail window, the procedure adds its component views into the default detail legend and new schematic legend. 
  * The procedure adds component views of the schematic component for the referencing feature into the new schematic legend.

###### Default Metadata for Non-editable Schematic Symbology Schemes
As a part of running the NetWorks Core [Upgrade Wizard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TzLTeAS72RGjfAkpnhZqhQ) or running \GTechnology\Services\CreateInitialDatabase\InstallGTechObjects.bat when you create a new schema, scripts populate the default schematic symbology scheme metadata. The default symbology scheme created by the upgrade scripts is a simple scheme that does not include label type schematic elements or port definitions. However, it does populate the following metadata: 
  * The script adds a row to the G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table for each feature defined in G3E_FEATURE that has a G3E_PRIMARYGEOGRAPHICCNO or G3E_PRIMARYDETAILCNO value. Nongraphic and dimension components and features from secondary connections are excluded. 
  * In the G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table, the G3E_PRIMARYVNO and G3E_PRIMARYSRNO are populated for each feature and a G3E_ALTERNATEVNO and G3E_ALTERNATESRNO are populated if the feature has a G3E_PRIMARYDETAILCNO defined. The G3E_PRIMARYVNO values are populated from G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION for the current FNO and primary geographic CNO (or primary detail CNO if a primary geo CNO is null). 
  * The G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_ALTERNATEVNO values are populated from G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION for the current FNO and primary detail CNO (unless a primary geographic CNO has not been defined). 
  * The G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_PRIMARYSRNO and G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_ALTERNATESRNO values are populated from G3E_LEGENDENTRY for the view. 
  * The G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY.G3E_DEFAULTSNO field is populated with the system-default point (G3E_USERNAME = G3E_POINT) or line style (G3E_USERNAME = G3E_LINEAR), depending on whether G3E_GRAPHGEOMETRY is 0 (point style) or 1 (line style).

##### Schematic Labels

###### Defining a Label for a Schematic Symbol
After you define a symbol, you can define a [label for it](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/73be5kLZWoOgZoM3YENRkA). 
  * To define a label for a schematic symbol:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Find, Queries, Traces, and Reports > Schematics > Schematic Symbology > <Scheme Name> <Feature Name> node. 
  2. Add a label to the symbol in the [G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lGZ0jC1ONXF4B7r_Mi2ZEA) table: 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259835) or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. In the G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE field, select Label. 
    3. In the G3E_PRIMARYVNO field, select the published view to drive the label rules.
    4. Optional: In the G3E_PRIMARYSRNO field, select the style rule to apply to the label. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259835) You can define the style for the FNO using the G3E_PRIMARYSRNO value or [using a G3E_STYLEID column value](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yOcXFQla8Qs_8l1km8Rmw) on the component view (as defined in G3E_PRIMARYVNO or G3E_ALTERNATEVNO), but not both. If a G3E_STYLEID column is already used with the component view, leave G3E_PRIMARYSRNO Null. 
    5. Optional: In the G3E_PRIMARYLRNO field, select a label rule to apply to the label. 
    6. In the G3E_LABELPOSITION field, select the value for the [label position](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lGZ0jC1ONXF4B7r_Mi2ZEA). 
    7. In the G3E_LABELAIGNMENT field, select the value for the [label alignment](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~6VeMGRDMTO4Znaq3Xabvw). 
    8. Select values in other fields as required.
    9. Click OK. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259835) The label specification appears under the <Feature Name> > Schematic Types node. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259835) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to commit the changes to the database.

##### Schematic Ports

###### Artificial Edges
When two or more elements are connected into or out of the same port on a node, the schematics software typically creates an artificial edge. When a wide port is used, an artificial edge may or may not be used. A linear component must exist for each feature that participates in an editable schematic. That includes node features that normally would not have a linear element. 
The general parameter [SchematicsArtificialEdgeStyleID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) is used to define the line style for the artificial edge. To more easily read your schematic diagram, select a line style for the artificial edge that differs from the line styles [depicting other edges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4Kt9M3SUDWLAUFHWzUWRfg) in the database. One line style represents all artificial edges in the database. 
If a line style to depict artificial edges is not set, an error message displays when the schematic software tries to display a schematic with artificial edges in it.   
|  Examples Two edges (shown in blue) are connected into the node, and two edges are connected out of the node. The artificial edges are shown in red.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259759) Two nodes (shown in brown) are connected directly out of a node (shown in green). The artificial edges are shown in red.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259759)  |  
| --- |  
  * To define a style for an artificial edge:


  1. Decide which line style to use for artificial edges:
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Line Styles node. 
    2. Select a style you think might be appropriate for the artificial edge style, and click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259759) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to view the style. 
    3. If none of the styles in the database meets the requirement, [define a new one](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V95KhfGh9X9UqzVdBbB7jA). 
    4. When you have made your selection, note the G3E_LINESTYLE.G3E_SNO value.
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Metadata Administration > General Parameter > SchematicsArtificialEdgeStyleID node. In the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_VALUE field, type the value noted in step 1d. 
  3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259759) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to commit the changes to the database. 
  4. To change the ColorOverride value on the XML Node element, you write custom code as in the sample AugNetAttSample project delivered with the software in \GTechnology\Services\Samples\NetSamples\Schematics\AugmentNetworkAttribution. This sample adds a new attribute, but you can use it as a guide for modifying an existing attribute.

###### Defining Ports for a Schematic Symbol
After you define a symbol, you can optionally define ports for it. The schematic software assigns a default port if you do not define your own ports. The default port is centered and has a Both direction, rather than In and/or Out. 
This example workflow defines two ports on a transformer symbol. Like a fuse or a switch, a transformer is a two-node device, but it is different from a fuse or a switch in that the transformer can have multiple connections going out of the symbol. The multiple connections going out are represented as a "wide" port. For a transformer, the In port is on the top, and the Out port is a "wide" port on the bottom of the symbol as shown in the following diagram: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814)
  * To define ports for a schematic symbol:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Find, Queries, Traces, and Reports > Schematics > Port Definitions node. 
  2. Add a port definition in the [G3E_PORTDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3GqB0DMMCvo_X6OpxUXI0w) table: 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a name such as Two-Node – Top/Bottom for the new port definition. 
    3. Click OK. 
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Find, Queries, Traces, and Reports > Schematics > Symbol Ports node from the tree view. 
  4. Define the ports for a symbol in the [G3E_PORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w) table: 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. In the G3E_PDNO field, select the port definition you defined in Step 1b.
    3. In the G3E_PORT field, type a 1 for the ID number of the port for this port definition.
    4. In the G3E_POSITIONX field or G3E_POSITIONY field, type the percentage of the x or y direction for the port. For port 1, the G3E_POSITIONX value is 0 and the G3E_POSIOTIONY value is 100. 
    5. In the G3E_DIRECTION field, select the direction for this port, In, Out, or Both. For port 1, select In. 
    6. To define a side of the symbol on which more than one port is located, in the G3E_BRANCHSIDE field, select Bottom, Top, Left, Right, or Any from the drop-down list. Select Top in the G3E_BRANCHSIDE field for port 1. 
    7. To define a width percentage of the symbol to equally space the connecting features, type a value from 0-200 in the G3E_WIDTH field. For port 1, G3E_WIDTH is Null. 
    8. In the G3E_MUTIPLECONNECTIONS field, select the number of connections this port can have, Only one or Unlimited. For port 1, select Only one. 
    9. Click OK. 
  5. To define a second port for the symbol, in Metadata Explorer, select the Find, Queries, Traces, and Reports > Schematics > Symbol Ports <Port Definition Name> node from the tree view. 
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    2. In the G3E_PDNO field, select the port definition you defined in Step 1b.
    3. In the G3E_PORT field, type a 2 for the ID number of the port for this port definition.
    4. In the G3E_POSITIONX field or G3E_POSITIONY field, type the percentage of the x or y direction for the port. For port 2, the G3E_POSITIONX value is 0 and the G3E_POSIOTIONY value is -100. 
    5. In the G3E_DIRECTION field, select the direction for this port, In, Out, or Both. For port 2, select Out. 
    6. In the G3E_BRANCHSIDE field, select Bottom for port 2. 
    7. Port 2 is a wide port. Type a number from 0-200 in the G3E_WIDTH field.
    8. In the G3E_MUTIPLECONNECTIONS field, select the number of connections this port can have, Only one or Unlimited. For port 2, select Unlimited. 
    9. Click OK. 
  6. To define more ports, repeat Step 5.
  7. Identify the transformer symbol used in a schematic, and associate it with the port definition you defined in Step 2. 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Graphic Display > Normalized Styles > Point Styles, and select the point style you want to associate with the port definition. 
    2. In [G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3GqB0DMMCvo_X6OpxUXI0w) G3E_PDNO field, select the port definition you defined in Step 2. 
  8. If you have not already done so, define a line style to depict [artificial edges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7GmBwuJ7QDjzSb7trtMcDA). 
  9. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to commit the changes to the database. 
  10. To test your edits, refresh the metadata:
    1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259814) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
    2. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Schematics under Analysis, Styles under Graphic Display, and click OK. 
  11. To view the new port assignments, [create a schematic from a trace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8KN~gPekdcr4pnt8FQaWXw) and display it.

###### Modifying Ports in a Schematic
To present a more accurate picture of the network connectivity, you modify the ports. By default, a schematic symbol contains only one connection point or port, positioned in the center of the symbol. Also by default, a port allows both In and Out connections. If the default is not suitable for your model, you can [modify it in metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kmfE9~tVjKrjmP69getibA).   
|  Example ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259812) In the fuse to the left of the highlighted conductor, the conductor line is drawn to the center of the symbol. Because this particular style includes a symbol mask, the non-highlighted presentation (in the left half of that fuse) is an acceptable drawing because it is clear that the conductors are connected to the fuse on the left and on the right.  By contrast, the transformer does not have a masking symbol, so all of the lines show below the symbol. There is no indication of how the conductors are configured around the transformer.   |  
| --- |  
If a symbol, such as a switch or a transformer in the example above, is a two-node device, you need to define two ports. Based on the way the transformer symbol is drawn in the True Type font, you want the In port at the top-center and the Out port at the bottom-center. The first step is to define this type of port definition. You can use a single port definition with any number of symbols. For example, you might define a port as "Two node - Top/Bottom". This indicates its use for two-node devices and the symbol is drawn with a distinct top and bottom presentation. 
  
[Next:  Define ports for a schematic symbol](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kmfE9~tVjKrjmP69getibA).

  6. To test your edits, refresh the metadata:

#### Building a Schematics Command

##### Locating Schematics
Editable schematics are technically detail components of the features that they represent. They follow the same locate behavior as standard detail components. The IGTLocateService includes API for custom software to locate schematics. If the custom software wants the service to pass back schematics in the located DDCKeyObjects collection, then it simply needs to set a property on the IGTLocateService calledIncludeSchematicComponents. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
If a DDCKeyObject returned from Locate represents a schematic, these are its characteristics:
  * A new property called SchematicFeatureRecordset is set. This is an ADO Recordset, each row containing the FNO and FID of one of the geo features that the located schematic element represents. 
  * Most of the other properties do not make sense, since they are feature-oriented properties and a schematic does not necessarily represent one feature. These properties are: ComponentViewName, FID, FNO, and Recordset. 
  * The Geometry property is populated, because a single schematic record does have a single geometry. 


If the DDCKeyObject returned from Locate does not represent a schematic, these are its characteristics: 
  * The SchematicFeatureRecordset is Nothing.
  * The other properties are populated as they have been.


It is important that the custom software not pass in a DDCKeyObject representing a schematic to other objects, since those objects might not know how to handle this different kind of DDCKeyObject.

##### Schematic XML

###### Index to XML Elements and Attributes

###### Edge Element Attributes
The Edge element attributes define the graphical attributes and connectivity information for individual edge elements. The key is the entity number and entity identifier that the schematic edge represents. The element also contains all the labels associated with the edge. The Edge element is a child of the Edges element. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder. 
Attributes  
|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259779) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

###### EdgeArc Element Attributes
The EdgeArc element attributes identify the ordinal position of the arc within the collection of geometries, the start and endpoints of the arc, the radius of the arc, and whether the sweep angle of the arc is greater than or less than 180 degrees. The EdgeArc element is a child of the EdgeGeometry element. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder. 
Attributes  
|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259781) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Ordinal  |  Read-write nonNegativeInteger  |  A non-negative value  |  Required  |  Defines the zero-based position of the arc in the collection of geometries.  |  
|  Locations  |  Read-write String  |  "double,double;  
double,double"   |  Required  |  Defines the real-world coordinates where the arc was placed by the GTSchematicGeneratorService. A valid arc must have exactly two points which represent the start and endpoints of the arc. The attribute contains a comma that separates the x and y coordinate of each point and a semicolon the separates each point.   |  
|  Radius  |  Read-write positiveDouble  |  A positive double value  |  Required  |  Defines the radius of the arc.  |  
|  GreaterThanPi   |  Read-write Boolean  |  True  
false   |  Optional  |  Defines whether the sweep angle of an arc is greater than or less than 180 degrees. The default value is False.   |  
|  Clockwise  |  Read-write Boolean  |  true  
false   |  Optional  |  Defines the direction of the arc. The default value is False.  |

###### EdgeGeometry Element
Each edge in a schematic is represented by a composite geometry, unless it has been simplified. A composite geometry is a collection of subgeometries where each subgeometry is either a polyline or an arc for the Edge element and a polyline for the Node element. The EdgeGeometry element is a child of its associated Edge or Node. For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder. Data types are .NET.

###### EdgePolyline Element Attributes
The EdgePolyline element attributes identify the ordinal position of the polyline within the collection of geometries and the locations of the polyline. The IGTSchematicGeneratorService adds each polyline to the collection. The EdgePolyline element is a child of the EdgeGeometry element. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder.

|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259796) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Ordinal  |  Read- write nonNegativeInteger  |  A non-negative value  |  Required  |  Defines the zero-based position of the polyline in the collection of geometries.  |  
|  Locations  |  Read- write String  |  "double,double;double, double[;double,double]*"  |  Required  |  Defines the real-world coordinates where the polyline was placed by the GTSchematicGeneratorService. A valid polyline must have at least two points. The attribute contains a comma that separates the x and y coordinate of each point and a semicolon the separates each point.   |

###### EdgeStyle Element Attributes

###### Node Element Attributes
The Node element attributes define the graphical attributes and connectivity information for individual node elements. The key is the entity number and entity identifier that the schematic node represents. The element also contains all the labels associated with the node, and it defines the location and rotation of the node symbol. The Node element is a child of the Nodes element. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder.

The NodeLabel and EdgeLabel element attributes also define the location and rotation in degrees between the escapement vector and the x-axis. The NodeLabel element is a child of its associated Node. The EdgeLabel element is a child of its associated Edge. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder.

###### Port Element Attributes
The Port Element attributes define the port or connection point information of a node style. A node style can have multiple ports and each port can have one or many connections to it. Edges should connect to the available port that is of the right type and is closest to the line created by extending the edge through the center of the node. For instance, the from end of an edge should connect to the closest available In or Both port that is created by extending the edge through the center of the node. The closest port may not be available if the port only allows for one connection and that connection is already being used. The Port element is a child of the Ports element. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder. 
Attributes  
|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259783) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Position  |  Read- write String  |  "[-100..100],  
[-100..100]"   |  Required  |  [Defines the position](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w) of the port as a percentage of the height and width relative to the center of the node.   |  
|  Direction  |  Read- write direction  |  In  
Out  
Both   |  Optional  |  Defines the direction in which an edge can connect to the port. An edge can connect into a port, or out of a port, or both. The default value is Both.   |  
|  Connections  |  Read- write connections  |  OnlyOne  
Unlimited   |  Optional  |  Defines the number of connections that can be made to a port. A port can have an unlimited number of connections or it can just have one connection. The default is Unlimited.   |  
|  BranchSide  |  branchSide  |  Bottom  
Top  
Left

|  Width  |  width  |  0-200  |  Optional  |  Defines the width of the port as a percentage of the size of the symbol to a maximum of 200 percent.   |

###### Schematic Element Attributes
The Schematic element attributes define the general drawing parameters for the layout of a schematic. The Schematic element also contains the node style definitions and their associated port information, edge style definitions, and the networks of schematic entities. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder. 
Attributes  
|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259747) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Type  |  Read- write type  |  Oriented  
Topological-Not used.  
Geographical-Not used.   |  Required  |  Defines the type of schematic graph to generate.  |  
|  Format  |  Read- write format  |  LeftToRight  
TopToBottom  
RightToLeft  
BottomToTop   |  Required  |  Defines the format of the schematic. This attribute applies only to Oriented entities within the graph and is ignored for the other types.   |  
|  SchematicDefinition  |  Read- write Integer  |   |  Required  |  Specifies the named schematic symbology definition number to use to represent the schematic entities.   |  
|  StraightLine  |  Read- write Boolean  |  true  
false   |  Optional  |  Defines whether the generated schematic folds the graph to minimize area. If the value is True, the schematic does not fold the graph to minimize area, giving it a more unidirectional structure.  If the value is False, the schematic layout folds the graph to minimize area and keep the diagram as compact as possible. This attribute applies only to Oriented entities within the graph and is ignored for the other types. [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KcUP0HuDsK3~~JiY2Sb1HA) to see an example schematic drawing before and after the Straightline attribute is used. The default is False.   |  
|  MinimizeEdgeCrossings  |  Read- write Boolean  |  true  
false   |  Optional  |  Not used. Specifies that the layout should attempt to lay out the entities so the edges cross each other the minimal number of times. If this value is True, it can result in a schematic that requires more space. The default is False.   |  
|  MinimumWhitespace  |  Read- write positive Double  |  A positive double value  |  Optional  |  Defines the minimum amount of whitespace in ground units that surrounds each entity in the schematic. The default is 1.0   |  
|  EdgeSimplificationTolerance  |  Read- write nonNegativeDouble  |  A non-negative value   |  Optional  |  Defines the tolerance value used to simplify or thin vertices in an edge. This attribute supports line simplification of edges between geo-placed nodes. This attribute applies only to geographical entities within the graph and is ignored for other graphic types. The default is 0.0 which indicates that simplification does not occur. Not used.   |  
|  PaperScale  |  Read- write positiveInteger  |  A non-negative value  |  Optional  |  Defines the nominal map scale. This allows the placement of labels and symbology with specific reference to the output map scale. The paper scale is used in calculating the relative size of the symbols and lines used in the orthogonal schematic. The default is 1.   |  
|  Simplified  |  Read- write Boolean  |  true  
false   |  Optional  |  Indicates whether the schematic has been processed with the IGTSchematicGeneratorService [Simplify ](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm)method.   |  
|  BusLayout  |  Boolean  |  true  
false   |  Optional  |  Specifies whether an optional bus layout algorithm is used to process the network data. The algorithm identifies the longest sequence of elements in each branch and positions these in a perpendicular arrangement. The layout is more orthogonal and less tree-like than the standard layout. Branches are organized in a way that minimizes the number of intersections between edges.   |

The schematic flows left-to-right, but the schematic section outlined in red flows bottom-to-top.

###### UserNodeAttribute and UserEdgeAttribute Element Attributes
The UserNodeAttribute and UserEdgeAttribute elements can have zero or more UserNodeAttribute child elements. The Edge XML element each may have zero or more UserEdgeAttribute child elements. These elements are generated if an IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution object was supplied to the IGTSchematicGeneratorService.Append method, and that object set the IncludeInXML property to True for one or more IGTSchematicAttribute objects. For each such attribute, a UserNodeAttribute or UserEdgeAttribute child element is generated for the node or edge. The UserNodeAttribute element is a child of Node element. The UserEdgeAttribute element is a child of the Edge element. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
For more information, see the Schematic.xsd in the \GTechnology\Program folder.
