|  Name  |  [Data Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259789) Data type is .Net.  |  Values  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ColumnName  |  Read- write String  |  The name of the component view column.  |  Required  |  Records the name of the column of the component view from whence this UserNodeAttribute or UserEdgeAttribute element came.   |  
|  Value  |  Read- write String  |   |  Required  |  Records the value obtained from the component view, converted to a string. The conversion is done using the locale of the client where the schematic was generated.   |

###### Schematic XML Definition
The major sections of the schematic XML are as follows: 
Schematic
The [Schematic element](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/miNcYVOYLmpqWMEoLz5HnQ) is at the top of the XML hierarchy. This element contains all the layout parameters for the schematic. For example, the Schematic element contains the type and format of the schematic, the minimum amount of whitespace between schematic entities, whether the layout should attempt to minimize the number of edge crossings. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information.   
|  Example <Schematic Type="Oriented" Format="LeftToRight" SchematicDefinition="2"   
MinimumWhitespace="2"  
PaperScale="1000"xmlns="http://www.intergraph.com/GTechnology/schematic">  |  
| --- |  
NodeStyles
The [NodeStyle element](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/quuOCAsS37CMOvgpJnFIDA) is a child of the root Schematic element. It contains all the information for each different symbolization of a node in the schematic.   
|  Example The schematic XML contains one entry for each permutation of the attributes associated with the display of a switch in the schematic—one for an open switch, one for a closed switch. Representation of a red switch and a blue switch requires more entries.   |  
| --- |  
Each NodeStyle indicates the size of the node and the [available ports](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9X0C_oCoNMdRveCrKVCHhA) with which edges can be connected to the node.   
|  Example <NodeStyles>  
<NodeStyle ID="31402012" Size="5.999999,5.916666" Alignment="TopCenter">  
<Ports>  
<Port Position="0,100" />  
</Ports>  
</NodeStyle>  
</NodeStyles>  |  
| --- |  
EdgeStyles
The EdgeStyles element is a child of the root Schematic element and owner to [EdgeStyle elements](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/z4~u9Gp2KYgRiLcEkN32vA) which contain the information for each different edge style. Each EdgeStyle specifies the width of the edge in ground units.   
|  Example <EdgeStyles>  
<EdgeStyle ID="30602002" Width="0.0005787024" />  
</EdgeStyles>  |  
| --- |  
UserData
This section supports custom software used to manipulate the schematic XML content. NetWorks Core creates all the XML sections except UserData. The UserData section is a place where the custom interface can store parameters used in its processing of the XML. For example, the [Schematic Manager Custom command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BR4RZUU4PQ7JgzBihu3yJA) adds trace parameter data to this section.   
|  Example <UserData SchematicName="Sample Schematic" NetworkDefinition="Adhoc trace">  
<Traces>  
<Trace ID="56170" TraceID="4" TraceName="Demo1" TraceSeedFID="8916" />  
</Traces>  
</UserData>  |  
| --- |  
Networks
There is one section for each input [network data set](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tTHbQRnrnnm~zLd95RWdlQ) and includes the nodes and edges (and their labels) their locations, keys, and so forth.   
|  Example <Networks>  
<Network ID="0" Name="ExampleNetwork" StartKeys="2,1" State="Added">  
<Nodes>  
<Node Key="1,1" FromConnector="2" ToConnector="15453099" StyleID="31402012">  
<NodeLabels>  
<NodeLabel Ordinal="0" Size="4.25,2.666666" Position="BelowCenter" Alignment="MiddleCenter"  
StyleID="31403002" Text="Example node label" />  
</NodeLabels>  
</Node>  
</Nodes>  
<Edges>  
<Edge Key="2,1" FromConnector="1" ToConnector="2" StyleID="30602007"></Edge>  
<Edge Key="2,2" FromConnector="2" ToConnector="3" StyleID="30602007"></Edge>  
<Edge Key="2,3" FromConnector="3" ToConnector="4" StyleID="30602007"></Edge>  
<Edge Key="2,4" FromConnector="3" ToConnector="5" StyleID="30602007">  
<EdgeLabels>  
<EdgeLabel Ordinal="0" Size="10.5,2.666666" Position="AboveCenter" Offset="2.00014467560686"  
Alignment="MiddleCenter" StyleID="30603002" Text="Example edge label" />  
</EdgeLabels>  
</Edge>  
<Edge Key="2,5" FromConnector="4" ToConnector="6" StyleID="30602007"></Edge>  
<Edge Key="2,6" FromConnector="6" ToConnector="7" StyleID="30602007"></Edge>  
</Edges>  
</Network>  
</Networks>  |  
| --- |

###### Schematic XML Hierarchy
As shown in the following diagram, the XML definition contains a specific hierarchy for describing a schematic. The Groups element is not used. ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/_urzKRrNKODARh0Q4~kYgg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=74c26ce7eff5d76c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
The remaining XML nodes define the networks of schematic entities as shown in the following diagram. 
Each network is broken down into the two types of entities, edges and nodes. Each node and edge contains instance-based layout information and the labels associated with it. Click [here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QGj4lyTDdzUP7Di6~YtZQQ) to see an example schematics xml. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/ClMVeqil0WizUO0da1sAxA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=de83ccede453eda1&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

###### Schematic XML Processing Points

###### Append Processing
Appending a network means adding one or more network data sets (usually trace or query results) to the schematic XML to retrieve the set of features that form the content of the schematic. The network data set must contain feature keys (G3E_FNO and G3E_FID), plus the information about how the features are connected. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259822) Data gathered by query must represent logically connected data, or you must build the connectivity in the recordset before calling the Append method. Connectivity can be modified after Append, but the connectivity identifier fields must exist in the network recordset. 
Each trace network must be appended to the schematic, and multiple networks can be appended to a single schematic. 
The implementation of this function is [IGTSchematicGeneratorService.](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm)Append. IGTSchematicGeneratorService.Append takes the network recordset and builds the XML from it, so it is where most of the XML manipulation occurs. This method is also where the majority of schematics-related metadata is used. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
XML Attributes
IGTSchematicGeneratorService.Append adds [all schematic XML](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~c3~hoK8mg8yA3~e2xJbwg) elements and attributes except those specified for the [Simplify](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iWpnwZWsNCYMRMrTe84VcA) and [Layout](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/f2jHhdF~mp9WhGbQCpRlhg) methods. The IGTSchematicGeneratorService.Append method is where [customization occurs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/f2jHhdF~mp9WhGbQCpRlhg) using the AugmentNetworkAttribution object. 
In the following example, the network data consists of the results from an electrical circuit trace.

AugmentNetworkAttribution
During Append processing, you can use [IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Interfaces_IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution.htm) object methods and properties to customize the default behavior of the IGTSchematicGeneratorService, for example, synthesize a single geometry from multiple elements or change the display of a feature that ties together two networks. The IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution object is called before style and label computation and is given the current feature data one feature class (FNO) at a time. The modified form of the feature data returned from the custom callout is processed for style and label data as normal. IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution object can also explicitly specify the style and label information in case the attribution is not available to achieve the required symbology. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259822) The descriptions of objects related to IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution use notation commonly used for COM objects. However, all of the objects related to this object are implemented as C# classes because the interface is implemented in Visual Studio .NET. Also, all documented collection types provide an enumerator capability, so that a "for each" loop can be used to iterate over the collection. The enumerator is not explicitly documented. 
In the example process, AugmentNetworkAttribution is used to append an attribute value to conductor feature elements (for example, phase attribute value).

###### Layout Processing
The [IGTSchematicGeneratorService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm).Layout method consists of two distinct steps. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
Compute the sizes for all styles involved in the schematic graph.
  * If an element does not have a style ID, Layout throws an exception. Layout performs this computation so that the custom command can fill in style information for elements for which there is no component view information. This computation is an alternative to implementing IGTAugmentNetworkAttribution to handle elements that have no style ID. 
  * Compute the locations of the nodes, edges, and labels of the graph.


XML Attributes
The Layout method adds the following attributes:
  * Location attributes to Node, NodeLabel, and EdgeLabel elements
  * EdgeGeometry elements to Edge elements. This includes all child elements (EdgePolyline, EdgeArc) and all attributes. 


Removes the following attributes:
  * State attribute from Network elements

###### Simplify Processing
The [IGTSchematicGeneratorService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm).Simplify method processes the nodes and edges of the XML, merging consecutive (connectivity-wise) edges that meet the following conditions. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
  * The two edges have the same value for an attribute whose name is specified in the call to Simplify. 
  * No other elements are connected at the connection point that is common to both edges.
  * If a particular edge exists in more than one network in the same schematic, then it is not merged in any of the networks. This is to avoid situations where one edge is represented by its own single graphic and also by a merged graphic with other edges. 


Edge merge processing includes the following:
  * Changes the GeoLocations attributes of the first edge in the merge list to include the GeoLocations attributes of all those edges merged. The geometries (Location and Locations attributes) are updated only after the IGTSchematicGeneratorService.Layout method used (then the geometries are merged). 
  * Marks the merged edges as having been merged and stores the identity of the edge they are merged into. This involves adding and populating a [SimplifiedOwnerKey](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5WRbX4~772tRwo~tWvfsFw) attribute. 
  * Changes the FromConnector and ToConnector values of the final edge to reflect the effect of combining these edges into one. The connected node (if any) connected to the last merged edge has its FromConnector or ToConnector value (whichever the merged edge was connected to) set to the appropriate node value for the resultant edge (resulting from the merge). 


Therefore, no data are deleted, and you can undo the simplify operation.
The Simplify method is optional. You should call it before the Layout method and after the Append method. When GeoLocations and SimplifiedKeys attributes are appended to, the values are delimited with a semicolon. When Simplify merges a child edge into an owner edge, the GeoLocations attribute value from the child is appended to the GeoLocations attribute value of the owner. The values are delimited with a semicolon. 
XML Attributes
The Simplify method adds the following attributes:
  * SimplifiedKeys attribute, where necessary, to Edge elements.
  * SimplifiedOwnerKey attribute, where necessary, to Edge elements. 


The Simplify method updates the following attributes:
  * ToConnector attribute for the “owner” key
  * GeoLocations attribute for the “owner” key


Simplify is used to merge adjacent linears (conductors) that share the same Phase attribute value. In this example only edges 2,5 and 2,6 were merged together. Edges 2,1 and 2,2 are connected. However, a node is connected at their junction, and so they cannot be simplified. Edges 2,4 and 2,5 are also connected, but they cannot be merged because they have different Phase attribute values.   
|  Example <Schematic Type="Oriented" Format="LeftToRight" SchematicDefinition="2" MinimumWhitespace="2" PaperScale="1000" xmlns="http://www.intergraph.com/GTechnology/schematic"> <NodeStyles> <NodeStyle ID="31402012" Size="5.999999,5.916666" Alignment="TopCenter"> <Ports> <Port Position="0,100" /> </Ports> </NodeStyle> </NodeStyles> <EdgeStyles> <EdgeStyle ID="30602007" Width="0.0002893512" /> </EdgeStyles> <Networks> <Network ID="0" Name="ExampleNetwork" StartKeys="2,1" State="Added"> <Nodes> <Node Key="1,1" FromConnector="2" ToConnector="15453099" StyleID="31402012"> <NodeLabels> <NodeLabel Ordinal="0" Size="4.25,2.666666" Position="BelowCenter" Alignment="MiddleCenter" StyleID="31403002" Text="Example node label" /> </NodeLabels> </Node> </Nodes> <Edges> <Edge Key="2,1" FromConnector="1" ToConnector="2" StyleID="30602007"> <EdgeUserAttributes Phase="1"> </Edge> <Edge Key="2,2" FromConnector="2" ToConnector="3" StyleID="30602007"> <EdgeUserAttributes Phase="1"> </Edge> <Edge Key="2,3" FromConnector="3" ToConnector="4" StyleID="30602007"> <EdgeUserAttributes Phase="1"> </Edge> <Edge Key="2,4" FromConnector="3" ToConnector="5" StyleID="30602007"> <EdgeLabels> <EdgeLabel Ordinal="0" Size="10.5,2.666666" Position="AboveCenter" Offset="2.000144675606" Alignment="MiddleCenter" StyleID="30603002" Text="Example edge label" /> </EdgeLabels> </Edge> <Edge Key="2,5" FromConnector="4" ToConnector="7" StyleID="30602007" SimplifiedKeys="2,6"> <EdgeUserAttributes Phase="2"> </Edge> <Edge Key="2,6" FromConnector="6" ToConnector="7" StyleID="30602007" SimplifiedOwnerKey="2,5"> <EdgeUserAttributes Phase="2"> </Edge> </Edges> </Network> </Networks> </Schematic>  |

#### Getting Started with Schematics

##### Displaying a Schematic Using the Open Schematic Window Command
These steps display an editable schematic using the Open Schematic Window command. They assume you have followed the initial steps outlined in [Getting Started with Schematics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EYmI9IJWOuPST3spYRFvGQ) and placed one or more schematic indicator components in a geographic or detail window. Editable schematics are not spatially filtered to an area of interest. 
See [Displaying a Schematic Using the Sample Command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8KN~gPekdcr4pnt8FQaWXw) for an alternative way to display a schematic. 
  * To display a schematic with Open Schematic Window:


  1. From the Windows tab in the Open group, select Schematic Window. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/378030) If a feature exists in the select set when you open a schematic window, the Related Schematics tab displays a list of schematic drawings associated with (owned by or participated in) the feature. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/378030) If the select set is empty, or the feature you selected does not own or participate in any details, the Related Schematics tab is disabled. 
![openschematicwindow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/tGewmkttpe0RvCSQJ5GVcA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=ccbdbd4590ab7a17&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Check the box next to a detail or schematic window listed in the Owned schematics or Details participated in lists. You can select more than one from the list. The items you select are added to the Selected schematic windows list. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/378030) If no feature exists in the select set when you open a schematic window, the All Schematics tab displays a tree view showing all schematics grouped by features with associated schematic indicator components. 
![OpenSchematicWindow_AllSchematicsTab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/Gy16QOiH_0t1sB2nrVh2Jg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=404837434b2ef321&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. Expand the appropriate top-level node in the Browse schematic windows tree view, and check one or more editable schematics from the tree view. 
The schematics you checked are added to the Selected schematic windows list. If you check a top-level node, it is not added to the Selected schematic windows list. 
  4. To search for schematics, type the exact schematic name (no wildcards), and press ENTER or click Add. 
The schematic is added to the Selected schematic windows list, the tree view expands, and the schematic is checked. This schematic is also checked on the Related Schematics tab, if present. 
  5. To remove a schematic from the Selected schematic windows list, click to clear the item. 
The software synchronizes the tabs. The schematic is cleared on all tabs. You can also remove items by clearing them from the Related Schematics and All Schematics tabs. 
  6. If only one schematic window is listed in Selected schematic windows, you can check the Replace contents of active window box to replace the contents of the active window (geographic or detail) with the selected schematic window. Leave the box cleared to create a new schematic window. 
  7. Click OK. 
A schematic window appears displaying the schematic drawing windowed to the minimum bounding rectangle (MBR). 


[Next: Interact with the schematic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1H7cVUNVRh19m7yYI962gQ)

##### Displaying a Schematic Using the Sample Command
These steps display a schematic using the sample Schematic Manager command delivered with NetWorks Core and one or more traces you have already run. They also assume you have followed the initial steps outlined in [Getting Started with Schematics](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EYmI9IJWOuPST3spYRFvGQ). 
See [Displaying a Schematic Using the Open Schematic Window command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o66JRntBa1Afv6q8ZXV1iA) for an alternative way to display a schematic. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259816) This sample command requires an active job, although the Schematics subsystem does not. 
  * To display a schematic with Schematic Manager:


  1. From the Analysis menu, select Schematic Manager. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/6pZuPzcG2jv0sRgUFE1DEw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=0300715eb3cf3571&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Click Add under the Non-Editable grouping for a non-editable schematic or click Populate under the editable grouping for an editable schematic. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259816) An editable schematic displays in the list for each schematic indicator placed in a geographic or detail window. Schematic indicators that reference an existing schematic window display only once in the list. Populate is enabled only if an editable schematic is selected. The type of the schematic displays in the Type column: E for editable and N for non-editable. See the image below for an example. 
![SchematicManager_Type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/n1o97PS6RM5nFmhaLJ~j8w-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=d331d2236021a49e&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. In the Name field, type Default Schematic. 
![AddSchematic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/sF9L1zNfi0_f3hLJmn~ZOA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=29cc4f0b49ff81ae&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259816), check the trace you just ran, and click Add. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259816)
  5. Check Use sampleAugmentNetworkAttribution interface to determine if the [sample implementation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1QvdqGLI9iNYuAxjQNv~PA) of the AugmentNetworkAttribution interface is used to display the schematic for non-editable schematics. This checkbox also controls the attribute used by the Sample command to simplify the network. If you check this option, the network is simplified on the Phase attribute, as added to the [UserEdgeAttribute](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/54dPWInp1n8UuQ3QG_iRlg) for the Sample command. If you do not check this option, the network is simplified on the StyleID attribute of the [Edge element](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5WRbX4~772tRwo~tWvfsFw). 
  6. Define the layout parameters:
    1. On the Add Schematic dialog box, select a format type from the Format drop-down list. 
       * Left to right — The schematic follows the is constructed from left to right, following the connectivity of the network. 
       * Top to bottom — The schematic is constructed from top to bottom, following the connectivity of the network. 
       * Right to left — The schematic is constructed from right to left, following the connectivity of the network. 
       * Bottom to top — The schematic is constructed from bottom to top, following the connectivity of the network. 
    2. To keep linear elements from [being bent to preserve space](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KcUP0HuDsK3~~JiY2Sb1HA), check Straight line. 
  7. To use a [predefined scheme for the schematic symbology](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CTsnz9yX8P4C21fSuVfBQA), select one from the Symbology Scheme drop-down list. 
  8. On the Add/Populate Schematic dialog box, click Create/Update. This generates the Schematic. Editable schematics are saved automatically. Non-editable schematics require you to select the schematic and click Save. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259816) Schematics generated for node-ordered traces are augmented with any related point features found. 
  9. On the Schematic Manager dialog box, highlight the schematic you just added, and click Display. 
  10. The non-editable schematic name appears in red on the Schematic Manager dialog box until you click Save. The schematic appears in a new map window. 


[Next: Interact with the schematic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1H7cVUNVRh19m7yYI962gQ)

##### Editable Schematics

###### Create a New Schematic Component and Its Component Views
From an SQL prompt, connect as schema owner and type the following to create new schematic component and its component views: 
SQL> execute G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByFNO(<RNO>, ‘<Indicator FNOs>’, <FNO>, <LNO>, ‘<Window types>’, ‘<Label>’);  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>  |  A number-type argument which is a relationship number (G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO) for the relationship associated with the traces that are used as network source. The relationship must be either node-edge or node-ordered connectivity.   |  
|  <Indicator FNOs>  |  A string-type argument which is list of the indicator FNOs. It is a comma-delimited number format. It should be the same value used previously to run G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure for the same RNO.   |  
|  <FNO>  |  A number -type argument that is the additional feature number in the connectivity table.   |  
|  <LNO>  |  A number-type argument that is the legend number that was created for the relationship number by running G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure for the same RNO.   |  
|  <Window types>  |  A string-type argument which is list of the window type which the indicator component is placed in. It is comma-delimited number format and is associated with <Indicator FNOs> order. It should be the same value used in running G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure for the same RNO last time.   |  
|  <Label>  |  An optional string argument that contains the label format content (for example, the value from G3E_LABEL.G3E_CONTENT) if the label rule does not exist in G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY table for the feature number in the <FNO> argument.   |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/378279)
  * If the procedure is run more than one time, <Indicator FNOs> and <Window types> values should be the same values all the time. 
  * When it is executed, set output buffer to off in versions of Oracle before 10.2 or set it to unlimited in versions of Oracle 10.2 and higher. 
  * The procedure creates the log file, Schematic_<RNO>.txt, under the NetWorks Core diagnostics log directory which is defined in GTECH_DIAG_LOG directory object on the server. <RNO> is the first input argument on the above procedure. It stores insert, update, and DDL statement. The following query shows the ‘GTECH_DIAG_LOG’ directory: 

  
|  Example After creating schematic components and component views for relationship number 8, if new feature, 12600, is added into the relationship table for RNO 8, then the following statement execution creates schematic components and component views for the additional feature, 12600.  SQL> execute G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByFNO(8, ‘12200,12400’, 12600, 10, ‘1, 0’);
  * 8 is the relationship number.
  * The values for <Indicator FNOs>, ‘12200, 12400’, and <Window types>, ‘1, 0’, are the same value used in running the G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure. 
  * 12600 is a new additional feature number.
  * 10 is the legend number that was created by running the G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel() procedure for the relationship number 8. 

 |  
| --- |  
  * SQL> SELECT DIRECTORY_PATH FROM DBA_DIRECTORIES WHERE DIRECTORY_NAME = ‘GTECH_DIAG_LOG’;

###### Create a Schematics Package
From an SQL prompt, connect as schema owner and type the following to create a new schematic component and its component views: 
SQL> execute G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel(<RNO>, ‘<Indicator FNOs>’, ‘<Window types>’);  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>  |  A number-type argument which is a relationship number (G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO) for the relationship that is associated with the traces that are used as network source. The relationship must be either node-edge or node-ordered connectivity.   |  
|  <Indicator FNOs>  |  A string-type argument which is a list of the indicator FNOs. It is a comma-delimited number format.   |  
|  <Window types>  |  A string type argument, which is list of the window type that the indicator component is placed in. It is comma-delimited number format and is associated with <Indicator FNOs> order. 0 means that it is placed in Geo window. 1 means that it is placed in Detail window.   |  
  * To add more relationships in the schematic, run the above procedure again, using the same <Indicator FNOs> and <Window types>. You can run the procedure as often as required to create the appropriate number of relationships. 
  * When the procedure is executed, set the output buffer to off in versions of Oracle before 10.2 or set it to unlimited in versions of Oracle 10.2 and higher. 
  * The procedure creates a log file, Schematic_<RNO>.txt, under the NetWorks Core diagnostics log folder, defined in the GTECH_DIAG_LOG directory object on the server. <RNO> is the first input argument on the procedure. It stores insert, update, and DDL statements. The following query shows the GTECH_DIAG LOG directory: 
SQL> SELECT DIRECTORY_PATH FROM DBA_DIRECTORIES WHERE DIRECTORY_NAME = ‘GTECH_DIAG_LOG’; 
  * To cleanup or delete the metadata created by the G3E_SCHEMATICS package, see the statements generated in the Schematic_<RNO>.txt log file. 
  * The package creates several [component views](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CAlvbxZ9ZozWf1SAKsbM6w). 

  
|  Example When the schematic components need to be created for the relationship number 8, execute the following statement:  SQL> execute G3E_SCHEMATICS.AddSchematicCompsByRel(8, ‘12200, 12400’, ‘1, 0’);
  * The schematic indicator component for feature number 12200 is placed in the Detail window. 
  * The schematic indicator component for feature number 12400 is placed in the Geo window.

#### Interacting with Schematics

##### Selecting Schematic Elements
Editable schematics are technically detail components of the features that they represent. They follow the same select behavior as standard detail components. 
Non-editable schematics can be selected in all scenarios except when the Edit tool is in single-component mode. For all other commands, as well as Edit tool in multi-component mode, non-editable schematics are always selected. This means that the default behavior is to enable the selecting of schematics. The Edit Tool command has to tell the non-editable schematics not to select in single component mode. This also means that except in the one Edit Tool scenario, there is no such thing as a single-mode selection criterion. Non-editable schematics are inherently feature-oriented and are selected based on that. 
The ability to select or deselect a non-editable schematic element with a mouse click or CTRL + click is [determined by the custom command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qOGERn8peO14uBBlOcKawQ). Even so, you can select only the entire feature in a schematic, regardless of the selection mode. In addition, non-editable schematic elements of selected features are always displayed in the select color, even if only one component of that feature was selected 
Highlighting
Selected schematic elements do not highlight by default. But, if the Edit tool and Select commands tell them to highlight, only the particular schematic graphic hovered over is highlighted in the active map view. 
Tooltips
The tooltip from the recordset of the schematic graphic displays. The tooltip comes from the specific geometry being hovered over. The content of the tooltip is an attribute in the [schematics XML](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EiTld4gNjBEFlnYRQrGJLQ). If that attribute does not exist, the default is used. 
PickQuick
If multiple schematic graphics representing different FNO/FIDs are located, PickQuick shows each with highlighting. A single entry for each schematic geometry is in the PickQuick box, regardless of which features that geometry represents. If multiple schematic graphics representing the same FNO/FIDs (the label and the edge, for example) are located, they are not combined into one row in the PickQuick box but follows the existing pattern for geographic data. 
If both schematic and feature components are clicked, then PickQuick puts both of them in its selection. 
The content of the PickQuick box is the same as the tooltip.
Deselecting Schematic Elements
Normally, CTRL + click is used to flip the select-state of the feature that was clicked. However, a schematic can represent several features, and these features can be in various select-states. CTRL + click works a little differently in schematics. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259880) CTRL + clicking on a schematic in effect temporarily places the system in multi-select mode. 
Multi-component  
|  CRTL + click on a selected schematic graphic  |  CTRL + click on a selected feature that is part of a schematic  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  All schematics that contain the FNO/FID of the selected schematic graphic are deselected.  |  If this is the last constituent feature for the schematic being deselected, the schematic graphic deselects. If other constituent features of the schematic are still selected, the schematic is not deselected.   |  
|  All feature components are deselected for all FNO/FIDs contained by the deselecting schematic graphic, whether those features were selected or not.   |  All feature components for the FNO/FID of the graphic are deselected.  |  
Single component  
|  CRTL + click on a selected schematic graphic  |  CTRL + click on a selected feature that is part of a schematic  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  All schematics that contain the FNO/FID of the selected schematic graphic are deselected.  |  If this is the last component of its feature to be deselected, the above logic applies: if this is the last constituent feature for the schematic that is being deselected, then the schematic graphic deselects. If there are still other constituent features of the schematic selected, the schematic does not deselect. If this is not the last component of its feature to be deselected, there is no change to the schematic entity.   |  
|  All feature components are un-selected for all FNO/FIDs contained by the "deselecting" schematic graphic. This is true whether those features were selected or not.   |  A single feature component is deselected.   |

Editable schematics are technically detail components of the features that they represent. They follow the same display control behavior as standard detail components. 
You control the display of a non-editable schematic through the Display Control. The following buttons on the toolbar are available for schematics:   
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  Status is enabled to show and hide the Locate and Display Status and the Display Scale Range checkboxes.   |

|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  Remove is enabled when the Schematic parent node, an individual schematic node, or a trace node is selected. If a trace node is removed, then the rest of the traces are still displayed. But the trace node that was selected is removed along with its associated data.   |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  Fit is enabled when the Schematic parent node, an individual schematic node, or a trace node is selected.   |  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  Symbology is enabled when the trace node is selected, but disabled when its parent nodes are selected. This parallels the queries. Note that when this override is selected, it overrides the entire trace, and does not respect any lower-level overrides in the Schematics XML.   |

|  ![Display Control Override Translucency BTN](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  The Override Translucency drop-down list and button let you override the specified metadata settings for foreground and background [translucency](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zADwGGNT_iyU4JUCGMmBZg) on a selected tree view node. Select a percent of translucency from 0 to 100 from the drop-down list. Then, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725) to update the map window. To set more complicated translucency overrides, click the button to display the Translucency dialog box.   |  
|  ![Display Control Reset Translucency Override BTN](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259725)  |  Reset Translucency Override restores translucency settings to the previous settings.   |  
Filter, Remove Filter, Reset Legend, and CAD are disabled. Schematics cannot be filtered. 
The DisplayStatus and LocateStatus checkboxes work as with queries. However, the DisplayScale checkbox is not available for schematics because there is no metadata to describe which scales to use to govern the turning off and on.

#### Saving and Plotting Schematic Diagrams
Editable and non-editable schematics are persisted. Editable schematic data are stored as component data. The geometries are stored with the schematic (detail) graphic components and the parameters that define the schematic are stored with the schematic (detail) attribute component. 
The non-editable schematic XML is stored in the SCHEMATICS table. The schematic public API uses schematic XML data as currency. This XML can also be saved to disk by the schematic custom command. 
Schematic diagrams can be plotted as map views in the plot sheet using the same workflow as the map view. Schematics can also be printed using the same workflow as for maps.

## Publishing

### Publishing Facility Data

#### Incrementally Publishing Facility Data
As data are added to the data tables of a configuration, you must republish the facility data to maintain an efficient graphics display in the NetWorks Core application. Facility data that has not been published into the DDCs must be brought into the system using deltas instead of being read from the DDCs. If there are numerous deltas, graphics display can be inefficient. 
To avoid the time-consuming task of a full data publish, you can use PublishMapFile.exe to incrementally update the existing DDCs based on changes since the last publish. The incremental publishing starts with the [high watermark](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256053) from the DDC and then queries the MODIFICATIONNUMBER column of the MODIFICATIONLOG to identify changes that have taken place since the last publish. 
Highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. When DDCs are published, they are burned with the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This is referred to as the watermark. Queries to the MODIFICATIONLOG use this watermark to limit the records returned. These queries yield new highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER/watermarks to be used in subsequent queries. 
These are the restrictions on the use of incremental publishing:
  * Whenever the definition of a component view is modified, you must do a full publish.
  * Whenever you want to change the DDC to which a given view is published, verify that the CCM file is correctly updated. You might have to edit it manually. 
  * The publish of secondary data are always a full publish because it is read-only data and no deltas are available. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256053) When you modify the definition of a component view, purge the MODIFICATIONLOG to [purge out old component view data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/36P2JjlfzXGWnwVEIkdiqQ). 
For each incremental publish, as with a full publish, a publish.log file is generated in the folder identified by the TEMP environment variable. This file contains information about the views that were published and lists errors encountered during the process. You should review this log file and resolve problems before making the DDCs available for use. 
Incremental publishing is controlled by a UDB file in the same manner as a full publish, and you should use the same UDB file for the full publish as for an incremental publish. The only change needed is that the PUBLISHTYPE parameter needs to be set to 0, indicating an incremental publish. As with a full publish, the publishing process can be executed from a command prompt. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256053) Incremental publishing is not a partial publishing of a DDC. If your original DDC contained five component views and you modify the UDB file so that the DDC contains only three views, the two views that you removed from the UDB file are also removed from the DDC. 
The publish process modifies certain files and, as such parallel processing must be controlled to avoid conflicts. Each process creates a log file in the %TEMP% folder. To run multiple processes on the same server, you must use separate user accounts. Additionally, the publish process always updates the CCM file and optionally modifies the FileUNCPaths.xml. To avoid conflicts when running the process in parallel on the same server, you must specify the command line parameter to skip the FileUNCPaths.xml and CCM file updates. If changes are required to these files as a result of data publishing, you have to manually update them. 
If you are running the operations in parallel but on different machines, the parameter value can be any of the three options. 
  * To republish facility data DDCs:


  1. Modify the data UDB file to indicate incremental publish. Remember if the structure of the DDCs is modified, you must do a full publish. The following example shows part of a data UDB file indicating incremental publish.   
|  Example MAPFILESIZE=0  
PUBLISHTYPE=0  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_LL.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_LL  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_ML.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_ML  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_PT.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_PT  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANCHOR_SL.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANCHOR_SL  
MAPFILE=\\\mymachine\mapfiles\dev\data\V_ANNOTXT_LB.ddc  
VIEWS=V_ANNOTXT_LB  
. . . [mapfiles and views continue . . . ]   |  
| --- |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256053)
     * MAPFILESIZE parameter is in bytes. For example, to restrict the size of the DDCs to 10 megabytes, set this parameter to 10485760. If there is no size limit to the DDCs to be created, set this parameter to 0. If the restricted size is exceeded, an error is logged for that component view in the publish.log file and the publish continues to the next view. PUBLISHTYPE parameter 0 indicates an incremental publish. A PUBLISHTYPE parameter 1 indicates a full publish. 
     * Because an incremental publish opens the existing DDC files to update views with the deltas from the server, you must specify a new location in the UDB file for the DDC files when doing an incremental publish. If you attempt to write the DDC files to the current location while doing an incremental publish, you get an error message in the publish.log file indicating that the DDC file could not be written. 
  2. From a command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and execute the following statement: 
PublishMapFiles<path to UDB file><ConfigurationName>.udb  
{0 or 1 or 2}  
Username/Password@alias [uid;pwd]
The user name, password, and alias match the current NetWorks Core configuration. The ConfigurationName portion of the file name must be the same as the configuration to be published. This name is matched against the G3E_LOCATION field of the G3E_DATACONNECTION table. This is done as a string comparison (case and spacing sensitive), so the names must match exactly. Before executing the PublishMapFiles command, a ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file that includes the configuration you are publishing must exist at either the <CurrentCCMPaths> or the <PrepCCMPaths> location, depending on the parameter you specify on the command line.   
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256053) Depending on the parameter value you type on the command line, the publishing process can update the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file specified by the <PrepCCMPaths> value to reflect the path to the DDC files specified in the UDB file. The second parameter on the command line indicates whether the CCM file if left unchanged and whether the <CurrentCCMPaths> and <PrepCCMPaths> values in the FileUNCPaths file should be left unchanged or swapped when publishing completes. It is the recommended that you select the option that leaves the values unchanged so that you can check the log file for errors and test the DDCs before the current CCM file is updated.   |  
| --- |  
0 indicates that the <CurrentCCMPaths> and <PrepCCMPaths> values are unchanged, but the CCM file is changed. 
1 indicates that the <CurrentCCMPaths> and <PrepCCMPaths> values are swapped in the FileUNCPaths file by the publish process, and the CCM file is changed. 
2 indicates the following:
     * The CCM file is not changed.
     * The <CurrentCCMPaths> and <PrepCCMPaths> values of the FileUNCPath.xml are not changed. 
The fourth parameter is a user ID and password for an MGE connection if views from an MGE secondary data source are included in the UDB file. 
The PublishMapFiles.exe returns an exit code based on publish status: 
0 = Publish success Publish Complete
-1 = Publish fails: Publish Complete with errors
  3. Check the publish.log file in the %TEMP% folder for errors that occurred during the publishing process. Depends on the exit code, a Publish Complete or Publish Complete with errors message is added at the end of the log file. Most of the errors reported are typically geometry errors that do not stop the publishing process. Decide if the geometries need immediate attention. Fix other kinds of errors before continuing. 
  4. Check the appropriate ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file (<CurrentCCMPaths> or <PrepCCMPaths>) make sure the paths and file names of the DDC files for your configuration are correct. There should be seven metadata DDC files in addition to the data DDC files. 
  5. Assuming you published to the <PrepCCMPaths> location, after testing the newly published DDC files from the Prep location, modify the FileUNCPaths file so that the <CurrentCCMPaths> location is now what was your <PrepCCMPaths> location and vice versa. 
  6. After publishing, the deltas in the central persisted deltas file are [obsolete and need to be flushed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ME_~Bajj6kuRIInCHaNbQA) and recreated.

#### Parallel Data Publish

##### Finding PublishMapFiles.exe
  * To find PublishMapFiles.exe:


  1. Check if the GTECHNOLOGY_PROGRAM_PATH environment variable is set to a non-empty value. 
  2. If yes, use this value to look up PublishMapFiles.exe in this path or under \Program. 
  3. If it is not found there, then read the Registry value of the (Default) Key under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\Path. 
  4. Append Program to this path and look for PublishMapFiles.exe.

##### Processing Modes
Auto
Auto mode is the default program setting. In this mode, input groups of views for DDC files are parsed and split to approximately equal batches depending on the number of workers (parallelism level). Example:
Explicit
In this mode, a split file is used to parse DDC files to batches using groups. The format of a split file is described further below. The program assigns batches to workers (parallel tasks) in the order they are defined in the split file. 
Size
Size mode parses and splits input UDB file to approximately equal batches depending on the number of workers (parallel tasks). The assignment of DDC files to each batch is done by examining the sizes of existing published DDC files, which export roughly a similar amount of data. Example:
Input Files
UDB file specifies views for every output DDC file and parameters like MAPFILESIZE and PUBLISHTYPE. The program validates this file. If it is not correct, an error is displayed. 
UDB File
Format of the UDB file is specified in the [Publishing Facility Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw) topic. 
Split File
This file is used in explicit mode.
Format:
GROUP=<id>
MAPFILE=<path>
MAPFILE=<path>
GROUP=<id>
MAPFILE=<path>
MAPFILE=<path>
…
Sample:
GROUP=1
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTOR-HV301.ddc
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTOR-MV302.ddc
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTOR-LV303.ddc
GROUP=2
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTORSEGMENT-HV304.ddc
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTORSEGMENT-MV305.ddc
MAPFILE=C:\INTERGRAPH\GINIUS\DDC\GINIUS\GINIUS\ELE-CONDUCTORSEGMENT-LV306.ddc

##### Running the Program
The program starts in command line with options. When it is used in explicit mode, a split file must be added in options. When any parameter is missing, the program displays help information. 
The program starts a number of threads depending on the -n parameter. Each thread publishes a single publish batch at a time. 
The PublishMapFiles.exe tool saves UDB files in the worker<id> folder, which is located in the temp folder, with "id" as the worker's identifier. Logs from PublishMapFiles.exe are saved in a folder named worker<id> in the temp folder, where "id" is also the worker's identifier. If the logging file option is used, the log will be saved in parallelDataPublish.log in the temp folder. 
Format for command line:
ParallelDataPublish.exe -c <configuration> -u <user> -p <password> -i <udb file> -a <alias> [-n <threads>] [-m <mode>] [-s <split file>] [-t <temp folder>] [-l <i or d>] [-g <y or n>]  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  -c  |  G/Technology configuration  |  
|  -u  |  Oracle user  |  
|  -p  |  Oracle password  |  
|  -a  |  Oracle alias  |  
|  -i  |  UDB file path  |  
|  -n  |  Number of workers. If not specified, defaults to 2.  |  
|  -m  |  UDB processing mode. Allowed values:
  * auto—automatic mode (default value)
  * explicit—explicit splitting mode
  * size—size bases heuristics

See [Processing Modes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F13~VeXp7XjCoTLTwoGLdg) for more details.   |  
|  -r  |  Retry number. Number of possible repeating of publishing in every worker thread. Default is 3, minimum is 1.   |  
|  -s  |  Split file. Mandatory when explicit mode is used.  |  
|  -g  |  Enables or disables the GDOoServer.log file. Values: 
  * y—enables
  * n—disables

 |  
|  -l  |  Logging option. Values:
  * i—logging to console (default)
  * d—logging to log file

 |  
|  -t  |  Path to temporary folder, where logs and temporary UDB files are stored. If not specified, %TEMP% is used.   |  
The following options are mandatory: -c <configuration>, -u <user>, -p <password>, -i <udb file>, -a <alias>. The -s <split file> option is mandatory only if explicit mode is used. 
Return codes:  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Success  |  
|  1  |  Invalid command line parameters  |  
|  2  |  Path to PublishMapFiles.exe not found   |  
|  3  |  Error during data publish  |  
|  4  |  Partial success. Data publishing has some failed batches.  |  
|  5  |  User canceled. Data publishing is canceled/interrupted by the user.  |  
|  9  |  Other unspecified error  |  
To terminate the program, use Ctrl+c (this terminates all ongoing tasks).

##### UDB Export Tool
This tool creates a UDB file from metadata in database for parallel data publishing.
Overview
Publishing of DDC files in NetWorks Core is driven by UDB files. These files are created by various means in the UDB Export tool. 
Requirements
UDB Export creates a UDB file for parallel publish program. This program creates metadata for a faster loading of maps in NetWorks Core. Metadata for a UDB file can be filtered by component view list, modification log or by a combination of component view list filtering and modification log filtering. 
Creating UDB File with UDB Export Tool
![UDB1](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/zWWlPy7hY3eisB3987SN6g-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=4ca3797cacc286f6&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
User Interface
Standalone application (.exe file). 
Command Line Reference
Usage:
UDBExport.exe -c <configuration> -a <alias> -u <user> -p <password> -o <udb folder path> -d <DDC base path> -m <> -f <fno/vno> -ff <filter file path> [-s <map file size>] [-t <publish type>]  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  -c  |  G/Technology configuration  |  
|  -a  |  Oracle database alias (EZCONNECT string)  |  
|  -u  |  Oracle user  |  
|  -p  |  Oracle password  |  
|  -o  |  Folder path to store the UDB file  |  
|  -d  |  DDC base path  |  
|  -m  |  When -m is not specified, the UDB Export function will create a full UDB file that includes all configured DDC files and component views. This is a standard form of UDB file creation using scripts.  When -m is specified, the tool checks the MODIFICATIONNUMBER in DDC files and the MODIFICATIONNUMBER in MODIFICATIONLOG, and creates UDB with only those DDCs which were affected since the latest data publishing.  In other words, if there was no change in any of the component views for a DDC file, there is no need to export it again.  The result UDB file might contain less DDC files and the data publishing can be shorter.  |  
|  -f  |  Filter mode. Allowed values: vno, fno. If not present, the filter is not used. Should be considered in conjunction with option -ff.  These are the actual values to be present in the command line: -f vno for filtering by a list of G3E_VNO,  -f fno for filtering by a list of G3E_FNO. List of values is specified in filter file in the -ff <filter file> parameter.  |  
|  -ff  |  Path to the filter file. It is a text file with one allowed value in each line. Mandatory if -f is used. Should be considered in conjunction with option -f Map file size. See the MAPFILESIZE parameter in [Publishing Facility Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw). Default is 0 (=no restriction on DDC size).   |  
|  -s  |  Map file size. See the MAPFILESIZE parameter in in [Publishing Facility Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw). Default is 0 (=no restriction on DDC size).   |  
|  -t  |  Publish type. See the PUBLISHTYPE parameter in in [Publishing Facility Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw). Default is 1 (=Full publish).   |  
Return codes  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Success  |  
|  1  |  Invalid command line parameters  |  
|  2  |  Database connection error  |  
|  3  |  No data to export  |  
|  9  |  Other unspecified error  |  
Example
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GINIUS\Program\UDBExport.exe" -c GINIUS -a muc-sgiv-presa5/GINIUS -u ginius -p ginius -o C:\Temp\CreatedUDB -d C:\Intergraph\GINIUS\DDC\Data\GINIUS -f fno -ff C:\Temp\FNO_VNOfiles\fno.txt -s 0 -t 1 
Workflows for Exporting UDB File
  1. Exporting UDB without any filtering
Description
In this workflow, the program loads metadata from a database and creates the UDB file from all the loaded metadata. 
Example
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GINIUS\Program\UDBExport.exe" -c GINIUS -a muc-sgiv-presa5/GINIUS -u ginius -p ginius -o C:\Temp\CreatedUDB -d C:\Intergraph\GINIUS\DDC\Data\GINIUS -s 0 -t 1 
  2. Exporting UDB filtered by modification log records
Description
In this workflow, metadata is first loaded from a database. Once loaded, the DDC files on a local storage will be opened in order to read information about them, such as name of views, watermark, or number of views. After this stage, the program will check the modification log for the modified number of views. If DDC has a view which has a smaller watermark or contains other views than the metadata in the database, the metadata must then be written to the UDB file. 
Example
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GINIUS\Program\UDBExport.exe" -c GINIUS -a muc-sgiv-presa5/GINIUS -u ginius -p ginius -o C:\Temp\CreatedUDB -d C:\Intergraph\GINIUS\DDC\Data\GINIUS -m -s 0 -t 1 
  3. Exporting UDB filtered by a file
Description
Before exporting UDB (with or without filtering by the modification log), the user can filter metadata from a database by optional file. This file contains the list of component views or the list of feature numbers. 
Example


  * Filtering by a feature number list:
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GINIUS\Program\UDBExport.exe" -c GINIUS -a muc-sgiv-presa5/GINIUS -u ginius -p ginius -o C:\Temp\CreatedUDB -d C:\Intergraph\GINIUS\DDC\Data\GINIUS -f fno -ff C:\Temp\FNO_VNOfiles\fno.txt -s 0 -t 1 
  * Filtering by a component view list and filtering by a modification log:
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GINIUS\Program\UDBExport.exe" -c GINIUS -a muc-sgiv-presa5/GINIUS -u ginius -p ginius -o C:\Temp\CreatedUDB -d C:\Intergraph\GINIUS\DDC\Data\GINIUS -m -f vno -ff C:\Temp\FNO_VNOfiles\fno.txt -s 0 -t 1 


Technical Prerequisites
  1. TNS admin (it is one of the conditions for connection via tns names). 
  2. DDC files in a folder on a local disk (specify the folder in the command line option -d) for modification log use. 
  3. Metadata tables specified in the section below.

#### Publishing Large Views
Publishing large views can take a long time. To increase performance, you can create new LTT views and add a new user that uses the new LTT views to do the publish. Install Grant_Privs_To_Publish.sql before running these procedures. Type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL>@grant_Privs_To_Publish.sql;  
SQL>@prvtGrant_Privs_To_Publish.plb;
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258077) This workflow is for publishing production schemas. 
  * To publish large views:


  1. Create the full publish user. This user can be named anything.
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258077) In this topic, the production schema is GPROD, and the full publish user is GPRODPUB. 
  2. To publish a set of LTT views owned by the GPRODPUB user, use an SQL editor to grant the following Oracle privileges: 
SQL> grant connect to GPRODPUB;
SQL> grant resource to GPRODPUB;
SQL> grant create any view to GPRODPUB;
  3. To grant specific NetWorks Core privileges, type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> execute gt_grant_privs_to_publish.grant_privs_to_publish('<Full publish user>');
You may need to be logged in as SYSTEM to run this procedure:  
|  Example SQL> execute gt_grant_privs_to_publish.grant_privs_to_publish('GPRODPUB');  |  
| --- |  
  4. Check that the SchemaOwner has the following privilege:
SQL> grant create any view to <SchemaOwner>;  
|  Example SQL> grant create any view to GPROD;  |  
| --- |  
  5. You can either create all the views or an individual view for GPRODPUB:
     * To create all the LTT views for GPRODPUB, log in as the GPRODPUB user, and type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> execute SchemaOwner.Create_Views.Create_All_LTT_Views('<SCHEMA_OWNER>');  
|  Example SQL> execute GPROD.Create_Views.Create_All_LTT_Views('GPROD'); Where the production schema name is GPROD.  |  
| --- |  
     * To create an individual LTT view for GPRODPUB, log in as the GPRODPUB user, and type the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> execute SchemaOwner.Create_Views.Create_LTT_View('B$TableName', '<SCHEMA_OWNER>');  
|  Example SQL> execute GPROD.Create_Views.Create_LTT_View('B$POLE','GPROD'); Where the production schema name is GPROD and B$TableName is B$POLE.   |  
| --- |  
The production schema name indicates that the view is not the regular LTT view. It also is the schema owner and indicates over which B$tables you should build the views so it can use the SchemaOwner.B$TableName syntax. The views are owned by GPRODPUB. 
  6. Copy the component views from the production schema to the GPRODPUB user. The full publish user must own its own set of the component views. 
  7. From the command line, use the GPRODPUB user to run the publish procedures.  
|  Example publishmapfiles c:\temp\gprod.udb 1 gprodpub/gprodpub@gprod  Where the database alias is gprod.  |  
| --- |  
  8. After publishing, the deltas in the mobile products and the central persisted deltas file are obsolete and need to be flushed and recreated. If you are running the mobile products or using the central persisted deltas file service, delete the PersistedDeltasFiles.

[Republishing Facility Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KMyb7We6CN6SLJS3Anpyuw)

### Publishing Metadata

#### Language Settings for Publishing Data and Secondary Data
If the language settings for Oracle on the publish machine are not consistent with the database, data and secondary data publishing fails. Verify that the following parameters are set correctly: 
  * The default language on the publish machine is the same language as the database.
  * The NLS_LANG parameter under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE > SOFTWARE > ORACLE in the registry is set to be consistent with the database you want to publish. This parameter is in the format of LANGUAGE_TERRITORY.CHARACTERSET. Make sure that LANGUAGE_TERRITORY is consistent with the database. 
You can use the following query to find out the NLS settings in the database: 
SQL> select * from NLS_Database_Parameters; 
The values for NLS_LANGUAGE and NLS_TERRITORY parameters are the ones that should appear in the NLS_LANG parameter.

#### Publishing Metadata as a Non-Schema Owner
Typically, you have to be the schema owner to publish metadata. However, at some NetWorks Core sites, users who are not the schema owner (perhaps a GIS administrator) might need to [publish metadata to test](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VBJF3YM8ZkpzkjPmOzCbTw) an update in a local environment. Additionally, NetWorks Core software allows an OS-authenticated user to publish metadata. 
Before you start, ensure that the non-schema owner has the [appropriate privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5gEZGSVWXjoIoe56YGidNA). 
The GIS administrator needs a way to execute changes to the database as a non-schema owner who does not have the DBA role. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261849) All administrative tools, for example, dataimport.exe, have the same requirement as metadata publishing when using non-schema-owner users. 
  * To set up the non-schema owner user without DBA role:


  1. Log on to the database as the SYS user, use an SQL editor to create a new user, grant the [required privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5gEZGSVWXjoIoe56YGidNA) to the user, and run the following grants: 
    1. SQL> grant connect, resource to <User Name>;   
|  Example The new username is TEST.  grant connect, resource to TEST;  |  
| --- |  
    2. SQL> grant ADMINISTRATOR, EVERYONE to <User Name>;   
|  Example grant ADMINISTRATOR, EVERYONE to TEST;  |  
| --- |  
  2. Log on to the database as the new user, and create the following logon trigger:
SQL> CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER <Logon Trigger Name>
AFTER LOGON
ON <User Name>.SCHEMA
BEGIN
execute immediate 'ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = <Schema Owner Name>'; 
END;
/  
|  Example CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER T_logon_set_CURRENT_SCHEMA AFTER LOGON ON TEST.SCHEMA BEGIN execute immediate 'ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = DEVELOPMENT933'; END;  
/  |  
| --- |  
  3. To publish metadata as the non-schema-owner user:
    1. Verify that the [G3E_SCHEMAOWNER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER is set to the schema-owner username. 
    2. Publish using the [Versions command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ) or from the command prompt as shown in the following example:   
|  Example From the command prompt, type the following:  Publishmetadatamapfiles DEVELOPMENT933 <PathToMapfiles> TEST/TEST@ALIAS  |  
| --- |

#### Publishing Metadata for the First Time
For users to see changes to the metadata, you must publish the metadata to the development schema. This requires running individual [optable ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258985)packages so the system creates optimized tables. 
Optimized tables; tables that result from joining metadata tables. Optables are published into the metadata mapfiles and ADO-based RAW files. Using optables makes the software run more efficiently. 
The first time you publish metadata, you must do it manually. After that, you can use Admin to republish. You need not exit the application or close the connection to publish metadata.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258985)
  * The [language settings for Oracle ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0X9oQyI8GXBmjQuIdUiWTg)on the publish machine must be consistent with the database. If they are not, publishing fails. 
  * Verify that the [G3E_SCHEMAOWNER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER is set to the schema-owner user name. If it is not, publishing fails. 

 |  
| --- |  
  * To publish metadata for the first time:


  1. From the command prompt on the client system, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and execute the following statement: 
PublishMetadataMapfiles - S <Configurationname> <Mapfile path> <username/password@alias>
-S is an optional argument that means to publish using the silent mode without displaying any message. If the argument is missing, the command displays messages to inform the user that there is an error or that publishing is finished. 
Replace username and password with the appropriate values for your configuration. The configuration name must match (not case sensitive) the entry in [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw). The mapfile path is the location to which to write the metadata files. 
  2. After publishing completes, check the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file to make sure the paths and file names of the DDC files for the configuration are correct. There should be six (seven if you publish a picklist) metadata DDC files listed. The ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file contains only paths and names of the DDC files. RAW files are published in the same folder as the LegendMetadata.ddc. 
You should now be able to establish a connection through NetWorks Core.

[Publishing Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ)

#### Publishing Metadata for UNIX
If your database resides on a UNIX machine, you can use the [Metadata Versions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ) command in Admin to review and validate metadata changes. However, you cannot use it to publish. You must publish metadata from the command prompt. 
  * To set up metadata publishing for UNIX databases:


Follow the publishing steps as outlined in [Publishing Metadata from the Command Prompt](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VBJF3YM8ZkpzkjPmOzCbTw), step 2.

#### Publishing Metadata from the Command Prompt
You can use the Metadata Versions command in Admin to [review and validate metadata changes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDGAu21AUa_I~XZxIPvJzw), or you can publish metadata from the command prompt.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256977)
  * The [language settings for Oracle ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0X9oQyI8GXBmjQuIdUiWTg)on the publish machine must be consistent with the database. If they are not, publishing fails. 
  * Verify that the [G3E_SCHEMAOWNER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER is set to the schema-owner user name. If it is not, publishing fails. 

 |  
| --- |  
  * To publish metadata from the command prompt:


  1. Decide where to publish.
The target folder is defined in the command line argument for <Mapfile path>. The target folder should have sufficient disk space for the published DDC and RAW files, and the user should have write permission to access it. 
The target folder path should not include the locale information. The command creates language locale subdirectories and puts each set of mapfiles into them. The name of the folders is defined in the G3E_METADATALANGUAGE table. 
  2. From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
PublishMetadataMapfiles [-c] [-s] [-t] [-g] <Configuration Name> <Mapfile Path> [XML PublishMode] [Username]/[Password]@<Alias> [MaxDegreeOfParallelism]
To publish as an OS-authenticated user, type the following:
PublishMetadataMapfiles [-c] [-s] [-t] [-g] <Configuration Name> <Mapfile Path> [XML PublishMode] /@<Alias> [MaxDegreeOfParallelism]
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256977) The Command line is not case sensitive. 
-C is an optional argument that means the command does not create optables and uses the current optables to publish. If the argument is missing, the command creates new optables during publishing. Usage of this parameter should be avoided except for workflows where there was no change in metadata. 
-S is an optional argument that means publish using silent mode without displaying any message. If the argument is missing, the command displays messages to inform the user that there is an error or that publishing is finished. 
-T is an optional argument that means reuse existing subtable constraints and triggers instead of recreating them. 
Historically, metadata publishing has also been used as a consistency tool. The software would, for example, drop triggers from specific metadata related tables and create a new version of them. Doing this ensured that the tables had the correct safety net around them, as maintaining this safety net during metadata publishing is a costly operation and under normal circumstances nobody (apart from the database upgrade wizard) should be modifying metadata supporting structures. The -T argument allows the administrator to skip this part of the publishing process. When the argument is not specified, the application defaults to the old behavior. It is recommended to run the application without this argument when metadata publish is run: 
     * for the first time 
     * after metadata upgrade 
     * after making any structural changes, such as adding an additional language
-G is an optional argument that means that the application will gather table statistics for metadata tables during metadata publishing. 
Historically, this improved performance of queries run during metadata publishing. However, with the newer versions of Oracle, gathering statistics can have a negative impact on the metadata publish performance. As this can differ per Oracle version, it is recommended to benchmark the behavior and: 
     * Run with the -G parameter if gathering of statistics improves publishing times. 
     * Run without the parameter when gathering of statistics has no or negative impact on publishing performance (default behavior). 
Configuration Name defines configuration name to publish and it must match an entry in G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION. It is not case sensitive. 
Mapfile Path is the folder to publish the metadata to. 
PublishMode is an optional argument used to publish RAW files. It has no effect on publishing DDC files. This argument has the following options. If the argument is missing, the command defaults to All. 
     * All means the publish process creates all RAW files. Use this option if you added picklists or changed them from unpublished to published. 
     * Metadata indicates that the command recreates only metadata RAW files and copies other RAW files from the original place to the folder holding new mapfiles so that all DDC files and RAW files reside together. You must use this option if you change default values defined in Oracle for your components. 
     * Picklist means the command recreates picklist raw files and does the copy work for other raw files. Use this option if you added values only to published picklists. 
     * DefaultFeatures means the command regenerates raw files for default. Use this option if you change the structure of your components but make no other metadata changes. 
     * AddOns means the command regenerates raw files for Add-Ons. Use this option if you change only the AddOns metadata. 
MaxDegreeOfParallelism is an optional argument that defines the number of threads to use to execute parallel tasks. If not specified, this argument defaults to 4 threads. If the machine has less than 4 logical processors, the default is capped at the number of available logical processors. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256977) You can get brief Help about this command by typing one of the following at the command prompt: 
PublishMetadataMapfiles -h  
PublishMetadataMapfiles /h  
PublishMetadataMapfiles -?  
PublishMetadataMapfiles /? 
Recommended argument usage:
After a language has been added in G3E_METADATALANGUAGE run with these arguments:
PublishMetadataMapfiles DEV c:\mapfiles\DEV ALL scott/tiger@DEVDB
Regular publish with 4 threads when metadata changed but there was no structural change:
PublishMetadataMapfiles dev -s –t c:\mapfiles\dev scott/tiger@DEVDB
The following command line will result in the publish process using 6 worker processes for metadata publishing: 
PublishMetadataMapfiles -S <Configuration> <Mapfile path> <PublishMode> <Username>/<Password>@<Alias> 6
  3. Update the ConnectionConfiguration.ccm file to point to the new DDC files. 
  4. Check errors in the mpublish<Configuration name>.log file in the %TEMP% folder of the local machine. The file is automatically generated by the command. You can also create a %TEMP%/gdooserver.log file to record more information about database access. The application creates a file named publishsuccess<Configuration Name> in the %TEMP% folder on successful completion. 
  5. [Post metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s6MYjSSpWFRvFCe1jwrnQA). Move the metadata from one database to another database. Create an Oracle.dmp file for export of metadata tables only. Create a batch file for importing metadata.
