### Publishing Secondary Data
Secondary data requires a full (not incremental) publish process. However, secondary data are typically less volatile than NetWorks Core data and should not need to be published very often. No deltas are involved because secondary data are read-only and generates no updates to the MODIFICATIONLOG table.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259714?tocId=4boSVS52DGpsx3rIfeZD4Q) You must publish secondary data into a DDC of its own. NetWorks Core data and secondary data cannot exist in the same DDC.   |  
| --- |  
  * To publish secondary data that has not been imported:


  1. [Create a connection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4hZMOeev0~m7R~J2LubcYA) to the GDO server. 
  2. [Generate the necessary metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IFe3ufPP_DKJ5bXW2kdD0w) for the GDO recordsets. 
  3. [Review and validate the changes to the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sDGAu21AUa_I~XZxIPvJzw) that have been generated for the secondary data. 
  4. Use Metadata Explorer to fine tune the generated metadata:
    1. [Define styles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GVwibq0NSEYvsKV~8WKhfA), [style rules](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q4dl7dWIs5NZfqbJsgqufQ), and [labels](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZsMmdgNiF72jdjOSKypTRQ) for your secondary data. 
    2. Define legend items for the secondary data on the [Display Control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/O9cxll~BWxmEI~RD5kLjmw). 
    3. [Define legend entries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DnvNHhZOfwOqsDzTuQ3cpA) for the secondary data. 
    4. [Define a legend](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8CMKUYPvnuScyWh3noLYSQ) for the secondary data. 
OR
Add the legend entries to an existing legend.
    5. [Edit the tooltip](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/w7IdMbVr9I28f0Eka8KQ2w) for each component (the default tooltip is the component name). 
  5. [Publish the secondary metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ). Use All on the Versions dialog box. 
  6. Do a [full publish of the secondary facility data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oEgzFrjdVK5_JRmGxEi4Dw).

## Roles and Application Access

### Controlling Application Behavior with Roles

#### Controlling Access to Commands

##### Metadata to Control Access to Commands
Because the software queries the roles you assign to commands in G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION to display the menu structure and command, you must carefully assign roles to commands that are available for the license of a specific user. The software queries for the objects identified in [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) as Command or Custom Command. To enable custom commands, use the value from the [G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND.G3E_CCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TnT4ya5S9F75dJaSN86qXg) field in the [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_OBJECTCONTROLID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) field. 
By default, the Admin commands are associated with the ADMINISTRATOR role rather than the EVERYONE role. While you can change this role, NetWorks Core does require that anyone who uses the Administrator commands be logged in as the schema owner. These commands access normalized metadata tables and are only visible to the schema owner. 
You can modify the default role Nobody in the G3E_OBJECTCONTROL field after metadata is configured and if the appropriate licenses have been purchased for your site. 
Related Topic
[Controlling Access to Commands](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/C0TBTd_M0hfeRLdpUjf64w)

#### Controlling Access to Feature Classes

##### Metadata to Control Access to Feature Classes
To control the edit or delete access of a user to specific features, update the [G3E_FEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) table. These are some issues to consider: 
  * What happens when a user changes from review to edit in Feature Explorer? 
  * What happens when a user selects data from a grid that displays as the result of a query? 
  * What happens when a user uses the Edit Geometry command to edit a feature? 
  * What happens when a user uses the Edit Tool command to edit or to delete a feature? 
  * What happens when a user adds a related feature to an existing feature?
  * What happens when a user attempts to edit relationships within the Edit Feature Relationships command? 


To make these metadata changes, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, select Core Schema Control > Data Connections and Features > <data connection name> > Features > <feature name>, and update the G3E_FEATURE table: 
  * Add the required roles for access to feature editing to G3E_FEATURE.G3E_EDITROLE.
  * Add the required roles for access to ad hoc query and spatial query displayed features to G3E_FEATURE.G3E_SELECTROLE. 
  * Add the required roles in G3E_FEATURE.G3E_DELETEROLE so users can delete features using the Edit Tool command. Then republish your metadata. 
  * Add the required roles in G3E_FEATURE.G3E_ADDRELATEDROLE to filter the list of features presented to users in the Add Related Feature command. Then republish your metadata. 
  * Add the required roles in G3E_FEATURE.G3E_EDITRELATIONSHIPSROLE to restrict the set of features that can have their relationships edited within the Edit Feature Relationships command. Then republish your metadata.

#### Controlling Attribute Presentation

##### Metadata to Control Attribute Presentation
To limit user access to a specific attribute, update the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table.   
|  Example  
 |  Attribute Name  |  Role  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Pole Number  |  Viewer  |  
|  Cost Basis  |  Supervisor  |  
|  Class  |  Clerk  |  
|  Height  |  Viewer  |  
The table shows three types of roles: Supervisor, Clerk, and Viewer. The Supervisor role includes the Clerk and Viewer roles. The Clerk role includes the Viewer role. If the user is defined as a Viewer, the dialog tab displays only two entries, Pole Number and Height. If the user is defined as a Clerk, the tab also includes a third entry, Class. The Supervisor can see all attribute entries.

#### Controlling Graphic Data Presentation

##### Metadata to Control Graphic Data Presentation
These metadata tables are associated with using roles to limit user access to graphic data. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257072) Based on metadata configuration, role handling prevents specific users from displaying data from restricted components/legend entries. When a user saves a legend to a work space - whether as a named legend or associated with a map or detail window - it retains the privileges of the user who created the work space or work space template. The software does not reapply any role checks if other users open that same work space and access that legend. 
G3E_LEGENDSETTING and G3E_LEGEND
  * To limit user access to a specific legend, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Graphic Display > Legends > <legend name> > Settings node and specify the user role in [G3E_LEGENDSETTINGS.G3E_ROLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5TsqlYTiAxwXTGbEqbC3Fg) table. 
  * To be sure legend roles changes are refreshed in the legend, select the Graphic Display > Legends > <legend name> > Legend node and update [G3E_LEGEND.G3E_VERSION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) with the correct version number. 


The user is warned if the legend is out of date. Additionally, the display fails if the user does not have the appropriate role to view a legend. 
G3E_LEGENDENTRY
You can assign roles to individual legend entries in the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table. When you publish, the Legend Entries and Display Control optimized tables are updated to include the role information. The Display Control control builds the legend Display Control tree and refreshes the map view for a legend. Because the software is fault tolerant of the absence of children under a group, this control leaves empty Display Control groups in the tree.   
|  Example  
 |  Legend Entry  |  Role  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Pole Symbol  |  Viewer  |  
|  Pole Label  |  Supervisor  |  
|  Cable Line  |  Viewer  |  
|  Cable Label  |  Clerk  |  
The table shows three types of roles: Supervisor, Clerk, and Viewer. The Supervisor role includes the Clerk and Viewer roles. The Clerk role includes the Viewer role. If the user is defined as a Viewer, the legend displays only two entries, Pole Symbol and Cable Line, since the Viewer role is required to view this data. If the user is defined as a Clerk, the legend also includes a third entry, Cable Label. The Supervisor can see all legend entries. 
 |

|  Find Intersection  |  [G3E_FINDINTERSECTION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QuIg__2USUlQTQ149z4HcA)  |  [G3E_FINDINTERSECTION_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PDWkN0yKvjTCYgyb1oUWSA)  |

The attribute definition tables that support these commands include the G3E_ROLE from the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) definition. You must ensure that the user has access to all of the attributes required to populate the query appropriately. For example, if a simple query requires the user to populate attributes A and B, the user must have a role that makes attributes A and B visible. If not, the user cannot see this simple query, and the query does not execute correctly.

### Granting Roles and Privileges to the GIS Administrator
Some companies have two administrator positions. The position responsible for the entire database and all the accompanying database privileges is typically the [schema owner](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/R93fVtbG8wHMUxbjSU6b3A). The other position is a GIS administrator, who has limited responsibility and privileges. 
A GIS administrator needs the following roles:
  * CONNECT
  * RESOURCE


The GIS administrator also needs privileges other than the CONNECT and RESOURCE roles, for example, to use [Metadata Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UTqIHC3d83TOn0KP~nqHeg) or to [publish metadata as a non-schema owner](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o1xmLAVbByQPnk6ojAJq9w). You can explicitly control the privileges that are granted to the GIS administrator. In most cases, you can exclude the ANY qualifier except on the Select and Execute privileges. 
The tables below list required, useful, and unused privileges for the GIS administrator.

### Granting Roles and Privileges
You grant users the database access they need by assigning roles and privileges. Admin provides predefined roles you can assign to users. These roles include the necessary privileges for different levels of access. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258449) All roles created by the schema owner are assigned to the schema owner by default. 
The following are the predefined NetWorks Core roles:   
|  Role  |  Privileges  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  EVERYONE  |  The basic default role to all objects in the [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg). If this role is assigned to a user, that user can run all commands and functions identified in G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.   |  
|  SUPERVISOR  |  Can create jobs, post jobs, discard job edits, discard single features, edit a job, view a job, undo job edits, review job edits, validate job edits, validate features, post partial, run conflict detection, and close a job. This role is also assigned the DESIGNER role, so any privileges the DESIGNER role has are given to the SUPERVISOR role. Has the DESIGNER role plus execute privileges on the LTT_ADMIN Package to create jobs.   |  
|  DESIGNER  |  Can discard job edits, discard single features, edit a job, view a job, undo job edits, review job edits, validate job edits, validate features. This role cannot create or post jobs. Has delete, insert, select, and update privileges on component tables, component tables, component views, and component view tables as well as select on certain sequences, and execute on LTT_USER.   |  
|  ADMINISTRATOR  |  Can perform administrative functions. If the user is not the schema owner, can run the Admin commands that do not require access to the normalized metadata tables, for example Save to Catalog. If the user is the schema owner, can run all the <Admin commands and publish metadata and data.   |  
|  FINANCE  |  Can post jobs, discard job edits, discard single features, view a job, review job edits, validate job edits, validate features, post partial, and run conflict detection. This role cannot create jobs. May be viewed as the cost-control interface point and has Execute privileges on the LTT_POST Package.   |  
|  MARKETING  |  Can discard job edits, discard single features, view a job, review job edits, validate job edits, and validate features. This role cannot create or post jobs.   |  
|  SHORTTERMTRANSACTIONS  |  Outside of NetWorks Core, this role can update, insert, and delete from any table without creating a job. The change is made directly against the master record and no copy is made. This is called Short-Term Transaction mode (STT) and requires the SHORTTERMTRANSACTIONS role. The user must still be assigned privileges to access the tables that you want them to update. The specification of this role is checked in the LTT triggers and lets the user bypass having a job.   |  
  * To install predefined roles:


All of these procedures should have already have been executed when the database was created and during each upgrade. 
Using an SQL editor connected to the schema as the schema owner, execute the following procedures:   
|  Example SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.CREATE_ALL_ROLES;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.GRANT_PACKAGE_TO_ROLE;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.GRANT_PRIVS_TO_ROLE;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.GRANT_METADATA_TO_ROLE;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.CREATE_PUBLIC_SYNONYM;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.CREATE_COMPONENT_VIEW_SYNONYM;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.CREATESYNPICKLIST;  
SQL>execute LTT_ROLE.CREATE_METADATA_SYNONYM;  |  
| --- |  
  * To create specific privileges by role:


All of the statements below are executed by LTT_ROLE.GRANT_PRIVS_TO_ROLE executed above. You can define your own roles for more specific access to tables within the NetWorks Core by executing similar GRANT statements for your role. 
Examples
  * SUPERVISOR role
SQL>grant DESIGNER to SUPERVISOR;
SQL>grant execute on LTT_POST to SUPERVISOR;
SQL>grant execute on LTT_ADMIN to SUPERVISOR;
SQL>grant execute on LTT_LOCKS to SUPERVISOR;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core sequences> to SUPERVISOR;
  * DESIGNER role
SQL>grant execute on LTT_USER to DESIGNER;
SQL>grant insert, select, update, delete on <all NetWorks Core table and views> to DESIGNER;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core sequences> to DESIGNER;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core metadata> to DESIGNER;
  * FINANCE role
SQL>grant execute on LTT_POST to FINANCE;
SQL>grant execute on LTT_USER to FINANCE;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core tables and views> to FINANCE;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core sequences> to FINANCE;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core metadata> to FINANCE;
  * MARKETING role
SQL>grant execute on LTT_USER to MARKETING;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core tables and views> to MARKETING;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core sequences> to MARKETING;
SQL>grant select on <all NetWorks Core metadata> to MARKETING;

## Schemas

### Setting Up a New Schema

#### Creating a CCM File
The ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm (CCM) file is simply a text file containing one or more connection configurations. A connection configuration consists of a configuration name and the Oracle alias and DDC files associated with the configuration name. 
The CCM file contains [DDC files](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yPXcvp7Vcm2gnqIMCRkXGw) for facility model data and metadata. However, if you are just now [creating a new development schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg), all you have is default metadata and no data. The CCM for that situation does not have a DDC file for facility model data.   
|  Example CCM file when creating a new development schema CONFIGURATION_NAME=GTECH_DEV;  
ALIAS=DB_ALIAS;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\FeatureComponentMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\LegendMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\DialogAttributeMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\RelationshipMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\PlacementMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\AnalysisIntegrationMetadata.ddc;   
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\PicklistMetadata.ddc; where the GTECH_DEV is the development schema owner and DB_ALIAS is the Oracle alias.  |  
| --- |  
After you create facility model tables and want to publish facility model data DDC files, you should have entries for those in your CCM file.   
|  Example CCM file with facility model data DDC files CONFIGURATION_NAME=GTECH_DEV;  
ALIAS=DB_ALIAS;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\DATA\COMMDEV92.DDC;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\FeatureComponentMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\LegendMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\DialogAttributeMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\RelationshipMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\PlacementMetadata.ddc;  
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\AnalysisIntegrationMetadata.ddc;   
MAPFILE=\\\GTECH\MAPFILES\GDEV\GDEV9S\Metadata\PicklistMetadata.ddc;  |  
| --- |  
Guidelines for CCM Files
  * Each line in the CCM file must end with a semicolon.
  * There can be no blank lines in this file, including the end of the file.
  * The CONFIGURATION_NAME in this file is case sensitive; the case must match the data in the database tables, [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) and [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw).

#### Creating a Diagnostics Schema
A diagnostics schema provides a way for you to find problems in PL/SQL.
  * To create a diagnostics schema:


  1. Log in as the SYS user or as a user with DBA privilege but not as the schema owner.
  2. Type the following in an SQL editor to install the following scripts in the database in order: 
SQL> @GTechnology\plsql\ltt\Diagnostics\InstallDiagnostics;
This script displays several prompts when run in Oracle SQL *Plus. The following are the prompts and example responses: 
Enter NetWorks Core installation folder:
This is prompting for the gtech_path. For this example, type C:\Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnology
Enter NetWorks Core schema owner (ALL UPPER CASE):
This is prompting for the gtech_schema_owner. For this example, type XCHG10
Enter NetWorks Core diagnostics log folder (must exist on server):
This is prompting for an existing folder on the Oracle server to store the diagnostics logs. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256590)
  * When you install diagnostics into an empty database during [initial database creation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg), the insertion of the diagnostics packages causes expected compile errors. The diagnostics system is dependent on NetWorks Core database objects that have not yet been installed. 
  * When you do an Oracle export, diagnostics are not exported. Therefore, you must install diagnostics manually after importing a NetWorks Core database.

#### Creating a Schema Owner
A schema owner is an Oracle user that owns all the NetWorks Core database objects and facility data model tables in the database. You must grant certain Oracle privileges (some explicitly, not using a role) to the schema owner for that user to perform successfully. 
  * To create a schema owner:


Using an SQL editor, create the Oracle user as follows:
SQL> create user <username> identified by <password> [default tablespace <tablespace name> temporary tablespace <temporary tablespace name>];
Granting Roles and System Privileges
Define the following roles for the NetWorks Core schema owner: 
  * CONNECT—This lets the schema owner connect to Oracle and create tables, views, sequences, clusters, synonyms, sessions, and links to other databases. 
  * RESOURCE—This lets the schema owner create tables, sequences, procedures, triggers, indexes, and clusters. 


The schema owner also needs system privileges granted explicitly. When a user executes a procedure or a package, Oracle looks at the privileges explicitly granted to the user, not at the privileges assigned with a role. 
  * To grant roles and system privileges to the schema owner:


Connect to Oracle as the system user, and use an SQL editor to execute the following:
SQL> grant connect, create procedure, create public synonym, create role, create sequence, create session, create table, create trigger, create type, create view, grant any role, resource, select any table, drop public synonym, unlimited tablespace, alter any procedure to <username>;
The schema owner created this way can perform administrative tasks like publishing metadata and data, running Metadata Explorer and GPT. The schema owner can also run most of the administrative commands except the Post section for the Administrative > Metadata Versions command because it involves data export and/or import. 
Granting Roles for Specific Tasks
So that the schema owner can perform some other administrative tasks that require data export and/or import, such as creating the initial database or importing an existing database dump, or running the Upgrade Wizard, you should grant the DBA role to the schema owner. However, if you do not want the schema owner to have the DBA role, you can grant the IMP_FULL_DATABASE and EXP_FULL_DATABASE roles instead of the DBA role. 
Granting Object Privileges
You must set specific object privileges and parameters for your schema owner or you may not be able to do the following: 
  * Query Oracle data dictionary tables
  * Connect to the database using NetWorks Core
  * Create a job
  * Edit a job.


  * To grant object privileges:


You must have SYS privileges to run the SQL statements.
  1. In an SQL editor, type the following:
SQL> grant select on DBA_ROLES to <schema owner>;
SQL> grant select on DBA_ROLE_PRIVS to <schema owner>;
SQL> grant select on GV_$SESSION to <schema owner>;
SQL> grant select on GV_$TRANSACTION to <schema owner>;
SQL> grant execute on DBMS_LOCK TO <schema owner>;
OR
An alternative to explicitly granting these privileges is to set the following Oracle parameter in init.ora: 
O7_DICTIONARY_ACCESSIBILITY = TRUE
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256578) This approach is not recommended in a production environment. Explicitly granting the privileges to the schema owner is preferred. 
  2. If you changed the Oracle parameter in init.ora, restart your database.

#### Installing Optional Metadata
When you are [setting up your development schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg), you can specify which optional functionality is required for your data model just one time in SetUpgradeEnv(CONFIGURATIONNAME).bat located in the \GTechnology\Services\AutoUpgrade folder, and you can use your settings for upgrades. The upgrade installs the appropriate metadata tables and database packages based on settings in SetUpgradeEnv(CONFIGURATIONNAME).bat. 
You can also [add optional functionality to an existing schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg). NetWorks Core optional functionality is located in the \GTechnology\PLSQL\MetaData\Optional folder. 
  * To install optional metadata to a new schema:


To install optional metadata for a [new schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg), set the Has<optional functionality name> flag to Y in the parameter file SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat.   
|  Example Electric Design Tools and Field Inspection set HasDuct=N  
set HasFeatureImport=N  
set HasFieldInspection=Y  
set HasLand=N  
set HasMobileNet=N  
set HasNetExport=N  
set HasEDT=Y  
set HasLoginMapping=N  
set IsComms=N  
set IsPipeline=N   |  
| --- |  
Set the parameter to Y if your data model has this optional functionality. Set the parameter to N if your data model does not use this optional functionality: 
  * HasDuct—This is for [duct management and duct configurations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * HasFeatureImport—This is for the Import Feature interface, which can be used to import features into NetWorks Core. 
[G3E_FEATUREIMPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bcCkgbpY6H2cj2n2TP2TjA)
  * HasFieldInspection—This is for [field inspection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * HasLand—This is for [land management](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
Your land features have these G3E_FNOs:  
|  Feature Number  |  Feature Name  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  101  |  Building  |  
|  107  |  Pipeline  |  
|  210  |  Technical Object  |  
|  220  |  Cadastral Node  |  
|  221  |  Cadastral Edge  |  
|  222  |  Parcel  |  
|  223  |  Block  |  
|  235  |  Technical Object Protection Zone  |  
|  236  |  Pipeline Protection Zone  |  
|  237  |  Protection Area  |  
  * HasMobileNet—This is for [NetViewer and Field Review](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * HasNetExport—This is for [Export](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * HasEDT—This is for [Electric Design Tools](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * HasLoginMapping—This is to [map the name](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw) with which the user logs in to the actual username in the database that has been granted appropriate privileges. 
  * Work Management
    * HasGenericWMS
    * HasLogica
    * HasSAP
    * HasStorms
  * IsComms—This is for the [communications industry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 
  * IsPipeline—This is for the [pipeline industry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JiKVacM0HObpe3picRqTgw). 


  * To install optional metadata to an existing schema:


Use an SQL editor or Metadata Query to run the following script:
SQL> @"\GTechnology\PLSQL\metadata\install<optional functionality>.sql" "<LogFilePath>" "<\GTechnology>";
This script creates the basic metadata tables and metadata table entries for the specified optional functionality and adds required triggers and constraints.

#### Setting Up Tablespaces
The database is made up of tablespaces, which are made up of one or more data files. This is where you create your tables, indexes, and so on. The layout of tablespaces can affect performance and administration (like backups). 
For optimal performance, spread appropriately sized and located [tablespaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256586) across physical drives. Separate the more frequently used tables from each other in different tablespaces for better performance. Tables that are accessed simultaneously (like tables joined in a view) should be separated so that the I/O can be performed in parallel. To make backups easier, you should separate read-only tables from writable tables. Put [indexes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256586) in their own tablespace, and separate them physically from the data. 
An area of disk consisting of one or more disk files. A tablespace can contain many tables, indexes, or clusters. A tablespace has a fixed size which can be altered. 
An optional structure associated with tables and clusters which you can create explicitly to speed SQL statement execution on a table. An index is logically and physically independent of the data. An index provides a faster access path to table data. 
Using a uniform datafile size gives flexibility in disk load balancing (not too large, not too small; not too few, not too many (overhead)). You should size proportionally to the total size of the database and allow for database growth. That is, it is easier to swap the datafiles from disk to disk for load balancing if they are all of uniform size. 
You can create tablespaces when you create the database, or you can add them afterward. Unless specified otherwise, users by default use the system tablespace. When creating users, add the default tablespace option, or alter the user after creation.   
|  Create Tablespace example create tablespace tabspace1 datafile  
'g:/DatabaseCreation/datafiles/tabspace_file1.dat'   
size 100M EXTENT MANAGEMENT LOCAL   
SEGMENT SPACE MANAGEMENT AUTO;  |  
| --- |  
The above example creates a 100-megabyte datafile. You can add more space in 10-megabyte extents up to a maximum of 1500 megabytes. The number of extents possible is dependent on the blocksize of the original database. A maximum of 121 extents are available for a 2048-block (the default for the operating system) database. This parameter is defined in the initialization file in the database folder.   
|  Alter command example alter user <username> default tablespace <tablespace name> temporary tablespace <temporary tablespace name>;  |  
| --- |  
You should consider the following when creating tablespaces:
  * Locally managed tablespaces (LMT)
  * Uniform extents (specified when tablespaces are created)
  * Automatic segment-space management


The following is a generic breakdown of a schema into groups of tables. You can create a tablespace for each group. This example only roughly matches your schema. 
  * Main feature—usually this is a network feature
  * Primary plant
  * Secondary/Equipment/InPlant
  * Common
  * Structure
  * Landbase
  * Dimensioning
  * Product tables (link to Data Reference Tables like Trace and PendingEdits 0
  * Picklist
  * MODIFICATIONLOG table
  * LTT_UNDO_LOG
  * Several miscellaneous


You can judiciously separate these tablespaces on different disks to minimize I/O collisions. 
You cannot have a tablespace per feature. However, you should try to put those tables that would interfere with the I/O of the other table in separate tablespaces. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256586) An alternative approach is documented in this article on striping and mirroring everything. <http://otn.oracle.com/deploy/availability/pdf/oow2000_sane.pdf>:

HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00

If the authentication mode is set to OIDC, and OpenID Connect is configured for the application using the All Applications Configuration Wizard, then the application redirects the user to the OIDC provider to execute the authentication sequence.  1 = Application bypasses the service and login with the user specified credentials.  |

The message appears when the application object reference count is not properly cleared for any reason at the time the application is being closed.  If the registry key flag value is '1', the above message is displayed to the user and is logged to diagnostics. ## The Facility Data Model
The terms data model and facility data model refer to the way you set up NetWorks Core to view data. Since the way you view data depends on the amount and type of data, the data model reflects how you use the data and why you use it in a certain way.   
|  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259289) The word KEY is a reserved word in SQL Server Express (SQL Server) and should not be used as a column name in any table.   |  
| --- |  
The NetWorks Core data model includes the following: 
  * [System tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cKG7KdVEYzxfeQ_5955GDw), which are created during system setup and which are required for the system to function 
  * [Data tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YyrpJSZjtKPzdI2Bzp8ATQ) and objects in the database, which comprise the facilities database model 
  * [Metadata tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sMcI_lxy9joYNal9DyZtJA) and objects in the database, which describe the facilities database model 
  * [DDC files](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yPXcvp7Vcm2gnqIMCRkXGw), which enable the display of facilities 
  * The [ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wsEiz1ZGsxe34kWQRuOuCg), which defines the configuration of database aliases and the DDC sets that make up the DDC. 


The basic NetWorks Core facilities database model consists of tabular and graphic components whose data records exist in various tables. Facilities (features) consist of different table records (components) in the database. These table records are bound together by common values in the [G3E_FNO and G3E_FID columns](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lLfp_1ij2BapLCwLmZwIyg) required in all data tables and by particular columns in the following metadata tables: 
  * G3E_COMPONENT
The [G3E_COMPONENT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) lists the components of the facility model and the tables where their records reside. 
    * The G3E_CNO column defines the component number. When making entries in this table, you should make G3E_CNO the next value of the G3E_CNO_SEQ sequence. 
    * The G3E_TABLE column contains the name of the table containing the component's records. Since a data table can contain data for more than one component, a data table may be listed more than once in the G3E_COMPONENT table. 
    * The G3E_TYPE column identifies the type of component, tabular or graphic, and geometry type. The supported types of graphic components are point, line, and area. Points can be point symbols or labels. 
  * G3E_FEATURE 
The [G3E_FEATURE table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) lists the facilities in the data model. The G3E_FNO column defines the feature number or feature type. When you make entries in this table, you should make G3E_FNO the next value of the G3E_FNO_SEQ sequence. 
  * G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT
The [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) identifies the relationship of features to components by pairing G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO.

# Core System Tables

## CONCURRENT_EDITS Table
The CONCURRENT_EDITS table captures the table and keys of records being edited in the active job that are also edited in other jobs. If the system is configured to detect concurrent edits this table is automatically populated with any conflicts that exist for the selected feature being edited.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  JOB_NAME  |  The name of a job whose edits are in conflict.   |  Varchar2 (30)   |   |  
|  LTT_ID   |  The LTT_ID of JOB_NAME.  |  Number  |   |  
|  LTT_STATUS  |  The LTT_STATUS of the modified record.   |  Varchar2 (6)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The G3E_FNO of the modified record.   |  Number (5)   |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The G3E_CNO of the modified record.   |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The G3E_FID of the modified record.   |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The G3E_CID of the modified record.   |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_Table  |  The LTT_STATUS of the modified record.  |  Varchar2 (38)  |   |  
|  SOURCE_JOB  |  The name of the job that this job is in conflict.  |  Varchar (30)  |  Can be null if conflict is with a master record.   |

## CONFLICTS Table
The CONFLICTS table captures the table and keys of records for jobs if they conflict with master records (for example, if the master record has changed since the job modified the record). This is only for Optimistic jobs. It is populated by calling LTT_USER.FINDCONFLICTS. Commands such as Post and Conflict Detection use this information.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  A unique identifier for this table.  |  Number (10)  |  You must put an index on this column to improve performance of database queries.  |  
|  TABLE_NAME  |  The table name of a record that has been modified in JOB_NAME.  |  Varchar (32)  |   |  
|  JOB_NAME  |  The name of a job whose edits are captured here.  |  Varchar (32)  |   |  
|  ROW_ID  |  The G3E_ID of the record in TABLE_NAME that has been modified as part of JOB_NAME and has a conflict with the Master record.   |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The G3E_FID of the modified record.  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The G3E_CID of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The G3E_FNO of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The G3E_CNO of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  LTT_STATUS  |  The LTT_STATUS of the modified record.  |  Varchar2 (6)  |  This may be ADD, EDIT or DELETE.  |  
|  LTT_ID  |  The LTT_ID of JOB_NAME.  |  Number  |   |

## LTT_Identifiers Table
The LTT_Identifiers table maintains the list of long-term transactions that have been opened (current jobs). It stores the mapping between the client's Job_ID and the database's internal LTT_ID.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  LTT_ID  |  A unique numeric value for a long-term transaction. The value for this column comes from the next value of the LTT_IDS sequence.   |  Number  |  This is populated by the LTT_ADMIN.CREATEJOB procedure. You must put an index on this column to improve performance of database queries.   |  
|  LTT_NAME  |  A unique user defined name for this identifier. A Job_ID from Job Management System.  |  Varchar2 (32)  |  This name is unique and is constrained by the UNQ_LTT_NAME constraint. You must put an index on this column to improve performance of database queries.   |  
|  LTT_OPTIMISTIC  |  A single character indicating where the identifier is to be used as an optimistic style of long-term transaction.   |  Varchar2 (1)  |  A Y indicates optimistic mode.  |  
|  LTT_CDATE  |  The date this job was created.  |  Date  |   |  
|  LTT_CUSER  |  The username that created this job.  |  Varchar2 (32)  |   |

## LTT_Sessions Table
The LTTSession table is populated with entries to support the required display. A record in this table indicates that a particular session is supposed to see a particular LTT. 
The LTT_ID and LTT_SESSIONID columns together are constrained to be unique by the UNQ_LTT_SESSIONS constraint. 
This table is populated by the LTT_USER.EDITJOB, LTT_USER.VIEWJOB procedures and cleaned by the LTT_USER.DONE procedure.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  LTT_ID  |  A valid LTT identifier from the LTT_Identifiers table.  |  Number  |  
|  LTT_SESSIONID  |  A numeric value containing the auditing session identifier associated with any given user.   |  Number  |  
Because NetWorks Core makes two connections to the database, this table records both connections' session IDs as accessing the job or LTT_ID. This makes it more difficult to determine how many users are really working in the job. These two columns should have a unique composite index with LTT_SESSIONID being the first column.

## LTT_Undo_Log Table
The LTT_UNDO_LOG table tracks every change that occurs as part of a long-term transaction. It supports the ability to undo or redo facility data edits, and it also supports the following workflows: 
  * [Validate](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Vf80LbonyfEAJpsWHOS2MQ)
  * [Fit All Job Edits](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_t8sLGt_93Hy4Q~Y_6NLhw)
  * [Discard Selected Edits](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qgvKGBWQ0~8XLZUTw~~yyg)
  * [Post Job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KjQgbJSTeMO172Qy1IDZBg)
  * [Conflict Detection and Resolution](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/heF3oex8IXnA60RkpnJEWw)

  
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  LTT_TID  |  A value that groups a list of data manipulation functions together.  |  Number  |  This is either the RDBMS transaction ID or the G3E transaction ID set by Set Checkpoint using the next value of the LTT_UNDO_ID sequence.   |  
|  LTT_SESSIONID  |  A numeric value containing the auditing session identifier associated with any given user.   |  Number  |   |  
|  LTT_ID  |  A value indicating which long- term transaction this entry is associated with.  |  Number  |  You must put an index on this column to improve performance of database queries.  |  
|  LTT_TABLE_NAME  |  Table name with which this transaction is associated.  |  Varchar2 (32)  |   |  
|  LTT_ROWID  |  A value indicating the key value (G3E_ID) in the table.  |  Number  |   |  
|  LTT_PID  |  A value indicating the previous transaction identifier to this entry.  |  Number  |   |  
|  LTT_UNDONE  |  A value indicating whether this transaction has been undone.  |  Number(2)  | 
  * 0 means the transaction has not been undone.
  * 1 means the transaction has been undone.

 |

## MODIFICATIONLOG Table

### Resetting the Modification Number
The MODIFICATIONNUMBER in MODIFICATIONLOG has a maximum value of 2,147,483,648 or 231. 
When the maximum value is exceeded, the system will not behave correctly. Some problems you will encounter include: 
  1. Placement of new or editing of feature
  2. Connecting to NetViewer
  3. Publishing
  4. ValidateJobConsistency.


  * To reset MODIFICATIONNUMBER:


Please consult your local Hexagon Support organization to confirm these steps should be run on the database. 
For both of the procedures below, ensure that there is no activity in the database.
Note: When the procedures instruct the customer to post or discard jobs, they might have to do these posts and discards from inside the database. 
If you can post or discard all the jobs, use this procedure:
  1. Backup MODIFICATIONLOG table. 
  2. Stop the Persisted Deltas service if you use one.
  3. Post all current job edits or discard them. Confirm that there are no entries with LTT_ID <> 0. 
  4. Truncate the MODIFICATIONLOG table.
  5. Reset the Modification Log sequence (G3E_MODLOG_SEQ) to start with 2. In most cases, the best way to do this is to drop the sequence and re-create it. 
  6. Perform a Full Publish of the data.
  7. Restart the Persisted Deltas service if you use one.


If you cannot post or discard all the jobs and the lowest MODIFICATIONNUMBER is high, use this procedure:
  1. Backup the MODIFICATIONLOG table.
  2. Stop the Persisted Deltas service if you use one.
  3. Post or discard as many jobs as you can, especially the oldest ones (i.e. those that have small MODIFICATIONNUMBERs). 
  4. Delete all the master records (LTT_ID = 0) in the MODIFICATIONLOG table.
  5. Find the minimum MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG table.
  6. Issue SQL to decrease each MODIFICATIONNUMBER by the minimum MODIFICATIONNUMBER minus one. 
  7. Reset the Modification Log sequence to start with the current maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER. In most cases, the best way to do this is to drop the sequence and re-create it. 
  8. Perform a Full Publish of the data.
  9. Restart the Persisted Deltas service if you use one.


This is a script that can be used to do Steps 4-7 when all jobs cannot be posted or discarded: 
DECLARE
nMinModLogNum NUMBER;
nMaxModLogNum NUMBER;
nCurrentSeq NUMBER;
BEGIN
-- Delete all the master records in the ModificationLog table.
DELETE FROM MODIFICATIONLOG WHERE LTT_ID = 0;
-- Find the minimum ModificationNumber in the ModificationLog table.
SELECT FLOOR(MIN(MODIFICATIONNUMBER)) INTO nMinModLogNum FROM MODIFICATIONLOG;
-- Issue SQL to decrease each ModificationNumber by the minimum Modification number minus one.
UPDATE MODIFICATIONLOG SET MODIFICATIONNUMBER = MODIFICATIONNUMBER - nMinModLogNum + 1;
-- Reset modlog sequence to start with the current maximum ModificationNumber.
SELECT FLOOR(MAX(MODIFICATIONNUMBER)) INTO nMaxModLogNum FROM MODIFICATIONLOG;
-- Recreate sequence with max ModificationNumber + 1
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'DROP SEQUENCE G3E_MODLOG_SEQ';
nMaxModLogNum := nMaxModLogNum + 1;
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'CREATE SEQUENCE G3E_MODLOG_SEQ NOCYCLE NOCACHE ORDER START WITH ' || nMaxModLogNum;
END;
/

## PENDINGEDITS Table
The PENDINGEDITS table captures the table and keys of the pending edits for jobs. It is populated by calling LTT_USER.FINDPENDINGEDITS. Commands such as Review Job Edits, Post, Discard and Validate Model use this information.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  A unique identifier for this table.  |  Number (10)  |  You must put an index on this column to improve performance of database queries.  |  
|  TABLE_NAME  |  The table name of a record that has been modified in JOB_NAME.  |  Varchar2 (32)  |   |  
|  JOB_NAME  |  The name of a job whose edits are captured here.  |  Varchar2 (32)  |   |  
|  ROW_ID  |  The G3E_ID of the record in TABLE_NAME that has been modified as part of JOB_NAME.  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The G3E_FID of the modified record.  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The G3E_CID of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The G3E_FNO of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The G3E_CNO of the modified record.  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  LTT_STATUS  |  The LTT_STATUS of the modified record.  |  Varchar2 (6)  |  This may be ADD, EDIT or DELETE.  |  
|  LTT_ID  |  The LTT_ID of JOB_NAME.  |  Number  |   |

## TEMP_CONSTRAINTS Table
The TEMP_CONSTRAINTS table captures constraints on tables before installing LTT support. Unique constraints must be discarded. Check constraints are modified to apply only to master records. After LTT support is installed, the appropriate(not unique) constraints are reapplied. If you have constraints, install LTT, and then drop the constraints and reinstall LTT, you should truncate the table first.   
|  Column  |  Description  |  Data Type  |  Comments  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  CONSTRAINT_NAME  |  The name of the constraint being dropped and stored.  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  CONSTRAINT_TYPE  |  The type of constraint.   |  Varchar2 (1)  |  Types are primary, unique, and check.  |  
|  TABLE_NAME  |  Name of the table with the constraints.   |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  OWNER  |  Name of the owner of the table.  |  Varchar 2 (30)   |   |  
|  COLUMN_NAME  |  Name of the column with the constraints.   |  Varchar2 (4000)  |   |  
|  POSITION  |  The position of the column in the constraint.   |  Number  |   |

## Configuring the Menu and Toolbar Layout
Using the Customize dialog box through Metadata Explorer, you can customize the menu and toolbar layout to display both [custom commands](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LCGaRCpQhSd842cjvEzvQ) and NetWorks Core commands. You can also configure metadata so that after you publish, the layout is imposed on users. The imposed layout is stored in [the registry for each user](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EuKv5e52~eOj8w0Uj~BfAA). If new commands are included in an upgrade, you have to configure a new menu layout for your users who need those commands. 
Before you configure menus for your users, you should review the users' workflows and define the most common configuration of toolbars and dockable controls. These settings (location of dockable controls, user-defined toolbars, pinned/unpinned state) should be made during the configuration of the other menu items. They are included in the published menu layout. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118) The position of floating dockable controls such as Feature Explorer is also saved. 
The user can customize menus and toolbars using the same Customize dialog box, but accessed through Tools > Customize. When the user exits NetWorks Core, the new layout is saved. When you design a new menu or toolbar layout, you can configure metadata to either impose the most recent layout on the user or prompt the user to accept the changes. 
The Customize dialog box accessed through Metadata Explorer works exactly like the one accessed through Tools > Customize with one exception. In the Metadata Explorer version, clicking Reset reverts menus and toolbars to the defaults delivered with NetWorks Core. When you click Reset in the Tools > Customize version, custom settings revert to the last settings you published. 
  * To configure the menu or toolbar layout:


  1. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar. 
  2. On the Customize dialog box, create new [toolbars](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/giSKUX9LyNi_v3fYRtok5A) and [menus](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uCrK7Ar_gq1VqHu_fiCvCg) and visually position NetWorks Core and custom commands and buttons to suit your data model. This process updates the [G3E_MENULAYOUT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PaWOsUbH5ZLHx1fVEGDVjA) table. 
  3. Click Close. 
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118) to commit your changes to the database or ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118) to roll back the edits. You must either commit the edits or roll them back before exiting Metadata Explorer. 
The menus and toolbars on your computer reflect the settings you just made.
  5. To test the layout, click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118). 
    1. On the Refresh Metadata Edits dialog box, check Menu/Toolbar Layout under Command Layout & Roles. 
    2. Click OK. 
    3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257118) to set the user role on your computer to a different role. 
    4. Log in as that user.
    5. The command and toolbar layout you just created should now be available.
  6. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, Navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version > Command Version node and increment the version number in the G3E_ROLE field. 
  7. To impose the new menu layout on users, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version Notification > Command Version Notification node and select Change in the G3E_ROLE field. 
OR
To allow users to make a decision about using the new menu layout, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version Notification > Command Version Notification node and select PromptToChange in the G3E_ROLE field. 
  8. [Publish metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ).

## Customizing Using .NET

### Deploying .NET Implementation Assemblies
This is a representative workflow for deploying .NET implementation assemblies to a network share. 
  * To deploy .NET implementation assemblies:


  1. Identify a network share on which to deploy custom assemblies. If necessary, create a new network share.   
|  Example \\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder  |  
| --- |  
  2. Move custom assemblies to the network share.
  3. Update the FileUNCPaths.xml to specify the network share. [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257108) to see an example. 
Example
<Customization>
<DotNet>
<Location Type="UNC">\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder</Location>
</DotNet>
</Customization>
  4. Update the .NET Framework security policy on every client machine to access custom assemblies using Code Access Security Policy Tool (Caspol.exe). [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257108) to see an example. 
To give the client machine full access to all files under the network share (\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder), create a new child code group under the LocalIntranet_Zone code group by typing the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -ag LocalIntranet_Zone -url "\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*" FullTrust -n "CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName" 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257108) CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName represents the child group name. This can be any name. 
To find that a custom assembly (\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\CustomAssembly.dll) belongs to what code groups, type the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -rsg
\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\CustomAssembly.dll 
Here is a partial output of the above command: 
1. All code: Nothing
1.2. Zone – Intranet: LocalIntranet
1.2.#. Url - \\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*: FullTrust 
Alternatively, you can create a new child group, CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName, under a different code group. For example, to create a new child group under the All_Code code group, type the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -ag All_Code -url "\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*" FullTrust -n "CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName" 
Edit the g3e.config file and add the tag <loadFromRemoteSources enabled="true" /> in g3e.config after </assemblybinding>:
![g3eexeconfig](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257108)

### General .NET Interfaces
Several .NET interfaces were originally developed for use with Plotting and NetViewer; however, these interfaces can also be called by any .NET solution. 
Intergraph.GTechnology.Services.dll contains two classes you can implement using any .NET programming language and environment. These classes retrieve a list of local printers. 
  * [LocalPrinters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ycOikijZ90TLWXfqrSD7lQ)
  * [PrinterInfo](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uaXnKciDyZRJvmhb_Ll31g)

### Implementing a .NET Custom Extension
This is an overview workflow for implementing a .NET custom extension in NetWorks Core. 
  * To implement a .NET custom extension:


  1. Produce a .NET custom extension type in a .NET custom extension assembly:
     * The .NET custom extension project must add a reference to the Intergraph.GTechnology.dll assembly located in the \GTechnology\Program folder. This assembly is not deployed in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC). The assembly contains the public namespaces Intergraph.CoordinateSystems, Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces, and Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * Inherit a .NET custom extension type from a NetWorks Core public interface defined in the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces. The .NET custom extension type can use .NET helper objects from the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * The .NET custom extension type should carefully consider the type of work performed and the access to feature data. On occasion, it is necessary to force system Garbage Corrector (GC) to reclaim unused memory. When the NetWorks Core session is terminated, the framework does the required cleaning. As part of the clean-up processing, the framework forces GC to run. However, if you manipulate a large number of ADO recordsets and/or a large number of NetWorks Core features, it is also appropriate to force GC to run in those .NET custom extensions. 
It is also an essential .NET coding practice to call the Dispose method, when available, and when you are done using those .NET objects. For example, call the IGTFeaturePlacementService.Dispose method when you are done using the .NET helper object from your .NET custom extension type. This is the proper garbage collection sequence: 
Call any Dispose methods on objects that you are using;
Release any objects that do not naturally fall out of scope
Call the garbage collection sequence noted here when you have processed a large number of ADO recordsets and/or IGTKeyObject. 
GC.Collect();
GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
GC.Collect();
     * ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257110) There are some programming practices that must be followed in custom code: 
       * Only use local variables to store pointers to NetWorks Core windows. Never store them as global variables or even class variables. 
       * Never call methods that refresh the database while there are objects in the select set. These APIs (and maybe more) refresh the database: 
- GTJobManagementService.RefreshJobEnvironment
- GTTransactionManager.RefreshDatabaseChanges
- GTTransactionManager.Commit
- The methods on JobHelper that change the job context
       * Never change the job context when writing functional interfaces, especially validation interfaces. 
  2. Place the .NET custom extension assembly in the \GTechnology\Program folder for testing purposes. 
  3. Using Metadata Explorer, populate the required NetWorks Core interface point metadata to add the .NET custom extension, and refresh or publish metadata. 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Software Interfaces node and navigate to the appropriate .NET interface, for example, Compute Partial Start Length 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257110), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Populate the new row in the interface table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel: 
      1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the object.  
This name appears in the tree view. 
      2. In the G3E_INTERFACE field, type a name for the .NET assembly. The value in the G3E_INTERFACE field must be in the following format:  
AssemblyName:TypeName  
where 
AssemblyName is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension, and TypeName is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.   
|  Example GTDotNetSamples:Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample  AssemblyName is GTDotNetSamples. TypeName is Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample with namespace as Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples and classname as GTDisableEditToolSample.  |  
| --- |  
      3. Click OK. 
    4. To update existing arguments for your object:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Select the argument you want to update.
      3. Update the fields that are available for edit, and click somewhere else on the screen.
      4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257110) to commit your edits to the database. 
      5. Repeat these steps for each argument.
    5. To add arguments to your interface:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257110), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
      3. In the argument table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel:
       * Type a number to indicate the order of the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL field.
       * Type a name for the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTNAME field.
       * Describe the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTDESCRIPTION field.
       * From the G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE drop-down list, select a data type.
       * Click OK. 
      1. Repeat Steps ii and iii for each argument you want to add.
    6. [Complete configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LDawReDio_37hAl4p5itA) of the new interface by associating it with a feature, component, attribute, and so forth so that a user can access it. 
  4. Test the .NET custom extension type by running a NetWorks Core command that exposes the interface point. If you are implementing a custom command, then you would invoke your custom command to test your code. 
  5. Publish and distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension assembly either to a shared location defined in the [FileUNCPaths.xml file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) under the <CUSTOMIZATION> and <DOTNET> tags or distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension to every local client machine. 
On the client machine, the .NET custom extension assembly should be either placed in the \GTechnology\Program folder or deployed into the GAC, so that users can access the assembly at runtime. 
The .NET custom extension assemblies can be deployed into the GAC by using Windows Explorer to drag assemblies into GAC, by using a Windows Installer package you have developed, or by using the developer GAC tool, Gacutil.exe, which is delivered with the .NET framework SDK. 


If a location is defined in FileUNCPaths.xml, and .NET custom extension assemblies exist on both local and remote machines, the local copy takes precedence.

### Metadata for .NET Extensions
A new metadata configuration is required for each .NET custom extension, and you can use Metadata Explorer to configure .NET custom extensions. The G3E_INTERFACE field must contain the .NET custom extension information in the following format: 
AssemblyName:TypeName
where
AssemblyName is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension and TypeName is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.   
|  Example GTDotNetSamples:Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample  where AssemblyName is GTDotNetSamples and TypeName is Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample with namespace as Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples and classname as GTDisableEditToolSample.  |  
| --- |

### Reducing Memory Consumption in .NET Customized Code
Some sites that have larger metadata models can run out of memory during long NetWorks Core sessions. To solve this issue, the NetWorks Core software accesses the largest metadata tables in most configurations through filtered DDC access. 
To reduce memory consumption in your custom code, NetWorks Core recommends that you modify how existing custom code accesses certain metadata tables. To access this functionality, use the public API and the registry key as discussed in this topic. 
Public API
Custom code that accesses any of the tables listed below needs to be changed to use the [IGTDataContext.MetadataRecordset Method (String, String, String)](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/Overload_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext_MetadataRecordset.htm) in the public API. A filter must be passed along with the metadata optimized table name. Performance is better if the filter expression uses the published indexed primary key for the table. This might require some algorithm changes. 
There are two overloads of the IGTDataContext.MetadataRecordset method. The first overload specifies both a table name and a filter clause. The second overload specifies a table name, a filter clause, and a sort clause. 
  * ADODB.Recordset MetadataRecordset(string OptimizedTableName, string Filter) 
  * ADODB.Recordset MetadataRecordset(string OptimizedTableName, string Filter, string Sort) 


Use of the, MetadataRecordset(table) method is not recommended because it loads the entire metadata table into memory.   
|  Optimized Table  |  Published Indexed Primary Key  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DIALOGATTRIBUTES_OPTABLE  |  G3E_DTNO  |  
|  G3E_STYLEFILTERS_OPTABLE  |  G3E_SRNO  |  
|  G3E_FEATUREPLACEMENT_OPTABLE  |  G3E_FNO  |  
|  G3E_STYLEOBJECTS_OPTABLE  |  G3E_SNO  |  
|  G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFO_OPTABLE  |  G3E_ANO  |  
|  G3E_ATTRIBUTEINFOFI_OPTABLE  |  G3E_CNO  |  
|  G3E_COMPVIEWCOMP_OPTABLE  |  G3E_FNO  |  
|  G3E_FEATURECOMPS_OPTABLE  |  G3E_FNO  |  
|  G3E_FIND_OPTABLE  |  G3E_FNO  |  
|  G3E_FINDCOMPATTR_OPTABLE   |  G3E_FCROWNO  |  
Registry Key
The LargeMetadataAccessWarning registry key enables pop-up warnings when one of the above-listed large DDC-published metadata tables is accessed without a filter value, and DDC access is enabled. No warnings are given for access to the ADO published RAW files that are not listed in the above table. The intent of this flag is to help you find all the call sites where your software i s reading the whole table into memory. 
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00]  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  LargeMetadataAccessWarning  |  Application developers who are using the public API see a message box when they call MetadataRecordset(table) if the following are true: 
  * No filter argument, or the filter argument is not compatible with ADO
  * The table is marked as G3E_USEDDCACCESS=1 in G3E_METADATAKEYS_OPTABLE
  * The LargeMetadataAccessWarning = 1

The default is 0.  |

### Troubleshooting

#### Failure While Loading a Custom .NET Framework 4.0 Type
Problem:  Failure has occurred while loading a type. 
AssemblyName:TypeName<AssemblyLocation><AssemblyName><TypeName>
Could not load file or assembly 'file: ///AssemblyLocation\AssemblyName.DLL' or one of its dependencies. This assembly is built by a runtime newer than the currently loaded runtime and cannot be loaded. 
Cause: NetWorks Core is built using .NET Framework 2.0, and .NET custom assembly is built using .NET Framework 4.0. 
Solution: [Configure NetWorks Core to use .NET Framework 4.0.](javascript:;)

#### Problems Displaying .NET Controls
Some .NET controls (for example, DataGridView and GroupBox) may not display properly on your computer when they are used in the NetWorks Core .NET custom extensions. However, the same controls may display correctly from a remote desktop and in .NET Windows Applications. This problem could be caused by an incompatibility between your monitor and your video card. To correct the display problem, try reducing the acceleration setting on your video card. 
  * To change the hardware acceleration setting on your video card:


  1. On the Control Panel, select Display. 
  2. On the Display Properties dialog box Settings tab, click Advanced. 
  3. On the dialog box that appears, select the Troubleshoot tab and reduce the hardware acceleration. 
  4. Click OK, and test the display of the controls.

##### Convert Overloaded Operators to Corresponding Public Methods
Certain.NET API objects had overloaded operators which cannot be exposed in the interface implementation. You must use the corresponding new methods. 
  * The GTPoint class had the following overloaded operators:
public static bool operator==(GTPoint pt1, GTPoint pt2)
public static bool operator !=(GTPoint pt1, GTPoint pt2)
public static GTPoint operator +(GTPoint p, GTVector v) 
public static GTPoint operator -(GTPoint p, GTVector v)
Public static GTPoint operator -(GTPoint p)
IGTPoint interface has the corresponding methods for each of the overloaded operators.
public bool Equals(IGTPoint pt1, IGTPoint pt2)
public bool NotEquals(IGTPoint pt1, IGTPoint pt2)
public IGTPoint Positive(IGTPoint p, IGTVector v)
public IGTPoint Negative(IGTPoint p, IGTVector v)
public IGTPoint Negate(IGTPoint p)


  * The GTFieldValue class had the following overloaded operators:
public static explicit operator int(GTFieldValue oValue)
public static explicit operator double(GTFieldValue oValue)
public static explicit operator bool(GTFieldValue oValue)
public static explicit operator string(GTFieldValue oValue)
public static explicit operator GTGeometry(GTFieldValue oValue)
IGTFieldValue interface has corresponding methods for each of the overloaded operators:
int GTFeldValueToInt(IGTFieldValue oValue)
double GTFeldValueToDouble(IGTFieldValue oValue)
bool GTFeldValueToBool(IGTFieldValue oValue)
string GTFeldValueToString(IGTFieldValue oValue)
IGTGeometry GTFeldValueToGTGeometry(IGTFieldValue oValue)
  * The GTGeometry class had the following overloaded operators:
public static GTGeometry operator +(GTGeometry geometry, GTVector delta)
public static GTGeometry operator *(GTGeometry geometry, GTMatrix xform)
IGTGeometry interface has corresponding methods for each of the overloaded operators:
public IGTGeometry Add(IGTGeometry geometry, IGTVector delta)
public IGTGeometry Multiply(IGTGeometry geometry, IGTMatrix xform)
  * The GTMatrix class has the following overloaded operators:
public static GTMatrix operator*(GTMatrix m1, GTMatrix m2)
public static GTPoint operator *(GTMatrix m, GTPoint p)
public static GTVector operator *(GTMatrix m, GTVector v)
IGTMatrix interface has corresponding methods for each of the overloaded operators:
public static GTMatrix Multiply(GTMatrix m1, GTMatrix m2)
public GTPoint TransformPoint(GTPoint p)
public GTVector TransformVector(GTVector v)
  * The GTVector type had the following overloaded operators:
public static GTVector operator +(GTVector v1, GTVector v2)
public static GTVector operator -(GTVector v1, GTVector v2)
public static GTVector operator -(GTVector v)
public static GTVector operator *(GTVector v, double factor)
IGTVector interface has corresponding methods for each of the overloaded operators:
IGTVector AddVectors(IGTVector v1, IGTVector v2);
IGTVector SubtractVectors(IGTVector v1, IGTVector v2);
IGTVector NegateVector(IGTVector v);
IGTVector ScaleVector(double value);

##### Update Access to Coordinate System Objects
With NetWorks Core version 10.1, the coordinate system support services are provided as a common Hexagon module. While the API is nearly identical to that provided in earlier releases, there are a few changes. As with other objects, the data reference is to an interface definition. It might be necessary to cast member variables when using the dot notation to access properties.   
|  Code Example before 10.1 using Intergraph.CoordSystems; … CoordSystemsMgr oCoordSystemsMgr; oCoordSystemsMgr = m_oDataContext.CoordSystemsMgr; CoordSystem oCoordSystem; oCS = oCoordSystemsMgr.CoordSystem; double dMeters2Database = 1.0 / CS.StorageToProjectionScale;  |  
| --- |  
You must change this code to the following pattern:  
|  Code Example for 10.1 and later using Intergraph.CoordSystems; … ICoordSystemsMgr oCoordSystemsMgr; oCoordSystemsMgr = (ICoordSystemsMgr)m_oDataContext.CoordSystemsMgr; ICoordSystem oCoordSystem; oCoordSystem = oCoordSystemsMgr.BaseCoordSystem; double dMeters2Database = 1.0 / oCoordSystem.StorageToProjectionScale;  |  
| --- |  
While most of the coordinate system API is identical, the core coordinate system object retrieved from the CoordSystemsMgr (by way of ICoordSystemsMgr) is now BaseCoordSystem instead of CoordSystem as shown in the preceding example.

##### Update Access to GTApplication Object
Before NetWorks Core version 10.1, the GTApplication object was globally available. In version 10.1 and later, you must create the object using the GTClassFactory. 
This is an example of a retrieving a reference to the Application object and setting the status bar.   
|  Code Example before 10.1 GTApplication oApp = GTApplication.Application; oApp.SetStatusBarText(GTStatusPanelConstants.gtaspcMessage,"Test.");  |  
| --- |  
You must change this code to the following pattern.  
|  Code Example for 10.1 and later IGTApplication oApp = GTClassFactory.Create<IGTApplication>() ; oApp.SetStatusBarText (GTStatusPanelConstants.gtaspcMessage, "Test.");  |  
| --- |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/289318) Only the first line is different, the status bar method is still the same as are all the other methods.
