##### Implementing Relationship Geometry Objects

###### RGI Calling Sequences
The calling sequences of RGI methods vary with the workflow. The following sections map commands to relationship service calls to RGI method calls. The Description columns contain the processing in an example CrossSection RGI. 
The calling sequences have been extracted from the many- to-many-ownership (MMO) relationship service. They may be slightly different for other relationship services. Any differences occur in the control flow as these relationship services update the connectivity components and attributes. 
MMO caches the changes in the memory and updates all connectivity records in IRelationshipInterface_Update. This means that all Before/AfterEstablish and Before/AfterDelete calls are accomplished between BeforeUpdate and AfterUpdate. Other relationships may not be caching the changes; they may just directly update relationship attributes and components in KeyObjects in other methods besides IRelationshipInterface_Update. Therefore, Before/AfterEstablish and Before/AfterDelete calls may be more scattered. 
Pipe and Cross Section are used as example feature classes in this topic.
Initialization
This method is called before any other method.  
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|   |  Initialize  |  The CrossSection RGI should get the input arguments if needed retrieve any metadata, such as CNOs of the label and Cross-section line components in the Cross- section feature.   |  
Placement
Commands: New Feature, New Component, Edit Feature, and any other commands creating new features and/or components 
Processing Mode: gtrgiEstablish 
While GetRelationshipCandidates is called before EstablishRelationship (first user click identifying a point in the map window for the component being placed), the ProcessingMode may be gtrgiUnknown because the relationship service may not have enough information about the context in which it is called.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_GetRelationshipCandidates  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic  |  
|   |  FilterLocatedCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates is called while the user moves the mouse. As the user did not click any point of the Pipe, the RGI does not have enough information for filtering. Therefore it does not do any filtering.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_EstablishRelationship  |  FilterLocatedCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates is called after each mouse click. The RGI has the partial Pipe geometry being placed in the Geometry parameter. It receives the Cross- section line items in the Candidates parameter. It should keep all Cross- section line items in the Candidates collection, which are intersected by the Pipe digitized so far.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_GetRelationshipCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates is called while the user moves the mouse. At this point, the CNO and CID of the component instance being placed and the partial geometry of the Pipe are available. The RGI should keep all Cross- section line items in the Candidates collection, which are intersected by the Pipe digitized so far.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_ComponentComplete  |  FilterCandidates  |  MMO may be configured to collect all the relationship candidates only after placement is completed. If configured this way, it builds a GTKeyObjects collection with relationship candidates and passes it to FilterCandidates as the Candidates parameter.  For the example CrossSection RGI, it makes sense to configure the MMO like this because all relationships established so far have been established only to Cross- section features within the maximum offset distance from the clicked points. The RGI should keep all those Cross- section features in the Candidates collection for which the Cross- section line is intersected by the Pipe just placed.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541) This way of collecting candidates is MMO- specific, and this call is made only if MMO is configured in metadata to do this processing.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Validation
Commands: Validate Feature, Validate Job Edits, Post Job Edits, Post Partial 
Proocessing Mode: gtrgiValidate 
The RGI is initialized with gtrgiUnknown, and gtrgiValidate is set immediately before the Validate call.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_ValidateRelationship  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|   |  Validate  |  For the Pipe being validated, the related Cross- section features is checked. The first check is whether the geometries intersect. If there are no intersections, a validation error is reported. The second check compares the order of labels and order of intersection between the Cross- section and related pipes. If there is a discrepancy, a validation error is reported.   |  
Reestablish Relationship by Point
Commands: Reestablish Relationship 
Processing Mode: gtrgiReestablish 
While GetRelationshipCandidates is called before ReEstablishRelationship, the ProcessingMode may be gtrgiUnknown because the relationship service may not have enough information about the context in which it is called.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_GetRelationshipCandidates  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|   |  FilterLocatedCandidates  |  The RGI should be tolerant to the CNO being 0, since it is not available in this workflow until the user clicks.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_ReEstablishRelationship  |  FilterLocatedCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates is called after the mouse click. The Candidates parameter contains the located objects where the user clicked the mouse. The RGI should keep all Cross- section line items in the Candidates collection, which are intersected by the active Pipe feature.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Reestablish Relationship by Geometry or Attribute Edit in the Triggering Component
Commands: Edit Tool and Edit Geometry (Move Vertex, Move Component, Rotate, Continue Geometry, Trim, Extend), Edit Feature 
Only when a triggering component that would fire relationship processing is modified.
Processing Mode:  gtrgiReestablish 
While GetRelationshipCandidates is called before ReEstablishRelationship, ProcessingMode may be gtrgiUnknown because the relationship service may not have enough information about the context in which it is called.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_GetRelationshipCandidates  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_ReEstablishRelationship  |  AdjustGeometry  |  After a geometry or attribute edit takes place on the Pipe, the RGI iterates through related Cross- sections. If no intersection is found between the related Cross- section and the Pipe, the Cross- section is extended to intersect the edited Pipe. The RGI further recalculates the order of labels on each related Cross- section.  AdjustGeometry returns True if it considers the processing complete. If it did not manage to adjust the related Cross- sections and/or reorder the labels, it should return False. In this way it leaves it to the relationship service to further process the relationships.  An additional factor to consider regarding the return value is whether the relationships have to be established if the modified Pipe happens to intersect new Cross- sections. If the relationships have to be established, False should be always returned.   |  
|   |  FilterCandidates  |  FilterCandidates is called in this scenario after AdjustGeometry returns False (if more RGIs are running parallel and at least one of them returns False from AdjustGeometry, FilterCandidates is called for all RGIs). The relationship service then calls FilterCandidates for the current relationships to determine whether they may be kept or it must be dropped.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Silent Establish
Commands: Placement Configurations 
Processing Mode: gtrgiUnknown   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_SilentEstablishRelationship  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Deleting a Triggering Component
Commands: Edit Tool (Delete) 
Processing Mode: gtrgiUnknown   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_VerifyDelete  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|   |  AllowDelete  |  There is no reason why a pipe should not be deleted if it is related to a Cross- section. The Pipe can always be deleted if there is a related Cross- section; so this method always returns True. Additional processing may be put to the update logic that deletes a Cross- section if this is the last related pipe feature.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Merging Features
Commands: Merge Features 
Processing Mode:  gtrgiMerge   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipMerge_Allow  |  Initialize  |  See Initialization in this topic.  |  
|   |  AllowMerge  |  AllowMerge is called right after the user selects both features to be merged. CrossSection RGI should have no reason to disallow the merge; so it should always return True.   |  
|  IRelationshipMerge_Approve  |  ApproveMerge  |  ApproveMerge is called right after the user completes the interactive merge of the geometries. CrossSection RGI should have no reason to disapprove the merge; so it should always return True.   |  
|  IRelationshipMerge_Process  |  AdjustGeometry  |  This is like geometry edit. After the geometry of the merged Pipe has been updated, the Cross- sections along the new pipe have to be updated.The processing should be the same as for Reestablish Relationship by Geometry or Attribute Edit in the Triggering Component in this topic.   |  
|   |  FilterCandidates  |  FilterCandidates is called in this scenario after AdjustGeometry returned False (if more RGI's are running parallel and at least one of them returns False from AdjustGeometry, FilterCandidates is called for all RGIs). Relationship service then calls FilterCandidates for the current relationships to verify whether they may be kept or some have to be dropped.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |   |  See Update Processing in this topic.  |  
Update Processing
Update processing is done after establishing or dropping relationships of the active feature and adjusting geometries of the related features. 
If multiple relationships are running parallel, the whole sequence below is executed for each relationship without interleaving with the other relationships.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  BeforeUpdate  |   |  
|   |  BeforeEstablish  |   |  
|   |  AfterEstablish  |  If a relationship to a new Cross- section has been established, the order of the labels in this Cross- section must be recalculated to reflect the position of the newly related Pipe.   |  
|   |  BeforeDelete  |   |  
|   |  AfterDelete  |  If a relationship with an existing Cross- section has been dropped, the label for the unrelated Pipe must be deleted and the positions of the other labels must be recalculated to eliminate the gap after the deleted label.   |  
|   |  AfterUpdate  |   |  
Placement of Point Feature Breaking a Linear Feature
Commands: New Feature, New Component, Edit Feature, and any other commands creating new features and/or components 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541) The following steps assume a Node and an Edge feature, as well as NodeEdge RGI and EdgeNode RGI. NodeEdge RGI is invoked while the Node feature is the active feature in the relationship. EdgeNode RGI is invoked when Edge is the active feature. The RGIs enforce the constraint that the relationship between the Node and Edge may be established only of the Node is identical with one of the endpoints of the Edge. 
The progression of breaking an Edge is illustrated below.
Original situation
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541)
Relationships:
Node1 – Edge1
Node2 – Edge1
Processing Mode: gtrgiUnknown   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_GetRelationshipCandidates  |  NodeEdge RGIInitialize  |  NodeEdge RGI is initialized.  |  
|   |  NodeEdge RGI FilterLocatedCandidates  |  If CNO and CID are not available, FilterLocatedCandidates cannot do any filtering. If CNO and CID are available, the RGI can use EstablishPoint as the tentative Node and do the processing described in Step 1.   |  
Step 1: User places Node3.
For the break to proceed, a relationship is established between Edge1 and Node3.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541)
Relationships:
Node1 – Edge1
Node2 – Edge1
Node3 – Edge1
Processing Mode: gtrgiEstablish   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_EstablishRelationship  |  NodeEdge RGI FilterLocatedCandidates  |  FilterLocatedCandidates is called after the mouse click. The RGI has the Node3 geometry being placed in the Geometry parameter. It receives located edges, including Edge1, in the Candidates parameter.  FilterLocatedCandidates keeps Edge1 in the Candidates collection if the position of the Node3 is identical with one of the endpoints of Edge1.  If the relationship service considers the possibility of breaking linear features, it sets the CanBreak parameter to True. For break to proceed, the relationship service needs to establish the relationship between Node3 and Edge1. When FilterLocatedCandidates is called and CanBreak is True, FilterLocatedCandidates should keep Edge1 in Candidates collection for all positions of Node3 along Edge1, where Edge1 may be broken.  In addition, FilterLocatedCandidates should also keep it in the Candidates collection for all conditions where it returns True for CanBreak = False (that is, Node3 is identical with one of the endpoints of Edge1).   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_ComponentComplete  |  NodeEdge RGI FilterCandidates  |  MMO can be configured to collect all the relationship candidates only after completing the placement. FilterLocatedCandidates is called for each relationship candidate after the placement of Node3 has been completed instead of after the mouse click.For a NodeEdge RGI the logic in FilterCandidates should be the same as in FilterLocatedCandidates.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  NodeEdge RGI BeforeUpdate  |   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  NodeEdge RGI BeforeEstablish  |  This call and the next call are made for the relationship between Node1 and Edge3. The ProcessingBreak parameter is True to indicate that this is part of the preparation for the break scenario.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  NodeEdge RGI AfterEstablish  |   |  
Step 2: Edge1 is broken and Edge2 is created.
The geometries are adjusted at the very beginning, the relationships of Edge1 and are copied to Edge2. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541)
Relationships:
Node1 – Edge1
Node2 – Edge1
Node3 – Edge1
Node1 – Edge2
Node2 – Edge2
Node3 – Edge2
No RGIs are called in this step.
Step 3: Relationships for Edge1 and Edge2 are resolved.
For the break to proceed, a relationship is established between Edge1 and Node3. ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262541)
Relationships:
Node1 – Edge1
Node3 – Edge1
Node2 – Edge2
Node3 – Edge2
The complementary relationship resolves the relationships created in Step 1 of the break processing. The processing in the table below is encapsulated in ProcessBreak method of the complementary relationship service. 
Since all relationships of Edge1 have been copied to Edge2, this step essentially means dropping surplus relationships. In this phase, there are two instances of the EdgeNode RGI: EdgeNode RGI 1 for Edge1 and EdgeNode RGI 2 for Edge2. The same calling sequence is executed for both RGIs. The calling sequences do not interleave; one starts after the other finishes. 
Processing Mode:  gtrgiBreak   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  EdgeNode RGIInitialize  |  The EdgeNode RGI is initialized.  |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  EdgeNode RGIBeforeUpdate  |   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  BeforeDelete  |  On EdgeNode RGI 1, this call would be made for deleting the relationship between Edge1 and Node2.  On EdgeNode RGI 2, this call would be made for deleting the relationship between Edge2 and Node1.   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  AfterDelete  |   |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  AfterUpdate  |   |  
Processing Mode: gtrgiEstablish 
The control is returned back to the relationship service where Node3 is the active feature.   
|  Called from  |  RGI Method  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  IRelationshipInterface_Update  |  NodeEdge RGIAfterUpdate  |   |

#### Interfaces Executed from Batch Executables
Four of the interface points in NetWorks Core have the potential to be executed in a context that does not involve the Designer/Analyst application: 
  * Functional interfaces
  * Relationship Attribute interfaces
  * Relationship Geometry interfaces
  * Attribute Edit Control interfaces


With the appropriate recordset edits, any of the first three interfaces can be launched from the Batch Validation and Job Life Cycle executables. Attribute Edit Control interfaces are not likely to execute, and there are limitations peculiar to the batch non-application context. 
In the context of the Designer/Analyst application, all interface points have access to the full suite of API available through the IGTApplication object and its related automation hierarchy. 
In batch non-application contexts, most of the IGTApplication object's API is not operational. Only its CreateService method succeeds. All other methods and properties raise errors or give undefined results, and none of the events fire. 
When writing these interfaces, you must ensure they function well in a desktop application context as well as in a batch non-application context. All the automation objects passed as properties or in methods on the interface are applicable. While they cannot navigate from IGTApplication to DataContext, they can access DataContext from their interface's property. The objects returned by CreateService are functional, although some of their methods may be hindered. For example, IGTHelperService can be created and operate correctly except for RunReport and RunPostProcess. These methods might work if the Report or PostProcess interface does not display a user interface, but their successful execution is not assured. 
Related Topic
[Custom Application Interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bDmUQoyc0wAd5lSldwnl8g)

#### Metadata for Custom Interfaces
Only the metadata for .NET custom interface implementations is stored in the database. The assemblies themselves are stored either in a shared location defined in the FileUNCPaths.xml file under the tags <CUSTOMIZATION> and <DOTNET> or to each local client machine. 
You can use Metadata Explorer to populate metadata tables required for the individual interfaces. You also use Metadata Explorer to [complete metadata configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LDawReDio_37hAl4p5itA) to use these interfaces, for example, linking the interface to a specific trace, attribute, or component, or refreshing the metadata before testing. Metadata Explorer provides the mechanism for defining new interfaces, for populating the metadata that associates these interfaces to particular interface points. For .NET assemblies, you Refresh Metadata Edits, then test the interface and publish the metadata when you are finished. 
Generally, the following metadata tables support custom interfaces:
G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND
The [G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TnT4ya5S9F75dJaSN86qXg) supports the command interface. This table contains most of the information necessary to define and support the use of custom commands in NetWorks Core. 
G3E_CONSTRUCTIONAID
The [G3E_CONSTRUCTIONAID table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OssNVZBN96cTTeDu5Cc_uw) supports the custom construction aid interface. This table contains most of the information necessary to define and support the use of custom construction aids in NetWorks Core. It contains information describing the custom and predefined construction aids. 
G3E_TEMPORARYGEOMETRYPLACEMENT
The [G3E_TEMPORARYGEOMETRYPLACEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/__D0mhsXjD55Yr6slEiMYg) table is used by the New Temporary Geometry command to retrieve the configuration of the Temporary Geometry shortcut bar and information necessary for placement of temporary geometry. 
G3E_GENERALPARAMETER
The [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) contains a parameter that allows custom commands to carry their own bitmaps for presentation on toolbar buttons. This table has an entry with a G3E_NAME="CustomCommandIconDRXFile" and a G3E_VALUE containing the file name of the DRX file that contains the custom icons for custom commands, much as custom bitmaps are made available for the New Feature control. 
In addition, two other parameters "CustomCommandAutoStartCCNO" and "CustomCommandAutoStartArgument" in this table give the user the ability to automatically start a custom command when a connection is made in the Designer/Analyst application.

That is, your custom help file must be in the same folder as the help file delivered with the NetWorks Core application. By default this is the C:\Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnology\Program\Resdlls\0009 folder. 
OR
On each client machine, copy your compiled custom help file onto the desktop.

#### Implementing a Custom Command

##### Command Termination
Normally, a modeless command terminates when you call the IGTCustomCommandHelper's Complete method to notify the command system in NetWorks Core that your command is finished. The command system then calls the custom command’s Terminate method. 
When the database connection is closed, or when the command project is reloaded due to a Metadata Refresh operation (function called from Metadata Explorer), the Terminate method of the IGTCustomCommandModeless object is called. All member data should be cleared, and any references to existing system objects should be disposed (that is, call the Dispose method, if supported) and set to null. 
In addition, the custom command may be asked to Terminate due to the selection of a new command that requires existing command operations to end. The CanTerminate method is called to determine if the modeless command is ready to terminate. Sometimes this means the command displays a dialog box and ask the user if they really want to end the command and lose any uncommitted work done so far, or if they want to ignore the request to start a conflicting command and return to working on this command. See the command-collision algorithm above.

#### Implementing Custom Command Objects
You define Custom Commands through Metadata Explorer and implement them by deriving your class from one of two abstract base classes: 
  * Derive your modal command class from the [GTCustomCommandModal](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Common_GTCustomCommandModal.htm) base class and override the Activate method. 
  * Derive your modeless command class from the [GTCustomCommandModeless](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Common_GTCustomCommandModeless.htm) base class and override the Activate and Terminate methods. Optionally, override the CanTerminate property and the Pause and Resume methods. 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120) To perform these steps, you must be connected to a database for which you have administrative privileges. 
To implement an interface using .NET, [click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120). 
This is an overview workflow for implementing a .NET custom extension in NetWorks Core. 
  * To implement a .NET custom extension:


  1. Produce a .NET custom extension type in a .NET custom extension assembly:
     * The .NET custom extension project must add a reference to the Intergraph.GTechnology.dll assembly located in the \GTechnology\Program folder. This assembly is not deployed in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC). The assembly contains the public namespaces Intergraph.CoordinateSystems, Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces, and Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * Inherit a .NET custom extension type from a NetWorks Core public interface defined in the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces. The .NET custom extension type can use .NET helper objects from the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * The .NET custom extension type should carefully consider the type of work performed and the access to feature data. On occasion, it is necessary to force system Garbage Corrector (GC) to reclaim unused memory. When the NetWorks Core session is terminated, the framework does the required cleaning. As part of the clean-up processing, the framework forces GC to run. However, if you manipulate a large number of ADO recordsets and/or a large number of NetWorks Core features, it is also appropriate to force GC to run in those .NET custom extensions. 
It is also an essential .NET coding practice to call the Dispose method, when available, and when you are done using those .NET objects. For example, call the IGTFeaturePlacementService.Dispose method when you are done using the .NET helper object from your .NET custom extension type. This is the proper garbage collection sequence: 
Call any Dispose methods on objects that you are using;
Release any objects that do not naturally fall out of scope
Call the garbage collection sequence noted here when you have processed a large number of ADO recordsets and/or IGTKeyObject. 
GC.Collect();
GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
GC.Collect();
     * ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120) There are some programming practices that must be followed in custom code: 
       * Only use local variables to store pointers to NetWorks Core windows. Never store them as global variables or even class variables. 
       * Never call methods that refresh the database while there are objects in the select set. These APIs (and maybe more) refresh the database: 
- GTJobManagementService.RefreshJobEnvironment
- GTTransactionManager.RefreshDatabaseChanges
- GTTransactionManager.Commit
- The methods on JobHelper that change the job context
       * Never change the job context when writing functional interfaces, especially validation interfaces. 
  2. Place the .NET custom extension assembly in the \GTechnology\Program folder for testing purposes. 
  3. Using Metadata Explorer, populate the required NetWorks Core interface point metadata to add the .NET custom extension, and refresh or publish metadata. 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Software Interfaces node and navigate to the appropriate .NET interface, for example, Compute Partial Start Length 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Populate the new row in the interface table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel: 
      1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the object.  
This name appears in the tree view. 
      2. In the G3E_INTERFACE field, type a name for the .NET assembly. The value in the G3E_INTERFACE field must be in the following format:  
AssemblyName:TypeName  
where 
AssemblyName is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension, and TypeName is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.   
|  Example GTDotNetSamples:Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample  AssemblyName is GTDotNetSamples. TypeName is Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample with namespace as Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples and classname as GTDisableEditToolSample.  |  
| --- |  
      3. Click OK. 
    4. To update existing arguments for your object:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Select the argument you want to update.
      3. Update the fields that are available for edit, and click somewhere else on the screen.
      4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120) to commit your edits to the database. 
      5. Repeat these steps for each argument.
    5. To add arguments to your interface:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257120), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
      3. In the argument table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel:
       * Type a number to indicate the order of the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL field.
       * Type a name for the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTNAME field.
       * Describe the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTDESCRIPTION field.
       * From the G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE drop-down list, select a data type.
       * Click OK. 
      1. Repeat Steps ii and iii for each argument you want to add.
    6. [Complete configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LDawReDio_37hAl4p5itA) of the new interface by associating it with a feature, component, attribute, and so forth so that a user can access it. 
  4. Test the .NET custom extension type by running a NetWorks Core command that exposes the interface point. If you are implementing a custom command, then you would invoke your custom command to test your code. 
  5. Publish and distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension assembly either to a shared location defined in the [FileUNCPaths.xml file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) under the <CUSTOMIZATION> and <DOTNET> tags or distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension to every local client machine. 
On the client machine, the .NET custom extension assembly should be either placed in the \GTechnology\Program folder or deployed into the GAC, so that users can access the assembly at runtime. 
The .NET custom extension assemblies can be deployed into the GAC by using Windows Explorer to drag assemblies into GAC, by using a Windows Installer package you have developed, or by using the developer GAC tool, Gacutil.exe, which is delivered with the .NET framework SDK. 


If a location is defined in FileUNCPaths.xml, and .NET custom extension assemblies exist on both local and remote machines, the local copy takes precedence.

#### Invoking a Custom Command
Custom commands are implementations derived from the [GTCustomCommandModal](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Common_GTCustomCommandModal.htm) or [GTCustomCommandModeless](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Common_GTCustomCommandModeless.htm) abstract base classes. As such, custom commands are defined in the [G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TnT4ya5S9F75dJaSN86qXg) metadata table and are loaded on demand by the NetWorks Core command and menu system. By default, all custom commands are available from the Tools tab in the Tools group under the Custom Command drop-down list. They are listed in the order specified in metadata (G3E_CCNO). Custom commands can still be moved by the user to any ribbon bar location, and these custom settings persist from session to session. 
Custom commands are enabled when the application’s conditions are appropriate for the command to function. The list of these conditions is the set of enabling conditions you specify when you define the command in Metadata Explorer. Typical enabling conditions include having an active job or a feature selected. 
When a user selects a custom command from the ribbon bar, the application creates the GTCustomCommandModal or GTCustomCommandModeless class associated to the ribbon bar entry and calls its Activate method. The response of the custom command depends on whether the implementation is modal or modeless. Modal commands complete their processing in the Activate method. Modeless commands are event driven from this point. 
Modeless commands give you an opportunity to receive mouse and keyboard events from a map window (IGTMapWindow). To receive mouse and keyboard events, store the IGTCustomCommandHelper parameter passed in the Activate method as a class member: 
_customCommandHelper = customCommandHelper;
Then subscribe to the any of the events provided by the IGTCustomCommandHelper interface:
_customCommandHelper.Click += OnCustomCommandHelperClick;   

After the Activate method exits, control is returned to the application, while the class waits on user input through mouse and keyboard events. 
You should unsubscribe from events in the command’s Terminate method:
_customCommandHelper.Click -= OnCustomCommandHelperClick;

#### Starting a Custom Command Using Metadata
After you have created a custom command using Metadata Explorer and the API, you can use two methods to automatically start it: 
  * Configure metadata to automatically execute a custom command when a user makes a connection to NetWorks Core. AutoStart is executed each time a work space is opened. 
  * Use [LaunchGIS.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k0ruVAfHLGEuk1Io57OHWw) to automatically execute a custom command within a NetWorks Core job. 


The custom command specified (either by the command line argument passed to LaunchGIS for AutoCustomCommand or the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_VALUE where G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME='CustomCommandAutoStartCCNO') is executed once all other processing to invoke NetWorks Core has been completed. This includes the setting of the active job and the attachment of the appropriate legend. 
  * To configure metadata to automatically start a custom command:


  1. Use Metadata Explorer to create the custom command.
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select Metadata Administration > General Parameters. 
  3. Edit the value in the [CustomCommandAutoStartCCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter to the CCNO value from the G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND table of the custom command you want to start automatically, 
  4. To pass a string value to the custom command, for example, an XML file name to draw a schematic, edit the [CustomCommandAutoStartArgument](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) general parameter. Type the actual string value you want to pass to the IGTApplication properties collection in the G3E_VALUE field.

### How to Use the API

#### Accessing Display Control Content
Display Control Nodes 
The [IGTDisplayService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDisplayService.htm) object provides methods for retrieving the contents of the Display Control as [IGTDisplayControlNode](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDisplayControlNode.htm). Each IGTDisplayControlNode represents a node in the Display Control tree view. The [NodeType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDisplayControlNode_NodeType.htm) property of IGTDisplayControlNode identifies the type of node. Custom software can use this information to isolate specific node types for processing. 
Example (C#): 
// Sample method. Get list of query display control nodes.
private IList<IGTDisplayControlNode> GetQueryDisplayControlNodes()
{
// Get display service
IGTDisplayService displayService = _application.ActiveMapWindow.DisplayService;
// Get all display control nodes
IGTDisplayControlNodes nodes = displayService.GetDisplayControlNodes();
// Create list of query nodes
IList<IGTDisplayControlNode> queryNodes = new List<IGTDisplayControlNode>();
foreach (IGTDisplayControlNode node in nodes)
{
if (node.NodeType == GTech.GTDisplayControlNodeTypeConstants.gtdctQuery) 
queryNodes.Add(node);
}
return queryNodes;
}
The [IGTAttachedFileDisplayControlNode](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTAttachedFileDisplayControlNode.htm) interface exposes file information, such as file name, file type, and display matrix for attached file display control nodes. These include raster image, MicroStation, CAD, and DDC files. Only nodes with a NodeType of gtdctImage, gtdctCAD, and gtdctDDC can be cast to this interface. 
Example (C#):
// Sample method. Process attached file display control node
private void ProcessAttachedFileNode(IGTDisplayControlNode node)
{
// Ensure specified node is an attached file node
IGTAttachedFileDisplayControlNode attachedFileNode 
= node as IGTAttachedFileDisplayControlNode;
if (attachedFileNode != null)
{
string fileName = attachedFileNode.FileName;
GTFileTypeConstants fileType = attachedFileNode.FileType;
LogFileInfo(fileName, fileType);
}
}
Legend Entries
The [IGTDisplayControlNode](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDisplayControlNode.htm) interface has a LegendEntry property which exposes an [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) object. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/540412) This object isn’t exposed for all display control nodes as some nodes are used for grouping. 
IGTLegendEntry exposes properties that describe its settings in the display control. This would include whether the entry is displayable or locatable. This interface also has an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) property which indicates the type of legend entry. Depending on its type a legend entry may implement additional interfaces which provide type specific legend setting information.   
|  Interface  |  Purpose  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  [IGTTranslucentLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTTranslucentLegendEntry.htm)  |  This interface derives from [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) and provides translucency override properties. Legend entry objects with an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) of gtletDDC, gtletImage, gtletImageMetadata, gtletMetadata, gtletQuery, gtletRedline, gtletSchematic, and gtletTemporaryGeometry implement this interface.   |  
|  [IGTOverridableLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTOverridableLegendEntry.htm)  |  This interface derives from [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) and provides symbology override properties such as color, fillcolor and width. Legend entry objects with an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) of gtletQuery, gtletRedline, and gtletSchematic implement this interface.   |  
|  [IGTImageLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTImageLegendEntry.htm)  |  This interface derives from [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) and provides a property for the binary raster color. It is implemented by legend entry objects with an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) of gtletImage and gtletImageMetadata.   |  
|  [IGTMetadataLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMetadataLegendEntry.htm)  |  This interface derives from [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) and provides properties for the upper and lower display scale extents of a legend entry. It is implemented by legend entry objects with an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) of gtletMetadata and gtletImageMetadata.   |  
|  [IGTQueryLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTQueryLegendEntry.htm)  |  This interface derives from [IGTLegendEntry](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry.htm) and provides properties for a query legend entry to indicate whether non-legend graphics or secondary graphics were excluded. It also exposes a recordset of feature instance identifiers for the query. It is implemented by legend entry objects with an [EntryType](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLegendEntry_EntryType.htm) of gtletQuery.   |  
Custom software can use this information to isolate specific legend entry types for processing. 
Example (C#):
// Sample method. Process legend entries.
private void ProcessLegendEntries(IGTDisplayControlNodes nodes)
{
// Iterate over display control nodes and process specific legend entries
foreach (IGTDisplayControlNode node in nodes)
{
if (node.LegendEntry != null)
{
switch (node.LegendEntry.EntryType)
{
case GTech.GTLegendEntryTypeConstants.gtletQuery:
ProcessQueryLegendEntry((IGTQueryLegendEntry)node.LegendEntry);
break;
case GTech.GTLegendEntryTypeConstants.gtletImage:
ProcessAttachedImageLegendEntry((IGTImageLegendEntry)node.LegendEntry);
break;
}
}
}
}

#### Accessing Feature Data
NetWorks Core requires a set of four keys be carried on every feature-component record: G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CNO, and G3E_CID. These keys uniquely identify an instance of a component of a feature. Support is provided for data retrieval using objects whose member data are based on these keys. 
Feature Data Objects
NetWorks Core provides the following feature data objects: 
  * IGTKeyObject and IGTKeyObjects 
The simplest object, [IGTKeyObject](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTKeyObject.htm) is the source of data for a single feature instance. IGTKeyObject carries the NetWorks Core keys, typically only G3E_FNO, and G3E_FID. 
The IGTKeyObject.Components property provides access to [ADODB.Recordsets](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp) for each component of the feature instance. 
The [IGTKeyObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTKeyObjects.htm) is a standard collection containing IGTKeyObject objects. 
  * IGTDDCKeyObject and IGTDDCKeyObjects 
The [IGTDDCKeyObject](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObject.htm) object provides access to the published data for a component, including the component view name, the geometry and published attributes of the component. IGTDDCKeyObject is the object returned when components are retrieved from the IGTSelectedObjects collection. The [IGTDDCKeyObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObjects.htm) object is a standard collection containing IGTDDCKeyObject objects 
Typically, this object carries the full set of NetWorks Core keys, thus representing the published data for a single component instance. 
The Recordset property contains the published attribution for the component view containing this component. The recordset is read-only, as it is built from the DDC files, not the database. The keys here can be used with the [IGTDataContext](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext.htm).OpenFeature call to retrieve a IGTKeyObject and provide read / write access to the component data for the feature instance. 
  * IGTComponent and IGTComponents 
A IGTKeyObject provides access to a collection of [IGTComponent](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTComponent.htm). The IGTComponent object provides access to the record information for a given component and contains properties for its geometry and name. 
Specifically, the IGTComponent object provides access to a disconnected [ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp) with the database information for the component instances associated to the component name and CNO. This ADO recordset is available from the Recordset property of the IGTComponent. Using the returned ADO recordset, rows can be added or deleted, and field values can be modified. Functional interfaces are fired as a result of manipulating these recordsets and any other client notification that lets the map window reflect changes to the component. 
[IGTComponents](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTComponents.htm) is a collection of IGTComponent objects, commonly all of the populated components for a given feature instance (FNO-FID). 


Querying the Database for Component Recordsets
A IGTKeyObject is obtained from the OpenFeature and NewFeature methods of the [IGTDataContext](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext.htm). If OpenFeature is used, NetWorks Core queries the database for a component recordset only when the Recordset property of the IGTComponent is retrieved. If the G3E_FNO and G3E_FID do not match for a specific component query, you get an empty recordset, not an error message, because the G3E_FID does not exist for that G3E_FNO. 
Accessing Select Sets
To manage and retrieve select sets, use [IGTSelectedObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSelectedObjects.htm). This object provides access to the system select set. User-located components can be retrieved here as IGTDDCKeyObjects. The IGTSelectedObjects object provides the ability add objects to the select set as well as to clear it.

#### Accessing Metadata
Metadata recordsets are retrieved from the NetWorks Core database using [IGTDataContext](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext.htm).MetadataRecordset with the metadata optimized table name as input. These recordsets are read-only.

#### Accessing Redline XML
Redline Service
The [IGTRedlineService](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTRedlineService.htm) object enables the retrieval of the XML representing map redlines and attached redlines. It is available on the [IGTMapWindow](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMapWindow.htm) and [IGTPlotMap](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTPlotMap.htm) interfaces using the [RedlineService](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/P_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMapWindow_RedlineService.htm) property. The [GetXML](its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/M_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTRedlineService_GetXML.htm) method of this service accepts a list of category names to include in the XML. This method also accepts a FilterMask which can be used to filter which redlines are returned in the XML. 
The GetXML method can also return XML for attached redlines from the Display Control. The specified category list must be null and the Display Status checkbox must be checked (On) for the attached redlines to be included in the returned XML. The FilterMask does not apply to attached redlines. 
Example (C#): 
// Sample method. Retrieve redline XML.
private void RedlineServiceSample()
{
// Get redline service from active map window.
IGTRedlineService redlineService = _application.ActiveMapWindow.RedlineService;
// Get XML for all redlines and categories (both map redlines and attached redlines)
string allRedlinesXML = redlineService.GetXML(null, GTRedlineFilter.NoFilter);
// Get XML with only the default category and selected map redlines
string selectedRedlinesXML = redlineService.GetXML("_Default", 
GTRedlineFilter.OnlySelected);
// Get XML for all persistable and plotable redlines and the default category
string allPandPRedlineXML = redlineService.GetXML(("_Default", 
GTRedlineFilter.OnlyPersistible | GTRedlineFilter.OnlyPlotable);
}

#### Accessing System Information and Services
The following objects provide access to system information and services: 
IGTApplication
  * [IGTApplication](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) is the top-level object in the automation model and is available automatically in all interface projects. 
  * IGTApplication represents a single instance of NetWorks Core and contains methods and properties to control the application through automation. 
  * IGTApplication provides information about, controls for, and/or access to the all of the following: 
    * Active database connection
    * Map windows
    * Preferences
    * Properties
    * Selected objects
    * Services
    * Units of measure
    * Measurement services and spatial math services
    * New map and detail windows
    * Arrangement and refreshing of windows
    * Status bar text, progress bar, and cursor states
    * Changes to preferences, selected objects, and the active job


In addition, IGTApplication broadcasts three events. See the section on system events below. 
IGTMapWindow and IGTMapWindows
The [IGTMapWindow](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMapWindow.htm) object, which represents a single window object containing a map view display, provides methods and properties to control and return information about the map window and its contents. 
The IGTMapWindow object is the source of mouse input for command writers, as are the IGTLocateService and the IGTDisplayService. The IGTLocateService performs locate operations (given a point, find all components with a distance of the point), and the IGTDisplayService provides the ability to add query results to the Display Control for visualization in the map window. 
Other functions include window manipulation methods, support for locating features, and converting coordinates from world to view and back. 
The IGTMapWindows object is a collection of the existing map windows. Plot windows are not in this collection. 
Service Objects
Service objects group together a set of related functions for a general functional area. Several service objects are retrieved through the IGTApplication.CreateService method. Some are properties of other automation objects. Service objects are intended to be created, used, and then discarded. They carry no persistent information. 
  * [IGTMeasureService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMeasureService.htm)
The GTMeasureService object provides the automation for calculating the area, length, and perimeter of a geometry object. Before performing the calculations, a coordinate system object, the reference space, and the geometry object for which the calculations are made must be specified. Referencing the applicable property or executing a method returns the measurements. 
The IGTMeasureService object is retrieved through a call to the IGTApplication.CreateService method. 
  * [IGTSpatialService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSpatialService.htm)
The IGTSpatialService object provides spatial filtering for an input recordset. The IGTSpatialService spatially filters DDC recordsets by applying one of several spatial operators to the recordset given an input geometry.   
|  Example Use the IGTSpatialService to filter recordsets of wooden poles to retrieve only those inside of an arbitrary polygon. The IGTSpatialService is retrieved through a call to the IGTApplication.CreateService method.   |  
| --- |  
  * [IGTHelperService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTHelperService.htm)
The GTHelperService object provides a miscellaneous group of functions, including the following methods: 
    * GeographicPointToStorage—Use to convert a point from geographic coordinates to storage coordinates. 
    * FindFile—Use to find files using the paths defined in the current FileUNCPaths file. 
    * GetComponentViewLabel—Use to get the label for a feature component. 
    * GetFeatureLabel—Use to get the label for a feature. 
    * RunReport—Use to run a metadata defined report given query results defined in a recordset. 
    * RunPostProcess—Use to run a metadata-defined query Post Processing interface. 
    * The GTHelperService is retrieved through a call to the IGTApplication.CreateService method. 
  * [IGTSnapService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSnapService.htm)
The IGTSnapService object provides the automation for snapping a point on or along a geometry object. The point that is snapped to can be constrained to snap to the ends, middle, or existing vertices on the geometry. 
The IGTSnapService is retrieved through a call to the IGTApplication.CreateService method. 
  * [IGTDisplayService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDisplayService.htm)
The IGTDisplayService object provides the ability to append to and remove queries and images from the Display Control. It is also used to retrieve the bounding range for the display item. 
The IGTDisplayService object is available as a property of the IGTMapWindow object.
  * [IGTLocateService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTLocateService.htm)
The IGTLocateService object contains methods for locating objects within a specified radius from a locate point. The locate operation can be restricted to a maximum number of candidates and can use the PickQuick dialog box for the selection of a subset of the located objects. The IGTLocateService object is available as a property of the IGTMapWindow object. 


Coordinate System Objects
Starting with the CoordSystemsMgr object, this hierarchy of objects provides access to all aspects of the coordinate system active in the work space. It also provides point transformation functions if given reference spaces to convert between. For more information, see the Intergraph.CoordSystems.chm delivered in the \CCS\bin\resdlls\0009 folder when you install the Hexagon Common Coordinate System (CCS) SDK. 
Preferences
The system maintains a list of user preferences and their values. These values are retrieved through the IGTApplication.GetPreference method. 
System Events
The [IGTApplication](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) object broadcasts three events for notification of changes to the system state. They can be received with the standard Dim WithEvents declaration. The events are as follows: 
  * PreferenceChanged
The PreferenceChanged event indicates that an addition, update, or removal of a name-value pair in the preference set has changed. The name of the preference, the new value and the action are passed as arguments to the event receiver. 
  * SelectedObjectsChanged
The SelectedObjectsChanged event indicates that the selected objects collection has been modified by the addition or removal of one or more components. 
  * ActiveJobChanged
The ActiveJobChanged event indicates that the Active job has changed. The new job identifier and the name of the configuration it belongs to are passed as arguments to the event receiver. 


Map Window Events
[IGTCustomCommandModeless](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Common_GTCustomCommandModeless.htm) interface projects can receive events from the active map window through the IGTCustomCommandHelper class, passed into the IGTCustomCommandModeless interface in the Activate method. These events are as follows:   
|  Activate  |  Deactivate  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Click  |  DblClick  |  
|  KeyDown  |  KeyPress  |  
|  GainedFocus  |  LostFocus  |  
|  MouseUp  |  MouseDown  |  
|  MouseMove  |  WheelRotate  |

#### Accessing the System Select Set
The following object provides access to the system select set: 
  * IGTSelectedObjects
[IGTSelectedObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSelectedObjects.htm) manages adding and removing feature components to the selected objects collection of the application. User-located components can be retrieved here as [IGTDDCKeyObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObjects.htm). The IGTSelectedObjects object provides the ability add objects to the select set and to clear it. 
If there is a transaction in progress, then this object disallows any changes to the select set.

#### Editing Feature Data
This is a typical workflow for editing a feature, given a located component in the select set. See [Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) for more information. 
  1. Retrieve the [IGTDDCKeyObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObjects.htm) collection from IGTApplication.[IGTSelectedObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSelectedObjects.htm). 
  2. Index to the particular [IGTDDCKeyObject](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObject.htm) from the collection. 
  3. If in a [Custom Command interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P8rvKiTKWta8s8WVd1XY3Q) or an [Import Feature interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/febj4h1vS8jhIYPWolfSyA), use IGTTransactionManager to begin a transaction. 
  4. Use [IGTApplication](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm).IGTDataContext.OpenFeature with this IGTDDCKeyObject to get a for the feature. 
  5. Perform any edits to the recordset.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262384) Edits made using[ IGTComponents](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTComponents.htm) do fire functional interfaces. 
  6. If in a Custom Command interface or an Import Feature interface:
    1. Use[ IGTTransactionManager ](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTTransactionManager.htm)to commit the transaction. The Commit method has an optional parameter to refresh job changes to the client. 
    2. Call Application.RefreshWindows to make sure the edits are properly visualized in all NetWorks Core windows. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262384) Edits made in the context of other interfaces, such as [custom application interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bDmUQoyc0wAd5lSldwnl8g), are already inside a NetWorks Core transaction and do not need the explicit begin and end transactions required for Custom Commands and Import Feature.

#### Enabling Miscellaneous Functions
The following objects enable such functions as controlling the display, selecting features, measuring, and processing geometry: See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
  * [IGTTransactionManager](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTTransactionManager.htm)
The IGTTransactionManager object manages database transactions. The IGTTransactionManager object's interface provides properties and methods to control database transactions. This is passed as part of a Custom Command interface and Import Feature interface. 
  * [IGTProperties](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTProperties.htm)
IGTProperties is a collection object that provides a convenient way of storing and retrieving global data. IGTProperties are not persisted when NetWorks Core exits. 
  * [IGTWorldRange](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTWorldRange.htm)
Returned from the GetRange method of a IGTMapWindow, the IGTWorldRange object stores the world coordinates of an area, which is defined by the lower left and upper right points of a rectangle. 
  * [IGTHighlightedObjects](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTHighlightedObjects.htm)
The IGTHighlightedObjects object collects IGTDDCKeyObject objects. This collection identifies features and components that are highlighted in the IGTMapWindow. 
  * [IGTSymbology](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSymbology.htm)
The IGTSymbology object defines symbology information that is used for displaying queries. The interface describes the visual graphic attributes of the text, symbols, areas and lines that are used to display a query.

#### Managing Queries
Queries can be composed and executed using the IGTDataContext.OpenRecordset method. The results of queries can also be added to the active display. 
These disconnected [ADODB.Recordsets](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp) can be edited and updated in the database. However, no client notification of these updates is done automatically, and no functional interfaces are fired as a result of these edits (use [IGTComponent](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTComponent.htm) to achieve this effect). Accordingly, the modified features are not reflect these edits until a user action resulting in an update of deltas—Broadcast Database changes, for example—is performed.

#### Manipulating Feature Geometry
Geometry is an explicit property of the [IGTDDCKeyObject](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDDCKeyObject.htm) and [IGTComponent](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTComponent.htm) objects. Geometry objects can be of several types, each with its own properties. Manipulations of these properties should be done in the same context as any component edit. 
You should assign the geometry object to a local variable of the appropriate type, perform the edits, then reset the Geometry property with the edited object. Geometry types include arcs, boundaries, composite polygons, composite polylines, line geometry, oriented points, points, polygon, polyline, raster, and text point. 
The update of the appropriate SDO_GEOMETRY columns in the database are taken care of for you when you commit the feature edits.

#### Performing Database Operations
The following object is the access point for all database operations for custom interfaces. See Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm for more information. 
  * IGTDataContext
The [IGTDataContext](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext.htm) object provides for executing SQL, opening recordsets, and accessing the active job, the active coordinate system, and metadata. 
The IGTDataContext.Execute method enables direct execution of SQL, while the UpdateBatch method commits the updates to an entire recordset. The IGTDataContext object is available from the IGTApplication object as well as IGTComponent. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262386) Recordsets opened with IGTDataContext.OpenFeature or NewFeature should not be processed with UpdateBatch. UpdateBatch can be used with recordsets retrieved through IGTDataContext.OpenRecordset, OpenRecordsetArray, Execute, or ExecuteArray.
