### Plotting API Examples

#### Paper Units of Measure in the Plotting API
Many properties and methods in the plotting API specify paper coordinates, paper units, or paper measurements. Unless stated otherwise, these values are all in units of 0.01 mm. Although these values are represented in the API as floating-point values, in many cases they may be rounded or truncated to a whole number of units of 0.01 mm. 
Custom software should not expect accuracy exceeding 0.01 mm. Also note that paper coordinates, or paper space, differs from world coordinates used in maps in that the y- coordinate in paper space increases downward—from the top of the page or display toward the bottom, and the y- coordinate in world coordinates increases upwards—from the bottom of the page or display toward the top.

#### Plotting API Example Removes Redlines Created by Insert Legend
|  Code Example Set oPlotWindow = Application.ActivePlotWindow  If Not oPlotWindow Is Nothing Then  Set oPlotRedlines = oPlotWindow.NamedPlot.GetRedlines(gtprcAll)  For I = oPlotRedlines.Count To 1 Step -1  Set oPlotRedline = oPlotRedlines(I)  If oPlotRedline.ObjectID = gtproInsertLegend Then oPlotRedline.Delete  End If  Next  Application.RefreshWindows  End If  |  
| --- |

#### Plotting API Example Removes Redlines
|  Code Example Set oPlotWindow = Application.ActivePlotWindow  If Not oPlotWindow Is Nothing Then  Set oPlotRedlines = oPlotWindow.NamedPlot.GetRedlines(gtprcAll)  For I = 1 To oPlotRedlines.Count  ' Since all redlines are being removed, index 1 can always be used.  Set oPlotRedline = oPlotRedlines(1)  oPlotRedline.Delete  Next  Application.RefreshWindows  End If  |  
| --- |

### Services

#### GTCUService Object

##### Implementing GTCUService Objects
The [GTCUService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTCUService.htm) object development environment lets you create custom commands and functional interfaces for filtering, selecting, and processing compatible units (CUs) by feature. 
CUs are feature attributes that describe the cost of an item or service. They are used by a work management system to determine the cost of fulfilling a work request. The GTCUService enables the managing and processing of CUs selected during the design of a work request. The object supports processing of both primary and ancillary CU data. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262412) CU processing applies only to data sets that have a work management system such as STORMS or Logica defined. 
This is a partial list of functionality you can provide through the GTCUService:
  * Return the description of a given CU.
  * Display the Compatible Unit Query dialog box to let the user interactively select CUs for one or more features. 
  * Add CUs to one or more features without going through the Compatible Unit Query dialog box. 
  * Replace an existing CU value with a new CU value.
  * Delete a specified CU.
  * Verify that the static attributes are consistent with the primary CUs of a given feature.
  * Display the Select CU Quantity dialog box. 
  * Display the Application Dependency Properties dialog box. 


  * To implement a GTCUService object:


  1. Enable Feature Explorer to allow a CU ID to be typed directly into the compatible unit attribute as follows: 
Modify the tab attribute metadata for the compatible unit and/or macro compatible unit attributes to make these attributes read-write. This metadata is defined in [G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_READONLY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DQvudRU4TKitmHAp03~qGQ). A value of 0 makes the attribute read-write. 
  2. Create the object by calling Application.CreateService(gtsvcCUService).


  * To use the GTCUService within a custom command:


  1. Identify a feature for CU processing.
  2. Invoke the .NET custom command to process CUs.
  3. Add a CU to the feature.
     * If the CU is a macro CU, it is expanded into multiple CU records or instances.
     * If the CU is a primary CU, processing of static attributes occurs.
     * Processing of application dependencies occurs.
OR 
Delete a CU from the feature.
     * If a macro CU, all CU instances associated with it are cleaned up.
     * Application dependenices associated with the CU are deleted.
OR 
Replace a CU on the feature.
     * If the existing CU is a macro CU, all CU instances associated with it are cleaned up. 
     * Application dependenices associated with the existing CU are deleted.
     * If the new CU is a macro CU, it is expanded into multiple CU records/instances.
     * If the new CU is a primary CU, processing of static attributes occurs.
     * Processing of application dependencies occurs for the new CU.
  4. Exit the custom command, saving the CU changes made to the feature.


  * To type a CU value into Feature Explorer:


  1. Identify a feature for CU processing.
  2. Invoke Edit Feature.
Feature Explorer displays in Edit mode. 
  3. Type a CU value for the Compatible Unit attribute displayed in Feature Explorer. 
     * If the CU is a macro CU, it is expanded into multiple CU records or instances.
     * If the CU is a primary CU, processing of static attributes occurs.
     * Processing of application dependencies occurs.
  4. Click Save Edits to save the changes made to the feature.

#### IGTFeaturePlacementService Object

##### Pole Run Placement Command (Sample)
The sample command in the \GTechnology\Services\Samples\GTCustomization\Commands\Modeless\PoleRunPlacement folder illustrates how to use [IGTFeaturePlacementService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTFeaturePlacementService.htm) to: 
  * Place a pole run.
  * Edit attribute values.


This command also illustrates how to use IGTDataContext to cache attribute values for attribute inheritance.   
|  The pole run consists of a series of alternating poles and conductors that are drawn within one transaction.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262415) The poles are coincident with the endpoints of the conductors, and the length of each conductor is limited to a maximum span width of 50 meters. The series starts and ends with a pole.  The first pole in the series is placed interactively. Once the first pole has been placed, placement of a conductor is started. The first point of the conductor is automatically derived from the location of the pole. All that remains to complete placement of the conductor is a click to locate its endpoint. The conductors within this pole run are limited to a maximum span width of 50 m. This is handled by the .NET placement technique defined for the conductors, where the maximum span width is determined by a placement technique argument. While drawing the conductors, the dynamics are truncated to the maximum span width defined. Once the endpoint of the conductor has been digitized, another pole is silently placed and located at the conductor's endpoint. This is accomplished with another .NET placement technique that silently places a point at the endpoint of a linear. Then placement of the next conductor begins at this pole. This sequence continues until the user double-clicks during the placement of a conductor to signal that the pole run is complete. A final pole is silently placed at the end of the last conductor to end the pole run. The pole run is drawn with a few simple clicks to locate the start point of the pole run and the endpoint of each conductor within the pole run.  When the pole run is started, the attribute dialogs for the first pole and the first conductor are displayed so that the user can set attribute values for each. These attribute values are saved and all remaining poles and conductors placed, as part of this pole run inherits their attribute values from these two initial features.   |  
| --- |  
Command Metadata
The command is a modeless .NET custom command classified as an Edit command.
Enabling conditions for the command are as follows:
  * An active job exists.
  * An active map window exists
  * An active work space is open.
  * A connection is open.
  * A new transaction is available.


No enabling conditions are leveraged against the select set.
Two special placement configurations are defined to allow the current pole or conductor to be placed relative to the previous pole or conductor. Placement configuration "Pole Run Conductor" is defined to place a conductor relative to a pole, and "Pole Run Pole" is defined to place a pole relative to a conductor. Each of these placement configurations contains an entry that defines an external relative component (a component that is not placed as part of the placement configuration). These entries are designated by a G3E_PLACECOMPONENT value of 0. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262415) The external relative component must have a lower G3E_ORDINAL value than the component that is placed relative to it. This allows the external relative component to show up as a candidate when defining the placement technique argument for the relative component. 
This is the basic definition of each placement configuration:
Pole Run Conductor  
|  Metadata Field  |  Values for Step 1  |  Values for Step 2  |  Values for Step 3  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  User name  |  Pole Run Conductor  |  Pole Run Conductor  |  Pole Run Conductor  |  
|  Feature  |  Pole  |  Conductor  |  Conductor  |  
|  Component  |  Pole  |  Conductor  |  Conductor Label  |  
|  Feature Index  |  1  |  1  |  1  |  
|  Placement Ordinal  |  1  |  2  |  3  |  
|  Placement Interface  |  InteractiveIPT  |  StartLinearAtPointIPT  |  OffsetPointSPT  |  
|  Relative Component  |  None  |  Pole in Step 1  |  Conductor in Step 2  |  
|  Required  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  
|  Place Component  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262415) The Conductor component (Step 2) is placed relative to the Pole component (Step 1). The Conductor Label component (Step 3) is placed relative to the Conductor component (Step 2). 
The Conductor and Conductor label components (Steps 2 and 3) are placed as part of this placement configuration, but the Pole component (Step 1) is not. This is determined by the value set for Place Component. 
Pole Run Pole  
|  Metadata Field  |  Values for Step 1  |  Values for Step 2  |  Values for Step 3  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  User name  |  Pole Run Pole  |  Pole Run Pole  |  Pole Run Pole  |  
|  Feature  |  Conductor  |  Pole  |  Pole  |  
|  Component  |  Conductor  |  Pole  |  Pole Label  |  
|  Feature Index  |  1  |  1  |  1  |  
|  Placement Ordinal  |  1  |  2  |  3  |  
|  Placement Interface  |  InteractiveIPT  |  StartAtEndPointOfLinearSPT  |  OffsetPointSPT  |  
|  Relative Component  |  None  |  Conductor in Step 1  |  Pole in Step 2  |  
|  Required  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  
|  Place Component  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262415) The Pole component (Step 2) is placed relative to the Conductor component (Step 1). The Pole Label component (Step 3) is placed relative to the Pole component (Step 2). 
The Pole and Pole label components (Steps 2 and 3) are placed as part of this placement configuration, but the Conductor component (Step 1) is not. This is determined by the value set for Place Component. 
Two special.NET placement techniques are also defined to place the poles and conductors relative to one another. The StartLinearAtPointIPT technique determines the first point of a conductor based on the last pole placed. The PointAtEndPointOfLinearSPT technique silently places a pole at the endpoint of the last conductor. No special concessions are needed in either technique to handle the external relative components defined for the pole run. External relative components are treated the same as internal relative components. The external relative components can be found in the GraphicComponents collection using the FNO/FIDX/CNO/Occurrence type specified in the relative component placement technique argument. Once found, its geometry can be accessed to determine the relative location of the new geometry. 
For attribute inheritance to occur, the specific attribute values to copy from one feature to another must be marked as such in metadata. Only those attributes whose G3E_COPY value is 1 are saved and copied to the next feature instance.

#### IGTGeometryCreationService Object

##### Arc Construction
[IGTGeometryCreationService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTGeometryCreationService.htm) enables the creation or appending of an arc in several ways: 
  * If the arc is constructed standalone or is the first subgeometry of the composite polyline or composite polygon, and the user workflow is to click the start, mid-, and endpoints, these three points can be appended to the geometry in the IGTGeometryCreationService using the AppendPoint method. Set ArcConstructionMode to True before appending the arc points. 
  * If the arc is constructed standalone or it is the first subgeometry of the composite polyline or composite polygon, and the user workflow is other than clicking start, mid, and endpoints—start point, endpoint, and origin, for example—then the .NET code must calculate the arc or use the Arc API. 
  * If the arc is the nth, but not the first, subgeometry of the composite polyline or polygon and the user workflow is to click mid- and endpoints (the start point is the same as the endpoint of the previous subgeometry in the composite polyline or polygon), these two points can be appended to the geometry in the IGTGeometryCreationService using the AppendPoint method. Set ArcConstructionMode to True before appending the two arc points. 
  * Once the resulting arc geometry has been determined, there are several options for appending it to IGTGeometryCreationService: 
    * For standalone arcs, call AddGeometry.
    * For composite polylines or polygons, call AppendGeometryToComposite.
    * Set ArcConstructionMode to True and then call AppendPoint for the start, mid, and endpoints of the calculated arc. 
  * If the arc is the nth (but not the first) subgeometry of the composite polyline or polygon and the user workflow is other than clicking start, mid-, and endpoints (for example, start point, endpoint and origin) then the .NET code must do the calculation of the arc or use the Arc API. Once the resulting arc geometry has been determined, there are several options for appending it to IGTGeometryCreationService: 
    * Call AppendGeometryToComposite. If the start point of the arc is the same as the current last point of the composite polyline or polygon, then the arc geometry is simply appended. If the points are different, the last point of the composite polyline or composite polygon is moved so that it is identical with the starting point of the arc being appended. 
    * Set ArcConstructionMode to True and then call AppendPoint for the mid and endpoints of the calculated arc. This assumes that the start point of the arc is the same as the current last point of the composite polyline or polygon.

##### Working with Indexes
The indexes returned by AddGeometry or CreateGeometry are used to reference the geometries in the methods manipulating these geometries, such as AppendPoint or RemoveLastPoint. The indexes are generated so that they use a contiguous range of integer values starting with 1. 
These indexes remain in sync with the geometries in IGTGeometryCreationService until one or more geometries are removed. Afterward, the geometries in IGTGeometryCreationService get reindexed to keep the range of indexes contiguous.   
|  Example If there are geometries with indexes 1, 2, and 3 in the IGTGeometryCreationService, and the geometry with index 2 is removed, the geometry that previously had the index 3 must be referenced with index 2 after the removal.   |  
| --- |  
The same logic applies also to indexes of holes in boundary geometries.

#### IGTJobManagementService Object

##### Populating a Recordset with Feature Keys (Example)
Some of the methods of [IGTJobManagementService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTJobManagementService.htm) require recordsets of feature keys as input. Some require a G3E_FID field and some require both G3E_FNO and G3E_FID keys. You can obtain these keys from a number of sources. The following.NET code is one example of how to create and populate the recordset of feature keys:   
|  Code Example private ADODB.Recordset CreateInMemoryADORS(IGTDDCKeyObjects DDCKeyObjects) { ADODB.Recordset shapeADORecordset = new ADODB.Recordset(); shapeADORecordset.Fields.Append("G3E_FNO", ADODB.DataTypeEnum.adInteger, 0, ADODB.FieldAttributeEnum.adFldFixed, null);  shapeADORecordset.Fields.Append("G3E_FID", ADODB.DataTypeEnum.adInteger, 0, ADODB.FieldAttributeEnum.adFldFixed, null);  shapeADORecordset.Open(System.Type.Missing, System.Type.Missing, ADODB.CursorTypeEnum.adOpenUnspecified, ADODB.LockTypeEnum.adLockUnspecified, 0);  foreach (IGTDDCKeyObject keyObject in DDCKeyObjects) { shapeADORecordset.AddNew(System.Type.Missing, System.Type.Missing); shapeADORecordset.Fields["G3E_FNO"].Value = keyObject.FNO; shapeADORecordset.Fields["G3E_FID"].Value = keyObject.FID; shapeADORecordset.Update(System.Type.Missing, System.Type.Missing); } return shapeADORecordset;  |  
| --- |

#### IGTMergeFeaturesService Object

##### Implementing a Custom Merge
When two geometries to be merged have a common endpoint, the Merge Features command merges components silently. This means the custom command has to adjust geometries so that they meet at the specified point. The [IGTMergeFeaturesService](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTMergeFeaturesService.htm) merges them without displaying the Merge Features dockable control since the merge mode is always the same. 
A IGTMergeFeaturesService object is created using CreateService method of the IGTApplication object. When calling this method, you must pass the reference to the IGTCustomCommandHelper object as the second parameter. This is necessary for IGTMergeFeaturesService to receive the mouse and keyboard events while the merge is in progress. 
The variable referencing the IGTMergeFeaturesService object has to be dimensioned WithEvents. 
Transaction Processing
The custom command must begin the database transaction before calling StartMerge. The custom command must also commit the transaction if the merge is successful (Finished event raised), or rollback the transaction if the merge is not successful (Aborted event raised). 
Mouse and Keyboard Event Processing
Although the IGTMergeFeaturesService receives mouse and keyboard events while in the process of merging, a custom command should not respond to any mouse or keyboard event while a merge is in progress. The IGTMergeFeaturesService listens for a double-click as a confirmation of the selected merge mode and merge option. IGTMergeFeaturesService also aborts the merge after the user has pressed ESC. 
Silent Merge
When two geometries to be merged have a common endpoint, IGTMergeFeaturesService merges these geometries at the common point without any user interaction. This means the Merge Features dockable control is not shown and the user is not required to confirm the merge. To implement a custom command that also merges geometries without common endpoints so that no user interaction takes place, the custom command must adjust geometries so that they have common endpoints before passing them to IGTMergeFeaturesService. 
IGTMergeFeatures Interfaces
You can customize a merge using an [IGTMergeFeatures](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_Interfaces_IGTMergeFeatures.htm) interface to merge the components. You could also implement such an interface to merge the cable geometries, depending on whether this merge mode is always required—that is, whether it should also occur in the Merge Features command and possibly in other custom commands. If so, you can use IGTMergeFeatures interfaces to implement the merge of cable geometries. Otherwise, the geometry merge needs to be implemented by the command. 
If you configure an IGTMergeFeature interface for a feature component, it is invoked from the custom commands, which use IGTMergeFeaturesService, and from the standard Merge Features command. Therefore, you should implement custom geometry merge using an IGTMergeFeature interface only if it is required in all merge workflows. Otherwise, the geometry merge needs to be implemented by a custom merge command.

## Embedding Manifest File to Custom Executable
The CPSDK is based on registry-free COM which requires the use of a manifest to allow executables to find the CPSDK files at runtime. Any custom executable which uses NetWorks Core Interfaces or references Common Coordinate Systems, Common Raster, or Common Math directly or indirectly should embed the manifest into the custom executable. 
Two files are delivered with the NetWorks Core Administrative Tools setup option to support this activity: 
  * CopyCPSDK.bat
    * Copies all CPSDK files from a NetWorks Core installation. 
    * The CopyCPSDK.bat file must be in the directory where the executable resides. Change the directory to this directory in CMD prompt when running the batch file CopyCPSDK.bat. 
    * This batch file is set up to copy from the NetWorks Core default installation directory: 
C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GTechnology\Program
If NetWorks Core is installed to a different directory, then the location in the batch file needs to be updated. 
  * GTechCPSDK.manifest
    * The manifest to be added to the custom executable. 


Visual Basic 6.0 Executables
If the custom code is written in Visual Basic 6.0 and the CPSDK is directly used, a special call must be made to create the CPSDK object. Call GTRegFreeCreateObject passing in the PROGID of the CPSDK objects to be created. 
  * To create the CPSDK object:


  1. Add declaration of GTRegFreeCreateObject to source file.
Private Declare Function GTRegFreeCreateObject Lib "GTActivateContext" (ByVal ProgID As String) As Object
  2. Create the object. 
Set m_obj = GTRegFreeCreateObject("<PROGID of object to create>")
Example: Creating Units of Measure object 
Set m_objUOM = GTRegFreeCreateObject("Intergraph.CCS.UnitsOfMeasure")


If using a language other than Visual Basic 6.0, then a similar worfklow is required. 
  * To embed the manifest file: 


  1. Run the Visual Studio command prompt in administrator mode. 
  2. Execute the command: 
mt.exe -manifest "<PATH TO MANIFEST FILE>\GTechCPSDK.manifest" -outputresource:<FULL PATH AND NAME OF EXECUTABLE>
mt.exe is used to embed the manifest file into custom executables that are delivered with Microsoft Windows Software Development Kit, which can be located under C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft SDKs\Windows\v7.1A\Bin.


These steps should create a new executable in the custom directory, and the custom software should work as it did before the upgrade. 
  * To copy CPSDK files:


  1. Open the command prompt in administrator mode.
  2. Change the directory to the location of the executable.
  3. Copy CopyCPSDK.bat from the NetWorks Core Program directory to the executable directory. 
  4. Run CopyCPSDK.bat.


All the CPSDK files are copied to the executable location so they can be found during the custom executable runtime.

## Further Information

### Code Access Security Policy Tool (Caspol.exe)
To give the client machine full access to all files under the network share (\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder), create a new child code group under the LocalIntranet_Zone code group by typing the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -ag LocalIntranet_Zone -url "\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*" FullTrust -n "CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName" 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/266205) CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName represents the child group name. This can be any name. 
To find that a custom assembly (\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\CustomAssembly.dll) belongs to what code groups, type the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -rsg
\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\CustomAssembly.dll 
Here is a partial output of the above command: 
1. All code: Nothing
1.2. Zone – Intranet: LocalIntranet
1.2.#. Url - \\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*: FullTrust 
Alternatively, you can create a new child group, CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName, under a different code group. For example, to create a new child group under the All_Code code group, type the following command line on a client machine: 
%windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework\<Framework Version Supported by G/Technology>\caspol -m -ag All_Code -url "\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder\\*" FullTrust -n "CustomAssemblyCodeGroupName" 
Edit the g3e.config file and add the tag <loadFromRemoteSources enabled="true" /> in g3e.config after </assemblybinding>:
![g3eexeconfig](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/266205)

### Example FileUNCPath
Example
<Customization>
<DotNet>
<Location Type="UNC">\\\DeploymentServer\DeploymentFolder</Location>
</DotNet>
</Customization>

### Implement a .NET Interface
To implement an interface using .NET, [click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265336). 
This is an overview workflow for implementing a .NET custom extension in NetWorks Core. 
  * To implement a .NET custom extension:


  1. Produce a .NET custom extension type in a .NET custom extension assembly:
     * The .NET custom extension project must add a reference to the Intergraph.GTechnology.dll assembly located in the \GTechnology\Program folder. This assembly is not deployed in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC). The assembly contains the public namespaces Intergraph.CoordinateSystems, Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces, and Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * Inherit a .NET custom extension type from a NetWorks Core public interface defined in the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.Interfaces. The .NET custom extension type can use .NET helper objects from the public namespace Intergraph.GTechnology.API. 
     * The .NET custom extension type should carefully consider the type of work performed and the access to feature data. On occasion, it is necessary to force system Garbage Corrector (GC) to reclaim unused memory. When the NetWorks Core session is terminated, the framework does the required cleaning. As part of the clean-up processing, the framework forces GC to run. However, if you manipulate a large number of ADO recordsets and/or a large number of NetWorks Core features, it is also appropriate to force GC to run in those .NET custom extensions. 
It is also an essential .NET coding practice to call the Dispose method, when available, and when you are done using those .NET objects. For example, call the IGTFeaturePlacementService.Dispose method when you are done using the .NET helper object from your .NET custom extension type. This is the proper garbage collection sequence: 
Call any Dispose methods on objects that you are using;
Release any objects that do not naturally fall out of scope
Call the garbage collection sequence noted here when you have processed a large number of ADO recordsets and/or IGTKeyObject. 
GC.Collect();
GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
GC.Collect();
     * ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265336) There are some programming practices that must be followed in custom code: 
       * Only use local variables to store pointers to NetWorks Core windows. Never store them as global variables or even class variables. 
       * Never call methods that refresh the database while there are objects in the select set. These APIs (and maybe more) refresh the database: 
- GTJobManagementService.RefreshJobEnvironment
- GTTransactionManager.RefreshDatabaseChanges
- GTTransactionManager.Commit
- The methods on JobHelper that change the job context
       * Never change the job context when writing functional interfaces, especially validation interfaces. 
  2. Place the .NET custom extension assembly in the \GTechnology\Program folder for testing purposes. 
  3. Using Metadata Explorer, populate the required NetWorks Core interface point metadata to add the .NET custom extension, and refresh or publish metadata. 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Software Interfaces node and navigate to the appropriate .NET interface, for example, Compute Partial Start Length 
    2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265336), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
    3. Populate the new row in the interface table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel: 
      1. In the G3E_USERNAME field, type a descriptive name for the object.  
This name appears in the tree view. 
      2. In the G3E_INTERFACE field, type a name for the .NET assembly. The value in the G3E_INTERFACE field must be in the following format:  
AssemblyName:TypeName  
where 
AssemblyName is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension, and TypeName is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.   
|  Example GTDotNetSamples:Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample  AssemblyName is GTDotNetSamples. TypeName is Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples.GTDisableEditToolSample with namespace as Intergraph.GTechnology.DotNetSamples and classname as GTDisableEditToolSample.  |  
| --- |  
      3. Click OK. 
    4. To update existing arguments for your object:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Select the argument you want to update.
      3. Update the fields that are available for edit, and click somewhere else on the screen.
      4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265336) to commit your edits to the database. 
      5. Repeat these steps for each argument.
    5. To add arguments to your interface:
      1. In the tree view under your new .NET interface, select the Arguments node.
      2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265336), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
      3. In the argument table that appears in the Metadata Explorer content panel:
       * Type a number to indicate the order of the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTORDINAL field.
       * Type a name for the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTNAME field.
       * Describe the argument in the G3E_ARGUMENTDESCRIPTION field.
       * From the G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE drop-down list, select a data type.
       * Click OK. 
      1. Repeat Steps ii and iii for each argument you want to add.
    6. [Complete configuration](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LDawReDio_37hAl4p5itA) of the new interface by associating it with a feature, component, attribute, and so forth so that a user can access it. 
  4. Test the .NET custom extension type by running a NetWorks Core command that exposes the interface point. If you are implementing a custom command, then you would invoke your custom command to test your code. 
  5. Publish and distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension assembly either to a shared location defined in the [FileUNCPaths.xml file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ) under the <CUSTOMIZATION> and <DOTNET> tags or distribute the metadata and .NET custom extension to every local client machine. 
On the client machine, the .NET custom extension assembly should be either placed in the \GTechnology\Program folder or deployed into the GAC, so that users can access the assembly at runtime. 
The .NET custom extension assemblies can be deployed into the GAC by using Windows Explorer to drag assemblies into GAC, by using a Windows Installer package you have developed, or by using the developer GAC tool, Gacutil.exe, which is delivered with the .NET framework SDK. 


If a location is defined in FileUNCPaths.xml, and .NET custom extension assemblies exist on both local and remote machines, the local copy takes precedence.

## Generic Work Management

### GTechHelper Object

#### Events

##### WorkspaceClosing Event
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
Raised by the GTechHelper object when the NetWorks Core Document.AboutToCloseDocument event is triggered in NetWorks Core. 
Syntax
Object_WorkspaceClosing()
Remarks
The Application property returns Nothing after this event is fired until another work space is opened. 
The WorkspaceClosing event occurs when the document or work space is about to close. This happens when GTechHelper.Quit or GTechHelper.CloseWorkspace are used, or if the user exits NetWorks Core manually with File > Exit. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256469) Users are expected to create New Work Spaces and Connections through GTechHelper methods, not directly through the GUI. Users should close NetWorks Core using GTechHelper.Quit, but they may also elect to close NetWorks Core from the GUI. 
The WorkspaceClosing event depends on the G3EListener.dll. If NetWorks Core is started before GTechHelper is created, G3EListener begins observing the document that is currently open in NetWorks Core. 
GTechHelper must be running for the G3EListener to work.

#### Methods

##### CloseWorkspace Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The CloseWorkspace method closes the specified workspace and, optionally, saves changes.
Syntax
Object.CloseWorkspace(SaveChanges, WorkspaceName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  SaveChanges  |  Boolean  |  Input  |  Required  |  Flag that indicates whether the workspace is saved.  |  
|  WorkspaceName  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  Name of the workspace used, if SaveChanges is True. WorkspaceName must be the full path; for example, D:/Dir/File.gfw.   |  
Remarks
Calling CloseWorkspace closes the document and any connections within that document, but NetWorks Core stays active and visible.

##### Connect Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The Connect method makes a connection to the specified configuration. If the username and password are not specified, the user’s operating system authentication login information is used. This method also sets the JobHelper.ConnectionObject property. 
Syntax
Object.Connect(ConnectionString, LegendName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ConnectionString  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  The string is as follows: Config=xxx;Username=yyy;Password=zzz; A semicolon is required after each element.  |  
|  LegendName  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  The name of a specific legend to be used. Default legend is used if none is specified.  |  
Remarks
The NewWorkspace method should be called before the Connect method to provide a document.
Calling the Connect method establishes the connection to the specified configuration. If this is the first connection, it is also set as the CurrentConnection. 
The Connect method also makes the application visible. Since the Connect method uses a specified legend or default legend, it does not work without an existing document.

##### NewWorkspace Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The NewWorkspace method starts NetWorks Core if it is not running and then creates a new workspace. Optionally, this method makes a connection to the specified data source if connection information is stored in the template. 
Syntax
Object.NewWorkspace(TemplateName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  TemplateName  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  The name of the template workspace. If omitted, the default NetWorks Core template, GTechnology.gft, is used.   |  
Remarks
If NetWorks Core is running when this method is called, the current workspace is closed without being saved and a new workspace is opened. NetWorks Core is not made visible by this method.

##### OpenRecordset Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The OpenRecordset method executes the query specified by the input argument. This method works without jobs in the job list and without an active job. The results of the query are returned. 
Syntax
Set ADODB.Recordset = Object.OpenRecordset(sSQLString) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  SQLString  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  The SELECT statement to process   |  
Return Type
[ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp)
Remarks
Calling OpenRecordset passes the SQLstring directly to the data server. No interpretation of the query is performed.

##### OpenWorkspace Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The OpenWorkspace method starts NetWorks Core if it is not running, and then opens the specified work space using the specified login information. If login information is not specified, prompts user for a username and password. 
Syntax
Object.OpenWorkspace(WorkspaceName, Username, Password, ConfigName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  WorkspaceName  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  The full path of the work space to open  |  
|  Username  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  The username for logging into the specified configuration  |  
|  Password  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  The password for logging into the specified configuration  |  
|  ConfigName  |  String  |  Input  |  Optional  |  The configuration name  |  
Remarks
If OpenWorkspace finds an instance of NetWorks Core is already running, it uses that instance to open the specified work space. If there is not a currently running instance of NetWorks Core, a new instance is created and used to open the work space. Only one NetWorks Core process runs at a time. GTechHelper does not start multiple GTech processes. 
If NetWorks Core is running, the current document is closed without saving and the specified document is opened. Calling the OpenWorkspace method starts NetWorks Core, if it is not already started, in the visible mode. The environment is restored from the work space. If the credentials of the user are passed in, the login dialog is not displayed.

##### SelectData Method
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The SelectData method sets the properties of the active map window as specified by the input arguments. The method also adds the items in the recordset to the select set. Based on the window properties, the data are fit in the active map. The SelectData method adds all of the components associated with the specified features to the select set. The select set is cleared based on the ClearSelectSet parameter. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256534) SelectData accepts an [ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp) as input. This recordset must contain the G3E keys G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CID, and G3E_CNO. 
Syntax
Object.SelectData(DataKeys, WindowBehavior, Percent, ClearSelectSet) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  DataKeys  |  ADODB.Recordset  |  Input  |  Required  |  The recordset of keys of the features to add to the select set. The recordset is assumed to be from the CurrentConnection. This information is needed to populate the NetWorks Core select set recordset.   |  
|  WindowBehavior  |  Integer  |  Input  |  Required  |  Indicates fit at current scale, center, or to fit and zoom to some percent 1 - Fit at current scale  
2 - Center  
3 - Fit and zoom at the percent specificed by the dPercent parameter   |  
|  Percent  |  Double  |  Input  |  Optional  |  If the WindowBehavior is zoom to a scale, Percent is the fraction to zoom out. If NetWorks Core shows 105%, this argument would be 1.05. Percent defaults to 300% (3.00), if not specified, but needed based on WindowBehavior.   |  
|  ClearSelectSet  |  Boolean  |  Input  |  Optional  |  Indicator that determines if the select set should first be cleared. The default is True.   |  
Remarks
Calling SelectData adds the features represented by the input recordset of keys to the NetWorks Core select set. This method fails if a connection is not associated with the CurrentConnection.

[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)

##### Application Property
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The Application property returns a [IGTApplication](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) object. 
Data Type
Read-only IGTApplication
Remarks  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256464) Before [GTechHelper.CloseWorkspace](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jhcRAOpcIYveESsvJtGvvQ) is called, all references to objects obtained through the IGTApplication object, such as IGTMapWindow, must be released.   |

This property is available only when there is an open NetWorks Core work space. When the work space is closed, any cached pointer to the IGTApplication object becomes invalid. 
For notification of when any cached IGTApplication pointer should not be used, users of the GTechHelper object can listen for the [WorkspaceClosing event](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TxtYhQvRH2RylNlvqnxHsw). 
This property returns Nothing when there is no open work space.

##### CurrentConnection Property
Applies To
[GTechHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jazgDO0GJhFlMTLKLweeAA)
Description
The CurrentConnection property returns or sets an internal variable that records the connection for all subsequent job and data requests. This property lets the user designate or determine the active connection, if there are several connections. 
Data Type
Read-write String
The connection name. This is the value in [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_LOCATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw). 
Remarks
Calling CurrentConnection simplifies subsequent API calls, since job and data requests use this connection. By default, when there is only one connection, it is the current connection. Setting the current connection is not associated with jobs or an active job.

##### DiscardFeatureEdits
Applies To
JobHelper Object 
Description
The DiscardFeatureEdits method calls the database procedure that discards all edits to a feature or set of features within the active job by removing: 
  * All rows in the [LTT_UNDO_LOG table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5KYguO2vvWlHTncvoBdRJw)
  * All edits from the B$ tables for the feature or set of features 


Syntax
Object.DiscardFeatureEdits(Features)
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Features  |  Recordset  |  Input  |  Required  |  Defines the feature or features to have their edits discarded.  See [Populating a Recordset with Feature Keys](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/UdkIeuL4s1_~FZ3ggPZQXg).  The input recordset must contain a populated G3E_FID field.  |  
Remarks
All edits to the features in the collection are discarded, regardless of the number of transactions in which the features participate. 
Because discarding feature edits could affect the outcome of a running edit operation, features may only be discarded when the client is not running a transaction. An error is raised if a transaction is active when this method is called. 
To refresh the job environment after DiscardFeatureEdits has been called, use RefreshJobEnvironment.

##### DiscardJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The DiscardJob method discards all edits associated with the job currently being edited.
Syntax
Object.DiscardJob()
Remarks
Calling DiscardJob clears the proposed data model changes for this job.

##### EditJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The EditJob method begins an edit session for the specified job.
Syntax
Object.EditJob(JobName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  JobName  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  The name of the job to edit.  |  
Remarks
This method adds the job to the connection, if it is not already the only one in the list, and makes it active for editing. If there are already jobs in the list, they are released. 
While multiple connections are possible, only one job can be attached to a connection. In other words, there can be only one attached connection when editing a job. 
The EditJob method is analogous to the Make Active operation in the job-management commands and the ltt_user.editjob database procedure.

##### EndEditJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)

##### FindConflicts Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The FindConflicts method returns a list of feature keys for job data that conflicts with master data. This method compares the job currently being edited against the master database and reports, at the table level, where conflicts exist. It does not report the specific conflict. 
Syntax
Set ADODB.Recordset = Object.FindConflicts
Return Type
[ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp)
Remarks
FindConflicts uses the database procedure to find the conflicts. It creates a recordset against the table populated by the procedure. FindConflicts works only if there is a job in Edit mode as, for example, when EditJob has been previously called. 
The output ADODB.Recordset includes the feature keys, the name of the table, the descriptive name of the feature, and the LTT status (edit, add, delete). The recordset returned is ordered by G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_cid, and G3E_CNO.

##### FindPendingEdits Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The FindPendingEdits method returns a set of keys for all the components that currently have proposed additions, modifications, or deletions. The method also exposes the LTT_STATUS field. This method works on the job currently being edited. 
Syntax
Set ADODB.Recordset = Object.FindPendingEdits
Return Type
[ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp)
Remarks
Calling the FindPendingEdits method lets the application determine if there is pending work associated with the job. The following recordset fields are returned: 
  * Keys
  * Base table name
  * A descriptive name
  * The type of edit (add/edit/delete)


The recordset returned is ordered by G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CID, and G3E_CNO.

##### PartialPost Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The PartialPost method posts the information for the specified features as it exists in the active job. The commit and rollback transactions are handled by the custom command, not by this method. That is, you are responsible for adding the commit and rollback in your code. 
Syntax
Object.PartialPost(Features) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Features  |  [ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp)  |  Input  |  Required  |  Specifies the features to be posted.  |  
Return Type
Integer
Remarks
The specified features are posted unless the G3E_POST field of the G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE is set to 0. 
State transitioning depends on the configuration of the [Job Life Cycle metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg). Set the G3E_TRANSITION field to 1 for the GENERIC PARTIAL POST entry in the G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE metadata table to enable state transitions during the post. 
Feature deletion depends on the configuration of the [Life Cycle metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_8zjvUTXpqWJGXxKtqBFw). Set the G3E_DELETE field to 1 in the G3E_LIFECYCLE metadata table to have the features deleted when they are transitioned to the state as part of the post. 
This method returns an integer value that describes the type of work that it actually performed:   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  PartialPost was successful  |  
|  1  |  PartialPost was not attempted because there were no pending edits for the active job.  |  
|  2  |  PartialPost was not attempted because the job life cycle metadata was not configured to allow for the PartialPost.   |

##### Post Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The Post method posts the edits made in the active job. The commit and rollback transactions are handled by the custom command, not by this method. That is, you are responsible for adding the commit and rollback in your code. 
Syntax
Object.Post()
Return Type
Integer
Remarks
The features in the job are posted unless the G3E_POST field of the G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE is set to 0. 
State transitioning depends on the configuration of the [Job Life Cycle metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg). Set the G3E_TRANSITION field to 1 for the GENERIC POST entry in the G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE metadata table to enable state transitions during the post. 
Feature deletion depends on the configuration of the [Life Cycle metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_8zjvUTXpqWJGXxKtqBFw). Set the G3E_DELETE field to 1 in the G3E_LIFECYCLE metadata table to have the features deleted when they are transitioned to the state as part of the post. 
This method returns an integer value that describes the type of work that it actually performed:   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Post was successful  |  
|  1  |  Post was not attempted because there were no pending edits for the active job  |  
|  2  |  Post was not attempted because the job life cycle metadata was not configured to allow for the post.   |

##### PostJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The PostJob method implements the default WMS post.
Syntax
Object.PostJob()
Remarks
Posting, state transitioning, and feature deletion are executed by this method if metadata is so configured. See the [Post method](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4tSJCp14jbV3PEV8SHXVgQ) for a description of the metadata that controls this behavior.

##### ValidateJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The ValidateJob method returns the results of the validation process (model validation pipe) on the job being edited. No validation priority filtering is done; so all validation errors are returned. 
Syntax
Object.ValidateJob()
Remarks
ValidateJob returns an [ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp) of the feature keys and the error description and priority. The recordset may be empty if there are no validation errors. Calling ValidateJob fails if there is no job currently being edited.

##### ViewJob Method
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The ViewJob method presents the data edits associated with the specified job for viewing.
Syntax
Object.ViewJob(JobName) 
Parameters  
|  Parameter  |  Data Type  |  I/O  |  R/O  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  JobName  |  String  |  Input  |  Required  |  The name of the job to view  |  
Remarks
Calling ViewJob is the same as adding a job in the job environment or using the ltt_user.viewjob procedure. This method may be called repeatedly to view multiple jobs.

#### Properties

##### ActiveJob Property
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The ActiveJob property returns as a string the name of the active job. The active job is the job currently being edited. 
Data Type
Read-only String
Remarks
A connection must be present for this property to work. If no job is active, the null string ("") is returned.

##### ConnectionObject Property
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The ConnectionObject property returns a reference to the NetWorks Core Connection object. 
Data Type
read-write Connection
Remarks
This object reference is assigned when the Connect method is called on either the JobHelper object or the GTechHelper object.

##### DataContext Property
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The DataContext property provides the IGTJobManagementService the IGTDataContext object for use in processing. 
Data Type
Read-write [IGTDataContext ](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTDataContext.htm)

##### JobList Property
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The JobList property returns a variant array of viewed job names on the connection.
Data Type
Read-only variant containing an array of strings
Remarks
A connection must be present for this property to work. The list of viewed jobs includes the active job.

##### PostErrors Property
Applies To
[JobHelper Object](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~gIOZn6EY0foW6awEzBKbg)
Description
The PostErrors property contains information about conflicts or validation errors that are determined during a call to the [Post](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4tSJCp14jbV3PEV8SHXVgQ) or [PartialPost](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mM329nu7N6GK8YXLSpw67w) method. If either method raises an error, then this property may be evaluated to determine what the errors were. 
Data Type
Read-only [ADODB.Recordset](http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/default.asp?url=/library/en-us/ado270/htm/mdobjodbrec.asp)
Remarks
If the Post or PartialPost methods raise G3E_E_JOBCONFLICTDETECTIONFAILED, then this is an error from conflict detection, and the PostErrors recordset contains the contents of the CONFLICTS table for the active job. 
If the Post or PartialPost methods raise G3E_E_VALIDATE_ERRORS, then this is an error from validation, and the PostErrors recordset contains information about the errors as described in the [Validating Job Edits help topic](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3OxdQ7_DWQa~vV8En6VvMw).

## Managing a Development Environment

### Change Process Procedure

#### Project Tracking Spreadsheet Example
The following is an example spreadsheet used to track important information as you customize and update your database. In this example, a new spreadsheet is used for each round of customization so that you know exactly what changes are included in a particular delivery. The spreadsheet is also a mechanism for communicating the order in which changes should be applied to the production database and other pertinent implementation information. 
A sample spreadsheet called ProjectName_log.xls is delivered in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries folder. Name the spreadsheet to reflect the project you are working on.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  File Name  |  Name of the file that produces the database or software change or update  |  
|  File Date  |  The date the file is created or entered into the spreadsheet  |  
|  TR/ECR  |  The number you get from your change tracking management system. Represents the change being made.   |  
|  Tables  |  Metadata tables affected by the change  |  
|  Description  |  Information about the change and important information concerning how to apply the change to a database   |  
|  Developer  |  Name of the developer who made the change  |  
|  Development DB  |  Name of the developer who made the change, and the date the change was incorporated into the development environment   |  
|  Test DB  |  Name of the database administrator who ran the script or added and/or updated the program into the Test DB and the date the change was made   |  
|  TRDB Set to Fixed  |  Name of the person who updated the change tracking management system and the date it was done   |  
|  Delivered to Users  |  The date this change was delivered to users  |

### Project Life Cycle Process
Every software development project goes through a life cycle before delivering the software to users. The following diagram shows the life cycle phases and the project delivery, which includes the NetWorks Core application and any customization changes made by on-site developers: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/9g9Bj6qE5lHTRBx9a6O9eQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=cf8049cfd650b35c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  * Development environment—This is where the on-site developer experiments with changes ranging from simple metadata edits to creating new commands. It is typically an unmanaged environment. 
  * Test environment—When the on-site developer has completed updating the software, it is migrated to the test environment. Because this environment is critical to the success of your software version delivery, it is carefully managed. 
  * Production environment—This is the environment in which users work each day. Because erroneous changes to the production environment can lead to downtime for clients, it is carefully managed.

## NetViewer and Field Review Customization

### Customizing from Outside the Viewer Applications
You can embed a NetWorks Core map to drive some part of the viewer functionality from inside another application. Typically, requirements for wrappering the viewer application are resolved by [IngrViewer.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V1YO_h7kpbe86gixw6SMRw) and [CAB module customization](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ODGGtoHCg5Adf9iv853v3Q) capabilities. 
If you cannot meet your customization requirements by adding CAB modules within the [IngrViewer.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V1YO_h7kpbe86gixw6SMRw) framework and your custom application is a .NET WinForms or IE browser based Web application, you can use the [oneViewerCtl](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Viewer.API.Reference.chm::/html/N_Intergraph_Controls_oneViewer.htm) to access NetWorks Core map functionality. The oneViewerCtl control can run disconnected or connected and makes all of the Net Page Extension API and events available in both modes of operation. 
If you cannot meet your customization requirements by adding CAB modules within the IngrViewer.exe framework and your custom application is VB 6.0 or C++ 6.0, you can use MobileViewerActiveXCtl.ocx located in the \GTechnology\Program folder for disconnected mobile applications or a combination of the Internet Explorer browser and the NetViewer [DOM](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/URuYQivKns2ufSBq5VmzDw) objects for connected viewer applications.

### Customizing Viewer Applications Using Smart Client Technology

#### CAB Custom Samples
NetWorks Core delivers several samples you can use to get started creating your own customized CAB solutions. The samples are delivered in the \GTechnology\Program\Samples\CAB folder. A Readme.txt file delivered in each folder gives instructions on how to use the sample, and more detailed instructions are included in the comments of the sample code. The following is a list of the samples and a brief description of what each one does: 
  * OptionsWPFSample
This sample loads a WPF SmartPart into the left deck work space. The SmartPart shows a couple of drop-down lists for setting the color of the map background and the selected feature color. Changing the colors calls the appropriate public APIs to update the map with the new color choices. 
  * MenuToolStripSample
This sample demonstrates how to customize menustrips and toolstrips in the common viewer architecture. In the Microsoft Composite UI Application Block (CAB) architecture, modules can add additional menu strip items and toolstrip items to named UIExtenstionSites during the ModuleController class' initialization. 
  * SimpleMapExtensionModule
This sample demonstrates how an add-on CAB module can extend the functionality of the Hexagon viewer products. It is also a simple example of the Smart Client Software Factory's Model-View-Presenter design pattern (see an explanation in SampleViewPresenter.cs). 
  * WPFPrintingSample
This sample demonstrates how an add-on CAB module can use Windows Presentation Foundation GUI in a SmartPart to extend the functionality of the Hexagon viewer products. You can customize this sample to: 
    * Enable printing maps using WPF XAML print templates.
    * Obtain a high resolution map image using the Hexagon viewer product's SaveAsPNG API of IMapViewService interface.

#### CAB Development Environment
The [sample projects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vd1nG0lVClH5dMYkqxMJgA) delivered in \GTechnology\Program\Samples\CAB are Visual Studio solutions written in C# and using the following: 
  * .NET Framework 4.5
  * Smart Client Software Factory (SCSF), version 3.0
  * Enterprise Library 5.0
  * Composite UI Application Blocks


Visual Studio 2012 and the above class libraries are prerequisites for writing custom CAB modules. Everything is freely downloadable except for Visual Studio 2012, which you must purchase. Smart Client Software Factory 2010 in MSDN explains the system requirements and source code requirements for installation. After downloading the source code, you must recompile in VS2012 targeting the .NET 4.5 Framework to make it compatible with NetWorks Core. There is extensive online documentation for writing CAB business modules in general, but, you also need to know how to integrate your custom logic with the NetWorks Core viewers. 
Upgrade the Development Environment
If you have previously developed custom CAB solutions, you need to upgrade your development environment. The upgrade instructions for SCSF 3.0 require that any of the previous software related to version 2.0 be removed from your system before running the installation utility for SCSF 3.0. It is very important to uninstall the pieces of the old version in exactly the reverse order of how they were installed; otherwise, your system is left in an inappropriate state. The old software components include the CAB, Enterprise Library 2.0, Guidance Automation Toolkit, Guidance Automation Extensions, and Smart Client Software Factory 2.0. See SCSF 2.0 online instructions for removal of 1.0. The installation instructions help you to install all the new dependency layers in the correct order. Even though the installation mentions .NET 3.5, you need to have .NET 4.5 on your system to upgrade the assemblies. 
You are not required to install the complete development environment, and if you have any of the common Viewer products installed on your system, you can begin developing CAB modules add-ons by copying one of the CAB sample projects and modifying it. However, installing all the development pieces provides a richer CAB module development experience. SCSF 2010 is the last version of the Smart Client Software Factory, but you can make your own enhancements with the source code. There are many samples and reference project implementations that can be studied. 
Runtime Libraries
The NetWorks Core Setup deploys the following set of runtime assemblies from the Microsoft Patterns and Practices group: 
  * Microsoft.Practices.CompositeUI.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.CompositeUI.WinForms.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.CompositeUI.WPF.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Caching.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Common.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Data.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Data.SqlCe.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.ExceptionHandling.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.ExceptionHandling.Logging.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Logging.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Security.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.ObjectBuilder.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.SmartClient.ConnectionMonitor.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.SmartClient.DisconnectedAgent.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.SmartClient.EndpointCatalog.dll
  * Microsoft.Practices.SmartClient.EnterpriseLibrary.dll


These are selected modules for the Composite UI Application Blocks, the Smart Client Software Factory 3.0, and the Enterprise 5.0 libraries. They are included in the runtime deployment so that custom modules can use them.

#### Developing, Testing, and Deploying a Custom CAB Module
This workflow assumes that you have installed and configured NetWorks Core and the viewer applications and have published one or more subsets of your data. It also assumes that you have installed all of the [software and libraries](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ODGGtoHCg5Adf9iv853v3Q) required to develop CAB modules: 
  * To develop, test, and deploy a custom CAB module:


  1. Install Field ReviewNetWorks Core Setup. 
  2. Build your output target, a custom CAB module, by either [modifying one of the CAB samples](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vd1nG0lVClH5dMYkqxMJgA) delivered with Field ReviewNetViewer, or [creating your own](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4X5sl9cbRV_Ue5gkNyMfxQ). The modules are .NET binary assembly DLLs. 
The CAB samples are delivered in the \GTechnology\Program\Samples\CAB folder. A Readme.txt file in each sample folder helps you to create a custom module. 
  3. Deploying your custom module for testing or for users is a two-step process. You have to make Field Review
    1. Make Field Review aware of your module (include the custom module) 
      1. Add a new ModuleInfo section for your custom CAB module assembly to the [ProfileCatalog.xml](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/umJHcX2YArQSU69tvO2Ccg) in the Field Review \Program folder. The AssemblyFile path can point to anywhere on disk (that is, the location of your module is not restricted to the Field Review product tree). 
      2. Register your custom module under the Plug-Ins key in the [CAB Module registry](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262685).   
|   |  
| --- |

#### ProfileCatalog.xml

##### Example ProfileCatalog.xml File
The following is an example of the ProfileCatalog.xml file. Comments are embedded in the code. 
In this example, a test module called APITesterModule.dll has been added to the Field Review \Program folder. The ProfileCatalog.xml has been modified so that when the command line /application argument is set to either APITesterConnected or APITesterDisconnected, only the GTMap.dll and APITesterModule.dll modules are included in the solution.   
|  Code Example <SolutionProfile xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/pag/cab-profile/2.0"> <Section Name="Layout"> <Modules></Modules> </Section> <Section Name="Services"> <Dependencies> <Dependency Name="Layout" /> </Dependencies> <Modules> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="Infrastructure.Module.dll" /> </Modules> </Section> <Section Name="Apps"> <Dependencies> <Dependency Name="Layout" /> <Dependency Name="Services" /> </Dependencies> <Modules> <!-- Reference all modules registered under Inservice key --> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="Inservice" /> <!-- Reference GTMap.dll assembly in executable directory  And set the list of applications. This entry will override the GTechnology\GTMap information in the registry. --> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="GTMap.dll" > <Applications> <Application Name="MobileViewer"/> <Application Name="NetViewer"/> <Application Name="SampleApplication"/> <Application Name="APITesterConnected"/> <Application Name="APITesterDisconnected"/> </Applications> </ModuleInfo> <!-- Reference all modules registered under Plug-Ins key --> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="Plug-Ins" /> <!-- Reference all modules registered under Samples key --> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="Samples" /> <!-- Reference the APITesterModule.dll assembly in executable dir. --> <ModuleInfo AssemblyFile="APITesterModule.dll" > <Applications> <Application Name="APITesterConnected"/> <Application Name="APITesterDisconnected"/> </Applications> </ModuleInfo> </Modules> </Section> </SolutionProfile>  |

### Customizing Web-Based Viewer Applications

#### Custom Tools

##### Adding Custom Analysis Functions

###### Find Feature by Attribute Metadata
The following metadata is required to expose Find Feature by Attribute in NetViewer: 
  * [G3E_NETCLASSES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MWQ8JnP~eAz5sVyDgqfuAA)
Add a row to this table to define a class of analysis commands that includes this find. 
  * [G3E_NETPAGES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U_jTtX9ywikMmvnfKR~U_w)
    * Add a row to this table for each Find Feature by Attribute. 
    * The G3E_OPTIMIZED_TABLE column must contain G3E_FINDMETHOD_OPTABLE.
    * The G3E_KEYFIELD column must contain G3E_FMOTROWNO.
    * The G3E_ROWID column must contain the value of the G3E_FMOTROWNO corresponding row for Find Feature by Attribute. 
    * The G3E_RANO field should be set to the row in the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table for this find method. 
  * [G3E_NETANALYSISOPTIONS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/o0P9Sdj7anCtwmlE9N4WOg)
Add a row to this table defining how the results are going to be displayed.


In addition, Find Feature by Attribute uses the find-feature metadata defined in the following tables: 
  * [G3E_FIND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k34upujY7Schco2~q76sMQ)
  * [G3E_FINDMETHOD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yh_nP3UzVZyGCMF8WCpQg)
  * [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw)

###### Find Feature by Attribute
Find Feature by Attributes is exposed on the Analysis panel of NetViewer. If the user does not have sufficient privileges to run find feature by attributes, the option does not appear on the Analysis panel. 
The user selects Find Feature by Attributes from the list of advanced finds. Then the user selects or types a feature type, an attribute, an operator, and a value. With this type of advanced find, you can define one or two attributes for the search. If you define two attributes, the user can select a conjunction operator (AND or OR), and then select or type a second attribute, operator, and value. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262745)
You can specify whether the results of the find are displayed on the map and/or in a report window below the map. The details of how the find results are symbolized on the map and whether the map is adjusted based on these results are defined in metadata and can be changed by the user using the Analysis Options panel. 
You can also suppress display of the results on the map until the user selects a feature from the find results report. This includes the suppression of the Analysis Options panel. 
If, while performing an AOI-constrained Find Feature by Attribute, the AOI threshold value is exceeded, users without sufficient privilege cannot perform the query. This lets you prevent users from overwhelming the database and/or the map server. Users with sufficient privilege receive a warning, but can continue processing.

###### Find Feature by Common Component
Find Feature by Common Component is exposed on the Analysis panel of NetViewer. If the user does not have sufficient privileges to run Find Feature by Common Component, the option does not appear on the Analysis panel. 
The user selects Find Feature by Common Component from the list of advanced finds. Then the user selects or types a common component, a component attribute, and an attribute value. 
With this type of advanced find, the user can select multiple attribute values by clicking Add Another Clause. If you define multiple attribute values, the user can select a conjunction operator (AND or OR), and then select or type the additional attribute and its value. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262748)
You can control whether the results of the find are displayed on the map and/or in a report window below the map. The details of how the find results are symbolized on the map and whether the map is adjusted based on these results are defined in metadata and can be changed by the user on the Analysis Options panel. 
You can suppress display of the results on the map until the user selects a feature from the find results report. This includes the suppression of the Analysis Options panel. 
While performing an AOI-constrained Find Feature by Common Components query, if the AOI threshold value is exceeded, users without sufficient privilege cannot perform the query. This lets you keep users from overwhelming the database and/or the map server. Users with sufficient privilege receive a warning, but can continue processing.
