## SynerGEE

### Conductor Configuration Values for SynerGEE
The following are valid conductor configuration values for SynerGEE:
0 = Wye-Ground  
1 = Delta  
2 = Wye  
3 = O-Delta AB  
4 = O-Delta BC  
5 = O-Delta CA  
6 = O-Wye A  
7 = O-Wye B  
8 = O-Wye C 
The parameter specification needs to specify only one of the following:  
|  Single  |  -1  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Wye-Ground  |  0  |  
|  Delta  |  1  |  
|  Wye  |  2  |  
|  O-Delta  |  3  |  
|  O-Wye  |  6  |  
The extract process looks at this value and the phase value specified for the Phase configuration parameter to specify the actual value for SynerGEE. 
The Single configuration value is interpreted as wye or delta based on number of phases on the feature. 
If there are two phases present, the Single value is interpreted as a delta connection. Otherwise, it is interpreted as a wye connection.

### Extracting Customer Analysis Objects
Use one of the following approaches to extract Customer Analysis objects:
  * Extract a single Customer Analysis object to create a single Customer Analysis object.
  * Extract multiple Customer Analysis objects to create one or more Customer Analysis objects, one for each for each row found for an attribute. 


These two approaches are identical to the ones provided for Distribution Transformer Analysis objects. They are supported for the Customer object because it is common for customer information to be retrieved from a feature that is related to a traced transformer feature, which may be modeled as a single banked feature or as distinct units. Regardless of your approach, you need to specify the analysis parameter definitions only once for each feature type that creates Customer Analysis objects. 
Extracting Multiple Objects
Use the [EXTRACT_AS_UNITS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/btgZb4hcGqj~Au~Qp1gEbw) parameter definition to extract separate Customer Analysis objects for each row in a component table. To do this, set this parameter value to the constant value Y. Setting the EXTRACT_AS_UNITS parameter to any other value or not setting it at all results in the extraction of a single Customer Analysis object. 
The number of customers to be extracted is determined by the number of rows found for the source feature for one of its parameter definitions. Typically, if multiple objects are expected to be extracted from a feature, there is a repeating nongraphic component for the feature that contains the information specific to each customer. 
Set the value of the [UNIT_CONTROL_PARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/btgZb4hcGqj~Au~Qp1gEbw) parameter to be the name of another parameter for the Customer object that is derived from an attribute of this repeating nongraphic component. This control parameter should be one of the unit parameter types listed in the table below. 
During the extraction of multiple Customer Analysis objects for a single feature, the Analysis object parameters are grouped into two categories: 
  * Static parameters — These parameter values are determined once and set to the same value for each customer that is extracted. 


Unit Candidate parameters — If these parameters exist in the repeating nongraphic component, they are determined once per row. Otherwise, a single value for the parameter is specified for each customer. 
  * To support varying values for these parameters per unit, define them as attribute- based parameters for the same repeating nongraphic component specified for the UNIT_CONTROL_PARAMETER value. That would make them part of the same row in the component table, which is the only way to ensure that the related values are grouped together. Parameters derived from attributes in this repeating component should not return Null as a value. 


The following table maps the Customer Analysis object parameters into the [appropriate categories](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/btgZb4hcGqj~Au~Qp1gEbw):   
|  Static Parameters  |  Unit Candidate Parameters  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Generic IDentifier  |  Name  
Phase  
Load   |  
|  Section Name  |   |

### Extracting Distribution Transformer Objects
Use one of the following approaches to extract Distribution Transformer Analysis objects:
  * Extract the source feature as a bank to create a single Distribution Transformer Analysis object. 
  * Extract each unit in the source feature to create one or more Distribution Transformer Analysis objects, one for each unit in the bank. 


Regardless of the approach you take, you need to specify the analysis parameter definitions only once for each feature type that creates Distribution Transformer Analysis objects. 
Extracting a Banked Feature
Use the [EXTRACT_AS_UNITS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AiRlP3XCUfdCsWJbyOY4Dw) parameter definition to extract separate Distribution Transformers for each unit in a banked feature. To do this, set this parameter value to the constant value Y. Setting the EXTRACT_AS_UNITS parameter to any other value or not setting it at all results in just a single Distribution Transformer Analysis object's being extracted. 
The number of units in the bank that is extracted is determined by the number of rows found for the source feature for one of its parameter definitions. Typically, if the individual units of a source transformer feature are expected to be extracted, there is a repeating nongraphic component for the source feature that contains the information specific to each unit. 
Set the value of the [UNIT_CONTROL_PARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AiRlP3XCUfdCsWJbyOY4Dw) parameter to be the name of another parameter for the Distribution Transformer object that is derived from an attribute of this repeating nongraphic component. This control parameter also should only be one of the unit parameter types listed in the table below. The Phase parameter is a typical unit control parameter. 
When extracting multiple Distribution Transformer Analysis objects for a single feature, the Analysis object parameters are grouped into two categories: 
  * Static parameters — These parameter values are determined once and set to the same value for each unit that is extracted. 


Unit Candidate parameters — If these parameters exist in the repeating nongraphic component, they are determined once per unit. Otherwise a single value for the parameter is specified for each unit. 
  * To support varying values for these parameters per unit, define them all as attribute- based parameters for the same repeating nongraphic component specified for the UNIT_CONTROL_PARAMETER value. That would make them part of the same row in the component table, the only way to ensure that the related values are grouped together. Parameters derived from attributes in this repeating component should not return Null as a value. 


The following table maps the Distribution Transformer object parameters into the [appropriate categories](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AiRlP3XCUfdCsWJbyOY4Dw):   
|  Static Parameters  |  Unit Candidate Parameters  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Generic IDentifier  |  Phase  
Size   |  
|  Section Name  |  Number of Customers  |

### Mapping Equipment to Sections

#### Determining the Connection Code of Loads
To determine the connection code of the loads on the section values, the extraction logic considers only those features whose objects are connected to the two nodes shared by the section. Once all of the connection code values are known, the final connection code value for the section is calculated. If all of the connection codes are delta, then the connection code for the loads is set to phase-phase. Otherwise, it is set to phase-ground. 
To ensure that only the connection types for loads are considered, you specify a value for the node's [CONN_CD parameter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xtqunL3b5_xFmMgKKLJ5JA) for those feature types that creates load objects.

#### Mapping Equipment Features by Extracting Sections
When you map equipment features by extracting sections, no adjustments to the network are needed to associate the equipment to a section. Instead, a new section is created for the network, and the equipment is associated to it. This new section is placed in the network at the same location as the feature from which it is derived. To create a section from the equipment feature, it should be added to the Section Template metadata. Do this only if the equipment feature is inline connected and is connected to two separate nodes. If the equipment feature is a single-node feature or it is tapped connected, then a section is not extracted for it and it is associated to a section using the algorithm for [mapping equipment without extracting sections](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fTww2YnLt2Qn5A9_W4EIWQ). 
This approach avoids some of the problems you might have with mapping equipment without extracting sections. First, it avoids the problem when the extraction cannot find a section to associate with the equipment because the equipment is associated to the new section. Load location problems are avoided because the section having the load is at the same place in the network where the equipment is modeled. And equipment sections help with tie switches because the circuit is not adjusted for them, no nodes are removed, and the two extractions see the switch connected to the same nodes. 
However, there are a few things that you should consider when using this approach. Since the purpose for these sections is to help keep equipment modeled where they are in the connectivity network, you should define the section's parameters so that the section has little to no impedance and has a very short length or no length at all. 
Modeling Loads
If the feature is modeling a load, the extraction looks for a section that is created from the feature. If the extraction does not find such a section, it follows the algorithm specified for no extraction. If the extraction finds such a section, the load is associated to this section, and its nearest node becomes its downstream node. 
Modeling Protective Devices
If the feature is modeling a protective device, the extraction looks for a section that is created from it. If the extraction does not find such a section, it follows the algorithm specified for no extraction. If the extraction finds such a section, the protective device is associated to this section, and its nearest node becomes its upstream node.

#### Mapping Equipment Features Without Extracting Sections
You can map an equipment feature without extracting a section from it. Instead, the network is adjusted to map the equipment to an existing, extracted section. In this approach, you add entries to the metadata tables to create loads or protective devices for the GIS feature data (for example, the object mapping). 
First, this extraction determines if the equipment is modeling a load or a protective device by looking at the Analysis object that is being extracted for the [feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8tPh7pi~_PY8Akb~SyHu9Q). 
Modeling Loads
If the feature is modeling a load, the extraction looks at the upstream node of the feature for a single section. If it finds one, the network is modified as follows: 
  * If the load is a single-node device or is tapped connected, the load is associated to that upstream section and its nearest node is its upstream node (the downstream node of the section). 


If the load is inline connected and is a two-node device:
  * The load is associated to that upstream section and its nearest node is its downstream node. 
  * The node shared between the load feature and the section is removed. 
  * The section is changed so that its downstream node is the downstream node of the feature from which the load is being extracted. 
  * Any other features at the original upstream node of the load are adjusted to connect to its downstream node. 


If the feature has no single section at the upstream node, then the extraction looks at the downstream node for a single section. If it finds one, the same types of adjustments are made as defined above, except that the downstream node of the load is removed and the other features at that node are moved to the upstream node of the load. 
Modeling Protective Devices
If the feature is modeling a protective device, the extraction looks at the downstream node for a single section. If it locates one, the network is modified as follows: 
  * If the protective device is a single-node device or is tapped connected, then it is associated to that downstream section and its nearest node becomes its upstream node (the downstream node of the section). 


If the protective device is inline connected and is a two- node device:
  * The protective device is associated to that downstream section and its nearest node becomes its upstream node. 
  * The node shared between the feature and the section is removed.
  * The section is changed so that its upstream node is the upstream node of the feature from which the protective device is being extracted. 
  * Any other features at the original downstream node of the protective device are adjusted to connect to the upstream node of the device. 


If there was no single section at the downstream node, then the extraction looks at the upstream node for a single section. If it finds one there, then the same types of adjustments are made as defined above, except that the upstream node of the protective device is removed and the other features at that node are moved to the downstream node of the device. 
Considerations when Mapping Equipment Features Without Extracting Sections
If you map equipment features without extracting sections, you must consider the following:
  * The extraction may be unable to modify the network using the above algorithm. In this case, an error is written to the log file and the equipment is not added to the SynerGEE model. This occurs mainly when there are multiple conductors connected to each node of the equipment feature. Neither the upstream nor the downstream node has a single conductor connected to it, so the algorithm fails. To be extracted, you must add a feature defined in the Section Template metadata before or after the equipment feature. This new feature should have little to no impedance and a very short length or no length at all. 
  * In SynerGEE, loads are located at the center of the section to which they are associated. If the section found by the above algorithm is a lengthy one, then the actual location of the load may be quite different from where it is in reality. This may affect where the loads are modeled in the resultant SynerGEE model. This problem is more prevalent when node reduction is applied to the extracted network by the MiddleLink compiler. 
  * If you extract adjacent circuits separately and then load them into the same SynerGEE/E database, the tie switches may not be modeled correctly, effectively preventing the circuits from being connected together. For each circuit, the above algorithm adjusts the circuit so that the tie switch is associated to the upstream section and the nearest node is the downstream node of that circuit. The extraction of the other circuit does the same thing. Thus, the tie switch is associated to two sections (one from each circuit) and the sections do not share a common node—they are disconnected, which is caused by the removal of the nodes by the above algorithm. The disconnection can be corrected in SynerGEE by stitching the two sections created by the above algorithm.

### SynerGEE Configuration Parameter Values
When defining the values for the Operating Status configuration parameters CURRENT_STATUS and NORMAL_STATUS in [G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION.G3E_VALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/95Dik0JxQHCezVJl5D2V8w), use SQL expressions to translate the values in your data schema into ones that can be understood by the SynerGEE analysis extraction. 
The analysis extraction does not know the specific method used by an application to model if each feature is open or closed. This value is different for each model. Therefor, the SQL expression defined for the configuration value must map into a string value that is understood by SynerGEE:   
|  'Open'  |  = The operating status for the feature is open.  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  'Closed'  |  = The operating status for the feature is closed.  |  
|  'Tie' (switches  
only)   |  = The switch is a tie switch.  |  
The SQL expression must evaluate to one of these character values regardless of the data type of the column used to store the value. 
DECODE function
The Oracle DECODE function is probably the best approach for specifying the expressions for SynerGEE. Use the DECODE function to map the status values in a schema to the values expected by SynerGEE. This method is beneficial when there are multiple values in the schema that must mapped to the values understood by SynerGEE. This method works for both numeric and character data types. 
Example:
The following SQL expression calculates valid operating status values for a schema that stores this information in a character column. For this schema, the CD_STATUS column in the Connectivity table is set to 'Closed' for closed and 'Open' for open. However, the data model needs to set all 'Open' values to tie in the SynerGEE model. This expression sets all 'Open' values to tie and leave all 'Closed' values as closed. 
DECODE(conn.CD_STATUS,'Open','tie',conn.CD_STATUS)
This expression assumes no Null values for the conn.CD_STATUS.

#### SynerGEE Node Data Analysis Object
The following parameters must be defined in the [G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~Ph4Bg4UcJzi2171RVz7w) table for the SynerGEE Node Data Analysis object:   
|  Description  |  Parameter Name  |  Data Type  |  Units  |  Comment  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Generic identifier  |  ID  |  Character  |   |  Must be NOD* (where * means any five or fewer characters)  |  
|  X Coordinate  |  GEOMETRY  |  Real  |   |  The single definition of the GEOMETRY parameter is sufficient for determining both the coordinate values.   |  
|  Y Coordinate  |  GEOMETRY  |  Real  |   |   |  
|  Node name or number  |   |   |   |  Set to the NetWorks Core connectivity node number by the extract process   |  
|  Voltage  |  VOLT  |  Real  |  Volts  |  This parameter is not output as part of the Node Data Analysis object information. Rather, it is used to help determine other parameters for other objects connected to the node, such as the high-side voltage of a primary transformer.  Only features that map to sections need to specify an actual value for this parameter. Other features should set the VOLT value to zero.   |  
|  Connection code  |  CONN_CD  |  Integer  |   |  This parameter is not output as part of the Node Data Analysis object information. Rather, it is used to help determine other parameters for other objects connected to the node, such as the section connection code.  0 = Phase-ground (wye)  
1 = Phase-phase (delta)  The parameter specification needs to specify only one of the following: Single -1  
Wye 0  
Delta 1  The extract process looks at this value and the phase value specified for the PHASE configuration parameter to specify the actual value for SynerGEE.  The Single configuration value is interpreted as wye or delta, based on number of phases on the feature.  If there are two phases present, then the Single value is interpreted as a delta connection; otherwise it is interpreted as a wye connection.  Only features that map to load analysis objects should specify an actual value for this parameter. Other features should not specify a value for this parameter at all. The SynerGEE load analysis objects are Customers, Distribution Transformers, Meters and Spot Loads.   |  
|  Location description  |   |   |   |  The extract process sets this to a meaningless value.  |

1 = Yes   |

1 = Yes   |

1 = Yes   |

1 for the downstream node as seen by the trace  
2 for NODE1_ID  
3 for NODE2_ID

LF = Locked Forward

IR = Reverse IDle  
BD = Bidirectional  
IN = Neutral IDle  
CG = Co- Generation

## The NetWorks Core to InService Interface

### Configuring Metadata to Export to InService
This is an overview of the metadata required for exporting data to InService. When you create an empty database, the [G3E_OMSIFACE (InService Interface Table)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/t6PIXMng8Axk9taE8DM1ig) table is automatically populated with the default entries defined by the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateOMSMetadata.sql script. 
  * To configure metadata to export NetWorks Core data to InService:


  1. Run the following procedure to create an OMS Export Feature table (G3E_OMSFEATUREx) and its optimized table package. Type the following in Metadata Query or an SQL editor: 
SQL> execute MG3EOMSExportUtils.CreateExpFeatureTableAndPkg ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>');
TableName must be less than or equal to 22 characters and TableAbbreviation must be less than or equal to 17 characters.   
|  Example execute MG3EOMSExportUtils.CreateExpFeatureTableAndPkg ('HelpTest', 'HelpTest');  |  
| --- |  
Use the procedure to create a table for each different set of data you want to export.
  2. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Outage Management > InService Interface > OMS Exports, and click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596) or right-click and select Insert a new row to insert a new row in the G3E_OMSEXPORTLIST table. See the following example: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596)
  3. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Outage Management > InService Interface > InService Parameters and insert a new row in the G3E_OMSIFACE table. 
    1. In the G3E_OMSELNO field, select the OMS export list you added in Step 2.
    2. In the G3E_TABLE field, select the table you created in Step 1.
    3. In the G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE field, type the table name appended with _OPTABLE. See the following example: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596)
  4. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596) on the Metadata Explorer toolbar to refresh the Metadata Explorer tree view. 
  5. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to Outage Management > InService Interface > OMS Exports > <OMS export added in Step 2> OMS Features > Display OMS Feature Definition node and insert as many new rows as you need for the export in the OMS feature table you created in Step 1. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596) The G3E_VNO is type NUMBER(5) in the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION table. Therefore, do not exceed a component view number (G3E_VNO) of 32767 (small int). If you do, an error occurs. See the following examples: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259596)
  6. To recreate the optimized table packages for all OMS Export Feature tables listed in the G3E_OMSIFACE table, run this procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EOMSExportUtils.InstallExportFeaturePackages;

### Export to InService
Use ExportToOMSUtility.exe to export NetWorks Core geometry data to a file that can be read by the InService Outage Management System. The output file is a modified design file (.dgn) format that InService can read. Using the optional ExportName parameter, you can export different data from the same data set for separate management regions or systems. You can specify separate sets of export parameters such as output location, seed file, paper scale, and the set of features to be exported for each export definition. 
A default export definition is created by the upgrade script. However, before you can define and export more than one named export definition to InService, [you must configure metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nhyLNFTikzzRXFS5X71rkg). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259594) Before exporting NetWorks Core geometry data to InService map files, you might want to map the NetWorks Core data to an existing design file (typically landbase). To do this, you must apply a global origin shift so that the data overlaps.   
|  Example You have landbase files delivered in MicroStation format that you want to align with NetWorks Core geometry data before you export to InService. In NetWorks Core, the coordinates are stored in real world values without any additional offset. In the landbase files, the coordinate readout matches the real world coordinates; however, to cover a larger design plane while exporting the NetWorks Core geometry, you can adjust the global origin and set it in the negative range.  To map NetWorks Core data to the landbase design files, you can apply a global origin shift to the extracted NetWorks Core data so that it properly aligns with the landbase before it is exported to InService map files. The ApplyGlobalOrigin flag indicates that a global origin defined in the seed file should be applied when generating the design files for NetWorks Core data. This is based on the assumption that the global origin in the seed file matches the global origin in the delivered landbase file.   |  
| --- |  
  * To export NetWorks Core data to InService:


From a command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
ExportToOMSUtility.exe
Login=<user/password@configuration>;[Job=<JobList>;][ApplyGlobalOrigin=0/1;][ExportName=<export name>;]
These are the parameters:  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Login  |  NetWorks Core user name, password and configuration name.   |  
|  Job  |  List of NetWorks Core jobs to export to InService.   |  
|  ApplyGlobalOrigin  |  Flag indicating whether a global origin shift should be applied to the generated design files. The default is 0.   |  
|  ExportName  |  Optional flag that describes the name for an OMS export definition.  |  
|  UseGlyphOutline  |  Value set to 1.  Because of the difference in the rendering of text between NetWorks Core and MicroStation, you must determine the appropriate text height and width when creating the DGN element.  By default, the utility uses the rendered text metrics to determine the text height and width. When the font is created by setting the font header information for both ascent and descent without redrawing the font itself, the computed text size may yield incorrect results.  To address this, the UseGlyphOutline parameter can be used to calculate the average text size by using the metric from the font glyph outline of each individual character within the specified text.   |  
|  Example ExportToOMSUtility.exe Login=yourname/yourpassword@COBBEMC; Job=O-232, O-343;ApplyGlobalOrigin=1; ExportName=Poles  |  
| --- |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259594) If an error occurs when you run ExportToOMS.exe, check the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION.G3E_VNO to be sure you have not exceeded a component view number (G3E_VNO) of 32767 (small int).

## Work Management System Interfaces

### Configuring CU Selection (Deprecated)

#### Configuring CU Selection—Additional Related Components (Deprecated)
For the STORMS and Logica work management systems, additional components that work together with the CU data are populated and processed by CU Selection. The following list of components indicates with which WMS they are associated. 
Application Dependencies—STORMS
An additional component records any application dependencies associated with the CU that the user selects. These application dependencies provide additional specific information about a CU to define it more completely, for example, the insulated type used for a conductor wire connection. When a user selects a CU with CU Selection, the software verifies that one or more application dependencies exist for this CU. If an applications dependency exists, the [Application Dependency Properties](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EB9vNDFHEaa6n7xbrNpR4A) dialog box prompts the user to type the correct values for the application dependency codes for this CU. 
These values are stored on the application dependency component for this feature and are associated to the CU record. If no application dependency values are entered, the CU record is not added to the component. 
Additional Cost Items
The following are several [data entry issues](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kuXIExwkv9EAyfz9BPUbfA) not directly related to CU data, but still part of feature placement and [edit operations](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kuXIExwkv9EAyfz9BPUbfA). 
Cost Entry and Processing—STORMS, Logica
If additional cost records are required by the design, they are added to either individual features, the work point features, or to the design area feature. The design area feature represents the work request revision characteristics/attributes and, therefore, stores any additional cost records. The standard attribute definition and processing are used in this workflow. For the Logica interface, the standard WMIS inbound message only supports sending cost items at the individual feature level. The message is not configured for design area and work points. 
Condition Factors—Logica
An additional component records condition factors at the CU, point/span, or revision level. The condition factor code and the percentage adjustment or value is recorded. 
Comments—Logica
An additional component records comments at the CU or point/span level. NetWorks Core tracks comments, and if they have already been sent, it does not send them again. 
Providers—Logica
An additional optional component records contractors at the CU level. The user defines only one contractor occurrence, but the export associates the contractor to all the primary and ancillary CUs of the feature. A second optional repeating component records third parties at the CU level. Third-party information must be mapped to a particular CU occurrence and is used when the utility does work for another utility.   
|  Example A local telephone company contracts with a utility to replace or install a pole that the local company owns. That primary CU is tracked and billed to the third party. However, the ancillary framing modules are the work (cost) of the utility for itself and should not be tracked or recorded with the third party. The NetWorks Core user is responsible for identifying the associated CU for the third-party information.   |  
| --- |

#### Configuring CU Selection—Data Consistency Check (Deprecated)
NetWorks Core provides a validation functional interface to ensure that edits of static attribute data are appropriate for their associated CUs. This functional interface relies upon the static attribute data set within the specified WMS attribute metadata table. 
The model validation pipe, in conjunction with the [DataConsistencyCheck functional interface](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) (FI), checks data consistency between static attributes and the CU. If any of the (related) static attribute values do not match those associated with the CU values when the CU attribute value is populated (not null), this functional interface returns the error recordset specifying the inconsistent field names and values. 
FIs are associated with the Primary CU attribute of the component so that all data fields are validated at once; thus, performance is improved. 
  * The DataConsistencyCheck FI returns an empty error recordset if the CU attribute is Null or all static attribute values (related to the Primary CU) match CU values when they were populated. 
  * If any of the (related) static attribute values do not match the CU values, the DataConsistencyCheck FI returns an error recordset specifying the inconsistent field names and values.

#### Configuring CU Selection—Finding Ancillary CU Data (Deprecated)
The following SQL statements must be available to the software for CU Selection. They must be accessible using the database links that are set up between NetWorks Core and the defined WMS. Each statement represents a part of the [Compatible Unit Query dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kuXIExwkv9EAyfz9BPUbfA) that is used to retrieve, filter, and assign CU data from the WMS to the feature components within NetWorks Core. 
Logica
Initial list of ancillary CUs for feature
SQL> select cu_id, cu_desc, unit_type_code from construction_unit, cucategoryxref 
where 
cucategoryxref.cu_category_code_='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and construction_unit.cu_category_code=cucategoryxref.cu_category_code_assoc and Mappable_yn='N' and Effective_date<SYSDATE and (Expiration_date>SYSDATE or expiration_date is NULL) order by cu_id;
List of first level ancillary groups (categories) for feature
SQL> select G3E_CATEGORY from cucategoryxref 
where 
G3E_FEATURENAME='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME';
List of ancillary CUs after selection of specific ancillary group (category) for feature
SQL> select cu_id, cu_desc, unit_type_code from construction_unit 
where 
cu_category_code='Category selected from first level group' and Mappable_yn='N' and Effective_date<SYSDATE and (Expiration_date>SYSDATE or expiration_date is NULL) order by cu_id;
List of ancillary CUs using wildcard filter on second level of filters if first level filter has not been selected and default (blank line) is used 
SQL> select cu_id, cu_desc, unit_type_code from construction_unit, G3E_LOGICACUXREF 
where 
G3E_LOGICACUXREF.G3E_FEATURENAME='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and construction_unit.cu_category_code= G3E_LOGICACUXREF G3E_CATEGORY and Mappable_yn='N' and Effective_date<SYSDATE and (Expiration_date>SYSDATE or expiration_date is NULL) and cu_id like '%CU substring%' order by cu_id;
List of ancillary CUs using wildcard filter on second level of filters if first level filter has been selected 
SQL> select cu_id, cu_desc, unit_type_code from construction_unit 
where 
cu_category_code='active category from first level group' and Mappable_yn='N' and Effective_date<SYSDATE and (Expiration_date>SYSDATE or expiration_date is NULL) and cu_id like '%CU substring%' order by cu_id;
List of second level fixed attribute filter names after selection of specific ancillary group (category) for feature 
SQL> select cu_attribute_code from cu_category_attribute 
where 
cu_category_code='Category selected from first level group' and Fixed_yn='Y';
Domain for second level fixed attribute filter names
SQL> select attribute_value from cu_attribute_value 
where 
cu_attribute_code='CU attribute code from above query' and cu_category_code='Category selected from first level group';
List of ancillary CUs after selection of second level filter values
SQL> select cu_id, cu_desc, unit_type_code from construction_unit 
where 
cu_category_code='active category from first level group' and Mappable_yn='Y' and Effective_date<SYSDATE and (Expiration_date>SYSDATE or Expiration_date is NULL) and 
/* For each keyword filter with value selected */ 
exists (select 'X' from cu_standard_attribute 
where 
cu_category_code='active category from first level group' and cu_attribute_code='fixed attribute filter name' and attribute_value='filter value selected' and construction_unit.cu_id=cu_standard_attribute.cu_id) order by construction_unit.cu_id;
STORMS
Initial list of ancillary CUs for feature
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU, TP_CU, CD_USAGE from TWMCU 
where 
(TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED is NULL or TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_FACILITY in (select TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and TWMFACILITY.FG_ACTIVE = 'Y')
List of first level ancillary groups (categories) for feature
SQL> select CD_FACILITY_ASSOC FIRSTLEVEL_KEYWORDS from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and FG_ACTIVE='Y'
List of ancillary CUs after selection of specific ancillary group (category) for feature
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU, TP_CU, CD_USAGE from TWMCU 
where 
(TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED is NULL or TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_FACILITY in (select TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = 'Category selected from first level group' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and TWMFACILITY.FG_ACTIVE = 'Y')
List of ancillary CUs using wildcard filter on second level of filters if first level filter has not been selected and default (blank line) is used 
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU, TP_CU, CD_USAGE from TWMCU 
where 
(TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED is NULL or TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_FACILITY in (select TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and TWMFACILITY.FG_ACTIVE = 'Y') and CD_CU like '%CU substring%'
List of ancillary CUs using wildcard filter on second level of filters if first level filter has been selected 
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU, TP_CU, CD_USAGE from TWMCU 
where 
(TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED is NULL or TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_FACILITY in (select TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = 'active category from first level group' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and TWMFACILITY.FG_ACTIVE = 'Y') and CD_CU like '%CU substring%'
List of second level fixed attribute filter names after selection of specific ancillary group (category) for feature 
SQL> select TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD From TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE, TWMKEYWORDTYPE 
where 
CD_FACILITY='Category selected from first level group' and TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD = TWMKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD and FG_ACTIVE = 'Y'
Domain for second level fixed attribute filter names
SQL> select CD_KEYWORD from TWMKEYWORD 
where 
TP_KEYWORD = 'TP_KEYWORD from above query'
List of ancillary CUs after selection of second level filter values
SQL> select distinct IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU, CD_USAGE from TWMCU 
where 
(TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED is NULL or TWMCU.DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or TWMCU.DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_FACILITY in (select TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC from TWMFACILITYXREF, TWMFACILITY 
where 
TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY_ASSOC = 'active category from first level group' and TWMFACILITYXREF.CD_FACILITY = TWMFACILITY.CD_FACILITY and TWMFACILITY.FG_ACTIVE = 'Y') 
/* For each keyword filter with value selected */ 
exists (select 'X' from CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE = 'active category from first level group' and CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE = 'fixed attribute filter name' and ATTRIBUTE_VALUE = 'filter value selected' and CONSTRUCTION_UNIT.CU_ID = CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE.CU_ID union select CU_ID from UNIT_ASSEMBLY 
where 
ASSEMBLY_ITEM_ID in (select CU_ID from CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE = 'active category from first level group' and CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE = 'fixed attribute filter name' and ATTRIBUTE_VALUE = 'filter value selected') and PRIMARY_ITEM_YN = 'N' and CONSTRUCTION_UNIT.CU_ID = UNIT_ASSEMBLY.CU_ID)

#### Configuring CU Selection—Finding Primary CU Data (Deprecated)
The following SQL statements must be available to the software for CU Selection. They must be accessible using the database links that are set up between NetWorks Core and the defined WMS. Each statement represents a part of the [Compatible Unit Query dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kuXIExwkv9EAyfz9BPUbfA) that is used to retrieve, filter, and assign CU data from the WMS to the feature components within NetWorks Core. 
Logica
Initial list of primary CUs for feature
SQL> select CU_ID, CU_DESC, UNIT_TYPE_CODE from CONSTRUCTION_UNIT 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and MAPPABLE_YN='Y' and EFFECTIVE_DATE<SYSDATE and (EXPIRATION_DATE>SYSDATE or EXPIRATION_DATE is NULL) order by CU_ID If Macro CU (construction_unit.unit_type_code='M'), list of CUs comprising Macro select ASSEMBLY_ITEM_ID, PRIMARY_ITEM_YN, UNIT_ASSEMBLY_QTY from UNIT_ASSEMBLY
where 
CU_ID='Macro CU';
List of fixed attributes for CU selected (non-Macro)
SQL> select B.CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE, ATTRIBUTE_VALUE from CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE A, CU_CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE B 
where 
CU_ID='CU SELECTED' and FIXED_YN='Y' and A.CU_CATEGORY_CODE=B. CU_CATEGORY_CODE and A.CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE=B. CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE;
List of fixed attributes for CU selected (Macro)
SQL> select B.CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE, ATTRIBUTE_VALUE from CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE A, CU_CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE B 
where 
CU_ID='CU FROM MACRO 
where 
PRIMARY_ITEM_YN='Y'' and FIXED_YN='Y' and A.CU_CATEGORY_CODE=B. CU_CATEGORY_CODE and A.CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE=B. CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE;
List of fixed attribute filter names for feature
SQL> select CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE from CU_CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and FIXED_YN='Y';
Domain of filter values
SQL> select ATTRIBUTE_VALUE from CU_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE 
where 
CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE='CODE FROM ABOVE QUERY' and CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME';
List of primary CUs after selection of filter values
SQL> select CU_ID, CU_DESC, UNIT_TYPE_CODE from CONSTRUCTION_UNIT 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and MAPPABLE_YN='Y' and EFFECTIVE_DATE<SYSDATE and (EXPIRATION_DATE>SYSDATE or EXPIRATION_DATE is NULL) and
/* For Each Keyword Filter With Value Selected */
exists (select 'X' from CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and CU_ATTRIBUTE_CODE='FIXED ATTRIBUTE FILTER NAME' and ATTRIBUTE_VALUE='FILTER VALUE SELECTED' and CONSTRUCTION_UNIT.CU_ID=CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE.CU_ID) order by CONSTRUCTION_UNIT.CU_ID;
List of primary CUs using a wildcard filter
SQL> select CU_ID, CU_DESC, UNIT_TYPE_CODE from CONSTRUCTION_UNIT 
where 
CU_CATEGORY_CODE='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and MAPPABLE_YN='Y' and EFFECTIVE_DATE<SYSDATE and (EXPIRATION_DATE>SYSDATE or EXPIRATION_DATE is NULL) and CU_ID like '%CU SUBSTRING%' order by CU_ID;
STORMS
Initial list of primary CUs for feature
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU from TWMC 
where 
CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and (DT_DISCONTINUED IS NULL or DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE)
List of fixed attributes for CU selected (non-Macro)
SQL> select CD_ATTRIBUTE, TXT_FAC_VALUE from TWMCUATTRIB 
where 
CD_CU = 'CU SELECTED'
List of fixed attributes for CU selected (Macro)
SQL> select CD_ATTRIBUTE, TXT_FAC_VALUE from TWMCUATTRIB 
where 
CD_CU = 'CU FROM MACRO 
where 
TWMMUSTRUCTURE.CD_SEQ in ('1', 'Y', 'y')'
List of fixed attribute filter names for feature
SQL> select TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD From TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE, TWMKEYWORDTYPE 
where 
CD_FACILITY='G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and TWMFACKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD = TWMKEYWORDTYPE.TP_KEYWORD and FG_ACTIVE = 'Y'
Domain of filter values
SQL> select CD_KEYWORD KEYWORD_VALUES from TWMKEYWORD 
where 
TP_KEYWORD = 'TP_KEYWORD FROM ABOVE QUERY'
List of primary CUs after selection of filter values
SQL> select distinct IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU from TWMCU 
where 
CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and (DT_DISCONTINUED IS NULL or DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and 
/* For Each Keyword Filter With Value Selected */ 
exists (select 'X' from TWMCUKEYWOR 
where 
TP_KEYWORD = 'FIXED ATTRIBUTE FILTER NAME' and CD_KEYWORD = 'FILTER VALUE SELECTED' and TWMCU.CD_CU = TWMCUKEYWORD.CD_CU)
List of primary CUs using a wildcard filter
SQL> select IND_CU_MU, CD_CU, DS_CU from TWMCU 
where 
CD_FACILITY = 'G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME' and (DT_DISCONTINUED IS NULL or DT_DISCONTINUED > SYSDATE) and (DT_EFFECTIVE IS NULL or DT_EFFECTIVE < SYSDATE) and CD_CU like '%CU SUBSTRING%' order by CD_CU"

#### Configuring CU Selection—Metadata Setup (Deprecated)
Logica
The metadata tables used in CU Selection for the Logica interface are G3E_ATTRIBUTE, G3E_COMPONENT, G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT, G3E_LOGICAIFACE, G3E_LOGICAATTRIBUTE, G3E_LOGICACUXREF and G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT. 
  1. For the CU and macro CU fields, specify the foreign key in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw). For Logica, CONSTRUCTION_UNIT is the foreign key table name containing all the CUs. CD_ID is the foreign key field name within this foreign key table. 
  2. Define the following components in the [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table and associate to the appropriate feature definitions using the [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) table: 
     * Primary CU component
     * Ancillary CU component
     * Voucher and contribution components
     * Comment component
     * Condition factor component
     * Contractor component


G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE
The metadata table [G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qNLsK9zzJX8y7qBc9dtZtA) is used in the Data Consistency Check functional interface. This table shows how to populate the DataConsistencyCheck FI in the G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE table:   
|  G3E_FINO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_INTERFACE  |  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  G3E_EDITDATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Data Consistency Check  |  PFIFace.DataConsistencyCheck  |  Null  |  Null  |  11/15/2002  |  
After the FI is populated in the G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE table, populate the G3E_FINO associated with the DataConsistencyCheck in the G3E_FINO field of the CU attribute in G3E_ATTRIBUTE of the primary CU component. 
STORMS
The metadata tables used in CU Selection for the STORMS interface are G3E_ATTRIBUTE, G3E_COMPONENT, G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT, G3E_STORMSIFACE, G3E_STORMSATTRIBUTE, and G3E_CUKEYFIELD. 
  1. For the CU and macro CU fields, specify the foreign key in G3E_ATTRIBUTE. For STORMS, TWMCU is the foreign key table name containing all the CUs. CD_CU is the foreign key field name within this foreign key table. 
  2. Define the following components in the G3E_COMPONENT table and associate to the appropriate feature definitions using the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table: 
     * Primary CU component
     * Ancillary CU component
     * Primary application dependency component
     * Ancillary application dependency component
  3. The G3E_STORMSIFACE table contains the component number (CNO) values that correspond to the primary and ancillary CU components and table names for the other metadata tables that are referenced. The field definitions within each of these components are mapped into the G3E_CUKEYFIELD table. 
  4. The mapping of the attributes for each of these components is located within the G3E_CUKEYFIELD table. CU Selection uses this mapping to populate the component record. The software uses the G3E_FIELDTYPE column to locate the appropriate ANO value. 
  5. The G3E_STORMSATTRIBUTE table contains a mapping of NetWorks Core attributes (ANOs) for each feature (FNO) to fixed/static attributes defined in STORMS. These mapped attributes are the ones populated as corresponding to the primary mappable CU that is applied to the feature. 
  6. For CU validation to work properly, the value of CUValidation in [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA) table must be 1 and G3E_FEATURE.G3E_NAME must be populated in data sets that have a work management system such as STORMS or Logica defined.

#### Configuring CU Selection—Query Menu (Deprecated)
The [Compatible Unit Query dialog box](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kuXIExwkv9EAyfz9BPUbfA) helps the user assign CU values from the WMS into NetWorks Core. This topic describes the process of initiating CU selection from Feature Explorer and the search and filtering operations. 
CU Selection Query Menu
The user right-clicks the [compatible unit or macro field](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WagkV~4M9M8WJ3WYNQ5K5g) to display the Query pop-up menu. 
Query processing
If the column below the right-click location contains an attribute defined with a domain or foreign key table reference, the software displays the query menu. When Query is selected, the software searches for the appropriate work management interface definition based upon the work management software license information used when NetWorks Core is installed. The definition is used to associate the appropriate work management SQL statements for the population and presentation of fields on the query dialog box. These SQL statements are embedded in the command and must be [accessible using the database link](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/N2oSU0iUuqQH~PRNdgv8qg). See [Configuring CU Selection—Finding Ancillary CU Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/iDOAWzXgKRVAlfhJWFPscA) and [Configuring CU Selection—Finding Primary CU Data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/g7HuhBatiWAc~M6dKuIzQw) for information about the SQL statements. 
Search Primary CUs
When the user clicks Query on the primary CU, component's CU, or macro unit (MU) attribute, the [Compatible Unit Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WagkV~4M9M8WJ3WYNQ5K5g) dialog box appears. 
The Values for query box on the dialog box includes a set of keyword attributes for narrowing the CU search. These are the keyword attributes defined within the configuration and setup of the WMS. It also contains the CU field itself. The Query results box presents the possible matches for the CU search. If the user selects values for the keywords or enters partial values for the CU field, the listing of CUs is filtered accordingly when the user clicks Execute. The user then has a smaller subset of CUs for this feature from which to select. 
Keywords are identical to fixed attributes defined in the WMS. The Query results box presentation fields include the CU identifier, the description, and the macro indicator. 
Processing Primary CUs
The Values for query box on the dialog box is populated with all keywords or searchable attributes associated with this feature class. The last row supports searching by the CU identifier. The software automatically appends a wildcard indicator (%) to the beginning and end of values specified in the CU identifier field. This field is used when the user enters part of the CU code as a wildcard for the CU filter instead of using the keyword attributes. 
The user can enter multiple conditions. Each condition is combined (AND'd) when the user selects Execute to query the database for candidate CUs. These are presented in the Query results box. The order and titling of the fields are controlled by the dialog definition. 
The user can select one CU from the list or start the filtering operation again. When the user clicks OK, a new record is added for the selected CU. If the feature is banked, such as a transformer bank, capacitor bank, or conductor, the user can select multiple CUs by running CU Selection multiple times, specifying the new record each time. 
If the user selects a macro CU, and the primary mappable CU contained in the macro has a quantity greater than one, the feature definition is checked. If the feature is banked, the macro can include more than one primary CU (or one primary CU with a quantity greater than one) and any number of ancillary CUs. If the feature is banked (allows multiple primary CUs), the appropriate discrete CU records with quantity of one are added to the component data. 
If the feature is not banked (repeating records not allowed), one record is entered as the primary CU, and the rest of the quantity for this CU is stored as ancillary CUs. Ancillary CU identifiers within the macro do not expand when the quantity is greater than 1. A single row for each defined CU is placed with a quantity that is set to the defined value within the macro. 
Any metadata-configured static attributes associated with the CU are copied. More static attributes can be defined in the WMS than what are copied into NetWorks Core. Fixed, or static, attributes are defined inside metadata. See the specific WMS section for the appropriate table to use within the interface. 
Search Ancillary CU
When the user clicks Query on the ancillary CU component's CU or macro unit (MU) attribute, the [Compatible Unit Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DugO6lwY_FMVBWb3bHbEsQ) dialog box appears. 
On the dialog box, the Ancillary Keyword Filter drop- down list contains categories for the ancillary CUs. These categories are defined within the WMS tables so that only specific categories for the current feature are available. The Values for query box includes a set of keyword attributes for narrowing the CU search within the selected category. These keywords are the WMS-fixed attributes. The dialog also contains the CU field itself. The Query results box presents the possible matches for the CU search. The Saved query results box shows the set of CUs the user has chosen for this feature. The user can select multiple CUs and place them inside the Saved query results box for processing. 
Processing Ancillary CUs
On the Compatible Unit Query dialog box, the drop- down combo box is defined as the CU categories associated with the active feature. The combo box defaults to blank, and no keywords are displayed in the Values for query box. 
The Ancillary Keyword Filter drop-down list is populated with all fixed or searchable attributes associated with the selected category from the combo box. The last row supports searching by the CU identifier. 
The user can enter multiple conditions. Each condition is combined (AND'd) when the user selects Execute to query the database for candidate CUs. These are presented in the Query results box. 
The user can select one or more CUs from the list or start the filtering operation again. Any CUs that the user assigns can be moved to the Saved query results box. 
When the user clicks OK, a new record is added for each selected CU. If the selected CU is a macro, the definition is traversed, and the appropriate discrete CU rows are added to the component data. Quantity does not translate into additional records but is retained. 
No static attributes are copied on CU selection for ancillaries.
Macro Processing
When editing a feature, if the primary or ancillary CU is deleted, and it is part of a macro CU, all CU entries associated with that macro are deleted from the feature. Also, if a record currently references a macro and the query is performed again to select a new CU, the macro entries are deleted.

### Configuring the Queue Processing Service as a DCOM Object

#### Configuring the DCOM Server and Client
The process for configuring messaging server and client machines is almost the same. The differences are identified in this topic. 
Verify Operating Systems
  * Your server machine must have Windows Server 2003 SP1 or higher installed.
  * Your client machines must have Windows XP SP2 or higher installed.


Specify DCOM User
  * For a server machine, identify a domain username (or domain user group) that has permissions to access the DCOM server object on the server machine. Add identified domain username (or domain user group) to the built-in Distributed COM Users group. 
  * For client machines, ensure that all domain usernames (or domain user group) that are allowed to run Designer/Analyst on the client machine are added to the built-in Administrators group. 


Verify that DCOM Is Enabled
  1. From the Control Panel, navigate to Administrative Tools > Component Services. 
  2. Select Console Root > Component Services > Computers > My Computer. 
  3. Right-click My Computer, and select Properties. 
  4. Select the Default Properties tab. 
  5. Ensure that Enable Distributed COM on this computer is checked. 


Verify Machine-Wide Permissions
If default machine-wide COM security values meet your requirements, you do not have to make changes to machine- wide COM security settings. See [DCOM Security Enhancements in Windows XP-SP2 and Windows Server 2003 SP1](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms679714\(VS.85\).aspx) on MSDN for default COM security values. 
If default machine-wide authentication and impersonation level values meet your requirements, you do not have to make changes to default values. See [COM Security Defaults](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms686599\(VS.85\).aspx) on MSDN for default authentication and impersonation level values. 
  * To update the DCOM Application (GTDCOM.exe) Location and Identity Settings: 


  1. From the Control Panel, navigate to Administrative Tools > Component Services. 
  2. Select Console Root > Component Services > Computers > My Computer > DCOM Config > {18354AD1-A0A8- 4B9C-8358-E37CED4F8FB8}. 
  3. Right-click {18354AD1-A0A8- 4B9C-8358-E37CED4F8FB8}, and select Properties. 
  4. For a DCOM server:
    1. Select the Location tab, and ensure that only the Run application on this computer is checked. 
    2. Select the Identity tab, and select This user. Type the domain user account information that you want the GTDCom.exe server DCOM object to run as. This domain user account must have access to queue client and must have Log on as a batch job user right. 
  5. OR For a DCOM client:
    1. Select the Location tab, and ensure that only the Run application on the following computer is checked with the DCOM Server machine name entered in the text box. 
    2. Select the Identity tab, and ensure Launching user is selected. 
  6. Test the GTDCOM.exe as DCOM server and client configuration by starting the [Messaging Test Application](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/l8O4q5U~KEtk2bhFtfRq4A) without errors. If you get permission errors when you start the Messaging Test Application, see the DCOM troubleshooting topics for [server](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CXRMY~Q5l_DoVBC1NuyeUw) and [client](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/8FmavpdXK1aOFQJAeqxn4g). 


Verify DCOM Application (GTDCOM.exe) Permissions 
If default application specific COM security values meet your requirements, you do not have to make changes to {18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C-8358-E37CED4F8FB8} application COM security settings. 
If default application specific authentication and impersonation levels meet your requirements, you do not have to make change to {18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C-8358- E37CED4F8FB8} application default values. 
See [Setting Process-Wide Security Using DCOMCNFG](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms678426\(VS.85\).aspx) on MSDN for step-by-step instructions.

#### Exporting DCOM Client Settings to Configure Another Client Machine
|   
 |  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256395) Verify with your IT department that these procedures do not compromise the computer security or IT requirements for your site. These steps outline one way to export DCOM settings for installation on other machines. There could be others that are more appropriate for your site.   |  
| --- |  
 |  
  1. On a configured client machine, use the Registry Editor (RegEdit.exe) to export all values under the registry keys described below and save them in .reg files.   
|  Registry Key  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Ole  |  Stores all DCOM machine- wide settings. See [Registry Entries](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms694355\(VS.85\).aspx) on MSDN for more information.   |  
|  HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\AppID\\{18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C- 8358-E37CED4F8FB8} HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\\{18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C- 8358-E37CED4F8FB8}  |  Stores all DCOM application-specific settings for GTDCOM.exe  |  
|  [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\AppID\\{18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C-8358-E37CED4F8FB8}] "RemoteServerName"=- [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\AppID\\{18354AD1-A0A8-4B9C-8358-E37CED4F8FB8}] "AuthenticationLevel"=dword:00000001  |  Unchecks Run application on this computer on the Properties dialog box Location tab. See [Configuring the DCOM Server and Client](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/oVwl1Ew5oSW2EvdIgMKDaQ) Help topic for further information.   |  
  2. Run the exported .reg files on other client machines.

#### Permission Error Troubleshooting for the DCOM Client
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256392) Verify with your IT department that these procedures do not compromise the computer security or IT requirements for your site. This is only one way to grant these permissions. There could be others that are more appropriate for your site.   |  
| --- |  
The following steps are for Windows XP SP2 or higher.
  * To verify machine-wide Settings:


  1. From the Control Panel, navigate to Administrative Tools > Computer Management. 
  2. Select Computer Management (Local) System Tools > Local Users and Groups > Groups > Administrators. 
  3. Add all domain user names (or domain user group) that are allowed to run Designer/Analyst on client machine to the built-in Administrators group. 
  4. Navigate to Administrative Tools > Component Services. 
  5. Select Console Root > Component Services > Computers > My Computer. 
  6. Right-click My Computer, and select Properties.

#### Troubleshooting Issue Related to Requiring MQSeries Client Software Being Installed on a DCOM Client 64 Bit Machine
On x64 operating systems, the 64-bit version of DCOMCNFG.EXE does not correctly configure the 32-bit queue processing service (GTDcom.exe) DCOM application for remote activation. This incorrect configuration causes the queue processing service to be activated locally instead of remotely, and the software displays an error message requiring the installation of MQSeries Client. 
Example error message when running Send to WMIS command from NetWorks Core:
Unable to call Send method of QueueProcessingService object.
Failed in Send
Unable to call ValidateRequiredProperties procedure.
Failed in SendMQSeries
ActiveX component can't create object
The workaround is to use the 32-bit version of DCOMCNFG. Follow the steps below:
  1. Run the 32-bit version of mmc.exe and 
  2. Load the 32-bit version of the Component Services snap-in by using the following command line. 
C:\WINDOWS\SysWOW64>mmc comexp.msc /32
The 32-bit version of Component Services correctly registers 32-bit queue processing service (GTDcom.exe) DCOM application for remote activation.

### Exporting a Design to a Work Management System

#### Exporting a Design to a Generic Work Management System

##### Send to Generic WMS Metadata
The following metadata tables are associated with the Send to WMS command: G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT
In the [G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s9GcPFxUsogokTRUglTFow) table, identify the export message format for exporting data to WMS. The NetWorks Core Message Format tool can assist in formatting metadata for this message along with other messages needed for Generic WMS processing. Be sure to format the export message name defined in metadata. This tool lets you select the features, components, and attributes that you need to include in any export message. For the data to be included in the export message, you must define valid attribute mapping values (G3E_ANO) for each of the element tags. See the [Message Format Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BpkKOMrwXQSfSpGNibZFgw) Help topic for more information. 
  * G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE
In the [G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ) table, specify G3E_TYPE definitions for the following parameter: 
ExportMessageNO
Be sure that the above type definition correctly maps to a message number defined inside the [G3E_MESSAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3rSs8kZREniCtp_VMhw~Aw) table and that all related message format and queue metadata is defined as well. 
  * G3E_WORKMGMT
In the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table, specify the G3E_TYPE definitions for the following parameter: 
ModifiedWorkRequestField

##### Send to Generic WMS
Once a design is completed, the user can send job edit information back to the WMS using the [Send to WMS command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j~rlCystpA88BZG7FqPDow). The Send to WMS command uses the NetWorks Core Queue Processing Service DCOM object for sending and receiving messages. Each workstation that runs these commands must have the appropriate queue software loaded for this [DCOM object service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6I_qCdpc57e0Hh0Io9falQ) to run locally. 
Workflow
The following is the software workflow:
  * Check the job identifier name to ensure that this is a WMS job. If the maintenance prefix exists, exit the command after issuing an informative message to the user. 
  * Search for data associated with the job. This search is based upon getting the list of pending edits for the active job. All features returned from this list are processed along with features that have the active job populated inside the Job Last Modified attribute. This ANO is also defined inside the G3E_WORKMGMT table. 
  * Format the export message.
  * Send a message to the defined message queue.
  * Wait for a response up to the time-out limit (if specified).
  * Present the status to the user.


Impact of Export on Other Users
From NetWorks Core, an export operation is the initiation of a client-side command. Another user (different machine) accessing the same job could simultaneously perform a separate export. There is no restriction about multiple users accessing the same job unless you have configured the system with that limitation. Performing an export does not lock out other users from NetWorks Core.

##### Send to WMIS Command (Deprecated)
Once a design is completed, the user can send the compatible unit information back to the WMIS using the [Send to WMIS command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/v7brqAwAkspSW9U1EoRINQ). Costs are determined when the WMIS application accesses the compatible-units (CU) tables that are maintained in the WMS following a successful execution of the command. 
The Send to WMIS command for Logica uses the NetWorks Core Queue Processing Service DCOM object for sending and receiving messages. Each workstation that runs these commands must have the appropriate queue software loaded so that this [DCOM object service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6I_qCdpc57e0Hh0Io9falQ) runs locally. 
Workflow
The following is the software workflow:
  * Check the job identifier name to ensure that this is a WMIS job. If the maintenance prefix exists, it exits the command after issuing an informative message to the user. 
  * Search for data associated with the job. Since this data may or may not already be posted, this is based on the specification of the Primary CU Job ID and Ancillary CU Job ID fields on the CU component definition of the features. The ANOs for these fields are defined in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table (G3E_SUPPORTANO where G3E_TYPE in ('PriCUJobIDField', 'AncCUJobIDField)). The features within the CU component that have the active job ID populated for these Job ID fields are assumed to be part of this job and are processed for export. A trigger populates these Job ID fields as the features are placed and/or edited. Features that have the active job populated inside the Job Placed/Modified attribute are included in the export. The ANO for this field is also defined inside the G3E_WORKMGMT table (G3E_SUPPORTANO = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField'). 
The following query is used to find which features to send to Logica when the Primary CUs and Ancillary CUs are stored in the same table: 
SQL> select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable
where 
PrimaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct A.G3E_FNO, A.G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable A, ModifiedWorkRequestTable B where (B.ModifiedJobField = 'Active Job Name' and A.G3E_FID = B.G3E_FID) 
The following query is used to find which features to send to Logica when the Primary CUs and Ancillary CUs are not stored in the same table: 
SQL> select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable 
where 
PrimaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from AncillaryCUTable 
where 
AncillaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct A.G3E_FNO, A.G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable A, AncillaryCUTable B, ModifiedWorkRequestTable C 
where 
(C.ModifiedJobField = 'Active Job Name' and (A.G3E_FID = C.G3E_FID) or (B.G3E_FID = C.G3E_FID)) PrimaryCUTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'PriCUJobIDField' PrimaryJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'PriCUJobIDField' AncillaryCUTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'AncCUJobIDField' AncillaryJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'AncCUJobIDField' ModifiedWorkRequestTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField' ModifiedJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField'
  * Search for associated work points for each feature found in the queries above using the defined relationships inside the [G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA) interface table (where G3E_TYPE in ('ParentToChildRNO', 'ChildToParentRNO')). 
  * Create new work points if needed. Configuration information about work points is stored inside the G3E_WORKMGMT table (where G3E_TYPE in ('WorkPoint', 'WorkPointAutoGenANO', 'WorkPointWorkRequestField')). Work point offset information is stored in the [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) table. 
  * For each CU record on each feature found, do the following:
    * Verify that the CU value is populated. If it is not, the CU is skipped. Processing continues with the next CU of this feature. If none of the CUs are populated for this feature, an error displays stating that this feature does not contain CU data. Processing then continues with the next feature. 
    * Verify that the Action attribute is populated. If it is not, the CU is skipped and an error displays noting that Action is not set. Processing continues with the next feature. 
    * If the Action is set to Remove, check the G3E_LOGICAFEATURE table to determine which removal activity (Remove or Scrap) to send to Logica. 
    * Check if the CU value was populated during the active job by checking the Job ID. If the Job ID is not set to the active job, change the CU Action to Existing. 
  * Format the export message with the CU data that was not skipped.
  * Send a message to defined message queue.
  * Wait for a response up to the time-out limit.
  * Present the status to user.


Impact of Export on Other Users
From NetWorks Core, an export operation is the initiation of a client-side command. Another user (different machine) accessing the same job could simultaneously perform a separate export. For Logica, WMIS processes these requests in the order they are received in the queue. There is no restriction about multiple users accessing the same job unless you have configured the system with that limitation. Performing an export does not lock out other users from NetWorks Core. 
Logic for Finding Data and Work Points for Export
To pass data to the WMIS, each facility must be associated with a work point. The user may place the work points explicitly, or NetWorks Core can place them automatically. 
The set of features allowed to export to WMIS is defined in the [G3E_LOGICAFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3P4pW21QlBBRb3_Y21P7Nw) metadata table. Also, the activity type (install, remove, scrap, transfer, abandon, and so forth) of the CU entries (primary as well as ancillary) must be non-null so the CU information can be passed to the WMS. Existing data, which is CU data populated in some previous job, is also passed to WMIS if there is CU activity on the feature. If the existing data are from a job other than the current job, the CU activity passes to WMIS as Existing. 
The work point feature is defined in the, [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) metadata table, where G3E_TYPE = 'WorkPoint.' The work point is owned by other features in the data model. These features are typically categorized as structural, although you can configure any feature as the owner. However, when several features exist close together, you only want to send one work point to WMIS. As such, the structural features are a natural choice for owning the other features (like transformers and conductors) and the work point feature. 
For the features that pass CU information to WMIS, the work point feature is found or created as described in the subsequent sections. 
Geographic and Geographic/Detail Features
Point Structures
For point features that are structures (that is, can own a work point), search for the work point as a child of this feature. Since the work point feature class is known, it is straightforward to determine if the work point is a child of the current feature. This can be accomplished either through a review of the relationship information or the [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) table list. If the child work point exists, the compatible unit information of the feature is sent if the activity is not Null. 
If the child work point does not exist, the work point feature is created as a child of this feature using the offset information in G3E_WORKPOINT to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation attribute is set to 1. 
Point Non-Structures
For point features that are children of structures, search for the work point as a sibling of this feature. That implies finding the parent of the current feature and looking for a child work point. If the sibling work point exists, the compatible unit information of the current feature is sent if the activity is not Null. 
If the sibling work point does not exist, the work point feature is created as a child of the parent of the feature using the offset information in [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation attribute is set to 1. 
Linear
Linear features (referred to as spans) can own the work point feature. Their CU information is passed, provided the activity value is not Null. This supports the variable material substitution better than deriving the work points from the two supporting structures. The work points are children to the active linear feature. The linear feature may also have structural features as owners, but this is not used to associate the linear with a work point. 
If the work point feature does not exist, the work point feature is created as a child of this linear using the offset information in [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation attribute is set to 1. 
If the span indicator is false, treat the linear as point non-structure.
Any ancillary CUs for linear features must be passed and associated to the work point record that is created as a child of the linear. 
Detail-Only Features 
Point Structures
If structures are placed in details, then the work point logic is the same as for geographic features. 
Point Non-Structures
For non-structural features, if it has a structure owner in the detail area, the logic is the same as for geographic features. If no owner exists, then search for the work point as a child of the feature defining the detail area. If the work point is found, process as for geographic features. 
If the work point is not found, it is created as a child of the feature defining the detail area. The remaining processing is the same as for geographic features. 
Linears
For linear features, if the feature span indicator is False, treat the linear as point non-structures. If True and the associated child work points are found, process as for geographic features. If the work points are not found, create them as specified in the work management interface definition. The remaining processing is the same as for geographic features.
