##### Creating SAP Remote Function Calls (Deprecated)
Perform the following steps on an SAP machine:
Using the Tools > Abap Workbench > Function Builder:
  1. Create function group or groups to which the RFC belongs.
    1. From the Function Builder dialog box, select GOTO > Function groups > Create group.
    2. Using custom SAP naming conventions, name the function group. You can create one function group for all the RFCs or a separate one for each RFC, as required.   
|  Example ZBAPIPM_CL (for func_loc_class_create), ZBAPIPMFL_CL_UPD (for func_loc_class_upd, or ZBAPI_PM_GIS (for all of the RFCs for NetWorks Core).   |  
| --- |  
    3. Type a short description of the function group.
    4. Click Save.
    5. When the Create Object Directory Entry screen appears, type the custom development class associated with these interfaces. 
  2. Create the RFC:
    1. On the Function Builder screen, type the RFC's name in the Function module field.  
|  Example Z_BAPI_FUNC_CLASS_CREATE  |  
| --- |  
    2. Click Create.
    3. Type the function group name that you created in Step 1 and click Continue (the green check mark). 
    4. On the Function Builder Create: Admin tab, type the application, for example, I for Plant Maintenance. 
    5. Type a short description, and select the Remote Function call supported button.
    6. Click Save.
    7. Select the Source code option.
    8. Using the Utilities > Upload/Download > Upload option, type the text file name that is uploaded, and click Transfer. 
    9. These files are delivered on the NetWorks Core installation CD in the /Program folder and are named to match the RFC.   
|  Example z_bapi_func_loc_class_create.txt  |  
| --- |  
    10. When the file is uploaded, click Save.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261727) You must redefine the import/export/tables/exception parameters documented in the comments in each RFC program. 
  3. Re-create RFC parameters:
    1. On the Interface component of the RFC, select the Import tab.
    2. Type the import parameter, the reference field/structure, and the option or required option. 
Example  
|  Import Parameter  |  Ref Field/Structure   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  FUNCLOC  |  ZSPM_BAPI_FL — flagged as optional   |  
Export:  
|  Export Parameter  |  Ref Field/Structure   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RETURN  |  BAPIRET2   |  
Tables:  
|  Table Parameter  |  Ref Structure   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  I_ZSPM  |  ZSPM_BAPI_CLASS   |  
  4. To activate the RFCs, select the menu Function module > Activate option on the Function Library initial dialog box. 
  5. Test the RFCs using Sngl. on the Function builder dialog box. Type the test data unique to the custom SAP system. 
  6. Configure the NetWorks Core metadata tables required for SAP support. 
  7. Test the NetWorks Core post commands that call these RFCs.

##### Installing RFCs on an SAP Server (Deprecated)
You must create custom structures to support parameters for the RFCs. Perform the following steps on an SAP machine: 
  1. Select Tools > Abap Workbench > Dictionary.
  2. Create the ZSPM_BAPI_FL structure with the following definition:  
|  Field Name  |  Data Element   |  Short Text  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  F_LOC_NUM  |  TPLNR  |  FUNCTIONAL LOCATION  |  
|  STRUC_IND  |  TPLKZ  |  FUNCTIONAL LOCATION STRUCTURE  |  
|  CATEGORY  |  FLTYP  |  FUNCTIONAL LOCATION CATEGORY  |

|  SORT_FIELD  |  EQFNR  |  SORT FIELD  |  
|  FUNC_LOC_POS  |  ILOM_POSNR  |  POSITION IN SUPERIOR FUNCT. LOC  |  
|  EQUI_ALLOWED  |  IEQUI  |  INSTALLATION OF EQUIP  |  
|  PLAN_PLANT  |  IWERK  |  MAINTENANCE PLANNING PLANT  |

##### SAP Custom Interface (Deprecated)
NetWorks Core provides seven [custom remote function calls](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LFMAajlG0zCq2WhbTFkr~w) (RFCs) and a [user exit](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Je10cfo1X5yb1wuwP0A_Pg) that you can use as a guide for developing customized software that interfaces with SAP systems. If the functionality and data structures supported by these RFCs satisfy your requirements, additional software is not required. If additional functionality is required, you can use these RFCs as a guide for writing custom software. However, you cannot make changes to the RFC interface.

##### SAP Remote Function Calls (Deprecated)
NetWorks Core delivers these remote function calls for SAP: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261725) The letter Z denotes a customized function call.   
|  RFC  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Z_BAPI_EQUIPMENT_CHANGE  |  Passes the acquisition, startup date, and serial number (SERGE) for an equipment to the SAP system   |  
|  Z_BAPI_EQUI_CLASS_CREATE  |  Works in update mode. Class/characteristics values are pushed through tables parameter each time a full set of values for class/char is required. There is provision for two classes, one of which must be GIS_SAP_COMMON. This RFC passes class/characteristics for an equipment number to the SAP system.   |  
|  Z_BAPI_EQUI_SYS_STAT  |  Changes the system status from active to inactive for a given equipment number. The GIS SAP interface uses this RFC to set the system status of equipment to INAK in the SAP system.   |  
|  Z_BAPI_FUNC_LOC_CLASS_CREATE  |  Creates a functional location along with its header information and assigns class and characteristics to the functional location. The only class passed is GIS_SAP_COMMON. Each time the RFC is called, full information about class/characteristics is required. The GIS SAP interface uses this RFC to create a function location and assign the class/characteristics in the SAP system.   |  
|  Z_BAPI_FUNC_LOC_CLASS_UPD  |  Updates already existing functional location in SAP. All the information can be updated along with class and characteristics. Full class/characteristics records are required each time this RFC is called. The GIS SAP interface uses this RFC to update a function location and assign the class/characteristics in the SAP system.   |  
|  Z_BAPI_FUNC_LOC_SYS_STAT  |  Changes the system status from active to inactive for a given function location. The GIS SAP interface uses this RFC to set the system status of a function location to INAK in the SAP system.   |  
|  Z_BAPI_USER_STAT_WO  |  Three possible user states are sent from GIS to SAP: GCLS PST PPST Code checks for the job to be not canceled and to be released the sequence of user status should not be changed through customization. The GIS SAP interface uses this RFC to set work order's user status in the SAP system.   |

#### Exporting a Design to STORMS (Deprecated)

##### Send to STORMS Command (Deprecated)
Once a design is completed, the user can send the compatible unit information back to STORMS using the Send to STORMS command. Costs are determined when the STORMS application accesses the compatible-units (CU) tables that are maintained in the STORMS database following a successful execution of the command. 
The data are sent as an estimate, unless the job record in G3E_JOB has been updated to as-built status. It would then be sent as as-built mode. 
You can send only one version of a job back to STORMS at a time.
Workflow
The following is the software workflow:
  * Check the job identifier name to ensure that this is a STORMS job. If the maintenance prefix exists, it exits the command after issuing an informative message to the user. 
  * Search for data associated with the job. Since this data may or may not already be posted, this is based on the specification of the Primary CU Job ID and Ancillary CU Job ID fields on the CU component definition of the features. The ANOs for these fields are defined in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table (G3E_SUPPORTANO where G3E_TYPE = 'PriCUJobIDField', 'AncCUJobIDField'). The features within the CU component that have the active job ID populated for these Job ID fields are assumed to be part of this job and processed for export. A trigger populates these Job ID fields fields as the features are placed/edited. Features that have the active job populated inside the Job Placed/Modified attribute are included in the search. The ANO for this field is defined inside the G3E_WORKMGMT table (G3E_SUPPORTANO where G3E_TYPE = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField'). 
The following query is used to find which features to send to STORMS when the Primary CUs and Ancillary CUs are stored in the same table: SQL> select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable where PrimaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct A.G3E_FNO, A.G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable A, ModifiedWorkRequestTable B 
where 
(B.ModifiedJobField = 'Active Job Name' and A.G3E_FID = B.G3E_FID)
The following query is used to find which features to send to STORMS when the Primary CUs and Ancillary CUs are not stored in the same table 
SQL> select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable
where
PrimaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from AncillaryCUTable 
where 
AncillaryJobField = 'Active Job Name' Union select distinct A.G3E_FNO, A.G3E_FID from PrimaryCUTable A, AncillaryCUTable B, ModifiedWorkRequestTable C where (C.ModifiedJobField = 'Active Job Name' and (A.G3E_FID = C.G3E_FID) or (B.G3E_FID = C.G3E_FID)) PrimaryCUTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'PriCUJobIDField' PrimaryJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'PriCUJobIDField' AncillaryCUTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'AncCUJobIDField' AncillaryJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'AncCUJobIDField' ModifiedWorkRequestTable = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_CNO_TABLE where G3E_TYPE = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField' ModifiedJobField = G3E_WORKMGMT_OPTABLE.G3E_ANO_FIELD where G3E_TYPE = 'ModifiedWorkRequestField'
  * Search for associated work points for each feature found in the queries above using the defined relationships inside the [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA) interface table where G3E_TYPE = 'ParentToChildRNO', 'ChildToParentRNO'. 
  * Create new work points if needed. Configuration information about work points is stored inside the G3E_WORKMGMT table (where G3E_TYPE in ('WorkPoint', 'WorkPointAutoGenANO', 'WorkPointWorkRequestField')). Work point offset information is stored in the [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) table. 
  * For each CU record on each feature found, do the following:
    * Verify that the CU value is populated. If it is not, the CU is skipped. Processing continues with the next CU of this feature. If none of the CUs are populated for this feature, an error displays stating that this feature does not contain CU data. Processing then continues with the next feature. 
    * Verify that the Usage and Activity attributes are populated. If they are not, the CU is skipped and an error displays noting which attribute is not set. Processing continues with the next feature. 
    * If the Activity is set to Remove, check the G3E_STORMSFEATURE table to determine which removal activity (Remove or Scrap) to send to STORMS. 
    * Verify that the CU value was populated during the active job by checking the Job ID. If the Job ID is not set to the active job, the CU is not sent to STORMS. The CU is skipped, and processing continues with the next CU of this feature. 
  * Populate the interface tables within the STORMS database with the CU data that was not skipped. 
  * Call the STORMS database procedure to process the contents of interface tables.
  * Check the error interface table.
  * Present the status to the user.


Impact of Export on Other Users
From NetWorks Core, an export operation is the initiation of a client-side command. Another user on a different machine and accessing the same job could simultaneously perform a separate export. STORMS processes the contents of the interface tables at the time the database procedure is called. There is no restriction about multiple users accessing the same job unless you have configured the system with that limitation. Performing an export does not lock out other users from NetWorks Core. 
Logic for Finding Data and Work Points for Export
To send data to STORMS, each facility must be associated with a work point. The user can place the work points explicitly, or NetWorks Core can place them automatically. 
The set of features that can be exported to STORMS is defined in the [G3E_STORMSFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Xyfm~4koseFL0dou9ndAuQ) metadata table. Also, the activity type (install, remove, scrap, transfer, abandon, and so forth) and usage (pole, light, meter, and so forth) of the CU entries (primary as well as ancillary) must be non-Null so the CU information can be passed to STORMS. Existing data, which is CU data populated in some previous job, is not sent to STORMS. 
The work point feature is defined in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) metadata table, where G3E_TYPE = 'WorkPoint.' The work point is owned by other features in the data model. These features are typically categorized as structural, although you can configure any feature as the owner. However, when several features exist close together, you only want to send one work point to STORMS. As such, the structural features are a natural choice for owning the other features (like transformers and conductors) and the work point feature. 
For the features that pass CU information to STORMS, the work point feature is found or created as described in the subsequent sections. 
Geographic and Geographic/Detail Features
Point Structures
For point features that are structures (that is, they can own a work point), you should search for the work point as a child of this feature. Since the work-point feature class is known, you can determine if the work point is a child of the current feature either by reviewing the relationship information or reviewing the [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) table list. If the child work point exists, the compatible unit information of the feature is sent if the activity is not null. 
If the child work point does not exist, the work point feature is created as a child of this feature using the offset information in G3E_WORKPOINT to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation attribute is set to 1. 
Point Non-Structures
For point features that are children of structures, search for the work point as a sibling of this feature. That implies finding the parent of the current feature and looking for a child work point. If the sibling work point exists, the compatible unit information of the current feature is sent if the activity is not null. If the sibling work point does not exist, the work point feature is created as a child of the parent of this feature using the offset information in [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation is set to 1. 
Linear Features
Linear features (referred to spans) cannot own the work point feature. The work points are children to the active structural owners of the linear feature. If both structural owners are found to have work points, then the linear CU information is passed using a span work- point record containing both structural work-point numbers. This span work-point record is inserted into the STORMS work-point interface table along with all the other work points. The CU activity value cannot be null. 
If the work point feature does not exist for one of the structural owners, the work point feature is created as a child of this structural feature using the offset information in [G3E_WORKPOINT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wwxclBjNoVuPATf0suSI3A) to determine the geographic position of the work point. The work point number is populated, and the automatic generation attribute is set to 1. 
If the span indicator is False, treat the linear as a point non-structure.
Any ancillary CUs for linear features must be associated to the work point record that is created and associated to this linear feature. 
Detail-Only Features
Point Structures
If structures are placed in details, then the work point logic is the same as for geographic features. 
Point Non-Structures
For non-structural features, if it has a structure owner in the detail area, the logic is the same as for geographic features. If no owner exists, then search for the work point as a child of the feature defining the detail area. If the work point is found, process as for geographic features. 
If the work point is not found, it is created as a child of the feature defining the detail area. The remaining processing is the same as for geographic features. 
Linear Features
For linear features, if the feature span indicator is False, then treat the linear as a point non-structure. If True and the associated child work points are found, then process as for geographic features. If the work points are not found, create them as specified in the work management interface definition. The remaining processing is the same as for geographic features.

### IMGS Work Management System Example

#### Creating a Job with IMGS WMS
  * To create a job with IMGS WMS:


  1. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, click Create Job. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256555)
  2. Type a work request number and a description.
  3. Click OK.

#### Getting a Polygon with IMGS WMS
  * To get a polygon with IMGS WMS:


  1. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, click Get Polygon. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256546)
  2. To send a request, type the X/Y coordinates of a point.
  3. Click OK. 
The polygon names are added to the Polygons drop-down list. 
  4. Select the appropriate polygon from the list
The polygon is added to the status bar.

#### Logging In to IMGS WMS
  * To login to IMGS WMS:


  1. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, click Login. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263109)
  2. Type a NetWorks Core user name and password. 
  3. Select the configuration name from the drop-down list. This list is populated from the .ini file. 
  4. Click OK. 
The Jobs tree is populated and buttons are enabled.

#### Performing a Query with IMGS WMS
  * To perform a query with IMGS WMS:


  1. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, type an SQL query in the text box. Do not end the query syntax with a semicolon (;). 
  2. Click Query. 
  3. The query in the text box is sent to the NetWorks Core configuration to which you are logged in. The data are displayed in a data grid or a report window.

#### Reviewing Jobs with IMGS WMS
The Review Jobs drop-down list contains the message ID, message name, and job ID (if it is specified in the message) of jobs that have queued messages. The messages are received from the Export Design, Post, and Partial Post commands. 
  * To review jobs with IMGS WMS: 


  1. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, select the job you want to review from the Review Jobs drop-down list. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/qNp7UpDKgzngoWFdj950dA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=c3757deddc2a946c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Click Accept to accept the message. 
  3. An acceptance message is sent to NetWorks Core through the message queue. 
OR
Click Reject to reject the message. 
  4. If you rejected the message, type a reason for rejecting the message in the dialog box that appears, and click OK.

#### Revising Jobs with IMGS WMS
  * To revise jobs with IMGS WMS:


  1. From the Jobs tree, select a valid job number (contains -1, -2, and so forth) or a valid work management work request number (does not contain a - character, but has some subelements like WORKREQUEST-xx). 
  2. On the IMGS Work Management System example dialog box, click Job Revision. If a work request number is selected, a new job with the next revision number is created (for example, 15591-2 or 15591-3). If a job number (for example 7777-2) is selected, this dialog box appears: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256558)
  3. Click Yes to make the new revision a copy of the displayed job. 
  4. Click No to create a new revision. 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256558) Functionality in the [MessageMonitor](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lYWD_9NHU7BHb5NZXei9sg) determines the next revision number based on metadata definitions and work request number.

  3. Click OK to add the feature to the select set and to fit it into the window.

#### Setting Up the Initialization File
The IMGS Work Management System example is executed by a parameter-driven script file that defines possible configurations, XML fields for message construction, feature IDs to query, and so forth. You can create the input script file by hand in a text file. 
The following are the parameters you need in the IMGSWMS.ini:   
|  Parameter Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Configuration  |  The NetWorks Core configuration for the database you are using   |  
|  MessageName  |  Name of the message sent or received. Stored in [G3E_MESSAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3rSs8kZREniCtp_VMhw~Aw).   |  
|  Query  |  Information required for finding features using the Select button   |  
|  XMLFields  |  Fields for message construction  |  
|  WorkRequest  |  Stored in [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ)  |  
|  Example [Configuration]  
Config1=MECPROD  
Config2=G3EALLPROD  
Config3=COBBEMC  
  
[MessageName]  
GetPolygoneIn=GWMS_GETPOLYGON  
GetPolygoneOut=GWMS_GETPOLYRESPONSE  
CreateJob=GWMS_CREATEJOB  
JobRevision=GWMS_JOBREVISION  
ApproveJob=GWMS_LKDNJOB  
PostJob=GWMS_POSTJOB  
CloseJob=GWMS_CLOSEJOB  
PrePost=GWMS_PREPOST  
PrePostResp=GWMS_PREPOSTRESPONSE  
PostPost=GWMS_POSTPOST  
PostPostResp=GWMS_POSTPOSTRESPONSE  
Export=GWMS_EXPORTJOB  
ExportResp=GWMS_EXPORTRESPONSE  
  
[Query]  
Table=COMMON_N  
Field=G3E_FID  
FieldDescription=Feature Identifier  
  
[XMLFields] ExportJobID=JOB:JOBID  
ExportJobOwner=JOB:JOBOWNER  
GetPolyResponseName=POLY:NAME  
GetPolyResponseType=POLY:TYPE  
ExportResponseStatus=MSG_STATUS  
ExportResponseText=MSG_TEXT  
PrePostResponseStatus=MSG_STATUS  
PrePostResponseText=MSG_TEXT  
PostPostResponseStatus=MSG_STATUS  
PostPostResponseText=MSG_TEXT  
CreateJobWRNo=CRJOB:WORK_REQUEST  
CreateJobWRVersion=CRJOB:VERSION  
CreateJobPolygon=CRJOB:ADDITIONALINFO  
CreateJobDesc=CRJOB:G3E_DESCRIPTION  
CreateJobDate=CRJOB:G3E_CREATION  
CloseJobWRNo=CLJOB:WORK_REQUEST  
CloseJobWRVersion=CLJOB:VERSION  
ApproveJobWRNo=LKDNJOB:WORK_REQUEST  
ApproveJobWRVersion=LKDNJOB:VERSION  
JobRevisionWRNo=JOBREV:WORK_REQUEST  
JobRevisionJobID=JOBREV:JOBID  
PostJobWRNo=POSTJOB:WORK_REQUEST  
PostJobWRVersion=POSTJOB:VERSION  
  
[WorkRequest]  
Field=WORK_REQUEST   |  
| --- |

#### Starting the NetWorks Core Work Management System Example
The following sample workflow interfaces to existing NetWorks Core software and metadata. 
  * To use the NetWorks Core WMS Work Management System:


  1. In the \GTechnology\Program folder, run IMGS_WMS.exe. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/KyE5cEubq3_CM9_PQ7cTvA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=da9f7cdd3db8fde0&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)  
|  User Interface Item  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Jobs  |  Frame that contains controls for selecting and filtering jobs. The job list is not populated until you log in. Requests for data should be made with the JobHelper's ConnectionObject property. Traverse to the IDataContext property of the object to get the database access for recordset creation.   |  
|  Job tree  |  Lists jobs by identifier or group by work request. The subelements are the actual jobs or revisions of the work request.   |  
|  Date  |  Filters jobs to those created within the last week. You can change the timeframe as required.   |  
|  Current User  |  Checkbox that filters the job list by the current user; can be combined with the date filter by selecting both at the same time.   |  
|  Refresh  |  Redisplays the job tree applying the current filters. Accommodates changes from job life cycle or the operations of the user that either added to or removed jobs.   |  
|  Status bar  |  Contains fields to represent the active job, the active polygon, and the current configuration.  |  
|  Approve Job  |  Operates on the job currently selected in the tree. Initiates sending a message to NetWorks Core. Updates the job record and initiates a job life cycle operation to discard other revisions and to post the job data in its current state (no transition).   |  
|  Post Job  |  Operates on the job currently selected in the tree. Initiates sending a message to NetWorks Core. Updates the job record and initiates a job life cycle operation to post the job.   |  
|  Close Job  |  Initiates the close operation by sending a message to process in the job life cycle. The prepost message is configured in the application. The application checks for this message and returns a failure message if a certain condition is not met.   |  
|  View Messages  |  Indicates if you want to see all the messages before they are sent or after they are received (inbound or response messages). Each message automatically displays in [XML format using the Internet Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/12IvffAMk3TemcGiHk~sSw) object as soon as the message queue from Message Monitor raises an event with a message.   |  
|  Launch  |  Starts NetWorks Core with the currently selected job as the active job.   |  
|  Activate Job  |  Makes the currently selected job active in the NetWorks Core session.   |  
You must start the [MessageMonitor](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lYWD_9NHU7BHb5NZXei9sg) service to test the following functions: 
     * Get Polygon
     * Create Job
     * Job Revision
     * Approve Job
     * Post Job
     * Close Job 
You must start the Message Monitor service and the [Job Life Cycle](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/C10rbfMdxaVIwwBNLidqEw) service to test the following functions: 
     * Approve Job
     * Post Job
     * Close Job
  2. Click Login. You can now use the following functions: 
     * [Get Polygon](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/HtrJykKgRWZWTxZCo6LZ7Q)
     * [Create Job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_QvZBWwT6N6IfBJoOC9Nfg)
     * [Job revision](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CwQxCOXLl6gxic8AbEgFrA)
     * [Approve J](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bGFzrCp56du3R2~2ltntYg)ob 
     * Post Job
     * Close Job
     * [Review a job message](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/u6y2UKK9dVYgjY5ppl1pjA)
     * Launch NetWorks Core
  3. Click Launch. You can now use the following functions: 
     * [Select feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/g0ufngtyH8RRcRIEhvaHQw)
     * [Activate Job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bGFzrCp56du3R2~2ltntYg)
     * [Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5Mgv9kPMFAye1mPqpyJbzA)

#### Viewing Messages with IMGS WMS
Check View Messages to automatically view messages you are sending or receiving from NetWorks Core to the queue system with the Job Revision, Get Polygon, Create Job, Approve Job, Post Job, and Close Job functions. Click OK to dismiss the Review Message dialog box. This is an example message:

#### Job Definitions Table
All job processing inside NetWorks Core is controlled through a database table known as the job table. This table is part of the data model and is, therefore, not delivered by the metadata creation procedures. Its contents are configurable for each site and are controlled through metadata. The metadata table, [G3E_JOBDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TBQDr_BsRYh8ej2Rr97t2g), defines the name of the job table. It also maps job fields to fields defined in the job table itself. The following is an example of this table:   
|  G3E_JNO  |  1  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Default  |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  JOBTABLE  |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIERFIELD  |  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTIONFIELD  |  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  
|  G3E_OWNERFIELD  |  G3E_OWNER  |  
|  G3E_STATUSFIELD  |  G3E_STATUS  |  
|  G3E_CREATIONDATEFIELD  |  G3E_CREATION  |  
|  G3E_POSTEDDATEFIELD  |  G3E_POSTED  |  
|  G3E_CLOSEDDATEFIELD  |  G3E_CLOSED  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  10/12/05  |  
|  G3E_ALLOWCONCURRENTJOBACCESS  |  1  |  
|  G3E_RESTRICTTORESPONSIBLEUSER  |  G3E_OWNER  |  
|  G3E_PROCESSINGSTATUSFIELD  |  G3E_PROCESSINGSTATUS  |  
|  G3E_JOBCOMPAREFIELD  |  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  
|  G3E_CREATEFIELDJOBS  |  MAINT%  |  
|  G3E_CLASSIFICATIONFIELD  |  G3E_JOBCLASS  |  
|  G3E_JOBSTATEFIELD  |  G3E_JOBSTATE  |  
The job table, as defined by the G3E_JOBDEFINITION table, displays a list of the jobs that are available for NetWorks Core users. Both open and closed jobs are displayed in this table. The population of and updates to this table are managed through the Job commands and LTT procedures that process and handle the job management aspect of NetWorks Core. 
The fields that are defined for the job table are defined as attributes within NetWorks Core and are, therefore, associated with a component in the data model. The component definition for these attributes is defined as other feature components, with the exception that the job component is not part of any feature. The following example shows this component definition. Not all columns are shown.   
|  G3E_CNO  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  G3E_NAME  |  G3E_TOOLTIP  |  G3E_TYPE  |  G3E_TABLE  |  G3E_DETAIL  |  G3E_DCNO  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  90  |  Job Attributes  |  G3E_JOBATTR  |  Job Attributes  |  1  |  G3E_JOB  |  0  |  1  |

### Job Setup

#### Job Setup—Generic
When a GIS work request is created in the work management system, it sends an XML based message to the queue. The NetWorks Core [MessageMonitor](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ) program receives the message from the queue and creates a corresponding NetWorks Core job in GIS database. 
The following are the parameters in the message:
  * Polygon type attribute
  * Polygon name attribute
  * Coordinate system.


You can derive the coordinate system from the database configuration specified as part of the connection information to the process. The coordinate system definition is stored in GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE. The definition is referenced by G3E_DATACONNECTION and G3E_CONFIGURATIONS. 
The polygon information is defined by new entries in the G3E_TYPE field of the G3E_WORKMGMT. The following entries are necessary:   
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Populated Field  |  Content Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  WorkManagementPolygon  |  G3E_PARAMETER1  |  Feature number of the polygon feature  |  
|  WorkManagementPolygonType  |  G3E_SUPPORTANO  |  Attribute number (G3E_ANO) of the attribute within the published component view for the primary graphic component of the WorkManagementPolygon feature that contains the type or classification attribute. This attribute would typically contain a value like TAX, SCHEDULING, LOCAL, or COUNTY. This value is returned with the polygon's name. Specific values associated with a particular configuration are identified in the project-specific metadata documentation.   |  
|  WorkManagementPolygonName  |  G3E_SUPPORTANO  |  Attribute number (G3E_ANO) of the attribute within the published component view for the primary graphic component of the WorkManagementPolygon feature that contains the name of the polygon. This value is returned with the polygon's type.   |

##### Installing User Exit on the SAP Server (Deprecated)
To upload the user exit, you create an add-on project and upload the text file of the user exit. Perform the following steps on an SAP machine: 
Using the Tools > Abap Workbench, select the following menu options: Utilities > Enhancements > Project Management. 
  * To install user exit on the SAP server:


  1. Enter the Project Name ZPMWORK, and select Project > Create. 
  2. Type a brief description in the short text field, and click SAP Enhancement. 
The Create Object Folder Entry screen appears.
  3. Type the development class associated with this user exit, and click Continue (green check mark). 
The SAP Enhancements in Enhancement Project ZPMWORK dialog box appears.
  4. Select the drop-down option on the first empty enhancement field.
The enhancements box appears.
  5. Click Continue (green check mark).
A list of available enhancements displays.
  6. Scroll down to development class (DCL) to IW01 IWO10009 PM order: Customer check at time 'Save'. 
  7. To select this enhancement, use the checkbox and the Copy option.
  8. Save this project, and return to the SAP Enhancements Project Management dialog box.
Your ZPMWORK project is still displayed in the Project field.
  9. Select the Enhancements Components button and then the Change button.
  10. Select the Edit Component button.
The exit_saplcoih_010 function displays.
  11. Double-click the include file ZXWOCU07. 
A Create Object dialog box appears asking you if you want to create this object.
  12. Select YES to create this include file.
The Program attributes dialog box appears.
  13. Type the Title and Application I. 
  14. Select Save, and type the Create Object Directory Entry information.
  15. Select the Source Code option.
  16. After you create the include file, use the Utilities > Upload/Download > Upload option to upload the user exit text file ZXWOCU07.txt. 
  17. Save the include file.
  18. To activate the project, select the Activate Project button on the SAP Project Management enhancements dialog box .

### Message Queue Processing

#### Considerations When Creating a Message Format
When creating message formats it is important to include certain format types, specified by G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE. The incoming XML message that is passed to the Job Processing Service is processed based on the action specified by G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION. Each action has expected message format types associated with it that are necessary for the correct processing of incoming and outgoing messages. The following describes the format types required by each action, as well as some other processing considerations. 
1 & 2: Convert Input Point to NetWorks Core Database Coordinates
G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION values of 1 or 2 identify a request to convert an input point to NetWorks Core database coordinates. The input point is in decimal degrees for G3E_ACTION=1 or radians for G3E_ACTION=2. The Job Processing Service retrieves the X and Y point values from the incoming XML message and converts them to NetWorks Core database coordinates. The converted values are returned in the outgoing message. 
When using either of these actions both a G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING and G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_OUTGOING message are specified. The incoming message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values "X" and "Y" defined. These are used to identify the X and Y input point values in the incoming XML message that should be converted. The outgoing message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values "X" and "Y" defined. These values are used to identify the X and Y converted coordinate values for the outgoing message. 
[Metadata Example](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/480796)

3: Find Polygons (Names and Types)
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 3 identifies a request to retrieve work management polygon names and types that contain the input point (in NetWorks Core database coordinates). The Job Processing Service retrieves the X and Y point values from the incoming XML message and performs a spatial query to find all work management polygons that touch that point. The names and types of those polygons are returned in the outgoing message. 
When using this action both a G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING and G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_OUTGOING message are specified. The incoming message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values "X" and "Y" defined. These are used to identify the X and Y coordinate values, representing the input point, in the incoming XML message. The outgoing message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values ‘POLYGON_NAME’ and ‘POLYGON_TYPE’ defined. These are used to identify the work management polygon name and type values in the outgoing message that contain the retrieved work management polygon information. The G3E_WORKMGMT.G3E_TYPE values ‘WorkManagementPolygon’, ‘WorkManagementPolygonType’, and ‘WorkManagementPolygonName’ are required to identify the work management polygon feature, type attribute, and name attribute used for this processing.

4: Create Record in the NetWorks Core Job Table
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 4 identifies a request to create a new record in the NetWorks Core job table and populate its fields with the input field values. The Job Processing Service retrieves the work request name, and work request number if provided, from the incoming XML message which it uses to create a new job. 
When using this action only the G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING message name needs to be specified. The incoming message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘WR_NAME’ defined. It is used to identify the work request name for the new job. If it is not defined the new job record is not created. The ‘WR_NO’ can also be defined to identify the work request number for a LOGICA WMS. Additional attribute values can be specified in the message which would map to attributes in the job table. 
The job identifier for the new job is formatted as work request name + "-" + work request number. For example: if the work request name is ‘12345’ and the work request number is 1 then the job identifier would be formatted as ‘12345-1’. If the ‘WR_NO’ type is specified for the incoming message its associated value is only honored as the work request number if the WMS is LOGICA. In all other cases the work request number defaults to 1. 
For a LOGICA WMS the create job processing validates the job identifier against existing job identifiers in the job table. If it is not unique an error is thrown. If the WMS is not LOGICA the create job processing validates that the work request name does not already exist in the job table. If it is not unique an error is thrown.

6: Create Record in the Job Status Table
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 6 identifies a request to create a record in the NetWorks Core job status table and set the status based on the value defined for G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_JLCNO. The Job Processing Service retrieves the work request name and work request number from the incoming XML message which it uses when creating a record in the job status table. 
When using this action only the G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING message name needs to be specified. The incoming message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘WR_NAME’ defined. It is used to identify the work request name that is set on the new job record. Optionally, the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘WR_NO’ can be defined. It is used to identify the work request number. If it is not provided then a default of 1 is used. The job identifier for the new job status record is formatted as work request name + "-" + work request number. For example: if the work request name is ‘12345’ and the work request number is 1 then the job identifier would be formatted as ‘12345-1’. The status values for the new job status record are defined by the job life cycle metadata specified by G3E_JLCNO for the message metadata. The G3E_STATUS_CODE for the new job status record is set to "NEW". The Job Life Cycle service queries the G3E_JOBSTATUS table and process the rows based on the value in WR_STATE_CODE. This value maps to G3E_WR_STATE_CODE in G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE.

7: Create Record in the Job Status Table and Update NetWorks Core Job Table
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 7 identifies a request to create a record in the NetWorks Core job status table and update the NetWorks Core job table. The Job Processing Service processes this action like a G3E_ACTION of 6 (Create Record in the Job Status Table) followed by a G3E_ACTION of 5 (Update NetWorks Core Job Table) both documented above. 
8: Parse the Export Response Message
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 8 identifies a request to parse the export response message for status and text elements. The Job Processing Service retrieves the text and status values from the incoming XML message which it uses to populate the response text and response status. 
When using this action the G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING message name and the G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_OUTGOING message name are specified. The incoming message is expected to have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values ‘TEXT’ and ‘STATUS’ defined. The values for these types are retrieved from the incoming message and returned in the response. The outgoing message would typically have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE values ‘FeatureNS’, ‘FeatureName’, ‘FNO’, ‘FID’, ‘FeatureDeleted’, ‘ComponentNS’, ‘ComponentName’, ‘CNO’, ‘CID’, ‘JobInfoNS’, ‘JobID’, ‘GTKEYS’ specified. These values are used to describe feature instances in the pending edits. As an example, the Before and After post messages, specified by G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE for G3E_TYPE values ‘BeforePostMessageNO’ and ‘AfterPostMessageNO’, are used to identify the features in the pending edits for the job. The above message numbers map to G3E_MSGNO in G3E_MESSAGE.

9: Create a Job Revision
A G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_ACTION value of 9 identifies a request to create a new job revision in the NetWorks Core job table. The Job Processing Service retrieves the work request name, and optionally the copy job identifier, from the incoming XML message which it uses when creating the job revision. 
When using this action only the G3E_MESSAGE.G3E_INCOMING message name needs to be specified. The incoming message must have the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘WR_NAME’ defined. It is used to identify the work request name that a new job revision is created for. If it isn’t defined no job revision is created. Optionally, the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘JobID’ can be defined. If it is defined for the incoming message it indicates that the data for that job identifier is to be copied to the new job revision. 
The new revision number is determined as follows: 
  * If a G3E_REVISIONNEXTFIELD is specified in G3E_JOBDEFINITION then the job table is queried for the maximum value for this field where the work request name matches the input work request name. This value is used as the new revision number. 
  * If a G3E_REVISIONFIELD is specified in G3E_JOBDEFINITION, but G3E_REVISIONNEXTFIELD is not, then the job table is queried for the maximum value for this field where the work request name matches the input work request name. This value is incremented by 1 and used as the new revision number. 
  * If neither the G3E_REVISIONNEXTFIELD nor the G3E_REVISIONFIELD are specified in G3E_JOBDEFINITION, or if no values exist for either field in the job table, then the job table is queried where the work request name matches the input work request name and the returned job identifier values analyzed. The job identifier is parsed to retrieve the value on the right side of the "-" character. The maximum value is incremented by one and used as the new revision number. 
  * If a new revision number cannot be determined an error is thrown.


If the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT.G3E_TYPE value ‘JobID’ was defined for this message the Job Processing Service retrieves the associated job identifier from the incoming XML message. Note: If this value does not contain the character "-" it is ignored. The data from the specified job is copied to the newly created job revision. If a G3E_REVISIONNEXTFIELD is specified in G3E_JOBDEFINITION then the new job revision record is updated with the next job revision number (current revision number incremented by 1).

#### Message Format Tool

##### Copying a Message Format
You can use a current message format and add or delete components and attributes to create the format for another message. 
  * To copy a message format:


  1. In the \GTechnology\Program folder, run MessageFormatTool.exe. 
  2. In the NetWorks Core Login dialog box, type the username and password, and select the configuration name for the NetWorks Core configuration from which you want to send messages, and click OK. 
  3. Select a message name from the Active message name drop-down field. 
  4. Type a new message name in the Message name field, and click any other field or select an existing message name. 
  5. Click Copy to. 
The following message appears:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256442)
  6. Click Yes to delete existing records for the current message before inserting new records. 
  7. Click No to append records to the current message records. 
  8. Follow Steps 5-7 in [Creating a New Standard Message Format](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xWP0MkeoJTNfbElc1V_Yug) to complete your message. 


Related Topics
[Creating a Custom Message Format](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/26E3OCcn2WlJRDR4UotY~Q)
[Creating a New Standard Message Format](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xWP0MkeoJTNfbElc1V_Yug)
[Message Format Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BpkKOMrwXQSfSpGNibZFgw)

##### Creating a Custom Message Format
If the standard message format does not meet the requirements of your NetWorks Core application, you can create a custom message. The format for a custom message is prescribed by the software sending or receiving the message, so you have to know how the message should look before you create the format for it. Generally, custom messages are sent from a work management system to NetWorks Core. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256445) You can copy the format of a previous standard or custom message and create a custom message. 
  * To create a custom message:


  1. In the \GTechnology\Program folder, run MessageFormatTool.exe. 
  2. In the NetWorks Core Login dialog box, type the username and password, and select the configuration name for the NetWorks Core configuration from which you want to send messages, and click OK. 
  3. Type the new message name in the Active message name field, and press ENTER. 
  4. Click Custom. 
  5. Click the Active message elements grid. 
The grid is blank, the message name appears in the Active message name field, and the components and attributes in the configuration are listed in the Attributes field. The attribute tree displays attributes for all components in your specific NetWorks Core configuration. 
  6. Type or select the parent tag name.
  7. Check the components and attributes required for the new message, and click >> to add them to the grid. 
  8. Click Review to see the format of the message 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256445)
  9. To delete items from the grid, select rows in the grid, and press DELETE. To select more than one consecutive row from the grid, highlight the first row, press SHIFT, and highlight the last row. You cannot select non-consecutive rows from the grid. 
OR
Uncheck items in the Attributes list, and click >>. The items disappear from the grid. 
  10. To move items up or down in the grid, select rows in the grid, and click the ordinal buttons. To select more than one consecutive row from the grid, highlight the first row, press SHIFT, and highlight the last row. You cannot select non-consecutive rows from the grid. 
  11. Click Discard to clear the grid, and start over. 
  12. When the message is formatted correctly, click Apply. 
The message format definitions are added to the [G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s9GcPFxUsogokTRUglTFow) table.

##### Creating a New Standard Message Format
A standard message contains specific information and has a specific format.
  * To create standard XML messages from scratch:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Message Format Tool. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256436)
  2. In the NetWorks Core Login dialog box, type the username and password, select the configuration name for the NetWorks Core configuration from which you want to send messages, and click OK. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/xzieQJw5Jhxhzfu_GVueuA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=a19d0f401f4a00b5&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. Type the new message name in the Active message name field. 
  4. Click the Active message elements grid. 
The grid is blank, the message name appears in the Active message name field, and the components and attributes in the configuration are listed in the Attributes field. The attribute tree displays attributes for all components in your specific NetWorks Core configuration. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256436) The XML message does not send graphic attributes. Each component node has a GTKeys child node (G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CNO, and G3E_CID). A component's GTKeys child node is automatically checked when you check any attribute of the component. 
  5. Check the components and attributes required for the new message, and click >> to add them to the grid. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256436) The Format type is predefined in the [G3E_MESSAGEFORMATTYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ReDFJixXZpmIWABC~bMNIQ) table. 
  6. Click Review to see the format of the message. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/pznmEWm9qKb55uGmZbH1fQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=8b5e4906a229d728&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
    1. Select the required features. To select more than one consecutive feature from the list, highlight the first feature, press SHIFT, and highlight the last feature. To select more than one non-consecutive feature from the list, press CTRL as you highlight each feature. 
    2. Check Job information to include job information in your message format. 
  7. Click OK. 
Example
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256436)
  8. To add more items to the grid:
    1. Click the grid where you want to add more items and check the item you want to add.
    2. Click >>. 
    3. Click Review, select features to include in the message, and click OK to see the format of the message. 
  9. To delete items from the grid, select rows in the grid, and press DELETE. To select more than one consecutive row from the grid, highlight the first row, press SHIFT, and highlight the last row. You cannot select non-consecutive rows from the grid. 
OR
Uncheck items in the Attributes list, and click >>. The items disappear from the grid. 
  10. To move items up or down in the grid, select rows in the grid, and click the ordinal buttons. To select more than one consecutive row from the grid, highlight the first row, press SHIFT, and highlight the last row. You cannot select non-consecutive rows from the grid. 
  11. To clear the grid and start over, click Discard. 
  12. When the message is formatted correctly, click Apply. 
The message format definitions are added to the [G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s9GcPFxUsogokTRUglTFow) table.

#### Message Queue Processing Metadata
Messages are used to pass information back and forth between NetWorks Core and any work management system that uses messages to communicate. The messages and their formats, queue names, types, and actions are configured in metadata. 
  * To configure message queue processing:


  1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Work Management > Logica WMS Interface > Queues node. 
  2. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261721), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  3. Populate the new row in the [G3E_QUEUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zo8XGsEl0tTLdslL6Qu5gg) table: 
    1. In the G3E_NAME field, type a name for the queue.
    2. In the G3E_DATACONNECTION field, select the data connection name from the drop- down list. 
    3. In the G3E_TYPE field, select the type of queue.
    4. In the G3E_MACHINENAME field, type the name of the machine that has this queue.
    5. In the G3E_LABEL field, type a description for the queue.
    6. In the G3E_AUTOCREATE field, select if you want the queue to be created automatically if it does not already exist. 
    7. In the G3E_PRIVATE field, select Yes if the queue should be private and No if the queue should be public. 
    8. In the G3E_RESPONSECORRELATION field, indicate the way to set the CorrelationID of the response message. 
    9. Click OK. 
  4. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, select the Work Management > Logica WMS Interface > Messages node. 
  5. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261721), or right-click and select Insert a new row. 
  6. Populate the new row in the [G3E_MESSAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3rSs8kZREniCtp_VMhw~Aw) table: 
    1. In the G3E_INCOMING field, select the incoming message name from the drop-down list.
    2. In the G3E_G3E_INQUEUENO field, select the incoming queue from the drop-down list.
    3. In the G3E_ACTION field, select the action to be performed by the message.
    4. In the G3E_OUTGOING field, select the outgoing message name from the drop-down list.
    5. In the G3E_OUTQUEUENO field, select the outgoing queue from the drop-down list.
    6. In the G3E_ERRORQUEUENO field, select the error queue from the drop-down list.
    7. In the JLCNO field, select the job life cycle number. This field is populated only when G3E_ACTION is Create job status record based on G3E_JLCNO (6) or Update job record and create job status record (7). 
    8. In the G3E_TIMEOUT field, type a time period in seconds for NetWorks Core to listen for a response message on the G3E_INCOMING queue. 
  7. Populate the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT table. Each row in this table specifies an XML element tag name and the G3E_ANO for the value. Use the [Message Format Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BpkKOMrwXQSfSpGNibZFgw) to populate this table. 
  8. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261721) to commit your edits to the database.

#### Messaging Test Application
The Messaging Test Application supports the simulation of sending messages to and receiving messages from a work management system. To fully test that your system is both sending and receiving messages, you should open two instances of the tool so you can see the messages and the responses. The following metadata tables must be populated for messaging, and you must [publish the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/liGwSHeRBi9gFccnbK5oiQ) before you can run the Messaging Test Application: 
[G3E_MESSAGE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3rSs8kZREniCtp_VMhw~Aw)
[G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s9GcPFxUsogokTRUglTFow)
[G3E_QUEUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zo8XGsEl0tTLdslL6Qu5gg)
  * To run the Messaging Test Application:


  1. At the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and run MessagingTestApp.exe. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/MtMP5Cr2OUQWM9afWLQoig-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=321c2b577e9c941e&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. In the Configuration name list, select the configuration for which you want to send or receive messages. 
You can select only one configuration at a time.
  3. In the Login dialog box, type the username and password for the configuration. 
When a configuration name is selected, the Message name list populates with distinct G3E_MESSAGE_OPTABLE.G3E_INCOMING and G3E_MESSAGE_OPTABLE.G3E_OUTGOING field values. If the G3E_MESSAGE_OPTABLE or G3E_QUEUE_OPTABLE table does not exist or if there is no message name available in the metadata, a message cannot be sent or listened for from that configuration. You can select a different configuration. 
  4. From the Message name list, select a message to send or receive. You can select only one message at a time. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/CU8JZ2oqJMnw2O0PX6a0eQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=be5d2ff2657fa5b5&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  5. The Message tags grid automatically populates with records from the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT_OPTABLE table for the selected message name. You cannot add to or delete from the grid. If the selected message format is not configured, the grid is empty. 
  6. The following are the message tags and their descriptions:  
  
|  Message Tag  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Element Tag  |  Lists element tags specified in the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT_OPTABLE. G3E_ELEMENTTAGNAME.  |  
|  G3E_FIELD  |  Lists field names for tags that have an ANO association.  |  
|  Data Type  |  Lists G3E field data types that have an ANO association.  |  
|  Value  |  You can type values in this field. The values are not restricted to NetWorks Core [data types](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~h41yaBjEX7V3RPf~WGcFw). All values are passed as text.   |  
  7. To provide correlation for sending a response to a previously received message, type the previously received message ID in the Correlation ID field. 
  8. Optional: To review, edit, or type an XML message to send, click Refresh. 
The XML message displays in the Message box for review or edit. The message format of the selected message is retrieved from the G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT_OPTABLE. You can modify the text in the Message box, but the edits are not reflected in the Message tags grid. The Message box has the following purposes: 
When the message format is configured, you can review and edit the generated XML document before sending the message. 
When the message format is not configured, you can type an XML message to send.
  9. In the Listen time field, type the maximum time (in minutes) that the application should listen for a response for the selected sent message or from the queue of the selected message. The default is 1 minute. 
If you set the value in the Listen time field to 0, the application is in constant listening mode. So, when it receives a message, it displays the message and keeps on listening. If you set the Listen time to 0, you must use the Task Manager to stop the listening process. 
  10. Check Listen for response from send to allow listening for a response from the sent message up to a time period specified in Listen time field. The response displays in the Message box. The application stops listening after the specified listen time period. The application uses metadata to find out the [queue name](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zo8XGsEl0tTLdslL6Qu5gg) to listen for the selected message. 
  11. To send the selected message type and the message tag values, click Send. 
  12. To listen for the selected message, click Listen for Incoming.

#### Configuring the System for Generic Work Management
The Generic Work Management System (WMS) provides multiple ways of interacting with NetWorks Core for common work management functions. The WMS uses a metadata configurable XML [messaging architecture](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j3dODE7yUK4XgK5dffnpqg) for communication between products. External message processing is provided by a [MessageMonitor Service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lYWD_9NHU7BHb5NZXei9sg). You can use the Generic WMS as delivered with NetWorks Core, or you can use the [Generic Work Management automation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ygp7GxIqyhg9n94GlYlJAw) which supports the interaction between a specific work management application and NetWorks Core and provide a means for accessing NetWorks Core functionality from within another application environment already familiar to users. 
The following are the integration points between NetWorks Core and the Generic WMS: 
  * Job Setup
The interface supports converting a lat/long coordinate to a NetWorks Core database coordinate. It also supports the requesting the names and types of the containing polygons for a given point. All of the polygons found are returned. The NetWorks Core message software provides processing.   
|  Example An external system needs database point information based upon external coordinate information (lat/long) The external system uses this database coordinate to request polygon(s) to assign to a work request (job) being created.   |  
| --- |  
  * Job Initiation
The WMS notifies NetWorks Core to create a job associated with a new work request and updates the Work Request/Job record information using messaging or triggers at specified points in the work management system workflow. The system also supports creation of non-work request jobs in NetWorks Core, for example, maintenance jobs, whose names are prefixed with "MAINT" and, which are never passed back to the work management system. 
  * Job Management
Work request revision processing is equivalent to a NetWorks Core job. Alternate design/revisions are created in NetWorks Core retain the same work request identifier, but the revision number is incremented. Available jobs can be filtered by the responsible person for controlling access through the [Job Environment](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/H0oMaEEu48VNP7XQP~CndA) and [Select Job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0P01jGw8RVtD3NL1e3Uaog) dialog boxes. 
  * Export of Engineering Design
When a user initiates the Export to WMS command, the following happens:
Features associated with the current active job and those that have the Job Last Modified attribute marked are processed. 
The command sends an export message, defined in metadata, and success or fail responses, if configured, can be returned to the user. 
Workpoints/PointSpans are not required for export of data.
The command uses [DCOM](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6I_qCdpc57e0Hh0Io9falQ) to send and receive messages independent of the Message Monitor Service. 
  * Job Life Cycle
At each significant work request event in the WMS, the interface manipulates the job data using [Messaging](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j3dODE7yUK4XgK5dffnpqg) and [Job Life Cycle processing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mSl5PizaLmQ2J6Uj9QtPuw). Events are configured using metadata (G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE). WMS event examples include Lockdown, Close, Cancel, Field Complete, and QA Complete. 
Post notification processing is also supported. For example, messages are sent to the WMS before and after posting a job. The response messaging is configurable. The [NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CvlskSKcYAGysNAmFC1xhw) processes job transitions using the JobLifeCycle batch program.   
|  Example An oncoming Job Life Cycle message is processed and entry placed in G3E_JOBSTATUS. The NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service retrieves the entry and calls the JobLifeCycle batch program to process the job.   |  
| --- |  
  * Launch GIS
[LaunchGIS ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/k626O2SXCxJMJxjpUqDyxA)is a standalone batch executable that launches NetWorks Core. The tool allows the WMS to instantiate NetWorks Core from within the WMS software. You must pass a fixed configuration name to the program, and login and job information can also be passed. If a features is defined and/or associated with the work request and/or job, LaunchGIS zooms the window in on the feature. 
If your system uses the NetWorks Core Generic WMS, you must configure the Generic Work Management server. Also, if you are creating a new schema, in [SetUpgradeEnv(CONFIGURATIONNAME).bat](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/siHnpyLxZ2Hz7PE4ZQ~Nig) located in the \GTechnology\Services\AutoUpgrade, verify that the variable for installing default Generic functionality is set to "Y." 


  * To set up the Generic WMS server:


The Generic WMS uses the [MessageMonitor and MessageMonitor service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ) to communicate with NetWorks Core. 
  1. On the Instance Specific tab of the Initialization Parameters in the Oracle Instance Manager, set the global_names parameter to False to allow maximum flexibility in naming the database link. 
  2. On the Oracle Schema Manager Fixed User Connection, set up a public database link between the WMIS instance and the Generic Work Management instance.

#### Configuring the System for Logica (Deprecated)
The architecture behind the Logica Work Management Information System (WMIS) is based on a centralized message hub called an Integration Framework. The WMIS Integration Framework can be used to define, create, and send messages between WMIS and any other application. You can use WMIS tables and/or views to configure messages. Standard inbound messages are provided with WMIS. The utility company can create outbound messages for any application, including the outbound messages that become inbound messages to WMIS (for example, the outbound message from NetWorks Core to create a new work request in WMIS). 
If your system uses the WMIS from Logica, you must configure both the GIS server and the WMIS server. Also, if you are creating a new schema, in [SetUpgradeEnv(CONFIGURATIONNAME).bat](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/siHnpyLxZ2Hz7PE4ZQ~Nig) located in the \GTechnology\Services\AutoUpgrade, verify that the variable for installing default Logica functionality is set to "Y." 
  * To set up the GIS server for WMIS:


  1. On the Instance Specific tab of the Initialization Parameters in the Oracle Instance Manager, set the global_names parameter to False to allow maximum flexibility in naming the database link. 
  2. On the Oracle Schema Manager Fixed User Connection, set up a public database link between the GIS instance and the WMIS instance (for example, WMIS.WORLD). 
  3. Set up the following synonyms for the GIS schema. All of these synonyms must use the database link established through the Remote Database option. 
CONSTRUCTION_UNIT
INIT_ASSEMBLY
CU_STANDARD_ATTRIBUTE
CU_CATEGORY_ATTRIBUTE
CU_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE
  4. Using an SQL editor, log in as the NetWorks Core database user to execute the following script: 
SQL>@GTechnology\plsql\WMS\wmoninsertg3e_job.sql; 
You can edit this file to match your job table definitions. See the Readme.txt file in the WMS folder for more installation information. 


  * To set up the WMIS server:


The WMIS interfaces uses the [MessageMonitor and MessageMonitor service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ) to communicate with NetWorks Core. 
  1. On the Instance Specific tab of the Initialization Parameters in the Oracle Instance Manager, set the global_names parameter to False to allow maximum flexibility in naming the database link. 
  2. On the Oracle Schema Manager Fixed User Connection, set up a public database link between the WMIS instance and the GIS instance (for example, ETPROD.WORLD).

### The Job Life Cycle

#### Configuring the JobLifeCycle Program
The JobLifeCycle executable delivered with NetWorks Core performs batch processing activities on a job using a command argument and allows updates and state transitions to occur against a job that has been updated within a work management system. A NetWorks Core work request is generated through a work management system, and a corresponding NetWorks Core job is created through a trigger for the STORMS interface or through the MessageMonitor service for the WMIS (Logica) and Generic Work Management interfaces. Updates are received from the work management system through triggers or through the [MessageMonitor service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ). These updates are flagged as entries in the [G3E_JOBSTATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GD8BWxQMRuSWnKE5qHh7JA) data table along with the processing action that is to occur. The NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service queries the G3E_JOBSTATUS data table and submits one of the records for JobLifeCycle to process by running the executable with the following command line parameters:   
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Config  |  The NetWorks Core configuration that is to be accessed   |  
|  Username  |  The username known by the Oracle installation. This user must have privileges on the NetWorks Core data tables equivalent to an interactive user that is allowed to post and close jobs and edit data.   |  
|  Password  |  The password for the username listed  |  
|  Jobname  |  The job identifier  |  
|  Example JobLifeCycle.exe Config=<configuration>; Username=<Myuser>;  Password=<Mypassword>; Jobname=<Job ID>;  |  
| --- |  
  * To configure JobLifeCycle:


  1. Populate the [G3E_JOBDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TBQDr_BsRYh8ej2Rr97t2g) table with a 'Default' type. 
  2. Populate the appropriate interface table based upon the work management system that is used ([G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA), [G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA), or [G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ).) 
  3. Populate the [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg) table. Additional entries can be made to this table to accommodate more triggers as long as the value in WR_STATE_CODE is unique. 
  4. Populate the [G3E_TRANSITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ACMZjVsrW8BQ2DZD8ftZdA) table. 
  5. Populate the [G3E_LIFECYCLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_8zjvUTXpqWJGXxKtqBFw) table and interface tables with the appropriate entries used by JobLifeCycle. The following entry types must exist for JobLifeCycle to process properly:   
|  Entry Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  AbandonedState  |  The G3E_USERNAME value from the [G3E_LIFECYCLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg) table that represents the abandoned state for batch transitioning ([G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ), [G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA), [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA)). The valued defined the interface table for the AbandonedState must exactly match a state value in G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_VALUE, include case sensitivity and spacing.   |  
|  OperationalState  |  The G3E_USERNAME value from the G3E_LIFECYCLE table that represents the operational state for batch transitioning ([G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ), [G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA), [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA)). The value defined in the interface table for the of the OperationalState must exactly match a state value in G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_VALUE, including case sensitivity and spacing.   |  
|  PrimaryCU  |  The CNO value where the Primary CU record is stored ([G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA), [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA))   |  
|  AncillaryCU  |  The CNO value where the Ancillary CU record is stored ([G3E_LOGICAIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tv6QyBZp2zACl6gcES_7cA), [G3E_STORMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eEbhntNS3hCuflwFGSvrZA))   |  
|  AfterPostMessageNO  |  The message number from G3E_MESSAGE that defines the message sent after a post operation to the database has been performed ([G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ))   |  
|  BeforePostMessageNO  |  The message number from G3E_MESSAGE that defines the message sent before a post operation. This message can be configured for a response message to be returned such that the post operation can continue or be suspended ([G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WdCQWt~w6RDEkBp18WPKsQ))   |  
  6. Populate the G3E_TYPE field in the [G3E_WORKMGMT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KME_1L76HZEDZ5lzihAbeQ) table. The following are the specific types used by JobLifeCycle: 
AncCUJobIDField
PriCUJobIDField
JobManagementOption
Feature
Lifecycle
WorkPoint
JobLifeCycle
MessageFormat
DesignArea
Transitions
ModifiedWorkRequestField
WorkPointWorkRequestField
  7. Populate the [G3E_JOBSTATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GD8BWxQMRuSWnKE5qHh7JA) table.

Using the [Message Format Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BpkKOMrwXQSfSpGNibZFgw) is the recommended way to populate this table.
