#### Configuring the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256341) The [configuration wizards](javascript:;) for each application or service stop and/or restart the application and service appropriately, depending upon the option selected in a configuration wizard. See the information below for manual steps.   |  
| --- |  
You can configure the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor service interactively or manually. [Click here](javascript:;) to read the interactive configuration steps. 
Manually configuring the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service involves setting the service owner, startup type, and Ccmmand line parameters. 
The NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service requires an owner. The privileges of the owner launch the service and allows access to system and network resources. By default, the service is launched using the SYSTEM account, which has all privileges on the local machine but does not have access to any shared network resources.NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service can use the SYSTEM account under the following circumstances: 
  * If the FileUNCPath key in the registry points to a local drive and folder.
  * If the FileUNCPaths file contained in this local folder points to a local ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file. 
  * If the mapfile entries in the configuration file point to local DDC files.


If the registry or the FileUNCPaths file or the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file contain UNC paths to another machine, start NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service using a network account that has privileges for the specified network resources. 
During installation, the service startup mode is set to Manual. If you want the service to start automatically when the machine reboots, set the startup option to Automatic. 
  * To configure the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service:


  1. From the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
/JLCMonitor.exe /Service /Install
The /Service option places the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service in the Services listing. The /Install option opens the Installation Parameters dialog box. 
![JLCInstall10.2.2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/XrpvT0LRPzuBZQAM0YEGsQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=3db518cb4e8e9c57&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256341) If you do not enter the /Install option, you can type the following at the command prompt: 
/JLCMonitor.exe USERNAME=<username>; PASSWORD=<password>; CONFIG=<configuration>; INTERVAL=<Interval in minutes>; DELAY=<delay to process>; 
  2. To set up the connnection and configuration values for NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service, type the appropriate information in each box:  
  
|  User Interface Item  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  User name  |  The username known by the Oracle installation. This user must have read- write/delete privileges.   |  
|  Password  |  The password for the username listed  |  
|  Configuration  |  The GIS configuration that is to be accessed  |  
|  Interval  |  How often the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service queries the G3E_JOBSTATUS table in minutes   |  
|  Delay  |  A time period to delay processing on a located record  |  
  3. Click OK. 
The entries are stored in the registry. Now each time the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service is stopped and restarted, these values are read from the registry. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256341) If you need to change the values for NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service, stop the service and run JLCMonitor.exe /Install again from the command prompt. Change the parameters as needed, and click OK. 
  4. From the Microsoft Windows Start menu or from the Control Panel, navigate to Administrative Tools > Services to confirm that the JLCMonitor Service is listed in the Services dialog box. 
  5. Double-click to select JCLMonitor Service from the list of services. 
  6. Select the Log On tab on the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service Properties dialog box. 
  7. Select This account. 
  8. Type the network account name and password. The account name and password must be an administrator on the machine where the service is installed. 
  9. Click Apply. 
  10. Select the General tab on the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service Properties dialog box. 
  11. Select Automatic in the Startup type: field. 
  12. Click Apply. 
  13. Click OK. 
  14. In the Event Viewer Application Log, verify that information log messages appear each time NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service starts successfully and that there is an instance of NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service in the Microsoft Windows Task Manager Processes listing.

#### JobLifeCycle Algorithm
Specific details about the executables involved in job life cycle processing are described in the diagram below: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/AvPhqpD7LL6iNOWSGKpJjQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=784fae7662f5e7eb&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
JobLifeCycle Processing Algorithm
  1. The work request revision progresses through the defined WMIS tasks.
  2. At significant events, a message is formatted and sent to the GIS signifying that event. See [Message Queue Processing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/j3dODE7yUK4XgK5dffnpqg) for more information. 
  3. The message is placed in the queue.
  4. The NetWorks Core MessageMonitor retrieves the message and determines the servicing program. 
  5. The NetWorks Core MessageMonitor enters a new row in the job status table for this message and associates a message identifier. 
  6. The NetWorks Core JLC Monitor processes each row in the job status table by executing the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycle program with Command line arguments that are obtained from the records in the table. 
  7. If the values from the job status table indicate that the update is defining a business process operation, the metadata is retrieved to determine the action to initiate for the update that is currently being processed. 
  8. The software finds the correct job record and updates it with the status value corresponding to the entry that was placed in the job status table by the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor. Metadata needs to define a WMIS status field. 
  9. The appropriate job life cycle operations are performed.


If an error occurs such that the job cannot be updated, information is logged in the [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE_ERROR table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DisCYAkebrotuuwQPDrL9Q). The JobLifeCycle also flags the error in the job status table. 
Configuration Control
The following operations are available for each event:  
|  Discard  |  Post  |  Transition  |  Close  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  0 - No discard operation  |  0 - No post operation  |  0 - No state transition  |  0 - No change for job status  |  
|  1 - Discard revisions  |  1 - Post all edits  |  1 - Transition from current state to next state  |  1 - Close job  |  
|  2 - Discard job and all revisions  |  2 - Partial post of specified data  |   |   |  
|   |  3 - Post all edits except work points  |   |   |  
|   |  4 - Partial post of specified data excluding work points  |   |   |

#### NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service Workflow
NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service is an executable program that monitors the contents of the [G3E_JOBSTATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GD8BWxQMRuSWnKE5qHh7JA) table. This executable runs as a service and periodically queries the G3E_JOBSTATUS table for records. Each record found is processed by NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service and is submitted as a command line argument to the JobLifeCycle executable. 
The JLCMonitor executable allows NetWorks Core to perform batch processing operations received from work management systems. 
Workflow Overview
The following is the general workflow for the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service program: 
  1. [Configure the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4c36P8tqBhFUculW~rr5pw) on your server. After this configuration is done, the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service should be running as a service and ready to process. 
  2. When NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service finds a record to process, it updates the record found in the G3E_JOBSTATUS table with a status of 'EXECUTING.' Then it runs the JobLifeCycle executable using the information found in the G3E_JOBSTATUS table and using the user name, password, and configuration information supplied for the startup of the JLCMonitor. 
  3. Any processing errors from NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service are logged in the Event Viewer > Application Log with one exception: if there is an error attempting to connect to the database, an error message is logged to the Event Viewer. The NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service continues to cycle and attempts to connect using the same parameters that you entered during the configuration of the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service. 


For each cycling of the NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service, the entire G3E_JOBSTATUS table is processed. All entries with a G3E_STATUS_CODE of 'NEW' are processed first; then all 'ERROR' entries are attempted. Any job that is listed in the table has its entries processed based on the order in which they were submitted. For instance, if an error occurs with an entry and subsequent entries are placed in the table (for this same job that had an error to occur) as new entries, these new entries for the same job are not processed until the error entry that is oldest has been processed. 
If you are using the MessageMonitor service, new entries in the G3E_JOBSTATUS table are processed by order of the G3E_ID value. If you are using triggers to populate this table, you should have no ordering problems. However, if you are using the Message Monitor service, you should start the queue designated for new work requests first and process all those entries before starting the queue designated for other events, such as lockdowns or closures. 
If you choose to have a separate queue for each event type, make sure to process all rows in a previous queue before starting the next queue. Even though the queues are started in the correct order, depending on the backlog within each queue, entries may still be processed too soon. 
Example
Consider the following set up:  
|  QUEUE TYPE  |  STARTING ORDER  |  NUMBER OF ROWS TO PROCESS  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  NewWorkRequest  |  1  |  100  |  
|  Lockdown  |  2  |  20  |  
|  Closure  |  3  |  1  |  
While these queues would be started in the correct order, the NewWorkRequest has 100 messages to process. The message that creates the job for the message that has been locked down has not had a chance to process yet. Since the Lockdown queue is immediately started, it processes its entries before the NewWorkRequest creates the referenced job; while starting the queues in the correct order is important, it is equally important to let each queue process its messages before starting the subsequent queue.

### Using MessageMonitor

#### Configuring NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256375) The [configuration wizards](javascript:;) for each application or service stop and/or restart the application and service appropriately, depending upon the option selected in a configuration wizard. See the information below for manual steps.   |  
| --- |  
To manually open the Installation Parameters dialog box, from the command prompt change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
GTMsgMonSvc.exe /Install
  1. The Installation Parameters dialog box opens. 
![MessageMonitorParameters10.2.2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/9GJUxxpWXPic1eJ38N0CrQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=44b8e09983169501&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Type the appropriate parameter in each box: 
     * User name—Username to log into theNetWorks Core database 
     * Password—Password for the username for the NetWorks Core database 
     * Configuration—Configuration to use to access the NetWorks Core database 
     * In Queue Names—Names of input queues for which the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service program starts the Message Monitor instances that poll queues 
If you do not enter the /Install option, from the command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
/GTMsgMonSvc.exe USERNAME=<username>; PASSWORD=<password>; CONFIG=<configuration>; INQUEUES=<Inputqueue1, Inputqueue2, Inputqueue3>; 
The command line parameters overwrite the values that were stored in the registry when you used the Installation Parameters dialog box. 
  3. Click OK. 
The parameters you entered are stored in the registry. NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service uses these parameters unless you enter new ones at the command line. 
MessageMonitor instances start polling the specified queues. When a MessageMonitor instance receives an incoming message, it uses the private Job Processing Service to process the message. The Job Processing Service sends a response to the appropriate output queue (for example, a response or error) that is specified in metadata. Any processing information or errors are logged in Event Viewer. 


To manually configure the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service, you must configure the service owner, the startup type, and the command line parameters for the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service. 
NetWorks Core Message Monitor Service requires an owner. The service is launched with the privileges of this owner and has access to system and network resources based on the owner’s privileges. By default, the service is launched using the SYSTEM account, which has all privileges on the local machine but does not have access to any shared network resources. Message Monitor service can use the SYSTEM account under the following circumstances: 
  * If the FileUNCPath key in the registry points to a local drive and folder 
  * If the FileUNCPaths file contained in this local folder points to a local ConnectionConfigurationMap.CCM file 
  * If the mapfile entries in the configuration file point to local DDC files


If the registry, the FileUNCPaths file, or the ConnectionConfigurationMap.CCM file contain UNC paths to another machine, start NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service using a network account that has privileges for the specified network resources. 
During installation the startup mode for NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service is set to Manual. If you want the service to start automatically when the machine reboots, set the startup option to Automatic. 
The NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service uses the NetWorks Core Queue Processing Service DCOM object. By default, this DCOM object runs on a local workstation without any configuration. However, if this DCOM object is to be shared or accessed by other client workstations or if the DCOM object is to be run remotely on another workstation, then it [must be configured.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6I_qCdpc57e0Hh0Io9falQ)
  * To configure NetWorks Core Message Monitor Service manually:


  1. From the Microsoft Windows Start menu, navigate to Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Services. 
  2. From the list of services, double-click NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service. 
  3. Select the Log On tab on the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service Properties dialog box. 
  4. Select This account:. 
  5. Type the network account name and password.
  6. Click Apply. 
  7. Select the General tab on the NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service Properties dialog box. 
  8. Select Automatic in the Startup type: field. 
  9. Click Apply. 
If you do not want to use the [parameters entered during registration](javascript:;), type the command line parameters in the Start parameters: field.   
|  Example <\GTechnology\Program>/GTMsgMonSvc.exe USERNAME=<username>; PASSWORD=<password>; CONFIG=<configuration>; INQUEUES=<Inputqueue1, Inputqueue2, Inputqueue3>;  |  
| --- |  
  10. Click OK.

#### Setting Up MessageMonitor Service
Message Monitor Service is a Windows Service program (GTMsgMonSvc.exe)that manages the number of input queues you set up in the [G3E_QUEUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zo8XGsEl0tTLdslL6Qu5gg) metadata table and on the Command linecommand line parameter. Message Monitor service software starts a separate [Message Monitor](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lYWD_9NHU7BHb5NZXei9sg) process thread for each input queue. 
Before you [register](javascript:;) and [configure](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rv6JqBW4_T8NjKJcKqx7mQ) Message Monitor service, install and configure one of the following queue software packages on the server. NetWorks Core does not deliver queue software. 
  * Microsoft MessageQueue, MSMQ
  * IBM MQSeries
  * Oracle Advanced Queue


If Oracle Advanced Queue is the queuing software, NetWorks Core and Oracle Advanced Queue can be separate database instances. However, the username and password of the NetWorks Core database and the Oracle Advanced Queue database must be the same. 
After you install and configure Message Monitor service, confirm that it is listed as NetWorks Core Message Monitor Service under Services in the Administrative Tools. To confirm that Message Monitor service is running, look under Processes in Task Manager for GTMsgMonSvc.exe, check the information/error log for Message Monitor service, and look under the Event Viewer in Administrative Tools.

#### Job Management—Logica (Deprecated)
For a Logica implementation, use the following workflow to manage jobs:
  1. Install and set up the [MessageMonitor service](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SjFkXpVwupbaDhMGFiBfzQ). 
  2. Populate the [G3E_MESSAGEFORMAT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/s9GcPFxUsogokTRUglTFow) table to map message fields to job and feature table fields. 


See [Configuring the System for WMIS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/g9sQD9Auhkh5aDigQQrbPg) for more information. 
Related Topic
[Job Setup - Logica](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mgoxXXtW2sXyyNkOoRdrhQ)

#### Job Management—STORMS (Deprecated)
For a STORMS implementation, use the following workflow to manage jobs:
  1. Install the following triggers that key on STORMS tables. The triggers are located in the \GTechnology\plsql\WMS folder. 
     * WMonUpdateTWMIFEXTWRDETAILS.sql — Contains triggers and procedures for maintenance of the G3E_JOB table and the creation of new jobs. This trigger must be installed on the STORMS database. 
     * WMonUpdateTWMIFSTATUSCHANGE.sql — Contains triggers and procedures for maintenance of the G3E_JOB table and is used to process status changes of a work request within the Storms Database. 
     * WMonUpdateTWMPOINTREPT.sql — Contains triggers and procedures for processing work point completion activities. 
  2. Set up database links to allow the STORMS database to access the tables that these triggers reference. 
  3. Set up links that allow the GIS database to reference the STORMS tables.


See [Configuring the System for STORMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/auyB5RmhpDOhQmPvHTX9sA) for more information. 
Related Topic
[Job Setup - STORMS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5iB9PGPZSzrDGzoPYCYA2g)

#### Processing Job Costs (Deprecated)
GframmeJobCosts.exe processes entries in the fixed asset table for the STORMS work management system and accumulates data to the feature tables. 
STORMS passes back job costs to GIS at the time the work request is closed by writing records to the [TWMIFFIXASSET table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hoU2dPhBdQU~TgukVB5c_Q). The NO_EQUIP attribute is the key field. The G3E_FID is passed into the NO_EQUIP field to be used as the NetWorks Core key for storing the CUs in the ISLAND tables. STORMS passes back this G3E_FID in the NO_EQUIP field for NetWorks Core to use for the record match. A subset of the AMT_ attributes shown in the subsequent sections contains values on the pass back. The NetWorks Core program accumulates or rolls up these amounts into a total job cost per feature. This activity is performed by the NetWorks Core batch program (GframmeJobCosts.exe) that is run as scheduled. This process is typically done in STORMS once a month.   
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261675) Because all costs may not appear in the month that the job was closed, when the cost is output a second or subsequent time, the entire job cost is output, not just the deltas. As such, the program that accumulates this information for each feature must take care to zero the work request balance before adding the new information. This is processed when there is a historical cost record per work request. If the cost is stored in an attribute of a single occurrence record, run the batch program only when you are certain that all costs have been recorded. In this case, the information output to the interface table is added to the preexisting costs.   |  
| --- |  
GframmeJobCosts.exe is invoked from the command prompt with command line parameters. If the job name is specified as one of the arguments, the entries that are processed from the fixed asset table are the entries associated with the work request related to the job specified. If no job is specified, GframmeJobCosts.exe processes all entries. The following are the command line parameters for GframmeJobCosts.exe:   
|  Parameter  |  Required/Optional  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Username  |  Required  |  The username known by the Oracle installation. This user must have privileges on the/ NetWorks Core data tables equivalent to an interactive user that is allowed to edit data and post and close jobs. Database links must exist to the STORMS island tables. This user must also have privileges to access these island tables through the database links established. (This also includes permission to make deletions from the TWMIFFIXASSET table.)   |  
|  Password  |  Required  |  The password for the username listed.  |  
|  Config  |  Required  |  The GIS configuration that is to be accessed.  |  
|  Request  |  Optional  |  This is the CD_WR value from the TWMIFFIXASSET table.  |  
If the job name is specified as one of the command line arguments, the entries that are processed from the fixed asset table are the entries associated with the work request related to the job specified. If no job is specified, GframmeJobCosts.exe processes all entries.   
|  Example GframmeJobCosts.exe USERNAME=myusername; PASSWORD=mypassword; CONFIG=AIRE_PROD; REQUEST=12345;  |  
| --- |  
If the job name is specified as one of the command line arguments, the entries processed from the fixed asset table are the entries associated with the work request related to the job specified. If no job is specified, GframmeJobCosts.exe processes all entries. 
Processing
The entire process is defined as follows:
  * GframmeJobCosts.exe queries the TWMIFFIXASSET table from the STORMS database for all records using CD_WR for the work request. 
  * These records are sorted by the NO_EQUIP and CD_USAGE attributes.
  * Multiple records can occur for a specific NO_EQUIP because ancillary CUs use the G3E_FID of the facility they are attached to and because repeating records use the same G3E_FID, for example, Transformers. 


For each record in the NO_EQUIP group, GFrammeJobCosts.exe does the following: 
  * Adds up costs for all AMT_ attributes (19) (subtract AMTSALV and AMTSCRAP).
  * Accumulates costs if multiple records for a total cost.
  * Within metadata, an entry is specified in the G3E_STORMSIFACE table that indicates the component to be used as the cost component. The G3E_STORMSIFACE table is queried where the G3E_TYPE='CostComponent'. This component information is retrieved and the common table is used to record the cost information. When this component is identified, NetWorks Core queries this table for a match on the G3E_FID using the NO_EQUIP attribute from the TWMIFFIXASSET table record. 
If a match occurs, NetWorks Core adds the rolled up costs to the JOB_COSTS attribute for that record. In most cases, the JOB_COSTS attribute is zero, but in the case of repeating records, a value could exist. In this scenario, the total job costs becomes final when the work request that places the last repeating record is closed. 
OR
If a match does not occur, NetWorks Core writes out any errors to error files and log files. 
  * Deletes records in TWMIFFIXASSET table after successful match. This deletion process has to be coordinated with any other customer program that also accesses these records. Use the FG_ERROR field to control coordination process. It starts with the value "N."

# Glossary

## AAMS
Application Advanced Metadata Service.

## abandoned
A feature state meaning abandoned in the field and not related to any open WMS work request. Abandoned features are excluded from a trace.

## active Z
The height value set in the Precision Coordinates control Height field. This value is the value used by default when setting the Z coordinate.

## ad hoc query
A query that uses standard SQL operators to find features in the active area of interest filtered by attribute values and relationships.

## Advanced Metadata Service (AMS)
COM object providing access to metadata information as well as methods for validation, secondary data integration, version management, and cache management.

## alias
A short substitute or nickname for a table name.

## allocate
The process of establishing a relationship, typically some sort of ownership or containment, between two features.

## allocation feature
The feature to which an [input feature](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200809) is to be allocated. In the Telecom industry, it is typically a duct, inner duct, or conduit. 
The feature to be allocated. In the Telecom industry, it is typically a cable.

## allow merge
After two features are selected for merge, but before any user interaction occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it allows the merge.

## AMS
Advanced Metadata Service.

## API
Application Programmer's Interface. A standard means of communicating between an application and a database or other system resource.

## Application Advanced Metadata Service (AAMS)
COM object providing an interface to metadata information analogous to AMS but for derived data. Derived data effectively creates new features, such as buffer zones.

## approve merge
After a merge occurs, Merge Features queries the relationship software to see if it approves the merge.

## arc
Curved shape within a polyline, polygon, or area boundary feature. An arc has a constant radius around a single center point.

## area boundary
A feature type displayed as a set of lines enclosing a region, such as a tax district.

## area feature
A feature containing one or more area geometries that can be noncontiguous. Area features can be polygons or boundaries. Although feature definitions are set by the administrator, a building is a typical polygon-type area feature, and a tax zone is an example of a boundary-type feature. A boundary-type area feature can contain one or more holes. A hole is an area feature that falls entirely inside the boundary of another area feature, such as a tax-free zone within a tax zone.

## area of interest (AOI)
Geographic area that you define, save, and use for spatial filtering.

## area of interest location identifier (AOILI)
An attribute for a feature that indicates a geographic location. Your system administrator can specify which attribute on the feature carries the location identifier. When using the location identifier for queries, the database is able to restrict the results to an area by attribute comparison, as opposed to true geometric spatial processing.

## argument
An independent variable upon whose value a function depends.

## assembly
A facility that consists of a small subnetwork of child facilities.

## at-to connectivity
Type of relationship that describes connectivity in telephony. The "at" feature identifies the current feature instance and the "to" feature identifies the feature to which the current one is connecting.

## attachment height
The height at which conductors, devices, or guys are attached to a utility pole.

## attribute filter
An SQL where statement.

## attribute inheritance
Obtaining attributes from different sources without need for user entry. This allows the user to more quickly place features, since many of the attributes of new feature can be inherited from other sources. Attribute values are inherited from database defaults, metadata based on job classification, previously-placed features, and metadata based on dialog tabs.

## attribute query
A search for features whose attribute values meet specified conditions.

## attribute
A column or field in a database table; nongraphic information stored in a table and linked to a feature.

## automatic field
Text field on a plot sheet to be automatically populated for use in batch plotting. Automatic field definition associates field information with a selected text object.

## axial load stress
Load applied along or parallel to and concentric with the primary axis of a utility pole.

## azimuth
Arc of the horizon measured between a fixed point (as true north) and the vertical circle passing through the center of an object.

## base component
Graphic component whose geometry is reused to create a synthesized component.

## base feature
A base feature, such as a building, is one for which an absolute position is known. Dimensions are drawn from base features to dimension features.

## baseline
Baseline is represented by the first line segment of orthogonal and polar dimension geometries (polylines). It indicates how the dimension is anchored to the base feature.

## bending stress
The normal stress that is induced at a point on a utility pole subjected to loads that can cause it to bend.

## binary
Consists of pixels that are either on or off to represent the foreground and background data. Uncompressed binary data requires one bit to store each pixel.

## bitmap
A representation of a graphic image as a set of dots. Each dot consists of one or more bits of information about the color and location of the dot, which the computer translates into pixels for screen display and into ink dots for printing.

## blanking component
A component of a raster feature whose geometry determines what pixels to remove from the associated raster image based on the portions of the image they obscure.

## boundary geometry
Set of lines and possibly arcs enclosing a region. The region might or might not have holes. Exterior of the boundary can be a polygon or a composite polygon. Holes might be polygons, composite polygons, or boundaries.

## breaking feature
A feature that is defined in metadata to break a linear feature at the point closest to the breaking feature when the breaking feature is placed within break tolerance to the linear feature.

## breaking strength
The approximate load which, when applied at a point on a utility pole, causes structural failure of the pole.

## broadcast database changes
A generic term that means synchronize deltas with most recent database changes. The software automatically performs this function, but the user can also click Refresh from Server from the menu. The act of broadcasting database changes means that the screen is refreshed with the latest data available from the database. Broadcasting local means that the screen is updated with just job-related changes. Broadcasting global means the screen is updated with job and master changes.

## buckling capacity
The structural failure by gross lateral deflection of a utility pole under compressive stress.

## buffer zone
A designated area around or within a feature or features on which you can perform spatial analysis.

## business object
COM objects that encapsulate the web application's main logic or business rules and any special data accesses.

## CAB
Composite UI Application Block. A set of .NET class libraries from the Microsoft Patterns and Practices group for creating complex user interfaces made of loosely coupled components.

## cable feature
Represents one continuous piece of cable.

## cable section
An instance of the cable linear component, either geo or detail. A cable section is typically a repeating component. Each cable feature must contain one or more sections. Each cable section represents a portion of the real-world linear feature with particular attributes.

## cadastral map
A large-scale map indicating the boundaries and dimensions of subdivisions and individual tracts of land to show ownership.

## cardinality
The nunber of cardinal (basic) members in a set. In tables, cardinality is the number of rows.

## cartographic
A physical entity commonly represented on a map by a symbol.

## CatalogRelationship
The number of an ownership relationship that should be used to traverse the entries in a catalog table. The G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_TYPE must be three (3) for this particular G3E_RNO.

## CatalogSchemaOwner
The name of the owner of the catalog data tables. The administrator must grant all users select permissions on this table. These tables are the E$ tables that match the facility data model.

## CCM file
[Connection Configuration Map file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200852). 
A text file containing one or more connection configurations maintained by the system administrator. The file must be named ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm. A connection configuration consists of a configuration name, the Oracle alias associated with the configuration name and used to connect to the Oracle Server, and a list of mapfiles associated with the configuration name.

## cell
A single attribute value for a feature displayed in the data window.

## center at current scale
Map-window property in which features in the select set are highlighted and centered in the map view, but the map window does not change scale.

## centroid
A point, text element, or text node used in area features to attach attribute information for those features. A centroid is not always placed in the exact center of an area feature.

## client-side deltas
Map-window property in which features in the select set are highlighted and centered in the map view, but the map window does not change scale.

## coincident lines
When two features are coincident they share geometry.

## collinear
Points which lie on a straight line.

## column
In a database table, a field that represents an attribute or property of a map feature.

## COM
Component Object Model. Foundation architecture that allows software applications to be built from binary components.

## common adjustments
Feature placement mechanisms that lets you move, rotate, or flip certain geometric components of the feature you are placing. Only the common adjustments that have been defined in the database (if any) are available when you place a feature or component.

## component configuration
A named grouping of components that acts as a shortcut for placing multiple components. They consist of an ordered list of components, each of which has an associated placement technique defined for it.

## component length
A label placed near the cable section to indicate an incremental length. It displays the length of cable from the beginning of a the cable section or from a physically- preceding component length, whichever is shorter. In the multi-section cable model, the sum of the component length labels associated with a cable section must be equal to the section length of that section.

## component view
The organization of data in the mapfile ([DDC)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200865). Component views feed into the Display Control. A component view is an Oracle view that contains the geometry of a particular component plus any attributes from any components that are necessary to display that geometry correctly. These views are the recordsets that are published. 
Dynamic Display Cache. Sometimes called DDC mapfile.

## component
One part or subset of a feature, such as the graphic symbol or label.

## composite polygon
A composite polyline that forms a closed area with first and last points being the same.

## composite polyline
A feature that contains polyline and arc type geometeries.

## conduit
The outermost container for facilities in an underground model. The conduit does not need to be an actual structure.

## configuration name
Name of the connection defined in the Connection Configuration Map file.

## conflict
A change to a record that is posted after you edit the same record but before you post your changes.

## Connection Configuration Map (CCM) file
A text file containing one or more connection configurations maintained by the system administrator. The file must be named ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm. A connection configuration consists of a configuration name, the Oracle alias associated with the configuration name and used to connect to the Oracle Server, and a list of mapfiles associated with the configuration name.

## connection
The link between a work space and a database.

## connectivity
The relationship between or among features that share a common node number. Each time a feature is placed, the system generates beginning and ending node numbers. When you append a new feature to an existing feature, the system then assigns the node number of the existing feature to the new feature.

## constant
A value that never changes.

## constructed point
Endpoint of the dimension, which touches the dimensioned feature.

## containment
A relationship of many features to many other features. For example, a duct can contain many cables, and a cable can be contained in many ducts.

## context menu
Pop-up menu. A list of available commands that appears when you right-click in a map window or in the toolbar area of the application window.

## contiguous geometry
A single geometry; for example, the boundary of the state of Colorado.

## continue
Continue a linear feature independently of other features.

## control files
Oracle files in a specific format that the SQL Loader process (an Oracle utility) uses to load data into the database

## control points
Objects or marks on the ground having either a known position (horizontal coordinates) or both a known position and elevation (vertical datum value), in an established network of ground control.

## coordinate readout
A dynamic readout of coordinates that indicates the projected or geographic location of the cursor in the map window.

## coordinate system
A system of intersecting coordinate lines, meridians and parallels, on a flat surface on which features from the curved surface of the earth are mapped and used to measure spatial location. Also the map projection, grid, or other system in which map data are stored.

## coordinates
The location of a point on the map along the X (horizontal) and Y (vertical) axes relative to the global origin. In a geographic coordinate system, for example, the X coordinate is called latitude and the Y coordinate is called longitude. Both are measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds. Latitude is measured from the equator; longitude is measured from a zero meridian, such as Greenwich.

## Copy Element
A placement mode in which you copy a linear element and place the copy where you want.

## Copy Parallel
A placement mode in which you copy an existing linear feature and place the copy parallel to the original linear feature.

## Copy Partial Element
A placement mode in which you copy a part of a linear element and place the copy where you want.

## Copy Partial Parallel
A placement mode in which you copy a part of a linear element and place the copy parallel to the original linear element.

## count
Unique assignment of a group of conductors within a cable throughout the entire cable network. The assignment is used to help engineering design and administration, construction work, record keeping, pair assignment and maintenance.

## crosshair cursor
Shape assumed by the cursor when you are placing or measuring items such as a feature or a fence.

## CRS
Coordinate Reference System. This is an (Open Geospatial Consortium) OGC-specific terminology used to define the coordinate system.

## CSF
Coordinate system file.

## CU
For STORMS and Logica workflows, compatible unit; used to determine the cost of fulfilling work requests.

## culture code
The culture name is a combination of an ISO 639 two-letter lowercase culture code associated with a language and an ISO 3166 two-letter uppercase subculture code associated with a country or region. The syntax is <ISO 639 two letter language code>’-‘<ISO 3166 three letter subculture code>. For example, all of the following are valid: en, en-US, en-UK, fr, fr-FR, and so forth.

## cursor
A graphical image, such as a pipe (|) or I-beam, in a window or dialog box that shows where a selection can be made or where text appears on the screen when you press keyboard keys.

## data server
Software program, such as Oracle, that the software uses to connect to a database.

## data type
The type of value allowed for a database attribute. For example, one attribute can only contain alpha-numeric characters, another only contains integer values, and another only real numbers.

## database export
Oracle utility executed from the operating system, used to extract data from a database.

## database import
Oracle utility executed from the operating system, used to put data into a database.

## database role
Classes or privileges of users to control access to operations that can consume significant database or network resources or to provide certain levels of data security. Use of database roles is not intended to replace database security, but primarily to constrain client software behavior.

## database
Repository of tables; collection of data that is organized so that its contents can easily be accessed, managed, and updated.

## DDC
Dynamic Display Cache. Sometimes called DDC mapfile.

## default Z
The value set in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_NAME (DefaultZ) field in metadata. If set, this value is the initial [active Z](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_649002) until it is changed. 
The height value set in the Precision Coordinates control Height field. This value is the value used by default when setting the Z coordinate.

## default
The setting or value that is automatically selected or entered if no other setting or value is specified.

## deltas
The component of the software that augments the DDC files with the most recent changes from the database since the DDC files were published. DDC's are static between publishes, so the deltas component augments their recordsets with changes to the database. Server-side deltas refers to the processing done in the database itself using a PL/SQL procedure called UpdateDeltas that updates the MODIFICATIONLOG with values from the correct component views. Client-side deltas refers to the software that runs on each client machine that reads the MODIFICATIONLOG with its component view values that update the screen of the user.

## derived component
Components that cannot be placed independently from other components. An example of a derived component is a pole riser for a pole. A derived component is placed automatically whenever an instance of the component from which it is derived is placed.

## descender
The part of a lowercase letter that descends below the main body of the letter. For example, g, j, p, q, and y all have descenders while a, b, c, d, and e do not.

## detail file
A nongeographic file containing an exploded or more detailed view of a feature or geographic area.

## detail relationship
Identifies the indicator component within one or more features. This definition simply controls the generation of the detail identifier and the name of the legend to use for display of the detail items.

## detail window
A map window that has a detail legend associated with it and in which detail data are displayed.

## detail
A drawing containing data that clarifies certain aspects of a map, such as underground facilities.

## development schema
Set of tables in the database used to define the data model for a site. The only difference between a development schema and a production schema is the value assigned to G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_ TYPE. This is where you develop metadata for your project. It is not to be used for production.

## dialog box
A form or secondary window that pops up temporarily on the screen to request input from you.

## dimension
A linear feature that displays the distance between a base feature and the dimensioned feature.

## dimensioned feature
A feature, such as a valve or switch, for which only a position relative to a base feature is known. Dimensions are drawn from base features to dimension features.

## Dimensioning IPT
Interactive placement technique that enables the construction of all types of dimension elements.

## directed relationship
A relationship in which a subordinate relationship exists, which suggests a direction from the superior to the subordinate related feature. For example, ownership, node-ordered connectivity, and many-to-many ownership.

## directional connectivity
A connectivity relationship where network components carry a sense of from and to in the connectivity component. See [node-ordered connectivity](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200916). 
A node-edge relationship that also maintains the direction of digitization of linear features. Allows only one-node and two- node elements and maintains a sense of the direction of the connections. A two-node device has a connectivity component that stores the FNO/FIDs of the two devices to which it is connected. A one-node device has no connectivity component; its connectivity is represented by having its FNO/FID stored as one of the nodes of a two-node device.

## directional hint
The second feature you place when tracing a feature.

## disassociate
To end a relationship between two related entities.

## disconnect
To end a connectivity relationship between two connected features.

## discontiguous feature
A single feature that is made up of multiple unconnected geometries. For example, the state of Hawaii is a discontiguous feature made up of several area geometries.

## disown
To end a relationship between a parent and a child feature. Used also to describe the termination of a relationship between a child and parent feature.

## Display Control
The dockable control with which you determine how features are displayed in the active map window, whether or not to honor the predefined scale range, and which features can be located by a query. The Display Control lists every class of feature available in the database.

## display scale denominator
The second number in the display scale ratio, for example, 1600 is the display scale denominator in a ratio of 1:1600.

## display scale
The ratio of the distance on the screen to the corresponding actual length or distance on the ground. Also, the scale at which map objects are displayed in the map window.

## dockable control
A sort of toolbar that contains buttons and controls, such as drop-down lists, specific to a particular function. A dockable control can be resized, moved, and docked or undocked, but not customized.

## driven dimension
A dimensioned feature that, when updated, updates the constructed points of the related driven dimensions so that their constructed points stay connected to the dimensioned feature.

## duct configuration
Placement of graphics related to ducts in underground infrastructure that contain cables for communications, electrical, or other transmission systems. Number of rows and columns of ducts.

## duct
In an underground model, a container of some sort, usually a pipe. A duct is used to contain other facilities like cables or conductors.

## dynamic display cache
Mapfile; a collection of component views published from the database. A recordset produced from a component view in the DDC is the same as the recordset produced from the same component view in the database, except that it is produced much faster. This is because the DDC is a spatially organized flat file.

## easting, northing (E,N)
Unscaled X and Y mapping coordinates; the same units of measurement as ground measurements, such as kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilofeet, feet, inches, miles, or survey feet.

## edge
A single linear geometry. An edge can be a two-point line or a circular arc, never a polyline.

## element Z
When this mode is active, the height value is calculated using the feature you snap to when placing or editing a feature.

## ellipsoid
The model used to represent the shape of the earth. Because the shape of the earth's surface differs from one geographic area to another, different ellipsoids describe different areas.

## EPSG
European Petroleum Survey Group is an organization that maintains a data set of coordinate reference systems and coordinate transformation which may be global, regional, national, or local in its application. Each of these coordinate reference systems have a code, which is known as EPSG code. By mapping your coordinate system configuration to one of these named definitions, your data can be shared through web services and appropriately matched to a location on the earth to align properly with other data.

## equipment assembly
A collection of hardware components such as racks, shelves, and cards that are arranged in a standard design for placement in equipment enclosures.

## exchange
One of the area types in the hierarchy of service areas. A typical hierarchy is [NPA](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200934) > Wire Center > Switch Center > Exchange. The most commonly used area for setting a context for day-to-day telecom engineering is the switch center. 
Numbering Plan Area. The equivalent to the geographic regions for an area code.

## export
The process of formatting data so it can be used by another application and sending it to that application.

## extend
Extend a linear feature to the nearest locatable feature.

## Extended Property Set (EPS)
COM objects providing access to the metadata information from a recordset or field object.

## facility model
A model containing information about the facilities that a utility company maintains in the field.

## facility
A physical asset of a utility company.

## failure direction
Represents the wind direction angle at which a utility pole is overloaded. Usually the guy angle is an angle opposite to the failure direction angle.

## feature definition
The feature name plus its components and relationships and which are the primary graphic (or geographic) and primary tabular components.

## feature hierarchy
The relationships among the features defined in a project database. In Feature Explorer, a hierarchical tree view of a specific feature, the relationships in which it participates, and the features to which it is related.

## feature
A set of graphic components and nongraphic attributes that collectively comprise the feature. A feature is represented graphically on a map by a geometry type and by the style defined in the database for that feature.

## fiber stress
The unit stress, usually in pounds per square inch (psi), on a utility pole that is subjected to an external load.

## field configuration
A grouping of the field database, DDC data, and database alias used primarily by field personnel.

## field database
The database where data are stored for disconnected field use.

## field
In a database table, a column that represents an attribute or property. In a dialog box, a text box or area into which you can enter data.

## fillet arc
An arc of a specified radius tangent to two adjacent lines.

## filter
An SQL where statement; used to define the search conditions in a query.

## final feature
For merge, component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature, resulting in a final feature that stays in the database.

## first feature
For merge, the feature the user selects first.

## fit and zoom out
Map-window property in which features in a select set are fit to the map view, and the view zoomed out according to the percentage you specify. The percentage is a constant factor of the scale at which features in the select set are fit. That is, if an item is fit at 1:5,000, a percentage of 200% doubles the scale to 1:10,000. A percentage of 300% triples the scale to 1:15,000, and so on.

## FixedSegmentLength IPT
Interactive placement technique that places the first segment of a polyline or a composite polyline with a fixed (metadata-specified) length.

## flip
Adjustment mask that rotates the geometry by 180 degrees, offset from a selected linear or area boundary element by the projected distance in the other direction.

## foreign data
See [secondary data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200955). 
Read-only data whose attributes and graphics exist in a secondary GDO data connection and whose metadata exists in the primary data connection; geographic data that is not created, edited, or deleted through NetWorks Core and does not meet the requirements for features. Typically, this is reference data, such as streets or parcels. Even though it is not managed by the application and can have no relationships, the data are integral to the management of the utility facility data. As such, the data are published in the mapfile as part of the facility data.

## foreign key
A column or combination of columns in a database table that references the primary key of another table in the database.

## format
How a value is to be displayed.

## formation
Ducts that are bundled together. A formation carries information such as the arrangement of the ducts, the number of ducts, and the number of spare ducts. A formation does not need to be a physical entity.

## Freehand
Construction Aid mode in which you place a component where you click on the map. This is the default mode.

## functional interface
Interface associated with an attribute of a component that provides the ability to interface to other systems or to gather information from another source during the placement, editing, and validation of a feature. When the interface is executed depends on its type.

## G3E_DEEPCOPY
Wrapped database script delivered with the Admin product that creates the catalog into which an administrator saves equipment assemblies using the Save to Catalog command.

## GDO
Geographic data object.

## Geo-tie-packets
Data packets that contain coordinates for the map image in a geographic coordinate system based on a WGS84 datum and design-file unit information.

## geodetic datum
Precise location of the ellipsoid relative to the earth's surface and a network of control points. Its definition usually includes the origin point of the ellipsoid, its orientation, and the radius and eccentricity of the ellipsoid.

## geographic coordinate system
A curvilinear nonprojected coordinate system defined with respect to the surface of the reference ellipsoid. Geographic coordinate systems express coordinates as lon,lat,h, where lon (longitude) is the angular distance from a zero meridian, lat (latitude) is the angular distance from the equator, and h is the height above the reference ellipsoid.

## geographic data
Data that has both size and spatial location and that is linked to attribute information stored in a database table. Size can mean physical dimension—height, length, depth, or area—or a relative aggregate amount, such as the population of a voting district. Spatial location means that data occupies a measurable position in space relative to the surface of the earth.

## geographic measurement
A method for measuring distances and areas geographically that takes the curvature of the earth into account.

## geometry
The graphic representation of a feature in the map window. A feature is represented graphically on a map by a geometry type and by the style defined in the database for that feature. This application contains the following geometry types: point, linear, and area.

## GeoTIFF
A data exchange standard for georeferenced raster imagery; a TIFF image with geo-tag information in its header. When the raster image is displayed, the appropriate transformation is applied to its display matrix. This transforms the data from its original coordinate system into the one in the active work space.

## GIS
Geographic Information System. Data management software and hardware that allow you to capture, store, analyze, and display geographic information.

## global changes
Synonym for master changes or master and job changes. This term is used for historical purposes.

## glyph
Symbol that appears on a cursor when the cursor moves to within a specified tolerance of a locatable feature.

## grayscale
Image format that uses shades of gray instead of color.

## ground line moment
The product of any horizontally applied load at any point on a utility pole multiplied by its height above ground.

## ground units
Linear measurement system associated with your data or calculations. For example, feet, meters, or inches are common ground units.

## handles
Small squares that appear around a select set. You can click and drag the handles to manipulate the geometry.

## high watermark
Synonym for [watermark](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_200977). 
Highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. When DDCs are published, they are burned with the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This is referred to as the watermark. Queries to the MODIFICATIONLOG use this watermark to limit the records returned. These queries yield new highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER/watermarks to be used in subsequent queries.

## himetric
Unit of measure used by Microsoft Windows to actually draw the elements. Points are converted to himetric where one himetric unit equals 0.01 mm. To convert to himetric, multiply your points by 35.277. The himetric value sent to the Windows draw operation is a double precision floating point number. There is no fixed limit on the size of an element to draw. However, at some point, Microsoft Windows can determine that the element is too thick or large and not draw it.

## hint feature
Feature connected to one node of the source that controls the direction that the trace takes. Used by the Trace command to determine when to prompt and obtain a hint feature.   
|  Example Your starting feature (before you run the trace) is a two-node device or a linear. Selecting the hint feature determines which of the two nodes, or which direction, the trace should go.   |  
| --- |

## hole
An area within an area feature; for example, a lake inside a tract of land.

## hybrid feature
A feature that is placed in a job context, but it is a master change. Design areas are the only hybrid features currently supported.

## Image IPT
Interactive placement technique that enables placement of raster images.

## impedance
Apparent opposition in an electrical circuit to the flow of an alternating current that is analagous to the actual electrical resistance to a direct current. Impedance is expressed as the ratio of effective electromotive force to the effective current.

## import
To bring in data from another application or source.

## In service
As a feature state, constructed and not related to any open Work Management System work request.

## inner ducts
A container within a duct modeled as a separate feature. It is also used to contain other facilities like cables. The types of feature in the inner ducts do not have to be the same as the types of features in the duct.

## input feature
The feature to be allocated. In the Telecom industry, it is typically a cable.

## inside-fence mode
Feature-selection mode in which only features that fall completely within the fence are selected.

## inspection feature
Feature that documents deficiencies on compatible units and inspectable features (such as poles, transformers, or conductors) or related features.

## Interactive IPT
Placement technique that enables interactive placement of points, lines, and areas with the Construction Aids control.

## InteractiveMiscText IPT
Interactive placement technique that enables placement of text labels whose contents consist of a simple value that you type.

## interface
The place where two separate entities meet or communicate. For example, a user interface connects a software program with the person using the program. An interface can also connect programs and devices. 
For the Telecom industry, a device, sometimes referred to as a cross-connect, where count assignments can be remapped/relabeled.   
|  Example A set of conductors designated as 10,1-100 can be connected to an interface, and then remapped (typically the remapping is stored in separate pairs assignment database, to 201,200-299). Tracing stops at the interface unless an Assignment Interface software component is present to retrieve the new mappings from the Pairs Assignment database.   |  
| --- |

## Intersect
Construction Aid mode in which you place a data point at the intersection of two lines.

## job classification
Characterization of the type of work you are performing; for example, residential or commercial, overhead or underground, or high or low voltage.

## job state
Representation of the progress of work associated with a particular job. You can transition the status of a job from one state to another—for example, from Proposed to Under Construction or from Under Construction to Closed (the specific state names are defined in your database).

## job
A project or task, such as a road widening project or the installation of a transformer, managed by a utility or communications company. In database terms, a job consists of a set of database edits and a link (job ID) to the Jobs Management table.

## key
Unique identifier; a field used to sort data.

## kickback
Condition in which the current vertex falls on the line segment between the previous two vertices.

## last modification key mark
Synonym for watermark.

## latitude
The Y coordinate (parallel) in a geographic coordinate system. Latitude is measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds from the equator.

## legend
The predefined control that determines what is displayed in the map window.

## linear feature
Feature represented graphically by line segments or arcs that are strung together. Rivers, street centerlines, and utility lines are usually linear features.

## LineByPtAngLenOffset SPT
Silent placement technique that places lines at specified point, angle, and length at an offset from the starting point.

## LineByTwoPointsOffset SPT
Silent placement technique that places a line between two specified points.

## listener
An object that opens a message queue associated with its host application and waits for messages to arrive. As a message arrives, the listener dispatches the message to another object that processes the message.

## load coil
Use of energy on a circuit. Load is determined by calculating the load on each transformer and primary meter in the selected circuit.

## load flow
Statistical analysis of the devices and conductors within a network.

## load
Use of energy on a circuit. Load is determined by calculating the load on each transformer and primary meter in the selected circuit.

## local changes
Synonym for job changes. This term is used for historical purposes.

## locatability
A characteristic that determines whether a map object can be located with the select tool or by a query.

## locate zone
The area within the circle at the tip of the cursor arrow or in the center of the cross-hair that defines the range within which objects can be located.

## locked-down dialog box
A dialog box that keeps its full size while you perform other tasks in the application.

## Long Term Transaction (LTT)
A working mode that lets someone make changes in the database while keeping those changes isolated and thus protecting the master database. The set of changed records edited in LTT mode constitutes a job. Until they are posted, jobs or individual changes made in LTT mode can be discarded without affecting the master database. When a job is validated and posted, its changes replace the master records.

## longitude
The X coordinate (meridian) in a geographic coordinate system. Longitude is measured in degrees, minutes, and seconds from the central or zero meridian.

## Loop Makeup
An analysis tool that ascertains the composition of a cable loop and determines compliance with design requirements. Loop Makeup computes signal loss and other network information about signal and potential for service to areas along the network.

## loop
The circuit from the central office to the customer location.

## loopback
A situation in which the feature is allocated to the same container (conduit or duct) going into and out of the loop. If the feature is allocated to different ducts in the same path, the software resolves the allocation successfully or marks the ambiguity.

## many-to-many ownership
A superset of the abilities defined in the ownership relationship. It supports an M-N cardinality between features in that a child can have many parents and can also be a parent to many entities. For example, a cable can be contained in many ducts and a single duct can contain many cables.

## Map file DDC
Synonym for DDC.

## map frame
A frame within a plot sheet that encloses a single embedded map with its own border, display scale, and geographic extents. Or in the Viewer products, a preconfigured area in the web application for viewing maps.

## map object
Feature or image that appears in a map window.

## map view
The contents of a map window. Or in the Viewer products, the named view of the data that is inside a map frame.

## map window
The window in which you view feature geometries and images, as well as the North arrow and scale bar.

## mapfile
Dynamic display cache (.ddc) file.

## mask
In component placement, the type of adjustment you make (move or rotate, for example). For a Point style, a symbol that goes behind the one you want to use for presentation. A mask symbol blanks out the background color. For example, if a pole symbol is a circle with an open interior, the mask symbol is the filled circle inside the ring of the pole.

## master configuration
A grouping of the master database, dynamic display cache data, and database alias.

## master database
For replication processing, the database from which data are extracted.

## metabase
A private registry for IIS.

## metadata cache
A copy of the optimized metadata database tables extracted from the database to reduce requests to the database.

## metadata
Data that describes the characteristics of, or provides informational reference to, the primary objects (data) of a system. For example, metadata about a database table would include the table name and type, column names, and column data types and length restrictions.

## method
In object-oriented programming, a programmed procedure that is defined as part of a class and included in any object of that class. A method in an object can have access only to the data known to that object, which ensures data integrity among the set of objects in an application.

## Midpoint
Construction Aid mode in which you place the next point of any geometry type at the midpoint of a selected linear element.

## minimum bounding rectangle (MBR)
The smallest rectangle that can encompass a set of map objects.

## minimum path
Trace type that starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, and keeps track of the cost from the seed to the goal. Once a goal is found, the trace continues to search for other paths to a goal that have a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal. The trace stops when there are no longer any valid rows as defined by the Stop and Filter criteria or there are no longer any potential paths having a lesser cost than the minimal cost path to a goal.

## modal dialog box
A dialog box that keeps control and must be dismissed before you can do anything else in the application.

## modeless dialog box
A dialog box that relinquishes control so you can toggle between the application window and the dialog box. Modeless dialog boxes have a lock-down arrow or roll-up arrow in the title bar, and you can toggle between them.

## Modification tracking trigger
This trigger is put on each component in the data model when NetWorks Core is set up. This trigger writes an entry into the MODIFICATIONLOG recording all changes to this component and all the component views this component participates in.

## MODIFICATIONLOG
A table in the database called MODIFICATIONLOG that records every change to every component and component view in the data model. The modification-tracking triggers record each change in the MODIFICATIONLOG, and UpdateDeltas record the values for the corresponding component view records.

## Move Along plus angle adjustment
An adjustment mask that lets you move the component at an angle to a linear element.

## Move Along with no angle adjustment
An adjustment mask that lets you move the component along a linear element.

## Move Independent
An adjustment mask that lets you move the component arbitrarily.

## multi selection
To select multiple items, press and hold the CTRL key as you click each item you want to select. 
To select items that are next to each other, press and hold the SHIFT key as you click the first and last item you want to select.

## multiple geometry
Different geometric representations of the same feature.

## node-edge connectivity
A relationship among features that share a common node number. Each time a feature is placed, the system generates beginning and ending node numbers for the feature. When you append a new feature to an existing feature, the system assigns the node number of the existing feature to the new feature.

## node-ordered connectivity
A node-edge relationship that also maintains the direction of digitization of linear features. Allows only one-node and two- node elements and maintains a sense of the direction of the connections. A two-node device has a connectivity component that stores the FNO/FIDs of the two devices to which it is connected. A one-node device has no connectivity component; its connectivity is represented by having its FNO/FID stored as one of the nodes of a two-node device.

## node
Connecting point on a linear feature.

## nominal map scale
The scale of a reduced earth model. The constant factor that multiplies all X,Y coordinates on the true-to-scale map to reduce it to the needed map scale. On a given map, the actual map scale is equal to the nominal map scale at the locations that have no scale distortion (for example, along the latitude of true scale).

## nominal paper scale (NPS)
The base unit or ratio used in calculations for the style object sizing. The NPS is associated with the legend definition in the G3E_PAPERSCALE column of the G3E_LEGEND table. This value determines the symbol or text size (line weight) when the data are viewed at this defined scale. When the current view scale as reflected in the application status bar matches the NPS, the symbols are the size calculated from the point size. The ratio 1:5000 means that 1 unit on the screen or on paper is the equivalent of 5000 ground units. For example, 1 inch on the screen is equivalent to 5000 inches on the ground.

## non-repeating component
A component which is not repeating. A single occurrence of the component exists within a feature.

## nongraphic component
A component that does not have geometry.

## normalized database tables
In relational database design, the process of organizing data to minimize duplication. Normalization usually involves dividing a database into two or more tables and defining relationships between the tables. Normalization simplifies the layout of tables and makes them easier to manage. Normalized tables often contain foreign keys to other metadata tables. In NetWorks Core, the administrator edits the normalized tables.

## north arrow
An image that indicates the direction on a map to the geographic North Pole.

## not-driven dimension
A dimensioned feature that if updated does not update the constructed points of the related not-driven dimensions. Thus their constructed points are no longer connected to the dimensioned feature.

## NPA
Numbering Plan Area. The equivalent to the geographic regions for an area code.

## null
The absence of a value. If a table cell is null, it indicates a value of no value; this is not the same as zero.

## object server
The application registered on your workstation associated to the particular file or object type. For example, Microsoft® Word is the object server for files with the .doc extension.

## ODBC
Open Database Connectivity. A standard interface between a database and an application that is trying to access the data in that database.

## Offset
Construction Aid mode in which you place the next point of any geometry type at an offset distance and bearing (direction) relative to an existing element.

## OffsetPointSPT
Placement technique that automatically places a point a specified distance from the starting point of a selected graphic component. This technique supports the Adjustment behavior but does not allow the relative component to be different for the point location and the angle location.

## OffsetValidationPriority
The default priority error used in processing of NodeEdgeConnectivity, Ownership, and Many-to-Many Ownership when the feature pair is related but geographically farther than their specified limit. The priority can also be specified per pair of features.

## OMS
Outage Management System. Hexagon Public Safety application now called InService Solutions.

## operational abandon
A feature state meaning abandoned in the field but having work requests that have not been closed.

## operational remove
A feature state meaning removed from the field but having work requests that have not been closed.

## operator
Symbol or expression, such as = (equals) or >= (is greater than or equal to), used to filter values in a database query.

## optables
Optimized tables; tables that result from joining metadata tables. Optables are published into the metadata mapfiles and ADO-based RAW files. Using optables makes the software run more efficiently.

## optimistic
A long-term transaction mode in which there can be multiple edits to the original database records by multiple jobs. The different jobs changes are isolated from each other.

## Oracle
Relational database management system used in NetWorks Core.

## ordinal
Order of execution for the interface.

## orientation
Alignment.

## origin
In coordinate geometry, the point where the x-axis and y-axis intersect at the coordinates 0,0.

## orthogonal dimension
Dimension that displays the perpendicular and the parallel offsets from a vertex of the base feature.

## orthogonal
Of or relating to right angles and perpendicular lines. As a drawing technique, places the current segment of a line or area at 0, 90, or 270 degrees relative to last line segment.

## overlap-fence mode
Selection mode in which all features that fall inside or are overlapped by the fence are selected.

## ownership
A relationship between two features, parent-to-child or child- to-parent. The system establishes ownership between a feature and the feature physically supporting it. An owner feature serves as the parent feature of one or more features that are supported by the owner; for example, in the relationship of a pole and a transformer, the pole is the parent and the transformer is the child.

## panning
Moving the view in any direction from a specific point in a map window to see other areas of the map.

## paper scale
The ratio of the contents of your screen to the printed page.

## pessimistic
A long-term transaction mode in which the database records that the user edits are locked so that users in other jobs cannot update them until the records are posted or discarded.

## picklist
A selectable list of suitable choices.

## PickQuick
A tool that helps you to select map objects that overlap or objects that are hidden by other objects. When multiple objects are within the locate zone, the cursor changes to an ellipsis (three dots) and you click the mouse to display the PickQuick dialog box.

## placement configuration
The feature selection lists and the logical groups of features and/or components used to drive the placement commands.

## plot sheet
Representation of the piece of paper you are going to print.

## plot window
Window in the work space that encloses a plot sheet and provides commands and toolbars for manipulating the plot sheet and its contents. All plotting operations must be performed within a plot window.

## PlotUnit
A PlotUnit is the main unit for processing a plot request; it:
  * Seeks new requests from the request queue.
  * Maintains a one-to-one relationship with the NetWorks Core process that it initiates. 
  * Maintains the lifetime of its NetWorks Core process. 
  * Recovers from various error states to ensure that it is always available to service a plot request. 
  * Runs in the background.

## point feature
A symbol or text that represents the location of a geographic element; a feature, such as a utility pole or fire hydrant, that is too small to be displayed at the defined map scale. Labels, control points, poles, and manholes are typical point features.

## point to point trace
Type of trace that starts at the seed feature and traces until it finds either the specific goal feature instance or any feature of the specified goal type, subject to the Goal and Filter criteria.

## point
Unit of measure defined by the printing industry. A point is 1/72 of an inch. Symbol and text sizes are defined in points. Line width and dash / gap lengths are defined in points as well.

## PointOnLinear IPT
Interactive placement technique that lets you place a point geometry on an existing linear geometry (polyline). The additional vertex is inserted on the selected linear geometry position that is identical to the position of the point geometry being placed.

## polar dimension
Dimension that displays the position as distance and angle relative to an edge of the base feature.

## pole moment
The magnitude of the force on a pole and the direction of the force based on attachments and wind force and direction.

## pole percentage usage
Defines the percentage usage of a pole. Typically if this value is above 100 the pole is overloaded.

## political map
