A map that shows government boundaries.

## polygon
A set of lines enclosing a region.

## polyline
A line with one or more vertices in addition to the beginning and ending points. An orthogonal line, for example, is a polyline.

## post process
A certain task performed after another specified operation, such as a trace. Post processing provides an extensible mechanism for manipulating a large amount of data in a controlled fashion.

## power factor
A ratio between real power and apparent power (kVA). A deviation from one indicates increased losses in the electrical distribution.

## precision
Number of decimal places to display for numeric data.

## primary data
Data originally created in G/Technnology. You can edit and delete primary data.

## primary graphic (or geographic) component
The primary graphic (or geographic) component is used by many NetWorks Core functions whenever a single location or geometry is needed to represent a feature.

## primary key
A column or combination of columns in a database table that uniquely identifies each row in the table.

## production schema
Contains data for end users. Reporting components and database procedures need the optimized metadata tables in the production schemas. Do not modify metadata in the production schema

## projected coordinate system
A right-handed Cartesian system with the X and Y axes in the plane of the map and the Z axis perpendicular to the plane of the map. Coordinates are expressed as X,Y,Z, where X (easting) normally points east on the plane of the map and Y (northing) points north, at the point chosen for the map's origin. The Z coordinate represents the height above either the reference ellipsoid or the geoid (roughly, mean sea level).

## projection
A representation of the 3D curved surface of the earth on a flat (2D) surface.

## proposed abandon
Feature state into which features to be abandoned in the field are translated during the design phase of an electrical project. These features are proposed only and are not physically abandoned.

## proposed add
Feature state into which new features are placed during the design phase of an project. These features are proposed only and are not constructed.

## proposed remove
Feature state into which features to be removed from the field are translated during the design phase of an electrical project. These features are proposed only and are not physically removed.

## protection area
Area where one or more protection zones overlaps a parcel.

## protection zone
A buffer zone around a pipeline or a square around a technical object. Creating a protection zone is the first step in creating a protection area

## publish
A way to present metadata in dynamic display cache files; increases the speed of data retrieval and convenience of metadata administration and distribution.

## quad tree index
Provides pointers into the DDC data based on spatial location.

## query
A request for information from the database.

## radius-of-two-points dimension
Dimension that displays the relative position as two distances from different vertices on one or two base features.

## raster data
Graphic images that display elements using pixels. See [bitmap](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_201111). 
A representation of a graphic image as a set of dots. Each dot consists of one or more bits of information about the color and location of the dot, which the computer translates into pixels for screen display and into ink dots for printing.

## record
A row in a database; a representation of some physical or conceptual object.

## Rectangle IPT
Interactive placement technique that enables interactive placement of a rectangle at a user-specified point and angle.

## Rectangle SPT
Placement technique that places a rectangle at a specified point and angle.

## RectangleByTwoPoints IPT
Interactive placement technique that places a rectangle at two points, which you specify, that represent the diagonal of the rectangle.

## redline objects
Markup information and marginalia. They are not geographic features. Redline objects include lines, text, symbols, and rectangles that you place on the plot sheet.

## Reference ellipsoid
The model used to represent the shape of the surface of the earth.

## refresh metadata
Edits to the metadata are applied to a subset of the metadata optimized tables. The optimized tables are updated in the database during a refresh, but their values are queried only by NetWorks Core; thus, their contents are not written to disk. Only the person who refreshes metadata edits sees these changes.

## refresh
To update displayed graphics in all open map views. Refreshing the view with database changes updates the data in all map windows with any changes made in the master database.

## register
To assign a coordinate system to existing graphic data. Registration requires at least three control points.

## regular dimension
Dimension which is not small.

## relational database management system (RDBMS)
Software that stores, retrieves, and manipulates information as a collection of 2D tables. NetWorks Core uses the Oracle RDBMS.

## Relationship Geometry Interface (RGI)
A module used by the relationship services for additional filtering of relationship candidates and modifications of related features after edit and delete.

## RelativeAngle IPT
Interactive placement technique that lets you place text labels or symbols using the Construction Aids control. The geometry is created and rotated by an angle and put in dynamics.

## repeating component
A feature component that can occur more than once on a feature instance; for example, a street name that appears several places along a street.

## reporting interface
The interface through which you customize the presentation of selections, queries, and traces. This interface can be used simply to build formatted reports, or it can be used to perform client-specific operations on a set of data.

## republish metadata
Creates a completely new set of DDC and RAW files in the metadata directory from the optimized tables in the database.

## required attribute
Attribute that must be defined for a feature before the feature can be posted to the database.

## required component
Component that must be placed on the map for a feature to be valid.

## resolution
Sharpness or clarity of an image; the number of addressable points across a given area. Screen resolution is usually given with two numbers that indicate the number of pixels across the width and height of the largest image that can be displayed; for example, 1024 x 768.

## reverse feed
A situation where the signal feed direction for some of the conductors in a cable is opposite to the cable's feed direction. Feed direction is normally from the signal source or central office to the customer or terminal device. The digitized direction of the cable is by default assumed to be the feed direction. The Changed Feed command can be used to reverse the feed (and thus the coordinate order) of a cable.

## RGB
Color definition method in which colors are defined by their red, green, and blue values (0-255).

## ripple
To bracket and throw pairs and fibers along a cable network. The ripple utility reflects a rippled count in the downstream network when cable pairs are thrown, energized, or cut dead.

## rolled-up dialog box
A dialog box that shows only the title bar.

## ROP (Raster Operations)
Codes that define how the graphics device interface (GDI) combines the bits from the selected pen with the bits in the destination bitmap.

## rotate around
An adjustment mask that rotates the geometry interactively relative to another component.

## rotate relative to origin
An adjustment mask that rotates the geometry interactively around the origin of the component.

## rule
Conditional statement that tells the system how to react to a particular situation.

## scale bar
A moveable bar in the map window that is marked at intervals to indicate the relationship between the distance on a map and the corresponding actual distances.

## schema
A collection of tables and views within the database. A schema is typically identified by the Oracle username which is the owner of these tables.

## SCSF
Smart Client Software Factory. A set of .NET class libraries and guidance package add-ins to Visual Studio that build on the Composite UI Application Block.

## seamless interface
The joining of two computer programs so that they appear to be one program with a single interface.

## search conditions
Criteria that narrow or restrict a database query. Search conditions include attributes and values.

## second feature
For merge, the feature the user selects second. Component instances and/or attributes are copied from the second feature to the first feature and the second feature is deleted from the database.

## secondary data
Read-only data whose attributes and graphics exist in a secondary GDO data connection and whose metadata exists in the primary data connection; geographic data that is not created, edited, or deleted through NetWorks Core and does not meet the requirements for features. Typically, this is reference data, such as streets or parcels. Even though it is not managed by the application and can have no relationships, the data are integral to the management of the utility facility data. As such, the data are published in the mapfile as part of the facility data.

## secondary metadata
Metadata for secondary data that exists in the primary data connection.

## secondary view
View that contains secondary features. A secondary view cannot have delta updates.

## section length
An attribute of each cable section, this value represents the actual amount of cable represented by that section. This may differ from the geographically measured length for several reasons: 
  * Detail sections are usually drawn as short lines but may represent cable through a conduit. 
  * Slack cable can be placed for future use.
  * Changes in elevation of the cable path can result in more physical cable than the path length indicates.

## section start location
An attribute of each cable section, this value represents a specific point along the physical cable where each section starts.

## select set
One or more map objects selected for simultaneous manipulation.

## Select tool
![arrow](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_201153) The function assumed by the cursor that lets you place map objects in a select set.

## sequence
A serial list of unique numbers for numeric columns of a database's table. A sequence simplifies application programming by generating unique numbers. Sequence numbers are independent of tables, so the same sequence can be used for one or more tables.

## server-side deltas
[Deltas](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_201155) processing that happens in the PL/SQL stored procedure UpdateDeltas. 
The component of the software that augments the DDC files with the most recent changes from the database since the DDC files were published. DDC's are static between publishes, so the deltas component augments their recordsets with changes to the database. Server-side deltas refers to the processing done in the database itself using a PL/SQL procedure called UpdateDeltas that updates the MODIFICATIONLOG with values from the correct component views. Client-side deltas refers to the software that runs on each client machine that reads the MODIFICATIONLOG with its component view values that update the screen of the user.

## service
The telecommunication capability provided to customers such as DSL or POTS (standard phone service).

## sheer force
The force acting perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of a utility pole.

## shortcut keys
Keyboard keys you press to select menu and dialog box items as an alternative to using the mouse. The predefined shortcut keys are underlined, and you access them by pressing ALT + the underlined key. You can also define custom shortcut keys for commands in the application.

## simple attribute query
Basic query you build on one of the predefined query types.

## simple dimension
Dimension that displays the distance between two features on the map

## SlopeHatching SPT
Enables automated placement of hatched lines between a given upper edge and lower edge after the user digitizes these two edges.

## small dimension
Small dimensions are used when the length of the dimension line is less than the reversal distance. On small dimensions, the dimension text is outside the dimension line, usually behind the endpoint.

## SmartLocate
A tool that lets you specify the size of the locate zone. Any locatable objects that fall within that locate zone can be selected.

## snap mode
Mode you can turn on or off to move (or snap) a data point to certain map elements when your cursor enters the locate zone. The snap tolerance is defined on the SmartSketch tolerances dialog box.

## snap tolerance
How close you must be to a point (the midpoint of an existing feature, for example) for a feature being drawn to snap to it. For example, when you are drawing a line perpendicular to another line, the new line snaps to the existing line when your cursor moves within the locate zone.

## snapshot
A tool that takes a picture of information in a map window and places that picture on the clipboard. The picture can be pasted into another document.

## source feature
The starting feature in a trace. The types of features that can be selected as source features are defined in the database, based on the extraction type.

## sourceexpression
Source Expression: Table Aliases. The trace attempts to populate any additional columns specified for it. The result columns themselves do not have to be qualified; they are understood to apply to the TRACERESULT table. However, any columns in the connectivity or TRACERESULT tables used in G3E_SOURCEEXPR to specify a value for the result columns must be qualified properly. The table alias used for the TRACERESULT table is 'tr' and the connectivity table alias is 'conn'. Failure to qualify these columns results in an SQL parsing error.

## span length
The length of the linear attachments on a utility pole.

## spatial analysis
The process of examining and interpreting the spatial relationships that exist among features.

## spatial difference query
A database search that finds the geometries in a "from" feature that remain after all overlapping geometries in a "subtract" feature are removed. Often the "from" or "subtract" feature is the result of another query.

## spatial index
See [quad tree index](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_264985). 
Provides pointers into the DDC data based on spatial location.

## spatial query
Request for information about features and their spatial relationship to each other.

## splice
A node in the connectivity model for the Telecom industry. Physically a place where conductors are spliced together.

## SQL
Structured Query Language. An industry-standard language, used to retrieve information in a database. Also used to create, manipulate, and control relational databases. NetWorks Core queries are based on SQL.

## stacked dimensions
Two or more orthogonal dimensions combined to form a single dimension. All these orthogonal dimensions must share the same baseline.

## stacking styles
Drawing the same linear geometry more than once, usually with a smaller width each time. U.S. interstate highways on road maps are a good example of using a stacked style. The highway is first drawn in, for example, red. Then, the highway is drawn again using a line with a smaller width and a different color, for example, blue.

## stale graphics flag
When you use Feature Explorer and the Duct Configuration control to change the layout of the ducts in a formation, the graphics on the map no longer match the layout as defined in the Duct Configuration control; the graphics are now stale with respect to the attribution that defines the formation layout. Use the Place Formation command to replace or update the graphics. The Duct Configuration control and the Place Formation command use the stale graphics flags (defined in metadata) to communicate this information.

## StartAtComponent IPT
Interactive placement technique that places a line or area whose first point is coincident with the specified graphic component element.

## status bar
Located at the bottom of the main window, a field that displays information about the current state of the application, the current location of the cursor, and information that can help you decide what to do next.

## stroke pattern
Line pattern.

## style rule
A description of when to use a particular style definition. The technique used to achieve attribute-based symbology.

## style
A collection of display properties, such as color, weight, and pattern of a line, that you can apply to features. The style properties available for a feature depend on its geometry type.

## sub-table
A copy of some subset of the fields from a normalized metadata table.

## symbol
A graphic pattern used to represent a feature.

## synonym
Name assigned to an object such as a table, view, or sequence that can thereafter be use to refer to it. For example, to more easily reference the table of another user, you create a synonym for it and refer to it by the synonym alone, without entering the name of the user as a qualifier.

## synthesized components
A means by which you can use the geometry of one component to display another component of the same or a different feature.

## system tables
The core system tables are required for the system to function. Most of these tables predate metadata tables. They are created during system setup.

## table
A collection of rows and columns in a database. Each row in a table constitutes a record.

## tablespace
An area of disk consisting of one or more disk files. A tablespace can contain many tables, indexes, or clusters. A tablespace has a fixed size which can be altered.

## technical object
A feature associated with a pipeline; for example, a signpost.

## template
An empty work space on which each new workspace is built. The template contains default settings and connections for work spaces.

## terminal
Termination point for one or more conductors; the location on the map of a phone customer; owned to the conductor network.

## throw
Takes the counts affected by a [ripple](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_264955) and removes the old historical count values (annotated by being enclosed in brackets) and updates the count attribution and annotation to show its new current assignment. Edits done before throw are maintained in the count annotation until actually completed in the field. 
To bracket and throw pairs and fibers along a cable network. The ripple utility reflects a rippled count in the downstream network when cable pairs are thrown, energized, or cut dead.

## trace all
Trace type that finds all features connected to the seed feature, subject to the Stop and Filter criteria. The trace stops executing once it can no longer find any new connected rows.

## trace
Operation performed by the system that selects all features with node-edge connectivity to one of the following: 
  * A single feature you select. This trace can exclude certain elements and stops when it meets the predefined conditions. 
  * Beginning and ending features that you select. 
  * The beginning feature and everything that lies in the direction of the second feature you select. This trace can exclude certain elements and stops when it meets the predefined condition.

## transaction
A sequence of SQL statements whose effect is not accessible to other transactions until all the statements have been executed.

## translucency
A feature that is 100 % translucent is invisible. A feature that is 0% translucent is opaque.

## tree view
Graphical representation of a hierarchy of items or relationships.

## trigger
A piece of code that tells a database management system what other actions to perform when certain SQL statements have been executed.

## triggering component
In relationship processing, a graphic component of a feature that, when placed or edited, causes the firing of relationship software resulting in the establishing of a relationship.

## TrueType font (TTF)
The format of character glyphs used by Microsoft Windows for presentation. A TTF file contains many [glyphs](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_264969). 
Symbol that appears on a cursor when the cursor moves to within a specified tolerance of a locatable feature.

## Twip
A screen-independent unit to ensure that the proportion of screen elements are the same on all display systems. A twip is defined as being 1/1440 of an inch.

## UDB file
A file created as a tool used by the publish process in creating DDC files. The UDB file contains a list of what component views to publish for a particular configuration.

## units
Repeating attribute records. You can transfer units from one feature to another without disrupting relationships.

## UpdateDeltas
PL/SQL stored procedure that modifies the MODIFICATIONLOG, essentially adding records containing the values for modified or added component view records. It also records if a component view record has been deleted. It also does some cleanup of the MODIFICATIONLOG. This is used in [Deltas ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_201190)synchronization. 
The component of the software that augments the DDC files with the most recent changes from the database since the DDC files were published. DDC's are static between publishes, so the deltas component augments their recordsets with changes to the database. Server-side deltas refers to the processing done in the database itself using a PL/SQL procedure called UpdateDeltas that updates the MODIFICATIONLOG with values from the correct component views. Client-side deltas refers to the software that runs on each client machine that reads the MODIFICATIONLOG with its component view values that update the screen of the user.

## user preferences
A setting you define that is saved to the current user’s registry located in HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\PreferenceSet location. These settings apply to all work spaces.

## validation interface
An ActiveX DLL (automated COM object) called by relationship management software that is executed when a relationship is attempted by NetWorks Core operations and during feature validation. Used to validate relationships between features.

## validation
Process of testing for consistency within a set of data. For example, validation of metadata definitions ensures that data adheres to the rules defined in metadata.

## value field
Name of the field containing the entries that are displayed in a picklist.

## variable
Quantity whose value can change.

## vector
A one-dimensional series of objects, all of which are the same size and type.

## version management tools
Utilities that move metadata information from one schema to another. Can also include tools to provide daily maintenance tasks such as picklist updates.

## vertex
An endpoint of a line segment or the intersection of one or more lines.

## view at current scale
Map-window property in which features in the select set are highlighted, but the map window does not shift or change scale.

## view
A database component that behaves exactly like a table but has no independent existence of its own.

## viewer applications
NetViewer and Field Review.

## watermark
Highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. When DDCs are published, they are burned with the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER in the MODIFICATIONLOG. This is referred to as the watermark. Queries to the MODIFICATIONLOG use this watermark to limit the records returned. These queries yield new highest MODIFICATIONNUMBER/watermarks to be used in subsequent queries.

## windows forms
A style of application built around classes in the .NET Framework. To write traditional GUI applications using Microsoft .NET, you need to use Windows Forms.

## witness line
Used in orthogonal dimensions to indicate how dimension lines are offset from their appropriate positions where they indicate the distance. Dimension lines are sometimes offset so that they do not overlap each other or other important information on the map.

## work management system (WMS)
Software program, such as Severn Trent STORMS or Logica, used by some utility companies to track and coordinate costs, materials, and work crews.

## work point
Feature that represents where the actual work is to be done. In the database, a work point is a child of the structural feature.

## work space
A configuration file containing the settings and connections defined for the working environment in NetWorks Core. Work space files have a .gfw extension

## WPF
Windows Presentation Foundation. A graphical subsystem of the .NET Framework 3.0. It provides a consistent programming model for building applications, and provides a clear separation between the user interface and the business logic.

## Z lock
Overrides the [active Z](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_649004) and [element Z](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/g_649004) values so that all subsequent Zs you place are set to that height. 
The height value set in the Precision Coordinates control Height field. This value is the value used by default when setting the Z coordinate. 
When this mode is active, the height value is calculated using the feature you snap to when placing or editing a feature.

# HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service
The HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service is a Windows Service that is primarily responsible for executing the trace based on the specified input criteria and generate a graph that can be dynamically interrogated based on different filter and cost criteria. There are two basic web API endpoints available within the service: LoadNetwork and Execute. The LoadNetwork endpoint accepts the inputs such as relationship number, seed feature, goal filter and filter criteria to generate a graph of various trace pathways that exists as part of the network. The Execute endpoint accepts the dynamic filter criteria, inclusions, exclusions and cost criteria to determine the best possible pathways that meet those conditions. For a given trace analysis, the LoadNetwork is called only once to load the network. Execute can be called multiple times with different criteria to analyze and determine the best possible pathway. 
The InMemory Trace Service is used by the Interactive Trace command in the NetWorks Core desktop. If the service does not exist or is not running, the Interactive Trace command will fail. 
  * To Install and Configure the InMemory Trace Service:


  1. From the Microsoft Windows Start menu in the HxGN NetWorks Core drop-down list, select All Applications Configuration Wizard. 
  2. Click Next until you reach the HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service page. 
  3. Check Install HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service InMemory Trace Service. 
  4. Select the type of account to be used to start the service:
    1. Select Use LocalSystem to use the local predefined account 
OR
    1. Select Specific Account and enter the account credentials to use a specific account 
  5. Click Next. 
  6. The service will be installed and started using the specified account.


  * To Uninstall the InMemory Trace Service:


  1. From the Microsoft Windows Start menu in the HxGN NetWorks Core drop-down list, select All Applications Configuration Wizard. 
  2. In the Configuration Maintenance: 
    1. Select Remove: 
      1. Click Next
      2. The service will be stopped and uninstalled along with the current configuration
OR
    1. Select Edit: 
      1. Click Next until you reach the HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service page 
      2. Uncheck HxGN NetWorks InMemory Trace Service InMemory Trace Service to stop and uninstall the service 
      3. Click Next
      4. The service will be stopped and uninstalled. The other current configuration settings will be maintained

This table defines the coefficient of friction for the Cable Pull command, which is a combination of the properties of a given duct and a given cable.

#### Conversion Factors Reference Table
This table contains information necessary for conversion factors needed during secondary calculation and cable pull tension. For cable pull tension, used to convert the values from the automation object to the units required for display. There must be a USERNAME value in this table to match the TensionConversion and SWBPConversion entries in the G3E_EDTIFACE table. For a successful conversion to occur, the string in the G3E_PARAMETER1 column of the G3E_EDTIFACE table must match the string in the USERNAME column of this table. If no match is found, the command fails. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262112?tocId=GcrHwFS_4FjbTkDnzHBpGA) This table is not a metadata table but is referenced by the [G3E_EDTREFTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e8FlNBWI84ygMHqITll0UQ) and the [G3E_EDTREFFIELD tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pNK_Hx~9UstlQIp2~WBSdg). The table name and column names are user-defined. The default format of the table is listed here as an example.   
|  Column Name   |  Description  |  Unique   |  Null   |  PK   |  FK   |  Type   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  USERNAME  |  Name of the power factor  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  
|  VALUE  |  Factor value  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

#### G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES (Database Messages)
Table name:  G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES 
Contains information necessary to [localize error messages](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AXU4GZfTAgYbvg8yl8rVQw) for the PL/SQL code. This table stores multiple versions of the same message, localized and distinguished by a locale identifier. 
This table must be referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FUNCTIONALID  |  The identifier to which a group of messages belongs. This typically is a set of NetWorks Core functionality contained within a database package.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  No  |  Number (38)  |  
|  G3E_MSGNO  |  The user-defined message number, typically an Oracle error message number, a negative integer in the range of -20000 to -20999. This number may or not be the same as the error number used in RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR. This number cannot exceed the range for the database NUMBER(5), and the message numbers within a functional subsystem must be unique.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  No  |  Number(5)  |  
|  G3E_LCID  |  The locale identifier for the message. This is a foreign key to [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE.G3E_LCID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ).   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (4)  |  
|  G3E_MESSAGE  |  The localized message  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2(2048)  |  
* The combination of G3E_FUNCTIONALID, G3E_MSGNO, and G3E_LCID is the primary key.

#### Study Case Rate Adjustments by Time Reference Table
This table contains information necessary to adjust device loads using Load Profile Selection in PTI Analysis. The Adjust Device Loads grid on the Adjust Load dialog contains ALL load devices from the base network. Load devices matching TRAN_TRAN (Device names) from the study case selected obtain grid Kw, kVar, numcust, and rate grouping values from the study case metadata. Load devices that do not appear in the study case obtain values from the ANO's defined for the feature classes.

#### Tap Adjustment Objective Types Reference Table
This table contains information necessary for the Transformer Tap Adjustment calculations in PTI Analysis to represent valid values for the PTITapAdjustPrimaryObjective and PTITapAdjustSecondaryObjective values. There are two types of primary objectives allowed by VTRM: 
  * VTRM_FIX—Fixes high or low voltages. The algorithm's eliminates high or low voltages in the network. The algorithm finishes if there are no voltages outside acceptable limits or nothing can be done to eliminate existing violations. 
  * VTRM_OPTIMIZE—Drives voltages closer to center of the acceptable range of voltages. The algorithm gets all voltages as close to the center of the acceptable region as possible. That is, transformers is adjusted to drive voltages toward: (Vmax + Vmin) / 2. After all voltages are within acceptable limits, the algorithm may continue changing transformer taps. The algorithm finishes if nothing can be done to drive voltages closer to the center of the acceptable range of voltages. 


There are three types of secondary objectives:
  * VTRM_IMPROVE—Improves the conditions without causing further violations. That is, transformer adjustments are allowed if one or more voltages improve but no voltage is made worse. 
  * VTRM_FIXLV—Relieves low voltage violations at the expense of high voltage violations. High voltage violations may become worse. 
  * VTRM_FIXHV—Relieves high voltage violations at the expense of low voltage violations. Low voltage violations may become worse.

#### Cable Reference Table
This table identifies a cable with all its characteristics needed for calculating the pull tension. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263356?tocId=dq8yppiBC2ExALkaUJbhUw) This table is not a metadata table but is referenced by the [G3E_EDTREFTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e8FlNBWI84ygMHqITll0UQ) and the [G3E_EDTREFFIELD tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pNK_Hx~9UstlQIp2~WBSdg). The table name and column names are user-defined. The default format of the table is listed here as an example.   
|  Column Name   |  Description  |  Unique   |  Null   |  PK   |  FK   |  Type   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  CINO  |  A unique identifier for this table  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  
|  USERNAME  |  Used to display the selected duct on the command dialog box  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  
|  NUMBEROFCABLES  |  Specifies the number of cables for this cable definition. The default is 1.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  CONFIGURATION  |  Specifies the configuration for three-cable cables (1="Cradled", 2="Triangular"). Foreign key to the CCNO column in the CABLECONFIGURATION table.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |  
|  OUTSIDEDIAMETER  |  Specifies the outside diameter (in inches) for one cable  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  WEIGHTPERFOOT  |  Specifies the weight (in pounds) per foot of cable  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  INITIALTENSION  |  Specifies the initial tension (in pounds) of the cable from the spool  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  MAXSWBP  |  Specifies the maximum side wall bearing pressure (in pounds per foot) for this cable  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  MINBENDRADIUS  |  Specifies the minimum radius (in feet) through which this cable can be pulled  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  MAXTENSIONEYE  |  Specifies the maximum pulling tension (in pounds) that can be applied to the cable when using a pulling eye   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  MAXTENSIONGRIPPER  |  Specifies the maximum pulling tension (in pounds) that can be applied to the cable when using a gripper   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  SWBPCHANGEPOINT  |  Specifies the value (in pounds per foot) at which the automation object switches from the low coefficient of friction to the high coefficient of friction when computing the tension and side wall bearing pressure for a bend   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  MAXLENGTH  |  Specifies the value (in feet) that is the maximum length a cable of this type can be pulled regardless of other factors   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

#### Conversion Factors Reference Table
This table contains information necessary for conversion factors needed during secondary calculation and cable pull tension. For cable pull tension, used to convert the values from the automation object to the units required for display. There must be a USERNAME value in this table to match the TensionConversion and SWBPConversion entries in the G3E_EDTIFACE table. For a successful conversion to occur, the string in the G3E_PARAMETER1 column of the G3E_EDTIFACE table must match the string in the USERNAME column of this table. If no match is found, the command fails. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/262112?tocId=g7bdSGKT4VIFfKNdQvk~QQ) This table is not a metadata table but is referenced by the [G3E_EDTREFTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e8FlNBWI84ygMHqITll0UQ) and the [G3E_EDTREFFIELD tables](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pNK_Hx~9UstlQIp2~WBSdg). The table name and column names are user-defined. The default format of the table is listed here as an example.   
|  Column Name   |  Description  |  Unique   |  Null   |  PK   |  FK   |  Type   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  USERNAME  |  Name of the power factor  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  
|  VALUE  |  Factor value  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

#### G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED (Equipment Required Table)
Table name: G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED 
Stores the names of equipment required for loop resistance ranges. Reference this table in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) and [G3E_METDATATSUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) tables. You must populate the data according to your design criteria and equipment characteristics. To create this table, run the script creLoopMakeupRefTables.plb. 
You must localize the EQUIP_REQ column in this table so the values can be used in picklists. These are the steps required to localize this column: 
  1. Create an additional locale-specific version of the EQUIP_REQ column.
  2. Append an underscore and a language identifier to the current name, for example, EQUIP_REQ_000C.

  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (38,0)  |  
|  EQUIP_REQ  |  Description of the equipment  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (60)  |  
|  MIN_RESIST  |  Minimum resistance  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10,2)  |  
|  MAX_RESIST  |  Maximum resistance  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10,2)  |

This table must be referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) and [G3E_METDATATSUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) tables. You must populate the data according to your design criteria and equipment characteristics. To create this table, run the script creLoopMakeupRefTables.plb. 
You must localize the SERVICE, TYPE, and TECHNOLOGY columns in this table so the values in the columns can be used to populate picklists of available service types. These are the steps required to localize these columns: 
  1. Create an additional locale- specific version of the SERVICE, TYPE, and TECHNOLOGY columns. 
  2. Append an underscore and a language identifier to the current name, for example, SERVICE_000C.

#### GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS (Named Plots in Plot Templates Table)
Table name:  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS 
Contains information necessary to support the NetViewer interface to Plotting. This table is referenced by the GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG view directly from the database; hence, it is not published. The view (GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG) must be entered into [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) with select permission for all users.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDR_PLOTID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION  |  A description of what should be plotted  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |  Same as GDR_PLOTNAME  |  
|  GDR_CONFIGURATION  |  Configuration name (from CCM) for plot template  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_PLOTUSERNAME  |  The user- visible name associated with this named plot.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_PLOTNAME  |  A named plot within the work space  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_WORKSPACENAME  |  Pathname of the GFW plot template file  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |  **  |  
|  [GDR_WEBSERVERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g)  |  Name of the Web server that can plot this template  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |  Null  |  
|  GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT  |  Height (in mm) of plot sheet  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Float (10)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH  |  Width (in mm) of plot sheet  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Float (10)  |  **  |  
|  [GDR_PRINTERCLASS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g)  |  Value for classifying printer devices  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  0  |  
|  GDR_WORLDTOMETERS  |  Scale factor for converting model to meters  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Float (10)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_STYLEMAPID  |  ID of the style substitution mapping. This should be the value of [G3E_STYLETYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/c27M~vRL2FzhPQcHTHljFw).G3E_STNO if you would like style substitution. If the value is 0, then there is no style substitution.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |  **  |  
|  GDR_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |  **  |  
** Value of this field is automatically populated by the GNVPlotConfig utility.
GDR_WEBSERVERNAME Values
If specified, setting this field provides a way to partition plot templates into groups by the Web servers that are set up to plot those templates. Because a separate Web server must be set up for each language the customer wants to support, associating named plots with a Web server provides a method for localizing this data. One way that this could be used is to partition the rows in the GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS tables so the GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION can be localized. The same approach is used if the actual work space plot template files are localized (for example, due to localized marginalia text). Because this is a metadata support table, the typical metadata localization strategy is not employed. If the same plot is used in multiple languages (directed through different Web servers), multiple rows must exist in the table so you can type the plot description for each of the languages. 
GDR_PRINTERCLASS Values
You define this value to represent a class of printer devices. In the default view definition, the printer class values form a hierarchy where higher printer class numbers mean the printer has more capabilities. 
Example
You can classify plot templates into the following groups:
Null = Printer requirements are unknown  
1 = Black & white printer required  
2 = Gray scale printer required  
3 = 256 color printer required  
4 = True color printer required 
You can change the meaning of this field and change how the printer class values are compared in the view definition.

#### GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG (GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG View)
View name: GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG   
|  Field Name  |  Source Table  |  Source Field  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDR_PLOTID  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTID  |  
|  GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION  |  
|  GDR_PLOTUSERNAME  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTUSERNAME  |  
|  GDR_PLOTNAME  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTNAME  |  
|  GDR_CONFIGURATION  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_CONFIGURATION  |  
|  GDR_WORKSPACENAME  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_WORKSPACENAME  |  
|  GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT  |  
|  GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH  |  
|  GDR_PRINTERCLASS  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PRINTERCLASS  |  
|  GDR_WORLDTOMETERS  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_WORLDTOMETERS  |  
|  GDR_STYLEMAPID  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_STYLEMAPID  |  
|  GDR_MAPFRAMENAME  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_MAPFRAMENAME  |  
|  GDR_FRAMEHEIGHT  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_FRAMEHEIGHT  |  
|  GDR_FRAMEWIDTH  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_FRAMEWIDTH  |  
|  GDR_DISPLAYSCALE  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_DISPLAYSCALE  |  
|  GDR_BACKGROUNDCOLOR  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_BACKGROUNDCOLOR  |  
|  GDR_LEGENDNAME  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_LEGENDNAME  |  
|  GDR_DETAILID  |  GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES  |  GDR_DETAILID  |  
|  GDR_WEBSERVERNAME  |  GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS  |  GDR_WEBSERVERNAME  |  
|  GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME  |  GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS  |  GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME  |  
|  GDR_PRINTERUSERNAME  |  GDR_GNVPRINTERS  |  GDR_PRINTERUSERNAME  |  
|  GDR_PRINTERNAME  |  GDR_GNVPRINTERS  |  GDR_PRINTERNAME  |  
|  GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION  |  GDR_GNVPRINTERS  |  GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION  |  
|  GDR_COLORMODE  |  GDR_GNVPRINTERS  |  GDR_COLORMODE  |  
SQL>
SELECT 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTID, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTUSERNAME, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTNAME, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_CONFIGURATION, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_WORKSPACENAME, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PRINTERCLASS, GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_WORLDTOMETERS, 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_STYLEMAPID, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_MAPFRAMENAME, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_FRAMEHEIGHT, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_FRAMEWIDTH, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_DISPLAYSCALE, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_BACKGROUNDCOLOR, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_LEGENDNAME, 
GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_DETAILID, 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME, 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS.GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME, 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PRINTERUSERNAME, 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PRINTERNAME, 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION, 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_COLORMODE
FROM 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS, GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES, 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS, GDR_GNVPRINTERS 
WHERE (
( 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME IS NULL 
OR 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME = 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME 
) 
AND 
( GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTID = GDR_GNVMAPFRAMES.GDR_PLOTID ) 
AND 
( GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PRINTERCLASS = 0 
OR 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PRINTERCLASS = 0 
OR 
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PRINTERCLASS <= 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PRINTERCLASS 
) 
AND 
( 
( ABS(GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT - 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PAPERHEIGHT) <= 3 
AND 
ABS(GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH - GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PAPERWIDTH) <= 3 
)
OR 
( ABS(GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETHEIGHT - 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PAPERWIDTH) <= 3 
AND 
ABS(GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTSHEETWIDTH - GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PAPERHEIGHT) <= 3 
) 
) 
AND 
( GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME IS NULL 
OR 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME = 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS.GDR_WEBSERVERNAME 
) 
AND 
( GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME IS NULL 
OR 
GDR_GNVPRINTERS.GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME = 
GDR_GNVPLOTSERVERS.GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME 
) 
) WITH READ ONLY;

#### GDR_GNVPRINTERS (Available Printers for Plotting Table)
Table name: GDR_GNVPRINTERS 
Contains information necessary to support the NetViewer interface to Plotting and describes the list of printer devices that are available to print plots of various sizes. The table is only referenced indirectly by the GDR_GNVPLOTCONFIG view.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDR_PRINTERID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION  |  A description of the printer device.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  GDR_PRINTERUSERNAME  |  The user-visible name for this named printer.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  GDR_PRINTERNAME  |  The full pathname to the printer.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  GDR_WEBSERVERNAME  |  Name of the corresponding Web server for the plot server. For NetViewer to Plotting integration, the NetViewer Web server is also the Web server for the plot server. Use the name of the NetViewer Web server in this field.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME  |  Name of the plot server machine.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  GDR_PAPERHEIGHT  |  Height (in mm) of a paper size supported.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Float (10)  |   |  
|  GDR_PAPERWIDTH  |  Width (in mm) of a paper size supported.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Float (10)  |   |  
|  GDR_PRINTERCLASS  |  Customer defined value for classifying printer devices.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  0  |  
|  GDR_COLORMODE   |  The capability and the default color selection for each printer  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  
(1,0)   |  0  |  
|  GDR_OUTPUTFILETYPE  |  To specify the output file type, such as PDF. Null means the printer is a physical printer.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (4)  |   |  
|  GDR_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
GDR_WEBSERVERNAME and GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME Values
These two fields are optional. If not specified, the row specifies a printer device accessible from any Web server / plot server combination. Specifying a plot server and/or web server name lets you make associations between the available network printers and specific combinations of Web server / plot servers or just plot servers. This is required to describe a local printer that is on the plot server machine. The association of printers to Web servers could also be used to localize the GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION fields. 
GDR_PAPERHEIGHT and GDR_PAPERWIDTH Values
You need a separate row in this table for each of the paper sizes the printer can support. However, only the paper sizes that match plot sheet sizes are required. You can change the view definition to control the match comparison between plot sheet size and paper size. 
GDR_PRINTERCLASS Values
Define this value to represent a class of printer devices. In the default view definition, the printer class values form a hierarchy where higher printer class numbers mean the printer has more capabilities. 
Example
You can classify plot templates into the following groups:
Null—printer requirements are unknown  
1—Black & white printer required  
2—Gray scale printer required  
3—256 color printer required  
4—True color printer required 
You can change the meaning of this field and change how the printer class values are compared in the view definition. 
GDR_COLORMODE Values
The default value for each kind of printer is initially set to 0. The GDR_COLORMODE value states the capability and the default color selection for each printer. Valid values are 0, 1, and 2. Any other value or the absence of this field is treated as a a GDR_COLORMODE value of 0. 
There are two methods NetViewer uses to determine the color capability of a printer. The method used is dependent on the type of printer. The two types of printers are Network and Local. Network printers are defined as printers installed on the Plot Server. Local printers are defined as printers installed on a local computer and shared on the network. 
Even if a printer supports color, you can set this value to 0 to prevent users from printing in color. 
Use the following table as a guide to set the GDR_GNVPRINTERS value to represent the capability and the default color selection for each printer.   
|  Printer Type  |  Printer Supports Color  |  GDR_COLORMODE Value  |  NetViewer Options  |  Default Selection   |  Resulting Printout  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  1  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  2  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |

#### G3E_BATCHPLOTMFA (Batch Plotting Attributes Table)
Table name: G3E_BATCHPLOTMFA 
Contains information necessary to support the batch plotting Web example. It describes the various Map Frame Assignments associated with a plot. This table is referenced in the G3E_DATASUPPORT. To create this table, run the creBatchPlotTables.plb script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  BATCH_PLOT_ID  |  Foreign key to the associated batch plot definition  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |  
|  NAME  |  Name assigned to the map frame  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (50)  |  
|  PLOT_DATA_QUERY  |  The SQL associated with the data query for display in this map frame.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (255)  |  
|  PLOT_FIELDS_QUERY  |  The SQL associated with the fields query to populate automatic fields from this map frame.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (255)  |  
|  LINE_WEIGHT  |  The line weight to assign (points) if a PLOT_DATA_QUERY is specified.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (38)  |  
|  COLOR  |  The color to assign (RGB) if a PLOT_DATA_QUERY is specified.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (38)  |  
|  FILL_COLOR  |  The fill color to assign (RGB) if a PLOT_DATA_QUERY is specified.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (38)  |  
|  DISPLAY_MODE_ON  |  The display mode to assign (True/False) if a PLOT_DATA_QUERY is specified.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (5)  |  
|  DISPLAY_SCALE_MODE  |  The display scale to assign (gplotDisplayScaleOff/gplotDisplayScaleOn/gplotDisplayScaleMetadata)  if a PLOT_DATA_QUERY is specified.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (26)  |  
|  MAP_SCALE  |  Scale to which the map frame should be zoomed to.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |

### PL_SQL Message Localization

#### G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES (Database Messages)
Table name:  G3E_DATABASE_MESSAGES 
Contains information necessary to [localize error messages](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AXU4GZfTAgYbvg8yl8rVQw) for the PL/SQL code. This table stores multiple versions of the same message, localized and distinguished by a locale identifier. 
This table must be referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FUNCTIONALID  |  The identifier to which a group of messages belongs. This typically is a set of NetWorks Core functionality contained within a database package.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  No  |  Number (38)  |  
|  G3E_MSGNO  |  The user-defined message number, typically an Oracle error message number, a negative integer in the range of -20000 to -20999. This number may or not be the same as the error number used in RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR. This number cannot exceed the range for the database NUMBER(5), and the message numbers within a functional subsystem must be unique.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  No  |  Number(5)  |  
|  G3E_LCID  |  The locale identifier for the message. This is a foreign key to [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE.G3E_LCID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ).   |  No  |  No  |  Yes*  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (4)  |  
|  G3E_MESSAGE  |  The localized message  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2(2048)  |  
* The combination of G3E_FUNCTIONALID, G3E_MSGNO, and G3E_LCID is the primary key.

### Portal Plot_Export Interface

#### GDRV_CLIENTSAUTOMATICFIELD (View)
|  Field Name  |  Source Table  |  Source Field  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  FIELD_ID  |  GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD  |  ID  |  
|  GDR_PLOTNAME  |  GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS  |  GDR_PLOTNAME  |  
|  CLIENT_ID  |  GDR_CLIENTAUTOMATICFIELDMAP  |  PLOTCLIENTID  |  
|  FIELD_NAME  |  GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD  |  AUTOMATICFIELD  |  
|  DEFAULTVALUE  |  GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD  |  DEFAULTVALUE  |  
|  FIELD_USERNAME  |  GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD  |  G3E_USERNAME  |  
SELECT 
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD.ID,
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTNAME,
GDR_CLIENTAUTOMATICFIELDMAP.PLOTCLIENTID,
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD.AUTOMATICFIELD,
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD.DEFAULTVALUE,
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD.G3E_USERNAME
FROM 
GDR_CLIENTAUTOMATICFIELDMAP,
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD,
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS
WHERE 
GDR_CLIENTAUTOMATICFIELDMAP.PLOTATTRIBUTECONFIGNUMBER = 
GDR_PLOTAUTOMATICFIELD.PLOTATTRIBUTECONFIGNUMBER
AND 
GDR_CLIENTAUTOMATICFIELDMAP.GDR_PLOTID =
GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS.GDR_PLOTID
WITH READ ONLY;

|  For Example:
  1. AutomaticField – Currentdate Default Value – TO_CHAR(sysdate,’DD-MM-YYYY’) G3E_USERNAME - Null The Plot field query would be – SELECT TO_CHAR(sysdate,'DD-MM-YYYY') as Currentdate FROM DUAL
  2. AutomaticField – ConductorType Default Value – Null G3E_USERNAME – Conductor Type Users must provide the value for this Automatic field through NetPlot command in Portal. The value would be of type “Conductor Type” attribute. The provided value would be used in the query.  User provided – Secondary as value. SELECT ‘Secondary’ as ConductorType FROM DUAL

#### Tap Adjustment Objective Types Reference Table
This table contains information necessary for the Transformer Tap Adjustment calculations in PTI Analysis to represent valid values for the PTITapAdjustPrimaryObjective and PTITapAdjustSecondaryObjective values. There are two types of primary objectives allowed by VTRM: 
  * VTRM_FIX—Fixes high or low voltages. The algorithm's eliminates high or low voltages in the network. The algorithm finishes if there are no voltages outside acceptable limits or nothing can be done to eliminate existing violations. 
  * VTRM_OPTIMIZE—Drives voltages closer to center of the acceptable range of voltages. The algorithm gets all voltages as close to the center of the acceptable region as possible. That is, transformers is adjusted to drive voltages toward: (Vmax + Vmin) / 2. After all voltages are within acceptable limits, the algorithm may continue changing transformer taps. The algorithm finishes if nothing can be done to drive voltages closer to the center of the acceptable range of voltages. 


There are three types of secondary objectives:
  * VTRM_IMPROVE—Improves the conditions without causing further violations. That is, transformer adjustments are allowed if one or more voltages improve but no voltage is made worse. 
  * VTRM_FIXLV—Relieves low voltage violations at the expense of high voltage violations. High voltage violations may become worse. 
  * VTRM_FIXHV—Relieves high voltage violations at the expense of low voltage violations. Low voltage violations may become worse.

### Roles

#### G3E_ROLES (User Roles Table)
Table name: G3E_ROLES 
Contains information about the roles currently assigned to the user. This table is not a table but is constructed dynamically in memory by querying USER_ROLE_PRIVS and ROLE_ROLE_PRIVS. This table is constructed dynamically. It is described as it is available through metadata on the client. Do not reference it in G3E_DATASUPPORT. It is not persisted in any way. 
This is the SQL statement the software executes. You can execute the statement to double check your role assignments. 
SQL> select distinct granted_role from dba_role_privs start with grantee = <the user login> connect by grantee = prior granted_role;   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |

#### Assembly Ownership Processing Table
Table name: TEMP$<Ownership Optable>
When performing an assembly placement, the assembly functionality uses the metadata information defined for the catalog ownership relationship to understand the ownership relationship between the features. During this processing, this ownership information is written to a temporary database table having the name TEMP$<OwnershipOptable> where <OwnershipOptable> is the name of the metadata optable defined for the catalog ownership relationship in [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA). Each NetWorks Core database schema should only have one Assembly Ownership Processing table within it. 
This table is a session-specific temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of the database session. It is an internal table used by the deep copy software.

In case of repeating components, G3E_PERCENT value itself does not help in extracting the total percentage of the feature within a given area. The combined information of this field value and G3E_PERCENT helps the user to determine the percentage of the complete feature component instead of just individual component occurrences. The value of this field 1 for point features. This does not require the user to differentiate between the point or linear (or area) feature when calculating the total percentage using supporting tools developed by the user.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

#### G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED (Equipment Required Table)
Table name: G3E_EQUIPMENTREQUIRED 
Stores the names of equipment required for loop resistance ranges. Reference this table in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) and [G3E_METDATATSUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) tables. You must populate the data according to your design criteria and equipment characteristics. To create this table, run the script creLoopMakeupRefTables.plb. 
You must localize the EQUIP_REQ column in this table so the values can be used in picklists. These are the steps required to localize this column: 
  1. Create an additional locale-specific version of the EQUIP_REQ column.
  2. Append an underscore and a language identifier to the current name, for example, EQUIP_REQ_000C.

  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  ID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (38,0)  |  
|  EQUIP_REQ  |  Description of the equipment  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (60)  |  
|  MIN_RESIST  |  Minimum resistance  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10,2)  |  
|  MAX_RESIST  |  Maximum resistance  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10,2)  |

#### G3E_JOB (Job Table)
Table name: G3E_JOB 
This table contains information necessary for the work management interfaces. Optionally, it can be included in a feature definition and used in relationship modeling. This table is typically defined as a component. The table is user defined. The table name and all the required columns in this table must be included in the [G3E_JOBDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TBQDr_BsRYh8ej2Rr97t2g) table.

|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  The unique alphanumeric identifier of the Job. Several parts of the NetWorks Core system require comma- separated lists of jobs.  A constraint should exist on the table to prevent the use of a comma (,) or a dot (.) as part of the job name. Dots in published job names can cause errors.   |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Unique identifier in the table.  |   |  Y  |   |   |  Number(10)  |

#### G3E_JOBSTATUS (Job Status Table)
Table name: G3E_JOBSTATUS 
Contains information about jobs that need to be processed by the job life cycle program. The work management interfaces create entries in this table. This table is monitored by the [JLCMonitor.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CvlskSKcYAGysNAmFC1xhw). This in turn launches [JobLifeCycle.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mSl5PizaLmQ2J6Uj9QtPuw). This table is referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table. To create this table, run the creStormsSupportTables.plb script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes1  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  
|  WORK_REQUEST  |  Number of the work request from the job system (STORMS, Logica, or Generic Work Management)  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (12,0)  |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  NetWorks Core job identifier corresponding to the work request   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes[2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g)  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  WR_STATE_CODE  |  Code or indicator from the work management system about the current state of the job - like Lock Down and Field Complete. The values are configurable for each implementation. They must match values used in [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE.G3E_WR_STATE_CODE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg).   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  
|  GIS_JOB_STATUS  |  Indicator of the state that should be associated with the GIS features corresponding to the WR_STATE_CODE. The values are configurable but are like NEW, DES, ASB, CAN, CLS, and so forth. They must match values used in [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE.G3E_GIS_JOB_STATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg).   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  
|  G3E_STATUS_CODE  |  Contains an indicator of what state the associated job is in relative to the life cycle processing. Possible values: NEW, EXECUTING, ERROR, COMPLETE   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  SUBMITTED_DATE  |  Date the request was inserted into the table. Also updated whenever GIS_JOB_STATUS is changed.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Date  |

#### G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER (Rippled Feature Log)
Table name: G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER 
Used by the Pair Count control, Ripple, and Trace commands. When a feature is rippled or when a piece of equipment has its pairs cut dead in Feature Explorer, a log of that feature is added to the G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER table. 
When the Throw command is selected, it retrieves the list of features to throw by selecting all the features from this table. This is done for performance. Therefore, the Throw command does not have to reanalyze the whole network. As each feature is thrown, its log entry is removed from the table. This table is referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
To [publish a subset job containing features that have rippled count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3zbeMTRB0mjF7ujd7R8H9Q), the feature that has the pair count component must reference this table in G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE and then in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_COMPONENT. 
To create this table, run the script crePairCountWorkOrderTable.plb.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Feature identifier  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  The job identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The feature identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5, 0)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The component identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The component number of the feature.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5, 0)  |

#### G3E_ROLES (User Roles Table)
Table name: G3E_ROLES 
Contains information about the roles currently assigned to the user. This table is not a table but is constructed dynamically in memory by querying USER_ROLE_PRIVS and ROLE_ROLE_PRIVS. This table is constructed dynamically. It is described as it is available through metadata on the client. Do not reference it in G3E_DATASUPPORT. It is not persisted in any way. 
This is the SQL statement the software executes. You can execute the statement to double check your role assignments. 
SQL> select distinct granted_role from dba_role_privs start with grantee = <the user login> connect by grantee = prior granted_role;   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |

|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the role associated with the current user  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |

#### G3E_TEMPKEYS (Temporary Keys Table)
Table name: G3E_TEMPKEYS 
A temporary repository for feature key information in the database and used by commands or other functionality that need to reference a collection of feature keys for processing in database logic. In most cases, it is more performant for database code to process sets of rows at a time instead of processing individual rows for a feature one at a time. Having the keys in a database table makes the set of them available for use in "set of rows" algorithms, that is, find and process all of them in a single query instead of querying for them individually. 
This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. Using a transaction-specific temporary table obviates any need to worry about data from different sessions conflicting with each other and also any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
This table is referenced in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Feature identifier  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number(10,0)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Feature number  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component number  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  Component identifier  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |

This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. Using a transaction-specific temporary table obviates any need to worry about data from different sessions conflicting with each other and also any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
The initial user for this table is the validation functionality, specifically the G3E_VALIDATESET and G3E_VALIDATESET_PROD packages. 
The table can be created by running the creG3EValidateSetTmp.plb script.

** Value of this field is automatically populated by the GNVPlotConfig utility.
GDR_WEBSERVERNAME Values
If specified, setting this field provides a way to partition plot templates into groups by the Web servers that are set up to plot those templates. Because a separate Web server must be set up for each language the customer wants to support, associating named plots with a Web server provides a method for localizing this data. One way that this could be used is to partition the rows in the GDR_GNVNAMEDPLOTS tables so the GDR_PLOTDESCRIPTION can be localized. The same approach is used if the actual work space plot template files are localized (for example, due to localized marginalia text). Because this is a metadata support table, the typical metadata localization strategy is not employed. If the same plot is used in multiple languages (directed through different Web servers), multiple rows must exist in the table so you can type the plot description for each of the languages. 
GDR_PRINTERCLASS Values
You define this value to represent a class of printer devices. In the default view definition, the printer class values form a hierarchy where higher printer class numbers mean the printer has more capabilities. 
Example
You can classify plot templates into the following groups:
Null = Printer requirements are unknown  
1 = Black & white printer required  
2 = Gray scale printer required  
3 = 256 color printer required  
4 = True color printer required 
You can change the meaning of this field and change how the printer class values are compared in the view definition.
