GDR_WEBSERVERNAME and GDR_PLOTSERVERNAME Values
These two fields are optional. If not specified, the row specifies a printer device accessible from any Web server / plot server combination. Specifying a plot server and/or web server name lets you make associations between the available network printers and specific combinations of Web server / plot servers or just plot servers. This is required to describe a local printer that is on the plot server machine. The association of printers to Web servers could also be used to localize the GDR_PRINTERDESCRIPTION fields. 
GDR_PAPERHEIGHT and GDR_PAPERWIDTH Values
You need a separate row in this table for each of the paper sizes the printer can support. However, only the paper sizes that match plot sheet sizes are required. You can change the view definition to control the match comparison between plot sheet size and paper size. 
GDR_PRINTERCLASS Values
Define this value to represent a class of printer devices. In the default view definition, the printer class values form a hierarchy where higher printer class numbers mean the printer has more capabilities. 
Example
You can classify plot templates into the following groups:
Null—printer requirements are unknown  
1—Black & white printer required  
2—Gray scale printer required  
3—256 color printer required  
4—True color printer required 
You can change the meaning of this field and change how the printer class values are compared in the view definition. 
GDR_COLORMODE Values
The default value for each kind of printer is initially set to 0. The GDR_COLORMODE value states the capability and the default color selection for each printer. Valid values are 0, 1, and 2. Any other value or the absence of this field is treated as a a GDR_COLORMODE value of 0. 
There are two methods NetViewer uses to determine the color capability of a printer. The method used is dependent on the type of printer. The two types of printers are Network and Local. Network printers are defined as printers installed on the Plot Server. Local printers are defined as printers installed on a local computer and shared on the network. 
Even if a printer supports color, you can set this value to 0 to prevent users from printing in color. 
Use the following table as a guide to set the GDR_GNVPRINTERS value to represent the capability and the default color selection for each printer.   
|  Printer Type  |  Printer Supports Color  |  GDR_COLORMODE Value  |  NetViewer Options  |  Default Selection   |  Resulting Printout  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Network  |  Yes  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Network  |  No  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  1  |  Black & White and Color  |  Black & White  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Local  |  Yes  |  2  |  Black & White and Color  |  Color  |  Black & White or Color, depending on user selection  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  0  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  1  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  
|  Local  |  No  |  2  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |  Black & White  |

#### GDT_POSTWATERMARKS (Posting Watermarks Table)
Table name: GDT_POSTWATERMARKS 
Used by posting, publishing, and processing deltas. The post procedure puts the next MODIFICATIONLOG sequence, which corresponds to the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER of the MODIFICATIONLOG, and its transaction number before it begins processing. At the end, it cleans any stale transactions out of the procedure, including its own. All maximum MODIFICATIONLOG queries (done by publishing and deltas processing) take the minimum of this table so any in-process posting jobs are considered when calculating watermarks. Its contents are temporary. This table should be referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDUSN  |  First of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDSLOT  |  Second of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDSQN  |  Third of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_MODLOGNUM  |  Next MODIFICATIONLOG sequence number.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |

#### GDT_RASTERFILELOCK (Raster File Locking Table)
Table name: GDT_RASTERFILELOCK 
Used by the raster delete and post processing. An entry is made in the table before post for each raster file that is to be posted with edits. The entry is removed after a successful post operation. Its contents are temporary. The [RasterFileLockingEnabled](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) parameter in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER indicates whether raster file locking should be turned on for the Erase Raster, Reregister Raster, New Feature, Edit Feature, Edit Tool, and Edit Geometry commands. Reference this table in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDT_RasterFileName  |  Raster file name  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  
|  GDT_JobId  |  Job identifier of the job in the job table  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  
|  GDT_EditDate  |  Date the table was edited  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Date  |

#### GDT_RASTER_SUPPORT_TMP (Raster Support Temporary Table)
Table name: GDT_RASTER_SUPPORT_TMP 
Used by the UpdateFilePaths.exe utility to store information about the raster files to be cleaned up as part of an unversioning process. The G3E_RASTER_SUPPORT.SpecifyRasterNamesForUpdate database procedure uses this table to store the raster file name information for the files to be unversioned. 
This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table. Any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. If you use a transaction-specific temporary table you prevent data from different sessions from conflicting with each other and any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
The SpecifyRasterNamesForUpdate and UpdateRasterNames procedures of the G3E_RASTER_SUPPORT database package use this table.

The table is automatically created by the utility if it does not exist. However, it is created only if the user login permits it. Otherwise the operation fails. |  G3E_MEASURED_LENGTH  |  Contains the calculated length (linear features) or area (area features). Populated only through Area Report Utility when Percent is populated. In case of repeating components, G3E_PERCENT value itself does not help in extracting the total percentage of the feature within a given area. The combined information of this field value and G3E_PERCENT helps the user to determine the percentage of the complete feature component instead of just individual component occurrences. The value of this field 1 for point features. This does not require the user to differentiate between the point or linear (or area) feature when calculating the total percentage using supporting tools developed by the user.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

#### TRACEID (Trace Identifiers Table)
Table name: TRACEID 
Lists traces that have been defined and potentially executed. It is a snapshot of the specific set of information that was used to perform a trace, which may no longer agree with the values in G3E_TRACE if it gets changed. This table is referenced in the G3E_DATASUPPORT. To create this table, run the creTraceTables.plb script. 
Because of limitations in the Visual Basic ComboBox list index value, Trace displays an error if the table has more than 32767 traces at any given time. To prevent the error, you should periodically [cleanup unwanted traces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ubXBuucgsLmTsrfR7yG_7A).

#### TRACERESULT (Trace Results Table)
Table name: TRACERESULT 
Contains the results of the traces. It contains the NetWorks Core keys and node number information for the rows in the connectivity table that were found by the trace. It also contains additional information needed by the trace algorithm to perform the trace as well as allowing queries to retrieve the trace information properly. It is possible, depending on the nature of the data and the specific type of trace being performed, that multiple rows for a particular connectivity occurrence for the same feature exist in the TRACERESULT table. For example, if a cost column was specified for the trace, then these duplicate rows can be eliminated through the use of a grouping function (like MIN on the cost column) in the SELECT statement retrieving rows from the table. It is best if the logic retrieving the rows from the TRACERESULT table expects and handles these cases. This table is referenced in the G3E_DATASUPPORT. To create this table, run the creTraceTables.plb script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TNO  |  Number of the trace (TRACEID.G3E_ID) that this data belongs to.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_GROUP  |  Grouping column for the results. It is defined in anticipation of supporting simultaneous trace operations. It keeps the data for each individual trace operation separate.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |  
|  G3E_TRACEORDER  |  The order in which this row was found in the trace. This value equates to the depth of the feature in the graph represented by the trace with the seed feature being the root (G3E_TRACEORDER = 1)   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCEID  |  The row in the trace results table to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This value only applies to the graph as it was built during this specific trace. A feature can have different parents in different traces. This column contains the G3E_ID value of the parent row.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFID  |  Partial identifier for the row in the trace results table to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This column contains the G3E_FID value of the parent row, which in combination with the G3E_SOURCEID value also uniquely identifies a parent row in the trace results. These two columns are required for uniqueness since features having more than two nodes of connectivity have multiple rows in the connectivity table for your model.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCECID  |  Partial identifier for the row in the trace results to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root.  This column contains the G3E_CID value of the parent row, which in combination with the G3E_SOURCEFID value, also uniquely identifies a parent row in the trace results. These two columns are required for uniqueness because features having more than two nodes of connectivity also have multiple rows in the connectivity table.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCENODE  |  This is the specific node number in the row in the trace results to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This column contains the G3E_NODE1 or G3E_NODE2 value of the parent row.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_COST  |  The cost required to get from the source feature to this feature for this particular case. If the G3E_PATHCOST value was defined for the trace, this column contains a true cost value based on the values found in the G3E_PATHCOST expression. Otherwise, G3E_COST calculates the cost by assigning each path a value of 1.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  G3E_NODE1  |  The Node1 value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_NODE2  |  The Node2 value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_ID  |  The G3E_ID value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The G3E_FID value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The G3E_FNO value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The G3E_CNO value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The G3E_CID value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_FNO1  |  For node-ordered connectivity models, this is the value of the From Feature Number for the row. This value is obtained from the connectivity table.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_FNO2  |  For node-ordered connectivity models, this is the value of the To Feature Number for the row. This value is obtained from the connectivity table.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_REVFLAG  |  For traces having implied direction and respect a reverse flag, this is the value of the Reverse Flag for the row. This value is obtained from the connectivity table.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Char (1)  |  
|  USER_COL1  |  Used for the trace that is needed for the electric analysis.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  USER_COL2  |  Used for the trace that is needed for the electric analysis.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |

### CES Interface

#### CES_FEATURETILEREL (CES Feature Tile Relationship – Incremental Table)
Table name: CES_FEATURETILEREL 
Contains information necessary to support the CES interface in Electric data models. The Feature Tile Relationship table contains all the facilities within a grid where the grid has been updated. This supports incrementally updating CES_FEATURETILERELATION. This table is referenced in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). To create this table, run the creCesInterfaceTables.sql script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Facility ID of the feature in the grid. For incremental Feature Tile Relationship this is the Facility ID of the Grid.   |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9)  |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Login identifier of the user associated with this query  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  
|  G3E_QUERYNAME  |  User- specified name of the query that groups the set of data for the particular analysis operation   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  
|  G3E_SECONDFID  |  Facility ID of the grid. For incremental Feature Tile Relationship this is the facility ID of the feature in the Grid.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (9)  |  
|  G3E_PERCENT  |  Percentage of overlap of G3E_FID within G3E_SECONDFID  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |  
|  G3E_MEASURED_LENGTH  |  Contains the calculated length (linear features) or area (area features). Populated only through [Area Report Utility](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/MVY9RPCzYcQhuaVTz78vew) when Percent is populated. In case of repeating components, G3E_PERCENT value itself does not help in extracting the total percentage of the feature within a given area. The combined information of this field value and G3E_PERCENT helps the user to determine the percentage of the complete feature component instead of just individual component occurrences. The value of this field 1 for point features. This does not require the user to differentiate between the point or linear (or area) feature when calculating the total percentage using supporting tools developed by the user.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

In case of repeating components, G3E_PERCENT value itself does not help in extracting the total percentage of the feature within a given area. ### Loop Makeup

#### G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER (Rippled Feature Log)
Table name: G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER 
Used by the Pair Count control, Ripple, and Trace commands. When a feature is rippled or when a piece of equipment has its pairs cut dead in Feature Explorer, a log of that feature is added to the G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER table. 
When the Throw command is selected, it retrieves the list of features to throw by selecting all the features from this table. This is done for performance. Therefore, the Throw command does not have to reanalyze the whole network. As each feature is thrown, its log entry is removed from the table. This table is referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
To [publish a subset job containing features that have rippled count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3zbeMTRB0mjF7ujd7R8H9Q), the feature that has the pair count component must reference this table in G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE and then in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_COMPONENT. 
To create this table, run the script crePairCountWorkOrderTable.plb.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Feature identifier  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  The job identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  G3E_FID  |  The feature identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number of the feature.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5, 0)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  The component identifier of the feature.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10, 0)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The component number of the feature.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5, 0)  |

### Many Ownership Allocation Relationship

#### TMP$G3E_MANYOWNALLOCREL (Many Ownership Allocation Relationship Temporary Table)
Table name: TMP$G3E_MANYOWNALLOCREL 
Used by the Many Ownership Allocation software to map additional relationship information to the features in an allocation set defined in an allocation results table. The G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP_ALLOCATION.CalculateExistingAllocationRel procedure can be called to populate this table with the information needed by the Many Ownership Allocation software. 
This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table. Any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. If you use a transaction-specific temporary table you prevent data from different sessions from conflicting with each other and any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
The CalculateExistingAllocationRel procedure of the G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP_ALLOCATION database procedure uses this table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |

|  G3E_LEVEL  |  The level at which the feature is found by the allocation.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_ALLOCATE  |  Whether or not the feature is allocated to the seed feature for the allocation. Allowable values are 0 or 1.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Feature identifier  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Feature number  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5)  |   |  
|  INS_BY_REL  |  Whether or not the row in the table is inserted by the relationship logic that finds related features. Allowable values are 0 or 1.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number(1)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_OWNERFID  |  The identifier of the owner feature found by the allocation.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |

### Raster

|  G3E_MEASURED_LENGTH  |  Contains the calculated length (linear features) or area (area features). Populated only through Area Report Utility when Percent is populated. In case of repeating components, G3E_PERCENT value itself does not help in extracting the total percentage of the feature within a given area. The combined information of this field value and G3E_PERCENT helps the user to determine the percentage of the complete feature component instead of just individual component occurrences. The value of this field 1 for point features. This does not require the user to differentiate between the point or linear (or area) feature when calculating the total percentage using supporting tools developed by the user.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |

### Specialized Commands

#### Assembly Ownership Processing Table
Table name: TEMP$<Ownership Optable>
When performing an assembly placement, the assembly functionality uses the metadata information defined for the catalog ownership relationship to understand the ownership relationship between the features. During this processing, this ownership information is written to a temporary database table having the name TEMP$<OwnershipOptable> where <OwnershipOptable> is the name of the metadata optable defined for the catalog ownership relationship in [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA). Each NetWorks Core database schema should only have one Assembly Ownership Processing table within it. 
This table is a session-specific temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of the database session. It is an internal table used by the deep copy software.

#### G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER (Rippled Feature Log)
Table name: G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER 
Used by the Pair Count control, Ripple, and Trace commands. When a feature is rippled or when a piece of equipment has its pairs cut dead in Feature Explorer, a log of that feature is added to the G3E_PAIRCOUNTWORKORDER table. 
When the Throw command is selected, it retrieves the list of features to throw by selecting all the features from this table. This is done for performance. Therefore, the Throw command does not have to reanalyze the whole network. As each feature is thrown, its log entry is removed from the table. This table is referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g). 
To [publish a subset job containing features that have rippled count](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3zbeMTRB0mjF7ujd7R8H9Q), the feature that has the pair count component must reference this table in G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE and then in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_COMPONENT. 
To create this table, run the script crePairCountWorkOrderTable.plb.

|  G3E_CNO  |  The component number of the feature.  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5, 0)  |

#### G3E_TEMPKEYS (Temporary Keys Table)
Table name: G3E_TEMPKEYS 
A temporary repository for feature key information in the database and used by commands or other functionality that need to reference a collection of feature keys for processing in database logic. In most cases, it is more performant for database code to process sets of rows at a time instead of processing individual rows for a feature one at a time. Having the keys in a database table makes the set of them available for use in "set of rows" algorithms, that is, find and process all of them in a single query instead of querying for them individually. 
This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. Using a transaction-specific temporary table obviates any need to worry about data from different sessions conflicting with each other and also any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
This table is referenced in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FID  |  Feature identifier  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number(10,0)  |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Feature number  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component number  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |  
|  G3E_CID  |  Component identifier  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |

#### G3E_VALIDATESET_TMP (Validate Set Temporary Table)
Table name: G3E_VALIDATESET_TMP 
Used by the validation code to store the information about the features to be validated as well as the features directly related to them. The G3E_VALIDATESET.DefineFeatures and G3E_VALIDATESET_PROD.DefineFeaturesFromPendingEdits procedures can be used to specify the initial set of features to be validated. The G3E_VALIDATESET.GetValidateSet procedure can be called to retrieve the set of feature information. 
This table is a transaction-specific Oracle temporary table, meaning any rows inserted into it can only be seen by the database session that inserted them and only for the lifetime of that database transaction. The rows are removed automatically once the database transaction is completed by a commit or a rollback. Using a transaction-specific temporary table obviates any need to worry about data from different sessions conflicting with each other and also any administration concerns regarding the size of this table. 
The initial user for this table is the validation functionality, specifically the G3E_VALIDATESET and G3E_VALIDATESET_PROD packages. 
The table can be created by running the creG3EValidateSetTmp.plb script. 
You should not replicate the contents to the field database.

#### GDT_POSTWATERMARKS (Posting Watermarks Table)
Table name: GDT_POSTWATERMARKS 
Used by posting, publishing, and processing deltas. The post procedure puts the next MODIFICATIONLOG sequence, which corresponds to the maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER of the MODIFICATIONLOG, and its transaction number before it begins processing. At the end, it cleans any stale transactions out of the procedure, including its own. All maximum MODIFICATIONLOG queries (done by publishing and deltas processing) take the minimum of this table so any in-process posting jobs are considered when calculating watermarks. Its contents are temporary. This table should be referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDUSN  |  First of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDSLOT  |  Second of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_TRANSID_XIDSQN  |  Third of three transaction ID parts.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |  
|  GDT_MODLOGNUM  |  Next MODIFICATIONLOG sequence number.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  NUMBER  |

### Trace

#### TRACEID (Trace Identifiers Table)
Table name: TRACEID 
Lists traces that have been defined and potentially executed. It is a snapshot of the specific set of information that was used to perform a trace, which may no longer agree with the values in G3E_TRACE if it gets changed. This table is referenced in the G3E_DATASUPPORT. To create this table, run the creTraceTables.plb script. 
Because of limitations in the Visual Basic ComboBox list index value, Trace displays an error if the table has more than 32767 traces at any given time. To prevent the error, you should periodically [cleanup unwanted traces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ubXBuucgsLmTsrfR7yG_7A).

#### TRACERESULT (Trace Results Table)
Table name: TRACERESULT 
Contains the results of the traces. It contains the NetWorks Core keys and node number information for the rows in the connectivity table that were found by the trace. It also contains additional information needed by the trace algorithm to perform the trace as well as allowing queries to retrieve the trace information properly. It is possible, depending on the nature of the data and the specific type of trace being performed, that multiple rows for a particular connectivity occurrence for the same feature exist in the TRACERESULT table. For example, if a cost column was specified for the trace, then these duplicate rows can be eliminated through the use of a grouping function (like MIN on the cost column) in the SELECT statement retrieving rows from the table. It is best if the logic retrieving the rows from the TRACERESULT table expects and handles these cases. This table is referenced in the G3E_DATASUPPORT. To create this table, run the creTraceTables.plb script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TNO  |  Number of the trace (TRACEID.G3E_ID) that this data belongs to.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_GROUP  |  Grouping column for the results. It is defined in anticipation of supporting simultaneous trace operations. It keeps the data for each individual trace operation separate.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |  
|  G3E_TRACEORDER  |  The order in which this row was found in the trace. This value equates to the depth of the feature in the graph represented by the trace with the seed feature being the root (G3E_TRACEORDER = 1)   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCEID  |  The row in the trace results table to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This value only applies to the graph as it was built during this specific trace. A feature can have different parents in different traces. This column contains the G3E_ID value of the parent row.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFID  |  Partial identifier for the row in the trace results table to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This column contains the G3E_FID value of the parent row, which in combination with the G3E_SOURCEID value also uniquely identifies a parent row in the trace results. These two columns are required for uniqueness since features having more than two nodes of connectivity have multiple rows in the connectivity table for your model.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_SOURCECID  |  Partial identifier for the row in the trace results to which this feature is connected that caused it to be included in the results. This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root.  This column contains the G3E_CID value of the parent row, which in combination with the G3E_SOURCEFID value, also uniquely identifies a parent row in the trace results. These two columns are required for uniqueness because features having more than two nodes of connectivity also have multiple rows in the connectivity table.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |

This is the parent of the feature in the graph represented by the trace, with the seed feature being the root. This column contains the G3E_NODE1 or G3E_NODE2 value of the parent row.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |  
|  G3E_COST  |  The cost required to get from the source feature to this feature for this particular case. If the G3E_PATHCOST value was defined for the trace, this column contains a true cost value based on the values found in the G3E_PATHCOST expression. Otherwise, G3E_COST calculates the cost by assigning each path a value of 1.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  
|  G3E_NODE1  |  The Node1 value for the row obtained from the connectivity record.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |

#### G3E_JOB (Job Table)
Table name: G3E_JOB 
This table contains information necessary for the work management interfaces. Optionally, it can be included in a feature definition and used in relationship modeling. This table is typically defined as a component. The table is user defined. The table name and all the required columns in this table must be included in the [G3E_JOBDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TBQDr_BsRYh8ej2Rr97t2g) table.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  The unique alphanumeric identifier of the Job. Several parts of the NetWorks Core system require comma- separated lists of jobs.  A constraint should exist on the table to prevent the use of a comma (,) or a dot (.) as part of the job name. Dots in published job names can cause errors.   |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Unique identifier in the table.  |   |  Y  |   |   |  Number(10)  |

|  G3E_STATUS  |  Indicates Open, Closed, Posted, Discarded status of jobs. Closed jobs are not automatically removed from the table.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |

#### G3E_JOBSTATUS (Job Status Table)
Table name: G3E_JOBSTATUS 
Contains information about jobs that need to be processed by the job life cycle program. The work management interfaces create entries in this table. This table is monitored by the [JLCMonitor.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CvlskSKcYAGysNAmFC1xhw). This in turn launches [JobLifeCycle.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mSl5PizaLmQ2J6Uj9QtPuw). This table is referenced in the [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) table. To create this table, run the creStormsSupportTables.plb script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ID  |  Unique identifier for this row  |  Yes1  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  
|  WORK_REQUEST  |  Number of the work request from the job system (STORMS, Logica, or Generic Work Management)  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (12,0)  |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIER  |  NetWorks Core job identifier corresponding to the work request   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes[2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g)  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  WR_STATE_CODE  |  Code or indicator from the work management system about the current state of the job - like Lock Down and Field Complete. The values are configurable for each implementation. They must match values used in [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE.G3E_WR_STATE_CODE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg).   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  
|  GIS_JOB_STATUS  |  Indicator of the state that should be associated with the GIS features corresponding to the WR_STATE_CODE. The values are configurable but are like NEW, DES, ASB, CAN, CLS, and so forth. They must match values used in [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE.G3E_GIS_JOB_STATUS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg).   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  
|  G3E_STATUS_CODE  |  Contains an indicator of what state the associated job is in relative to the life cycle processing. Possible values: NEW, EXECUTING, ERROR, COMPLETE   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  
|  SUBMITTED_DATE  |  Date the request was inserted into the table. Also updated whenever GIS_JOB_STATUS is changed.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Date  |  
1Generated by G3E_JOBSTATUS_SEQ sequence.  
2G3E_JOB.G3E_IDENTIFIER

#### G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION.G3E_TYPE Values
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Command  |  The G3E_OBJECTCONTROL value is the command identifier or ProgID of the command. The Admin commands are assigned the administrator role so users cannot access them.   |  
|  CustomCommand  |  The G3E_OBJECTCONTROLID value is the unique identifier of the Custom Command table ([G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND.G3E_CCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TnT4ya5S9F75dJaSN86qXg)). The metadata triggers create this entry with the default role for each custom command defined.  An individual user can access a total of 300 custom commands.  |  
|  Behavioral  |  The G3E_OBJECTCONTROL value is the software-defined name of the role checked by a particular command to limit or modify its behavior.   |  
|  Version  |  The G3E_OBJECTCONTROL can have a value of either CommandVersion or CommandVersionNotification. Based on these entries, when metadata for command/role association changes, you have the option to change the version information and you can specify how the users are notified that a change has occurred. If G3E_OBJECTCONTROL = CommandVersion, G3E_ROLE must be set to a numeric value reflecting the current version.  If the G3E_OBJECTCONTROL = CommandVersionNotification, set G3E_ROLE to one of the following values:  NoNotification PromptToChange (default) Change  |  
|  Sub-Object  |  The G3E_OBJECTCONTROL value is the name of the command or a subset or option within a command. This type is used to help you to find the proper place to add/update role information at the sub-object level and is not used by the software in any way. The G3E_ROLE field can be left Null for this type.   |

## Add-On Support Tables

### G3E_ADDON (Add-on Support Table)
Table name: G3E_ADDON 
Defines an add-on in NetWorks Core metadata. This table replaces the use of the G3E_ANALYSIS for defining non-NetWorks Core functionality and metadata. If there are entries in G3E_ANALYSIS to support add-on type functionality, they should be moved to this table. The use of G3E_ANALYSIS is still supported for small custom functionality with no Upgrade Wizard needs. If the custom functionality is large and requires upgrades, creating an add-on for it allows the Upgrade Wizard to automatically upgrade the add-on metadata and functionality.

### G3E_ALLOCATIONIFACE (Feature Allocation Interface Table)

### G3E_ALLOCATIONRULE (Allocation Business Rules Table)
Table name:  G3E_ALLOCATIONRULE 
Contains a list of the allocation business rules. An allocation business rule consists of a database package that implements the allocation business rule functions and an associated argument data list. This means that you can create multiple allocation business rules by associating a single package with multiple argument lists. Each allocation business rule must have a unique G3E_USERNAME.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |

|  G3E_USERNAME  |  The name of the business rule displayed by the user interface.  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_ARPNO  |  G3E_ARPNO of the Allocation Business Rule package that implements the algorithm for this allocation business rule. This field corresponds to the G3E_ARPNO in the G3E_ARPACKAGE table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ARAGROUPNO  |  Argument data for this business rule. This field corresponds to the G3E_ARAGROUPNO column in the G3E_ALLOCATIONRULEARGVAL table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

Table name: G3E_ALLOCRULEARGVAL 
Used to specify the argument values to be passed to the database package that implements an allocation business rule. When a particular allocation rule ([G3E_ALLOCATIONRULE.G3E_ARNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/02GSTlMYF2i3uBj4cHuHzA)) is being used, the package is determined by looking at the G3E_ARPNO column in the [optimized table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/A3WJC1NdvKXTTFhE3LeoIQ). G3E_ARPNO is used to query this table, G3E_ALLOCRULEARGVAL, to get the values of the parameters to use for that package. Each parameter value is set on the package by using the argument name (present in the optimized version of this table) and the argument value (G3E_ALLOCRULEARGVAL.G3E_VALUE).

### G3E_ANALYSIS (Analysis Table)
Table name: G3E_ANALYSIS 
Identifies the name of the table that describes analysis information. This table must in turn have the columns G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE. The structure must be the same as the columns in this table. The values in that table can be Null, but the columns must exist. 
The entries in the G3E_ANALYSIS table enable publishing of metadata related to the analysis tables. You should not add references to customized or project metadata to this table. Instead, use the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. G3E_ANALYSIS is reserved for product metadata supplied by NetWorks Core. You can, however, use SQL tools to remove rows that reference functionality not used by your model.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Name for this analysis type, for example, Node- Edge Trace.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  [G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zc6dkrFRdGueQ730a2RlWg)  |  Key name indicating the type of analysis. The type is used to control access to analysis commands. Multiple instances of a particular analysis type can exist within one model.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  Name of the table that describes the analysis information. When the optional analysis definitions are added, the product scripts populate these fields. Do not change the name of any product table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (22)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  Name of the optimized table that describes the analysis information for publishing.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_TOOLTIP  |  Text used in the user interface to describe the analysis.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_SUPPORTINTERFACE  |  ProgID of the command that performs the analysis. It should contain no space and begin with a letter.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION (Analysis Configuration Table)
Table name: G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION 
Contains information about the paths in the connectivity network that were traced rather than to the features that were traced. The electric analysis functionality needs this information to determine which features were traced and to properly interpret the traced network. For one- and two-node devices, the information is identical for the feature and the connected path. For features with more than two nodes, the information is not identical for the feature and the connected path. 
Examples of this type of data are the operating status of the path (open/closed) and the phase of the path. One of the parameters the analysis functionality needs is G3E_CFGPARAMETER. The G3E_VALUE column defines this value. 
The combination of G3E_ANALYSISPKG, G3E_RNO, and G3E_CFGPARAMETER is unique.
The analysis functionality can query these configuration parameters from the G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION table:   
|  G3E_CFGPARAMETER  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CURRENT_STATUS  |  The current operating status of the path.  |  
|  NORMAL_STATUS  |  The normal operating status of the path..  |  
|  PHASE  |  The phases contained on the path  |  
The values for each of the configuration parameters must be specified as a valid SQL expression, either column name or scalar function, against the connectivity table specified by the relationship number. 
This information is not defined like the other analysis parameters in G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS because those parameter definitions are defined per feature number. A column or other expression from the connectivity table is the only valid definition for these configuration parameters. Also, if a feature has more than two nodes (multiple rows in the connectivity table), some rows for the feature in the connectivity table may not be traced. If attribute parameter definitions are used for this information, specification of some rows from the connectivity table may not be traced. 
This information is also tied to a relationship number since features can participate in multiple connectivity relationships (can have multiple connectivity tables as components), and the relationship number uniquely identifies a single connectivity table. 
You must qualify all columns used in the analysis configuration parameter value using 'conn' as the alias for the connectivity table. Failure to qualify the column existing in the connectivity table causes an SQL parsing error. 
An entry is required in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for this table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ACNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_ANALYSISPKG  |  Name of the analysis package that uses the trace. Foreign key to [G3E_ANALYSISPACKAGES.G3E_ANALYSISPKG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  The relationship (G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO) for which the configuration parameters apply. This value indirectly specifies the name of the connectivity table containing the columns referenced by the configuration parameters. Foreign Key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_CFGPARAMETER  |  Name of a configuration parameter.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALUE  |  The value for the configuration parameter. [CADPAD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nSlvrD5e5gSaq82LZVw37Q) [SynerGEE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OS49SDS0tqA0H5HHf0UNyw) This should be expressed as some form of an SQL expression that is evaluated to a value when applied against the connectivity table corresponding to the relationship number. Do not use a column alias when specifying this expression.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ (Feature to Analysis Object Mapping Table)
Table name:  G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ 
Lists the basic mappings between the features modeled by the application and the objects modeled by the analysis packages. The combination of G3E_PKGOBJID, G3E_FNO, and G3E_FILTER is unique   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FEATOBJID  |  Internal identifier.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number. Foreign key to [G3E_FEATURE.G3E_FNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_PKGOBJID  |  Identifier for an analysis package object. Foreign key to [G3E_ANALYSISPKGOBJS.G3E_PKGOBJID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jSpdelE4UmZkhg5SeEH8dw).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  An attribute-based filter to further restrict when this analysis object is created based on the feature. Only traced features that meet the filter criteria have analysis objects created for them.  Set the G3E_FILTER column to an SQL expression containing the G3E_ANO values of one or more attributes defined for the feature. Multiple attributes can be defined only if they exist in the same component table. Use square brackets to delineate the attribute numbers in this expression.   
 |  Example '[153] = ''Y''' Create an instance of the analysis object if the value of the attribute = 'Y'  |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_OUTPUTSUFFIX  |  For the applicable packages, this field defines the suffix portion of the output file name that stores the extracted information for the analysis object modeling the feature. Typically, this is a standard file name suffix (including the period), but it can include text before the period.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO  |  The number of the parent/child relationship for which child attribute type parameter definitions apply. This is only used if the G3E_VALUE_TYPE value specifies a child feature attribute value. This value explicitly defines which particular parent/child ownership type relationship should be used to find the children of the traced feature. For the child features to be determined properly, the row defining this relationship in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tKaXJUFR2b_peyQoF1h3zA) table must have G3E_TYPE = 3 and G3E_SUBORDINATE = 0.  If the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column is set, the G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO column also should be set. If either the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO or G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO value is specified, the specified analysis object is extracted only if a child of the traced feature is found. The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found:  If the analysis object supports the banked feature logic If the metadata definition states that multiple analysis objects should be created for each unit in the bank  Foreign key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO  |  The number of the child/parent relationship for which child attribute type parameter definitions apply. This is only used if the G3E_VALUE_TYPE value specifies a child feature attribute value. This value explicitly defines which particular child/parent ownership type relationship corresponds to the relationship specified in the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column. For the child attributes to be determined properly, the row defining this relationship in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tKaXJUFR2b_peyQoF1h3zA) table must have G3E_TYPE = 3 and G3E_SUBORDINATE = 1.  If the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column is set, the G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO column also should be set. If either the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO or G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO value is specified, the specified analysis object is extracted only if a child of the traced feature is found. The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found, subject to the following:  The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found: If the analysis object supports the banked feature logic If the metadata definition states that multiple analysis objects should be created for each unit in the bank  Foreign key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

### G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL (Analysis Parameter SQL Lookup Table)
Table name: G3E_ANALYSISPARAMSQL 
Lists the SQL statements used to retrieve the values of the analysis parameters defined with the SQL lookup value type. Each SQL statement can be used for multiple analysis parameters. ### G3E_ANALYSISPKGOBJS (Analysis Package Objects Table)
Table name:  G3E_ANALYSISPKGOBJS 
Lists all the objects used for each of the different analysis packages. The analysis packages are defined in the [G3E_ANALYSISPACKAGES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg) table, and the objects are defined in the [G3E_ANALYSISOBJECTS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xwapz0TYuwBMG7xyE03lgA) table. Only objects listed in this table are created for electrical analysis. The parameters for each object are defined in the [G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~Ph4Bg4UcJzi2171RVz7w) table. 
Only certain analysis object types are valid for each analysis package. This table should be sparsely populated, containing only values for the required objects for the particular package or packages used. Delete the values for any packages not used for specific objects. 
An entry is required in [G3E_ANALYSIS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2bLFqVwB0MTsyBVENDw8bg) for this table.

### G3E_APPLCONTEXTTYPE (Application Context Variable Types Table)
Table name: G3E_APPLCONTEXTTYPE 
Contains information necessary to support the description of application context variables. These variables are session- based values that can be useful in constructing find and query definitions. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw). This table does not have to be published. It is used to describe the type of value that the find or query retrieves as part of their parameters. This table is used to constrain attribute references (G3E_ANO values) in find and query functions.

|  G3E_IDENTIFIERANO  |  Identifies which field in the area feature table is considered the unique area ID for the table. Normally, this is the G3E_FID field, but if the area data was imported from another system, it can be an artificial ID. All attributes populated by the Area Manager command must be contained in the same component.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LINKANO  |  To help storing area hierarchies, identifies which field in the area feature table is used to point to a parent of an area feature to help storing area hierarchies. If, for an instance of an area, the value of the field is Null, the area is displayed in the root of the area tree. Otherwise, it is displayed as a child of the area whose G3E_IDENTIFIERANO is referenced by the link column.  This field must be in the same component as G3E_IDENTIFIERANO.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |  0  |

|  G3E_NAMEANO  |  The field in the area feature table used to store the user- entered name for an instance of an area.  This field must be in the same component as G3E_IDENTIFIERANO.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCATIONANO  |  The field in the area feature table that specifies the location identifier when an instance of this area feature is set as the active area of interest. ### G3E_ARPACKAGE (Allocation Business Rules Packages Table)
Table name: G3E_ARPACKAGE 
Contains a list of the allocation business rule packages. An allocation business rule definition consists of a database package that implements allocation business rule functions and an associated argument description list. This means that you can create multiple allocation business rules by associating a single package with multiple argument data lists, uniquely naming each combination. Each package appears once in this table, but could appear more than once in [G3E_ALLOCATIONRULE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/02GSTlMYF2i3uBj4cHuHzA), each time with a different set of argument values.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ARPNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PACKAGE  |  Name of the database package containing the implementation of a specific business rule.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTE 
This table contains a row for every attribute in each component and component view that is manipulated by the NetWorks Core client software. The attribute property information provides additional description and control not enabled by the database. Information in this table is used in the system for these reasons: 
  * To enhance the display of information in dialog boxes.
  * To enable more intelligent processing in software components like the Find command, the functional interfaces, and model validation. 


You need an entry in this table for any field in a component with a database default that needs to be presented to the user. This includes values you want to present on the dialog box tabs and values such as text alignment from the component's alignment field. 
The attribute can be a field on a component defined in G3E_CNO or a field on a component view defined in G3E_VNO. You cannot use the G3E_CNO and G3E_VNO fields at the same time, nor can they both be empty.

### G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY (Attribute Query Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY 
Contains information necessary for the Attribute Query command. This table is referenced in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_AQNO  |  Attribute query number. Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the query as it appears in query type combo box in the command  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Explanation of the query operation  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_SQL  |  The [SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) SELECT statement, including the substitution parameters. Substitution parameters are always indicated by question marks (?). You must explicitly include all the columns you want in the result set. You cannot include the SDO_GEOMETRY column, nor can you specify SELECT * in your query. If you use aliases, they must contain only underbar and alphanumeric characters.  Occasionally, you might use an Oracle query that is extremely complicated, such as when you are composing SQL for queries and finds. If you are having problems running a complicated query, Hexagon suggests one of the following solutions: 
  * Put the query into an Oracle view, which is used in the SQL statement.
  * Add the query as code in a PL/SQL procedure, which is called from inside the SQL statement.

  
 |  Example SQL> select G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from GC_MANHL where GC_MANHL.route = ? and GC_MANHL.number = ?   |  
| --- |  
If the SQL is marked for AOI processing, it is modified before being issued to the database. NetWorks Core software converts the query into a join on the [AOIQUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yBNbOEGUr6KKiCjros7_vw) table. It also appends queries to add detail features to the result set. It then issues the resulting query to the database. 
NetWorks Core can process specialized removable [optional parameters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YeiChl92c~QRq7zCYa_8Sw) in the SQL. 
Numeric values in the SQL should be language independent. Always use a period as a decimal separator. For instance, in the case of “N.DIAMETER > 10.3”, the “10.3” should always be specified with the period, never with “10,3” in any locale. 
This field can be Null to support a requirement to provide spatial processing output as input to custom user reports. If no G3E_SQL is provided, either G3E_AOI or G3E_AOILI must be set to 1 (True). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) If the number of parameters (question mark placeholders) in the statement does not match the number of attributes defined for the query, the software may yield unexpected results, including possibly getting into an infinite loop. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) Because SQL Server 2012 and 2014 do not support TRIM, use RTRIM and/or LTRIM in statements in the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_SQL and G3E_FINDQUICK.G3E_SQL columns for Field Review. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) The SQL statement must return G3E_FNO and G3E_FID. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) Because the results of the query go through xml special characters are limited to hyphen, underscore, and period in column aliases. 
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_AOILI  |  Indicates whether an AOI Location Identifier is required to execute this predefined query.  0 = An AOI Location Identifier is not required. 1 = An AOI Location Identifier is required.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_AOI  |  Indicates whether an AOI is required to execute this predefined query. Each query that has this flag set must have each feature class found by the query listed in [G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IPzFsM76U2_yKiAgpL06cQ) table. This is necessary to optimize the performance of simple attribute queries when an AOI is applied.  0 = An AOI is not required. 1 = An AOI is required.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The specific type of simple query is available to the user that has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_APPLICATION  |  Contains the bit mask value representing the product combination. Each product with the bit enabled in the mask will show the query on the list of available queries.  1 = Designer only  2 = NetViewer only  4 = Field Review only  8 = Portal only  16 = Mobile only  To make the query available in multiple products, merge the bitmap masks of individual products. For example, if you configure a query with mask 9 (8+1), it will be available in the Portal application and in the Designer application.  If you specify a query as being in the NetViewer application, then it is not visible in Designer. You must configure the G3E_NETPAGES to include the query in NetViewer or Field Review.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

### G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION (Relationship Attribute Validation and Copy Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION 
Contains rules for attribute validation.  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_AVNO  |  Key associated with this validation row.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVEFNO  |  Feature number of the feature being placed or validated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVEANO  |  Attribute number of the feature being placed or validated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDFNO  |  Feature number of the feature to which the active feature is being related. The candidate feature.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDANO  |  Attribute number of the feature to which the active feature is being related.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPERATOR  |  Operator that defines the type of validation to be performed. This value should be Null if the interface does not need further specification. If the value of G3E_VINO is Null for this row, one of the [legal relational](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) or simple algorithm operators should be used for validation (simple validation). If G3E_VINO is not Null, this value triggers specific validation operations internal to the given interface. Use specialized function operators such as Phase and CircuitNumber when G3E_VINO is not Null.  These are the simple algorithm operators: EitherOr — Compares the active feature's attribute value to the validation value specified or, if no validation value is specified, compares it to the related feature's attribute value. A match in either case passes validation.  InSetEitherOr — Compares the active feature's attribute value to a range of validation values as specified in G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE.  RelatedNotEqualTo — Indicates [exclusion of a candidate](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~sTq6BQTYdrbngf8Q~WGyQ) based on a set of attribute values and is considered when G3E_VINO is Null, G3E_OPERATIONTYPE = 1, and G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE is not Null. When this operator is detected, the software compares the attribute specified by G3E_RELATEDANO to the value or values specified in G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE, which can contain more than one value delimited by a semicolon (;). The attribute being validated needs to be part of the triggering component's published view.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPERATIONTYPE  |  Value that defines the operation to be performed: 1 = Validation  
2 = Copy  
3 = Validate and copy   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_VINO  |  Number of the specialized validation interface. If simple validation is to be used, this column should be Null.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE  |  The value validation checks for during processing. This string can contain numerical information or range information. This value can be Null if the row in question is being used for an operation that does not require a validation value, such as CircuitNumber copy.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  If the G3E_VINO value is populated for this row, this column contains binary large object (blob) data that is sent to the relationship attribute interface for this ANO combination. The contents of this blob are a variant array of variants. These variants are parsed in the function called through the interface. Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |

If the attribute is only checked during mouse move, the G3E_RELATEDANO can reference a component view attribute. If it references a component attribute, the attribute in the view must have the same name as the attribute in the component.  1 = The attribute should be checked during mouse move 0 = The attribute should be checked only during the click operation  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

### G3E_CABLEEDITATTR (Cable Edit Control Data Table)
Table name: G3E_CABLEEDITATTR 
Contains information necessary to support the [Cable Edit control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zn_9lmDaJE11oZfURbtkRg). This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. This table is used to specify key cable attributes that the Cable Edit control needs to know about to keep the cable valid and updated as it is edited. 
This metadata is also used by [break cable](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DeChXzTi0q4ymBnkKAENOg) to determine if a break can occur between cable sections. Specifically, the Cable Edit control needs to know about these attributes for both geographic and detail components: 
  * ComponentLengthLabel.Length
  * CableSection.Length
  * CableSection.StartLocation


The Cable Edit control also needs to know about the Cable.TotalLength attribute for the entire cable feature. 
The Cable Edit control updates the CableSection.Length, CableSection.StartLocation, and Cable.TotalLength attributes in response to edits to the ComponentLengthLabel.Length attribute. Occasionally, the Cable Edit control allows editing of the CableSection.Length and/or CableSection.StartLocation attributes, which affect the Cable.TotalLength attribute.

### G3E_CALCULATIONINTERFACE (Calculation Interface Table) (Deprecated)
Table name: G3E_CALCULATIONINTERFACE 
Contains a list of the functions available as calculation interfaces. Each function is effectively an automated object that supports the calculation interface definition. The calculation interfaces are called according to the rules in a number of metadata tables. Each interface calculates or derives a value from the feature's attribution, but the needed value is not stored in the feature. 
Input to the function is the recordset of the active feature. Any additional arguments are defined by the technique. This table is used in the creation of analysis output and in the interface to SAP.

### G3E_COLORSCHEME (Color Scheme)
Table name: G3E_COLORSCHEME 
Contains a set of predefined colors to form a scheme that can be used by the Map Output control to provide the color and fill color overrides. Within the same scheme, the Color and Fill Color parameters need not be synchronized. You can define fewer fill color values than color values. However, the software cycles through the fill color definitions more frequently than the color definitions. If G3E_TYPE = 'Fill Color' and G3E_COLOR for that ordinal is Null, then the fill type is considered to be 'Transparency'.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_CSNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_GROUPNO  |  The group number.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Allows the RGB values to be grouped under a single type. These are the valid values: Color Fill Color  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_COLOR  |  The RGB value that defines either the Color or Fill Color.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The order in which the color scheme should be used within a particular group. This value must be unique for a given combination of G3E_GROUPNO and G3E_TYPE.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUP (Color Scheme Group Table)
Table name: G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUP 
Contains the group number and group name for the particular color scheme group which allows a cycle or rotating set of colors to be used each time the trace is executed. The user can distinguish the results of traces that start at different features or perhaps use different attribute criteria.

|  G3E_GROUPNAME  |  The group name.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY (Command Dependency Table)
Table name: G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY 
Contains information necessary to support dynamic metadata edits. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for publishing. The table is used to define how each command or logical functional area uses the optimized table definitions. Because metadata is managed only in the default language, the functional group names are not localized. The contents of this table are provided by Hexagon. Do not add records to this table or delete records from it.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_CDNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Name of the command or logical functional group.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_OTSNO  |  Index into the set of optimized tables used by this command or logical group. If not Null at a non-leaf level, these tables must be updated for any of the subentries, even if this level is not selected. This field is a foreign key to [G3E_OPTABLESET.G3E_OTSNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qRTCgelWutUCWwW5QNpSAA).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LEVEL  |  Level of the item in the tree. One is a root or top level.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LEAFINDICATOR  |  Indicates if this entry is a leaf in the tree. 0 = The command or logical functional group can be expanded further. 1 = The command or logical functional group cannot be expanded further. G3E_OTSNO must be populated   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  Indicates the order of the complete tree layout to support publishing the tree in order.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |
