### G3E_METADATALANGUAGE (Language Definitions Table)
Table name: G3E_METADATALANGUAGE 
Used by the Metadata subsystem to allow you to define the languages supported for the client operations. This allows the metadata to be localized to the appropriate language. The table must contain one default language and can only have one default language. Other languages should be flagged as non-default. An entry is required in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for this table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_MLNO  |  Identifier for the language record.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LCID  |  Value of the language identifier as defined in the Microsoft® Software Developers Kit (SDK) for national language support. This is a four character representation of the hexadecimal value the long integer returned from MAKELANGID. It is a value in the range '0200' to '03FF' for user defined languages. Other values are system defined. The default for English as the system language is '0009'.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (4)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Description of the language for informational purposes only.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_DEFAULT  |  Boolean indicator to specify the base or default language. 0 = Not the default language. 1 = The default language. Only one row can contain a value of 1.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_METADATASUPPORT (Metadata Support Table)
Table name: G3E_METADATASUPPORT 
Supports publishing of the metadata. It is also used to drop the metadata when posting metadata between schemas. Any table referenced in this table is published if there is an entry in the optimized table column. 
Use the G3E_METADATASUPPORT G3E_XMLKEY and G3E_XMLQUERY columns to add customized or project metadata to your model. Use a consistent prefix for your custom metadata table names to distinguish them from the NetWorks Core metadata tables which have a G3E_ prefix.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_MSNO  |  Identifier for the metadata support definition.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  The name of the table that describes the metadata information. The field can be Null if G3E_XMLKEY is populated.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  The name of the optimized table that describes the metadata information for publishing. The procedure for performing the optimization must be named like the table with a _PKG suffix.   |  Yes  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_XMLKEY  |  The key for the additional metadata for publishing. This key name must not conflict with any of the other metadata optimized table names in this table or any other optimized tables.   |  Yes  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_XMLQUERY  |  The full SQL needed to publish additional metadata for the key specified in G3E_XMLKEY. The G3E_XMLQUERY cannot be Null if G3E_XMLKEY is specified. These two entries ensure that all necessary views are included in the G3E_METADATAKEYS_OPTABLE for RAW file publishing without requiring each configuration to remember the list of views.   |  Yes  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_METADATAVERSION (Metadata Version Table)
Table name: G3E_METADATAVERSION 
Records information about the release status of the metadata information. This information is necessary to support the publishing process and to assist in any published or cached metadata. An entry in this table is either created or updated every time the metadata is published.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_VERSIONNO  |  Identifier of this set of metadata.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSTDATE  |  Date this metadata was published.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  G3E_POSTTYPE  |  This is either g3eFull or g3eIncremental (constant values).  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Name of the configuration whose metadata was published.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_COMMENTS  |  History or comments on the nature of the changes. The publishing and refresh metadata commands use this field to determine if a metadata publish is occurring before continuing to the next step.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (1000)  |   |  
|  G3E_PROCEDUREVERSIONNO  |  Number of the procedure's version that this metadata was published with.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |  1.1  |  
|  G3E_DATABASECMVERSIONNO  |  The database version number with which this metadata was published. This number is used to retrieve the database version number for Field Review subsets.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |

### G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME (Metadata Explorer Name Table)
Table name: G3E_METAEXPLORERNAME 
Contains a list of names that are displayed to the user in Metadata Explorer. This table is not published in the traditional meaning of the term. A separate standalone executable, [PublishMENames.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/E2W8bt5rdDQ6O0yPsKkNSQ), reads the localized version of this table and loads the information into structures used by Metadata Explorer at runtime. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258503?tocId=d2texECkBoX_LSx6qPG2tg) Because this table is used only by the PublishMENames.exe, do not include it in the list of tables that are published. An optimization process is performed to support localization. You can access the optable so that the publishing utility can access the correct locale data. This entails the entry in G3E_DATASUPPORT for the SELECT and SYNONYM privileges. Normally, optimized tables are listed in G3E_METADATASUPPORT, and the optables are constructed and readied for publishing through this list. Even though this table is not published, you must post the normalized table between schemas, so only the normalized table is populated in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. The optimized table is listed in [G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_MENID  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  The type of Metadata Explorer name. This column can be one of the following values: 
  * TreeNodeName
  * QueryNodeName
  * ParameterName
  * DescriptiveNodeName
  * CommandNodeName. 

This field is defined by the product center and should not be modified.  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPEID  |  A unique value within a type of name. This field is defined by the product center and should not be modified.   |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Number (10,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  A string containing the name displayed to the user for this type and identifier.  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_NETANALYSISOPTIONS (Net Page Extension Analysis Options Table)
Table name: G3E_NETANALYSISOPTIONS 
Defines all of the analysis commands in NetViewer and Field Review. This table is referenced in the G3E_NETPAGES_OPTABLE. All of the rows in this table have a corresponding row in the [G3E_NETPAGES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/U_jTtX9ywikMmvnfKR~U_w) table. 
An entry must exist in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for the table and its optimized table to include this metadata in the published cache. The optimized table is [G3E_NETPAGES_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SzrCscOZZqMJxEWNCIAwtg). The G3E_NETPAGES_OPTABLE is a join between the G3E_NETPAGES and G3E_NETANALYSISOPTIONS.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_NAONO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OUTPUTXSL  |  The file name of the stylesheet used to format the result of the analysis command and, optionally, the type of XML to generate.  The type is specified by adding a comma then the value 0 or 1 after the .xsl file name.  0 = Converts ADO output recordset results into the standard Recordset.Save adPersistXML format  1 = Converts ADO output recordset results into a compressed XML format that preserves Null-valued fields.  If no comma and number follow the .xsl file name, then the default is 1 because most of the template GComms.xsl files are written for this format. This .xsl file must be in the Customize folder of the NetViewer Web application.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260146?tocId=o0P9Sdj7anCtwmlE9N4WOg) The generated column names in the query and quick- find results must match the column names that the .XSL stylesheet is looking for.  For example, if the KeyRS.xsl stylesheet is used, then the result recordsets must contain the column names G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CID, but not necessarily in that order.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (255)  |   |  
|  G3E_OUTPUTFRAME  |  Describes which frame is used to display the formatted result of the analysis function. NONE = Do not display formatted report output BOTTOM = Display formatted report output in the bottom analysis output frame within viewer applications.  WINDOW = Display formatted report output in a separate Internet Explorer window.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  NONE  |  
|  G3E_SHOWREPORT  |  Specifies how the report is to be displayed. This provides a page-specific default setting for the corresponding analysis option presented in Viewer applications. The user may override this value before executing the task.  0 = Option is off and enabled. User can change this default 1 = Option is on and enabled. User can change this default 2 = Option is off and disabled. User cannot change this default 3 = Option is on and disabled. User cannot change this default  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_MAPDISPLAY  |  Indicates whether the report is to be displayed in the map view. This provides a page-specific default setting for the corresponding analysis option presented in Viewer applications. Depending on the option you configure, the user may be able to override this value before executing the task.  0 = Option is off and enabled. User can change this default. None is selected in the Show on map drop-down list, and the map display options are enabled.  1 =Active View Only. Option is on and enabled. User can change this default. Active View Only is selected in Show on map drop-down list, and the map display options are enabled.  2 = Option is off and disabled. User cannot change this default. None is selected in the Show on map drop-down list, and the map display options are disabled.  3 = Active View Only. Option is on and disabled. User cannot change this default. Active View Only is selected in the Show on map drop-down list, and the map display options are disabled.  4 = All Views. Option is on and enabled. User can change this default. All Views is selected in the Show on map drop-down list, and the map display options are enabled.  5 = All Views. Option is on and disabled. User cannot change this default. All Views is selected in the Show on map drop-down list and map display options are disabled.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  1  |

### G3E_NETCLASSES (Net Analysis Classes Information Table)
Table name: G3E_NETCLASSES 
Describes the analytical groups or classes or operations available in the Web-based applications. Available groups are Search, Report, and Trace. 
This table contains information necessary to support the grouping of analysis commands in NetViewer. Additionally, it is used for the NetViewer [Page Extension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gUTAPdmES3p7L4w6bZXSxg) architecture to add classes of custom analysis commands and tools to NetViewer. This table defines the classes of analysis commands and general tools commands presented in the Analysis and Tools pages within NetViewer and Field Review.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_NACNO  |  Unique row identifier  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name for the group or class. One approach to defining these classes is to parallel the command functionality in NetWorks Core (for example, Trace, Query, and Report). Alternatively, you can combine the Query and Find into a Search class. These class definitions control presentation only and are not specifically tied to the functionality of operations within each class. That is, you can define a class that includes find and trace operations.   |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_APPLICATION  |  The mask value representing the product combination 2 = NetViewer only  4 = Field Review only  6 = NetViewer and Field Review  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  6  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  Indicates order of item on the Web page. If not unique, the order is determined by the return from Oracle and can differ from one publish operation to the next.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_COMMANDLOCATION  |  Type of command (analysis or general tool) used to determine whether this class of commands goes on the analysis or tools page. The valid values are Analysis or Tools.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (30)  |  Analysis  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_NETJOBFILTERATTR (Net Job Filter Attribute Table)
Table name: NETJOBFILTERATTR 
Contains information required for filtering jobs within NetViewer. This table represents a join between G3E_NETJOBFILTERATTR and [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) on G3E_ANO, pulling G3E_FIELD, G3E_USERNAME, and G3E_DATATYPE from G3E_ATTRIBUTE. This table is referenced in the [G3E_NETJOBFILTERATTR_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_kjhIDDIw5Ll2HFaylzhuA). Each row in this table represents an attribute within a job filter used within the NetViewer the Jobs tab. 
An entry must exist in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for the table and its optimized table to include this metadata in the published cache.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_JFANO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_JFNO  |  Foreign key to the [G3E_NETJOBFILTER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GgE6CQIJTshfBLcjkGh19A) table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

If this attribute value is used more than once in the filter, there needs to be as many rows for this ANO as the number of times it is referenced in the query. The order in which it is referenced is specified in G3E_ORDINAL column.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_NULL  |  Flag to indicate that a value is not required for this attribute in the filter. If the attribute can be Null, the filter must use the WHERE clause convention that checks for attribute equals single space for string type and checks for attribute is Null for non-string types. For example, if ATTRIBUTEFIELDNAME1 is a string type, the WHERE clause is (? = ' ' or ATTRIBUTEFIELDNAME1 = ?). If ATTRIBUTEFIELDNAME2 is a non-string type, the WHERE clause is (? is Null or ATTRIBUTEFIELDNAME2 = ?).  0 = Cannot be Null. 1 = Can be Null.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The order of the value parameter for this attribute in the filter.  |  Yes*  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_REFERENCEORDINAL  |  Specifies if a repeating attribute (ANO) is presented to the user to get a different value. If an ANO is repeating and the same value is replaced in multiple places in the filter, the value for this column is the G3E_ORDINAL of the associated ANO for all repeating records of the same ANO. Contrarily, if the repeating ANO is to be presented to the user, this is 0. In such cases, you can enter a different name than the username in the G3E_PROMPT column to present it to the user. This is a logical key to G3E_ORDINAL for this attribute.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes Logical  |  Number (5,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_PROMPT  |  The alternate name for an attribute username when it is repeating in the user interface.  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (80)  |   |

### G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY (Node-Edge Connectivity Relationship Table) (Sample)
Table name: G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY 
The G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table describes which feature pairs may be connected using the node-edge connectivity relationship. The semantics of this relationship requires two columns named NODE1_ID and NODE2_ID to store the node identifiers. Connectivity is maintained through database relationships and may or may not involve graphic coincidence. The [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table specifies the component that carries the connectivity information. 
A not null or zero value in the node identifier fields in the instance data indicates the feature is not connected. Each pair of connectible features must have two rows in this table. That is, if feature 3 can connect to feature 7, a row defining that feature 7 can connect to feature 3 must also exist.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_NECNO  |  Row identifier  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  Feature being placed or the active feature in an edit operation  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CONNECTINGFNO  |  Feature to which the source feature can connect  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  Component in the source feature that initiates the relationship software  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ENFORCEMENT  |  Indicates if connectivity is required or optional. Optional indicates that the G3E_SOURCEFNO can be placed and posted without connectivity.  0 = Connectivity is optional. A warning appears if features are improperly connected. 1 = Connectivity is required. An error appears if features are improperly connected. 5 = Connectivity is optional. A warning message does not appear if features are improperly connected.  Relationships that have the same G3E_SOURCEFNO value must have the same G3E_ENFORCEMENT value. For example, features that have a G3E_SOURCEFNO value of 301 must all have the same G3E_ENFORCEMENT value (of either 0, 1, or 5).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_BREAKLINEAR  |  Determines whether the source feature breaks linear features during connection 0 = Does not break linear features during connection. 1 = Breaks linear features during connection.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_SOURCECONNECTINGNODE  |  An integer value representing the node number to connect to for the corresponding device. Allowable values in the node columns are either a positive integer, or - 1, or Null. A positive integer signifies a node to connect to for the corresponding device. A Null value signifies that the user must make a choice in the connection such as which end of a switch to connect a primary conductor to. A -1 is a placeholder for linears (Null is acceptable). Linears acquire their appropriate node number based on the endpoint proximity to the connection. A value of -1 means that node values from metadata are ignored for this device (a linear).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDCONNECTINGNODE  |  An integer value representing the node number to connect to for the corresponding device. Allowable values in the node columns are either a positive integer, or - 1, or Null. A positive integer signifies a node to connect to for the corresponding device. A Null signifies that the user must make a choice in the connection such as which end of a switch to connect a primary conductor to. A -1 is a placeholder for linears (Null is acceptable). Linears acquire their appropriate node number based on the endpoint proximity to the connection. A value of -1 simply means that node values from metadata are ignored for this device (a linear).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CONNECTINGTRIGGERINGCNO  |  An integer value representing the G3E_CNO value of the component in the connecting feature that triggers the relationship. This value filters which components can participate in connectivity and allows the software the opportunity to avoid highlighting components of features that do not participate in any relationship.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_MAXOFFSET  |  Used in relationship validation, the maximum allowable offset that is valid for this pair of features in this relationship. This value is also used in the creation of a tolerance square to be used in placement. This tolerance square is the area around a relationship point that the user can interactively place a feature and still maintain a relationship with related features.  A maximum offset may not be needed for a given feature relationship. For instance, the user may want the ability to move a related feature with no restraints as to relationship validity. In this case, the value of G3E_MAXOFFSET would be set to -1.00.  The G3E_MAXOFFSET can be a whole or fractional number of database units, for example, feet, meters, and so forth, that matches the projected coordinate system of your data.  When G3E_MAXOFFSET is set, it should be the same or greater than AverageSymbolSize in the  [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  - 1.00  |  
|  G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY  |  The severity of the error to report if the related pair of features is not within the specified G3E_MAXOFFSET. Valid values are P1-P5. If this value is NULL, the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority is used.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (4)  |   |  
|  G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE  |  The maximum allowable distance between two features before initiating a break operation. This value is used to create a tolerance square for placement. This tolerance square is the area around a relationship point in which a user can interactively place a feature and initiate a break operation.  The G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE can be a whole or fractional number of database units, for example, feet, meters, and so forth, that matches the projected coordinate system of your data.  G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE must be less than or equal to G3E_MAXOFFSET * SQRT 2.  If G3E_MAXOFFSET is -1, G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE defaults to zero. For the metadata upgrade, the value is copied from G3E_MAXOFFSET unless G3E_MAXOFFSET is -1, in which case the value is zero.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |

If this parameter is 1, the G3E_BREAKLINEAR parameter is ignored.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

### G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY (Node-Ordered Connectivity Relationship Table) (Sample)
Table name: G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY 
The G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table contains information necessary for the node-ordered connectivity relationship. It is modeled on node-edge connectivity. This relationship is modeled by storing information for each edge that identifies the node to which each end of that edge is connected. The G3E_FNO and G3E_FID for the node are stored at each end. A G3E_FNO and G3E_FID of zero indicates that the corresponding end of the linear feature is not connected. Both the FID and FNO are zero or both are not zero. Any other data combination is invalid. 
For a given pair of features that can be connected in the model, there are two rows in this table, with each feature in the pair having its G3E_FNO in the G3E_SOURCEFNO field. Exactly one of those features must have the component (specified as G3E_SUPPORTCNO in [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)) used to represent connectivity. The feature that has that component is regarded as the two node device; the feature that does not have the component is regarded as a single-node device. Another way to look at this is from a node-edge graph view: the feature with the support component is an edge, and the feature without the component is a node. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259102?tocId=tMxlPZA20x7Zb1PWZXWOow) G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY does not have a G3E_ENFORCEMENT field. Connectivity is always enforced during validation.

Allows the software the opportunity to avoid highlighting components of features that do not participate in any relationship.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

Because only point features can break linears, this value should be 0 for area and linear features.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

### G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE (Stroke Pattern Table)
Table name: G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE 
Describes how a stroke pattern is defined. There is one row for each stroke pattern. Stroke patterns are defined only once for the entire configuration. You must populate the G3E_SEQUENCE_0 and G3E_SEQUENCE_1 columns. The remaining G3E_SEQUENCE_x columns, if populated, must be populated in pairs; for example, populate two columns, four columns, and so forth. The G3E_SEQUENCE_x field can contain a [negative value](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wqbG4nmQgWZVsWW6GLLt_Q), which indicates that the dash or gap is stretchable. 
An entry must exist in G3E_METADATASUPPORT for this table and its optimized table to include this metadata in the published cache. The optimized table is G3E_STROKENAME_OPTABLE.

### G3E_OMSFEATUREx (InService Feature Extraction Table)
Table name: G3E_OMSFEATUREx 
Used by the InService interface to determine the views to extract according to the named extraction. Several tables of this format exist. Each table is required to be populated in the G3E_OMSIFACE table with G3E_TYPE = 'Feature Extract'. The table must exist before it is populated in the G3E_OMSIFACE table. A metadata package named MG3EOMSExportUtils is provided with the product to create the table. Run the following procedure to create an OMS Export Feature table and its optimized table package: 
SQL> execute MG3EOMSExportUtils.CreateExpFeatureTableAndPkg ('<TableName>', '<TableAbbreviation>');
TableName must be less than or equal to 22 characters and TableAbbreviation must be less than or equal to 17 characters. 
If you want to recreate the optimized table packages for all OMS Export Feature tables listed in the G3E_OMSIFACE table, run this procedure: 
SQL> execute MG3EOMSExportUtils.InstallExportFeaturePackages;

### G3E_OMSIFACE (InService Interface Table)
Table name: G3E_OMSIFACE 
Contains information necessary for the various aspects of InService Extraction tool. It contains a single row for each named export (as defined in the [G3E_OMSFEATUREx](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/32DbnSHuzNdnu5gGIvirKg) table) and a single, independent row for G3E_TYPE= 'Style'. When you create an empty database, this table is automatically populated with the default entries defined in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateOMSMetadata.sql script.

### G3E_OWNERSHIP (Ownership Relationship Table) (Sample)
Table name: G3E_OWNERSHIP 
The G3E_OWNERSHIP table defines which feature pairs may be related using the ownership relationship. Only one row for each pair of related features is required. For example, if feature 4 can own feature 7, only one row is required in the G3E_OWNERSHIP table to define this relationship.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ONO  |  Row identifier  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  Feature being placed or the active feature in an edit operation  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OWNERFNO  |  Feature that owns or is associated with the source feature  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCECNO  |  Component in the source feature that contains the attribute field that holds the feature identifier of the parent   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OWNERFIELD  |  Attribute that holds the feature identifier of the parent in the source feature  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_OWNERCNOFIELD  |  Attribute that holds the component number of the parent in the source feature. If Null, the ID value that is stored is assumed to be globally unique so the parent can be located. The G3E_ID value from the parent must be retrieved from a common record, or the feature can have only one type of parent. All parents must use the same primary attribute component, or the relationship must be described as using a supporting component in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2  |   |  
|  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  Component in the source feature that initiates the relationship software  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OWNERTRIGGERINGCNO  |  Component in the owner feature that initiates the relationship software  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ENFORCEMENT  |  Indicates if ownership is required or optional. Values indicate if the G3E_SOURCEFNO can be placed and posted without ownership.  In the case of a child (G3E_SOURCEFNO) feature that is a point, area, or a linear defined to have only one owner, you can control the validation error message. Features do not generate a P1 error if at least one node is validly connected. For this field, specify:  0 = To make ownership optional. The relationship software returns a P4 ownership error. P4 messages are typically treated as warning conditions.  1 = To make ownership required. The relationship software returns a P1 ownership error when a parent is not found for this feature  In the case of a linear child feature that is set up to allow two owner fields, you can control the validation error message. For this field, specify:  2 = To make ownership optional. The relationship software returns a P4 ownership error when the child has zero or one owner.  3 = To define at least one owner. The relationship software returns a P1 ownership error when the child does not have at least one owner.  5 = To make ownership optional. No warning message appears if features are orphans (no parent).  There is no parameter available to specify that a linear must have two parents.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DELETE  |  Indicates if the child (owned) feature [should be deleted, reowned, or orphaned](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/cIwJGUHDCJLpdT2jZerT8A) on the deletion of its parent. The parent feature should not be deleted as long as any child exists—DoNotDelete (4). All the children of a particular instance of a parent feature must have the same G3E_DELETE value when the parent is deleted. Selective feature-based deletes of parents is not supported.   
 |  Example Feature A is in a parent-child ownership relationship with three different sets of child features:  B1, B2, B3 C1, C2 D1, D2, D3 For any given feature A, it only has a particular set of children. For example, Feature A with G3E_FID = 107 might have one child from each feature class B1, B2 and B3. But Feature A with G3E_FID =222 might have one child from Feature Classes C1 and C2. So, the delete of Feature A with G3E_FID = 107 succeeds as long as the metadata parameters for B1, B2 and B3 are the same even if the values for C1 and C2 are different.  The G3E_DELETE values for B1, B2, and B3 must be the same, the G3E_DELETE values for C1 and C2 must be the same, and the G3E_DELETE values for D1, D2, and D3 must be the same. However, the values for B1, B2, B3 do not have to be the same as the values for D1, D2, D3 or C1, C2, as long as Feature A only owns one type of feature at a time.   |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_BREAKLINEAR  |  Controls whether the source feature breaks linear features during ownership 0 = Does not break features during ownership. 1 = Breaks features during ownership.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_SECONDOWNERFIELD  |  Attribute that holds the feature identifier of the second parent in the source feature. A second parent in the same type of relationship might occur in linear features, for example, two poles that support or own the cable.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30  |   |  
|  G3E_SECONDOWNERCNOFIELD  |  Attribute that holds the component number of the second parent in the source feature. If Null, the ID value is assumed to be globally unique so that the parent can be located. The G3E_ID value from the parent must be retrieved from a common record, or the feature can have only one type of parent. All parents must use the same primary attribute component, or the relationship must be described as using a supporting component in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30  |   |  
|  G3E_MAXOFFSET  |  Used in relationship validation, the maximum allowable offset that is valid for this pair of features in this relationship. This value is also used in the creation of a tolerance square to be used in placement. This tolerance square is the area around a relationship point that the user can interactively place a feature and still maintain a relationship with related features.  A maximum offset may not be needed for a given feature relationship. For instance, the user may want the ability to move a related feature with no restraints as to relationship validity. In this case, the value of G3E_MAXOFFSET would be set to -1.00.  The G3E_MAXOFFSET can be a whole or fractional number of database units, for example, feet, meters, and so forth, that matches the projected coordinate system of your data.  When G3E_MAXOFFSET is set, it should be the same or greater than AverageSymbolSize in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  - 1.00  |  
|  G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORITY  |  The severity of the error to report if the related pair of features is not within the specified G3E_MAXOFFSET. Valid values are P1-P5. If this value is NULL, the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority is used.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (4)  |   |  
|  G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE  |  The maximum allowable distance between two features before initiating a break operation. This value is used to create a tolerance square for placement. This tolerance square is the area around a relationship point in which a user can interactively place a feature and initiate a break operation.  The G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE can be a whole or fractional number of database units, for example, feet, meters, and so forth, that matches the projected coordinate system of your data.  G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE must be less than or equal to G3E_MAXOFFSET * SQRT 2.  If G3E_MAXOFFSET is -1, G3E_BREAKTOLERANCE defaults to zero. For the metadata upgrade, the value is copied from G3E_MAXOFFSET unless G3E_MAXOFFSET is -1, in which case the value is zero.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ALLOWINTERIORRELATION  |  Indicates if ownership can be established interior to linear elements (not just at endpoints)  0 = Ownership is established at endpoints of related features. 1 = Ownership is established if the related features are within the specified tolerances. If this parameter is 1, the G3E_BREAKLINEAR parameter is ignored.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_PAIRCOUNT (Pair Count Table)
Table name: G3E_PAIRCOUNT 
Contains the delimiters the pair count service uses to parse pair counts and control behavior. When you create an empty database, this table is automatically populated with the default entries defined in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateCommMetadata.sql script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PCNO  |  Unique identifier for this table  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PARAMETER  |  Values in the G3E_PARAMETER field are defined by the business rules of the utility. The rows define the tokens used in company-specific nomenclature for defining pair counts.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALUE  |  The value of the parameter. Entries in this field must be language independent since they are used in the construction of a string stored in the database. This should be Null for the G3E_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_MESSAGE parameter.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_MESSAGE  |  Specifies the message to be displayed that describes what steps required to properly set the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute and allow counts to be entered for the current feature instance. This is only populated for the G3E_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_MESSAGE parameter.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. Used by the database administrator for informational purposes only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
Count Subsystem Validation
The Count subsystem has the following naming conventions: pair count and the strip count. 
Several of the parameters serve as delimiters in the count labels. These are suffixed by _DELIMITER. The other parameters serve as message prioritization for the different parts of the count data that can fail to meet system expectations. To support configurability of messaging for count validation, the count validation error reporting is configurable. Using metadata, you can configure four of the discrete count validations to return ignore, warning, or error. If an ignore or warning is returned, the database update is allowed to proceed. If an error is returned, the database update is prevented. 
To prevent posting a count with these problems, you can write a custom functional interface. The parameters are configured based on the following priorities:   
|  Priority  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  The Count subsystem ignores the error. The user is not informed the error occurred.  |  
|  1  |  The Count subsystem presents the error to the user. The user can ignore the error or go back and fix it.   |  
|  2  |  The Count subsystem presents the error to the user. The user cannot continue until the error has been resolved.   |  
|  Key  |  Description  |  Mandatory  |  Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SIZE_MISMATCH  |  Specifies the error priority when the total number of pairs entered does not match the total size of the feature that owns the count.  If the current feature does not have a TOTAL_SIZE attribute in its primary attribute component than this validation is skipped as there is no total size to compare the number of entered pairs with.   |   |  N  |  
|  G3E_DUPLICATE_COUNT  |  Specifies the error priority when one or more duplicate counts exist for an instance of a feature.   |   |  N  |  
|  G3E_NO_SOURCE_FEED  |  Specifies the error priority when one or more entered counts were not found in the located sources feeds.   |   |  N  |  
|  G3E_DEAD_QUANTITIES  |  Specifies the error priority when one or more quantities of dead count have been entered.  |   |  N  |  
|  G3E_DISPLAYWARNINGS  |  Add this key to the G3E_PAIRCOUNT table and set it to 0 if you want to supress warning messages. If this key is set to 0, the count command does not interactively display features with count validation warnings as they occur. The command accepts all warning messages but sends the warning for that feature to the resulting report. To turn on warning messages, delete this key from the table (decreases processing time) or set this key to -1.   |   |  N  |  
Count Subsystem Keys
Some keys are duplicated in the different naming conventions because the default values may be different. These are the available Count subsystem keys and their default values: 
Prefix  
|  Key  |  Description  |  Mandatory  |  Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PREFIXDEFAULT  |  Specifies whether the label is to include the prefix or not by default.  |  N  |  True  |  
|  G3E_PREFIX_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter that separates the designation prefix from the designation. For example, OWSDON59/10,1-100   |  N  |  No Delimiter  |  
|  G3E_PREFIXOPTIONAL  |  Specifies whether the prefix is optional in a count or not.  |  N  |  True  |  
Formatting  
|  Key  |  Description  |  Mandatory  |  Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DEFAULT_FORMAT  |  Specifies the default notation used to annotate counts to map views and reports and the notation used to parse lines of count entered in the Pair Count control. These values are supported:  1 = Pairs 2 = Strips  |  N  |  1 = Pairs  |  
|  G3E_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_MESSAGE  |  Specifies the message to be displayed that describes what steps need to be performed to get the G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute set properly and allow counts to be entered for the current feature instance.   |  N  |  G3E_COUNTFORMAT attribute not set. Unable to format counts.  |  
|  G3E_COUNT_EXTENDER  |  Defines the class that implements the count extender interface. If you want further validation of your pair counts to adhere to these rules:  Upgrade the severity of size mismatch validation failures to critical for cables, wires, capacitors, load coils, interfaces, resistors, and terminals. All other count bearing features use the global G3E_SIZE_MISMATCH severity level.  Allow duplicate dead count assignments in capacitors, load coils, resistors and terminals. All other count bearing features use the global G3E_DUPLICATE_COUNT severity level.  Include the G3E_COUNT_EXTENDER parameter with the value GcommsValidation.clsValidate in this table. If this validation is not required by your business practices, remove this parameter from the table. Specifying the GcommsValidation.clsCLLIPrefixValidate class provides the same validation as the default class but also includes designation prefix validation. This validation ensures that an eight- character prefix is included for each designation. This validation extends to the Throw Count and Trace Count commands.  The validation does not apply to dead or special counts, for example, 100D or counts belonging to a pair count class that is not defined to be validated against total size. See [G3E_PAIRCOUNTCLASS.G3E_VALIDATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/y~0mmKEqDqkr38WG5Iojhg) for more information.   |  N  |  GcommsValidation.clsValidate  |  
Pair Count  
|  Key  |  Description  |  Mandatory  |  Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DESIGNATION_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to separate the designation from the pair range. For example, 10,1-100   |  N  |  ,  |  
|  G3E_RANGE_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to separate the low and high parts of the pair range. For example 10,1-100   |  N  |  -  |  
|  G3E_RANGES_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to separate multiple non-contiguous pair ranges that occur on the same line. For example, 10,1- 100+201-300.  If this key is added to G3E_PAIRCOUNT, ensure the attribute, range_seq is added to the count table.   |  N  |  No Delimiter. Multiple noncontiguous ranges not supported.  |  
|  G3E_REVERSE_FEED_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to identify that a line of count is fed in the reverse direction to the cable. For example, [R]10,1-100   |  N  |  [R]  |  
|  G3E_DEAD_INDICATOR  |  Specifies a comma- delimited list of delimiters or tokens that indicate that a pair range is dead. For example, D1- 100. Dead indicators exhibit the same behavior as special indicators, except that a dead indicator has a definite direction while a special indicator does not. A dead count can be forward or reverse, therefore, [R]D1-100 is also a valid dead count.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260487?tocId=iHTy1jqvRAU~kZXlIFqV7A):  The following script renames the current dead indicators to the G3E_SPECIAL_INDICATOR key. Type the following in an SQL editor:  SQL> UPDATE G3E_PAIRCOUNT SET G3E_PARAMETER = 'G3E_SPECIAL_INDICATOR' WHERE (G3E_PARAMETER = 'G3E_DEAD_INDICATOR'); To use current reverse dead counts, remove the appropriate dead indicators from the G3E_SPECIAL_INDICATOR key and move them back to the dead indicators key. Type the following in an SQL editor:  SQL> INSERT INTO G3E_PAIRCOUNT (G3E_PCNO, G3E_PARAMETER, G3E_VALUE, G3E_EDITDATE) VALUES (G3E_PAIRCOUNT_SEQ.NextVal, 'G3E_DEAD_INDICATOR', 'D,Dead', SYSDATE);  |  N  |  None  |  
|  G3E_SPECIAL_INDICATOR  |  Specifies a comma- delimited list of the delimiters or tokens that indicate that a pair range is special. For example, 50SP  |  N  |  None  |  
|  G3E_COLLAPSERIPPLEDCOUNTS  |  Specifies whether or not to collapse contiguous lines of count after a ripple has been performed. If 0, contiguous lines of count are not collapsed until the feature is thrown.   |  N  |  -1  |  
|  G3E_OPEN_THROW_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to identify the start of a thrown count. For example, (10,1-100)20,1-100   |  N  |  (  |  
|  G3E_CLOSE_THROW_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to identifier the end of a thrown count. For example, (10,1-100)20,1-100   |  N  |  )  |  
|  G3E_CLASS_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the token to place between the pair count class name and the line of count when annotating pair information in a map view or report. For example, In BP: 10,1-100   |  N  |  :  |  
Strip Count  
|  G3E_LONGESTLOOP.G3E_TYPE Values  |  Description  |  Mandatory  |  Default Value  |

Type the following in an SQL editor:  SQL> INSERT INTO G3E_PAIRCOUNT (G3E_PCNO, G3E_PARAMETER, G3E_VALUE, G3E_EDITDATE) VALUES (G3E_PAIRCOUNT_SEQ.NextVal, 'G3E_DEAD_INDICATOR', 'D,Dead', SYSDATE);   |  N  |  None  |

|  G3E_COLLAPSERIPPLEDCOUNTS  |  Specifies whether or not to collapse contiguous lines of count after a ripple has been performed. If 0, contiguous lines of count are not collapsed until the feature is thrown.   |  N  |  -1  |  
|  G3E_OPEN_THROW_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to identify the start of a thrown count. For example, (023:001- 010)024,001-010   |  N  |  (  |  
|  G3E_CLOSE_THROW_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to identifier the end of a thrown count. For example, (023:001- 010)024,001-010   |  N  |  )  |  
|  G3E_CLASS_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the token to place between the pair count class name and the line of count when annotating pair information in a map view or report. For example, In BP: 023:001-010   |  N  |  :  |  
|  G3E_STRIP_CHARWIDTH  |  Specifies the number of digits to pad each strip value when displaying it. For example, a value of three displays the first strip as: 023:001   |  N  |  3  |  
|  G3E_PAIRS_PER_STRIP  |  Specifies the number of pairs that are bundles into each strip. This value is constant for all count- bearing features.   |  N  |  10  |  
|  G3E_PARALLEL_INDICATOR  |  Specifies the token that indicates a parallel strip. For example, 023:001- 010P1  |  N  |  P  |  
|  G3E_PAIR_OPEN_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token that indicates the beginning or individual pairs within a strip. For example, 023:001A[5]   |  N  |  [  |  
|  G3E_PAIR_CLOSE_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token the indicates the end of individual pairs within a strip. For example, 023:001A[5]   |  N  |  ]  |  
|  G3E_PAIR_RANGES_DELIMITER  |  Specifies the delimiter or token used to separate multiple non-contiguous pairs within a strip. For example, 023:001A[1,5]   |  N  |  ,  |  
|  G3E_ANNOTATE_SPLIT_STRIP_PAIRS  |  Specifies whether or not to annotate the split strip pair range  |  N  |  False  |  
|  G3E_SPLIT_IDENTIFIERS  |  Identifies which values can follow a strip number to indicate that the strip is split. If no value is specified for this parameter, split identifier validation is not performed and users can use any strip identifiers.   |  N  |  No Delimiter  |

|  G3E_KEYFIELD  |  Field that contains the key to store into the actual feature attribute field. This can be the same as the G3E_VALUEFIELD, or it can be different as in code list indirection. This field must have a primary and/or unique constraint.   
 |  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256601?tocId=1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw) The word KEY is a reserved word in SQL Server Express (SQL Server) and should not be used as a column name in any table.   |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALUEFIELD  |  Field that contains the actual entries that are displayed in the drop-down list for user selection.   |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALIDATION  |  [Type of validation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0AnQVPEPY~yfXab7NP_F0w) done against this list.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  [Attribute expression](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) that limits the content of the specified table. This allows one picklist table to be used for multiple purposes. The Null filter (catch-all case) should contain an empty string or a Null value. Do not include the word Null in the field. For example, a table is defined for voltage, but there are two classifications, high and low. Rather than defining two tables, one table can store voltage but can define two picklists using the Filter to control the contents of the list. You would have a specification of a LowVoltage picklist where the filter is Voltage less than or equal to 100 and a HighVoltage picklist where the filter is Voltage greater than or equal to 100.  The LIKE operator and wildcard characters (% and _) are supported only when G3E_PUBLISH is No (0). If you reference the same table from multiple picklists, the columns exposed must be the same if you choose to publish the picklists.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS  |  Specifies a comma- separated list of additional column names to include when querying for picklist values. These columns are inserted directly into the SELECT statement issued on the table identified in the G3E_TABLE column. The drop-down list for this attribute is multi-column. If Null, or an empty string, then the value is not included in the query. Column names in the comma- separated list must be uppercase.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

In the case of multi-column ordering, list the fields, and the DESC clause if needed, as a comma(,) separated list.  If the picklist should be published (G3E_PUBLISH = 1), the value in this field is different from the value of G3E_KEYFIELD or G3E_VALUEFIELD, and the value in this field is not listed in G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS, then list this field in G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_PUBLISH  |  Boolean value to indicate if this picklist should be published or not. May not be used with extensible lists. The default is based on validation.  0 = Do not publish the picklist. 1 = Publish the picklist. If you are referencing a table multiple times, you can publish it only once. If you are referencing a standard metadata table, you cannot specify the picklist to be published. This causes duplicate key entries and publish operation failure. If you must use the same table for multiple picklists (different value fields), define a database view and reference the view in G3E_TABLE.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  Based on validation  |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS  |  Specifies a comma- separated list of additional column names that need to be published but not shown on the multi- column drop- down. The columns listed in the G3E_KEYFIELD, G3E_VALUEFIELD, and G3E_ADDITIONALFIELDS should not be listed here. The column names in the comma- separated list must be uppercase.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (240)  |   |

### G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION (Placement Configurations Table)
Table name: G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION 
Defines feature sets and specialized feature types. A feature set consists of multiple features and their components that are best placed as a group. A predefined layout is used when placing features relative to the other features within the feature set, such as a switch gear box and the switches and busses inside it.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PCROWNO  |  Identifier for the row in the placement configuration table.  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PCNO  |  Identifier for the set of rows in the placement configuration table that comprises a placement configuration.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the placement configuration that appears in the user interface:
  * On the Feature Explorer Graphic Components tab. 
  * On the dialog displayed by the New Component command.

 |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Number of the feature of which this component is a part.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Number of the component included in this placement configuration. The same CNO can be listed multiple times in a given placement configuration. It can also occur in more than one placement configuration. Metadata validation should include checking that the G3E_CNO is appropriately associated with the specified G3E_FNO.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  Specifies the order that this FNO/CNO is constructed in this configuration.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_AUTOREPEAT  |  Indicates whether a repeating component should automatically repeat during placement. 0 = The user must initiate each occurrence. 1 = The component automatically repeats during placement. Autorepeat can only be set on components that are marked as repeating in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w).  If G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING = 1, G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_REPEATING can be either 0 or 1. However, if G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING = 0, G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_REPEATING must also be 0. This field can be overridden, but only in one direction.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_PINO  |  Information that controls placement of the component. This is a key into the [G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fy4Cx0Y1oeQuVI6b1cIi6A) table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  Array of variants containing arguments for the placement technique. The technique is automatically passed the SelectSet and the current FeatureRecordset arguments that you set. Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_TOOLTIP  |  String that is displayed for the tooltip or status message. All component entries with the same G3E_PCNO value must have the same tooltip. This value is only visible in the New Feature control.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_FEATUREINDEX  |  Index number of the feature associated with this feature- component entry. Lets you define a configuration with multiple instances of the same type of feature. For example, a switch cubicle might be defined as a switch box and three switches. The feature index is unique and sequential to each feature class. For this example configuration, the switch box has a feature index of 1, and the switches are numbered 1 - 3. Even when a feature does not exist more than once within the configuration, the index of 1 must be specified for each feature type.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_REFRESH  |  Used during feature placement and edit operations. Refresh causes the Graphic Component grid and the data grids to update. This value indicates whether a refresh should occur.  0 = a refresh should not occur 1 = a refresh should occur. These are typical occasions to set this value to Yes (1): If the attribute from a graphic component is shown on a dialog tab, which allows additions or deletions of components from other dialog tabs to be reflected on the Graphic Components tab.  If the attribute appears on multiple dialog tabs. If the attribute participates in a style rule and consequently affects dynamics. To avoid extraneous refreshing (a performance penalty), set this property to Yes (1) in these cases or when the addition of an attribute (or graphic) component generates a corresponding graphic (or attribute) component through a functional interface.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

It allows the configuration to automatically build a relationship without interaction from the user. It can only build a relationship to another feature in the configuration. The definition allows some relationships to be defined silently and others to be interactive. However, you cannot do part of a relationship silently and part of it interactively. A new G3E_SILENTRGNO should be generated for each FNO/CNO/FIDX combination for which relationships can be established silently.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_REQUIRED  |  Indicates whether the component is required. 0 = The component is not required. 1 = The component is required This does not override the definition of the component within the feature (or for validation of the feature), but it does allow you to change the behavior of the component placement (consequently, the auto-start capability for the component) within the configuration. The value for this field, if left unassigned, is the same as [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REQUIRED](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for the specified G3E_FNO/G3E_CNO.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_REPEATING  |  Indicates the cardinality of the component within the feature. A repeating component may have one or more instances. The combination of required and repeating provides the following combinations: 0 or 1, 1, 0 - n, and 1 - n.  0 = Multiple occurrences are not supported. 1 = Multiple occurrences are supported. ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256886?tocId=wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ) This does not override the definition of the component within the feature (or for validation of the feature), but it does allow you to change the behavior of the component placement (and consequently the repeating capability for the component) within the configuration.  The value for this field if left unassigned is the same as [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) for the specified G3E_FNO/G3E_CNO.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  [G3E_CCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YYMU5srt0d6T6dwkYAqfpA)  |  An index into the [G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YHO9TgRk7Beh5fF22~iN_g) table defining the component configuration to be placed. This field must match a value in G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION.G3E_CCNO. This field should be set to a non-null value only when a component configuration is to be specified as part of a feature. When this field is set, the G3E_CNO field in this table should be set to Null. If an individual component is to be specified instead of a component configuration, then G3E_CCNO should be Null and G3E_CNO should be set. This may be a logical foreign key.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PLACECOMPONENT  |  Indicates whether the component should be placed as part of the placement configuration. By default, all components within a placement configuration are placed (G3E_PLACECOMPONENT = 1). However, some placement configurations contain external relative components that should not be placed. External relative components are components that are placed before the placement configuration and are used to determine the relative location of the configuration. External relative components have these characteristics:  A G3E_PLACECOMPONENT value of No (0). Serve as an aid in selecting the correct relative component for placement techniques. G3E_ORDINAL value is lower than that of the components that use them ,thus allowing the external relative components to appear in the list of relative components available as placement arguments.  Only the GTFeaturePlacementService supports this field. The New Feature command does not.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_RINO  |  An index into the G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE table defining the custom validation interface to be used by the New Feature and Edit Feature commands before committing data for this particular feature to the database. This field must match a value in [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_RINO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA). The type of the relation interface must be Feature Validation.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO  |  The group number of the arguments to the custom validation interface (if any) specified in G3E_RINO. This field should be Null if the custom object requires no arguments. If the field is not null, this value must match one of the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) values.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO  |  A detail component number that corresponds to the geographic G3E_CNO value in a given row. You can optionally populate G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO in rows where G3E_CNO is a geographic component. It should be Null when G3E_CNO is a detail component.  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO should only be populated for these reasons:
  * To specify implicit geographic versus detail component placement for the two components identified in G3E_CNO and G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. When a geographic window is active, G3E_CNO is placed. When a detail window is active, G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is placed. 
  * To reduce the number of items seen in these user interfaces:

Graphic Components tab in Feature Explorer (New/Edit Feature commands)  New Component dialog (New Component command) If populated, the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO value must correspond to a row in G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION where G3E_PCNO, and G3E_FNO, and G3E_FEATUREINDEX match that of the geographic component and where G3E_CNO has the same value as the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. 
  * Among other things, the corresponding row defines the placement technique and parameters for placing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. 
  * This row should have a G3E_ORDINAL value that is higher than the G3E_ORDINAL value of the geographic G3E_CNO. 
  * When a G3E_CNO in one row is used as the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO of another row, it is not automatically placed as part of the placement configuration (even if G3E_PLACECOMPONENT is 1). It is placed only if a detail map window is active when the geographic row with the populated G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO value is processed. 
  * In these additional rows, G3E_PLACECOMPONENT must be 1. However, even though G3E_PLACECOMPONENT is 1, this detail component is not listed separately in the Graphic Components user interface because G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is populated in the row of the geographic component. This reduces the contents in the user interface. 

 |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

### G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE (Placement Technique Table)
Table name: G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE 
Lists the functions available to support placement operations. Called during the creation of graphic components, each function is effectively an automated object that supports the placement interface.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PINO  |  Identifier for the placement interface.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the technique. This appears in the user interface list.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACE  |  ProgID of the software component to support this function. It must begin with a letter and contain no spaces. When formatted as Project, the interface is assumed to be a .NET implementation.  [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255963?tocId=fy4Cx0Y1oeQuVI6b1cIi6A) for more information about .NET implementations.  The G3E_PROGID value for [analysis packages table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg). The G3E_INTERFACE value for the interface tables.  <AssemblyName>:<TypeName> where <AssemblyName> is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension and <TypeName> is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension. ### G3E_PORT (Schematic Symbol Ports Table)
Table name: G3E_PORT 
Supports the [Schematic Generator service](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm). This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. G3E_PORT contains metadata to override the implied ports on a schematic symbol. By default, a schematic symbol contains only one port that is positioned in the center of the symbol. Through this port, you can make connections both into and out of the symbol. This table defines the ports, the position of each port on the symbol, the directions in which connections can be made, and the number of connections that can be made to the port. 
The [G3E_PORTDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3GqB0DMMCvo_X6OpxUXI0w) table associates a name to a set of port definitions defined in this table. The [G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KkSHDKALPAaJHyESmRqk9Q) table associates a port definition to a style and thus to the symbol used by that style. The position of the port is described as a percentage of the size of the symbol with the center being (0,0) as displayed in the following diagram: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w)
You can define a branch side and width for the port to indicate that connected features branch at equal spacing in and/or out along a specific side of the symbol. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w)
The branch side value can be Bottom, Top, Left, Right, or Any with values of 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. A value of 5 (Any) indicates that the port can occur on any of the four sides of the symbol and is determined by the [schematic layout processing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/f2jHhdF~mp9WhGbQCpRlhg). 
The width value indicates the width of the port as a percentage of the size of the symbol to a maximum of 200 percent. 
This diagram shows a port with a width percentage of 100.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w)
This diagram shows a port with a width percentage of 200.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=ujLHo9TduouoBKqNqm6P9w)
Schematic symbol ports need to be defined only for features that are encountered in schematic generation traces. Port definitions for schematics are like the hot spots that can be defined for the [Connectivity PickQuick](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VfbJLUnk4lGa5XMUeX83Jw) dialog box. Schematic port definitions differ from these hot spots in that they also define the type and number of connections.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PDNO  |  The port definition number to which this port belongs.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PORT  |  The identifier of the port number for this port definition. This is an arbitrary number; however, numbering ports from 1-n is recommended.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONX  |  The percentage in the x direction of the port. Must be between -100 and +100.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONY  |  The percentage in the y direction of the port. Must be between -100 and +100.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DIRECTION  |  Identifies the direction of the port. 1 = In 2 = Out 3 = Both In general, a symbol must have at least one port designated as Both, or at least one In and one Out port.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_MULTIPLECONNECTIONS  |  Identifies whether a port is limited to a single connection or can have an unlimited number of connections.  0 = Unlimited 1 = Only one  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_BRANCHSIDE  |  The side of the symbol where more than one port is located. 1 = Bottom 3 = Left 4 = Right 5 = Any  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_WIDTH  |  The width of the port as a percentage (0 - 200) of the size of the symbol.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(3,0)  |   |

### G3E_POSTBREAKMAPPING (Post Break Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_POSTBREAKMAPPING 
Describes the post break operations that should be executed when the specified feature-component is broken. Multiple post break operations can be performed and are executed in ascending order of the G3E_ORDINAL. In addition to the Post Break relation interface, this table contains the references to the relation interface for the types Compute Marker Location, Compute Geo Point, Create Marker, Custom Plot, and Loop Makeup. These additional entries are not executed during the break operation, but allow you to associate arguments to these interface types.

|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number. The specified number must already exist in the feature table. This field is only populated when G3E_TYPE is Post Break.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes (G3E_FEATURE)  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The component number. The specified number must already exist in the component table. This should be a linear component. This field is only populated when G3E_TYPE is Post Break.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes (G3E_COMPONENT)  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The order of execution of the post break processes. This field is only populated when G3E_TYPE is Post Break.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RINO  |  Index into the [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) table defining the custom interface to be used. This field must match a value in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_RINO. The type of the relation interface must be Post Break, Compute Marker Location, Compute Geo Point, Create Marker, Custom Plot, or Loop Makeup.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

### G3E_POSTMAPPING (Post Process Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_POSTMAPPING 
Defines the post processing that can be used by specific queries to prevent query and/or trace results from being sent to a post process that cannot process them or to prevent incorrect trace contents from being used as input to the post process. While the metadata is defined to allow any query to be used as input, the user interface only exposes trace results to post processing. 
The Metadata subsystem uses this mapping table to provide a list of all post processes that can be used by a particular query or type of query operation.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |

|  G3E_PPNO  |  Identifier of the report from G3E_POSTPROCESS.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_QNO  |  The number of the attribute query or trace that can use this post process. Foreign key to [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AQNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) or [G3E_TRACE.G3E_ID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg). If the value is Null, the information is available for all traces based on the G3E_TYPE specification. This field should only be populated when G3E_TYPE is Attribute or Trace.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Post process type. It also indicates to which table the previous key maps. 1 = Attribute 2 = Trace 3 = Spatial 4 = SelectSet 5 = AdhocAttribute 28 = SavedQuery. Includes attribute, spatial, ad hoc. 29 = ReviewFeatureAllocation. Minimize the number of reports displayed in the Report Selection control of Review Feature Allocation command  30 = Report. Minimize the number of reports displayed in the post-process control of Review Feature Allocation command and the Generic Map Output report.   |  30  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The specific type of post process is available to the user who has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_QUEUE (Queue Table)
Table name: G3E_QUEUEContains information necessary to support XML message queues for work management. Table name: G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY 
Records information used in the placement and validation of related features and components and provides rules for offset placement of related features and stores attributes such as offset distances and orientations.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |
