|  G3E_RELATEDFNO  |  Feature class identifier. Feature number of the feature to be related to (owned to or connected to).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDCNO  |  Component class identifier. Component number of the feature to be related to (owned to or connected to). The geometric relationship is based on this component.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  Feature class identifier of the feature to be related to the feature in G3E_RELATEDFNO. This is the active feature, either in placement or the one being edited.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCECNO  |  Component class identifier of the feature to be related to the CNO above. This is the component in the active feature.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA  |  Determines whether the G3E_POSITIONDELTA value should be used (along with the vector of the related feature) or whether the G3E_XDELTA and G3E_YDELTA should be used to offset the active geometry from the closest endpoint (if linear) or the point (if the related feature is a point).  0 = The software uses the G3E_X and Y DELTA values. 1 = The software uses G3E_POSITIONDELTA value.  
 |  Example
  * You can project all transformers 10m off of the end of a primary conductor by setting the G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA to Yes (1) and the G3E_POSITIONDELTA to 10. 
  * If you always want transformers to be a given X,Y away from a pole, you can set the G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA to No (0) and then set the G3E_X and Y DELTA values to the appropriate offset. 

 |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONDELTA  |  The offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used only when there is a vector to use in calculating the relationship position, as when placing a transformer adjacent to a primary conductor. The vector for a point oriented component is based on the orientation.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_XDELTA  |  The X offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used when the relationship does not provide a vector for use in the offset calculation, as when placing a light on a pole.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_YDELTA  |  The Y offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used when the relationship does not provide a vector for use in the offset calculation, as when placing a light on a pole.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_ORIENTATION  |  The orientation a feature should take when being placed coincident to a given feature. This value is given in decimal degrees. Application of the value is based on the Boolean G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION. If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is Yes (1), the value given in the G3E_ORIENTATION column should be applied to the related feature as is (G3E_ORIENTATION + 0 degrees). If the If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is No (0), the value given in the G3E_ORIENTATION column should be added to the vector of the feature to be related to. This new angle of rotation should be applied to the source feature. If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is Null, this field value is ignored.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION  |  Determines whether this feature should be oriented in relation to the horizon or to its related feature. If the value is Null, do not do any orientation adjustment to the geometry even if the position is adjusted based on G3E_POSITIONDELTA.  0 = Orient to the related feature. 1 = Orient to the horizon.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FORCEPARALLELTO  |  Determines whether this feature should be placed parallel to the related feature from the nearest point regardless of its proximity to an endpoint.  0 = Offset based on proximity to endpoint (normal operation). 1 = Offset parallel to the related feature. If Null, this field is checked on all relationships.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |

### G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING (Relationship-to-Feature Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING 
Maps which feature participates in which relationships as the active feature.
A child feature is the active feature in "child to parent" relationship, and a parent feature is the active feature in "parent to child" relationship. The other feature (the parent feature defined for a "child to parent" relationship, for example) does not have a row in this table. 
The content of this table answers the question: If I have this feature, which relationships do I have to run for it?   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RMNO  |  Row identifier for the table..  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  Identifier of the relationship from [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Feature that participates in this relationship as the active feature.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component of the feature that initiates the relationship software. This value is pulled from the column specified by the relationship as the triggering component.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_REPAIRIFACE (Repair Indication Interface Table)
Table name: G3E_REPAIRIFACE 
Contains information required when breaking a linear that has potentially invalidated the data model. Based on information in this table, NetWorks Core can place an instance of a feature to indicate to you that some repairs are required before posting data. 
Since this table contains several different kinds of information, it is organized as a general parameter table. However, two parameter columns are provided since most of the information consists of pairs of values. This table needs an entry in [G3E_ANALYSIS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2bLFqVwB0MTsyBVENDw8bg). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260693?tocId=2TUSsCOJLmRvbbgVeifteQ) NetWorks Core places all required graphic components whenever it generates a repair flag feature. If an X Offset and Y Offset are not specified for one of those components, NetWorks Core uses a default value of 0.0 for both offsets, thus placing the component exactly at the break point location.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  [G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4xJgGeK0diVZmVC6WAblww)  |  A string indicating the information stored in this row.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_TABLE  |  Database table.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (22)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE  |  Optimized database table.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_PARAMETER1  |  Represents a valid value to the corresponding G3E_TYPE. See the [G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4xJgGeK0diVZmVC6WAblww) description for the meanings of this parameter.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PARAMETER2  |  Represents a valid value to the corresponding G3E_TYPE. See the G3E_TYPE description for the meanings of this parameter. This column is not used for all rows.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_REPAIROFFSET (Repair Offsets Table)
Table name: G3E_REPAIROFFSET 
For each structure, identify the offset (X,Y) for the repair feature from each break feature. You must still make the appropriate ownership entries in [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) (or other such table) for the repair feature. 
If a linear feature has both geographic and detail components that can be broken, you must list both of those components in the G3E_CNO column of this table. For the geographic component, make an entry in this table for each geographic component of the repair feature that you want placed when the geographic component is broken. For the detail component, make an entry in this table for each detail component of the repair feature that you want placed when the detail component is broken.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RONO  |  Unique row number.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Number of break feature.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component number of break feature. This is the component that was broken.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_REPAIRCNO  |  Component number of repair feature to place relative to the break location.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_XOFFSET  |  Delta X units to add to the break location for positioning the repair instance.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |   |  
|  G3E_YOFFSET  |  Delta Y units to add to the break location for positioning the repair instance.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_REPLICATION_OBJECTS (Replication Objects Information)
Table name: G3E_REPLICATION_OBJECTS 
This table contains information necessary for replicating database objects to an external database using the Replicate Data for Field Work command.. 
This table is populated running the following SQL statement:
SQL> execute MG3EReplication.populateAl(‘<Configuration Name>’)l;
This procedure is run during metadata publish to update the table with any metadata changes. This table should not be manually modified outside the calling of the procedure.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  OBJECT_NAME  |  Identifies object name should be replicated. Unique identifier for this table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Varchar2(30)  |   |  
|  OBJECT_TYPE  |  Identifies object type of the object defined in this row. This value should be 'TABLE', 'VIEW', 'TYPE', 'FUNCTION', 'PROCEDURE', 'PACKAGE', 'TRIGGER', or 'SEQUENCE'   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (15)  |   |  
|  REPLICATION_CATEGORY  |  Identifies category in which the object in this row is replicated. This value should be ‘METADATA’, ‘PICKLISTS’, ‘LTT’, ‘DATASUPPORT’, ‘SEQUENCES’, ‘COMPONENTS’, ‘SOURCE’, ‘TRIGGERS’, ‘DEPENDENCY’, or ‘VIEWS’   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (12)  |   |  
|  DATE_STAMP  |  Identifies date the record is populated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
This table is not available in Metadata Explorer.

### G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION (Role Association Table)
Table name:  G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION 
The G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table contains information necessary to support the definition of role names and their association to NetWorks Core objects. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. It is published as [G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/n9l4uQMeFN85NHvv01mcQg) and [G3E_COMMANDROLE_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/CjuMkBZ~BJDulAj8lH724g) to support command manager lookups and behavioral adjustments to software processing by roles. It is also joined to other metadata tables that need to constrain their behavior or access to objects by roles. 
The table specifies a programmatic name for each system object. This is the key into the table for commands that limit their behavior by a role. In some cases, the programmatic name is the identifier of the object, such as the CUSTOMCOMMAND command number. This table also contains the interface information for commands. 
Default entries for this table are provided by Hexagon. The entries for G3E_TYPE FindMethod, Legend, and CustomCommand are populated by the triggers on the table when a record such as new find method, legend, or custom command is added to the table. 
The default role EVERYONE is defined as part of the PL/SQL upgrade. However, it is not associated with any specific NetWorks Core user. Admin commands are assigned the ADMINISTRATOR role so users cannot access them. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256946?tocId=zh3qB4osHGP2VkpCluxGBg) Some of the commands listed in this table may be designated as commands that are automatically started by the product and thus cannot be removed from the menu. Example: Temporary Geometry Shortcut and Placement Shortcut.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RANO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  [G3E_OBJECTCONTROL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_hdkj6tAY9Z9jKlKzivAgQ)  |  Name of the operation this role controls. For commands, this is the ProgID of the software component.   |  Yes  |  Yes1  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  G3E_OBJECTCONTROLID  |  Identifier for the object associated with the role. For custom commands, this value is the value in [G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND.G3E_CCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TnT4ya5S9F75dJaSN86qXg).   |  No  |  Yes1  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control.  |  No  |  Yes2  |   |  No  |  No  |  Vachar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_OBJECTNAME  |  Descriptive name of the command. Used only when the G3E_TYPE is Command. It is not used programmatically and is only for descriptive purposes.   |  No  |  Yes3  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Vachar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Description of how the object is controlled by this role.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (240)  |   |  
|  [G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/lqEgSF7rgbkzGYKhC588hg)  |  Indicates the system-defined type of the control specification for this object. This helps in matching the object to the metadata it might control.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (30)  |   |

This should be populated only when the G3E_TYPE = Command.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO  |  The group number of the arguments to the interface specified in G3E_RINO. This field should be Null if the .NET object requires no arguments. If non-null, this value must match one of the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) values. This column should be populated only when G3E_TYPE = Command.   |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

### G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION (Schematic Definition Table)
Table name: G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION 
Contains metadata to define symbology schemes for rendering features in a schematic window. You can define several different types of schematics, and each schematic type could need different symbology to make them unique. This table is used to give a name to each set of schematic metadata. You must define at least one set to use the GTSchematicGeneratorService. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table.

|  G3E_USERNAME  |  The schematic definition name.  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  The role associated with the inclusion of this schematic.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are used within the application. This information is provided by the DBA and is not defaulted.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

### G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY (Schematic Symbology Definition Table)
Table name: G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY 
Defines symbology and labeling for each feature class that participates in a schematic drawing. The [G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JerQL7TjZz8sXZDybg_9xA) table defines the values for G3E_SDNO in this table. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. 
For each unique value of G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION.G3E_SDNO, there should be at least one entry in this table for each feature class that can participate in that type of schematic drawing. If only one entry for a feature class is specified, it must have G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE=1 (Primary). A second entry, with G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE=2 (Label) can also be specified for a feature class. If a label entry is specified, labels are generated for instances of that feature in the schematic drawing.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SSNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SDNO  |  The schematic definition number.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number of a feature to be displayed in a schematic.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE  |  The type of schematic entity. A Primary entry is required for every feature class. Label entries are optional and are only needed if you want a label to be generated in the schematic for that feature.  1 = Primary   
2 = Label   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_GRAPHGEOMETRY  |  Indicates whether a given feature should be treated as a node or an edge in the schematic layout  Generally, you treat point features as nodes and linear features as edges, but there can be exceptions. For example, an electrical bus can be drawn as a linear in the map, but buses are typically single-node devices that are represented as a node in a schematic layout. You can also include area features in your schematic, and you can represent them as nodes. If you specify a feature as an edge, verify that it has at least two connections in the network to assure a reasonable layout.  0 = Node   
1 = Edge  This field is not used when the G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label).  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PRIMARYVNO  |  The published view number for values to drive style and label rules. This view must contain any attributes referenced by the style rule specified in G3E_PRIMARYSRNO. If the G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label), this view must contain any attributes referenced by the label rule specified by G3E_PRIMARYLRNO.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PRIMARYSRNO  |  The style rule to apply to the schematic entity. If this value is Null, a G3E_STYLEID column must exist on the component view described by G3E_PRIMARYVNO or G3E_ALTERNATEVNO.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PRIMARYLRNO  |  The label rule to apply to the schematic label. Only used if G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ALTERNATEVNO  |  The alternate published view number for values to drive style and label rules in case no data was found in the primary view. This view must contain any attributes referenced by the style rule specified by G3E_ALTERNATESRNO. If G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label), this view must contain any attributes referenced by the label rule specified by G3E_ALTERNATELRNO.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ALTERNATESRNO  |  The alternate style rule to apply to data found in the alternate view.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ALTERNATELRNO  |  The alternate label rule to apply to data found in the alternate view. Only used if G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DEFAULTSNO  |  Style number of a default style to use if there is no data available for the schematic entity.This value is only used if G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 1 (Primary).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LABELPOSITION  |  The position of the label with respect to the schematic entity. This value indicates where the label is located relative to the element it is labeling. This field is only used if G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label). G3E_LABELPOSITION and G3E_LABELALIGNMENT work together. There are nine [possible positions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QOfT3aOT_ecERAgwrt6ySw) of a label on a feature. Each position has nine possible valid alignment values as determined in G3E_LABELALIGNMENT.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LABELALIGNMENT  |  The [alignment of the text string ](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~6VeMGRDMTO4Znaq3Xabvw)with respect to the label position. This field is only used if G3E_SCHEMATICTYPE is 2 (Label). G3E_LABELALIGNMENT and G3E_LABELPOSITION work together.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TOOLTIPLRNO  |  The label rule number to build the tool tip with.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USEGEOMETRY  |  Not used.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are used within the application. This information is provided by the DBA and is not defaulted.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_SETTINGSTABLE (Legend Entry Settings Table)
Table name: G3E_SETTINGSTABLE 
Contains one or more groups of legend settings information for a single legend. These groups define multiple ways to view the same legend. For example, the same Electric legend can be configured so users can view it with different data displayed (G3E_DISPLAYMODE=1). Legends are used to populate a map window or an embedded map on a plot sheet. The actual name of this table is specified in the [G3E_LEGEND](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dkXBUKhJYRP6rlMPMUk7Kg) table. An instance of the settings table contains the display scale range, default statuses, and properties. 
The complete legend entry is defined by joining this table and G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE to the G3E_LEGENDENTRY table. 
If the G3E_LEGENDENTRY table is populated when an upgrade script is run, the G3E_SETTINGSTABLE is automatically populated. The G3E_SETTINGSTABLE is the primary table that drives the layering for output to PDF.

|  G3E_LENO  |  The number of the legend entry. A legend entry appears only once per G3E_LSNO, but may be referenced by multiple display groups within a legend. The combination of G3E_LENO and G3E_LSNO must be unique.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LSNO  |  Foreign key into the G3E_LEGENDSETTINGS table. Defines the different legend settings that can be applied to a given G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE. The combination of G3E_LENO and G3E_LSNO must be unique.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_LAYERNAME  |  Name of the layer on which the legend entry is placed in exported PDF files using the Export to PDF command. If this field is not set, the legend entry is put on the default PDF layer.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |

### G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP (Silent Relationship Group Table)
Table name: G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP 
Describes the parameters to the SilentEstablish method on the relationship services. It allows a placement configuration to preconfigure the relationship to avoid prompting the user during the configuration construction. 
When processing each component in the placement configuration, the placement software checks for a non-null G3E_SILENTRGNO in the placement configuration optimized table. If the placement software finds a non-null value, it queries the [G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jd5ouYu2f3o91r5e2JQGiA) looking for rows that match the current RNO and silent relationship group for each of the relationships associated with the component: 
  * If no rows are returned, the relationship processes using the Establish method.
  * If rows are returned, placement calls SilentEstablish to establish relationships.


Either Establish or SilentEstablish is called for a particular relationship for a particular feature instance. For linear or polygon components, after the first point is placed the software checks for returned rows. If SilentEstablish should be called, the software can skip processing on the endpoint. When multiple rows are returned for a group/relationship combination, Relationships are silently established for each row.

|  G3E_SILENTRGNO  |  Identifier for the set of rows in the silent relationship table that comprise the relationship parameters for a particular FNO/CNO/FIDX combination.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  Number of the relationship that these parameters apply to.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVECONNECTPTINDICATOR  |  Represents the connection point in the active feature (the one being placed) that should be set silently. For the node- edge connectivity relationship, this is the node number to set represented by the number 1 or 2. For the ownership relationship, this is the first (1) or second (2) parent attribute when processing a child. When processing a parent, the value is 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATECONNECTPTINDICATOR  |  Represents the connection point in the related feature (the one identified by G3E_RELATEFNO and G3E_RELATEFEATUREINDEX) that should be set silently. For the node- edge connectivity relationship, this is the node number to set represented by the number 1 or 2. For the ownership relationship, this is the first (1) or second (2) parent attribute when processing a child. When processing a parent, the value is 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEFNO  |  Number of the related feature included in this configuration that should build a relationship with the active feature.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

The static attribute mapping table (G3E_STORMSATTRIBUTE) defines the mapping for each feature between the STORMS static attributes and the location to store the value in the GIS feature. 
NetWorks Core also provides a functional interface to [check consistency of the CU and its static or derived attributes](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg). ### G3E_STYLELANGMAPPING (Style Language Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_STYLELANGMAPPING 
Contain information necessary to support different style objects for non-default languages. For a style object, if the style number is the same as the alternate style number, then the blob value is the same for the default and non-default language. Otherwise, the style has a different blob value in the non-default language, and the blob value can be found through G3E_ALTERNATESNO. This table contains all entries in all non-default language sub-tables for [G3E_STYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA). None of these fields are localized because they represent the localized metadata. 
An entry must exist in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for the table. The table is not published.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SLMNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SNO  |  Identifier for the style.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LCID  |  Value of the locale identifier found in [G3E_METADATALANGUAGE.G3E_LCID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/J_swCLicivDPWmDMyDJePQ) for this particular instance.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2(4)  |   |  
|  G3E_ALTERNATESNO  |  Row identifier for the table for the style that has a different blob value in the language sub- table. If the blob value in the sub- table is the same as the value in G3E_STYLE, G3E_ALTERNATESNO has the same value as G3E_SNO.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PLOTNAME  |  Descriptive name found in G3E_STYLE_NNNN.G3E_USERNAME  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2(240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_STYLERULE (Style Rule Table)
Table name: G3E_STYLERULE 
Maps a [style rule](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256634?tocId=Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA) to the possible formats that can be returned by that rule (StyleRule-StyleFormat Mapping). Also includes the expressions used to choose the style. 
A description of when to use a particular style definition. The technique used to achieve attribute-based symbology. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256634?tocId=Jm_ou6DGz8E1PSeRsGtPxA) Every style rule should have a Null filter. This is effectively the default style for the particular legend entry for this component view. It should always be the last filter evaluated. This is a Null value or empty string, not the word Null.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SRROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SRNO  |  Identifier for this style rule. Not actually a primary key, but the display cache treats it as a key for grouping purposes.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RULE  |  Name of the style rule referenced in the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table. Because the style rule is associated with a legend entry, you can define different style rules for the different ways you need to display a given type of component.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  [SQL WHERE clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) based on the attributes of the associated component view definition. The successful (True) evaluation of this expression renders the geometry in the style specified by the G3E_STYLEINDEX property. The Null filter (catch-all case) should contain an empty string or a Null value. Do not include the word Null in the field. Any field references must be uppercase. Oracle built-in functions are not supported.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  Order in which the filters should be evaluated. The filter that is most common in that it encompasses most of the associated data should be assigned a value of 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SNO  |  Identifier associated with the required style object from the [G3E_STYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA) table. The associated style is used to render the geometry when the filter evaluates to True.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

This value should be defaulted with the [G3E_STYLE.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA) where G3E_SNO matches.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_SYMBOLOGYOVERRIDE (Symbology Override Table)
Table name: G3E_SYMBOLOGYOVERRIDE
Contains the symbology override information used by the Map Output control to display traces or queries. Alternately, you can use a [color scheme group](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EshKn2qdlebarQZcNe9efg) which allows a cycle or rotating set of colors to be used each time the trace is executed. The user can distinguish the results of traces that start at different features or perhaps use different attribute criteria.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SONO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_COLOR  |  The RGB value for the color override. If this value is Null, the Map Output control uses the next color in the given group defined by G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO field. If no color scheme exists under the given group, the Map Output control uses the default color override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILLCOLOR  |  The RGB value for the fill color override. If this value is Null, the Map Output control uses the next fill color in the given group defined by G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO field. If no fill color scheme exists under the given group, the Map Output control uses the default fill color override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO  |  The group number of the group defined within G3E_COLORSCHEME table. This field value is only applicable if either G3E_COLOR or G3E_FILLCOLOR is Null. If the value of G3E_COLOR, G3E_FILLCOLOR, and this field is Null, the Map Output control uses the default color and fill color overrides.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LINEWEIGHT  |  The line weight override. If this field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the default line weight override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |   |  
|  G3E_TRANSLUCENCY  |  The default translucency for the MapOutputControl’s translucency override combo box. The legal values can be from 0 to 100, -1, or Null. Null is interpreted to mean no override. A value of 0 means that the feature being drawn is opaque. Nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the feature being drawn is invisible. Everything behind it is visible.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_FILLTRANSLUCENCY  |  The default translucency for the MapOutputControl’s fill translucency override combo box. The legal values can be from 0 to 100, -1, or Null. Null is interpreted to mean no override. A value of 0 means that the interior area of the area feature being drawn is opaque. Nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the interior area of the area feature being drawn is invisible. Everything is visible behind it.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_STROKEPATTERN  |  The stroke pattern ID from the G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE table. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing pattern of the line style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_POINTSIZE  |  The point size override. If this field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the default point size override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_FONTNAME  |  The symbol font name which is selected from the list of fonts installed in the machine. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing symbol font name of the point style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (40)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_SYMBOL  |  The symbol character (Unicode character from 33 to 255) which is selected from the list of characters for a particular symbol font name. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing symbol of the point style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (1)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257473?tocId=oMk8~MjPY9tN3rUC_XgC5Q) The translucency overrides apply to the same parts of the style as the colors, [with the exception of hatches](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257473?tocId=oMk8~MjPY9tN3rUC_XgC5Q). 
  * The normal color and translucency overrides apply to all parts of all styles that are not area fills. 
  * The fill color and translucency overrides apply to only area fills.
  * The hatches are an exception to this. The hatches get their override color from the normal button, but their override translucency from the fill drop-down list.

### G3E_TABATTRIBUTE (Property Dialog Attribute Lists Table)

Thus, the filter can be defined as something like #5107=JOB_STATE|#5107 is null.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

The type of the relation interface in [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) must be Temporary Geometry.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO  |  The group number of the arguments for the Temporary Geometry Placement Interface (if any). This field should be Null if the custom object requires no arguments. If non-null, this value must match one of the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) values.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes*  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LEGENDBEHAVIOR  |  Determines how the temporary geometries are added to the legend. 0 = Do not add any legend entry. The Temporary Geometry Placement Interface creates a legend entry. This option is useful if the legend entry should be created under any other root node than Temporary Geometries.  1 = New legend entry is created. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME> > <ordinal>, where <ordinal> is determined as the highest ordinal in this subtree placed so far + 1.  2 = Append to existing legend entry. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME>. If the legend entry exists, the newly placed geometries are appended. If the entry does not exist, it is created and the geometries are added.  3 = Replace existing legend entry. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME>. If the legend entry exists, the newly placed geometries replace the existing ones. If the entry does not exist, it is created and the geometries are added.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_AUTOREPEAT  |  Determines placement behavior. 0 = The command deactivates when placement is finished 1 = Placement automatically repeats until the user presses ESC  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable access to the attribute. The specific attribute is available to the user who has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2(240)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Administrator-supplied description of the temporary geometry placement. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
* The foreign key relationship is implemented as a validation since G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO is not a true primary key.

### G3E_TEXTSTYLE (Text Style Table)
Table name: G3E_TEXTSTYLE 
The table corresponds to the information in [G3E_STYLE.G3E_VALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA) and describes how a text style is defined. There is one row for each style definition. 
Because these fields represent the localized metadata, none of them are localized.
An entry must exist in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for the table and its optimized table to include this metadata in the published cache. The optimized table is G3E_TEXTSTYLEFONT_OPTABLE. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256782?tocId=0yRaZQ44AZMeTckCYodWaQ) All fonts must be installed on the publish server during metadata publish.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SNO  |  Identifier for the style. This value is copied from the G3E_STYLE table. You cannot edit this value.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name found in [G3E_STYLE.G3E_USERNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0sEp1oH8BhJknBDlWdc4uA).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_COLOR  |  RGB value for the color of the text.  -3 = The style color is the same as the background color. Setting this value to -3 might be useful in the case where you want the text box to have a specific color, but want the actual text in the background color. This creates the necessary contrast to see the actual text   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TRANSLUCENCY  |  The translucency applied to the actual text of a style. The legal values can be from 0 to 100 or Null. Null is interpreted to be 0. A value of 0 means that the text is opaque, that is nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the text is invisible, that is everything is visible behind the text.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |

Using G3E_FONTWEIGHT gives you more choices in font selection.  0 = No bold formatting. 1 = Bold formatting is applied. The G3E_FONTBOLD value is a shorthand for specifying a weight; selecting Bold formatting is applied (1) in Metadata Explorer is generally equivalent to specifying a value of Bold (700) for G3E_FONTWEIGHT.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_FONTITALIC  |  Specifies whether the italic formatting is applied in the text style. 0 = No italic formatting. 1 = Italic formatting is applied.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_FONTNAME  |  Name of the text font.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FONTSTRIKETHROUGH  |  Specifies whether the strikethrough formatting is applied in the text style. 0 = No strikethrough formatting. 1 = Strikethrough formatting is applied.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_FONTUNDERLINE  |  Specifies whether the underline formatting is applied in the text style. 0 = No underline formatting. 1 = Underline formatting is applied. Using G3E_FONTWEIGHT gives you more choices in font selection. The G3E_FONTWEIGHT value is equivalent to the Weight property of the Windows GDI font object. Some True Type fonts support multiple weights, while others do not, although most support a bold weight (700). Therefore, specifying a weight value other than normal (400) may or may not have an effect.  This value can be any integer between 0- 1000. The following are typical values and their meanings:  0 = Defaulted by the font implementation 100 = Thin 200 = Extra light 300 = Light 400 = Normal 500 = Medium 600 = Semi-bold (also known as demi-bold) 700 = Bold 800 = Extra bold (also known as ultra-bold) 900 = Black  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

Null is interpreted to be 0. A value of 0 means that the background fill of the text box is opaque, that is nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the background fill is invisible, that is everything is visible behind the fill area of the text box.  0 = Typical value to mask features behind the text.  100 = Typical value to put a frame around the text without masking.  To partially obscure features, set to an intermediate value.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |

|  G3E_TEXTBOXHATCHTRANSLUCENCY  |  The translucency applied to the foreground fill for the area style of the text box surrounding the text. This translucency is applied to any hatch pattern required for the style. The legal values can be from 0 to 100 or Null. Null is interpreted to be 0. A value of 0 means that the hatching is opaque, that is, nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that any hatching is invisible, that is everything is visible behind any hatching.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |

A value of 0 means that the boundary is opaque, that is, nothing is visible behind it. ### G3E_TRACE (Trace Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACE 
Defines the types of traces supported by the application. An entry should be made in this table for each type of trace to be performed. Entries in this table define the particular trace configurations that the user can choose from the trace command. It also includes trace definitions required for some of the analytical commands like the Electric Design Tools. Each entry defines the behavior of the trace including how the algorithm is controlled (G3E_TRACE.G3E_TRACETYPE) and the criteria for stopping the trace or restricting the results to specified features. As you complete these entries, you need to define the features that can start the trace ([G3E_TRACEFEATURE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/90tgoPo8OSNicHgNcpXrUw)) and what commands can use the trace ([G3E_TRACEMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Ptbq1EbJSIGFkvwVGnClEQ)). Depending on your criteria and what you plan to do with the results, you may also need to define additional columns associated with the trace ([G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1f~vq~Sp6_UgJrOEhThl8Q), [G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4JEiLQX9fCdOtc8E6UHuhA) and [G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCfScaS0GVxKHwguY94sfw)).

### G3E_TRACEADDCOLTYPES (Trace Additional Columns Types Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEADDCOLTYPES 
Defines the different types of additional column definitions that can be specified for the traces. Also provides referential integrity for the [G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCfScaS0GVxKHwguY94sfw) table so that the user cannot specify non-supported additional column types. 
The following additional column types are supported:
  * For seed feature. These additional column definitions are used when populating the seed feature in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table. Additional column definitions of this type in the G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table cannot reference any rows from the TRACERESULT table (contain a column with the tr table alias). They may only reference columns from the Connectivity table using the conn table alias. 
  * For features other than the seed. These additional column definitions are used when populating all traced features other than the seed in the TRACERESULT table. Additional column definitions of this type in the G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table can reference any rows from the TRACERESULT or Connectivity table by using the tr and conn table aliases respectively. 

  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ADDCOLUMNTYPE  |  Internal identifier for the additional column type.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Description of the additional column type.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (40)  |   |

### G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS (Trace Additional Result Columns Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS 
Maps user-defined columns in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table to the SQL expressions defining their source values. The G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table specifies which of these columns should be populated in the TRACERESULT table for each trace defined in the [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) table. Since these additional columns may not be populated by all traces, the columns must be defined either to allow Null values or to have default values. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257984?tocId=1f~vq~Sp6_UgJrOEhThl8Q) This table is not published but is accessed by the trace procedure at runtime. The table must be replicated for field use and as such must appear in the analysis lists.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TRACNO  |  An internal identifier used to define a particular user- defined column on the TRACERESULT table and the source of its value   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALCOLUMN  |  Name of the user- defined column on the TRACERESULT table  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEEXPR  |  SQL expression that defines the value to be set for the additional column during the trace operation.  Table Aliases The trace attempts to populate any additional columns specified for it. The result columns themselves do not have to be qualified; they are understood to apply to the TRACERESULT table. However, any columns in the connectivity or TRACERESULT tables used in G3E_SOURCEEXPR to specify a value for the result columns must be qualified properly. The table alias used for the TRACERESULT table is tr and the connectivity table alias is conn. Failure to qualify these columns results in an SQL parsing error.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (50)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES (Trace Attributes Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES 
Supports attribute parameter substitution in the different criteria of the traces defined in [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg). The Trace command recognizes that a substitution needs to take place and uses the attribute numbers defined in this table to determine the valid values to allow the user to choose for the substitution. This table defines which attributes should be substituted and the ordinal for the specific placeholder for which to make the substitution. 
Refer to the descriptions of the G3E_STOPCRITERIA, G3E_FILTERCRITERIA, and G3E_PATHCOST columns of the G3E_TRACE table for information on how to specify the placeholders for the attribute substitution. 
Only attributes of substitution type User are presented to the user for input. The other values are derived by the software.

### G3E_TRACETYPES (Trace Types Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACETYPES

Also provides referential integrity for the [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) table so that the user cannot specify non-supported trace types.

### G3E_TRANSFER (Transfer Unit Support Table)
Table name: G3E_TRANSFER 
Identifies the feature-component combinations that can be manipulated by the [Transfer Units](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kiO9jkfx~Eo84xaoICp_cw) command. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261148?tocId=u3HaNjIu_ruhkOpKNvFcsQ) The combination of G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO must be unique within the table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TROWNO  |  Unique number assigned to this row.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature with which this component is associated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  The component within the feature that can be manipulated by the transfer units command.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  [G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jnO_TNtrfZsw6JHGhGtUbg)  |  Controls whether or not the component can be transferred to another feature during a transfer unit operation. The value can be 1, 2, 3, or 4.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_KEYFIELD  |  Used to select the correct subset of secondary components to transfer with the primary unit. If the value of G3E_TYPE is 1, this is the name of the field in this component that contains a unique key or name value. This is expected to be associated with the other secondary components for transfer. If the value of G3E_TYPE is 2, this is the name of the field in this component that contains the value of the key field for the primary (G3E_TYPE=1) component.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_DTNO  |  If the value of G3E_DTNO is the tab to use to present the primary transfer unit on the command dialog box. It need only be populated for the primary unit within the feature (G3E_TYPE = 1 or 3). The same tab can be used as is used for placement or edit.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RETENTIONVALUE  |  If the value of G3E_TYPE is 1 or 2, this field is Null. If the value of G3E_TYPE is 3 or 4 and this field is not Null, this is the name of the field in this component followed by an equal sign and the value to assign to the specified field. This lets you keep the original component, but indicate that it is retired. If the value of G3E_TYPE is 3 or 4 and this field is not populated, no change is made to the original component but it is still retained.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_TRANSITION (Life Cycle Transitions Table)
Table name: G3E_TRANSITION 
Contains a mapping of transition states that allows the JobLifeCycle executable to determine what state a feature- component should transition to based on the current state the feature-component is in and the work management event that is currently being processed.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TNO  |  Row for this transition.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FROMSTATE  |  Key value of the "from" or current state value.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TOSTATE  |  Key value of the "to" state value.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DEFAULT  |  If the G3E_TRANSITION.G3E_DEFAULT value = 1, this record is used to set the state in which to transition in batch processing (based on the current state of the feature). If a specific state has multiple states that are valid as a destination, you must define a default so you can do batch processing.  0 = The transition row is not a default. 1 = The transition row is a default. Example  
 |   |  G3E_DEFAULT  |  G3E_FROMSTATE  |  G3E_TOSTATE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  (Constructed)  |  1  |  3 (In Service)  |  7  |  
|  (Constructed)  |  0  |  11 (Out of Service)  |  7  |  
|  (Operational Removed)  |  1  |  6 (Proposed Removed)  |  9  |  
|  (Operational Removed)  |  0  |  12 (Removed)  |  9  |  
A feature currently has a state of Constructed and a transition is requested by batch processing. The batch process performs a query to find all possible destination (or G3E_TOSTATE) states based on the current state of the feature. The query in the example returns the records for In Service and Out of Service. Because In Service is set as the default value, the feature is transitioned to In Service. 
|  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_JLCNO  |  Key value of job life cycle value that should execute this transition if data are found that meets the G3E_FROMSTATE criteria.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

|  G3E_SETNO  |  Logical grouping number. This value is repeated in the table for any set of attributes that together trigger the auto-population of other attributes   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

(This is the driven attributes picklist.)   |  No  |  No*  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (240)  |   |

### G3E_UNITFORMAT (Units and Formatting Information Table)

Contains all of the information needed to determine how to format distance and coordinate values for presentation to the NetViewer user. ### G3E_VALIDATIONINTERFACE (Validation Interface Table)
Table name: G3E_VALIDATIONINTERFACE 
Lists the functions available as validation interfaces. Each function is effectively an automated object that supports the validation interface definition. It is called according to the rules in the [G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wu5b0VFREvrf2zqsFMydkQ) table. The functions are always provided the active feature recordset. Other system variables can be added during the implementation design. Any additional arguments are defined by the technique.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_VINO  |  Row identifier for the validation interface.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the interface which appears in the user interface list. For administrative use only and is done in the primary language.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACE  |  ProgID of the software component to support this function. It must begin with a letter and contain no spaces. When formatted as Project, the interface is assumed to be a .NET implementation  [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256918?tocId=mjofNzYibqeHFKBQSJveFQ) for more information about .NET implementations.  The G3E_PROGID value for [analysis packages table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg). The G3E_INTERFACE value for the interface tables.  <AssemblyName>:<TypeName> where <AssemblyName> is the filename of the assembly containing the .NET custom extension and <TypeName> is the type name (namespace.classname) of the .NET custom extension.  See [Metadata for .NET Extensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aOcRgNV~zssw9YmOFCG54A) for an example.   
 |   |  
| --- |  
|   |  
|  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT  |  Prompts describing the arguments for the validation interface. For administrative use only and is done in the primary language.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE  |  [Data types](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Fq1pfuicpDm0jwjnFaF0tA) of the arguments for the validation interface.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Administrator-supplied description of the validation interface. For information only.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |

### G3E_VERSIONMAPPING
Table name: G3E_VERSIONMAPPING
Associates an add-on version to NetWorks Core. This allows the add-on scripts to be run in order according to the NetWorks Core version. It is the responsibility of the add-on to provide a script to keep this information up to date.

### G3E_WORKMGMT (Work Management Integration Table)
Table name: G3E_WORKMGMT 
Contains information necessary for the various aspects of the work management integration. It is necessary for JobLifeCycle to be able to gather the necessary parameters for its batch processing cycle. This table is referenced in the [G3E_ANALYSIS](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2bLFqVwB0MTsyBVENDw8bg) table.

### G3E_WORKPOINT (Work Point Table)
Table name: G3E_WORKPOINT 
Work Point features are necessary as a grouping mechanism within GIS for data manipulation. The work point is sent to work management systems with the associated work (data manipulation) at that location. You must identify the work point feature in the interface table. You must also identify the attribute that contains the work point number. The work point feature must be set up as child of structural features in your data model using the ownership relationship. Work points can be placed interactively by the designer, or they are automatically generated when CU data are sent to your work management systems. 
For each structure, identify the offset (X,Y) for the work point from each owner feature. You must still make the appropriate ownership entries in [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) for the work point.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Number of parent feature.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_XOFFSET  |  Delta X units to add to the location of the parent feature for positioning the work point instance.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_YOFFSET  |  Delta Y units to add to the location of the parent feature for positioning the work point instance.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE (Coordinate System Specification Table)
Table name: GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE 
The database server and the application use this table to determine the coordinate system of the data. Use the [Define Coordinate System command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Or1aBR2d0n3BsevDKXaLSg) to populate GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE. If this table is not populated, the default coordinate system (Cylindrical Equirectangular) is used. See Intergraph.[GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) for more information.

|  CSGUID  |  The GUID of this coordinate system. The server is responsible for setting this to a new valid GUID when a record is added. If clients can persist this value (depending on the value of CSGUIDTYPE), the server must update the CSGUID when the coordinate system values are modified (because the coordinate system is no longer the same).  The GUID is of the form {12340001-4980- 1920-6788- 123456789012}. Valid values are Null or a GUID.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (38)  |   |

### G3E_DIALOG (Property Dialogs Table)
Table name: G3E_DIALOG 
Presentation of attribute data are governed by the definition of tabs on the dialog box. This table defines the group or set of tabs that are presented as a unit. Single components (required, nonrepeating) can be combined on a single tab. Optional or optional/repeating components are typically presented in a horizontal grid that is limited to attributes from a single component. The individual tabs are defined in G3E_DIALOGTAB. The software supports an unlimited number of tab types or classifications to support placement configurations. However, each secondary feature should define a Properties type that describes the display of attributes for the component view definition. For Feature Explorer, each feature should define a Review type of tabs for displaying reviewable attributes. 
For job data, attribute presentation is controlled by the definition of tabs on the dialog boxes. The definition for the G3E_TYPE = G3E_EDITJOB is required.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_DROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DNO  |  Identifier for the dialog box (set of tabs). The number is repeated in the table and consequently it is not actually a primary key. However, the display cache treats it as a key for grouping purposes. This should be assigned for a Type and FNO combination since access to the set of tabs is based on this information. The same number is assigned to each tab within the set, even if not all of the tabs are displayed due to filtering. The same dialog box number must be assigned to each tab in the group.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DTNO  |  Identifier of the tab to include in this dialog box display. This is a reference to the identifier defined in [G3E_DIALOGTAB](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IKdrSlfHQUZZzLVLFu5dTQ).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  The context in which this tab is used. The type is user definable. You can define as many types as you want to support placement configurations. The Properties type is used to define a tab for presentation of the component views in the display cache for secondary data. There should be only one tab of this type per feature, and it should correspond to the view of the primary graphic component. There should also be one definition per feature with the type Placement, one or more definitions with the type Edit, and one or more definitions with the type Review for use by Feature Explorer.  Additionally, the type can reference a placement configuration. These are the reserved type values: Placement Edit Review Properties Bulk Edit Single Edit Multi Edit Single Review Merged Placement Merged Review Merged Edit For any of the Single * or Multiple * entries, only one dialog tab pair should be referenced for a given G3E_FNO value. This check occurs only in metadata validation. These G3E_Type values are used by the [Duct Configuration control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AKYI3Kuz~5qBsCiyjhGFrQ) and [Cable Edit control](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Zn_9lmDaJE11oZfURbtkRg). The [Bulk Edit dialog tab](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/e6vZLByjrTVM4DuZIv9IQg) is only used for the features that can be bulk edited. Only features with [G3E_FEATURE.G3E_BULKEDIT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ) set to Yes (1) can have this kind of dialog tab defined.  For the Merged * entries, all of the dialog tabs referenced for a given G3E_FNO value should have the same structure: the attributes referenced should have the same column names and the same data types and formatting. These dialog tabs are used to form a horizontal grid containing multiple components merged together so that they appear to be one single component with common attributes.  Only one pair of components can be specified per feature—one detail component and one geographic component. If the associated dialog tab references the Cable Edit control, no other merged entries can be defined.  These types are allowable for attribute presentation for the job commands: G3E_EDITJOB G3E_NEWJOB G3E_JOBENVIRONMENT G3E_POSTJOB G3E_DISCARDJOB G3E_CLOSEJOB G3E_COPYJOB G3E_NETJOBS  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  G3E_FNO of the feature that this tab should be used in conjunction with. If a tab is to be used by multiple features, it must be listed for each feature. If this dialog box represents a configuration in the Type field, this field should still be populated. Multiple features within one configuration can use the same dialog tab.  A G3E_FNO of zero is allowed in the case where type equals the following: G3E_EDITJOB G3E_NEWJOB G3E_JOBENVIRONMENT G3E_POSTJOB G3E_DISCARDJOB G3E_CLOSEJOB G3E_COPYJOB G3E_NETJOBS  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The position of this tab when displayed during feature placement or edit. A value of 1 indicates the first tab in the sequence from left to right.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  [SQL clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) used to control the selection of the tabs to use during the review or edit of a feature. This query is a not a database query, and works only for filters against the primary geographic component’s view, like a style rule filter works. The G3E_FILTER column is ignored when the placement or named configuration dialog boxes are requested. An evaluation of True for the filter includes the tab. An evaluation of False excludes the filter. Filter ordering is not used here, and all filters are evaluated. The Null filter (catch-all case) should contain an empty string or a Null value. Do not include the word Null in the field.  If the feature is defined as nongraphic, the primary attribute component is used instead of the primary geographic component view. The same restrictions on the filter apply. If the feature is geographic, the logic checks for occurrences of first the primary geographic, primary detail, and alternate geographic until it finds an occurrence. If no occurrence is found, it uses the primary attribute component. The filter clause must be valid for all of these components or component views.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

The specification is in the resolution independent unit called TWIPS. You can approximate the width as a more familiar measurement unit as follows:  There are approximately 15 twips in one pixel. On Microsoft Windows-based machines, there are approximately 96 pixels per logical inch. So, to make the column one inch wide, you would set the twips to 1440. ### G3E_TABATTRIBUTE (Property Dialog Attribute Lists Table)

#### Column Pairs
Any number of pairs can be specified; they are connected by the AND operator, indicated by an ampersand (&), in the WHERE clause to select values from the [picklist table](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/1Hghbgy9rikks~bnc1MKiw). 
The definition includes OR capabilities indicated by a vertical line ( | ). In place of the attribute number, a literal value can be specified. For example, a filter of #1 = TRANS_IND | ‘BOTH’ = TRANS_IND retrieves values from the picklist where the TRANS_IND column contains either the value BOTH or the current value in attribute number one (G3E_ANO = 1). 
The SQL statement generated to query the picklist table looks like this (assuming that the current value of attribute number one is TRANSMISSION): 
SQL> select <columns> from mypicklist where ‘TRANSMISSION’ = TRANS_IND OR ‘BOTH’ = TRANS_IND;
Field names must be in uppercase. In addition, IS NULL can be used to qualify the attribute number. So the filter can be defined as something like #5107=JOB_STATE|#5107 is null. 
For more information about filters and the AND (&) and OR (|) operators, see[Field Value Filters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/RTfE9n4VqdlpjpZ18oZDaw). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265502) The # symbol should preface each attribute number within a given field value filter. If you have a filter that contains several column pairs joined together with AND's and OR's, each attribute number of each pair should be prefaced with a #. If the attribute number of each pair is not preceded with a #, the attribute number is treated as a literal value. For example, the filter #10=STATE&11=TYPE contains one attribute number to be converted to a field name, and one literal. The filter #10=STATE&#11=TYPE contains two attribute numbers to be converted to field names.

### G3E_TRIGGERSET (Tab Attributes Trigger Set)

#### Filter Syntax
The syntax of the filter's relational operators must be compatible with the ADO recordset Filter property. The software substitutes the #<ANO> reference for the actual value, but you control the allowable operators and ordering. For conjunctions (AND, OR), use the ampersand (&) for AND and the vertical bar (|) for OR. The software makes the appropriate substitution. Field names must always precede the relational operator. This is the syntax: ALPHA_CODE=#1001 & TOTAL_SIZE=#1002 
Where ALPHA_CODE and TOTAL_SIZE are the names of the columns in the picklist table. and 1001 and 1002 are the [G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_ANO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) values of the attributes within the feature that contain the values to compare.

## Core Schema Control Tables

### Detail Tables

#### G3E_DETAIL (Detail Relationship Table)
Table name: G3E_DETAIL 
The detail relationship is the mechanism by which unique detail group identifiers are generated. These identifiers are stored in the detail identifier field of each detail graphic component. The G3E_DETAIL table defines which features can reference detail components. This table also defines which component (within a referencing feature) triggers the creation of detail or schematic windows and which component is used to store window attribution. 
The identifier information stored in the attribute component of the referencing feature enables the review of the detail graphics from various feature classes associated with this identifier. The detail relationship software lets you generate a new identifier and description of the detail area. It also lets you link to another existing detail area. The reestablish method on the relationship software allows the generation of another detail area only if the attribute component containing the detail information is a repeating component. 
A feature can reference or define a detail area and not actually have any of its own components participate in that detail. For example, a geographic substation references several detail windows: for breaker details, bus details, or regulator details. Each of these detail windows contains features that are within the substation, but the substation itself is not in the detail window.

### Dimensioning Tables

#### G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL (Orthogonal Dimension Component Table)
Table name: G3E_DIMORTHOGONAL 
Contains metadata of orthogonal dimension components. This table also contains information about dimensioning relationship fields. Lengths and distances are interpreted by NetWorks Core to be in the same unit of measure as the ground unit of the coordinate system definition. 
This table contains multiple fields which reference entries in [G3E_ATTRIBUTE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw) table. G3E_CNO of all these referenced entries must match the G3E_CNO in the referencing row in this table.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  G3E_DIMTEXTLRNO1  |  G3E_LRNO of the label rule used to generate the first dimension text.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTLOC1  |  Default position of the first dimension text along the dimension line. The value is in percent with 0% as the start point of the dimension line and 100% as the endpoint of the dimension line.  For [stacked dimensions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vAsnjYWXINWTtu_hw2cVKg), the dimension text is placed between the endpoint of the associated dimension line and the endpoint of the longest shorter dimension line. The endpoint of the longest shorter dimension line is 0%, and the endpoint of the associated dimension line is 100%.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,2)  |  50  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETX1  |  [Offset](javascript:;) of the first dimension text in the direction parallel with the dimension line.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETY1  |  Offset of the [first dimension text](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V6RM4nVFNzCgeMon~w~QOA) from the dimension line in the direction perpendicular to the dimension line. The distance is measured in the ground units of the coordinate system.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTOFFSETXREV1  |  Offset of the first dimension text in the direction parallel with the dimension line for small dimensions.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_DIMTEXTALIGN1  |  Horizontal and vertical [alignment](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~6VeMGRDMTO4Znaq3Xabvw) of the first dimension text.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  8  |
