|  GuyDescription  |  Input  |  This defines a short description that the user wants to display indicating the type of guy or any descriptive information.   |  
|  GuyAttachmentHeight  |  Input  |  Attribute representing attachment height of the guy.  |  
|  GuyDistanceFromPole  |  Input  |  Attribute representing guy distance from pole.  |  
|  GuyBreakingStrength  |  Input  |  Attribute representing guy breaking strength. This parameter can be retrieved either from feature attribute data or from catalog table.   |  
|  GuyBearing  |  Input  |  Attribute representing guy bearing.  |  
|  GuyAngle  |  Output  |  Calculated guy angle.  |  
|  GuyHorizontalTension  |  Output  |  Calculated guy horizontal tension.  |  
|  GuyVerticalTension  |  Output  |  Calculated guy vertical tension.  |  
|  GuyMoment  |  Output  |  Calculated guy moment.  |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265395) Because a guy feature can be a component of the pole feature and there can be more than one guy associated with the same pole, GuyAnalysisIdentifier parameter value is used to find the repeating occurrence of the guy instance.

##### G3E_EDTPOLEMOMENTCATEGORY (Electric Design Tools Pole Moment Category Table)
Table name: G3E_EDTPOLEMOMENTCATEGORY 
Since some utilities model their guys based on individual feature category, this table provides an ability to list the categories they want to use. For example, a feature category may be primary, secondary, or neutral. Even if the guys are not modeled based on individual feature category, this table should contain at least one entry with a default category. 
An entry must exist in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for the table. The optimized table [G3E_EDTFEATURE_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/if19uumcXZuDk462Cts4QA) should contain the category information. [G3E_EDTFEATURE.G3E_EDTPMCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jIJyyrPrDZ5543k9snLd_g) is a foreign key that points to G3E_EDTPOLEMOMENTCATEGORY.G3E_EDTPMCNO. The optimized table should contain G3E_NAME and G3E_GUYATTACHMENTHEIGHT from this table as G3E_CATEGORY and G3E_GUYATTACHMENTHEIGHT, respectively.

#### Electrical Analysis

##### G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION (Analysis Configuration Table)
Table name: G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION 
Contains information about the paths in the connectivity network that were traced rather than to the features that were traced. The electric analysis functionality needs this information to determine which features were traced and to properly interpret the traced network. For one- and two-node devices, the information is identical for the feature and the connected path. For features with more than two nodes, the information is not identical for the feature and the connected path. 
Examples of this type of data are the operating status of the path (open/closed) and the phase of the path. One of the parameters the analysis functionality needs is G3E_CFGPARAMETER. The G3E_VALUE column defines this value. 
The combination of G3E_ANALYSISPKG, G3E_RNO, and G3E_CFGPARAMETER is unique.
The analysis functionality can query these configuration parameters from the G3E_ANALYSISCONFIGURATION table:   
|  G3E_CFGPARAMETER  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CURRENT_STATUS  |  The current operating status of the path.  |  
|  NORMAL_STATUS  |  The normal operating status of the path..  |  
|  PHASE  |  The phases contained on the path  |  
The values for each of the configuration parameters must be specified as a valid SQL expression, either column name or scalar function, against the connectivity table specified by the relationship number. 
This information is not defined like the other analysis parameters in G3E_ANALYSISPARAMETERS because those parameter definitions are defined per feature number. A column or other expression from the connectivity table is the only valid definition for these configuration parameters. Also, if a feature has more than two nodes (multiple rows in the connectivity table), some rows for the feature in the connectivity table may not be traced. If attribute parameter definitions are used for this information, specification of some rows from the connectivity table may not be traced. 
This information is also tied to a relationship number since features can participate in multiple connectivity relationships (can have multiple connectivity tables as components), and the relationship number uniquely identifies a single connectivity table. 
You must qualify all columns used in the analysis configuration parameter value using 'conn' as the alias for the connectivity table. Failure to qualify the column existing in the connectivity table causes an SQL parsing error. 
An entry is required in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for this table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ACNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_ANALYSISPKG  |  Name of the analysis package that uses the trace. Foreign key to [G3E_ANALYSISPACKAGES.G3E_ANALYSISPKG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aLqq6lgk57QK1rsmsVKLmg).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  The relationship (G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO) for which the configuration parameters apply. This value indirectly specifies the name of the connectivity table containing the columns referenced by the configuration parameters. Foreign Key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_CFGPARAMETER  |  Name of a configuration parameter.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALUE  |  The value for the configuration parameter. [CADPAD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nSlvrD5e5gSaq82LZVw37Q) [SynerGEE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OS49SDS0tqA0H5HHf0UNyw) This should be expressed as some form of an SQL expression that is evaluated to a value when applied against the connectivity table corresponding to the relationship number. Do not use a column alias when specifying this expression.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

##### G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ (Feature to Analysis Object Mapping Table)
Table name:  G3E_ANALYSISFEATOBJ 
Lists the basic mappings between the features modeled by the application and the objects modeled by the analysis packages. An entry is required in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for this table. The combination of G3E_PKGOBJID, G3E_FNO, and G3E_FILTER is unique   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FEATOBJID  |  Internal identifier.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature number. Foreign key to [G3E_FEATURE.G3E_FNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VFyFq8MbVW9PQDgb03TtpQ).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_PKGOBJID  |  Identifier for an analysis package object. Foreign key to [G3E_ANALYSISPKGOBJS.G3E_PKGOBJID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jSpdelE4UmZkhg5SeEH8dw).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  An attribute-based filter to further restrict when this analysis object is created based on the feature. Only traced features that meet the filter criteria have analysis objects created for them.  Set the G3E_FILTER column to an SQL expression containing the G3E_ANO values of one or more attributes defined for the feature. Multiple attributes can be defined only if they exist in the same component table. Use square brackets to delineate the attribute numbers in this expression.   
 |  Example '[153] = ''Y''' Create an instance of the analysis object if the value of the attribute = 'Y'  |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_OUTPUTSUFFIX  |  For the applicable packages, this field defines the suffix portion of the output file name that stores the extracted information for the analysis object modeling the feature. Typically, this is a standard file name suffix (including the period), but it can include text before the period.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO  |  The number of the parent/child relationship for which child attribute type parameter definitions apply. This is only used if the G3E_VALUE_TYPE value specifies a child feature attribute value. This value explicitly defines which particular parent/child ownership type relationship should be used to find the children of the traced feature. For the child features to be determined properly, the row defining this relationship in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tKaXJUFR2b_peyQoF1h3zA) table must have G3E_TYPE = 3 and G3E_SUBORDINATE = 0.  If the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column is set, the G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO column also should be set. If either the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO or G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO value is specified, the specified analysis object is extracted only if a child of the traced feature is found. The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found:  If the analysis object supports the banked feature logic If the metadata definition states that multiple analysis objects should be created for each unit in the bank  Foreign key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO  |  The number of the child/parent relationship for which child attribute type parameter definitions apply. This is only used if the G3E_VALUE_TYPE value specifies a child feature attribute value. This value explicitly defines which particular child/parent ownership type relationship corresponds to the relationship specified in the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column. For the child attributes to be determined properly, the row defining this relationship in the [G3E_RELATIONSHIPS_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tKaXJUFR2b_peyQoF1h3zA) table must have G3E_TYPE = 3 and G3E_SUBORDINATE = 1.  If the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO column is set, the G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO column also should be set. If either the G3E_PARENTCHILD_RNO or G3E_CHILDPARENT_RNO value is specified, the specified analysis object is extracted only if a child of the traced feature is found. The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found, subject to the following:  The number of analysis objects created equals the number of children found: If the analysis object supports the banked feature logic If the metadata definition states that multiple analysis objects should be created for each unit in the bank  Foreign key to [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the number of the attribute (G3E_ANO) that contains the first circuit/feeder name. The G3E_PARAMETER2 field contains the number of the attribute (G3E_ANO) that contains the second circuit/feeder name.   |  
|  SourceFeature  |  The feature or features that are the primary source for the analysis. This is typically the breaker feature but can be the substation transformer. The G3E_PARAMETER1 field is the G3E_FNO. If specified, the G3E_PARAMETER2 field is the attribute number (G3E_ANO) of the attribute that contains the circuit name (source feature name). The attribute specification supports the extraction option to query by circuit name. If omitted, the circuit one and two fields from the connectivity table are used to find the candidate source features. You can specify multiple source features.   |  
|  Substation  |  The feature that defines the substation and supports the extract option to locate a substation and all of the source features owned by the substation. The G3E_PARAMETER1 field is the G3E_FNO. G3E_PARAMETER2 is Null.   |

Combination with G3E_FEATOBJID is unique.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |

Foreign key to [G3E_ANALYSISPARAMTYPES.G3E_VALUETYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ilPvbADUnqRH3~NiQkpP0Q).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (3)  |   |

Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |

##### G3E_LDPROIFACE (LD-Pro Interface Table)

###### G3E_LDPROIFACE.G3E_TYPE Values
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Feature Extract  |  Points to the supporting metadata table containing names of the component views to extract for feature reference. The design area instance of a job plus the percentage specified in G3E_PARAMETER1 determine the size of the area to extract for the views listed in the supporting metadata table.   |  
|  Land Extract  |  Points to the supporting metadata table containing names of the component views to extract for land or backdrop reference. The design area instance of a job plus the percentage specified in G3E_PARAMETER1 determine the size of the area to extract for the views listed in the supporting metadata table.   |  
|  OutputFileName  |  The MicroStation output file name. This file is placed in a job-named subfolder of the OutputLocation parameter. This value applies only to the IGDS format.   |  
|  OutputFormat  |  The output format for the FME translator. These values are case sensitive. The valid values are MapInfo® and IGDS.   |  
|  OutputLocation  |  Identifies where the extracted files are output. This can either be 'Registry=<registry key>' where the contents of the key identifies the folder location. Or, it can be 'Directory=<folder path>' where the path identifies where the files are placed. The name of the work order (jobTable) is specified as a subfolder of this location.   |  
|  LDProExecutable  |  The name of the LD-Pro executable with path information. This can either be 'Registry=<registry key>' where the contents of the key identifies the LDPro executable with location information. Or it can be 'Directory=<folder path>' where the path identifies where the executable resides.   |  
|  SeedFile  |  The location of the seed file for the MicroStation output format. This value applies only to the IGDS format.   |  
|  CellLibrary  |  The name of the cell file for the MicroStation output format. The NetWorks Core symbols are output as cells. This value applies only to the IGDS format.   |  
|  Style  |  Points to the supporting metadata table containing style mapping of NetWorks Core styles and the output format styles.   |  
|  PaperScale  |  The scale to use when calculating element size and widths. If not specified, the coordinate system paper scale in the database is used.   |

### G3E_AREAMGR (Area Manager Table)
Table name: G3E_AREAMGR 
Contains information necessary for the area management function. This table lists the area feature tables that Area Manager can use to store area information. Area Explorer also uses this table to provide its read-only view of area features.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Unique row for this format and the identification of the feature class(es) for which this interface can manage areas.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_IDENTIFIERANO  |  Identifies which field in the area feature table is considered the unique area ID for the table. Normally, this is the G3E_FID field, but if the area data was imported from another system, it can be an artificial ID. All attributes populated by the Area Manager command must be contained in the same component.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LINKANO  |  To help storing area hierarchies, identifies which field in the area feature table is used to point to a parent of an area feature to help storing area hierarchies. If, for an instance of an area, the value of the field is Null, the area is displayed in the root of the area tree. Otherwise, it is displayed as a child of the area whose G3E_IDENTIFIERANO is referenced by the link column.  This field must be in the same component as G3E_IDENTIFIERANO.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_TYPEANO  |  The field in the area feature table used to store the user- selected type or classification for an instance of an area. In an area hierarchy, the types might be Region, State, and County. This attribute must include a picklist definition of valid types.  This field must be in the same component as G3E_IDENTIFIERANO.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_NAMEANO  |  The field in the area feature table used to store the user- entered name for an instance of an area.  This field must be in the same component as G3E_IDENTIFIERANO.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCATIONANO  |  The field in the area feature table that specifies the location identifier when an instance of this area feature is set as the active area of interest. If this value is Null, it is ignored by the command and no AOI Location Identifier (AOILI) is set.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_ATTRIBUTE (Attribute Properties Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTE 
This table contains a row for every attribute in each component and component view that is manipulated by the NetWorks Core client software. The attribute property information provides additional description and control not enabled by the database. Information in this table is used in the system for these reasons: 
  * To enhance the display of information in dialog boxes.
  * To enable more intelligent processing in software components like the Find command, the functional interfaces, and model validation. 


You need an entry in this table for any field in a component with a database default that needs to be presented to the user. This includes values you want to present on the dialog box tabs and values such as text alignment from the component's alignment field. 
The attribute can be a field on a component defined in G3E_CNO or a field on a component view defined in G3E_VNO. You cannot use the G3E_CNO and G3E_VNO fields at the same time, nor can they both be empty.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ANO  |  Identifier for the attribute definition  |  No  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component number. The associated table can be retrieved from G3E_COMPONENT. This value must be Null if G3E_VNO is set.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_VNO  |  Component view number. The associated table or view can be retrieved from [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw).  To allow the user to perform ad hoc attribute filter queries in the Display Control for this component view, populate a row for each field in the view. To provide a picklist on the Filter dialog box, populate the G3E_PNO field, as well.  This value must be Null if G3E_CNO is set.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  
 |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FIELD  |  Field you are describing in the table associated with the component. This is the physical name of the column in the database. There should only be one entry in this table for a given G3E_CNO/G3E_FIELD or G3E_VNO/G3E_FIELD combination.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the field. This name appears in the property dialog boxes.  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FORMAT  |  Specifies how the [value](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/dc7vaYweQMJvMTl8GkE9_Q) contained in the field should be displayed or interpreted   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_PRECISION  |  The number of decimal places to display for numeric data. It is used in all numeric formats except General Number.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DOMAINTABLE  |  Legitimate values for this field. If a picklist is specified in the property dialog box, it overrides the use of the domain table. Domain tables do not appear automatically as picklists. You must create a picklist definition for this table and reference it either in the G3E_PNO field or on the tab attribute.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_DOMAINFIELD  |  Field containing the values that appear in the property dialog box drop-down lists. This is the actual value in the attribute field. If special filtering or key reference is required, define a picklist. If specified, model validation verifies the attribute's value is in this list.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_REQUIRED  |  Indicates if the attribute must be entered—required before post  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FINO  |  Denotes if an attribute value is provided by some mechanism other than user input or triggers processing of other attributes. This is the name of the ProgID of the object to perform the operation. As a new row is created, the Placement/Edit command calls the defined interface so that the program can populate this value. The Edit command also processes these attributes passing information to the function indicating a feature edit.  The G3E_FUNCTIONALORDINAL and G3E_FUNCTIONALTYPE fields are used in conjunction with this field to control the firing of the interface software. So, for a given component, the set of [functional interfaces](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/V3R13AOaIqDt48GFIejEkg) are retrieved and ordered as specified. Based on the [functional interface types](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2vg~r4cpGZUP0cam_lMlPA), the following behavior is evident:  Component edit also occurs when the feature is edited. All interfaces defined for a component are fired on the Edit or Update method. Only the one specifically associated to the attribute is fired on SetValue.  A help context identifier is not associated with the functional interface. These are typically background processes that do not interact with the user. Those that do interact present dialog boxes. The dialog boxes themselves can receive the F1 input and process their own help request.  This field is a key into the [G3E_FUNCTIONALINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0aEQqZ6jM5KfJzxNSY6S5w) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

|  G3E_FUNCTIONALTYPE  |  Indicates the timing of execution for the functional interface program. The possible values are AddNew, Edit, Update, or SetValue. During an edit, only these specifications apply: Edit, Update, or SetValue. AddNew applies any time a new component occurrence is generated.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  An array of variants containing arguments for the functional interface. The object automatically passes the feature component recordset and a variant containing arguments. These arguments are additional specifications from the DBA. Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |

Relationships between features, however, are controlled through the appropriate relationship definition. This specification is appropriate for references to non-feature tables within the database.  Foreign key tables do not appear automatically as picklists. You must create a picklist definition for this table and then reference it either in the G3E_PNO field or on the tab attribute. A field cannot be defined to have both a domain and a foreign key reference. Because picklists are not automatically created for foreign key or domain tables, this field definition is ignored unless you have specified a G3E_TABATTRIBUTE.G3E_FIELDVALUEFILTER for this attribute. If the flag is set to Yes (1), the component is copied from the original feature to the new feature. Then the attributes are reviewed. If this flag is set to Yes (1), the attribute is not copied. Any database default is picked up for the attribute.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

If this value is Null, the software determines a best fit by calculating the width of the field descriptions. You can approximate the width as a more familiar measurement unit as follows:  A screen-independent unit to ensure that the proportion of screen elements are the same on all display systems. A twip is defined as being 1/1440 of an inch.  One pixel contains approximately 15 twips. On Microsoft Windows-based machines, there are approximately 96 pixels per logical inch. |  G3E_WRAPTEXT  |  Indicates whether the attribute's WrapText property presents wrapped text on the [horizontal grid](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255991?tocId=DAbXd_mERK3FbWaGcZJfJw). It turns line wrapping on and off for text presentation, not text entry. You can set G3E_WRAPTEXT to Yes or No.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255991?tocId=DAbXd_mERK3FbWaGcZJfJw) Yes (1)—presents wrapped text; wrapping occurs before words that would otherwise be partially displayed. The wrap point does not exist as a line break in the data, and the presentation with wrapping does not change the data. You must build that into your business rules.  0 = The attribute does not have a unique constraint on the related table. 1 = The attribute has a unique constraint on the related table.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |

### G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION (Component View Composition Table)

#### G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION.G3E_FIELDS Format
When G3E_FIELDS is left blank, the resulting recordset used for display is defaulted to contain all the input fields for that particular component. G3E_FIELDS is used so the software can apply the style and label rules for presentation of dynamics while drawing or editing a feature component. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265346) These two formats are easily distinguishable because the second token begins with an alphabetic character for an input-field name and a non-alphabetic character for a hard-coded value. 
Format for input-field name
Alias
The field alias specified in the Oracle view for the component view. If no alias is used, this is the same as the input-field name. 
Input-field name 
The name of the input field being pulled from the graphic component table or attribute component table. 
ANO 
Acts as a flag to determine if the field participates in codelist logic or relationships and as the actual attribute to be used in the traversal. This value is zero if the field does not participate in codelist logic or relationships. 
Format for hard-coded value
Alias 
The field alias specified in the Oracle for the component view.
Hard-coded value
The hard-coded value has the following format for the various types. The characters must be localized. 
Integers
Begin with a digit, a plus sign, or a minus sign. The token does not contain a decimal point. 
Doubles 
Begin with a digit, a plus sign, a minus sign, or a decimal point. The token contains a decimal point. 
Dates
Begin and end with the pound sign #. The date is between the two pound signs. No localized dates use the pound sign. 
Strings
Begin and end with an equal sign =. The required string is located between the two equal signs. If an equal sign is required in the string itself, the embedded equal sign must be preceded by a backward slash \\.

### G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION (Component View Definitions Table)
Table name: G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION 
Contains the rules used to generate the display cache. You use the database tools to define the views. This list of data are used to feed into the legend Display Control commands. 
A [component view is defined](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VPnAdb8GziKP4NU7jimaVw) for graphic components to enable the organization of data in the display cache. Data are published in the display cache for efficiency of indexing and retrieval. The granularity of display groups—component views—enables efficient visualization of the data set (quick on/off capability).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  G3E_VIEW  |  The view name in the SQL statement that creates the view. Example SQL> create view <ViewName> as select <G3E keys and required columns> from ComponentTable1 C1, ComponentTable2 C2 where C1.G3E_FID=C2.G3E_FID;   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  The feature with which the view is associated. Include only one feature class in a view definition. With [synthesized components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BHztsPXCkqRWc8ufJn_Dkg), the data can be retrieved from multiple features.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component within the feature with which this view is associated. You can specify only one component with the view. A view must have a one- to-one correspondence with a graphic component as associated with a particular feature. This component need not be part of the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT list for a synthesized component view. See the description of [synthesized components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BHztsPXCkqRWc8ufJn_Dkg) for certain extensions.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/255993?tocId=FrXfQBwG3PSFRds3hV2VRw) The combination of G3E_FNO and G3E_CNO must be unique within the table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LENO  |  Legend entry identifier in [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) that should be used to construct a legend entry for a query. This provides the appropriate style rule information. It is also used for default style information during placement.  If the field is Null, the proper style rule is not applied during placement, and metadata validation raises an error.  For synthesized views, check if the style rule can be obtained from the legend entry of another component view.   |  Yes  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

 |  Example For a component view defined as SELECT A.G3E_GEOMETRY A.OPENCLOSED FROM A WHERE OPENCLOSED = 'OPEN', this flag must be set to Yes (1).   |  
| --- |  
Because most component views are not defined using the value of an attribute to determine membership, this column is generally set to No (0). 
|  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

### G3E_DATACONNECTION (Data Connections Table)

### G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT (Feature-Component Relationship Table)

#### G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_CCNO Values
When you set the CCNO, you must also set certain fields in this table as described below. The G3E_REPEATING field in this table is ignored. Set these fields to Null:
G3E_CNO
G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT
G3E_DERIVEDFROMCNO
G3E_ALTERNATEREQUIREDCNO
G3E_GEOPROXIMITYTOLERANCE
G3E_BREAKLINEARCNO
G3E_RINO
G3E_RIARGGROUPNO
G3E_MERGEMAXDISTANCE
G3E_MERGECOMMONPRECOND
G3E_MERGEPRECOND
G3E_MERGERINO
G3E_MERGERIARGGROUPNO
Set these fields to the default value They must not be set to Null:
G3E_REFRESH
G3E_REPLACE
G3E_ALTERNATEGEOGRAPHIC
G3E_ALTERNATEGEOORDINAL
G3E_BREAKACTION
G3E_COMPONENTELIMINATION
G3E_COMPONENTASSIGNMENT
G3E_COMPONENTADJUSTMENT
Set these fields to 1. They must contain a non-zero integer value:
G3E_INSERTORDINAL
G3E_DELETEORDINAL
Populate these fields with a valid foreign key value from their corresponding foreign table:
G3E_PINO
G3E_FNO

### GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE (Coordinate System Specification Table)
Table name: GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE 
The database server and the application use this table to determine the coordinate system of the data. Use the [Define Coordinate System command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Or1aBR2d0n3BsevDKXaLSg) to populate GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE. If this table is not populated, the default coordinate system (Cylindrical Equirectangular) is used. See Intergraph.[GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) for more information.

|  CSGUID  |  The GUID of this coordinate system. The server is responsible for setting this to a new valid GUID when a record is added. If clients can persist this value (depending on the value of CSGUIDTYPE), the server must update the CSGUID when the coordinate system values are modified (because the coordinate system is no longer the same).  The GUID is of the form {12340001-4980- 1920-6788- 123456789012}. Valid values are Null or a GUID.   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (38)  |   |

### Land Management Tables

## Dynamic Metadata Edits

### G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY (Command Dependency Table)
Table name: G3E_COMMANDDEPENDENCY 
Contains information necessary to support dynamic metadata edits. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) for publishing. The table is used to define how each command or logical functional area uses the optimized table definitions. Because metadata is managed only in the default language, the functional group names are not localized. The contents of this table are provided by Hexagon. Do not add records to this table or delete records from it.

### G3E_OPTABLESET (Optimized Table Sets Table)
Table name: G3E_OPTABLESET

### G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY (Attribute Query Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY 
Contains information necessary for the Attribute Query command. This table is referenced in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_AQNO  |  Attribute query number. Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the query as it appears in query type combo box in the command  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Explanation of the query operation  |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_SQL  |  The [SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=JUGhmbMqNrvahOyoce06Tg) SELECT statement, including the substitution parameters. Substitution parameters are always indicated by question marks (?). You must explicitly include all the columns you want in the result set. You cannot include the SDO_GEOMETRY column, nor can you specify SELECT * in your query. If you use aliases, they must contain only underbar and alphanumeric characters.  Occasionally, you might use an Oracle query that is extremely complicated, such as when you are composing SQL for queries and finds. If you are having problems running a complicated query, Hexagon suggests one of the following solutions: 
  * Put the query into an Oracle view, which is used in the SQL statement.
  * Add the query as code in a PL/SQL procedure, which is called from inside the SQL statement.

  
 |  Example SQL> select G3E_FNO, G3E_FID from GC_MANHL where GC_MANHL.route = ? and GC_MANHL.number = ?   |  
| --- |  
If the SQL is marked for AOI processing, it is modified before being issued to the database. NetWorks Core software converts the query into a join on the [AOIQUERYRESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yBNbOEGUr6KKiCjros7_vw) table. It also appends queries to add detail features to the result set. It then issues the resulting query to the database. 
NetWorks Core can process specialized removable [optional parameters](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/YeiChl92c~QRq7zCYa_8Sw) in the SQL. 
Numeric values in the SQL should be language independent. Always use a period as a decimal separator. For instance, in the case of “N.DIAMETER > 10.3”, the “10.3” should always be specified with the period, never with “10,3” in any locale. 
This field can be Null to support a requirement to provide spatial processing output as input to custom user reports. If no G3E_SQL is provided, either G3E_AOI or G3E_AOILI must be set to 1 (True). 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=JUGhmbMqNrvahOyoce06Tg) If the number of parameters (question mark placeholders) in the statement does not match the number of attributes defined for the query, the software may yield unexpected results, including possibly getting into an infinite loop. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=JUGhmbMqNrvahOyoce06Tg) Because SQL Server 2012 and 2014 do not support TRIM, use RTRIM and/or LTRIM in statements in the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_SQL and G3E_FINDQUICK.G3E_SQL columns for Field Review. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=JUGhmbMqNrvahOyoce06Tg) The SQL statement must return G3E_FNO and G3E_FID. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257481?tocId=JUGhmbMqNrvahOyoce06Tg) Because the results of the query go through xml special characters are limited to hyphen, underscore, and period in column aliases. 
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_AOILI  |  Indicates whether an AOI Location Identifier is required to execute this predefined query.  0 = An AOI Location Identifier is not required. 1 = An AOI Location Identifier is required.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_AOI  |  Indicates whether an AOI is required to execute this predefined query. Each query that has this flag set must have each feature class found by the query listed in [G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/IPzFsM76U2_yKiAgpL06cQ) table. This is necessary to optimize the performance of simple attribute queries when an AOI is applied.  0 = An AOI is not required. 1 = An AOI is required.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The specific type of simple query is available to the user that has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_APPLICATION  |  Contains the bit mask value representing the product combination. Each product with the bit enabled in the mask will show the query on the list of available queries.  1 = Designer only  2 = NetViewer only  4 = Field Review only  8 = Portal only  16 = Mobile only  To make the query available in multiple products, merge the bitmap masks of individual products. For example, if you configure a query with mask 9 (8+1), it will be available in the Portal application and in the Designer application.  If you specify a query as being in the NetViewer application, then it is not visible in Designer. You must configure the G3E_NETPAGES to include the query in NetViewer or Field Review.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_FINDCOMPATTRIBUTE (Find Component Attributes Table)
Table name: G3E_FINDCOMPATTRIBUTE 
Supports the Find Component command associated with the [Find](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eibHzMS7HpF1oSe8Du2j1Q) command. The Find Component command looks at entries in this table. If no entries are found in this table to match one of the find component operations, all of the attributes of the specified components are used. If at least one entry exists in this supporting table, only the attributes listed for a query are used in the user interface for the Find command.

### G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING (Simple Query Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING 
Identifies the features that might be found by each query. This is necessary for correctly processing the query. Simple query is the only user of this table.

|  G3E_FNO  |  A valid feature number for an attribute query number. If the query returns multiple features, you should have one row for each feature referencing the same G3E_AQNO value.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TABLEALIAS  |  The table or alias name for an attribute query. This is the table or query used for the FNO in the Select list. Example The G3E_SQL statement in G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_SQL reads as follows: SQL > select C.G3E_FID, C.JOB_PLACE_NAME, C.LOCATION, FEATURE_N.VOLTAGE, FEATURE_N.PHASE from COMMON_N C, FEATURE_N <Do not alias where C.G3E_FID=FEATURE_N.G3E_FID.... If these tables are defined in the G3E_SIMPLEQUERYMAPPING table, the G3E_TABLEALIAS for the COMMON_N table is C and the G3E_TABLEALIAS for the FEATURE_N table is FEATURE_N  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### Map Output

#### G3E_COLORSCHEME (Color Scheme)
Table name: G3E_COLORSCHEME 
Contains a set of predefined colors to form a scheme that can be used by the Map Output control to provide the color and fill color overrides. Within the same scheme, the Color and Fill Color parameters need not be synchronized. You can define fewer fill color values than color values. However, the software cycles through the fill color definitions more frequently than the color definitions. If G3E_TYPE = 'Fill Color' and G3E_COLOR for that ordinal is Null, then the fill type is considered to be 'Transparency'.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_CSNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_GROUPNO  |  The group number.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Allows the RGB values to be grouped under a single type. These are the valid values: Color Fill Color  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_COLOR  |  The RGB value that defines either the Color or Fill Color.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The order in which the color scheme should be used within a particular group. This value must be unique for a given combination of G3E_GROUPNO and G3E_TYPE.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

#### G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUP (Color Scheme Group Table)
Table name: G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUP 
Contains the group number and group name for the particular color scheme group which allows a cycle or rotating set of colors to be used each time the trace is executed. The user can distinguish the results of traces that start at different features or perhaps use different attribute criteria.

|  G3E_GROUPNAME  |  The group name.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

The user can distinguish the results of traces that start at different features or perhaps use different attribute criteria.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  G3E_COLOR  |  The RGB value for the color override. If this value is Null, the Map Output control uses the next color in the given group defined by G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO field. If no color scheme exists under the given group, the Map Output control uses the default color override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILLCOLOR  |  The RGB value for the fill color override. If this value is Null, the Map Output control uses the next fill color in the given group defined by G3E_COLORSCHEMEGROUPNO field. If no fill color scheme exists under the given group, the Map Output control uses the default fill color override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |

If the value of G3E_COLOR, G3E_FILLCOLOR, and this field is Null, the Map Output control uses the default color and fill color overrides.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LINEWEIGHT  |  The line weight override. If this field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the default line weight override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |   |  
|  G3E_TRANSLUCENCY  |  The default translucency for the MapOutputControl’s translucency override combo box. The legal values can be from 0 to 100, -1, or Null. Null is interpreted to mean no override. A value of 0 means that the feature being drawn is opaque. Nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the feature being drawn is invisible. Everything behind it is visible.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |

Null is interpreted to mean no override. A value of 0 means that the interior area of the area feature being drawn is opaque. Nothing is visible behind it. A value of 100 means that the interior area of the area feature being drawn is invisible. Everything is visible behind it.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (3,0)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_STROKEPATTERN  |  The stroke pattern ID from the G3E_NORMALIZEDSTROKE table. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing pattern of the line style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_POINTSIZE  |  The point size override. If this field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the default point size override.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,2)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_FONTNAME  |  The symbol font name which is selected from the list of fonts installed in the machine. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing symbol font name of the point style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (40)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_SYMBOL  |  The symbol character (Unicode character from 33 to 255) which is selected from the list of characters for a particular symbol font name. If the field is Null, the Map Output Control uses the existing symbol of the point style on which the trace/query is executed   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (1)  |  Null  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  ![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257473?tocId=EJ6BjA505SvApdFaFkHSYQ) The translucency overrides apply to the same parts of the style as the colors, [with the exception of hatches](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257473?tocId=EJ6BjA505SvApdFaFkHSYQ). 
  * The normal color and translucency overrides apply to all parts of all styles that are not area fills. 
  * The fill color and translucency overrides apply to only area fills.
  * The hatches are an exception to this. The hatches get their override color from the normal button, but their override translucency from the fill drop-down list.

### Post Processing

#### G3E_POSTMAPPING (Post Process Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_POSTMAPPING 
Defines the post processing that can be used by specific queries to prevent query and/or trace results from being sent to a post process that cannot process them or to prevent incorrect trace contents from being used as input to the post process. While the metadata is defined to allow any query to be used as input, the user interface only exposes trace results to post processing. 
The Metadata subsystem uses this mapping table to provide a list of all post processes that can be used by a particular query or type of query operation.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PPMNO  |  Row identifier for the table..  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PPNO  |  Identifier of the report from G3E_POSTPROCESS.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_QNO  |  The number of the attribute query or trace that can use this post process. Foreign key to [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_AQNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw) or [G3E_TRACE.G3E_ID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg). If the value is Null, the information is available for all traces based on the G3E_TYPE specification. This field should only be populated when G3E_TYPE is Attribute or Trace.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPE  |  Post process type. It also indicates to which table the previous key maps. 1 = Attribute 2 = Trace 3 = Spatial 4 = SelectSet 5 = AdhocAttribute 28 = SavedQuery. Includes attribute, spatial, ad hoc. 29 = ReviewFeatureAllocation. Minimize the number of reports displayed in the Report Selection control of Review Feature Allocation command  30 = Report. Minimize the number of reports displayed in the post-process control of Review Feature Allocation command and the Generic Map Output report.   |  30  |  No  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. The specific type of post process is available to the user who has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

#### G3E_FINDQUICK (Quick Reference Find Table)
Table name: G3E_FINDQUICK 
Contains information necessary to support [Quick Reference Find](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SgekrGq__JC7N5L2OYpoEg). An entry must exist in [G3E_FINDMETHOD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~yh_nP3UzVZyGCMF8WCpQg) for the table and its optimized table to include this metadata in the published cache.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FQNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the predefined query that appears in the Quick Reference Find dialog box.   |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_SQL  |  The [SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256628?tocId=u5BKDMTJIq12tqWxjhCn1A) statement with substitution parameters. The Order By clause is not supported in Quick Reference Find.  Occasionally, you might use an Oracle query that is extremely complicated, such as when you are composing SQL for queries and finds. If you are having problems running a complicated query, Hexagon suggests one of the following solutions: 
  * Put the query into an Oracle view, which is used in the SQL statement.
  * Add the query as code in a PL/SQL procedure, which is called from inside the SQL statement.

Substitution parameters must be indicated by question marks (?). ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256628?tocId=u5BKDMTJIq12tqWxjhCn1A) If the number of parameters (question mark placeholders) in the statement does not match the number of attributes defined for the query, the software may yield unexpected results, including possibly getting into an infinite loop.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256628?tocId=u5BKDMTJIq12tqWxjhCn1A) Because SQL Server 2012 and 2014 do not support TRIM, use RTRIM and/or LTRIM in statements in the G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_SQL and G3E_FINDQUICK.G3E_SQL columns for Field Review.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256628?tocId=u5BKDMTJIq12tqWxjhCn1A) The SQL statement must return G3E_FNO and G3E_FID.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256628?tocId=u5BKDMTJIq12tqWxjhCn1A) Because the results of the query go through xml special characters are limited to hyphen, underscore, and period in column aliases.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_AOILI  |  Flag to indicate if an AOI Location Indicator is required to execute this Quick Reference Find.  0 = An AOI Location Indicator is not required to execute this Quick Reference Find. 1 = An AOI Location Indicator is required to execute this Quick Reference Find.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role that the user must have to enable the object control. If the user has the role, the specific type would be displayed on the Quick Reference Find dialog box.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  VarChar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  G3E_APPLICATION  |  Contains the bit mask value representing the product combination. Each product with the bit enabled in the mask will show the query on the list of available queries.  1 = Designer only  2 = NetViewer only  4 = Field Review only  8 = Portal only  16 = Mobile only  To make the query available in multiple products, merge the bitmap masks of individual products. For example, if you configure a query with mask 9 (8+1), it will be available in the Portal application and in the Designer application.  If you specify a query as being in the NetViewer application, then it is not visible in Designer. You must configure the G3E_NETPAGES to include the query in NetViewer or Field Review.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  1  |

### Schematics

#### G3E_PORT (Schematic Symbol Ports Table)
Table name: G3E_PORT 
Supports the [Schematic Generator service](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTSchematicGeneratorService.htm). This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table. G3E_PORT contains metadata to override the implied ports on a schematic symbol. By default, a schematic symbol contains only one port that is positioned in the center of the symbol. Through this port, you can make connections both into and out of the symbol. This table defines the ports, the position of each port on the symbol, the directions in which connections can be made, and the number of connections that can be made to the port. 
The [G3E_PORTDEFINITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3GqB0DMMCvo_X6OpxUXI0w) table associates a name to a set of port definitions defined in this table. The [G3E_POINTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KkSHDKALPAaJHyESmRqk9Q) table associates a port definition to a style and thus to the symbol used by that style. The position of the port is described as a percentage of the size of the symbol with the center being (0,0) as displayed in the following diagram: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=wI5pK7brPC2ZYDXUBFDdOw)
You can define a branch side and width for the port to indicate that connected features branch at equal spacing in and/or out along a specific side of the symbol. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=wI5pK7brPC2ZYDXUBFDdOw)
The branch side value can be Bottom, Top, Left, Right, or Any with values of 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. A value of 5 (Any) indicates that the port can occur on any of the four sides of the symbol and is determined by the [schematic layout processing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/f2jHhdF~mp9WhGbQCpRlhg). 
The width value indicates the width of the port as a percentage of the size of the symbol to a maximum of 200 percent. 
This diagram shows a port with a width percentage of 100.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=wI5pK7brPC2ZYDXUBFDdOw)
This diagram shows a port with a width percentage of 200.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/256753?tocId=wI5pK7brPC2ZYDXUBFDdOw)
Schematic symbol ports need to be defined only for features that are encountered in schematic generation traces. Port definitions for schematics are like the hot spots that can be defined for the [Connectivity PickQuick](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VfbJLUnk4lGa5XMUeX83Jw) dialog box. Schematic port definitions differ from these hot spots in that they also define the type and number of connections.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_PROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PDNO  |  The port definition number to which this port belongs.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_PORT  |  The identifier of the port number for this port definition. This is an arbitrary number; however, numbering ports from 1-n is recommended.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONX  |  The percentage in the x direction of the port. Must be between -100 and +100.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONY  |  The percentage in the y direction of the port. Must be between -100 and +100.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |   |

#### G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION (Schematic Definition Table)
Table name: G3E_SCHEMATICDEFINITION 
Contains metadata to define symbology schemes for rendering features in a schematic window. You can define several different types of schematics, and each schematic type could need different symbology to make them unique. This table is used to give a name to each set of schematic metadata. You must define at least one set to use the GTSchematicGeneratorService. This table is referenced in the [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw) table.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SDNO  |  The schematic definition number.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  The schematic definition name.  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  The role associated with the inclusion of this schematic.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are used within the application. This information is provided by the DBA and is not defaulted.   |  No  |  Yes  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

#### G3E_SCHEMATICSYMBOLOGY (Schematic Symbology Definition Table)

##### Label Position Values
0 = On entity Center 
1 = On Entity Left
2 = On Entity Right
4 = Above Center
5 = Above Left
6 = Above Right
8 = Below Center
9 = Below Left
10 = Below Right
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265761)
In the following diagram, point feature X is the feature being labeled, and ABC is the label. The label (ABC) is positioned at the Above Right (position 6) of the feature (X). Label alignment of this point feature is Below Left. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265761)
In the following diagram, label ABC is also positioned at Above Right of the linear (edge) feature. Label alignment on the edge feature is Below Left. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265761)
The labels on both features are offset. Offset is defined as the minimum whitespace value plus, for edges, ½ the line weight. Labels are also adjusted so that the [text reads correctly](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ggFaiKt9NqW~WksePI7QZg).

### Trace Tables

#### G3E_TRACE (Trace Table)

##### Use these Legacy Filters when Upgrading Databases
When upgrading databases, use these legacy filters.  
|  Value  |  Definition  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  If all of the following are true: 
  * The filter uses picklist attribute substitution
  * Any hard-coded values in the filter are in human-readable GUI values (not that database values) 
  * The database does not store the human-readable GUI values

These traces have probably been used for the Designer/Analyst, not the Viewer products.   |  
|  1  | 
  * For those traces that do use picklist attribution substitution and the hard-coded values in the filters reflect the database values (not the human-readable GUI values). These traces have probably been used in the Viewer products, not the Designer/Analyst. 

 |  
| 
  * For those traces that have no filters. This field has no affect on these traces, but if you add filters to these existing traces, write them with picklist key substitution (not value substitution). 

 |  
| 
  * For those traces that have no picklist attribution substitution involved in any of their filters. This field has no affect on these traces, but if you add picklist attribute substitution to these existing traces, write them with picklist key substitution (not value substitution). 

 |  
| 
  * For those traces that use picklist attribution substitution, and the database values are the same as the human-readable GUI values. This field has no affect on these traces, but if you add non-same picklist attribute substitution, write them with picklist key substitution (not value substitution). 

 |  
| 
  * For those traces that have a mixture of hard-coded values that reflect the human-readable GUI values, as well as the database values, the criteria themselves should be rewritten to use the database values. 

 |

#### G3E_TRACEADDCOLTYPES (Trace Additional Columns Types Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEADDCOLTYPES 
Defines the different types of additional column definitions that can be specified for the traces. Also provides referential integrity for the [G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rCfScaS0GVxKHwguY94sfw) table so that the user cannot specify non-supported additional column types. 
The following additional column types are supported:
  * For seed feature. These additional column definitions are used when populating the seed feature in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table. Additional column definitions of this type in the G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table cannot reference any rows from the TRACERESULT table (contain a column with the tr table alias). They may only reference columns from the Connectivity table using the conn table alias. 
  * For features other than the seed. These additional column definitions are used when populating all traced features other than the seed in the TRACERESULT table. Additional column definitions of this type in the G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table can reference any rows from the TRACERESULT or Connectivity table by using the tr and conn table aliases respectively. 

  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_ADDCOLUMNTYPE  |  Internal identifier for the additional column type.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (5)  |   |  
|  G3E_DESCRIPTION  |  Description of the additional column type.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (40)  |   |

#### G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS (Trace Additional Result Columns Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEADDCOLUMNS 
Maps user-defined columns in the [TRACERESULT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/rEIilX75Id0H0dKOTllwFA) table to the SQL expressions defining their source values. The G3E_TRACEADDCOLSPERTRACE table specifies which of these columns should be populated in the TRACERESULT table for each trace defined in the [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg) table. Since these additional columns may not be populated by all traces, the columns must be defined either to allow Null values or to have default values. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257984?tocId=Enc5AFdKL6zAf4DZYMvJcw) This table is not published but is accessed by the trace procedure at runtime. The table must be replicated for field use and as such must appear in the analysis lists.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TRACNO  |  An internal identifier used to define a particular user- defined column on the TRACERESULT table and the source of its value   |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_ADDITIONALCOLUMN  |  Name of the user- defined column on the TRACERESULT table  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEEXPR  |  SQL expression that defines the value to be set for the additional column during the trace operation.  Table Aliases The trace attempts to populate any additional columns specified for it. The result columns themselves do not have to be qualified; they are understood to apply to the TRACERESULT table. However, any columns in the connectivity or TRACERESULT tables used in G3E_SOURCEEXPR to specify a value for the result columns must be qualified properly. The table alias used for the TRACERESULT table is tr and the connectivity table alias is conn. Failure to qualify these columns results in an SQL parsing error.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (50)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

#### G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES (Trace Attributes Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEATTRIBUTES 
Supports attribute parameter substitution in the different criteria of the traces defined in [G3E_TRACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg). The Trace command recognizes that a substitution needs to take place and uses the attribute numbers defined in this table to determine the valid values to allow the user to choose for the substitution. This table defines which attributes should be substituted and the ordinal for the specific placeholder for which to make the substitution. 
Refer to the descriptions of the G3E_STOPCRITERIA, G3E_FILTERCRITERIA, and G3E_PATHCOST columns of the G3E_TRACE table for information on how to specify the placeholders for the attribute substitution. 
Only attributes of substitution type User are presented to the user for input. The other values are derived by the software.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_TRANO  |  Identifier for the trace attribute number.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_TNO  |  Identifier for the trace defined in the G3E_TRACE table. Foreign key to [G3E_TRACE.G3E_ID](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/trnr4poliwRg4MV7egOufg).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_ANO  |  NetWorks Core attribute number that is used in the trace definition. Foreign key to [G3E_ATTRIBUTE.G3E_ANO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7SEquKvasMNJcZ25A9H4yw).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  The placeholder for which the attribute value should be substituted  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (10)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTERTYPE  |  A specification of the filter with which this attribute is associated. These are the valid values:  FilterCriteria StopCriteria PathCost  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  FilterCriteria  |  
|  G3E_PROMPT  |  A prompt or description of what value the user is being asked to enter.  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |  Enter value  |  
|  G3E_SUBSTITUTIONTYPE  |  A specification of the handling of this attribute. User - The user is prompted to specify a value. Circuit - The value is derived by the software and applied to the appropriate filter expression. You can only specify the Circuit type if the trace is used for the Extract For Analysis commands.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (20)  |  User  |  
|  G3E_OUTPUTFIELDNAME  |  Represents the name of the field that is part of the output recordset. When this field is populated, the trace command appends the user-supplied value to the output trace result. This field name must not match any of the fields that are part of the trace result output recordset. This field is applicable only if G3E_SUBSTITUTIONTYPE = 'User'.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257907?tocId=at1yhFmF0EFSYGthOtTxeA) This field is not added to the TRACERESULT table but is part of the input recordset sent to the report or post process interface.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

#### G3E_TRACEMAPPING (Trace Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACEMAPPING 
Defines the traces that can be used by specific commands so that particular trace results are sent only to a command that can process them. A one-to-many relationship exists between the G3E_TRACE and this table where the same trace can be associated with multiple configurations.

#### G3E_TRACETYPES (Trace Types Table)
Table name: G3E_TRACETYPES

## Graphic Display Tables

### G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE (Sample Legend Definition Table)
Table name: G3E_DEFINITIONTABLE 
Contains the definition of the legend entry order for a single legend. Legends are used to populate a map window or an embedded map on a plot sheet. The actual name of this table is specified in the G3E_LEGEND table. An instance of the definition table contains the ordered list of legend entries (from the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table) to display. 
The complete legend entry is defined by joining this table and G3E_SETTINGSTABLE to the G3E_LEGENDENTRY.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_LENO  |  Number of the legend entry.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  [SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) [WHERE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) [clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) indicating the subset of instances from this component view that should actually be displayed. If no filter is wanted, this field should contain an empty string or a Null value. Do not include the word Null in the field.  Before populating this field, consider using synthesized components. They yield much better display performance. See [Create Synthesized Components (Display by Feature State Example)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bq8KPGX7I0bun0GXV1G04g).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_DISPLAYORDINAL  |  Relative position in the legend. A value of 1 has the highest priority and is drawn on the top of all other data. If duplicate values are used rather than making the value unique per table, you are not guaranteed that the order of the displayed data is constant from one metadata publish to the next. Metadata publishing uses the Oracle sorting algorithm on this column. When two values are the same, Oracle does not guarantee the order in which rows are returned. If guaranteed order is important, you must make the values unique. For some graphic elements like text nodes within the same feature, order may not be important for your display and non-unique values are acceptable.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

|  G3E_LEVEL  |  Level of item in the tree. One is a root or top level.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  Order of item in tree construction.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LEAFINDICATOR  |  Indicates if this entry is a leaf in the tree. 0 = G3E_LEGENDITEM is a not legend entry. 1 = G3E_LEGENDITEM is a legend entry.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to see this item displayed in the Display Control's user interface (tree view). A trigger on the table sets it to 'EVERYONE' if it is left Null.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |

### G3E_LABELRULE (Label Rule Table)
Table name: G3E_LABELRULE 
Manages the mapping between a label rule and the possible formats that can be returned by that rule. Also includes the filters used to choose the label format. 
Every G3E_LABELRULE entry should have a Null expression. This is effectively the default label for the feature. It should always be the last filter evaluated. This is a Null value or the empty string. Do not use the word Null.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_LRROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LRNO  |  Identifier for the label rule. The number is repeated in the table and is not actually a primary key. However, the display cache treats it as a key for grouping purposes. Referenced in the [G3E_LEGENDENTRY](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kofwLrmyr06Gi_I92qslWw) table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RULE  |  Name of the label rule.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTER  |  [SQL WHERE clause](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) based on the attributes of the associated component view definition. The successful (True) evaluation of this filter renders the text based on the format specified by the G3E_LABELINDEX property. The Null filter (catch- all case) should contain an empty string or a Null value. Any field names referenced in the filter must be in uppercase. String literals used in comparisons must be quoted. Oracle built-in functions are not supported.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |  
|  G3E_FILTERORDINAL  |  Ordinal value indicating the order that the filters should be evaluated. The filter that is most common in terms of the most associated data should be assigned a value of 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LFNO  |  Identifier associated with this particular label format from the G3E_LABEL table. The associated format is used based on a True evaluation of the filter.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_LEGEND (Legends Table)
Table name: G3E_LEGEND 
Preconfigured legends available to the NetWorks Core client. Each entry in this table corresponds to a table representing the individual legend instances. The metadata system provides storage for this information, and Metadata Explorer provides the GUI.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
