## Placement Tables

### G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION (Component Configurations Table)
Table name: G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION 
Defines chained groups of components that participate in component configurations. Component configurations let a user quickly and easily place a group of components as a single unit, for example, a grouping of several labels and a leader line used to label a feature. 
To ensure that all of the components are automatically placed, all components defined as part of a component configuration are required. If you want derived components to be placed when the component configuration is placed, you must define the derived component as part of the component configuration. This table requires an entry in [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw).   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_CCROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CCNO  |  Identifier for the set of rows in this table that comprise a component configuration.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the component configuration that appears in the user interface: On the Feature Explorer Graphic Components tab.  On the dialog displayed by the New Component command.  |  No  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Number of the feature of which this component is a part.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Number of the component included in this component configuration. The same CNO can be listed multiple times in a given component configuration. It can also occur in more than one component configuration. Metadata validation should include checking that the G3E_CNO is appropriately associated with the specified G3E_FNO.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ORDINAL  |  Specifies the order that this component is placed when this component configuration is placed.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_AUTOREPEAT  |  Denotes if a repeating component should automatically repeat during placement of a component configuration.  0 = Only one instance of the component is placed before moving on to the next component defined in the configuration.  1 = Placement loops on this component, continuing to place more and more instances, until the user presses SHIFT+ESC to move on to the next component within the configuration  Autorepeat can be set only on components marked as repeating in [G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Rjj_uDxsdrE5MNsL_z1Q5w) or [G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_REPEATING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/wv7TUo~kYJ6ZhasaVrDMXQ).  Metadata validation checks that only components marked as repeating in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT and G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION are marked as autorepeating in G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_PINO  |  Value to indicate information that controls placement of the component. This is a key into the G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE table and identifies the placement technique to be used to place this component when the configuration is being placed.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  Array of variants containing arguments for the placement technique. The technique is automatically passed the SelectSet and the current FeatureRecordset arguments that you set. Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  RAW (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_REFRESH  |  Used during feature placement and edit operations. Refresh causes the Graphic Component grid and the data grids to update. This is a Boolean value where Yes (1) indicates that a refresh should occur. These are typical occasions to set this value to Yes:  If the attribute from a graphic component is shown on a dialog tab. (This allows additions or deletions of components from other dialog tabs to be reflected on the Graphic Components tab.)  If the attribute appears on multiple dialog tabs. If the attribute participates in a style rule and consequently affects dynamics. To avoid extraneous refreshing (a performance penalty), set this property to Yes in these cases or when the addition of an attribute (or graphic) component generates a corresponding graphic (or attribute) component through a functional interface.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_SILENTRGNO  |  Number of the silent relationship group. This number is a reference into the [G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fkOOdphFCekSUjtVVUyL_Q) table for this component when this component configuration is defined to be part of a placement configuration. It allows the component configuration to automatically build a relationship without interaction from the user. It can only build a relationship to another feature in the placement configuration. The definition allows some relationships to be defined silently and others to be interactive. However, you cannot configure part of a relationship to be silent and part of a relationship to be interactive. If this value is Null, all the relationships are processed interactively. Generate a new G3E_SILENTRGNO for each FNO/CNO/FIDX combination for which relationships can be established silently.  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/260733?tocId=XtglMy3PDvX_h7IMeG2P~w) This field applies only when the component configuration is part of a placement configuration in the G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION table. It is ignored if the component configuration is part of a feature in the G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO  |  A detail component number that corresponds to the geographic G3E_CNO value in a given row. You can optionally populate G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO in rows where G3E_CNO is a geographic component. It should be NULL when G3E_CNO is a detail component.  G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO should only be populated for this reason: To specify implicit geographic versus detail component placement for the two components identified in G3E_CNO and G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO. When a geographic window is active, G3E_CNO is placed. When a detail window is active, G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO is placed.  If populated, the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO value must correspond to another row in G3E_COMPCONFIGURATION where G3E_CCNO and G3E_FNO match that of the geographic component and where G3E_CNO has the same value as the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO.  Among other things, the corresponding row defines the placement technique and parameters for placing the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO.  This row should have a G3E_ORDINAL value that is higher than the G3E_ORDINAL value of the geographic G3E_CNO.  When a G3E_CNO in one row is used as the G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO of another row, it is not automatically placed as part of the component configuration. It is placed only if a detail map window is active when the geographic row with the populated G3E_DETAILPLACEMENTCNO value is processed.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |  
|  G3E_LOCALECOMMENT  |  String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are used within the application. This information is provided by the administrator and is not defaulted.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (240)  |   |

### G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION (Placement Configurations Table)

#### G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION.G3E_CCNO Values
When setting the CCNO, the G3E_REPEATING field within this table is ignored. When setting the CCNO, the following fields within this table should be set to Null: 
  * G3E_CNO
  * G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT


When setting the CCNO, the following fields must be populated with a valid foreign key value from their corresponding foreign table: 
  * G3E_PINO
  * G3E_FNO


A component configuration can be marked as required by setting G3E_REQUIRED in this table to 1. This allows the configuration to be started automatically for placement. If G3E_REQUIRED is set to 0, this is an optional component configuration. The user must select <New> from the Active column to invoke placement of the configuration. 
Autorepeat of a component configuration is possible by setting the G3E_AUTOREPEAT field in this table to Yes (1). This allows the configuration and all the components that comprise it to be placed repeatedly, providing that all components within the configuration are marked as repeating. G3E_REPEATING must be set to Yes (1) if G3E_AUTOREPEAT is set to Yes (1) to ensure that metadata validation passes.

### G3E_TRANSFER (Transfer Unit Support Table)

#### G3E_TRANSFER.G3E_TYPE Values
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Component is the primary transfer unit; no copy is retained by the original feature. A feature can have no more than one primary transfer unit.   |  
|  2  |  The component should also be transferred with the primary component. Component is a secondary transfer unit that is associated to the component where G3E_TYPE = 1 or 3. However, it does not appear on the user interface. If one or more subordinate or secondary components are to be transferred, then the G3E_KEYFIELD must be populated for all of the components. No copy is retained by the original feature.   |  
|  3  |  Same as 1, but a copy is retained by the original feature.  |  
|  4  |  Same as 2, but a copy is retained by the original feature. There can only be one component within a feature that is either a 1 or a 3.   |

## Relationship Tables

### G3E_ADD_RELATIONSHIP_PARAMS (Additional Relationship Parameters Table)

#### Parameters for Many-to-Many Ownership Related to Duct Management
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>-InfrastructureNodeEdgeConnectivity   |  Node-edge connectivity relationship that exists between the infrastructure features like conduit, manhole, and passage connectors.   |  
|  <RNO>-DuctAssignmentANO   |  Assignment attribute of the duct feature, which is used to match duct assignments to resolve ambiguities.   |  
|  <RNO>-InnerDuctAssignmentANO   |  Assignment attribute of the inner duct feature which is used to match duct assignments to resolve ambiguities.   |  
|  <RNO>-LocateGeoSectionTolerance   |  Tolerance to use when searching for geo sections of the broken feature near the end of an infrastructure path whenever a detail reference feature is not present.   |

#### Parameters for Node-Edge Connectivity
Prefix the parameters for node-edge connectivity with the G3E_RNO value from G3E_RELATIONSHIP so that multiple models can have different characteristics. The values required by node-edge connectivity are as follows:   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>-NodeEdgeConnectivitySequence  |  Name of the sequence for generating node numbers for this RNO.  |  
|  <RNO>-Node1_ID   |  Name of the column that contains the node 1 value in the published view.  |  
|  <RNO>-Node2_ID   |  Name of the column that contains the node 2 value in the published view.  |  
|  <RNO>-MaximumNumberOfNodes   |  Maximum number of nodes per feature for this RNO.  |  
|  <RNO>-PipelineConnectivity   |  Indicates a rule that limits the connections at nodes to two features per node number. Because the existence of this parameter enforces the rule, the parameter's value is not important.   |  
|  <RNO>-end pointValidationPriority   |  Priority to display when encountering the error in which the wrong endpoint of a linear is used to connect to a related device. Because P5 is set as the default, this parameter is not required.   |  
If your model contains more than one NodeEdgeConnectivity relationship and node numbers are to be published, the same feature cannot participate in more than one NodeEdgeConnectivity relationship. If the same feature participates in two or more NodeEdgeConnectivity relationships, the node values written to the DDC collide. If you need a feature like this in your model, you must name the columns containing the node values differently between the two relationships.

#### Parameters for Node-Ordered Connectivity
Prefix the parameters for node-ordered connectivity with the G3E_RNO value from G3E_RELATIONSHIP so that multiple connectivity models can have different characteristics. The values required by node-ordered connectivity are as follows:   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>-InputIdentifier   |  Name of the column in the connectivity table that contains the node 1 value (Input G3E_FID).   |  
|  <RNO>-InputFeatureNumber   |  Name of the column in the connectivity table that contains the G3E_FNO of the input identifier. The trace procedure writes this value out to the TRACERESULT table.   |  
|  <RNO>-OutputIdentifier   |  Name of the column in the connectivity table that contains the node 2 value (Output G3E_FID).   |  
|  <RNO>-OutputFeatureNumber   |  Name of the column in the connectivity table that contains the G3E_FNO of the output identifier. The trace procedure writes this value out to the TRACERESULT table.   |  
|  <RNO>-ReverseField   |  Name of the column in the connectivity table that contains the reverse direction indicator.  |  
|  <RNO>-ReverseValue   |  The value stored in <RNO> - ReverseField for the feature when it is reverse fed. This should be R.   |  
|  <RNO>-ForwardValue   |  The value stored in <RNO> - ReverseField for the feature when it is forward fed. This should be F.   |

#### Parameters for Ownership
The parameters for the Ownership must be prefixed by the G3E_RNO value from G3E_RELATIONSHIP.  
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <RNO>-MaximumLocatedObjects  |  The Maximum locatedObjectCollection count to display on the PickQuick dialog.  |

### G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION (Relationship Attribute Validation and Copy Table)
Table name: G3E_ATTRIBUTEVALIDATION 
Contains rules for attribute validation.  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_AVNO  |  Key associated with this validation row.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVEFNO  |  Feature number of the feature being placed or validated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVEANO  |  Attribute number of the feature being placed or validated.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDFNO  |  Feature number of the feature to which the active feature is being related. The candidate feature.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDANO  |  Attribute number of the feature to which the active feature is being related.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPERATOR  |  Operator that defines the type of validation to be performed. This value should be Null if the interface does not need further specification. If the value of G3E_VINO is Null for this row, one of the [legal relational](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5~KO3Xd1dc9bIaicqthjuA) or simple algorithm operators should be used for validation (simple validation). If G3E_VINO is not Null, this value triggers specific validation operations internal to the given interface. Use specialized function operators such as Phase and CircuitNumber when G3E_VINO is not Null.  These are the simple algorithm operators: EitherOr — Compares the active feature's attribute value to the validation value specified or, if no validation value is specified, compares it to the related feature's attribute value. A match in either case passes validation.  InSetEitherOr — Compares the active feature's attribute value to a range of validation values as specified in G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE.  RelatedNotEqualTo — Indicates [exclusion of a candidate](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/~sTq6BQTYdrbngf8Q~WGyQ) based on a set of attribute values and is considered when G3E_VINO is Null, G3E_OPERATIONTYPE = 1, and G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE is not Null. When this operator is detected, the software compares the attribute specified by G3E_RELATEDANO to the value or values specified in G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE, which can contain more than one value delimited by a semicolon (;). The attribute being validated needs to be part of the triggering component's published view.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_OPERATIONTYPE  |  Value that defines the operation to be performed: 1 = Validation  
2 = Copy  
3 = Validate and copy   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_VINO  |  Number of the specialized validation interface. If simple validation is to be used, this column should be Null.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_VALIDATIONVALUE  |  The value validation checks for during processing. This string can contain numerical information or range information. This value can be Null if the row in question is being used for an operation that does not require a validation value, such as CircuitNumber copy.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACEARGUMENT  |  If the G3E_VINO value is populated for this row, this column contains binary large object (blob) data that is sent to the relationship attribute interface for this ANO combination. The contents of this blob are a variant array of variants. These variants are parsed in the function called through the interface. Not all techniques require [additional arguments](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GwhfuMU_SR9gkPE_ULIEkQ).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Raw (2000)  |   |  
|  G3E_MOUSEMOVECANDIDATEFILTER  |  Boolean indicating if the attribute should be checked during mouse move or only during the click operation. If the attribute is only checked during mouse move, the G3E_RELATEDANO can reference a component view attribute. If it references a component attribute, the attribute in the view must have the same name as the attribute in the component.  1 = The attribute should be checked during mouse move 0 = The attribute should be checked only during the click operation  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE  |  The G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_TYPE value associated with the relationship upon which the validation operation should be performed. If Null, this field is checked on all relationships.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_PRIORITY  |  Error priority to be returned for a validation error.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (10)  |  P1  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP (Many-to-Many Ownership Relationship Table) (Sample)

#### ChildByNodeEdge
When a child feature participating in a many-to-many ownership relationship is broken, you can configure the relationship to be reestablished based on the connectivity of the containing features or owners, for example, the conduit network containing cables. NetWorks Core [makes several assumptions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5qc_gOoYeZMTTEX8YRRIlg) about this ownership model when ChildByNodeEdge is configured for use. 
In general, when a contained feature is broken, the container features are retrieved and sorted based on their node-edge connectivity. Using this network and related information and the spatial distance from the contained (child) feature to the container (parent) feature, NetWorks Core attempts to reallocate each of the broken child (contained) features to the appropriate parents. NetWorks Core also handles the case where the contained feature is graphically present in a detail window, as in the case of a cable in a manhole. The connectivity of the manhole to the conduit is additional information used to sort out the allocation. 
Example  
|  Example Conduit A connects to a Manhole A1 and to Manhole A2. Add Conduit C that connects Manhole A2 to Manhole A3. Cable D passes through Conduits A and C, passing through Manholes A1, A2, and A3. The cable is broken in the detail belonging to Manhole A2. If ChildByNodeEdge is configured, NetWorks Core can determine that one portion of the cable is to be allocated to Conduit A, and the other to Conduit C if the cable has a cable section present in each manhole. Otherwise, NetWorks Core cannot determine the proper allocation and marks the ownership as ambiguous. If the conduits contain ducts, and the cable is contained in a duct, and the duct graphics are drawn in the manhole, then ChildByProximity should be used to allow the allocation of the cable to be resolved.  If the conduits contain ducts, and the cable is contained in a duct, and the duct graphics are drawn in the manhole, use ChildByProximity to resolve the allocation of the cable.   |  
| --- |

#### ChildByProximity
When a child feature participating in many-to-many ownership is broken, the relationship is reestablished based on geographic proximity.In general, if the relationship service cannot decide unambiguously, the relationship is established with both the original and the copy feature.   
|  Example Feature A is broken into A1 and A2. Feature A was originally related by many-to-many ownership to feature B.  In the following cases, within tolerance means within the tolerance used to establish the relationship during placement. Matching triggering component means the pairing of triggering components in the G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP table, and the two components are in the same detail drawing, or both are in geo.  Using these example features, the following cases (not mutually exclusive) can occur: The software can find no matching pair of triggering components for B and A1. Ambiguous case, because the software has nothing on which to base a spatial comparison. The software relates B to A1. (The reasoning is that A1 is what is left of the original feature A, and B was related to A in the beginning. But with nothing on which to base a spatial comparison, the software cannot tell if feature B should remain related to A1 or not.) If you have a repair feature configured in your model, the software automatically places a repair flag.  The software can find no matching pair of triggering components for B and A2. This case is ambiguous because the software has nothing on which to base a spatial comparison. Relate B to A2. If you have a repair feature configured in your model, the software automatically places a repair flag.  If both of the preceding cases are true, feature B is related to both features A1 and A2. If only one of the cases is true, feature B may end up being related to either or both, depending on what happens with the following cases: 
  * For each pair of matching triggering components of features B and A1, the software checks the distance between those components. 
  * If at least one pair falls within tolerance, the software relates B to A1. (This should be the normal case, because B was originally related to A. The exceptions occur because either the user moved a component with relationship processing turned off, or the related the features through Feature Explorer or Feature Allocation.) 
  * If no pair falls within tolerance, the software removes the relationship between B and A1, in hopes that the processing for B and A2 results in a relationship. The processing strategy is like reestablish, where the geo proximity rules apply. If one of the features resulting from break is not close enough, the feature does not establish a relationship. 
  * The software repeats the previous case for features B and A2 with the same choices.
  * If any of the preceding results completely orphans feature B (that is, B is related to neither of A1 nor A2), the software relates B to both A1 and A2. If you have a repair feature configured in your model, the software automatically places a repair flag. 

 |  
| --- |

#### Example Merge and Break Metadata for Communications Data Models
|  <Parent>  |  <Child>  |  G3E_PARENTMERGEALLOW  |  G3E_CHILDMERGEALLOW  |  G3E_MERGEBEHAVIOR  |  G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR  |  G3E_DELETE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Conduit  |  Formation  |  3  |  3  |  3  |  3  |  1  |  
|  Conduit  |  Cable  |  2  |  1  |  1  |  2  |  3  |  
|  Formation  |  Duct  |  1  |  3  |  1  |  3  |  1  |  
|  Duct  |  Cable  |  1  |  1  |  1  |  2  |  3  |  
Merge of conduits is allowed if the model has matching subtrees with formations in the root (thus formation is the structural child of the conduit). The other values in G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR indicate that the duct is a structural child of the formation and the cable is a content child for the duct. After the merge, the tree is deleted, where formation is related to the second conduit is in the root. 
Looking at G3E_DELETE for formation-duct and duct-cable, the duct children of the deleted formation are also deleted, and the cable children of the deleted ducts are orphaned. However, these cables are owned by multiple ducts (certainly by the ownership hierarchy of the first conduit being merged). Therefore they lose one parent relationship. Set G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR = 3 for the conduit- formation relationship, so that when a conduit is broken, the tree of child features with formations in the root is duplicated and assigned to the new conduit. 
Furthermore, merge of conduits is allowed if both conduits being merged directly own the same cables (you do not want to create a situation when the cable leaves a conduit somewhere along). Hypothetical merge of formations (they are not typical linear features) is allowed if both are owned by the same conduit. There is no restriction on the owned ducts. If two formations are merged, they are still owned by the same conduit, and the resulting formation owns ducts previously owned by the two merged formations. 
Hypothetical merge of ducts (they are not typical linear features) is allowed if owned by the same formation. There is no restriction on the owned cables. If two ducts are merged, they ware still owned by the same formation, and the resulting duct owns cables previously owned by the two merged ducts. 
The merge of cables is always allowed with respect to the owners. After the merge, the resulting cable inherits the owners of the two merged cables (the two merged cables might run through several ducts and conduits, and the resulting cable runs through the union of those ducts and conduits).

#### G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP.G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR Values
[You can define](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TPZC3LMqS7HcyxkFNRJbmw) what should happen to the child feature if the parent feature is broken (duplicated) into two new features. You can also define what should happen to the parent feature when a child feature is broken. 
The G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR field is a bitwise OR of the constants for the parent feature and the constants for the child feature. 
These are the values when a parent feature is duplicated as a result of a break:  
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Do nothing  |  The child feature remains owned by the original parent but not the copy of the parent generated because of the break.   |  
|  Duplicate (3)  |  The child feature stays related to the original parent feature. A copy of the child feature is made, and the copy of the child features is related to the copy of the parent and not to the original parent.   
When the child feature is being copied, the parameter G3E_COMPONENTELIMINATION, as defined for components of the child feature in G3E_FEATURECOMPONENT, is honored.   |  
|  RelateNew (2)  |  Relate to new. The child feature is owned by both the original parent and by the copy of the parent that was generated because of the break.   |  
|  Undefined (0)  |  Reestablish the Many-To-Many ownership relationships on the original and copy features based on the geographic proximity. The result is geographically correct established relationships to the original and the copied feature (only the existing relationships are assigned to the two features; no new relationships are established).   |  
These are the options when a child feature is broken:  
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  [ChildByNodeEdge (16)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/aPX48dtDA0TmVg0MRUiWNg)  |  Indicates that the relationship should be resolved to allocate the original or copy cable to the ducts, inner ducts, or conduits. Using a value of 16 leaves 4 bits available for the parent-to-child choices.   |  
|  [ChildByProximity (0)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/DbHuuGttD6U9Fjoqo~oBwQ)  |  Indicates that the child-to-parent relationship should be resolved using spatial proximity between the child and its parents.   |  
Considering the values above, these are the valid values for the G3E_MANYOWNERSHIP.G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR field:   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Reestablish children based on geographic proximity when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on geographic proximity when breaking a child.   |  
|  1  |  Do nothing for children when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on geographic proximity when breaking a child.   |  
|  2  |  Relate children to new when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on geographic proximity when breaking a child.   |  
|  3  |  Duplicate children when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on geographic proximity when breaking a child.   |  
|  16  |  Reestablish children based on geographic proximity when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on node-edge connectivity when breaking a child.   |  
|  17  |  Do nothing for children when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on node- edge connectivity when breaking a child.   |  
|  18  |  Relate children to new when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on node- edge connectivity when breaking a child.   |  
|  19  |  Duplicate children when breaking a parent, and allocate parents based on node-edge connectivity when breaking a child.   |  
Processing recurs if you choose the Duplicate option for related children.  
|  Example An instance of feature A is broken. Feature A owns feature B. Feature B owns feature C.  If the relationship specifies Duplicate for G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR between A and B, the software makes a copy of the B instance.  Original feature B is owned by original feature A. The new copy of B is owned by the new instance of feature A.  Further, original feature B owns an instance of feature C. The software duplicates feature C, and the copy of feature C is owned to the copy of feature B.  If feature C owns any features, the software repeats this behavior. This implies that there must be no cycles in a relationship that specifies Duplicate as its G3E_BREAKBEHAVIOR.   |  
| --- |

### G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY (Node-Edge Connectivity Relationship Table) (Sample)
Table name: G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY 
The G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY table describes which feature pairs may be connected using the node-edge connectivity relationship. The semantics of this relationship requires two columns named NODE1_ID and NODE2_ID to store the node identifiers. Connectivity is maintained through database relationships and may or may not involve graphic coincidence. The [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) table specifies the component that carries the connectivity information. 
A not null or zero value in the node identifier fields in the instance data indicates the feature is not connected. Each pair of connectible features must have two rows in this table. That is, if feature 3 can connect to feature 7, a row defining that feature 7 can connect to feature 3 must also exist.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  Feature being placed or the active feature in an edit operation  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CONNECTINGFNO  |  Feature to which the source feature can connect  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_TRIGGERINGCNO  |  Component in the source feature that initiates the relationship software  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ENFORCEMENT  |  Indicates if connectivity is required or optional. Optional indicates that the G3E_SOURCEFNO can be placed and posted without connectivity.  0 = Connectivity is optional. A warning appears if features are improperly connected. 1 = Connectivity is required. An error appears if features are improperly connected. 5 = Connectivity is optional. A warning message does not appear if features are improperly connected.  Relationships that have the same G3E_SOURCEFNO value must have the same G3E_ENFORCEMENT value. For example, features that have a G3E_SOURCEFNO value of 301 must all have the same G3E_ENFORCEMENT value (of either 0, 1, or 5).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_BREAKLINEAR  |  Determines whether the source feature breaks linear features during connection 0 = Does not break linear features during connection. 1 = Breaks linear features during connection.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_SOURCECONNECTINGNODE  |  An integer value representing the node number to connect to for the corresponding device. Allowable values in the node columns are either a positive integer, or - 1, or Null. A positive integer signifies a node to connect to for the corresponding device. A Null value signifies that the user must make a choice in the connection such as which end of a switch to connect a primary conductor to. A -1 is a placeholder for linears (Null is acceptable). Linears acquire their appropriate node number based on the endpoint proximity to the connection. A value of -1 means that node values from metadata are ignored for this device (a linear).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

Allowable values in the node columns are either a positive integer, or - 1, or Null. A positive integer signifies a node to connect to for the corresponding device. A Null signifies that the user must make a choice in the connection such as which end of a switch to connect a primary conductor to. A -1 is a placeholder for linears (Null is acceptable). Linears acquire their appropriate node number based on the endpoint proximity to the connection. A value of -1 simply means that node values from metadata are ignored for this device (a linear).   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CONNECTINGTRIGGERINGCNO  |  An integer value representing the G3E_CNO value of the component in the connecting feature that triggers the relationship. This value filters which components can participate in connectivity and allows the software the opportunity to avoid highlighting components of features that do not participate in any relationship.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_MAXOFFSET  |  Used in relationship validation, the maximum allowable offset that is valid for this pair of features in this relationship. This value is also used in the creation of a tolerance square to be used in placement. This tolerance square is the area around a relationship point that the user can interactively place a feature and still maintain a relationship with related features.  A maximum offset may not be needed for a given feature relationship. For instance, the user may want the ability to move a related feature with no restraints as to relationship validity. ### G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY (Node-Ordered Connectivity Relationship Table) (Sample)
Table name: G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY 
The G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY table contains information necessary for the node-ordered connectivity relationship. It is modeled on node-edge connectivity. This relationship is modeled by storing information for each edge that identifies the node to which each end of that edge is connected. The G3E_FNO and G3E_FID for the node are stored at each end. A G3E_FNO and G3E_FID of zero indicates that the corresponding end of the linear feature is not connected. Both the FID and FNO are zero or both are not zero. Any other data combination is invalid. 
For a given pair of features that can be connected in the model, there are two rows in this table, with each feature in the pair having its G3E_FNO in the G3E_SOURCEFNO field. Exactly one of those features must have the component (specified as G3E_SUPPORTCNO in [G3E_RELATIONSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)) used to represent connectivity. The feature that has that component is regarded as the two node device; the feature that does not have the component is regarded as a single-node device. Another way to look at this is from a node-edge graph view: the feature with the support component is an edge, and the feature without the component is a node. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259102?tocId=vdHE0fxK47GVvoHSvVFJwQ) G3E_NODEORDCONNECTIVITY does not have a G3E_ENFORCEMENT field. Connectivity is always enforced during validation.

|  G3E_CONNECTINGTRIGGERINGCNO  |  An integer value representing the G3E_CNO value of the component in the connecting feature that triggers the relationship. Used to filter which components can participate in connectivity. Allows the software the opportunity to avoid highlighting components of features that do not participate in any relationship.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

Because only point features can break linears, this value should be 0 for area and linear features.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |

In this case, the value of G3E_MAXOFFSET would be set to -1.00.  The G3E_MAXOFFSET can be a whole or fractional number of database units, for example, feet, meters, and so forth, that matches the projected coordinate system of your data.  When G3E_MAXOFFSET is set, it should be the same or greater than AverageSymbolSize in the [G3E_GENERALPARAMETER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ) table.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  - 1.00  |

### G3E_OWNERSHIP (Ownership Relationship Table) (Sample)

#### G3E_DELETE Values
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Delete child when deleting the parent  
When the parent is deleted all children with value of 1 are deleted along with the parent.   |  
|  2  |  Re-own the child feature to another parent feature if the current parent is deleted  
The parent feature is deleted, and the child tries to locate some other parent feature. If the child features finds another parent feature, a new relationship is established between the child and the found parent.   |  
|  3  |  Orphan the child feature if the current parent is deleted.  
The parent feature is deleted, and the child does not try to establish relationship with some other parent.   |  
|  4  |  Refuse to delete the parent if this child exists  
Do not delete the parent feature as long as any child having this value (4) exists.   |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/265582) When a parent is moved or the geometry changed in some way, the relationship software revalidates and reestablishes relationships. While a child feature is not deleted during an edit, it might be orphaned if it no longer meets the proximity validation rules for the relationship.

### G3E_POSTBREAKMAPPING (Post Break Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_POSTBREAKMAPPING 
Describes the post break operations that should be executed when the specified feature-component is broken. Multiple post break operations can be performed and are executed in ascending order of the G3E_ORDINAL. In addition to the Post Break relation interface, this table contains the references to the relation interface for the types Compute Marker Location, Compute Geo Point, Create Marker, Custom Plot, and Loop Makeup. These additional entries are not executed during the break operation, but allow you to associate arguments to these interface types.

Based on the processing performed by Compute Marker Location, this interface projects a point in the geographic map when the result from Compute Marker Location is within a detail. The interface generates a record that is added to the input recordset.  .NET Host Class – ComputeGeoPoint  |  
|  Compute Marker Location  |  Used by the OTDR report object to determine the appropriate points on each cable. These points represent the marker location that is used later for placing the marker symbol.   |  
|  Compute Partial Start Length  |  These objects are used by the Trace command to calculate a value representing a part of the seed feature. The value is based on a selected point and can represent the partial length.   |  
|  Create Marker  |  Used by the OTDR report object to actually create the geometry representing the marker and to display it on the map.  .NET Host Class – CreateMarker  |  
|  Custom Plot  |  Used by Plotting to customize aspects of the plot. Typical usage is to adjust elements of the plot in response to changes in the size of the plot sheet or to accommodate different paper sizes or output devices.  .NET Host Class – CustomPlot  |  
|  Disable Edit Tool  |  Used by the Edit Geometry command to allow you to disable operations that are enabled by the command.  Used by the Edit Tool command to allow you to disable buttons on the Edit Tool control that are enabled by the command.  .NET Host Class – DisableEditTool  |  
|  Feature Validation  |  Used by the feature placement command to allow you to write your own custom feature validation methods.  .NET Host Class – FeatureValidation  |  
|  Foreign Key Query  |  Common interface point where users can get the current value of a selected attribute, replace it with a new value based on queries against the foreign or domain table (or foreign system data), add new rows, or edit attributes in other components based on the current value of the selected attribute, such as compatible unit.   |  
|  Loop Makeup  |  Used by the Temporary Loop Makeup utilities to allow you to customize the loop makeup reports.  .NET Host Class – LoopMakeup  |  
|  Merge Features  |  Used by the relationships services when called from the Merge command. It lets the relationship perform special processing during feature merges.   |  
|  Post Break  |  PFIface.PostBreakCableLengths PFIface.PostBreakAdjustByRatio  |  
|  Relationship Geometry  |  GTRGI.HigherToLowerLevelAreaRGI GTRGI.LowerToHigherLevelAreaRGI GTRGI.EdgeAreaRGI GTRGI.AreaEdgeRGI GTRGI.NodeEdgeRGI GTRGI.EdgeNodeRGI  |  
|  Temporary Geometry  |  Used by the Temporary Geometry Placement command to construct transient or temporary geometry. This geometry is useful in creating construction lines or guides for placing facility data relative to other features.  .NET Host Class – TemporaryGeometry  |

### G3E_RELATIONSHIP (Relationship Table)

#### G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS Values for Many-to-Many Ownership
You can set several parameters in the G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_ADDITIONALPARAMETERS to control the functionality of the many-to-many ownership software. Separate the arguments with commas.   
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CandidatesViaEntireGeometry  |  Picks up candidates that are not near to any of the vertices but touch the geometry of the feature. Relationship service does this after the component placement is finished, on relationship validation, and on reestablish.   |  
|  ManyToOne  |  Enforces one-to-many in ManyToOne mode. The relationship only allows establishing relationship with one related feature for the active feature. This means that when the software has multiple relationship candidates, the user is asked to select only one feature to which to establish a relationship. If there is one relationship already established, no other candidate is highlighted.  When reestablishing relationships, the original relationship is dropped and a new one replaces it. This ManyToOne constraint is weak, and it can easily be violated during placement. However, it is enforced by validation. Relationship validation returns an error in case there is more than one related feature connected to the active feature.   |  
|  Parent=  |  Provides a way for user- defined (possibly localized) relationship point naming for the parent type feature. Use the string following "parent=" for naming the parent relationship points.   
 |  Example Parent=Owner  |  
| --- |  
 |  
|  Child=  |  Provides a way for user-defined (possibly localized) relationship point naming for the child type feature. Use the string following "child=" for naming the child relationship points.   
 |  Example Child=Owned  |  
| --- |  
 |

### G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY (Relationship Geometry Table)
Table name: G3E_RELATIONSHIPGEOMETRY 
Records information used in the placement and validation of related features and components and provides rules for offset placement of related features and stores attributes such as offset distances and orientations.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RGNO  |  Value associated with this relationship geometry.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDFNO  |  Feature class identifier. Feature number of the feature to be related to (owned to or connected to).   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEDCNO  |  Component class identifier. Component number of the feature to be related to (owned to or connected to). The geometric relationship is based on this component.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCEFNO  |  Feature class identifier of the feature to be related to the feature in G3E_RELATEDFNO. This is the active feature, either in placement or the one being edited.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SOURCECNO  |  Component class identifier of the feature to be related to the CNO above. This is the component in the active feature.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA  |  Determines whether the G3E_POSITIONDELTA value should be used (along with the vector of the related feature) or whether the G3E_XDELTA and G3E_YDELTA should be used to offset the active geometry from the closest endpoint (if linear) or the point (if the related feature is a point).  0 = The software uses the G3E_X and Y DELTA values. 1 = The software uses G3E_POSITIONDELTA value.  
 |  Example
  * You can project all transformers 10m off of the end of a primary conductor by setting the G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA to Yes (1) and the G3E_POSITIONDELTA to 10. 
  * If you always want transformers to be a given X,Y away from a pole, you can set the G3E_USEPOSITIONDELTA to No (0) and then set the G3E_X and Y DELTA values to the appropriate offset. 

 |  
| --- |  
|  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_POSITIONDELTA  |  The offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used only when there is a vector to use in calculating the relationship position, as when placing a transformer adjacent to a primary conductor. The vector for a point oriented component is based on the orientation.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |  0  |  
|  G3E_XDELTA  |  The X offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used when the relationship does not provide a vector for use in the offset calculation, as when placing a light on a pole.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_YDELTA  |  The Y offset distance that the feature to be related should be placed from the feature to relate to. Used when the relationship does not provide a vector for use in the offset calculation, as when placing a light on a pole.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_ORIENTATION  |  The orientation a feature should take when being placed coincident to a given feature. This value is given in decimal degrees. Application of the value is based on the Boolean G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION. If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is Yes (1), the value given in the G3E_ORIENTATION column should be applied to the related feature as is (G3E_ORIENTATION + 0 degrees). If the If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is No (0), the value given in the G3E_ORIENTATION column should be added to the vector of the feature to be related to. This new angle of rotation should be applied to the source feature. If G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION is Null, this field value is ignored.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number  |   |  
|  G3E_HORIZONORIENTATION  |  Determines whether this feature should be oriented in relation to the horizon or to its related feature. If the value is Null, do not do any orientation adjustment to the geometry even if the position is adjusted based on G3E_POSITIONDELTA.  0 = Orient to the related feature. 1 = Orient to the horizon.  |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FORCEPARALLELTO  |  Determines whether this feature should be placed parallel to the related feature from the nearest point regardless of its proximity to an endpoint.  0 = Offset based on proximity to endpoint (normal operation). 1 = Offset parallel to the related feature. If G3E_FORCEPARALLELTO is Yes (1), the feature is placed parallel to the related feature from the nearest point. A snap is done to the related linear to find the nearest coincident point of the related linear, and the new feature is placed parallel to the feature from that coincident point.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_FORCEPROJECTFROM  |  Determines whether this feature should be projected from the nearest endpoint on the related feature regardless of its proximity to an endpoint.  0 = The behavior of the geometry adjustment is controlled by the other parameters. 1 = Project from the nearest endpoint on the related feature even if the point identifying the related feature is not near the endpoint.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_PROJECTINTERIOR  |  Determines whether this feature should be projected interior to the related feature from the nearest endpoint. For example, this Boolean could be used to force a fuse to be placed back onto the primary conductor to which it is related.  0 = Offset from endpoint based on X and Y deltas or PositionDelta and related vector (normal operation).  1 = Project interior from the nearest endpoint on the related feature. This value is only for endpoint placement, not for active features placed on interior segments.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ALIGNMENT  |  Used in placement, this integer determines the alignment point for the active feature in relation to the related feature. A value of -1 in this field indicates that the alignment should not be changed.  This column should contain a value from the set 0-10. The values should correspond to one of the [valid values](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Nvd43rB_pYWjjXs_AJY5wg).  You must have an alignment field in the geometry table for storing this value. The default field name is G3E_ALIGNMENT if not specified in the [G3E_COMPONENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw) table.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIGHTREADINGANGLE  |  Used in placement, this value determines if the symbol should have the right-reading angle adjustment applied after processing the geometry adjustment. This field cannot be Null.  0 = Indicates no adjustment. 1 = Indicates adjustment.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_RINO  |  An index into the [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) table defining the custom interface to be used. This field must match a value in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_RINO. The type of the relation interface must be Relationship Geometry.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO  |  The group number of the arguments to the relationship geometry interface (if any) specified in G3E_RINO. This field should be Null if the custom object requires no arguments. If the field is not Null, this value must match one of the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) values.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATIONSHIPTYPE  |  The [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) value associated with the relationship upon which this validation operation should be performed. If Null, this field is checked on all relationships.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Varchar2 (30)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING (Relationship-to-Feature Mapping Table)
Table name: G3E_RELATIONSHIPMAPPING 
Maps which feature participates in which relationships as the active feature.
A child feature is the active feature in "child to parent" relationship, and a parent feature is the active feature in "parent to child" relationship. The other feature (the parent feature defined for a "child to parent" relationship, for example) does not have a row in this table. 
The content of this table answers the question: If I have this feature, which relationships do I have to run for it?   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_RMNO  |  Row identifier for the table..  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  Identifier of the relationship from [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA)  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Feature that participates in this relationship as the active feature.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_CNO  |  Component of the feature that initiates the relationship software. This value is pulled from the column specified by the relationship as the triggering component.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

### G3E_RELPARAMS (Relationship Parameters Types Table)
Table name: G3E_RELPARAMS

This table should be prepopulated by the product center. ### G3E_REPAIRIFACE (Repair Indication Interface Table)

#### G3E_REPAIRIFACE.G3E_TYPE Values
A string indicating the information stored in this row. The following types of information are supported:   
|  Repair Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Repair Flag Feature  |  Parameters specifying the feature to use to flag needed repairs. G3E_PARAMETER1 is the FNO of the feature and G3E_PARAMETER2 is the ANO of the text attribute for repair description information. If these parameters are not specified, BreakLinearService does not attempt to place a feature to flag relationship problems.   |  
|  Repair Offsets  |  Repair Offsets identifies the supporting table for positioning the repair feature. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  Repair Relationship  |  Specifies the G3E_RNO of the relationship to establish between the repair feature and the features resulting from the break. Only ownership and many-to-many ownership are supported. The RNO specified here determines whether the repair feature is a parent or a child feature. If this parameter is not specified, no relationship is established. You must specify both the Repair Relationship and the Repair Flag Feature parameters.   |

### G3E_REPAIROFFSET (Repair Offsets Table)
Table name: G3E_REPAIROFFSET 
For each structure, identify the offset (X,Y) for the repair feature from each break feature. You must still make the appropriate ownership entries in [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) (or other such table) for the repair feature. 
If a linear feature has both geographic and detail components that can be broken, you must list both of those components in the G3E_CNO column of this table. For the geographic component, make an entry in this table for each geographic component of the repair feature that you want placed when the geographic component is broken. For the detail component, make an entry in this table for each detail component of the repair feature that you want placed when the detail component is broken.

### G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP (Silent Relationship Group Table)
Table name: G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP 
Describes the parameters to the SilentEstablish method on the relationship services. It allows a placement configuration to preconfigure the relationship to avoid prompting the user during the configuration construction. 
When processing each component in the placement configuration, the placement software checks for a non-null G3E_SILENTRGNO in the placement configuration optimized table. If the placement software finds a non-null value, it queries the [G3E_SILENTRELATIONSHIP_OPTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jd5ouYu2f3o91r5e2JQGiA) looking for rows that match the current RNO and silent relationship group for each of the relationships associated with the component: 
  * If no rows are returned, the relationship processes using the Establish method.
  * If rows are returned, placement calls SilentEstablish to establish relationships.


Either Establish or SilentEstablish is called for a particular relationship for a particular feature instance. For linear or polygon components, after the first point is placed the software checks for returned rows. If SilentEstablish should be called, the software can skip processing on the endpoint. When multiple rows are returned for a group/relationship combination, Relationships are silently established for each row.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_SRROWNO  |  Row identifier for the table.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_SILENTRGNO  |  Identifier for the set of rows in the silent relationship table that comprise the relationship parameters for a particular FNO/CNO/FIDX combination.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RNO  |  Number of the relationship that these parameters apply to.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ACTIVECONNECTPTINDICATOR  |  Represents the connection point in the active feature (the one being placed) that should be set silently. For the node- edge connectivity relationship, this is the node number to set represented by the number 1 or 2. For the ownership relationship, this is the first (1) or second (2) parent attribute when processing a child. When processing a parent, the value is 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATECONNECTPTINDICATOR  |  Represents the connection point in the related feature (the one identified by G3E_RELATEFNO and G3E_RELATEFEATUREINDEX) that should be set silently. For the node- edge connectivity relationship, this is the node number to set represented by the number 1 or 2. For the ownership relationship, this is the first (1) or second (2) parent attribute when processing a child. When processing a parent, the value is 1.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEFNO  |  Number of the related feature included in this configuration that should build a relationship with the active feature.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number (5,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RELATEFEATUREINDEX  |  Index number of the related feature included in this configuration that should build a relationship with the active feature.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (5,0)  |   |

### G3E_STATIONING (Stationing Relationship Information Table)

#### G3E_STATIONING.G3E_CHARACTERISTIC Values
Indicates the stationing characteristic of the feature class. Valid characteristics (as metadata contstants) are as follows:   
|  Value Name  |  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  StationSeries  |  1  |  FNO is the Station Series feature  |  
|  PointInflection  |  2  |  FNO is the Point of Inflection feature  |  
|  Branch  |  3  |  FNO is a Branch Connection feature  |  
|  RangeEvent  |  4  |  FNO is a Range Event feature  |  
|  PipelineFacility  |  5  |  FNO is a Pipeline facility It excludes 1,2,4 but includes 3. It must be set to distinguish from, for example, structures.   |  
|  Length  |  6  |  If set on an FNO, the length cannot be 0 (for BMS to equal EMS). Used in validation.  |  
|  OverlapItself  |  7  |  If it is set on a feature, instances of that Range Eventfeature CAN overlap other instances of the same feature. Used in placement and validation.   |  
|  Crossstn  |  8  |  Applies only to Range Events. If not set on an FNO, the placement technique should prompt only for station series (not BSS and ESS). Used in validation.   |  
|  NoLength  |  9  |  If set on an FNO, the length must be 0 (BMS must equal EMS). Used in validation.  |  
|  Arc  |  10  |  The geometry of a feature instance of this FNO must be an Arc (Kummer- Elbow).  |  
|  Enforcement  |  11  |  The stationing columns of the stationing component of a feature instance of this FNO MUST be populated. This is not flagged until post. Not currently used, reserved for future use.   |  
|  RangeEventUnBreakableByTranslateState  |  18  |  A feature instance of this FNO is a Range Event, and it is not to be broken into multiple Range Events if a subsection of the pipeline facilities that it spans is translated to a new state.   |  
|  OverlapOthers  |  19  |  Applies only to Pipeline Facilities. If it is set on a feature, instances of that feature CAN overlap other instances of other features. It is used in placement and validation.   |  
|  NotOnPipeline  |  20  |  Applies only to Range Events. If it is set on a feature, that feature can be placed off (or coincident to) the pipeline. Features with this characteristic are not automatically moved when moving a PI.   |

### G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND (Custom Command Table)

#### G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND.G3E_COMMANDCLASS Values
These values are valid only for modeless commands.  
|  Hex Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  These commands do not listen to map view events. For example, New Job and Print are commands that do not listen to map views.   |  
|  1  |  Tracker commands receive events from the map view or views but do not participate in view collisions. That is, they are assumed to simply track/report on mouse events such as precision coordinates, but not do any transaction based on them. They continue running even when placement and edit commands are running. For example, Feature Explorer and Precision Coordinates are tracker commands.   |  
|  4  |  Edit commands manipulate data and require a database transaction. For example, Move and Delete are edit commands.   |  
|  5  |  The Temporary Geometry Placement command.   |  
|  6  |  Sub-view commands can interrupt another command for view manipulation. For example, Zoom Out and Pan are sub-view commands.   |  
In command processing, the command class is used to determine command priority or hierarchy in terms of interrupt ability. The following algorithm is used when attempting to start a new command: 
Attempting to start a New Command
If NewCommand is Modeless
If NewCommand.CommandClass > gmTrackerCommand (1)
For i = 1 to Number views If NewCommand wants to listen to this view 
For j = 1 To NumCommandsListening 
If NewCommand.CommandClass <= cmd(j).CommandClass 
CanQuit = Cmd(j).
CanDeactivateByID(View,NewCommand.ID) If CanQuit Then 
Start NewCommand 
Else 
Don't start NewCommand 
End If 
End If 
Next j 
End If 
Next I 
End If 
End If

|  Hex Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Command is always enabled.  |  
|  10  |  Enable command if an active job (writable connection) exists.  |  
|  20  |  Active plot window.  |  
|  40  |  Enable command if a map view, or activated map view, is active.  |  
|  400  |  Enable command if a Development connection is open.  |  
|  800  |  Enable command if an active work space is open.  |  
|  2000  |  Enable command if a NetWorks Core connection is open.   |  
|  10000  |  Enable command if a map view is active.  |  
|  40000  |  Enable command if the select set count is exactly 1.  |  
|  80000  |  Enable command if the select set count is 1 or more.  |  
|  100000  |  Enable command if the feature count is exactly 1.  |  
|  200000  |  Enable command if select set criteria is checked.  |  
|  800000  |  Enable command if a new transaction is available to begin.  |  
|  1000000  |  Active detail window.  |  
|  4000000  |  Enable command if a raster image is attached.  |

### G3E_FEATUREIMPORT (Feature Import Interface Table)

#### G3E_FEATUREIMPORT.G3E_FILETYPE
This is the file type format:
Description1 | filter1 | description2 | filter
Where DescriptionN is a text string indicating the type of file. It can include the file extension filter. FilterN is the filter on the file names. Each description and filter must be paired. Each pair must be separated by a vertical bar or pipe (|) symbol. In the filter parameters, multiple extensions must be separated by a semicolon. Do not use a terminating semicolon.   
|  Example All Files (*.*)|*.*|Text Files (*.txt)|*.txt|Batch Files (*.bat; *.prl)|*.bat;*.prl  |  
| --- |

### G3E_GEOMGENINTERFACE (Geometry Generation Interface Table)
Table name: G3E_GEOMGENINTERFACE 
Contains a list of the functions available to support placement operations in [duct generation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/683BYJfXgkU_aNo6BK5ZgA). Each function is effectively an automated object that supports the geometry generation interface. It is called during the creation of graphic components. 
The [Place Formation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/76EATu7MgiaMcS7PvLjl_Q) command uses geometry generators to generate the geometries of the components it creates. The geometry generators are like silent placement techniques, except that they typically use information from the attributes of the feature and the formation as a whole to compute the geometry. This table is populated in the default metadata and updated by metadata upgrade scripts, so you should typically not need to modify this table. 
NetWorks Core supports two generators: DuctPoint and FormationPoint. Use FormationPoint for all formation components and DuctPoint for all duct and innerduct components. 
When you create an empty database, this table is automatically populated with the default entries defined in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\PopulateDuctMetadata.sql script.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |

|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Descriptive name of the technique which appears in the user interface list.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (80)  |   |  
|  G3E_INTERFACE  |  ProgID of the software component to support this function. It should contain no space and begin with a letter.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (256)  |   |  
|  G3E_TYPEMASK  |  Indicator of the component type (see [G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mnr8C95rrztI1ZOL48OYBw)) values to which this technique applies.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

|  G3E_USERNAME  |  Value that determines the tooltip of the toolbar button and legend entry name.  |  Yes  |  No  |  Yes  |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2(8-0)  |   |  
|  G3E_ICONORDINAL  |  Indicates the ordinal of the icon in the [PlacementSelectionIconDRXFile](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/OQ5eJGmN8hHE5WKzX6N1fQ). The G3E_ICONORDINAL specifies the 1- based index into the icon file.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(9,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_RINO  |  Foreign key that specifies the relation interface object in G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE (Temporary Geometry Placement Interface Custom Placement Interface) to be instantiated. The type of the relation interface in [G3E_RELATIONINTERFACE.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hg0kAC7Ab1z2iY~gjbrvQA) must be Temporary Geometry.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  Yes  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_RIARGGROUPNO  |  The group number of the arguments for the Temporary Geometry Placement Interface (if any). This field should be Null if the custom object requires no arguments. If non-null, this value must match one of the [G3E_RELATIONIFACEARGS.G3E_RIARGGROUPNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BW094q8l_9y34RIrCDNtKA) values.   |  No  |  Yes  |   |  No  |  Yes*  |  Number(9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_LEGENDBEHAVIOR  |  Determines how the temporary geometries are added to the legend. 0 = Do not add any legend entry. The Temporary Geometry Placement Interface creates a legend entry. This option is useful if the legend entry should be created under any other root node than Temporary Geometries.  1 = New legend entry is created. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME> > <ordinal>, where <ordinal> is determined as the highest ordinal in this subtree placed so far + 1.  2 = Append to existing legend entry. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME>. If the legend entry exists, the newly placed geometries are appended. If the entry does not exist, it is created and the geometries are added.  3 = Replace existing legend entry. The path name of the legend entry is Temporary Geometries > <G3E_USERNAME> > <G3E_USERNAME>. If the legend entry exists, the newly placed geometries replace the existing ones. If the entry does not exist, it is created and the geometries are added.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_AUTOREPEAT  |  Determines placement behavior. 0 = The command deactivates when placement is finished 1 = Placement automatically repeats until the user presses ESC  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number(1,0)  |  0  |  
|  G3E_ROLE  |  Name of the database role the user must have to enable access to the attribute. The specific attribute is available to the user who has the role.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Varchar2 (30)  |  EVERYONE  |

### G3E_COMMIFACE (Communications Interface Table)

#### G3E_COMMIFACE.G3E_TYPE Values
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CableSectionLengthANO  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the section length attribute of the cable feature.   |  
|  CableSegmentStartANO  |  The segment start location of the cable feature.  |  
|  CountTraceFeedDirCol  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the column on the TRACERESULT table that the PROPOSED_FEED_DIR field is copied into. Traces that perform pair count filtering require the PROPOSED_FEED_DIR field from the pair count table to be copied into the TRACERESULT table during trace. This information is used by the trace post processor.   |  
|  CountTraceName  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the trace name to use when performing a trace count.   |  
|  Customer Assignment Interface  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the ProgID of the automation class that supports the Customer Assignment interface. Certain commands must retrieve this value and create the interface object to complete their tasks.   |  
|  Equipment Ownership RNO  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type indicates the relationship number that points from the parent feature down to the equipment feature.   |  
|  Equipment Owned By RNO  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type indicates the relationship number that points from the equipment feature up to the parent feature.   |  
|  FindPhoneNumber  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the feature and attributes (comma separated list with the format G3E_FNO, G3E_ANO, G3E_ANO, ...) of the feature to be queried using a phone number as the search criteria.  The G3E_ANO values specified in G3E_COMMIFACE for the Find Phone Number command map to fields with the same naming convention as the field names used in the recordset returned by the Customer Assignment interface query.   
 |  Example The Find Phone Number command specifies G3E_ANO values of 5110 and 5213. These G3E_ANO values map to the fields SWITCH_CENTRE_CLLI and OLD_ADDRESS in the tables GC_ADDRESS and GC_NETELEM. When the user types a phone number in the command's user interface, the Find Phone Number command calls the GetPhoneNum method on the Customer Assignment interface and expects the recordset returned to contain fields with these same names.   |  
| --- |  
The Customer Assignment interface queries an external database and finds specific values for the row identified by the user-supplied phone number. The command then builds SQL with a WHERE clause that uses the field names and table names identified by the G3E_ANO values and the values returned by the Customer Assignment interface, for example, WHERE switch_centre_clli = ‘OWSDON59’ AND old_address = ‘123 Main St’. The command uses this SQL to query Oracle for the feature matching these values. The Find Phone Number command displays the feature. 
If the Customer Assignment interface is not specified in metadata, the command uses the specified G3E_ANO to determine the component and field name of a feature in Oracle that is identified by the phone number supplied by the user. In this case the command expects only one G3E_ANO to be specified. 
 |  
|  InterconnectionPointFeatures  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies features that could contain cross-connected pairs. The value is a comma-delimited list of FNOs. These values are used when a loop is traced to check for potential cross connects.   |  
|  Interface Types  |  Provides a foreign key for the G3E_COMMINTERFACETYPE table, which is populated by Hexagon with values expected by the NetWorks Core. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE field.   |  
|  Location Code Field  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the location identifier attribute of a feature for various communications analysis commands such as Cable Fill, Loop Makeup, View Pairs, and Trace Count. The location identifier is used when querying the customer assignment interface.   |  
|  Longest Loop  |  The G3E_LONGESTLOOP table. This table is used by the Ripple command. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  Longest Loop Interface  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the progID of the object that processes the longest loop calculation used by the Find Longest Loop command.   |  
|  LongestLoopTraceName  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the trace name to use when performing a longest loop.   |  
|  Mobile Assignment Interface  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the ProgID of the automation class that support the assignment interface when operating under mobile/disconnected mode. The system first attempts to connect to the ProgID of the standard interface (Customer Assignment Interface). If this parameter is not present or the object cannot be created, the system fails over to this interface.   |  
|  Pair Count  |  The G3E_PAIRCOUNT table and the pair count component in the G3E_PARAMETER1 field. The pair count service automatically updates the COUNT_ANNOTATION field, if it exists, in the specified feature's primary attribute component recordset with the pair count text block. The field name must be COUNT_ANNOTATION.   |  
|  Pair Count Class  |  The G3E_PAIRCOUNTCLASS table, which the pair count service uses to identify the name of the pair classes. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  Pair Count Source  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the list of features (comma- separated list of G3E_FNO values) to be considered when looking for source feed on dependent features.   |  
|  Reverse Feed  |  The G3E_REVERSEFEED table, used by the [Change Feed](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/knD2pR_WNK4~bB3j35ffJg) command. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  Ripple  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the G3E_RIPPLE table, used by the [Ripple](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jbawKjKaBg4C1w1ooSVvdw) command.   |  
|  RippleTraceName  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the trace name to use when performing a ripple count. The type of the trace must be Trace All   |
