This table cross-references to G3E_SAPTYPE for determining the retrieval of the attribute values. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  EquipmentFeature  |  The table containing the list of features considered equipment. Equipment features must be defined as children of functional locations.   |  
|  FunctionalLocationAttributes  |  The table containing the information about the attributes to pass from GIS to SAP for functional location objects. This includes standard SAP structure attributes as well as class characteristics. This table cross-references to G3E_SAPTYPE for determining the retrieval of the attribute values. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  FunctionalLocationDescription  |  The table containing the rules for constructing the description values for each functional location object. This table cross-references to G3E_SAPTYPE for determining the retrieval of the attribute values. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  FunctionalLocationFeature  |  The table containing the list of features considered functional locations. Functional Location features must be defined as owners (parents) of equipment. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  JobModifiedAttribute  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the attribute within all features that contains the name of the job that modified this feature.   |  
|  JobPlacedAttribute  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the attribute within all features that contains the name of the job that placed this feature.   |  
|  PlanningArea  |  The planning area feature and the attribute within that feature that contains the name of the planning area. This feature must be an areal feature type. It is part of the functional location hierarchy. Each functional location is contained within one distinct area. This list in G3E_PARAMETER1 is [fno], [ano], [qualifying select]. The third parameter is a qualifying SELECT statement that must return the G3E keys of the instances within the feature that are true planning areas. This is only needed if other types of features are stored in this feature.   |  
|  SAPAllowedStates  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the list of [G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_LCNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_8zjvUTXpqWJGXxKtqBFw) state numbers that functional locations and equipment must exist in before adding to or updating SAP technical objects. This is a comma-separated list of states.   |  
|  SAPDATEFORMAT  |  Specifies an eight-character date format of the SAP system. The default is MMDDYYYY with alternative values YYYYMMDD and DDMMYYYY.  If G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null, MMDDYYYY is the default format. If G3E_PARAMETER1 is not Null, YYYYMMDD is the default. If G3E_PARAMETER1 has a fomat other than one of these three, the default is YYYYMMDD.  |  
|  SAPDATESEPARATOR  |  Specifies a single character separating month, day, and year in the SAP system. Typical values are slashes (/) or dashes (-) and must match the SAP system.  If G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null, / is the default. If G3E_PARAMETER1 is not Null and the value is more than one character, / is the default. If G3E_PARAMETER1 is not Null and the value is one character, use that character. Applicability of the characters used is not validated.   |  
|  SAPDeactivationStates  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the list of G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_LCNO state numbers that functional locations and equipment exist in when they should be dismantled or deactivated in their corresponding SAP technical objects. This is a comma-separated list of states.   |  
|  SAPHierarchySeparator  |  The value used as a separator in the functional location identifier.  |

##### SAP Support Software (Deprecated)
The following calculation interface objects support the output of information for SAP:   
|  Object  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  GetCoordinates  |  Returns the X,Y values for the current feature from the primary geographic component. This should return the concatentated coordinates as well as distinct X and Y values.   |  
|  GetOwnerCoordinates  |  Returns the X,Y values for the current feature's owner feature. The triggering component in the owner is used to retrieve the X,Y value. This should return the concatenated coordinates as well as distinct X and Y values.   |  
|  GetFunctionalLocationIdentifier  |  Returns the appropriate functional location identifier for the feature based on the planning area and the feature orientation (overhead or underground). The planning area information can be found using metadata in the G3E_SAPIFACE table. The orientation (OH or UG) must be passed as an argument to the calculation interface.   |  
|  GetChildFeederList  |  Returns the array of strings identifying the feeders of all of the children of this feature. The table name and fields within the child features are passed as arguments.   |  
|  GetFeederList  |  Returns the array of strings (one or two) from the connectivity record of this feature. A pair of attribute names are passed to indicate where to retrieve the values from as well as the component name.   |

#### G3E_STORMSIFACE (STORMS Interface Table) (Deprecated)

##### G3E_STORMSIFACE.G3E_TYPE Values (Deprecated)
|  Value  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  AbandonedState  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the [G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_VALUE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/F_8zjvUTXpqWJGXxKtqBFw) of the state that represents abandoned data. This is necessary if cost information is stored on the feature so that it can be zeroed when the feature is abandoned.   |  
|  AdditionalItemsCU  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the component number for the Additional Items component. The component attributes are further defined (mapped) in the G3E_CUKEYFIELD table. This can be a component defined in several features and must have the same component number for all features.   |  
|  AncillaryCU  |  The component defined as the ancillary CU for any feature passing to STORMS. The G3E_PARAMETER1 field for this type contains: 
  * The number of the component (G3E_CNO) that contains the ancillary CU data.
  * Optional: An integer (0 or 1) after the component number:
    * 0=False (default)
    * 1=True (the appropriate records are deleted from features in the STORMS closing process) 

Example: 32,1   |  
|  AncillaryCUKeyword  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field for this type contains the value of the keyword to use at the level one for filtering for ancillary CU selection. If the entry in the table does not exist or the value in the parameter is Null, then the STORMS feature name is used for filtering.   |  
|  ApplicationDependencyCU  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains:
  * The component number for the Application Dependency component. 
  * Optional: An integer (0 or 1) after the component number:
    * 0=False (default)
    * 1=True (the appropriate records are deleted from features in the STORMS closing process) 

Example: 32,1  The component attributes are further defined (mapped) in the G3E_CUKEYFIELD table. This can be a component defined in several features and must have the same component number for all features.   |  
|  ChildToParent RNO  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO of the child-to-parent ownership relationship used in the STS-related features.   |  
|  CostAttribute  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field for this type contains the attribute number within the feature that is used to hold the cumulative cost of work on this feature. This may be omitted if costs are not maintained or if they are maintained on the CostComponent.   |  
|  CostComponent  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field for this type contains the component number for the historical feature cost records. This may be omitted if the costs are not maintained or are maintained on the CostAttribute. The component is further defined in the [G3E_CUKEYFIELD](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3TA0h4NSRbRLAc8aSckAMA) table.   |  
|  CUKeyFields  |  The table containing the information about the primary and ancillary compatible unit components. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  CUValidation  |  Determines whether to validate the CU value against the STORMS database. The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains a number and has two possible values. If the value is 1, then it will validate the CU value against STORMS database. If the value is 0, then it will not validate the CU value against STORMS database. The default value is 1.   |  
|  DataSource  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the Oracle database alias required to support the pass back of CU data to STORMS using the [Send to STORMS command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/AJOS_8bbmYp4pg8OeHGvdQ). This is required so the STORMS database procedure that is called can return errors correctly back to the Send to STORMS command. The username/password for the Login parameter will be used with this value. This login must have permissions to execute the phExternalDesign.pDriver procedure.   |  
|  Feature  |  The table containing the list of features considered in work management. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  JobTypeException List  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the comma separated list of JOB_TYPE values that are looked at by JobLifeCycle. If the current job's JOB_TYPE matches a value in this list, then no processing is performed on the job even though it has been specified in [G3E_JOBLIFECYCLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PGIkuZ_ksfECk7uIxOOBDg).   |  
|  Login  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the username/password combination that is used with the DataSource alias to call the phExternalDesign.pDriver procedure for the Send to STORMS command. There is no encryption used on this username/password.   |  
|  OperationalState  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type identifies the G3E_LIFECYCLE.G3E_VALUE of the state that represents operational state data. This is necessary for batch processing purposes.   |  
|  OverheadParameters  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the name of the database table that contains the overhead percentage values used in the Field Cost Estimate calculations. Every field in this table is output as part of the reporting activity.   |  
|  ParentToChild RNO  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the [G3E_RELATIONSHIP.G3E_RNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/kNLtlT57qrNKkSWlV3r3IA) of the parent-to-child ownership relationship used in the STS-related features.   |  
|  PrimaryCU  |  The component defined as the primary CU for any feature passing to STORMS. The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains: 
  * The number of the component (G3E_CNO) that contains the primary CU data.
  * Optional: An integer (0 or 1) after the component number:
    * 0=False (default)
    * 1=True (the appropriate records are deleted from features in the STORMS closing process) 

Example: 32,1   |  
|  PrimaryApplicationDependencyCU  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the component number for the application dependency component associated with the primary CU component. The component attributes are further defined (mapped) in the G3E_CUKEYFIELD table. This can be a component defined in several features and must have the same component number for all features. The underlying table can be the same as that used for ApplicationDependencyCU but should be a different component definition.   |  
|  PrimaryCUKeyword  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the value of the keyword to use at level one for filtering by feature during CU selection.   |  
|  QueryTable  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 field contains the name of the foreign key table associated with the feature attributes that initiate the CU selection dialog box.   |  
|  StaticAttribute  |  The table containing the static attribute mapping. For this type, G3E_PARAMETER1 is Null. Values are pulled from the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE fields.   |  
|  WorkPointCompletionAttribute  |  The G3E_PARAMETER1 value for this type is the ANO value of the attribute on the work point feature which indicates that this work point has been completed. This attribute is a character value that is updated with the word Yes if the work point has been completed.   |

#### G3E_WORKPOINT (Work Point Table)
Table name: G3E_WORKPOINT 
Work Point features are necessary as a grouping mechanism within GIS for data manipulation. The work point is sent to work management systems with the associated work (data manipulation) at that location. You must identify the work point feature in the interface table. You must also identify the attribute that contains the work point number. The work point feature must be set up as child of structural features in your data model using the ownership relationship. Work points can be placed interactively by the designer, or they are automatically generated when CU data are sent to your work management systems. 
For each structure, identify the offset (X,Y) for the work point from each owner feature. You must still make the appropriate ownership entries in [G3E_OWNERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qg4U6UhE0YMmyPrKGNwqeQ) for the work point.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Unique  |  Null  |  Localize  |  PK  |  FK  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  G3E_FNO  |  Number of parent feature.  |  Yes  |  No  |   |  Yes  |  Yes  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_XOFFSET  |  Delta X units to add to the location of the parent feature for positioning the work point instance.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |   |  
|  G3E_YOFFSET  |  Delta Y units to add to the location of the parent feature for positioning the work point instance.   |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Number (9,0)  |  1  |  
|  G3E_EDITDATE  |  Date the record was created or last edited.  |  No  |  No  |   |  No  |  No  |  Date  |   |

![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/1212786?tocId=xC~rhN~6yrr6EkBQYKyiRw) Populate the table G3E_MARKFEATUREFEATURE using this sql statement: 
insert into g3e_markfeaturefeature (G3E_WNO, g3e_fno, G3E_MFfNO)
select G3E_WNO, g3e_fno, G3E_MARKFEATUREfeature_seq.nextval from (
--anything that needs to be configured for all workflows/attributes
select distinct w.G3E_WNO, f.g3e_fno from 
g3e_feature f, G3E_MARKFEATUREWORKFLOW w, G3E_MARKFEATUREattribute wa, g3e_attribute a, g3e_featurecomponent fc where
w.g3e_wno = wa.g3e_wno and a.g3e_ano = wa.g3e_ano and a.g3e_cno = fc.g3e_cno and f.g3e_fno = fc.g3e_fno
-- optionally AND w.g3e_wno=<the new workflow being added>
minus
--anything that is already configured
select g3e_wno, g3e_fno from g3e_markfeaturefeature);
If any features should not be edited in a specific workflow, delete the appropriate row in this table mapping feature to a workflow.

### G3E_MARKFEATUREWORKFLOW (Mark Feature Workflows Definitions Table)

#### G3E_MARKFEATUREWORKFLOW.OPERATION Values
|  Operation Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Add  |  If the component does not contain a row yet OR if the component contains a row but is a repeating component, row will be added.   |  
|  Update   |  Only existing rows will be updated.  If the component does not contain a row yet no row will be added.  If the user specifies a filter, only component rows matching the specified filter will be updated.   |

Executables marked with an asterisk (*) can be accessed by navigating to the NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools menu. The rest can be accessed through a Command window.

## NetWorks Core Simulator

### Creating INI Files
The initialization (INI) file tells the Simulator what scripts to run, how often to run the scripts, and what details you want in the output. You can type the INI file for small tests or use the script generator to create files for large tests. These are the parameters you need in an INI file.   
|  Keyword  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  NUMBEROFSCRIPTS  |  The number of scripts to run. Default is 0.  |  
|  SCRIPTX  |  The name of the script file to run. X is a number from 1 to NUMBEROFSCRIPTS and is used to uniquely identify a script entry in the INI file.   |  
|  LOOP  |  The number of times the list of scripts are to be run. The default is 1.  |  
|  TOTALS  |  Output detail. If this value is Y, only totals are written to the simulator output file. If the value is N, all subtotals and totals are written to the simulator output file. The default is N.   |  
|  EXACTSLEEP  |  Determines if the specified sleep time of sleep tasks is used or if the sleep time is calculated based on the time of the previous task. If EXACTSLEEP is Y, the sleep time specified for the sleep task is used. If EXACTSLEEP is N, the sleep time is calculated by subtracting the time of the previous task from the specified sleep time of the sleep task. If the calculated sleep time is 0 or a negative number, no sleep occurs. The default is Y.   |  
|  CONNECTSCRIPT  |  Name of the script to be used to connect to the database. This script is run only once during each simulation. This entry is optional. If this entry is not present, the other scripts must contain the database connect task. This is provided to allow only one database connection while the other scripts defined can be run in a loop without reconnecting to the database.   |  
|  DISCONNECTSCRIPT  |  Name of the script to be used to disconnect from the database. This script is run only once during each simulation. This entry is optional. If this entry is not present, the other scripts must contain the database disconnect task. This is provided to allow only one database disconnection while the other scripts defined can be run in a loop without reconnecting to the database.   |  
Example
[SCRIPTS] NUMBEROFSCRIPTS = 1  
SCRIPT1 = JOB45.txt  
LOOP = 4  
NOFEATURES = 5  
REVIEW = N  
POST = N  
DISCARD = N  
TOTALS = Y  
IGNOREERRORS = Y  
TOTALSLEEPTIME = 1317

### Creating Script Files
The script file is a comma-delimited text file that defines categories (functionality areas) and tasks the simulator runs. The script files that run when you invoke the Simulator are [defined in the .ini file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/r1diM4HkP4auGtUku3zmnw). Each line in the script file contains a category, a task to perform that is related to the category, and parameters required for the task. These are the defined categories: 
  * Database
  * Job
  * Feature
  * Execute
  * Sleep

  
|  Example DATABASE,CONNECT,BCNVWPRD,gcomm,gcomm  
SLEEP,60  
JOB,CREATE  
SLEEP,109  
FEATURE,ADD,2100,1,713,663,723,673,733,683,743,673,713,763  
SLEEP,190  
FEATURE,ADD,19400,1,140,90,150,100,160,110,170,100,140,190  
SLEEP,171  
FEATURE,ADD,10900,1,124,74,134,84,144,94,154,84,124,174  
SLEEP,206  
FEATURE,ADD,10600,1,180,130,190,140,200,150,210,140,180,230  
SLEEP,215  
FEATURE,ADD,3000,1,538,488,548,498,558,508,568,498,538,588  
SLEEP,165  
JOB,REVIEW  
SLEEP,135  
JOB,POST  
SLEEP,126  
DATABASE,DISCONNECT   |  
| --- |  
The Database Category
The Database category performs both connect and disconnect tasks.  
|  Task  |  Parameters  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  CONNECT  |  CONFIGURATION,USERNAME,PASSWORD[,JOBNAME]  |  Tells the simulator to connect to the specified database using: CONFIGURATION as the configuration to connect to USERNAME as the database user to connect as PASSWORD as the password for USERNAME.JOBNAME as an optional argument that specifies a job name that is activated after a successful connection to the database is made. If not specified no job is activated after the database connection is made.   |  
|  DISCONNECT  |   |  Tells the simulator to disconnect from the database  |  
|  Example DATABASE,CONNECT,BCNVWPRD,GCOMM,GCOMM  
DATABASE,DISCONNECT   |  
| --- |  
The Job Category
The Job category performs job-related tasks.  
|  Task  |  Parameters  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  CREATE  |   |  Tells the simulator to create a new job. Any job created using the simulator is named GTechSimXXXX, where XXXX is a unique number generated from the G3E_JOB_IDENTIFIER sequence. After the job is created, it is activated.   |  
|  ACTIVATE  |  JOBNAME  |  Tells the simulator to activate the specified job or a random job. If JOBNAME is the word RANDOM, a random job is activated. A random job is considered as any job whose G3E_PROCESSSTATUS field is 0.   |  
|  VIEW  |  JOBNAME  |  Tells the simulator to view the specified job or a random job. If JOBNAME is the word RANDOM, a random job is viewed. A random job is considered any job whose G3E_PROCESSSTATUS field is 0.   |  
|  REMOVE  |  JOBNAME  |  Tells the simulator to remove the specified job or a random job from the environment. If JOBNAME is the word RANDOM, a random job is removed. A random job is considered any job that was added to the environment using the Job create, activate, or view tasks.   |  
|  REVIEW  |   |  Tells the simulator to review job edits for the currently active job. A job must be active for this task to be performed.   |  
|  POST  |   |  Tells the simulator to post the job edits for the currently active job. A job must be active for this task to be performed.   |  
|  DISCARD  |   |  Tells the simulator to discard the job edits for the currently active job. A job must be active for this task to be performed.   |  
|  Example JOB,CREATE  
JOB,ACTIVATE,RANDOM  
JOB,ACTIVATE,JOBNAME  
JOB,VIEW,RANDOM  
JOB,VIEW,JOBNAME  
JOB,REMOVE,RANDOM  
JOB,REMOVE,JOBNAME  
JOB,REVIEW  
JOB,VALIDATE  
JOB,POST  
JOB,DISCARD   |  
| --- |  
The Features Category
This category performs feature-related tasks.  
|  Task  |  Parameters  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  ADD  |  FNO,TIMES,X1,Y1..X5,Y5  |  The simulator places a feature corresponding to the FNO value. The feature are placed TIMES times at the points specified.   |  
|  DELETE  |  FNO,FID  |  The simulator deletes the feature whose feature identifier is FID.  |  
|  EXPLORE  |  FNO,FID  |  The simulator explores the feature whose feature identifier is FID.  |  
|  Example FEATURE,ADD,100,2,10,10,10,20,20,20,20,10,10,10  
FEATURE,DELETE,100,1000  
FEATURE,EXPLORE,100,1000   |  
| --- |  
The Execute Category
This category performs miscellaneous database tasks. There is no specific task defined for this category. The Simulator passes the defined SQL statement directly to the database for execution.   
|  Example SQL> execute,select * from G3E_DATACONNECTION_OPTABLE;  |  
| --- |  
The Sleep Category
This category causes the simulator to sleep for a specified time in seconds. There is no task for this category. There are two ways to specify sleep time. 
  * A single value causes the simulator to sleep that number of seconds.
  * Two values separated by a comma tells the simulator to sleep for a random time, in seconds, between the two specified times 

  
|  Example SLEEP,20  
SLEEP,20,100   |  
| --- |

### Generating Scripts for the Simulator
Because creating scripts for the Simulator can be a very tedious and time-consuming operation, the Script Generator lets you create Simulator files to analyze large tasks. 
To run the Script Generator, at the command prompt change to the \GTechnology\Program folder
GTechSimScriptGenerator.exe <Path to INI File>\<Name of INI File>
The file that defines parameters to generate the text and INI files for the Simulator is divided into two sections: 
System
This section defines global parameters that apply to all folders.  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CONFIGURATION  |  The NetWorks Core configuration the Simulator is to use   |  
|  USERNAME  |  The database username of the database to which to connect  |  
|  PASSWORD  |  The password for the specified database user  |  
|  ALIAS  |  The Oracle alias for connecting to the database  |  
|  SEED  |  The random number seed value  |  
|  NUMBEROFFOLDERS  |  The number of machines that are used in the Simulator test  |  
|  OUTPUTPATH  |  The local path to which to write the Simulator files  |  
|  EXCLUDEFNO  |  A comma delimited list of feature numbers (G3E_FNO) to be excluded from any Simulator activity   |  
|  TOTALS  |  If set to Y, writes only totals (includes all deltas activities) to the output file. If set to N, totals and subtotals are written to the output file.   |  
|  EXACTSLEEP  |  If set to Y, sleeps the specified time defined in each sleep task. If set to N, the sleep time of sleep tasks are calculated by subtracting the previous task time from the specified time. If the resulting value is 0 or less, no sleep occurs. Default is Y.   |  
|  RANDOMSLEEP  |  If set to Y, the sleep time of each sleep task is dynamic. The value is between the min and max sleep times defined for the task. If set to N, the sleep time of the sleep task is the minimum sleep time defined for the task. The default is N.   |  
|  Example [SYSTEM]  
CONFIGURATION=BCNVWPRD  
USERNAME=gcomm  
PASSWORD=gcomm  
ALIAS=BCNVWPRD  
SEED=80  
NUMBEROFFOLDERS=4  
OUTPUTPATH=c:\temp\simscripts\New\Scenario1  
EXCLUDEFNO=24000,24099,24100,24200,24300,24400,24500,24600,24700  
TOTALS=Y  
EXACTSLEEP=N  
RANDOMSLEEP=N  
CONNECTSCRIPT=Y  
DISCONNECTSCRIPT=Y   |  
| --- |  
Folder
This section defines folder-specific parameters. A folder is a logical breakdown of tests either by functional test or machine. There should be one folder section for each folder defined. The name of the section is the word FOLDER followed by a number. The number must be in the range of 1 to NUMBEROFFOLDERS as specified in the SYSTEM section.   
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  NAME  |  The name of the folder. The folder is created under the OUTPUTPATH parameter specified in the SYSTEM section if not already present. This entry must exist for each FOLDER section.   |  
|  NUMBEROFSCRIPTS  |  The number of scripts to generate. The default is 0.  |  
|  LOOPS  |  The number times to run the scripts. The default is 1.  |  
|  PERCENTJOBCREATION  |  Percentage of all scripts that create and activate jobs.  |  
|  PERCENTJOBACTIVATION  |  Percentage of all scripts that activate an existing job.  |  
|  PERCENTJOBVIEW  |  Percentage of all scripts that view an existing job. Scripts with job view only do not place features.   |  
|  PERCENTJOBPOST  |  Percentage of scripts that create or activate jobs that post their job edits.  |  
|  PERCENTJOBDISCARD  |  Percentage of scripts that create or activate jobs that discard their job edits.  |  
|  PERCENTJOBREVIEW  |  Percentage of scripts that create, activate, or view a job that performs a review job task.   |  
|  NUMBEROFFEATURESTOPLACE  |  The number of features each script places if a job is created or activated. The default is 0.   |  
|  NUMBEROFFEATURESTOEXPLORE  |  The number of features to explore within a script if a job is created, activated, or viewed. The default is 0.   |  
|  BATCHFILESLEEP  |  The sleep time, in seconds, between each invocation of the simulator. This value is used in the batch file. The default is 10.   |  
|  MINDATABASESLEEP  |  The minimum sleep time, in seconds, after a database task. The default is 10 seconds.  |  
|  MAXDATABASESLEEP  |  The maximum sleep time, in seconds, after a database task. The default is 30 seconds.  |  
|  MINFEATURESLEEP  |  The minimum sleep time, in seconds, after a feature placement task. The default is 10.   |  
|  MAXFEATURESLEEP  |  The maximum sleep time, in seconds, after a feature task placement. The default is 30.   |  
|  MINJOBSLEEP  |  The minimum sleep time, in seconds, after a job task. The default is 10.  |  
|  MAXJOBSLEEP  |  The maximum sleep time, in seconds, after a job task. The default is 30.  |  
|  EXECUTIONPATH  |  The path on the test machines where the scripts are located. The default is the %TEMP% path as specified on the machine that generates the scripts.   |  
|  CONNECTSCRIPT  |  Y to use a separate connection script to prevent every script from having its own connection task. N to have a database connect task in every script. The default is N. If set to Y, the name of the connection script must be CONNECT.CSV. The script generator does not generate the connect script.   |  
|  DISCONNECTSCRIPT  |  Y to use a separate disconnect script to prevent every script from having its own disconnect task. N to have a database disconnect task in every script. The default is N. If set to Y, the name of the disconnect script must be DISCONNECT.CSV. The script generator does not generate the disconnect script.   |  
|  Example [FOLDER1]  
NAME=UCX2  
NUMBEROFSCRIPTS=6  
LOOPS=2  
NUMBEROFFEATURESTOPLACE=0  
PERCENTJOBCREATION=100  
BATCHFILESLEEP=22  
MINDATABASESLEEP=112  
MINFEATURESLEEP=0  
MAXFEATURESLEEP=0  
MINJOBSLEEP=0  
MAXJOBSLEEP=0  
EXECUTIONPATH=c:\GTechSim\Scenario1  
  
[FOLDER2]  
NAME=UCX4  
NUMBEROFSCRIPTS=6  
LOOPS=2  
NUMBEROFFEATURESTOPLACE=0  
PERCENTJOBCREATION=100  
BATCHFILESLEEP=22  
MINDATABASESLEEP=112  
MINFEATURESLEEP=0  
MAXFEATURESLEEP=0  
MINJOBSLEEP=0  
MAXJOBSLEEP=0  
EXECUTIONPATH=c:\GTechSim\Scenario1  
  
[FOLDER3]  
NAME=UCX5  
NUMBEROFSCRIPTS=6  
LOOPS=2  
NUMBEROFFEATURESTOPLACE=0  
PERCENTJOBCREATION=100  
BATCHFILESLEEP=22  
MINDATABASESLEEP=112  
MINFEATURESLEEP=0  
MAXFEATURESLEEP=0  
MINJOBSLEEP=0  
MAXJOBSLEEP=0  
EXECUTIONPATH=c:\GTechSim\Scenario1  
  
[FOLDER4]  
NAME=UCX10  
NUMBEROFSCRIPTS=7  
LOOPS=2  
NUMBEROFFEATURESTOPLACE=0  
PERCENTJOBCREATION=100  
BATCHFILESLEEP=18  
MINDATABASESLEEP=112  
MINFEATURESLEEP=0  
MAXFEATURESLEEP=0  
MINJOBSLEEP=0  
MAXJOBSLEEP=0  
EXECUTIONPATH=c:\GTechSim\Scenario1   |

## Tools for Working with Metadata

### NetWorks Core Project Tool (also known as GPT)

#### Connecting to a Data Source
In NetWorks Core Project Tool (also known as GPT), a data source is the Oracle alias. A NetWorks Core data source contains one or more data connections. Using GPT, you can connect to one data source at a time and see the contents of the data connections within that data source. 
  * To connect to a NetWorks Core data source:


  1. From the File menu, select Open Configuration. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259325)
  2. Type the username and password, and select the service name for the data source you want to open. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259325) If you are already in a data source, it closes before the new data source can open. 


Related Topics
NetWorks Core[ Project Tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/E7m~K_5GdHVzot5L0Ghb1g)  
[Navigating GPT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6OphOLRVC5UPPQsHhmtoOQ)  
[Importing a FRAMME Schema](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/otoHhy6~LhNVEOi80e52Yw)  
[Defining a Simple Query](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/q9nxoVvIDjI_hHImUiSHMg)

#### Creating a Data Model Using GPT
You can [use NetWorks Core Project Tool (also known as GPT)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/E7m~K_5GdHVzot5L0Ghb1g) to create a schema from scratch. 
  * To create your data model using GPT:


  1. If you do not already have a schema, [create one](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZrEqfbjH8rI5BSbWzK7Arg). 
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Project Tool. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259341)
  3. Type the username and password, and select the service name for the schema you just created. 
  4. Click OK. You are ready to start [creating features and components](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Howx6sCalUg70z318y_~Lg).

#### Creating a Database Document

##### dtl Tags
The following are GPT .dtl tags: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259530) User-provided text is displayed as orange italic. 
<?INGR:TEMPLATE> header tag
The TEMPLATE tag must be the first line in a .dtl file and is the only required tag. This field determines the default and enabling options on the Select Output screen of the Document Generation Wizard. 
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="type"?>
Attributes:
OUTPUT_TYPE—Required. The value of this attribute is the output type: xml or html. If xml is the output type, all three output options (XML, HTML, and Word) are enabled, and XML is the default selected on the Select Output screen. If html is the output type, only HTML and Word are enabled, and HTML is the default selected on the Select Output screen. 
Example
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="xml"?>
<INGR:SCRIPT> user procedure tag
After the TEMPLATE header, the optional SCRIPT tag defines a user procedure.
<INGR:SCRIPT LANGUAGE="language-name">  
ProcedureName(Param1, Parem2,…, ParamN)  
…Code…  
</INGR:SCRIPT>
Attributes:
LANGUAGE—Required. The value of this attribute is the Active Scripting language used for the functions defined within this element. If left unspecified, Microsoft® JScript® (compatible with ECMA 262 language specification) is used. This attribute accepts the same values as the language attribute on the HTML <SCRIPT> element. See MSDN for more information. 
Example
<INGR:SCRIPT LANGUAGE="VBScript">  
function ComponentType(intType)   
If intType=1 then ComponentType="Nongraphic"  
Else ComponentType="-"  
End if   
end function  
</INGR:SCRIPT>
<INGR:QUERY> tag
The SELECT statement is evaluated, and [Variable and Field substitutions](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qcVfN6FgUoZPKnyH1rQing) are applied. Filters in the [active view](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/LvaHo8qwmny2CY~RCUcO0w) are also applied to the query. The query is executed on the database, and for each record retrieved, processes the context inside the tags. 
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT … FROM … WHERE … ">  
…context…  
</INGR:QUERY>
Attributes:
VALUE—Required. The value of this attribute is a SELECT statement that is evaluated and then executed to retrieve records from the database. 
Example
DTL text parsed:
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="xml"?>  
<?xml version="1.0"?>  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME, G3E_REGIONNAME, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_EDITDATE FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1">  
<FEConfiguration K="<INGR:VALUE- OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME"/>">   
<DATA>  
<F N="G3E_REGIONNAME" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_CSNAME" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CSNAME"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_EDITDATE" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_EDITDATE"/>" />  
</DATA>   
</FEConfiguration>  
</INGR:QUERY>
The <INGR:QUERY> tag generates the following query executed on the database:
SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME, G3E_REGIONNAME, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_EDITDATE   
FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1 
The result of this query is metadata information about configurations in a particular connection. 
The context is highlighted in green. For each G3E_CONFIGURATIONS record retrieved, the context inside the <INGR:QUERY> tag is processed. 
<INGR:VALUE-OF> tag
Expression is evaluated (Variable, Field, and Function substitutions are applied, respectively ) and dumped as a literal. 
<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="expression"/>
Attributes:
SELECT—Required. The value of this attribute is an expression which is evaluated and written to XML. 
Example
DTL text parsed:
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="xml"?>  
<?xml version="1.0"?>  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME, G3E_REGIONNAME, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_EDITDATE FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1">  
<FEConfiguration K="<INGR:VALUE- OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME"/>">   
<DATA>  
<F N="G3E_REGIONNAME" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_CSNAME" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CSNAME"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_EDITDATE" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_EDITDATE"/>" />  
</DATA>   
</FEConfiguration>  
</INGR:QUERY>
The <INGR:QUERY> tag generates the following query that is executed on the database:
SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME, G3E_REGIONNAME, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_EDITDATE   
FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1 
For each G3E_CONFIGURATIONS record returned, the <INGR:VALUE-OF> tags are evaluated:
Evaluate G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_CONFNO  
Evaluate G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME  
Evaluate G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_REGIONNAME  
Evaluate G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_CSNAME  
Evaluate G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_EDITDATE  
Next

<?xml version="1.0?>  
<FEConfiguraton K="1" N="GPTDEV93">  
<DATA>  
<F N="G3E_REGIONNAME" V="1"/>  
<F N="G3E_CSNAME" V="LCC"/>

![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259530) To produce a legible and compact output, if any opening or closing of a tag (for example, the <DATA> tag) is alone in a line, it does not produce carriage returns (CrLf), spaces, or tabs in the XML file. The exception is the <INGR:VALUE-OF> tag. In this example, the carriage returns in the .dtl file are maintained in the produced XML file. 
<INGR:VARIABLE> tag
The variable NAME is defined with the value Expression. Field substitutions are applied to the expression. 
<INGR:VARIABLE NAME="MyVarName" SELECT="Expression"/>
Attributes:
NAME—Required. The value of this attribute is a variable name.
SELECT—Required. The value of this attribute is an expression, which is evaluated and assigned to the variable name. 
Example
DTL text parsed:
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="xml"?>  
<?xml version="1.0"?>  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME, G3E_REGIONNAME, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_EDITDATE  
FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1">  
<FEConfiguration K="<INGR:VALUE- OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME"/>">  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_DCNO, G3E_USERNAME, G3E_LOCATION, G3E_CONNECTINFO, G3E_GDOTYPE, G3E_TYPE, G3E_OUTPUTDIRECTORY,  
G3E_LASTASSIGNEDFID, G3E_CSNAME, G3E_OFFICE, G3E_EDITDATE  
FROM G3E_DATACONNECTION   
WHERE G3E_LOCATION='?G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME' ORDER BY G3E_TYPE">  
<FEDataconnection K="<INGR:VALUE- OF SELECT="?G3E_DCNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_USERNAME"/>">  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_FNO, G3E_USERNAME, G3E_TOOLTIP, G3E_PRIMARYGEOGRAPHICCNO, G3E_PRIMARYATTRIBUTECNO, G3E_DCNO, G3E_PRIMARYDETAILCNO, G3E_EDITDATE, G3E_NUMBEROFNODES, G3E_IMPORTFEATURENAME, G3E_REPLACE, G3E_NAME, G3E_LOCALECOMMENT, G3E_MERGE, G3E_CLASSIFICATIONANO, G3E_IDENTIFIERVIEW, G3E_BULKEDIT   
FROM G3E_FEATURE  
WHERE G3E_DCNO=?G3E_DCNO ORDER BY G3E_USERNAME">  
<INGR:VARIABLE NAME="Facility" SELECT="?G3E_FNO" />  
<FEFacility K="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="$Facility"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_USERNAME"/>">  
<DATA>  
<F N="G3E_FNO" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_FNO"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_USERNAME" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_USERNAME"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_TOOLTIP" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_TOOLTIP"/>" />  
</DATA>  
</FEFacility>  
</INGR:QUERY>  
</FEDataconnection>  
</INGR:QUERY>  
</FEConfiguration>  
</INGR:QUERY>
The variable Facility, as shown in green text, is defined as the value of the field substitution ?G3E_FNO. The field substitution ?G3E_FNO evaluates to be the G3E_FEATURE.G3E_FNO of the current recordset's record. When in the next line, <INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="$Facility"/> is evaluated, $Facility is replaced by the feature number. 
The following queries were executed on the database. This information is in the log file. A view filter, shown in green, is applied to the G3E_FEATURE query.

<INGR:IF> tag
If the first CONDITION evaluates to True, the associated context inside is processed. If not, the <INGR:ELSE> branch is processed. The <INGR:ELSIF> and <INGR:ELSE> branches are optional. Variable and Field substitutions are applied, respectively. 
<INGR:IF CONDITION= "expression" />  
…context…  
<INGR:ELSIF CONDITION="expression" />  
…context…  
<INGR:ELSE>   
…context…  
</INGR:IF>
Attributes:
CONDITION—Required. The value of this attribute is an expression which evaluates to True or False. 
Example
<?INGR:TEMPLATE OUTPUT_TYPE="html"?>  
<?xml version="1.0"?>  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_CONFNO, G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME FROM G3E_CONFIGURATIONS WHERE G3E_CONFNO=1">  
  
<FEConfiguration K="<INGR:VALUE- OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME"/>">  
  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_SNO, G3E_USERNAME, G3E_TYPE FROM G3E_STYLE ORDER BY G3E_TYPE, G3E_USERNAME">  
  
<FEStyle K="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_SNO"/>" N="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_USERNAME"/>">  
<DATA>  
<F N="G3E_SNO" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_SNO"/>" />  
<F N="G3E_TYPE" V="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_TYPE"/>" />  
</DATA>  
<INGR:IF CONDITION="""?G3E_TYPE""=""PointStyle""">  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_SIZE FROM G3E_POINTSTYLE WHERE G3E_SNO = ?G3E_SNO">  
<POINTSTYLE  
SIZE="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_SIZE"/>"   
/>  
</INGR:QUERY>  
<INGR:ELSIF CONDITION="""?G3E_TYPE""=""TextStyle""">  
<INGR:QUERY VALUE="SELECT G3E_SIZE FROM G3E_TEXTSTYLE WHERE G3E_SNO = ?G3E_SNO">  
<TEXTSTYLE   
SIZE="<INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_SIZE"/>"   
/>  
</INGR:QUERY>   
<INGR:ELSE>  
<!--skip this style type since we are only processing text and point styles-->  
</INGR:IF>  
</FEStyle>  
</INGR:QUERY>  
</FEConfiguration>  
</INGR:QUERY>

##### GPT Document Generation XML Hierarchy
To produce the new XML hierarchy for the first time, run the [Document Generation Wizard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/X3c5hKouhrk~TPFcEUgWtg) with the following options: 
  * Select source screen—Select the Default template. 
  * Select output screen—Select XML document as the output type, and specify an output file name. 
  * Select template screen—Uncheck the Use template box.

<?xml version="1.0" ?>

##### GPT Document Templates
GPT retrieves data from the database by following the structure of a custom template (.dtl) file or by using the default template stored inside GPT. The custom template delivered in \GTechnology\templates\GPT\Custom.dtl produces the same output as the default template. However, Custom.dtl gives you a sample to use for designing additional custom templates. Standard templates are delivered in \GTechnology\templates\GPT\GPT DDD.dot and \GTechnology\templates\GPT\GPT FRS.dot. Style sheets are delivered in \GTechnology\templates\GPT\DDD.xsl and \GTechnology\templates\GPT\FRS.xsl. 
The document generator template (.dtl) is a language for producing XML, which is transformed into output documents (XML, HTML, or Microsoft Word). DTL template files contain text to be parsed. The template description is a Hexagon format not based on a standard technology. All text after the header and any user procedures are processed as a context. A context can have literal text that should be dumped to an output file and can have some special tags that must be interpreted by GPT. [Each tag](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BUuTJe61VSvsF_EwS8gkCg) can contain one or more contexts that must be evaluated.

##### GPT Style Sheets
Style sheets specify how the XML data are presented and transform XML into readable, well-formed documents. The style sheet templates delivered in the \GTechnology\templates\GPT folder translate the XML hierarchy produced by the document generator. See XSL Transformation - XSLT in MSDN for more information on style sheets. 
Example
The following lines from the sample style sheet that is delivered with GPT show the use of the key statement. See MSDN, XML Standards Reference-XSLT Elements for more information. 
<xsl:variable name="varCNO" select="DATA/F[@N='G3E_CNO']/@V"/>  
<xsl:for-each select="key('fecomponent- match',$varCNO)/FEAttribute">  
<xsl:sort data-type="text" select="@N"/>  
<TR>  
<TD>  
<xsl:value-of select="DATA/F[@N='G3e_USERNAME']/@V"/>  
</TD>  
<TD>  
<xsl:value-of select="COLUMN/@DATA_TYPE"/>  
</TD>

##### Template Substitutions
The following are GPT document template substitutions:   
|  Document Template Substitutions  |  Description  |  Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Variable substitutions  |  In expressions, the token "$" denotes a variable.  |  If $Facility=5, the expression <INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="$Facility" /> is "5".   |  
|  Field substitutions  |  In expressions, the character "?" denotes a recordset field. The value of field in the current recordset is used.   |  If field "G3E_FNO" is "3000" in the current recordset, the expression <INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="?G3E_FNO" /> is "3000".   |  
|  Function substitutions  |  In expressions, "f(…)" (where f is a string) denotes function.  |  f Max(a,b) is defined, <INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="Max(2,3)" /> is "3". If an expression with this name is not defined, a substitution is not performed. Functions can be user-defined or system. User-defined functions must be defined in the header, while system functions are hard coded inside GPT. A user-defined function can never replace a system function.   |  
|  System function Position()  |  This system function returns the current record number of the processed query.  |  If it is being processed as the third record of current query, <INGR:VALUE-OF SELECT="Position()" /> is "3".   |  
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259532)
  * Nested substitutions — Substitutions are processed in order, so expressions like "Max(2,?$MyVar)" are possible. First, $MyVar is substituted by its value "G3E_FNO". Then "?G3E_FNO" is substituted by "3" and, finally, "Max(2,3)" is substituted by "3". 
  * Escape character (") — The document generator enables the use of the escape character (") in attribute values. You can pass the character " as text by repeating it twice.   
|  Example $Myvar=Two, the expression <INGR:IF CONDITION="""$Myvar""=""One""" evaluates "Two"="One", resulting in FALSE.   |  
| --- |

#### Creating a GPT Script File
You can create a named script file that keeps a record of the SQL statements the NetWorks Core Project Tool (GPT) executes while you are using the tool. You can then use the SQL statements to help undo changes made in GPT or to apply all changes from one schema to another. You can start or stop script generation and override information in an existing script or append information to an existing script. The script contains time stamp information at the start of the file and at any point where the script is appended. 
  * To create a GPT script file:


  1. From the GPT Tools menu, select Script > Record Script. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259504)
  2. Type a path and a name for the script; or click Browse, navigate to the appropriate location, type a name for the script in the File name field of the Save As dialog box and click Save. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate the script in the Comment field. 
  4. Click OK. The following snapshot is an example of what you would see: 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259504)
  5. To stop recording the SQL, from the Tools menu, select Script > Stop Recording <script name>. 


  * To append to an existing GPT script file:


  1. From the GPT Tools menu, select Script > Record Script. 
  2. Select the script from the Script name drop-down list. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate this portion of the script in the Comment field. 
  4. Click OK, then click Yes on the message box that appears. 


  * To overwrite an existing GPT script file:


  1. From the GPT Tools menu, select Script > Record Script. 
  2. Select the script from the Script name drop-down list. 
  3. Type appropriate comments to designate this script in the Comment field. 
  4. Click OK. 
  5. Click No. 
  6. Click OK on the message boxes that appear.

#### Creating a Spreadsheet of Your Database

##### Configuring Excel for the Create Spreadsheet Tool
Before you can use the [Create Spreadsheet tool](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/fZq34GPrT9v3Rm8l8P6YHg) to output information about the contents your database, you must configure some special security settings in Excel. These security settings are required to activate the macros that display the toolbar buttons. 
  1. Close all other Microsoft Office applications.
  2. On the Excel File menu, select Options. 
  3. Select Trust Center. 
  4. Click Trust Center Settings. 
  5. Select Macro Settings
  6. Select Enable all Macros. 
  7. Check Trust Access to the VBA project object model.

#### Creating and Editing GPT Views
In GPT, you can create named views to help you filter the information in your database. The views are saved for future GPT sessions. Even if you do not create and activate a new view, any filter you create is added to the default view, which is active by default. Refresh the tree view to display the filtered items in the active view. Every configuration has its own views defined independently from other configurations. All view and filter information is stored in the registry. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259510) Filters in the currently active view are automatically included when you create a [GPT database document](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/X3c5hKouhrk~TPFcEUgWtg). 
  * To create a GPT view:


  1. From the Tools menu, select Preferences. 
  2. On the Views tab, click New. A new view appears in the Defined views list. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259510)
  3. Double-click the new view.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259510)
  4. Type the new name in the Rename View dialog box, and click OK. 
  5. To add filters to the new view, check the box to make it active.
  6. Click OK. 
  7. [Create a filter](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/gttMh2sZyBUAwLILqaZaeg)
Any filters you create while a view is active are added to that view. All of the filters you defined in the tree view are displayed in the Defined filters in views box for both active and inactive views. 
  8. Click the view name to display the filters defined for that view.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/cu7E3b21qrKN6O0iTtKEVg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=7f1efb5a9f1c5eb2&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)


  * To edit a GPT view:


  1. Check the view you want to edit.
  2. Double-click the filter statement.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/tqM5k2fMks_IPOQ5~QyKLQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=4b1b0168e9b290be&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. Edit the statement, and click OK. 


  * To delete a GPT view:


  1. Uncheck the view you want to delete to deactivate it. You cannot delete an active view. 
  2. Select the view you want to delete.
  3. Click Delete.

#### Defining a Simple Query
In the GPT, simple attribute queries are children of the Attribute Queries node.
  * To define a simple attribute query:


  1. In the tree view, select the Attribute Queries node to display all the queries defined in the model. To display the properties of a specific query, double-click the query name in the content panel, or click the query name in the navigation panel. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259452)
  2. From the Edit menu, select Add New Simple Attribute Query. 
OR
Right-click the Attribute Queries node, and select Add New Simple Attribute Query. 
OR
Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259452), and select Add New Simple Attribute Query. 
The query is added at the end of the Attribute Queries list.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/rLQq4tT_CGJWoEitjHYkDg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=24ce311c666e9a0d&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. Review the information in the content panel:

|  Application  |  [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_APPLICATION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw)  |  
|  The table of the main component  |  [G3E_ATTRIBUTEQUERY.G3E_SQL](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zk79M~vl5q_AJkS_5B~YXw)  |

  4. In the Name field, type a name for the query. The name is stored in the database and appears in the simple query settings of the application. 
  5. In the Description field, type a description for the query. 
  6. In the Application field, select the product in which the attribute query is available. 
  7. In the Query tables box, do the following: 
    1. Check Graphical, Attribute, Value list, or Foreign as necessary for the presentation in the Tables available list. This list displays component table names depending on which boxes you check. 
    2. Use the ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259452), ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259452), or ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259452) to add tables to or remove tables from the Main component's table field and the Additional query tables field. The Main component's table field is the one used to build the column list for the resulting query. The Additional query tables field is the list of tables which can be used in the simple attribute query. 
  8. In the Query box, do the following: 
    1. Select the name of the field to use in the query.
    2. Select the type of relational operator. If you select the Between operation, you must specify two filter values. 
    3. Select a value type, either Field, Parameter, or Value. 
    4. Select an SQL filter value: Fixed value, if the value type is Value; Field name, if the value type is Field; Parameter, if the value type is Parameter. 
    5. Use the buttons to compose the SQL statement.
    6. Use Reset to clear the WHERE clause from the query. 
    7. Click Reload to set the query to information currently in the database. 
  9. In the Query parameters box, do the following: 
    1. In the Parameter field, select a parameter. Parameters are applicable only when the query was built with parameters. 
    2. Type a prompt for the query in the Prompt field. 
    3. Check if nulls are allowed.
    4. Click Apply. 
  10. Click Update to save the query.

#### Defining Dialog Boxes, Dialog Tabs, and Tab Attributes in GPT

##### Defining a Dialog Tab
In the Project Tool (GPT), dialog tabs appear as child nodes of the Dialogs node.
  * To define a dialog tab:


  1. In the tree view, select a feature, navigate to a dialog box under the Dialogs node, and expand it. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259394)
  2. Highlight the Dialog Tabs node.
  3. From the Edit menu, select Add New Dialog Tab. 
OR
Right-click the Dialog Tabs node, and select Add New Dialog Tab. 
OR
Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259394) and select Add New Dialog Tab. The new dialog tab also appears under the Tabs node for the facility with a new node for Tab Attributes. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259394)
  4. In the Name field, type a name for the dialog tab entry. 
  5. In the Ordinal field, type the order in which you want the tab to appear. 
  6. Click Update.

##### Defining Dialog Boxes
You can use the Project Tool (GPT) to define the three standard dialog boxes—Review, Edit, and Placement—or any number of user-defined dialog boxes. 
  * To define a default dialog box:


  1. In the tree view, select the Dialogs node.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259389)
  2. From the Edit menu, select Add Default Dialogs. 
OR
Right-click the Dialogs node, and select Add Default Dialogs. 
OR
Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259389) and select Add Default Dialogs. 
The default dialog boxes are added under the Dialogs node. Default dialogs are created only if the feature contains components with attribute names to be presented on the dialog tab in [Feature Explorer](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/52pN2fzrriwgeUjUOoh6mw). The following attribute fields are excluded and are not presented on the dialog tab: G3E_CNO, G3E_ID, G3E_FNO, G3E_FID, G3E_CID, G3E_GEOMETRY, G3E_ALIGNMENT, or ALIGNMENT 
  3. Highlight one of the default dialog box choices: Review, Edit, or Placement. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259389)
  4. Review the information in the content panel:  
|  Panel Item  |  Reference   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Name  |  [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw)  |  
|  Number  |  [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_DNO](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw)  |  
|  Type  |  [G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/JliNbi7cNRgf~rtlez7_mw)  |  
  5. If necessary, select a new dialog box type from the Type drop-down list. 
  6. Click Update. 


  * To add a user-defined dialog box:


  1. From the Edit menu, select Add New Dialog. 
OR
Right-click the Dialogs node, and select Add New Dialog. 
OR
Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259389) and select Add New Dialog. 
A User Defined node appears under the Dialogs node.
  2. Highlight the User Defined node.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259389)
  3. If necessary, select a new dialog box type from the Type drop-down list. 
  4. Click Update.
