## OpenID Connect Glossary
  * OpenID Connect (OIDC) Provider: OIDC Provider is an Identity Provider (IDP) that implements the OIDC protocol on top of OAuth2. OIDC Provider may also be called Authorization Server. 
  * End-User: A user that is using the registered client application to access their authorized data. 
  * Client (Application):  A client is software entity that requests tokens from the OIDC provider either for authenticating a user or accessing a resource (also known as a relying party). A client must be registered with the OIDC provider. In the case of a web application, the host (server) where the application resides, acts as the client while the browser, which the end-user uses to interact with the application, takes the role of an end-user. However, in the case of a desktop application, the host acts as both a client and as an end-user. 
  * ID Token: An identity or ID token represents the outcome of a successful authentication process. It contains a subject or "sub" claim that uniquely identifies the user. 
  * Access Token: An access token is used by a client (application or service) to access authorized resources. These tokens have a short life span for improved security and are delegated as bearer tokens to the services. A bearer token means that the bearer can access any authorized resource without requiring further authentication. 
  * Refresh Token: A refresh token represents a long-lasting authorization of certain resources on behalf of a relying party (client). Whenever an access token expires, the refresh token is used to renew the access token. 
  * Authorization code: An authorization code represents the intermediate result of a successful end-user authorization process. It is used by the client to obtain access and refresh tokens. 
  * Scope: Scopes are identifiers for resources that a client wants to access. The scope is sent to the OIDC provider during an authentication or token request. For example, a "profile" scope requests a group of claims (first name, last name, gender, profile picture, and so forth.) that represents the profile of a user and an "address" scope value requests the address claim. 
  * Client ID:  The client identifier represents a unique string assigned to a registered client within the OIDC provider. 
  * Client Secret: If the client type is confidential, the OIDC provider issues a client secret that can be included along with the client ID during the authorization process or when requesting tokens. The client secret is only known to the client application and the authorization server. 
  * Offline Access: The offline_access scope is used by the client to request non-expiring refresh tokens from the OIDC provider. It is called offline access because the client authorization is not needed for the client to obtain a new access token.

OR
Start the All Application Configuration Wizard from the Microsoft Windows Start > Intergraph G/Technology > All Applications Wizard.

ForceUserLogin
NetWorks Core products supports two possible values (0 or 1) for the ForceUserLogin registry key (REG_DWORD) located under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00. 
  * 0 - When ForceUserLogin is set to 0, the application looks for the authentication mode set within the application configuration file. If the authentication mode is set to Anonymous, then the user is prompted to enter the username and password. If the authentication mode is set to OIDC, and OIDC is configured for the application using the All Applications Configuration Wizard, then the application redirects the user to the OIDC Provider to execute the authentication sequence.

Export and Plotting
Once the user is successfully authenticated and authorized through Designer/Analyst or NetViewer, the access token is delegated as a bearer token to Plotting or Export web service, based on whether you are using NetViewer to Plotting or Designer/Analyst to Export integration. The Export or Plotting web service interrogates the claims to extract the gtechnologyDBConnect claim (attribute). The gtechnologyDBConnect claim is used to make a database connection the NetWorks Core configuration. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/918979) OpenID Connect is an HTTP based protocol, so you need the browser to execute the OIDC authentication flow. For both Designer/Analyst and NetViewer, the application relies on the embedded browser to execute the sequence.

### OpenID Connect in Export
When OpenID Connect is configured as the authentication type for NetWorks Core, Export to CAD attaches the access token as a bearer token to the Authorization header before Export service request is made. The Export service extracts the access token, validates, and transforms it into a claim set. The service then interrogates the claim set to find out if a gtechnologyDBConnect claim exists. The database connection string extracted from the gtechnologyDBConnect claim is then delegated to the ExportExport clients that are consuming the Export service.The client application is responsible for executing the OIDC authentication sequence, getting the access token after a successful authentication, and then delegating the access token as bearer token to the Export service. Mixed mode authentication type is not supported. If a client is configured to use OpenID Connect, then the Export service should also be configured to use OpenID Connect. 
If you do not want to use OpenID Connect as the authentication type then both the application and the service should be configured to run with Anonymous authentication type. In this case, the connection string embedded as part of theExport
Changes to Export Web Service
  * Export
  * ASMX is still supported for backward compatibility for existing clients that are directly referencing and consuming the Export
  * The same RESTful APIs (GetFiles, GetRequestStatus, SubmitExportRequest, SubmitImportRequest) that were supported through ASMX are also supported through the Web API Controller. The OpenID Connect protocol is only supported through the Web API layer and not through ASMX service calls. 


Changes to Export Client
  * The old ActiveX Export Control is replaced with a new managed client proxy. The new client proxy class is available through GNetExportWebProxy.dll assembly. 
  * The old ActiveX control is still available for backward compatibility. 
  * The new client proxy cannot be embedded within an HTML page in a single page client application. Such clients should be updated to directly use the RESTful APIs through the ASP.NET Web API Controller. 
  * Export Client applications that do have managed .NET code behind can make calls to the Export
  * All the properties and methods that were supported by the Active control are supported through the new client proxy. The new client proxy does add a new UseOIDC property. When this property is set to true, the client proxy attaches the access token as a bearer token when generating a RESTful Web API request. The proxy derives the access token from the current claims principal of the application. The name of the access token claim should be access_token. 


Configuring Export Web Service for OpenID Connect
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/927251) After running the All Applications Configuration Wizard to configure the client for [OpenID Connect authentication type](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/PCblz~DnTSusA6DqgJ3nlA), you should rerun the Export Configuration Wizard. 
This ensures that the Export Web Service is configured for OpenID Connect. If the Export Client and Export Web Service exist on two different servers, then the All Applications Configuration Wizard should be executed on both of the servers to match the OpenID Connect configuration before running the Export Configuration Wizard on the Export server.

### OpenID Connect in Plotting
When OpenID Connect is configured as the authentication type for NetViewer, and if you are using NetViewer toPlotting integration, then the NetViewer application attaches the access token as a bearer token to the Authorization header before a Plotting service request is made. The Plotting service extracts the access token, validates it, and transforms it into a claim set. The service then interrogates the claim set to find out if a gtechnolgoyDBConnect claim exists. The database connection string extracted from the gtechnologyDBConnect claim is then delegated to the Plotting application server to connect to the database and process the plotting request. The same principles are applicable to external Plotting clients that are consuming the Plotting Web Service. The client applications are responsible for executing the OpenID Connect authentication sequence, getting the access token after a successful authentication, and then delegating the access token as a bearer token to the Plotting service. Mixed mode authentication type is not supported. If a client is configured to use OpenID Connect, then the Plotting service should also be configured to use OpenID Connect. 
If you do not want to use OpenID Connect as the authentication type, then both the client application and the services should be configured to run with the Anonymous authentication type. In this case, the connection string embedded as part of the Plotting request payload is used to connect to the database and process the plotting request. 
Changes to Plotting Web Service
  * Plotting Web Service is upgraded from ASMX technology stack to ASP.NET Web API 2.0. 
public static void AttachBearer (ref HttpWebRequest request)
{
ClaimsPrincipal user = HttpContext.Current.User as ClaimsPrincipal;
if (user != null && user.Identity.IsAuthenticated)
{
var accessToken = user.FindFirst("access_token");
if (accessToken != null && !String.IsNullOrEmpty(accessToken.Value))
{
request.Headers.Add("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken.Value); 
}
}
} 
  * ASMX is still supported for backward compatibility for existing clients that are directly referencing and consuming the Plotting
  * The same RESTful APIs (SendPlotRequest, GetPlotRequest) that were supported through ASMX are also supported through the Web API Controller. The OpenID Connect protocol is only supported through the Web API layer and not through the ASMX service calls. 


Changes to Plotting Client
  * For custom clients that want to support OpenID Connect, they should be updated to execute the OpenID Connect authentication sequence, acquire the access token after a successful authentication, and then delegate that access token as a bearer token to the Plotting Web Service. 
  * The client application cannot use the proxy generated by referencing the ASMX service when including support for OpenID Connect. The client application should be updated to make direct RESTful API calls to the Plotting Web Service by routing it through the ASP.NET Web API Controller. 
  * The client application is responsible for attaching the access token as a bearer token to the Authorization header of the Plotting web request. 
Example:
public static void AttachBearer (ref HttpWebRequest request)
{ 
ClaimsPrincipal user = HttpContext.Current.User as ClaimsPrincipal;
if (user != null && user.Identity.IsAuthenticated)
{
var accessToken = user.FindFirst("access_token");
if (accessToken != null && !String.IsNullOrEmpty(accessToken.Value))
{
request.Headers.Add("Authorization", "Bearer " + accessToken.Value); 
}
}
}

### User Claims for NetWorks Core

#### Custom Claims for NetWorks Core
NetWorks Core products expect two claims: role and gtechnologyDBConnect. The role claim represents an array of application roles (Gtechnology-Desktop, Gtechnology-NetViewer) that the user is a member of and gtechnologyDBConnect represents a multi-value attribute with multiple database connection strings assigned to a user. The claim is represented by the following: 
<Username>/<Password>@<Configuration>:<Application>
When determining what connection string to use, NetWorks Core products use the following filtering rule: 
  * For Designer/Analyst, the application looks for any connections whose Application value matches G/Designer and Configuration matches the selected configuration during login. If no such connection is found, it chooses the connection string with no Application value but whose Configuration matches the selected configuration. 
  * For NetViewer, the application looks for any connection whose Application value marches G/NetViewer and Configuration matches the selected configuration. If no such connection is found, the application chooses the connection string with no Application value but whose Configuration matches the selected configuration. 
  * Username and password can be blank (/@<Configuration>) for Designer/Analyst as this represents the connection string for Oracle Native Windows Authentication. But such a connection string is not supported for NetViewer as this can cause a significant performance bottleneck due to the connection context switch. 


If gtechnologyDBConnect claim is missing or no connection string was found for the current configuration, the user is prompted to enter the database credentials. 
As far as role claim is concerned:
  * The user can only use the Designer/Analyst application if the role claim includes Gtechnology-Desktop role. 
  * The user can only use the NetViewer application if the role claim includes Gtechnology-NetViewer role. 


![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/918978)
  * In addition to the application roles, NetWorks Core products use data base roles for application behavior. Database roles are acquired based on the Oracle user login. 
  * There is a distinction between application role and the Application value of the connection string. The application role (for example, Gtechnology-Desktop) is used to control the application accessibility and Application value within the connection string is used to assign different connection strings to different products depending on the role of the user in the company. For example, if the user is not assigned the Gtechnology-Desktop role, then they are denied access to Designer/Analyst application. If the user is allowed to use more than one product (Designer/Analyst and NetViewer) then the Application value within the connection string helps to distinguish the connections based on the application the user is connecting to. If the user is connecting to Designer/Analyst, then the connection string containing G/Designer as the Application value is chosen to make a connection to the database; otherwise the connection string with the blank Application value is used. If no such connection string is found in the gtechnologyDBConnect claim then the user is prompted to enter the database credentials.

#### NetWorks Core Authentication and Connection Mapping
With OpenID Connect, the application remains agnostic to the authentication method used. When you launch Designer/Analyst or NetViewer, the application redirects the user to execute the authentication sequence configured within the OIDC Provider. On successful authentication, the user is redirected back to the application with the access token. The access token contains the necessary claims required to authorize the application. One of the required claims returned from the identity store is the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute, which contains the NetWorks Core configuration database connecting mapping data. It is a multi-value attribute that you can use to store database connection data for each user. The following are possible authentication and connection mapping options: 
  * Windows credentials are used for authentication and an Oracle Windows authenticated user exists. In this option, the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute is not mapped to a database user. Instead the windows login credentials are used to authenticate database users. The option should not be used for NetViewer as it causes a significant performance bottleneck including the Kerberos Double Hop issue. 
  * Windows credentials are used for authentication and the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute is mapped to an Oracle username and password. In this option, the mapped username and password is used to connect to the NetWorks Core configuration database. 
  * If the OIDC Provider is configured for Basic Authentication, the entered username and password are used for authentication and the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute is mapped to an Oracle username and password. With this option, after the user is authenticated, the mapped username and password combination are used to connect to the NetWorks Core database. 


The format for the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute value is <Username>/<Password>@<Configuration> OR <Username>/<Password>@<Configuration>:<Application>, where the Application value indicates that the connection belongs to either Designer or NetViewer. The attribute represents a multi-value attribute and can allow multiple combinations of NetWorks Core database connection mapping per user. 
The gtechnologyDBConnect attribute value can have the following: 
  * Multiple entries—The <Configuration> is required for each entry. NetWorks Core products can connect to only the defined configuration by using the mapped username and password. 
  * Empty entry—NetWorks Core products can connect to any configuration defined in the .CCM file by using the Windows login when the database has been configured with a Windows authenticated user. 
  * Only one entry—If <Configuration> is provided, NetWorks Core products can connect to only the defined configuration by using the mapped username and password. If the <Configuration> is not provided, NetWorks Core can connect to any configuration defined in the .CCM file by using the mapped username and password. 


Unsupported Configurations
  * If the basic credentials (username and password) entered by the end user during login also represent the database connection username and password with the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute missing or set to NULL (empty), then this configuration is no longer supported by OIDC since the application is unaware of the credentials entered during the login process. 
  * In the case of NetViewer, you were previously allowed to configure the web application for Anonymous Authentication with the login user set to a domain user. The gtechnologyDBConnect attribute mapped to this domain credentials were used to perform the NetWorks Core database connection. Since the authentication pipeline is completely owned by the OIDC Provider and the application only care about the redirected access token, this configuration is no longer supported. 
  * With the introduction of OIDC, the type of identity store used depends on the OIDC Provider, so the management of the identity store is done by the toolkit provided by the corresponding vendor of the identity store. For example, AD LDS can be managed by using the ADSI Edit (MMC Snap-in tool) from Microsoft. The User Management Tool previously delivered with Identity and Access Management (IAM) is no longer available from the OIDC integration. With the User Management Tool, you were allowed to encrypt gtechnologyDBConnect attribute directly within the LDAP identity store. This is no longer supported with OIDC integration so you need to ensure that the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute value within the identity store is always available as clear text.

### ADFS 2016

#### Configure AD LDS for Custom Claims
If you are planning to use AD LDS for authentication and authorization, or just for authorization, you need to follow these steps. 
  * To configure AD LDS for Custom Claims:


  1. [Install AD LDS](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2008-R2-and-2008/cc754486%28v%3dws.10%29%20%20). 
  2. [Create an AD LDS instance](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2008-R2-and-2008/cc725619\(v%3dws.10\)%20). 
     * Use your own unique instance and partition name. 
     * Note the partition name. 
  3. Add application roles. NetWorks Core products support two application roles, Gtechnology-Desktop and Gtechnology-NetViewer, while NetWorks Core supports only one role, NetWorks-Portal. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/920915) These are the roles that control authorization; if a user does not have a particular application role assigned, the user is not authorized to run that application. 
    1. Create an LDIF (.ldf) file with the following content: 
dn: CN=Gtechnology-Desktop,CN=Roles,CN=SGI,DC=Intergraph,DC=COM
changetype: add
objectClass: top
objectClass: group
cn: Gtechnology-Desktop
distinguishedName: CN=Gtechnology-Desktop,CN=Roles,CN=SGI,DC=Intergraph,DC=COM
instanceType: 4
name: Gtechnology-Desktop
groupType: 4
dn: CN=Gtechnology-NetViewer,CN=Roles,CN=SGI,DC=Intergraph,DC=COM
changetype: add
objectClass: top

#### Configure ADFS 2016

##### Configuring for Basic Authentication
  * To configure (basic authentication):


In addition to performing the steps for general configuration (see [General Configuration Steps](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tjsqYn4JiVHn6j4QhlRzjw)), perform the following steps using the ADFS Management tool. 
  1. Click Service > Authentication Methods. 
  2. Click Edit Primary Authentication Methods in Actions. 
  3. Click Form Authentication for Extranet and Intranet. 
  4. Remove all other options for Extranet and Intranet. 


Using the powershell script
If you want to use AD LDS for authentication and authorization, you need to use the following powershell script to create a Local Claims Provider Trust. This Claims Provider Trust is not visible in the ADFS Management tool, so it must be managed by using the powershell script. 
When you provide credentials for the powershell script, they should be in the form User Principal Name (upn.) 
Example: user@domain.com. 
$Credential = Get-credential
$ldap_dir=New-AdfsLdapServerConnection -hostname <AD LDS Server FQDN> -port 389 -sslmode None -AuthenticationMethod negotiate -Credential $Credential
$email=New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute mail -ClaimType "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/email"
$givenName = New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute givenName -ClaimType "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/givenname"
$surname = New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute sn -ClaimType "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/surname"
$name = New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute name "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name"
$windowsaccountname = New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute name "http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/windowsaccountname"
$upn= New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute userPrincipalName -ClaimType "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/upn"
$gtechnologyDBConnect = New-AdfsLdapAttributeToClaimMapping -LdapAttribute gtechnologyDBConnect -ClaimType "http://schemas.intergraph.com/IAM/2009/01/identity/claims/attribute/gtechnologyDBConnect"
Add-AdfsLocalClaimsProviderTrust -Name "HSI AD LDS" -Identifier "urn:infrastructureADLDS" -type ldap `
-LdapServerConnection $ldap_dir `
-UserObjectClass organizationalPerson -UserContainer "CN=SGI,DC=Intergraph,DC=COM" `
-LdapAuthenticationMethod basic `
-AnchorClaimLdapAttribute userPrincipalName `
-AnchorClaimType "hhttp://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/upn" `
-AcceptanceTransformRules "c:[] => issue(claim=c);" -Enabled $true `
-LdapAttributeToClaimMapping @($email, $givenName, $surname, $upn, $name, $windowsaccountname, $gtechnologyDBConnect) `
The script should be changed as needed depending on your AD LDS instance configuration. The AnchorClaimLdapAttribute parameter represents the user name, so if you are using userPrincipalName as the anchor attribute, ensure that it is populated in the AD LDS instance and when logging in, ensure that the en user uses the value as the user name. Also, the UserContainer parameter represents the distinguished name (DN) where the users reside. 
In case you want to change something and recreate the Local Claims Provider Trust, you first need to remove the AD LDS identity store added as Claims Provider Trust. Use the following command line to remove it: 
Remove-AdfsLocalClaimsProviderTrust -TargetName "HSI AD LDS"
See [Configure AD FS to authenticate users stored in LDAP directories](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/operations/configure-ad-fs-to-authenticate-users-stored-in-ldap-directories) for more information.

##### Configuring for Single Sign-On
  * To configure (single sign-on):


In addition to performing steps for general configuration (see [General Configuration Steps](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tjsqYn4JiVHn6j4QhlRzjw)), perform the following steps using the ADFS Management tool. 
  1. Click Service > Authentication Methods. 
  2. Click Edit Primary Authentication Methods in Actions. 
  3. Click Forms Authentication for Extranet. 
  4. Remove all other options for Extranet.
  5. Click Windows Authentication and Forms Authentication for Intranet. 
  6. Remove all other options for Intranet.
  7. Configure the list of user agents using [Microsoft Help](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/operations/configure-intranet-forms-based-authentication-for-devices-that-do-not-support-wia). 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/918504) You need the powershell administrative command window to execute the cmdlets.

##### Configuring for Token Lifetime
Access Token Lifetime 
Configure Access Token Lifetime
By default, the Access Token Lifetime is set to zero, which means one hour. You can change this by running the following command line. 
Set-AdfsWebApiApplication -Name <Name of the web api application added> -TokenLifetime <value in minutes>
Example: Set-AdfsWebApiApplication -Name "NetWorks WebApp - Web API" -TokenLifetime 480
This sets the access token lifetime to eight hours.
Refresh Token Lifetime
By default, the Refresh Token expires after eight hours. To find the current value, run the following powershell commandlet. 
Get-ADFSProperties
Then check the value of SSOLifetime. The value is specified in minutes. 
To increase or decrease the lifetime of a Refresh Token use the following command line: 
Set-AdfsProperties –SsoLifetime <value in minutes>
Example: To increase the Refresh Token Lifetime: 
Set-AdfsProperties –SsoLifetime 1800

Use [Microsoft Help](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/operations/ad-fs-user-sign-in-customization) to customize the login page.

##### General Configuration Steps
  * To perform general configuration steps:


Regardless of the scenario you are using, you need to perform some general configuration steps to add an Application Group. 
  1. Launch AD FS Management through Server Manager. 
  2. Go to Service > Claim Descriptions. 
  3. Add a custom gtechnologyDBConnect claim: 
     * Display name: GTechnology Database Connection
     * Short Name: gtechnologyDBConnect
     * Claim type: http://schemas.intergraph.com/IAM/2009/01/identity/claims/attribute/gtechnologyDBConnect
  4. Add Application Group using the Add Application Group Wizard. 
     * Name: <Any Custom Name>
     * Template: Server application accessing a web API.
     * Client Identifier: Use a custom client identifier or use the default GUID. 
Note the Client Identifier value; you need to know the value during NetWorks Core configuration. 
     * Redirect URI: URL of your NetWorks Core Web App.
       * Ensure that it ends with a "/". 
       * Optional:  If you are using OpenID Connect with Designer/Analyst add "http://www.hexagonsafetyinfrastructure.com/"
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/920713) Since Designer/Analyst is not a web application and OpenID Connect is an HTTP based protocol, the URL serves as a facade URL for validation purpose. 
  5. Select Generate a Shared Secret. 
  6. Note the Client Secret value. You need to know the value during NetWorks Core configuration of the OpenID Connect provider using All Applications Configuration Wizard. 
  7. Configure Web API.
     * Name: Keep the default.
     * Identifier: Enter the same URL as the Redirect URI because there are not Web APIs at the application level. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/920713) All services use the same access token as bearer token delegated by the web application. 
     * Optional:  If you are using OpenID Connect with Designer/Analyst add http://www.hexagonsafetyinfrastructure.com/
     * Choose an access control policy: Permit everyone
     * Permitted Scopes: openid 
  8. Optional: If you are using AD LDS for storing your authorization claims (gtechnologyDBConnect and application roles), you need to add the AD LDS by clicking Service > Attribute Stores > Add Attribute Store in the Action pane. 
     * Display name:  <Any Custom Name>
     * Attribute store type: LDAP
     * Connection string: LDAP://<Server FQDN>/<Distinguished name for the LDAP Store>. Example: LDAP://PSL-MBRE-APP.infrastructure.local/cn=HSI,dc=Intergraph,dc=com
  9. Add Issuance Transform Rules by going to Relying Party Trusts. 
  10. Click Edit Claim Issuance Policy. 
The rule varies based on the scenario. You need to ensure that:
     * A rule is added to transform a unique username to a Subject claim.
     * A rule is added to extract the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute. 
     * A set of rules are added to return the user group membership as roles.
The following represents the required rules for using AD for authentication and AD LDS for authorization. These rules may vary from one scenario to another. 
     * Transform Windows Account Name into Subject claim.
Claim rule template: Transform an Incoming claim
Claim rule name: Transform Windows Account Name into Subject claim 
Incoming claim type: Windows account name
Outgoing claim type: Name ID
Outgoing name ID Format: Unspecified
Select: Pass through all claim clauses. 
     * Send GTechnology DBConnect attribute as claims.
Claim rule templates: Send Claims Using a Custom Rule
Claim rule name: Send Gtechnology DBConnect attribute as claims
Claim rule: c:[Type == "http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/windowsaccountname"]
=> issue(store = "LDAP Attribute Store", types = ("http://schemas.intergraph.com/IAM/2009/01/identity/claims/attribute/gtechnologyDBConnect"), query = "name={0};gtechnologyDBConnect", param = regexreplace(c.Value, "(?<domain>[^\\\\]+)\\\\(?<user>.+)", "${user}"));
LDAP Attribute Store represents name of your attribute store that you want to use. If your gtechnologyDBConnect attribute exists directly in AD or AD LDS without requiring cross mapping of user identity from one identity store (AD) to a different identity store (AD LDS), then you can directly create a pass through claim that maps the LDAP attribute to a claim. 
  11. To pull list or roles, you need to add three distinct custom rules: 
     * Pull memberOf attribute and add as phase1. 
Claim rule template: Send Claims Using a Custom Rule.
Claim rule name: Pull memberOf attribute and add as phase1.
Claim rule: c:[Type == "http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/windowsaccountname"]
=> add(store = "LDAP Attribute Store", types = ("http://test.com/phase1"), query = "name={0};memberOf", param = regexreplace(c.Value, "(?<domain>[^\\\\]+)\\\\(?<user>.+)", "${user}"));
LDAP Attribute Store represents name of your attribute store that you want to use. If the attribute store is Active Directory then instead of name=, you have to use sAMAccountName=. 
     * Drop everything after the first comma and add as a phrase2Claim rule template: Send Claims using a Custom Rule. 
Claim rule name: Drop everything after the first comma and add as phase2.
Claim rule: c:[Type == "http://test.com/phase1"]
=> add(Type = "http://test.com/phase2", Value = RegExReplace(c.Value, ",[^\n]*", ""));
     * Drop CN, add to outgoing role claimClaim rule template: Send claims Using a Custom Rule. 
Claim rule name: DropCN, add to outgoing role claim.
Claim rule: c:[Type == "http://test.com/phase2"]
=> issue(Type = "http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role", Value = RegExReplace(c.Value, "^CN=", ""));
  12. Add additional claim rules for attributes that you need to include in the access token.

#### Install ADFS 2016
Prerequisites 
Before you begin the installation and setup of ADFS 2016, you need the following prerequisites:
  * A Windows Server 2016 machine that is registered to the same Domain Active Directory that the ADFS instance communicates with. 
  * Domain Administrative Account. This account is required to either register the new ADFS instance to an existing ADFS farm or a new ADFS farm. 
  * An SSL certificate to service HTTPS requests. This certificate can be a third party certificate that can be imported or a certificate from either a Standalone or Enterprise Certificate Authority. 


See [AD FS Requirements](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/overview/ad-fs-requirements) for further details. 
Installing and Configuring ADFS 2016
Before you can install and configure ADFS, you need to import an SSL Certificate as it is required by ADFS for authentication. You can either use a third party SSL Certificate or Microsoft's Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) for establishing a Standalone or Enterprise Certificate Authority. 
See the following articles that describe in detail how you can setup ADFS with AD CS. 
  * [Installing AD Federation Service on Windows Server 2016](https://geekdudes.wordpress.com/2017/01/03/installing-ad-federation-service-on-windows-server-2016/)
  * [Windows 2016 Active Directory Services (AD CS)](https://www.vembu.com/blog/windows-2016-active-directory-certificate-services-ad-cs/)


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/918501) The content at the above links does not belong to Hexagon's Safety & Infrastructure division and Hexagon's Safety & Infrastructure division cannot guarantee that the content at the above links will not be modified, removed, or otherwise changed by its owners. 
You can fix the Service Principal Name (SPN) errors by creating the SPNs for the server machine where ADFS 2016 is installed. The following command lines need to be executed on the domain controller, which may require assistance from the domain administrator: 
setspn -s http/<Net Bios Name of the Server> <Service Account provided during ADFS installation>
setspn -s http/<FQDN of the Server> <Service Account provided during ADFS installation>
You can ignore the SSL certificate errors, but if you would like to resolve them, see this article on [AD FS Support for Alternate Hostname Binding for Certificate Authentication](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/operations/ad-fs-support-for-alternate-hostname-binding-for-certificate-authentication).

#### Migrating to OIDC Using ADFS 2016
When migrating from an existing Identity and Access Management (IAM) based solution, you need to consider the following scenarios: 
  * Using Active Directory (AD) for both authentication and authorization. In this scenario, the user is authenticated using Windows (domain) credentials and the authorization claims are stored in AD. See the following topics to address this migration scenario: 
    * [General Configuration Steps](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tjsqYn4JiVHn6j4QhlRzjw)
    * [Configuring for Single Sign-On](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5ljb4ZXdk5HUeTX11AvNFg)
  * Using Active Directory Lightweight Directory Service (AD LDS) for both authentication and authorization. In this scenario, the user provides the username and password for authentication and the authorization claims are stored in the AD LDS instance. See the following topics to address this migration scenario: 
    * [General Configuration Steps](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tjsqYn4JiVHn6j4QhlRzjw)
    * [Configuring for Basic Authentication](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Wy_nh5Cl6aD9CWlQSrENpg)
  * Using Active Directory (AD) for authentication and Active Directory Lightweight Directory Service (AD LDS) for authorization. In this scenario, the user is authenticated using Windows (domain) credentials and the authorization claims are stored in the AD LDS instance. See the following topics to address this migration scenario: 
    * [General Configuration Steps](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/tjsqYn4JiVHn6j4QhlRzjw)
    * [Configuring for Single Sign-On](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/5ljb4ZXdk5HUeTX11AvNFg)

### Encrypting Text with GTEncTool
Overview
GTEncTool is a command line tool that encrypts a string from the command line (standard input) and displays the encrypted value in standard output (console). 
This tool provides an encryption and decryption mechanism for the database connect attribute at rest (in the OpenID Connect Provider storage) and during transit (in the access token). 
It provides a means to decrypt the attribute in consumer applications (HxGN NetWorks Core Designer, HxGN NetWorks Core Web Services, HxGN NetWorks Core Comms). 
Workflow
The input string is symmetrically encrypted using a fixed key, with the encrypted value being stored in the OIDC provider. The input string is received from the access token and decrypted when the user logs into NetWorks Core Designer. The decrypted value is then used by components down the execution pathway. 
Command Line Reference
Usage:
GTEncTool.exe <input>  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  <input>  |  Input string to be encrypted  |  
|  -h  |  Writes help to console  |  
|  -help  |  Writes help to console  |  
Return codes:  
|  Option  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  0  |  Success  |  
|  1  |  None or empty input string  |  
|  9  |  Other unspecified error  |  
Return codes appear in the exit code of the GTEncTool.exe process. For example, when called from a .bat file, the return code will be available in the %ERRORLEVEL% variable. 
Example:
GTEncTool.exe string

### General Guidance for OpenID Connect Provider Configuration
  * The clients, or relying parties, rely on the discovery endpoint to dynamically obtain information about the authorization server. The "issuer" parameter is combined with ".well-known/openid-configuration" when requesting the discovery document. You need to ensure that this discovery endpoint is available to the client. 
  * The web application delegates the access token as a bearer token to the services. Since possession of a bearer token is enough to use the token, it is important that the communication between endpoints is secured so that only authorized endpoints may use the token. 
  * An access token is used by a client to access a resource. Access tokens typically should have a short life span (minutes or hours.) An access token may be refreshed by using a refresh token. A refresh token, coupled with a short access token lifetime, can be used to grant access to resources without requiring end-user authorization. The lifetime of both the access token and the refresh token are controlled by the authorization server. The authorization server can revoke the refresh token at any time, causing the access to be revoked once the current access token expires. Because of this, it is important that the token has a short lifetime. 
  * An access token can either be transparent or opaque. If you want the client application to parse the access token and retrieve the required claims without having to go back to the UserInfo endpoint, then you need to configure the authorization server to include the custom required claims within the access token payload. Such access tokens are referred to as transparent because the client needs to see through them to control accessibility. Transparent access tokens may contain critical custom claims, so the transmission of such a token should be protected when these tokens are delegated to the services as bearer tokens. Passing the bearer token as opaque to the service and letting the service request the user profile information through the UserInfo endpoint is considered more secure as the token needs to be validated by the authorization server before claims are issued. However, this may not be feasible with some OIDC providers (for example, Active Directory Federation Services or ADFS) whose UserInfo endpoint always returns a single "sub" claim. 
  * An authorization code represents the intermediate result of a successful end-user authorization and is used by the client to obtain both the access token and refresh token. The authorization code is sent as part of the redirect URI of the client, which exposes the protocol parameters to potential attackers through query parameters. To reduce the potential threat, short-lived authorization codes are passed to exchange them for tokens over a more secure direct connection between the client and the authorization server. 
  * The client identifier is used to collate associated requests to the same originator. To maintain the confidentiality of a client, OAuth allows the client identifiers to be associated with a client secret. It is important to secure this client secret as it can be used to replay the refresh tokens or authorization codes. It can also be used to obtain tokens on behalf of the attacked client. 
  * A potential attacker could use the end-user authorization endpoint and the redirect URI parameter to abuse the authorization server as an open redirector. An open redirector is an endpoint that automatically redirects a client to the specified parameter without validation. To prevent this, the software validates both the client ID and the redirect URI. You need to ensure that the full redirect URIs are registered within the authorization server for a given client. 
  * All communications between the authorization server and the client should be protected using HTTPS for the following reasons: 
    * Access tokens are shared secrets between the authorization server and the resource server. They should be treated with the same care as other credentials. An attacker may attempt to eavesdrop access tokens that are in transit from the authorization server to the client. 
    * An attacker could try to get access to the client secret, enabling the attacker to use the stolen refresh tokens or authorization codes for replay attacks. 
    * An attacker could try to eavesdrop transmission of the authorization codes between the authorization server and client. In addition, the authorization codes are passed through the browser, which may unintentionally leak those codes to untrusted web sites and attackers. 
    * Refresh tokens are considered as long-term credentials that may be subject to eavesdropping and theft. Protecting refresh tokens during transport is crucial for reducing the attack surface. 
  * To prevent potential attackers from reusing old refresh tokens to gain access to multiple applications, it is important to change the refresh token with every refresh request. This means that refresh tokens must have a one-time use. With every refresh request, along with getting a new access token, the authorization server also issues a new refresh token. Once a refresh token is used to issue a new access token, the refresh token is no longer valid. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/919468) It is important to develop a high-level risk mitigation strategy by first understanding the threat model associated with deploying such a solution. Most of the policies and configuration to mitigate the risk level is configured within the authorization server (OIDC provider.) 
Related Topic
[OAuth2.0 Threat Model and Security Considerations](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6819#page-25)

### Keycloak

#### Migrating to OIDC Using Keycloak

##### Use Active Directory (AD) for Authentication and Active Directory Lightweight Directory Service (AD LDS) for Authorization
  * To use Windows Authentication: 


The built-in Kerberos User Federation in Keycloak links Keycloak to your Active Directory, enabling your users to sign on using their Windows accounts. 
  1. Click User Federation in Keycloak. 
  2. Click add a new Kerberos provider from the drop-down. 
  3. Complete the required fields in the Required Settings display. 
![Required Settings](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/kelTcDW9Ut63ZIk2nI8RaA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=2634349f81f2e094&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/921255) The realm and principal you provide here must match those you used in generating the keytab file. 
  4. Click Save. 
Users can now log in using Windows Authentication. 


  * To map user attributes:


  1. Click Client. 
  2. Click your client from the drop-down list.
  3. Click Mappers. 
  4. Click Create New. 
  5. Complete all fields in the Create New display. 
![GtechnologydbConnect](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/bJ2JSxfWTucdyK3eZIg2WQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=aa3526a840a59eba&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
User Attribute is the name of the Attribute in the AD LDS that you want to map. 
Token Claim Name is the name you should give the attribute in Keycloak. The Token Claim Name is also the name that the attribute has in your claims. 
Claim JSON type is usually String. 
  6. Click Save. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/921255) Your attribute is typically kept with the userinfo, however, if you want it sent back with the ID or Access Token, you must set them to On. 


Importing AD LDS User Attributes
Next, you need to import the AD LDS user attributes into Keycloak. Keycloak does not work with a "mixed bag" configuration where Authentication is in one store and User Attributes is in another. Because of this, user attributes stored in AD LDS must be migrated into Keycloak, where Keycloak can manage and store the attributes. This requires manual steps. 
User attributes can be set per user, but this may not be feasible if there are many users. The easiest way to set attributes for multiple users is to put the users into groups based on their user attributes. Keycloak can automatically assign users to default groups, giving them the user attributes of that group. But using this function, you do not need to set individual values for each user. 
Setting up Keycloak to Match the AD LDS Configuration
To set up Keycloak to match the configuration of your AD LDS, you need to run this script that you can use to profile your system. The script produces a CSV file that shows a list of users, the groups they belong to, and their gtechnologyDBConnect claims that our products use. This way, you can model your Keycloak environment after your AD LDS environment. 
  * To create user attribute groups:


For example, let's assume most of your users share a gtechnologyDBConnect claim with the value "Networks." 
  1. In Keycloak, click Group. 
  2. Click New.
  3. Enter a name for the group in the field. 
  4. Click Attributes. 
  5. Add any attribute that you want the members of the group to have. 
![NetWorksDBClaim](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/yxBGPa5qSieS651aT6P79g-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=16906a1c94f4003a&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  6. In Default Groups, you can assign a group for new users to join. 
     * Click Groups > Default Groups to assign a new default group. 
OR
If you do not want to use a default group for new users, you can assign users to a specific group by editing the page of the user. 
     * Click Users to view user pages and add users to groups. 
Example: Any user added to the NetworksDBClaim group, would get the gtechnologyDBConnect attribute.

##### Use Active Directory (AD) for Both Authentication and Authorization
  * To let users use Windows Authentication:


The built-in Kerberos User Federation in Keycloak links Keycloak to your Active Directory, enabling your users to sign on using their Windows accounts. 
  1. Click User Federation in Keycloak. 
  2. Click add new Kerberos provider from the drop-down list. 
  3. Complete all fields in the Required Settings display. 
![Required Settings](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/kelTcDW9Ut63ZIk2nI8RaA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=2634349f81f2e094&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/921251) The Kerberos Realm and Server Principal you provide must match those you used in generating the keytab file. 
  4. Click Save. 
Users can now log in using Windows Authentication. 


  * To map user attributes:


The user attributes are pulled automatically with the account from the Active Directory. The user attributes must be mapped so that they display as Keycloak attributes. 
  1. Click Client. 
  2. Click your client from the drop-down list.
  3. Click Mappers. 
  4. Click Create New. 
  5. Complete all fields in the Create New display. 
![GtechnologydbConnect](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/bJ2JSxfWTucdyK3eZIg2WQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=aa3526a840a59eba&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
User Attribute is the name of the Attribute in the Active Directory that you want to map. 
Token Claim Name is the name you want to give the attribute in Keycloak. This is also the name that it has in your claims. 
Claim JSON type is typically String. 
Your attribute is typically kept with the userinfo, however, if you want it sent back with the ID Token or Access Token, you must set them to On. 
  6. Click Save. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/921251) User Attribute is the mapper type that is applicable for most situations. This is for mapping LDAP user attributes to value you want to use in Keycloak.

##### Use Active Directory Lightweight Directory Service (AD LDS) for Both Authentication and Authorization
If you are using AD LDS for both authentication and the user attribute storage, you have a few options when migrating to Keycloak. Keycloak can act as a front end manager and broker for AD LDS, letting you edit, add, and remove users, while keeping AD LDS as the storage system. You can also import all the users and their settings, storing them internally to Keycloak. In the second case, you can remove AD LDS, now using only Keycloak to manage your users. 
  * To use Basic Authentication: 


  1. Click User Federation. 
  2. Click Create New LDAP from the drop-down list. 
![migrating 2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/VZ_sdM1A2NY7sj5jtuEm6Q-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=d1acd9285a6d9d5c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. To use Keycloak as a broker to manage AD LDS, click Writable from the Edit Mode drop-down list. 
OR
To import users into Keycloak and remove AD LDS:
    1. Click On for Import Users. 
If this is turned off, Keycloak does not store the users. 
    2. Click Unsynced from the Edit Mode drop-down list. 
The values are now brought into Keycloak and they do not need to be validated back to the AD LDS. 
    3. After the users are imported, the User Federation connect can be removed by deleting it or disabling it in the User Federation tab. 


  * To map user attributes:


The user attributes are pulled automatically with the account from AD LDS. The user attributes must be mapped so that they display as Keycloak attributes. 
  1. Click Client. 
  2. Click your client from the drop-down list. 
  3. Click Mappers. 
  4. Click Create New. 
  5. Complete all fields in the Create New display. 
![GtechnologydbConnect](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/bJ2JSxfWTucdyK3eZIg2WQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=aa3526a840a59eba&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
User Attribute is the name of the Attribute in the Active Directory that you want to map. 
Token Claim Name is the name you want to give the attribute in Keycloak. The Token Claim Name is also the name that the attribute has in your claims. 
Claim JSON type is usually String. 
Your attribute is typically kept with the userinfo, however, if you want it sent back with the ID Token or Access Token, you must set them to On. 
  6. Click Save. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/921252) User Attribute is the mapper type that is applicable for most situations. This is for mapping LDAP user attributes to value you want to use in Keycloak.

#### Quick Install Guide

##### Create a New Realm
Keycloak, by default, has a Master realm. It is recommended that you create your own realm to work with. Each realm separates your users and administrators into the appropriate configurations. Without creating realms, the administrators have access to all the users and all the configurations. 
Related Topics
[Master Realm Information](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#the-master-realm)
[Creating a New Realm](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#_create-realm)

##### Disable or Configure HTTPS
By default, Keycloak is configured to only allow external requests through HTTPS/SSL. Until that is configured, Keycloak cannot be accessed externally. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/917289) For development purposes only, HTTPS/SSL can be disabled, letting all external requests in. 
Related Topic
[Enabling HTTPS/SSL](http://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_installation/index.html#setting-up-https-ssl).

##### Managing Users
You should set up users so that potential users can login and use OIDC. 
There are many ways to manage users in Keycloak. 
  * You can use Keycloak as a user store directly, managing and creating the users directly inside of Keycloak. Keycloak is also able to act as a broker and essentially a management front-end for whatever store you are using. 
  * Typically, though, your users are in their own store, like Active Directory, and you should use these stores for OIDC. Depending on how you want this configured, you can import the users into Keycloak and manage them or Keycloak can simply link to your user store for authentication. 


Related Topics
  * [To create users directly into Keycloak.](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#user-management)
  * The Keycloak guide to using Windows Authentication with Active Directory or AD LDS: 
    * [To set up Kerberos.](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#_kerberos)
    * [To set up User Federation.](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#_user-storage-federation)
  * Hexagon's Safety & Infrastructure division's guide to migrating to OIDC using Keycloak, specifically dealing with a few scenarios of User Stores and how to create User Stores with Keycloak. 
    * To migrate to OIDC using Keycloak. (see [Migrating to OIDC Using Keycloak](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ytqaesXs0Gb7PgrcO8ZHKA))

##### Mapping User Attributes
Your users need to have various attributes to work with NetWorks Core products.
NetWorks Web Services Claims
The only custom claim expected by NetWorks Web Services is gtechnologyDBConnect, which is a multi-value attribute with multiple database connection strings assigned to a user. 
The claim is represented by the following format: 
<Username>/<Password>@<Configuration>:<Application>
NetWorks Core Claims
NetWorks Core products expect two claims: "role" and gtechnologyDBConnect. The role claim represents an array of application roles (for example, NetWorks Core-Desktop or NetWorks Core-NetViewer) of which the user can be a member. gtechnolgoyDBConnect represents a multi-value attribute with multiple database connection string assigned to a user. The claim is represented by the following format: 
<Username>/<Password>@<Configuration>:<Application>
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/917274) For multi-value attributes, Keycloak uses a "##" separator. For example, when using gtechnologyDBConnect: username1/password1@configuration1:app1##username2/password2.....
Related Topics
  * [To set attributes manually in Keycloak or use groups to manage attributes.](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#user-attributes)
  * [To map attributes to claims so that NetWorks Core can use them.](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#_protocol-mappers)
Example: This maps the gtechnologyDBConnect user attribute (either from your store or set in Keycloak itself) and assigns it to the value gtechnologyDBConnect in the OIDC Claim. 
![GtechnologydbConnect](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/bJ2JSxfWTucdyK3eZIg2WQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=aa3526a840a59eba&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

### G3E_COMPONENTINFO_OPTABLE (Component Info Optimized Table)
Table name: G3E_COMPONENTINFO_OPTABLE 
This optimization should include synthesized geometry.
NetWorks Core uses the G3E_SRID column to set the SDO_GEOMETRY.SDO_SRID value during new feature placement; however, the application does not use SDO_SRID or set it during edit operations. NetWorks Core uses the information in the GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE rather than Oracle spatial referencing technology.

### G3E_FINDFEATURE_OPTABLE
This optimized table is used to populate the drop-down list of features in the Find Feature command. It is used to ease reduction of memory consumption. This table is a subset of the G3E_FIND_OPTABLE and is automatically generated during metadata publishing. This table is reserved for the Product Center. As with other optimized tables, you should not edit it directly.

### G3E_STYLECOLORS_OPTABLE
This optimized table contains all of the color values that are used in the metadata styles. It is used to quickly create color palettes for various workflows. It is used to ease reduction of memory consumption. This table is reserved for the Product Center. As with other optimized tables, you should not edit it directly.

### G3E_COMPONENTINFO_OPTABLE (Component Info Optimized Table)
Table name: G3E_COMPONENTINFO_OPTABLE 
This optimization should include synthesized geometry.
NetWorks Core uses the G3E_SRID column to set the SDO_GEOMETRY.SDO_SRID value during new feature placement; however, the application does not use SDO_SRID or set it during edit operations. NetWorks Core uses the information in the GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE rather than Oracle spatial referencing technology.

## Reduce Metadata Consumption Optables

### G3E_FINDFEATURE_OPTABLE
This optimized table is used to populate the drop-down list of features in the Find Feature command. It is used to ease reduction of memory consumption. This table is a subset of the G3E_FIND_OPTABLE and is automatically generated during metadata publishing. This table is reserved for the Product Center. As with other optimized tables, you should not edit it directly.

### G3E_STYLECOLORS_OPTABLE
This optimized table contains all of the color values that are used in the metadata styles. It is used to quickly create color palettes for various workflows. It is used to ease reduction of memory consumption. This table is reserved for the Product Center. As with other optimized tables, you should not edit it directly.

# Raster Information

## Controlling the Amount of Memory for Raster Display
These keys are located in the registry tree.
Several registry keys control the amount of memory and the size of the cache used by the raster display system. It is recommended that these be left at their default values unless you experience significant raster performance problems. 
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RasMemLimit  |  This value affects only the performance of binary raster images. It indicates how much memory (in megabytes) the raster display system can use for image data. The value is a string, and the default value is 10, indicating 10 megabytes of memory. This string value is the default and not an added key. If you have a lot of memory on your system, and you display a lot of raster data, increasing this value might improve performance. Conversely, if you have low memory, decreasing this value improves performance of the product overall.   |  
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\RasterCache  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  cacheLimit  |  This value sets the number of images that are retained in memory in the raster cache for the process. This includes all images. The raster cache holds information on images and pointers to the raster engine used to display them. No pixel data are contained in the cache. This is handled by the raster engines. The value is a string, and the default value is 300.   |  
|  MemoryMapUNC  |  This value determines if memory mapping is done on images specified by a UNC path. The default value is 1. This entry is only necessary to allow memory mapping to be cut off for UNC-specified images if necessary to avoid network drop out problems with handling of UNC paths that are memory mapped.  1=Memory mapping is done. 0=Memory mapping is not done.  |  
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\RasterCore  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RasStripBuffer  |  This value affects only the performance of binary raster images. It indicates the approximate amount of memory used for internal operations (such as resampling and rotating) on raster images before displaying or printing the images. The value of this key is not set by default. If the registry key is not set, NetWorks Core computes the size of this buffer based on the size and resolution of the display device, creating a buffer size that is typically about 3 megabytes.  In most cases, raster images are acceptably displayed and printed using the default buffer size. Printing and plotting operations with large page sizes and large images or rotated images may benefit from a significantly larger buffer size. For example, large plots (up to A0 size) that contain rotated raster images on HP-PCL printers can produce huge spool files if the default buffer size is used. You can reduce the size of the spool files by 80 percent or more by changing the buffer size to 50 megabytes. This change can have a correspondingly positive effect on printing and/or plotting performance. To affect batch plotting performance, change the registry setting on the Plotting application server.  Conversely, if you increase this buffer size too much, the change can negatively affect behavior and performance of NetWorks Core and your system in general. For example, NetWorks Core could run out of memory, fail to access DDC files, or perform poorly (due to excessive paging) if excessive memory is allocated to this buffer. Each installation is different, so test your behavior and performance carefully after changing this setting.   |

## Displaying Raster Images
NetWorks Core supports the display of raster images that use these compression algorithms:   
|  Format  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CCITTG4  |  Consultative Committee on International Telephone and Telegraph Group 4 format is standard for transmission and storage of bilevel facsimile images.   |  
|  JPEG  |  Joint Photographic Experts Group format uses a block-by-block conversion to frequency space and stores a discrete cosine series representation of the frequency space. Hardware dependent: Requires Hexagon JPEG compression board (CLIX) or Hexagon Video Engine board (Intel).   |  
|  LZW  |  Lempel-Ziv & Welch algorithm compresses binary, grayscale, or color data.  |  
|  PB  |  Packbits algorithm compresses binary, grayscale, or color data. Packbits and Hexagon Type 29 are good for general- purpose raster data, continuous-tone imagery, and RLE data. For certain types of images, such as map images, significantly better disk compression is achieved with a different RLE format, such as Hexagon Type 9.   |  
|  RLE  |  Run-Length Encoded. A run length is a unit that describes a series of contiguous pixels in a raster line that all have the same value. Run lengths are used to achieve data compression in binary scanned data and color run-length data. Long sequences of 0s, 1s, or identical color indexes are identified and recorded using less data than would otherwise be required to list the individual values of the series of pixels.   |  
|  Wavelet  |  An algorithm for grayscale and color data. Used by MrSID, ECW, and JPEG2000 format images.   |  
|  Tiling  |  When raster data becomes large, it may be necessary to subdivide it into smaller sections that can be loaded into memory and manipulated individually. These sections are called tiles. A tiled raster file consists of the standard raster-file header, immediately followed by additional data specifying the tile information. Tiling does not make the raster file smaller, so it is not a compression technique. Rather, it breaks a raster file into manageable parts that the system can use more easily. Tiling a file often speeds up interactive display and editing operations. But tiling a run-length- encoded file can make the file much larger on the disk.   |

|  Placement Mode  |  File Types and Extensions  |

|   |  .tif, .tiff  |  .jpg, .jpeg  |  .sid  |  .ecw  |  .cot, .rgb, .cit  |  .doq, .key  |   |  
|  Hexagon Geo-Tie Information  |  -  |  -  |  -  |  -  |  X  |  -  |   |  
|  GeoTIFF  |  X  |  -  |  -  |  -  |  -  |  -  |   |

|  Other With External Coordinate System  |  -  |  -  |  -  |  X  |  -  |  -  |   |  
Note: Most ECW files do not require a World file. Use the Other with external coordinate system file mode of georeferencing, and provide a .csf that defines the coordinate system of the ECW files. This is the preferred method for georeferenced placement of ECW. Also, be sure to use the [ImageStation Raster Utilities](javascript:;) Display Header option to determine file format; file extensions are often incorrect or misleading.

## Supported Data Types for Raster Images
NetWorks Core supports the following data types for raster images:   
|  Data Type  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Binary  |  Consists of pixels that are either on or off to represent the foreground and background data. Uncompressed binary data requires one bit to store each pixel.   |  
|  Grayscale or continuous tone  |  Contains coded intensity values usually ranging from 0 to 255. Generally uses one byte (8 bits) of data to represent each pixel.   |  
|  8-Bit Color  |  Uses a color table in the file header to identify the color of each pixel. As with grayscale data, each uncompressed pixel is represented by one byte of data. This byte of data points to a color- table entry containing a 24-bit color definition. There may be up to 256 slots in a color table, although all of the slots may not necessarily be used.   |  
|  24-Bit Color  |  Requires three bytes of data to represent the color of each pixel. Each byte represents the intensity of a color: one byte for red, one byte for green, and one byte for blue. The different intensities of all three colors combine to create all other possible colors. For example, a lemon-yellow pixel might be stored with an intensity value of 255 red, 219 green, and 109 blue.   |

## Supported Raster Formats
Placement options:
  * G = Georeferenced (if GeoTIFF tags or geo- tie packet is available)
  * H = By header (requires .csf file or .dgn file) 
  * I = Interactive
  * W = Georeferenced through World File support (*.tfw, *.sdw, *.jgw). You must provide a .csf or .dgn file that names the coordinate system along with the World File information.
