# System Administration and Maintenance

## Add-Ons

### Configuring a NetWorks Core Add-On
The following are basic steps for configuring a NetWorks Core add-on: 
  1. Implement the IGTAddOn interface located in the public API Intergraph.GTechnology.dll assembly. 
Check out the sample class GTAddOn.cs located in C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries\NetSamples\DotNetSamples folder, 
  2. The add-on \Program folder should contain all the binaries for add-ons including the implemented IGTAddOn interface assembly and the \Program must exist underneath the path defined by the InstallDir
Example:
When you installHxGN NetWorks CommsNetWorks Core add-on), the folder structure is as shown below. The \Program folder contains the binaries for HxGN NetWorks Comms and the \IncrementalUpgrades folder contains the incremental upgrade scripts. 
![GTechAddOn](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/HYbQdamX5ZvTKFwTfxzgfA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=72c3741126ef184a&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
TheInstallDir path in the registry is the parent add-on folder, which in the case ofHxGN NetWorks Comms is C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\FiberOpticWorks. 
  3. Populate the G3E_ADDON.G3E_INTERFACE column with the implemented IGTAddOn class name in the format shown below: 
<AssemblyName>:<TypeName>
where:
<AssemblyName> is the filename of the assembly and <TypeName> is the type name. 
(namespace.classname) of the class which implements the IGTAddOn interface.
  4. Populate the G3E_ADDON.G3E_NAMEPREFIX column with the unique prefix you have chosen for your add-on objects, for example, GAO_FIBER. To find a unique prefix and report it back to the Support team:: 
    1. Go to [Support](https://smartcommunity.hexagonppm.com/s/). 
    2. Under the Please Sign In heading, type your username and password and click Login. If you are not a registered user, click the Not a Registered User? link. 
    3. In the Knowledge Search field, type NOTE574,and click Search. 
    4. Open the document and follow the instructions in it.
  5. If your add-on includes custom commands, you must provide a resource-only DLL called Icons.drx in the \Program folder for the add-on. 
  6. If your add-on supplies placement icons, they must be merged into the resource-only DLL file identified in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.G3E_VALUE where G3E_NAME is PlacementSelectionIconDRXFile. For more information, see the [Placement Selection](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/jFXGGj6Okzub1tAkZoFYlg) and [Creating Placement Selection Icons](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xGgxn7TZS~Le32Qi7DBg6w) topics. 
  7. Publish metadata.

### Configuring a Ribbon for NetWorks Core Add-On
It is possible to configure tabs/groups/commands available on the ribbon using proper metadata. Thanks to this capability, users will not lose any of their previous ribbon customizations. 
  * To configure the ribbon for NetWorks Core Add-on:


  1. Customize the ribbon through metadata by defining tabs, groups, and commands information in the G3E_ADDONRIBBONTABS, G3E_ADDONRIBBONGROUPS, and G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAYOUT metadata tables. 
  2. By default, G3E_RIBBONVER field value in G3E_ADDON table is set to 0.
  3. After adding the data to G3E_ADDONRIBBONTABS , G3E_ADDONRIBBONGROUPS, and G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAYOUT tables, increment G3E_RIBBONVER value to 1 and publish the metadata. 
  4. G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAOYUT_OPTABLE table is generated.
  5. When NetWorks Core application is opened by the administrator/analyst, the ribbon appears. It contains all changes made in Step 1 (new tabs, groups, and custom commands). The previous customers’ customizations are available. 
  6. The administrator can make further changes through the Metadata Explorer and publish them. All the information will be saved to G3E_MENULAYOUT table. These modifications will be available to all users, including the Add-on tabs created from G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAOYUT_OPTABLE. 


  * To upgrade the NetWorks Core Add-on:


For a subsequent release of the Add-On product, there can be new commands and new layout required to be updated on the ribbon. In that case, the new layout of the ribbon can be configured using the following steps: 
  1. Customize the ribbon bar by adding new tabs, groups, and commands information for the new release in the G3E_ADDONRIBBONTABS , G3E_ADDONRIBBONGROUPS and G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAYOUT metadata tables. 
  2. The new customization is applied only if G3E_RIBBONVER is increased by at least 1. This resets the ribbon with the data in the G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAOYUT_OPTABLE. 
  3. If the G3E_RIBBONVER is not increased, the existing ribbon layout is displayed.


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/1390371) It is recommended not to add any customizations for the tabs created with G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAOYUT_OPTABLE. Whenever the G3E_RIBBONVER is upgraded, it resets the tabs with the data in G3E_ADDONRIBBONLAOYUT_OPTABLE, so the user’s changes for these tabs will be lost. 
  * To assign a shortcut key to the add-on custom commands:


  1. Right-click the ribbon and click Customize the Ribbon.... 
  2. The Customize dialog appears. In this dialog, click Customize.... 
![Ribbon3](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/NnHHLKeEFvbDQJj25oUDHQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=2abe18bf16065a5a&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  3. The Customize Keyboard dialog is opened: 
![Ribbon2](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/fe_GVjghr5Mh2uCIL7Brhw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=220686056a774a63&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  4. Select All Commands in the Categories list, then select a desired command from the Commands list to update the shortcut command. 
  5. Enter a shortcut key in the Press new shortcut key text box with keyboard (for example, Shift + B) and click Assign. 
  6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 for all the required custom commands to assign the shortcut keys.
  7. Close the dialog.
  8. The shortcut keys are ready to use. 


![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/1390371) The administrator can customize shortcut keys using the Metadata Explorer command and publish these changes to all the users.

### Upgrading NetWorks Core Add-ons

#### Administrative Hooks
NetWorks Core add-on products are required to implement a database package identified in the G3E_ADDON.G3E_METADATAPACKAGENAME field. This package has several procedures that are executed during Upgrade Wizard and metadata support and publish operations.   
|  Procedure  |  Description  |  Arguments  |  Returns  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  CMVersion  |  Function that returns the add-on version where the package was installed from.  |  None  |  String representing the add-on version  |  
|  CreateConstraints  |  Creates all the constraints for the add-on. Used during the Upgrade process to create the add-on constraints.   |  None  |   |  
|  CreateSequences  |  Creates all the sequences for the add-on.  |  None  |   |  
|  CreateSynonyms  |  Creates all the synonyms for the add-on.  |  None  |   |  
|  CreateAllSubTables  |  Creates all metadata sub tables for the add-on. Used during the Upgrade process and metadata publish to generate add-on language sub tables.   |  None  |   |  
|  CreateSubTables  |  Creates all the metadata language sub-tables for the add-on using the specified locale identifier.   |  LCID: language for which to generate the sub tables  |   |  
|  DropAllSubTables  |  Drops all the metadata language sub-tables for the add-on for all the locales in G3E_METADATALANGUAGE.  |  None  |   |  
|  DropSubTables  |  Drops all the metadata language sub-tables for the specified locale identifier.  |  LCID: language for which to drop the sub tables  |   |  
|  SynchronizeSubTables  |  Synchronizes the metadata language sub-tables for the add-on before publishing.  |  None  |   |

#### Error Handling
Each script run is required to return an error when an error is encountered. This allows the Upgrade Wizard to stop on the error, so you can take corrective action. After that, the upgrade resumes. Without this error handling, any error in a script does not halt the upgrade and subsequent upgrades may run with unexpected or unintended results. 
The exception to this rule is for scripts that only drop database objects. To easily handle the case where the object being dropped does not exist, error handling is optional for scripts that only drop database objects. 
Error Handling in SQL Scripts
Error handling in SQL scripts is done within the script by defining what the script should do when an error is encountered. Use the WHENEVER SQLERROR EXIT -1 clause to cause the script to exit when a SQL error is encountered. 
Use the WHENEVER SQLERROR EXIT -1 clause to cause the script to exit when a operating system error is encountered. 
Error Handling in Executables
Return a non-zero value to halt the upgrade process when the executable encounters an error. 
Error Handling in Batch Files
Set %ERRORLEVEL% to a non-zero number to halt the upgrade process when the batch file encounters an error. 
Error Handling in Deltas
If Deltas processing finds problems with a geometry, it skips the record with that geometry and continues processing. It writes an error to the log file DeltasErrors.log in your %TEMP% folder and writes one message to the Event Viewer. Review the Event Viewer and the DeltasErrors.log file regularly to fix the reported geometry errors in your data 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/401289) Errors can have a mixture of English and localized errors.

#### Example List File Entries
Modifiable Script
This script displays for site specific-modifications
SM;ConditionalMetadataChanges09.02.00.0101.sql
Import Insert
II;G3E_REPORTINTERFACE;;;COMMDEV933;G3E_RINO;G3E_REPORTINTERFACE_SEQ
  * This entry imports a delivered DMP file G3E_REPORTINTERFACE.dmp. 
  * The name of the dump file must be the name of the table being updated, in this case G3E_REPORTINTERFACE. 
  * Dump file contains a table named the table to update appended with _TMP. In this case the DMP file contains a table names G3E_REPORTINTERFACE_TMP. 
  * The dump file was exported by user COMMDEV933.
  * G3E_RINO is the key field for the table
  * G3E_REPORTINTERFACE_SEQ is the sequence to set the key field to when inserting to the destination table G3E_REPORTINTERFACE. 


Import Update
IU;G3E_REPORTINTERFACE;;;COMMDEV933
  * This entry imports a delivered DMP file G3E_REPORTINTERFACE.dmp.
  * The name of the dump file must be the name of the table being updated in this case G3E_REPORTINTERFACE. 
  * Dump file contains a table named the table to update appended with _TMP. In this case the DMP file contains a table names G3E_REPORTINTERFACE_TMP. 
  * The dump file was exported by user COMMDEV933.
  * Add-on is required to supply a support script to set fields to update and the where clauses to identify the value and the rows to update. The name of this support script must be named ImportUpdate<TABLENAME>.sql. 
  * The support script makes calls to UpgradeUtils to perform the updates to the specified table. 
    * SetUpdateImportField:
      * Called for each field to be updated
      * Arguments
fieldname: Name of field to update
whereClause: Where clause to be used in update statement
    * CompleteUpdateImport
      * Called only once after all calls to SetUpdateImportField.
      * Arguments
tableName: name of table to update
updateWhereClause: Where clause to be used for overall update.
  * Example
    * Set field G3E_ARGUEMENTPROMPT to be updated if G3E_INTERFACE is GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT
    * execute UpgradeUtils.SetUpdateImportField ('G3E_ARGUMENTPROMPT', 'G3E_INTERFACE = ''GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT'''); 
    * Set field G3E_ARGUEMENTTYPE to be updated if G3E_INTERFACE is GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT
    * execute UpgradeUtils.SetUpdateImportField('G3E_ARGUMENTTYPE', 'G3E_INTERFACE = ''GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT''');
    * Update specified fields in table G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE where G3E_INTERFACE = GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT
    * execute UpgradeUtils.CompleteUpdateImport('G3E_PLACEMENTINTERFACE', 'G3E_INTERFACE = ''GFPlaceTech.LineByTwoPointsOffsetSPT'''); 


Batch File
B;%GTECHPATH%\NormalizeStyleDefinitions.exe;;;%CONNECTSTRING% %CONFIGURATION% %LOGPATH% Extract
  * This entry runs the executable NormalizeStyleDefinitions.exe located in the \GTechnology\Program folder. %GTEC to be executed during the upgrade process. 
  * Arguments to executable
  * These arguments are specific to the NormalizeStyleDefinitions.exe and may be different for your batch files or executables.HPATH% is a predefined constant used in batch-type scripts. It is set to the \GTechnology\Program folder. Allows executables delivered by NetWorks Core
    * %CONNECTSTRING%
Predefined constants used in batch type scripts. It is the Oracle connect string to allow the executable to connect to the database being upgraded. 
    * %CONFIGURATION%
Predefined constant used in batch type scripts. It is the configuration being upgraded.
    * %LOGPATH% 
Predefined constant used in batch-type scripts. It is the log path where log files are created by the Upgrade Wizard. It is defined as ‘Upgrade log file path:’ on the Upgrade Wizard – Settings dialog. 
    * Extract
Type of operation the executable is to perform.


Cross-Version Update
SM;ConditionalMetadataChanges09.32.1401.sql;;09.32
  * If an update is done in a maintenance release and is followed by a release that contains the update there is a possibility the update may be run twice if upgrading through the maintenance release that originally contained the upgrade to the new release. 
  * To prevent double running the script a version number can be used to indicate which starting version the script should be run. In this case this script only runs if the source version begins with 09.32. 
  * If the add-on starting version begins with the build version in the list file the script is run. 
  * Only supports specification of 5 or 8 digit version numbers (i.e 09.32 or 09.32.05)


Update Based on Conditional Query
SQ;metadataChanges09.01.47.03.sql;;;SELECT COUNT(*) FROM G3E_ANALYSIS WHERE G3E_USERNAME=’Feature Import’;>;0
  * Script metadatadataChanges09.01.47.03.sql is only run if Feature Import is defined in G3E_ANALYSIS. If Feature Import is not defined in G3E_ANALYSIS the script is not run. 
  * May be used with modifiable option (M) to allow user modification of the script before it is run.

#### Folder Structure
The Upgrade Wizard requires a specific folder structure for identifying the files it needs to upgrade the add-on. 
IncrementalUpgrades
The \IncrementalUpgrades folder must be present underneath the path defined by the InstallDir registry entry for the add-on. This folder contains the incremental upgrade folders and list files required by the Upgrade Wizard. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/BJiZRqlqZsbY99US825uLg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=2cd0e482f674b19a&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
Build<ADDON_VERSION>
The \Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder contains the list files and scripts to upgrade the database to the version specified by <ADDON_VERSION>. If this folder exists, it must contain at least one of the incremental list files – UpgradeScripts.lis or DataUpgradeScripts.lis.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/cxGB4v5REC5EZLUiTRAOwQ-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=ad475b4ac92b3205&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
Metadata Upgrade
This folder exists underneath the \Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder. It is required if there are incremental metadata upgrades for the add-on version and the list file UpgradeScripts.lis exists in the \Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder. UpgradeScripts.lis references scripts in this folder. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/u4O~JUmWbVVP3M7hgV8Pvg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=5b026925b7c2d2de&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
Data Upgrade
This folder exists underneath the \Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder. It is required if there are incremental data upgrades for the add-on version and the list file DataUpgradeScripts.lis exists in the \Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder. DataUpgradeScripts.lis references scripts in this folder. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/XpRSoXUX0pyNzWY4Nel7zw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=275c3b27e86e3951&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

#### List File Format
The list file is a semi-colon-delimited file that specifies a script to run and under what conditions the script is run. There are seven different arguments in the list file for each script. The first four arguments are common to all script types. The remaining three are specific to the type of the file to be run. 
Common Arguments  
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Type  |  The type of the file to run. Valid values are: E – Execute Procedure  II – Import insert  IU – Import update  P – PLSQL script  S: – SQL script  SQ – SQL script with conditional query  B – Batch or executable  Scripts of type II, IU, S, or SQ may be modifiable scripts. If a script is modifiable, to run the Upgrade Wizard you might have to change the script to specify site-specific values. To identify a script as being modifiable, the type specified for the script ends with M (that is, SM for an SQL script that requires user modification). A script identified as modifiable displays in the Upgrade Wizard user interface to allow you to specify site values in the script.  For the type of II and IU, they can be III or IUI. The third letter, I, means that the IGNORE parameter on the import command (IMP.EXE) is set to YES. In this case, the importing dump file has a table that has a blob-type column. Create the table before importing the dump file.   |  
|  2  |  File name  |  The name of the file to process.  For type S, SQ, and P, the name of the script file to run.  For II and IU types, it is the name of the table being modified.  For B type files, you can use a predefined path. %GTECHPATH% specifies the NetWorks Core installation folder. This lets you call any executable or batch file in the GTechnology\Program folder. For your Add-On, you can use a predefined path, %ADDONPATH%, which lets you call any executable or batch file in your Add-On\program folder.  For type E,  |  
|  3  |  Functional Condition  |  Not supported for Add-ons. The add-on itself is considered the functional condition.  |  
|  4  |  Build number  |  The first two or three digits including the period to indicate in which build the script is to run. This handles the case where there is an upgrade in a previous version and the current version and the upgrade only needs to be run once.   |  
Specific SQL Arguments
File types of SQ are SQL scripts to be run based on a query. For this type, additional fields in the list file are used.   
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  SQL Statement  |  The SQL statement to run and whose return value is compared to Value. Only queries that return a number are supported (for example, select count(*) …)   |  
|  6  |  Expression  |  The expression to use in the evaluation. Valid values are: < <= = >= > <>  |  
|  7  |  Value  |  The value to compare to the value from the query. If the comparison is true, the script is run. If the comparison is false, the script is not run.   |  
Specific Import Arguments
Files of type II and IU are Oracle export files that are to be loaded into the database. For this type of upgrade script, additional fields in the list file are used. 
Import files are Oracle export files generated using EXP.EXE.  These files_TMP appended. The key fields in the temporary table are updated based on a defined sequence then inserted into the metadata table. Procedures in the [UpgradeUtils](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/H~B76hiY~HDCHHspBKs4kg) package, loaded in the preparation phase of the upgrade process, are used to complete this type of upgrade. 
Only Oracle export files produced from the Oracle’s export command EXP.EXE are supported. 
  * Insert
Insert type of import upgrade insert rows into the runtime table from the imported temporary table. With this type of import activity the rows imported into the temporary table are inserted directly into the target table with appropriate primary key values generated from a sequence to prevent duplicate key errors.   
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  From User Name  |  The database user that owned the table when the export file was created.  |  
|  6  |  Key Field Name  |  The name of the key field whose value comes from the sequence.  |  
|  7  |  Sequence Name  |  The name of the sequence to use to generate key field values.  |  
  * Update
Update type of import upgrade updates existing rows in the metadata table from the imported temporary table. A companion script must accompany the export file to specify the fields to be updated. This companion script must be named ImportUpdate<TABLENAME>.sql where TABLENAME is the name of the table being updated.   
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  From User  |  The database user that owned the table when the export file was created.  |  


PL/SQL Arguments
PLSQL type upgrade scripts can be located in a folder other than the folders where incremental upgrade scripts reside. This path is appended to the add-on INSTALLDIR registry entry to locate any script delivered with the add-on.   
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  Alternate location  |  Specifies an alternate location of the script to run. This alternate location must be under the add-on registry entry INSTALLDIR.   |  
Batch Arguments  
|  Position  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  5  |  Arguments  |  Specifies arguments to be passed to the batch file. Predefined arguments can be used. %CONNECTSTRING% defines the Oracle connection string. %CONFIGURATION% defines the NetWorks Core configuration being upgraded.  %LOGPATH% defines the log folder the user selected in the Upgrade Wizard user interface.  |

#### Logging
The user-specified log path is passed to each script that is run. It is up to the script to create a log file in this path to log the activities of the script. The name of this log file should be the same as the script with an .log extension. 
To avoid confusion, the Upgrade Wizard expects the log file and the script to have the same name. When the Upgrade Wizard detects an error, a message displays indicating the log file to view to see the error. 
This implies that all scripts should have unique names or log files are overwritten. This can become a problem with the incremental scripts as the number of these scripts increases. Appending or prepending the add-on name and version number to the name of the script and log file ensures script and log file name uniqueness across all versions. 
View Log on the Ugprade Wizard progress dialog also expects the name of the log file to be the name of the script. If the log file name does not match the script name, this button is disabled and you must manually open the log folder to locate the log file of the failed script. 
Log Files forSQL Scripts
Logging using SQL scripts is done with the SPOOL statement in the script being run. Each script should contain the log file creation statement 
SPOOL &&1\<NAME OF SCRIPT>.log
Each script should contain the log file save statement. Without this the log file is empty. 
SPOOL OFF
&&1 is the passed in argument specifying the log folder the user selected in the Upgrade Wizard user interface. 
Executables
User defined.
Batch Files
User defined

#### Registry Entries
Each add-on is responsible for installation of the add-on and for required registry entries. 
For add-ons, the Upgrade Wizard uses the following registry entries:
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GTechnology\Add-Ons\NetWorksAdministrator  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  InstallDir  |  The location where the add-on is installed on the machine  |  
|  Product Name  |  The name of the add-on  |  
|  Product Version  |  Version of the add-on installed on the machine  |  
|  MinimumCoreVersion  |  The minimum NetWorks Core version that is compatible with the add-on. NetWorks Core installation checks this value against the version of NetWorks Core being installed. If this value is greater than the NetWorks Core version being installed, the installation is terminated.  This value must be formatted according to the guidelines in the [Software Version](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WLdcBzHsT1h1rhU_78mwqw) topic:  Valid values are:
  * Major Version: AA.MM (for example, 10.02) 
  * Minor Service Pack version: AA.MM.mmss (for example, 10.02.0101) 
  * Minor Service Pack Build version: AA.MM.mmss.bbbbb (for example, 10.02.0101.34001) 

This registry entry is optional. If it does not exist or is empty, NetWorks Core installation skips this check for the add-on, and the installation proceeds.   |  
Example
![Add-OnRegWithNetWorks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/dOkVDqluVR5DnB3wzBYCZg-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=203c9465af682427&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)

#### Required Files
Each add-on is required to create files to be used by the Upgrade Wizard to upgrade the metadata, data, and database functionality required by the add-on. 
List Files
List files drive the upgrade process. They define the scripts to run and under what conditions the scripts should be run. Each step of the upgrade process has an associated list file that defines the scripts to be run for that step of the upgrade process. List files are optional. If an add-on has no scripts to run for an upgrade step, the list file need not exist. The list files should be delivered to the add-on \INSTALL_DIR/IncrementalUpgrades except for the incremental list files, UpgradeScripts.lis and DataUpgradeScripts.lis, which reside in the \BUILD<ADDON_VERSION> folders underneath the \INSTALL_DIR/IncrementalUpgrades folder 
Scripts
Scripts are any file that the Upgrade Wizard runs. These include batch files, executables, and SQL scripts. Each SQL- and PL/SQL-type script the Upgrade Wizard runs is passed three arguments. The exception is a PL/SQL-type script, which is called within [Upgrade Metadata Structure and Upgrade Data Structure step](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/9wHMQrKFmTgfnJkUsTSOHQ). 
  * The first argument passed into a script is the user-specified log path.
  * The second argument passed into a script is the path where the Add-On is installed.
  * The third argument passed into a script is the configuration being upgraded.


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/401288) The paths passed are in 8.3 format which requires that 8.3 filename format must be turned on.   
|  The example script below creates a log file and calls a procedure which has two parameters, Add-On installation folder and Configuration name.  Spool &&1\<NAME OF SCRIPT>.log execute <PROCEDURE NAME> (&&2, &&3); spool off &&1 is the first argument specifying the log folder. &&2 is the second argument specifying add-on installation folder. &&3 is the third argument specifying the NetWorks Core configuration being upgraded.   |  
| --- |  
There are no rules for naming the scripts that the Upgrade Wizard runs as long as the script defined in the list file exists in the\Build<ADDON_VERSION> folder or a specified alternate path. However, the names of the scripts should be unique. 
All scripts must do the following:
  * Log their actions
  * Set up error handling to stop the upgrade process when an error is encountered
  * End with an exit statement so the script exits when complete. If the exit is not present the script does not exit and it appears as if the Upgrade Wizard has hung. 


It is recommended to keep the scripts as small as possible and focused on a single area of metadata or data. This makes correcting the script a little easier when an error is encountered. 
Scripts are run in NetWorks Core-version order. First, all the NetWorks Core scripts are run for a particular version then any add-on upgrades associated with that NetWorks Core version are run. 
Incremental scripts are copied to %GTECHPATH%\IncrementalUpgrades\Build<ADDON_VERSION>\<Upgrade Type>\<Configuration> before executing. This prevents the modification of delivered scripts for modifiable type scripts or user modifications to overcome upgrade errors. The open Script button on the UpgradeWizard progress dialog opens the copied filed. 
PopulateVersionMapping.sql
This script updates the G3E_VERSIONMAPPING table which relates an add-on version to a NetWorks Core version. This table maps add-on version to NetWorks Core version to ensure that add-on upgrade scripts are run in NetWorks Core version order. There needs to be one row in the G3E_VERSIONMAPPING for each add-on version that has incremental metadata or data updates. This file resides in the add-on \INSTALLDIR/IncrementalUpgrades folder.

#### Upgrade Steps
Prepare the Database for Upgrading
Load any database object that supports the upgrade process. Load only scripts that are general in nature and support the upgrade process. For example, the package [UpgradeUtils](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/H~B76hiY~HDCHHspBKs4kg) contains procedures that support the upgrade process. This package is loaded during this phase of the upgrade process. Pre-upgrade validation to ensure the database is ready for upgrading. 
The list file UpgradePrepare.lis is located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder. This file is optional. 
Use the information in the topics listed below:.
Upgrade Metadata Structure
Incrementally upgrade normalized metadata tables to the version specified in the folder name. The upgrade processes each <ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades\Build<ADD-ON VERSION> folder. If the folder contains the list file upgradescripts.lis, all the scripts defined in the list file are executed. 
Each add-on version that has incremental updates must be associated to a NetWorks Core version. This mapping is maintained in G3E_VERSIONMAPPING. Add-on upgrades are processed in version order. It is up to the add-on creator to ensure that the versions are sequential. 
Add-on upgrade scripts are run after the NetWorks Core scripts have been run for the NetWorks Core version associated with the add-on version in G3E_VERSIONMAPPING. 
If an add-on upgrade related to a NetWorks Core version does not have an incremental update, the add-on scripts run when the NetWorks Core scripts would have been run if they existed. 
Incremental scripts are run for add-on versions whose associated NetWorks Core version is less than the current NetWorks Core database version. 
All normalized metadata tables are upgraded to the version of the add-on installed on the machine running the upgrade. 
All the following must be true:
  * One folder per version under \IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. 
  * The folder must be named \Build<ADD-ON VERSION> where add-on version is the add-on version number with which the incremental upgrade is associated. 
  * Only updates to normalized metadata tables are permitted during this phase of the upgrade process. 


You must follow all of these rules:
  * Do not call any packages that are dependent on the optimized metadata tables.
  * Drop an optimized table whose structure is modified.
  * Do not load the new/updated optimized package.
  * Do not call a procedure to create an optimized table.
  * Drop the modified/removed constraints to the normalized table.
  * Install new/modified constraints to the normalized table.
  * Install new/modified triggers to the normalized table.
  * When you insert or update the G3E_NETPAGES table, do the following:
    * Disable M_T_BIUR_G3E_NETPAGES trigger.
    * Insert or update the G3E_NETPAGES table.
    * Enable M_T_BIUR_G3E_NETPAGES trigger.
  * When you create a new component, create a table whose name is the value in G3E_COMPONENT.G3E_TABLE before adding attribute to G3E_ATTRIBUTE table. 
  * When you insert or update the G3E_ATTRIBUTE table to add columns to the existing component table, do the following: 
    * Alter the <B$ table> table to add the column 
    * Disable M_T_BIUR_G3E_ATTRIBUTE trigger. 
    * Add the new attributes to G3E_ATTRIBUTE. 
    * Enable M_T_BIUR_G3E_ATTRIBUTE trigger.
  * When you import a dump file that has a table with a blob-type column, you must create the table before you import it. 


The list file is named upgradescripts.lis and has the following characteristics: 
  * Located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades\Build<ADD-ON VERSION> folder. 
  * Required if the folder exists and there is no dataupgradescripts.lis in the \Build<ADD-ON VERSION> folder. 
  * References scripts in the \Metadata Upgrade folder located at the same level as the list file unless overridden. 
  * Optional: The\Build\ADD-ON VERSION> folder exists and the dataupgradescript.lis exists in the \Build folder. 


Upgrade Metadata Packages
The Metadata PLSQL upgrade packages to the version of the add-on installed on the machine running the upgrade. 
The packages do the following:
  * Load all metadata packages.
  * Install metadata triggers.
  * Generate metadata packages required to generate optimized tables.


The list file is named InstallMetadataPLSQL.lis, and it is located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. This file is optional. 
Process Metadata
You process metadata to do any processing necessary to generate the metadata optimized tables. Now the database is prepared to generate metadata optimized tables. 
Process metadata does the following:
  * Drops/installs metadata constraints. 
  * Creates/populates sub-language tables.


The list file is ProcessMetadata.lis, located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. This is an optional file. 
Generate Optimized Metadata Tables
This step generates optimized metadata tables for the add-on. This step is internal to the Upgrade Wizard. There is no list file because creation of the optimized tables is internal to the upgrade process. 
Post Generate Optimized Metadata Tables
This step upgrades all metadata packages which depend on the optimized tables to version of the add-on installed on the machine running the upgrade. 
This step does the following:
  * Installs packages which depend on the optimized table.
  * Creates metadata sequences.


The list file is ProcessPostOptableMetadata.lis located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. This is an optional file. 
Upgrade Data Structure
This step incrementally upgrades the data structure for the add-on version of the database to the add-on version installed on the machine running the upgrade. 
The step does the following:
  * Executes InstallOneTable to install new components.
  * Updates data table values.START HERE
  * Installs triggers and constraints on the data tables.


When you modify the existing component table structure, do the following: 
  * Populate new column if necessary.
  * Re-create the component view for modified table if it contains the newly added attribute or excludes the removed attribute. 
  * Purge the MODIFICATIONLOG if there are modlog entries. Using the component view name that has been changed, execute the following: 
SQL> execute G3E_MANAGEMODLOG.SyncToComponentView(‘<Component View Name>’);


The list file is dataupgradescripts.lis located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades\Build<ADD-ON VERSION> folder. This file is required if folder exists and there is no upgradescript.lis in the \Build<ADD-ON VERSION> folder. The file references scripts in the \DataUpgrade folder located at the same level as the list file unless it is overridden. The file is optional if the \Build\<ADD-ON VERSION> folder exists and dataupgradescript.lis exists in the \Build folder. 
Runtime PLSQL
This step Installs all add-on Oracle objects to support NetWorks Core runtime and loads all database PL/SQL to support the runtime functionality 
The list file for this step is InstallPLSQL.lis located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. It is an optional file. 
Process Runtime
This step generates all Oracle runtime objects.
This step does the following:
  * Generate LTT_VIEWS
  * Generate LTT triggers
  * Generate modification tracking triggers.


The list file for this step is ProcessRuntime.lis located in the \<ADD-ON INSTALLDIR>\IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. It is an optional file. 
Post Process
This step does any post upgrade processing necessary for the add-on.
The list file for this step is PostProcess.lis located in the \IncrementalUpgrades folder of the add-on. It is an optional file. 
Update Add-On Version
This step updates G3E_ADDON table. The value of G3E_GTECHVER is set to the version which database is upgraded to. The value of G3E_ADDON is set to the AddOns’ client version. This step is internal to the UpgradeWizard. There is no list file for this step because upating of G3E_ADDON is internal to the upgrade process. 
Publish Metadata
This step publishes the metadata DDC and RAW files to include all metadata changes done during the upgrade. This step is internal to the Upgrade Wizard. Add-on metadata is published to RAW files only. They are not published to DDC files. There is no list file because publishing of metadata is internal to the upgrade process. 
Validate
This step does any post upgrade validation necessary to ensure that the upgrade was successful. This step has no list file because validation is internal to the upgrade process.

#### UpgradeUtils
UpgradeUtils is an upgrade support package loaded during the preparation phase of the upgrade process. The primary purpose of this package is to support import type upgrades and post upgrade validation.   
|  Procedure  |  Arguments  |  Purpose  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  CheckMetadataVersion  |  targetVersion varchar2  |  Verifies the version passed in is the current version of the database. An error is raised if this version is not the current version of the database.   |  
|  CompleteImport  |  table_name varchar2 key_field varchar2 sequence_name varchar2  |  Runs after the temporary table has been imported into the database Resets sequence to max key field value + 1 Updates key field in temporary table using reset sequence Inserts rows from the temporary table into table_name Only used for Insert Imports Automatically called from Upgrade Wizard  |  
|  SetUpdateImportField  |  fieldname varchar2 whereClause varchar2 (Optional)  |  Runs after the temporary table has been imported into the database FieldName: Defines field name to update whereClause: If specified, is the WHERE clause to run against the imported temporary table to identify the value to set fieldname to.  Must be run before running CompleteUpdateImport Can be run more than once for updating multiple fields in the same table. Only used for Update Imports Called from add-on-supplied script.  |  
|  CompleteUpdateImport  |  TableName varchar2 updateWhereClause varchar2  |  Runs after temporary table has been imported and SetupdateImportField has at least been run once  tableName: The table to update updateWhereClause: Where clause to use to identify the rows in the table to be updated. Only used for Update Imports Called from add-on-supplied script.  |  
|  CheckCMVersion  |  buildNumber ivarchar2  |  Verifies the CMVersion of all Oracle packages for NetWorks Core and any defined Add-On. For the Add-On, the package name should begin with the value in G3E_ADDON.G3E_NAMEPREFIX column.  Automatically called from Upgrade Wizard.  |  
|  CheckForInvalidObjects  |   |  Validates all Oracle objects Dumps out all Oracle objects that are invalid. Automatically called from Upgrade Wizard  |

#### Versioning
The upgrade process is version based which makes versioning an important aspect of the integration of add-on upgrades with NetWorks Core upgrades. There are several versions used during the process and an understanding of what these versions are and where they come from is important: 
  * NetWorks Core database version—This version is the source version for the upgrade. All upgrade scripts for versions greater than the NetWorks Core database version is executed. This version is stored in the database. 
You can identify it by executing the database procedure METADATAVERSION.CMVERSION. To determine the NetWorks Core version of the database, execute this statement in a SQL tool 
SQL> SELECT METADATAVERSION.CMVERSION FROM DUAL;
  * NetWorks Core client version—This version is the target version for the upgrade. The file plsqlversion.txt under the PL/SQL folder is used to identify the version of the client. The Upgrade Wizard processes all incremental updates up to and including any updates for this version. 
  * Add-on database Version—This version is the source add-on version. The version of any add-on is stored in [G3E_ADDON. G3E_ADDONVER](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VBl9fkdnZlDTNU50bY_XFA). All incremental updates for the add-on greater than this version is executed. The add-on version in the G3E_ADDON table is set to the add-on client version as defined by the INSTALLDIR registry entry by the Upgrade Wizard. 
  * Add-on client version—This version is the target add-on version. The add-on registry entry PRODUCTVERSION defines the version of the add-on client. The Upgrade Wizard processes all add-on incremental updates up to and including any updates for this version. 
  * Mapping NetWorks Core to add-on version—Each incremental upgrade for an add-on must be associated with some version of NetWorks Core. Without this, the Upgrade Wizard does not know when to run the add-on upgrade scripts as it processes the NetWorks Core upgrade scripts. This information is stored in the [G3E_VERSIONMAPPING](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Omy9GEIM3yzCpH90qasqgQ) table. It is the responsibility of the add-on to maintain their entries in this table. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/401273) The NetWorks Core client version should be greater than or equal to the maximum NetWorks Core version in G3E_VERSIONMAPPING which is populated in runtime by each add-on [PopulateVersionMapping.sql](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/epPZgK4S7gF~f8DWUQD16A)

## Bulk Loading Images
Load Images lets you bulk load images (place multiple images associated with a feature class). Only files that support automatic placement can be bulk loaded. Automatic placement inserts geo-registered images directly into a database, preserving image geometry. There are two modes of automatic placement, georeferenced and by header. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261619) You must be [in a job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SyT9lcV2eeceSwXLzo0KfA) to use this command. 
  * To bulk load images:


  1. From the Administrative menu, select Load Images. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/BvdGGKNfRuQiuNd70cHDlw-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=ea3ebf90d0b8ac41&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Select a folder:
    1. In Select directory, select the drive and folder where the image files exist. 
    2. If your users do not have access to the folder in which the image files are located, you must copy the files to a file path listed in <OTHERPATHS> in the [FileUNCPaths.xml](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ). 
  3. Select the file type. This selection determines what file types display in Select files. 
  4. Select the feature class with which you want to associate the images.
  5. Select one of the following placement modes:
     * Georeferenced—Use this placement mode for GeoTiff type images or for Hexagon types 2, 9, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, and 31 with geo-tie-packets. 
     * By header—Use this placement mode images that are Hexagon type 2, 9, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30, or 31. Browse to or type the name of the file containing the coordinate system information needed to insert the images. 
  6. Select the image files you want to bulk load. You can press SHIFT + click to select sequential files or CTRL + click to select multiple files that are not sequential. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261619)
  7. Optional: To make one or more colors transparent: 
    1. Click Colors. 
A temporary window is created, and the [Raster Transparent Colors (RTC)](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/alTBzPOb8HAMVWqQUSDt7w) control displays. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261619) [Click here](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261619) to read important information regarding behavior of the Colors button. 
       * Some raster files cause Colors to be disabled, even if you select only one file. For example, binary raster files cannot support transparent colors. 
       * If you select more than one file for bulk load, all the files selected must have the same kind of raster transparent colors data or Colors are disabled. 
The selected files must have these things in common:
         * One of the following kinds of files: RGB, gray scale, or color index.
         * Internally-specified transparent color information. They all have to specify the same transparent color: RGB, gray, or index, or lack thereof. 
         * If they are color-indexed files, they all have to have the same color table.
         * They all have to be able to apply any user-specified transparent colors the same way.
    2. Use the temporary window in conjunction with the RTC control to choose colors to be transparent. 
    3. When you are finished, you are returned to the Bulk Load Image dialog box. 
  8. Click OK.

## Configuring RemoteApp
RemoteApp enables you to make programs that are accessed remotely through Remote Desktop Services appear as if they are running on a local computer. These programs are referred to as RemoteApp programs. Instead of being presented to you in the desktop of the Remote Desktop Session Host (RD Session Host) server, the RemoteApp program is integrated with the client's desktop. The RemoteApp program runs in its own resizable window, can be dragged between multiple monitors, and has its own entry in the taskbar. 
Programs on a Remote Desktop Session Host (RD Session Host) server are available to users through RemoteApp. You can deploy RemoteApp programs through .rdp files, Windows Installer packages, or by using RD Web Access to make the programs available through RemoteApp and Desktop Connection. 
  1. On Windows Server, open the Server Manager and install the Remote Desktop Services role. 
    1. Select the server, the Remote Desktop Services installation type, the Quick Start deployment type, and the Session-based desktop deployment option. 
    2. Check the box next to Restart the destination server automatically if required. 
  2. Note the RD Web Access URL provided after the role is successfully installed. You need this URL later to create a RemoteApp session from the client machine. 
  3. On the Remote Desktop Services page of the Server Manager, remove the default QuickSessionCollection collection. 
  4. Create a new session collection with an appropriate name. 
    1. Add the session host to the Selected list on the RD Session Host servers page.
    2. Add User groups to the session collection.
    3. Be sure to uncheck Enable user profile disks. 
  5. Publish your applications from the session collection. These applications are added to the available REMOTEAPP PROGRAMS. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/798284) Before publishing, make sure that the applications that need to be published are [installed](javascript:;) and configured on the host server. 
  6. Enter the RD Web Access URL you noted earlier into the client machine's web browser. 
  7. Log in with your domain credentials.
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/798284) If you receive an Unknown publisher error message when attempting to log in, click Connect and follow the directions to successfully connect the application. 
  8. Once the Remote App session is successfully connected, a new system tray icon indicates the connection to a Remote Work Place. 
  9. Click an application icon to open the application within the RemoteApp session.

## Creating Log Files
If you need to create a log file, use any text editor to create an empty text file in the location specified below.   
|  What You Are Doing  |  Log File Name  |  How the File Is Created  |  Content  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  Metadata publishing  |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/mpublish<Configuration name>.log   |  Automatic  |  Records the process for publishing the selected DDC file for the specified configuration. The software flushes this file when you publish.   |  
|  mapfile reading  |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/mapfileRlog.txt  |  User creates and software appends to the file.  |  Shows access to each DDC file. Because this file can get quite large, create it only for specific diagnostic needs.   |  
|  mapfile writing  |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/mapfileWlog.txt  |  User creates and software appends to the file.  |  Shows creation of each DDC file. Because this file can get quite large, create it only for specific diagnostic needs.   |  
|  Batch processing  |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/GframmeBatch.log  |  Automatic  |  Shows processing status for NetWorks Core when run in silent or batch conditions. The file only records errors. Because this file does not get too large, you can flush it periodically.   |  
|  Database query  |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/gdooserver.log  |  User creates and software appends to the file  |  Shows access to the Oracle database for certain limited operations. This file can get quite large. Flush it periodically or create it for specific diagnostic tasks.   |  
|  Functional Interfaces   |  %TMP% or %TEMP% folder/FunctionalIpipe.log  
and  
%TMP% or %TEMP% folder/FunctionalInterfaces.log   |  Automatic  |  Records problems that occur with functional interfaces. These files only record errors and while they are not flushed automatically, they do not get very large.   |  
|  Data publishing  |  %TEMP%/publish.log  |  Automatic  |  Shows progress of publishing data. Delete this file after each successful publish operation. The software appends to the file and does not flush it automatically. After numerous publish operations, the file can get large.   |  
|  Loop Makeup  |  %TEMP%/LMU debug.xml  |  User creates, software flushes and rewrites contents (if the file exists, logging is optional)   |  The file is the ADO recordset that is sent to the loop makeup DCOM object, persisted to XML. Depending on the size of the data analyzed by the Loop Makeup command, this file can get quite large, so create it only for specific diagnostic tasks.   |  
|  System startup  |  %TEMP%/GTechStartup.log  |  User creates and software appends to the file  |  When NetWorks Core is launched, the system pauses for 1- 3 seconds on the Citrix environment. The software executes procedures to help determine where a problem may be occurring. Create this file only for specific diagnostics tasks. Because the information is limited to the application startup, the size of this file does not grow rapidly.   |  
|  System monitoring  |  %TEMP%/CommandLog.txt  |  Automatic  |  Records each command started by the user. Overwritten on each startup of NetWorks Core. File size is limited to the number of commands run within one session, so size should not be a concern.   |

## Database Backups

### Backing Up Required Files
The following files required for NetWorks Core can be time-consuming to recreate. In a production environment, you should back them up for easy restoration: 
  * DDC files
DDC files can be located on the client or server systems. You can quickly and easily recreate metadata DDC; however, recreating the data DDC files can take hours if your model is large. The location of the DDC files is in the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file. Using a ZIP utility, archive the files. After a data publish, make sure the new DDC files are backed up. 
  * CCM files
During a data publish, the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm is updated with the current path and data DDC file name. The old data DDC file entry is not removed. Back this file up with the DDC files. 
  * FileUNCPaths
The local client system registry entry HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE \SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\Path\FileUNCPath indicates the location of the [FileUNCPaths file](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vh0Kk8wYIT3X~Tvx5EvjTQ). This file contains the paths to the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file for current connections, preparatory publish locations, and other paths as needed. Back up this text file with the DDC files. 
  * Hyperlink files
NetWorks Core can store hyperlinks as feature attributes. These hyperlinks can reference external files such as Microsoft Word and Excel files and image files. Ideally, these files should be stored in a central location referenced by the other paths section of the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file. NetWorks Core stores only a reference to these files—it does not store the actual file in the database. Back up these files when you back up other data. 
    * You can create hyperlinks to files that reside on a local client machine. However, this causes access problems for other users and problems in backing up data. It is best to store hyperlink files in the central location referenced by the "other paths" section in the CCM file. 
    * Raster files
You can store raster files on a local machine or in a central data repository. Back up these files when you back up other data. 


Related Topic
[Database Backups](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hFJvstFtkRfJKgmenRqAvw)

## Display Differences for NetWorks Core Version 10.1 and Later

### Dashed Line
For NetWorks Core version 10.1, the underlying algorithm for drawing dashed lines has changed. Dashed lines have much more consistent behavior when zooming or panning than in previous versions. When compared to previous versions, the position of the dashes along the lines may be different, but the dash lengths and the spacing between dashes is similar. 
The following are notable differences concerning dashed lines:
  * Stretchable dashes and gaps can stretch or shrink, depending on the overall length of the line. This is an attempt to give a "best" representation of the dashed line definition. 
  * A given line is always have the same number of dashes and gaps along its length, and the spacing is always the same, regardless of how much of the line is visible in the view and regardless of the zoom scale. 


Before version 10.1, the positions of the dashes and gaps on a line's length were influenced by how much of the line is visible in the view, specifically, whether or not the start of the line is visible in the view and, if not, how far outside of the view the start of the line is located. In version 10.1, the dashes are always calculated based on the start of the line. Dashes are not affected by whether or not the start of the line is actually visible.

### Display of Raster or Vector Data

#### Printing Differences Related to Translucency
When a map window or a plot sheet that contains some translucent data are printed, some data that is not translucent might output to the printer differently than if the map window or plot sheet did not contain any translucent data. If a map window or a plot sheet has even a single feature that displays using translucency, then all of the data must pass through a special process to maintain that translucency on the paper. Essentially, an image of the map window or plot sheet contents is created and is sent to the printer rather than the vectors, text, and raster data that are being displayed. 
The rendering line weights can be affected by the imaging process used to maintain translucency. Some lines might be rendered much thinner than expected. Generally, the data can appear to be more faint on the paper than if no translucency is involved. To manipulate the quality of the output, you might have to use the image processing settings of your printer, if it has them. 
Some common image processing settings supported by printers include compression and halftoning. Hexagon has found that the best results are achieved by disabling compression and halftoning. If you do choose compression, try to choose a lossless or less lossy algorithm. Finally, if you choose halftoning, try to choose an algorithm that favors linework or small text. 
Color can also be affected by the imaging process used to maintain translucency. Some colors display in a different shade if printed directly to the printer (that is, if there is no translucency at all in the map window or plot sheet) compared to if they are printed through an imaging process. Even colors that are (a) not translucent, (b) not drawn on top of translucent data, and (c) do not have translucent data drawn on top them can print differently. 
In particular, text can be affected. Depending on the capabilities and settings of your printer, text might display in its defined color or it might display in black, or it might display in a color that is "near" its defined color. When data are printed using the imaging process that is used to maintain translucency, text color is not likely to be affected by the "preference" of your printer for black text or for drawing text in a color that is "near" the defined color.

### Fit Selected
For NetWorks Core version 10.1, you might see some slight changes in the way that the Fit Selected command fits the map window. Some of the underlying calculations have changed, so the range of the fitted data can be slightly different than it was before version 10.1. Fitted data that contains text or point components is more likely to be different than if it contains only linear or area data. The difference is not large and should not affect any of your current workflows.

### Line Styles Used to Underline Text
For NetWorks Core version 10.1, you can configure a text style such that the text is underlined with a line style. Before version 10.1, if the line style used to underline text used an offset, the offset was interpreted opposite of how offsets were interpreted for line styles used only to draw lines. To get the underline line style to offset to the left, it had to be configured in metadata to offset to the right. As part of the replacement of the rendering system in version 10.1, the behavior of the underline line style was modified to make it consistent with line styles used only to draw lines. 
This change in behavior means that the metadata for line styles used to underline text styles had to be modified to change the offset direction. If a line style with an offset was used to underline text in a text style, that line style's offset was flipped. This metadata change happens automatically as part of the metadata upgrade. So, if that line style had been configured to offset to the right, it is now configured to offset the left and if it had been configured to offset to the left, it is now configured to offset to the right. 
Another result of this change is that if a line style with an offset is used to underline text but is also used to draw lines, the display results for the lines are different. The display results for lines are the opposite of what it had been in previous versions. If a line style had been configured to be offset to the left, and the line style had also been used to underline text as part of a text style, the result of drawing lines with the modified metadata is that the line is offset to the right. This difference occurs only if you have line styles that were previously used to underline text as part of a text style and the same line styles are used to draw lines.

### Point Style Alignment Differences
Beginning in version 10.1, if the fonts that are used as symbols do not meet the guidelines described in the [Creating Symbol Fonts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/C5zi718155FcdOKeTpc0RA) topic, some symbols might align differently than in previous versions. 
Examples
In these examples, the green square represents the em-square, and the X indicates the center of the em-square. Even though the borders of the em-square are not visible when you place a symbol, the entire area of the em-square is placed with the symbol. 
Your symbol should appear in the center of the em-square, as in the following illustration:
If the symbol does not appear in the center of the em-square, as in the following example, the center alignment when placed might be inaccurate. 
When you place the symbol, the extents of the em-square are used to calculate the origin and alignment. In the following illustration, both symbols were placed at the same location in respect to the black line. Of course, the green line representing the em-square would not be visible, but as you can see, the symbols do not appear to be in the same location with respect to the black line.

### Point Style Size

#### Font Size Conversion Utility
NetWorks Core provides a command line utility that creates an .sql script. The script can be used to upgrade the G3E_POINTSTYLE.G3E_SIZE values. This utility, FontSizeConversion.exe, is delivered in the \GTechnology\Program folder. You must run the FontSizeConversion.exe on a computer that has all of the fonts referenced in G3E_POINTSTYLE installed on it. 
Essentially, the utility computes a multiplier for each font that is applied to the G3E_POINTSTYLE.G3E_SIZE value. No user input is necessary. The script backs up the G3E_POINTSTYLE table to a table called G3E_POINTSTYLE_PREFCSBACKUP before any values are modified. 
After the G3E_SIZE values have been modified and the styles republished, most of the point styles should display at approximately the same size as they did before version 10.1. Hexagon has found a few instances of fonts that do not display the same size in version10.1 as they did in previous versions, even after converting the G3E_SIZE values. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/289848) You do not have to run the conversion utility. You do not have to convert your custom fonts simply to run NetWorks Core version10.1. 
  * To run the Font Size Conversion utility:


  1. From the command prompt, change directories to \GTechnology\Program, and run FontSizeConversion.exe. 
An .sql script, FontSizeConversion.sql, is generated in the \GTechnology\Program folder. The script contains the conversion factors for each font installed on the computer where the utility is executed. 
  2. Review the FontSizeConversion.sql script to see how much a point style would differ in size in version 10.1 without converting as compared to previous versions. 
     * If the conversion value is 1.0, the point style displays at the same size in version 10.1 as it did in previous versions. 
     * If the conversion value is greater than 1.0, the point style displays smaller in version 10.1 than it did in previous versions. 
     * If the conversion value is less than 1.0, the point style displays larger in version 10.1 than it did in previous versions. 
  3. After the .sql script is generated, execute it in the database and commit the changes. 
The script applies the multiplier to the G3E_POINTSTYLE.G3E_SIZE values.
Before running the script, you can modify it so that it does not upgrade certain fonts by deleting the lines for fonts that you do not want to convert. 
You do not have to delete lines that were created for fonts that are installed on your computer but do not exist in the G3E_POINTSTYLE table. 
For example, if your custom fonts do not adhere to the [Creating Symbol Fonts](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/C5zi718155FcdOKeTpc0RA) guidelines and you plan to modify the fonts themselves, you might choose to upgrade the G3E_POINTSTYLE.G3E_SIZE values for standard fonts only and leave the values for G3E_POINTSTYLE.G3E_SIZE corresponding to custom fonts alone. 


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/289848) If your custom fonts do not adhere for the Creating Symbol Fonts guidelines, you might have alignment problems, as described in the [Point_Style_Alignment_Differences](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/mVmObwHNkDAPenRkuHuRBw) topic.

### Text Box Fill and Height
Before NetWorks Core version 10.1, when a text element that is symbolized with a filled text box was highlighted, the text box itself highlighted and the text displayed on top of the highlighted box. As part of replacing the rendering system, the highlight behavior of filled text boxes has changed. When a text element is highlighted, the text itself is highlighted and the fill is not. If the text box has a frame, the frame is highlighted as well.

### Text Box Fill Color
Before NetWorks Core version 10.1, there were inconsistencies in how the application handled the fill color for text boxes. Generally in NetWorks Core styles, if a color is specified and that color is equal to the background color of the map, the color is "flipped" before it is used. For example, if the map background is white and a style is configured to draw in white, the style color is changed to black so that the data that is drawn is visible against the background. 
There is a special color value that can be assigned to a style that directs NetWorks Core to use the background color. So, you could configure a style that draws using this special color. It would draw in white if the map background color is white and it would draw in black if the map background color is black. 
Before version 10.1, area styles (and text box styles) with solid fill (or with hatching and fill) did not obey that rule. You could configure an area style to fill with white and it would fill with white, even if the background of the map was white. As part of replacing the rendering system, the color behavior (relative to the background color) of fill styles has been modified to be consistent other color behaviors. A step has been added to the metadata upgrade to modify the fill color for any text box styles. If a text box has a non-null or non-transparent fill color, that fill color has been modified to use the special background color value. The underlying assumption is that most text that uses a filled text box is being used for text masking and the intended behavior is to "blank" out the portion of the map where the text is to be drawn before drawing the text. Hexagon realizes that there may be text box styles that are intended to be filled with some color other than the background color. Therefore, as part of the metadata upgrade, the G3E_TEXTSTYLE table is copied before it is modified. That way, after the table is modified by the upgrade script, you can pull rows that you did not want to be modified from the copied table back into G3E_TEXTSTYLE. There are more details on this issue in the upgrade process itself.

### Text Size Differences
The rendering system used to calculate font size in NetWorks Core 10.1 has changed. 
Therefore, the labels for features might display at a slightly different size, either smaller or larger than before. If the text displays larger, labels can overlap or run into labels or features where they did not before (see Examples 1 and 2). You can change the size of the text, if necessary, in [G3E_TEXTSTYLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/0yRaZQ44AZMeTckCYodWaQ).G3E_SIZE.   
|  Example 1 Current version: ![TextSizeDifferences2EX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/290806) Example 2 Before version 10.1: ![TextSizeDifferences1EX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/290806)  |  
| --- |  
Why this Happens
NetWorks Core must convert the font size from points, as specified in metadata, to the appropriate pixel size for drawing on the screen at a given display scale. Pixel sizes are restricted to integer values. Before version 10.1.0, the rendering system computed the font size in pixels at a given scale and then truncated the result to an integer. In version 10.1.0, the rendering system computes the same font size in pixels and rounds the result to an integer. Therefore, font sizes for the two results should differ by no more than one pixel. However, the smaller the font size, the larger the influence one pixel can have. 
This can also affect the appearance of the text when zooming out to a high display scale. In both version 10.1.0 and prior versions, there are special cases to handle text that is too small to be represented on the screen. In those cases, a simpler graphic is drawn. Before version 10.1.0, the simpler graphic was very small and faint. In version 10.1.0, the algorithm for drawing the simpler graphic has changed causing it to be somewhat larger and more noticeable. Before version 10.1.0, the simpler graphic was typically a single pixel per line of text. In version 10.1.0, the simpler graphic is a small rectangle. Note that this only happens when text is being displayed at a significantly higher display scale than the text would be readable.   
|  Example 3 Before version 10.1.0 ![TextSizeDifferences3EX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/290806)  |  Example 4 Current version ![TextSizeDifferences4EX](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/290806)  |  
| --- | --- |

## Generating Diagnostics from NetWorks Core Products

### Database Diagnostics

#### Database Diagnostics API
Use the GTECHIDAG.G3E_DIAGCONTROL package to initialize diagnostics and enable the modules and categories for which to generate diagnostics output. 
  1. Initialize
Initialize the diagnostics system by providing information of the Oracle session to enable diagnostics for. These procedures will add an entry to DIAG_INFO table.   
|  Procedure  |  Arguments  |  Purpose  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  InitializeSession  |  SessionId V$SESSION.AUDSID%TYPE  |  This function initializes the G/Tech diagnostics for the specified session. It returns the diagnostic identifier for the session.  |  
|  InitializeSession  |  Sid V$SESSION.SID%TYPE,   
Serial V$SESSION.SERIAL#%TYPE   |  This function initializes the G/Tech diagnostics for the specified session. It returns the diagnostic identifier for the session.  |  
|  InitializeMySession  |   |  This procedure initializes the G/Tech diagnostics for the current session. Use this to turn diagnostics if running procedures in SQLDeveloper or another SQL tool.  It returns the diagnostic identifier for the session.  |  
  2. Enabling
The diagnostics needs to know what diagnostics to capture. Call an EnableLoggingModule procedure to enable a Module and categories to diagnose.

| --- | --- | --- |

It inserts a row into the MODULES_TO_DIAG table for the diagnostics id for each module that is enabled.   |

|  EnableLoggingSubsystems  |  DiagId DIAG_INFO.DIAG_ID%TYPE SubsystemNames G3E_STRING_TABLE  |  This procedure enables diagnostic logging for the diagnostic modules in the specified subsystems for the specified diagnostic identifier.  It inserts a row into the MODULES_TO_DIAG table for the diagnostics id for each module that is enabled.   |

#### Database Diagnostics Tables
Metadata Tables
These tables define the modules, subsystems, and categories of the database diagnostics system. 
  1. DIAG_CATEGORIES
This table defines the diagnostics categories that be turned on. The categories are like the Diagnostics categories in the NetWorks Core Diagnostics Manager.

|  DESC  |  The description of the category Used in enabling and disabling procedures  |  VARCHAR2(50 CHAR)  |  Y  |  N  |  
Values  
|  Category  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  -1  |  All  |  
|  0  |  None  |  
|  1  |  Error  |  
|  2  |  Enter/Exit  |  
|  3  |  Return Value  |

This table defines the modules that are available for diagnosing. Rows may be added to this table to define custom user modules to support database diagnostics.
