Runtime Tables
These tables define the Oracle session for which to turn diagnostics and the modules and categories to include in the diagnostics output. Rows are inserted and updated to this table with the enabling and disabling diagnostics procedures. 
  1. DIAG_INFO
This table defines the properties for a single diagnostics id. Entries are added to this table by the enabling procedures.   
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  DIAG_ID  |  The diagnostics id  |  NUMBER  |   |  
|  AUDSID  |  The Oracle session AUDSID being diagnosed  |  NUMBER  |   |  
|  USERID  |  The Oracle user for the Oracle session  |  VARCHAR2(30)  |   |  
|  TIMESTAMP_FORMAT  |  This is the format to be used to write out time stamps. The procedure SetTimestampFormat may be used to change the time stamp format.   |  VARCHAR2(50 CHAR)  |  MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI:SSXFF3  |  
|  LOGTOFILE  |  If "Y," the diagnostics will be logged to a file. This is set by the EnableFileLogging procedure.   |  CHAR(1)  |  N  |  
|  LOGTODBMSOUTPUT  |  If "Y," the diagnostics will be output via DBMS_OUTPUT calls. This is set by the EnableDBMS_OutputLogging procedure.   |  CHAR(1)  |  N  |  
|  FILE_TYPE  |  This is the type of the file to create. This may be overridden with EnableFileLogging procedure. Valid values are INIX or WINDOWS.   |  VARCHAR2(7 CHAR)  |  UNIX  |  
|  FILE_MODE  |  This is the mode of the file. It may be overridden with EnableFileLogging procedure. Valid values are TEXT or BYTE.   |  VARCHAR2(4 CHAR)  |  TEXT  |  
|  FILE_CHARSET  |  This is the character to use for the diagnostics output.The default is the Oracle character set. May be overridden with EnableFileLogging procedure.   |  VARCHAR2(64)  |   |  
|  FILENAME  |  This is the name of the diagnostics file. It is set by the EnableFileLogging procedure.  |  VARCHAR2(36 CHAR)  |   |  
  2. MODULES_TO_DIAG
This table defines the modules and categories to be diagnosed for a diagnostics id.  
|  Column Name  |  Description  |  Type  |  Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|  DIAG_ID  |  The diagnostics id  |  NUMBER  |   |  
|  MODULE_ID  |  The module id  |  NUMBER  |   |  
|  CATEGORIES  |  The category bitmask for the diagnostics and module ids  |  RAW(16BYTE)  |  hextoraw('00000000000000000000000000000000')  |

#### Enabling Database Diagnostics Example
There are several steps to enable the database diagnostics. This example shows the steps to enable database diagnostics. 
  1. NetWorks Core
Start NetWorks Core and connect to the database. 
  2. Find logging directory
This query will return the path to where the log file will be written to on the database server: 
select directory_path from all_directories where directory_name = 'GTECH_DIAG_LOG';
  3. Find session to enable diagnostics
The diagnostics system needs to know the Oracle session for which to turn on diagnostics. Run the query below to find the session id of the NetWorks Core session for which to set diagnostics. 
This is just one example of how to find the Oracle session.
<MACHINENAME> is the name of the machine that is running NetWorks Core. 
select AUDSID from v$session where program = 'G3E.exe' and machine = '<MACHINENAME>';
  4. Initialize diagnostics
To initialize the diagnostics system, call InitializeSession giving it the AUDSID value from the find session query above. The InitializeSession function returns the diagnostics id that is input to most of the other calls to the diagnostics system. 
InitializeSession inserts a row into DIAG_INFO.
Execute the PL/SQL block below to initialize the diagnostics system for the Oracle session id. The output from this PL/SQL block will be the diagnostics id to be used below. 
<SESSION ID> is the AUDSID value returned from the find session query above. 
set serveroutput on size 999999
declare 
diagID number;
begin
diagID := GT_DIAG_CONTROL.InitializeSession(<SESSION ID>);
dbms_output.put_line(diagID);
end;
/
set serveroutput off
  5. Module to diagnose
Set the module to diagnose for a diagnostics id. 
EnableLoggingModule inserts a row into MODULES_TO_DIAG with CATEGORIES column set to all zeros. 
Run the SQL below to enable a module to diagnose. Execute for each module for which to enable diagnostics. <DIAGNOSTICS ID> is the value return from the call to InitializeSession; <MODULE> is the name of the module on which to enable diagnostics. See description of the DIAG_MODULE table. 
exec GT_DIAG_CONTROL.EnableLoggingModule(<DIAGNOSTICS ID>,'<MODULE>');
commit;
  6. Categories to diagnose
Set the categories to be diagnosed for the diagnostics id and module. 
EnableCategoryModule updates the row in MODULES_TO_DIAG for the diagnostics id and sets the CATEGORIES to the bitmask for the category. 
Run the SQL below to specify the categories for a module that has been enabled.
<DIAGNOSTICS ID> is the value return from the call to InitializeSession; 
<MODULE> is the name of the module for which to enable categories. 
<CATEGORY> is the name of the category to be enabled to the module. See description of the DIAG_CATEGORIES table. 
exec GT_DIAG_CONTROL.EnableCategoryModule(<DIAGNOSTICS ID>,'<MODULE>','<CATEGORY>');
commit;
  7. Enable file logging
Turn file logging on for the diagnostics id.
EnableFileLogging updates the row in DIAG_INFO for the diagnostics id setting the FILENAME column to the filename returned. 
Execute the PL/SQL block below to define set the filename for the diagnostic id.
<DIAGNOSTICS ID> is the value return from the call to InitializeSession. 
set serveroutput on size 999999
declare
filename varchar2(48);
begin
filename := GT_DIAG_CONTROL.EnableFileLogging(<DIAGNOSTICS ID>);
dbms_output.put_line(filename);
end;
/
set serveroutput off
commit;
  8. Run workflow
Run the NetWorks Core workflow to capture the diagnostic information. 
  9. Disable logging
To turn off diagnostics logging for the diagnostics id and module, run the SQL below to turn off diagnostics logging where 
<DIAGNOSTICS ID> is the value return from the call to InitializeSession;
<MODULE> is the name of the module for which to enable categories. 
exec GT_DIAG_CONTROL.DisableLoggingModule(<DIAGNOSTICS ID>,'<MODULE>');

### Diagnostics Manager

#### Running Diagnostics Manager
You can generate diagnostics about certain areas of the NetWorks Core products using Diagnostics Manager. You can enable and disable diagnostic logging while you are running the product. 
  * To generate diagnostics from NetWorks Core products:


  1. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Diagnostics Manager. 
The Diagnostics Manager dialog displays. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259047) Some executables require administrative privileges to run properly. Due to UAC restrictions, these executables might not run correctly without elevated privileges. To do this, right-click and select Run as administrator.See the [Running HxGN NetWorks Core Executables with Elevated Privileges](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/access/sources/AITM/topic?ait:code=1462188) topic in the HxGN NetWorks Core Installation Guide for more details. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/jEzt2ZGZjueCH2QP3GTtng-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=130420ee72d23a1c&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  2. Check Diagnostic logging. 
  3. Type a name and location for the log file.
  4. To clear the log, check Flush diagnostics now and with each session. 
  5. Select only the product, [categories](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/7xX7B_vERfkLcHh~OUHqFA), and subsystems for your problem. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259047) NetViewerPlotting[diagnostic tracing](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Z0A6UY87N1cAOX_BUaTRjQ) for troubleshooting. 
  6. Optional: Click the Advanced tab. This tab contains the following parameters that are to be used only in conjunction with Hexagon Support. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259047)
Use special naming convention—If this option is checked, the diagnostic process generates a unique log file name, which is in the following format: 
<Specified log filename without extension>-<Username>-<Parent G3E Process ID>- <Date-Time stamp>.<Specified log file extension>
Use shared memory—Instead of directly writing to the log file, the diagnostic process records the information into a shared memory and use a separate process called Diagnostic Logger to write that information to the specified log file. This preserves information in the event of a system failure and reduce the overhead to the NetWorks Core application. This checkbox does not influence any running processes; that is, it does not change the mode of a running process from log file to shared memory or vice versa. This checkbox enables the following options: 
     * Remove log file on normal exit—If checked, the log file is removed when the application exits. 
     * Number of blocks—Specify the number of blocks of shared memory to be allocated by the diagnostic object. 
     * Timeout to check exit status—Used by the Diagnostic Logger to check whether its parent NetWorks Core process is still running. When this time is elapsed and the parent NetWorks Core process has terminated either normally or abnormally, the logger writes the remaining information from the shared memory to the log file. 
     * Size of diagnostic log file—Specify the size of the log file. If this value is 0, the Diagnostic Logger continues to write to a single log file regardless of its size. If this value is greater than 0, the Diagnostic Logger generates a log file with <- 1> appended to the log file name before the extension. If the first log file reaches the specified size, the Diagnostic Logger starts writing to the second log file with <-2> appended to the name of the log file name before the extension. If the second file also reaches the specified size, the logger reverts back to the first file, and so on. This results in retaining at least one full log file, but no more than two files, regardless of the run-time of the application. 
     * Size of shared memory—A label that indicates the size of the shared memory (in megabytes). This label provides the actual shared memory that is allocated so that you can adjust the number of blocks required. 
  7. Click Apply. 
  8. Open and run the appropriate product until the problem occurs.
  9. Review the log file. 
  10. To disable diagnostics logging, repeat Step 1 to open the Diagnostics Manager dialog box, uncheck Diagnostic logging, and click Apply. 
  11. Continue to run the product.

#### Viewing Diagnostic Results
The log file generated is a text file that can either be opened with any text editor or by using the Diagnostic Viewer (DiagViewer.exe). The Diagnostic Viewer displays the diagnostics file by dynamically loading the information as it is generated. Microsoft Excel can also be used to view the file by using the vertical bar (|) as the column separator. 
  * To review diagnostics results:


  1. Run [Diagnostics Manager](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pSK1xlRfgXNzARFgnmjggA), make selections, and click Apply. 
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Diagnostics Viewer. 
  3. Open and run a NetWorks Core product to the point of failure. 
  4. Note that the diagnostics are displayed in the Diagnostics Viewer window as they are generated. Because multiple running images can share the same log file, multiple copies of a running object, or several threads, the identity of the logging software is recorded in the following fields: 

  
|  Field  |  Description   |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Process  |  Process ID  |  
|  Thread  |  Thread ID  |  
|  Instance ID  |   |  
|  SourceFileName   |   |  
|  ProcedureName  |   |  
These are the other fields used in the Diagnostics Viewer:   
|  Field  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Date  |  Date diagnostics are run  |  
|  Time  |  Time diagnostics are run  |  
|  Duration  |  Reports the length of time a process step took in seconds  |  
|  Subsystem  |  Corresponds to subsystems listed in Diagnostic Manager  |  
|  Category  |  Corresponds to Diagnostic Categories shown in Diagnostic Manager  |  
|  Message  |  Used for textual progress type messages  |  
|  Value1  |  Used for variable values  |  
|  Value2  |  Used for variable values  |  
|  Value3  |  Used for variable values  |

## Metadata Scripts

### Adding Data Support
[G3E_DATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/_ZuCX4G4mblLkZOTURP~6g) supports the definition of data required for appropriate software functions in Field Review. This table lets you tell the PublishSubset about tables that are part of the data model but are not referenced in the metadata. 
The field G3E_DATASUPPORT.G3E_TABLE can be any table, view, sequence, package, or procedure object. The specification is used by the NetWorks Core server to create sequences and synonyms and to grand permissions to objects. PublishSubset also uses the information to determine what tables or views, that are not already specified in the metadata, must be replicated. The metadata content already specifies components, foreign key tables, domain tables, and picklists for replication as well as the metadata tables themselves. 
PublishSubset
Although the PublishSubset process already knows what metadata tables and data model tables (components) to include in a subset, it does not know which special data tables or result tables are required to support the Field Review commands and services. If PublishSubset should copy the contents of the tables as well as the structure of the tables, then set G3E_DATASUPPORT.G3E_COPYDATA to Yes (1). 
Examples of tables or views to include in G3E_DATASUPPORT  
|  Table or View  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Data tables  |  These tables are comparable to picklists but are not defined in metadata as picklists. For example, you have a post- process object that performs some static lookups. The lookup data are stored in a table. You should list this table so the post-process object performs correctly on the field unit. Do not list picklist tables here. Normally, G3E_COPYDATA is set to Yes (1) for this type of table.   
 |  ![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/261586) The word KEY is a reserved word in SQL Server Express (SQL Server) and should not be used as a column name in any table.   |  
| --- |  
 |  
|  Result tables  |  These are tables required by commands to hold temporary results. For example, the TRACERESULT table holds the keys of the traced data. To run traces in the field unit, you must be sure that this table is replicated. Normally, G3E_COPYDATA is set to No (0) for this type of table.   |  
Permissions
As NetWorks Core is a database application, users must be granted permissions to perform certain functions or access certain data. The Data Support table lets you configure permissions on data or result tables you add as well as to control permissions on the NetWorks Core packages. 
Permissions are defined under named [roles](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/KfGUZVurERUNF384ngn2ug) and assigned to users. The default metadata expresses the expected constraints using the default roles. However, the metadata provided here lets you specify other roles and does not limit you to the constraints of the system default roles. You should not specify component tables or views here. You are responsible for those roles.   
|  Role  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Synonyms  |  The LTT_Role package uses the items of type table and view to create synonyms in both the office and field database.   |  
|  Procedures, tables, views  |  The LTT_Role package uses all of the items to grant privileges to the appropriate roles of users within the environment.   |  
The G3E_GRANTPRIVILEGE and G3E_GRANTROLE fields together control the application of permissions to the data objects. 
  * If populated, the fields contain comma-separated lists of privileges and roles.
  * If you leave these fields null, NetWorks Core defaults the privileges and roles. 


If you introduce multiple sets of privileges, you must define the associated roles. When different privileges are assigned to multiple roles, semicolons separate the expressions.   
|  Example The data table is MY_SPECIALVALUES. The built-in roles are DESIGNER, FINANCE, MARKETING, and SUPERVISOR. For users with FINANCE and MARKETING roles, you want to limit access to the table to SELECT.  The following definition provides this control:  
 |  G3E_TABLE   |  MY_SPECIALVALUES  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  G3E_GRANTPRIVILEGE  |  SELECT;INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE,SELECT  |  
|  G3E_GRANTROLE  |  MARKETING,FINANCE;DESIGNER,SUPERVISOR  |  
Since two sets of privileges are separated by semicolons: 
Select
Insert, update, delete, select 
There must be two sets of roles separated by semicolons: 
Marketing, finance
Designer, supervisor
 |  
Populating G3E_DATASUPPORT
The metadata upgrade scripts should be the primary source of content for this table. However, you can get out of sync with the upgrades. Entries are created in this table through PopulateBasicMetadata.sql for all data models. 
Additional entries are added for specific data models or functionalities. Each of these scripts is run when the [installation script for that functionality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/siHnpyLxZ2Hz7PE4ZQ~Nig) is run. Do not run these scripts directly unless your metadata configuration is empty.   
|  Data Model or Functionality  |  Script  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Communications  |  PopulateCommMetadata.sql  |  
|  Electric  |  PopulateEDTMetadata.sql  |  
|  Field inspection  |  PopulateFieldInspectionMetadata.sql  |  
|  NetViewer and Field Review  |  PopulateMobileNetMetadata.sql  |  
|  CES  |  PopulateCESMetadata.sql  |  
|  Login Mapping  |  PopulateLoginMappingMetadata.sql  |  
|  SAP  |  PopulateSAPMetadata.sql  |  
|  STORMS  |  PopulateSTORMSMetadata.sql  |

### Adding Metadata Support
NetWorks Core metadata is structured for discoverability. This means that, instead of using a fixed set of metadata tables that require constant maintenance, NetWorks Core finds the tables within a particular configuration. The system does have a core or fixed set of tables, but most tables are found by searching G3E_ANALYSIS, any of its associated interface tables, and the Metadata Support table, [G3E_METADATASUPPORT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/P0SCSQgrxakO8MZiQ2MQQw). 
G3E_METADATASUPPORT supports the publishing of metadata by keeping the list of tables unrelated to a particular analysis or interface known to the publishing algorithm. Any table referenced in this table is published if there is an entry in the optimized table column. 
This table allows NetWorks Core to introduce customized views of metadata. If all the metadata information exists but is just needed in a new form to control processing, then rather than specifying the G3E_TABLE and G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE names, you can populate the G3E_XMLKEY and G3E_XMLQUERY fields. 
G3E_XMLKEY is like the name of the optimized metadata table. This key name must not conflict with any of the other metadata optimized table names in this configuration. G3E_XMLQUERY contains the full SQL needed to publish additional XML metadata for the key specified in G3E_XMLKEY. These entries are populated in G3E_METADATAKEYS_OPTABLE for RAW file publishing. 
Populating G3E_METADATASUPPORT
The table can be populated by running the script @PopulateBasicMetadata.sql. However, you should not run this directly unless your metadata configuration is empty. Additional entries are added for specific data models or functionalities. Each of these scripts is run when the [installation script for that functionality](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/siHnpyLxZ2Hz7PE4ZQ~Nig) is run so there is no need to run these scripts directly.   
|  Data Model or Functionality  |  Script  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Communications  |  PopulateCommMetadata.sql  |  
|  Electric  |  PopulateEDTMetadata.sql  |  
|  Export  |  PopulateNetExportMetadata.sql  |  
|  Pipeline  |  PopulatePipelineMetadata.sql  |  
|  NetViewer and Field Review  |  PopulateMobileNetMetadata.sql  |  
|  Electrical Analysis  |  PopulateElecAnalysisMetadata.sql  |  
|  SAP  |  PopulateSAPMetadata.sql  |  
|  STORMS  |  PopulateSTORMSMetadata.sql  |  
If required tables are omitted from G3E_METADATASUPPORT, the client software may not function correctly. If you have errors in NetWorks Core that seem fundamental, you may have missing table references. Review the script and add the appropriate entries. Then republish metadata.

### Loading Default Values
You can populate the default values for basic operational control by running the scripts delivered in the \GTechnology\Services\MetadataEntries folder. You can update the values in these columns to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat, or update them afterward.   |

|  PopulateMobileNetMetadata.sql  |  Enables Field Review and NetViewer metadata. This script is run if you set the HasMobileNet flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file.   |  
|  PopulateNetExportMetadata.sql  |  Enables Export metadata. This script is run if you set the HasNetExport flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file.   |  
|  PopulateOMSMetadata.sql  |  This script is run if you set the HasOMS flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file.  You can update the G3E_PARAMETER1 column in the G3E_OMSIFACE table to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat.   |  
|  PopulatePipelineMetadata.sql  |  Enables pipeline data model metadata. This script is run if you set the IsPipeline flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file.  This script contains insert statements for populating the G3E_VALUE column in the G3E_GENERALPARAMETER table.  You can update the values to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat.   |  
|  PopulateSAPMetadata.sql  |  This script is run if you set the HasSAP flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file. The G3E_PARAMETER1 column can be updated to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat.   |  
|  PopulateSTORMSMetadata.sql  |  This script is run if you set the HasStorms flag to Y in the SetUpgradeEnv(ConfigurationName).bat parameter file. Contains insert statements for populating the G3E_PARAMETER1 column in the G3E_STORMSIFACE table.  You can update these values to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat.   |

Contains insert statements for populating the G3E_PARAMETER1 column in the G3E_GENERICWMSIFACE table.  You can update these values to match your database before running InstallGTechObjects.bat.   |

### Metadata Management Fields
These fields help you to manage and maintain metdata: 
G3E_EDITDATE
All metadata tables contain the G3E_EDITDATE field. The Metadata subsystem maintains this date and uses it to identify fields modified since the last publishing operation. 
G3E_LOCALECOMMENT
A field in all metadata tables that contain localizable fields such as G3E_USERNAME. You can populate this field with instructions for the translator to describe the meaning and usage of the fields. See the [localization](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ULLV~0L5tT_sOephmL16yQ) topic for details on this process.

### The Metadata Optimization Process
Create optimized tables by executing the following scripts in an SQL editor:
SQL> execute MG3EConfiguration.SetConfiguration('<your database configuration name>;');
SQL> execute MG3EOTCreateOptimizedTables;
These scripts do the following tasks:
  * [Populate the metadata keys list](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Wk5qmpMRpvtotFbC3RMxxw). 
  * Optimize every table in [G3E_METADATAKEYS.G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLENAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/6aZcCuzHiRLhK8MY3VQKhg). 
  * Optimize each legend table.
  * Optimize each Display Control table.


The following scripts grant privileges and define synonyms to give all users access to the optimized metadata tables in the production schemas: 
SQL> execute LTT_Role.Grant_Metadata_To_Role;
SQL> execute LTT_Role.Create_Metadata_Synonym;
SQL> execute LTT_Role.Createsynpicklist;

## Recovering the Database from Backups

### Offline Recovery
Execute offline or cold backup recovery on a database that was shut down normally. Offline recovery replaces the corrupt database files with copies that have been saved off after a normal shutdown of the database. You can recover the database to the point in time the offline backup was taken. You must replace all files, even ones that are not corrupt, because Oracle database files (data files, control files, and log files) have time stamps and sequence numbers in the headers of each file. So, all files must be synchronized. 
  * To recover a database from offline backup:


  1. Shut down the database. If necessary use the abort parameter.
  2. Delete the existing corrupt data files, control files, log files, and the initialization parameter file. 
  3. Place the backup files from the cold backup in the correct folders. Be sure to place the files in the original folders from which they were backed up. 
  4. Start up the database.

### Online Recovery
To recover a database using online or archive log mode, the database must be running in archive log mode. Archive log mode copies all log files to the archive log destination based on the parameter, LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST. 
  * To recover a database online:


  1. Shut down the database.
  2. Copy the corrupt or missing file from the backup location to correct location.
  3. 'Startup mount' the database.
  4. 'Set autorecovery on'.
  5. 'Recover database'.
  6. 'Alter database open'. The correct log files from the archive log file are applied.

## Setting Up Work Space Templates
You can deliver one or several [work space templates](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VhXWMx3pWz3QNSu5HKUrfg) to each client machine as a part of your remote delivery process. Each template could be for a different purpose, such as a plotting template, but all users would be using the same templates for their work. Give each template a descriptive name with a .gft extension. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263025) Work space templates can also be placed on a common share, for example \\\ShareName\templates. 
By default, work space templates are stored in the \GTechnology\Templates\GeoWorkspaces folder. You can [change this folder](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/sEj6oPyxL8VSq2u3KQ6svw) through Tools > Options > File Locations or through the registry: 
HKEY_CURRENT_USER > Software > Intergraph > GFramme > 02.00 > PreferenceSet > GeoWorkspaceTemplateFileLocation  
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263025) Changing the registry improperly can damage the computer configuration.   |  
| --- |  
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263025) Based on metadata configuration, role handling prevents specific users from displaying data from restricted components/legend entries. When a user saves a legend to a work space - whether as a named legend or associated with a map or detail window - it retains the privileges of the user who created the work space or work space template. The software does not reapply any role checks if other users open that same work space and access that legend.

## Starting NetWorks Core from the Command Line

### Starting a Custom Command from the Command Line
You can use LaunchGIS.exe to automatically execute a custom command from the Command line. The utility activates a job before executing the custom command. The custom command specified (either by the command line argument passed to LaunchGIS for AutoCustomCommand or [configuring metadata to automatically start a custom command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uagBp1BNNUcuW0QM9scU1w)) executed once all other processing to invoke NetWorks Core has been completed. This includes the setting of the active job and the attachment of the appropriate legend. 
  * To automatically start a custom command from the Command line:


From the Command prompt, change to the \GTechnology\Program folder, and type the following: 
LaunchGIS.exe Config=<Configuration name> Username=<username> Password=<Password> AutoCustomCommand=<CCNO of custom command> AutoCustomCommandArgument=<Argument string> ActiveJob=<Job number>  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Username  |  The username to use during connection  |  
|  Password  |  The password to use during connection  |  
|  Config  |  The configuration to which to connect  |  
|  AutoCustomCommand  |  The CCNO value from the G3E_CUSTOMCOMMAND table of the custom command you want to start   |  
|  AutoCustomCommandArgument  |  String value added to the [IGTApplication's](Ms-its:Intergraph.GTechnology.Desktop.API.Reference.chm::/html/T_Intergraph_GTechnology_API_IGTApplication.htm) properties collection, for example, the path to an XML file.   
 |  Example Application.Properties.Item("AutoCustomCommandArgument")  |  
| --- |  
 |  
|  ActiveJob  |  The name of the job to activate before the custom command executes  |  
|  Example LaunchGIS.exe Config=ALLTEST Username=Myusername Password=Mypassword  
AutoCustomCommand=50 AutoCustomCommandArgument="A string" ActiveJob=12345-1  |  
| --- |  
Related Topics
[Implementing Custom Command Objects](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LCGaRCpQhSd842cjvEzvQ)
[Starting a Custom Command Using Metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/uagBp1BNNUcuW0QM9scU1w)

### Starting NetWorks Core from a WMS
To invoke NetWorks Core from a work management environment and to reference a specific job or work space associated with a work request, you execute LaunchGIS.exe with the Command line arguments listed below. 
Required Command-line Arguments  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Username  |  The username to use during connection  |  
|  Password  |  The password to use during connection  |  
|  Config  |  The configuration to which to connect  |  
|  Request  |  The work request number  |  
|  Version  |  The job version  |  
Optional Command-line Arguments  
|  Parameter  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Legend  |  The legend to attach when bringing up the work space  |  
|  Template  |  The template to use if accessing the job for the first time and when creating the initial work space   |  
|  Menu  |  The menu option from the work management interface that was used to invoke LaunchGIS. If this value is APPLICATION, NetWorks Core is launched in read-only mode with no active job regardless of the work request and version that is passed.   |  
|  ViewParam  |  A debugging tool that if set to 1 displays the Command line arguments as LaunchGIS receives them. This is especially useful when trying to determine if the work management application is passing the necessary expected arguments.   |  
|  Example <\GTechnology\Program>/LaunchGIS.exe USERNAME=<Username>;  
PASSWORD=<Password>; CONFIG=<Configuration>;   
REQUEST=<Work Request>; VERSION=<Version Number>; LEGEND=<Legend>;  
TEMPLATE=<Template>;VIEWPARAM=<0 or 1>;  |  
| --- |  
Results
If the work request and version combination is being accessed for the first time on the client machine, a new work space is opened that is the name of the job, for example, 15425-1.gfw. If the work space is not saved, then the next time this work request/version is accessed, it performs as if accessing the work space for the first time. 
If the work request/version is generated into a NetWorks Core job, this job becomes active when the NetWorks Core launch is complete. 
In the following circumstances, NetWorks Core is launched in a read-only mode (a connection is made but no job is active): 
  * The job does not exist in the job table.
  * The job has already been closed.
  * The Menu parameter was passed to the LaunchGIS executable with a value of APPLICATION.


If the work space was saved, the LaunchGIS application uses that work space when initializing NetWorks Core. The area that was last saved in the work space is the area that is displayed, just like a work space that has been saved and is reopened from within NetWorks Core. 
If region metadata has been set up and if a job is created and the region data are populated, it is used to window to the area of the region when a work request/version is accessed for the first time. If the work space has been saved for this work request/version, the saved area view is brought back up as it was saved, and the region is ignored. To use the region in this manner, [set up metadata that defines the region areas](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/QRd0wuOWkqGRnYo38GGbFA).

## Trimming the Table GDT_TABLEMODLOG
Entries are recorded in the GTD_TABLEMODLOG table whenever edits are made to NetWorks Core master facility data with the following sub-systems enabled across the enterprise: 
  * CES Extraction
  * CIM Export
  * Publish Subsets


As more and more edits are performed over time, this table could grow to an excessively large size, resulting in performance issues. In order to overcome such a performance bottleneck, it is important to periodically trim the rows from the GDT_TABLEMODLOG table. Deciding when to trim depends on the sub-system (or combination) used within the enterprise. The database administrator needs to be careful when deleting rows from this table, as each sub-system interacts with this table at different times: 
  * CES Extraction—This system uses the table for creating the incremental dump of data files used by CES Outage Management System. 
  * CIM Export—After the creation of full export XML, any subsequent data edits performed are used to generate the incremental export XML. This is similar to the way the table is used by Publish Subset. 
  * Publish Subset—This system uses the table for generating the first incremental (after a full publish) and any subsequent incrementals, based on the High Watermark recorded for previous incrementals. 


The wrongful deletion of rows within this table can invalidate the process of creating incrementals, thereby requiring the execution of the full cycle for a given sub-system, which can be costly. Take care when using the combination of these sub-systems. 
  * To trim the GDT_TABLEMODLOG table:


  1. Run the following anonymous PL/SQL block and note the High Watermark it displays.
SET SERVEROUTPUT ON SIZE 999999
DECLARE
nTableModLogNum NUMBER := 0.0;
BEGIN
G3E_MANAGEPOSTWATERMARKS.GetMaxTableModLogWatermark( nTableModLogNum );
DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE( 'High Watermark = ' || nTableModLogNum );
END;
/
SET SERVEROUTPUT OFF
  2. Execute the full cycle for a given sub-system. 
     * For CES Extraction, create the full data dump or perform the incremental extraction.
     * For CIM Export, export the full or incremental XML.
     * For Publish Subset, publish a full subset. When using regional subsetting, the full subset should be generated for each of the regions before trimming the contents of the table. 
  3. Verify the veracity of the full cycle. Validate the data after importing or visualizing into the targeted sub-system. 
  4. Trim GDT_TABLEMODLOG via the following SQL:
DELETE FROM GDT_TABLEMODLOG WHERE MODIFICATIONNUMBER < FLOOR(<<High Watermark obtained from first bullet>>);

### Configuring HTTPS
To configure HTTPS protocol on NetViewer, make sure that NetViewer is properly configured and running using HTTP. Follow the steps in the given order. If any point is omitted or an error is made, it will be necessary to drop the configuration and start from the beginning. 
  * To configure HTTPS: 


  1. Configure SSL bindings on the IIS (customer’s IT department assistance might be required to provide SSL certificate). 
  2. Enforce SSL for GViewerApp and Maps under both application by selecting SSL Settings > Require SSL; click Apply. 
  3. Restart all services by running Restart Web Applications from Start Menu > GTechnology\NetViewer. 
  4. Clean temporary files and GNetCache folder from %temp% user profile. 
  5. Start IngrViewer.exe /webserver:https:<your netviewer https bind host name>. 
  6. Check if NetViewer client starts successfully. 
![Warning](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/1267515) If you do not want to remove HTTP protocol from IIS, exit the workflow here. 
  7. Remove HTTP binding from IIS.
  8. Open NetViewer server web.config in a text editor (located under GTechnology\Program\GViewerApp). 
  9. Navigate to the services section under "system.serviceModel" and replace all bindingConfiguration="GNetViewerWebHttpBinding" with bindingConfiguration="GNetViewerWebHttpsBinding". 
  10. In the same section, replace - endpoint address="mex" binding="mexHttpBinding" with - endpoint address="mex" binding="mexHttpsBinding". 
  11. In the webHttpBinding section, remove or comment out the section - binding name="GNetViewerWebHttpBinding". 
  12. In the same section, find - binding name="GNetViewerWebHttpsBinding" and change the transportation protocol by adding proxyCredentialType="None" to <transport clientCredentialType="None"/>. 
  13. Clean temporary files and GNetCache folder from %temp% user profile. 
  14. Start IngrViewer.exe /webserver:https:<your netviewer https bind host name>. 
  15. Check if NetViewer client starts successfully. 


  * To restart the procedure from the beginning: 


  1. Delete GViewerApp and Maps applications from IIS. 
  2. Delete GNetViewerPool from IIS. 
  3. Run GNetViewerConfiguration wizard and configure services.

### Configuring Licensing On the Client Machine
The NetWorks Core All Applications Configuration Wizard configures licensing on client machines. The following text file contains license information: 
%PROGRAMDATA%\Intergraph\Licensing  
|  File Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  CLCR_LICENSE_PATH  |  License server and/or location of the client license file using semicolon as a separator.  The contents of the client license file may contain only the license server details, as shown in the example below.  Example @mylicserver Or @129.135.186.195 Alternatively, if you have configured a specific port (for example, 40000), you can specify the following value:  40000@mylicserver  Or 40000@129.135.186.195 Alternatively, Web Server IP can also be configured for a specific port (for example, 3000), and you can specify the following value:  40000@mylicserver+3000 Or 40000@129.135.186.195+3000 If TCIP/IP and Web Server Port numbers are not provided, default port numbers are assigned.  5053@mylicserver+5054 Node lock license file (any file name with .lic extension) can be used to access licenses for a specific machine:  Assuming that the client license file is stored at %PROGRAMDATA%\intergraph\Licensing\nodelocked folder, you can specify the above path in Client License File section in AllAppWizard.  This nodelock license Path is appended to CLCR_LICENSE_PATH file. Nodelock license and server details can be provided simultaneously If needed, you can specify license details in both ways using a semicolon as a separator in CLCR_LICENSE_PATH:  C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\Licensing\nodelocked;@mylicserver  |

### Connection Problems
If you cannot connect to your database configuration, use the following checklist to help you determine the problem: 
  * Run [ValidateDeltasConsistency.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EDODAmcLctOR521WtAnL0w) to check for DDC, MODIFICATIONLOG, and database consistency. The tool ensures that the definitions of the component view in the three locations are consistent and identifies mismatches in the definition of the database view against the published DDC; either the oracle view needs to go back to the prior definition or the DDCs need to be republished. 
  * Run DDCScan.exe to verify that the DDCs have not been corrupted during network transfer or during the publish operation as the result of a packet failure. 
  * Use an SQL Editor to log into the database using the same username and password as the user who encountered the error. Ensure that the alias specified for that configuration in the CCM file is used for this connection test. This determines if the problem is the database access. 
  * Check the size of [the MODIFICATIONLOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4SuOwTsXAXirwxZCrM8VSQ) paying particular attention to the [number of entries after the watermarks](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Iw2pQKvtbosIFYBpV9Q~gw) represented by the various DDC files. If a large number of deltas need to be processed, the problem could be that the system is taking a long time to query for modifications but it is progressing. 
  * Using [Diagnostics Manager](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/pSK1xlRfgXNzARFgnmjggA), turn on the following subsystems: Command Management, Component Data Access, Connection, Data Context, Deltas. Repeat the connection attempt. Review the log file to determine if additional error messages are recorded that might help correct the environmental problem. 
  * Use the following steps to determine if the connection problem is caused by invalid geometry: 


  1. Save the MODIFICATIONLOG to another name.
  2. Delete the entries of the MODIFICATIONLOG after a point of time where the user is sure to have been able to connect. Use the MODIFIEDDATE field to help identify this point. 
  3. If the user can connect, then the problem is very probably a bad geometry. If not, then there is another reason. 
  4. To find the bad geometry, remove entries (one half at a time) or add back entries, until you narrow down the specific entry that is causing the bad connection. Move the saved MODIFICATIONLOG back (assuming that nobody has changed anything), and fix that bad geometry in the job where it is found. You can delete this modification entry for the specific feature and redigitize the geometry in the original job. 
When you delete and add MODIFICATIONLOG entries, do not separate entries that share the same integral part of the MODIFICATIONLOG number (MODIFICATIONNUMBER field). In other words, if the MODIFICATIONLOG has entries 2, 2.0001, 2.0002, 2.0003, then make sure that these four entries are deleted together or added together.

### Feature Placement and Edit Problems
Here are some tips for troubleshooting feature placement and edit problems: 
A feature disappears from the screen when placed
  1. Make sure the current map window has a legend attached to it, the feature you placed is on that legend, and the display of that feature is turned on. 
  2. Verify that the zoom scale is appropriate for the feature:
    1. On the [Display Control](javascript:;), disable ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263056). 
    2. Update the map window.
If the feature appears, it was out of the display scale range. Try to place it when zoomed in or out appropriately. 
  3. Verify that the new feature is not hidden behind an existing feature with a higher priority on the legend: 
    1. On the Display Control, turn off all features except the one that was placed.
    2. Update the map window.
  4. If the placement occurred because of a [custom command](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/2LCGaRCpQhSd842cjvEzvQ), the problem may be in the custom command. After database manipulations and committing all transactions, call RefreshDatabaseChanges and RefreshWindows. 
  5. Determine if any filters on the appropriate legend entries are preventing the display of the placed feature: 
    1. On the Display Control:
      1. Select the legend entry in the Display Control for the component view that is not showing. 
      2. If ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263056) is enabled, a filter might be preventing feature display. 
      3. Click ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263056) and check the filter against the values in the database to see if a record is being filtered out. Or, you can remove the filter from this legend entry and see if the feature displays. 
Check the filtering for the legend entry hierarchy that does not display. There could be a filter on any level. 
    2. Use an SQL editor to check for any metadata-defined filters:
      1. Find the current legend in the database in the G3E_LEGENDS_OPTABLE.
      2. To determine which optable corresponds to the current legend, find the field G3E_JOINTABLE value in G3E_LEGENDS_OPTABLE. 
      3. Query that optable for the fields G3E_LEGENDENTRY and G3E_FILTER.
      4. Determine if a legend filter is preventing the display of the feature.
Because this optable lists the bottom level legend entries, there is only one entry to check. 
  6. Check for the consistency of the [MODIFICATIONLOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4SuOwTsXAXirwxZCrM8VSQ) sequence generator and the consistency of the component views between the DDCs, the database, and the MODIFICATIONLOG. To do this, run [ValidateDeltasConsistency.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EDODAmcLctOR521WtAnL0w). 
If this tool reports problems, republish the appropriate facility data, purge the MODIFICATIONLOG, and place the feature again. If the tool reveals problems with the MODIFICATIONNUMBER sequence generator, reset the sequence generator to something higher than any watermark in any DDC and the MODIFICATIONNUMBER of the MODIFICATIONLOG in the database. 
  7. Verify that the [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/X9EcOVIWIsiQzIZGdzin3A) table has an entry for every CNO that lends data to the disappearing component view. If one or more CNOs are missing or incorrect, correct the problem, republish metadata, and reinstall the [modification tracking triggers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yx6ZJuobhZM62uk4hDv2Vg). 
  8. Verify that component view definition in Oracle is correct. Check the TEXT field of USER_VIEWS for the disappearing component view. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263056) More than one component view could be defined to display the particular graphic. Be sure to investigate all of them. 
  9. In the USER_VIEWS table for the disappearing component view, determine if the component view definition in Oracle is filtering out that particular feature. 
  10. Check the coordinate system metadata. Coordinate system problems could make the feature jump to a position other than where it was placed. Check these fields for the appropriate configuration: 
    1. [G3E_DATACONNECTION.G3E_CSNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XVSORnBdhQjIxL9aNJ0TPw) — The coordinate system of the database 
    2. [G3E_CONFIGURATIONS.G3E_CSNAME](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/vWwv39pUkFaofbuloNJ4lQ) — The coordinate system for the DDCs for the configuration 
If these two values are correct, look in the [GCOORDSYSTEMTABLE](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XwuKVI_U5ObpDp0hIkR1tA) to see if those coordinate systems exist and if they have reasonable values. 
  11. Check the styles defined for the feature in the legend. The style could be the same as the background color of the screen or the same as a feature that is hiding the new feature. 
  12. Verify that data are placed in the database for that component view:
    1. [Create a new job](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/SyT9lcV2eeceSwXLzo0KfA), and place only the disappearing feature in it. 
    2. Use an SQL editor to query the LTT_IDENTIFIERS for LTT_NAME to determine the LTT_ID for the new job: 
SQL> select * from LTT_IDENTIFIERS WHERE LTT_NAME ='<Name of new job>';
    3. Use an SQL editor to query the MODIFICATIONLOG to determine the FID for the new feature:
SQL> select * from MODIFICATIONLOG where LTT_ID = <value you discovered earlier>; 
If this query yields nothing, skip the rest of the checks in this step, and go to the next step. 
    4. Use an SQL editor to query the new job:
SQL> execute LTT_USER.EDITJOB('<New job name>');
    5. Use an SQL editor to query the data for the disappearing feature:
SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID from <offending component view name> where G3E_FID =<FID for feature>;
    6. If there is no data, correct the feature placement and feature composition metadata.
  13. Verify that there are entries in the MODIFICATIONLOG:
    1. Place a single feature in a new job.
    2. Use an SQL editor to query the MODIFICATIONLOG for entries with that job. Base your query on the LTT_ID of the new job. You can use the job name to query the LTT_IDENTIFIERS table and determine the LTT_ID. When a component view is added to the MODIFICATIONLOG, the PROCESSED_FLAG value for the view is 2, the TABLENAME has the value of the component view added, and the row should have the SDO_GEOMETRY and attributes columns populated. 
If this data are missing, either the G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION is incorrect, or the modification tracking triggers are not properly installed. 
  14. Republish metadata and place the feature again.


A feature disappears from the screen when moved or edited 
  * If the tips in the section above do not solve this problem, consider the following:
  * If an attribute is edited, the feature may be eliminated based on a filter:
    * A metadata filter
    * A user-placed filter
    * The actual filter on the Oracle view that defines the component view
  * Editing an attribute could cause the feature to change its membership to another legend entry in whose display scale the feature does not display. 
  * The MODIFICATIONLOG should have data like an added record. See Step 13 above.


A feature appears twice when moved—the old location and the new location
  1. Use an SQL editor to see if there is more than one row in the component view representing the FID of the component you moved: 
SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID from <component view that has the duplicate> where G3E_FID =<FID of component>; 
  2. You can also use an SQL editor to further limit the query based on the CID of the component that was moved: 
SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID from <component view that has the duplicate> where G3E_FID =<FID of component> and <component view that has the duplicate> where G3E_CID = <CID of component>; 
If there is more than one row in the results, see if they match the two rows on the screen. If so, then you successfully moved one component, and you did not move another that happened to exist at the same location as the moved component. 


A feature continues to stay on the screen after it is deleted
  1. Check for the consistency of the [MODIFICATIONLOG](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/4SuOwTsXAXirwxZCrM8VSQ) sequence generator and the consistency of the component views between the DDCs, the database, and the MODIFICATIONLOG. To do this, run [ValidateDeltasConsistency.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/EDODAmcLctOR521WtAnL0w). 
If this tool reports problems, republish the appropriate facility data, purge the MODIFICATIONLOG, and attempt to place the feature again. If the tool reveals problems with the MODIFICATIONNUMBER sequence generator, reset the sequence generator to something higher than any watermark in any DDC and the MODIFICATIONNUMBER of the MODIFICATIONLOG of the database. 
  2. Verify that the [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWCOMPOSITION](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/X9EcOVIWIsiQzIZGdzin3A) table has an entry for every CNO that lends data to the disappearing component view. If one or more CNOs are missing or incorrect, correct the problem, republish metadata, and reinstall the [modification tracking triggers](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/yx6ZJuobhZM62uk4hDv2Vg). 
  3. Verify that the definition for the component view in Oracle is correct. Check the TEXT field of USER_VIEWS for the disappearing component view. 
  4. Check the MODIFICATIONLOG. There should be just one row in the MODIFICATIONLOG corresponding to the LTT_ID, component view, and G3E_FID for the disappearing component view. It should have a PROCESSED_FLAG of 2, and the SDO_GEOMETRY column should be Null. If this data are missing, install the modification tracking triggers and try again. 
  5. Determine if there are multiple component view rows that appear to be identical. One instance of the component view could have been deleted, but there are other instances, thus indicating that no records were deleted. This situation can occur in NetWorks Core when the Oracle definition for the component view has particular join criteria that include multiple records. To check for this, follow this workflow: 
    1. Use an SQL editor to query the job being edited on the desktop:
SQL> execute ltt_user.editjob('<job name being edited>'); 
    2. Run this query statement:
SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID from <component view> where G3E_FID = <FID of feature/component being deleted>; 
If this query reveals multiple records, then it is likely that only one instance of the feature was deleted. If this query reveals one record, then perhaps another instance was deleted, or perhaps the original delete was not successful. 
  6. If the graphic did not disappear when it should have because of changing an attribute value, check the [G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION.G3E_ATTRAFFECTSMEMBERSHIP](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3HXuJCbhR4Htau5yrp55kw) field. If an attribute determines membership in a component view, set this field to Yes (1). 
  7. Republish metadata.


A feature reports NULL geometry but geometry exists in the database
The geometry as presented in Feature Explorer is retrieved from the DDC or Deltas. The deltas are constructed from the graphic component view defined in G3E_COMPONENTVIEWDEFINITION for the component. 
  1. Using an SQL editor, query the graphic component view:
SQL> select G3E_ID, G3E_FID, G3E_FNO, G3E_CNO, G3E_CID, G3E_GEOMETRY from <graphic component view that corresponds to the component with NULL geometry> where G3E_FID =<FID of component>;
  2. If no rows are returned, review steps 6-9 and 12-13 in the first workflow to make sure the graphic view is valid and that deltas are created for this graphic component view.

### Help Problems
The following are common problems you may encounter using this Help: 
Text is too large or too small
The default size of text in NetWorks Core Help and other Internet Explorer applications depends on the screen resolution for your monitor. To change or check this, select Display from the Windows Control Panel, and click the Settings tab on the Display Properties dialog box. 
If your mouse has a wheel, you can increase or decrease the text size by clicking the Help topic pane to give it focus and then pressing CTRL while rolling the mouse wheel up or down. 
If your mouse has no wheel, you can resize the text with the Text Size options on the View menu in Internet Explorer. 
Help cannot be displayed over a network
Microsoft security update 896356 prevents certain features in NetWorks Core HTML Help from working. These problems can be fixed, but you need to understand the security implications of using the workarounds. See <http://support.microsoft.com/kb/896905/>. NetWorks Core setup does not add this entry to your registry. 
These registry settings are located in the registry tree under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE.
SOFTWARE\Microsoft\HTMLHelp\1.x  
|  Key Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ItssRestrictions  |  To get Help to display over the Web or network, add the following to your registry: Data type: REG_DWORD Value name: MaxAllowedZone Value data: 3 Base: Hexadecimal ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/263040) This key overrides a Microsoft security patch, so using it is not recommended.   |

### Launching NetWorks Core Using a Command Prompt or as a Published Application in Citrix
[Application registration](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ee872121\(v=vs.85\).aspx) is a capability provided by Microsoft to find an application executable and to prepend the PATH environment variable during execution to search for its dependencies. From version 10.1 SP2 and forward, the ZIRFL library required by the raster engine is delivered in the shared <drive>:\Program Files \Intergraph folder. To resolve the dependency, NetWorks Core setup adds the App Paths registry keys for standalone applications including G3E.exe (NetWorks Core) under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths or HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/430093) This information applies to both Designer/Analyst and Field Review.
This capability works only if the executable is launched in a shell. When you launch the application through a shortcut or Windows Explorer, it is always launched in a shell; however, if you launch the application through a command prompt or as a published application in Citrix, you might get an error or see unexpected behavior such as listed below: 
  * Attempted an unsupported operation.
  * Error creating a new work space Source:GFrammeCommandDescription:Automation Error.  
The object invoked has disconnected from its clients. 
  * You are unable to load a legend after invoking Field Review from the command prompt. 


  * To update the environment variable: 


  * The application is launched in an interactive session (for example, from a command prompt). 
Add the path <drive>:\Program Files \Intergraph or <drive>:\Program Files (x86)%\Intergraph to the user or system PATH environment variable. 
  * The application is launched from a non-interactive environment (for example, in a Citrix environment). 
Add the path <drive>:\Program Files \Intergraph or <drive>:\Program Files (x86)%\Intergraph to system PATH environment variable. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/430093) If you add the path to the system PATH environment variable, reboot the computer.

### Locating Debug Files
If you need information about a NetWorks Core problem, call Customer Support (see [](javascript:;)). The support personnel directs you to unpack the files in the /PDB folder on the NetWorks Core delivery DVD. 
This folder contains compressed ZIP files that hold program database files used for debugging. Each .pdb file contains debugging information for the program element indicated by its name. These files are not installed by setup and are not necessary for normal operation of NetWorks Core software.

### Memory Usage Problems With Corrupt Raster Images
Some customers have reported out-of-memory errors or excessive use of memory when displaying raster images. In some cases, the problems have been traced to a corruption in the tiles or overviews stored in the raster image. Recreating the tiles or overviews solves the problem. Although it is not easy to determine if an image has a corrupt tile or overview, the ImageStation Raster Utilities (ISRU) package, [available from the Support site](https://support.hexagonsafetyinfrastructure.com/infocenter/index?page=browse&productref=1_4HD47M&channels=SUPPORT_FILE&category=UTILITIES__TOOLS&downloads=yes), can recreate the tiles and overviews. 
If you encounter errors or excessive memory usage when displaying raster images, first try to isolate the problem to the specific images.   
|  Example If the problem occurs when a specific image is panned into view, that image is suspect.  |  
| --- |  
Once you identify the suspected images, use the ISRU tools to recreate the tiles and overviews. If that does not solve the problem, then please contact your Hexagon representative for assistance.

### Menu Layout Problems
Menu and toolbar layout for a given user is a combination of the role of the user as assigned in G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION, the menu and toolbar layout you establish in G3E_MENULAYOUT before you publish a configuration, and menu and toolbar settings persisted in the registry of the user. See [Configuring the Menu and Toolbar Layout](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zSZsIpXCcgAPF~FlMbQ8JQ) for more information. 
The menu and toolbar settings of the user are preserved at the following registry location: 
HKEY_CURRENT_USER > Software > Intergraph > GFramme > 2.0 > Menus > <configuration name>-<user name>
The following diagram shows the logic for menu layout:
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/257127)
If you have unexpected problems with menu layout or commands that are missing, check the following areas: 
  * Verify that the command is listed in the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table. The command must be listed in this table, and the command's user must have the role assigned to the command. 


Verify that you did not accidentally remove commands, add commands, delete toolbars, and so forth, and then publish the layout. Users see the layout you have published. Adding the appropriate role to the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table does not make the command reappear. The [correct layout](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/zSZsIpXCcgAPF~FlMbQ8JQ) must be published. 
Because, the menu and toolbar layout for a user is persisted in the registry when they log into and exit a database and close a work space, the user could "lose" a command. The following is an example workflow:   
|  Example
  * The command is missing from the G3E_ROLEASSOCATION table.
  * The user logs into NetWorks Core, finds the command missing, and then exits NetWorks Core. The menu layout is persisted. 
  * The command is added back into the G3E_ROLEASSOCATION table and published.
  * The user logs back into the database as the same user. The command does not automatically appear on the menu in its proper location because the menus and toolbar layout is persisted from the last NetWorks Core session of the user. 
  * This workflow is the same as the user logging in to a NetWorks Core database, running [Tools > Customize](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ITbElKQSLidrszAnG7ZECg), removing the command from the menu, and exiting the database. When the user logs in to the same database, menus and toolbars display as customized in the previous session. 

 |  
| --- |  
Menus and toolbars can be reset to the published layout several ways:
  * The individual user can, from the Tools menu, select Customize and click Reset on the Customize dialog box Menu tab. (This resets to the currently published menu layout.) 
  * You can use Metadata Explorer to impose a new menu layout, or you can use an SQL editor to delete all rows from the G3E_MENULAYOUT table (which gives the user the default layout), and ask the user to accept a new layout as follows: 
    1. In the Metadata Explorer tree view, Navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version > CommandVersion node and increment the version number in the G3E_ROLE field. 
    2. To impose the new menu layout on users, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version Notification > CommandVersionNotification node and select Change in the G3E_ROLE field. 
OR
    3. To allow users to make a decision about using the new menu layout, in the Metadata Explorer tree view, navigate to the Access Control > Version > Command Version Notification > CommandVersionNotification node and select PromptToChange in the G3E_ROLE field. 
    4. Publish the metadata changes.


The following is an example of an incomplete administrative workflow. The administrator's intent is to add the missing command for the user. However, because the menu layout and version control were not updated, the command is still missing. In this workflow, log in with administrator privileges:   
|  Example
  * The command is missing from the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table.
  * You create a new menu layout in G3E_MENULAYOUT and publish both the layout and the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table. 
  * The command is missing from menus and from the published layout.
  * You add the missing command to the G3E_ROLEASSOCIATION table but not to the menu layout and publish. 
  * You log on with user privileges and try to get back to the default menus by removing the <configuration name>- <user name> key from the registry. However, the published menu layout overrides the default menus. The command is still missing from the user menu. 

 |  
| --- |

### NetWorks Core Registry Keys

#### Add-On Registry Entries
Each add-on is responsible for installation of the add-on and for required registry entries. 
For add-ons, the Upgrade Wizard uses the following registry entries:
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GTechnology\Add-Ons\NetWorksAdministrator  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  InstallDir  |  The location where the add-on is installed on the machine  |  
|  Product Name  |  The name of the add-on  |  
|  Product Version  |  Version of the add-on installed on the machine  |  
|  MinimumCoreVersion  |  The minimum NetWorks Core version that is compatible with the add-on. NetWorks Core installation checks this value against the version of NetWorks Core being installed. If this value is greater than the NetWorks Core version being installed, the installation is terminated.  This value must be formatted according to the guidelines in the [Software Version](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/WLdcBzHsT1h1rhU_78mwqw) topic:  Valid values are:
  * Major Version: AA.MM (for example, 10.02) 
  * Minor Service Pack version: AA.MM.mmss (for example, 10.02.0101) 
  * Minor Service Pack Build version: AA.MM.mmss.bbbbb (for example, 10.02.0101.34001) 

This registry entry is optional. If it does not exist or is empty, NetWorks Core installation skips this check for the add-on, and the installation proceeds.   |  
Example

All of these keys are managed by Diagnostics Manager. The values should only be set by the application.   
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  DiagExitStatusTimeout  |  Used by the Diagnostic Logger to check whether its parent NetWorks Core process is still running. When this time is elapsed and the parent NetWorks Core process had terminated either normally or abnormally, the logger writes the remaining information from the shared memory to the log file.   |  
|  DiagFile  |  Name of the file to capture the diagnostics  |  
|  DiagFlush  |  Zero or one to indicate if the diagnostics should be flushed with each session (1) or not (0)   |  
|  DiagLogFileSize   |  Specify the size of the log file. If this value is 0, the Diagnostic Logger continues to write to a single log file regardless of its size. If this value is greater than 0, the Diagnostic Logger generates a log file with <-1> appended to the log file name before the extension. If the first log file reaches the specified size, the Diagnostic Logger starts writing to the second log file with <-2> appended to the name of the log file name before the extension. If the second file also reaches the specified size, the logger reverts back to the first file, and so on. This results in retaining at least one full log file, but no more than two files, regardless of the run-time of the application.   |  
|  DiagMaskN Where N is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4  |  Programmatic mask variables that indicate the subsystems to monitor  |  
|  DiagNumOfBlocks  |  Specify the number of blocks of shared memory to be allocated by the diagnostic object DiagRemoveLogFileOnNormalExit. If checked, the log file is removed when the application exits   |  
|  DiagState  |  Application property used in conjunction with diagnostic monitoring  |  
|  DiagUseSharedMemory  |  Instead of directly writing to the log file, the diagnostic process recordd the information into a shared memory and use a separate process called Diagnostic Logger to write that information to the specified log file. This preserves information in the event of a system failure and reduce the overhead to the NetWorks Core application. This checkbox does not influence any running processes, that is, it does not change the mode of a running process from log file to shared memory or vice versa.   |  
|  DiagUseSpecialName  |  If this option is checked, the diagnostic process generates a unique log file name, which is in the following format:  <Specified log filename without extension>-<Username>-<Parent G3E Process ID>-<Date-Time stamp>.<Specified log file extension>  |

#### Raster Registry Keys
Several registry keys control the amount of memory and the size of the cache used by the raster display system. It is recommended that these be left at their default values unless you experience significant raster performance problems. 
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RasMemLimit  |  This value affects only the performance of binary raster images. It indicates how much memory (in megabytes) the raster display system can use for image data. The value is a string, and the default value is 10, indicating 10 megabytes of memory. This string value is the default and not an added key. If you have a lot of memory on your system, and you display a lot of raster data, increasing this value might improve performance. Conversely, if you have low memory, decreasing this value improves performance of the product overall.   |  
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\RasterCache  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  cacheLimit  |  This value sets the number of images that are retained in memory in the raster cache for the process. This includes all images. The raster cache holds information on images and pointers to the raster engine used to display them. No pixel data are contained in the cache. This is handled by the raster engines. The value is a string, and the default value is 300.   |  
|  MemoryMapUNC  |  This value determines if memory mapping is done on images specified by a UNC path. The default value is 1. This entry is only necessary to allow memory mapping to be cut off for UNC-specified images if necessary to avoid network drop out problems with handling of UNC paths that are memory mapped.  1=Memory mapping is done. 0=Memory mapping is not done.  |  
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\RasterCore  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  RasStripBuffer  |  This value affects only the performance of binary raster images. It indicates the approximate amount of memory used for internal operations (such as resampling and rotating) on raster images before displaying or printing the images. The value of this key is not set by default. If the registry key is not set, NetWorks Core computes the size of this buffer based on the size and resolution of the display device, creating a buffer size that is typically about 3 megabytes.  In most cases, raster images are acceptably displayed and printed using the default buffer size. Printing and plotting operations with large page sizes and large images or rotated images may benefit from a significantly larger buffer size. For example, large plots (up to A0 size) that contain rotated raster images on HP-PCL printers can produce huge spool files if the default buffer size is used. You can reduce the size of the spool files by 80 percent or more by changing the buffer size to 50 megabytes. This change can have a correspondingly positive effect on printing and/or plotting performance. To affect batch plotting performance, change the registry setting on the Plotting application server.  Conversely, if you increase this buffer size too much, the change can negatively affect behavior and performance of NetWorks Core and your system in general. For example, NetWorks Core could run out of memory, fail to access DDC files, or perform poorly (due to excessive paging) if excessive memory is allocated to this buffer. Each installation is different, so test your behavior and performance carefully after changing this setting.   |

#### Subset Registry Keys
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Intergraph\GNetViewerPublishSubset  
|  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  PublishThread  |  Data type: REG_DWORD  
Value data: 00000004 If the entry does not exist, the default value of 4 is used. The combination of SQL Server and the multithreaded capabilities in Publish Subset causes the transaction log files (.ldf) of the generated subsets to significantly grow in size. This increased size has several adverse consequences. 
  * Subsets with large .ldf files take longer to connect to, sometimes causing timeout errors. 
  * You have to store and copy these files tying up critical system resources.

The information in these transaction log files is used by SQL Server to restore corrupted databases. Because these subsets are not generated interactively over time, but are generated using a batch or bulk process, this information is not needed and is really more of a burden to the system.  During subset publishing, the SQLServer transaction log file (*.ldf) may become very large. To solve this issue, Publish Subset can shrink the subset database and the associated transaction log file.  You can configure how often the database is shrunk during the publish subset process using a registry variable to control how many component tables are pulled before the database is shrunk. A value of 0 indicates shrinking only occurs at the end of the process, not between component tables. The default is 0. You can modify the value by changing the ShrinkAfterXComponentTables registry setting.   |  
|  ShrinkAfterXComponentTables  |  Data type: REG_DWORD  
Value data: 00000000 If the entry does not exist, the default of 0 is used.  |  
|  Data  |   |
