### Oracle Connection Problems
When you upgrade your Oracle client, the default Oracle home and the Oracle client interface location might not be updated correctly. As a result, you cannot make an ADO connection using the Microsoft Provider for Oracle, and the following error message appears when you try to connect: 
Oracle error occurred, but the error message could not be retrieved from Oracle.  
| 
  * To set the default Oracle home:


  1. See if your registry lists one or more Oracle home keys under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ORACLE. If there is more than one key with a Home prefix, such as Home0, Home1, or Home2, there is more than one Oracle home. 
  2. Browse through each home key and look at the ORACLE_HOME and ORACLE_HOME_NAME values. If the path set as the value for ORACLE_HOME does not exist, you may delete that home key. 
  3. Set the value of DEFAULT_HOME under the key to a valid home name—that is, the ORACLE_HOME_NAME HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ORACLE\ALL_HOMESvalue of a valid home key, such as Home0, Home1, or Home2. 
  4. Under the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ORACLE key, set the ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_HOME_NAME, and ORACLE_GROUP_NAME values to the Oracle home key (Homex) that was set as default. 
  5. Under the same HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ORACLE key, change any other entry that points to a removed Oracle folder to the valid Oracle folder that was set as default in step 3. 

 |  
| --- |

### PNG Files
NetViewer, Field Review, Legend Builder, and the NetWorks Core WMS and WMTS services all use MapServer helper processes to create PNG images for map results. Previously, the map images were always compressed 8 bit PNG format files. Performance (specifically the time required to transfer the map from server to client) was the reason for the original design. Creating 8 bit instead of 24 bit PNG provided a 3 times improvement in size even when every pixel was different from the surrounding pixels. That scenario never happens, and the PNG format compression algorithm saves space by recognizing that adjacent pixels are the same value most of the time. 
When more than 256 colors were used by the renderer, the image was post processed to optimize the color palette down to just 256 colors by applying one of two color reduction algorithms. If the registry value, MostUsedColorsPNG, was set to 1, then that algorithm was used; otherwise the original color reduction algorithm was used. Both algorithms would reassign color values in the image that were not in the 256 palette to a nearest color that was in the palette. When the colors that got reassigned came from raster image data, or were introduced by translucency styles drawing on top of other features below, or from font smoothing, then the effects were not noticeable; but when one of the metadata style colors got reassigned, you would see a dramatic change in the look of the map as you panned and zoomed. An important side effect of the color optimization was that raster data (especially photo realistic data) was changed to use less than 256 colors which enabled the PNG compression algorithm to find more opportunity to save space, and that saved transfer time from the server to the clients. 
Shifting colors from one map rendering to the next can be confusing. The MapServer helper process creates true color, 24 bit PNG files by default, unless the image can be accurately represented by an 8 bit PNG file. With high speed networks, the network bandwidth is rarely the main performance bottleneck; but in cases where it is, switching to 24 bit PNG files could slow that network performance down. For that specific case, a special registry key, Create24BitPng set to 0, forces creation of the 8 bit, color reduced PNG files. When this key is missing or the value is set to 1, then the MapServer creates either an 8 bit or 24 bit PNG file based on how many colors were used to create the image.

### Run RemoveUserMenus.exe
If you remove NetWorks Core from a server and then reinstall it, Designer might crash when you run NetWorks Core. 
Solution:
Run RemoveUserMenus.exe from the GTechnology\Program folder.

### Running Complicated Oracle Queries
Occasionally, you might use an Oracle query that is extremely complicated, such as when you are composing SQL for queries and finds. If you are having problems running a complicated query, Hexagon suggests one of the following solutions: 
  * Put the query into an Oracle view, which is used in the SQL statement.
  * Add the query as code in a PL/SQL procedure, which is called from inside the SQL statement.

### Setting Up User Rights for a Windows Service
Several NetWorks Core software applications and executables are [Windows services](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms685967\(VS.85\).aspx). They are as follows: 
  * HxGN NetWorks Comms NetViewer MapServerManager Service 
  * HxGN NetWorks Core Plotting Application Service 
  * HxGN NetWorks Core Export Application Service 
  * NetWorks Core MessageMonitor Service 
  * NetWorks Core JobLifeCycleMonitor Service 
  * NetWorks Core Persisted Deltas Service 
  * HxGN NetWorks Comms Field Review Service 


A user account is needed to execute a Windows service. Based upon your site requirements, you choose the user account needed to execute a Windows service. A user account can be built-in (local), domain, or a special [service user account](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms686005\(VS.85\).aspx). Some set of [user rights ](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms878695.aspx)are needed by the chosen user account to execute a Windows service. Depending upon your Windows operating system and the chosen user account, some of the user rights are enabled by default but are configurable. Typically, [Log on as a service](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms813948.aspx) is required when a domain user account is chosen to execute a Windows service. 
See the following topics for examples of typical required user rights:

### Symbols Disappear at Different Map Scales
If you experience issues with symbols disappearing, shifting, or chopping off while you are zooming in or out, your True Type Font (.ttf) might need to have hinting added to it. 
The example workflow below to add hinting to a True Type Font file uses free font editing software called FontForge. 
  1. Open MMMI5.ttf in FontForge software. 
  2. Press CTRL+A to select all the fonts in the file.
  3. Click Hints > Remove Instr Tables. 
  4. Select Hints > AutoHint. 
  5. Select Hints > AutoInstr. Click OK on the message box that displays. 
  6. Select Hint > Clear Instructions. 
  7. Select File > Generate Fonts to save the file by generating new font file. 
![FontForge](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/YNy5cVhCbF09rxRvorsj3Q-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=898d714f4d09ba6d&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
    1. When the Generate Fonts dialog box displays, TrueType should be selected from the first field. Leave rest of the settings. 
    2. Type the file path, and click Save to generate a file at that location. 
  8. An errors detected dialog box appears. Click Save. 
The file generated in the specified location has hinting.

### Unable to Repair a NetWorks Core Installation
If you see an error stating that MDAC cannot be installed when you repair a NetWorks Core installation on a Windows 8.1 or on a Windows 2012 operating system, you must uninstall NetWorks Core and reinstall the product. The repair function is not supported on these operating systems.

### WMS Configured to Use HTTPS
Error: No legend entry corresponds to the input name. 
Solution: In the g3e.exe.config file, add the following line: 
<AppContextSwitchOverrides value="Switch.System.Net.DontEnableSchUseStrongCrypto=false"/>
to the <configuration> <runtime> section. 
If there is a manual proxy configuration in the internet options, add:
<system.net>
<defaultProxy useDefaultCredentials="true" />
</system.net>

### Checking VBA References in a Data Set
Because support for Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) has been removed in NetWorks Core 10.2, before you can use the Upgrade Wizard to upgrade your data set to 10.2 you must follow these steps to find out if you still have VBA projects referenced in your dataset and what actions you need to take: 
  1. Navigate to the \GTechnology\Services\MigrationTools\RemoveVBATool folder. Install the database procedure in script CheckVBAReferences.sql as schema owner. 
  2. Run the database procedure:
SQL> execute CheckVBAReferences;
This procedure generates two log files in the same folder as the [metadata validation folder](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/b3Hcmsjkheh0xRouaU8Rrw): 
     * VBARef_<schema owner name>.txt – Logs all the referenced and non-referenced VBA projects in your dataset in plain text format. 
     * VBARefForExcel.csv – Logs the same information in Microsoft Excel. 
If you have multiple datasets and want to collect VBA reference information for all datasets in one single Excel file: 
       1. Run the procedure without argument for the first database. 
       2. Run the procedure for the subsequent database like the following which appends instead of overwriting the results: 
SQL> execute CheckVBAReferences(1);
  3. Open the .txt log file generated above. 
If it says “No referenced VBA projects found.” go to Step 6.
OR
If the log file lists VBA projects, review the VBA project list and decide which projects you should convert to .NET to preserve the functionality and which you can remove. 
  4. To remove a VBA project, delete the related row from the interface table that references the VBA project. The database trigger on the interface table deletes the related row from the G3E_VBAPROJECT table automatically. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/398402) You should save all existing VBA projects to an archive location before you start converting them to .NET. 
  5. To convert a VBA project to .NET, do the following:
    1. Create a new .NET interface to replace the VBA project. Refer to steps 1 to 3 in [Implementing a .NET Custom Extension](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/BswFj09xt6MEoiBdTN5z~A). 
    2. Make sure to change the associated metadata (feature, component, attribute, and so forth) that references the original VBA project to reference the new interface row. 
    3. Test the new .NET interface to make sure the functionality is the same as the original VBA project. 
    4. Remove the original VBA project by deleting the related row from the interface table that references the VBA project. 
  6. The G3E_VBAPROJECT table should be empty after you convert all the VBA projects to .NET. However, it may contain a VBA project that is not referenced by other metadata. Be sure to remove any projects. 
  7. Drop the CheckVBAReferences procedure.

### Database-Software Version Compatibility

#### Mixing NetWorks Core Versions
For every release of the NetWorks Core product family, a base suite of automated tests and a set of manual workflow tests are performed before the release is made available to customers. The scope of testing depends on the nature of the release; major releases with architectural changes undergo the most thorough certification. 
With every product release, care is taken to minimize the effect to existing configuration and customization that is in production use at customer sites. When new configurable functionality is introduced, defaults are set, whenever possible, to maintain previous behavior. Configuration wizards are provided to step administrators through configuration decisions. Regarding customization, backward compatibility with the previous version’s API is maintained so that existing custom code runs after product upgrades. In the few cases where backward compatibility is not possible because of technological constraints, effects and recommended resolutions are documented in the Database-Software Version Compatibility document delivered with NetWorks Core. 
Enterprise production deployments of NetWorks Core often involve hundreds, or even thousands, of users running several different client applications (for example, desktop, web, and mobile). Upgrading all users simultaneously to a new NetWorks Core version can present real challenges for a company’s IT organization and business operations. When new versions of NetWorks Core are made available, compatibility of client applications with previous maintenance releases of the same release version and, when possible, previous release versions are maintained. This allows flexibility in making upgrade roll-out plans for client users. 
Utmost effort is applied to have newer versions compatible with lower versions of other NetWorks Core client applications. However, version compatibility is not always possible due to factors such as adoption of new technologies or architectures. For example, new capabilities that have been added to a newer version of NetWorks Core applications are not available to prior versions of the NetWorks Core applications. If mixed-version compatibility is not possible, this is communicated in the documentation delivered with the product and posted to the [Support page](https://smartcommunity.hexagonppm.com/) when the new software is made publicly available. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/484273) In general, software from a quarterly update runs alongside other components of the system that remain at the base major release version. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/484273) Any new functionality available in a new release may not function in a mixed-version environment. 
![Note](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/484273) The publish subset database should be produced from the same SQL Server version or lower version used by the HxGN NetWorks Core Field Review machine when opening that subset. 
The sections below provide specifics of mixed-version compatibility support with various combinations of NetWorks Core products. 
The term database in these sections refers to the metadata structure, as well as the database packages and procedures. The packages and procedures support metadata and NetWorks Core operations like LTT, trace, and job management. 
If you upgrade the database, the administrative users must operate with that same version of software to use metadata or to use API functions provided in the release. 
If you do not upgrade the database, new software that relies on the new metadata does not operate.

For every release of the HxGN NetWorks Core product family, a base suite of automated tests and a set of manual workflow tests are performed before the release is made available to customers. The scope of testing depends on the nature of the release; major releases with architectural changes undergo the most thorough certification. 
With every product release, care is taken to minimize the effect to existing configuration and customization that is in production use at customer sites. When new configurable functionality is introduced, defaults are set, whenever possible, to maintain previous behavior. Configuration wizards are provided to step administrators through configuration decisions. Regarding customization, backward compatibility with the previous version’s API is maintained so that existing custom code runs after product upgrades. In the few cases where backward compatibility is not possible because of technological constraints, effects and recommended resolutions are documented in the HxGN® NetWorks Core Release Notes.

### Detecting and Removing Optional Unsupported Metadata from the Database
To ensure a smooth and successful upgrade of your NetWorks Core database, the Upgrade Wizard automatically detects optional metadata subsystems that are installed and displays the result on the Upgrade Wizard — Verification screen. Use this information to verify which optional metadata is currently functional in the database and which optional metadata you must remove from the database to appropriately configure the data model for your installation. 
  * To detect and remove optional unsupported metadata from the database:


  1. Use your current business model to determine what optional metadata subsystems are required for your database. 
  2. Verify that a path is set in the DatabaseLocalDirectory entry in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER.
  3. Install the current version of the CHECKOPTIONS package by executing the following in an SQL editor: 
SQL> @"<\GTechnology>\PLSQL\ltt\checkoptions.sql";
SQL> @"<\GTechnology>\PLSQL\ltt\prvtcheckoptions.plb";
  4. Type the following in an SQL editor:
SQL> Execute CHECKOPTIONS.ALLOPTIONS
This database procedure creates a list of all the optional metadata currently in the database and which ones are installed. 
The procedure generates the <UserName>_AllOptions.log file on the database server in the path set by the DatabaseLocalDirectory entry in G3E_GENERALPARAMETER. The log file contains an entry for each optional area. The procedure checks each [optional area](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xd3~VxyrfT~E3miVdWRYnw) and determines if the optional area is: 
    1. Completely installed and supported
    2. Completely installed and not supported
    3. Not completely installed and supported
    4. Not completely installed and not supported
  5. If the report displays results b or c for an optional area, use an SQL editor to [remove the metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eLhsIu7HmUKRtVZ9mB1VpA) for that optional area.

### Handling Upgrade Wizard Errors
If the upgrade process fails, you see error messages, and information is stored to allow you to resume the upgrade at the point of the failure. All text and error messages displayed in the Upgrade Progress screen are written to the log file you determined on the Settings screen: <LogPath>/Upgrade<ConfigurationName><Upgrade To Build>.log. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259004) Infrequently when the upgrade process fails, you see no error messages, and the ResumeUpgrade<ConfigurationName>.rsm is not generated. If the <LogPath>/ResumeUpgrade<ConfigurationName>.rsm file is not created, you need to create an Upgrade Wizard resume file. See the [Upgrade Wizard Resume File](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/XUWjsI_2PJxNgfXl0kqGNA) topic for details. 
  * To resume after an upgrade failure:


An error can occur during one or more of the following processes: 
Structure upgrade
  1. To identify the script that failed and its log file name, review the lines in the Upgrade Progress screen: 
Structure upgrade error occurred in <scriptname>
See log file <logfilename> for details
    1. Click View Errors to open the log file. 
    2. Click Open Script to open the script file. 
  2. Determine the line in the script that failed.
  3. Comment out all lines to the point of failure, and correct the line that failed.
OR
Take corrective action in the database.
  4. Save your changes.
  5. Click Resume to continue the upgrade process. 
The upgrade process begins with the script that failed.


Metadata PL/SQL
  1. To identify the script that failed and its log file name, review the lines in the Upgrade Progress screen: 
Metadata PLSQL upgrade error occurred in <scriptname>
See log file <logfilename> for details
    1. Click View Errors to open the log file. 
    2. Click Open Script to open the script file. 
  2. Determine the line in the script that failed.
  3. Determine the cause of the error, and take corrective action in the database.
Errors in this process are usually due to the following:
     * Improper modifications made to modifiable scripts
     * Improper determination of optional database functionality
  4. Save your changes.
  5. Click Resume to continue the upgrade process. 
The upgrade process begins with the script that failed.


Data Structure Upgrade
  1. To identify the script that failed and its log file name, review the lines in the Upgrade Progress screen: 
Structure upgrade error occurred in <scriptname>
See log file <logfilename> for details
    1. Click View Errors to open the log file. 
    2. Click Open Script to open the script file. 
  2. Determine the line in the script that failed.
  3. Comment out all lines to the point of failure, and correct the line that failed.
OR
Take corrective action in the database.
  4. Save your changes.
  5. Click Resume to continue the upgrade process. 
The upgrade process begins with the script that failed.


Metadata publish
  1. To identify the publish log file, review the lines in the Upgrade Progress screen: 
Metadata Publish failed <scriptname>
See log file <logfilename> for details
  2. Click View Errors to open the log file. 
  3. Determine the cause of the error, and take corrective action in the database.
Errors in this process are usually due to the following:
     * Improper modifications made to modifiable scripts
     * Improper determination of optional database functionality
  4. Close the log file.
  5. Click Resume to continue the upgrade process. 
The upgrade process begins with the script that failed.


Runtime PL/SQL
  1. To identify the script that failed and its log file name, review the lines in the Upgrade Progress screen: 
Runtime PLSQL upgrade error occurred in <scriptname>
See log file <logfilename> for details
  2. Click View Errors to open the log file. 
  3. Determine the line in the script that failed.
  4. Determine the cause of the error, and take corrective action in the database.
  5. Close the log file.
  6. Click Resume to continue the upgrade process. 
The upgrade process begins with the script that failed.

### Optional Metadata
The following lists the support criteria used by CHECKOPTIONS.ALLOPTIONS and the corrective actions for each optional Metadata subsystem. 
Industry
Electric
Support Criteria: Entry in G3E_ANALYSIS where the G3E_TABLE value is G3E_EDTIFACE. 
Corrective Action:  If the subsystem is supported and partially installed, remove the entry from G3E_ANALYSIS where G3E_TABLE is G3E_EDTIFACE and drop the identified tables. 
If the subsystem is not supported and partially installed, drop the tables identified in the log file. 
Communications
Support Criteria: None. 
Corrective Action: Drop the tables identified in the log file. 
Pipeline
Support Criteria: The existence of the table G3E_STATIONING. 
Corrective Action: Drop the tables identified in the log file. 
Miscellaneous Functionality
CSS
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/259000) This capability is not supported in NetWorks Core version 9.3 and later. However, the table can be used by custom software. 
Support Criteria: Entry in G3E_ANALYSIS where the G3E_TABLE value is G3E_CSSIFACE. 
Corrective Action: If the subsystem is supported and partially installed, remove the entry from G3E_ANALYSIS where G3E_TABLE is G3E_CSSIFACE and drop the identified tables. 
If the subsystem is not supported and partially installed, drop the tables identified in the log file. 
Duct
Support Criteria: Entry in G3E_ANALYSIS where the G3E_TABLE value is G3E_DUCTIFACE. 
Corrective Action: If the subsystem is supported and partially installed, remove the entry from G3E_ANALYSIS where G3E_TABLE is G3E_DUCTIFACE and drop the identified tables. If the subsystem is not supported and partially installed, drop the tables identified in the log file. 
Feature Import
Support Criteria: Entry in G3E_ANALYSIS where the G3E_TABLE value is G3E_FEATUREIMPORT. 
Corrective Action:  If the subsystem is supported and partially installed, remove the entry from G3E_ANALYSIS where G3E_TABLE is G3E_FEATUREIMPORT and drop the identified tables. 
If the subsystem is not supported and partially installed, drop the tables identified in the log file.

### Running the Database Upgrade Wizard
The UpgradeWizard.exe automatically imports dump files, performs the standard updates to metadata and data tables, and automatically executes the SQL statements required for a database upgrade. The wizard retrieves the information required to execute the upgrade from the database, the registry, and the delivered files. The wizard sequentially runs all incremental upgrades starting with the upgrade that follows the build of the current database and ending with the upgrade for the build currently installed on the upgrade machine. 
Full or Partial Upgrade
The database Upgrade Wizard checks the version number on the current database and the latest version you have installed to determine if a full database upgrade is necessary. If you are upgrading from one major product version to the next, for example 9.3.2 to 9.3.3, the Upgrade Wizard automatically runs a full upgrade. If you are installing upgrades within a major product version, the Upgrade Wizard considers some of the upgrade steps as optional and can skip them. This makes your upgrade process faster. 
Version Compatibility
You do not have to upgrade all the computers at your site at the same time. You can upgrade a few computers and conduct some tests on the new software, or perhaps upgrade one group of users at a time to limit the affect of upgrade on production. You can also upgrade your Field Review users and not upgrade your Designer/Analyst users. NetWorks Core [software is compatible](javascript:;) with databases that were built on a previous version of the software. 
Add-On Metadata Requirement
If Add-On functionality software is installed on the same computer as the Upgrade Wizard, only the database that contains related Add-On metadata can be upgraded. 
For example, HxGN NetWorks Comms software is installed on a server. When the Upgrade Wizard is run from the same server, it verifies that required Add-OnComms metadata exists in the database, so you can only upgrade a Comms database. If you need to update a non-Comms database, install Comms software and the Upgrade Wizard on different computers.   
|  ![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) Because the Upgrade Wizard uses 8.3 short names to process the SQL scripts run during a database upgrade, disabling 8.3 name generation may interfere with the Upgrade Wizard and is not supported.  The following registry key defaults to 1 for Windows 2008 and 2012: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE > SYSTEM > CurrentControlSet > Control > FileSystem > NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation.  Changing this key to 2 enables 8.3 name generation. Reboot your system after changing this setting.  If the /Program Files (x86) folder does not have an 8.3 short name, then you need to generate it. 
  1. Restart your computer.
  2. Run Windows in Safe mode.
  3. Log in with your domain credentials.
  4. Navigate to the drive where /Program Files (x86) folder resides and type following from the command prompt, for example:  Cmd> cd C:\
  5. Execute fsutil.exe to create an 8.3 short name for Program Files (x86). folder.  Cmd> fsutil file setshortname "Program Files (x86)" PROGRA~1

![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) If a PROGRA~1 short name already exists for another folder, you can use a different number as the last letter in the short name.   |  
| --- |  
The upgrade process does the following:
  * Loads support PL/SQL.
  * Runs all metadata incremental upgrades.
  * Loads all metadata PL/SQL.
  * Executes metadata procedures (optional when upgrading within a major version).
  * Drops and reinstalls constraints on all metadata tables and repopulates sub-language tables. 
  * Creates optimized tables and their views.
  * Runs all data incremental upgrades.
  * Loads all non-metadata PL/SQL.
  * Executes non-metadata procedures.
  * Loads MetadataVersion package to update the NetWorks Core database version. 
  * Updates the G3E_ADDON table if Add-On functionality is supported.
  * Publishes metadata.


![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) Use Replication_FieldUpgrade.bat to [upgrade a field database](javascript:;). 
  * To run the upgrade wizard:


  1. If you have not already done so, [install a new version](javascript:;) of NetWorks Core on the upgrade machine. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) During the installation, select the subfeatures under the NetWorks Core Administrative Tools for installation. The PLSQL and Services subfeatures are required to run the Upgrade Wizard. 
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Core > Administrative Tools > Database Upgrade Wizard. 
The Upgrade Wizard — Welcome screen appears and displays the software version installed on your computer. 
  3. Click Next. 
  4. On the Upgrade Wizard — Connection screen: 
    1. In the User Name field, type the Oracle username for the schema to be upgraded. The username must be the schema owner of the NetWorks Core database to be upgraded. 
    2. In the Password field, type the password for the Oracle user. 
    3. In the Configuration field, select the configuration to be upgraded. 
    4. Click Next. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) In NetWorks Core version 10.2, support for VBA is removed. You may get a message asking if you want to drop the G3E_VBAPROJECT table. If you are not sure the proper action to take, click No and read the [Checking the VBA References in a Data Set](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Z0Jzm0ze3eB_8xIWZMRv8w) topic. 
  5. On The Upgrade Wizard – Settings screen: 
    1. In the Metadata mapfile path field, browse to the location where the software should publish metadata. The default is the path defined in the ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm file for the LegendMetadata.ddc file. 
    2. In the Upgrade log file path field, browse to the location where the software should write the upgrade log files. The default is the path specified by the TEMP environment variable. 
    3. To view the current build version number, the build version number to which you are upgrading, and information such as supported industries and optional functionality, click Database Settings. 
The information on this dialog box is read-only.
    4. Click Next. 
The settings in Steps a and b are added to your registry for a specific configuration. You are not required to specify them the next time you use the Upgrade Wizard to upgrade that configuration. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/api/khub/maps/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/resources/YSzbI0kofEUzRV4lGyMJPA-_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/content?v=f037a1a2653804c3&Ft-Calling-App=ft/turnkey-portal)
  6. On the Upgrade Wizard – Script Modifications screen: 
    1. Use the arrows to navigate through the entire list of modifiable files. 
Each script name displays in the Current file field. The build number associated with the script being modified appears in the NetWorks Core version field. If the modifiable file is from an add-on application, the build number associated with the script on the display appears in the Add-On version field and the NetWorks Core build number associated with add-on’s version appears in the NetWorks Core version field. 
![](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/en-US/HxGN-NetWorks-Core-Admin-Help/258989) When you restart an upgrade after a failure, only the scripts that the Upgrade Wizard has not already run are displayed. 
    2. Use the instructions displayed in each script to modify the statements.
    3. Save each script even if you do not modify it. The script name changes from red to black when you have saved it. 
    4. When you have viewed or modified each script and saved each script, click Next. 
  7. On the Upgrade Wizard — Verification screen, review information about the upgrade. If the identified optional metadata is found but not used, the upgrade could fail. If you need to [take corrective action](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/hL5aS623yJTdhbVBVZqX7Q) in the database to remove the tables that identify [optional metadata](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/xd3~VxyrfT~E3miVdWRYnw), click Cancel. Make corrections and begin the upgrade process again. 
If you must make corrections and restart the upgrade, the Upgrade Wizard resumes the upgrade at the point where the failure occurred. 
  8. When the information is correct, click Finish.

### The Upgrade Wizard Resume File
When the Upgrade Wizard encounters errors, information is typically written to a file referred to as the resume file. On rare occasions, a resume file is not created. This topic discusses what you should do if a resume file is not created. 
The name of the resume file is ResumeUpgrade<ConfigurationName>.rsm and it is located in the log folder you specified on the Upgrade Wizard Settings screen. This file contains information to allow the Upgrade Wizard to continue the upgrade from the point of failure. 
If the Upgrade Wizard terminates abnormally, the resume file is not generated, which means that you cannot resume the upgrade from the point of failure. In this case, you must manually create the resume file. 
Resume File Format
The resume file contains five lines as shown in the table below:  
|  Line  |  Name  |  Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  1  |  Build Number  |  The incremental build number where the failure occurred.  |  
|  2  |  Failed Step  |  The upgrade step that failed  |  
|  3  |  Failed Script  |  The script that failed. This is the script that the upgrade resumes with.  |  
|  4  |  PublishMetadata  |  Not used  |  
|  5  |  Execute PL/SQL  |  Not used  |  
  * To create a resume file:


  1. Open the <LogPath>/Upgrade<ConfigurationName><Upgrade To Build>.log which resides in the log folder specified in the on the Upgrade Wizard Settings screen. 
  2. Identify the failed step.
Each step of the upgrade process is flagged in the <LogPath>/Upgrade<ConfigurationName><Upgrade To Build.log with a begin and end pair flag. If the upgrade process terminates abnormally, there is no ending flag to indicate that the step completed. The incomplete step is the one that abnormally failed and is the step to be specified in the resume file. The table below defines the beginning and the ending flags for each step of the upgrade process. This table depicts a successful upgrade. Each step of the process has a beginning and an ending line.   
|  Step  |  Log Message  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  PREPARATION  |  Beginning line: Preparing database for upgrade . Ending line: Upgrade preparation complete  |  
|  STRUCTURE  |  Beginning line: Metadata Upgrading to build <Version Number> . Ending line: Metadata Upgrade to build <Version Number> complete  |  
|  METADATAPLSQL  |  Beginning line: Upgrading Metadata PLSQL . Ending line: Upgrade of Metadata PLSQL complete  |  
|  PROCESSMETADATA  |  Beginning line: Processing metadata . Ending line: Metadata processed  |  
|  USERCONSTRAINTS  |  Beginning line: Installing constraints on user-defined metadata  Ending line: Constraint installation complete  |  
|  PROCESSOPTMETADATA  |  Beginning line: Generating the optimized tables and views Ending line: Completed to generate the optimized tables and views.  |  
|  PROCESSPOSTOPTMETADATA  |  Beginning line: Processing post optable metadata . Ending line: Post optable metadata processed  |  
|  DATASTRUCTURE  |  Beginning line: Data Upgrading to build <Version Number> . Ending line: Data Upgrade to build <Version Number> complete  |  
|  RUNTIMEPLSQL  |  Beginning line: Upgrading runtime PLSQL . Ending line: Upgrade of runtime PLSQL complete  |  
|  PROCESSRUNTIME  |  Beginning line: Processing server PLSQL . Ending line: Processing Server PLSQL complete  |  
|  POSTPROCESS  |  Beginning line: Post Process Ending line: Post processing complete  |  
|  PUBLISHMETADATA  |  Beginning line: Publishing metadata . Ending line: Metadata publish complete  |  
  3. Identify the build number.
     * If the upgrade step that failed is STRUCTURE or DATA STRUCTURE the build number can be determined by the log file. The begin flag for these steps contain the build number. It is this build number that is to go into line 1 of the resume file. 
     * If the upgrade step fails while running the Add-Ons incremental script in the STRUCTURE or DATA STRUCTURE steps, the build number is the corresponding NetWorks Core version number. 
Example
If a HxGN NetWorks Comms metadata upgrade on version 01.02.0000.01002 fails and you are based on NetWorks Core version 10.01.0002.12001, the version number displayed in the log file is the NetWorks Core version number (10.01.0002.12001), not the Comms version number (01.02.0000.01002). In other words, Comms version number 01.02.0000.01002 corresponds to NetWorks Core version number 10.01.0002.12001. 
     * For all steps other than STRUCTURE or DATA STRUCTURE, the build number is the NetWorks Core version to which you are upgrading. 
  4. Identify the failed script.
     * You can determine the script that failed from the log file. The name of the failed script is the last line in the log file. 
     * If the file extension in the script you see on the last line of the log file is .dmp, the failed script name is file name without a file extension. 
Example
If you see the line below on the last line of the log file, the failed script name is G3E_MENULAYOUT. 
Processing Import script C:\Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnology\Services\IncrementalUpgrades\Build10.02.0000.02001\Metadata Upgrade\ALLTEST1013\G3E_MENULAYOUT.dmp
     * If the failed upgrade step is PROCESSOPTMETADATA, the log file does not show the script name. For this step, use GenerateMetadataOptimizedTables.sql for the script name. 
     * If the failed upgrade step is PUBLISHMETADATA, the log file does not show the script name. For this step, use PublishMetadataMapfiles.exe for the script name. 
  5. Use the example below to create your own resume file, ResumeUpgrade<ConfigurationName>.rsm. Store the file in the log folder you specified while running the Upgrade Wizard. 
Example
Log file contains:
Metadata Upgrading to build 10.01.0003.17002
Running scripts in C:\Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnology\Services\IncrementalUpgrades\Build10.01.0003.17002\upgradescripts.lis
Processing SQL script C:\Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnology\Services\IncrementalUpgrades\Build10.01.0003.17002\Metadata Upgrade\COMMTEST1012\metadataChanges10.01.0003.17002.sql.
The resume file should look like this:
10.01.0003.17002
STRUCTURE
metadataChanges10.01.0003.17002.sql
FALSE
FALSE
  6. Resume the Upgrade Wizard process.

### Uninstalling Optional Metadata
You can use a script to uninstall optional metadata.
  * To uninstall optional metadata to an existing schema:


To uninstall optional metadata for an existing schema, use an SQL editor or Metadata Query to run the following script: 
SQL> @"\GTechnology\PLSQL\metadata\uninstall<optional functionality>.sql" "<LogFilePath>" "<\GTechnology>";
This script drops the basic metadata tables and related database objects and removes the metadata table entries for the specified optional functionality.

### Upgrading from 10.02.0000 to 10.02 SPx
To upgrade from NetWorks Core version 10.2.0 to version 10.2 SPx, follow the general workflow below: 
  1. Uninstall the existing version of the software.
  2. Run the [Upgrade Wizard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TzLTeAS72RGjfAkpnhZqhQ). 
  3. Recompile any of your VB6 custom implementation DLLs.
  4. Optional: Upgrade any [add-on applications](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GJged1rW88We97SNKl_NSw).

### Upgrading from 10.2 SP2 to 10.2.1
The Setup Wizard checks for the appropriate environment as you install version 10.2.1.
  1. Uninstall the existing version of the software.
  2. Run the [Upgrade Wizard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TzLTeAS72RGjfAkpnhZqhQ). 
  3. Recompile any of your custom implementation DLLs.
  4. Optional: Upgrade any [add-on applications](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GJged1rW88We97SNKl_NSw).

### Upgrading from Version 10.1 SPx to 10.2.x
To upgrade from NetWorks Core version 10.1 SPx to version 10.2.x, follow the general workflow below: 
  1. Uninstall the existing version of the software.
  2. [Find and remove](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/Z0Jzm0ze3eB_8xIWZMRv8w) references to Visual Basic for Application (VBA) from your data set. 
  3. [Run the Upgrade Wizard](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/TzLTeAS72RGjfAkpnhZqhQ). 
  4. Review .NET API you [created before version 10.1](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/O7rYU647ACjN3FFJFWjz8A). 
  5. Address any [licensing](javascript:;) issues for your users. 
  6. Optional: Upgrade any [add-on applications](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/GJged1rW88We97SNKl_NSw).

### Upgrading from Version 9.4.x to 10.2.x

#### Spatial Data Upgrade (SDU) Tool
Between NetWorks Core versions 9.4.x and 10.0, the storage format for data in a NetWorks Core database changed from the Oracle relational model to the Oracle spatial object model. The Spatial Data Upgrade (SDU) tool enables you to upgrade your data. 
The SDU tool and help are available in the Downloads section on the[ ](http://support.intergraph.com/)NetWorks Core[ page on the Support page](http://support.intergraph.com/). 
  1. Log in to the site using the credentials supplied by Support.
  2. Click Downloads. 
  3. Type SDU in the Knowledge Search box. In the box on the right, type G/Technology. You can select NetWorks Core (Product Family) from the list after you start typing) and click the search icon. 
  4. Select the most recent version (for example, 01.00.1501), from the Results list. 


For complete information about using the SDU tool, see the Spatial Data Upgrade Help (SpatialDataUpgrade.chm) installed by default in the \Program Files\Intergraph\GTechnologySpatialDataUpgrade\Program folder after you install the tool. The help is also available before you install the tool in the \Main\program files\Intergraph\GTechnologySpatialDataUpgrade\Program folder in the zip file. 
To upgrade to NetWorks Core version 10.2.1 from a version before 10.0, you must first upgrade to Oracle 11.2.0.4 or higher and upgrade your data in the new database model. The process of upgrading the data makes two major changes to your database: 
  * Moves your database from geometry that is stored in *_SDOGEOM tables to geometry that is stored in SDO_GEOMETRY columns. 
  * Changes the G3E_GEOMETRY column of the graphic component table from type CHAR(1) to SDO_GEOMETRY and populates that column value with the SDO_GEOMETRY object. 


You can upgrade your data from the Oracle spatial relational model to the Oracle spatial object model using the Spatial Data Upgrade (SDU) Tool. Just follow the instructions in the [Spatial Data Upgrade (SDU) Workflow](javascript:;) in the Spatial Data upgrade Help. 
Before upgrading from the Oracle Spatial Relational Model to the Oracle Spatial Object Model, become familiar with all phases of this workflow as shown below. 
  * [Preparation Phase](javascript:;): In this phase, the administrator plans the upgrade steps and prepares the database for upgrading to the Oracle Spatial Object Model. 
  * [Validate Phase](javascript:;): This phase is an iterative process where the administrator validates the metadata, data model, and geometry before proceeding to the Stage phase. 
  * [Stage Phase](javascript:;): This phase is an iterative process where geometry in *_SDOGEOM tables is upgraded to objects of type SDO_GEOMETRY. From this phase, you can return to the validation phase as often as necessary until the data are ready to Merge. 
  * [Merge Phase](javascript:;): In this phase, the administrator locks users out of the system, validates and upgrades the final geometries, and merges all the resultant SDO_GEOMETRY objects back into the graphic component tables. 
  * [Finalization Phase](javascript:;): After the data upgrade is complete, there are a few things left to do.

### Work Space Version Compatibility
In general, work spaces created with any version of NetWorks Core can be opened and read by any later version of NetWorks Core. The opposite is not true, however. If you save a work space with version 10.2, you typically are not able to open that work space with version 10.1. This applies to Plotting as well asDesigner/Analyst users. 
If you intend to support users running different versions of NetWorks Core you need to be careful that work spaces used by clients running an older version are not overwritten by users running a later version. See the [Database-Software Version Compatibility](javascript:;) topic for more information. 
Although version incompatibilities are not introduced by every new version of NetWorks Core, you should assume that they might be.

## Validation Errors

### Attribute Validation Interface Errors
The circuit number validation failed for the component <Component name> related to the component <related component name>.
Cause: The software compares the circuit identifier values in the current feature and the related features. If one of the attribute values in the active or related feature is Null, this error is generated. If both values are Null, the validation passes. To accommodate switchable features, two fields typically contain the circuit identifiers. For non-switchable features, only one attribute must be populated. It must match the identifier of the related feature. For switchable features, both attributes must be populated and must match the identifiers in the related features. 
Priority: Configurable 
Phase Validation failed for feature <feature name> <FID> with phase <phase value>.
Cause: The software compares the phases found in the active feature with the phases found in each of the related features at each node. Validation passes if all of the phases of the active feature are found in the phases of related features at a given node. If a phase is not found in the union of the phases of the related features for at least one node, the error is reported. Neutral phases (N or n) are ignored. 
Priority:
The simple copy validation failed for the component <Component name> related to the component <related component name>.
Cause: The software compares the value in the current feature to the related feature. If one or both contain Null values, this error is generated. If the values are not Null but do not match, this error is generated. 
Priority: Configurable

### Limits to Validating Features
NetWorks Core [validates feature data](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/bkC5QQFQjQ0pm0E~HMXffg) using the validate commands, as well as when features are posted to the database. During the [validation](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/3OxdQ7_DWQa~vV8En6VvMw) or [posting of a job](javascript:;), validation software gathers information about each feature edited in the job, as well as the features related to those in the job, whether or not those related features have been edited. Normally, the software checks the feature data against constraints set in metadata and reports discrepancies to the user. 
Validating features is a complicated process that can run into these limitations:
  * Memory consumption limits
  * Internal program constraints.


For this reason, NetWorks Core software divides the features up into groups so that only a portion is processed at a time. To specify how many features are to be validated in a group, use the general parameter [ValidationGroupSize](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/eDk~4toba4mPAMjGVowX~g). 
It is slightly possible to surpass internal program limits with the use of this parameter. Each group of features, plus each feature’s related features, cannot surpass 32,767. If this happens, a message displays to the user. To avoid this message, take one of the following actions: 
  * Set the ValidationGroupSize general parameter to a lower value.
  * Use the Partial Post command to interactively post and validate smaller sets of features from the job at a time. 
  * Post the job to master using the LTT_POST package, and then use the [BatchValidation.exe](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/ZDpy9VMt3TffCTvfGKMCYQ) to validate the larger set of data at one time.

[Validation Errors](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/nv8qth0e6HLUvXkTfwTVkw)

The feature is not part of the connected model and a connection is required.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifiers are zero, null or the component does not exist and [G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_ENFORCEMENT](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/qtGEWVGTKGMEyq1xdmQpYg) = 1. 
Priority: P1 
The feature is not part of the connected model and a connection is optional.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifiers are zero, null or the component does not exist and G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 0. 
Priority: P4 
The connectivity (node identifier value) is invalid or no longer exists in the database.
Cause: Compares the node identifiers in the connectivity component and the metadata parameter. This error is reported if the node identifier is not found in the connectivity table. You can get this error in the Post Partial command because the related feature is not part of the partial posting operation. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = 1 Else P4 
This feature has more than one other feature connected at node <node identifier>. Only one feature should be connected to this node.
Cause: Determines the number of feature pairs that share this node identifier. This only occurs in the pipeline connectivity model. This error is reported if more than one pair is found. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
The node 1 and node 2 connectivity fields for <feature name> <feature identifier> have different identifier values. One node features should have identical node 1 and node 2 identifier values.
Cause: A one node device has two node values. Both node values should be identical for one node devices. 
Priority: : P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
The distance between <feature class> <feature identifier> and <feature class> <feature identifier> is <actual distance>. This exceeds the MaxOffset value of <maximum offset value>.
Cause: Compares the geometry of the active feature to the related features. This error is reported if the distance between endpoints and related features is greater than the value specified in G3E_NODEEDGECONNECTIVITY.G3E_MAXOFFSET. 
Priority: Uses the value specified in G3E_OFFSETVALIDATIONPRIORIT. If this is NULL, uses the value for the General Parameter OffsetValidationPriority. 
The node value <node identifier> that connects <active feature name-FID> and <related feature name-FID> is not on graphically adjacent endpoints.
Cause: Assumes that node identifier one of a linear corresponds to the start point of the geometry, and that node identifier two corresponds to the endpoint of the geometry. This test compares the distance between the expected points to the actual related features. This error is reported if the beginning point of the line is not a shorter distance to the related feature at node identifier one than the endpoint of the line. This check is performed to help ensure the presentation of data in the [graphical node-edge connectivity dialog](https://hexagonppm.fluidtopics.net/r/_OIjXZnxNqnWnqZEcXwqLA/VfbJLUnk4lGa5XMUeX83Jw) is logical and understandable. Even though the node identifiers may be reversed from this definition, the software properly traces the network, but the graphical node-edge connectivity presentation may be difficult to understand. 
Priority: P5 or the value specified in G3E_ADD_REL_PARAMS_OPTABLE for the entry <RNO>-end pointValidationPriority 
The node 1 and node 2 connectivity fields for <feature name and identifier> have different identifier values. Single-node features should have identical node 1 and node 2 identifier values.
Cause: Compares the values in the node 1 and node 2 identifier fields in the connectivity component for the feature. This error is reported if these values are not the same for a single-node feature. 
Priority: P1 if G3E_ENFORCEMENT = (1) Else P4 
Phase Validation failed for feature <feature name> <feature identifier> with phase <phase value>
Cause: This error is reported if phase validation is defined for the feature being validated and the phase values are out of range with related features. 
Priority: P4

Cause: Attempts to locate the feature specified by the FNO/FID values stored in the relationship data of the active feature. The feature cannot be found. This may be the result of a post partial operation that does not include the related feature.

Edge feature not connected in Node-Ordered Connectivity
Cause: No node ordered connectivity record exists in this feature. 
Priority: P1 
The edge feature has more than one connectivity record in the Node-Ordered Connectivity model. It should have just one.
Cause: There is more than one node ordered connectivity record for this feature 
Priority: P1 
The edge feature is not connected for <Node Ordered Connectivity relationship instance name>.
